The amount will be paid in four equal payments of $3,828,785.04, due March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31, 2026.
Since a provincial reform came into force on July 1, 2024, Québec pays municipal judges and cities reimburse it for these advances.
The payment is authorized "subject to" conditions, because it is an estimate: the ministère will send the actual amount owed for 2026 no later than February 1, 2027.
The expense will be funded from the 2026 operating budget of the Service des affaires juridiques and paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
Paying on time makes it possible to avoid the interest set out in the provincial regulation.
City council adopts a new by-law governing the supplementary-plus retirement benefits plan for the City's professional employees (architects, legal professionals, general professionals, scientists).
This by-law replaces By-law 94-119, adopted in 1994, and applies retroactively to January 1, 2010.
It brings the text into line with the pension plan harmonization agreement reached in 2010 with the four professional unions, which came into force on January 1, 2011.

Certain professionals who transferred their entitlements from the white-collar plan to the professionals' plan before 2010 will receive a lump sum to offset the effect of this change; they are named in Schedule 1 of the by-law.
The City covers the full cost of the benefits and the plan's administration fees.
The document states that the delay in adoption did not deprive members of their benefits, which were already paid out under the agreement, and that this matter has no additional financial impact.
City council is amending the by-law governing the pension plan for the City's white-collar employees, retroactive to January 1, 2014.

The City is restoring the automatic indexing of retirees' pensions, which had been suspended since January 1, 2017, and will pay the retroactive amounts for the period from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2024.
This restoration follows a 2020 Superior Court judgment, upheld on appeal in 2023, and the Supreme Court's dismissal of the applications for leave to appeal in April 2024.
The amendment is based on an agreement reached on November 1, 2024 between the City and the Syndicat des fonctionnaires municipaux de Montréal (SCFP).
The by-law also incorporates the new requirements of the Québec regulation on the funding of municipal pension plans, which came into force on February 22, 2024.
Active and inactive members of the plan received a notice of amendment and a notice of consultation on the use of surplus assets on October 10, 2025.
The decision summary states that no financial aspect applies; the by-law will then be registered with Retraite Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency.
City council is amending the by-law governing the pension plan for the Ville de Montréal's foremen, retroactive to January 1, 2014.

The amendment restores the indexing of pension benefits that had been suspended since January 1, 2017, after the courts ruled that the suspension was unconstitutional (Cour supérieure in 2020, Cour d'appel in 2023, refusal to hear an appeal by the Cour suprême in 2024).

The restoration follows an agreement reached on November 7, 2024 with the Association des contremaîtres municipaux employés par la Ville de Montréal, approved by the executive committee on December 4, 2024.
The by-law also incorporates the requirements of the new provincial regulation on the funding of municipal pension plans, in force since February 22, 2024.
The amortization period for actuarial deficits will gradually go from 15 to 10 years, with a 5-year transition, for valuations after December 31, 2023.
Active and inactive members of the plan received a notice of amendment and a notice of consultation on November 18, 2025.
The by-law will then be registered with Retraite Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency. The document states that there is no applicable financial aspect.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $19,576 to the Table de concertation du Faubourg Saint-Laurent to run activities at the Kahéhtaien Jardin Lumb collective garden, in the Quartier chinois.
The agreement runs until November 2, 2026, and the money comes from the borough's Fonds de soutien financier en développement social.
The "Cultiver ensemble" project includes monthly workshops, activities with Projets autochtones du Québec (PAQ) and summer programming.
According to the file, the garden's activities (gardening workshops, shared meals, artistic activities, ceremonies) draw 30 to 80 people per gathering.
The garden is located on city-owned land at the corner of rue Viger and rue De Bullion, in front of the Hôpital chinois de Montréal, lent free of charge by the Ville until December 1, 2026.
In 2025, it was the Table ronde du Quartier chinois that ran the garden, with $5,000 from the urban agriculture program.
The organization must report back to the borough and follow the visibility protocol set out in the agreement.

The urban agglomeration council adopts an accompanying document ("Tableau indicatif des modifications") related to by-law RCG 14-029-8, which amended the Schéma d'aménagement de l'agglomération de Montréal.
This document confirms that the cities and boroughs of the agglomeration do not have to change their urban planning plans and by-laws to comply with this amendment to the Schéma.

The amendment to the Schéma responded to a request from the ministre des Affaires municipales, in order to incorporate the government's housing orientation (access to quality, available and affordable housing).
The amended by-law came into force on November 3, 2025; it adds a diagnosis, an indicator and housing targets to the Schéma.
The document and the by-law will be sent to partner organizations.
No financial impact.
The executive committee approves a confidentiality agreement between the Ville de Montréal and VIA HFR – VIA TGF inc. (Alto), the promoter of the high-speed train project between Québec and Toronto.
The agreement sets out the rules for exchanging the confidential information needed to plan the project and fit it into Montréal's public property.
Alto will be allowed to pass on the information it receives from the City to the private consortium Projet Cadence Rail s.e.c., which is in charge of development, design and construction.
Without this agreement, the City says it could neither share nor receive the information required to plan the project.
Since the funding comes mostly from federal public funds, Québec had to authorize the signing through an order in council (1495-2025) adopted in December 2025.
Alto will hold a three-month public consultation from January to March 2026; in Montréal, open house sessions will take place on January 21 and 22, 2026 at the Y des femmes, 1275 av. De Lorimier.
According to the document, the first segment of the network will link Montréal to Ottawa, with construction expected to begin in 2029.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is cancelling its February 3, 2026 decision, which had upheld the refusal of the demolition permit for the commercial building at 13300, rue Sherbrooke Est, in Pointe-aux-Trembles.
The demolition is to make way for the construction of a new fast-food establishment.

The director of Développement du territoire et des études techniques is authorized to sign an agreement with the company 9371-2511 Québec inc. (Groupe Immobilier Taillefer) setting out the conditions of the project.
Conditions imposed: a visual and sound barrier along the entire southern boundary of the property, trees and shrubs in the back yard, and a final layout that complies with the attached site plan.

The file was the subject of a legal dispute: after checking with the Service des affaires juridiques, the borough concludes that the company's arguments would lead to a contentious legal debate before the courts.
Three notices of opposition from residents had been submitted in August 2025, before the demolition committee's decision.
In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, residential buildings will no longer need a permit to put the snow from their parking lot or driveway on public property.

The conditions that came with the former permit now apply at all times: the snow is still a nuisance if it blocks a fire hydrant, a bus stop, a driveway entrance or the area around an intersection, or if it interferes with traffic or visibility.
The snow will have to be put out before the snow-loading operation begins.
Industrial, commercial and institutional buildings must still get a permit, because of the larger volumes of snow.
Notice of motion and tabling of the draft by-law on February 2, 2026, with adoption planned for March 9, 2026.
No financial impact is expected in this file.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is closing 28 loan by-laws adopted between 2001 and 2020, because the projects they covered are finished.
These loans were used for road repairs, lighting and signage, park development, protecting and improving buildings, as well as buying vehicles and computer equipment.
Each by-law leaves an unused loan balance, which cannot be used for anything else: the authorized amounts are therefore reduced to the amount actually borrowed.
The borough is asking the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation to erase these balances from its register and will send it the resolution.
The borough states that this closing has no financial impact and does not reduce the budget funds available under the capital works program.
The borough of Outremont is changing who holds the vice-chair position on its comité consultatif d'urbanisme (CCU), the committee that reviews urban planning files.
Councillor Mercedez Plante is appointed vice-chair and member of the CCU, for a renewable two-year term beginning on the day of her appointment, as of February 3, 2026.
The appointment of Mayor Caroline Braun as vice-chair and member of the CCU, adopted on November 18, 2025, is repealed.
The chair and vice-chair positions on the CCU come with additional annual pay set out in the by-law on the remuneration of Outremont's elected officials.
The resolution will be sent to the Service du greffe of the Ville de Montréal.
The borough of Outremont is shortening the term of an elected official sitting on the urban planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme, CCU) to one year instead of two.
This one-year term may be renewed four times, for a maximum of four years.
The two-year rule stays in place for the committee's resident members.
The committee still has 10 members: 3 elected officials (including the mayor) and 7 residents, 5 of whom are professionals in urban planning or related fields.
Timeline: notice of motion and tabling of the draft by-law on February 3, 2026, adoption on March 10, 2026, coming into force in March 2026.
The borough of Outremont is asking the Directeur de l'état civil to designate five elected officials as "competent officiants" for civil marriages and civil unions.
The people concerned: Mayor Caroline Braun and councillors Amélie Cliche, Maude Choko, Mercedez Plante and Georgia Haloulos.
These elected officials will be able to officiate at marriages and civil unions in the territory of Outremont only, and for the duration of their term of office.
The Directeur de l'état civil must then assign each of them a unique identification number to be written on marriage or civil union declarations.
The step is voluntary: the five elected officials have expressed the intention of being appointed.
No amount of money is attached to the decision.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is refusing to authorize the use "collective housing for care and services" at 3794-3796, avenue Girouard, in the Notre-Dame-de-Grâce district.
Since 2014, the building has housed a private residence for vulnerable people living with mental health disorders, with a capacity of 16 people in 14 rooms, without an occupancy certificate.
The Direction cites a history of cleanliness problems (vermin, bed bugs), nuisances and a non-compliant fire system, found during inspections since January 2025.
It also considers that the project, in its current form, does not contribute to the friendliness or the quality of the urban environment, for lack of suitable outdoor landscaping.
The urban planning advisory committee had nevertheless recommended approval on January 15, 2025, on the condition of a maximum of 16 people housed.
If the application is refused, the dozen residents still living there will have to be relocated in collaboration with the CIUSSS.
A public notice appeared in the newspapers on January 16, 2026 and a sign was posted on the building on January 15, 2026; the resolution is scheduled to be adopted on February 2, 2026.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is refusing the work to replace the canopy above the front steps of the semi-detached house at 4032, avenue de Hampton (Notre-Dame-de-Grâce district).
The owner wanted to change the size and shape of the canopy, in a way that differs from what a permit already granted in November 2023 allowed.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had given a favourable opinion on August 13, 2025, but on the condition that the plans already approved by the 2023 permit be followed.
On September 19, 2025, the applicant replied that he did not wish to comply with that condition.
The Division de l'urbanisme finds that the new application does not meet the criteria of the planning by-law that apply to this heritage sector classified as "significatif à normes B".
The borough council can only approve or refuse the plans; it cannot require changes as a condition.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is authorizing the "care and services housing" use for the duplex at 3479-3481, avenue Walkley (Loyola district), in a residential area zoned for 2 dwellings.
The authorization brings into compliance a residence that has already been operating since 2022 without an occupancy certificate.
The residence houses people aged 16 and over who have functional limitations or mental health disorders, referred by the Institut Douglas, CLSCs or CIUSSSs on the island of Montréal.
The authorization comes with one condition: a maximum of 9 people housed in the property as a whole (7 rental units).
The services offered include meals, housekeeping, laundry, help with medication, recreation and security; 3 part-time employees and at least 2 volunteers work there.

The urban planning advisory committee unanimously recommended the application on February 12, 2025; a public notice appeared in the newspapers on January 16, 2026 and a sign was posted on site on January 15, 2026.
There is no financial aspect attached to this file.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is amending its planning by-law to allow a new accessory use of "extensive recreation" in the zone of the cimetière Notre-Dame-des-Neiges.
This change opens the door to an immersive outdoor multimedia night trail on the cemetery site, on mont Royal.
The project comes from the Fabrique de la paroisse Notre-Dame, the owner of the cemetery, with the company Moment Factory; the installations are described as temporary and reversible.
In a letter dated April 16, 2026, the cemetery committed to monitoring disturbances to wildlife during operations and to applying corrective measures.
The public consultation of February 18, 2026 drew 0 citizens and 12 representatives of the applicant; there were no questions or comments, and no referendum request was filed.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité (heritage) must also issue an authorization under the Cultural Heritage Act.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is authorizing the business Piano Vertu, at 5223, boulevard Décarie, to enlarge its mezzanine (35 m² maximum) and to set up piano teaching rooms.
The building, built in 2022 in the former théâtre Snowdon, has 56 housing units and 2 commercial spaces.
Three practice rooms will be set up under the existing mezzanine; they will have to be soundproofed according to the construction specified in the resolution.

The authorization allows two planning rules to be set aside: the maximum height of 6 storeys (the building will go to 7 storeys, with no change to the exterior) and the ban on a music studio next to a housing unit.
An acoustic study was carried out; the Direction states that no noise should be audible outside the space.
At the public consultation on February 18, 2026, no citizen came forward and no request for a referendum was received.

The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is submitting its 2025 annual report on its use of the power to authorize residential projects that do not comply with its urban planning rules (section 93 of the Québec housing act passed in 2024).
Three authorizations were granted in 2025, for a total of 365 social or affordable housing units, all awaiting confirmation of funding.
Project at 5460, avenue Connaught: demolition of a 3-storey institutional building and construction of a 4-storey residential building (92 units).
Project at 7330-7380, chemin de la Côte-Saint-Luc / 5421-5499, rue Robert-Burns: demolition of a commercial building and construction of an 18-storey building (203 units).
Project at 6470-6490, rue Sherbrooke Ouest / 3383, boulevard Cavendish: construction of an 8-storey building (70 units).
The exemptions mainly concern height, lot coverage, permitted uses and the requirement to have businesses on the ground floor. No application was refused.
The borough secretary will send the report to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing; the report will be published on the City's website.
The City is awarding a contract worth $1,260,873.34 (taxes included) to Innotex inc. to supply 300 firefighting suits to Montréal firefighters.
The suits will be used by the 120 new recruits of the Service de sécurité incendie (2 suits each), plus 60 suits kept for emergencies.
Innotex was the only company to bid: 5 organizations had obtained the tender documents, and 3 declined to take part (contract management, delivery times, specifications considered too restrictive).
The price accepted is $143,327.83 (10%) lower than the City's estimate, which was $1,404,201.17.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration, since fire safety is an agglomeration responsibility.
The previous agreements with Innotex ($4,808,139.52 in 2025) have been fully spent; since standard NFPA 1971 will be replaced by NFPA 1970, the City cannot sign a multi-year agreement for now.
The purchase order is to be issued in February 2026, and Innotex's performance will be evaluated.
The borough secretary of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal files the certificate for the register held from January 19 to 23, 2026 on loan by-law 2025-13 for $2,000,000.
No signatures were recorded during the register; 6,532 were needed to trigger a referendum.
The by-law is therefore deemed approved by the qualified voters.
The loan will be used for work to repair and protect the borough's municipal buildings, as part of the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
It also covers professional fees, studies, design and supervision of the work.
The term of the loan will not exceed 20 years, and the costs are borne by the borough's residents.
Next steps: approval by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation, then a public notice that it has come into force.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $44,315 to 10 non-profit organizations to carry out 11 activity projects in parks and public squares in 2026.
The activities must be free and open to everyone, spread over the four seasons and across the whole territory.
The amounts range from $2,400 to $6,315 per project, with a maximum of $7,500 per project; the Club de Marche des Loisirs Sportifs CDN/NDG receives the largest share ($6,315).
Among the funded projects: Célébration du 150e à NDG, Exposition historique, ItalFest, Les bancs racontent NDG, Baojardins, Fête de bienvenue aux voisins, Festivités culturelles.
The projects run from January to December 2026; 22 applications had been received during the call for applications in the fall of 2025.
The program, launched as a pilot project in 2024-2025 ($200,000 for 22 projects), is being renewed for one year.

The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council is authorizing organizations and event organizers to occupy public property (parks, squares, streets) for a list of public events submitted at the February 2, 2026 meeting.
These events are local in scale: community, sports, cultural, commemorative or festive events, or fundraisers, and they are free and open to everyone.

The City is temporarily setting aside certain rules: noise from sound equipment outdoors, street closures or slowed traffic, the sale and consumption of alcohol, and the sale of food and promotional items.
Noise is limited to 80 dBA measured 35 metres from the sound equipment, and alcohol must be served in plastic containers, on the event site only.
Each organizer must submit their civil liability insurance endorsement and the other required documents no later than 72 hours before the event in order to receive their authorization.
The borough's support costs are taken from operating budgets; additional costs are paid by the organizers.
The City will pay $125,167.62 (taxes included) to Hydro-Québec for unpaid rent from 2014 to 2025 on 19 pieces of land it occupies within power line rights-of-way.

These pieces of land are used for bike paths, parks, community gardens, parking lots and access to the river, in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Saint-Léonard, Anjou, Ville-Marie and Saint-Laurent.
Hydro-Québec initially claimed about $1.9M based on market value; after negotiation, it applied the rate schedule from the Union des municipalités du Québec–Hydro-Québec agreement.
As soon as the payment is received, Hydro-Québec will bring the balance of the 19 files down to zero.
Starting January 1, 2026, new leases will be negotiated for these 19 rights-of-way, using the same rate principles, and presented file by file to the decision-making bodies.
According to the document, without this agreement, Hydro-Québec would no longer allow access to these facilities and the City would have to dismantle them.
The expense is covered by the central city, out of the operating budget of the Service de la stratégie immobilière; the amounts were already set aside in 2023 and 2024.

The borough of Ville-Marie is changing the rules for refunding the cash guarantee required from the developer for the landscaping of the buildings at 2095-2181 avenue Papineau, 2005-2093 avenue Goulet and 2100, rue Cartier.
The site is divided into four sectors: the guarantee can be released in the amount of $188,130 for sector 1, $117,581 for sector 2, $117,581 for sector 3 and $47,035 for sector 4.
Each amount can now be returned as soon as the landscaping work in the sector concerned is finished, without waiting for the work in the other sectors to be completed.
If the work in one or more sectors does not substantially comply with the permits, the developer must first submit a new guarantee letter equivalent to the amounts for the sectors involved.
The developer must still submit, as soon as the first permit application is made, an overall landscaping plan along with a cash guarantee estimated by a professional.
The changes were presented at the public consultation meeting of December 10, 2025, where no one asked any questions about this project.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing the Y des Femmes, at 1275, avenue De Lorimier, to install a sign somewhere other than where the planning by-law requires.
The illuminated sign, made of separate letters, measures 3.79 m² (9.6 m x 0.39 m), is 8.9 cm deep and would be placed 11.9 m above the ground.
It would be placed on the side of the building facing rue Sainte-Catherine, between the third-floor and fourth-floor windows, rather than above the ground floor.

The organization mainly occupies the second and third floors of the building (phase 2 of the Esplanade Cartier project, built in 2022); according to the borough, the location required by the by-law does not reflect this occupancy and causes serious harm to the applicant.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on December 11, 2025, by a majority, with one dissenting voice.
Next steps: publication of a public notice, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The borough of Verdun is receiving a $5,000 grant, non-taxable, from Sport et loisir de l'île de Montréal (SLIM).
The money comes from the "Ça bouge sur l'eau – Été 2025" program and is for the "Prêt de kayaks et de planches à pagaie" event.
The grant application was accepted on August 26, 2025.
The executive committee must amend the City's budget so that Verdun can spend this amount; the borough's funding allocation is increasing by $5,000.
With this money, the borough is enhancing its water sports programming and offering introductory kayaking and paddleboarding activities to day camps.
The Verdun borough council adopted the request unanimously on December 9, 2025.
The borough of Verdun is authorizing three events on public property, with exemptions from its by-laws on the occupancy of public property, traffic, parking, nuisances and temporary sales.

The Société de développement commercial Wellington is receiving an "agility order" to hold activities on rue Wellington, between boulevard LaSalle and 6e Avenue, for a maximum of 25 days between March 1, 2026 and March 1, 2027, including parc des Madelinots (3651, boulevard LaSalle).

The 14th Cabane Panache will be held on rue Wellington between rue de l'Église and rue Willibrord: street closure from March 16, 2026 at 6 a.m. to March 24, 2026 at 6 p.m., with setup and takedown from March 9 to 27.
The Cabane Panache gatherings will take place on March 19 (5 p.m. to 9 p.m.), March 20 (5 p.m. to 10 p.m.), March 21 (11 a.m. to 6 p.m.) and March 22, 2026 (11 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
The Éthel parking lot (no. 438) will be reserved from March 9 to 27, 2026: 30 spaces, plus 30 additional spaces from March 16 to 24.
The borough will hold a Disco Patin at parc Willibrord (1018, rue Willibrord), on a Saturday or a Sunday between February 14 and March 8, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.
The events are free; services provided by the City are billed according to the 2026 rates by-law, with some services possibly provided free of charge.

The City orders the acquisition, by expropriation or otherwise, of five parcels of land along rue Jean-Talon Est, at the intersections of boulevard Lacordaire and boulevard Langelier, in Saint-Léonard.
The parcels are small: from 3.9 m² to 156.4 m², for a total of about 295 m².
A spending of $1,520,000, plus taxes, is authorized; a maximum amount of $1,595,810, net of rebate, will be funded by a loan by-law and paid 100% by the central city.

The land will be used for the redevelopment of rue Jean-Talon Est: a new street layout for an express bike network (REV), wider sidewalks and car traffic, as well as an underground urban utility network.
The project is tied to the extension of the metro's blue line, near the future Césira-Parisotto and Madeleine-Parent stations.
Planned timeline: expropriation notice in the summer of 2026, taking possession in the first quarter of 2027, and construction work from 2027 to 2031.
The Service des affaires juridiques is mandated to handle the proceedings, and the chief land surveyor is authorized to sign the cadastral documents.
The City is giving up on collecting $97,344.88 (plus any outstanding balance) claimed from Placements Sergakis inc. and is writing the debt off its books.
The amount was for fees for temporarily occupying public property after the fire of October 22, 2022 at 4359, rue Saint-Jacques.
The Service des finances had ordered collection efforts on April 9, 2024; the reviews concluded that there were major difficulties in proving the claim.
The City will not take legal action, also citing the resources needed to prepare for and hold a trial.
The write-off applies to account 26-277928-1 and is charged to the borough of Le Sud-Ouest.
The decision falls to the borough council of Le Sud-Ouest.
The City is asking the Government of Canada for money from the Active Transportation Fund for five projects to build facilities for cyclists and pedestrians.

The five areas covered: rue Prieur Est (from Saint-Firmin to the borough boundary), avenue de l'Esplanade (from Legendre to Louvain), rue de Terrebonne (from Saint-Ignatius to Girouard), avenue Émile-Journault (from Henri-Julien to Papineau) and rue Legendre (from Lajeunesse to Meilleur).
Eligible expenses total $468,369 and the grant requested comes to 60% of that amount, or up to $281,021.
The City commits to paying the share of the costs not covered by the federal grant.
The director of land use planning and development is designated to sign the agreement and the follow-up documents.
Projects funded by this fund must be completed no later than March 31, 2030.
According to the document, these projects include greening and street safety measures, particularly at intersections.
The executive committee authorizes the City to apply for grants from Québec for three cycling projects, through two programs of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
Project 1: bike path on rue Ernest-Anctil, rue des Pyrénées and rue des Équinoxes (Bois-Francs area), cost of $1.5M, grant requested of $500,000.
Project 2: sustainable mobility corridor on boulevard Henri-Bourassa, cost of $14.8M, grant requested of $1M.
Project 3: bike path on rue Guy, between Sainte-Catherine and William, cost of $2.15M, grant requested of $1.6M.
The City commits to paying at least 50% of eligible expenses and 100% of non-eligible expenses, out of the budgets of the Direction de la planification et de la mise en valeur du territoire.
The applications were already sent to the ministère before the November 26 deadline; the resolution is being sent to the ministère on January 9, 2026 to complete the files.
The director of the Direction de la planification et de la mise en valeur du territoire is authorized to sign the documents and agreements with the ministère.
The City is closing a lane that is not open to traffic, located southeast of 1re Rue between 55e and 56e Avenue, in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.
The four adjoining owners, who already partly occupy the lane, will receive the land free of charge; all of them said they were in favour.
The transferred areas range from 36.9 m² to 74.7 m², for a total of 223 m², at addresses on 55e and 56e Avenue.
The City is keeping an easement on these lots for telecommunications and energy distribution installations.
The process began with a request from a resident who wanted to acquire the lane next to his property.
The City will now be able to collect property taxes on the transferred lots and will no longer have to manage the lane.
The city clerk will publish the notice of adoption in a daily newspaper and serve it on each adjoining owner.
The Ville de Montréal is transferring, free of charge, four leftover portions of a closed lane to the adjoining owners, south of rue Sherbrooke between 6e and 7e Avenue, in Lachine.
The transfer is made without payment, under the Programme d'acquisition de ruelles non requises par la Ville (program for acquiring lanes the city does not need).
Before the municipal merger, Lachine had sold the lane halves to the adjoining owners for $1; four owners had not done so and today occupy those pieces of land.
The transfer legalizes the encroachment and the occupation of the land, and will allow the city to collect property taxes on these lots.
An easement is created on two of the lots for telecommunications and energy distribution.
Consulted by petition, three of the four owners said they were in favour and one did not reply; the required two-thirds threshold was reached.
The clerk will publish the notice of adoption in a daily newspaper and serve it on each adjoining owner.
City council is renewing the membership of the Conseil du patrimoine de Montréal, the body that advises the City on heritage conservation and promotion.
Giovanni (John) Diodati, a built heritage conservation architect and already a regular member, becomes vice-chair for three years starting March 25, 2026.
Jean-François Sabourin, an urban planner, moves from substitute member to regular member on March 25, 2026, until the end of his first term on September 17, 2027.

Nelly Charpentier, an architect specializing in the restoration of heritage buildings, becomes a substitute member for a first three-year term, starting March 25, 2026. Her application came from the pool of candidates set up in 2024.
Philippe Lupien, an architect and landscape architect, has his term as a regular member renewed for three years starting April 18, 2026. This term cannot be renewed.
Ève Wertheimer is leaving the vice-chair position on March 25, 2026, and council thanks her for her contribution.
Members' pay is covered by the budget of the Service du greffe; no amount is specified.
The City is extending the verification period granted to the buyers of the Îlot Voyageur Sud by 12 months, until June 25, 2027.
The building involved is located at 505, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, in Ville-Marie: 7,062 m² with a building, sold for $20,000,000 payable with interest, plus applicable taxes.
The buyers are 9536-1135 Québec inc. (Mondev) and Utile Développement.

The buyers have already estimated the costs of asbestos decontamination, issued a call for tenders for the demolition, obtained a zoning change and carried out a title search, but the remaining time is not enough.
Coordination work with the STM is underway (analyses, concept studies, drilling) to determine the scope of the work and assess the costs.
A first addendum had already pushed the deadline from December 25, 2025 to June 25, 2026; all other conditions of the promise remain unchanged.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is buying a table of ten tickets, at a cost of $1,600 including taxes, for the 40th Grand Prix du Conseil des arts de Montréal.
The event will take place on April 2, 2026 at the Palais des congrès de Montréal.

The tickets will be used by local elected officials, the borough director, representatives of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social, as well as people from the area's cultural community (artists, organizations, presenters, producers).
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough takes part in this event every year: $1,550 in 2025 and $1,450 in 2024, also for ten tickets.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is asking the Minister of Justice to designate four elected officials as officiants for marriages and civil unions.
The people concerned: borough mayor Stephanie Valenzuela and councillors Émilie Brière (Côte-des-Neiges), Milany Thiagarajah (Darlington) and Alexandre Teodoresco (Loyola).
Once appointed, they will be able to officiate marriages within the territory of the Ville de Montréal, for the duration of their term only.
The request is needed because the authorization ends with the elected term; Stephanie Valenzuela changed roles by becoming borough mayor in the election of November 2, 2025.
Peter McQueen (Notre-Dame-de-Grâce) and Sonny Moroz (Snowdon), who were re-elected to the same position, do not have to be designated again.
The resolution will be sent to the Minister, and then the Directeur de l'état civil will assign an authorization number to each elected official.
No financial impact is expected in this file.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the Centre culturel afro-canadien de Montréal to expand and occupy the former École des beaux-arts, at 3450, rue Saint-Urbain, which has been vacant since 2009.
The building will be able to host cultural and community uses (museum, performance hall, gallery, artists' studios, offices, specialized school), with no housing at all.
Only one bar and one restaurant are allowed, limited to the ground floor and the lower level; no outdoor service except with a sidewalk café permit.
A loading area will be built on the neighbouring lot at 125, rue Sherbrooke Ouest, which means cutting down three trees bordering Place Sainte-Famille, to be replaced one for one.
Two other trees will be cut down near the future rain garden; at least 15 trees will have to be planted, transplanted or kept on the site.

Before the expansion permit is issued, the developer must acquire a neighbouring strip of land, carry out the cadastral operation and sign an easement for the loading area; an archaeological study is also required.
The authorization becomes void if the project is not started within 60 months; the second draft resolution will be followed by a referendum approval process.
The borough of LaSalle is adding $11,115 to its agreement with the organization Héritage Laurentien, raising the maximum spending from $137,288 to $148,403.
This agreement funds the Éco-quartier program in LaSalle for the year 2024 (from January 1 to December 31).
The additional amount covers costs already incurred by the organization for removing graffiti on private properties.
According to the document, requests for graffiti removal rose by 43% in 2024 compared to 2023.
Héritage Laurentien manages the 5 components of the program, including beautification and greening, which includes graffiti.
The Ville de Montréal is renewing its membership in the Fédération canadienne des municipalités (FCM) from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
It will pay a membership fee of $481,081.46, taxes included, covered entirely by the central city.
The calculation combines a base rate of $5,540 and $0.2423 per resident, for a population of 1,762,949 people.
The fee goes from $465,068.55 last year to $481,081.46 this year.
The FCM brings together more than 2,000 members and carries municipal requests to the federal government (public transit, infrastructure, affordable housing, the environment).
Montréal has three designated seats on the FCM's board of directors, and the mayor sits ex officio on the Caucus des maires des grandes villes.
The invoice, dated November 18, 2025, is payable no later than March 31, 2026.

The borough of Anjou is proposing to city council that it take charge itself of the design and carrying out of the work to replace lead water service lines, on both private and public property, for the year 2026.

The work involves replacing water connections made of lead or of non-compliant materials on Place Blain, between avenue de la Roche-sur-Yon and the end of the street, by pulling, torpedoing or excavation.
Related roadwork and landscaping work is also planned on various street sections in the borough.
The central city pays in full for the work and the outside professional services; the borough covers in-house labour and incidental expenses.
Planned schedule: call for tenders in March 2026, work and supervision from May to July 2026.
The borough will have to report on the progress of the work to the Direction de la gestion des actifs and stay within the budget allocated.
The urban agglomeration council is to appoint Denis Pelletier, mayor of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, as the borough's representative on the board of directors of PME MTL Est-de-l'Île.
He replaces Lisa Christensen, who had held this seat since her appointment in 2020.
The change stems from the municipal elections of November 2, 2025, which require that a new elected official be designated.
According to the document, this seat serves to coordinate the borough's actions with those of the local economic development organization.
PME MTL Est-de-l'Île supports and finances business projects of companies in the borough.
The borough council adopted the recommendation unanimously on December 2, 2025; no amount is attached to the file.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving after the fact a $298.94 expense, taxes included.
The amount covers two tickets at $149.47 each for a Chambre de commerce de l'Est de Montréal event held on December 17, 2025.
The two tickets were used by councillors Giovanni Rapanà and Gerlando Guarraggi.
The event was the first public appearance by the mayor of Montréal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, since her election, with ministers Mélanie Joly, Christine Fréchette and Chantal Rouleau.
The expense is charged according to the financial information in the file.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing a residential redevelopment project at 90, rue Sainte-Catherine Est, under section 93 of the provincial housing act.

The project will be allowed to depart from the planning rules on minimum and maximum height, maximum density and roof greening — the amendment that was added allows, in particular, for not greening the roof of the section kept along rue Sainte-Catherine.
The entire residential portion must be carried out under a government or municipal program guaranteeing the affordability of the housing units for at least 20 years.
Before demolition, the developer must provide a quote for the conservation and restoration of the old façades and a structural reinforcement quote for the exit stairway of the building being kept.

When applying for the permit, the developer must submit a waste management study (weekly volumes, storage, collection point) and go through a project review covering the landscaping on De Bullion, the interface on rue Berger and the colour of the commercial canopy.
Demolition work must begin within 24 months of the adoption, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

At the public consultation of January 21, 2026 (about 7 people), the Comité logement Ville-Marie considered the 60 planned affordable housing units to be unaffordable for the neighbourhood's tenants and challenged the height exemptions.
Saint-Léonard is amending its by-law on building demolition to bring it in line with the City's Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050, which came into force on June 25, 2025.
More buildings will have to go before the demolition committee: schools and industrial buildings are being added to the list.
Demolition projects aimed at creating social or affordable housing will no longer go before the committee, and the list of documents they must provide is shorter.
Demolishing a heritage building or a building of heritage interest will require a heritage study carried out by a heritage consultant.
In an area of archaeological interest (a small part of parc Giuseppe-Garibaldi), a study of archaeological potential will be required.
Demolishing an industrial, public or institutional building will require a study on the reuse of materials and a plan to divert construction waste from landfill.
The minutes of the public consultation of February 11, 2026 are being filed; the borough has until June 16, 2027 to adopt all of its concordance by-laws.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is amending its by-law on specific projects (PPCMOI) to bring it into line with Montréal's Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050, in effect since June 25, 2025.
The minutes of the public consultation meeting held on February 11, 2026 are filed with the council.

New studies become mandatory for certain applications: a traffic impact study for the redevelopment of a large commercial complex, an expert study for a heritage building or a place of worship, and an archaeological potential study in the areas concerned.
A waste management plan will be required to build or enlarge a residential building of nine units or more, or a commercial, industrial, institutional or mixed-use building.

The by-law adds evaluation criteria targeting specific addresses, including houses and public buildings on rue Jarry Est, rue Dujarié, boulevard Lavoisier, and the churches Saint-Gilbert, Saint-Léonard-de-Port-Maurice, Sainte-Angèle and Saint-Léonard Seventh Day Adventist.
Before the consultation, two corrections were made to the draft: an additional criterion for large commercial complexes and the addition of the buildings' historical names in Appendix B.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for the borough to adopt all of its concordance by-laws; other sets will follow, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.

The City is awarding Orange paysagement inc. a $327,411.63 contract (taxes included) to maintain the landscaping in the middle of boulevard Pie-IX, for a total expense of up to $392,893.95 including contingencies and quantity variations.

The contract covers the planters near the SRB Pie-IX shelters and the planted medians along the centre line, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension and Montréal-Nord.
The work is done in the summer season, from May 15 to October 31, in 2026 and 2027; an extension of one season is possible, estimated at $170,528.24 (taxes included) for the renewal.
The landscaping along the sides of the boulevard remains the responsibility of the boroughs.
The expense is borne by the agglomeration and fully funded by the Autorité régionale de transport métropolitain (ARTM), which covers the extra maintenance cost tied to the SRB corridor.
Seven companies submitted bids out of eight that picked up the tender documents; four bids were rejected for administrative non-compliance.
The winning bid is 30.86% below the City's latest estimate ($473,567.08 before contingencies); the company's performance will be evaluated at the end of the contract.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding Creusage RL (9083-0126 Québec inc.) the hydro-excavation service contract, for a maximum of $233,341.76 including taxes.
The contract runs from April 7, 2026 to December 31, 2028 (about 33 months), with no possibility of extension, and with fixed prices for the whole term.
Hydro-excavation involves digging with pressurized water near electrical, gas or telecommunication lines, to avoid breaking them during water and sewer work.
The contract includes hauling and dumping the waste material at a site authorized by the ministère de l'Environnement.
Quantities planned each year: 175 hours on weekdays, 13 hours on weekends, 13 emergency hours outside regular hours and 100 tonnes of waste material.
Creusage RL was the lowest of the 5 compliant bidders in public call for tenders 25-21256; its price is 1.91% below the City's estimate.
The expense is funded by the operating budget tied to water management, spread over 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is renting a concrete saw with an operator, maintenance and accessories from VITOM Excavation inc., for a maximum of $142,798.95 including taxes.
The contract runs from April 13, 2026 to November 12, 2027, with an option to renew for the 2028 season (prices adjusted according to the CPI).
The equipment will be used for sawing for water main and sewer cuts, sidewalk and asphalt repairs, tree pits and public utilities (catch basins, manholes, valve chambers).
The borough says it does not own the equipment needed to do this work itself.
Three companies submitted bids for public call for tenders 25-21249: VITOM at $142,798.95, Formax Forage-Sciage at $168,668.33 and Construction GC-Merineau at $174,876.98.
The winning bid is $7,243.43 (4.83%) lower than the City's latest estimate.
No performance evaluation of the company is planned for this contract.
The City is awarding a contract without a call for tenders to Bentley Systems inc. for $457,415.79, taxes included.
The contract covers technical support and updates for Bentley software licences from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027.
This software is used for geomatics, mapping, land use planning, road design and wastewater network analysis.
About twenty boroughs and central departments use these products, including the Service de l'évaluation foncière.
The contract is a direct-award contract because only Bentley can provide the updates and support for its own software, which has been used at the City since 2006.
The cost is going up by 10.42% compared with last year ($414,257.32), because of a price adjustment by the manufacturer applied since April 1, 2025.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information.

The City is awarding UAP inc. a contract worth $867,933.26 (taxes included) for a cloud-based vehicle diagnostics and technical reference solution, over 36 months, with two possible extensions of 12 months each.
The tool will be used in the 26 municipal garages and will cover about 80% of the fleet, or roughly 7,000 vehicles.
The contract includes the licences, the cables and adapters, training for mechanics, and support and maintenance service.
The spending is spread out from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029: $550,424.83 in the first year, $151,746.28 in the second, and $165,762.15 in the third.
Of the 3 bids received, 2 were found not to meet the technical requirements; UAP inc. is the only compliant bidder.
The price chosen is $529,819.00 (37.91%) lower than the City's latest estimate.
The City will assess UAP inc.'s performance, and the expense falls under the by-law on mixed expenditures.
Outremont is closing a section of avenue de l'Épée to car traffic, between avenue Fairmount and a point 61 metres further north, near the Nouvelle-Querbes and Sainte-Anne - Buissonnière schools.
The closure runs from the week of May 9 to the week of June 25, 2026, then from the week of August 25 to the week of October 18, 2026; the street reopens as of October 24, 2026.
The request comes from the two schools' management, following a request from students' parents.
Concrete planters and flexible bollards will be installed; the costs are paid by the Fonds de sécurisation, with no amount specified.
The SPVM expects more congestion in the neighbourhood, especially at the intersection of l'Épée and Fairmount; the SIM raises no constraints.
Some residents will lose school bus service at their door, because the buses cannot enter the dead end; the borough strongly recommends not holding school activities there.
The borough plans to inform and survey the residents of the section and to meet with the school management.
The borough of Outremont is hiring the agency Trimax Sécurité to supply the patrollers and officers of its Sécurité publique service for $709,563.19, taxes included.
The contract covers 12 months, from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027, and is paid entirely out of the borough's operating budget.
The team includes 1 lieutenant, 1 sergeant and 1 patroller on site 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Two more patrollers are added: one to enforce the rules on the use of public property (Monday to Friday) and one for the pedestrian-only stretch of avenue Bernard (Wednesday to Sunday).
Five of the thirteen agencies that picked up the tender documents submitted a bid; Trimax offered the lowest price, 9.2% below the estimate of $781,354.58.
The document states that the contract keeps the current team in place, including the lieutenant and the sergeant who have held their positions for about fifteen years.

The City is paying an additional $1,055,231.53 to Duroking Construction (9200-2088 Québec inc.) for work to rebuild a 750 mm water main and replace service connections under rue Saint-Antoine Ouest, between Rose-de-Lima and avenue Atwater.
The contract, awarded in May 2021, thus goes from $4,814,562.49 to $5,869,794.02, taxes included.
The work, planned for 120 days, took 280 days; it was meant to secure the drinking water supply for the Saint-Henri, Ville-Émard and Côte-Saint-Paul areas, in the Sud-Ouest.
The company is claiming $2,082,984.14 before the Superior Court, since no agreement was reached with the City; some amounts are still being contested.
The authorized amount covers $435,662.65 in quantity overruns, $556,020.02 in additional work and $63,548.86 in late-payment interest.
The urban agglomeration is covering $963,248.04 of the expense and the Ville de Westmount $91,983.50, since its lead service connections were replaced on the north side of the street.
The City says it wants to pay now to stop interest from adding up and to shorten the upcoming trial.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing a reduction in the floor area of some of the units in the building at 3683-3691, rue Sainte-Catherine Est.
Purpose: to build a second exit on the 2nd and 3rd floors, leading to the back lane, in order to comply with the National Building Code.
The new exit will encroach on two units on the 2nd floor and one on the 3rd floor; according to the borough, the floor area being removed is not significant.
The units concerned have been vacant for several years and no tenant would be evicted.
No exterior work is planned on the building.
Condition imposed: the divisions between the units must follow the plans in permit application 3003453724.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on January 28, 2025; a public notice and a posting on the building will precede the adoption of the resolution.
The borough of Verdun is extending the cleaning services contract for Quai 5160 – Maison de la culture, at 5160, boulevard LaSalle, by one year.
The contract is renewed with Placement potentiel inc. for a maximum of $81,590.77, taxes not included (the company is tax-exempt).
The renewal applies retroactively from January 1 to December 31, 2026, under the same conditions as the 2023 call for tenders.
The hourly rate rises to $27.20 in 2026, an increase of 2.6% based on the consumer price index, for about 3,000 hours planned.
Placement potentiel inc. is a social economy business that employs people living with functional limitations.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Division culture, bibliothèques et développement social.

The borough of Verdun is renting the chalet in parc Arthur-Therrien (3750, boulevard Gaétan-Laberge) to the Centre d'intégration à la vie active pour les personnes vivant avec un handicap physique (CIVA), from September 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
CIVA is being relocated to Verdun because its premises in the borough of Le Sud-Ouest have been under renovation since September 2025 and the work is taking longer than expected.
The lease will bring the borough $6,627 before taxes over the 10 months.
No rent from September to December 2026, $862 in January 2027, then $1,153 a month from February to June 2027: this allows the organization to recover a credit of $4,901.40 that it had overpaid.
The borough no longer does the housekeeping for the chalet: CIVA takes care of the washrooms and the floors during the periods when it uses the building, in exchange for reduced rent.
This is a renewal: a similar lease already covered September 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is adopting changes to its zoning by-law, which has been in force since 2009.
The main change sets rules for creating a parking area in the front yard when a basement garage is removed (residential uses in classes H.2 and H.3).
A new section sets rules for small-sized parking spaces.
The definitions of "front yard" and "façade" are revised and a definition of "inner courtyard" is added, along with a list of accessories allowed in an inner courtyard.
Two sections specify when a flat or projecting sign may encroach on public property.
A public consultation meeting was held on January 21, 2026 and its minutes have been filed; the by-law contains no provisions that could be subject to a referendum.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving the plans for a proposed residential building at 15681, rue Sherbrooke Est, backing onto parc de la coulée Grou.
This is the first of the two phases of the "La petite coulée" project: a building of 4 to 8 storeys, 200 dwellings of varied types and 180 underground parking spaces.

The façades will combine brick and light cladding in various colours; equivalent materials and colours, or ones of higher quality, may be used with the agreement of the Direction du développement du territoire.
The site will be planted with 46 trees and with plants that are mostly native, along with ground covers that need little watering.
A landscaped swale in the middle of the site will carry rainwater from both phases toward the coulée Grou; the design was approved by the Service de l'eau.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on February 6, 2026; one member wanted a more subdued colour for the metal cladding on block C.
The decision allows the requested building permit to be issued; a separate file seeks to exempt the project from providing 10 parking spaces.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is exempting a construction project at 15681, rue Sherbrooke Est (district of La Pointe-aux-Prairies) from providing 20 of the 200 parking spaces required by the zoning by-law.
In exchange, the developer will pay $36,000 into the borough's parking compensation fund, an amount that may be used for parking needs elsewhere in the borough.
The project calls for 200 affordable housing units on a vacant lot on the north side of rue Sherbrooke Est, east of 80e Avenue, with 180 spaces built underground (subsoil).
According to the decision summary, removing these 20 spaces avoids digging a second underground level or enlarging the slab, which makes it possible to plant large-growth trees and keep green spaces.
The decision summary notes that the new Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité sets no minimum number of parking spaces.
The site is served by several bus routes, is about 2 km from the gare de Pointe-aux-Trembles, faces a bike path, and a grocery store is set to open 250 metres away.
The decision was scheduled to be made at the borough council meeting of March 10, 2026.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is entrusting the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie with the maintenance of lighting, signage and road markings for the year 2026.
The bill for this service is $2,358,700, funded according to the financial intervention attached to the file.
A team from Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie (the DEESM) has been carrying out this work since 2004 for the nine boroughs from the former Ville de Montréal.
The City explains that this centralized management reduces management costs and the number of interventions for the client boroughs.
If this were refused, the borough would have to turn to outside suppliers for road markings and signage.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving $40,268 to four cultural organizations to support their mission in 2026.
Each organization receives $10,067: l'Atelier d'histoire de la Pointe-aux-Trembles, la Corporation du Cinéma Station Vu, la Société Historique de Rivière-des-Prairies and le Théâtre de l'Oeil Ouvert.
The money covers the period from January 1 to December 31, 2026, after the previous agreements end on December 31, 2025.
The amounts match the 2025 contributions ($9,870 each) increased by 2%.

The money goes to activities such as the Écomusée de la Pointe at the Centre Roussin, the screening of auteur films at the salle Marie-Claire-et-Richard-Séguin, guided tours for elementary school students and cultural mediation projects.
The organizations must provide management follow-ups, an activity report and financial statements, and must acknowledge the borough's participation in their communications.
The City is renewing Groupe Écorécréo inc.'s lease at the Marché Bonsecours, at 350, rue Saint-Paul Est, for two years, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028.
The company occupies 2,265 square feet on the 3rd floor, for office use, and has been a tenant there since 2021.
The total rent collected by the City will be $105,951.51 before taxes, or $23.63 per square foot; property taxes are paid separately by the tenant.
The tenant is responsible for fit-up, maintenance, cleaning and tenant repairs; operating and energy costs are included in the rent.
The City may terminate the lease at any time with 90 days' written notice.
City departments indicate that the space is not needed for municipal purposes; operating costs projected for 2025 were about $37,000.
The City is lending the former église Sainte-Bibiane, at 5600, 12e Avenue in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal free of charge.
The space will be used as a warming centre for women experiencing homelessness, with a capacity of about 50 people.
The loan lasts 137 days, from December 15, 2025 to April 30, 2026, covering an area of about 768 square metres.
The value of the rent not charged (a real estate subsidy) is estimated at $57,076, calculated at $198/m² per year.
The City pays for the building's maintenance, repairs and operation; the organization pays for cleaning.
Part of the building will remain off-limits, as work is needed there.
The borough supports the project; the decision rests with the urban agglomeration council.

The urban agglomeration council appoints Dimitrios (Jim) Beis, mayor of the borough of Pierrefonds-Roxboro, to the board of directors of the Agence municipale de financement et de développement des centres d'urgence 911 du Québec.
He replaces Daphney Colin, who now holds another position.
This non-profit agency collects and redistributes to municipalities the proceeds of the tax paid by telephone service subscribers (landline, cellphone, Internet) to fund 911 emergency centres.

The board of directors has 6 members: two for the Union des municipalités du Québec, two for the Fédération québécoise des municipalités and two for the Ville de Montréal, in each case one elected official and one employee.
Decisions on the redistribution of the tax must be made unanimously.
There is no pay attached to this position for the city's representatives.

The City is lending one SPVM police officer, at the rank of detective sergeant, to the Gendarmerie royale du Canada for three years, from January 7, 2026 to January 6, 2029, with the possibility of a one-year extension.
This officer will work with the RCMP's National Weapons Enforcement Support Team (NWEST): liaison between police forces, training, and support for firearms trafficking investigations.
According to the document, the resource will not take part in any operational intervention; the officer will only provide training and advice.
The SPVM keeps one police officer position over and above its authorized staffing level for the entire duration of the loan.
The SPVM states that more than 50% of this officer's tasks directly serve Montréal, and that he is one of only two expert witnesses in Québec on armed violence and firearms trafficking.

The agreement departs from the usual agreements: the RCMP indemnifies the seconded officer, but not the City, except for reimbursement if the City pays amounts on his behalf; there is no indemnification if the officer did not act in good faith or acted outside his duties.
The director of the SPVM is authorized to sign the agreement on behalf of the City; the decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.

The City is moving $121,873.50 (taxes included) from one budget line to another for the Ateliers municipaux Viau construction site, at 2269, rue Viau, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. No new spending is added.

The money comes from the contingency spending in the works contract, which will not all be used, and will pay additional fees for the firms Bouthillette Parizeau inc. and Lafontaine Langford Architectes.
The contingency reserve for professional services goes from $139,376.13 to $261,249.63, which is 37% of the base contract.
The project is replacing the garage's ventilation and gas capture systems to bring them up to CNESST standards. The work was 86% complete as of January 31, 2026.
The cost overruns come from Hydro-Québec work on a nearby high-voltage line, contaminated soil, lead and asbestos that were found, and outdated buried equipment.
The Viau garage is the only one in Montréal that maintains Service de sécurité incendie vehicles and must stay open 7 days a week during the work.
The bill is shared: 50.1% to the agglomeration, 49.9% to the central city. The project could receive funding under the Plan de mise en œuvre pour une économie verte.

The City is amending its by-law on the sanitation, maintenance and safety of dwelling units (03-096) so it can continue to register "deterioration notices" in the Registre foncier du Québec when an owner lets their building fall into disrepair.
A deterioration notice stays attached to the building: if the property is sold, the new owner must carry out the required work, and the notice remains registered until the work is done.

If the work is not done within 60 days after the notice is registered, the City may buy the property by mutual agreement or expropriate it, under the conditions set out in the Loi sur l'aménagement et l'urbanisme.

The by-law sets out the standards to be met: no uncleanliness or clutter, no mould, a watertight exterior envelope and windows, a sound structure, watertight bathroom and laundry room floors, and a floor slope of less than 20 mm per metre.
According to Service de l'habitation data for 2025, 60% of the buildings covered by a notice were brought into compliance in less than one year and 80% in less than two years.
Next steps: notice of motion and tabling at city council, a public consultation meeting, then adoption of the by-law with or without changes.
Montréal-Nord is hiring Construction Vert Dure inc. to build a permanent dog exercise area at parc Sauvé, at the corner of boulevard Henri-Bourassa and avenue Balzac, for $491,130.66 including taxes.
With contingencies ($73,669.60) and incidental costs ($49,113.07), the total spending comes to $613,913.33, paid 100% by the borough.
The new dog park will replace the temporary area at parc Pilon, which will be removed for phase 2 of the development work at that park in the summer of 2026.
The planned facilities: two separate enclosures for large and small dogs, lighting, a water point, a pergola, accessible furniture, and play structures and obstacles for dogs.
The work starts at the end of April 2026 and must be finished by mid-June 2026, to avoid an interruption in service; final acceptance in June 2027.
Five companies submitted bids out of the 18 that picked up the tender documents; one bid was rejected because it did not use the right bid form. The price chosen is about 9% below the estimate.
Information panels will be installed at parc Pilon and parc Sauvé, an article will appear in the Info-Nord, and an opening event is planned for the end of the work.
The executive committee is adding two construction zones to the grant program for commercial development corporations (SDCs) affected by major infrastructure work.
First zone: rues Barré and Notre-Dame, between rue Guy and rue Eleanor (SDC Quartiers du Canal), for work from August 18, 2025 to October 31, 2026.
Second zone: rues Atateken and Berri, between rue Robin and boulevard René-Lévesque (SDC du Village).
The City is also amending the order covering the zone "Rues Ontario Est et Sainte-Catherine Est (Hochelaga) et ses abords" to change the dates of the major work.
The designated SDCs will be able to apply for money for cleanliness, landscaping, greening, advertising, animation, construction-site mitigation measures and filling vacant premises.
To be designated, a zone must undergo public works by the City or the STM lasting at least 180 days, with obstructions to car traffic.
City council had set aside $6,500,000 for this program on March 18, 2025.

The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. for the repair of heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, in the Grand parc de l'Ouest. The contract goes from $1,029,619.56 to $1,174,331.77, which is 14% more.

The cost overruns come from unforeseen conditions on the work site: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, more mortar than expected, underestimated sod, and a deteriorated culvert that had to be replaced.
The contract was also delayed, which forces the contractor to reinstall guardrails, impact attenuators and machinery in 2026.
The work was 60% complete as of December 1, 2025; it resumes on May 15, 2026 and must be finished by July 10, 2026.
The bill is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, including $144,712.21 in new credits coming from a loan by-law; the net cost after tax rebates is $132,141.54.
According to the document, a refusal would force the City to issue a new call for tenders, since the remaining contingency budget ($19,484.34) is not enough to finish the work.
The City is extending its crushed stone purchase agreement with Amrize Canada inc. (formerly named Lafarge Canada inc.) by 12 months, starting April 24, 2026.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $2,121,767.30, taxes included: $1,845,015.04 for the planned purchases and $276,752.26 (15%) in case quantities increase.
The total value of the agreement therefore rises from $5,673,498.14 to $7,795,265.44, taxes included.
The stone is used mainly for road and park work done by the City's own crews; the agreement is open to all City units, which pay out of their own budgets.
The City is not required to buy any specific quantity; each purchase order must be approved.
Transportation prices will not be indexed, since the CPI is below the 3% threshold set out in the call for tenders; only the royalties change ($0.70/MT in 2025, $0.71/MT in 2026).
The extension ends on April 23, 2027; this was the last of the two options provided for in the 2023 contract.
The urban agglomeration council is adding 5,632 buildings in the Ville-Marie borough to the inventory of heritage buildings built before 1940.

These buildings become "heritage buildings" within the meaning of the Loi sur l'aménagement et l'urbanisme: their demolition and their upkeep will be governed by Ville-Marie's demolition by-law and the municipal by-law on the occupancy and maintenance of buildings.
The process stems from a requirement of the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel: the agglomeration must have inventoried all of its pre-1940 buildings of heritage value by April 1, 2026 at the latest.
The inventory is being adopted in pieces, one borough or related city at a time; an estimated 100,000 pre-1940 buildings are located in the agglomeration's territory.
The work is being paid for under an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications: up to $5,000,000 from the Government of Québec and an equal contribution from the Ville.
The Ville-Marie borough took part in the exercise and supports the adoption of the list.
The Ville and the ministère plan to publish the inventory data as open data.
The urban agglomeration council is adding 7,572 buildings in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce to the inventory of buildings built before 1940 that have heritage value.

These buildings become "heritage buildings" within the meaning of the land use planning act: they will be subject to specific borough rules for demolition and for the occupancy and upkeep of buildings.
The borough took part in the inventory and supports its adoption in a letter dated January 16, 2026.
The process responds to the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel, which requires the agglomeration to complete its inventory by April 1, 2026 at the latest.
The inventory is being adopted in parts: about 100,000 buildings built before 1940 are estimated to be on the agglomeration's territory, and other areas will follow.
The work is funded through an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications, namely maximum funding of $5,000,000 and an equal contribution from the Ville.
The data collected must eventually be published as open data.
The borough of LaSalle is amending its construction by-law to bring it in line with the new fee by-law adopted on December 8, 2025.

Residents will no longer need a certificate of authorization to put up a fence, a low wall or a hedge, unless the project has to be approved under the by-law on site planning and architectural integration programmes.
The same requirement is being removed for building or installing an accessory building for a residential use, with the same exception.
The by-law also removes the distinction between installing a commercial antenna support and installing a commercial antenna.
Adoption is planned at the borough council meeting of March 2, 2026, with the by-law coming into force in March 2026.
The borough of LaSalle is accepting a $71,720 grant from the Fédération canadienne des municipalités, paid out through the Fonds municipal vert.
The money goes to the detailed planning project for the Newman area, specifically to drawing up the detailed plan and its action plan.
The project cost $227,822.88 (net amount) in total for all of its stages.
LaSalle is paying 50% of the expenses eligible for the grant and 69% of the project's total budget.
The operating budget of LaSalle's Direction de l'aménagement urbain et des services aux entreprises is going up by $71,720 in both revenue and expenses.
The FCM had confirmed that the application was eligible on January 31, 2024; the grant was confirmed on March 25, 2025.

The City is awarding Le Groupe Centco inc. a contract worth $1,165,731.53 (taxes included) to replace the natural gas heating equipment at fire station 08 with equipment that produces no greenhouse gas emissions.
With contingencies ($174,859.73) and incidental costs ($58,286.58), the total authorized expenditure comes to $1,398,877.84.
The work includes dual-energy electric boilers, electric water heaters, a new 347/600 V electrical connection, enlarging the electrical room, and changes to the ventilation and control systems.
According to the document, the project will cut emissions by about 97 tonnes of CO2 equivalent and is part of the goal of making the municipal building portfolio operationally zero carbon by 2030.
An agreement with the gouvernement du Québec covers 58% of the costs, provided they are incurred before March 31, 2026.
The contract starts in March 2026, provisional acceptance is expected in March 2027, and the contract ends in March 2028; the cost is borne by the urban agglomeration (public safety).
Eight bids were received and found to be compliant; the lowest is 29.4% below the professionals' estimate. Starting in 2027, the building's operating budget will have to be increased by 8%.
The City is awarding Le Groupe Centco inc. the work to replace the natural gas heating equipment at fire station 25, for a total expense of $898,587.12, including taxes.
The contract itself is $733,540.50, plus $110,031.08 for construction contingencies and $55,015.54 for related costs (commissioning, Hydro-Québec, industrial hygiene).
The work includes electric and gas boilers, electric water heaters, a new 347/600 V electrical connection, electronic controls and architectural work.
According to the document, the project would cut about 78 tonnes of CO2 eq. and is part of the Plan climat goal of making the city's building stock zero-carbon by 2030.
A grant from the gouvernement du Québec covers 59% of the expenses, provided they are incurred before March 31, 2026.
Eight companies submitted bids; the winning bid is 43.6% below the professionals' estimate ($566,711.77 less).
Work is scheduled to start in March 2026, with the contract ending in March 2028; starting in 2027, the building's operating budget is to rise by 17%. The expense is paid by the agglomeration.
The City is awarding Le Groupe M.E.A.S. inc. the work to replace the natural gas heating system at fire station 47, at 2111, rue Saint-Zotique, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
Total expense of $1,305,578.38 including taxes: $1,087,981.98 for the contract, $163,197.30 for contingencies and $54,399.10 for incidental costs.
The work includes electric and gas boilers, electric water heaters, changes to the electrical distribution, ventilation and controls, plus architectural work.
The City estimates the reduction at about 113 tonnes CO2 eq. for this building; the project is part of the goal of making the real estate portfolio zero carbon by 2030.
A grant from Québec covers 44% of the expenses, on the condition that they are committed before March 31, 2026; the work must mostly be finished before the 2026-2027 heating season.
Starting in 2027, the City plans to increase the energy and technical maintenance budgets tied to this building by 40% (SGPI and borough).
Seven companies submitted bids; the lowest bid is 28.5% below the professionals' estimate. The expense is paid by the agglomeration.
The City is awarding Tuyauterie Expert inc. a contract worth $1,055,470.50 (taxes included) to replace the natural gas heating equipment at fire station 66, at 4398, boulevard LaSalle, in Verdun.
With $158,320.58 in contingencies and $52,773.53 in incidental expenses, the total spending comes to $1,266,564.61, taxes included.
The work includes electric boilers (dual-energy), electric water heaters, changes to the electrical distribution, and the addition of electronic controls.
The document states that the project would cut about 141 tonnes of CO2 eq. and is part of the Plan climat goal of making the real estate portfolio zero carbon by 2030.
Tuyauterie Expert inc. was the lowest of the 7 bidders, at 33.3% below the professionals' estimate.
A grant covers 67% of the spending, provided it is committed before March 31, 2026; the work must mostly be finished before the 2026-2027 heating season.
Starting in 2027, the building's energy and maintenance costs would rise by 76% according to estimates, charged to the budgets of the Service des immeubles and the borough of Verdun.
The LaSalle borough is giving $8,000 to four organizations, $2,000 each, for Black History Month activities in February 2026.

The organizations receiving support are the Centre d'accompagnement KEDA (CED'AKEDA), the Centre multiculturel de ressources de LaSalle, the conseil des personnes âgées de la communauté noire de Montréal and the Association Cameroon Goodwillers de Montréal.
The month opens on February 3, 2026 at l'Octogone, followed by four events on February 7, 14, 21 and 28.
The program includes talks, workshops for young people, intergenerational storytelling circles, dance, poetry and drum music.
The money comes from the budget for contributions to other organizations of the Direction culture, sports, loisirs et développement social (cultural diversity plan).
The council also recognizes the commitment of Keslie Datus (CED'AKEDA) and Martin Albino (Savoys, steel drum workshop), as well as the contribution of Black communities in LaSalle.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $4,000 to the organization Accueil pour Immigrants et Réfugiés du Sud-Ouest de Montréal (AIR-SOM Centre Prisme).
The money supports the Festival Expressions artistiques d'ici et d'ailleurs, presented free of charge to the public.
The festival has already taken place: launch on July 11, family day on August 2, then shows from August 12 to 16, 2025 at the Centre culturel et communautaire Henri Lemieux.
The council is therefore approving after the fact a contribution that was already granted, since the organization submitted its application late.
The amount represents no more than 70% of the event's budget, the limit set out in the LaSalle event support program.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
