The organization had received $10,000 in 2022 and $10,000 in 2023 for previous editions of the festival.
The City is entering into a 36-month master agreement with Novexco inc. (Hamster) to supply office supplies, ink cartridges and printing paper to all of its departments and boroughs.
The contract is worth $7,302,147.84, plus a budget of $1,095,322.18 for variations in quantities, for a total of $8,397,470.02, taxes included.
The agreement runs from January 18, 2026 to January 17, 2029, with two possible 12-month extensions, up to January 17, 2031.
Novexco was the lowest of the two bidders: its price is 13.51% below the City's estimate and 7.89% below Grand and Toy's.
Prices are fixed for the first year, then indexed each year according to the CPI (office supplies and ink) or the IPPI (paper).
The expense is shared: 49% central city, 38% agglomeration (heavy use by the Service de police) and 13% boroughs.

Since the contract exceeds $4M and Novexco is obtaining a third consecutive contract, the file goes before the Commission permanente sur l'examen des contrats, and the supplier's performance will be evaluated.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is renting a mini-backhoe with an operator, transportation, maintenance and accessories from 9259-0728 Québec inc. for $152,916.75, taxes included.
The machine will be used to plant trees and add greenery in the borough in 2026, with a goal of more than 600 trees planted by in-house crews.
The contract lasts one year and provides for a maximum of 1,000 hours of use, including 800 guaranteed hours and up to 50 weekend hours.
Planting must start in April 2026 and finish in November 2026.
Three companies submitted bids and all three were compliant; the winning bid is the lowest, 10.74% below the estimate of $171,312.75.
The money comes from the operating budget of the borough's Direction des travaux publics.
According to the document, without this contract the plantings planned for this year could not be carried out, because the Division des parcs et de l'horticulture does not own this type of machinery.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving $99,900 to the organization L'Anonyme U.I.M. for its project "Intervention en cohabitation sociale dans RPP".
The money covers the period from February 3 to December 31, 2026 and comes from the borough's operating budget.
The project involves outreach work with people experiencing homelessness, in public spaces, municipal facilities and encampments, and with the people who use these places.

The borough says it is responding to a report by the Centre international pour la prévention de la criminalité (2023) that identified the sharing of public space, damage to street furniture and social tensions.
Only one organization responded to the invitation-only call for projects launched on November 5, 2025.
The organization must submit a final report no later than the month following the end of the project.
In 2025, $97,900 had been shared between L'Anonyme U.I.M. and PACT de rue for the same program.
The City is raising the property value caps that determine who can receive a grant under the RénoPlex program, which is intended for residential buildings with 1 to 5 units.
Reason given: the new 2026-2027-2028 property assessment roll came into effect on January 1, 2026; without an adjustment, fewer buildings would be eligible.
The general value cap per square metre is going from $3,476 to $3,860, and the maximum total value (building and land) from $1.6M to $1.9M.
The caps specific to each borough for block 2 work are also going up, for example from $1,280 to $1,530/m² in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève and from $1,790 to $2,040/m² in Pierrefonds-Roxboro.
New caps of $1,430/m² for real estate complexes and $1,210/m² for mixed-use buildings; co-operatives and non-profit organizations remain eligible regardless of their property value.
The City states that the change does not create any additional budget spending and that no information campaign is planned.
The City is extending its agreement with the firm Stantec experts-conseils ltée by 12 months for professional and technical services in biology (botany, ornithology, herpetology, geomatics).
Additional spending of $1,264,392.63 taxes included: $1,099,471.85 for the assignments and $164,920.78 in contingencies (15%).
The total contract therefore rises to $3,732,831.15, an increase of 51.2% over the initial value of $2,468,438.52.
The extension runs from April 19, 2026 to April 18, 2027; the company accepted the renewal on December 5, 2025.
These studies are used to prepare development projects and ecological restoration work in the network of large parks.
Payment is made at an hourly rate; prices will be adjusted according to the consumer price index if the change exceeds 2%.
Without a renewal, the City would have to issue a new call for tenders, since the work cannot start without preliminary studies.

The city is entering into three 36-month agreements to buy personal protective equipment for its employees: safety glasses, helmets, face shields, hearing protection, masks, filters, cartridges and disposable coveralls.

Canadian Bearings is awarded two lots ($242,853.36 for safety glasses and accessories, $329,596.06 for helmets, face shields and hearing protection) and Acklands-Grainger one lot ($266,634.34 for masks and coveralls).
An additional amount of $125,862.56 is authorized in case the quantities purchased vary, for an estimated total of $964,946.32, taxes included.
The agreements are available to all boroughs and departments, which will pay out of their own budgets as their needs arise.
Prices will be adjusted each year based on the consumer price index for the Montréal region.
Lot 1 (work gloves) was cancelled because no bidder was found to be compliant.
The three selected bids are below the city's estimates (by 10.81% to 48.97%); the suppliers' performance will be evaluated.
The City is buying 11 BMW R1300 RT-P 2026 motorcycles for the Service de police de Montréal (SPVM), which will be used for road patrol from April to mid-December.
The contract goes to Gabriel Moto B Montréal S.E.C., the lowest bidder, for $459,082.53 including taxes, out of three compliant bids.
Added to this are $68,862.38 for contingencies and $22,954.13 for related expenses, bringing the total expense to $550,899.04.
The motorcycles must be delivered before the end of May 2026; a delay results in a penalty of $100 per week, up to 10% of the value of the contract.
The winning bid is 19.34% lower than the City's estimate.
The expense is funded by a loan by-law and paid 100% by the urban agglomeration, under public safety.
The City is hiring Trois Diamants Autos (1987) Ltée to maintain and repair its light vehicles, for an estimated amount of $16,298,564.44, taxes included.
The agreements last 5 years, with two possible extensions of 12 months each.
The contract is divided into 5 lots by sector: Centre, Est, Sud, Ouest and reserve fleet. The same supplier gets all five.
The supplier must pick up and return the vehicles free of charge anywhere on the City's territory, and guarantee parts and labour for 1 year.
Prices stay firm for the initial term and the City does not commit to ordering all the planned quantities.
Public call for tenders 25-20885 received 5 bids out of 18 people who took out the tender documents; one bid for lot 4 was found to be non-compliant.
Lot 1 goes before the Commission d'examen des contrats on January 21, 2026, because of its value of more than $4M and gaps of more than 20% with the internal estimate and with the second bidder.
The City is extending its research agreement with Polytechnique Montréal for the Chaire industrielle en eau potable by one year, from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027.
No additional money is being paid: the extension is on the same terms as the agreement already approved in October 2022.
The extension allows the Chaire to complete its ongoing research projects with the funds it has left from the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada.
The City has taken part in this chair since 2005; its contribution had been set at $364,650, indexed by 2% per year, for the period up to May 30, 2026.

The work deals with the treatment and distribution of drinking water and with reducing health risks; other cities (Laval, Longueuil, Repentigny, L'Assomption, Joliette) and Veolia Water Technologies Canada are taking part.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council, and the authorization is planned for February 2026.
Montréal is paying $5,000 for its 2025 membership fee to Mayors for Peace, an organization based in Hiroshima that campaigned for the elimination of nuclear weapons.
The money comes out of the budget of the Bureau des relations internationales and is paid entirely by the central city, with no effect on the financial framework.
The City has paid the same amount of $5,000 every year since 2018; the invoice sets the payment deadline at December 31, 2025.
A member since 1989, Montréal has served as vice-president of the organization's executive cities since 2022.
The organization brings together more than 8,256 members in more than 166 countries, including more than 100 Canadian cities.
The decision falls to the executive committee; no communications activities are planned.
The City is buying a vacant lot of 1,535.1 m² from Investissements 1919 William inc., east of rue Chatham and north of rue William, in the borough of Le Sud-Ouest.
Purchase price: $9,293,113, plus applicable taxes, an expense paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
The land is intended for social housing: the City estimates that about 105 housing units could be built there, depending on the project and the organization selected.
The City plans to resell the land to a social housing organization or a housing co-operative, which has yet to be determined.
The sale stems from two agreements reached in July 2025 with developers for the residential projects at 1810, rue des Bassins and 1990, rue William; the deadline for the sale is August 12, 2026.
The City will not sign until it receives written confirmation that the decontamination and backfilling of the land are complete to its satisfaction.
The document states that the price, set under by-law 20-041, does not match the market value estimated by the City in January 2025.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is asking city council to hand over to it the design and carrying out of work on rue Boyer, between boulevard Rosemont and rue Beaubien Est.
The work includes rebuilding the water and sewer pipes, the roadway and the traffic lights at the intersections involved.
Improvement work is also included: repairing the sidewalks, planting, changes to signs and road markings, and adding street furniture.
The request is made under section 85 of the Charter of Ville de Montréal because this stretch is part of the City's administrative arterial road network.
The Service de l'eau is paying for the water and sewer work, the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier for the roadway and sidewalk work, and the borough for the improvement work.
Preliminary timeline: plans 50% complete in the fall of 2026, call for tenders in February 2027, work in 2027.
A communications effort and a construction site sign are planned for when the contracts are awarded.
The City is awarding its banking services to the Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec for $2,291,231.87, taxes included, over five years.
The contract covers collecting taxes and payment of statements of offence, paying suppliers, employee payroll, and managing the City's bank accounts.
The new contract takes effect in June 2026, as the current one ends on May 31, 2026, and it allows for two possible three-year extensions, estimated at $5,679,349.75.
Annual costs rise from $256,636.02 (June to December 2026) to $455,063.26 in 2030, an increase of 46% compared with the last year of the current contract.
The City attributes this increase to the processing of post office boxes for taxes and statements of offence, and to fees on cheques and paper instruments.
Of nine companies that obtained the tender documents, three submitted bids and two bids were rejected; the winning bid is 47% below the City's estimate.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is removing one paid parking space (parking meter PG201) on avenue Mont-Royal Ouest, south side, about 34 metres west of boulevard Saint-Laurent.
The space being removed is about 6.2 metres long.
The STM reported that adding a hatched zone had shortened the neighbouring bus stop; the stop will be moved west to get back to the required minimum length.
The Agence de mobilité durable estimates a revenue loss of $5,800 per year and will pay for the parking meter removal work itself.
The parking meter is to be removed and the signage updated in February 2026.
The Agence de mobilité durable and the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité both came out in favour of the removal.

The City is changing the rules of the AccèsLogis Montréal program to allow housing co-operatives and non-profit organizations to repay at any time the loan taken out to create their contingency reserve, instead of waiting for their mortgage renewal.
The repayment will require the City's prior approval; the amended agreement with the Fédération des caisses Desjardins, in effect since August 15, 2025, allows this repayment without penalty.
According to the document, organizations will therefore pay less in mortgage interest charges.
The contingency reserve is now built up through annual contributions rather than a single initial contribution.
The City will reimburse the organizations that had already paid the initial contribution for their AccèsLogis Montréal projects.
The Service de l'habitation states that the change entails no additional cost for the City; the decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.
The City is giving $300,000 to the Bureau du cinéma et de la télévision du Québec (BCTQ) for its plan to promote Montréal's audiovisual industry, from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2028.

The money is used to seek out international clients outside Québec, host delegations in Montréal (Vitrine 360 and CAFÉ-VFX events, scouting of filming locations) and build up a photo library of filming sites.
Some of the activities focus on environmentally responsible filming practices, through the On tourne vert program and a target of fifteen certified sets.
The payment is made in four instalments: $70,000 and $100,000 in 2026, $100,000 in 2027, $30,000 in 2028, conditional on accountability reporting and an annual action plan.
The City is funding 12% of the annual budget of the $853,000 project; Québec covers 46% of it, Ottawa 30%, with the rest coming from self-generated revenue and the private sector.
The document points to a drop in foreign investment in 2025, the change to the federal tax credit for production services and the threat of 100% American tariffs on films shot abroad.
The three-year agreement replaces the annual $100,000 grants awarded since 2022 and puts an end to funding paid after the fact.
The executive committee is allowing 12 public events to take place in city parks between April 26 and October 25, 2026.
The activities will be held at parc Frédéric-Back (8 events) and at parc du Mont-Royal, including the tam-tams at the piedmont, from May 17 to October 25.
The organizers include Jamais Lu, the Centre Philou, the Fondation de l'Hôpital Jean-Talon, Sclérose en plaques Canada, as well as schools and colleges.
The decision grants exemptions from the city by-laws on noise and on peace and order on public property.
The organizations will be allowed to sell food and promotional items to help fund their activities; the events are free and open to everyone.
The City will cover the support costs out of the operating budgets of the departments and boroughs involved.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing spending of $398,627.42, taxes included, for road repair work in 2026.
The work will be done "in-house", meaning by the City's own employees.
On the list: repairs to sidewalks, curbs and roadways, speed bumps in laneways, driveway entrances, excavation cuts, and requests from residents.
The work will run from April 27 to November 20, 2026.
The amount covers machinery rental, the purchase of materials, signage and related unforeseen expenses.
The amount is 4% higher than that of the last three years ($383,295.63), which had been renewed without any increase since 2023.
The City is granting $25,000 to the Foyer pour femmes autochtones de Montréal, an organization that offers housing and support to First Nations, Inuit and Métis women and their children.
The money will be used to organize mobilization and commemoration events, including the September 30 march for the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.
The money comes from the Indigenous affairs budget of the Bureau des commissaires and will be paid 100% by the central city, with no effect on the financial framework.
An agreement sets out the conditions for payment and requires the organization to apply a City visibility protocol.
The City links the decision to its Strategy for Reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples 2020-2025, which provides for supporting Indigenous organizations and square Cabot.
Without this funding, the organization would have to look for other partners to maintain its services.
The borough of Ville-Marie is accepting a $49,500 grant from Sport et Loisir de l'île de Montréal (Circonflexe program).
The money will be used to set up an "active station" at place Henri-Dunant in 2026.
A four-season container will allow sports equipment to be borrowed free of charge all year round: soccer, volleyball, badminton, snowshoes, snow scooters.
A neighbourhood organization will manage the equipment lending, with schedules adapted to how busy the site is.
Occasional activities will be offered to introduce people to using the equipment.
The project is aimed at the whole population, with attention to young people, families and vulnerable groups.
In 2025, the borough had accepted $87,325 from the same program.
The City is paying $25,110,800 to Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel, a non-profit organization, to build 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.

The project includes four buildings connected by walkways: 121 one-bedroom units, 134 two-bedroom units and 95 three-bedroom units, plus 225 parking spaces, 225 storage spaces and ground-floor businesses.

The units are reserved for low- or modest-income households, according to the income limits of the Programme habitation abordable Québec; the organization will have to go through the Office d'habitation de Montréal to assign the units.
Rents must remain affordable for at least 35 years after occupancy begins in the last of the three projects set out in the agreement with the Société d'habitation du Québec.

Occupancy is planned for no later than April 30, 2027; the total cost of the project is estimated at $174,800,000, also funded by a $56,777,000 grant and an interest-free loan of $12,000,000 from the SHQ, as well as loans from Desjardins.
The payment is made in three stages: 50% when the agreement is signed, 40% halfway through the work, and 10% at substantial completion; the City is taking a 4th-rank mortgage guarantee.
The expense is covered by the urban agglomeration and reimbursed by the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal.
The City is paying $3,071,550 to SOVERDI, a non-profit organization, to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional land from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

In 2026, SOVERDI and the roughly 80 partners of the Alliance forêt urbaine are to plant 14,500 trees and 2,500 shrubs, including 6,300 on dense planting sites, and maintain part of the 2024 and 2025 plantings.
The amount is paid in 4 instalments: $1,382,197 on signing, $307,155 after the July 31 report, $307,155 after the October 31 report and $1,075,043 on the final report.
The amount is lower than the contributions of previous years: $3,464,250 in 2025, $3,540,250 in 2024 and $3,464,090 in 2023.
The expense is funded by a loan by-law on the urban forest and paid entirely by the central city.
The City ties the agreement to its goal of planting 500,000 trees in Montréal by 2030, with priority given to areas vulnerable to heat waves.

SOVERDI must submit progress reports on July 31 and October 31, 2026, its accountability report no later than December 31, 2026, and then its summary report and financial statements on March 31, 2027.

The Ville de Montréal is selling 4,352 square metres of vacant land in the Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough to the Société québécoise des infrastructures (SQI) for $1,171,123 plus taxes.
The land is located in the block formed by boulevard Saint-Jean-Baptiste and boulevard Industriel; the SQI wants to add it to its existing property in order to set up an outdoor vehicle storage lot.

This decision cancels the resolution adopted on September 22, 2025, because four lots included in the draft deed had been left out of the text of the resolution (lots 1 260 692, 1 260 693, 1 260 694 and 1 260 733).
The price was negotiated directly between the parties and falls within the market value range set by the City in April 2025.
The sale is made without warranty of quality, at the SQI's own risk; the signing depends on the buyer's verifications and on government authorizations.
The amount of $1,171,123 will go into the operating budget of the Service de la stratégie immobilière.
The City of Montréal is receiving from the Government of Canada the 50% of the rights it holds in a piece of land on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost.
The City already owned the other half of the land, so it becomes the sole owner.
The land measures 3,658.8 square metres and is located south of boulevard de Pierrefonds, west of boulevard Saint-Jean.
The land is then to be transferred to a non-profit organization to build off-market housing (social housing).

An incomplete environmental study shows that the soil does not meet the criterion for residential use; soil studies will be carried out after the acquisition, either by the City or by the organization.
The City estimates the market value of the 50% acquired at more than $150,000.
The deed is expected to be signed in January 2026; a delay could jeopardize the resale of the land to the organization.
The City officially becomes the owner of the Planétarium de Montréal building, in the Parc olympique (Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough).

The Société de développement et de mise en valeur du Parc olympique is transferring ownership to the City free of charge, as set out in an agreement reached in 2011 to allow the City to build the museum there.
The transfer settles the property titles: the Planétarium is already built and operated by the City, but the City did not have a title that could be asserted against others.

The deed creates many shared easements: access to the P5 parking lot, a pedestrian passage to the Centre Pierre-Charbonneau, emergency exits, retention basins, sewers, and works of art (Cadran solaire and Monument à Nicolas Copernic).
The City must use the building only for museum or institutional purposes and cannot change its use or transfer its rights without the written consent of the Société.
A path located on the lot must remain free of any construction in perpetuity; otherwise, the Société can have the transfer cancelled and take back the property without compensation.
The transfer deed is scheduled to be signed in February 2026.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is renewing the lease of the organization Espace-Famille Villeray at the chalet de Normanville, at 7470, rue de Normanville.
The lease runs for 58 months, from March 1, 2026 to December 31, 2030, for a total of $63,800, taxes included.
The rent is $1,100 per month, with no annual increase: this is a decrease compared to the previous lease of $69,000 over 5 years.
The organization is losing space (its administrative office is cut in half) to make room for a service point of ÉCO Quartier Villeray, which arrived at the chalet in December 2025.
Espace-Famille Villeray rents about 1,805 square feet (offices, drop-in daycare, storage) and remains responsible for the housekeeping of the chalet.
The organization offers perinatal support, fitness and leisure activities, and a drop-in daycare for families with children aged 0 to 5.
The borough plans monthly follow-up meetings and an annual report from the organization.
The borough of Ville-Marie is amending its by-law on commercial promotions, which governs sidewalk sales and festive events organized by SDCs and merchants' associations.
New application deadlines: before March 1 for a promotion held between May 1 and October 31, and before September 1 for a promotion held between November 1 and April 30 of the following year.
Each application must include a bank draft for $4,000, a resolution from the association's board of directors, and liability insurance of at least $3,000,000 naming the Ville as a co-insured party.
The $4,000 bank draft is returned to the association within 90 days after the end of the promotion, less any cleaning costs or borough interventions related to failure to meet the requirements.

The association must submit a complete specifications document (occupancy of public property, programming, security, logistics) at least 60 days before the event, and must guarantee access for private waste collection on neighbouring streets and lanes.
Only associations incorporated as legal entities may apply, and the Ville accepts no responsibility for economic losses caused by the cancellation of a promotion.
Notice of motion given on February 10, 2026, with adoption expected on March 10, 2026; the SDCs and merchants' associations will be notified and the information will be posted online.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles takes note of the minutes of the February 24, 2026 public consultation and adopts specific project PP-154-1.

The decision concerns the Espace Rivière project, at 9001, boulevard Perras: a new building that would bring together an expanded library, a maison de la culture, community and recreational spaces, and the Rivière-des-Prairies bureau Accès Montréal.
The deadline to move forward changes from 24 months to start the work to 48 months to file an application for a construction permit, starting from the date the resolution comes into force.

Reason for the postponement: the plans and specifications were delayed; the work site should begin in the spring of 2027, the plans are expected in the spring of 2026, and the work is still scheduled to be completed in 2029.

The project is allowed to depart from the subdivision by-law, which required the two properties involved (the one with the current library and the one with the aquatic centre and the aréna René-Masson) to be combined into a single lot.
According to the borough, the resolution is not subject to approval by referendum, and the comité consultatif d'urbanisme had given a unanimous favourable opinion on January 9, 2026.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is adopting the second draft by-law amending its zoning by-law.
The by-law clarifies which uses fall into the "Institutions locales" (P.1) class and adds definitions for: community centre, cultural creation and presentation centre, balcony, gallery, patio.

It relaxes the standards for projecting structures: the maximum projection goes from 1.5 m to 2.5 m for a balcony and from 1.5 m to 3.5 m for a gallery in front of the most advanced part of the façade.
The "patio" becomes a recognized projecting structure, with rules for roofs, screens and permanent shelters.
"Film screening" becomes a permitted accessory use within a P.1 use, up to 430 m² or 15% of the floor area, whichever limit is more restrictive.
The notion of "recreation" is added to the "Community or sociocultural activity" use.
Council takes note of the minutes of the public consultation held on January 21, 2026; sections 3 to 11 may be subject to approval by referendum.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving two zoning exemptions for the single-family home at 10150, boulevard Gouin Est.
The owner will be allowed to build a permanent carport in the front yard, above the area leading to the garage door, even though the by-law prohibits this in that yard.
The carport will also be allowed to sit 1.42 m from the side property line, instead of the required minimum of 1.5 m.
The carport measures 6.45 m wide by 7.39 m deep and 3.27 m high, with a roof and white details matching the cornice of the house.
According to the file, the carport is located nearly 9 m from the front property line, and the setback difference comes from the angle of the lot, which is less than 90 degrees.
The urban planning advisory committee unanimously recommended the application on December 5, 2025, and the immediate neighbour submitted a letter of support.
At the meeting, no one asked a question or made a comment about the application.
The City is renting out a 120-square-foot space (space 384) at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The tenant is Lucie Leroux, a self-employed worker operating under the name Laboratoire textile, who uses the space for research, creation, outreach workshops on textile art, and silkscreen printing.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for a total rent of $5,349.60 before taxes ($6,150.70 taxes included).
Either of the two parties may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The City supplies the energy and pays for maintenance and repairs; the tenant pays the property taxes and the housekeeping.
This is the renewal of an existing occupancy: the previous lease, for 12 months starting February 1, 2025, was $2,400.
The occupancy is proposed by Atelier Entremise, the organization the City has put in charge of managing the transitional occupancy of the site.
The City is renting a 90-square-foot space (unit 389-B) at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the Cité-des-Hospitalières, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The tenant, Sophie Gailliot, a self-employed worker, will set up a research project office there and give leather marquetry classes.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, and will bring the City $4,012.20, before sales taxes.
The first year's rent works out to $22 per square foot; the tenant had already been occupying the space since February 2025 ($1,800 for 12 months).
The City supplies the energy and pays for maintenance and repairs; the tenant covers the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The rental is part of the transitional occupancy of the heritage site, whose management has been entrusted to the organization Atelier Entremise.
The City is renting a 205-square-foot space (unit 186) at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The tenant is the community of the Religieuses Hospitalières de Saint-Joseph, which will use the space for offices, research and participatory workshops.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, and brings the City $10,793.25, before sales taxes.
The first year's rent works out to $26 per square foot; the previous lease, which lasted one year, was $4,920.
The City supplies the energy and covers maintenance and repairs; the sisters pay the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The City acquired the site in 2017 and has entrusted its transitional occupancy to the organization Atelier Entremise, which recommended this rental.
The City is renting a 90-square-foot space (unit 389-A) at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, to Anne-Laure Bixquert (Enlacés), for a workshop and an office.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, and brings the City $4,012.20 before taxes ($4,613.23 taxes included).
The first year's rent works out to $22 per square foot; the previous lease, for 12 months, was $1,800.
The City pays for energy, maintenance and repairs; the tenant pays the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The rental is part of the transitional occupancy of the heritage site, whose management has been entrusted to the organization Atelier Entremise.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is asking to take charge itself of the plans, the call for tenders and the reconstruction work for three intersections located on the City's arterial road network.
The intersections concerned: Island and Châteauguay, Laurendeau and De Maricourt, as well as Saint-Rémi and Palm. A pedestrian crossing in front of the school on rue Du Couvent is also affected.
In total, 8 pedestrian crossings will be made safer and about 348 m² will be greened or de-paved; about 260 m of streets will be redeveloped.
At Island and Châteauguay: two double curb extensions with planting pits and two concrete medians, following a first phase carried out in 2025 at Island and Saint-Patrick.
At Laurendeau and De Maricourt: adding curb extensions to shorten the crossings and to eliminate non-compliant parking near the intersection.
At Saint-Rémi and Palm: the borough cites complaints about drivers not respecting the school crossing, pedestrian safety and motorists' speed.
Planned schedule: call for tenders and awarding of the contract from March to May 2026, work from June to October 2026. Ten lead water service lines will be replaced.
The City is awarding Applied Electronics Limited the contract to replace the LED display system at the pool of the complexe sportif Claude-Robillard.
The contract is worth $160,483.25, plus a contingency budget of $24,072.49, for a total expenditure of $184,555.74, taxes included.
The old scoreboard no longer worked and was dismantled during upgrading work; the equipment is used during sports competitions.
The installation must be done within 90 days of the contract being awarded and will not require closing the sports facility.
The price includes training, cabling and accessories, two additional years of warranty from the supplier on service and three years from the manufacturer on the LED wall.
Applied Electronics was the lowest of the compliant bidders: $36,587.15 (22.8%) below the second-lowest bid and 3.9% below the City's estimate.
The expenditure is fully covered by the central city, through the Programme de protection des équipements sportifs corporatifs.
The City is paying $168,472.14 (net of taxes) to the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, taken from the environmental liability reserve for contaminated soil.
The money covers the decontamination and environmental rehabilitation of parc George-Vernot, at 8475, 13e Avenue, a site of more than 38,000 m² built on a former quarry filled in with waste.
The amount also pays for environmental monitoring during and after the work, including biogas monitoring required 4 times a year for at least 5 years.
The suppliers involved are Les Entreprises Roseneige ($107,228.88 net), WSP ($57,743.13 net) and Traces Québec ($3,500.14 net).

Work to develop the park is already under way: a pee-wee baseball field brought up to standard, tennis, basketball, synthetic-turf soccer, water games, climbing, pétanque, a washroom building, a mini stage, paths, lighting and a community garden.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city; the borough must report every quarter, with invoices to back it up, and the final amount could be lower.
According to the document, this funding frees up money from the borough's investment program for other projects.
The borough of Verdun is approving a specific project (PPCMOI) at 3837-3847, rue Allen: the construction of a 4-storey residential building with 8 units.
The existing building at 3836-3844, boulevard LaSalle will also be converted, with the rear setback reduced to 1 metre.
The project does not comply with several zoning standards: number of storeys, lot and building width, floor area ratio, rear setback and bicycle parking requirements (no cargo-bike space required).
Conditions imposed: masonry façades, a rooftop terrace of at least 40 m², a minimum of 8 m² for urban agriculture with composting and a water point, 25% of the open space in permeable substrate.
All units must be accessible under the National Building Code and at least 2 must be adaptable; no fence is allowed between the two lots and a clear 1-metre passage must remain accessible.
The building permit requires an irrevocable bank guarantee of 10% of the value on the assessment roll, renewable each year until the work is completed.
The permit application must be filed within 24 months after the resolution comes into force, once a site planning and architectural integration plan has been approved.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $137,983 to the organization Prévention Sud-Ouest for its urban safety work in 2026.
The same amount was granted for each of the years 2023, 2024 and 2025; it was $135,278 in 2022.

The organization carries out crime prevention activities throughout the territory of Le Sud-Ouest: safety of property and people, workshops for seniors, women and young people, mediation, and safety assessments with residents.
The seven areas of action also include information and communication, the urban environment and community resilience (training ambassadors, interventions after an incident).
The work is done in a way that complements the SPVM, the borough's departments, the health and school sectors and neighbourhood organizations.
The expense is paid entirely by the borough, out of the budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, du loisir et du développement social.
Prévention Sud-Ouest must submit a mid-point report and a final report at the end of the year.
The Ville-Marie borough is awarding Orange Paysagement inc. the planting and horticultural maintenance of rue De Champlain, between rue Sainte-Catherine and rue La Fontaine.
The contract covers 40 trees and more than 3,400 perennial plants over 810 m² of planting areas, replacement plants as needed, and one year of flower bed maintenance (watering, growing soil, mulch).
Cost: $224,045.93 for the contract, plus $22,404.59 in contingencies, for a maximum expense of $246,450.52, taxes included.
A 36-month term, from April 15, 2026 to April 15, 2029, with the possibility of a one-year extension.
Orange Paysagement was the lowest of the 7 bidders; the highest bid reached $570,034.55 and the internal estimate was $386,747.16.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité is paying $187,309.67 and the borough's operating budget, $59,140.85.
These plantings complete the redevelopment of the street following the water main and sewer work, which also included adding a bike path.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the mayor's report on a contract awarded on December 22, 2025 without going through the usual decision-making bodies, under her emergency powers.
The contract goes to the security firm SECO for security guard services at two warming centres: the YMCA Centre-Ville and the pavillon Le Royer of the Hôpital Hôtel-Dieu.

The new contract has been in effect since December 25, 2025 and can reach $815,000, the amount expected if operations continue until March 31, 2026. As of January 5, 2026, about $95,000 had been committed.
The previous contract ($135,888.60 before taxes, for November 1, 2025 to April 1, 2026) was used up around December 24, 2025, as the cold weather arrived earlier than expected.
The City opened 135 emergency spaces to make up for spaces not yet opened among the 500 additional winter spaces granted this year.
The guards must have two years of experience with people experiencing homelessness, be trained in first aid, CPR, AED and naloxone, and be deployed in less than 4 hours after a request.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is officially removing 18 paid parking spaces on avenue du Mont-Royal Ouest, between rue Saint-Urbain and avenue du Parc; the spaces have already been removed since the start of the construction work.
These spaces are disappearing to make room for bike lanes and widened sidewalks, as part of the bike link between chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine and rue Saint-Urbain.

In exchange, 15 new paid spaces are being created nearby: 7 on rue Jeanne-Mance, 5 on avenue de l'Esplanade (including one reserved for people with reduced mobility) and 3 on avenue du Mont-Royal Ouest.
The taxi stand on the south side of avenue du Mont-Royal Ouest, between l'Esplanade and avenue du Parc, is being removed and moved to avenue de l'Esplanade, over 18 metres.
The Agence de mobilité durable estimates the lost revenue at $25,000 and has covered the cost of the work related to removing the spaces.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité and the Agence de mobilité durable gave a favourable opinion with no conditions.
The City is borrowing $18,500,000 to restore heritage buildings it owns, as part of the Entente sur le développement culturel de Montréal.
The money will go toward preliminary studies, preservation and enhancement work, fire protection and extinguishing systems, and universal accessibility when buildings are converted for public use.
The ministère de la Culture et des Communications reimburses 50% of the projects: the share paid by Montrealers drops to $9,250,000.
Each project must first be authorized by the ministère; the funding covers 100% of eligible costs up to $5M, with the rest coming from the borough or the department making the request.
This by-law applies to buildings governed by the Loi sur l'aménagement et l'urbanisme; a second file (1266188001) covers those subject to the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel.
It replaces loan by-laws 14-032 and 20-001, which are expiring; the financing cannot exceed 20 years.
Next steps: approval by the ministre des Affaires municipales, then publication of the by-law.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is approving the plans for a 3-storey, 6-unit residential building at 4272, rue D'Iberville, on a vacant lot.
The revised plans, signed by architect Maurice Martel, were received on November 14, 2025; the permit application was filed on April 30, 2025.
The planned cladding is beige clay brick, with grey metal cladding for the mezzanine, considered compatible with the area (Village De Lorimier).
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on September 30, 2025, and its conditions were included in the amended plans.
Before the permit is issued, the developer must submit the working drawings at about 70% completion and provide a monetary guarantee.
The borough council is to adopt the proposal on February 2, 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is approving the plans for a new 3-storey residential building with 6 units at 4284, rue D'Iberville.
The lot was vacant; it was subdivided in April 2025, and the building permit application was filed on April 30, 2025.
The revised plans, signed by architect Maurice Martel, were received on November 14, 2025 and include the conditions set by the urban planning advisory committee.
The urban planning advisory committee had given a favourable opinion at its meeting of September 30, 2025.
The planned cladding is beige clay brick, with grey metal cladding for the mezzanine, considered compatible with the area (Village De Lorimier).
Before the permit is issued, the developer must submit the working drawings at about 70% completion and provide a monetary guarantee.
Adoption by the borough council is scheduled for February 2, 2026.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is giving $81,700 to the organization Solidarité Mercier-Est for the year 2026.
The money must be used only in the Mercier-Est neighbourhood (south sector, priority zone), for phase 21 of the integrated urban revitalization process.
The funds may pay for outreach, coordination, consultation, training, studies and social development projects set out in the revitalization plan.
The amount comes from the budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and does not replace the regular programs of government departments.
The payments are spread out: 70% after signing, 20% after the mid-term report (by July 31, 2026 at the latest), 10% after the final report (by January 31, 2027 at the latest).
The contributions in previous years were $152,818 in 2025 and 2024, and $136,151 in 2023.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is giving $81,700 to La Table de quartier Hochelaga-Maisonneuve for the year 2026.
The money must be used only in the southwest part of the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve neighbourhood, where close to 15,000 people live.

It funds the 15th year of the integrated urban revitalization effort: coordination, mobilization, joint planning, training, studies and social development projects (recreation, culture, employment, transportation).
The amount comes from the budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and is not recurring.
The payment is made in three parts: 70% within 30 days of signing, 20% after the mid-point report (no later than July 31, 2026), and 10% after the final report (no later than January 31, 2027).
In 2025, the same organization received $128,368 for phase 14.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is awarding a $143,005.91 contract (taxes included) to Creusage RL (9083-0126 Québec inc.) for hydro-excavation services, including the handling of waste materials.
Hydro-excavation digs into the ground using high-pressure water to avoid damaging underground electricity, gas and telecommunications networks during street work.
The contract covers 90 hours per year for regular weekday calls, 8 hours on weekends and 20 hours for emergencies.
The contract runs for 34 months, from March 10, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with no possibility of renewal.
Creusage RL was the lowest of the three bidders, ahead of G-Tek ($145,503.16) and Sanivac ($148,324.65); the price is 8.87% above the City's estimate ($131,359.51).
The borough already owns its own hydro-excavation truck and will call on the contractor only when it cannot do the work itself.
The expense is drawn from the water fund and spread over the 2026, 2027 and 2028 budgets.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is extending the timeline for La musique aux enfants' El Sistema project until June 2027, instead of ending it in December 2026.
The payment schedule is being adjusted to match the school year (September to June), at no additional cost: the total amount of $100,000 stays the same.
The contribution was granted on June 30, 2025: $50,000 in 2025 and $50,000 in 2026, drawn from the borough's surplus.
Each payment remains conditional on the submission of the required reports and on approval by the person responsible for follow-up.
The council is approving a new agreement with the organization setting out these terms.
The El Sistema OSM project provides free orchestral music training to 195 young people aged 6 to 16, including students from école Saint-Rémi.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Marie-Josée Lafontant as the 11th and final member of its Conseil des personnes aînées, completing its membership.
Her nomination comes from the reserve list drawn up by the review committee on August 11, 2025, made up of representatives from the borough and Concertation Montréal.

The Conseil has 11 volunteer members responsible for advising elected officials on issues affecting seniors: parks and public spaces, libraries, sports, recreation, culture, mobility, safety and access to municipal services.
Members must be 65 years of age or older, live in the borough and be available for about 7 meetings a year, during the day.
The Conseil stems from the Plan d'action collectif des personnes aînées de Montréal-Nord adopted on September 3, 2024 and from the Stratégie municipale pour les personnes aînées 2023-2030.
There is no financial aspect associated with this file.

The City is awarding a $1,939,714.48 contract (taxes included) to Gagné & Roy inc. to replace seven roof basins (nos. 4 to 10) at the Pointe-Claire water filtration plant, at 243, chemin du Bord-du-Lac-Lakeshore.
The amount includes the bid of $1,492,088.06, $298,417.61 in contingencies (20%) and $149,208.81 in incidental expenses (10%).

The work covers 2,450 m² of roofing: a new waterproofing system, correction of the slopes toward the drains, replacement of damaged concrete panels, guardrails, fall protection and secure access points.
Six of the seven companies that picked up the tender documents submitted bids and all were found compliant; the winning offer is 29.45% ($622,887.52) below the professionals' estimate.
Work is to start in April 2026 and finish in July 2026, before the fall, to avoid working in winter conditions.

The plant, built in the late 1960s, supplies drinking water to part of Montréal's population; the expense is borne by the agglomeration and paid out of the Service de l'eau's 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The City is awarding a sole-source contract of $166,713.75 (taxes included) to Hublot51 inc. to organize the Jardin botanique's summer 2026 music program, "Les arts s'invitent au Jardin".
The contract covers 8 months: artistic direction, selecting and supporting the artists, producing and running the concerts, technical work and stage setup.
Eight concerts are planned on Sundays at 2 p.m., from July 5 to August 23, 2026, at the Jardin botanique.
Admission is free for holders of the carte Accès Montréal, according to the document.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, out of the budget of the Service de l'Espace pour la vie; all payments will be made in 2026.
The same supplier had been awarded the contracts for the 2023 ($137,938.96), 2024 ($137,970) and 2025 ($183,960) editions.
A final report is expected on September 30, 2026.
The City is paying $125,000 to the Société du Parc Jean-Drapeau to coordinate the celebrations of the 50th anniversary of the 1976 Olympic Games, from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The contract is awarded by mutual agreement, without a call for tenders, and extends a similar $125,000 mandate awarded in April 2025 for planning.
The Société must keep the calendar of activities in the agglomeration territory up to date, lead the steering committee and carry out the communications plan.
The steering committee brings together the City, the Parc olympique, the Société du Parc Jean-Drapeau and partners such as Tourisme Montréal and the Comité olympique canadien.
Payment is made in two instalments: 70% after the preliminary deliverables, 30% after the final deliverables.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration and is not taxable.
According to the document, the celebrations would be limited if the contract were not approved.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is lending the aréna Rodrigue-Gilbert free of charge to the organization Action Secours Vie d'Espoir, a free loan valued at $3,570.56 including taxes.
The loan is for the "Souper Homard" charity event on May 29, 2026, organized with the chambre de commerce des gens d'affaires.
The profits fund the distribution of breakfasts in seven schools of the Centre de services scolaires de la Pointe-de-l'Île.
The value breaks down into $1,780 in rental (20 hours at $89/hour), $924.63 in supervision and $865.93 in maintenance.
The borough is making an exception to its by-law on rates (RCA23-30119); it specifies that the measure is not recurring for the applicant's future events.
Similar free loans were granted for the 2019, 2020, 2023, 2024 and 2025 editions.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is adding $147,052.67 (taxes included) to the professional services contract for the development of the Simon-Valois shared space zone, bringing the contract to $624,302.40.
The contract is held by the consortium made up of Civiliti, François Courville, UDO Design and AXOR Experts-Conseil, selected in 2018 following a design competition.
The project transformed the area around place Simon-Valois into shared streets on rue Ontario and avenue Valois, doubling the size of the public square.
The additional work already completed includes the Ontario/Nicole intersection, a BIXI station, street lights, the replacement of lead water connections and electrical repairs.
The money comes from savings and unused contingencies within the project: no impact on the 2026-2035 capital works program, with the expense covered 100% by the borough.
The final accounting and the closing of the project are scheduled for February 2026.
The City is renewing its maintenance contract with LexisNexis Coplogic Solutions inc. for the DORS solution by mutual agreement, from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2029.
Total cost: US$143,317.39 including taxes, or C$211,393.15 including taxes, paid by the urban agglomeration.
DORS lets citizens fill out reports online, on the SPVM website, for events that do not require an investigation: bicycle theft, graffiti, mischief, lost item, hate incidents, etc.
The SPVM received 13,733 reports through this system from January 1 to October 31, 2025, and close to 15,000 in 2024.
The contract covers technical support, updates and the correction of defects.
Contract awarded without a call for tenders: the supplier is the only one offering this solution, which is integrated into the NicheRMS system used by the SPVM.
After negotiation, the increase is 3% per year instead of the 5% set out in the initial estimate.
The City is adding $536,301.40 (taxes included) to its agreements with Bell Canada for traditional telephone service (digital and analog lines), bringing the total to $18,294,324.12.
This amount serves as a contingency budget: it covers needs and unforeseen items not included in the 2022 call for tenders, and represents 5% of the budget for lot 2.
The money will be used to add about thirty services and products: advanced management of incoming calls, shared voice mailboxes, Internet fax, ring transfer, and personalized call service.
The City has more than 12,190 active telephone lines spread across more than 800 sites; the services covered include public safety, the boroughs and the central services.
The expense will be paid out of the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information, as needs arise, and each expense will have to be validated by that department.
The agreements with Bell were extended by 12 months in August 2025, until October 26, 2026.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the installation of 3 signs at the Centre Sanaaq, at 1200, rue du Sussex, in the Peter-McGill district.

The authorized signs: one window sign of 6.7 m² near the entrance on the boulevard René-Lévesque side, a 2.9 m² stele at the corner of place Henri-Dunant and rue du Sussex, and one of 0.77 m² near the loading dock.
These signs depart from the district's planning rules, which limit window signs to 2 m² and allow only one ground-mounted sign support per building.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme required that the large window sign facing place Henri-Dunant be removed from the project (the temporary 28.71 m² sign that has been in place since the opening).
A 4 m² illuminated sign on the canopy of the main entrance is still planned: it complies with the rules and did not require special authorization.
According to the borough, the signage is meant to make the centre easy to spot from René-Lévesque and to mark the delivery dock in order to reduce unplanned stops.
The file does not provide for any spending; a draft resolution was adopted on September 30, 2025, to be followed by a public consultation before final adoption.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the installation of 18 new signs for the Place des Arts, at 105, rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest, in the Quartier des spectacles.

The project includes 6 aluminum steles 6.5 to 7.5 m high with electronic screens (static content, no animation), 2 round signs at the top of the Édifice des Théâtres, 2 vinyl banners of 31.59 m² at the corner of Sainte-Catherine and Saint-Urbain, a neon sign for the Salle Claude-Léveillée and 7 display cases on rue Saint-Urbain.
The total display area will reach 107.17 m², whereas the planning by-law allows 20 m².
The City is granting exemptions from several signage rules: number of signs, height, area, lighting and the ban on signs at the top of a "building of interest".

The signs in the display cases on rue Saint-Urbain and the two banners may be changed without a new authorization certificate, as long as the dimensions and location remain in line with the approved plans.
Installation work on at least one sign must begin within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The borough council adopted the draft resolution unanimously on September 30, 2025.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is amending its 2026 fee schedule, which was adopted on December 1, 2025 and has been in effect since January 1, 2026.
A new fee is being added for the installation of a fire hydrant.
A new permit is being created for café-terraces with 3 tables and 12 chairs.
The per-square-metre fee for occupying public property (café-terrace or fruit and vegetable stand) is being updated.
An error is being corrected in the section on parking stickers and the issuing of an annual parking permit.
Notice of motion given on December 17, 2025, with adoption planned for the February 2, 2026 meeting, followed by a public notice of coming into force.
No fee amount is specified in the decision summary.
The City is removing lot 6 704 095 from the public domain — a small piece of land created under a wall at 4175-4177, rue Rivard, in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
This step completes the City's abandonment of its party-wall rights in the northwest side wall of this building, which runs along a public lane owned by the City.
The executive committee had approved this abandonment on June 25, 2025, after an owner reported in March 2025 that the wall was unstable and claimed it was a party wall.
According to the Service des affaires juridiques, neither the titles nor the 1989 expropriation plans indicate a party wall; a location certificate provided by the owner says the opposite.
By abandoning this right, the City frees itself from any obligation to pay for maintaining, strengthening or renovating the wall, now and in the future.
A notice of abandonment will be published in the Registre foncier du Québec and sent to the owner.
The file does not provide for any spending.
The City is adding $240,000, taxes included, to the fees of the law firm IMK, which represents it in a class action about paid parking. The total funding rises to $806,981.

The class action, authorized by the Superior Court in 2021, claims against the City and Société en commandite stationnement de Montréal that time paid at parking meters or through a mobile app cannot be carried over or used by the next user.

The plaintiff, Catherine Bergeron-Duchesne, is claiming a refund of the amounts overcharged since June 15, 2015, as well as punitive damages; experts valued the claim at several tens of millions of dollars.
On September 8, 2025, the Superior Court dismissed the class action and ruled in the City's favour. The plaintiff side has announced an appeal.
The new funding covers an additional day of trial in June 2025, the upcoming appeal, travel costs (the case was filed in the district of Québec) and the debate over $534,000 in expert fees.
Ville de Québec, also named in the case, reached an out-of-court settlement.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city.
The City is buying 7 self-propelled electric mowers from Kubota Montréal (Lange Patenaude Équipement ltée) for $285,712.88, plus $34,285.55 in contingencies: a total of $319,998.43, taxes included.
The mowers will be used to maintain green spaces in the boroughs and will replace equipment that has reached the end of its life or meet new needs.
These are rear-discharge, zero-turn mowers with a 60-inch cutting width and 8 hours of run time without charging.
Delivery starts in January 2027 and must be completed by the end of March 2027 at the latest; a delay carries a penalty of 2% per month on the value of the goods not delivered.
The warranty covers 5 years or 2,000 hours of use, and parts must remain available for 12 years.
Kubota's bid was 17.91% below the City's estimate and 37.02% below the other compliant bidder; a third bid was rejected as non-compliant.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, through a loan by-law for replacing vehicles and specialized equipment.

The urban agglomeration council is authorizing a loan of $213,405,000 to replace vehicles and mechanical and specialized equipment, including those of the SPVM and the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal.
The money covers the needs forecast from 2026 to 2030: $41.6M in 2026, $43.8M in 2027, $38.5M in 2028, $44.8M in 2029 and $44.7M in 2030.
The largest share goes to fire service vehicles ($114,068,000), followed by City vehicles ($57,223,000), the SPVM ($37,364,000) and mechanical equipment ($4,750,000).
The debt will be repaid over a maximum of 10 years, out of the agglomeration's general revenues; no subsidy is expected for this expense.
The City says it manages a fleet of about 9,162 vehicles and pieces of equipment and wants to replace those that have become obsolete or non-functional.
The request stems from the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program; the previous by-law (RCG 23-006) was meant to cover 2023 to 2027, but some purchases were made earlier than planned.
The borough of Outremont is amending its by-law on the delegation of powers to speed up the issuing of permits and certificates.

A level 2 public servant will now be able to approve, on their own, the plans for all work covered by the by-law on site planning and architectural integration programmes (PIIA), except for the construction of a new main building.
This approval remains conditional on a favourable opinion from the urban planning advisory committee, either without reservation or with a reservation accepted by the applicant.
The new section lists the projects that are excluded from the delegation rather than those that can be delegated, to make it easier to read.
Notice of motion scheduled for March 10, 2026; adoption of the by-law by the borough council on April 9, 2026.
There is no financial aspect associated with this file.
The borough of Lachine is cancelling the rate of $55 per hour per technician (with a two-hour minimum) that was planned for 2026.
Borrowing audio-visual equipment from the loan counter becomes free again ($0) for recognized organizations, subject to availability.
Having technical staff present at events organized by a recognized organization also becomes free again ($0).
The borough says it wants to support local community life and avoid adding to the financial burden of recognized organizations.
The borough keeps the right to refuse the presence of technical staff if the staff or the equipment is not available.
SOCAN licence fees (music rights) remain the responsibility of the user.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is adding mandatory stops on rue de Liège Ouest, at the east and west approaches to the intersections with rue Clark, rue Saint-Urbain and rue Waverly.
The City will also install small signs showing the layout of the intersection, along with stop lines and marked pedestrian crossings.
The decision responds to requests from residents about safety at these intersections, where young pedestrians walk, near elementary schools, daycares and churches.
Signs announcing the new traffic signs will be put up 30 days before the stop signs are installed, and kept in place for 30 days afterward.
Planned schedule: adoption in March 2026, installation of the signs in March and April 2026, road markings in April 2026.
The work will be done by the Division de l'entretien de l'éclairage, de la signalisation et du marquage de la chaussée, which will bill the borough.
The City is awarding Magil Construction Est du Canada inc. the design-build contract for the new piscine Baldwin, at the corner of rue Fullum and Terrasse Guindon, in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The total expenditure comes to $27,157,357.37 including taxes: $22,500,607.50 for the work, $2,948,918.82 in contingencies and $1,707,831.05 in incidental expenses.
The project includes a bathers' pavilion, a main pool, a wading pool, a rest area and outdoor landscaping, with a capacity of 1,000 users.
The City is adding $714,489.81 net of rebates, taken from the environmental liability reserve, to decontaminate the soil on the terrain Baldwin Nord.
The expenditure is shared: 87.41% by the central city, 9.71% by the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and 2.88% by the environmental liability reserve.
The former pool, built in 1964, reached the end of its useful life in 2019; soil studies in 2021 revealed a former landfill site under the pool, hence the move to the north end of the park.
Eight companies submitted bids out of 38 that took out the tender documents; six failed to reach the 70% passing mark and their prices were not opened.
The executive committee takes note of a report listing 6 real estate decisions made in September 2025 by an official of the Service de la stratégie immobilière, with no new authorization to be given.
Among these decisions: the City obtains from Aéroports de Montréal the right to occupy 424.7 m² of lot 3 117 006 to maintain a water main, for $1.
The ministère des Transports lends the City, free of charge and for 12 months, about 252,762.70 m² of land in the Turcot area, for characterization, geotechnical and topographical studies.
The City is leasing to Devimco immobilier a piece of land in the Square Children project, in Ville-Marie, retroactively from May 16, 2020 to February 19, 2021, for $10,940.40 before taxes.

The lease of Racine Croisée Solidarité Sawa at 505, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est is extended by 3 months starting November 1, 2025, for about 1,410 sq. ft. used for food distribution, at a cost of $3,701.40 before taxes.
The City is buying from Carmela Triventi a vacant lot of 1,106.8 m² in Beaconsfield, for regional park purposes, for $19,900 plus taxes.
La Coopérative d'Habitation Monde-Uni is authorized to carry out due diligence checks on land at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is reclassifying the $2,500 paid to the Chambre de commerce et d'industrie de Montréal-Nord: it is a taxable purchase of tickets ($2,500 including taxes) and not a non-taxable contribution.
The amount is now charged as entertainment expenses, with an expense report produced in accordance with the applicable administrative framework.
The money was for the borough's participation as a partner in the CCIMN's "Gala Reconnaissance 2025 - La magie de la réussite", held on November 13, 2025.
In exchange, the CCIMN provided two free tickets for borough representatives, along with visibility before and during the event.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
In previous years, the borough had granted $10,000 to the CCIMN for its galas (2015 to 2018, 2022, 2023).

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is reopening the pedestrian crossing on the south side of chemin de la Côte-Saint-Luc, at the intersection with boulevard Décarie, and is having the 4 prohibition signs removed.
This crossing had been prohibited during the work on the échangeur Turcot (2014-2021) in order to increase the intersection's vehicle capacity.
Turning left becomes mandatory in the left lane for vehicles coming from the east, at the intersection with Décarie sud.
The requirement to turn left is being removed in the left lane for vehicles coming from the west, at the intersection with Décarie nord.

On the north side of chemin de la Côte-Saint-Luc, 5 metres west of Décarie sud and over about 50 metres: stopping becomes prohibited at all times, replacing the no-stopping restriction from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. and the no-parking restriction from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday.
The work orders for the signs are planned for March 2026 and the work itself for spring 2026, in coordination with the new traffic light programming.
"New signage" signs will be installed when the change is made; the cost of the signs is billed by the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
The LaSalle borough is extending the cleaning contract for the borough hall with Entretien Mana inc. by one year.
The extension is worth $98,700.99 including taxes and covers March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027.
This is the second and last option year provided for in the contract awarded through a public call for tenders in 2022 ($302,456.45 for three years).
The rates are indexed to the consumer price index: the regular hourly rate goes from $22.90 to $23.50, and the emergency rate from $29.78 to $30.56.
The borough justifies the extension by the continuity of cleaning service at the borough hall.

The Ville de Montréal agrees to receive, on permanent loan, the collection of archaeological objects found on the site of the faubourg à M'lasse during the digs carried out for the construction of the new Maison de Radio-Canada.
The collection consists of 47 archive-size boxes; it remains the property of Radio-Canada and Société en commandite La Nouvelle Maison.
The objects will be kept at the City's Réserve des collections archéologiques, at 333, rue Peel, a space that meets museum standards (controlled temperature and humidity).
The City will be able to use the objects for research, analysis, exhibition and outreach, and to lend them temporarily to museum, scientific and university partners.
The City becomes responsible for any loss of or damage to the objects caused by its own negligence or that of a third party to whom it lends them.
The loan is free of charge and for an unlimited period; there is no additional cost for the City, as storage and management costs are absorbed by the Réserve's operating budget.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough council approves the plans to add an entrance vestibule at the front of 7185, rue Marquette, a two-storey duplex in the François-Perrault district.
The vestibule is 1.5 m deep and about 3 m wide, on a single storey, with stone cladding similar to the existing one and a door reached by a concrete landing.
The owner wants to correct a non-compliance issue: the two units are not separated by doors and fire separations that meet the rules. The vestibule will provide access to a door for each unit.
The urban planning advisory committee had turned down the project on September 3, 2025 (the volume was considered too bulky and the roof not suited to the neighbourhood).

The applicant then replaced the two-slope roof with a single slope in grey sheet metal, reduced the width by about 30 cm and changed the door model; the CCU gave a favourable opinion on December 10, with conditions about the colour of the door and the addition of a gutter.
The work is estimated at $46,573; the permit review fees are $456.42 and the PIIA fees are $484.
The plans will have to be corrected before the permit is issued, to move the garbage enclosure off public property and onto the private lot, hidden by a 1.5 m plant screen.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing the conversion of a duplex into a single-family home at 7571-7573, avenue Casgrain, which removes one rental unit.
The owners live on the ground floor; the 2nd-floor unit is currently rented. They want to combine the two units to create three bedrooms and an office.
Three conditions apply: keep the outdoor staircase and the 2nd-floor door on the front of the building, limit the residential area to 250 m², and file the permit application within 12 months.
The Direction du développement du territoire supports the application: the lot is 6.05 m wide, which limits any expansion, and the change can be reversed.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme recommended approval on December 10, 2025, under the same conditions.
The fees to review the application come to $3,224.
At the meeting, no one asked to be heard on the application.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension approves the plans for a 3-storey, 26-unit building at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie.
The social housing project is led by the Coopérative d'Habitation Monde-Uni, with funding from the Société d'habitation du Québec; delivery is hoped for before the end of 2026.
The units break down into 17 studios (about 42 m²) and 9 one-bedroom units (about 52 m²), without air conditioning.
No car parking spaces: 29 bicycle spaces in the basement, plus bike racks in the side yard.
The ground floor will be accessible by a ramp and three units there will be of adaptable design; there is no elevator.
Six trees will be planted and 68% of the unbuilt land will be greened, but most of the existing trees and two trees on public property will be cut down for the construction in prefabricated modules.
Approximate value of the work: $9,586,218, with permit fees of $93,944.94 and site planning and architectural integration programme (PIIA) fees of $426.40.
City council takes note of the report by the Office de consultation publique de Montréal (OCPM) on the draft by-law governing the redevelopment of the Van Horne warehouse, in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The project calls for the transformation of 1, avenue Van Horne and the demolition of the building at 55, avenue Van Horne, to be replaced by a four-storey commercial building.

The complex would include affordable artists' studios and creative spaces (3,888 m², or 31% of the rental space) managed by Les Ateliers Belleville, a hotel with about 120 rooms, stores on the ground floor, a greenhouse on the roof and a public lookout.
An underground parking lot with 50 spaces for vehicles and 31 for bicycles is planned; "daycare" use would be prohibited and the painted signs would have to be restored.

The consultation was held from September to October 2025: an information session on September 15, a participatory workshop on September 30, a hearing of opinions on October 14, online submission of opinions and nearly 10,000 flyers distributed.

The commissioners make 10 recommendations; participants welcome the mix of uses and the artists' studios, but express reservations about the hotel, the long-term affordability of the studios, the impacts on heritage and the risk of gentrification.
The urban agglomeration council is adopting a by-law that authorizes a loan of $10,880,000 for the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM).
The money will be used to buy and replace specialized public safety equipment, along with the parts and accessories needed, between 2026 and 2030.
The loan must be repaid over a maximum of 5 years, out of the general revenues of the agglomeration of Montréal.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration, since police service is an agglomeration power; no government subsidy is planned.
The document cites the SPVM's obligation, as an employer, to provide equipment that is in good condition and meets standards.
Next steps: approval of the by-law by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation, then a public notice that it has come into force.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is paying about $6,500 (plus taxes) to send five elected officials to an event in Nicolet.
The event, the second edition of the Nouvelle Vague Municipale, takes place on March 18 and 19, 2026.
The elected officials concerned: Mayor François Limoges and councillors Jocelyn Pauzé, Ericka Alneus, Josefina Blanco and Olivier Demers-Dubé.

The document describes the Nouvelle Vague Municipale as a group of five elected officials that wants to renew the value of the municipal elected official's role and encourage citizen involvement in municipal politics.
About 250 people are expected at the forum, with the mayor of Nicolet, Geneviève Dubois, as honorary chair.
The spending is approved by the borough council.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is renting six sidewalk sweepers with operators, maintenance and accessories, for $272,352.78 including taxes.
The contract goes to Déneigement et excavation M. Gauthier inc., the lowest compliant bidder; the other bid (Benco Canada) was $330,301.80.
The machines will be used for spring cleaning of sidewalks from April 1, 2026 to May 15, 2028, for about 840 hours per year between April 1 and May 15.
Work may start earlier than planned depending on weather conditions.
The borough says it does not have enough machines to clean its whole territory; it has been renting from private companies since 2006.
The expense is paid entirely by the borough, out of its operating budget; the bid price is 26.61% below the estimate of $344,834.70.
The company's performance will be evaluated at the end of the contract.
The City is signing two 2025-2026 funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec (SHQ) to help households that lose their housing.
Part 1: the SHQ reimburses the City 50% of eligible expenses (moving, storage of belongings, temporary accommodation), up to $0.80 per resident, for a maximum of $1,558,998.

Part 2: the housing search assistance service of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal receives $500,000, of which $450,000 comes from the SHQ and $50,000 from the City, plus up to $75,000 for a dedicated resource person for households that need sustained follow-up.
Claims cover costs incurred from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.
In 2024, the service helped 2,075 households find new housing and temporarily housed 402 households, for an average stay of 83 days.

The rehousing assistance budget comes 100% from the operating budget of the Service de l'habitation; the funding envelope planned for the Office municipal d'habitation in 2026-2028 reaches $16,970,109.
The management of the Service de l'habitation is authorized to sign both agreements on behalf of the City.
The City is giving Université Concordia technical support valued at an estimated $9,400 for a research project on the canal de l'aqueduc de Montréal.
No money is being paid out: the contribution takes the form of about 110 hours of work by employees of the Direction de l'eau potable.
The "Hydromancie" project aims to make citizens, especially those living nearby, aware of the usefulness of the canal de l'aqueduc and its water intake.
The researchers will conduct interviews with employees and site visits (including the usine Atwater and water intakes), with photos, videos, sound recordings and 3D scanning.
A participatory lab with citizens will lead to a collective artistic creation activity.
The agreement runs from February 4, 2026 to February 3, 2028 and covers confidentiality, publications, intellectual property and termination.
The expense is fully covered by the urban agglomeration; the project is also co-funded by federal and Québec granting agencies.

The City is awarding a contract of $810,798.76 (taxes included) to Les Terrassements Multi-Paysages inc. to prepare the site for a future pumptrack at parc Adrien-D.-Archambault, on Île-des-Sœurs, in Verdun.
With contingencies ($121,619.81) and incidentals ($40,539.94), the total expense comes to $972,958.51.

The work includes brush clearing, soil decontamination and management, earthworks, drainage, a biogas protection system, lighting, a pipe for a drinking fountain, plantings and measures to protect the brown snake.
