The operating budget of the borough of Verdun is being increased by $311,866 (net of rebates), paid 100% by the central city out of the reserve for the environmental liability of contaminated sites.
The Programme des installations sportives extérieures is providing assistance of up to $157,200 (net of rebates); any cost overrun will be absorbed by the borough.
Nine companies submitted bids out of 19 that picked up the documents; the winning bid is 1.70% below the borough's estimate.
The work to build the track itself had already been awarded in 2024; an authorization from the ministère de l'Environnement is still under review before any work can start.

The borough of Lachine is appointing its mayor, Julie-Pascale Provost, as the borough's representative on the board of directors of PME MTL Ouest-de-l'Île (West-Island), a local economic development organization.
The borough council adopted the appointment unanimously at a special meeting on December 18, 2025.
The appointment must be confirmed by the urban agglomeration council, which has jurisdiction over local development centres.
The document does not mention any amount of money or any term length.
The borough of LaSalle is approving four new parking spaces reserved for people with reduced mobility.
One space on 2e Avenue, one on 8e Avenue, one on avenue Alepin and one on rue Simonne.
Each space will be reserved at all times and placed as close as possible to the home of the person who requested it.
The measure responds to requests from residents found to be eligible after review, following the borough's procedure.
Signs will be installed to mark off the spaces.
The costs will be paid out of the operating budget of the Direction des travaux publics; no amount is specified.
The borough of LaSalle will sign an agreement with a resident, Yordan Yordanov, for the construction of a 150 mm drinking water main over about 47 metres, on 41e Avenue.
The main will serve the homes on 41e Avenue and supply the sprinkler system of Résidence à la Bonne Étoile inc., at 660-664, 41e Avenue.
The work includes the water main, service connections, the roadway, paving, curbs, sidewalks, driveway entrances, tree planting and lighting.
The estimated cost of the work is $178,500.00, all taxes included, plus $12,000.00 in supervision fees; everything is payable by the resident.
A bank guarantee equal to 100% of the cost of the work is required before the first building permit is issued.
The work is planned from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027, with daily cleaning of the surrounding streets and dust reduction.
When the work is finished, the resident must provide the "as-built" plans, the watertightness tests and the material quality control report.
The City is extending by 12 months, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, the cleaning and maintenance contract for the headquarters of the Service de police de Montréal (SPVM).
The contract remains with Service d'entretien Alphanet inc., which has been working in this building since 2017.
Additional cost of $302,519.82 including taxes: $275,018.02 for the services and $27,501.80 in contingencies (10%).
The total contract therefore rises to $1,512,599.09, including taxes.
The company provides the labour, the sanitation maintenance equipment and the hygiene products, 7 days a week, 365 days a year, plus one major annual cleaning.
The bill is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, since policing is an agglomeration responsibility.
The Service des immeubles states that the services provided are satisfactory and that the supplier has accepted the extension.
The City is extending the maintenance contract for the historic gardens of the Cité-des-Hospitalières, at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, by 12 months.
The contract stays with Jardin de lumière (Richard Archambault), who agreed to the renewal.
Additional spending of $87,406.05 including taxes: $72,838.37 for the services and $14,567.68 in contingencies (20%).
The total contract therefore rises to $331,778.25 including taxes.
The extension runs from November 16, 2025 to November 15, 2026; prices are adjusted by 2.21% based on the consumer price index.
The work covers cleaning, horticultural maintenance, watering, plant health monitoring and winter preparation; the vegetable garden and lawn mowing are excluded.
The spending is paid out of the operating budget of the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles, and is borne by the central city.

The City is awarding SES-Intégration inc. (Darspec) the maintenance, inspection and testing of backflow prevention devices, for $218,124.82, plus $43,624.96 in contingencies (20%), for a total of $261,749.79, taxes included.
The contract covers about 163 devices spread across 80 City buildings, in order to comply with the Code de construction du Québec (standard CSA-B64.10).
It runs from May 1, 2026 to January 31, 2029 (33 months), with two 12-month renewal options ($88,669 and $90,442).
The services included: preventive maintenance, regular and emergency calls, corrective maintenance, and repair, replacement or upgrade work.
Two companies picked up the tender documents and only one submitted a bid; its price is 16.36% ($42,667.22) below the City's estimate.
The cost is paid by the agglomeration (80.37%), the central city (4.91%) and the boroughs (14.72%).
According to the document, delaying the contract would affect the protection of the buildings' drinking water system against contamination risks.

The City is extending by 12 months, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, the contract for the annual deep cleaning of fire stations and the washing of garages for the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal.
The contract stays with 9119-5867 Québec inc. (Entretien Avangardiste inc.), which accepted the renewal on November 21, 2025.
Additional spending of $166,718.05 including taxes: $151,561.87 for the work and $15,156.19 in contingencies (10%).
Prices are indexed by 2% compared with the previous year, under a clause in the contract.
The contract therefore goes from $644,181.78 to $796,040.83, including taxes, since it was awarded in 2022.
The spending is paid out of the operating budget of the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles and is fully covered by the agglomeration.
The work includes dusting and cleaning walls, ceilings, mechanical equipment, exposed piping and fixed furniture; the company supplies the labour and materials.
The City is extending its agreement with EBI Envirotech inc. by 12 months to empty the oil separators, drains, gutters and catch basins of various municipal buildings.
The extension runs from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027 and costs $349,566.86 including taxes, of which $291,305.72 is for the services and $58,261.14 is for contingencies (20%).
The total value of the agreement thus rises to $1,269,718.17 including taxes.
The locations covered include municipal garages and workshops and fire stations; the agreement also covers the spring emptying of outdoor pools and the pumping of arena snow pits.
The supplier handles the pumping, transportation, disposal and decontamination of liquid and solid residues, in accordance with environmental regulations.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles, as needs arise.
Since the buildings involved are spread across the whole territory, the agreement may lead to agglomeration expenses; the decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is ending the lease for the 650 m² premises in the basement at 5205, rue Saint-Zotique Est, rented from the Fabrique de la paroisse Saint-Bonaventure.
The termination takes effect September 22, 2025, the date of a fire that made the premises inaccessible. The lease was to run until December 31, 2029.
The premises were used for community, sports and recreational activities.
The total rent planned for the rest of the lease was $166,409.59. Payments stopped on September 22, 2025.
Part of the 2025 balance was used to add hours to the agreement with the Centre Épic; the 2026 amounts could fund a relocation agreement.
The borough has temporarily relocated some activities and is looking at a lasting solution, including a possible reopening of the premises for the winter 2026 session.
The borough of Ville-Marie is removing lot 6 412 466 from the public domain, a small city-owned parcel used as a pedestrian passage near rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest and rue Mackay.
This removal is the step needed to transfer the land to the company Les Immeubles Prime inc., owner of the neighbouring building at 1449-1457, rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest.
The transfer is being made as damages and closes an out-of-court settlement approved in March 2020, after the City withdrew from an expropriation planned in order to create a park.

The transferred lot will remain subject to a public passage and park servitude, in continuity with the future local park planned on the land acquired around the St-Jax church (1439, rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest).
The borough states that the transfer will have little impact compared with the current situation, because of these servitudes.
The file does not involve any financial aspect.

The City is awarding the repair of the railway bridge over rue Wellington, between rue de la Congrégation and rue de la Sucrerie, in Le Sud-Ouest, to the Canadien National (CN) without a call for tenders.

The total expense is estimated at $9,253,975.58, taxes included: $8,036,936.46 for the work, management and professional services of the CN, $1,205,541.62 in contingencies (15%) and $11,497.50 for the City's internal costs.
The work paid for by the City includes repairing the concrete columns and abutment walls, rebuilding the structural sidewalks, replacing the guardrails, as well as pavement markings and signage.

The Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM) is paying for its own work, estimated at $234,951.41: a concrete duct bank with 8 conduits and the demolition and reconstruction of a structural sidewalk.
The CN is acting as the project manager; it will issue the call for tenders in spring 2026 and the work would be spread over 2026 and 2027.
The CN requires an advance of 50% of the amount as soon as the contract is signed; the final cost will not be known until after the work is done and could require additional funds.

The bridge, built in 1961, has deteriorated (freeze and thaw, de-icing salts, water infiltration) and has been the subject of complaints from residents; a 1966 order requires the City to pay for the upkeep of certain parts.
The City is adding $1,075,199.20 (taxes included) to the contract with Les Entreprises Michaudville inc. for work on avenue Christophe-Colomb, between Rosemont and Henri-Bourassa.
The contract therefore goes from $9,682,098.87 to $10,757,298.07, an increase of 11.11% over the original amount.
The work affects Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension and Ahuntsic-Cartierville; it is 95% complete.

The money covers quantities that went over budget: 900 sq. m of sidewalks redone, 7 catch basins replaced, management of 840 tonnes of soil, roadway repairs, bus shelter slabs, and labour cost indexation.
The Service explains the overruns by a call for tenders launched on a fast-track basis and the late inclusion of electrical assets (CSEM) in the design.
Work resumes in April–May 2026 and is to be completed in May 2026; the contractual deadline of 210 days could be extended.
The expense is borne by the agglomeration; the Service indicates that no further increase will be requested in this file.
City council is adopting a loan by-law of $26,000,000 to fund the Programme d'acquisition de mobilier d'éclairage between 2025 and 2029.
The money will be used to improve street lighting on the arterial road network: electrical work, installation of light fixtures, conduit banks, concrete bases, and repair of affected surfaces.
According to the document, 70% of the lighting equipment on the arterial network is obsolete; standard light fixtures will be replaced with LED fixtures, which use less energy.
The planned breakdown is $4M per year from 2025 to 2028, then $10M in 2029.
The loan also covers professional fees, studies, design, work supervision and unforeseen expenses, with financing over a maximum of 20 years.
The by-law must be approved by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation; contracts would be awarded starting in December 2025 and work would begin in January 2026.
The City is committing to pay $827,820 (taxes included) for its share of repairs to the boulevard Lacordaire bridge over autoroute 40, in Saint-Léonard.
The ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec is running the work site and pays the bills first; the City then reimburses it.
The City's share represents about 5.8% of the total project cost, estimated at $14,327,034.75, taxes included.

The work paid for by the City: repairing the guardrails, sidewalks and concrete median, replacing the lighting on and under the bridge, and moving the traffic lights to make it easier for trucks to turn.
Timeline: call for tenders in winter 2026, work from spring 2026 to fall 2027.

During the work: at least 2 lanes in each direction and a pedestrian corridor will be kept open on Lacordaire, a single lane in each direction on the service roads, and full nighttime closures of autoroute 40, one direction at a time.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city, through the loan by-law on the rebuilding of road structures.

The City is awarding Construction Demathieu & Bard (CDB) inc. the rebuilding of the four retaining walls of the Querbes underpass, beneath autoroute Métropolitaine, for $20,067,967.56 including taxes.
With contingencies ($3,010,195.13) and incidental expenses ($1,663,239.95), the total spending comes to $24,741,402.64, paid 100% by the central city.
The work affects the boroughs of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension and Ahuntsic-Cartierville, and is scheduled from March 2026 to November 2027.

On the program: rebuilding of the walls and the lighting, resurfacing of the roadway on boulevard Crémazie Ouest, changes to the geometry of the lanes and intersections, and removal of the sidewalks next to the walls.
The approaches to the CPKC railway level crossing will be modified to allow universal accessibility.
A negotiated contract of $508,656.47 is being awarded to Canadian Pacific Kansas City for railway signalling and technical assistance during the work.
Three companies submitted bids out of 18 who took out the tender documents; the lowest bid is 4.31% below the estimate, and a delay would cost the contractor $13,727.10 per day.

The City is awarding Insituform Technologies Limited a contract to rehabilitate sewer pipes on various streets in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, for a total expense of $9,133,917.15, taxes included.
The amount breaks down into $8,179,179 for the contract, $817,917.89 in contingencies (10%) and $136,820.26 in incidental expenses.
About 8.1 km of combined sewer pipes will be rehabilitated using lining, a trenchless technique that keeps traffic moving during the work.
The work is to begin in April 2026 and be completed in October 2026.
Three companies submitted bids; the winning bid is the lowest, 8.84% below the professionals' estimate.
The contractor will pay 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city; part of the work is subsidized at 98% through the TECQ24 program.

The City is awarding Les Pavages Céka inc. a contract worth $12,548,770.97 (taxes included) to replace lead water service lines and redo roadways; with contingencies ($1,254,877.10) and incidental costs ($363,843.11), the total expense comes to $14,167,491.18.

The work covers various streets in Anjou, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Montréal-Nord, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. The list of street sections is attached to the file.
About 302 lead water service lines will be replaced with copper, in addition to the resurfacing of about 50,400 m² of roadway and the rebuilding of 4,365 m² of sidewalks.
The replacement includes the private portion of service lines made of lead or of galvanized steel that has been in contact with lead, in accordance with by-law 20-030.
The City is aiming to eliminate lead on its territory by the end of 2032.
The contractor faces daily penalties for delays: up to $3,500 per day per street depending on the impact, and $1,000 per day for street cleaning not done within 48 hours. No bonus is provided for.
Five bids were received; the winning bid is 2.49% above the professionals' estimate and 18.32% below the second-lowest bid. The expense is paid entirely by the central city.
The City is hiring Insituform Technologies Limited to rehabilitate about 4.5 km of sewer pipes using lining, a technique that requires no excavation and keeps traffic moving during the work.
The work will affect streets in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Anjou, L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Montréal-Nord, Pierrefonds-Roxboro and Saint-Laurent; the list of streets is attached to the file.
Total spending of $3,318,238 including taxes: $2,972,000 for the contract, $297,200 in contingencies and $49,038 in incidental costs.
Three companies submitted bids; the one chosen is the lowest and is 14.21% below the professionals' estimate.
The contractor will pay a penalty of 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day; no bonus is provided for.
The spending is paid 100% by the central city; part of the work is subsidized at 96% by the TECQ24 program, and $121,199.74 net remains to be paid by taxpayers.
The City will assess the company's performance under this contract.
The City is awarding Procova inc. the contract to build the pavilion in parc Irma-LeVasseur, in Outremont, for $1,370,502, taxes included.
With contingencies ($205,575.30) and incidentals ($159,815.25), the total spending comes to $1,735,892.55, paid entirely by the central city.
The pavilion, about 55 m², will include two washrooms (one of them universally accessible), a storage room and a utility room, with a power supply for the mobile stages of place Alice-Girard.
The building will be built next to the STM metro ventilation station and will partly incorporate it; the rest of the station will be covered with the same brick.

The park, 18,500 m² in size and located south of avenue Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux between avenue Dollard and avenue Wiseman, will also serve as a schoolyard park as of the start of the school year in August 2026.
Procova was the lowest of 14 bidders, at 32.41% below the professionals' estimate; its performance will be evaluated.
The work is being coordinated with the park landscaping carried out by Charex inc., which is to be finished in the fall of 2026.

The City is awarding Construction NRC inc. a contract worth $421,791.54 (taxes included) for lighting work in Ville-Marie; with contingencies ($63,268.73) and incidental costs ($285,138), the total expense comes to $770,198.27.
The work covers six street sections, or 565 metres: replacing outdated street lights and wiring, bringing equipment up to standard and making it uniform, LED lighting and buried electrical wires.
Work to connect to the network is planned on rues Brésoles, Saint-Jean, de L'Hôpital and Notre-Dame, by the Commission des services électriques.
Work is to start on November 30, 2026 and finish on December 18, 2026; the contractor will pay 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day.

Six companies submitted bids; the winning bid is 17.31% below the estimate made by the professionals. The bid from Néolect inc. was rejected because its insurance coverage was $1,000,000 instead of the required $2,000,000.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, through a loan by-law for the purchase of lighting equipment.
The City will evaluate Construction NRC inc.'s performance under this contract.
City council awards Insituform Technologies Limited a $6,378,378 contract (taxes included) to rehabilitate sewer pipes using lining.
The total spending comes to $7,148,437.05: the contract, $637,837.80 in contingencies and $132,221.25 in incidental costs, paid entirely by the central city.
About 6.1 km of combined sewer pipes will be rehabilitated in the boroughs of Le Sud-Ouest, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Verdun and Ville-Marie. The list of streets is attached to the file.
The lining technique is trenchless: traffic is maintained during the work and disruptions are reduced.
Three companies submitted bids out of six that took out the tender documents; the winning bid is 14.79% below the professionals' estimate.
The contractor will pay 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day. No bonus is provided for.
Part of the work, $5,871,053.69 net, is eligible for the TECQ subsidy program; the City will assess the company's performance.

The City is awarding FER-PAL Construction Ltd. a contract worth $8,988,084.11 (taxes included) to rehabilitate water mains and roadways; with contingencies ($898,808.41) and incidentals ($258,911.04), the total expense reaches $10,145,803.56, paid by the central city.
The work affects various streets in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Pierrefonds-Roxboro and Saint-Laurent; the list of streets is attached to the file.
On the agenda: about 2.5 km of secondary water mains rehabilitated by lining (trenchless), 40,820 m² of roadway redone by milling and resurfacing, and about 913 m² of sidewalks repaired.
About 16 lead water service lines will be replaced on the public portion and 6 on the private portion.

Three bids were received from ten parties that took out the tender documents; the winning bid is 14.74% above the professionals' estimate ($1,154,415.56 more), a gap linked to maintaining mobility and to overhead costs.

The contractor faces daily penalties in the event of delay: from $1,000 to $3,500 per day depending on the street, plus $1,000 per day if street cleaning is not done within 48 hours. No bonus is provided for.
FER-PAL Construction Ltd.'s performance will be evaluated.
The City is awarding Uniroc Construction inc. a $615,423.28 contract (taxes included) to redo the asphalt at 21 bus stops, by milling and asphalt paving.
With contingencies ($92,313.49) and incidentals ($16,096.50), the total expense comes to $723,833.27, paid 100% by the central city.
The work affects six boroughs: Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Anjou, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, LaSalle, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension and Saint-Laurent.
The work site is planned from May 2026 to July 2026; the contractor pays a penalty of 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day.
Of the 9 bids received, Uniroc's is the lowest: 18.71% below the professionals' estimate and 26.1% below the second-lowest bid.
One stop (William MacDonald/Georges V) was removed from the contract by addendum, since it had already been done in 2025.
The City will assess the contractor's performance at the end of the contract.

The City is awarding Les Pavages Céka inc. a contract worth $4,284,066.54 (taxes included) to replace lead water service lines and redo road surfaces in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and Outremont.
With contingencies ($428,406.65) and incidental costs ($107,101.66), the total expense comes to $4,819,574.85, taxes included, paid entirely by the central city.
The work covers about 108 lead water service lines to be replaced with copper, 17,418 m² of planing and resurfacing, and 988 m² of rebuilt sidewalks.
The replacement also covers the private portion of service lines made of lead or of galvanized steel that has been in contact with lead.
Seven companies submitted bids; the winning bid is 7.45% above the professionals' estimate ($3,987,184.22).
Penalties of $500 to $3,500 per day of delay are provided for, notably for failing to meet the deadlines for each street and for street cleaning.
The City was aiming to eliminate lead across its territory by the end of 2032; it will assess the contractor's performance.

The City is awarding Pavages Métropolitain inc. a contract worth $9,288,604.50 (taxes included) for asphalt planing and resurfacing; with contingencies and incidental costs, the total expense comes to $10,589,009.13.

The work covers about 19.77 km of streets in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Saint-Léonard and Ville-Marie, including about 2.42 km of bike path.

The contracts are limited to redoing the roadway: no sidewalk repairs and no improvements to the existing layout. The list of streets was sent to the boroughs in February 2025 so they could redo the sidewalks they consider critical themselves.

The contractor will pay $8,078.80 for each day of delay (before taxes) if it exceeds the time allowed for a street, and $500 per day if it is late rebuilding the speed bumps. No bonus is provided for.
Seven companies submitted bids; the winning bid is 15.25% lower than the professionals' estimate ($10,960,382.42).
The City will assess the contractor's performance. The expense is paid 95.55% by the central city and 4.45% by the agglomeration.
According to the surveys cited, the share of the arterial network in poor or very poor condition rose from 25% in 2020 to 29% in 2024.

The City is awarding FER-PAL Construction ltd. a contract worth $14,462,658.69 (taxes included), for a total expense of $16,415,129.11 including contingencies ($1,446,265.87) and incidental costs ($506,204.56).
The work involves replacing about 387 lead water service lines, rehabilitating about 37,500 m² of roadway and rebuilding 6,513 m² of sidewalks.
The streets involved are in the boroughs of Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
The contract also covers the replacement of the private portions of service lines made of lead or galvanized steel that have been in contact with lead.
The City aimed to eliminate lead from its territory by the end of 2032, on both public and private property.
Penalties of $500 to $3,500 per day of delay are provided for depending on the failure (schedule, time limit per street, cleanup, deficiencies); no bonus is provided for.
FER-PAL was the lowest of the 4 compliant bidders; the price is 14.25% above the professionals' estimate ($12,658,836.79). The expense is borne by the central city.
The City is awarding CGI Environnement inc. a contract worth $11,386,952.49 (taxes included) to rehabilitate sewer pipes in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
With $1,138,695.24 in contingencies and $187,884.72 in incidental costs, the total expense comes to $12,713,532.45.
About 10.7 km of combined sewer pipes will be rehabilitated by lining, a technique that requires no excavation and keeps traffic flowing during the work; the list of streets is attached to the file.
CGI Environnement is the lowest of the three bidders; its price is 21.16% below the professionals' estimate ($14,442,970.12).
The contractor will pay a penalty of 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day. No bonus is provided for.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city; part of the work is subsidized at 94% by the TECQ24 program, leaving $696,548.98 to be paid by taxpayers.
The file is going before the Commission permanente sur l'examen des contrats, and the City will evaluate the company's performance.
The City is awarding Gérald Théorêt inc. a contract worth $5,852,168.79 (taxes included) to rebuild the sewer, water main and roadway on rue Rochon and rue Crevier, in Saint-Laurent.
With contingencies ($585,216.88) and incidental costs ($579,364.70), the total expense comes to $7,016,750.37, paid 93.53% by the central city and 6.47% by the borough of Saint-Laurent.

The work covers rue Rochon between Grenet and Cardinal and rue Crevier between Côte-Vertu and 1225 Crevier: about 593 m of combined sewer and 622 m of water mains rebuilt, plus the replacement of 4 lead service lines on private property.
The roadway will be rebuilt over about 5,355 m² and repaved (milling and surfacing) on rue Rochon between Cardinal and avenue Décarie, over about 2,120 m².
The street will be narrowed to 8.4 metres, the sidewalks widened to 1.8 metres, and planted curb extensions will be built at the south intersection of Crevier and Rochon.
The pipes in question date from 1941 to 1958, and the sewer was found to be in very poor condition during inspections.
Of the 14 bids received, the lowest is 27.92% below the professionals' estimate; the contractor's performance will be evaluated.
The City is awarding a $7,830,000 contract (taxes included) to Services d'infrastructures Vortex inc., the lowest of the three bidders, for water main and road work.
With contingencies ($783,000) and incidental costs ($196,453.61), the total expense comes to $8,809,453.61, paid by the central city.
The work affects various streets in the boroughs of Lachine, Le Sud-Ouest, Outremont and Verdun.
Planned work includes: about 1.56 km of secondary water pipes rehabilitated by lining (without excavation), 12,115 m² of roadway resurfaced and 2,276 m² of sidewalks repaired.
About 146 lead water service lines will be replaced on the public side and 59 on the private side.
The contractor faces daily penalties for delays, up to $3,500 per day for a street with major impact.
The file is going before the Commission sur l'examen des contrats: cost of more than $4M and a 20% gap with the second-lowest bidder.

The City is awarding Les Entrepreneurs Bucaro inc. a road work contract worth $8,265,081.77, for a total expense of $9,380,867.81 including taxes (the contract, $826,508.18 in contingencies and $289,277.86 in incidental costs).
The work covers Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Anjou and Montréal-Nord, on about 11 km of streets, including about 0.13 km of bike path.
The work involves planing and laying new asphalt surfacing, with no work on sidewalks and no redevelopment; the list of streets is attached.
Bucaro was the lowest of the 6 bidders, at 7.96% below the professionals' estimate ($714,323.13 less).
The contractor will pay a penalty of $7,188.59 (before taxes) per day if it goes past the planned deadline for a street; no bonus is provided for.
The expense is paid 99.61% by the central city and 0.39% by the urban agglomeration, and the contractor's performance will be evaluated.
According to the surveys cited, the share of the arterial network in poor or very poor condition rose from 25% in 2020 to 29% in 2024.

The City is awarding FER-PAL Construction ltd. a contract worth $9,448,748.17 (taxes included) to rehabilitate water mains and roadways in Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
With contingencies ($1,417,312.23) and incidental expenses ($237,423.38), the total expense comes to $11,103,483.78, paid entirely by the central city.
The work calls for about 2.6 km of secondary water mains to be rehabilitated by lining, a trenchless technique, and about 30,000 m² of roadway to be redone by milling and resurfacing.
About 53 lead water service lines will be replaced on the public side and 15 on the private side; about 420 m² of sidewalk will be repaired.
The contractor faces daily penalties ranging from $500 to $3,500 depending on the type of delay and the impact on the street affected; no bonus is provided for.
FER-PAL was the lowest of the 3 bidders; its price is 5.62% above the estimate made by the City's professionals.
The City will assess the contractor's performance under this contract.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is adding about 91 paid parking spaces on avenue Papineau, between rue Saint-Grégoire and rue Sherbrooke.
The time-limited spaces (15 min, 30 min, 60 min, 2 h or more) in front of businesses will be removed and replaced by these paid spaces.
The supply of resident-only parking permits (SRRR) will be adjusted to reach a ratio of 70%, as elsewhere in the borough.
The stated goal: improve vehicle turnover and reduce cruising for parking around the businesses.
The Agence de mobilité durable estimates gross annual revenues of about $149,000, of which about $96,850 would go to the borough.
Installation of the signs, sub-panels and payment terminals is planned for summer-fall 2026; residents and businesses will receive a notice 1 to 2 weeks beforehand.
The borough of Lachine is offering to handle the design, coordination and completion of minor sidewalk repair work itself, on streets of the City's arterial road network located within its territory.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is funding the work 100%, with a budget of $400,000 (net of rebates) for Lachine.
The work targets deteriorated sidewalk sections, described as dangerous; the list of streets is in request RMT26_LAC.
The project provides for new universal access ramps with tactile warning plates at the intersections of the targeted sections.
City council is to accept the offer in April 2026; the contract is expected to be awarded in April 2026.
Residents will be informed during the work in order to reduce its impacts.
If the offer is turned down, the objectives of the arterial network sidewalk repair program cannot be met.
The City becomes the owner of the traffic lights installed at the intersections of rue Honoré-Beaugrand with avenue Souligny and avenue Dubuisson, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.

The company Renouveau La Fontaine C-C s.e.n.c., which carried out the work on the tunnel Louis-Hippolyte-La Fontaine, is transferring this equipment at no cost; its market value is estimated at $70,765.53 before taxes, and the taxes are $0.
The transfer also includes the changes to the CN level crossing warning system and the equipment added to the existing traffic lights at the intersection of Honoré-Beaugrand / Hochelaga.
The equipment is transferred as is, with no warranty other than the manufacturer's; the City pays the costs of publishing the deed.

The detour route related to the tunnel work was removed on December 1, 2025; the City is keeping the traffic lights in place until the permanent redevelopment of the Honoré-Beaugrand / Souligny / Dubuisson intersection, planned for 2028.

Rue Honoré-Beaugrand is to return to two-way traffic between Dubuisson and Hochelaga before the end of March 2026, with adjustments to the traffic light programming, the road markings and the signage.
Signing and publication of the deed are planned for the week of February 4, 2026.

The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the construction of a building at 810, rue Saint-Antoine Est that is taller than what the urban planning rules allow (height in metres, height in storeys, and uses).
The maximum authorized height is 65 m, including rooftop structures.

Following the public consultation of September 24, 2025, the tower was reduced by two storeys (62 m), the volume on rue Saint-Christophe is lowered to 4 storeys, façade setbacks were added for sunlight, and one storey was added on rue Saint-Hubert (10 storeys in total).
Indoor public parking is allowed only on the levels below the ground floor.
With its permit application, the developer will have to submit a wind impact study and a waste management plan.

The project will have to go through an architectural review: appearance of the plans, integration of the rooftop structures, pedestrian walkway between the east and west parts of the site, universal accessibility, and an open interface with the park under the viaduc Notre-Dame.
Work must begin within 60 months of the adoption, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The borough of Verdun is allowing the duplex at 1745-1747, rue Leclair to be converted into a single-family home, meaning the loss of one housing unit.
Normally, the zoning by-law prohibits reducing the number of housing units in a building; here the City is using the by-law on conditional uses to make an exception.
The owners, who bought the building in October 2025, point to a building that is nearly unfit for habitation and in need of renovation, and to their family's need for space.
The work mainly affects the interior (a bedroom and living area in the basement, an open area on the ground floor, three bedrooms upstairs) plus exterior upkeep: roof, brick, balconies, windows.
No relocation is required: the building has been vacant since October 2025 and without a tenant since December 2024.
The urban planning advisory committee voted unanimously in favour on December 16, 2025; the decision is being made at the borough council meeting of February 3, 2026.
The borough of Outremont is adding $12,000 to the funding for the Brigade Neige project, on top of the $10,000 already granted on November 18, 2025.
The money goes to Carrefour Jeunesse Emploi Côte-des-Neiges, Ville Mont-Royal et Outremont, which is coordinating the project from November 19, 2025 to April 30, 2026.
Young people shovel snow for free from the entrances, stairs, access ramps and balconies of seniors or people with reduced mobility in Outremont, at least twice a week.
The borough explains that the many snowfalls at the start of the winter caused the planned budget to be exceeded and that the initial amount was not enough to last until April 30, 2026.
The expense is funded entirely from the borough's operating budget.
An addendum agreement sets the payment conditions; the borough secretary is authorized to sign it.
The organization must submit its final report in May 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the demolition, conversion and construction of a building at 1225-1249, rue Metcalfe, according to the Sidlee Architecture plans stamped September 19, 2025.
The project is granted exemptions from the planning by-law: minimum height, extra height, maximum density, side setback, one use above the 2nd floor, and a rooftop café-terrace.
The façade of 1243, rue Metcalfe (the former taverne Dominion) must be kept and restored, with its openings, fire pots, canopy and windows incorporated into the new building.
Before the demolition, the developer must submit two letters of guarantee: 15% and 10% of the assessment-roll value of the building to be demolished and of its land.
If the work does not comply with the permit, the council may use the guarantee to carry out the work itself or keep it as a penalty.
A café-terrace is allowed on the roof at level 3, where a landscaped area is required and tree planting must be encouraged.
The work must begin within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The City is awarding St-Denis Thompson inc. a $9,111,585.36 contract (taxes included) to build a sports park under Highway 15, between rue Saint-Patrick, rue Hadley, rue Roberval and rue Cabot, in Le Sud-Ouest.
With contingencies ($1,366,737.80) and incidental costs ($1,693,171.12), the total expense comes to $12,171,494.28, taxes included.
The park will include a wheeled sports park, basketball and ball hockey courts, ping-pong tables, fitness equipment, lighting and plantings.
The work also includes sewers, drinking water, roadwork, the management of high-risk asbestos-containing soils and excavation under archaeological supervision.
The work must be completed within a maximum of 400 days, with winter shutdowns from December 18 to April 19 in 2026 and 2027.
The ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable is funding 73% of the expense; the project offsets the nuisances caused by the work on the échangeur Turcot.
The City is adding $3,504,606.80 net to the operating budget of the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité through the Passif environnemental.
The executive committee approves a collaboration agreement between the City and Québec's ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (MTMD).
The agreement sets out the rules for operating two pumping stations, SP-01 and SP-02, built by the Ministry in the échangeur Turcot area during the Turcot project.
The MTMD remains responsible for maintaining and operating its stations, while the City manages the Contrôle intégré des Intercepteurs (CIDI) system and sends instructions in real time.
A coordinating committee bringing together both organizations is planned to coordinate operations.
Goal: to avoid an increase in overflows downstream of the collecteur Saint-Pierre and to protect the road network against flooding, in line with the MELCCFP's environmental requirements.
No new construction work: the stations are already built. This file has no impact on the City's budget.

City council is authorizing the borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve to carry out work on the former marché Maisonneuve, at 4375, rue Ontario Est, a building located in the classified heritage site of the Ancienne-Cité-de-Maisonneuve.
The authorization covers two elements: bringing the side exits up to code and replacing the copper roof.
In concrete terms, two walls and two exterior doors will be moved about 525 mm to bring two of the building's exits into compliance; the architectural style will be reproduced at the new location.

Other work is planned but is not part of this authorization: removal of asbestos, lead and mould, securing the ceilings, upgrading the elevator, redeveloping the basement, repairing the water service entrance, correcting water infiltration, and a new exit stairway.
The Division du patrimoine finds that the project will have no negative impact on the site and preserves the building's Beaux-Arts-influenced architecture.
The Conseil du patrimoine de Montréal issued a favourable opinion, considering that the new doors fit in with the building without competing with the main entrance.
The borough council had already authorized this work on September 29, 2025. The former market now houses community organizations from the neighbourhood.

The City is awarding Les Services EXP inc. a contract to oversee (audit) the design and construction of the new service yard in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, for a total expense of $1,386,606.55, taxes included.
The base contract is $1,260,551.41, plus $126,055.14 (10%) in contingencies for unforeseen costs.
The firm must check that the project documents comply with requirements, carry out site visits and act as site controller, without taking part in the design.
The contract runs from March 24, 2026 to April 30, 2029, with an option to extend it by 12 months.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, spread over four years: 60% in 2026, 25% in 2027, 10% in 2028 and 5% in 2029.
Of the 11 firms that obtained the tender documents, 3 submitted bids; one bid was found to be non-compliant. The winning bid is 14.88% below the City's latest estimate.
The construction work for this service yard had been awarded to Pomerleau inc. in June 2025 ($42,752,148.22).
The agglomeration wants to increase its borrowing for the disinfection plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant: from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000, an increase of $184,000,000.
The money is to be used to finish building the ozonation unit (lots 4, 5 and 6), to install liquid oxygen tanks, and to build the oxygen production plant needed to operate it.
The ozonation process aims to disinfect the treated wastewater discharged into the fleuve Saint-Laurent, in order to reduce bacterial contamination downstream from the outfall.
The ozone plant is expected to start operating in 2029; the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 are to be completed in the last quarter of 2028.
The total project budget was raised to $1,147M in July 2025.

The project is receiving help from the federal gas tax (TECQ) and the Fonds Chantiers Canada-Québec; the related municipalities will pay shares based on their fiscal potential, with the option of paying their share in cash.
The loan and any refinancing cannot exceed 20 years and must be approved by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is approving a specific project for the buildings at 8770 and 8780-8786, rue Sainte-Claire.
The decision allows up to eight dwelling units on the lot, while the by-law allows a maximum of three in this zone.
It also allows two buildings to be kept on the same lot, which the subdivision by-law normally prohibits.
Both buildings already exist and are occupied: three dwelling units at 8770 and four at 8780-8786. Their layout and occupancy are not changing.
The planned cadastral operation is meant to allow for a divided co-ownership, make it easier to obtain financing under CMHC rules, and allow parking and green spaces to be shared.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on December 9; the number of dwelling units was raised from seven to eight after the public consultation on February 11, 2026.
Residents can ask for the project to be approved by referendum; a register or a vote could follow.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the creation of two housing units in part of the ground floor at 590, rue Viau.
The units will occupy the part of the ground floor facing rue Viau, a space that is currently unused; the business fronting on rue Sainte-Catherine Est is being kept.
The building, built in 2023, already has 20 housing units on the two upper floors; it will now have 22.
The owner will have to modify the façade on rue Viau to make it look more "residential" and to create a green space with planter boxes on the private land in front of the units.
The planning rule that prohibits housing units on the ground floor in this area is being set aside for this project.
The Société de développement commercial Hochelaga-Maisonneuve said it was in favour, and the comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on December 9, 2025.
The project may be subject to a public consultation and to a request by residents for approval by referendum.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is granting a minor exemption to the owner of 2642, rue Sicard.
The exemption allows a sunken courtyard of 1.35 m², whereas the planning by-law requires at least 5 m².
The applicant wants to create a "stepped" planting area to add greenery to the property, absorb water and limit water seeping into the building.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain finds that the exemption does not affect the neighbours or the surrounding buildings and that it increases the amount of planted surface.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion at its meeting of December 9, 2025.
Next steps: a public notice announcing the application, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The City is giving $100,000 to the Institut national de la recherche scientifique (INRS) over three years for a research project on stormwater management and adaptation to climate change.
It is adding in-kind support valued at $57,765: 500 hours of work by the Service de l'eau over three years (data collection, technical advice) and hosting one intern.

The research measures the effects of structures such as bioretention, permeable paving, under-roadway retention and stormwater basins, using data from seven municipalities: Québec, Montréal, Laval, Boucherville, Rivière-du-Loup, Victoriaville and Saint-Charles-Borromée.
The City will be able to use the results, the data and the intellectual property rights from the work in its stormwater, planning and development work and policies.
Payment is made in three instalments: $60,000 within 60 days after signing, then $20,000 after an activity report as of October 31, 2026 and $20,000 after a report as of October 31, 2027.
The money comes from the surplus set aside for the climate emergency ($80,000) and from the operating budget of the Service de l'eau ($20,000); the expense is paid by the central city.
The agreement ends on December 31, 2028. The project is also co-funded by the NSERC Alliance program.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the demolition of two 2-storey commercial buildings at 6654-6690 and 6700-6710, rue Sherbrooke Est, near the Langelier metro station.
In their place, a mixed-use building of 10 to 14 storeys will be built: 479 housing units, about 510 m² of commercial space and 280 m² of common space on the ground floor.

The project includes 195 non-market housing units delivered turnkey to a non-profit organization to house students; at least 20% of the private units will be affordable for 20 years under the CMHC program.
The resolution sets aside several planning rules: permitted height raised from 6 to 14 storeys (55 m), density, siting, alignment and the percentage of masonry on the façade.
The developer must provide three letters of guarantee of $500,000 each before the demolition, released as the work progresses.
The site must include a green roof of at least 225 m²; the project announces 2,174 m² of landscaping at ground level, the planting of at least 72 trees, 124 parking spaces and 485 bicycle spaces.

The construction permit must be applied for within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; breaching the conditions carries a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
The Ville de Montréal is signing an agreement with the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) so it can build a pavilion in the future parc Irma-LeVasseur, in Outremont.
The pavilion, about 55 m², will be built against the metro ventilation station (avenue Wiseman) and will contain public washrooms, a storage space and a technical room.
The City is paying for the design and the work, and must keep the metro ventilation station running without interruption.
The City will reimburse the STM for its costs for the preparatory work (removing and reinstalling outdoor equipment, replacing bypass pipes).
The STM will become the owner of the masonry cladding installed on its ventilation station and will take care of its upkeep.
The work is planned from April 2026 to the fall of 2026; a delay in the agreement could jeopardize the full opening of the park in 2026.
The 18,500 m² park, south of avenue Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux between Dollard and Wiseman, will serve as a “school park” and a “sponge park” for rainwater.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is formally approving the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb, between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse.
These bike lanes, built in 2025, had not been approved by the borough.
New mandatory movements (straight ahead, right turn or left turn depending on the lane) are imposed on drivers at every intersection along Christophe-Colomb, between des Carrières and Jean-Talon Est.

The intersections affected include Rosemont, de Bellechasse, Beaubien, Saint-Zotique, Bélanger and Jean-Talon Est; several former requirements that applied only to buses or were in effect from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. are being removed.
The signs are scheduled to be installed in early 2026, and their cost is paid by the City's Service des infrastructures du réseau routier.
The bike lanes on Christophe-Colomb link 4 boroughs over about 7 km, from boulevard Gouin to rue Saint-Grégoire.
All other regulations in effect remain in force.

The City is awarding two contracts without a call for tenders to Innovative Interfaces inc. for maintenance of the Sierra library management system ($1,318,185.02) and of the RFID components and licences linked to Sierra ($244,918.63), for a total of $1,563,103.65 including taxes.
The contracts cover three years, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029; the current contracts end on March 31, 2026.
The system affects the network's 46 libraries, in all 19 boroughs: online catalogue, holds, borrowing and returns, self-service loans, smart book drops and sorting robots.
The City is awarding the contracts directly because Innovative Interfaces owns Sierra's source code and, according to the document, is the only company able to provide support for it.
The negotiated price is $54,500 (3.37%) lower than the City's estimate; the increase is 1.64% for 2026-2027, then 3.5% for each of the following two years.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information and is borne entirely by the central city.
The City is extending until September 30, 2026 the validity of its promise to purchase a 223 m² piece of land at the intersection of avenue Saint-Pierre and rue Notre-Dame, in Lachine.
The land is to be used for the redevelopment of road infrastructure; the purchase price remains $200,000, plus taxes.
The extension is needed because the cadastral operation cannot be completed before January 31, 2026.
The City is adding an expense of $5,748.75, taxes included, to prepare the subdivision plan and carry out the cadastral operation, funded by a loan by-law.
The agreement will be signed with 9519-5228 Québec inc. or any person or entity acting on its behalf, as the company was dissolved on December 30, 2025.
The decision falls to city council; the original promise was signed on July 31, 2025.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is banning the conversion of ground-floor commercial spaces into housing in about thirty zones on its territory.
Housing units that already exist on the ground floor remain allowed: only new conversions are blocked.

The measure targets streets such as Jarry, Tillemont, Villeray, L.-O.-David, Everett and Bélanger in Villeray-Est, de Liège Ouest and Saint-Roch in Parc-Extension, and Legendre and Émile-Journault in Saint-Michel.
The Direction du développement du territoire says it wants to slow the loss of local businesses, since rising residential rents have already led to several conversions.
The ban is presented as temporary, pending a commercial consolidation study of the Villeray-Est area planned for 2026, funded with $53,000 from the Service du développement économique.
A written consultation was held from February 5 to 12, 2026, and a public meeting on February 12, 2026: no one took part in the written consultation and no comments were received.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is amending its by-law on the demolition of buildings to bring it in line with the City's Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité (24-017).

The by-law lists cases in which a demolition no longer needs authorization from the demolition committee: buildings without a foundation, temporary buildings, outbuildings, non-compliant buildings at the rear of a lot or in a backyard (except for residential use), and projects already authorized by the council.
A demolition tied to a social or affordable housing project, or to servicing land for that purpose, is added to the cases exempt from the committee's authorization.

These exemptions do not apply to heritage buildings, to buildings of heritage and architectural interest, or, following an amendment requested by the Service d'urbanisme et de mobilité, to buildings located in an area of archaeological interest.

The by-law sets out the documents required for a demolition application: photos, a certificate of location, the reasons for the demolition, and, when the committee must rule on it, an expert assessment of the building's condition, a heritage study, a report on vegetation, the end dates of the leases, and the conditions for rehousing tenants.
The council also receives the minutes of the public consultation meeting of March 18, 2026 and the report on the written consultation held from March 11 to 18, 2026.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing école secondaire Dorval-Jean-XXIII to hold a race on the pedestrian and bike path along boulevard LaSalle on Friday, April 24, 2026.
This is the 13th edition of the Grand Défi Guy Labelle: 250 young people will run 5, 10, 15 or 21 km depending on their abilities.
Starts will take place between Verdun and Lachine, depending on the route chosen, and the finish line is at the school, in Dorval.
No street will be closed, since the runners will use the pedestrian and bike path.
Volunteers, public safety officers, the Lachine, LaSalle and Verdun police, and Ambulance Saint-Jean will be present along the route.
No money is being given to the school: the decision has no financial impact.
About 30 young people from the school's running club will be chosen for the Grand Défi Pierre Lavoie 2026.
The borough of LaSalle is revising its sports excellence support program, which takes effect in 2026.
Grants are going up by 25%: up to $1,250 (regional), $2,500 (provincial) and $5,000 (national) per team.
For individual sports, the support ranges from $250 to $1,000 per athlete, for up to 5 athletes.
A new component provides up to $9,000 per organization for pre-professional teams, in addition to the first component.
The criteria become the same for all sports: you only need to show that the athlete or team competes at the regional, provincial or national level.
Organizations will have to report on how the funds are used; the provincial transportation component is being removed (it is already covered elsewhere).
In 2026 only, applications are due on June 1 rather than February 1; one application per organization, per component, per year.

The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the organization Les Kilomaîtres LaSalle to hold the 45th Course et Marche populaires de LaSalle on Sunday, March 29, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to about 12:30 p.m., starting from the Pearson Adult Career Center school.
The borough is giving $4,000 to the organization: $2,800 after the February 2026 decision and $1,200 upon receipt of the final report, no later than 90 days after the event.
Streets along the route will be closed from 7:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., with partial reopening possible as early as 11 a.m. on the SPVM's signal.

Parking will be banned on Raymond, George, Centrale, LaSalle and 35e Avenue (sections of the route); it remains allowed on other closed streets, including 30e, 34e, 36e, 39e and 40e Avenues and Vachon.
The borough is also providing services valued at $30,000 free of charge: staff, loan of equipment and of the school, rental of signage, and snow removal if needed.
Homes and businesses along the route or enclosed by it will receive a notice, and posters announcing the closures will be put up 10 days in advance.
The borough of LaSalle is lending space free of charge to the Association du soccer mineur de LaSalle, from March 3, 2026 to December 31, 2028.

The space being lent is located in the chalet at parc Raymond (administrative offices, reception area, change rooms, storage) and in the chalet at the sports complex of parc Riverside (four change rooms and two storage areas).
The club also has a container near the Keith-Ewenson field and shares the garage with the football club, Les Kilomaîtres and the borough.
No money is being paid out: the estimated annual rental value is $39,941.14 at parc Raymond, $4,361.03 at parc Riverside and $1,310.76 for the container.
In winter, the public works department clears snow from the accesses to the chalet Raymond and from one parking area.
According to the document, without this free loan of space, the club could not pay rent or rent storage facilities, which could drive up participation costs.

The City will pay the Société du Musée d'archéologie et d'histoire de Montréal Pointe-à-Callière $10,019,500 in 2026 and $10,280,007 in 2027 to operate the museum, in Vieux-Montréal (350, Place Royale, 150, rue Saint-Paul Ouest and four addresses on Place d'Youville).
For 2028, the contribution will equal the 2027 amount, indexed to the consumer price index for the Montréal region, with a cap of 3% and no decrease if the index goes down.
On top of that, $116,000 per year from 2026 to 2028, for a total of $348,000, for energy, security, maintenance and insurance for Caserne no 1, at 335, Place d'Youville.
The total contribution comes to $10,135,500 in 2026 and $10,396,007 in 2027, paid 100% by the central city.
A new three-year agreement covers January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028; the Société commits to maintaining the museum's activities and to showcasing the archaeological remains.
The $116,000 for 2026 comes from the budget set aside for the administration's priorities; it responds to a request filed by the Société on September 29, 2025 and accepted on January 8, 2026.
The previous agreement, of $9,358,900 to $9,832,700 per year, ended on December 31, 2025.
The urban agglomeration council is adopting a $29,000,000 loan by-law to redevelop nature parks under its authority.
The money will fund the projects of the first five years (2026-2030) of the nature park rehabilitation program, for which the required funds are estimated at $28,886,000.

Work is planned at parc-nature de l'Île-de-la-Visitation (site des Moulins, the threshold of the maison du Meunier, shorelines), at Bois-de-Saraguay (heritage low walls) and at Bois-de-Liesse (entrée des Champs).

Other work sites at parc-nature du Ruisseau-de-Montigny (île Lapierre, signage) and at Grand parc de l'Est, secteur Pointe-aux-Prairies (footbridges, shed, secteur Héritage, water management structures).
Street furniture, signage, site rehabilitation and asset maintenance are also planned in various nature parks.
This by-law replaces RCG 16-049, of which only $5,700,000 remains; the loan will be repaid over a maximum of 20 years, with no subsidy.
The request must be approved by the ministre des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation; it is hoped that it will come into force in the summer of 2026.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is accepting a cash payment, instead of a transfer of land, as the park fee contribution for a subdivision project at 695, rue Cherrier.
The owner wants to split the land in two: a 5,000 m² residential lot with the single-family home built in 1878, and a 202,086.9 m² agricultural lot.
The amount to be paid is equal to 10% of the market value of the residential lot only; the agricultural part is not included.
The exact amount is not yet known: it will be set by a certified appraiser hired by the Ville.
For reference, the whole property is worth $846,400 on the Ville's assessment roll.
The land is in an agricultural zone, next to the urban perimeter of L'Île-Bizard; the decision is scheduled for the February 3, 2026 borough council meeting.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève is renewing the terms of three citizen members of its planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme, CCU): Steve Bergeron, Franck David and François Allard, from February 3, 2026 to February 2, 2027.
Jean-Pierre Tanguay is appointed as a substitute citizen member for the same period; this position had been vacant since June 2022.
The CCU reviews matters of urban planning, zoning, subdivision and construction and issues opinions; the borough council may accept, amend or reject its recommendations.
The committee has 7 members: 5 residents and 2 city councillors, plus a maximum of 2 substitutes.
Each member receives $100 for each meeting attended.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving $55,000 (taxes included) to the non-profit organization "Biquette – Écopâturage" for its 2026 season, taken from the operating budget.
The money will mainly be used to pay human resources (shepherds) for sixteen weeks of activities.

The "Le Repaire de Biquette" project will be set up in the north part of parc Maisonneuve, near the jardins communautaires Rosemont and de l'Églantier: a sheepfold, henhouse, beehive, edible and medicinal plantings, composters, signs and furniture.
Up to twenty sheep and four hens will be on site; the sheep arrive between June 25 and 27, 2026 and leave between October 13 and 15, 2026.
Free workshops on urban agriculture, permaculture and animal well-being will be offered every week.
The borough is granting the permit to occupy public property free of charge from March 10 to December 31, 2026 and is giving free access to the grazing areas.
The organization is proposing to continue until 2028, but only the year 2026 is funded; the borough can withdraw its authorization if the agreement is not respected.
The City is renting to the Pointe-à-Callière museum a 551 m² space at 335, place d'Youville, in the former fire station number 1, to hold museum activities there.
The lease runs for 3 years, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028, and replaces the former lease that expired on December 31, 2025.
The total rent charged is $5,535 before taxes ($6,363.87 taxes included) for the three years.
The City estimates the real estate subsidy granted at $162,423.78, which is the gap between the estimated rental value ($96.77 to $106.45 per m²) and the rent charged.
The City expects about $25,000 in operating costs for this space in 2026 (contracted maintenance and vertical transportation).
The Service de la stratégie immobilière considers that the building is not needed for municipal purposes; the lease was negotiated by mutual agreement.
The space houses an exhibition on the archaeological site of the Marché Sainte-Anne, the Parliament of the Province of Canada and fire station number 1.
The City is renting 50 indoor parking spaces from the Société de la Place des arts, on the first basement level of 260, boulevard De Maisonneuve, in Ville-Marie.
The lease runs for 25 years, retroactive to October 1, 2025, until September 30, 2050.
The total rent comes to $3,547,501.89 including taxes ($3,085,455 before taxes).
The annual rent will be increased each year starting October 1, 2027, based on Statistics Canada's consumer price index (Montréal).
These spaces are used for the vehicles of units at the SPVM headquarters, at 1441, rue Saint-Urbain.
The previous lease had expired on September 30, 2025 and included no extension option; the new lease was negotiated directly with the owner.
The cost is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration, since police services fall under agglomeration jurisdiction.
The City is approving the construction of a greenhouse complex in the southwest section of parc Frédéric-Back, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, near the composting platform.
The complex will include 1,500 m² of research and training greenhouses (Collège Ahuntsic, ÉTS, AULAB, UQAM) and 1,000 m² of community greenhouse for the Saint-Michel neighbourhood.
The production target is about 62 tonnes of fruits and vegetables per year, intended mainly for food security in the neighbourhood; part of it may be sold at social pricing.

The construction budget is estimated at $2,185,000: 35% comes from the agglomeration budget (participatory budget) and 65% from external sources, including $500,000 from the federal Local Food Infrastructure Fund.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is leading the project; the urban agglomeration council is delegating the carrying out of the work and the management of the project to the city council.
The organization AULAB will operate the greenhouse; Vivre Saint-Michel en santé and Collège Ahuntsic will use some of the greenhouse bays.
Connecting the greenhouse to the waste heat from the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel is being postponed to a later phase, subject to funding and studies.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is appointing councillor Nicolas Jolicoeur (Saint-Paul–Émard–Saint-Henri-Ouest district) as its representative on the board of directors of PME MTL Grand Sud-Ouest.
He replaces Anne-Marie Sigouin, former councillor for the same district.
The urban agglomeration council must confirm the appointment; the borough council adopted it unanimously on December 8, 2025.
PME MTL Grand Sud-Ouest supports and finances private and social economy businesses in Verdun, LaSalle and Le Sud-Ouest (management advice, business plans, mentoring).
Its board of directors has 13 members: 3 borough representatives and 10 people from the business community.
The document states that the appointment has no financial aspect.
The borough of LaSalle is creating an advisory committee on economic and urban development, by adopting By-law 2404-LAS.
The committee will make recommendations to the borough council on economic and urban development issues in the area.

Its mandate covers the monitoring of local planning and major projects, real estate development practices, regulatory changes in urban planning and heritage, as well as economic development and its programs.
The by-law sets out the committee's composition, the number of members and their role.
No financial impact is expected.
The notice of motion and the tabling of the draft by-law took place on February 2, 2026; a public notice will be published on the borough's website once it comes into force.
The borough of LaSalle is creating an advisory committee on social development and diversity, by adopting by-law 2402-LAS.
The committee will look at issues of social development, universal accessibility and living together, and will make recommendations to the borough council.
It will follow the progress of action plans and major projects, and propose measures for social inclusion, equity and citizen participation, using a gender-based analysis plus (GBA+).
The by-law sets out the committee's composition, the number of members and their role.
The borough states that there is no financial impact.
A notice of motion was given and the draft by-law was tabled on February 2, 2026; a public notice will be published on the borough's website after it comes into force.
The borough of LaSalle is creating an advisory committee on finances and relations with the public.
The committee will look at budget issues and relations with citizens, then make recommendations to the borough council.
Its mandate: transparent financial management, a citizen experience that meets the needs of the public, and increased citizen participation.
The by-law sets out the committee's make-up, the number of members and their role.
The borough states that there is no financial impact.
A public notice will be published on the borough's website after the by-law comes into force.
The notice of motion and the tabling of the draft by-law took place at the February 2, 2026 meeting.
The borough of LaSalle is creating an advisory committee on sports, culture and recreation, by adopting by-law 2403-LAS.
The committee must make recommendations to the borough council on directions, programs, events and initiatives in sports, culture, recreation and amateur artistic practice.
It must also look at the development of infrastructure, facilities and spaces dedicated to sports, culture and recreation in the borough.
The by-law sets out the committee's composition, the number of members and their role.
The file indicates no financial impact.
A notice of motion and the tabling of the draft by-law took place at the February 2, 2026 meeting; a public notice will be published on the borough's website after it comes into force.

The City is approving its first "Plan de gestion des actifs municipaux en eau" (municipal water asset management plan) and sending it to the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation, as it had committed to do by no later than December 31, 2026.
Filing this plan is a condition for receiving additional funding from the provincial PRIMEAU program, which could reach $86M, out of total funding of $430M for Montréal's water assets.
The plan covers 10 years and puts the replacement value of the water assets (drinking water, wastewater, stormwater) at $44B, or about 46% of all of the City's assets.
The financial needs calculated using the ministère's method reach $15.2B over ten years, while the planned budgets are $9.9B, or about 65% of the needs.

The overall maintenance deficit is estimated at 8%, but climbs from 10% to 50% for wastewater treatment, sewer mains, pumping stations and retention basins; about 20% of the assets are considered highly critical.
The City will aim to bring the asset maintenance deficit down to 5% within ten years by concentrating investments on critical assets and postponing certain non-urgent improvements.
Starting in 2028, the plan will have to be updated every two years, with a full review in 2030 and then every four years.
The City is hiring Construction Arcade to repair the escalier Duluth, in parc du Mont-Royal, for $267,699.99 including taxes.
With contingencies ($53,540) and incidentals ($57,500), the total cost comes to $378,739.99.
The work involves the steel structure, the guardrails, the painting, the replacement of the wooden decking, a granite threshold and the patching of the path.
The stairway links the east side of the park to chemin Olmsted; the wooden decking has reached the end of its useful life.
The work is to start at the end of August 2026, in order to comply with wildlife protection laws, and to finish at the end of November 2026.
Three companies submitted bids; the winning bid is 41% below the City's estimate.
The agglomeration is paying the bill; the ministère de la Culture et des Communications is providing a $122,223 grant.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is paying $235,000 (taxes included if applicable) to the organization Prévention Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce to extend the Intervention de proximité jeunesse program by one year, in 2026.
The program targets young people aged 12 to 25 in areas considered vulnerable: outreach workers go out to meet them in the field, mainly in and around public high schools.

These workers act as the link between young people and available resources: neighbourhood organizations, the borough's summer programming, neighbourhood police stations 9 and 26, and health services (Aire ouverte).
The money comes from the operating budget of the borough's Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The borough presents 2026 as a transition year before these activities are folded into a new local social development program now being designed.
The organization must submit a final report no later than one month after the end of the project and follow a visibility protocol.
The program had already received $790,916.13 for 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is giving $51,120 to the Corporation de développement communautaire de Côte-des-Neiges (CDC CDN) for the year 2026.

The money goes to the project "Renforcer le filet de solidarité pour les ménages vulnérables du quartier (phase 4)," carried out with the organizations of the table famille in the Côte-des-Neiges neighbourhood.
Two goals: better equipping the organizations that help vulnerable households, especially those who arrived recently through immigration, and making the community sector more responsive in a crisis.

Examples of planned activities: training and a community of practice for front-line workers, emergency help with school supplies, collecting and handing out winter clothing, and taking stock of the neighbourhood's resources.
The amount is the same as the one given in 2025 and is included in the borough's 2026 operating budget.
2026 is presented as a transition year: the borough has to review its guidelines and design a new local social development program.
The organization will have to follow the City's visibility protocol.

The City is asking Québec's ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for financial assistance of up to $2,000,000 for work at parc Frédéric-Back, in the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel.
The project in question calls for a 900-metre multi-purpose path crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge of about 150 metres.
This east-west link, along the line of rue Émile-Journault, will connect two neighbourhoods that have until now been separated by the former quarry.
The work also includes rainwater management structures and a 12.7-hectare meadow ("Secteur de la plaine centre"), almost entirely greened.
The application is being submitted under the TAPU program, whose call for projects closes on November 26, 2026.
Parc Frédéric-Back covers 153 of the complex's 192 hectares; a little more than 55 hectares have already been developed and opened to the public.
In September 2024, the City had awarded WSP Canada inc. a professional services contract worth $1,934,458.16 for this same project.
The City is extending by 12 months the contract for mowing overgrown land (grasses and shrubs) awarded to 9398-7561 Québec inc. (Cèdres Lachenaie), from February 16, 2026 to February 15, 2027.
It is adding $57,223.06, taxes included ($47,685.88 for the contract, $4,768.59 in contingencies and $4,768.59 for variation in quantities), which brings the contract to $168,126.26.

The work covers the Grand parc de l'Ouest (Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-l'Île-Bizard, Cap-Saint-Jacques) and the nature parks of Bois-de-Liesse, Bois-de-Saraguay, l'Île-de-la-Visitation, Ruisseau-De Montigny and Pointe-aux-Prairies.
About 70 hectares will be mowed in 2026, an area similar to previous years.
According to the file, mowing serves to maintain open habitats and to curb the regrowth of shrubs and invasive exotic species.
The expense, included in the operating budget of the Service des grands parcs, is paid 100% by the agglomeration.
The City is awarding two contracts to Artémis Faune inc. for technical wildlife management services, for a total expenditure of $199,138.01, taxes included.

The first lot ($109,023.89) covers the monitoring and capture of coyotes and turkeys, the management of injured, sick or dead animals, nesting monitoring and the tagging of Canada geese, in parks and elsewhere on the territory.
The second lot ($56,924.12) deals with beaver management in the nature parks: site monitoring, population control, sterilization and damage mitigation.
The contracts run from January 2026 to December 31, 2027, with an option to extend for 12 months valued at $82,974.01.
An additional $8,297 is set aside for contingencies and $24,893 for variations in quantities.
Only one company bid on the two calls for tenders: its price is 4.6% above the estimate for lot 1 and 14.3% below it for lot 2.
The cost of the beaver lot is paid by the agglomeration; the cost of lot 1 is shared 50-50 between the agglomeration and the central city in 2026.
The City is awarding two contracts to plant 1,374 trees on public property: 519 trees in the fall of 2026 (lot 1) and 855 trees in the spring of 2027 (lot 2).
7574479 Canada inc. gets lot 1 for $735,096.11 and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. gets lot 2 for $1,230,176.33, taxes included.
With contingencies ($196,527.24) and quantity variations ($294,790.87), the maximum spending reaches $2,456,590.55, paid entirely by the central city.

The trees will go to seven boroughs: Saint-Laurent (423), Verdun (281), Pierrefonds-Roxboro (265), Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (148), Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve (123), Montréal-Nord (106) and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension (28).

The contracts also cover watering, maintenance and the replacement of some trees, from planting until the end of November 2029 (excluding winter), with daily penalties if the specifications are not followed.
The public call for tenders received 8 bids; the selected prices are 33.3% lower (lot 1) and 40.3% lower (lot 2) than the City's estimate.
The performance of both companies will be evaluated.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is allowing Impact de Montréal F.C. to occupy parc Champêtre for 15 years, with automatic 5-year renewals unless notice of non-renewal is given.
The site must remain sports-oriented, open to the public and devoted first and foremost to soccer.
The agreement covers the synthetic fields, the natural fields and the park chalet.
The Impact takes on the upkeep and repair of the fields and the chalet; it had also carried out the development work.
