More than 100 hours are set aside for the borough's programming and for access to the chalet.
No funding is being requested from the borough.
First reading is planned for April 2026, with adoption in May 2026.
The City is awarding a contract worth $780,310.03 (taxes included) to Plomberie Charbonneau inc. to replace the boilers at the Centre sportif Côte-des-Neiges, at 4880, avenue Van Horne.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,014,403.04, including $117,046.50 in contingencies and $117,046.50 in incidental expenses.
The two current boilers have reached the end of their useful life; they will be replaced by a dual-energy boiler room (one electric boiler and natural gas boilers).
The document states that the Centre sportif is among the ten largest greenhouse gas emitters among the City's buildings.
The work is scheduled to be done by the end of fall 2026, because of the delivery times for the new boilers.
Six companies submitted bids out of 11 holders of the tender documents; the lowest bid is 43.9% below the professionals' estimate ($1,390,879.02, taxes included).
The funding comes from the PEV-DIM program ($356,619.80 net of tax rebate) and from a Ten-Year Capital Works Program carry-over ($569,665.39).

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is adding $326,905.26 (taxes included) to the fees of the firm CIMAISE, which is designing and supervising the redevelopment of the chalet in parc Jean-Brillant and the construction of a wading pool.
The professional services contract therefore goes from $567,617.20 to $894,522.46, taxes included.

The increase is explained by the cost of the work: initially estimated at $3,000,000 before taxes, it was awarded at $4,613,813 before taxes to Groupe DCR in September 2024. The contract provides that the fees follow the actual cost of the work.
The added amount breaks down into $244,274.14 in fees, $45,990.00 in contingencies and $36,641.12 in incidental expenses, taxes included.
The expense is paid 100% by the borough, out of the parks fund.
The work began in October 2024; the end of the work and the end of the warranties are expected in spring 2026.
The borough will evaluate the performance of the firm CIMAISE.
The City is selling the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) a 364.3 m² piece of land for $495,150, plus applicable taxes.
The land is located at the corner of rue Saint-Jacques Ouest, rue Notre-Dame Ouest and place Saint-Henri, in the borough of Le Sud-Ouest.
The sale is for the expansion of the entrance building of the Place-Saint-Henri metro station, with the addition of elevators to make the station universally accessible.
The work is already finished: the City had authorized the STM to build in 2020, before the transaction was concluded; the sale sets its property titles in order.
The lot is closed and withdrawn from the public domain before the sale; it is sold without warranty, at the STM's risk.
The amount of $495,150 will be recorded as revenue in the operating budget of the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation.

The City is awarding a professional services contract worth $8,479,406.25 (taxes included) to the winning team of the architecture competition, made up of L'OEUF Architectes, Lapointe Magne et associés, NIPPAYSAGE, Eurêka Environnement, L2C Experts-Conseils and Dupras Ledoux.
The team will design the new bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson, in the Villeray neighbourhood, and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost (Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough).
Added to this are $1,271,910.94 in contingencies and $847,940.63 in incidental costs, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included.
The cost will be shared: 19% by the borough, 81% by the central city; the project is eligible for funding from the ministère de la Culture et des Communications du Québec.
The new library will replace the bibliothèque Le Prévost, currently housed in the Patro Villeray, and will aim for LEED-NC Gold and PassivHaus certifications.
Parc Le Prévost is to be converted into a resilient park, with stormwater management practices.
The contract stems from a two-stage competition (call for tenders 28-20831) that received 28 anonymous applications; each finalist team received $160,000, plus taxes.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a 3-storey residential building with 32 units at 4605, rue d'Amiens.
The project replaces a garage and a service station, whose demolition was approved by the demolition committee on December 2, 2025.
The building will have 5 studios, 17 one-bedroom units, 6 two-bedroom units and 4 three-bedroom units.
An underground parking garage with 16 spaces (including one for people with reduced mobility) and 9 bicycle spaces are planned, with an access ramp from avenue Armand-Lavergne.
The lot, which currently has no vegetation, is to be landscaped with 13 new trees planted in the ground, shrubs and perennials, and planters on a rooftop terrace (24% greening).
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work is required when the permit is issued.
This is a second application for the same building, as the first authorization from November 2023 expired in April 2025.
The borough of Montréal-Nord has to decide whether to allow only two parking spaces instead of four for the building at 12375, boulevard Rolland.
The owner wants to remove one of the two garages in order to create a dwelling in the basement (the building already has seven dwellings).
The front yard would be filled in, with a tree and grass planted; removing the driveway entrance would free up one on-street parking space.
According to the borough's analysis, the lot does not allow parking spaces to be relocated or added.
The authorization would require the building to be rebuilt according to the regulations in force if it loses at least half of its value (fire, demolition, etc.).
The urban planning advisory committee recommended accepting the request on December 2, 2025; the decision is expected at the borough council meeting of February 9, 2026.
A public notice was published on December 17, 2025: any interested person may be heard at that meeting.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a two-storey building with a dwelling in the basement at 11915, avenue Balzac.
The project includes three dwellings with two bedrooms each: about 66 m² in the basement, 71 m² on the ground floor and 75 m² on the second floor.
The lot is vacant: the building that stood there was the subject of a demolition order in December 2024 because it was putting the public in danger.
The building will be mainly red brick, with charcoal grey aluminum panels on the front, a flat roof and one parking space in the left side yard.
Four trees will be planted on the lot and one tree will be cut down because it is within the construction area.
Work must start within 18 months, otherwise the authorization lapses; the developer must post a guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released when the work is finished.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave the project a favourable recommendation on December 2, 2025.

The City is hiring Sanexen Services Environnementaux and Loiselle to receive its contaminated soil (recovery, treatment or disposal) for 24 months, from April 20, 2026 to April 19, 2028, with two possible 12-month extensions.
Estimated amount of the agreements: $2,300,286.14, taxes included.
Breakdown: Sanexen gets lot 1 (zone 1 - AB) at $594,305.78 and lot 3 at $191,088.45; Loiselle gets lot 4 (zone 2 - BC, odourless) at $1,214,854.59.
Added to this are quantity variation budgets of $271,374.06 (urban agglomeration council) and $28,663.27 (executive committee), taxes included.
The service is for all boroughs and the central services, which will pay out of their own budgets as their needs arise.
The prices do not include hauling the excavated material or the fees paid to the ministère de l'Environnement; they are fixed for 24 months, then indexed to the CPI if renewed.
Public call for tenders 25-21166 drew 11 people who took out the documents and 4 bidders; Loiselle's bid for lot 3 was found to be technically non-compliant.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is applying for financial assistance from the City's Bureau de la transition écologique et de la résilience to expand the jardin communautaire Villeray.
The project calls for setting up new growing spaces in this garden, in order to offer more room to garden and access to fresh fruits and vegetables.
The application is being made through the component of the municipal program devoted to creating new gardening spaces, which is tied to the Stratégie d'agriculture urbaine 2021-2026.
The borough commits to paying its share of the project costs; no amount is stated in the file.
The director of culture, sports, recreation and social development is authorized to sign the application and to follow up on it.
The deadline for submitting projects to the Bureau was December 12, 2025; the resolution will be sent afterwards, with no effect on the review of the project.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is entrusting the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie with the maintenance of street lighting, traffic signs and road markings on its territory for 2026.
Cost of the agreement: $2,857,500, funded by the borough.
This service has been provided by Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie since 2004 for the nine boroughs of the former Ville de Montréal.
The borough cites centralized management, lower management costs and fewer interventions to carry out on its own side.
Without this agreement, the borough would have to hire private suppliers to maintain road markings and traffic signs.
The City is giving $405,000 to the non-profit organization AlterGo Événements to hold the Défi sportif AlterGo in 2026, 2027 and 2028, that is, $135,000 per year.
It is adding support in the form of facilities and equipment valued at $1,550,350: $506,585 in 2026, $516,715 in 2027 and $527,050 in 2028.
This technical support includes the loan of rooms, equipment and staff at the Complexe sportif Claude-Robillard, the aréna Michel-Normandin and the aréna Maurice-Richard.
The event brings together athletes of all ages with a functional limitation, from the school level up to the elite level; it has been organized since 1984.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, as support for sports elite and major sporting events.
The financial support represents about 4.2% of the organization's 2026 budget; with the technical support, about 17%.
The previous agreement ended on December 31, 2025. The events are planned for April-May from 2026 to 2028.
City council is raising parking fines in Montréal, on both the arterial road network and the local road network.
Illegal parking (general) goes from $65 to $67 in 2026.
Double parking or parking that obstructs traffic, as well as parking in a space reserved for people with disabilities, go from $77 to $79.
Parking in a no-stopping zone or in a reserved lane goes from $293 to $299.
Court registry fees set by the Government of Québec are added to the fine when a ticket is issued.
The City estimates about $2.2M in additional fine revenue in 2026.
The by-law comes into force on the date it is published; the systems of the municipal court and the Agence de mobilité durable will have to be adjusted before then.
The City is renewing its summer jobs plan for young people under youth protection, this time with no end date.
It is dropping the target of 25 student positions per year and focusing instead on the quality of the experience offered.
The Service des ressources humaines et des communications continues to lead the selection and hiring process centrally.
No special budget: each business unit pays the young person's salary out of its own operating budget.
Between 2021 and 2025, 74 young people obtained a summer job and 57 completed it; nearly 170 since 2014.
The City is working with the Union des municipalités du Québec and the CIUSSS du Centre-Sud and de l'Ouest-de-l'Île.
The coordination team will launch the 2026 edition as soon as city council adopts it.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is paying $691,426.66 to 12 organizations for 17 projects, from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The money comes from the Prévention Montréal program, which targets children, young people under 30 and their families in vulnerable situations.

The projects cover the districts of Hochelaga, Tétreaultville, Maisonneuve–Longue-Pointe and Louis-Riel: youth centres open on weekends, dance workshops, respite for families, street outreach work, and intervention in public housing (HLM).
The largest amounts go to L'Anonyme U.I.M. ($263,087 for "Se sentir en sécurité dans MHM"), Dopamine ($65,716) and Projet Ado Communautaire en Travail de rue ($54,726).
The borough is drawing $30,333 from its surpluses; the rest of the expense is covered by the central city.
This is an extension into 2026 of projects already funded in 2025, with amounts adjusted to the available budget.
City council is keeping, for five more years starting March 22, 2026, the power to regulate the parking of self-service vehicles (car-sharing) on local streets and to issue their permits.
It is also keeping responsibility for installing, removing, maintaining and replacing electric vehicle charging stations on those same streets.
Without this extension, each borough would once again be responsible for these rules and for funding the charging stations on its local street network, as was the case before 2016.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité will have to present a progress report after 30 months.
The document states that the car-sharing service covers 17 boroughs and had 3,208 vehicles at the end of 2025, and that about 1,900 charging stations are installed across all boroughs.
Since December 2025, the Agence de mobilité durable has been issuing parking permits.
The City states that no net spending results from this decision; adoption requires a two-thirds vote of council.

The City is entering into a 3-year master agreement with Groupe Conseil CHG inc. for building structural engineering services, for up to $517,387.50, taxes included, with an option to extend for 12 months.

The firm will be called on as needed for design, expert assessment, diagnostic or intervention assignments: steel framing, concrete, wood framing (including heritage buildings), seismic assessment and upgrading, and structural reinforcement.

No budget is set aside in advance: each assignment will be authorized as it comes up through a purchase order, and the expenses will be charged to the boroughs, the central services and the related cities.
The master agreement is limited to projects of the Service de la gestion et planification des immeubles, but may involve the City's entire territory.
Public call for tenders 25-21074 received 9 bids out of 12 people who took out the tender documents; the price selected is 32.19% ($245,620.02) below the City's latest estimate.
The document notes that the selected firm received one of the lowest scores for the experience of the assigned staff and of the project manager.
The firm's performance will have to be evaluated, since the contract exceeds $500,000. It is expected to come into force in February 2026.
The City is hiring Nadeau Blondin Lortie Architectes inc. to prepare a conservation plan for 8 heritage buildings of the Cité-des-Hospitalières, at 201, 209 and 251, avenue des Pins.
The contract is worth $308,523.11, plus $61,704.62 in contingencies, for a total expense of $370,227.73, taxes included.

The mandate includes reviewing existing documents, technical inspections, a building health record and the façade inspection (Loi 122) of the Maison Mère and the chapelle Sainte-Famille, including the dome.
The study covers the exterior walls and their interior face, from the foundation to the frame, and runs for about 52 weeks. The gardens and the surrounding wall are excluded.
The Fonds du patrimoine culturel québécois is providing $370,227.73 in funding, covering all of the costs; the expense is paid by the agglomeration.
Of the 22 people who obtained the tender documents, 6 submitted bids and 4 passed the 70% mark. The winning price is 72.65% higher than the City's estimate, which was based on 2021 inspection costs.
The city is extending its agreement with Éco Entreprises Québec (ÉEQ), the organization that represents packaging producers in selective collection, by one year.

Until December 31, 2026, the city will continue to handle the processing of empty aerosol containers brought to the seven ecocentres and of glass dropped off at two voluntary drop-off points in Ahuntsic-Cartierville.
ÉEQ was normally supposed to take back these two services on January 1, 2026, but said in the fall of 2025 that it was not ready; the city is taking over to avoid an interruption in service.
ÉEQ will reimburse the city 100% of the amounts spent, upon presentation of invoices, every three months.
In practical terms, the city must award a glass processing contract for 2026 and extend its aerosol processing contract.
The amendment applies retroactively to January 1, 2026 and ends on December 31, 2026.

The City is extending by three years, starting February 1, 2026, the lease of the organization L'Atelier d'Artisanat Centre-ville inc. on the 2nd floor of 3680, rue Jeanne-Mance (Centre Strathearn), in Ville-Marie.
The organization occupies 9,523.68 square feet for community purposes and will pay total rent of $393,967.08, before taxes.
The rent works out to an average of $13.78 per square foot, while the market rate for this type of space is about $25. The difference represents a real estate subsidy estimated at $320,567.07.
L'Atelier offers the practice of arts and crafts as a therapeutic and social tool for people living with mental health challenges.
The organization is responsible for the fit-up, housekeeping and tenant repairs; the City remains responsible for the structure and the mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems.
Either party may end the lease before it expires with six months' written notice.
The City estimates its operating costs for these premises (energy, routine maintenance) at about $50,190 for 2025.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is allowing an air conditioning unit to be installed on a balcony in a front yard, at 5312, Place de Jumonville.
The planning by-law normally prohibits this type of unit in a front yard; the City is granting a minor exemption here.
Reason given: the applicant's unit has only one balcony, located in the front yard, and the sloped roof does not allow the unit to be installed there.
The administration finds that the exemption does not increase any safety or health risk and does not affect neighbouring properties.
A public notice must be published 15 days before the meeting; the borough council is to make its decision on March 9, 2026, after a question period.
The work has not yet started.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is authorizing nine public events on its territory in 2026, including "Le temps des sucres sur la Plaza Saint-Hubert", the "Course des Vikings" and the "Défi YMCA 2026".

Three ordinances allow, at the planned sites, dates and times: noise from sound equipment outdoors, the sale of promotional items, food and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks, as well as the consumption of alcohol.
One of these ordinances also allows painting on sidewalks and roadways, using water-soluble paint.
The borough is approving a technical support agreement with the Fondation du CHU Sainte-Justine for its "Triathlon d'hiver de Sainte-Justine 2026".
The promoters take on the financial and logistical responsibility for their events; the borough provides logistical support according to its capacity, out of its existing budgets.
Permits to occupy public property will be issued by the borough's culture and public works departments; the ordinances will be published on the borough's website.
Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is amending its planning by-law (the "2026 omnibus by-law") to clarify and simplify several rules applied to permit applications.

Trees and greening: front yards will have to be planted with greenery (with some exceptions), a newly planted tree will have to be at least 3 cm in diameter measured 1.3 m above the ground, and moving a tree will be allowed on the advice of an arboriculture expert.

On Plaza Saint-Hubert, at least 60% of the ground floor will have to be used for businesses or for community and institutional facilities, with the main entrance on Saint-Hubert and access by the lane or by rue Saint-André.

Housing: subdividing a unit larger than 192 m² becomes allowed if the two new units are each at least 96 m²; a unit set up in a basement before September 1, 2025 does not count in the building's number of units.
Coworking spaces are allowed wherever offices already are; performance halls may be allowed as a conditional use in certain C.2 zones.

Yards: heat pumps allowed at least 1.5 m from a property line (not allowed in the front yard); stairs, ramps and guardrails made of mechanically assembled steel on the front facade are now prohibited, with the possibility of an approved exemption.
Timeline: notice of motion on February 2, 2026, public consultation in February, referendum process in March, adoption on April 7, 2026 and coming into force expected at the end of April 2026.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie approves a minor exemption for the building at 2705, rue Masson, at the corner of 3e Avenue, occupied by the Centre d'activités Masson and owned by the City.

The exemption allows the installation on the roof of a heat pump and an acoustic screen that rise more than 2.28 m above the roof, while the by-law limit is 2 m, and that do not respect the required setback (twice their height).
The new heat pump replaces obsolete equipment and reuses a metal structure already in place on the roof; the work has not started.
According to the acoustic report attached to the file, the screen and the "super silent" configuration bring the noise below the thresholds of the Règlement sur le bruit for residential neighbours.
The Direction du développement du territoire states that an installation on the central flat roof would cost more, because of the load transfer onto the structure.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme issued a favourable opinion with conditions on November 12, 2025; public notice on January 19, 2026 and adoption on February 2, 2026, with a public question period.
The City is transferring $2,840,600 in 2026 to the borough of Pierrefonds-Roxboro, taken from the reserve for sociocultural and sports infrastructure.
Starting in 2027, the borough's annual budget will increase permanently by $3,479,286 (indexed) to operate the new aquatic complex.
This money will be used for maintenance, operations and asset upkeep: the annual budget provides for $4,192,918 in expenses and $713,632 in revenues.
The complex includes a 25-metre pool with 8 lanes and an access ramp, a recreational pool with a sloped-entry beach area, a universal change room, bleachers and multi-purpose rooms.
It is scheduled to be commissioned on March 27, 2026 and to open to the public on July 8, 2026.
The project aims to fill the shortage of indoor aquatic facilities in the area, particularly for Pierrefonds-Roxboro and L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève.
The building has a replacement value of $64,681,302 net of rebate; its construction was awarded to Tisseur inc. in 2023.

The City would pay $870,000 to Les Amis de la montagne and the Centre de la montagne to support their mission from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2029, which works out to $290,000 per year with no indexing.

The money mainly pays staff in two areas: education (interpretation, cultural mediation, school and family activities) and conservation (volunteer work parties, awareness patrols, greening) on mont Royal.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration and charged to the budget of the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports.

Visitor welcome services and equipment rental are being taken out of this agreement and will be covered by separate service contracts ($457,650 over three years, handled in a separate file), following compliance requirements from the Vérificateur général and the legal affairs department.
In total, the organization would receive $1,327,650 over 2026-2029, compared with $1,308,964 for 2023-2026.

The organizations will have to submit two reports per year (May 20 and December 1); payments follow approval of these accountability reports, and a City-organizations follow-up committee will meet at least twice a year.
The City also lends space free of charge (Maison Smith, Grand Chalet, pavillon du Lac-aux-Castors, building K30, storage), a benefit valued at about $600,000.

The City is giving an additional $174,471.56 (net of taxes) to the borough of Verdun, taken from the environmental liability reserve, for the preparatory work on the redevelopment of parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard.
Verdun is awarding a professional services contract to Groupe ABS inc.: $166,147.05 including taxes, plus $24,922.06 in contingencies, for a total expense of $191,069.11.
The mandate covers an environmental assessment (phase 1), a geotechnical study and an environmental characterization (phase 2) before the park's play areas and water games are redone.
The park was built on a former dump site: the City will have to ask the ministère de l'Environnement (MELCCFP) for an authorization.

The redevelopment comes from the winning project "Des aires d'activités accessibles pour toutes les générations" of the 2nd edition of Montréal's participatory budget; three Verdun parks were selected.
The document mentions work being considered on a preliminary basis: new play equipment, paths, improved lighting and a retention basin.
Reasons given: safety issues and the low level of stimulation offered by the current play equipment, which has been the subject of many redevelopment requests.
The City is awarding a $249,660.12 contract (taxes included) to Bétons préfabriqués du Lac inc. to manufacture and deliver concrete ballast blocks for the Quartier des spectacles.
The order includes 40 blocks of 1,000 kg, 10 blocks of 500 kg, as well as EPDM pads and bolts.
These blocks are used to provide logistical support for entertainment activities and events, and to control vehicle traffic in public spaces.
Only one bidder responded to public call for tenders 25-21145, issued on August 4, 2025; its bid is $59,251.26 (19.18%) below the City's estimate.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city; $227,972.97 net of tax rebates comes from the Quartier des spectacles asset maintenance program, financed by a loan.
The contract starts in February 2026 and final delivery is expected in May 2026, so everything is ready before the summer 2026 activity schedule.
The bid is valid until February 1, 2026: a delay could lead to the cancellation of the call for tenders.
The borough of LaSalle confirms the authorization given to Anciens de LaSalle to hold the Classique hivernale at the Bleu, Blanc, Bouge rink in parc Hayward on January 31 and February 1, 2026.
The organization will be able to apply to the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux for a permit to sell alcohol in parc Hayward during the event; no sales to minors.
No entry fee will be charged. The tournament welcomes about 20 teams from LaSalle's adult leagues and minor hockey.

The borough is providing technical support valued at $2,200 in free services: coordination, equipment loan and delivery, access to the rink starting Friday, January 30, monitoring and park attendants.
The profits go to 11 youth organizations in LaSalle, including minor hockey, football and soccer, the Maison des jeunes and the Special Olympics.
The organizer estimates its expenses at $5,000 and its revenues at $9,000, mostly from registration fees.
This is the 12th edition of the tournament.
The City is awarding a $4,815,802.61 (taxes included) direct contract, without a call for tenders, to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for BIXI equipment, over 18 months.
The purchase includes 75 mechanical bikes, 235 electric-assist bikes, 10 electric terminals (stations) with solar kits, 600 complete docking points and 1180 CLAW docking points.
The contract goes ahead without a call for tenders because PBSC holds the patents and the source code for the BIXI system and is the only supplier of 100% compatible parts.
The net expense of $4,397,469.68 is paid by the central city, financed through a loan by-law, and subsidized at 50% by an active transportation assistance program.
Since this is a fourth consecutive award without a call for tenders of more than $4M, the file goes before the Commission permanente sur l'examen des contrats.
The performance of PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. will have to be evaluated, since the net expense is over $500,000.
The bikes belong to the City and are operated by BIXI Montréal, which recorded 13.9 million trips in 2024.
The City is authorizing Hydro-Québec to occupy municipal land to install fast-charging stations at 15 sites, between 2026 and 2029.
These sites will provide a total of 40 electrified parking spaces reserved for fast charging.
Boroughs affected: Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, LaSalle, Outremont, Saint-Léonard, Saint-Laurent, Ville-Marie, Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ahuntsic and Verdun.
The locations include parking lots at arenas, libraries and parks, a neighbourhood police station and several Agence de mobilité durable parking lots.
Hydro-Québec pays for everything: purchasing the stations, building the sites, operation and maintenance. No cost to the City.
Hydro-Québec remains the owner of the fast-charging stations, unlike the level 2 stations, which belong to the City.
Installation work is planned from May 2026 to December 2029.

The City is adding $3,400,000 (taxes included) to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors (traffic lights, civil and electrical work, bike paths), bringing the contract to $11,399,999.99.
The work affects Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve: rue Hochelaga between Frontenac and avenue Desjardins, and rue du Havre between Hochelaga and Ontario.
The extra cost comes mainly from roadway work that turned out to be heavier than expected near the Préfontaine and Joliette metro stations ($3,270,000), after core samples were taken on site.
The STM also asked for three additional bus platforms on Hochelaga, near Hogan, Wurtele and Davidson, for universal accessibility ($130,000).
The work, which began in June 2025, is 70% complete; the worksite resumes in spring 2026 for delivery in spring/summer 2026.
Without a decision before March 2026, the City warns that the improvements near the Joliette station would not be built and that the worksite on Hochelaga would remain incomplete.
The expense is covered 100% by the agglomeration, including $3,104,653.19 (net of rebate) financed by a loan by-law related to the bike path network.

The borough of LaSalle is renewing its lease with the Government of Canada (Parcs Canada) for a piece of land of about 5,765 m² in parc Dollier-de-Casson, within the Lieu historique national du Canal-de-Lachine.
The land is used as a parking lot and holds two mini-soccer fields, for competitions, classes or practices.
The rent is $100 per year, plus taxes, payable each October 1. The previous lease was $1 per year.
The lease runs from October 1, 2023 (retroactively, since the previous one had expired) to September 30, 2033, with the possibility of a 10-year extension until September 30, 2043.
Parcs Canada alone decides on the extension and could then raise the rent.
Signing depends on an authorization from the Government of Québec by order in council, expected in the spring of 2026.
The borough mayor and the borough secretary are authorized to sign the lease.
The City is extending by two years the lease held by the company Cytec Canada inc. at the Centre d'affaires at 7140, rue Albert-Einstein, in the Technoparc de Saint-Laurent.
The new term runs from March 1, 2026 to February 29, 2028, for units 103, 105 and 111, that is 609 square feet of office space.
The total rent is $48,000 before taxes, at a rate of $39.41 per square foot. This is revenue for the City, not an expense.
The previous lease, from March 2024 to February 2026, covered the same area for $58,800.
The tenant also pays the property tax directly to the Service des finances; it does not have to pay the administrative fee again.
Only the City can end the lease before the end of the term, with at least three months' notice.
The decision rests with city council.
The City is awarding Lemay CO inc. a $717,012.84 contract (taxes included) to prepare the preliminary plans and specifications for the new production greenhouses at the Jardin botanique de Montréal.
With contingencies ($107,551.93) and incidental costs ($50,000), the total authorized spending comes to $874,564.77.

Audits carried out in 2021 and 2022 concluded that the current greenhouses are obsolete: electrical and mechanical systems, foundations, and single-pane glazing that led to emergency work after breakages in early 2024.
The mandate includes updating the functional and technical program, the schedule and the specifications document for the future design-build call for tenders.
The contract runs from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027; the spending is paid by the central city, 60% in 2026 and 40% in 2027.
Five firms submitted bids out of 17 that obtained the specifications document; the selected price is 37% higher than the latest internal estimate ($192,577.37).
A $140,000,000 loan by-law to finance the construction of the greenhouses was the subject of a notice of motion on February 16, 2026.
The City is allowing three evenings of cultural events to serve alcohol and keep their doors open later than the usual closing time, between January 31 and February 28, 2026.
The organization Sans Visage will be able to welcome the public and serve alcohol until 6 a.m. on February 28, 2026, at the Grand Quai du Port de Montréal.
The Société des arts technologiques (SAT) will be able to do so until 4 a.m. on January 31, 2026 and until 5 a.m. on February 14, 2026.

The organizers are committing to mitigation measures: security guards and searches, greeters and mediation staff, an on-site medical team, signs asking people to keep noise down, and notices to neighbours with a contact line.
Since May 2025, it is the executive committee that grants these extended hours, not the Régie des alcools, provided the activity does not harm the public interest, safety or peace and quiet.
The decision is part of the Politique de la vie nocturne and does not create any additional cost to the Service de la culture's budget.
The City is allowing the venue Le National to keep its patrons on site and serve alcohol until 4 a.m. on January 18, 2026, for an event it is organizing.
It is allowing Bar Datcha to do the same until 6 a.m. on January 25, 2026.
The two establishments are located in the boroughs of Ville-Marie and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.

The organizers must put mitigation measures in place: security guards and searches, greeting and mediation staff, a medical team and a GRIP-type organization on site, and signage asking people to keep noise down.
They must also notify neighbours about the event and give them a way to reach the organizers during the evening.
The decision is based on the Politique de la vie nocturne, which lets the City (rather than the Régie des alcools) extend alcohol-serving hours for cultural events.
The Service de la culture says the authorization does not add any cost to its budget.
The borough of Saint-Léonard approves the expansion of a single-family home at 9030, boulevard Lacordaire, in the COOP area (Saint-Léonard-Ouest district).
The work adds space on the ground floor and in the basement on the front yard side, with a new basement entrance; two walls of the front facade and part of the left side wall will be demolished.
The flat roof will be replaced by a four-sided roof covered with asphalt shingles; the new brown brick and grey stone match the look of the existing materials.
The building will cover 162.30 m² on a 529.54 m² lot, or 30.64% (maximum allowed: 40%), for a floor area of 147.09 m².
The public tree in front of the property and the four trees in the back yard are being kept; a no-excavation perimeter must be respected around the public tree.
The expansion adds 11.84 m² of hard surface, but the new walkway will be made of permeable paving stones.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on December 3, 2025, as did the urban planning department.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is granting a minor exemption for the Banque TD branch at 8940, boulevard Viau (Saint-Léonard-Ouest district).
The display area for signs mounted flat on the walls goes from the maximum allowed of 17.32 m² to 30 m², which is 12.68 m² more.
The signs must be replaced to comply with section 68.1 of the Charte de la langue française, in effect since June 1, 2025, which requires French to be clearly predominant.
The City discovered that the signs installed in 2003, even though they were approved by a certificate, had been non-compliant from the start because of calculation errors.
The borough notes in particular that the signs have been in place for more than 20 years and that smaller signs would damage the exterior cladding.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on December 3, 2025; the public notice was published on January 14, 2026.
Replacing the signs will require a permit application.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is approving the addition of a second storey to a single-family home at 5805, rue Maricourt, in the Saint-Léonard-Est district.
The house, built in 1963, goes from one storey to two; a 4.16 m² entrance porch is being added, but otherwise the building footprint stays the same.
The second storey is set back from the first, which the City presents as a way to limit the sense of bulk for the neighbours.
The exterior walls will be brown brick and the roof grey asphalt shingle; doors, windows and architectural features will be white.
The public tree in front of the property is being kept, with a no-excavation perimeter around it; a linden tree will be planted in the back yard.
The outdoor landscaping is not changing and no new impermeable surface is being added.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on February 5, 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving up to $30,000, including taxes and fees, to the non-profit organization Amis du champ des possibles for the year 2026.
The money will fund free activities (artistic, cultural, educational and community) at the Champ des Possibles, in the Mile-End.
The organization must also submit an update of its "Plan d'aménagement 2015", which will lay out its vision for the site ahead of the redevelopment following the decontamination of the land.
Planned timeline: signing of the agreement in July 2026, project carried out from July to December 2026, annual report submitted no later than January 31, 2027.
The Champ des Possibles, a former rail yard turned green space, was zoned as a natural space in 2013 and was transferred to the public domain for use as a local park in 2017.
The borough has already supported the organization several times since 2015, including $66,626 for 2023-2024.
The City wants to borrow $43,176,275 to fund street and underground infrastructure work in the Parc d'entreprises de la Pointe-Saint-Charles, in the borough of Le Sud-Ouest.

The work includes redeveloping rue Fernand-Seguin and rue Marc-Cantin, creating two new streets (north-south and east-west), new sidewalks with street furniture and plantings, and reviewing the lighting.
The city's excavated soil management platform will be reconfigured, its entrance moved to rue Marc-Cantin and its surroundings landscaped.
Access to the businesses Bell, TATA and Tidan will be by way of the new east-west street.

This work goes along with the transformation of autoroute Bonaventure into an urban boulevard and the creation of a linear park, a project of nearly 300 million dollars led by the federal Jacques-Cartier and Champlain Bridges corporation.
The loan will be repaid over a maximum of 20 years and will receive no government subsidy.
First contract expected in June 2026, with work starting in April 2027, after approval by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is authorizing the use "adult school" in the building at 5055, boulevard Métropolitain Est, in the Saint-Léonard-Ouest district.

The Centre de services scolaire de la Pointe-de-l'Île, already a tenant of the building, wants to offer full-time daytime training there: literacy, high school level courses, courses preparing for cégep or vocational training, and French-language instruction.

The borough has had no full-time general adult education service point since the Centre Ferland was turned into an elementary school; only the école Antoine-de-Saint-Exupéry offers part-time evening courses.
The City is lifting the requirement to remove 5 parking spaces when the use changes: all existing spaces are kept, but the requirement would come back for any other future change of use.
The project must provide at least 34 bicycle parking units.
Applications for the transformation permit and the certificate of authorization of use must be filed within 18 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The authorization concerns a provision subject to approval by referendum; the public consultation was held on January 14, 2026, and final adoption was planned for March 2, 2026.
Saint-Léonard is removing from its zoning by-law the sections on residential pool safety (safety fence, exceptions to the fencing requirement, pool accessories).
From now on, the borough will directly apply the standards of the provincial by-law on residential pool safety, to avoid duplicating rules.

Owners remain subject to the provincial requirements: a fence at least 1.2 metres high, chain-link mesh of 30 mm maximum (unless slats are inserted), and secured access points such as ladders and decks.
Pools installed before November 1, 2010 must comply with the new provincial standards by 2027, the deadline having been pushed back from 2025.
The rules apply to all outdoor pools 60 cm deep or more: in-ground, semi-in-ground, above-ground or removable.
The minutes of the public consultation meeting of February 11, 2026 are tabled; the by-law is scheduled to be adopted on March 9, 2026.
The draft by-law contains no section that can be subject to approval by referendum.
The agglomeration City is entering into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply, on request, clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel.
The agreement is worth up to $41,944,604.63 taxes included, plus $6,291,690.69 in contingencies, for an estimated total of $48,236,295.32.
Two 12-month extensions are possible.

The fuel will be used by central services, the boroughs and twelve related cities (including Dorval, Westmount, Pointe-Claire, Côte-Saint-Luc); each one pays out of its own budget according to its needs.
Prices will be adjusted every Monday based on the Montréal loading-rack prices published by the Régie de l'énergie; the discount stays fixed for the whole term.
Three companies submitted bids out of the nine that obtained the tender documents; one was set aside for lack of a bid guarantee. The City reports prices 10% cheaper than before.
Because the contract is over 20 million, it is reviewed by the Commission permanente sur l'examen des contrats, and the supplier's performance will be evaluated.

The City is awarding the supply of work clothing to two companies for 36 months, with two possible 12-month extensions: Cintas Canada ltée (lots 1 and 3) and Équipement de Sécurité Universel inc. (lot 4).
Value of the agreements: $820,581.33 and $105,856.31 for Cintas, $852,729.33 for Équipement de Sécurité Universel, taxes included, for an estimated total of $2,046,042.02.
In addition, there is an expense of $266,875.05, taxes included, for quantity variations and contingencies.
The clothing is for blue-collar workers, white-collar workers and managers in all boroughs and central departments; the City must supply it under CNESST rules and the collective agreements.
The products will be available at the City's Centre de distribution, and units will also be able to order directly from the supplier.
Five of the twelve companies that took out the tender documents submitted bids; the accepted prices are below the City's estimates by 39.6% (lot 1), 50.8% (lot 3) and 12.7% (lot 4).
The contracts for lots 1 and 4, which exceed $500,000, will be subject to a supplier performance evaluation.
The City is borrowing $1,200,000 to pay for the bike facilities in phase 2 of the avenue des Pins redevelopment, including design fees and work supervision fees.
The streets involved: avenue des Pins between Peel and avenue du Parc, avenue du Docteur-Penfield between McTavish and des Pins, and rue University from Milton to its north end.

The project follows phase 1 (from du Parc to Saint-Denis), carried out from 2021 to 2025, and goes along with the redevelopment of the former Royal Victoria hospital site, which is expected to welcome close to 6,000 new users.
The work is divided into five packages spread out from 2027 to 2033: a first professional services contract is planned for spring 2026, with work on package C starting in spring 2027.
The by-law must be approved by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation in spring 2026; the loan and its refinancings cannot exceed 20 years.
No government subsidy is expected; asset owners such as the CSEM, Bell and Énergir cover their own costs.
City council is adopting a loan by-law of $98,000,000 to finance phase 2 of the redevelopment of avenue des Pins.
The work covers avenue des Pins between rue Peel and avenue du Parc, avenue du Docteur-Penfield between McTavish and des Pins, and rue University north of rue Milton.
Planned work includes: replacing sewer and water mains and building connections, rebuilding the roadway, sidewalks, lighting and traffic lights, plus street furniture and plantings.

The project stems from the redevelopment of the former Royal Victoria hospital site, planned with the Société québécoise des infrastructures and Université McGill; the City mentions about 6,000 new users once completed.
The work is divided into five lots, spread out from 2027 to 2033 according to the schedule filed.
The ministère des Affaires municipales must approve the loan in spring 2026; the first design contract is expected at the same time.
The loan and any refinancing cannot exceed 20 years, and no government subsidy is expected.
The borough of LaSalle is renting 45 parking spaces at place Newman for users of the Centre récréatif et communautaire de LaSalle (CRCL), at a cost of $33,738.71 including taxes.
The lease covers the year 2026 (January 1 to December 31), retroactively, with Services Immobiliers Crofton Moore Inc., on behalf of the landlord Les Investissements 650 Wellington Ltée.
The spaces are available 7 days a week, from 6 a.m. to 11:30 p.m., and are free for CRCL users.
Of the 45 spaces: 2 are reserved for people with reduced mobility near the entrance, and 43 are located at the corner of Dollard / Uniprix.
The CRCL, built in a park, has no dedicated parking; since the fall of 2024, the owners of place Newman have posted no-parking signs and have been towing vehicles.
The borough also encourages on-street parking: 25 spaces on Émile-Nelligan / boul. Shevchenko and 15 spaces on rue Hardy, reachable by gravel paths.
The 2025 lease, for the same 45 spaces, cost $32,698.89 including taxes.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $3,000 to the organization Ville en vert to run a subsidy program for cloth diapers and sustainable hygiene products in 2026.
The amount breaks down as follows: $2,500 for the subsidies given to people and $500 for the organization's administrative costs.
The program is for families and residents of Montréal-Nord and covers sustainable hygiene products (cloth diapers, menstrual products, incontinence products).
The program ends on December 31, 2026 or as soon as the funds run out; any unused money goes back to the borough.
Ville en vert promotes the program; the borough supports it through Montreal.ca, its newsletter, its social media and InfoNord.
Follow-up meetings are planned for May and August 2026, and a review in December 2026.
This is the program's third year: the borough had granted $3,000 to Ville en vert for 2024 and for 2025.
The borough of Montréal-Nord supports a by-law adopted by Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles on November 26, 2025.
This by-law bans trucks and tool vehicles from driving at all times on boulevard Perras, between boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine and the western boundary of the borough.
The support is being requested because the policy of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable requires a resolution from neighbouring boroughs, with reasons for supporting or refusing.
Montréal-Nord's urban planning team found the by-law to comply with the applicable rules.
RECYC-QUÉBEC will pay the Ville de Montréal up to $24,834.60 (taxes included), in two payments spread over 2025 and 2026.
The money will be used to produce guides to help applicants for demolition permits prepare a "resource diagnosis" and a management plan for construction, renovation and demolition waste.
An assessment guide will also be created for the boroughs' demolition committees.
These documents become required for permit applications to demolish buildings with collective, institutional or industrial uses, under the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050 adopted in June 2025.
The firm SURCY was awarded the contract in November 2025; the guides must be completed in March 2026 and distributed to the boroughs.
The director of Gestion des matières résiduelles is authorized to sign the agreement with RECYC-QUÉBEC.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce will pay $210,000 to the Société de développement commercial Côte-des-Neiges, that is, $70,000 per year from 2026 to 2028.
The annual contribution goes from $60,000 to $70,000; it had stayed at $60,000 since 2018.
The money must be used for the salaries of the SDC's staff and to rent a space, in order to keep a permanent office running.
By ordinance, the council is setting aside the ceiling set out in the by-law on grants to SDCs so as to allow the increase of $10,000 per year.
A payment of $70,000 is planned no later than February 15, 2026, February 15, 2027 and February 15, 2028.
The SDC must provide, among other things, civil liability insurance of $5,000,000, a financial report on the previous contribution, and an action plan by June 30, 2026.
The three-year agreement aims to give the SDC better financial predictability.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is proposing Milany Thiagarajah, councillor for the Darlington district, to sit on the board of directors of PME MTL Centre-Ville.
PME MTL Centre-Ville supports, advises and finances the businesses and entrepreneurs in its territory, which also covers Ville-Marie, Outremont, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Westmount.
One seat on the board of directors is reserved for an elected official from the borough; it had to be filled again after the November 2 elections.
She replaces Magda Popeanu, who had held this seat since 2015.
The borough council adopted the recommendation unanimously on December 8, 2025; the urban agglomeration council must approve it in January 2026.
No financial aspect is indicated in the file.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is renewing the permits allowing a refreshment bar (food, café-terrace and alcohol) to operate at the pavilion in parc Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, from April 1 to December 31, 2026.
Selling food and promotional items is allowed Monday to Saturday from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 7 p.m., inside the pavilion and on the terrace.
Alcohol must be served in plastic or cardboard containers and consumed on site only; the organization will have to obtain its own alcohol permit.

Music and outdoor activities are allowed despite the noise by-law: Monday to Saturday from noon to 9 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 7 p.m., at a maximum of 80 dBA measured at 20 metres. Megaphones remain banned, except for safety purposes.

A call for prices was issued at the end of February 2026; the organization that will run the project will be confirmed in April 2026. The project, called le Rendez-vous, was run by the non-profit Rendez-vous NDG in 2024 and 2025.
The borough reports more than 50,000 visitors during the 2025 season and, in 2024, more than 20,000 visitors and 66 days of operation for the refreshment bar, including 56 evenings of shows.
No financial details are listed in the file.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is removing the lane reserved for buses and taxis (bicycles allowed) on the south side of rue Bélanger, between 40e and 43e Avenue.
The reserved lane applied Monday to Sunday, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
The STM had already removed this section in November 2025; the borough council order is expected in March 2026.
According to the decision summary, the removal is intended to bring back on-street parking and make it easier to access businesses, institutions and deliveries in the area.
This reserved lane had been put in place as a temporary measure during the work to extend the métro's blue line.
The City is authorizing the installation of the required signage; in spring 2026, signage encouraging turnover of parked vehicles will be added.
No cost for the City: the STM is removing the signage at its own expense.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the expansion of the resto-bar Benelux, at 235A-245, rue Sherbrooke Ouest, by adding the neighbouring space left vacant by a dry cleaner.
The establishment would grow to about 321 m² of floor space, while the by-law normally limits a craft brewer's consumption area to 200 m²; the authorization allows up to 250 m².
A café-terrace of about 36.5 m² for 22 people is planned on the private property, facing Sherbrooke Ouest, at least 1.2 m from the building.

The business will have to add two barrier-free entrances with push buttons, a universal washroom, an accessible route and an accessible counter, all certified by an architect before the occupancy certificate is issued.
The sound system will have to be limited to 80 dBA, and a noise study will have to show that noise standards are met in neighbouring dwellings before opening.
Five bicycle parking spaces will have to be set up in the front yard.
The authorization becomes void if it is not used within 60 months; a public consultation was held on December 9, 2025, with no questions or comments.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing Boutique 5e Avenue, at 371-375, avenue Laurier Ouest, to extend its retail business to the 2nd floor, into a space that is currently vacant.
This authorization departs from the planning by-law, which allows retail businesses only on the ground floor and lower levels in this area.
The work is entirely indoors: a new interior staircase, a platform lift, sales space, storage, offices and an employee room on the 2nd floor. The total area will reach 719 m².
The business must carry out accessibility measures: two automatic door openers, one accessible fitting room per floor, a universal washroom, a lowered counter and a platform lift.
Before obtaining its occupancy certificate, the applicant must submit a statement signed by an architect confirming that these measures have been carried out.
Deliveries will remain unchanged: private courier, small vehicles, rear door accessible from the lane.

The authorization becomes void if it is not used within 60 months; the project received a favourable opinion from the comité consultatif d'urbanisme (December 9, 2025) and a public consultation was held on February 10, 2026, with no questions or comments.

The City is extending its emphyteutic lease with the Coopérative d'habitation Bonheur d'Occasion by 13 years, for the building at 1746, 1760, 1800 and 1822, rue Darling, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve: from March 31, 2039 to March 30, 2052.
The annual rent will drop to $6,400 ($200 per unit), compared with $9,024 in 2025. The City puts the value of this reduction at a subsidy of at least $1,160,000 over the period.

The goal: to allow the cooperative to obtain mortgage refinancing for work estimated at about $1,456,253.62 (masonry, balconies, building envelope, windows, roof). Banks require that the emphyteutic lease end at least five years after the mortgage.
The building has 32 units; 2 are occupied by households receiving a rent supplement from the Société d'habitation du Québec, and the other rents are about 54% below the average rent in the area.

The cooperative will have to provide an inspection report by an expert every 5 years, a five-year work plan, its financial statements on request, set up a maintenance reserve and preserve the building's social purpose.
The city clerk will be able to sign the deed once the cooperative has provided confirmation of financing from its mortgage lender and proof of insurance; signing is expected in April 2026.
The City says that some sixty cooperatives and non-profit organizations are in a similar situation and that extensions are granted on a case-by-case basis.
The City is giving a 789.6 m² lot at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni free of charge.
The co-op must demolish the vacant building and build 26 modular housing units on three floors, to be completed within four years after the deed of sale is signed.
The sale will only go through if the co-op gets written confirmation of its funding under the Société d'habitation du Québec's Programme d'habitation abordable Québec.
The City is authorizing a $110,000 write-down from the operating budget of the Service de l'habitation, which is the building's current book value.
The City had bought the building for $1,800,000 in 2021 by exercising its pre-emptive right; a write-down of $1,691,704.22 had already been recorded at the end of 2021.
The borough and the Service de l'habitation support the project; the deed is expected to be signed in 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is appointing city councillor Marie Plourde (Mile-End district) as its representative on the board of directors of PME MTL Centre-Ville.
She replaces Maeva Vilain, who was appointed to the position in 2018 and again in 2022.
The appointment is needed following the municipal elections of November 2, 2025, in order to comply with the organization's by-laws.
PME MTL Centre-Ville is a non-profit economic development organization that also serves Ville-Marie, Outremont, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and Westmount.
No spending is attached to the decision.
The borough council votes on December 17, 2025; the executive committee, the city council and the urban agglomeration council must then ratify the appointment.
The City is awarding Communications Tremblay Ménard inc. a contract to supply and install signs in five parks, for a total expense of $144,883.03 including taxes.
The contract itself is worth $111,448.49; on top of that are $16,717.27 in contingencies, $11,144.85 for variations in quantities and $5,572.42 for incidental costs.
108 signs will be installed: 33 in parc La Fontaine, 29 in parc Jarry, 18 in parc Angrignon, 17 in parc Jeanne-Mance and 11 in parc Maisonneuve.
The signs will cover park by-laws, play areas, sports fields, shared paths and barbecue zones; some outdated signs, in place for about ten years, will be removed.
The work is planned from April to July 2026, with manufacturing and installation starting in April 2026.
Only one company submitted a bid; its price is 43.61% below the in-house estimate, which is $107,777.85 less.
The agglomeration is paying 9.67% of the bill (parc Jeanne-Mance is part of the Mont-Royal heritage site) and the central city, 90.33%.

The City is extending by two years, until December 31, 2027, its agreement with the Université de Montréal on the use of the Vincent-d'Indy sports field, built on the réservoir Bellingham, in Outremont.
The Université keeps an exclusive right to use the field for 2026 and 2027.
The 500 hours per year reserved for the City now benefit all Montréal users, with the Outremont borough served first.

Management of the agreement moves from the Outremont borough to the Direction des sports of the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports, since the delegations of power expired on December 31, 2025.
The amendment also updates the parties' addresses; no additional financial impact is expected.
The two parties intend to negotiate a new agreement applicable as of January 1, 2028, if applicable.

The Ville-Marie borough is approving a specific project on the Université McGill campus, which allows exceptions to the current rules on height, density, uses and building coverage ratios for the campus.
McGill will be allowed to install ground signs (sign monuments or post-mounted signs) at the locations and according to the plans stamped by the borough on September 9, 2025.
Landscaping is planned in one area of the campus, according to a map prepared by the borough in April 2026.
Any application to expand or make major renovations to the aréna McConnell or the stade Percival Molson will have to include a landscaping plan for the outdoor parking lot.
Any new construction on lot 1 338 662 will have to come with a landscaping certificate and aim to maximize planting directly in the ground.
Permit applications in the areas concerned will have to aim to preserve trees with a trunk measuring 10 cm or more (DBH), and meet criteria for fitting in with the streetscape of rue Peel.
The borough council adopted the 2nd draft resolution on June 9, 2026, unanimously, following a public consultation held on May 27, 2026.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $364,724 to 8 organizations for 14 projects to be carried out from January 1 to December 31, 2026.

The money comes from the Prévention Montréal program of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, which targets children, young people under 30 and their families in vulnerable situations.
The projects fall under two areas: helping young people reach their full potential, and prevention in urban safety.

The largest amounts go to the Maison des Jeunes de LaSalle (including $102,434 for "Rejoindre mon quartier" and $38,085 for "Poing final") and to the Maison des Familles de LaSalle ($43,285 for "Contact humain").

Other organizations receiving funding: Destination Travail du Sud-Ouest, Corporation Espoir (inclusive day camps), Bienvenue à L'immigrant, Association de soccer mineur de LaSalle, Programme de basketball des Leaders and Cumulus Agir.
This is a one-year extension: the City is granting the boroughs the same amounts as in 2025, after reviewing the reports on the projects.
The borough mayor and the borough secretary are authorized to sign the 14 agreements with the organizations.
The borough of LaSalle is amending its agreement with the Table de développement social de LaSalle, under the Prévention Montréal program.
The original project was not carried out as planned: the organization will be able to adjust its activities and will have until December 31, 2026 to complete them.
No new money is being paid out: the $24,237 granted in 2025 will be spent in 2026.
The project provides for at least four free training sessions on urban safety for youth organizations in LaSalle, coordinated by the TACEFJAL.
A second component, with the Maison des familles de LaSalle, organizes discussions on the issues facing families who are very vulnerable and hard to reach.
The organization will have to submit its final report no later than 30 days after the end of the project.

The City is extending its agreement with the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation by two years for a study project aimed at reducing flood-related risks in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: the end date moves from March 31, 2026 to March 31, 2028.

The project budget stays at $1,647,000: $1,235,250 from the ministère (75%), $311,750 from the borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville and $100,000 from the Bureau de la transition écologique et de la résilience.

The postponement is due to the complexity of the modelling work, the time needed to consult with partners and residents, and the delay of the MÉRIGE project on economic risks, whose results are expected in 2027.
The project's objectives and the financial commitments do not change.
Next steps: completion of the analyses in 2026, design of the development measures in 2026-2027, and final reporting in 2028.
No communications activities are planned.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is lending two pieces of land free of charge to the organization Éco de la Pointe-aux-Prairies to manage community gardens.
The jardin collectif du Citoyen, in parc Saint-Jean-Baptiste (lot 1 092 602), is being lent for 1 year; the jardin collectif des Prairies (lot 1 075 894) for 3 years.
Each plot is 150 m². The loans cost nothing: the City values the plots at $52,500 and $105,000.
The organization must engage the community, manage the gardens and hold workshops there; part of the harvest will go to a food bank.
The gardens are grown without pesticides or chemical fertilizers and are open to the public.
Activities in the gardens are to resume in the spring of 2026, after approval by the borough council on February 3, 2026.
Without these agreements, according to the document, residents would lose access to the two community gardens.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is awarding Excavation E.S.M. inc. a contract worth $150,885.14 (taxes included) to rebuild the stairs and the path in parc Simone-Dénéchaud.
The total authorized spending is $181,145.53, including $15,088.51 in contingencies and $15,171.88 in incidental costs. The borough is funding the project, whose net cost is $165,410.01.
The path crosses the wooded area between boulevard Gouin and rue Simone-Dénéchaud, in the Rivière-des-Prairies area.
The stone steps, which have shifted out of place, will be replaced with precast concrete steps with a handrail; the path will be rebuilt with stone screenings and widened to 2 metres.
Four light fixtures and two benches will be installed, and vegetation will be cut back 1 metre on each side of the path.
Work is scheduled to start in May 2026 and finish in the summer of 2026.
Eleven bids were received; the lowest is 29% below the internal estimate. No performance evaluation of the company will be done, since the contract is worth less than $500,000.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is paying $8,000 to the organization Éco de la Pointe-aux-Prairies to manage the subsidy program for the purchase of reusable hygiene products, from June 3 to December 31, 2026.
Borough residents can be reimbursed up to 50% of the purchase price, or 75% if the product is made in Québec.
The limit is $100 per person for washable diapers ($125 for a Québec-made product) and $50 for other reusable hygiene products ($75 for a Québec-made product).
Products covered: washable diapers for babies and adults, swim diapers, inserts and wipes, training pants, menstrual cups and pads, washable toilet paper and tissues, and underwear for urinary leaks.
To take part, you must fill out a form on the organization's website or at its premises and provide supporting documents. Only one application per person per category, every three years.
If there are fewer applications than expected, the borough can take back the unused amounts or extend the program until the funds run out.
The organization is responsible for promoting the program; the borough also shares the information on its website.
The Lachine borough council turns down the project to build a 3-storey building with 11 rental units and indoor parking at 776, 5e Avenue.
The project called for demolishing the existing house and building 10 indoor parking spaces, with 11 units ranging from studios to 3-bedroom apartments.
It did not comply with the area's zoning, which limits buildings to 8 units and lot coverage to 55% (58% was proposed), and which required 17 parking spaces.
Valid requests to hold a referendum were received on September 16, 2025, after the public consultation meeting of August 20, 2025.
The council finds the residents' concerns well founded: number of units, parking and traffic, sewer capacity, construction nuisances, green spaces, expected rents and property values.
The adoption process ends here, and the borough's management must explain the reasons for the refusal to the developer and to the residents who took part.
The City is extending by two years the wheeled bin repair contract awarded to USD Global inc., from March 23, 2026 to March 22, 2028.
It authorizes an additional expenditure of $307,526.60, taxes included, bringing the total contract to $1,084,168.76.
The service covers all 19 boroughs: repairs are done on site, at the resident's address, within 5 business days of the request (made mostly through 311).
Starting February 16, 2026, Éco Entreprises Québec will take over the repair of recycling bins; the City keeps the repair of brown and grey bins, which is about 60% of the work.
The supplier must also dismantle bins that cannot be repaired and reuse the parts that are still good in later repairs.
Repair prices will be indexed on January 1, 2027 and on January 1, 2028; the expenditure is paid entirely by the central city.
The executive committee is changing the waste collection rules in two boroughs: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
In L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, the day, the schedule and the sectors for recyclable materials collection are changing.
In Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, the day, the schedule and the sector boundaries are changing, in particular for laneway collections, following the new boundaries that came into effect on November 1, 2025.
These changes stem from two public calls for tenders (24-20671 and 24-20797) and from the new collection and transportation contracts.
The City says it wants to improve collection performance, reduce calls to 311 and make the new rules applicable to users of the service.
The ordinances come into effect as soon as they are published; the boroughs will handle local communications themselves if needed.
No spending is attached to this file (financial aspect: not applicable).

The executive committee authorizes the Biosphère and the Jardin botanique (Espace pour la vie department) to each submit a grant application to the ministère de la Culture et des Communications du Québec.
The two applications total $1 million: $500,000 for the Biosphère and $500,000 for the Jardin botanique.
The Biosphère wants to create a permanent exhibition in its largest space (264 m²), to be shown for about 10 years, on environmental issues.
The Jardin botanique wants to replace the exhibition "Chercheurs tout-terrain," shown for the past 11 years at the Centre sur la biodiversité, with an immersive exhibition about Marie-Victorin.
This new exhibition will mark the 150th anniversary of the Université de Montréal and the 100th anniversary of the Jardin botanique, using the UdeM archives and the herbier Marie-Victorin.
The applications had to be submitted no later than January 30, 2026; the directors of both institutions are authorized to sign them.
The ministère requires authorization from the municipal bodies for the applications to be accepted.
The City is awarding a direct-negotiation contract to Transvrac Montréal-Laval inc. to rent trucks with drivers, at a maximum cost of $1,829,028.05, taxes included.
The contract starts on March 23, 2026 and ends on March 31, 2027.

The trucks will haul excavated soil from the Parc d'entreprise de la Pointe Saint-Charles and from the biomethanation construction site in Montréal-Est, snow-melting residue from disposal sites, as well as leaves, mulch and other bulk materials in various boroughs.
About 13,000 tonnes of lightly contaminated soil will go to the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel for parc Frédéric-Back; about 700 tonnes will go to Énergie Carboneutre inc. in Montréal-Est.

The City says it does not own the trucks it needs and is therefore turning to the private sector; Transvrac is a non-profit organization that holds the bulk trucking brokerage permit for Montréal and Laval.

The rates follow the ministère des Transports' Recueil des tarifs de camionnage en vrac (bulk trucking rate schedule); the expense is paid by the central city, with possible transfers to the Service de l'environnement or to the boroughs that use the service.
The previous contract with the same company, awarded in February 2025, was worth $1,341,052.67.

The City is awarding a $336,185 (taxes included) direct-award contract to the Société des Amis du Biodôme de Montréal to handle the administration and finances of the Espace pour la vie day camps in 2026, including the childcare service.
The camps, for children aged 7 to 12, will offer 868 spots at the Biodôme and the Jardin botanique/Insectarium, from June to the end of August 2026.

The Société des Amis du Biodôme will collect registration fees and remit them to the City, hire the camp counsellors and run the childcare service; Espace pour la vie keeps control of programming, pricing and science activities.

Council is authorizing an additional budget of $431,115 in revenue and the same amount in spending, matching the estimated registration income and the contributions from the Fondation Espace pour la vie.
About 200 to 220 children from low-income backgrounds will attend the camps free of charge thanks to the Bourse Jérôme-Brisson-Curadeau, which is 20 to 25% of the spots.
Total spending is estimated at $600,475; the $169,360 gap not covered by revenue is included in the Espace pour la vie budget and paid by the central city.
The City is extending its agreements with GardaWorld s.e.n.c., Teltech Signalisation inc. and Béton Brunet ltée - Division Signalisation by 12 months, from February 20, 2026 to February 19, 2027.
These firms provide road signage services on request: rerouting cars and pedestrians during obstructions, roadwork or emergencies such as floods.
No additional spending: the value of the agreements stays at $4,521,468.22, taxes included, plus $678,220.23 set aside for changes in quantities.
The services remain available to all boroughs and all City business units; each order will be paid for by the unit that uses it.
As of November 19, 2025, the City had used $1,404,240.82 of the agreements, or 27% of the contracts.
Prices will be indexed on the anniversary date of the contracts based on the average change in the consumer price index for the Montréal region.
The spending is shared: 40% central city, 20% the boroughs, 40% the agglomeration, because of use by the Service de l'eau.

The City is extending its contract with Telus Health (CANADA) Ltd by five years for the hosting, support and maintenance of the Ariel software, which manages its pension plans, from March 16, 2026 to March 15, 2031.
The additional spending totals $5,157,101.77 including taxes: $4,297,584.82 for the contract and $859,516.95 in contingencies, bringing the total contract to $9,824,111.
The software is used to administer the pension plans of about 44,000 members and is used every day by about 50 employees of the Bureau des régimes de retraite.
The contract includes legal updates, technical support, data hosting and up to 700 hours per year of on-demand services, which can be carried over from one year to the next.
Beyond these 700 hours, the City will pay $280 an hour in 2026, with an annual indexation of 2%; these hours will be taken from the contingency budget.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders because Telus Health holds the source codes for the Ariel software; prices increase by 2% per year from 2027 to 2031.
The spending will be paid out of the operating budget of the Bureau des régimes de retraite, with no impact on the City's financial framework.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding Groupe Piché Construction inc. the contract to renovate and expand the Centre sportif Trenholme, for $8,786,218.31 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $11,250,752.55, which is the contract plus $1,317,932.75 in contingencies and $1,146,601.49 in incidental costs.
The work covers architecture, mechanical, electrical, civil and structural components, and includes demolition, decontamination and the redevelopment of the building.
The project adds change rooms, storage areas, meeting rooms and an elevator, renovates the gymnasium, and installs a geothermal system.
The Québec government's PAFIRS financial assistance program covers 66.66% of the cost; the borough pays 33.34%.
Construction is to begin in the spring of 2026.
The public call for tenders received 18 bids; the winning bid is 13.11% below the professionals' estimate.
The Ville-Marie borough is releasing $166,190.26 ($182,000 including taxes), taken from its deferred revenue for parks and playgrounds, to develop parks in 2026.

$57,000 will be used to buy about 665 shrubs and 4,160 perennials, planted notably in parc Fleury-Mesplet, parc Emery, Place Vauquelin, parc des Faubourgs, parc Saint-Jacques, parc Simone-Monet-Chartrand and parc Walter-Stewart.

$100,000 will go toward buying about 350 trees, planted mainly on île Sainte-Hélène (including potentially on the land occupied by Six Flags), at the entrance to the îlots Bonaventure, at Place du Sable Gris and at Place du Commerce.
$25,000 will be used for materials for park furniture at square Viger (centre and east sectors), at Espace Pierre-Bourgault and at parc Charles-S.-Campbell.
The document explains that significant tree clearing has taken place in recent years on île Sainte-Hélène because of the emerald ash borer.
Planned timeline: contracts for wood and hardware and calls for tenders for plants before March 1, spring contracts before March 15, fall tree contracts before September 15.
The spending covers the period from February 15 to December 31, 2026; any unused amounts will go back to their original account.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is amending its by-law on site planning and architectural integration programmes (PIIA) to bring it in line with Montréal's Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité.

New construction of accessory housing units (an additional dwelling on a lot already occupied by a residence) will now be subject to architectural review on properties with buildings of heritage interest and in heritage areas.
The by-law adds a criterion calling for permeable surfacing to be favoured over asphalt or concrete in new construction.
New parking and loading areas, and their access ways, will have to be limited and positioned so that they are less visible from the street.

The text sets rules for major projects affecting heritage places of worship and institutional heritage complexes, with specific thresholds (for example, removing more than 20% of a building's volume).
