New definitions are added, including one for a "charging hub" for electric vehicles (a minimum of four level 2 charging stations or three fast-charging stations, among other configurations).
The council is also receiving the minutes of the public consultation meeting of March 18, 2026 and the report on the written consultation held from March 11 to 18, 2026.
The City is extending its contract with Imprime-Emploi by 12 months to print and distribute the construction notices, letters and invitation cards sent to residents.
Additional spending authorized: $671,469.74, taxes included, bringing the total contract to $1,953,656.23.
The extension covers the period from February 26, 2026 to February 25, 2027; the company accepted the offer on November 21, 2025.

The documents are used to inform people in the neighbourhoods and boroughs affected by construction sites: the nature and length of the work, traffic obstructions, temporary water shut-offs and information sessions.
The supplier must deliver anywhere on the island of Montréal within a maximum of 24 hours, or even the same day if needed.
Estimated breakdown before taxes: $287,069.30 for the letters sent before and after the work, $339,930 for the black-and-white construction notices, and $30,655.25 for the colour invitation cards.
The spending is covered by the existing budget of the Service des ressources humaines et des communications, with no impact on the City's financial framework.
The borough of Lachine is awarding Ascenseurs Vertec inc. a $311,582.25 contract (taxes included) to modernize a hydraulic elevator at the Lachine city hall.
With contingencies ($37,389.87) and incidentals ($24,926.58), the total expense comes to $373,898.70, paid 100% by the borough.

The work includes replacing the electronic controller, upgrading the hydraulic components, renewing the electrical circuits, new doors, a safety system that meets CSA/B44 standards and a digital display.

According to the decision summary, the current elevator has reached the end of its life: replacement parts can no longer be found, it stops at the wrong floor and it breaks down often, which limits access to services for people with reduced mobility.

Public call for tenders LAC-PUB-2517, published on October 14, 2025, drew two people who obtained the tender documents, but only one bid; the price is 3.71% ($11,142.23) higher than the professionals' estimate.
A communication plan will be prepared after the contract is awarded to inform the people affected by the work.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is drawing $545,000 from its operating surplus (contingency reserve) to fund its cleanliness plan in 2026.
The money goes to the Direction des travaux publics, which has been coordinating the plan since receiving a mandate in October 2024.

The funds will be used in particular for citizen engagement, by-laws and street furniture, and to take into account local realities such as homelessness, students, tourist rentals and pedestrianization.
Any amount not spent in 2026 will be carried over to the following year for the same purpose.
The borough had already allocated $500,000 to the same plan in April 2025.
The initiatives will be announced through on-site signage, social media, the website and the newsletter.
The City is adding $25,392 (taxes included) to its contract with the firm Adlib Publishing Systems inc., bringing the total contract to $350,621.78.
This money pays for a bank of technical support hours to finish upgrading the Adlib software, which is used to produce the agendas and decision files for borough, city and agglomeration councils.
The current version of the software (version 7), purchased more than ten years ago, is no longer supported by the supplier; the City wants to reduce the risk of breakdowns when producing agendas.
The expense is charged to the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information for the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
The original contract was awarded without a call for tenders in March 2024 (exclusive supplier) for $325,229.78, until March 31, 2027.
The director of the Direction espaces de travail et services aux utilisateurs is authorized to sign the documents related to the contract on behalf of the City.
The City is joining the group purchasing program of Québec's Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales (CAG) to buy or lease printers, multifunction devices and original ink cartridges.
The agreement is worth a maximum of $3,008,100, taxes included, over 34 months, from January 30, 2026 to November 29, 2028.
Purchases will be made as needs arise; the costs will be paid by the boroughs, the central services and the related cities.
The City will pay the CAG a management fee of 1% of the amount of each order, billed by the supplier.
The agreement also covers maintenance, ink, labour and training, billed at a cost per page for equipment bought or leased with service.
The equipment offered is EPEAT Silver or Gold certified and ENERGY STAR compliant; the cartridges meet ISO standards 19752, 19798 or 24711.
The director of the Direction espaces de travail et services aux utilisateurs is authorized to sign the contract documents.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing two elected officials to represent it on the board of directors of le Pôle, the organization formerly known as CDEC Montréal-Nord.
The people appointed are Jean-Marc Poirier, borough councillor, and Youssef Hariri, city councillor, both from the Marie-Clarac district.
Le Pôle is a non-profit organization that works on employment and entrepreneurship for residents of Montréal-Nord, particularly young people and immigrants.
The appointment replaces the one made in 2021, which placed borough mayor Christine Black and Mr. Poirier on this board of directors.
The borough council adopted the proposal unanimously on December 1, 2025; the appointment must be confirmed by the urban agglomeration council.
The document does not provide for any spending.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is approving the installation of a wooden fence at 530, rue Cherrier.
The fence will be put up along the entire length of the right side property line.
It will consist of screen-type panels made of vertical wood boards, 1.83 metres (6 feet) high.
The property is in an area described as "of exceptional value" that is visible from the street, which means the project must be reviewed before a permit is issued.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme, which met on December 9, 2025, said it was in favour of the project.
The permit application was filed on October 1, 2025; the borough council makes its decision on February 3, 2026.
No money is involved in this matter.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is approving the conversion and renovation of a single-family home at 45, chemin North Ridge.
The planned work: converting the built-in garage into living space and replacing the exterior siding.
The approved materials are specified: white brick, brown wood panels, dark grey aluminum panels, foundation stucco, and windows and a door in natural mahogany-coloured wood.
The house, built in 1964 in the "mid-century" style, is described as being in an advanced state of deterioration; it was the home of Claire Kirkland-Casgrain.
The street is located within a humanized landscape area, between the Saint-Raphaël and Royal Montréal golf courses, which makes the project subject to the architectural integration rules (PIIA).
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on December 9, 2025; the borough council will decide on February 3, 2026.
No amount is attached to this file.
The City is adding $43,805.21 (taxes included) to the contract with Sports Montréal inc. for managing the Jeux de Montréal, bringing the total to $1,012,805.21.
This money is being used to mark the 50th anniversary of the 1976 Summer Olympic Games during the 2026 edition of the Jeux de Montréal.
Sports Montréal inc. will have to coordinate 26 sport disciplines instead of 15, change the visuals on promotional materials and medals, and produce video clips on highlights of the Olympic Games.
The Jeux de Montréal are aimed at young people aged 6 to 13 from the boroughs and related municipalities who are enrolled in an introductory program.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, in two payments, out of the budget of the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports.
The contract ends on June 30, 2026.
Without this addition, the contract stays unchanged and the 50th anniversary of the Olympic Games will not be marked.

The City is entrusting the Association régionale de soccer Concordia (ARSC) with managing bookings and supervising the Stade de soccer de Montréal, at the complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2030.

The agreement works as an exchange of services: no money is paid. The ARSC's services are worth $398,257.70 over five years, and in return the City provides it with premises and free rental hours for the same amount.
The City is lending the ARSC administrative premises (1,416 sq. ft.), indoor storage (220 sq. ft.) and outdoor storage (156 sq. ft.), plus 100 hours of facility loan.
The ARSC must manage the soccer programming (1,300 h), provide supervision (175 h) and supervise the facility during its activities (1,026.80 h).
The ARSC must respect the client priorities set by the City, apply the municipal rates, collect the money and remit it to the City.
The organization must submit an accountability report each year and bill twice a year.
The previous contract with the ARSC ended on December 31, 2025; the Stade's programming gives priority to young people from the 19 boroughs.
The City is lending the Club de lutte Inter-Concordia an administrative office and a training room at the complexe sportif Claude-Robillard, free of charge.
The agreement starts when it is signed and ends on December 31, 2027.
The loan is part of the Politique de soutien aux organismes qui œuvrent dans les installations sportives corporatives, under the "Clubs sportifs" program.
The organization must submit an accountability report no later than October 31 each year and follow a visibility protocol.
Three organizations had applied; the other two applications were approved in December 2025. The Club de lutte's application required additional checks before it was found eligible.
According to the document, a refusal could lead to higher registration fees or a smaller Olympic wrestling offering in Montréal.
No money is being paid out: the support takes the form of space lent free of charge.
The City is giving $25,300 in 2026 to two regional sports associations: $15,000 to Volleyball Montréal and $10,300 to Handball Montréal.
The money is used to coordinate competition schedules, train officials and coaches, and carry out sports development projects.
This is the City's first grant to Volleyball Montréal; Handball Montréal had received $7,500 in 2025.
Both grants cover a single year, since the cycle of the Programme de soutien aux associations sportives régionales ends in 2026.
With these additions, 24 regional sports associations will be supported by the program in 2026.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, out of the budget of the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports.
The organizations must sign an agreement setting the conditions for payment and follow a visibility protocol.
The City is giving $300,000 to the organization Montréal - Métropole en santé for two years, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2028, which is $150,000 per year.
The money is used to carry out the action plans of two groups: Montréal physiquement active and the Conseil du système alimentaire montréalais.
These plans aim to encourage physical activity (facilities for active transportation, urban outdoor activities, sports) and access to healthy, affordable and local food.
The payments are planned as follows: $135,000 in 2026, $150,000 in 2027 and $15,000 in 2028, after accountability reports are submitted.
The expense is paid by the agglomeration and funded by the Fonds régions et ruralité; it represents 8.7% of the organization's expected annual revenue.
The City has been supporting this organization with $150,000 per year since 2017; the current agreement ends on March 31, 2026.
MAPAQ, the Direction régionale de santé publique, M361 and Centraide also fund these action plans.
The executive committee is recognizing two sports organizations for 2026: Patinage Bourassa (figure skating) and Accès escalade Montréal (sport climbing).
This status gives them access to City support: financial, professional, event-related, and the loan of sports facilities.
Three applications had been received before October 1, 2025; the third will have to be resubmitted in 2026 with more details on the regional reach of its activities.
The recognition applies to 2026 only, after which the organizations will have to apply for a 3-year renewal.
The organizations must submit an accountability report within 120 days after the end of their fiscal year, otherwise their status can be revoked.
Next deadlines: financial support applications must be submitted by June 1, 2026, and funding for 2027 will be confirmed in the fall of 2026.
The recognition itself does not involve any spending; 31 organizations had already been recognized for 2024-2026.

The City is changing its definition of "business assistance" so that grants to "nightlife vitality establishments" performance venues no longer fall under the urban agglomeration council, but under the city council.
This change paves the way for a future financial assistance program reserved for these venues, aimed at responsible and safe nightlife practices.
The program itself will be presented later to the city council in a separate file.
The establishments covered are those designated by resolution of the executive committee under the Politique de la vie nocturne adopted in November 2024.
The Service de la culture cites the preservation of independent venues and commercial streets, and coexistence with residential neighbours.
The document states that the change has no financial impact.
City council is adopting a by-law that creates a support program for performance venues recognized as "établissements de vitalité nocturne" (nightlife vitality establishments).
Each qualified establishment can receive a lump sum of $5,000 and a licence to use the "Nuits Montréal" label.
The program has a one-time budget of $200,000 and ends when the funds run out or when the executive committee decides to end it.
To qualify, venues must hold an occupancy certificate as a performance venue and be recognized by a resolution of the executive committee; applications for support are made through an online form.
Applications for qualification are accepted three times a year: June 1, October 1 and February 1.
The boroughs of Ville-Marie, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and Le Sud-Ouest are affected.
The program is expected to come into force on March 24, 2026, with the qualified establishments to be announced in spring 2026.
The urban agglomeration council is adding 391 buildings in the borough of LaSalle to the inventory of heritage buildings constructed before 1940.
These buildings will now be considered heritage buildings: they will be subject to specific rules for demolition, as well as for the occupancy and upkeep of buildings.
Québec law requires the agglomeration to complete this inventory by April 1, 2026; Montréal is adopting it in parts, borough by borough.
The agglomeration has roughly 100,000 buildings constructed before 1940 to review; 26 territories have already had their portion of the inventory adopted.
The work is funded through an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications: up to $5,000,000 from the ministry and an equal contribution from the Ville.
The information on each building must be published as open data by the Ville and the ministry.
The borough of LaSalle took part in the exercise and supports the adoption of the list.
The City is extending its Internet service contracts with Beanfield Technologies (lot 1) and Bell Canada (lot 2) by 12 months, from February 23, 2026 to February 22, 2027.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $306,585.33, taxes included, bringing the total of the two contracts to $1,205,311.15.
The contracts cover the City's Internet connection and protection against DDoS (denial of service) cyberattacks.
Using two separate suppliers serves to provide primary and secondary links and to reduce dependence on a single supplier.
The expense is charged to the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information, with monthly payments.
The contracts awarded in February 2023 were worth $898,725.82 for three years and included two 12-month extension options; this is the first one being exercised.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.
The borough of Lachine is ending, as of December 14, 2025, the professional services contract with Avizo Experts-Conseils inc. for the shoreline development of parc Stoney Point - Phase 2.
The project was cancelled on December 3, 2025: the ministère de l'Environnement required additional environmental studies whose timelines and changes go beyond the scope of the project.
The contract, awarded in 2023, was worth a maximum of $221,326.89, taxes included.
Avizo has already been paid $57,532.50 (before taxes) for the work completed; an amount of $3,238.75 (before taxes) remains to be paid for work done between 2024 and 2025.
Under the contract, no compensation is paid for anticipated profits or other damages related to the termination.
The company has 10 days to hand over all documents produced (reports, studies, plans, data) in open and reusable formats, along with its final invoice.
Ville-Marie is adopting a by-law that allows it to fund its commercial development corporations (sociétés de développement commercial, SDC) to turn streets into pedestrian streets in 2026.
An SDC can receive up to 66% of the cost of its project, up to a maximum of $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street, or $700,000 for projects from the 2022-2024 call for projects.
For a new project, the ceiling is 66% of eligible expenses, up to $425 per linear metre or $180,000.
Applications must be submitted in writing no later than February 16, 2026, with a design plan, a budget, a timeline and audited financial statements.
The grant is paid in two instalments: 75% after the council's decision, and the balance within 30 business days after the end-of-project documents are submitted.
The grant is granted only if the borough council adopts an ordinance temporarily closing the street in question to car traffic.
Adoption is planned for February 10, 2026, coming into force through publication in Le Devoir around February 14, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is extending by one year the temporary position of planning advisor assigned to the Complexe aquatique et sportif project, until December 31, 2026.
The expense planned for 2026 comes to $152,100 (salary of $119,000, $3,200 in premiums and adjustments, $29,900 in payroll taxes) for 1,820 hours.
The money comes from the borough's reserved surplus, that is, the reserve created for this project; the expense must be renewed each year for as long as the project lasts.
The advisor remains the resource person and coordinator for the project within the borough, working with the City's central services.
The project received $85M from the City in February 2024 for phase 1 (aquatic component) and $15M from the federal government in March 2025 (Green and Inclusive Community Buildings program).
Studies are under way, including a mobility study around the future complex carried out with the Agence de mobilité durable de Montréal.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is awarding a professional services contract worth $21,471.58 (taxes included) to the firm GLT+ inc., plus $3,220.74 for contingencies, for a total of $24,692.32.
The mandate: have a construction economist estimate the construction costs of the future Complexe aquatique de Montréal-Nord.
The money comes from the financial reserve for the Complexe aquatique et sportif, funded by the borough's surplus; the net expense is $22,547.38.
These preliminary studies are not eligible under the Programme aquatique de Montréal (PAM – construction), so the borough is covering the cost on its own.
The study is to be carried out in January and February 2026, with the final report delivered at the end of February 2026.
The document states that without this study, the borough could not complete the documents required to move on to the next stage of the project, which would delay the timeline.
No communications activities are planned at this stage.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Jeffry St-Cyr as development officer for cultural, physical and sports activities, in the Division des sports et loisirs, effective February 21, 2026.
Permanent status in the position depends on successfully completing the probation period set out in the collective agreement for municipal professionals.
The position involves advising the borough on organizing sports activities, analyzing residents' needs and supporting the management of sports facilities.
The position became vacant after its previous holder left for the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports.

The expected cost from February 21 to December 31, 2026 is $78,200 ($61,200 in salary, $1,600 in premiums and adjustments, $15,400 in payroll taxes and benefits), charged to the borough's operating budget.
The position was posted internally within the Ville from November 13 to 21, 2025.
The City is ending its contract with Veille sur toi inc. for the supply of 12 items in the Bienvenue bébé box, no later than December 31, 2026.
The contract, awarded in June 2025 for 3 years (plus 2 possible extensions), was worth up to $7,476,249.38, taxes included.
The Bienvenue bébé project is not being renewed in the budget; the City cites the prioritization of its spending.
The contract allows termination without cause: the company cannot claim compensation for lost profit, only for services rendered and costs incurred.
Costs to be paid despite the end of the contract: $911,280 for the purchase of 4,000 Bienvenue bébé boxes and $100,000 in costs incurred, for a total of $1,011,280.
The department concerned has $300,000 on hand; the City is transferring $711,280 from unforeseen contingency expenses to cover the rest, and any unused balance will be returned there.
The supplier will be evaluated after the file is approved.

The City is extending two contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. by six months to process food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration, at an additional cost of $3,269,055.43, taxes included.
With this extension, the total value of the two contracts rises to $10,460,977.38, taxes included (lot 1: $1,611,058.44; lot 2: $1,657,996.99 for the extension).
The extension runs from March 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026 and covers about 18,475 tonnes of food waste.
The company receives the materials at its Montréal-Est site and transports them to composting sites in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario.
Food waste from 15 boroughs and 2 related cities continues to be collected while waiting for the Montréal-Est biomethanation plant to start operating.
The City can end the contracts at any time with 30 days' written notice if the Montréal-Est plant becomes fully operational.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration; the contracts include no price indexation.
The City is extending the contract of Remorquage Météor inc. by one year, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027, to tow and store vehicles that must undergo a forensic examination.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $360,007.71, taxes included, bringing the contract to $943,109.17.
The company keeps the exclusive right to tow and store these vehicles throughout the island of Montréal, with some trips outside the island at the SPVM's request.
The contract also covers an impound lot service and the towing of boats and pleasure craft.

The maximum amount provided for in the 2024 contract ($583,101.46) will be reached in February 2026, before the August 22, 2026 expiry date, because of the increase in the number of tows and the annual indexation.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration and is provided for in the SPVM's 2026 budget.
According to the file, a refusal would force the City to launch a new call for tenders, with a service interruption.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is extending until December 1, 2026 the agreement signed with the organization A.G.C. Art Public for the creation of a mural.
The original agreement, approved on July 7, 2025, granted $9,500 (all applicable taxes included) under the Programme Muralité 2025.
The mural, designed by the collective TYXNA, has been postponed to 2026 for reasons related to the collective's artist.
The deadline for reporting also moves to December 1, 2026, and a new schedule is attached to the addendum.
The organization has already signed the addendum; the borough mayor and the borough secretary (or their substitutes) are authorized to sign the documents.
The Programme Muralité funds up to 70% of a mural project's budget, through a call for projects open to building owners, non-profit organizations and artists.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is transferring $250,000 from its management surplus to its 2026 budget in order to make the last promised payment to the Musée de l'Holocauste de Montréal.
This amount was not spent in 2025; it completes the City's total contribution of $1,500,000, paid in three payments.

The money helps fund the construction of the new museum at 3535, boulevard Saint-Laurent: a 55,000-square-foot building, a permanent exhibition, a temporary gallery, a commemorative space, a research centre and a 150-seat auditorium.

The project's total budget is $120M, including $25M for a programming and operating fund; as of June 2024, $113.5M had been collected or confirmed ($20M from Québec, $25M from Ottawa, $1.5M from Montréal, $67M from the private sector).
The work is to be completed in 2026 and the opening is planned for the same year; the agreement ends on December 31, 2026.
The final payment will only be made once the audited statement of the project's final costs is received.
Le Plateau-Mont-Royal borough is giving $15,000 (all applicable taxes included) to two local history societies for their 2026 activities.

La Société d'histoire du Plateau-Mont-Royal is receiving $10,000, in part for its 20th anniversary: a collection of history newsletters from 2021-2025, two lectures and the exhibition "Le Plateau littéraire" in the fall of 2026.
Mémoire du Mile End et de La Main is receiving $5,000 for its activities for the year.
The borough council is approving the agreements with the two organizations and is authorizing the mayor and the borough secretary (or their substitutes) to sign them.
The borough presents this support in the context of the 150th anniversary of mont Royal in 2026 and of the promotion of local heritage.
The amount is higher than the $10,000 granted to two organizations in 2025 and in 2024.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal will spend a maximum of $1,600, all taxes included, to take part in the 40th Grand Prix du Conseil des arts de Montréal.
The money will be used to buy a table of ten seats at the event's breakfast.
The event takes place on April 2, 2026, at the Palais des congrès de Montréal.
The ten seats will go to borough representatives and to partners from the local cultural community.
The borough has taken part for several years: $1,550 in 2025, $1,450 in 2024 and $1,350 in 2023.
The borough of LaSalle authorizes the City's lawyers to sue snow removal company B. Frégeau et Fils inc. and its insurer L'Alpha Compagnie d'Assurances.
The City is claiming $169,664.19, "subject to adjustment", plus interest: this is the difference between B. Frégeau's prices and those of the companies hired to replace it.
In 2023, B. Frégeau had been awarded a $700,255.24 contract to rent out five loader tractors with operators for snow removal in LaSalle until the winter of 2025-2026.
The company announced in September 2024 that it could no longer carry out snow removal in LaSalle, then in April 2025 that it was ceasing all of its operations.

The City issued two new calls for tenders and assigned the five sectors to Terrassement Deux-Étoiles, C.M.S. Entrepreneurs Généraux, 9213-4675 Québec, Excavation Pascal Beaulieu and Groupe Thermo-Lite.
The insurer, which did not respond to two formal demand letters, is jointly and severally liable up to $2,500 per lot, for a maximum of $12,500.
The final amount will be adjusted based on the number of snow removal hours actually worked during the winter of 2025-2026.
The City is entering into a by-mutual-agreement contract with La Presse inc. to buy advertising space for Espace pour la vie in 2026, for a total value of $574,875, taxes included.
Half of that, $287,437.50, is paid in cash; the other half, $287,437.50, is an exchange of visibility and tickets.
The exchange includes 170 museum tickets ($4,335), the La Presse logo on ads and posters for two events, and visibility on the museums' screens.
The ads will appear in La Presse+, on the website and on the mobile app, from February 1 to December 31, 2026.
The ads promote the programming of the Biodôme, the Biosphère, the Insectarium, the Jardin botanique and the Planétarium; the goal is 2.4 million visits in 2026.
The expense will be covered 70-80% by the central city and 20-30% by the urban agglomeration, since the Biosphère falls under the urban agglomeration.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders, an exception provided for in the Cities and Towns Act for media space.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is changing how it splits the funding for work at parc Vinet (sports play areas, green infrastructure and electrical work), without changing the project's total amount.
The contract of $2,501,734.17 (taxes included) remains awarded to Bau-Québec ltée, for a total authorized expenditure of $3,443,607.90 including contingencies and incidental costs.
The federal Ressources naturelles Canada grant, which reimburses 50% of tree-planting expenses (about $305,749 net), will now be shared between two central departments rather than just one.
The split is 63% for the Programme des installations sportives extérieures ($193,000) and 37% for the participatory budget ($113,000), plus contingencies and incidental costs.
Stormwater management, estimated at $72,000, remains 100% funded by the PEV program, at no net cost to the City.
Two separate accounting projects are being created to track each department's eligible expenses separately.
The borough of Verdun is authorizing the construction of a new building at 169-177, rue Galt, after the demolition of the existing building, which was found to be run-down and unsafe.
The project calls for a three-storey semi-detached building with a rooftop structure and terraces, containing 6 housing units.
The front of the building will be red brick (Colony Blend model) with two vertical projections, semi-recessed balconies and a carriageway entrance on the ground floor on the right.
The lot will include a vehicle area in permeable paving stone, lawn seeded with white clover, native perennial plants and 5 trees, plus planters on the roof.
Bicycle racks are planned under the ground-floor balcony.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with conditions: correct the plans, align the parapet with that of the neighbour on the left, improve the greening of the yards, and review the terraces and planters.
The file is going to the borough council rather than being handled as a delegated decision because of the value of the work.
The Verdun borough council approves the plans (PIIA) for the construction of a building at 3967-4003, rue de Verdun.
The project calls for a 4-storey building with 60 units, 13 of which have 3 bedrooms, along with underground parking with 15 spaces (2 accessible) and 86 bicycle spaces.
The façades combine four types of brick on the first three storeys and metal cladding on the fourth, which is set back and has terraces.
The front and rear yards are to include 18 medium-sized trees, vegetated swales, urban agriculture in planter boxes, a play area, a bicycle repair station and areas for waste bins.

The urban planning advisory committee voted 5 in favour and 1 against, with 6 conditions: integrate the vents, provide details on the flashing and the lighting, remove some sheet metal panels, correct the notes on the drawings and replace 6 trees with large trees (15 m and over), 3 of them at the front.
The information on the modified trees will be provided before the permit is issued.
One committee member raised a risk of soil contamination; the City states that the land is not on its list of contaminated sites and that a rehabilitation program would be required if needed.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is approving the expansion of a house at 10186, avenue de Cobourg.
The work involves adding a storey with a 7.49 m² basement toward the backyard and a new patio door on the side wall.
The existing dormers and the addition will be covered with Norwood metal panels (white oak) from Mac métal.
No financial guarantee is required, since the value of the work is less than $150,000.
The work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; the outdoor landscaping must be finished before the permit expires.
According to the document, no tree will be planted and the green space ratio stays essentially the same.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended the application favourably on December 2, 2025.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is approving a minor exemption for the building at 10186, avenue de Cobourg, built in 1930.
The exemption concerns the cladding material for a planned one-storey addition (7.49 m) and for two existing dormers, currently covered with shingles and vinyl.
The owner will be allowed to use "blanc chêne" Norwood steel siding from Mac metal architectural instead of the material required by the zoning by-law.
Urban planning staff are in favour because it is technically impossible to install masonry on the existing dormers, and in order to match the addition with them.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted mostly in favour of the project; the work must follow the architectural plan filed on January 19, 2026.
A public notice was posted online on February 3, 2026, and the decision is being made at the borough council meeting of March 9, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is amending its zoning by-law in the area around boulevard Langelier and rue Jean-Talon Est, where the STM plans a blue line station to open in 2031.
The zone boundaries are being redrawn: zone C-2120 is repealed, two new zones are created (Cm-2120 and Cm-2515), and four existing zones are enlarged or reduced.
The change prepares the way for a future by-law on comprehensive development plans (PAE), which the borough wants to adopt in the coming months, in order to avoid piecemeal development.
In zone Cm-1730, daycares, multi-family and collective housing, and more than one building per lot will be allowed, but the maximum number of storeys goes to 6 and the maximum density to 3.00.
In zones Cm-2500, Cm-2510 and Cm-2520, businesses related to motor vehicles and large-footprint businesses become prohibited; amusement arcades are excluded in two of these zones.
The minimum construction density is raised (2.00 or 2.20 depending on the zone) in order to meet the minimum number of housing units per hectare set out in the City's plans.
The master development and planning plan for the Langelier area had been adopted by city council on September 22, 2025, following public consultations in 2023 and 2025.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is paying $50,000 to PME MTL Centre-Est to manage the Fonds d'initiatives locales in 2026.
The money is for managing the fund, promoting the call for projects and supporting the project leaders who are selected.
The fund targets the Assomption Sud – Longue-Pointe area and finances projects that improve how industries and homes coexist.
The 2026 call for projects has two streams: social cohesion (recreational, cultural, artistic or environmental projects) and transformation of the area (urban development and greening).
Timeline: the call is launched in February 2026, selection in March, projects start in the spring, and reporting in December 2026.
This is the fund's fourth year; the three previous contributions were $100,000 each.
The amount is included in the 2026 budget of the borough's Direction de l'aménagement urbain et des services aux entreprises.

The executive committee is responding to the 13 recommendations from the Commission sur les finances et l'administration that came out of the 2026 pre-budget consultation; city council is taking note of it.
The City says it carried out a review of its activities and programs, including cutting about 200 positions, for annual savings of about $79M in total.
It expects to meet its debt ratio of 100% of revenues as early as the 2026 budget, rather than in 2027, and to stabilize its capital works program at around $2B per year.
Central city transfers to the boroughs will be indexed by 3% instead of 1.9%, which is $8.3M more.
The executive committee is being asked to mandate the Direction générale to implement the recommendations according to the directions set out in its response.
The City is giving $285,000 to eight organizations for projects marking the 50th anniversary of the 1976 Olympic Games, to be carried out in 2026.

Seven organizations are receiving $40,000 each: Courons Montréal (Marathon de Montréal), Scouts du Montréal Métropolitain, Musée McCord Stewart, Club aquatique CAMO Montréal, Vélo Québec Association, Conseil du sport de Montréal and — in the amount of $39,000 — Club Gymnix.
Loisirs récréatifs et communautaires de Rosemont is receiving $6,000 for the project "Héritage 1976 Rosemont en action, jeunesse en mouvement".
The projects range from sports competitions to murals, scout olympiads and a museum exhibition.
Each organization receives 80% of the amount when it signs its agreement and 20% after submitting its accountability report.
There will be no new call for projects in 2026: this is a renewal of the projects chosen in 2025, plus the addition of Club Gymnix.
The expense is paid entirely by the Montréal agglomeration and uses up the budget set aside for it.
The City is giving $276,636 to 20 organizations to hold 28 sporting events in Montréal in 2026.
The money is divided into three streams: $115,000 for 7 international events, $42,000 for 7 national events and $119,636 for 14 metropolitan events.
The largest amounts go to the Coupe du Monde de canoë (Canoe Kayak Canada, $25,000), to International Gymnix ($25,000) and to the ISU short track world championships ($22,500).

Among the events supported: BougeBouge marathons and races (Verdun, RDP-PAT, Mont-Royal, Villeray–Saint-Michel, Beaconsfield, Cap-Saint-Jacques), the Demi Marathon de Lachine, the Demi-marathon au parc Jean-Drapeau and the Course St-Laurent.
Of the 31 applications received, 28 were selected; 3 were turned down (insufficient sanctioning level or not meeting the criteria).
The cost is paid entirely by the agglomeration; the program's total budget for 2026 is $450,000 and a final application deadline is set for April 15, 2026.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is authorizing the construction of housing units partly located below ground level, at 3451-3515, rue Masson.
The site currently holds two vacant buildings: a former bingo hall and a garage.
The project calls for a mixed-use building with 53 housing units and 4 commercial spaces, with underground parking that includes a water retention basin.
The ground-floor units would extend into the garden level, partly below the natural ground level.
The urban planning department notes that the project meets the criteria, that the site is not next to a low point on public property, and that several measures protect against flooding.
The urban planning advisory committee came out in favour of the project on January 14, 2026; a public notice was posted on February 20, 2026.
The executive committee accepts a donation of books from Céline Arseneault for the library of the Jardin botanique de Montréal.
The City will issue the donor an official tax receipt for $2,200.
The donation includes 57 titles in French and English on botany, gardening and gardens, published from the 1970s to today.
The books will be added to the collection so they can be consulted and borrowed by Jardin botanique staff and its broader clientele.
The market value was assessed on June 12, 2025 by François Côté, bookseller and archivist.
The same donor had already made a book donation accepted in March 2025, valued at $910.68.
The City accepts the donation of archives from Patricia Kéroack to the library of the Jardin botanique de Montréal and approves the donation agreement.
The donation consists of a single item: an architectural drawing of the Jardin botanique's administrative building (Édifice Marie-Victorin), signed by architect Lucien F. Kéroack (1886-1951).
The document was handed over on July 10, 2025 and will be added to the archive collection of the Jardin botanique library.
The archive will be preserved and made accessible to the public and to the research community.
No money is being paid: the value of the donation has not been assessed and no donation receipt will be issued.
The decision falls to the executive committee; no communications activities are planned.
The executive committee accepts a donation of two antique books offered by Michel Cloutier to the library of the Jardin botanique de Montréal.
The donation includes an original 1935 edition of « Flore laurentienne » signed by frère Marie-Victorin and the « Supplément à la Flore laurentienne » by Ernest Rouleau (1947).
An outside appraiser, bookseller and archivist François Côté, sets the fair market value of the donation at $750.
The City authorizes the issuing of an official tax receipt of $750 to the donor.
The books were handed over on August 21, 2025 and will be preserved and made available to the public and to researchers.
No communications activities are planned for this file.
The City is accepting the donation of an antique book given by Yves Lefebvre to the library of the Jardin botanique de Montréal.
It is the original edition of "Flore laurentienne" by frère Marie-Victorin (1935), signed by the author and dated June 5, 1937.
An outside bookseller and archivist, François Côté, values the book at $500.
The City will issue the donor an official receipt for $500 for income tax purposes.
The donation was received on September 4, 2025; the book will be preserved and made available to the public and to researchers.
No communications activities are planned for this file.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is renting machinery with operators for the spring 2026 cleaning of streets, lanes, bike paths and sidewalks, for a total expenditure of $285,623.79 including taxes.

Four companies are awarded contracts following a public call for tenders (5 bidders): Les Équipements Benco (4 sidewalk washers, $85,033.80), Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier (2 mechanical sweepers, 1 lane sweeper, 1 mini sidewalk washer, 1 tank truck, $118,801.37), Balaye-Pro (3 vacuum sweepers, $59,603.04) and Groupe Villeneuve (1 tank truck, $22,185.58).
The 4 sidewalk washers will clean the sidewalks of 4 sectors (CDN-111, 112, 113, 114) at $385/km; the other equipment will cover the entire borough, at hourly rates of $120 to $138.
The mini sidewalk washer will continue occasional bike path cleaning operations until September 2026.
The work is planned for April and May 2026; the goal is to remove the abrasives spread during the winter.
The expenditure will be paid out of the public works operating budget; the net cost after tax rebates is $260,812.58.
The borough states that it does not have the equipment or the staff needed to cover its entire territory.
The City is giving $9,750 to the organization MU to maintain a mural, under the Programme d'entretien des murales – Volet 2, 2026 edition.
The mural in question, "Rencontre au sommet," is located near métro Jarry, at 500-504, rue Jarry, and was created in 2014 (initial cost of $40,053 for three murals).
Only one application was received and accepted during the call for projects, which ended on May 19.
The maintenance work must be done from July to November 2026, and the organization must submit its accountability report no later than November 30, 2026.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city, out of the budget of the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne.
The program is for Montréal non-profit organizations that have created murals funded by the Programme d'art mural – Volet 2, or that have been given the mandate to maintain them.

The City is appointing Gabrielle Rousseau-Bélanger, councillor for the district of Pointe-aux-Trembles (Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles), as an observer member of the conseil du système alimentaire montréalais (CSAM).
Her term lasts three years, until February 11, 2029.

The CSAM, created in 2018, brings together 26 members (community, government, business, university, agri-food, citizen, etc.) and acts as the decision-making body of the Système alimentaire montréalais.
The City's representatives sit on it as observers; the role is to promote joint action on food and against food insecurity.
The appointment has no financial impact.
She replaces Virginie Journeau, who was appointed to the same position in August 2022.
City council is amending the by-law on subsidies for owners who have to redo their electrical service entrance because of the burial of wires.
The address 261, rue du Séminaire, in the Griffintown area, is being added to the list of eligible buildings, with a maximum subsidy of $8,000.
The deadline to submit a subsidy application is being moved from 2024 to 2027.
The project in question buries the electrical and telecommunications networks in Griffintown, notably on rue William between rue Guy and rue de la Montagne.
The City says it is aiming for "no cost" to owners affected by the burial work.
The $8,000 expense, taxes included, will be charged to the Programme d'élimination des poteaux.
After adoption, the Commission des services électriques will send a notice to the owners concerned before they have their service entrance modified.

The City is amending its subsidy by-law to increase the amounts offered to owners of businesses and industrial properties in the Griffintown area who have to bring their electrical service entrance up to standard.
The area covered is rue William between rue Guy and rue de la Montagne, where the Commission des services électriques is burying the electrical and telecommunications networks.
The increase amounts to $119,400, taxes included, in additional subsidies, funded by the agglomeration budget.
Three groups of addresses are added to the by-law's appendix: $28,200 (Ottawa/William/Saint-Thomas), $79,300 (William/Barré/de la Montagne) and $11,900 (1332-36 William).
The deadline to submit a subsidy application is moved from 2024 to 2027.
Stated objective: that the connection work be done at "no cost" to the owners concerned.
Notice of motion planned for March 2026, adoption in April 2026; payments should be made in 2026 and 2027, after the work and a notice to the owners.
The City is extending its contract with SNF Canada inc. by 12 months, from June 20, 2026 to June 19, 2027, for the supply of polymers to the Jean-R.-Marcotte treatment plant.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $2,966,475.89, taxes included, bringing the total contract to $8,880,010.31.
These chemicals are used to remove suspended matter and phosphorus from wastewater, and then to dry out the sludge before it is incinerated.
Prices stay the same as in the first year: the agreement provides for no indexation when the chemical products price index is below 2%.
The plant treats wastewater from the entire island of Montréal; the expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration (net cost of $2,708,787.88).
The City cites the need for a continuous supply in order to meet the treatment requirements of the ministère de l'Environnement.
The City is awarding a direct-award contract to Astral Affichage to buy advertising space in 2026, for a maximum of $172,462.50 including taxes.

These ads will promote the events, films and exhibitions of the five Espace pour la vie museums (Biodôme, Biosphère, Insectarium, Jardin botanique, Planétarium), which are aiming for 2.4 million visits in 2026.
The posters will appear in the STM metro and buses (lumiquais, panobus, Métrovision, Azur) as well as on Astral's outdoor and indoor billboards.
The contract is being awarded without a call for tenders because Astral is the only manager of this type of advertising in the STM metro and buses.
In exchange for a commitment of at least $125,000 to $150,000 before taxes, Astral is granting discounts of 5% to 60% and bonus advertising placements worth about $700,000.
The advertising placements will run from April 1 to December 31, 2026.
The expense is already included in the Espace pour la vie budget: 75% to 90% paid by the central city, 10% to 25% by the agglomeration (since the Biosphère falls under agglomeration jurisdiction).

The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough takes note of the 2025 report of its Division des services techniques et du soutien logistique aux installations (DSTSLI), which maintains arenas, synthetic turf fields, libraries and maisons de la culture for nine boroughs, the Service des grands parcs and the Bureau des relations internationales.
The division ends the year with a surplus of $150,547 on an initial budget of $4,323,400.

This surplus will not be redistributed to the client boroughs and departments: it will be paid into the division's reserve, as the administrative framework allows as long as the surplus stays under 10% of the budget (here 3.49%).
Revenues reached $310,183, while the target was $213,200, an overrun of 45.4%.
The DSTSLI carried out 6,006 interventions in 2025, a decrease of 1.88% compared with the 6,121 in 2024.
Out of 565 surveys sent to clients (a response rate of 34%), overall satisfaction stands at 95%.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is paying $367,248, taken from its surplus, to two organizations for housing-related projects, from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2029.

LogisAction is receiving $183,624 for "Ensemble pour des logements plus sains à NDG": one-on-one meetings, workshops on tenants' rights, service points in community organizations and door-to-door work in NDG's priority areas.
Projet Genèse is receiving $183,624 for "RénovAction": support for tenants affected by renovictions in Côte-des-Neiges, identifying buildings sold with renovation permits, and handing out pamphlets.
LogisAction plans to work with Centre Eva Marsden, Bienvenue à NDG, le Dépôt, the CIUSSS and the borough to reach seniors, immigrants and low-income tenants.
The organizations must submit a final report no later than July 31, 2027, July 31, 2028 and July 31, 2029, through the GSS platform.

The document notes that the neighbourhood round tables (tables de quartier) of CDN and NDG identified housing as a priority, and that some tenants have difficulty defending their rights (language barrier, lack of knowledge of the laws, discrimination, precarious situations, isolation).
The City agrees to pay a total of $1,000,000 to Rosemary Lafrenière to settle her disguised expropriation lawsuit out of court, without any admission of liability.
Since $367,556.84 has already been paid, a cheque for $632,443.16 remains to be issued, payable to the firm Miller Thomson in trust or to Ms. Lafrenière.
The dispute concerned the value of three vacant lots (lots 1 456 704, 1 456 705 and 1 456 725), with a total area of 5,537.1 m², already sold to the City in October 2025.
The two parties' appraisers were far apart: $1,296,000 according to Ms. Lafrenière, $326,300 according to the City. A trial was scheduled for May 14 and 15, 2026.
The possession date is set at October 28, 2022 solely to adjust the property taxes; Ms. Lafrenière will receive a refund of less than $200 and will get back the $13,678.31 held in trust.
The expense is borne by the urban agglomeration, through the loan by-law tied to the natural areas acquisition program.
The Le Sud-Ouest borough is lowering the minimum required density from 4.6 to 4.17 for the lot at 1810, rue des Bassins.
The project planned for this lot: a mixed-use building 25 metres tall, 286 housing units, one commercial space on the ground floor and 113 underground parking spaces.
Reasons given: the lot is triangular in shape, a 10-metre shoreline strip limits where the building can be placed, and the building already reaches the maximum permitted height.
The discrepancy was noticed during the review of the permit application, after the authorizations obtained in March and April 2025 (the project then had 238 housing units).
The developer plans to hand over a building as its contribution under the by-law on social, affordable and family housing.
Next steps: a public consultation meeting held by the borough (public notice at least 7 days beforehand), then final adoption of the resolution.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing up to 11 units at 232, rue Saint-Philippe, whereas the zoning allows 8.
The owner wants to demolish the garage in the back yard and replace it with a three-storey extension containing three new units.
The two existing buildings on the lot (a triplex and a five-unit building) would not be changed on the outside.
The land used to be two separate lots allowing 12 units; merging them brought the limit down to 8.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion at its meeting of April 7, 2026.
Next steps: posting, public notice, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is granting a minor exemption for the future building at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest, at the corner of rue Vinet.
The planning by-law requires buildings with 12 or more units to set up a temporary outdoor drop-off area for waste on their own property; the exemption removes this requirement.
Instead, occupants will place their waste on a neighbouring public lot (lot 1 573 770), in front of the building, without blocking the rue Vinet right-of-way.
The original plan was for the developer to buy this small piece of land from the City, but the transfer did not take place and the land became public property.
A drop-off area that complies with the Règlement sur les services de collecte will still be set up.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on April 7, 2026; a public notice will be issued before the borough council adopts the measure.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is approving a minor exemption for the building at 2385, rue Jolicoeur.
The permitted rear setback goes from 4 m (required by the planning by-law) to 3.2 m.
The exemption allows an extension in the rear yard, lined up with an existing part of the building that already sits 3.16 m from the rear property line, next to a lane.
According to the file, the difference is about 84 cm and would have no impact on the privacy, sunlight or use of neighbouring properties.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion at its meeting of May 5, 2026.
Next steps: public notice, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing up to 6 units in the building at 1652, rue De Roberval, between rue Saint-Rémi and rue Angers, across from autoroute 15.
The current zoning (H.1-3) limits the property to 3 units, so the authorization has to go through the conditional use procedure.
The detached two-storey building currently has a single unit, plus a garage at the back of the yard.
The project, which is entirely residential, calls for an expansion upward and on the side and rear yard sides.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain estimates the density at about 97 units per hectare, close to the target of 100 units/ha in the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 9, 2026.
Next steps: posting of a notice, public notice, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.

The City is approving its "Cadre d'intervention pour la vitalité du territoire," a planning document required by Québec under the 2025-2028 agreement of the Fonds régions et ruralité, which provides for payments of $30,058,161 to Montréal.

The framework sets four priorities: supporting local entrepreneurship, revitalizing economic spaces, supporting business innovation, and developing a greener and more inclusive economy (social economy, local purchasing, access to affordable food).

The issues targeted include the revitalization of downtown and of the East of Montréal, the modernization of industrial sectors, commercial vitality, the reduction of greenhouse gases, and support for vulnerable populations.
The actions planned for 2026 will mainly go through the PME MTL network (support and financing) and through three funds: social economy, young businesses, and the Fonds PME MTL.

Budget planning provides for $23,008,161 for services to businesses and entrepreneurs, $300,000 for the social economy, and $356,444 in compensation, over 2025-2028, with an available balance of $6,393,556.

The framework must be sent to the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation and published on the City's website no later than March 31, 2026; an activity report will be submitted each June 30 from 2026 to 2028.
The priorities and actions may be revised each year when the activity report is submitted.
The Ville-Marie borough is changing traffic in the Centre-Sud neighbourhood, near école primaire Saint-Anselme and parc Médéric-Martin.
Rue de Rouen becomes one-way eastbound between rue Bercy and rue Hogan; rue Bercy becomes one-way northbound between Ontario and de Rouen.
Stop signs are being added on rue de Rouen, at the east and west approaches to the intersection with rue Wurtele.
Left turns onto rue Montgomery from rue de Rouen become permitted (southbound from the east, northbound from the west).

The borough says through traffic has increased since the work on the pont Louis-Hippolyte-La Fontaine and that some measures put in place in the summer of 2025 are not being respected: the SPVM has issued 200 tickets at the intersection of Bercy and de Rouen since the fall.
Schedule: adoption on May 5, 2026, notice to local residents and posting for 30 days, signage change planned for mid-July 2026.
The signage work will be done by the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough and billed to Ville-Marie.
The Ville-Marie borough is lowering the speed limit to 20 km/h on rue Magnan, between rue Dufresne and rue Fullum, and making it a "shared street".
The measure will take effect once the street's redevelopment work is finished, expected in the fall of 2026.
Rue Magnan will be redeveloped in the summer of 2026 to rebuild the sewer and water mains, in the Centre-Sud area near the pont Jacques-Cartier.
The new design calls for a street at a single level: a 4 m shared corridor, a reserved pedestrian corridor of 1.8 m on the south side and a corridor of 1 to 1.5 m on the north side.
Planter boxes, curb extensions, trees and better lighting are planned; obstacles in the pedestrian space will be removed.
Parking spaces will be redistributed alternately from one side of the street to the other to create a deviation in drivers' path.
The borough will pay for changing the traffic signs, at the rates of the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough.
The borough of Ville-Marie is making rue Cathcart two-way between avenue Union and boulevard Robert-Bourassa, downtown.
The street is currently one-way eastbound, which forces valets at the Birks hotel to make a long detour via Union, René-Lévesque, Robert-Bourassa and Sainte-Catherine to reach the underground garage.
All parking on the north side will be removed: two paid spaces and four 15-minute spaces reserved for the hotel. Some of the hotel's spaces could be moved to the south side.
The City will add junction boxes at the intersections with Robert-Bourassa and Union to make turns easier for delivery vehicles, and will allow new right-turn movements.
Planned schedule: legal notice posted for 30 days in mid-June 2026, with the change of direction taking effect in mid-July 2026.
Local residents will receive a notice, and the signage work will be done by the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, which will bill Ville-Marie.
Vana Nazarian, an elected official in Saint-Laurent, is appointed to sit on the board of directors of PME-MTL Centre-Ouest, starting in February 2026.
PME-MTL Centre-Ouest serves Côte-Saint-Luc, Hampstead, Montréal-Ouest and Mont-Royal, as well as the boroughs of Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Saint-Laurent.
This organization supports and funds business projects for companies, including those in Saint-Laurent.
Its board of directors has 13 members: 4 elected officials and 9 people from the business community; Saint-Laurent has one elected official and three business people on it.
The borough council adopted the recommendation unanimously on February 3, 2026; the executive committee, the city council and then the urban agglomeration council still have to decide on it.
PME-MTL Centre-Ouest will announce the final makeup of its board after its next meeting.
Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie accepts Ville-Marie's offer to provide a public works team dedicated to cleanliness work related to homelessness.
The team has 8 people (1 foreman and 7 blue-collar workers) and 4 vehicles: 1 packer truck and 4 pickup trucks.
It works days, Tuesday to Friday, for 12 months starting in the spring of 2026.
The work locations will be chosen jointly by the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie teams and the Ville-Marie managers.
The budget comes from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and will be transferred to Ville-Marie, which manages the team; no amount is stated.
The team had already been deployed in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie in 2025; the agreement is being renewed for 2026.

The City is awarding a contract worth $1,935,440.42 (taxes included) to Oslo Construction inc. to replace the gas heating system at fire station 31, at 7041, rue Saint-Dominique, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
The work includes electric boilers and water heaters, a new heating and radiator network, a 347/600 V electrical connection and an electronic control system.
The amount breaks down into $1,612,867 for the contract, $241,930.06 in contingencies (15%) and $80,643.36 in incidental expenses (5%).
According to the document, the project will cut emissions by about 105 tonnes of CO2 eq. and is part of the Plan climat goal of making the real estate portfolio operationally zero-carbon by 2030.
An agreement with the gouvernement du Québec covers 52% of the expenses, provided they are incurred before March 31, 2026; otherwise, the City covers the rest.
The contract starts in March 2026, provisional acceptance is expected in March 2027 and the contract ends in March 2028; the work must mostly be finished before the 2026-2027 heating season.
Seven companies submitted bids, all found to be compliant; the winning bid is 43.4% below the professionals' estimate. The expense is covered by the urban agglomeration.

The City is awarding Plomberie Charbonneau inc. a contract of $168,208.43 (taxes included) to replace the gas heating system in the édifice Madison, at 2140, avenue Madison, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
With contingencies ($33,641.69) and incidental costs ($33,641.69), the total expense comes to $235,491.81, taxes included.
The work in the boiler room includes adding an electric boiler, a concrete base, variable frequency drives on the pumps, balancing valves, and modifying the controls.
The project is expected to reduce the building's emissions by about 48 tonnes CO2 eq.; it is part of the action aiming for a zero-carbon municipal building portfolio by 2030.
A grant from the gouvernement du Québec covers 100% of the expenses, on the condition that they are incurred before March 31, 2026; otherwise the City assumes them.
Six companies submitted bids, all compliant; the lowest bid is 44% below the professionals' estimate.
Work is scheduled to start in March 2026, with provisional acceptance in March 2027 and the end of the contract in March 2028.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is authorizing the closure of part of rue Jean-Talon Est, between rue de Candiac and boulevard Lacordaire, for the "Fête des voisins 2026".
The street will be closed to car traffic from 11:30 p.m. on June 5 to 11:30 p.m. on June 6, 2026.
The event, organized by the Société de développement commercial de la rue Jean-Talon, will take place on June 6 from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. and will be free.
On the program: entertainment, a petting farm, fairground games, a face painter, a small fruit and vegetable market, merchants' booths and shows.
Whether the event goes ahead depends on approval from the Service d'incendie de Montréal, because of access to the nearby Hôpital Santa-Cabrini.
An occupancy permit for public property will have to be issued to the organizer.
Similar closures had been authorized for the 2024 and 2025 editions.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is closing part of rue de Pontoise, between Jean-Talon Est and Le Maître, for three events organized by the SDC de la rue Jean-Talon in the summer of 2026.

The closures: from July 3 at 8 a.m. to July 4 at 10 p.m. (Week-end Vitalité 1), from July 10 at 8 a.m. to July 11 at 10 p.m. (Week-end Vitalité 2), and from September 3 at noon to September 5 at 9 p.m. (Festival Fringale).
Rue Jean-Talon Est will also be closed in front of the La Perla building (5715, rue Jean-Talon Est) on August 28, 2026, from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m., for an outdoor movie night.
On the program: family activities, shows, fairground-style games and promotion of local businesses; the events are free.
The SDC is organizing these activities in the context of major construction work on rue Jean-Talon Est, to bring life to the commercial area.
The closures depend on approval from the Service de sécurité incendie (because of access to Hôpital Santa Cabrini) and from the blue line project team.
A permit to occupy public property will have to be issued by the borough.
The City is giving $100,000 to Société Makivik in 2026 to design a multi-service centre for vulnerable Inuit in Montréal.
The money will be used to develop a service model: needs analysis, operational framework, identification of inspiring practices and performance indicators.
The project targets about 2,000 Inuit living in or passing through Montréal, in a context of some 14,000 trips a year from Nunavik.

The City says it wants to fill a gap identified by the Ombudsman de Montréal and the intergovernmental committee on Inuit homelessness: housing instability, violence, exploitation and fragmented services.
The project runs from June 16 to December 31, 2026, with a final report on January 31, 2027.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, out of the budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale.
The organization must follow a visibility protocol set out in the agreement.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is taking $500,000 from its surpluses to maintain its infrastructure.
$300,000 goes to the upkeep of public trees: pruning, cutting down trees when needed and emergency work, carried out by accredited professionals.
The borough has more than 27,215 public trees, including 19,942 street trees; the cutting down of ash trees and unpredictable weather have created backlogs in pruning requests.
$200,000 is used to create an extra road repair crew working all summer long, to repair sections of road surface of 2 to 10 m² at a time.
The goal: redo about 4,000 m² of damaged road surface, in the spots where potholes keep coming back, anywhere in the borough based on the condition observed.
The amount covers the crews' wages, materials, equipment and the hauling of excavated soil, which must be tracked in the Traces Québec system.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest accepts Ville-Marie's offer: a public works team will come and work in its territory, on request, on cleanliness work related to homelessness.
The agreement lasts 12 months and begins in mid-April 2026; the schedule is daytime, Tuesday to Friday.
The team has 8 people (1 foreman and 7 blue-collar workers) and 4 vehicles: 1 packer truck and 4 pickup trucks, including one pickup truck added in 2026 for minor interventions.
The budget set for 2026 is $931,328 and comes from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale.

Ville-Marie's offer also covers Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, with occasional interventions possible elsewhere.
The intervention locations will be chosen jointly by the Le Sud-Ouest teams and the Ville-Marie managers, who manage the team.
Activities can only begin once all the boroughs covered have adopted their acceptance.
The borough of Ville-Marie is submitting its annual report on the upkeep of parc du Mont-Royal for 2025, a task the City assigned to it.
The budget set for this upkeep was $2,558,200, including $2,184,700 for salaries and payroll costs.
Actual spending reached $2,683,124, which is $124,924 more than planned (4.88%).
The overrun comes from pay ($239,335 more, including $168,671 in salaries and $70,664 in overtime).
This overrun was partly offset by $114,411 in savings on other expenses (professional services, rentals, goods, etc.).
The report is to be submitted to the executive committee of June 25, 2026.
Montréal confirms that by-law 1440-2 of Ville de Mont-Royal complies with the agglomeration's land use planning and development plan (Schéma d'aménagement de l'agglomération).
This by-law changes the land use designation of 1000, chemin Lucerne (lot 1 679 307): from "Institutional" to "High-density housing".
The new designation allows 80 to 150 dwellings per hectare; the Schéma requires a minimum of 80 dwellings per hectare in this area.
The land is in a "mainly residential" zone under the Schéma, which allows housing.
Mont-Royal adopted the by-law on November 25, 2025, following a public consultation on January 7, 2025.
Next steps: Montréal's city clerk issues a certificate of compliance and sends it to Mont-Royal.

Montréal's executive committee finds that Dollard-des-Ormeaux's new subdivision by-law (R-2025-204) complies with the agglomeration's land use planning and development plan (Schéma d'aménagement de l'agglomération).
This by-law, adopted on September 30, 2025 by Dollard-des-Ormeaux, replaces the former by-law 640 on subdivision plans and the transfer of land for parks.
It sets the rules on lot area and dimensions, traffic lanes, subdivision and construction permits, and contributions for parks, playgrounds and natural spaces.
It prohibits cadastral operations and the subdividing of land located in wetlands of interest and their protection area, except for exceptions provided for in the zoning by-law.
Fines range from $500 (first offence, individual) to $2,000 (repeat offence, other cases).
Next steps: the clerk issues a certificate of compliance and sends it to Dollard-des-Ormeaux.

The executive committee confirms that three Côte Saint-Luc by-laws (zoning, subdivision operations, construction), adopted on December 8, 2025, comply with the land use planning framework of the Montréal urban agglomeration.
These by-laws protect Côte Saint-Luc's wetlands of interest: new maps identify these wetlands and their protection area.
They prohibit, with some exceptions, construction, uses, excavation or backfilling work, and the removal of topsoil or native plants in a wetland of interest and its protection area.
They also prohibit planting invasive species less than 100 metres from a local park that includes natural areas or wetlands of interest.
Subdividing lots is prohibited, with some exceptions, in a wetland of interest and its protection area.

An owner who wants to encroach on a wetland or its protection area must submit a characterization study; projects on undeveloped land go through a site planning and architectural integration programme (PIIA) review.
The construction by-law only partly meets the requirements of the planning framework: Côte Saint-Luc will have to adopt an adjustment by-law later on.
Montréal confirms that by-law 1000-1 of the Ville de Hampstead complies with the agglomeration's land use planning and development plan.
Hampstead adopted this by-law on March 9, 2026 to amend its urban plan and increase the building density allowed.
The by-law creates a new density sector IV: buildings of 1 to 3 storeys, with a floor area ratio of 0.25 to 1.4.
Hampstead points to growing housing needs to justify revising its density.
According to the analysis, these parameters make it possible to reach the threshold of 60 dwellings per gross hectare set out in the land use planning and development plan.
Montréal's city clerk will issue a certificate of compliance and send it to Hampstead.

Montréal's executive committee finds that Dollard-des-Ormeaux's new by-law on permits and certificates (R-2026-217), adopted on May 12, 2026, complies with the agglomeration's land use planning and development plan.
This Dollard-des-Ormeaux by-law replaces its former by-law on permits and certificates (91-808).
In Dollard-des-Ormeaux, an authorization certificate will be required for any work in a wetland or body of water, or in its protection area.
Cutting down a tree 10 cm in diameter or more (measured 1.3 m from the ground) will require a certificate; in practice, the City prohibits cutting down a tree 15 cm or more measured at the stump.
Creating a public right-of-way in the Bois-de-Liesse archaeological area will have to be accompanied by a study of the archaeological potential.
A sensitive use near a railway will have to provide an assessment of how viable the proposed layout is.

New mixed-use buildings or buildings with more than 12 units will have to submit additional plans and studies (residual materials, snow, sunlight, acoustics, traffic, soil, environment, photometry, construction site management).
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing in advance the payment of $41,196,000 in expenses for the year 2026.
These are what are known as non-discretionary expenses: salaries, utility bills, contracts, and vehicle registrations.
The goal is to pay these bills when they come due, without delay or penalties, before the file is submitted to the council.
The amounts are charged to various 2026 budget lines, according to the lists attached to the decision summary.
By comparison, the borough had authorized $39,991,700 for 2025 and $38,753,000 for 2024.
The borough of Montréal-Nord approves a $400 expense for advertising space with Ringuette 96 Mtl-Nord Inc.
The ad appears as part of the 28th edition of the ringette tournament, held from February 2 to 8, 2026.
The amount is taken from the elected officials' advertising and hospitality expenses budget for 2026.
According to the document, the tournament welcomes about 800 players, from the Moustique to Open categories.
The borough had paid the same amount of $400 for the 27th edition, in February 2025.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is approving a $500 expense to buy advertising from La Fondation de la Pointe-de-l'Île.
The advertising is tied to the gourmet dinner for school perseverance, scheduled for February 12, 2026.
The money comes from the elected officials' advertising and hospitality expense budget.
La Fondation received the same amount in 2025 for the February 20, 2025 edition.
La Fondation is a non-profit organization registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $250 to Regroupement Jeunesse en Action, taken from the elected officials' discretionary budget.

The money supports the 18th edition of the recognition gala "Hommage à nos Prédécesseurs et Prix de la Relève", on March 15, 2026 at 5 p.m., at the salle Mirella et Lino Saputo (8370, boul. Lacordaire).
The organization was asking for $250 per elected official, for a total of $1,250; that overall amount would allow the up-and-coming talent contest prize to bear the borough's name.
The funds will go toward recognition prizes given to young people, mentoring young artists and holding the event.
In return, the partner elected officials get visibility: a photo on the posters, a mention in the magazine Souche, and thanks on stage and on social media.
Last year, the borough granted the same amount of $250 for the 17th edition of the gala.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is awarding a contract worth $68,985, taxes included, to the firm Point Cardinal inc.
The firm will support the borough and write its new strategic plan.
This plan replaces "Oser ensemble Montréal-Nord", which expired in December 2025.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating surplus.
The process is to draw up a portrait of the territory, identify its major issues and set development priorities.
The borough states that the consultation will have to reach the cultural and linguistic diversity of its population.
The contract is approved by the borough council.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving out $2,500 in school perseverance scholarships, or $500 per school.
The five schools involved: the high schools Calixa-Lavallée, Henri-Bourassa and Lester B. Pearson, the École hôtelière de Montréal Calixa-Lavallée and the École Amos.
The scholarships will be handed out to graduating students at the graduation ceremonies and the 2026 Galas d'excellence.
The money comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for 2026.
An identical contribution of $2,500 was granted last year for the 2025 galas.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $300 to the organization Les productions Kulturmania.
The money supports the musical Fantasia, presented on February 28, 2026.
The amount comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget (hosting and representation budget) for 2026.
The borough council is approving the contribution after the event has taken place.
Kulturmania is a non-profit organization with its head office in Montréal-Nord.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to the Société d'histoire et de généalogie de Montréal-Nord.
The money is specifically for buying a computer to support the organization's activities.
The amount comes from the discretionary budget of the borough's elected officials and is charged to the operating budget.
The decision falls to the borough council; no related earlier decision is reported.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to the organization Fonds 1804 for school perseverance.
The money will fund two school scholarships of $250 each, awarded at the 11th edition of the Gala pour la persévérance scolaire.
The money comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for 2026.
The organization must provide proof of how the money was used and propose a replacement activity if the gala does not take place.
In 2024, the same organization received $500 for two scholarships of $250; in 2023, $1,000 for two scholarships of $500.
