The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to Carrefour Jeunesse Emploi Bourassa-Sauvé.
The money is used to fund a trip to Martinique as part of the Programme Départ à 9.
The money comes from the 2026 discretionary budget of the borough's elected officials.
The expense is charged to the operating budget and the funds have been certified.
The decision falls to the borough council, and there is no earlier decision linked to this file.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is tabling its 2025 report on the 2023-2025 Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Plan, which targeted the borough's staff.
This is the third report on the plan, after those of 2023 and 2024.
The report presents the actions carried out in 2025 and the results of a survey of employees on the plan's progress.

The plan follows the seven stages of an employee's "life cycle", from attraction through to departure; the borough had made onboarding and reintegration a priority in 2023, then added retention and departure in 2024.
An EDI monitoring committee, in place since May 2023, tracks how the plan is progressing and suggests adjustments.
The file does not involve any spending.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to the Ligue de Tennis de Montréal-Nord.
The money comes from the 2026 discretionary budget of the borough's elected officials.
The amount is taken from the borough's operating budget.
The document states that elected officials occasionally grant such contributions to sports, community, recreational or cultural organizations.
The decision falls to the borough council.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $4,250 to the organization Les Fourchettes de l'Espoir for its Festival des boulettes 2026.
The Festival des boulettes is a friendly competition of meatball recipes from different culinary cultures, presented as an exchange and a sharing experience.
The money comes from the elected officials' 2026 discretionary budget and is charged to the operating budget.
Councillor Chantal Rossi declared an interest in the matter and abstained from voting.
The decision was made by the Montréal-Nord borough council.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to the Société d'histoire et de généalogie de Montréal-Nord for its 25th anniversary.
The money comes from the 2026 discretionary budget of the borough's elected officials.
The decision falls to the conseil d'arrondissement of Montréal-Nord.
The financial section of the decision summary mentions an amount of $250, while the rest of the document refers to $500.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $750 to the Agence de Développement Durable de Montréal-Est Centre Nord (ADMECN).
The money comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for 2026.
The amount is for environmental activities held in Montréal-Nord.
Planned activities: Earth Day and an intergenerational sugar shack event on April 11, an eco-responsible literary festival from April 23 to 26, and a literary circle on April 25 and 26.
On August 10: the 3rd edition of the Festival International de la mangue de Montréal et des fruits exotiques.
The organization had received $750 in 2025 and $500 in 2024, 2022 and 2021.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $5,000 to the Fondation des médecins canado-haïtiens for its "La foire santé 2026" event.
The money comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for 2026 and will be charged to the operating budget.
The fair offers screening for chronic diseases such as diabetes, glaucoma and high blood pressure.
It brings together booths on women's, men's, teens' and seniors' health, sickle cell anemia, dental health, eyes, sexual health, mental health and nutrition.
The event also aims to promote healthy lifestyle habits and to direct people to the appropriate clinics.
A contribution of the same amount had been granted to the same organization for the 2024 fair.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to école secondaire Calixa-Lavallée for its robotics club, Spartiates 3544.
The money helps pay for the team's participation in the FIRST Global Challenge, in Houston, from April 29 to May 2, 2026.
The club, founded at the school in 2011, represents Canada in this competition, which brings together 192 national teams.
The money comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for 2026.
The elected officials had already given $500 to the same club in 2025 for the competition held in Panama.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is paying $500 to Escadron 801 de Montréal-Nord (Cadets de l'aviation royale du Canada).
The money is used to buy advertising space in the squadron's year-end newspaper, handed out at the 2026 year-end ceremony.
The expense is taken from the elected officials' representation budget for the 2026 fiscal year.
In 2025, the borough had given $300 to the same squadron for a similar advertisement.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to the Troupe de danse Mapou Ginen.
The money is for the 12th edition of Konbit, a fundraiser in the form of a dance and singing marathon held on May 3, 2026.
The amount comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for the 2026 fiscal year.
The organization must use the money as set out in its request and provide proof of how it was used.
If the activity does not take place, the organization must notify the City and propose a replacement activity.
Last year, the same troupe received $300 for the 11th edition of the event.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is buying a $500 advertisement from the Fondation Marie-Louise Clarac.
The money comes from the elected officials' representation and advertising budget for 2026.
The Fondation, created in 1989 by parents and the management of the École Marie-Clarac, raises funds for the development of young people (educational, cultural, sports).
The borough gave the same amount to this foundation in 2024 and in 2025.
The decision rests with the borough council.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is buying a $500 advertisement from the Fondation de l'hôpital Fleury, also known by its former name, Fondation d'Ahuntsic et Montréal-Nord.
The expense is taken from the elected officials' hospitality and advertising budget for the 2026 fiscal year.
The borough's elected officials occasionally buy advertising space at sports, community, recreational or cultural activities held in the area.
The Fondation, created in 2005 through the merger of three foundations, says it has given more than $2 million to the Centre de santé et de services sociaux d'Ahuntsic et Montréal-Nord.
The decision falls to the borough council.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to the organization Vision Charitable (VICHA).
The money supports the show "Racontinuons", presented on April 17, 2026 at the Pavillon Henri-Bourassa.
The contribution is approved after the event and comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for 2026.
In 2025, the elected officials had granted $2,650 to six organizations out of this same budget.
The Montréal-Nord borough is giving $350 to Festival Italiano inc. to promote the activities of the festival's 31st edition.
The festival will take place from August 14 to 16, 2026.
The money comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for 2026, charged to the operating budget.
The same organization had received $350 in 2025 and $250 in 2024 and in 2023.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $500 to the Association des Bénévoles du CHSLD Vigi Marie-Claret inc.
The money goes to the Soutien à l'action bénévole program, which offers activities adapted to elderly residents and people with reduced mobility.
The amount comes from the elected officials' discretionary budget for 2026.
The same amount of $500 was granted to this organization for the year 2025.
The association is a non-profit organization registered with the Registraire des entreprises.
The Ville-Marie borough is approving a minor exemption for the "IG – Gestion de patrimoine" sign at 1360, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, in Tower II of the Cité du commerce électronique.
The sign may be installed on the horizontal metal band above the main entrance, at a height of 5.9 m, which the planning by-law does not normally allow.
It measures 0.62 m by 2.00 m (about 1.24 m²), made of white acrylic and dark blue vinyl in a grey aluminum box backlit with LEDs.

According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, the by-law would cause serious harm to the applicant, since the only compliant location (the curtain wall) does not correspond to the entrance of the business.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on December 11, 2025; a public notice was published on January 24, 2026.
The approved plans are those of Pattison ID, stamped by the borough on January 20, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing housing units on the ground floor of a new building to be built at 1821, rue Atateken, between rue Ontario and rue Robin, in the Village.
In this area, the planning by-law normally prohibits residential use on the ground floor; the authorization goes through the conditional uses procedure.
The new building will have four storeys plus a mezzanine and a basement, and will contain 25 housing units: 5 studios, 15 one-bedroom units, 4 two-bedroom units and 1 three-bedroom unit.

The current three-storey building has 12 housing units that have been vacant since 2021 and was declared run-down and beyond repair by an expert assessment dated April 18, 2025; a demolition application and a building permit application are under review.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain notes that 3 of the 20 businesses on this section of the street are vacant and that the area is predominantly residential.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on December 11, 2025, suggesting a more durable finish in the entrance alcoves and an access ramp at the rear for universal accessibility.
A notice was posted on the site on January 23, 2026 and published in the newspaper on January 24, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing housing units to be built on the ground floor of 1231, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est (at the corner of Beaudry), which is normally prohibited in this area.
The 4-storey building, built in 1923 and vacant for more than 6 years, will be fully renovated to house about twenty studio units.
The social, affordable and permanent housing units will be reserved for women who have experienced homelessness, with rents adjusted to income, community spaces and on-site psychosocial support.
The SHDM owns the building and Mission Old Brewery will manage it; the project complements what is offered at the neighbouring Pavillon Patricia Mackenzie, at 1301.
The exterior stays the same, except for masonry repairs, the replacement of all the windows and the addition of a rooftop terrace.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on January 22, 2026, on the condition that all the doors and windows of the ground floor and the half-basement be kept.
An application for a construction permit will follow the approval of this use.

The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the creation of a 225 m² storage space on the 2nd floor of 1500, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, for the Maxi grocery store that has occupied the ground floor since August 2025.

The authorization goes through a specific project, because the planning by-law prohibits the "grocery store" use above the ground floor and limits this type of business to 1,000 m² (the addition brings the total to about 1,216 m²).
Work must begin within 36 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The Le QinzeCent building has a 36-storey residential tower and a 3-storey podium; the floor in question is unoccupied and no housing is planned there.
According to the document, the storage space will reduce how often heavy trucks make deliveries; no changes to the outside of the building.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion with no conditions on February 12, 2026; the exemptions may be subject to approval by referendum.
Steps: 1st draft adopted on March 10, 2026, public consultation on March 25, 2nd draft on April 14, final adoption expected on May 5, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing Radio-Canada to hold events on Place Radio-Canada, the private forecourt at 1000, avenue Papineau (corner of René-Lévesque Est and Alexandre-DeSève).
The authorization covers 24 months, from June 2026 to June 2028, for community, sociocultural and educational activities.
Planned for 2026: six outdoor Québec film nights on Friday evenings in July and August, projected onto the wall of Studio A facing René-Lévesque Est.
Concerts could be added occasionally, in particular in the summer, at the launch of the fall programming in September, and at Nuit blanche in March.
The programming is free and about 200 people are expected at a time; the building's washrooms will be open to the public and two waste and recycling stations will be added.
Conditions imposed: lighting directed toward the ground, installations taken down after each event, and a noise exemption order request to be filed for the summers of 2026 and 2027.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on April 16, 2026; the nearest homes are more than 100 m away, on the other side of René-Lévesque Est.
The borough of Ville-Marie is approving a minor exemption at 1231, boulevard de Maisonneuve Est, at the corner of rue Beaudry.
The exemption allows the installation of an emergency exit door whose panels extend 450 mm over the sidewalk on rue Beaudry, which is about 1800 mm wide.
Conditions imposed: no access system from the outside, and internal devices limiting use of the door to emergency evacuations only.
The project must be carried out in accordance with the GMAD plans stamped by the borough on June 17, 2026.
The 4-storey building, built in 1923 and vacant for more than 6 years, will be renovated to create about twenty studio apartments.
These are affordable social housing units intended exclusively for women who have experienced homelessness, with the SHDM as owner and Mission Old Brewery as manager.

According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, a beam under the ground-floor slab makes it impossible to set the door back; the comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 11, 2026.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is asking city council for permission to take charge itself of minor sidewalk repair work on arterial streets in its territory.
The Service des infrastructures et du réseau routier of the central city is paying for all of the work: a budget of $395,000, net of rebate, for 2026.
The work includes rebuilding concrete sidewalks and curbs, vehicle entrances and universal access ramps with tactile warning plates, as well as catch basin repairs.
The sidewalks will be rebuilt exactly as they were: no geometric redesign of the streets is planned.
The worksite will cause a partial closure of the parking lane, with access maintained for local residents.
Approximate schedule: work starting in May 2026, finishing in September 2026.
The borough will do the design and the tender documents in-house, at no additional cost to itself.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is proposing to city council that it take charge itself of the design and completion of work to build tree pits on streets of the City's arterial network located within its territory.
The work provides for the construction of new single and double tree pits, bringing existing pits up to standard, and improving the living conditions of trees already in place.
The borough cites the fight against heat islands, the greening of the streets concerned, and better absorption of rainwater to relieve the sewer system.
The work would be paid for out of the borough's budget; no amount is given in the document.
Approximate schedule: work starting in May 2026 and ending in September 2026, with a public call for tenders (no. 59-26-ET-07).
The precise location of the work will be determined by the Division des études techniques et de la mobilité together with the Division de la voirie-parcs.
Since the streets concerned are part of the City's arterial network, city council must accept the borough's offer.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is awarding a $747,229.58 contract (taxes included) to Groupe ABF inc., the lowest of 6 bidders, to repair sidewalks, curbs and public utilities.
The total authorized spending comes to $909,334.54: the contract, plus $74,722.96 in contingencies and $87,382.00 in incidental costs.

The work covers 39 sidewalk locations and 12 catch basins on local streets, as well as two arterial stretches: chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine (from Côte-des-Neiges to Darlington) and chemin de la Côte-Saint-Antoine (from Décarie to Botrel).
Planned work includes: rebuilding sections of sidewalk, repairing watercourses and catch basins, rebuilding driveway entrances and universal access ramps with tactile warning plates.
On the arterial streets, the sidewalk work comes before the central city's future roadway work planned for 2027 or later.
The arterial street share, up to $432,576.49 taxes included, is paid by the central city; the local streets are paid out of the borough's capital budget.
The call for tenders was issued on April 1, 2026 and the bids were opened on April 23, 2026.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is proposing to take charge of the design and carrying out of roadway repair work on streets of the City's arterial network, within its territory.
Three sections are involved: Gatineau (from Côte-des-Neiges to Maréchal), chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges (from Gatineau to Decelles) and avenue Goyer (from Côte-des-Neiges to Decelles).
The work is intended to prepare the course for the UCI 2026 cycling championship, which will be held in Montréal in September 2026.
The worksite provides for milling, repair of the roadbed as needed, laying of a new asphalt surface and adjustment of public utilities.

The work on the sections tied to the UCI is estimated at $570K and paid for by the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier; the cost of the Goyer section will be borne by the borough and has yet to be estimated.
The approximate schedule calls for the work to start on July 20, 2026 and end on August 20, 2026.
The design and the tender documents (no. 59-26-ET-16-TRC-2026) will be done in-house, with no additional expense for the borough.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding Les Entreprises Ventec inc. the construction of enlarged tree pits, under a contract worth $233,025.58 including taxes.

The total authorized spending comes to $296,328.14, which is the contract plus $23,302.56 in contingencies, $10,000 in incidental costs and $30,000 in professional services (laboratory and environmental monitoring).
The work covers 12 pits: nine on rue Sherbrooke Ouest (between Grey and Décarie) and three on chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges... pits 10 to 12 are on Décarie, between Bourret and Van Horne.
The project includes new pits, the enlargement or redevelopment of existing pits, reinforced concrete slabs, repairs to the surrounding surfaces and traffic management.
The work is planned from August to September 2026; the list of pits may change depending on what is found during excavation.
Only one company submitted a bid; the offer is 13.64% below the City's estimate ($269,820.47).
Residents along the affected streets will receive a letter explaining the nature and length of the work.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding Construction Viatek inc. a contract worth $679,844.88 (taxes included) to resurface roadways, and is authorizing a total spending of $881,821.61, including contingencies, incidental costs, laboratory work and supervision.

The work affects chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges (from Decelles to Gatineau), Gatineau (from Côte-des-Neiges to Maréchal), Kensington (from Somerled to Godfrey), Goyer (from Côte-des-Neiges to Decelles) and Vézina (from Décarie to Westbury).
The work includes planing the asphalt, repairing the base if needed, laying bituminous pavement and rebuilding the speed bumps.
The document links part of the work to preparations for the UCI Road World Championships, scheduled to take place in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026.
Funding is shared: $424,834.84 for streets in the arterial road network, paid by the central city, and $456,986.76 for local streets, paid by the borough.
Six companies submitted bids; Viatek was the lowest compliant bidder, at 23.54% below the estimate of $889,101.68.
Worksite supervision will be done in-house for the local portion; the borough may choose a hybrid approach depending on available resources.

The City is extending the 10 exclusive towing contracts for the agglomeration territory by 12 months, and is adding an expense of $1,680,874.73 (taxes included), which brings the total value of the contracts to $6,723,498.98.

The contracts cover the moving of vehicles that break parking or traffic rules, vehicles involved in an offence or abandoned, vehicles that have been in an accident or have broken down, and City vehicles that have broken down.
Five companies share the 10 sectors: Remorquage Kar-Pro (2015), Remorquage Burstall-Conrad, Remorquage Centre-Ville, Remorquage Météor and Bélanger S.R.
The extensions take effect on July 1, 2026, except for lots 6 and 7 (Remorquage Météor), which start on April 1, 2026 because the budget for those contracts will run out in April.
Lot 9 (Remorquage Centre-Ville, sector of poste de quartier 38) is being renewed with no contingency budget, so as not to go over the $1,000,000 threshold set by the Autorité des marchés publics.
The SPVM manages these contracts under the Règlement sur le remorquage des véhicules; the expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration.
The Ville-Marie borough is awarding Demix Construction (Groupe CRH Canada) the contract to rebuild the sewer and drinking water pipes on rue Magnan, between rue Dufresne and rue Fullum.
The contract is worth $2,204,040.43, taxes included; with contingencies, incidental costs and supervision, the authorized spending comes to $3,085,656.60.

The work includes redesigning the street as a "rue jardin" (garden street): a roadway and sidewalk in concrete pavers, granite curbs, new lighting, a rebuilt electrical network and the replacement of lead service lines.
The borough says it wants to enlarge the space for pedestrians, move bulky street furniture, add greenery while maximizing the number of parking spaces.
Work is planned from June 2026 to September 2026, about three months.
The cost is shared: $1,666,984.38 paid by the Ville-Marie borough (54%) and $1,418,672.22 by the Direction de la gestion des actifs (46%).
Seven companies submitted bids and all were found to be compliant; Demix submitted the lowest price, 27.56% below the City's estimate.
The Ville-Marie borough is awarding Excavations Darche inc. the work on avenue de Seaforth, from chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges to the end of the street.
The contract is worth $824,580.00 including taxes; with contingencies, incidental costs and supervision, the authorized spending comes to $1,216,255.50.
The work includes rebuilding the drinking water main, replacing some lead service lines, repairing the roadway and the sidewalk, and upgrading the street lighting.
The work is to start in June 2026 and finish in September 2026.
Funding comes from the Direction de la gestion des actifs ($777,296.37, 64%) and the Ville-Marie borough ($438,959.13, 36%), entirely in 2026.
Six companies submitted bids for the public call for tenders launched on April 21, 2026; Excavations Darche inc. was the lowest compliant bidder, at 58.36% below the estimate.
The borough will assess the company's performance at the end of the contract, and the communications team will keep residents informed during the work.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is approving the final accountability report for the MobilisActions project, which will be sent to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
This project, "Vers une mobilité active à Montréal-Nord", is funded through an agreement signed with the ministère on February 1, 2024 for 2024 and 2025.
The financial assistance provides for $48,000 paid when the agreement is signed and $12,000 after the minister accepts the documents.
The report must be accompanied by supporting documents (invoices, slips, salaries of the staff assigned to the project).
Without this approval and the filing of the report, the borough will not receive the second payment of $12,000.
The City is approving an estimated expense of $2,145.91 to send three elected officials to the Assises annuelles of the Union des municipalités du Québec (UMQ), in Québec, from May 13 to 15, 2026.

The people concerned: Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada, executive committee vice-chair Aref Salem, and Andréanne Moreau, member of the executive committee responsible for culture, heritage, design and the French language.
The expense covers meal and accommodation costs: $946.68 for the mayor and $665.17 for Aref Salem, according to the attached forms.
The registration fees of $890 per person are already included in the partnership agreement with the UMQ, and the UMQ reimburses the first night's stay.
The amount is provided for in the budget of the Division du soutien aux personnes élues and is paid entirely by the central city.
The City justifies the expense by its participation in the UMQ's bodies, of which it has been a member since 2013, to defend municipal interests with the Government of Québec.
In 2025, a comparable expense of $2,204.12 had been approved for the Assises held in Québec.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is giving $150,000 to the Société de développement commercial Hochelaga-Maisonneuve for the year 2026.
The money is to be used only for the salaries and benefits of the SDC's staff, both temporary and permanent, and cannot be used to pay its members.
The money will be paid in two instalments of $75,000: the first within 30 days of the decision, the second within 30 days of the filing of the audited financial statements.
The SDC's 2026 budget provides for $395,000 in salaries and benefits and $527,800 in member dues; the by-law caps the grant at $150,000.
The SDC runs activities on the commercial streets of the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve neighbourhood: buying local, sustainable business practices, and cultural and commercial events.
Same amount as in 2025 and 2024 ($150,000), compared with $144,083 in 2023.
The borough council must approve the resolution on June 1, 2026.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is allowing street food trucks on public property from June 2 to October 31, 2026, with the sale and consumption of food and non-alcoholic drinks.
Three sites have been chosen: parc Carlos-D'Alcantara (up to 3 trucks, rue De Contrecœur), parc de la Promenade-Bellerive (1 truck, starting in July) and carré Notre-Dame-des-Victoires (2 trucks).
The trucks may set up every day, from 8 a.m. to 11 p.m.
The City is entrusting the management of the sites to the Association des restaurateurs de rue du Québec (ARRQ), which assigns the spots each day and promotes the activities.

The ARRQ must check that operators are in compliance (SAAQ, MAPAQ, CNESST, fire safety), require $3M in liability insurance for the benefit of the City, and confirm that each truck is linked to an active production kitchen in Montréal.
The sites were chosen outside the commercial areas of Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Tétreaultville, so as not to compete with restaurants, and in areas with few food options.
The file has no financial aspect.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough did not spend $9,653,000 of its capital works budget in 2025; this amount is carried forward to the 2026-2035 investment program.
With this carry-forward, the borough's capital works budget goes from $7,102,000 to $16,755,000.
The borough council allocates this amount among the various already-planned projects, so they can continue or be completed.
The carried-forward balance comes from projects that were not carried out, projects that were started but not finished, and projects completed at a lower cost than expected.
The carry-forward does not increase the level of borrowing charged to taxpayers.
The borough can use this additional budget as it wishes.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is removing the parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility in front of 510, 26e Avenue.
The request comes from the citizen concerned, the father of a young girl with permanent physical limitations, who says he no longer needs this space.
This space had been created in 2019 by an order that the new decision cancels.
Any other parking rule already in place at the location remains in effect.
The signage will be removed as soon as the borough council approves it.
The cost of the removal is covered by the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, which manages a centralized budget for this type of work.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is reserving a parking space for people with reduced mobility in front of 12660, avenue Léon-Ringuet.
The space will be available at all times; any other signage already in place remains in effect.
The request comes from a resident with permanent physical limitations; as the tenant of a building with no driveway entrance, she has no access to off-street parking.
The decision is based on a medical assessment and a home visit, and the applicant is eligible under the borough's procedure.
The document states that installing and maintaining the signage are centralized activities whose costs are covered by the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
The signs will be installed as soon as the borough council approves the decision.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is authorizing a parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility in front of 571, 81e Avenue.
The space will be available at all times; the signage already in place stays in effect.
The request came from a tenant with permanent physical limitations, whose building has no driveway entrance.
The decision follows the review of a medical assessment and a visit to the applicant's home.
The signs will be installed as soon as the borough council approves the request.
The document states that the costs of installing and maintaining the signage are paid by the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, which has a budget for this purpose.

The City is awarding the firms Bouthillette Parizeau inc. and Leclerc architectes inc. a professional services contract in engineering and architecture for the administrative building of the usine d'eau potable Atwater, in Le Sud-Ouest.
The total expense comes to $497,781.96, taxes included: $332,875.62 for the contract, $49,931.34 in contingencies and $114,975 in incidental costs.
The mandate covers the heating, ventilation, air conditioning and geothermal problems seen since 2019, which cause discomfort for the occupants, especially in the summer.
The firms must analyze the existing systems, propose optimization measures, prepare the plans and specifications, then supervise the work and follow up on performance.
The contract runs from March 2026 to March 2031, with an option to extend it by 12 months.
Four firms submitted bids; the winning bid is 19.11% below the City's latest estimate.
The bill is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, since this involves water supply and wastewater treatment.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is creating a 15-minute limited parking drop-off zone over about 20 metres on avenue Jeanne-d'Arc, near 4026, rue Ontario Est.
The zone will be used by parents of Garderie Ho Ma (about 34 children) to drop off and pick up children, from 7 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. and from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday.
Three metered parking spaces (MA691, MA692 and MA693) will have their paid periods changed, representing an estimated revenue loss of $5,740 per year.
The document states that nearby spaces will be able to absorb the displaced demand.
Installing and maintaining the signs costs about $60, paid by the borough.
A work order will be sent to the signage division of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie after approval; the daycare and the parking officers will be informed.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is changing the signage around école Saint-Nom-de-Jésus, at 4131, rue Adam.
A no-stopping ban will apply over about 36 metres, from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday to Friday, from August 20 to June 30, except for school buses.
Two parking zones limited to 15 minutes are being created, from 7 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. and from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. on weekdays, from August 20 to June 30 (about 30 metres in total).
The zones are located on avenue Desjardins, on the west side, and across from 4131, rue Adam, for picking up and dropping off students.
The request comes from the school's management; the document mentions that the installation of the SRB on boulevard Pie-IX caused the loss of parking spaces in the area.
Estimated cost of the signage: about $840, paid by the borough.
The work order will be sent as soon as the authorization is given; the school and the parking officers will be informed.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve will create a 15-minute parking zone in front of école Irénée-Lussier, at 4420, rue Hochelaga.
The zone will be about 12 metres long and will serve as a drop-off area for parents dropping off and picking up their children.
The 15-minute limit will apply from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, from August 20 to June 30.
The request comes from the school's management, which cites children's safety when they are moving about.
Signage costs are estimated at about $560 and are paid by the borough.
Once approved, a work order will be sent to the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie signage service; the information will be passed on to the school's management and to parking officers.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is creating a 15-minute parking zone on the west side of avenue Desjardins, south of rue Hochelaga, for picking up and dropping off students.
The measure affects the schools Saint-Jean-Baptiste-de-La-Salle and Chomedey-de-Maisonneuve, whose principals had requested it.

The school bus drop-off zone goes from a no-parking rule (7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., school days) to a no-stopping rule from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, from August 20 to June 30, except for school buses.
According to the file, some parents double-park on avenue Desjardins or block the private parking lot behind école Chomedey-de-Maisonneuve; police have intervened several times.
The written signs will cost about $640, paid by the borough.
The work order will be sent to the signage service as soon as it is authorized; the schools and the parking officers will be informed.
The City is reorganizing its administrative structure: the general manager must put the changes in place by April 20, 2026 at the latest.

Three assistant general manager departments are being abolished (Sécurité, urbanisme et conformité; Habitation et économie; Services de proximité) and a new one is being created: Développement et affaires institutionnelles.
The reorganization abolishes 7 senior management positions; the exact savings will be known once the changes are fully in place.
The City confirms its intention to reduce central department staff by 1,000 positions over four years, with savings of $16M forecast in the 2026 budget.
The SPVM, the Service de sécurité incendie and the Service des affaires juridiques will report directly to the general manager.

Several departments are merging or changing names: Espace pour la vie + large parks and sports, housing + real estate strategy, environment + ecological transition; a Bureau de lutte contre l'itinérance is being created.
The by-law on departments must be adopted by city council on March 23, 2026, after a notice of motion on February 16, 2026.
The Ville-Marie borough is receiving $4,800 from Service national des sauveteurs inc. (Société de sauvetage) for swimming lessons offered free of charge to school-age youth.
The money comes from the "Nager pour survivre" program, which teaches 8- to 14-year-olds how to survive an unexpected fall into deep water.
During the 2025-2026 school year, 192 young people were trained: 26 students in grades 5 and 6 at école Saint-Anselme and 166 students in secondary 1 and 2 at école Chomedey-De Maisonneuve.
The grant is capped at a maximum of $25 per participating student.
The amount covers pool rental, teaching materials and the wages of the aquatic staff who give the lessons.
Last year, the borough received $500 from the same organization for the same program.
The Ville-Marie borough is receiving $22,569 from the ministère de l'Éducation du Québec for phase 4 of the program offering free lifeguard and aquatic instructor training.
The money was used to provide free training sessions held between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026.
The free courses covered: bronze medallion, bronze cross, Standard First Aid/AED, national lifeguard pool option, swimming instructor, and two combined packages.
The borough says it is aiming for two results: making this training accessible to people who cannot afford to pay for it, and training a new generation to fill its aquatic staffing needs.
The grant is paid in a single payment at the end of the period, based on the amount actually used, confirmed on June 8, 2026.
The mayor of Ville-Marie signed the financial assistance agreement in January 2026.
The borough of Outremont is approving a new agreement with the Centre de services scolaire Marguerite-Bourgeoys on the layout and use of the parc-école Saint-Germain.
The agreement runs for 15 years, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2041, and then renews automatically each year unless one of the parties gives written notice to the contrary.
The borough is paying $150,000, all taxes included, taken from the reserved fund for parks and playgrounds; the amount will be paid within 60 days of receiving the school service centre's invoice.
The money will be used to redo the play structure and its shock-absorbing surface, used by children aged 5 to 12 in the area; the total cost of the renovation work is estimated at $350,000.
For its part, the school service centre plans to enhance the rest of the yard: a synthetic soccer field, a multi-sport field and two concrete ping-pong tables.
The former agreement, signed in 2003 and renewed in 2018, ended in 2024.
The public will be informed when the renovations are finished and of the hours when the general public can use the site.
The borough of LaSalle is renewing for one year the maintenance contract for the elevators and other vertical transport equipment in its buildings, awarded to Ascenseurs Néoservices Inc.
The maximum authorized spending is $25,827.98 including taxes: $21,523.32 for the contract and $4,304.66 in contingencies (20%) to cover repairs.
The contract covers full maintenance, periodic preventive inspections and repair calls in the event of a breakdown.
The annual price is going up by 4% compared with the original contract, as provided for in the specifications.
The mandate runs from February 1, 2025 to January 31, 2027, according to the schedule set out in the file.
The money comes from the borough's buildings operating budget.
This is the first of the two renewal options provided for in the contract awarded in January 2023 ($74,503.80 for three years).
The borough of LaSalle is extending Navada Ltée's contract by one year for the preventive maintenance of natural gas heating equipment in various borough buildings.
The authorized expense is $58,516.98, taxes included, taken from the buildings operating budget.
The contract covers full maintenance of the equipment, preventive inspections and repair calls in the event of a breakdown.
The renewal applies from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
As provided for in the contract, the price for the final year is increased by 4%.
The original contract, awarded in May 2023 following a public call for tenders, was worth $165,423.25 for three years with two one-year renewal options; one option remains after this one.

The borough of LaSalle is awarding a direct-negotiation contract of $269,311.12 (taxes included) to Cardin Julien Inc. to supervise the rest of the work on the former city hall, at 13, avenue Strathyre.
The total authorized expense comes to $353,173.34: the contract, plus $53,862.22 in contingencies (20%) and $30,000 in incidental expenses, paid out of LaSalle's capital works program.
The building is being converted into a new cultural centre; the work began in June 2024 with the contractor Procova inc.

Completion of the work, planned for December 2025, is pushed back to the fall of 2026 after the collapse of a portion of the Maison Brunning (work site shut down for about two months) and additional requirements from the CNESST.
The mandate covers meetings and site visits, shop drawings, payment certificates, coordination and follow-up on LEED certification.
The mandate took effect on December 11, 2025 and continues until final provisional acceptance.
The firm had already been awarded the project's professional services contracts since 2019, including a mandate increased to $1,723,690.16 in September 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is adding $46,958.06 (taxes included) to the contract with the firm COEX Architecture for the roof repairs at the complexe aquatique Michel-Leduc.
The total cost of the project thus rises to $444,300.16, taxes included. The original contract, awarded in May 2025, was $397,342.11.
The extra money will pay for unplanned expert studies: geotechnical studies, soil permeability tests, water table level measurements and other analyses.

These studies are required because site-specific constraints were discovered and because the by-law on stormwater management (underground retention basin, perimeter drains) calls for additional technical validations.
According to the borough, the plans and specifications cannot move forward until the results of these expert studies are available.
The funding comes from LaSalle's Ten-Year Capital Works Program (PDI). The assignment, already underway, continues until the end of the contract.
The borough of Ville-Marie is ending the horticultural maintenance and cleanliness contract for Square Dorchester and Place du Canada, which had been awarded to 9032-2454 Québec inc. (Techniparc).
This 12-month contract (April 1, 2025 to March 30, 2026) had been awarded in March 2025 for a maximum expenditure of $162,354.02, including taxes and contingencies.
The borough cites numerous shortcomings: mowing and weeding that had to be redone, snow removal and salt spreading not carried out during precipitation.
Four notices of default were sent to the supplier (November 12 and 18, 2025, December 5, 2025, January 8, 2026) and three penalties were imposed on it, including $250 for November 17, 2025.
The notice of termination was sent to the supplier on January 30, 2026, along with an unsatisfactory performance evaluation.
According to the borough, the termination results in no costs for it: the penalties will be deducted from the supplier's invoicing before the purchase order is closed.
The Ville-Marie borough is taking $1,661,054 from its surpluses to step up cleanliness across its territory in 2026.
The plan has three parts: a big clean-up as soon as the snow melts, ongoing cleanliness brigades, and targeted actions.
Busy areas are given priority: downtown, Quartier chinois, Vieux-Montréal, the Village, Quartier latin, and the areas around metro stations, CPEs and parks.

The amount covers $1,169,054 in wages (blue-collar workers, inspectors, students) and $492,000 for vehicle rentals ($107,000), street furniture ($120,000) and outside contracts for cleaning tree pits, removing graffiti at height and a cleanliness audit ($265,000).
The borough is announcing stronger enforcement of the by-laws on waste collection and cleanliness, and the creation of a committee tasked with recommending changes to the by-laws.
The amounts allocated in previous years were $2,145,125 in 2025, $2,245,458 in 2024 and $1,830,000 in 2023.
The Ville-Marie borough is hiring 9176-7277 Québec inc. (Go Cube) to collect and store furniture and personal belongings left on the sidewalk after an eviction.
The contract is worth $695,972.42, taxes included, from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2029, with the possibility of a one-year extension.
The company handles everything without borough teams stepping in: inventory, photos, loading, fumigation and storage in closed containers.
The belongings are kept for 60 days, as required by law; after that, the company disposes of them if the person has not picked them up.
The public call for tenders was published from March 9 to April 7, 2026: three companies obtained the tender documents and only one submitted a bid.
The borough will assess the company's performance; without this contract, it would no longer have a service in place for these evictions.
The borough of Ville-Marie is extending by one year the concrete and asphalt sawing contract awarded to 2632-2990 Québec inc. (Les excavations DDC), from June 12, 2026 to June 11, 2027.
The extension adds an expense of $267,472.09, taxes included, bringing the contract to $800,019.04 in total.
The amount is paid by the borough out of its operating budget: about $133,736 in 2026 and the same amount in 2027.
The sawing is used to cut the roadway and sidewalks before excavation work, or after an emergency repair to connect neatly to what is already there.
The borough says it does not have the expertise or the equipment to do this work itself; it uses about 1,600 hours of sawing per year, including evenings, weekends and the winter period.
The borough will carry out a performance evaluation of the company.
The contract comes from public call for tenders 24-20513, which had received three compliant bids in 2024.
The borough of Saint-Laurent is submitting its 2025 spending report for the management of residual materials (collection, transport and disposal), a responsibility the City delegates to it.
The report goes to the borough council on February 24, 2026, to the executive committee on March 11, 2026, and then to city council on March 23, 2026.
The household waste item shows an overrun: $240,004.01 spent against a budget of $189,100, for a deficit of $50,904.01.
The collection of recyclable materials ($261,974.33) and organic materials ($209,625.22) ended within their revised budgets.
Dry materials cost $157,291.16, against an original budget of $58,000 revised to $157,292.
No communications activity is planned for this submission.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing spending of $112,254.12, taxes included, with Amrize Canada inc.
The company will supply and transport crushed and pre-mixed stone from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
This stone is used for excavations, for repairs to water main, sewer and catch basin breaks, and as a base for asphalting.
The purchase is made under master agreement no. 1594243 entered into by the Ville de Montréal, in effect until April 2026.
The spending is paid out of the operating budget.
In 2025, the borough had authorized $136,149.95 for the same type of supply, with Lafarge Canada inc.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is creating a permanent signage attendant position in the Division de la voirie et de l'aqueduc, effective April 18, 2026.
In exchange, the borough is abolishing a permanent works and maintenance attendant position in the same division.
The change raises the position's hourly rate from $30.25 to $34.22.
The move makes permanent a blue-collar employee who has accumulated more than 1,260 hours in higher-level duties, as required by the blue-collar workers' collective agreement (SCFP 301).
The expense, for the period from April 18 to December 31, 2026, is paid out of the operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is awarding Sanivac (9363-9888 Québec Inc.) a contract worth $253,772.82, taxes included, for hydro-excavation services, including the disposal of the waste material.
The contract starts on May 4, 2026 and ends on December 31, 2028, with no possibility of renewal.

Hydro-excavation is used to maintain the sewer and water supply networks: pressurized water breaks up the soil, and the material is vacuumed into the truck. The City says this method avoids damage to underground infrastructure.
Each year, the contract covers 100 hours of regular weekday calls, 40 hours on weekends and 20 hours for emergencies.
Four companies submitted bids; Sanivac was the lowest of the three compliant ones. JMV Environnement was rejected for failing to meet the experience requirement.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is paying an additional $106,150.97 (taxes included) to the company 404077 Canada (De Sousa) for the rental of a grader with an operator.
This brings the total bill for this rental to $232,628.07, whereas the contract had provided for $126,477.10 for the period from November 2025 to April 30, 2026.
The borough explains that it rented an additional grader that had not been planned for, because of the winter conditions of the 2025-2026 season.
The original contract comes from public call for tenders 23-20152, in which De Sousa was the lowest compliant bidder for lot 5.
The spending is for snow removal and maintenance of the borough's road network.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is adding $99,024.42 (taxes included) to its purchase of de-icing salt for the 2025-2026 winter.
The total spending with Compass Minerals Canada corp. thus rises to $512,198.58, after an initial authorization of $413,174.16.
The salt is used to de-ice the borough's roadways and sidewalks during the winter period.
The purchase is made through a City master agreement reached after public call for tenders 25-21090.
The additional spending ($90,422.49 net) is paid out of the operating budget and the snow reserve.
The borough says that going through the master agreement ensures supply and avoids stock shortages during the winter.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is creating a finance committee tasked with monitoring the borough's financial situation and making recommendations to the borough council.

The committee will look at how spending and revenues change over time, the tracking of major financial commitments, budget preparation, tax adjustments, cost-cutting measures and the use of surpluses.
It will also have to set or lower priorities for projects based on what the document describes as the borough's currently limited financial capacity.
Two elected officials will sit on it: borough mayor François Limoges and city councillor Josefina Blanco (Saint-Édouard district), until November 1, 2029.

They will be joined by the borough director, the director of citizen relations, administrative services and the borough clerk's office, the head of the financial and material resources division, and the chief of staff.
At least six meetings a year, every six to eight weeks; the first meeting is planned for June 2026.
No spending is attached to this decision.
The City is lending archaeological artifacts to the Pointe-à-Callière museum for its "Montréal Capitale" project.
The artifacts come from digs at the site of the marché Sainte-Anne and the parliament of the Province of Canada, at place D'Youville.
The loan lasts three years and is intended for research, restoration, conservation and promotion of the collection.
The museum must cover the costs of the loan, keep the artifacts under surveillance, meet specific temperature and humidity conditions, and prevent visitors from handling them.
It may not clean or restore the artifacts, or lend them to a third party, without the City's written permission.
The City may take the artifacts back if it finds that the museum has not taken proper care of them.
The agreement involves no additional cost for the City: the costs are paid out of the budget of the Réserve des collections archéologiques.
The City is lending archaeological objects found at Pointe-aux-Trembles to the Atelier d'histoire de la Pointe-aux-Trembles.
These artifacts will be used in a free permanent exhibition at the Écomusée d'histoire de la Pointe-aux-Trembles, at the Centre Roussin.
The loan is for five years, and the objects may be used only for the exhibition.

The organization must cover the costs of the loan, keep the objects under surveillance, respect temperature and humidity conditions, and not clean or restore them without written authorization from the City.
The City may take the objects back if it considers that the organization has been negligent or has not respected the conditions.
According to the document, the agreement involves no additional cost for the City; collection management costs are paid out of the budget of the Réserve des collections archéologiques.
The City is lending archaeological objects from its Réserve des collections to the Musée national de l'histoire du Québec, in Québec, for the permanent exhibition "Le grand parcours historique".
The artifacts being lent come from the site of the marché Sainte-Anne and the parliament of the Province of Canada.
The loan is planned to last ten years, and the objects are to be used only for exhibition purposes.
The objects are scheduled to be transported on March 9, 2026, and the exhibition is to open in June 2026.
According to the document, the agreement involves no additional cost for the City: storage, management and promotion costs are paid out of the Réserve's annual budget.
The agreement sets out the terms for preserving, managing and promoting the objects; the list of objects is attached as an appendix.
The City is giving the ministre des Transports et de la Mobilité durable the archaeological objects it holds from the site of the former village of Saint-Henri-des-Tanneries.
These artifacts and ecofacts were found between 2015 and 2020, during digs carried out while the échangeur Turcot was being redeveloped.
The digs took place on neighbouring pieces of land, one belonging to the City and the other to the ministère: the collection was therefore split between two owners.
The donation brings all the pieces together into a single collection, so that objects from the same historical context stay together.
The minister will place all of the objects at the Laboratoire et à la Réserve d'archéologie du Québec, in order to make them accessible to the public.
The City is also providing the digital versions of the reports and technical files related to the digs.
The agreement involves no additional cost for the City.
The City agrees to receive, as a perpetual loan, the collection of archaeological objects found during the digs carried out while the REM was being built on Montréal's territory.
The ministère de la Culture et des Communications remains the owner of the objects; the City is responsible for conserving, managing and promoting them.
The objects will be stored at the Réserve des collections archéologiques de la Ville, at 333, rue Peel, a place that meets museum standards for temperature and humidity.
The City will be able to lend the objects temporarily to museum, scientific and academic partners, but only the ministère can authorize these loans.
The City becomes responsible for any loss or damage caused by negligence and would pay the restoration costs.
The loan is free of charge and for an unlimited period; there is no additional cost for the City, as the expenses are absorbed by the Réserve's operating budget.
The city is signing a new collective agreement with the Syndicat des brigadier(ère)s scolaires (SCFP 930), running from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2030.
Wages go up by 2.50% per year, each August 15, from 2026 to 2030.
The split-shift premium will be built into the hourly wage as of August 15, 2026, at a recurring cost of about $180,000 per year.
Each crossing guard receives a signing bonus equal to 1% of their annual salary, or about $175,000 in 2026.
The maximum number of permanent mobile crossing guard positions goes from 30 to 40.
The agreement creates crossing reassignments (with no travel costs paid) and pushes back the bumping procedure to 4 weeks of suspended activities.
An employment equity, diversity and inclusion committee is created, with 2 representatives from the city and 2 from the union.
The borough of Lachine accepts two objects donated to the Musée de Lachine and authorizes the signing of the donation agreements.
First object: a 1964 graduation ring from Collège Sainte-Anne, made by Birks, donated by Andrée Matte, a former student.

Second object: a watercolour by Montréal painter J. Mercure, made in the early 1980s, showing the English-language school Resurrection of our Lord High School, donated by Sharon Norton and Colleen Raven.
An acquisitions committee that met on December 4, 2025 assessed the two offers, submitted in 2017 and 2022, and voted to add them to the collections.
No cost: the donors are not asking for a tax receipt and storage does not require any additional fees.
The borough directs its departments to store and preserve the objects according to the standards in force, and will then inform the donors.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is awarding a $113,641.29 contract (taxes included) to NIPPAYSAGE inc. to design the reunification of parc du Père-Marquette, as part of the project to turn rue de Bellechasse into a pedestrian street.

The mandate includes a public consultation process (a survey on Réalisons Montréal, workshops, focus groups, an information session for local residents), followed by plans and specifications, with the firm Atelier Urbain handling the consultation portion.
Stated goals of the project: make the areas around the school safer, create gathering spaces, add greenery and remove pavement around the parks, and make active transportation easier.
Approximate timeline: contract awarded on February 3, 2026, consultation from February to April 2026, plans and specifications from February to August 2026.
The contract was awarded by mutual agreement: 6 firms were contacted by email on October 9, 2025, 5 proposals were received, and NIPPAYSAGE received the best score.
The price is $4,415.04 (4%) higher than the borough's estimate of $109,226.25; the net expense after tax refunds is $103,769.65.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving $75,000 to SIDAC Promenade Masson and $75,000 to SIDAC Plaza St-Hubert for 2026, for a total of $150,000.
The money can only be used to pay the salaries and benefits of the commercial development corporations' staff and the rent for their premises.
Of the $150,000, $100,000 comes from the 2026 budget of the project office and economic development, and $50,000 from a transfer out of the appropriated management surplus.
The SDCs must display the borough's contribution (logos provided) in their documents and advertising related to the subsidized activities.
The contribution to SDC Petite-Italie–Marché Jean-Talon is not included here: it will be the subject of a file at the next borough council meeting.
The same amount of $75,000 per SDC was granted in 2024 and in 2025.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie wants to appoint Jocelyn Pauzé, city councillor for the Marie-Victorin district, as its representative on the board of directors of PME MTL Centre-Est.
The final decision rests with the urban agglomeration council, to which the borough is making this recommendation.
The seat is to be filled after the municipal elections of November 2, 2025.

According to the document, having an elected official from the borough present is intended to support joint planning and follow-up of shared initiatives with this local economic development organization.
No expense is attached to this appointment.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving $75,000 to the SDC Petite-Italie – Marché Jean-Talon for its operations in 2026.
Of this amount, $50,000 comes from the operating budget of the economic development division and $25,000 from a transfer out of the allocated management surplus.
The money can only be used for the salaries and benefits of the SDC's staff and for the rent of a space.
The SDC must mention the borough's contribution, using the logos provided, in its documents and advertising related to the subsidized activities.
The same amount of $75,000 was granted to this SDC in 2024 and in 2025, compared with $50,000 in 2022 and 2023.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie appoints Olivier Demers-Dubé, city councillor for the Vieux-Rosemont district, to the board of directors of the Société de développement commercial Promenade Masson.
The law requires that a member of city council or of the City's staff sit on the board of directors of a commercial development corporation, which has nine members.
This power of appointment was delegated to the borough councils by city council.
The economic development commissioner will also sit on this board of directors, as an observer.
The appointment replaces the one made in 2022, which designated the councillor for the Étienne-Desmarteau district for the Promenade Masson.
No expense is associated with the decision.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is appointing councillor Josefina Blanco (Saint-Édouard district) to the board of directors of two commercial development corporations: Petite-Italie – Marché Jean-Talon and Plaza St-Hubert.
The law requires each SDC to include, on its nine-member board, a person designated by the City from among its elected officials or its employees.
The borough's economic development commissioner will also sit on these boards, as an observer.
This is a renewal: Ms. Blanco had already been appointed to these two boards in December 2022.
The matter involves no spending.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving $4,000 to the organization Marchés d'ici to hold the Marché Angus during the 2026 season.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget.

Marchés d'ici, a non-profit active for twenty-five years, is taking over the organization of the market: weekly setup of the installations, equipping the site, and recruiting food producers and artisans.
Last year, the borough granted $16,250 for the 2025 season.
The borough secretary is authorized to sign the agreement on behalf of the City.
According to the decision summary, without this approval, the Marché Angus programming could not take place.
The organization takes charge of communications and must mention the borough's support in its publications.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving $75,000 to the Association des commerçants et des professionnels de la rue Beaubien Est, for the period from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
The money is to be used to continue the organization's relaunch: activities planned in its strategic plan and the salary of the person in charge of operations, business outreach and communications.
The payment is made in three parts: $45,000 within 30 days after signing, $22,500 after the mid-year report is accepted, and then $7,500 after the final accounting.
The Association will have to display the borough's contribution (logos provided) on all promotional material related to the funded activities.
The money comes from the borough's 2026 miscellaneous surplus; it is a non-recurring contribution.
The organization, relaunched in 2023, had received $75,000 in 2024 and $75,000 in 2025.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is authorizing a farmers' public market, the marché P'tit Beaubien, at parc Joseph-Paré, every Saturday from June 27 to September 5, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. (vendors may set up starting at 8:30 a.m.).
La Maison de l'Amitié will coordinate and run the market; it takes on the financial and logistical responsibility for it.
The borough will provide logistical support: access to water and electricity, and the loan of equipment (tables, chairs), out of existing operating budgets.
Three ordinances allow noise from sound equipment outdoors, the sale of promotional items, food and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks, and the consumption of alcohol on site during market hours.
Posters, banners and pennants bearing the name of the event and its partners are allowed on rue Beaubien Est and in parc Joseph-Paré from June 1 to September 7, 2026.
According to the document, the market is aimed at the Petite-Louisiane and l'Assomption neighbourhoods, which are considered less well served in fresh and local products.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is closing the north and south lanes of place du Marché-du-Nord to traffic, along marché Jean-Talon, between avenue Casgrain and avenue Henri-Julien.
The closure applies on Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., from June 4 to October 18, 2026.
It also applies on statutory holidays: June 24, July 1, September 1 and October 12, 2026.
All road vehicles are covered, including goods delivery vehicles.
The borough will put up signs before the period begins, and its blue-collar workers will operate the retractable bollards during the closure hours.
Each party covers the costs of its own work; the order will be published on the borough's website.
The pedestrian-only area has existed since 2006 and has run from Thursday to Sunday since 2017; in 2025, it ran from June 12 to October 19.
Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is allowing the sale of food and non-alcoholic drinks from street food trucks and three-wheeled cargo bikes from May 15 to October 31, 2026.
One three-wheeled cargo bike will be able to operate in parc Maisonneuve every day, according to the park's hours, but not within 100 metres of the park chalet.

Two trucks will be allowed near parc Père-Marquette (rue Garnier between des Carrières and Rosemont, east side; rue des Carrières between Marquette and Garnier, north side), every day from 8 a.m. to 11 p.m.
Two trucks will be allowed near parc Lafond, on boulevard Saint-Joseph between 13e and 16e Avenue, north side, every day from 8 a.m. to 11 p.m.
No truck is allowed on the residential side of these street sections, and events already authorized by the borough have priority over these locations.
L'Association des restaurateurs de rue du Québec handles communications for the events it promotes.
The file does not include any financial aspect.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie will allow people to drink alcohol while eating on the shared terraces set up on public property, at the Quais Masson and at the small squares on rue Beaubien Est.
The permission applies from May 15 to October 31, 2026, at the designated locations.
Authorized hours: Sunday to Wednesday from 10 a.m. to 11 p.m., and Thursday to Saturday from 10 a.m. to midnight.
These terraces are open to everyone and are not attached to an establishment holding a liquor licence; food and alcohol must be bought nearby.
The project is being carried out with the Société de développement commercial Promenade Masson and the Association des commerçants et professionnels de Beaubien Est.
No spending is associated with this file; the borough plans to put up information signs near the locations concerned.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is releasing $75,000 from its management surplus to pay for a study on the future of the Bain Saint-Denis, at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert.
The bath has been closed since the end of summer 2024 because the building is run-down and major work is needed.
In the winter of 2025-2026, the building was used temporarily as a warming station, lent to a community organization.
An outside firm will have to propose two to three redevelopment scenarios with a cultural, commercial or collective purpose; the residential option is excluded.
The study will also compare the possible ownership statuses (keeping the building public or transferring it) and will suggest governance and funding models.
Planned timeline: project parameters in May 2026, call to the market in June, awarding of the contract by mutual agreement and start of the work in July 2026.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving an additional $7,000 to the non-profit organization Marchés d'ici to hold the Marché Angus in the summer of 2026.
This amount is on top of the $4,000 already granted on April 7, 2026, for a total of $11,000 this season ($16,250 had been paid in 2025).
The money will cover new costs imposed by regulations, in particular a signage plan.
Marchés d'ici is taking over the organization of the market: weekly set-up of the installations, equipment, and recruitment of food producers and artisans.
The organization also handles communications and must mention the borough's support in its publications.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing outdoor sound broadcasting (loudspeakers, sound systems) for a first series of events planned for 2026 on public property.
This permission is an exception to the Règlement sur le bruit (noise by-law); it applies only to the sites and times listed in the Tableau des événements 2026 (part 1).
The events covered are family, social, sports or cultural events, free and open to all, organized by recognized organizations, non-profit organizations or private promoters.
Each organizer will have to provide their documents (proof of insurance, notice from the Service des incendies, setup plan) before receiving final authorization.
The costs of municipal support for the events are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved, with no additional spending announced.
The promoters will advertise their own events (social media, websites, neighbourhood newspapers).
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing a second series of events on public property in 2026.
Noise from sound equipment broadcasting outdoors will be allowed at the sites and times listed in the 2026 events table (part 2).
Consuming and selling food and drinks (alcoholic or not), as well as selling promotional items, will be allowed in booths set up for that purpose.
The events are free and are organized by recognized organizations, non-profit organizations or private promoters.
Each promoter will have to provide their documents (insurance, notice from the Service des incendies, site layout plan) before receiving their authorization.
The costs of supporting the events are covered by the operating budgets of the departments and services involved.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is approving a third set of events on public property for 2026.
Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors despite the noise by-law, at the locations and times listed in the events table.
The sale and consumption of food, as well as the sale of promotional items, will be allowed in booths set up on site.
Streets may be closed or traffic obstructed at the places and times planned for each event.
The events are free and open to everyone; they are organized by recognized organizations, non-profit organizations or private promoters.
Each promoter will have to provide its documents (insurance, notice from the Service des incendies, site layout plan) before receiving its authorization.
The costs of supporting the events are covered by the operating budgets of the departments and services involved.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is approving a new series of events on public property in 2026 (part 4).
Noise from sound equipment broadcasting outdoors will be allowed at the sites and times listed in the table of events.
Streets may be closed or traffic may be blocked during these events.
The sale and consumption of food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, and the sale of promotional items will be allowed in booths set up for that purpose.
The events are free and organized by recognized organizations, non-profit organizations or private promoters.
The costs of city support are covered by the operating budgets of the departments and services involved.
Each promoter will have to provide their documents (insurance, notice from the Service des incendies, site plan) before getting their authorization.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing a new series of events on public property in 2026 (part 5).
At the sites and times listed in the events table, organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors despite the noise by-law.
They will also be allowed to close streets or obstruct traffic, and to sell food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks and promotional items at kiosks.
The events are free and open to everyone; they are organized by recognized organizations, non-profit organizations and private promoters.
Each promoter will still have to provide its documents (insurance, notice from the Service des incendies, site plan) before receiving its authorization.
The costs of supporting the events are absorbed into the operating budgets of the departments concerned.
The borough of Verdun will auction off, on or around June 25, 2026, property left on the public road after evictions that took place between February 13, 2024 and March 13, 2026.
The sale will be held at the municipal workshops, at 1177, rue Dupuis, where the property is stored in containers.
Five eviction addresses are involved: 648, rue Galt; 4444, boulevard LaSalle (suite 206); 5348, rue de Verdun; 3717, rue Ethel; 3812, rue Evelyn.
An owner can have their property removed from the sale if they take it back within the set time limits.
More than 60 days have passed between each eviction and the sale date, as required by article 943 of the Civil Code of Québec.
The borough says it wants to free up space for the next people who are evicted.
The money from the sale will go to the borough's operating budget.
The Verdun borough council takes note of the 2025 report on the Plan de développement stratégique, which closes out the 2015-2025 plan.
Of the 109 priority actions in the 2022-2025 plan, 90% have been completed or partially completed.

Living environment: 75 events for the 150th anniversary (more than 100,000 people), new sports fields at the patinoire BBB, improved universal accessibility in 18 projects, progress on the District Atwater (up to 200 social housing units).

Environment and mobility: redevelopment of parc Dan-Hanganu and parc Joannette, 1,266 trees planted, 9.24 hectares of natural areas protected, 5.85 km of bike paths rebuilt and 13 intersections made safer.
Local economy: 2.45 million visits on rue Wellington (+6.3%), a new public square and mobilization of L'Île-des-Sœurs merchants.
Services to residents: 12,300 requests handled (73% within the expected time), 23 public consultations bringing together close to 3,800 people, relaunch of the Natatorium restoration project.
The report will be posted online on Verdun's Plan de développement stratégique page; no amount is attached to the decision.

The City is hiring L'Archevêque et Rivest ltée to build two new greenhouses at its nursery in L'Assomption, in Lanaudière, for $1,173,000, plus $140,760 in contingencies — a total of $1,313,760, taxes included.
The two current greenhouses (627 m² in total), moved from Terrebonne in 2001, will be taken down and replaced by two greenhouses of 418 m² each (836 m²).
The document states that the current greenhouses are worn out: heating units replaced twice since 2023, the large greenhouse's tarp changed after leaks, and repeated repairs to the motors.
The nursery has about 64,000 trees and supplies some 3,300 caliper trees a year to 10 boroughs, from mid-April to mid-November.
The work is to last 120 days after the order to start; the spending is spread over 2026 and 2027 and is paid 100% by the central city through a loan by-law.
Three of the eleven parties who took out the tender documents submitted a bid; the bid chosen is 10.01% lower than the City's most recent estimate.
A first call for tenders launched in April 2025 was cancelled because there was only one bidder, whose price differed too much from the estimate.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing a series of public events on its public property in 2026 by temporarily setting aside three by-laws: noise, sales on public property, and signage.
Noise from sound equipment outdoors becomes permitted at the planned sites and times, as does the sale of non-alcoholic drinks, food and promotional items, and the installation of signs or banners.

About a dozen sports and recreation organizations (soccer, tennis, basketball, ball, futsal, hockey, youth centres) will be able to hold games and practices from May 1 to October 31, 2026, some until November 22, 2026 or May 18, 2027.
The parks covered include Angrignon, Ignace-Bourget, De La Vérendrye, Louis-Cyr, Le Ber, Vinet, Oscar-Peterson, Clifford, Jacques-Viger, Campbell-Ouest and the Carré d'Hibernia.
One-time events at parc Angrignon: Faites un pas vers les jeunes on May 3, Défi Entreprises on May 23 and 24, La Marche Percée DT1 on June 7, 2026.
The Olympiades Intergénérationnelles will be held at square Sir-George-Étienne-Cartier on May 23, 2026, from 9:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.
The costs of the City's services to support these events are absorbed by existing operating budgets; the events are free.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing 11 public events on its public property between May 16 and July 26, 2026.

Parc Angrignon will host 10 of these events: Défi Entreprises, Course pour les Femmes AIMEZ-VOUS, Marche pour l'Alzheimer, the brain tumour walk, Bougeons pour le côlon, Course Nocturne Sun Life, Fête champêtre des policiers, Festival culturel Yemba, Rendez-vous familial des pompiers and La Palestine au parc.
The Fête familiale des Chevaliers de Colomb will take place at parc St-Paul and on rue Brisset (between Caron and Champigny) on May 16, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m.
The orders temporarily lift the rules on noise from outdoor sound equipment, the sale of food, promotional items and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks, and the installation of signs and banners.
Some streets may be closed to motor vehicle traffic according to the locations and times set out in the table of events.
The events are free, and the costs of the City's services will be paid out of the operating budgets of the departments concerned.
A public notice announcing the orders will be published on the borough's website.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $20,000 to the organization La Lutinerie de Montréal.
The money will be used to organize summer activities tied to the Fête nationale du Québec 2026 in Le Sud-Ouest.
An agreement sets out the funded project and the payment terms.
The expense is paid entirely by the borough.
The borough has been working with this organization on the Fête nationale since 2022; in 2023, it granted the organization $30,000 per year for 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The organization pays for its own promotional materials, which the borough must approve, and must follow a visibility protocol.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $790 in one-time financial contributions to three local organizations.
Bâtiment 7 is receiving $300 to buy three tickets to its fundraising event on May 21, 2026.
Club de patinage artistique Gadbois is receiving $200 to help pay for its end-of-year show.
Rues Principales is receiving $290 for one ticket to Colloque 2026, which takes place on April 15, 2026.
The money comes from the borough's unallocated surplus, and the borough is covering the expense.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is paying out $4,918.43 in one-time financial contributions to five organizations.
$2,500 goes to the Association des jeunes de la Petite-Bourgogne to organize the Fête nationale du Québec.
$2,000 goes to the Chambre de commerce de Montréal Centre Sud-Ouest for the 12th Gala Unio, on May 28, 2026 at Théâtre Paradoxe.
