$300 goes to the Association des Popotes Roulantes du Montréal Métropolitain for its 30th anniversary, and $75 to Maison-Répit Oasis for 3 tickets to its April 18, 2026 evening event.
$43.43 is being added to a contribution already granted to Rues Principales for the Colloque 2026.
The money comes from the borough's free surplus, and the borough is covering the entire expense.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving out $3,000 in one-time contributions to organizations and schools in its territory.

Five schools in the Centre de services scolaire de Montréal each receive $500, taken from the 2026 fund for student perseverance: Honoré-Mercier (the "Implication bénévole" bursary/Prix Gélinas), Saint-Henri (videos on eco-responsible behaviour), Victor-Rousselot (end-of-year party), Cœur-Immaculé-de-Marie (the "De la terre à l'assiette" project) and Notre-Dame-du-Perpétuel-Secours (environmental clean-up).
The Centre africain de développement et d'entraide receives $250 to mark its 25th anniversary.
The Centre d'intégration à la vie active pour les personnes vivant avec un handicap physique receives $250 to fund its mission.
The money comes from an allocation of uncommitted surplus and is paid entirely by the borough.
The decision rests with the borough council, at its meeting of June 8, 2026.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $9,250 in one-time contributions to five neighbourhood organizations, taken from its unrestricted surplus.

Concertation Ville-Émard et Côte-Saint-Paul receives $2,800 for a mural at the Centre Hortense-Duclos (5599, avenue Laurendeau) and $1,000 for Opération Sac à Dos, which will give a backpack to 200 children.

The Association des Jeunes de la Petite-Bourgogne receives $1,700 for medals for young soccer players in Saint-Henri and Petite-Bourgogne, and $750 for the Fête nationale du Canada on July 1, 2026 at parc Oscar-Peterson.
Action-Gardien receives $1,000 for the 8th edition of Bric-à-Brac, which provides the required school supplies to kindergarten, elementary and high school students.
The Association Parcours Céramique receives $1,800 for the 10th edition of Parcours Céramique.
The Centre communautaire des femmes actives receives $200 to mark its 20th anniversary.
The borough is paying for these expenses in full.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is adding a stop sign on rue Marie-Anne Est, on the west approach to the intersection with rue Drolet.
The decision responds to several requests from residents received over the past few years.
Stop lines and pedestrian crossings will be painted, and small signs showing the layout of the intersection will be added under all the stop signs.
The borough cites the safety of pedestrians, cyclists, children and other vulnerable users, even though one of the ministère des Transports' criteria is not met.
Signs warning of the new traffic signs will be put up 30 days before they are installed, and then for 30 days afterward.
The order is to be adopted and the stop signs installed in March 2026; the pavement markings will be done during the 2026 season.
The work is being carried out by the Division de l'entretien de l'éclairage, de la signalisation et du marquage, which bills the borough; no amount is given.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is permanently closing avenue Coloniale to car traffic between rue Elmire and rue Demers, in front of école Saint-Enfant-Jésus, to create a "place école" (school plaza).
The closure will be marked out with bollards, planters and concrete blocks.

Rue Elmire becomes one-way eastbound between Coloniale and avenue de l'Hôtel-de-Ville; avenue Coloniale becomes two-way between Demers and Villeneuve Ouest, at the request of the Service de sécurité incendie.
Parking is being removed on avenue Coloniale between rue Elmire and rue Villeneuve Ouest.
The borough expects more traffic on Saint-Dominique at school drop-off and pick-up times, more southbound traffic on Hôtel-de-Ville and Drolet, and detours for some residents of Elmire and Coloniale.
Signage and road marking costs are estimated at about $8,000, paid out of the borough's operating budget.
A notice to residents is planned for mid-April 2026, an information session for late April, and implementation for late May or early June 2026.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is reversing the one-way direction of five streets between avenue Laurier Est and boulevard Saint-Joseph Est: De Brébeuf and Garnier will run southbound; Chambord, Fabre and Chabot will run northbound.
Goal: cut down through traffic in the Petit Laurier Est area. The study by CIMA+ measured up to 50% of vehicles as through traffic on Chambord and 35% on Fabre during rush hours.
The work involves pavement marking ($2,500), signage ($10,000) and traffic lights (about $40,000), paid out of the borough's operating surplus.
A few parking spaces will be removed near intersections to improve visibility.
Notice to residents in June 2026, information session on June 8, 2026, warning signs 30 days in advance, implementation in July 2026.
The borough expects an adjustment period, particularly for delivery drivers and people looking for parking.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal will install stop signs on rue Gilford, at the intersection with rue Garnier.
One sign will be placed on the west side for vehicles and another on the east side for cyclists, with tab signs showing the layout of the intersection.
The road markings will include stop lines for vehicles and cyclists, as well as pedestrian crossings at the east and west crossing points.
The request comes from the governing board of école Paul-Bruchési, the board of directors of CPE St-Louis and residents of the area.

According to the standards of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, all-way stops are not warranted at this intersection, which was redesigned in 2023 with a diverter island and curb extensions.
Timeline: adoption of the order in May 2026, advance signs in May, permanent signs in June 2026 and road markings during the 2026 season.
Signs announcing the new signage will be installed 30 days before, and then 30 days after it is put in place.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is making rue Fullum one-way southbound, between avenue Laurier Est and rue Sherbrooke Est.
Bike facilities will be added along the sidewalk in both directions, separated from parking by a buffer zone and bollards.

The change will happen in two phases: from Mont-Royal Est to Sherbrooke Est in August 2026, then from Laurier Est to Mont-Royal Est in the spring of 2027. The phasing takes into account the operations of the STM's centre de transport Mont-Royal.
A few parking spaces will be removed near intersections to improve visibility.
Expected costs: $20,000 for pavement markings, $50,000 for signage and $40,000 for traffic lights, paid by the borough.
Residents will be notified on June 9, 2026 and an information session is planned for June 22, 2026; signs will announce the change 30 days in advance.
A study by the firm CIMA+ concludes that traffic and access to the area would be only slightly affected, with short detours.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is creating a pedestrian crossing on rue Saint-Dominique, between Saint-Viateur Est and Bernard Est, in front of the entrance to the aréna Saint-Louis.
Work at the arena includes a rainwater retention basin in the former parking lot: users will now have to park on the street.
On the list: yellow crossing markings, a painted centre median to narrow the lanes, signs, flexible bollards and rapid flashing beacons.
Estimated costs: $800 for markings and signage, $13,000 for the flashing beacons and $3,000 for the bollards.
Timeline: order in July 2026, installation between August and early September 2026; the arena is expected to reopen in the fall of 2026.
Sidewalk work is planned for 2027 to add a universally accessible ramp on the east side of the street.
"New signage" signs will stay in place for 30 to 60 days after the order takes effect.
The City is giving $2,000 to ACFAS inc. and providing it with technical support valued at $8,000 for two activities held from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The $2,000 will be used to pay the prize money for the "Humain-Nature" award of the La preuve par l'image contest, presented at the Gala de l'Acfas in November 2026.

Espace pour la vie will print, install, take down and promote, at its own expense, the exhibition of the 20 finalist photos on the Biodôme's forecourt, from May to November 2026, with no admission fee.

For the Vulgarisathon marathon (5th edition, performing arts), the Biodôme's head of the public programs and education division will support 8 selected candidates: workshops, monthly follow-ups, dress rehearsal, about 45 hours from January to May.
The final show will be presented on May 14, 2026 at the Cabaret de la vulgarisation scientifique, during the 93rd Congrès de l'Acfas at the Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières.
Acfas will pay the travel costs of the Biodôme employee to Trois-Rivières; the $2,000 expense is covered by the central city.
The organization will have to apply the City's visibility protocol.
The City is giving $450,000 to the Institut de recherche en biologie végétale (IRBV) to support its mission in 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The money will be paid in three instalments of $150,000: the first when the agreement is signed, the other two after an accountability report is submitted, due January 31, 2027 and January 31, 2028.
The IRBV, created in 1990 and jointly managed by the City and the Université de Montréal, is located at the Jardin botanique de Montréal.
The support is to be used for research in plant biology and biodiversity, conservation of research collections, student training and the transfer of scientific results.
The expense is included in the budget of the Service de l'Espace pour la vie and is paid 100% by the central city.
The agreement is to be signed in March 2026 and ends December 31, 2028; a visibility protocol is attached to it.
Support of the same amount had been granted in January 2023 for the years 2023 to 2025.
The City is transferring to the company 9560-8303 Québec inc. the professional services contract awarded in January 2026 to artist Anne Lagacé, who is a shareholder of the company.
The contract, worth $574,696.75 including taxes, covers the design and installation of the light artwork "Résonances" at the Jardin des Premières-Nations of the Jardin botanique.
All other terms of the original contract remain the same for the rest of the agreement.
The artist had signed in her own personal name because her company was not yet registered; it was registered on February 17, 2026.
The artwork is part of the Jardins de lumière 2026 event, which is scheduled to open on August 28, 2026.
The installation must be taken down between November 2 and 13, 2026.
The City is giving an additional $28,750 to the Université du Québec à Rimouski for a research project on the chevalier cuivré, a threatened fish found only in Québec.
The City's total contribution to this project therefore rises from $50,000 to $78,750.
The agreement with the UQAR is extended by three months, until July 31, 2026, which keeps a postdoctoral intern's contract in place.
The money comes entirely from a contribution by the Fondation Espace pour la vie; the expense is covered 100% by the central city.
The payments: $43,500 in the summer of 2025, $28,750 on the signing of the addendum, and $6,500 on July 31, 2026.
The Biodôme is taking part in the project, which deals with indicators of the fish's health and detection techniques using environmental DNA.
The City is accepting a $519,391 donation from the Fondation Espace pour la vie to fund projects at its museums (Insectarium, Biodôme, Biosphère).

The largest amount, $346,453, goes to the "Les Sentinelles du Nunavik" program: an inventory of insects and spiders north of the 52nd parallel, carried out with young people from northern communities, until December 31, 2027.
$145,673 will be used for the Biodôme's conservation projects (wood turtle, Blanding's turtle, western chorus frog), also until the end of 2027.
$22,265 will go toward developing a lobster fishing bait made from microalgae and insect products, and $5,000 to the free "Quartier vivant" workshops offered in neighbourhoods, in 2026.
The expense is covered 99.04% by the ville centre and 0.96% by the agglomeration, because the Biosphère is located in parc Jean-Drapeau.
The money will be used for operating expenses, including temporary hires; any unspent amount will have to be returned to the Fondation.

The borough of Outremont is hiring Névé Réfrigération inc. to service, repair and maintain the heating, air conditioning, ventilation, refrigeration and dehumidification systems in its municipal buildings.
Total authorized spending of $373,542.98, taxes included: $266,816.41 for the contract, plus $53,363.28 in contingencies and $53,363.28 in incidental costs (20% each).
The contract runs from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2029, with two possible 12-month renewals.

Nine buildings are covered, including the arena and intergenerational community centre, the borough hall, the piscine J.F.-Kennedy, the bibliothèque Robert-Bourassa, the service yard and the chalets in parc Pratt and parc Saint-Viateur.
The contract covers planned preventive maintenance and an on-call emergency service 24/7, with labour, materials and tools provided.
Névé Réfrigération was the lowest compliant bidder, 7% below the estimate; the current provider, Black & McDonald, ranked third at $349,648.85.
The spending is fully paid for by the borough, out of its operating budget.
The City is accepting $30,000 in financial support from the Fondation de la faune du Québec to protect the northern map turtle, a species at risk.
The money will be used to build five artificial nesting mounds in the Rapides-du-Cheval-Blanc area, in the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
The work includes clearing vegetation and invasive species, buying and installing geotextile and substrate, and then monitoring how well the mounds work.
Activities begin in March 2026 and the agreement ends in March 2027, with a final monitoring report.
Monitoring carried out at this site since 2023 shows a high death rate among eggs and newborns, mainly because of unsuitable soil.
The agreement has no impact on the City's financial framework: $18,000 in 2026 and $12,000 in 2027, in both revenue and spending.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is making permanent the tree pruner position held by Jessica Boudreau-Galarneau, in the Division des parcs of the Direction des travaux publics, as of February 21, 2026.
The appointment to permanent status depends on successfully completing the trial period set out in the blue-collar workers' collective agreement (S.C.F.P. 301).
The hourly wage for the tree pruner position is $36.11 (pay group 14-013).
The position had to be filled because the previous holder left for another borough.
An internal posting within the Ville took place from December 16 to 22, 2025 to fill the position.
The expense, from February 21 to December 31, 2026, will be paid out of the operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is cancelling call for tenders 1165 for the replacement of two pumps at the tunnel Lacordaire pumping station.
Flooding damaged two of the station's three pumps; they have passed their service life and cannot be repaired.
Three compliant bids had been received, the lowest from GASTIER M.P. INC. at $295,017.93 (taxes included), but the Service de l'eau chose not to fund the project.
Instead, the borough will issue a new call for tenders to replace the three existing pumps, with submersible pumps recommended by CIMA +.
New plans and specifications will be prepared by a firm and submitted to the Service de l'eau for comments before the new call for tenders is issued.
The Service de l'eau will fund the plans and specifications as well as the work to replace the three pumps.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Joanie Arredondo as horticulture and parks foreperson in the Division des parcs of the Direction des travaux publics, effective May 16, 2026.
The position becomes permanent if she successfully completes the probation period set out in the working conditions for the City's managers.
The 2026 salary scale for this job (group 04-FM05) ranges from $86,897 to $108,618.
The position was vacant following the departure of Stéphanie Colassin; the job posting was published internally and externally from April 7 to 13, 2026.
The expense, for the period from May 16 to December 31, 2026, is paid out of the operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is renewing for one year the mechanical maintenance contract awarded to Navada ltée, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
The contract covers two arenas and the patinoire Bleu Blanc Bouge, for $95,604.05, taxes included.
An additional amount of $29,000, taxes included, is being added to buy the parts and equipment needed for this maintenance.
The total expense comes to $124,604.05, taxes included, funded from the operating budget.
Last year, the same contract was renewed at $126,573.87, taxes included, plus $29,000 for parts.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is paying $9,300 (taxes included) to the Regroupement des éco-quartiers for the summer 2026 "Patrouille verte".
Environmental students will meet with citizens in parks and at public events in the borough.
The topics covered include: waste management, eco-citizenship, greening, water management, urban forest, and biodiversity.
The file description mentions 2 students for 12 weeks, while the financial section mentions the hiring of three students.
The project runs from June 1 to August 31, 2026, under the supervision of the Environment and Parks section.
The amount comes from the borough's operating budget and is not recurring.
In previous years, the contribution was $2,000 (summer 2024), $5,400 (2023), and $4,800 (2022 and 2021).

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding Urbex Construction inc. the landscaping of green alleys for $113,937.24, taxes included, with a total authorized expenditure of $168,877.83 ($17,090.59 in contingencies and $37,850 in incidental costs).

A new green alley will be laid out in the block bounded by rue Gilford, rue Mont-Royal, rue Christophe-Colomb and rue Boyer: about 160 m² of greening, flower beds, a stone-screening path, trees and rocks.
An existing green alley will be improved between rue Gilford, rue de Bienville, rue Mentana and rue Saint-André: about 145 m² of greening, new flower beds, trees, a path and planters.
The incidental costs cover, among other things, $23,000 for plants and horticultural materials, $5,000 for materials testing and $3,600 for furniture.
Urbex was the lowest of the 8 compliant bids, 26.65% below the borough's estimate ($154,600.27).
A start-up meeting is planned for June 2026 and work around August 2026; a notice will be distributed to residents before the work begins.
Maintenance and activities in the green alleys will be handled by the residents living along them.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding Biothec Foresterie inc. a stump removal contract worth $141,292.78, taxes included (net cost of $129,019.14).
The contract covers the removal of 300 stumps throughout the borough, filling the holes with planting soil and seeding them with grass.
The work starts within 5 days of the council resolution of April 13, 2026, and must be finished by August 31, 2026.
Biothec Foresterie submitted the lowest of the 5 compliant bids received (6 bids were submitted, 1 was found non-compliant), coming in $38,007.22 or 21.19% below the borough's estimate ($179,300).
The contract includes an option to renew for 12 months, subject to an agreement between the parties.
The borough says it does not have the staff and equipment to handle stump removal requests itself, requests linked in particular to trees cut down because of the emerald ash borer.
Affected residents received a door hanger giving the work period when the stump was marked; the information is also on montreal.ca.

The City is extending the emphyteutic lease of the Coopérative d'habitation de Sainte-Cécile, at 7342-7360, avenue de Gaspé, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, by 6 years: the agreement will run until December 20, 2056.
The annual rent will be $4,800 during the extension ($200 per unit, 24 units), for a total of $28,800; the City values the benefit granted at at least $519,000.
This extension allows the co-operative to obtain a loan amortized over 25 years from the Caisse d'économie solidaire Desjardins, which required a longer emphyteusis.
The money will go toward work estimated at $505,280 between 2026 and 2030: roofing, paving of the back yard, electrical upgrades to code, and floor renovations.
The co-operative will have to provide an inspection report every 5 years, a five-year work plan, its financial statements on request, and set up a maintenance reserve.
The building must keep its social and community purpose; 4 of the 24 units house households receiving federal rent assistance.
The deed is expected to be signed in spring-summer 2026.
The Sud-Ouest borough is renewing the lease of CPE Patapouf inc., which has occupied space in the parc Vinet chalet, at 560, rue Vinet, since October 1, 1986.
The lease covers 435.90 m² on the ground floor and the 2nd floor, for five years, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031.
The rent goes from $72,370.18 per year to $74,541.29 in the first year, then increases by 3% per year up to $83,896.87 in 2030-2031, for a total of $395,749.81 plus taxes.
The basement is not included in the lease: the CPE may store educational materials there, but the borough can take it back without notice.
The lease includes an option to renew for five more years.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding the firm Parizeau Pawulski Architectes a master agreement for architecture and engineering services, for a maximum of $732,787.41, taxes included.
The services will be used to upgrade or renovate the borough's buildings: libraries, community centres, sports centres, bathers' pavilions and park chalets.
The contract runs from August 11, 2026 to August 10, 2028, with a possible one-year extension until August 10, 2029, which would bring the estimated total to $1,166,478.86.
Assignments will be given as needs arise: plans and specifications, feasibility studies, cost estimates, worksite supervision, and analysis of reports on asbestos and lead, among others.
Eleven firms submitted bids; Parizeau Pawulski obtained the best final score and its price is 6.27% below the City's latest estimate ($781,807.01).
The expense is fully covered by the borough of Le Sud-Ouest, and the firm's performance will have to be evaluated, since the contract is over $500,000.
Rue Ontario Est will be closed to cars, from rue Darling to boulevard Pie-IX, from June 15 to September 18, 2026 — a seventh year of pedestrianization in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.
On the pedestrianized street and at Place Simon-Valois, the City is allowing the sale and consumption of food, goods and drinks, alcoholic or not, including on shared terraces.
To sell alcohol, a business must have a restaurant or bar use, obtain a permit from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux and mark off its terrace.
Businesses may put back, enlarge or set up café-terraces and sales counters on the roadway, with no platform or construction — and free of charge.
Noise from sound equipment playing outdoors is allowed on the street and at Place Simon-Valois during this period.
Signage (signs and banners on lampposts or walls) is allowed for public, cultural, tourism and community purposes, by the SDC Hochelaga-Maisonneuve with the borough's agreement.
The event programming is handled by the Société de développement commercial Hochelaga-Maisonneuve; the file has no financial aspect.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève is raising the rent paid to it by CPE La Campamuse by 5.4% for 2026.
The monthly rent goes from $2,991.45 to $3,152.99, plus taxes, which is $161.54 more per month.
The increase follows the January 2025 consumer price index for the Montréal region, as provided for in the lease.
The CPE rents the building at 265, boulevard Chevremont, in L'Île-Bizard, under a lease signed in 2023 that runs from January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2028.
The rent will again be indexed to the CPI in 2027 and in 2028.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève is recognizing a new non-profit organization: the Comité d'action des locataires de l'Ouest-de-l'Île (CALODI), with "supralocal" status.
The recognition runs from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
Thanks to this status, the organization can receive support from the borough: premises and rooms for its activities, financial support and promotional support.
In exchange, the organization must comply with the borough's policies and by-laws and submit to annual accountability reporting.
The file does not provide for any amount: the financial section indicates "N/A".
The borough will send a letter making the recognition and its terms official.
In April 2026, the borough council had already recognized or renewed 44 organizations for the same period.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is giving $40,000 to the organization Action jeunesse de l'Ouest-de-l'Île to extend the "Travail de rue et animation AJOI" project by one year.
The project covers the year 2026, from January 1 to December 31.
A street worker remains present in the borough's public spaces: parks, streets, commercial areas, restaurants, areas around schools, buses, open gyms.
The activities component continues in schools during the year and in parks during the summer.
The money comes from the Prévention Montréal program, which has $42.5M over three years, and is already included in the borough's operating budget.
Goals: reduce violence and delinquency, improve the feeling of safety, and make services better known to young people.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is adopting the second draft resolution PP-167, which would allow a residential building with a maximum of 20 units at 15825, rue Notre-Dame Est.
The project calls for the demolition of the vacant three-unit dwelling at 15825 to 15829, rue Notre-Dame Est, on a 1,153.70 m² lot at the corner of rue Antoine-Chaudillon.
The building may have up to 3 storeys and a height of 12.50 metres, cover a maximum of 52% of the lot, and be located at least 2.6 metres from rue Notre-Dame Est.
All parking must be indoors, with at least 0.75 space per unit; no outdoor spaces are allowed.
The developer must plant at least 3 trees, provide a landscaping plan signed by a landscape architect, and post a $15,000 bank guarantee for the green spaces.
Construction work must begin within 24 months after the resolution comes into force; the landscaping must be completed within 6 months after construction.
The council also takes note of the minutes of the public consultation meeting held on August 18, 2026.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving the plans for a residential project at 10985, boulevard Maurice-Duplessis, at the corner of 86e Avenue (La Pointe-aux-Prairies district).
The project: a three-storey building, 11.5 metres high, with five housing units, each with its own entrance and indoor garage.
The lots, currently vacant, total 1,412.70 m² and will have to be combined; the subdivision aims to create a horizontal co-ownership.
Nine trees will be planted along boulevard Maurice-Duplessis and 86e Avenue, in addition to shrubs and plantings around the entrances.
The site provides for five outdoor bicycle spaces and two outdoor parking spaces.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion by majority on March 13, 2026; the project had already been authorized by resolution PP-161 adopted on July 2, 2025.
The zone only allowed single-family housing; multi-family use was permitted through specific project PP-161.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles approves the conversion of the building at 12780, rue Notre-Dame Est to add a dwelling unit.
The ground-floor commercial space (formerly a paint store, then a computer business) becomes a dwelling unit.

The façade changes: a glazed residential door, commercial display windows replaced by three fixed windows, brown "barista" cladding instead of the dark green, and electric green elements repainted in neutral tones.
A window and a porch are added on the left side wall, and a patio door with a terrace at the rear.
The front parking space and the asphalt are removed in favour of landscaping; the parking is moved to the rear, with driving strips made of permeable paving stone.
Conditions imposed: plant a columnar tree in the front yard and deposit a $5,000 bank guarantee to secure the landscaping work.
The landscaping work must be completed within 12 months after the end of the work, not counting the period from November 15 to May 15.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving a minor exemption at 9300, boulevard Maurice-Duplessis, on the boulevard between 54e Avenue and avenue Lucien-Gendron.
The exemption allows a small building to be built in the front yard of an industrial building, which the zoning by-law normally prohibits.
This building, measuring 6.1 m by 7.9 m (48.19 m²) and 6.1 m high, will house a pump to increase water pressure on the site, in order to meet fire safety standards.
The company involved repairs rolling stock (railway cars); this use is no longer permitted in the zone, but it is protected by acquired rights.
The shelter will be located more than 32.7 metres from the street, and a row of conifers will be planted to hide it.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 10, 2026, and is asking that the use of a darker brick near the new plantings be studied.
At the meeting, no one in the audience wished to speak about the application.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving the plans to expand an industrial building at 9750, boulevard Maurice-Duplessis, in the Rivière-des-Prairies district.
The company, located on the site since 1960 and specializing in metal stamping and sheet metal manufacturing, is adding 2,791 m² on one storey, for a total of 8,962 m².
The current loading docks, which block 60e Avenue during deliveries, will be removed and replaced by a glassed-in alcove serving as a terrace for employees.
An outdoor storage area will be eliminated; the ground occupancy rate will reach 65.7%.
26 trees, along with shrubs and grasses, will be planted, mainly along the streets; a concrete curb will mark the boundary of the private property on 60e Avenue and formalize parallel parking.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme, which is in favour by a majority, is asking that the least allergenic tree species possible be chosen.
The project is based on specific project resolution PP-156 adopted on October 1, 2024.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is approving the signage plans for a Ford Fortier car dealership at 12345, boulevard Métropolitain Est, in the Pointe-aux-Trembles district.
Three illuminated signs will be mounted flat on the main façade: "Ford" (4.19 m²), "Fortier" (6.71 m²) and "Service" (3.92 m²).
Two double-sided illuminated signs will be added to the main pylon: "Ford" (17.38 m²) and "Fortier" (2.14 m²), for a total signage area of 34.34 m².
The two-storey building, built in 1988 and previously used for storage, has been converted to house the car dealership.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion by a majority; the Direction finds that the signs meet the design criteria and the specific project PP-165 adopted on February 3, 2026.
No amount is associated with this decision.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is renewing its graffiti removal contract with 9291-6287 Québec Inc. (Groupe R-Net) for one year, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
The authorized spending is $775,666.97 including taxes, of which $87,996.48 is for variations in quantities; the money comes from the borough's management surplus.
Graffiti removal on private properties remains free for owners, as it has been since 2006.
Graffiti is identified through calls to 311 and through rounds made by the graffiti officers.
The company must clean at least 2,000 m² per week; otherwise it pays a penalty of 50% of the unit price for each missing square metre.
Most of the work will be done from April to October; the rest will be used for urgent requests in winter.
The contract calls for biodegradable products with no solvents or VOCs, and limits the use of aerosols.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is renewing its contract with 9154-6937 Québec Inc. (Location Guay) for one year, to rent a backhoe with an operator, maintenance and accessories.
Total cost: $184,482.93, taxes included, at a rate of $175.94 per hour. The 2025 price ($180,511.67) is being indexed by 2.2%.
The contract runs from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
The machine is used to plant trees, to dig and enlarge planting pits, and to manage heeled-in trees within the borough.
The borough says it does not have the equipment or the workforce to do this work itself, and that its seasonal needs do not justify buying a backhoe.
The supplier received 96% on its performance evaluation, above the 70% threshold required for the renewal.

The City is registering four elements of the libraries' Coup de poing program as official marks: the logo and the phrases "collection Coup de poing," "animations Coup de poing" and "Coup de poing, des livres qui ébranlent."
The Service des affaires juridiques is mandated to file the applications with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office.
The expense amounts to $2,976.40, taxes included, paid out of the program's budget and assumed entirely by the central city.
Coup de poing has existed since 2007: a collection of picture books for young people on subjects such as grief, war, racism, violence or mental health disorders, with promotional tools.
According to the file, registration will allow the City to take legal action in the event of unauthorized use of the name or logo.
No communications activity is planned.
The City is transferring $1,879,500 from the local road reserve to the 2026 operating budget of the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité.
The money will pay for the first studies on replacing the viaduc Rosemont–Van Horne, which links Rosemont–La-Petite-Patrie and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
Three components are being funded: a feasibility study for a passage under the railway tracks, a preliminary design project, and a public consultation process.
Built in 1971, the viaduct is used by 22,000 people a day and is expected to reach the end of its useful life around 2030.
The schedule calls for studies from 2026 to 2029 and construction work from 2030 to 2033.
According to the file, without these funds in 2026, the studies cannot begin and the risk of an unplanned closure of the viaduct increases.
The expense is being covered 100% by the central city.
The City is adding $388,954.57 (net) to the 2026 operating budget of the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité to pay for an environmental and geotechnical characterization study.
The study concerns the Parc d'entreprises de la Pointe-Saint-Charles – Bonaventure project, in the Bridge-Bonaventure area, where the City wants to build a new street grid.
The site is a former waste landfill, recognized as contaminated and as a source of biogas; the study is required to obtain the provincial authorization certificate.
The contract awarded to the firm GHD totals $425,955.97 including taxes and contingencies.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, from the reserve for the Passif environnemental des sites contaminés (environmental liability for contaminated sites).
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité will have to report on the spending every quarter to the Service de l'environnement.
Planned schedule: study in 2026, work from 2027 to 2029.
The City is moving $6,000,000 from its 2026 capital budget for the Service de l'eau to the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité.
The money goes to the redevelopment of rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest, phase 2, between rue Mansfield and rue Atwater.
The transfer is meant to follow the contractor's new work schedule (public call for tenders 503001), which would allow the work to move ahead faster.
The amount comes from the program for secondary water and sewer networks, whose 2026 budget goes from $184,042,000 to $178,042,000, thanks to the postponement of some projects.
The 2026 budget for the Sainte-Catherine Ouest project goes from $29,200,000 to $35,200,000.
The transfer adds no net spending: the overall budget envelope stays the same.
The file is being reviewed behind closed doors by the executive committee on April 29, 2026.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing 36 public events (35 approved, 1 ratified) and 39 performances under the Programme de soutien aux actions culturelles on its public property in 2026.
Organizers will be allowed to temporarily occupy streets, parks and public squares, at the locations and times detailed in the tables attached to the file.
Orders lift certain municipal rules: noise from sound equipment outdoors, the sale of promotional items, food and drinks (alcoholic or not), and the temporary closure of boulevards and traffic lanes.
The events are free and open to everyone, according to the borough.
The City covers support for the events out of its operating budgets; the costs and risks of the projects are paid by the promoters.
Each promoter must provide civil liability insurance that also covers the City and, if a street is closed, must put up signs 10 days before the event.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $36,600 to Maison de l'Amitié de Montréal to hold three farmers' markets during the summers of 2026 and 2027 ($18,300 per year).
Marché Saint-Louis: Tuesdays from 3 p.m. to 7 p.m., from June 2 to October 27, 2026, at square Saint-Louis, on the rue Saint-Denis side.
Marché Baldwin: Wednesdays from 3 p.m. to 7:30 p.m., from June 3 to October 28, 2026, at terrasse Mercure, between rue Chapleau and rue Fullum.
Marché Laurier: Thursdays from 3 p.m. to 7 p.m. from May 14 to November 12, 2026, and Sundays from 12 p.m. to 4 p.m. from May 17 to November 15, at place du Côteau-Saint-Louis.
The 2027 dates have yet to be determined.
The increase of $1,300 per year is meant to boost the markets at parc Baldwin and to pay for support from the Association des marchés publics du Québec.
The organization gets to occupy public property free of charge and must submit a progress report on January 30, 2027 and January 30, 2028.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is providing technical and financial support of up to $7,800, all taxes included, to the organization Les Productions Funambules Médias.
This money is for holding the Cinéma sous les étoiles 2026 festival, from June 25 to August 5, 2026.
Six evenings of documentary film screenings followed by discussions will take place on Wednesdays, at parc Sir-Wilfrid-Laurier, parc des Compagnons-de-Saint-Laurent and parc Baldwin.
The first evening launches the program with a short show; a gala evening will hand out awards for a short film competition.
The amount includes free rental for the use of public property and technical support.
The organization must submit its accounting report on September 5, 2026.
Support of the same amount had been granted to the same organization in June 2025 for the 2025 edition.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing 7 public events on public property: 3 are approved in advance and 4 are ratified after the fact.
The locations and schedules for each event are listed in a table attached to the file.
The City is allowing the use of sound equipment outdoors for these events, despite the noise by-law.
Organizers will be allowed to sell promotional items, food and drinks, alcoholic or not, at the event sites.
Streets, boulevards and traffic lanes may be closed temporarily; organizers must post notice of the closures 10 days in advance.
The costs and risks of the events are borne by the organizers; the City's support is covered by existing operating budgets.
Each organizer must provide civil liability insurance that names the Ville de Montréal as a co-insured party.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing 11 public events to occupy public property: 6 approved and 5 ratified (sites and schedules are in the table attached to the file).
The council is allowing noise from sound equipment broadcasting outdoors for each of these events.
It is also allowing the sale of promotional items, food and drinks, alcoholic or not, at the sites.
Boulevards and traffic lanes may be temporarily closed for the events.
Promoters must post the closed streets and the closing times ten days before the event, and provide civil liability insurance that also covers the Ville.
The costs of the Ville's support are covered by the operating budgets; the costs and risks of the projects are borne by the promoters.
Events on public property are free and open to everyone.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is ending its agreement with the organization MURAL for the mural "Toucher l'horizon," which was to be painted at 5450, chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges.
The project fell through because the wall's owner turned down the artistic proposal after the fact.
The borough and the Service de la culture offered extra time to postpone the project to 2026 with a new wall, but the organization did not submit an application.
The planned contribution was $20,000; $18,000 was paid to MURAL on August 7, 2025.
MURAL will receive a notice of termination and will have to repay the unused amounts, with supporting documents.
The unpaid balance of $2,000 and the recovered amounts will go back into the budget of the borough's Division culture et bibliothèques.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $10,000 to the organization Notre-Dame-des-Arts for the Semaine des arts, in the summer of 2026.
The event is planned for August 2026, with creative workshops, exhibitions, artistic activities in the streets and parks, including parc Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, and the Parade Fête à la main.
The program is mainly aimed at families, children and young people, and is part of the 150th anniversary of Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The money comes from the 2026 operating budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The organization must hand in the signed artist contracts by September 30, 2026 and its report by October 31, 2026.
The organization handles its own communications and must mention the support of the Ville and the borough.
The borough had given $12,000 to the same organization in 2025 and $10,500 in 2024 for the Parade Fête à la main.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is giving $53,000 to ten non-profit organizations for 12 projects marking the 150th anniversary of the Notre-Dame-de-Grâce neighbourhood.
The projects will take place between July 7 and December 31, 2026.
The largest amounts go to Notre-Dame-des-Arts ($10,000 for a mosaic in the tunnel Melrose) and to Dépôt alimentaire NDG ($7,500 for "Imaginer ensemble").
Five projects each receive $5,000: Jeunesse Loyola, Bienvenue à NDG, Biz NDG, and two projects from P.A.A.L. Partageons le monde; Espoir Nouveau also receives $5,000.
Smaller amounts: Carrefour Jeunesse-Emploi de NDG ($2,500), Conseil communautaire NDG ($1,500 and $500) and the NDG minor baseball league ($1,000).
The call for projects launched on January 19, 2026 had received 19 applications totalling $145,848.59; the spending is funded by the borough's unallocated surplus.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is ending its agreement with the organization MURAL for the mural "Échos d'un quartier" (or "Ode au quartier"), which was to be painted at 3435, avenue Lacombe.
Reason given: MURAL was unable to confirm a suitable wall, despite a postponement to 2026 and deadlines set for February 17 and then March 2, 2026.
The planned contribution was $12,500, of which $11,250 had already been paid to the organization on August 7, 2025.
The borough will ask for the unused amounts to be repaid, upon submission of supporting documents.
The unpaid balance of $1,250 and the amounts recovered will go back into the budget of the Division culture et bibliothèques.
The order that allowed the mural despite the by-law on graffiti is repealed.
In April 2026, the borough had already cancelled another agreement with MURAL, for the mural "Toucher l'horizon".

The City is entering into a 5-year framework agreement with Simco Technologies inc. (formerly Cosigma inc.) for structural engineering services at Service de l'eau facilities, for an estimated amount of $3,607,196.91, taxes included.
The contract itself is worth $3,216,425.63, plus $229,950 in contingencies and $160,821.28 in incidental costs.
The agreement can be extended by 2 years, for an additional estimated amount of $1,378,550.25.

The firm will assess the condition of concrete structures affected by the alkali-aggregate reaction and design reinforcements or repairs: 6 treatment plants, 14 reservoirs, 9 booster pumping stations and 3 chlorination stations.
Of the 14 companies that obtained the tender documents, 4 submitted bids and only one bid remained compliant; the City negotiated the price, which remains 19.57% ($564,004.11) above its estimate.
The expense is covered by the urban agglomeration, since drinking water production is an agglomeration responsibility; the firm's performance will be evaluated.

The borough of Ville-Marie is asking city council to let it take charge itself of the planing and repaving of roadways and minor sidewalk repairs on sections of the arterial road network in its territory.

The planned work: planing, a new layer of asphalt, repair of defects in the foundation and in paving-stone roadways, levelling of frames and covers, and sidewalk repairs (concrete, granite, paving stone, etc.).
The work is planned for 2026 and 2027 and covers, among others, segments required for the UCI Road World Championships, from September 20 to 27, 2026 in Montréal.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier (SIRR) is fully funding the work and the professional services; no amount is set out in the document.
The borough will have to have its plans and specifications approved by the SIRR, obtain the authorizations before the work, provide the final plans and report on expenses and schedules.
The borough undertakes not to exceed the authorized credits without the prior agreement of the municipal bodies.
The City cites the maintenance backlog on Ville-Marie's arterial network and the desire to avoid the delays of centralized calls for tenders.
The executive committee is delegating to a level A official of the Service de la stratégie immobilière the power to waive the City's right of first refusal, regardless of the value of the building.
The same official will also be able to use the right of first refusal to buy a building worth $150,000 or less, as is already allowed for by-agreement purchases.
The right of first refusal allows the City to buy certain targeted buildings ahead of any other buyer, for projects such as social housing, affordable housing, regional parks or planning areas.

The City says it wants to shorten response times for citizens: at present, no waiver files are prepared and sellers and buyers generally wait for the 60-day legal deadline to expire before closing their transaction.
The official will also be able to request the cancellation, in the land register, of the notice that the building is subject to the right of first refusal.
No financial impact is expected and no communications activities are planned.
The City is paying $795,000 to the Chambre de commerce de l'Est de Montréal for a partnership to revitalize the East End, from February 2026 to December 2028.
The payment is made in instalments: $300,000, $350,000, $100,000 and $45,000.
The money goes to three areas: support for priority projects in the East End, economic mobilization events (including the Sommet de l'Est 2027), and hosting delegations and investors.
The area covered is east of boulevard Saint-Laurent, where the Chambre says it represents 1,250 members and 32,000 businesses.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration; the funds come from the budget of the Service du développement économique.
The City and the organization have set targets and indicators that are assessed each year, and a visibility protocol applies.
In 2023, the City had granted $300,000 to the same Chambre for the D'est en Est project.
The City is giving $5,407,736 to 15 community organizations for new projects related to homelessness, over three years, until December 31, 2028.
It is adding $3,942,461 to 10 organizations already funded in August 2025, bringing their total support to $9,477,116.
An amount of $42,667 is also going to Dîners St-Louis for its Fête de quartier project, decided by the executive committee.

The projects deal with including people experiencing homelessness, sharing public space and raising awareness, in areas such as downtown, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Pointe-aux-Trembles, Verdun, le Sud-Ouest, Centre-Sud and the Quartier chinois.
The funded organizations include: Accueil Bonneau, Mission Bon Accueil, Maison du Père, La rue des Femmes, Plein Milieu, Spectre de rue, Sentier urbain, les YMCA du Québec and En Marge 12-17.
The City says it is tripling its budget for the fight against homelessness in 2026; the expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
The 16 new projects had been judged relevant in July 2025, but had not been selected because of a lack of budget.
The City is giving $515,000 to Montréal International to attract and keep international organizations in Montréal in 2026, in a single payment.
Of this amount, $215,000 goes to the operations of the vice-presidency for international organizations and $300,000 to attracting new organizations.
Montréal International will also be able to use $47,449 in contributions from past years that had not been spent as of December 31, 2025.
The organization must give the City the documents showing how the money was used and keep a City representative on the FODIM advisory committee.
The main project targeted in 2026 is attracting the head office of the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB), which could create up to 3,500 jobs over 5 years.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration of Montréal; the same amount of $515,000 was granted in 2024 and 2025.
The City is paying $65,000 to the Conseil des relations internationales de Montréal (CORIM) for the year 2026 only, as a pilot project.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city; any additional or multi-year support will have to be assessed separately.

This amount matches the cost of renting CORIM's offices, which the City had been paying up to now at 1550, rue Metcalfe (estimated value of $65,750 net of taxes in 2025). This support in the form of office space ended when the lease ended.
In exchange, the City gets the status of "Grand partenaire institutionnel", access to the head table for 10 events and up to 80 tickets for activities in the 2025-2026 to 2027-2028 seasons.
The City is also the exclusive presenter of the "Initiatives urbaines" theme and has its logo displayed on CORIM's website and documents.
CORIM, a non-profit organization founded in 1985, holds more than 35 events a year on international issues.
The organization must follow a visibility protocol and report on how the funds are used.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the Communauté grecque orthodoxe de la région Sud-Ouest de Montréal to hold its annual Easter procession on April 10, 2026, from 7:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.
The route starts at the église orthodoxe grecque Saint-Dionysios (7707, boulevard LaSalle) and goes along boulevard LaSalle, 8e Avenue, rue Édouard and 6e Avenue before returning to the church.
No street will be closed to traffic; the procession will take place under the supervision of the Service de police.
An outdoor mass will be held on April 11, 2026, from 11:45 p.m. to 12:15 a.m., in the parking lot in front of the church.
The borough does not expect any financial commitment in this matter.
Religious organizations are no longer recognized under LaSalle's organization support policy, but a grandfather clause allows them to continue receiving the same services.
The borough of LaSalle is allowing the paroisse Saint-Nazaire to hold a religious procession on Sunday, April 12, 2026, from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m.
The route starts at 111, avenue Bélanger and goes along avenue Bélanger, rue Centrale, rue Stinson and rue Airlie, before returning to the starting point.
No street will be closed: participants will be escorted by patrol cars from the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal.
The event involves no expense for the borough, since no loan of equipment is requested.
This is the third year in a row that this procession has been authorized (2024, 2025, 2026).
Religious organizations are no longer recognized under LaSalle's support policy for recreation organizations, but a grandfather clause keeps the same services available to them.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the paroisse Madre dei Cristiani to hold a Good Friday procession on April 3, 2026, from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m.
The route starts at 7935, rue Lefebvre and follows rue Thierry, rue Verdi, rue Robert, rue Proulx, rue Denise and rue Tétrault, before returning to the starting point.
No street will be closed to traffic, but patrol cars will escort participants along the entire route.
The procession takes place under the control of the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal.
No expense is involved: the borough is not lending any equipment.
The parish keeps access to the same services as before thanks to a grandfather clause, even though religious organizations are no longer recognized by the borough.

The LaSalle borough is authorizing Association Gurdwara Guru Nanak Darbar inc. (Association du Temple Sikh) to hold a procession on Sunday, May 17, 2026, from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m., for the Khalsa celebration.
Rues Cordner, Lapierre, Juliette, Préville, Danièle and Gervais will be closed to traffic between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m., then reopened gradually behind the parade.
The SPVM will oversee the street closures and the safety of participants and drivers.
The borough is providing free services valued at $4,000.
A letter will be sent to residents along the route to inform them of the street closures and the schedule.
The council is granting an exemption from section 287 of by-law 2030 on public safety, which governs parades and processions.
The organization has been filing such a request since 1996; as a religious organization, it keeps an acquired right to the support it received in 2014.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing école Notre-Dame-des-Rapides to hold its RAPIDOMÈTRES run on Thursday, May 28, 2026, a one-kilometre loop through the schoolyard and the nearby streets.
36e Avenue and rue George between 36e and 41e Avenue will be closed to traffic between 8 a.m. and 1 p.m.
No-parking signs will be put up on May 27 along the route; the borough is lending 12 crowd-control barriers and will send a street sweeper.
The SPVM will look after the safety of participants and drivers during the street closures.
The school will hand out a notice to affected residents at least 10 days before the event, around May 18.
The borough is providing these services free of charge, at an estimated value of $750.
About 350 students and parents are expected; this is the third edition of the activity.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing école primaire Henri-Forest to hold its Course des couleurs on Friday, June 19, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 10 a.m., with its 375 students.
Four streets around the school will be closed and parking will be banned from 7 a.m. to 12 p.m.: avenue du Trésor-Caché, rue Centrale, avenue Bélanger and rue Airlie.
The SPVM will ensure the safety of participants and drivers while the streets are closed.

The borough is lending 15 crowd-control barriers, putting up the no-parking signs on June 18, sweeping the streets before the race and cleaning up the coloured powder afterwards, in front of 100, avenue du Trésor-Caché.
These services are provided free of charge, for an estimated value of $750.
The school agrees to hand out a notice to residents of the affected streets at least 10 days beforehand, that is, on June 9.
This is the fifth year in a row that the school has organized this race.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the paroisse Madre dei Cristiani to sell roses on Sunday, May 10, 2026, for Mother's Day.
The sale will take place in front of the church, at 7935, rue Lefebvre.
The profits will be used to provide financial support to the church and its activities.
No cost to the borough: the parish is not asking to borrow any equipment.
Religious organizations are no longer recognized by LaSalle, but a grandfather clause lets them keep the same services as before.
The City is giving $15,000 to Université Laval for a research project on bumblebees in 2026.
The study looks at the effect of climate change on bumblebees and at the potential of treed flower strips to strengthen their resilience.
The money covers logistical costs (travel, field equipment) and partly supports a graduate student.
The research is being done in an agricultural setting, but its findings are meant to help better design urban spaces for pollinators.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, through the Service de l'Espace pour la vie (Insectarium).
The agreement ends on December 31, 2026. No communication activities are planned.
The file is being reviewed behind closed doors by the executive committee on February 25, 2026.
The borough of Anjou is awarding a contract for hydro-excavation services, including the handling of residual materials, to 9083-0126 Québec Inc. (Creusage RL).
The contract is worth $257,141.59 including taxes; with $25,714.16 in contingencies, the authorized spending reaches $282,855.75.
The work covers 34 months, from March 4, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with no possible extension.
Each year, the contract provides for 210 hours of regular work (including 75 guaranteed hours), 30 hours for emergency calls and 75 tonnes of residual materials to be hauled and disposed of.
These services are used to maintain the sewer and water supply systems in places with restricted access, as the borough does not own this equipment.
Five companies submitted bids for lot 7; Creusage RL is the lowest compliant bidder, 4.42% below the City's estimate.
The City will assess the company's performance at the end of the contract.
The borough of Anjou is extending by six months its contract with Pavages Chartrand inc. for the rental of a grader with an operator, used for snow clearing and snow loading.
The extension costs a maximum of $104,511.18, taxes included, which is $95,010.17 for the contract and $9,501.02 set aside for unforeseen costs.
With this addition, the total spending on the contract goes from $203,190.72 to $307,701.90, taxes included.
The extension covers the 2026-2027 winter season, from November 15, 2026 to April 15, 2027.
The borough explains that it does not own all the equipment needed for snow removal and that the rental includes maintenance and accessories.
According to the document, refusing the extension would cause delays in snow clearing and snow loading.
The City is awarding a direct contract of $190,612 (before taxes) to the non-profit organization Nature-Action Québec for two years.
The organization will hold advisory committee meetings, along with information and public participation activities for residents, merchants and groups in the Île-Bizard area.
It will also carry out the conservation plan: tracking biodiversity targets, awareness projects, and getting citizens, farmers and landowners involved in voluntary conservation.
The contract covers the western portion of île Bizard, which Québec has designated a "projected humanized landscape" since 2021.
The expense is paid 100% by a grant from the ministère de l'Environnement (MELCCFP) and is borne by the urban agglomeration.
The contract starts in June 2026 and ends in March 2028 ($95,597 in 2026-2027, $95,015 in 2027-2028).
The submitted price is 8.91% lower than the internal estimate of $209,265.40.
The City is entering into a negotiated agreement with Mabarex inc. for $1,831,254.25 (taxes included) to buy 20-kilowatt UV lamps.
These lamps are used in the ultraviolet reactors that disinfect drinking water at the Atwater and Charles-J.-Des Baillets plants.
The agreement lasts 36 months, starting June 18, 2026, with two possible 12-month extensions, until December 31, 2030 at the latest.
About 375 lamps are planned in total: 225 for the first three years and 150 more during the extensions, with the supplier requiring a minimum of 75 lamps per year.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders: Mabarex is the exclusive distributor in Québec and no other company responded to the notice of intent published from April 23 to May 8, 2026.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration, since drinking water production falls under its jurisdiction.
The City will assess the supplier's performance.
The City is awarding Mécanique Northerm inc. a contract worth $935,681.50 (taxes included) to replace the oil heating system at the SPVM cavalry station, at 1515, chemin Remembrance.
With contingencies ($187,136.30) and incidentals ($187,136.30), the total authorized spending comes to $1,309,954.10.
The work includes an electric boiler, a heat pump, new ventilated radiators, replacement of the hot water pipes and removal of the fuel oil and diesel tanks in the basement.
The project is part of action 24 of the Plan climat 2020-2030, which aims to eliminate fuel oil in municipal buildings.
A grant from the Québec green economy program covers 80% of the amount; the remaining expense is paid by the urban agglomeration.
The contract is to start on April 28, 2026 and end on September 30, 2027; the company's performance will be evaluated.
Seven companies submitted bids; the lowest compliant bid is 33% ($455,911.10) below the professionals' estimate.
The City is transferring $6,700,000 from the Direction générale to the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers, as part of the 2026 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The money will be used to pay for vehicle purchases that have already been approved but did not have enough budget to go ahead.
Some vehicles ordered for 2025 were not delivered on time because of supply delays; the deliveries have been pushed back to 2026.
The amount is taken from a provision (Programmes / projets d'immobilisations) and paid into the City's vehicle replacement program.
According to the document, this transfer has no impact on the City's financial framework.
The file goes to the executive committee on March 11, 2026, and is being reviewed behind closed doors.
The City is awarding Distributions Maranda inc. the supply and installation of telescopic cranes with dump bodies on truck chassis that the City itself provides.
The contract is worth $1,219,955.67 including taxes, plus a contingency reserve of $243,991.13, for a total expense of $1,463,946.80.
Four units are being ordered: two cranes on regular-cab chassis and two on extended-cab chassis, to be delivered within 425 to 635 days.
A late delivery results in a penalty of 2% per month on the value of the goods not delivered; the company guarantees parts, labour and transportation.
Distributions Maranda was the lower of the two bidders: its price is 62.10% below that of the second bidder and 22.07% below the City's estimate.
The equipment will be used for borough operations and will replace obsolete machines; the expense is paid 100% by the central city through a loan by-law.
The company's performance will be evaluated; the purchase order is expected at the end of May 2026.
The City is transferring $5,400,000 from the Direction générale to the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers, within the 2026 capital works program.
The money will be used to pay for equipment purchases that were already approved, whose delivery was planned for 2025 but has been pushed back to 2026 because of supply delays.
The purchases involved: ice resurfacers for the boroughs' arenas, specialized vehicles for the SPVM and the Service de sécurité incendie, and jacks for the mechanical workshops.
The document states that this transfer has no impact on the City's financial framework.
No communications activities are planned; the decision falls to the executive committee.
The Saint-Léonard borough council takes note of the filing of a revised report on the housing project authorizations granted in 2025 under section 93 of the Québec housing act.
The report filed on March 9, 2026 left out the projects authorized by the city council; two projects of this type were authorized in 2025, and no application was refused.
The report must describe the exemptions from urban planning rules that were granted and the number of housing units built or created thanks to these authorizations.

Three projects had been authorized by the borough in 2025: a 14-storey mixed-use building at Jean-Talon Est and Viau, a 5-storey residential building at Bélanger and d'Avila on city-owned land, and a 10-storey mixed-use building at Jean-Talon Est and Buies.
The report will be sent to the minister responsible for housing by the Service de l'habitation and published on the Ville's website.
The borough of Saint-Léonard approves the plans for modifying an exterior wall of the Carrefour Langelier shopping centre, at 7373, boulevard Langelier (Saint-Léonard-Est district).
The work consists of building two walls to close off the side and rear façades after the partial demolition of the building.
The new side wall will be about 20 metres long and will be visible from parc du Boisé-Jean-Milot and boulevard Langelier.
The cladding will be ivory-coloured vertical metal siding, identical to that of the existing walls.
According to the urban planning department, the relationship between the building and the street stays the same until the next phases of the site's redevelopment.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on March 12, 2026.
The Le Plateau-Mont-Royal borough council authorizes its borough secretary (or their replacement) to sign the federal funding agreement on short-term rentals.
The funding comes from Logement, Infrastructures et Collectivités Canada, through its Short-Term Rental Enforcement Fund, and was granted to the Ville de Montréal.
The agreement totals $3,131,332: $1,565,666 for 2025-2026 and $1,565,666 for 2026-2027. It takes effect upon signing and ends on June 30, 2027.

The money can be used to raise public awareness, handle complaints, manage permits and registration, carry out investigations and inspections, issue warnings and statements of offence, and support court proceedings.
Signing the agreement allows the borough to access the funds to control and monitor illegal tourist rentals on its territory.
Public communications about this funding must be coordinated with the federal government.
In 2025, the council had already authorized the signing of the funding application (resolution CA25 0140).

Notice of motion: the City announces that it will later adopt a by-law amending the rules for delegating maintenance of the main water and sewer system to the related cities in the urban agglomeration.
The amendment updates Appendix D, the rate schedule for agglomeration equipment and vehicles (revision 13, dated February 16, 2026), to reflect the 2025 consumer price index adjustment.
The schedule sets hourly rates by type of equipment, for example $115.74/h for a sewer flusher truck and $293.11/h for a 7 cu. yd. wheel loader.
The Fonds de l'eau reimburses the related cities for the costs of maintaining and repairing the delegated main system infrastructure.
A technical committee made up of five members from Montréal and four from the other related municipalities recommends the changes.
Once adopted, the by-law and its appendices will be sent to the boroughs and the related cities.
The Société de transport de Montréal (STM) wants to borrow $45,800,000 over 20 years to repair and replace parts of its metro and bus infrastructure.
The full cost of the program comes to $46,000,000, with $200,000 taken from the operating budget.
The money would be split between the metro ($27.5M) and the bus network ($18.3M): architectural features, structures, mechanical and electrical systems.
The STM says it lacks funding envelopes for small urgent interventions, particularly cases deemed critical that are found during its inspections.
Québec could cover $28,556,574 through the SOFIL program; a grant application must be submitted to the ministère des Transports. The non-subsidizable share is estimated at $13,399,623 (29%).
The STM expects impacts on metro and bus service during the work.
The decision rests with the urban agglomeration council, which must also approve a change to the Programme des immobilisations 2026-2035.
The STM wants to borrow $11,159,588 to launch the start-up phase of the program to replace the MR-73 metro cars and the train control system.
The money is used to define the need, document the options and plan the studies — not yet to buy trains.
The 40 MR-73 trains, purchased between 1976 and 1980, have had their life extended to 2036, but the STM says they are up to 11 times less reliable than the Azur trains.
Delivery of the first new trains is now expected around 2040, since this kind of project spreads over more than 15 years.
The program must also look at the end of life of train control on the orange, green and yellow lines, increasing the network's capacity and securing the platforms.
Québec has included the project in its infrastructure plan with a contribution of $39.6M (2025-2035), including $9.4M for 2025-2028.
The urban agglomeration council is also asked to approve an amendment to the STM's 2026-2035 Capital Works Program.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing a new series of events on public property for the 2026 season (3rd part A), at the sites, dates and times listed in the appendix.
Organizers will be allowed to close streets, occupy parks, plazas or squares, and paint or draw on the roadway in the designated locations.
Music and outdoor sound equipment are permitted, up to a maximum of 75 dBA and 90 dBC measured 5 metres from the speakers; megaphones remain prohibited, except for safety purposes.
The sale and consumption of food, promotional items and beverages (alcoholic or not) are permitted at the sites concerned; containers must be plastic and recyclable materials must be collected.
Organizers will also be allowed to attach things to street furniture and hand out sponsors' samples, at booths set up for that purpose.
Each promoter must keep its written authorization on site and provide its civil liability insurance endorsement before the event.
The ordinances take effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir; the costs of the City's support are absorbed by existing operating budgets.
The borough of Ville-Marie is approving a series of events on public property for the 2026 season (part 4A), at the sites and times listed in the appendix.

For these events, the City is temporarily lifting several by-laws: noise from outdoor sound equipment, street closures, the sale and consumption of alcohol and food, painting on the roadway, posting notices on street furniture, and handing out sponsors' samples.
Noise is capped at 75 dBA and 90 dBC (measured 5 metres from the equipment); megaphones remain banned, except for safety purposes.
Food and drinks must be served in plastic containers, and recyclable materials must be collected.
Organizers must be able to show their written authorization on site at all times, and must provide proof of civil liability insurance before receiving it.
The events are local in scale, free of charge and open to everyone; the costs of city services are covered by existing operating budgets.
The orders take effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir, in May 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is approving a new series of events on public property for the 2026 season (part 5A), at the locations, dates and times listed in the appendix.
Organizers will be allowed to close streets and occupy parks, squares and plazas for the duration of their events.
Noise from outdoor sound equipment is permitted, up to 75 dBA and 90 dBC measured at 5 metres; megaphones remain banned except for safety purposes.
Selling and consuming food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks and promotional items is permitted at these sites; plastic containers and recycling collection are mandatory.
It also becomes permitted to paint on the roadway, attach things to street furniture and hand out sponsor samples at booths set up for that purpose.
Organizers must be able to show their written authorization at all times and provide a civil liability insurance endorsement.
The events are free and local in scale; the costs of city services are covered by existing operating budgets.

The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing a series of local events to use public property (parks, squares, plazas, streets) during the 2026 season, on the dates, at the sites and during the hours listed in the appendix.
This is the 6th batch of events approved for 2026: community, sports, cultural, commemorative or festive activities, free of charge and open to everyone.
Organizers will be able to close streets, play sound outdoors, sell and allow the consumption of food and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks, paint on the roadway and set up sponsor booths.
Sound is limited to 75 dBA and 90 dBC, measured 5 metres from the equipment; megaphones remain prohibited except for safety purposes.
Food and drinks must be served in plastic containers, and recyclable materials must be collected.
Organizers must be able to show their written authorization at all times and provide proof of civil liability insurance.
The costs of the municipal services required are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved; the ordinances take effect on the day they are published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension wants to install a materials lift (type B) at the Centre Ogilvy, at 7405, avenue Champagneur.

The equipment will be used by the organization Cuisines et vie collectives Saint-Roch, whose kitchen is on the 2nd floor of a building with no elevator: employees climb 34 steps several times a day to hand out food to more than 150 families, three times a week.
The work includes modifying the stairs, some demolition, partial rearrangement of interior spaces, new metal shelving in the food storage area and temporary partitions to control dust.

The building also houses a fire station, which falls under the urban agglomeration's authority: this is why the urban agglomeration council must authorize the work before the construction contract is awarded.
The borough will pay all of the costs, since the work affects only the community spaces.
Three professional services contracts have already been awarded (Groupe Geniex, ARI Bureau d'Études, Riopel + associés architectes) and a public call for tenders has been launched for the work.
Work is expected to start in the summer of 2026; the building will remain occupied during construction.
The City is giving $15,000 to the organization Vivre en Ville to organize the 10th edition of the Rendez-vous Collectivités viables.
The event will take place on June 18, 2026 at the marché Bonsecours, on the theme "S'adapter - Pour des communautés résilientes".
The gathering is aimed at elected officials, specialists and civil society, and deals with adapting to climate change (floods, heat, ice storms, forest fires).
The amount represents 5% of the event's total budget and gives the City the status of Platinum partner, with the visibility set out in its protocol.
An agreement with the organization sets out the payment conditions; the expense is paid entirely by the central city.
The City has been financially supporting this event since 2017; it gave $15,000 in 2024 and in 2025.
The agglomeration is adding $303,927.75 (taxes included) to a contract to buy chemical products from Kemira Water Solutions Canada inc., bringing the agreement to $883,374.16.
The money is used to buy more acidified aluminum sulphate 5%, a product used to treat water at the Pointe-Claire drinking water production plant.
As of January 1, 2026, about 80% of the quantities planned under the contract had already been used; the reserves were not enough to finish the year.
The rise in consumption is explained by the increase in the volume of water treated and by the longer use of the product, from June to December 2025 instead of four months in the summer.
Neither the unit price, nor the nature of the product, nor the length of the agreement changes: only the quantities increase, until December 31, 2026.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration, out of the operating budget of the Direction de l'eau potable.
The Service de l'eau says it ruled out two other options: reducing the doses (a risk to water quality) and buying outside the contract (higher costs and longer delays).
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding 9083-0126 Québec inc. (Creusage RL) a contract of $520,836.75, taxes included, for hydro-excavation services during water main and sewer work.
The contract runs about 33 months: it starts on the date of the borough council resolution and ends on December 31, 2028.
The contract includes the rental of a hydro-excavation truck with an operator, as well as the transportation and disposal of 200 tonnes of residue per year at an authorized site.
The planned hours increase each year: 400 h of regular calls in 2026, 420 h in 2027, 440 h in 2028, plus 50 h of emergency calls per year.
Creusage RL was the lowest of the three compliant bidders, ahead of Sanivac ($598,950.77) and G-Tek ($709,165.80); one bid was rejected for lack of the appropriate RBQ licence.
The borough says it does not have the staff or the specialized equipment to do this work itself.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is renting four types of cleaning equipment with an operator, for three years (2026 to 2028), at a total cost of $921,524.63, taxes included.
Balai Le Permanent inc. receives $349,753.95 for a vacuum sweeper (street cleaning, 900 hours, from April 1 to December 1).
Balaye-Pro inc. receives $42,540.75 for a mechanical sweeper used to clean back lanes (100 hours, in the spring and fall).
Entretiens J.R. Villeneuve inc. receives $341,245.80 for a compact sweeper for pedestrian streets and bike paths (800 hours, from May to November).
Les Équipements Benco Canada Ltée receives $187,984.13 for two sidewalk-washing tractors used for the spring and fall cleanup (500 hours).
Six companies bid on public call for tenders 25-21204; the contracts go to the lowest compliant bidders for each lot.
The borough says it does not have enough staff or equipment to do this work itself; the prior estimate was $920,000.

The City is renting pumps and accessories from Industries Toromont ltée (Location d'équipement Battlefield) to deal with spring flooding, from April 23 to June 23, 2026, with the option to renew for one year.
