Total authorized spending of $578,002.78 including taxes: $444,617.52 for the contract, plus $66,692.63 in contingencies and $66,692.63 for variations in quantities.
The pumps are used to drain rainwater when the level of the rivière des Prairies rises, in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Pierrefonds-Roxboro and Ahuntsic-Cartierville.
Seven installation sites are planned, including parc de la Rive boisée, pont Jacques-Bizard, the Pierrefonds drinking water plant, the Lavigne pumping station and parc Cardinal.
Only one bid was received for this lot, at 42.52% above the City's estimate; the attempt to negotiate a lower price went nowhere.
A first call for tenders (25-21223) had been cancelled because all the bidders were found to be non-compliant.
The City will use the equipment only if the situation requires it; the contract is awarded with no budget charge.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding Romcobat Bâtiments inc. a $282,493.58 contract (taxes included) to replace the windows of the chalet in parc Clifford, in Côte-Saint-Paul.
The total authorized spending comes to $385,804.37: the contract, plus $42,374.04 in contingencies (15%) and $60,936.75 in incidental costs (air infiltration testing, alarm systems, communications).
The work includes removing the windows on the south façades, installing curtain walls, windows and emergency exit doors, ceiling work and replacing joists.

The original windows are in poor condition: some sections are boarded up with plywood and the garage doors are sealed shut. The work will make it possible to open the chalet to the public for 3 seasons.
Romcobat was the lowest of 5 bidders, at 5.5% below the February 2026 estimate.
Schedule: the park and chalet are slated to open in the summer of 2026, with window work in the fall of 2026 and the chalet closed during the work.
The cost is paid 100% by the borough, through its 2026-2034 investment program.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is hiring Environnement Routier NRJ inc. to build two new bus stops on rue Saint-Patrick, for $221,647.83 including taxes.
The stops will be located at the intersections of Saint-Patrick with avenue de l'Église and with rue Eadie.
The work includes sidewalks and concrete curbs, a slab for a bus shelter, safety bollards, sod, and electrical work at the Eadie intersection.
The total authorized spending comes to $265,977.40, with $22,164.78 in contingencies and $22,164.78 in incidental costs.
The work is to take place from June 22 to August 31, 2026, that is 70 days; nearby residents will receive notices before it begins.
The bill is paid 100% by the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité; the winning bid is 32.93% lower than the City's estimate.
Five companies submitted bids, ranging from $221,647.83 to $294,290.01 including taxes.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $5,000 to the organization Les Filles Électriques to organize the 5th Parade Phénoménale 2026.
The parade will take place on October 3, 2026 (postponed to October 4 in case of heavy rain), as part of the 15th edition of the Festival Phénomena.
The route runs through Mile End, along boulevard Saint-Laurent, from parc Lahaie to parc Warrior (an unnamed park), and ends with a line-dancing session.
The contribution is described as exceptional: the 2026 UCI Road World Championships, held within the borough, are forcing a change of date.
This change of date prevents the organization from sharing equipment, technical staff and programming elements with the POP Montréal festival, which creates additional costs.
The money will be paid according to the terms of the approved agreement; the project and the reporting of accounts must be completed in 2026.
The City is awarding a $366,117.31 contract (taxes included) to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, between numbers 294 and 296, in the Village de Senneville.
With contingencies ($73,223.46) and incidental costs ($42,509.68), the total expense comes to $481,850.45, taxes included.
The work includes the new culvert and an insertion liner, road resurfacing, replacement of the guardrails, protection of the plants and seeding.

The culvert, which is undersized, was damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024; temporary repairs have kept the site safe since then, and the City is moving this work up to prevent further deterioration.

The culvert carries watercourse no. 5 from the Bois-de-la-Roche area to lac des Deux-Montagnes; the project is part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, in the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
Two companies submitted bids out of the five that had obtained the tender documents; the winning bid is 6.11% above the control estimate.
The expense is paid by the urban agglomeration and will be fully spent in 2026, through a loan by-law.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is adopting a first draft resolution to allow a "care and wellness clinic" on the ground floor of 6058, rue Jean-Talon Est (the building at 6052-6066, between rue de Côme and rue Valdombre).

The 370.2 m² space, vacant for a few years, would host acupuncture, massage therapy, osteopathy, physiotherapy, podiatry and naturopathy, plus wellness workshops, and an esthetics corner of about 7.15 m².

The zoning by-law requires a retail sales area of at least 25% of the space, taking up the entire width of the frontage on Jean-Talon; the project provides for 15.24% at the entrance, hence the requested exemption.
Conditions imposed: keep commercial display windows, limit signage on glass to 25% of the glazed surface, and begin occupancy within 12 months after the resolution comes into force.
The planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on June 4, 2026.
The section authorizing the use may be subject to approval by referendum.

The City is awarding Fer-Pal construction ltd (Technologies Sans-Tranchée CoreAqua) the rehabilitation of a 600 mm grey cast iron water main along autoroute 15 Nord and the bretelle Atwater, in Le Sud-Ouest.
Total spending of $741,026.71 including taxes: $619,812.98 for the contract, $74,377.56 in contingencies and $46,836.17 in incidental costs.

The water main had been overlooked during the reconstruction of the pont Samuel-De Champlain and the realignment of autoroute 15; it will be rehabilitated with an interior lining rather than replaced.
Work is scheduled to start in September 2026, with 40 days of work in two phases, to be completed no later than December 18, 2026.
Three companies submitted bids; the winning bid is 7.51% above the City's internal estimate.
A penalty of 0.1% of the contract price applies for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day; no bonus is provided.
The spending is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration and financed through a loan by-law.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $50,000 to the Corporation de développement communautaire Plateau Mont-Royal (CDC PMR) for 2026-2027, to coordinate the Table de quartier du Plateau-Mont-Royal.

The money comes from three sources: $18,620 from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, $16,380 from the agreement between the city and the ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale, and $15,000 from the borough's budget.
Adding in Centraide ($75,000) and the Direction régionale de santé publique ($18,873), the Table de quartier is receiving $143,873 for the period.
The amount is higher than in previous years: the borough had granted $33,613 in 2023-2024, 2024-2025 and 2025-2026.
The money funds the Plan de quartier 2024-2028, which focuses on community living together, the local food system, access to housing and community spaces, and support for vulnerable people.
The organization must comply with an agreement with the city, apply two visibility protocols and submit annual documents; a borough councillor follows up on an ongoing basis.
The borough of Ville-Marie is proposing to take charge itself of the design and construction of curb extensions on two avenues that fall under the city council's authority.
Two simple curb extensions will be built on avenue du Docteur-Penfield, at the intersection of chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges.
Two other simple curb extensions will be built on avenue des Pins, at the intersection of avenue Steyning.
The work is planned for 2026 and aims to make pedestrian routes safer as part of the Programme de sécurisation aux abords des écoles.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité will pay 100% of the costs; Ville-Marie will manage the call for tenders.
Local residents and the school administrations concerned will be notified by letter of the nature and duration of the work.
According to the document, if the borough does not take charge of the work, it cannot be carried out.
The Ville-Marie borough is approving spending of $428,385, taxes included, to repave 15 local streets in 2026.
The milling and paving work will be done in-house, mainly by the borough's roadworks employees.
The amount covers equipment rental ($101,328), transportation ($49,846) and materials such as asphalt mix and concrete ($277,211).
Sewer and water main fittings (catch basins, manholes) will be replaced with adjustable equipment.
Timeline: contracts from May to June, sidewalk repairs from May to July, milling and surfacing in September and October 2026.
Funding comes 60% from the local budget for streets east of rue Atateken and 40% from the corporate budget for those to the west.
Residents along the streets will be informed of the upcoming work on their street.
The borough of Verdun is giving $500, non-taxable, to the organization Demain Verdun.
The money will be used to buy basic tools and to promote the Café réparation verdunois.
The Café réparation offers free workshops of about three hours where volunteers help people repair their everyday objects.
The initiative relies on a group of 64 volunteers; 24 were present at the April 26, 2026 activity.
To date, 80 people have registered objects to be repaired, a level similar to the first edition on February 22, 2026.
The decision falls to the Verdun borough council.
The borough of Verdun is giving $500 to Ensemble vocal Chant de La Fontaine, a cultural organization active in Montréal since 1998.
The money supports the show "L'Heptade 50 ans !", a choral version of the Harmonium album, presented at Quai 5160 – Maison de la culture de Verdun.
The show has already taken place on March 13, 14 and 15, 2026: the contribution is therefore retroactive.
The performances were aimed at about 800 spectators and involved a choir conductor, five musicians and 45 choir singers.
The request does not fit into any existing grant program; it is paid out of the elected officials' discretionary budget.
The borough of Verdun is giving $2,000 (non-taxable) to the Fabrique de la paroisse Notre-Dame-de-La-Trinité for its summer 2026 activities.
The money supports the free concert series "Les mercredis en musique," presented on Wednesday evenings at the église Notre-Dame-des-Sept-Douleurs.
According to the document, the series reaches more than 19,000 people and remains free for the public.
The amount covers part of the series' logistics, equipment and communications.
In return, the borough is named as a partner in the event's communication materials.
Verdun has supported this Fabrique in the past: $2,000 in 2024 for the summer, and $10,000 in 2025 for universal accessibility work.
The City is ending the lease of the restaurant located in inhabited storefront A, at 1485, rue Jeanne-Mance, in Ville-Marie, rented to Services culinaires Kamuy inc.
The space is 2,723 square feet, with a 980-square-foot terrace; the lease was to run until October 31, 2030.
The City is giving up $172,583 in rent (before taxes) for the period from June 1, 2027 to October 31, 2030.
The lease allows each party to terminate with one year's written notice, without compensation; an early termination between June 1, 2026 and May 31, 2027 remains possible if both parties agree.
The City cites major work planned in the medium term, late payments and unpaid amounts from the tenant, as well as lease clauses that were not respected.
The part of the land occupied by the terrace (part of lot 5 171 922) will return to the public domain on the termination date.
The Service de la culture is looking at other uses for the inhabited storefronts: production offices for festivals, event lounges or an office for Tourisme Montréal.

The City is renting a 957 m² lot to the Société environnementale de Côte-des-Neiges (SOCENV) free of charge. The lot is at the southeast corner of chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges and the railway line, next to the écocentre Côte-des-Neiges.
The lease covers one year, retroactively from January 1 to December 31, 2026. The free rent amounts to a subsidy of $13,428, based on the 2026 assessment roll value ($223,800 × 6%).
The lot is used for composting and for public activities for residents, as part of the Éco-quartier program. The organization also processes food waste from the Multicaf community cafeteria there.
The organization pays all operating costs and property taxes, if any; the City does not maintain the lot during the lease.
Either party may end the lease at any time with two weeks' written notice.
SOCENV has occupied this lot since 2016 under a series of agreements; the previous one ended on December 31, 2025.
The decision is up to the urban agglomeration council; the file was submitted late because of discussions about whether it complies with the City's policy directions.
The City is extending by 1 year and 9 months the loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to the non-profit organization Ville en vert, from April 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027.
The lot is located in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, south of rue Louvain Ouest and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, in the District Central area.

Since 2024, the organization has been growing a vegetable garden there in smart pots; the fruits and vegetables, grown without pesticides, are sold to local residents and to more vulnerable communities at public markets.
The rent is free: the City puts the value of this real estate subsidy at $121,100 for the 21 months (rental value of $6.92 per square foot).
Ville en vert pays all operating costs and taxes, if any.
Either party may terminate the lease with 60 days' written notice; the agreement provides for no renewal.
Without the extension, the vegetable garden and its installations would have had to be dismantled, according to the document.
The City is extending by one year, from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027, the free loan of a piece of land to the non-profit organization Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine (Au Lab).
The 3,316 m² (35,695 sq. ft.) property is located south of rue Louvain Ouest, west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, on the site of the Esplanade Louvain.

The organization plants sunflowers there and runs a greenhouse; the greenhouse will mainly be used to grow flowers and native plants, and possibly vegetables handed out free of charge on site and through the Ville en vert garden.
There is no rent: the City puts the value of this real estate subsidy at $247,009 for the year, calculated at $6.92 per sq. ft.
The organization pays the operating costs and property taxes, if any, and must restore the land to its original condition at the end of the lease.
The tenant may end the lease with 30 days' written notice; the agreement does not provide for any renewal.
Without this extension, the vegetable garden and the facilities would have to be dismantled, according to the document.
The City is extending by 8 months, from May 1 to December 31, 2026, the lease it rents to the Agence de mobilité durable at 1500, rue des Carrières, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
The Agence occupies 785.62 m² (8,456.39 sq. ft.) of office space there, along with 46 parking spaces used by parking officers.
The City will collect $122,330 in rent, before taxes: $96,570 for the offices ($17.13/sq. ft.) and $25,760 for the parking ($70 per space, per month).
The number of spaces rented has gone from 86 to 46, as the Agence gave up 40 of them when it deployed its teams to other hubs across the territory.
The tenant may terminate the lease or reduce the rented area with 90 days' written notice; the rent is then adjusted on a pro rata basis. No renewal is planned.
The Agence will pay property taxes if there are any. Occupying the site until the end of 2026 is in line with the City's master plan currently being carried out.
City council is starting the process of adopting a by-law to borrow $177,837,000 to build, renovate and improve sports and aquatic facilities.
The money will mainly go to two projects: building the Centre récréatif sportif Gadbois (Le Sud-Ouest) and designing the Complexe aquatique et sportif de Montréal-Nord.
The spending is spread out from 2026 to 2030, from $2.6M in 2026 up to $61.8M in 2030, according to the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The loan will be paid back over a maximum of 20 years, out of the City's general revenues.
The City points to the aging network of aquatic and sports facilities and a lack of facilities in certain areas.
Next steps: notice of motion on June 15, 2026, adoption expected on August 24, 2026, then approval by the ministère des Affaires municipales.
The City is adding $5,007,540.38 (taxes included) to nine household waste disposal contracts, raising their total from $34,015,415.37 to $39,022,955.75 — an increase of 14.72%.
The suppliers involved are Complexe Enviro Connexions, GFL Environmental, Recyclage Notre-Dame and WM Québec; the contracts end on October 31, 2027.
Territories affected: Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Montréal-Est, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Montréal-Ouest, Anjou, Le Sud-Ouest, Lachine, Montréal-Nord, Outremont and Verdun.
The amount is divided into $4,111,478.69 for higher-than-expected waste quantities and $896,061.69 in contingencies.
The document explains that the needs had been underestimated: the waste reduction and landfill diversion forecasts in the 2020-2025 master plan were optimistic.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration of Montréal, without increasing the budget of the department responsible.
Without this increase, the City says it would have to go back to an emergency call for tenders, at the risk of interrupting service and paying more.
The borough of LaSalle is signing an agreement with the Lester B. Pearson school board to use part of the yard of the former Allion school.
The site will be used for a program of summer activities, from June 1 to November 1, 2026.
The project comes from a proposal by the organization Allions-Nous.
Use of the yard is granted free of charge and without warranty.
The borough will set up a security perimeter and will pay for the electricity supplied by the school board.
Similar agreements were already made for the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève is proposing to city council that it take charge itself of the design, coordination and carrying out of minor sidewalk repair work on streets of the City's arterial network located within its territory.
The work is part of the Programme de maintien des infrastructures routières (PMIR) 2026 and aims to restore sidewalks and curbs.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is funding the project 100%; no amount is stated in the file.
Planned schedule: design contract and call for tenders in March 2026, awarding of the construction contract in May 2026, work from June to December 2026.

The list of targeted street sections (request RMT26_IBZ) has been sent for approval to the Direction de la gestion des infrastructures urbaines et des entraves, which retains the power to authorize the works.
A similar agreement had been approved by city council for the 2025 work.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is awarding MLC Associés inc. a master agreement for engineering services: studies, surveys, expert assessments, plans and specifications, and work supervision.
Estimated value of the agreement: $931,947.11, taxes included, for 2 years, with 2 renewal options of 12 months each.
The assignments cover roadways, sidewalks, the water supply system, sewers, lighting, traffic lights, urban utility networks and borough buildings.
The public call for tenders (2026-04) ran from November 28, 2025 to January 12, 2026; 8 firms submitted bids, and MLC Associés obtained the best score and the lowest compliant bid.
The selected bid exceeds the borough's most recent estimate ($866,164.16) by $115,722.34, or 9.37%.
Each assignment will require a separate spending authorization; the firm's performance will be evaluated.
Schedule indicated in the file: start on May 31, 2026, end on May 31, 2027.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is accepting a donation from the non-profit organization Buckets & Borders to renovate two outdoor basketball courts in parc Martin-Luther-King, in Côte-des-Neiges.
The donation is valued at about $95,000 in work: replacing the backboards and rims, acrylic resurfacing, and painting basketball and netball lines.
Buckets & Borders will design and paint a mural on the two playing surfaces (108 ft × 50 ft and 94 ft × 50 ft), with help from young people from the neighbourhood.
No visual branding of the organization will be installed on or around the courts.
Planned schedule: surface preparation from July 7 to 12, installation and painting from July 13 to 24, and the opening on July 25, 2026.
The work will be carried out by Gagné Sports (equipment) and Indik Inc. (surface); access to the city-owned courts remains free.
The SHDM is authorized to build a six-storey, 72-unit building on the "Solotech" site, on 2e Avenue between boulevard Saint-Joseph and avenue Mont-Royal, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.

Of the 72 units: 43 will be affordable (60%) and 29 will be mid-range (40%); the plan includes 38 one-bedroom units, 28 two-bedroom units and 6 three-bedroom units, plus 15 parking spaces in the basement.
The project is estimated at about $27.4M and will be paid for by the SHDM.
Financing: a PHAQ-type grant of about $7,107,000, an interest-free loan of $4,613,000, $4,100,000 of the SHDM's own funds and a long-term loan of $8,000,000.
Ville de Montréal is providing a grant of $3,600,000, which is $50,000 per unit.
Timeline: public call for tenders in late summer or early fall 2026, construction starting by the end of 2026, delivery in May 2028.
The SHDM had bought the land, already decontaminated, in October 2025; a communications strategy will keep the neighbourhood informed as soon as construction begins.
The City is giving $49,500 to the organization Réseau réussite Montréal for its project to promote French in day camps in the summer of 2026.
The money comes from a $1,250,000 agreement between the City and the ministère de la Langue française; no expense is paid by the boroughs.
The project involves 16 day camps in 15 neighbourhoods, targeting 750 young people aged 5 to 16 and 400 families.
230 camp staff members (camp counsellors, assistant counsellors, coordinators) will receive three hours of training, plus a guide and a bank of activities in French.
Each camp will have six hours of activities co-led with counsellors specialized in literacy, and an intercultural officer will devote 300 hours to supporting the teams.
The neighbourhoods are chosen with the school service centres (CSSMB, CSSDM, CSSPI) based on the number of welcome classes and how close immigrant families are.
Support goes from $96,500 in 2025 to $49,500 in 2026; the City had given $49,800 in 2024.
The borough of Pierrefonds-Roxboro is paying $52,773.53 to the organization Écohabitation, from its surplus.
The money funds the JeRénovÉco service, which helps homeowners protect their homes against rainwater flooding and sewer backups.
The service includes 75 diagnostics, 75 personalized work plans, the analysis of 15 contractor bids, and follow-up until the end of the work, including information on financial assistance.
The support is offered to 75 residents of the borough, in French and in English.
Signing of the agreement and launch in August 2026; diagnostics and work in 2026-2027, followed by a summary report.
The document cites the heavy rains of June 20 and the vulnerability of several residential areas in the borough.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $27,000 to six organizations, $4,500 each, for events held between July and December 2026.

The organizations receiving support: Table de quartier de Parc-Extension, Centre Haïtien d'Animation et d'Intervention Sociales, Loisirs communautaires Saint-Michel, À portée de mains, Centre éducatif et communautaire René-Goupil and Centre socioéducatif Lasallien.

The events covered are a neighbourhood party (July 4), a youth festival (August 15), two back-to-school parties (September), an intercultural flavours festival (September 25-26) and a Halloween party (October).
The money must be used for free outdoor cultural or artistic events, open to the general public, in the districts of Parc-Extension, François-Perrault and Saint-Michel.

The money comes from the Programme de soutien aux festivals et événements 2026-2027, funded by an annual increase of $1.25M announced by the elected administration in November 2025, of which $485,000 is divided among the boroughs.
Each organization receives its contribution in a single payment when the agreement is signed, and must follow a visibility protocol.

The City is hiring the firm Infrastructel inc. to oversee the work sites connected to work on the underground conduit network of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM), for a maximum of $849,808.97, taxes included.
The master agreement lasts 36 months: services are planned from March 2026 until the end of the 36 months or until the amount is used up.
The hourly rate submitted for the site supervisors is $64.72 an hour.
The CSEM says it manages about 90 work sites a year and that its 19 technical officers are not enough, especially in the summer.
Five firms submitted bids out of the nine that picked up the tender documents; Infrastructel got the best final score, with a price 11.02% below the CSEM's estimate.
The expense is paid entirely by the CSEM, funded through the Ten-Year Capital Works Program and repaid through fees charged to CSEM users.
The City plans to assess the firm's performance and authorizes the president of the CSEM to sign the agreement.

The City is awarding Groupe Geninov inc. the supervision of work sites related to work in the underground conduit network of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM), for a maximum of $843,286.67 including taxes.
The agreement lasts 36 months, starting in April 2026, or until the planned amount is used up.
The hourly rate submitted for supervisors is $64.72 per hour.
The CSEM says it manages about 90 work sites per year and cannot supervise them all with its 19 technical officers, especially in the summer.
Five firms bid on public call for tenders S-2349; one was set aside for a score below 70 out of 100. The winning bid is 11.70% below the CSEM's estimate.
The expense is paid entirely by the CSEM, funded through the Ten-Year Capital Works Program and reimbursed through fees charged to CSEM users.
The firm's performance will be evaluated.

The City is awarding Geninovation (9152-4629 Québec inc.) a contract worth $785,624.18, taxes included, to track the traceability of contaminated soil excavated at the worksites of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM).
The mandate covers 24 months, from May 2026 until April 30, 2028, or until the contract amount is used up.

Since 2021, a Québec regulation has required computerized tracking of trucks hauling contaminated soil, certified by an environmental professional; the CSEM says it does not have the resources to do this itself.
Five firms submitted bids out of 10 that picked up the tender documents; Geninovation obtained the best score and the lowest price, 13.77% below the internal estimate of $911,036.20.
The expense is paid entirely by the CSEM, funded through the PTI and reimbursed through fees charged to CSEM users.
The firm's performance will be evaluated; Geninovation had already been awarded a similar contract in 2023 ($1,030,811.81).

The City is hiring Aqua Data inc. to inspect access shafts using a 360-degree camera on the underground network of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM), for a maximum of $297,296.04, taxes included.
The contract covers the inspection of 1,840 structures at various locations across the City's territory.
The inspections are used to assess the condition of the structures and how crowded the cables are, in particular for projects tied to the Programme de réfection routière des arrondissements.
The work is to begin around April 15, 2026 and end around October 15, 2027; the master agreement is described as lasting 12 months, with assignments issued over 18 months.
Four firms submitted bids out of ten that picked up the tender documents; Aqua Data obtained the best score and the lowest price, 2.35% below the estimate of $304,453.80.
The second-lowest bid (Infrarouge Kelvin) was $364,470.75, which is 22.50% higher.
The expense is fully covered by the CSEM and reimbursed through fees charged to users; the firm's performance will be evaluated.
The City is awarding Intervia inc. (Groupe Intervia) a professional services contract worth no more than $804,250.13, taxes included, for 18 months.

The firm will prepare the traffic specifications, monitor the maintenance of traffic flow and manage the impacts during the underground conduit work of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM).
The mandate runs from May 2026 to November 2027, or until the planned budget is used up.
Of the 8 firms that obtained the documents for public call for tenders S-2353, 4 submitted bids; Intervia obtained the best final score.
The winning bid is $127,622.25 (-13.7%) lower than the City's latest estimate; the document states that no conclusive explanation could be established.
The expense is paid entirely by the CSEM and reimbursed through fees paid by its users.
Intervia will hand out work notices to nearby residents, which will also be published on the CSEM website, and its performance will be evaluated.
Montréal and Laval are signing a 3-year agreement so that their fire departments can lend each other resources (trucks, staff, specialized vehicles) when needed.
Montréal will also lend its specialized teams to Laval; Laval must first use up its own resources before calling on Montréal.
Laval will pay Montréal $309,377 in three annual payments: $100,590 (2025), $103,105 (2026) and $105,682 (2027), with no indexing.
Each city bills the other according to the attached rates, with 15% in administrative fees, and must pay within 60 days. The City states that it has never received an invoice from Laval in the past.
The assistance provided must never compromise the safety of the citizens of the city lending the help.
The costs are covered 100% by the urban agglomeration; the matching revenue is used to operate the specialized teams of the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal.
This decision replaces and repeals the one adopted on October 30, 2025, following receipt of the documents from the Ville de Laval.
The executive committee is retroactively approving an expense of $334.19 for a trip by Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada to Ontario on February 4 and 5, 2026.
The purpose of the trip was to take part in the Big City Mayors' Caucus of the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM), which brings together 23 of the country's largest cities.
The amount covers only hotel accommodation costs for the night of February 4; no transportation, meal or registration costs are being claimed.
The expense is paid by the central city, out of the budget already set aside for the Division du soutien aux personnes élues of the Service du greffe.
The document notes that the Ville joined the FCM for $465,068.55 (taxes included) from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.
According to the document, the priorities Montréal defends in this forum are social and affordable housing, public transit and infrastructure.

The executive committee authorizes an estimated expense of $5,738.13 to send Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada and Chantal Gagnon, who is responsible for economic development and the green economy, to the Farnborough International Airshow in the United Kingdom, from July 19 to 23, 2026.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city, out of the budget of the Division du soutien aux personnes élues.

The two elected officials are taking part in an economic mission organized by Investissement Québec International: meetings with investors and contract-awarding companies, networking and official representation.
Costs incurred between July 16 and 19 are paid by the mayor herself, except for the outbound plane ticket and the entry tax (ETA); Chantal Gagnon pays for her own plane ticket and accommodation.
The City plans to offset the greenhouse gases from the trip through its carbon credit purchase program.
The document does not provide for any communications activities.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is updating the list of buildings of heritage interest in its zoning by-law so that it matches the list in the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050, which came into force on June 25, 2025.
The list is getting longer: several school buildings, places of worship and buildings connected to heritage places of worship, including presbyteries, are being added to it.
The newly listed buildings fall under the conservation rules in Chapter VIII of the zoning by-law: changes must respect the building's original appearance and character.
Any work on these buildings will first have to be accompanied by a heritage study.
500, boulevard Crémazie Est (École Saint-Alphonse-d'Youville) is being added to the list of buildings of local interest, even though it was removed from the list in the Plan d'urbanisme.
The ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation is giving the borough until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; the zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
A public consultation meeting was held on March 18, 2026 at 405, avenue Ogilvy, with a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026; four citizens attended.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is amending its by-law on conditional uses to bring it in line with the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050.

The by-law sets rules for two new uses: lodging facilities (maximum 60 beds) and service facilities for people in unstable housing situations, for example people who are homeless or victims of violence.
Service facilities may be allowed in zones where institutional or commercial uses are permitted; lodging facilities, in residential zones H.1 to H.4.

Any developer will have to provide an analysis of the impacts on the surrounding area (pedestrian and vehicle traffic) and a study of measures to reduce noise, sanitation problems and traffic problems.
Each application will be assessed based on the needs of the area, the presence of other resources in the same zone, how well it fits into its surroundings, and the peace and quiet of neighbours.
After a review by the City's Service d'urbanisme, the definitions of the two uses were made more precise before adoption.
A public consultation meeting was held on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation ran from March 11 to 18, 2026; four citizens attended the meeting.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is approving a specific project that will allow a parking area and a loading area to be built in the front yard of an industrial building to be constructed on a vacant lot on 56e Rue, near the Pie-IX train station.

The one-storey building (10.97 m high, 10,898 m² of floor area at ground level) will be put up on the side facing the borough of Montréal-Nord; the planned use, heavy industrial or commercial, is not yet confirmed.
Conditions imposed: a maximum of 50 parking spaces, at least 82 trees planted, and entrances no more than 13 metres wide.
The project includes 21 loading docks, greening of 65% of the open space, a green roof on 20% of the roof, 6 charging stations and 64 bicycle spaces.
The deadline to obtain the permits goes from 24 to 36 months, following a request from the developer (groupe MACH), agreed to with Montréal-Nord; otherwise the authorization becomes void.
An Hydro-Québec easement of 30.48 m crosses the lot and prohibits any construction or planting more than 2 m high, which explains why the building is located at the back of the lot.

Because of the nearby railway line used to transport hazardous materials, the Centre de sécurité civile recommends non-combustible materials, fewer openings on the railway side, and a shelter-in-place room with a 2-hour rating.
No residents came to the public consultation meeting of April 15, 2026; the review fees are $7,184.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is amending its zoning by-law for houses with 1 to 3 units located in "basin areas" (zones at risk of flooding).
In the basement, only the extension of the ground-floor unit is allowed, and only within the extension of that unit's walls. Creating a separate unit in the basement is prohibited.
The remaining basement space can only be used for three purposes: shared storage, parking or mechanical equipment.
Two conditions remain: no opening in a façade wall below the natural ground level, and the land must be graded to eliminate any slope toward the building.
The rule that limited habitable basement space to less than 50% of the unit's area is being removed from the text.

The borough says it has received permit applications seeking to exclude staircases and bathrooms from the calculation in order to increase habitable space, hence the clarification of the standards in force since May 2025.
A written consultation (March 11 to 18, 2026) and a public meeting (March 18, 2026) were held; some provisions may be subject to approval by referendum.

The City is asking Hydro-Québec to design the burial of overhead electrical and telecommunications wires along rue Jean-Talon Est, between 24e Avenue and rue Buies, in Saint-Léonard (about 670 metres).
The poles are located in the right-of-way of the future sidewalk: removing them is meant to allow an obstacle-free pedestrian route and universal accessibility.
This work is part of the redevelopment of 3.5 km of rue Jean-Talon Est, coordinated with the extension of the metro's blue line, which is scheduled to open in 2031.
The Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM) will act as technical integrator and manager of the civil works; the City agrees to reimburse it for these costs plus administration fees.
The City agrees to reimburse Hydro-Québec for the design costs, estimated at $330,000 before taxes, only if it postpones or abandons the burial project.
Announced timeline: submission of the request in June 2026, design in 2027-2028, start of civil works in 2029.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is removing three paid parking spaces (PK492, PK495, PK496) on rue Fullum, between avenue du Mont-Royal Est and terrasse Guindon.
This removal goes along with making rue Fullum one-way southbound and building bike paths in both directions.
The spaces are disappearing because stopping must be prohibited at all times in these locations.
The Agence de mobilité durable estimates the lost revenue at $6,578.58 per year.
Planned schedule: signage ordered in July 2026, removal of the sign panels and installation of the new signage in August 2026.
No information campaign is planned; the borough will notify the Agence de mobilité durable of the date of the change in traffic direction.
The City will pay its 2026 membership fee to the Association internationale des villes portuaires (AIVP): 6,794 euros, or about $11,000.
The payment is scheduled for April 2026 and will be paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, out of the operating budget of the Service du développement économique.
Montréal has been a member of the AIVP since 2021 and vice-president of its board of directors since 2023, for a three-year term that can be renewed once.

The membership is used to work with the Port de Montréal and the international network on the Agenda AIVP 2030, which includes 10 commitments (climate, sustainable mobility, city-port interface, biodiversity, etc.).
The 2025 fee was 6,794 euros (about $10,000) and the 2023 fee was 6,596 euros.
No communications activities are planned.
The City is granting $150,000 to Cyclo-club Lachine for the event Les Mardis cyclistes de Lachine, which is $50,000 per year from 2026 to 2028.
In 2025, the central city's contribution was $35,000: it therefore rises to $50,000 per year for the next three years.
The races take place on Tuesday evenings from June to August, over 10 weeks, on a closed circuit in the streets of Lachine; street closures are planned.
Close to 200 racers compete each week in five categories; the 2026 edition adds a race with an all-women pack.
A free cyclovia, open to the public, is planned for a 4th year and would be funded by the Programme de soutien aux initiatives locales de cyclovia ($11,200 in 2025).

To pay for this, the City is transferring $15,000 from contingency expenses to the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs in 2026, and is adding $15,000 on a recurring basis to its budget base in 2027 and 2028.
The expense is fully borne by the urban agglomeration; the borough of Lachine is also providing $10,100 and about $60,000 in goods and services.
The City is giving $525,000 to the organization Beach Volleyball Évènements to put on the Montréal Beach Pro Tour: $125,000 in 2026, $200,000 in 2027 and $200,000 in 2028.
The beach volleyball event takes place at parc Jean-Drapeau in August 2026, 2027 and 2028: 96 matches over 5 days, 55 teams, 126 athletes from 21 countries.
The Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs will have its budget base adjusted by $75,000 on a recurring basis for 2027 and 2028.
The cost is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, out of the operating budget.
The City had given $25,000 to this organization in 2025; the new request went beyond the usual funding parameters of the Direction des sports.
The organization pays for all parc Jean-Drapeau services itself and handles the logistics; it must follow a visibility protocol.
The document states $1.2M in economic and tourism benefits, and 19,000 paying spectators at the previous edition.
The City is giving an additional $2,850,000 to the organization Événements GPCQM for the Grand Prix Cycliste de Montréal: $250,000 in 2026, then $1,300,000 per year in 2027 and 2028.
With the addition of 2026, the annual contribution goes from $1,050,000 to $1,300,000.
On top of this, there is support in goods and services of $1,410,000 in 2027 and $1,420,000 in 2028.
The agreement with the organization is extended to 2028; the event will be held in September 2026, 2027 and 2028.

The City is moving $250,000 from its contingency spending to the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs in 2026, and is adding $250,000 on a recurring basis to its budget base for 2027 and 2028.
The race will lead to street closures around mont Royal, with a traffic detour plan announced before the event, at the promoter's expense.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration; the organization cited its rising costs and the lack of indexing.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is paying $45,900, taxes included, to the organization Marché public de Pointe-aux-Trembles for the 2026 season.
The amount is the usual $45,000 contribution, increased by 2% to account for inflation.
The market will be held at Place du Village-de-la-Pointe-aux-Trembles, every Saturday from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., from May 30 to September 26, 2026, plus a gardening event on May 23.
It will also take part in the Cabane à sucre (March 21) and Magie d'Automne (October 24) events, and coordinate a Christmas market on December 5 and 6, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
An ordinance allows the market to be set up on public property on the planned dates and times.
In 2025, the market welcomed 20,338 visitors and 75 exhibitors, and 92 vulnerable households used food coupons with three local organizations.
The organization handles communications and must mention the borough's support in its publications.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is paying $45,900, taxes included, to the Marché public de Pointe-aux-Trembles.
The money will pay for a feasibility study for a future permanent public market in Rivière-des-Prairies and for four pilot markets.
The four markets will be held at parc Saint-Joseph on Sunday, July 12, Sunday, August 9, Sunday, August 23 and Sunday, September 13, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., with about 15 food-sector vendors.

The Rivière-des-Prairies public market in its current form, run since 2024 by the Association des gens d'affaires de RDP at parc Armand-Bombardier, is suspended; residents and vendors found the site too far out of the way.
The market study will be entrusted to the firm Raymond Chabot Grant Thornton, in collaboration with the Association des marchés publics du Québec.
An order authorizes setting up the market at the planned site, dates and times, and an agreement is signed with the organization.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is removing the public property occupancy fee for commercial terraces.
In practice, businesses that apply for a permit to set up a terrace will no longer have to pay this fee.
The change amends the borough's by-law on fees for the 2026 fiscal year.
The borough council cites the desire to stimulate economic activity and liven up living environments, particularly where there is major construction work in commercial areas.
The borough describes the lost revenue as minimal, because very few commercial terraces occupy public property on its territory.
Next steps: adoption by the borough council, publication of a public notice on the website, then coming into force.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing a permanent mural on the north wall of the building at 739-749, avenue Walker, between rue Saint-Jacques and rue Saint-Antoine Ouest, across from parc Charles-Drew.
The project comes from the agency Les Productions LNDMRK inc.; the mural by artist Whatisadam Wia will evoke American wildlife and landscapes in a style reminiscent of old comic books and pop art.
An order was needed because the building is in a zone where only residential uses are allowed, which normally prohibits murals.
The mural will have to be protected against graffiti and maintained for at least 5 years; the organization has committed to doing so.
The paint used will be exterior, water-based, weather-resistant and will let the brick breathe.
The document does not provide for any spending by the City.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is accepting $103,400 from the owner of a lot at 1720, rue De Roberval, instead of a transfer of land for park purposes.
The amount is equal to 10% of the value of the new buildable lot (6 685 130), appraised at $1,034,000 by the firm PCG Carmon in January 2026.
The owner is dividing the 1,091.7 m² lot into two lots: one of 813.7 m² freed up for future construction and one of 278 m² with the existing building.
The lot is located on the south side of rue De Roberval, between rue Angers and rue Laurendeau; the zoning allows a residential building with a maximum of 3 units on 3 storeys.
No building permit application has been filed; the owner mentions the possibility of a duplex.
The money is paid into the park fund account; the next step is approval of the subdivision permit.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing a permanent mural on the southeast wall of the Maison Benoît Labre, at 257-259, avenue Greene and 250, avenue Atwater.
The authorization is needed because the by-law on mural art normally prohibits murals on the façade where a building's main entrance is located.
The organization will have to keep the mural in good condition for at least 5 years.
The borough is giving a financial contribution of $10,000 to the project.
The mural will be created by the artist Simon Bachand, of the Collectif Art du Commun, using a weather-resistant water-based exterior paint.
The wall is located near the Lionel-Groulx metro station, the Marché Atwater and the tunnel Atwater.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is allowing Hydro-Québec and its subcontractor Intervia to make noise at night, between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m., on rue Bridge and rue Wellington.
Three nights are covered: the night of July 17, 2026, with August 15 and August 22, 2026 as backup dates if the work cannot go ahead.
The work is to build a duct bank under the roadway, then rebuild the roadway that was torn up.

During the work: rue Wellington will be completely closed between rue Saint-Patrick and rue Condé (local traffic only), and rue Bridge will be closed northbound between rue Mill and rue Saint-Patrick, with one contraflow lane heading south.

The borough explains that the width of the roadway and the central island at the Wellington/Bridge intersection make it impossible to keep one lane in each direction, which is why the work is being done at night.
These new dates replace the ones authorized on June 8, 2026, because of adjustments tied to the work on the pont Samuel-De Champlain.
A communications effort must be carried out before the work begins.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is accepting a $450,000 donation from the organization Patro Villeray – Centre de loisirs et d'entraide to renovate the centre Patro Villeray, a building owned by the City.
This donation covers about 4% of the total cost of the work; the rest comes from the provincial PAFIRS grant and from the borough.

Planned work: redoing the floor and painting the quadruple gymnasium, bringing the anchors up to standard (including the basketball ones), repairing an exterior wall that lets water in, and separator curtains.
Also on the program: complete renovation of the men's and women's locker rooms, adding a universal locker room, reorganizing the offices and the reception area, and asbestos removal in several areas.
The donation must be used only for work eligible under PAFIRS; the organization is not asking for a tax receipt or anything in return.
The borough is committing to return the $450,000 to the organization if the work is abandoned.
The document states that refusing the donation could delay the work or reduce its scope, as the building is described as run-down.
The borough of LaSalle is paying $8,072.49 to six local cultural organizations for winter 2026.

The amounts: Association Musicale De LaSalle $2,055.20, Guilde des Tisserands $1,977.50, L'Avant-Scène $1,910.00, Société Historique Cavelier $1,000.00, Club Photo LaSalle $954.79 and Association des Artistes de LaSalle $175.00.

The money will be used, among other things, to hire outside resource people for talks and workshops, to buy percussion instruments, weaving supplies and a laptop, and to cover copyright fees, costumes and set design.
The projects must be carried out within the territory of LaSalle within a maximum of twelve months.
The funding covers up to 70% of expenses, with a maximum of $1,000 per organization for hiring a resource person and $2,000 for artistic creation and heritage.
The expense comes from the budget for contributions to other organizations of the Division culture et bibliothèque.
The borough of LaSalle is adding $152.77 (taxes included) to the contract to upgrade the equipment at the Théâtre du Grand Sault, in the centre culturel et communautaire Henri-Lemieux.
The contract awarded to Solotech Inc. goes from $339,992.64 to $340,145.41, taxes included.
The increase represents 0.05% of the original contract awarded on September 8, 2025.
A discontinued Denon player is being replaced with a Tascam model (an increase of $242.57 before taxes), and two lighting parts are being removed from the order (a decrease of $109.70 before taxes).
The expense is funded by a loan charged to the borough's taxpayers, through the 2025-2034 capital works program.
According to the document, these adjustments serve to finalize the work and close out the project.
The borough of LaSalle is putting $1,000 toward the Salon du printemps of the Association des artistes de LaSalle, held from April 16 to 27, 2026.
Of that amount, up to $600 goes toward buying a work shown at the Salon.
The remaining $400 goes toward awarding a third prize at the event.
The works on display are by members of the association, selected by an outside jury.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget (purchases of non-capitalized goods and contributions to organizations).
The borough has paid the same amounts for this event every year since 2022.
The borough of LaSalle approves a $1,600 expense, taxes included, to take part in the 40e Grand Prix du Conseil des arts de Montréal.
The money is used to buy a table for ten people at the event held on Thursday, April 2, 2026, at the Palais des congrès de Montréal.
The delegation will bring together elected officials, administrative staff and partner organizations of the borough.
The expense is charged to the budget of the elected officials' responsibility centre (CR# 301702).
The expense is authorized after the event took place, with the borough council deciding on April 13, 2026.
In previous years, LaSalle had paid $1,550 in 2025, $1,450 in 2024 and $1,450 in 2023 for the same event.
The borough of LaSalle is approving a $5,000 expense, taxes included, so that its elected officials can attend a benefit evening.
The money is being used to buy a table for eight people at the Grand Variété, organized by the Société de la Salle Jean-Grimaldi.
The event takes place at the Théâtre Desjardins on Thursday, June 4, 2026, with Francine Grimaldi as honorary chair.
The evening includes a cocktail reception, a three-course dinner and a show hosted by Jean-François Breau, with Marie-Élaine Thibert and Marc-André Fortin.
The fundraiser marks the 30th anniversary of the Théâtre Desjardins and is meant to fund the organization's local cultural activities in the Grand Sud-Ouest.
The expense is charged to the borough's elected officials' budget (responsibility centre 301702).
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the creation of a mural on the exterior wall of the west gymnasium of école secondaire Cavelier-De LaSalle (9199, rue Centrale), on the rue Centrale side.
The work will be created collectively with the school's students, guided by muralist Izabelle Duguay; a participatory creation session was held on April 7, 2026.

The project costs the borough nothing: it is funded by a crowdfunding campaign among parents, residents and community organizations in LaSalle, as well as by the « La culture à l'école » grant from the ministère de l'Éducation.

The comité d'analyse d'art mural found the six evaluation criteria satisfactory on April 14, 2026; the Centre de services scolaire Marguerite-Bourgeoys and the school's administration gave their approval, and the condition of the wall was certified by a mason.
Planned schedule: authorization certificate in May 2026, creation and unveiling of the mural in May and June 2026.
The design depicts water and the river, birds, an arch and a window, as well as a fleur-de-lys, in connection with the students' educational journey.
The borough of LaSalle is asking Patrimoine canadien for $188,000 to fund the celebrations of the 200th anniversary of the Moulin Fleming, located in parc Stinson.
The application must be sent before June 1, 2026; Michaël Benoit, cultural development officer, is designated as the borough's representative.
The cultural activities will take place from June to September 2027, in collaboration with LaSalle organizations and artists.
The borough plans to invest more than $45,000 in money and human resources in the event.
A communications campaign is planned: website, newsletter, video clip, social media, media relations, banners, posting and radio advertising.
The stone windmill was built in 1827 by miller William Fleming and mason William Morrison.
The borough of LaSalle appoints the head of the culture and library division as the signatory for the legal and tax documents required by Patrimoine canadien.
These documents concern the project for the 200th anniversary of the Moulin Fleming and include the funding agreement and the direct deposit form.
On May 29, 2026, the borough submitted a $188,000 funding request to Patrimoine canadien to support the celebrations.
The celebrations for the 200th anniversary of the Moulin Fleming will take place from June to September 2027.
Patrimoine canadien requires this municipal resolution for the project to be eligible for the grant; the resolution must be submitted to it by August 7, 2026.
The borough plans a communications campaign (website, newsletter, video, social media, media relations, posting, radio advertising).
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is cancelling a $100 contribution granted on November 25, 2025 to Club des anciens combattants à l'âge d'or 3055 inc.
The money was to pay for organizing Christmas activities.
The organization has changed its name: it is now called Comité des loisirs de la Maison Jean-Brillant inc.
The payment was therefore impossible under the old name; the contribution will be granted later under the new name.
The contribution was part of a $12,800 package paid to various organizations in the borough.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $850 in one-time financial contributions to three organizations.
$100 goes to the Comité des loisirs de la Maison Jean-Brillant inc. to organize Christmas activities.
$250 goes to the Association des popotes roulantes du Montréal métropolitain for two tickets to its 40th anniversary fundraising cocktail event on January 30, 2026.
$500 goes to CRE-Montréal for two tickets to the 19th Gala on January 29, 2026, where a borough project is nominated.
The money comes from unallocated surpluses and is paid entirely by the borough.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is lending room 2B of the Pavillon du parc Henri-Bourassa (6100, rue Pascal) free of charge to the Fondation de la famille Mathurin.
The free use covers 7 Saturdays, from March 21 to November 28, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
This exemption from the 2026 rates amounts to $7,295: $7,007 for the rental ($143/hour) and $288 for a facility attendant ($24/hour, 12 hours).
The Fondation will hold activities there with residents; its mission focuses on young people through sport, education and mentorship.

The Montréal-Nord borough is lending the gymnasium at the Centre de loisirs, at 11 121, rue Salk, free of charge to Héma-Québec for a blood drive on Saturday, June 20, 2026, from 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.
The free use covers the room rental, supervision of the facility and cleaning, which are normally billed according to the borough's 2026 fee schedule.
The value of this exemption is $1,545.50: $1,320.50 for the gymnasium (9.5 h at $139/h), $36 for one attendant (1.5 h at $24/h) and $189 for cleaning (3 h at $63/h).
The borough justifies the measure by Héma-Québec's mission, which is to supply Québec's health care facilities with blood and biological products.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is exempting Club Juventus Canada from the rental, supervision and maintenance fees for the Centre de loisirs for two events.
The bookings covered: May 28, 2026 from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. (room 2-4) and September 25, 2026 from 5:30 p.m. to 10 p.m. (gymnasium).
The exemption represents about $1,123.50: $291 for the first date and $832.50 for the second.
These fees applied because the Club is not an organization recognized by the borough and because the events take place outside opening hours.
The borough had granted a similar exemption to the same club for an event on May 18, 2025.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorized to submit an application for financial assistance to the Bureau de la transition écologique et de la résilience to redo community gardens.
Two projects are being submitted under the "rehabilitation" component: the jardin Faubourg Saint-Laurent (rue Saint-Dominique) and the jardin Sainte-Marie (rue La Fontaine).
At the jardin Faubourg Saint-Laurent: moving and renovating the shed, adding three planter boxes, one of which is universally accessible, and reorganizing the common area.
At the jardin Sainte-Marie: replacing the 20 worn-out planter boxes, restoring the back plots damaged by roots, and rebuilding the pergola.
Timeline: plans and specifications in winter 2026 and work in spring 2026 for Faubourg Saint-Laurent; plans in spring-summer 2026 and work in October 2026 for Sainte-Marie.
Ville-Marie has 14 community gardens and 562 garden plots; the borough council's support was required for the application to be eligible for the program.
The Ville-Marie borough council is approving new gardening and conduct rules for its 14 community gardens, taking effect for the 2026 season and the seasons after that.
Each garden plot holder will have to pay an annual fee to their garden committee, with the amount set at the annual general meeting.
Plot holders will have to cultivate the entire area of their plot, and the plot must be seeded before June 1 or the holder faces immediate expulsion.
Chemical fertilizers are now banned, in addition to the herbicides already covered.
End-of-season cleanup is set for November 1 (or as decided by the committee); the gardens operate from May 1 to November 1.
The rules set out the maximum height for plants and stakes, the banned materials, and they define verbal and physical assaults as well as disruptive behaviour.
Warnings may be sent by email, must be kept on file by the committee, and will add up cumulatively over three years.
The borough of Ville-Marie is placing two organizations, Accueil Bonneau inc. and Ma Chambre inc., in category B of its Politique d'accès au soutien, until December 31, 2028.
Category B covers non-profit organizations whose mission matches the borough's areas of responsibility, but which plan their own activities and serve part of the Ville-Marie population.
Each category (A or B) comes with a "basket of services": financial support, the loan of premises, or the supply of goods and services.
In April 2026, the borough must confirm the rating to the two organizations, specify the nature and terms of the support, and assign them a contact person.
The organizations have agreed to meet the requirements tied to their rating.
The file lists no amount: the financial aspects section does not apply.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving a total of $7,000 to 14 community garden committees, that is $500 per garden.
The money comes from stream 2 of the Fonds en agriculture urbaine, 2026 edition, and must be spent during the funding year.
The agreements with the committees end no later than November 1, 2026.
The money will be used in particular to buy compost, seeds, shared tools and plants, and to organize workshops and work parties.

Among the gardens covered: Ste-Marie, Panet, Habitations Jeanne-Mance, Sainte-Catherine, Médéric-Martin, Saint-Eusèbe, Ambroise-Casale, Saint-André, des 50 citoyens, Versailles, Faubourg Saint-... and the rooftop garden Au Sommet du Courant.
The program aims to support activities in the gardens, access to healthy food, education about urban agriculture and greening.

The borough of Ville-Marie is placing two non-profit organizations, Les Drags Patronesses and l'Union française de Montréal, in category B of its Politique d'accès au soutien (support access policy), until December 31, 2028.
Category B covers organizations whose mission touches on the borough's areas of responsibility, but which plan their own activities and serve part of the population of Ville-Marie.
This rating gives access to a "basket of services" from the borough: financial support, loan of premises, or goods and services.
Without this categorization, the two organizations could not receive support from the borough.
In June 2026, the borough will confirm to the organizations their rating, the type of support, the terms for granting it, and the name of the contact person.
No money is committed in this decision (the financial aspect is listed as not applicable).
The borough of Ville-Marie is accepting a $20,000 grant from Sport et Loisir de l'île de Montréal, under the "Circonflexe" program.
The money will be used to operate an "active station" at parc des Faubourgs: free loans of sports and recreational equipment (balls, nets, goals, etc.).
The amount will pay for a contract covering supervision, activity leadership and management of the equipment loans for the summer of 2026.
The Corporation du Centre Jean-Claude-Malépart will manage the service point and offer occasional led activities.
The service is intended for the whole population, with particular attention to young people, families and people in vulnerable situations.
According to the file, without this grant, the active station could not be used by the community.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough proclaims September 4 as National Polycystic Kidney Disease (PKD) Awareness Day.
The borough council invites the public to support the Canadian PKD Foundation.
The document notes that Health Canada recognizes this date and that the disease affects 66,000 people in Canada.
No expenses are planned for this file; the borough has adopted the same proclamation every year since 2022.
The borough of Pierrefonds-Roxboro proclaims September as "Arthritis Awareness Month."
This action aims to support the Arthritis Society of Canada in getting its message out to residents of the borough.
The document notes that six million people in Canada, or one in five, live with arthritis and that there is no known cure.
It states that this number could reach nine million by 2040 if the issue remains unaddressed.
No spending is planned: this is a proclamation, renewed every year since 2023.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough council adopts a motion in support of the SPVM following the shooting on June 22 in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
It offers its condolences to the family, loved ones and colleagues of officer Mohamed Lamine Benredouane, who died in the line of duty.
It highlights the everyday courage of SPVM members and reaffirms its commitment to the service in order to strengthen public safety and the population's trust.
It invites the Montréal population to show its support for those who ensure its safety.
The motion does not involve any expense or new obligation.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough council adopts a motion that condemns all forms of hatred, violence or discourse targeting women, including incel ideologies and other misogynistic movements.
The motion refers to a tragedy that occurred in Montréal, where the shooter's manifesto expressed hostility toward women, as an example of the consequences of misogynistic radicalization.
The borough reaffirms its support for the women of Montréal and Québec and their right to live free from fear, violence and discrimination.
It states that it supports organizations that prevent violence against women, support victims, and promote gender equality.
It encourages the development of resources and education to prevent radicalization and promote non-violent models of masculinity.
No amount of money is attached to the motion; the document indicates that it does not apply to Montréal 2030 commitments.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is removing the taxi stand located on avenue Mercier, between rue Notre-Dame Est and rue Bellerive, over about 30 metres.
The freed-up space will become five parking spots open to the public, which residents, visitors and people going to the promenade Bellerive will be able to use.
The signs already in place will continue to prohibit parking on Thursdays, from 12:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.
The borough says it received several requests from citizens to this effect and observed on site that the taxi stand was not being used.
Installing the new signs is estimated at about $60, paid by the borough.
The residents concerned will be notified of the new signs; a work order will be sent as soon as the file is approved.
The borough of LaSalle supports the Journées de la persévérance scolaire 2026 campaign, which will be held from February 16 to 20, 2026.
This year's theme is "La persévérance, ça mène loin."
This is the 22nd Québec edition of the Journées and the 16th Montréal edition, coordinated by Réseau réussite Montréal.
The support is meant to publicly express solidarity with young people and with workers in the education system.
No spending is planned in this file; LaSalle has supported the campaign every year since at least 2022.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $4,000 to the Fondation du Cégep André-Laurendeau.
The money supports the regional final of "Cégeps en spectacle", set for March 21, 2026.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under contributions to other organizations.
In return, the Fondation will display a borough banner at the event, provide official photos and post thank-you messages on social media.
The borough had already supported the Fondation, including $1,000 for its scholarship program in 2021.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $2,500 to the Chambre de commerce de Montréal Centre Sud Ouest.
The money will be used to organize the 12th edition of the Gala UNIO, on May 28, 2026 at the Théâtre Centaur, in Vieux-Montréal.
The gala showcases businesses, stores, organizations and entrepreneurs from the area.
In return, LaSalle receives two passes, its logo in the program, a banner in the cocktail room and a mention in the opening speech.
The money comes from the borough council's budget.
The borough had already funded the 11th edition and an earlier edition of the same gala.
The borough of LaSalle is increasing the amount authorized to buy a work of art at the Association des artistes de LaSalle's Salon du printemps 2025 from $600 to $800 (taxes included).
The $200 increase is due to the actual price of the work purchased, which comes to $800.
The Salon du printemps was held from April 10 to May 2, 2025; the works on display are chosen by an outside jury.
The March 2025 decision also provided for a $400 contribution for a third prize awarded at the event.
The expense is paid out of the borough council's budget.
The borough of LaSalle is reducing its contribution to the "Grand Variété" benefit evening from $5,000 to $2,500.
This amount pays for LaSalle's elected officials to attend the event, organized by the Société de la Salle Jean-Grimaldi.
The evening will take place on June 4, 2026 at the Théâtre Desjardins, which is marking its 30th anniversary, with Francine Grimaldi as honorary chair.
The expense will be charged to the elected officials' accounting code set aside for financial contributions.
The decision corrects a resolution adopted on April 13, 2026, after the expense was reviewed.
The LaSalle borough is moving its regular council meeting from Monday, October 5, 2026 to Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 7 p.m.
The change is meant to avoid the day of the provincial general election, set for Monday, October 5, 2026.
Residents will be informed of the new schedule through a public notice after the decision is adopted.
No spending is associated with this change.
The borough of LaSalle is paying $250 to the Centre de services scolaire Marguerite-Bourgeoys.
The money is used as a bursary given to a student for their involvement in the community.
The bursary was awarded at the graduation ceremony of école secondaire Caroline-Dawson, on Friday, June 12, 2026.
The council is retroactively approving an authorization that was already given.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under the line for contributions to other organizations.
In October 2025, a similar contribution had been paid for école secondaire Cavelier-De LaSalle.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $250 to LaSalle Community Comprehensive High School (LCCHS).
The money is used as a scholarship given to a student for their involvement and dedication in the community.
The scholarship was given out at the graduation evening on Friday, June 19, 2026; the council is approving the authorization after the fact.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under contributions to other organizations.
A scholarship of the same amount had been granted to the same school the previous year.
The borough of LaSalle is committing to carry out the three projects chosen by residents during the 2025-2026 participatory budget, with a total envelope of $200,000.
The selected projects: les Armoires d'abondance ($25,000), Pause fraîcheur ($100,000) and Le cœur du parc Leroux ($70,000). The remaining $5,000 will be used to enhance these projects.
Voting was held from May 25 to June 19, 2026, and was open to residents aged 12 and over, who could choose up to 4 projects out of 11. In all, 1,296 valid votes were counted.

Under the Charte du budget participatif, ecological transition projects are funded first, up to a maximum of $50,000, which explains why les Armoires d'abondance and Pause fraîcheur were chosen ahead of the most popular project.
The projects will be carried out using the borough's operating budget, from the winter of 2027 to the end of the winter of 2028, with a commitment to deliver them by the end of 2028.
The 122 initial ideas came from residents and were collected from November 4 to 30, 2025.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is reorganizing several positions as of February 10, 2026, following a review of its activities.
Three installation carpenter positions are moving from the Division des parcs to the Division du soutien technique, in public works.
One office agent position is moving from the Division des sports et loisirs to the Division de la culture et des bibliothèques.
One programmer analyst position is being abolished in the Division de l'informatique and replaced by a management systems agent position.
Two permanent administrative support clerk positions are being abolished in the Division des ressources financières et matérielles and replaced by two equivalent temporary positions.
The document does not put a figure on the spending: the section on financial aspects is empty.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is appointing its mayor, Danielle Myrand, as its representative on the board of directors of PME MTL Ouest-de-l'Île.
She replaces Doug Hurley, the former borough mayor, who had held this seat since 2024.
PME MTL Ouest-de-l'Île is a non-profit organization that supports and finances entrepreneurs and businesses in the western part of the island.
Its services cover nine municipalities (including Dorval, Pointe-Claire and Kirkland) and the boroughs of Lachine, L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève and Pierrefonds-Roxboro.
Its board has 15 voting directors: 5 municipal elected officials and 10 business people.
According to the document, this presence is intended to ensure follow-up and coordination between the organization and the borough.
The appointment must be approved by the urban agglomeration council.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève is amending its by-law on the pay of local elected officials.
The chair of the new advisory committee on culture, sports, recreation and social development will receive additional pay.
The chairing of the development and land use planning committee moves from the borough mayor to a borough councillor, who will be paid for this role.
The amendment applies retroactively to January 1, 2026.
The additional pay will come out of the borough's budget; no amount is specified in the file.
Steps: notice of motion on February 3, 2026, public notice in February, adoption and notice of enactment in March 2026.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève is asking the Directeur de l'état civil to designate the borough mayor, Danielle Myrand, as an officiant for marriages and civil unions.
Once designated, she will be able to perform marriages and civil unions only within the borough's territory.
This authorization would be valid for the duration of her term as an elected municipal official.
The Directeur de l'état civil would assign her a unique identification number to be written on marriage or civil union declarations.
The step is voluntary: the borough mayor has expressed the intention to officiate at these ceremonies.
Next step: send the resolution to the Directeur de l'état civil.
No amount is associated with this file.
The L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève borough is preparing to offer a service for celebrating marriages and civil unions.
A notice of motion is given to amend the 2026 fees by-law in order to add a fee for this service, which did not have one.
The fee would be the one set out in section 25 of the Tariff of judicial fees in civil matters, indexed each January 1.
In 2026, the fee is $422 when the ceremony takes place outside the courthouse.
The by-law is expected to be adopted at the June 2026 borough council meeting, followed by a public notice of promulgation.
Another item submitted at the same meeting asks the Directeur de l'état civil to designate the borough mayor as the officiant.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is giving $1,000 to Service des loisirs Saint-Fabien.
The money comes from the $5,100 contribution budget of the borough's elected officials' office; this $1,000 is granted at the discretion of the councillor for the Louis-Riel district.
The organization, founded in 1963, offers sports, cultural and community activities to families in Mercier-Ouest, as well as to young people and seniors.
The money will be used to fund one-time initiatives that do not meet the criteria of the Politique de reconnaissance et de soutien des organismes.
The decision must be approved by the borough council.

The executive committee authorizes the Société du Parc Jean-Drapeau to apply for a grant from the Government of Québec for phase 2 of the restoration of the Pavillon des activités nautiques, at plage Jean-Doré.
The work is estimated at $1.8M; funding from the Programme d'aide financière aux infrastructures récréatives, sportives et de plein air could cover up to 66% of eligible costs, or about $1.19M.

The planned work includes: masonry on the façades, a new path to the beach with adapted parking, an access ramp at the main entrance, and replacement of the floating docks with access for people with reduced mobility.
Also included are a secure bicycle cage with surveillance, a boat washing station, and outdoor lighting along the path leading to the site.
The Société could not submit its application without this authorization, since it owns the building in question.
A first restoration phase on the same building took place from November 13, 2023 to June 5, 2025.
Next step: wait for the Government of Québec's decision on the application.
The borough of Ville-Marie recommends that the urban agglomeration council appoint elected official Leslie Roberts to the board of directors of PME MTL Centre-Ville.
PME MTL is a network of six non-profit organizations that supports, advises and finances businesses and entrepreneurs on the island of Montréal.
The Centre-Ville hub covers Ville-Marie, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Outremont, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and the city of Westmount.
The organization's by-laws provide that the Ville-Marie borough council designate one of its members to the board of directors; the seat must be filled after the elections of November 2, 2025.
