The position had been held by Vicky Grondin since 2022, and by Sophie Mauzerolle before her.
The file must go before the executive committee, the city council and the urban agglomeration council in August 2026.
There is no financial aspect attached to this decision.
The City accepts the donation of 8 bonsai trees given by Pierre Séguin to the Jardin botanique de Montréal.
It will issue him an official tax receipt for $196,509, the average of three outside appraisals ($166,396, $192,132 and $231,000).
The trees: one Rocky Mountain juniper, one blue spruce, two limber pines, one ponderosa pine and three mountain hemlocks; some are more than 150 years old and nearly 4 feet tall.
The ceramic pots, made by recognized ceramic artists, are included in the value of the donation.
The bonsai trees were delivered in November 2025 and found to be in good health by the Jardin's horticulturist and three outside appraisers.
The specimens will be displayed to the public; the Jardin says it does not expect any additional expenses to care for them.
The City states that the receipt does not make it liable if the tax authorities challenge the amount.
The Jardin botanique de Montréal will give away its surplus plants and harvests (fruit, vegetables, herbs) free of charge to six Montréal non-profit organizations.

The organizations involved: La ruelle de l'avenir, Espace Jeunesse en marche, Nature-Action Québec, On sème, Jeunesse au Soleil and Bouffe-Action de Rosemont. Other requests could be added, depending on the quantities available.
Bouffe-Action de Rosemont and Espace Jeunesse en marche will receive harvests every week; the surplus plants will be handed over once planting is finished, at the end of June.
No money is being paid out: the surplus given away represents less than 1% of production and no monetary value has been estimated.
According to the document, these donations keep the surplus out of the compost and improve access to healthy food for people in need.
In 2025, 501 bins of vegetables from the Jardin nourricier were given to collective kitchens; the City adopted similar decisions in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

The Ville-Marie borough council confirms the authorization to demolish the former YWCA building at 1355, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest (corner of Crescent), built in 1951 and occupied until April 2025.
Residents had appealed the decision; the council upholds the decision of the demolition application review committee of February 18, 2026, under the same conditions.
The reasons given: asbestos, mould, water infiltration, a structure unable to bear any more loads, and a restoration that would cost close to triple the cost of demolition and reconstruction.
The replacement project calls for a 30-storey building (95 m) on a 7-storey podium (23 m), with 401 housing units, 914 m² of commercial space, 74 car parking spaces and 225 bicycle spaces.
The 401 housing units break down into 123 studios, 198 one-bedroom, 60 two-bedroom and 20 three-bedroom units.

Opponents were asking that the YWCA's function be preserved (102 rooms for people in need) and that 20% social housing and 20% affordable family housing be required; these conditions are not retained.
The project's architecture will be reviewed at a later meeting of the urban planning advisory committee before the demolition certificate is issued.
The City is awarding Keleny inc. a contract worth $2,364,083.76 (taxes included) to provide court interpreters and translators for the Montréal municipal court.
The contract covers two years, from June 18, 2026 to June 17, 2028, with an option to extend for one year that would cost $1,217,503.14 (taxes included), based on an assumed indexation of 3%.

The municipal court has a legal and constitutional obligation to provide interpreters to parties and witnesses who need them; the specifications provide for 4,000 requests per year (4,380 filled in 2025).
Two companies submitted bids for public call for tenders 26-21352, but only one was compliant: the other did not have the required certification from the Autorité des marchés publics.
The price selected is 10.3% lower than the City's estimate, but 9.7% higher than current prices; the City explains this by a market limited to two suppliers in the Montréal region.
The file is going before the Commission permanente sur l'examen des contrats: more than $2M, only one compliant bid, and a third consecutive contract with the same supplier.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, and the City will assess Keleny inc.'s performance.

The City is awarding a $765,701.31 contract (taxes included) to Cloud Monitored Objects inc. (Gestion d'objets distants CMO) for the support and maintenance of the communication equipment installed in the vehicles of the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal.
The contract runs for 2 years and allows for two possible extensions of 12 months each.
The supplier must provide on-site maintenance and support 24/7, maintenance of modems and software, the installation or removal of equipment, and management of the inventory of in-vehicle computers.
The contract replaces two existing contracts ending in April 2026 and covers a fleet of 262 vehicles.
Of the four companies that obtained the tender documents, two submitted bids; only one was found to be compliant administratively and technically.
The winning bid is 37% below the internal estimate of $1,214,771.93, according to the City because the two contracts were combined into one.
The expense is fully paid by the urban agglomeration; the firm's performance will be evaluated.
The City is giving $15,000 to Propulsion Québec, the industrial cluster for electric and smart vehicles, to organize the "Vekta 2026" event.
The event takes place on February 16, 2026 at the Salon Richmond, in Montréal, and is expected to bring together close to 400 people from the electric transportation industry.
On the program: talks, three themed panels, networking sessions between businesses and decision-makers, and discussions with three elected officials.
The event is aimed in particular at young businesses with fewer than five employees, as well as buyers, manufacturers and transportation operators.
The support is paid in two instalments: $12,000 first, then $3,000.
The money comes from the budget of the Service du développement économique; the organization must submit a final report in July 2026.
The City had already granted $50,000 to this organization in 2023 and $50,000 in 2025 for the Impulsion event.

The City is giving $140,000 to the Institut international d'études administratives de Montréal (also known as the Forum économique international des Amériques) to organize the 32nd edition of the Conférence de Montréal.
The organization had asked for $175,000; the amount granted is the same as for the 2024 and 2025 editions.
The event will take place from June 8 to 10, 2026 at the Hôtel Bonaventure, on the theme "Thriving in an Uncertain World."
The contribution will be paid in two instalments in 2026: $128,000 and then $12,000, and will be paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
The City is providing 4.7% of the event's $3M budget; the governments of Québec and Canada are providing 32.5% and the private sector 63%.
The City is invited to take part in the content of two panels, including one on the circular economy.
Next steps: agreement in April 2026, communications in May 2026, review report in the fall of 2026.
The City is changing the household garbage collection rules in the borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.
From November 1 to April 30, garbage will be picked up once every two weeks.
From May 1 to October 31, garbage collection stays weekly.
The change was prepared with the borough and takes effect as soon as the order is published.
No spending is attached to the decision and no information campaign is planned.
The Service de l'environnement manages the collection contracts for the boroughs until December 31, 2027.
The City is appointing Céline-Audrey Beauregard, mayor of Verdun, as the borough's representative on the board of directors of PME MTL Grand Sud-Ouest.
She replaces Véronique Tremblay, a former councillor appointed to the position in January 2018, a change made necessary by the latest municipal elections.
PME MTL Grand Sud-Ouest is the local economic development organization serving Verdun, LaSalle and Le Sud-Ouest; it supports and funds business projects.
Its board of directors has 13 members: 3 elected officials and 10 people from the business community, including the chair. Verdun holds one elected official's seat and three business community seats.
Business community representatives do not have to be appointed by the borough council.
The appointment must be approved by the executive committee, the city council and the urban agglomeration council, and then sent to the management of PME MTL Grand Sud-Ouest.
There is no spending associated with this decision.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is receiving $155,325 from the ministère de la Sécurité publique for the "Animation et intervention au pôle René-Masson" project.
The money comes from the Programme de soutien à la création et à la consolidation d'espaces jeunesse montréalais 2022-2026 and covers the period from September 1, 2025 to August 30, 2026.
The borough is asking the executive committee to amend the City's operating budget to add $155,325 in revenue and in spending for 2026.
The program is used to offer young people more activities and facilities to welcome them.

Three organizations are already sharing the amount under an earlier decision: Équipe RDP ($73,002.75), Société Ressources-Loisirs de Pointe-aux-Trembles ($62,130) and Maison des jeunes de RDP ($20,192.25).
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is paying $101,432 to its two neighbourhood round tables for the period from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
La Corporation de développement communautaire de Rivière-des-Prairies is receiving $50,813 and the CDC de la Pointe, région est de Montréal, $50,619.
The money comes from three sources: the Ville-MTESS agreement ($32,760), the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale ($43,841) and the borough's budget ($24,831).
With the contributions from Centraide and the Direction régionale de santé publique, each round table has $147,236 (RDP) and $148,042 (La Pointe).
The council is approving two agreements setting out the payment conditions.
The round tables work on such things as food security, housing, mobility, welcoming new immigrants and the feeling of safety.
The City increased its contribution in 2026 to reach a target of $50,000 per neighbourhood round table.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough council approves the minutes of the traffic and road safety committee meetings of May 14 and June 25, 2026.
By approving them, the council accepts the committee's findings and recommendations.
This approval allows for changes to Schedule "A" of by-law 868 on traffic and public safety (former City of Pierrefonds) and by-law 98-596 on parking (former City of Roxboro).
The document does not detail the specific measures recommended; it states that they are aimed at the safety of users of the borough's road network.
No amount of money is associated with this decision.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is announcing an amendment to its by-law on delegation of powers, tabled as a notice of motion for adoption at a later meeting.
The change would give a level 2 official the power to make decisions on traffic and parking matters, including authorizing temporary exemptions.
Each authorization would have to specify the area covered, the duration of the exemption, and the safety and mobility conditions.
The borough director could at any time exercise this power personally or reserve its exercise for themselves.
Reason given: the Agence de mobilité durable requires confirmation by council resolution, which lengthens delays during storms, disasters, works, or unforeseen events.
The summary indicates that there is no significant financial impact associated with this amendment.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough council must decide on a minor exemption for a multi-unit residential building located at 14,101-14,103 avenue Anselme-Lavigne and 4,500 rue René-Émard.
The owner wants to install three canopies (awnings) separate from the main building, in the front and side yards facing a street.
The current zoning by-law prohibits canopies in a side yard adjacent to a street and those that are not attached to the building.
The document cites technical constraints: the structure of the new canopies must be independent from that of the existing canopies.
The urban planning advisory committee unanimously recommended acceptance on July 15, 2026, judging that the exemptions do not harm the property rights of neighbours.
A 15-day public notice precedes the borough council's decision, scheduled for August 3, 2026.
No financial impact is expected for this file.
An owner at 992, chemin de la Rive-Boisée, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, is requesting a minor exemption to expand their detached single-family home.
They want to install two double garage doors and two single garage doors, while the zoning by-law allows a maximum of two single doors or one double door.
The urban planning advisory committee unanimously recommended refusing the request, on June 3, 2026.
The committee finds that the refusal does not cause serious harm, since the expansion project can be carried out in compliance with the regulations.
The borough council must decide on August 3, 2026, following a 15-day public notice.
The City ended 2025 with an overall surplus of $256.6M: a $263.8M surplus for the local portion (the City and the boroughs) and a $7.1M deficit for the agglomeration portion.
City council is paying out $56,263.2 thousand in surplus to the 19 boroughs and is authorizing the transfers, using a calculation method approved at the same time.
It is setting aside $1,506.9 thousand to cover the 2025 deficit of certain boroughs, until those deficits are recovered.

It is allocating $171,957.1 thousand to other requests, including $50M to the snow reserve, $26.4M to debt management, $15.6M to the Championnats du monde de cyclisme, $11.4M to housing projects and $8M to a climate emergency fund for the boroughs.
Two strategic reserves are being created: $9,905.2 thousand for inflation and $10,000.0 thousand for an economic slowdown.

The City is recovering $9,890.3 thousand from the royalty rate stabilization fund of the Commission des services électriques and is returning $343.5 thousand in unused surplus to the unallocated surplus.
The money will be available to the units as soon as city council approves it, which is expected on June 15, 2026.
The City is setting the final rate for the drinking water it supplies to the 16 related municipalities of the agglomeration at $0.2908 per cubic metre, for the 2025 fiscal year.
This rate replaces the rate of $0.2764 per cubic metre applied for 2024.
The calculation is based on a direct water supply cost of $109.4M (supply, treatment, distribution network and administrative fees) for 376,212,730 m³ of water distributed.
Each related city has already paid a provisional share; the amount will be adjusted according to its actual consumption, with terms for payment, reimbursement and interest.
The by-law stems from a 2016 agreement that, since 2017, has divided drinking water expenses according to the consumption of each related city.
This is a notice of motion and a tabling: adoption will take place at a later sitting of the urban agglomeration council.
The City is giving out 9,733 free family passes to low-income families and children to visit an Espace pour la vie facility of their choice.
The four facilities covered: Jardin botanique, Biodôme, Insectarium and Planétarium. The Biosphère is handled in a separate file.
Validity dates: Jardin botanique from July 1 to August 27, 2026; Biodôme from July 1 to December 18, 2026; Insectarium and Planétarium from September 8 to December 18, 2026.
One pass is good for one visit per family, meaning a maximum of two adults and three children under 18; day camps and other groups are excluded.
Espace pour la vie divides the passes among the boroughs on a pro rata basis; the boroughs hand them out to organizations that work with families in financial hardship.
The passes will be sent to the boroughs in mid-May; each one carries a QR code to track its use.
The number of passes is the same as in 2025; the measure does not create any additional spending or any revenue for Espace pour la vie.
The City is giving free access to the Biosphère from July 1 to December 18, 2026 to low-income families holding a pass, as part of the Semaine québécoise des familles.

10,000 family passes will be handed out in total: 9,733 to the boroughs (valid at one of the five Espace pour la vie institutions, of their choosing) and 267 to the reconstituted municipalities for the Biosphère.
The passes are shared out based on 2021 census data on low-income children aged 0 to 17; the quantities are the same as in 2025.
One pass is good for one visit per family, meaning a maximum of two adults and three children under 18; day camps and other groups cannot use them.
The boroughs and the reconstituted municipalities will receive the passes around mid-May and will give them to organizations that serve low-income families and children.
A QR code on each pass will make it possible to track use, with a report at the end of the year.
The measure does not create any additional spending for Espace pour la vie and does not generate any revenue.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is giving $4,162 to two organizations for the 2026 family celebrations.
Pointe-aux-Fêtes is receiving $2,081 for the Fête famille de Pointe-aux-Trembles, on May 30, 2026 at parc St-Jean-Baptiste.
Initiative 1, 2, 3 Go! Rivière-des-Prairies is receiving $2,081 for the Fête famille de RDP, on June 27, 2026 at parc Ferdinand-Biondi.
The activities offered at these events are free for the public.
The borough is also providing material, logistical and professional support, as well as promotion through its communication channels.
The amount matches the 2025 contribution ($4,080) with a 2% increase; it is not recurring.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is authorizing the Association communautaire Maria-Auxiliatrice to hold a religious procession in the streets on August 8, 2026, from 7:30 p.m. to 9:30 p.m.
Participants will follow a set route through the streets near the church, with prayers, songs and the carrying of a statue of the Virgin Mary.
This authorization has been required since a law came into force in 2026 that, as a rule, prohibits collective religious practices in streets and parks unless the municipality gives permission.
City council delegated this power of authorization to the boroughs at its meeting of June 12.
The activity must meet four conditions: it must not compromise safety, it must be short in duration, it must be open to everyone, and it must not unduly block access to public property.
The document states that the procession has been held for more than 30 years and that it involves no expenses.
Some streets will be temporarily occupied during the event, with a specific route set out in cooperation with local authorities.
The borough of Anjou is removing three parking spaces reserved for people with reduced mobility: in front of 7442, avenue du Cellier, 6212, boulevard Roi-René and 7151, rue Bélanger.
Reasons given: two of the permit holders have moved (or are moving after March 1) and a third has died, making these spaces unnecessary.
The signs will be removed: one on avenue du Cellier, two on rue Bélanger; the one on boulevard Roi-René will be relocated.
The costs are covered by the borough, which already has a budget set aside for this type of work; no amount is specified.
Advance notice signs will be put up 30 days before the change, and a public notice will be posted on the borough's website.
The 2017 and 2018 decisions that had created two of these zones are repealed.

The borough of Anjou is changing the signs on boulevard des Roseraies, northbound, between rue Beaubien and rue Saint-Zotique: the end of the no-parking zone is being moved, which removes one parking space.
The traffic committee points to the lack of parking after the blue line work and the need for space on collection days.

At the intersection of rue Colbert and rue Ravenel, the City is marking a pedestrian corridor on the south side and lowering the sidewalks at the northeast and northwest corners, to provide access to the bus stop.
Posts and no-parking signs will be installed on the east side of rue Colbert, which removes four parking spaces; the sidewalk ramp on the southwest side will be removed.
The borough is paying the costs out of the budget it had already planned for these activities.
The new signs will be announced by notices posted 30 days in advance, and the order takes effect on the day it is published.
The borough of Anjou is permanently closing a section of avenue de Spalding, at the intersection of avenue Goncourt.

This closure makes way for the redevelopment of parc de Spalding and a new "Parc-école inclusif" (inclusive school park) built partly on the grounds of Dalkeith Elementary School (Commission scolaire English Montreal).
The stop sign on avenue de Spalding at the corner of Goncourt is being removed, along with the no-parking signs and the 30 km/h sign in the area of the future school park.
Some on-street parking spaces are being removed on the portion taken up by the school park.
On avenue Goncourt, the two stop signs are being moved further south, on either side of the entrance to the new parking lot; the sidewalk ramps on the west side are being removed.
The dead-end sign is moving to the northwest corner of avenue de Spalding and avenue Merriam; signs are being installed in the new parking lot, which is accessible from avenue Goncourt.
The costs are covered by the borough out of its own budget; advance notice signs will be put up 30 days before the changes.
The borough of Anjou is changing road signs at three locations to clarify situations considered confusing.

Boulevard du Golf, northbound, approaching boulevard Henri-Bourassa: two new signs will show the movements allowed in each of the three lanes (left: left turn; centre: straight ahead or right; right: right turn).

Boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine, northbound, north of avenue Chénier: the 50 km/h sign will be moved to a new post, near parc Félix-Leclerc, because it is too close to the speed display board that shows 30 km.
Median at the entrance to croissant Montrichard: the no-parking sign will be turned to face north and the dates will be changed to the period from December 1 to April 1.
The costs are paid by the borough, out of a budget already planned for this type of activity.
Advance notice signs will be put up 30 days before the new signs are installed.
The borough of Anjou is changing the signs at three locations to improve safety for pedestrians, cyclists and drivers.
Avenue de Bourgneuf, west side, between boulevard de Châteauneuf and avenue Trémolières: two no-parking signs will be removed, since the loading dock no longer exists.

Intersection of boulevard des Sciences and boulevard du Golf: the right lane will now allow drivers to go straight or turn right. Only the pavement markings and the signs are changing, not the traffic lights.
Boulevard des Galeries-d'Anjou, between avenue des Jalesnes and avenue de Malicorne: parking is allowed on both sides of the central median, because of the lack of parking in the area.
Boulevard des Galeries-d'Anjou, between Malicorne and place des Groseilliers (northbound): drivers in the left lane must turn left.
The costs are covered by the borough out of its existing budget; advance notice signs will be put up 30 days before the new signs take effect.
The order takes effect on the day it is published on the borough's website.
The borough of Anjou is changing the signs on rue De Lamartine, at 7690.
Two parking spaces are being removed, one on each side of the driveway entrance at 7690, rue De Lamartine.
No-parking-at-any-time signs will be installed on both sides of this entrance.
Reasons given: trucks have difficulty getting into the parking lot safely, and heavy vehicles do not have enough room to turn.
The borough is paying the costs out of its existing budget; no amount is specified.
The order takes effect on the day it is published on the borough's website.
The borough of Anjou is adding mandatory stop signs on avenue des Ponts-de-Cé, at the intersection with avenue Judith-Jasmin, in both directions.
The traffic committee recommended this change because of concerns about vehicle speed at this location.
Advance notice signs announcing the date the change takes effect will be installed 30 days before the stop signs, at the southeast and northwest corners.
After one month, the advance notices will be removed and replaced by the stop signs; a small sign panel will also be added at the northeast corner.
The costs are covered entirely by the borough, out of a budget already set aside for this type of work.
The public notice that the change is taking effect will be published on the borough's website.
The City is granting $2,465,694 in financial support to 79 projects by cultural or community organizations, under the Participation culturelle dans les quartiers 2026 program.
The projects will take place in 18 boroughs; 26 of the selected organizations (33%) had never been supported by the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs before.
The amounts range from $4,602 (Parkinson Montréal-Laval) to $90,000 for three organizations: Centre Turbine, La Maison de jeunes de St-Léonard and Quartier des arts du cirque.
The money goes to cultural mediation activities, cultural leisure and amateur practice, heritage promotion and digital creativity.

The call for projects launched on October 14, 2025 closed on February 10, 2026; 193 eligible projects were received and assessed by peer committees, then allocated using a territorial grid (population, immigration, vulnerabilities, distance from the centre).
No grant may exceed the maximum for its funding stream, or 85% of the project's eligible expenses.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city, through the Entente sur le développement culturel de Montréal 2024-2027.

The City is ending its Programme d'appui à l'acquisition résidentielle (PAAR), which refunded transfer duties on the purchase of an existing property and provided a lump-sum payment for a new property.
No new applications will be accepted as of July 2, 2026; the program ends on December 31, 2026.
Applications already submitted will be processed by the end of 2026, and eligible applicants will receive their grant.

Households that have not submitted an application lose access to this municipal assistance, but they can turn to the Québec government's new refundable tax credit for transfer duties, announced on April 17 and retroactive to purchases made since January 1, 2026.
The City cites the overlap with the Québec measure and wants to review its approach to home ownership.
The PAAR's 2026 budget is expected to be spent in full; starting in 2027, it will be reallocated under terms yet to be determined.

The City is awarding Roland Grenier Construction ltée and Mécanicaction inc. general work (demolition, repairs, masonry, doors and windows, mechanical, electrical, etc.) in various municipal buildings, on request.
Estimated amount of the agreements: $9,588,954.94, taxes included, plus a contingency budget of $1,598,159.15.

Three lots: heritage buildings to Roland Grenier Construction ($2,966,441.83); fit-out of administrative spaces ($1,152,054.97) and development of housing to fight homelessness ($3,872,298.98) to Mécanicaction.
The agreements last 36 months, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029, with two extension options of 12 months each.
Public call for tenders 25-21232 drew 7 takers of the tender documents and 3 bidders; the prices selected are below the City's estimates (from -2.36% to -9.58%).
The City will assess the performance of the two firms; the decision is up to the urban agglomeration council.
The City is transferring $765,000 in capital funding between two departments to pay for the project "Notre serre 4 saisons à Saint-Michel".
The project includes 1,500 m² of greenhouses for research and training, plus a 1,000 m² community greenhouse to grow fresh fruits and vegetables for the Saint-Michel neighbourhood.
The greenhouses will be built in parc Frédéric-Back, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
The project will also serve as a training site, in particular for Collège Ahuntsic and its new urban agriculture program.
The transfer is needed because parc Frédéric-Back falls under the urban agglomeration: the money must therefore come from the agglomeration budget rather than the local budget.
This is one of the twelve winning projects from the first edition of Montréal's participatory budget; the operation has no impact on the City's financial framework.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is putting $50,000 into an emergency fund so it can carry out health and sanitation work itself when an owner fails to do so.
The money is used only for urgent, one-time work that requires immediate action for health and safety.
The bill is then passed on to the owner: the costs can become a priority claim on the building or be secured by a legal hypothec.
The fund is financed by the borough's unallocated surplus.
The document states that 72% of households in Montréal-Nord are renters and that 10,500 households spend more than 30% of their income on housing.
The problems covered include insulation, mould, cockroaches, bed bugs and rodents.
The same amount of $50,000 had been authorized in 2025, after $25,000 in 2024 and in 2023.
The Montréal-Nord borough is abolishing two borough inspector positions in the Division des permis et inspections and creating two municipal inspector positions.
The two current employees are transferred into the new positions as of June 14, 2025, or later if the position is created or the appointment is made after that date.
This change comes out of an overhaul of white-collar inspection jobs led by the Service des ressources humaines together with a borough subcommittee.
The new municipal inspector job is classified in salary group 09.
A letter of agreement (EV-2025-0060) was reached with the Syndicat des cols blancs on transitional measures.
Converting the two positions results in an additional expense from January 1 to December 31, 2026, funded from the operating budget; the amount is not stated in the text.
The City will pay $719,761.40 (taxes included) to the ministère de la Justice du Québec before February 20, 2026.
This amount is a final adjustment for the pay of municipal judges in 2025: the total bill rises to $14,252,219.50, of which $13,532,458.10 has already been paid in four instalments.
Since July 1, 2024, Québec pays municipal judges directly and cities reimburse it for these advances, under a law assented to in December 2023.
The payment is made "under reserve": discussions are continuing between the cities and Québec about the basis for the billing and the sharing of costs, which could lead to adjustments.
The City is paying by the due date to avoid the interest set out in the provincial regulation.
According to the document, the expense does not affect the 2025 financial framework, since a provision was recorded in December 2025.
The municipal court falls under the agglomeration, so the decision is made by the urban agglomeration council.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is renewing for one year the terms of four citizen members of its urban planning advisory committee: Daniel Abi Kalam, Gloria Battista, Pierre Beauséjour and Jean-Marc Pustelnik (from May 4, 2026 to April 4, 2027).
It is also appointing three new resident members for one year, from May 4, 2026 to May 3, 2027: Darin Bentaleb, Michael R. Filato and Franco Conciatori.
These three positions were vacant following one resignation and two terms that expired on February 3, 2026 and were not renewed.
A call for applications published on December 19, 2025 on the borough's website and in the weekly paper Est-Média drew 13 applications; 8 people were interviewed.
The committee must have five members to reach quorum, which is why the appointments are needed according to the document.
The urban planning advisory committee is made up of two elected officials and seven borough residents.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving $151,420 to four organizations to run "Stations loisir" (recreation stations) in parks this summer.

Each organization receives $37,855: Sports Montréal (parc Beaubien), Services des loisirs Angus-Bourbonnière (parc André-Lavallée), Les loisirs du centre Père-Marquette (parc du Père-Marquette) and Rap Jeunesse (parc Joseph-Paré).
The stations offer free loans of sports and outdoor equipment, plus free activities, with at least two activity leaders on site at all times.
Open from June 6 to September 27, 2026: Saturday and Sunday from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m., and from June 22 to August 23 also Wednesday to Friday from 12 p.m. to 8 p.m. (schedule subject to change).
Free special activities are planned for the first day, Saturday, June 6, 2026.
The borough is also providing electricity, logistical support, maintenance of the sports facilities and access to park chalets.
The organizations receive $30,284 after signing and $7,571 after handing in the final report, due no later than October 25, 2026.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving $11,040 to AQDR Pointe-de-l'Île for the Aînés actifs à vélo 2026 project.
The project offers seniors in the borough free bike-taxi rides, accompanied by summer employees or volunteers, to run errands or take neighbourhood outings.
The service will run for 12 weeks, from early June to early September 2026.
The money covers part of the salaries and coordination costs not paid by the federal Canada Summer Jobs program.
The contribution represents 27% of the project's expenses and matches the 2025 amount indexed by 2%.
In 2025, 1,061 residents used the service for 549 trips.
According to the document, the project cannot go ahead without this funding from the borough.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is giving $20,138 to four organizations to support young people with a functional limitation at the summer 2026 day camps.
Breakdown: Société Ressources-Loisirs de Pointe-aux-Trembles $7,652, Équipe RDP $5,840, Loisirs communautaires le Relais du Bout $4,632, Centre de leadership pour la jeunesse Don Bosco $2,014.
The money is used to hire support workers present at the day camps from June 25 to August 21, 2026.
About 100 young people with a physical, hearing, visual, intellectual, autistic or psychological disability are expected to benefit.
The amount matches the 2025 amount ($19,742) indexed by 2%; it comes on top of the $18,316 given by the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, for a total of $38,455.
The organizations will have to send follow-up reports (number of support workers, number of young people served and not served, budget) in September 2026 and meet with the borough for an evaluation.
The amount from the provincial PALIM program, administered by AlterGo, is not yet known.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is entrusting the management of the Centre récréatif de Rivière-des-Prairies to the Société Ressources-Loisirs de Pointe-aux-Trembles for $358,274.88, taxes included.
The contract covers reception, supervision, cleaning services (including two deep cleanings per year) and management of the use of the premises, from July 13, 2026 to July 12, 2027.
The contract is awarded directly, without a call for tenders, to a non-profit organization; only one compliant bid was received.
The centre welcomes an average of 70,000 people per year and is open 14 hours a day, 7 days a week, except on statutory holidays.
The price is $2,725.12 (0.7%) below the estimate of $361,000; the current contract with Axia Services cost $304,000 for 2025-2026 and ends on July 12, 2026.
The contractor supplies the cleaning products and materials; the borough supplies the heavy maintenance equipment and plans to buy new equipment.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving the organization Société Ressources-Loisirs de Pointe-aux-Trembles responsibility for managing reception, supervision and use of the rooms in the chalet at parc Armand-Bombardier.
The negotiated contract is worth $75,433.54, taxes included, from July 13, 2026 to July 12, 2027.
A staff person in charge will be on site 252 days a year, Tuesday to Saturday, for 2,113 hours, including a bank of 250 flexible hours.
The chalet, open 12 hours a day, 6 days a week, 52 weeks a year except on statutory holidays, welcomes an average of more than 6,000 people a year.
Only one organization submitted a bid; the price accepted is $566.46 (0.7%) lower than the borough's estimate of $76,000.
The borough is authorizing the expense and the credit transfers, and is approving the agreement with the organization.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is giving $125,000 to 11 community organizations under the Fonds d'initiatives locales en développement social 2026.
The amounts range from $8,000 to $25,000: the highest go to Frigo de l'Est ($25,000), Escale Famille Le Triolet ($21,294), Solidarité Mercier-Est ($12,518) and CCSE Maisonneuve ($10,188).
The projects deal with food (cooking workshops, community meals, gardens), family support, youth, harm reduction, and a dance project for young adults with disabilities.
The districts covered are Hochelaga, Maisonneuve–Longue-Pointe, Louis-Riel and Tétreaultville.
Of the 24 projects submitted ($357,375.89 requested), 11 were selected after an evaluation committee held on February 19 and 20, 2026.
The projects run from May 5 to December 31, 2026, with final reports to be submitted no later than January 30, 2027.
The cost is covered entirely by the borough: $100,000 from the social development and culture budget, and $25,000 from ecological transition.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve will apply to renew its "Municipalité amie des enfants" (Child Friendly Municipality) accreditation for 2026 to 2028, with the organization Espace MUNI.
The application will be submitted between June 8 and September 2, 2026; the director of culture, sports, recreation and social development is authorized to sign the documents.
The borough has been accredited since 2009 and has carried out five three-year action plans since then.
If the accreditation is renewed, the borough commits to carrying out three commitments, to publicly announcing the accreditation, and to marking World Children's Rights Day every November 20.
It will also have to report to the public on the progress of its commitments and submit a mid-point report to Espace MUNI after 18 months.
The accreditation is aimed at young people aged 0 to 17 and their families, and covers recreation, safety, transportation, urban planning, accessibility and support for community organizations.
The file involves no spending: the financial section is "not applicable."
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough council is appointing Councillor Elvira Carhuallanqui as acting mayor.
Her term runs from March 11 to July 7, 2026.
She succeeds Councillor Martine Musau Muele, whose term ended on March 10, 2026.
The acting mayor allows council meetings to be held when the borough mayor is absent.
There is no spending tied to this decision.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving the borough director the power to authorize a collective religious practice on a public road or in a park.

This authorization comes from the Loi favorisant le vivre-ensemble, assented to on April 2, 2026, which bans these practices on public property unless the municipality gives exceptional authorization, case by case.
To be authorized, the practice must meet four conditions: it must not compromise safety, it must be short, it must be open to everyone, and it must not unduly block access to public property.
Wearing a religious symbol is not covered; the notion of public road includes streets, laneways, sidewalks, bridges, pedestrian paths and bike paths.
City council had first delegated this power to the boroughs, which remain responsible for local rules (noise, traffic, occupancy of public property).
The borough says the delegation will speed up the processing of permit applications; no spending is attached to the file.
Notice of motion given on June 18, 2026, adoption planned for the July 7, 2026 meeting, followed by a public notice of coming into force.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough council appoints councillor Sylvain Ouellet as acting mayor.
His term runs from July 8 to November 3, 2026.
He replaces councillor Elvira Carhuallanqui, who was named acting mayor from March 11 to July 7, 2026.
The role is to chair council meetings when the borough mayor is absent.
According to the document, there is no cost associated with this appointment.
The City is appointing four new trustees to four municipal pension plan boards, for three-year terms.
Geneviève Ouellet will sit on the board of the firefighters' plan and Julie Gamache on the board of the professionals' plan.
Martine Simard will sit on the board of the white-collar workers' plan and Kim-Phung Ho Quan on the board of the blue-collar workers' plan.
All four are replacing Gabriel Morin, who held these seats reserved for people appointed by the executive committee.
These boards manage the finances and day-to-day administration of the pension plans for the City's employees.
The document does not provide for any spending related to these appointments.
The executive committee is renewing for three years the terms of three people it appoints as trustees on six of the City's pension plan boards.
Richard Audet is reappointed to all six boards: managers, white-collar workers, blue-collar workers, foremen, firefighters and professionals.
David Bélanger is reappointed to the white-collar and blue-collar boards; Olivier Roberge, to the firefighters' and professionals' boards.
These boards manage the finances and day-to-day administration of the pension plans; provincial law limits each term to three years, renewable.
The City says it chose these people based on their interest in the field, their availability for meetings, and their knowledge of pension plans or their experience on a board of directors.
No spending is attached to the decision.
The City is authorizing spending of $203,899, taxes included, to provide civil liability insurance for the trustees of its pension plans, from July 19, 2026 to July 19, 2027.
Of that amount, $197,399 goes to the insurance premium and $6,500 to fees.

The insurance covers the trustees of the pension commissions (managers, white-collar workers, blue-collar workers, foremen, firefighters, professionals), those of the Caisse commune, and City employees who carry out delegated duties.
The policy is shared between a primary insurer and 7 excess insurers, based on a proposal negotiated by the broker AON on June 5, 2026.
The director of the Bureau des régimes de retraite is authorized to sign the contracts.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city; last year, the same coverage cost $318,957.98.
The Caisse commune, where all the plans invest, held assets of $11.558B as at December 31, 2025.

The executive committee is renewing Richard Audet as the City's representative on the board of directors of the Association de bienfaisance et de retraite des policiers et policières de la Ville de Montréal (ABRPPVM).
His term is also being renewed on the Comité des placements of the same association.
The term lasts three years.
The renewal is being done because his previous term, granted in August 2023, is coming to an end.
The document states that no financial aspect applies to this decision.
The borough of Ville-Marie is granting $2,100,240 (taxes included) to three organizations to keep community mediation teams running until December 31, 2027 at the latest.
The breakdown: $872,815 to Société de développement social, $629,637 to Groupe communautaire l'Itinéraire and $597,788 to L'Anonyme U.I.M.
About fifteen workers are active in 6 targeted areas to reduce tensions in public spaces and support vulnerable people.

L'Anonyme covers the Village (Saint-Hubert/Papineau/Sherbrooke/René-Lévesque); the SDS covers the Quartier des spectacles, the Quartier chinois and the Quartier latin, including place Émilie-Gamelin; l'Itinéraire covers square Cabot, the Lucien-L'Allier and Bonaventure metro stations and gare Windsor.

According to the borough, from May 2025 to May 2026 the 15 workers logged 21,235 hours in the field, more than 7,000 interventions or defused crises, 1,700 referrals and more than 60 training sessions.
No call for tenders was issued: the law does not require the City to go to market for this type of service contract with a non-profit organization.
The mandate is in addition to street work and EMMIS, and does not replace them.

The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $150,000 to three neighbourhood round tables, $50,000 each: the Corporation de développement communautaire Centre-Sud, the Table Inter-Action du quartier Peter-McGill and the Table de concertation du Faubourg Saint-Laurent.
The agreements end on March 31, 2027.
The money is used for local consultation and for the fight against poverty and social exclusion, under the framework of the Initiative montréalaise de soutien au développement social local.

The priorities targeted: food, culture, housing and social diversity in Centre-Sud; a human-scale downtown and neighbourhood life in Peter McGill; sharing public spaces, affordable housing and active mobility in Faubourg Saint-Laurent.
In its 2026 budget, the City increased its contribution so that each neighbourhood round table receives $50,000 from the three funders.
For 2026-2027, the three funding partners are providing a total of a little more than $4.7M, or a minimum of $143,000 per neighbourhood round table.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $100,000 to 12 sports organizations for their 2026 programming, the same total as in 2025 ($90,000 in 2024).
The grants range from $304.78 (Club de volley-ball celtique) to $25,000 (Association du soccer de Saint-Léonard), which reaches the maximum allowed per year.
The calculation is based on the number of members under 18 living in the borough: $46.82 per member to start in 2025, then the rest is divided up.
Two rules limit the amounts: a maximum of $25,000 per organization and a maximum increase of $1,000 per year.
The organizations had to submit their membership lists to the Direction de la culture, des loisirs et des bâtiments before January 31, 2026.
The agreement ends on December 31, 2026.
The borough says it wants to allow young people to take part in sports at a lower cost.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $10,000 to Corporation de football junior de St-Léonard inc.
The money is used only to pay part of the purchase of 40 football helmets for young players.
The price of a helmet ranges from $290 to $500 depending on the age category.
The organization lends the equipment to young people free of charge and said it feared having to raise registration fees without help.
An agreement sets out the terms of the funding; it ends on December 31, 2026.
The organization made its request by letter on November 25, 2025; the priorities committee supported the project on March 16, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $1,600 to the Corporation de football junior de St-Léonard (Les Cougars de St-Léonard).
In exchange, the borough gets an ad in the 2026 season souvenir program and visibility on the team's jerseys.
The amount is not subject to taxes, and the funds are already set aside in the budget for contributions to other organizations.
The borough says it has been giving this contribution for several years to promote the participation of young Saint-Léonard residents in football.
The same amounts of $1,600 were granted in May 2025 and in September 2024.
The priorities committee recommended the funding at its meeting of April 13, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is making the use of its tennis courts and two school gymnasiums free of charge for 2026 for the non-profit organization Tennis Montréal inc.
The value of the fees waived is $28,350: $27,540 for the tennis courts and $810 for the gymnasiums.
Tennis Montréal inc. will take over from the organization 40-0, whose contract ended at the end of 2025, to offer supervised tennis programming.

The courts covered are those in parc Coubertin, parc Ferland, parc Giuseppe-Garibaldi, parc Hébert, parc Ladauversière, parc Luigi-Pirandello, parc Pie-XII and parc Delorme, plus the gymnasiums of écoles Gabrielle-Roy and Wilfrid-Bastien.
An agreement for the loan of sports facilities will be signed between the borough and the organization.
According to the decision summary, the loan of the courts has no additional direct financial impact and maintenance remains unchanged.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is accepting a $25,000 sponsorship from Caisse Desjardins du Centre-est de Montréal for the Fête du citoyen 2026.
The event will take place on September 13, 2026; the money will be used to support the event's activities.
In exchange, Desjardins gets visibility: its logo on an invitation card delivered to 34,000 doors, mentions in the Léonardois newspaper, the newsletter, Facebook, the website and the advertising.
At the event site, the area for families will bear the Desjardins name, and Desjardins will also give a speech at the closing show and have its name displayed on the giant screen.
The mayor and the borough secretary are authorized to sign the agreement.
The sponsorship is rising from $20,000 in 2024 and 2025 to $25,000 in 2026.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving minor exemptions for a single-family home at 12172, rue Reeves, built in 1971.
The request comes from a notary following a sale of the property; no work is planned on the building.
The house will be allowed to stay 4.40 m from the street instead of the required 6 m, and 1.04 m from the property line on the right instead of 1.5 m.

The eaves will be allowed to stay 0.09 m from the property line on the right and 1.18 m on the left, instead of the required 1.2 m, and the eaves on the right will be allowed to extend into the side setback.
This allowance for the eaves on the right is conditional on compliance with construction and fire protection standards.
The planning advisory committee had unanimously recommended the request on April 10, 2026; no one spoke at the public consultation.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is allowing two pieces of electrical equipment that are larger than the standard at 8601, boulevard Henri-Bourassa Est.
The Hydro-Québec transformer will be 4.46 m³ and 1.88 m high, instead of the maximums of 1.5 m³ and 1.6 m set out in the zoning by-law.
The electrical distribution cabinet will be 4.87 m³ and 2.31 m high, instead of the same maximums of 1.5 m³ and 1.6 m.
A school bus transportation company operates the site and is electrifying its fleet; the equipment is used to power its charging stations.
Condition imposed: install an opaque fence from the left side wall of the building to the property line to hide the equipment and the parking area from the street.
The urban planning advisory committee had unanimously recommended the application on May 1, 2026.
No one present at the meeting asked a question or made a comment about the application.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is exempting the developer of a residential project from providing one of the three required parking spaces: two will be built instead of three.
The project is located at 11762 to 11766, rue de La Gauchetière, between 5e and 6e Avenues, in the Vieux-Pointe-aux-Trembles area.
In exchange, the owner is paying $2,500 into the borough's parking compensation fund.
Two accessory buildings on the lot will be demolished to make way for a three-storey residential building with three units.
The Direction du développement du territoire justifies the exemption by on-street parking that is not overloaded, several STM bus routes less than 400 metres away, and bike paths nearby.
Next steps: borough council decision on June 2, 2026, then issuance of the demolition and construction permits.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles approves the signage plans for a business at 12020, rue Notre-Dame Est, at the corner of boulevard Saint-Jean-Baptiste.
The ground-floor commercial space will soon be occupied by a restaurant and an alcoholic beverage outlet (microbrewery).
Four signs are authorized: two flat signs (2.51 m² on Notre-Dame Est, 0.46 m² on Saint-Jean-Baptiste) and two projecting LED illuminated signs of 0.58 m² each.
The signs are made of aluminum, black steel, acrylic and vinyl, in shades of black, white and green.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 5, 2026; the department considers that the signage fits in with the building's architecture.
The mixed-use building (residential and commercial) where the business is located comes from a specific project authorized in 2022 and is now built.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is asking the Directeur de l'état civil to designate three elected officials as officiants for marriages and civil unions.
They are Mayor Chantal Gagnon, Councillor Alexandre Devaux-Guizani (Maisonneuve–Longue-Pointe) and Councillor Sarah V. Doyon (Hochelaga).
Once designated, they will be able to perform marriages only within the borough's territory, and only for as long as they hold elected office.
Councillor Julien Hénault-Ratelle (Tétreaultville) has been an officiant since 2022: no new request is needed for him.
The Directeur de l'état civil will assign a unique identification number to each new officiant.
This matter involves no spending.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve will hold its council meeting of June 29, 2026 at 6 p.m. at parc Carlos-d'Alcantara, at 5508, rue de Contrecoeur.
In case of rain or an extreme heat warning, the meeting will be moved to the maison de la culture Mercier, at 8105, rue Hochelaga, at the same time.
The meeting scheduled for August 10, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. is cancelled; the borough says it still meets the minimum of 10 meetings per year required by law.
The meeting of October 5, 2026 is postponed to October 14, 2026, at 6:30 p.m., to avoid a conflict with the provincial elections held on October 5.
Residents will be informed of the location through a public notice, the borough's website, Facebook, Instagram and the newsletter.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is accepting the help of a public works team from Ville-Marie that specializes in cleaning around encampments and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
The team has 8 people and 4 vehicles, works daytime hours on weekdays, and starts its activities in mid-April 2026 for 12 months.

The intervention sites will be chosen together with the managers of the boroughs being served; the same team also serves Ville-Marie, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and Le Sud-Ouest.
The borough points to the spread of tents and encampments in its parks and green spaces, which require cleanliness work beyond regular maintenance.
The staff are trained on cohabitation issues and work with the social development teams, ÉMMIS and the SPVM.
The agreement has no financial impact for Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.
A similar agreement had been accepted in 2025 for a period of 6 months.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is allocating a management surplus of $3,509,728 for the 2025 fiscal year, granted by the Ville.
The largest share, $2,500,000, goes toward setting up a reserve for the 2028 budget balance.
$1,000,000 is added to the 2027 budget balance reserve, which rises to $2,549,338.
$100,000 goes to snow removal (reserve raised to $301,366) and $100,000 to a reserve for other purposes related to elected officials.
$309,728 is paid into the unallocated surplus, which reaches $482,152, while the unallocated budget balance reserve of $500,000 is reduced to zero.
After these transfers, the borough's reserves total $6,742,188.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is receiving $472,200 from the ministère de la Sécurité publique for its youth project.
The money will be used to carry out "Animation, jeunesse, actions à Saint-Léonard, version 4", from September 1, 2025 to August 31, 2026.
The ministère confirmed by letter on February 17, 2026 that the 2025-2026 funding had been approved.
The executive committee is being asked to adjust the City's 2026 operating budget by adding $472,200 to the borough's revenues and expenses.
The amount must be spent during the 2026 fiscal year, with the possibility of extending the period if the ministère agrees.
The funding follows an application submitted by the borough, authorized by a borough council resolution on December 1, 2025.
The borough of Saint-Léonard received $9,700 from the ministère de l'Emploi et du Développement social du Canada, under the "Nouveaux Horizons pour les aînés" program.
The money will be used to enhance the organization of the "Semaine des personnes aînées de Saint-Léonard 2026" project.
The executive committee is asked to adjust the City's 2026 operating budget: the borough's revenues and expenses each increase by $9,700.
The ministère approved the request on February 12, 2026, and the agreement was signed on March 6, 2026.
The amount must be spent during the 2026 fiscal year.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is taking $200,000 from its surplus to cover snow removal cost overruns for 2026.
The money will mainly be used to pay staff wages and to buy abrasives (salt, sand).
Since November 15, 2025, there have been 39 abrasive-spreading operations, whereas the budget had provided for 20 for the season.
The cold during the first three months of the year and the periods of freezing rain drove up the amounts of salt used.
The borough's base budget covers a normal winter: 180 cm of snow, 5 snow-hauling operations, 15 roadway clearings and 20 sidewalk operations.
Any amount not used by the end of the financial year will go back into the snow management surplus.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is drawing $400,000 from its surplus to pay for work that goes beyond its regular budget.
The money will go toward the spring cleaning of streets and public spaces, where debris, gravel and garbage pile up.
Part of it will go toward filling potholes, using temporary staff and targeted contracts to shorten repair times.
The rest will fund one-time projects that the borough's departments consider priorities, related to safety, economic development and services to residents.
Actual spending may vary from one category to another, but without going over the $400,000 authorized.
The amounts will be added to the budget as soon as the borough council makes its decision.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is allocating $3,355,200 in surplus from its 2025 fiscal year.
The largest share, $3,184,900, goes to the "miscellaneous" surplus, which the borough can use freely to give itself some flexibility or to meet needs.
$155,100 goes to the reserve for occupational health and safety, and $15,200 to the contingency reserve.
According to the document, the allowed ceilings have already been reached for the other surplus categories (including the snow removal reserve).
The allocation follows the 2025 surplus policy adopted by city council on June 15, 2026.
The Service des finances will pay the amounts to the boroughs once their allocation has been submitted.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is carrying over $7,705,000 in capital works budget that was not spent in 2025 to its 2026 budget.
This money will be used to fund local projects already committed to or under way that were not completed or that were postponed.
City council had authorized this carry-over on June 15, 2026 for all boroughs.
According to the document, the carry-over has no effect on the level of borrowing charged to taxpayers.
The transfers will be made as soon as the resolution is adopted by the borough council.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is presenting its financial picture as of May 31, 2026, as the law requires before the next budget is adopted.
The borough expects to end the year 2026 with a net surplus of $936,600, or about 2.1% of its amended budget.

The spending budget went from $44,188,700 to $46,113,600, in particular with $897,200 in surplus funds used (snow removal, potholes, spring cleanup, dismantling of the inflatable structure at parc Hébert).
The borough received $616,200 in government assistance, including $472,200 from the ministère de la Sécurité publique for youth spaces.

Projected revenues ($3,301,200) fall short of target by $270,900, partly because of the cancellation of the spring session at the aquatic complex (about $175,000 in losses) due to delays in the renovation work.
After five months, spending totals $15,449,251, which is $691,171 more than on the same date in 2025, mainly because of the new operating contracts for the aquatic complex and the stade Hébert.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is renewing its graffiti removal contract with 9181-5084 Québec inc. (Solutions Graffiti) for one year.
The contract costs $38,024.53, taxes included, and covers April 1, 2026 to March 30, 2027.
Graffiti is removed by applying paint or with cleaning products, partly on private property and mostly on public property.
The current contract ends March 31, 2026; call for tenders 24-20802 provided for this 12-month renewal option.
The previous year, the same contract had been awarded for $36,562.05, taxes included.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles agrees to let the Ville-Marie borough take charge of cleaning up and dismantling encampments on its territory, from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027.
The Ville-Marie team, managed by its Division des parcs et de l'horticulture, steps in at the request of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles; the work sites are chosen together.
The team has 6 people and 4 vehicles (a packer truck or dump van, two vans, a foreman's vehicle), working daytime hours during the week.
The document explains that the number of interventions in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles does not justify creating a local team dedicated to and trained for these situations.
Ville-Marie works with its social development teams, ÉMMIS and the SPVM, and an agreement with the Syndicat des cols bleus ensures the team's stability.
The project is funded by the Stratégie Centre-Ville, led by the Service du développement économique; no amount is given.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is hiring Construction Urbex inc. to install a synthetic turf surface in the 6-12 year old play area of parc Giuseppe-Garibaldi.
Maximum spending of $147,155.81: $133,778.01 for the contract and $13,377.80 in contingencies.
Urbex was the lowest of the four compliant bidders; the other bids ranged from $191,122.94 to $218,452.50.
The bid is 40.5% below the $225,000 estimate; the borough explains this by a subcontractor using Chinese rather than American products.
The work is to take place from February 3 to May 29, 2026, so that the play area can open to the public as soon as summer begins.
The cost is covered by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux, funded by a loan by-law.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is awarding the marking of roadways and certain sidewalks to Les Revêtements Scell-Tech inc., the lowest compliant bidder.
The authorized spending totals $1,003,168.49: $911,971.35 for the contract and $91,197.14 in contingencies.
The contract runs 36 months, from March 10, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with two possible one-year renewals (up to December 31, 2030).
Prices will be indexed each year according to the consumer price index, starting January 1, 2027.
The bid comes in $317,788.89 (25.8%) below the borough's estimate, which the file attributes to the stability of paint prices and to the fact that the company already held the previous contract.
Without this contract, there would be no marking in the spring and the roadways would remain without lines or symbols for weeks, or even months.
The company will be subject to a performance evaluation, since the contract exceeds $500,000.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is renewing, for a final year, the rental of four graders with operators, from April 16, 2026 to April 15, 2027.
Two contracts are being renewed: $247,117.49 to Entreprise Guillaume Dufour inc. (Machinerie TEK) for lots 1 and 3, and $288,549.89 to Pavages Chartrand inc. for lots 2 and 4.
The maximum total comes to $535,667.38, to which an increase based on the consumer price index for the Montréal region will be added.

The graders are used for snow removal in the areas of the borough handled "in-house", in support of the blue-collar employees, in order to meet the deadlines set out in the City's snow removal policy.
The machines are rented at an hourly rate, as needed and at the borough's request.
Part of the contract will be paid out of the management surplus set aside for snow removal, to cover unforeseen operating costs.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is awarding a $221,183.16 contract to 9083-0126 Québec inc. (Creusage RL) for hydro-excavation services, including the handling of waste materials.
The contract is for digging around sewer and drinking water pipes in order to repair them or locate underground services, using a method that is less invasive than conventional excavation.
The work will be done as needs arise, between April 8, 2026 and December 31, 2028 (approximate dates).
The spending is spread over three years: about $73,727.72 of the contract per year for 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The company was the lowest compliant bidder in group call for tenders 25-21256 (lot 8), opened on January 27, 2026.
The bid is $36,504.56 lower (-14.17%) than the $257,687.72 estimate, because the costs of disposing of sludge had been overestimated.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is hiring Limoges et Fils inc. to develop the îlot Paimpol, a triangular grassy lot at the corner of boulevard Lacordaire and rue de Paimpol.
The authorized spending comes to $2,367,043.69: $2,151,857.90 for the contract and $215,185.79 in contingencies.
The centrepiece of the project will be the construction of a monumental fountain; access to the site will be universally accessible.
The work is to run from May 5, 2026 to May 31, 2027 (approximate dates).
Limoges et Fils inc. was the lowest of the five compliant bidders; its bid is 3.9% below the estimate of $2,240,000.
The Service des grands parcs is covering $794,986 (net of rebates) through the local parks refurbishment and greening program; the rest is paid by the borough.
The lot could be added to parc Ladauversière after the blue line extension work.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is awarding 9190-8673 Québec inc. (Les Entreprises Rose Neige) the work to create a green space on rue Puyseaux.
The maximum authorized expense is $670,536.53: $609,578.66 for the contract and $60,957.87 in contingencies.
The work aims to add greenery to the section of rue Puyseaux that has been closed to traffic for the past few years, described as a paved-over space.
The company submitted the lowest of the 14 bids; the contract had been estimated at $815,000, which is 25.2% more than the winning bid.
The work is to start around May 5, 2026 and be completed around September 26, 2026.
The expense is funded by an allocation from surplus; the entrances to the site will be designed to be universally accessible.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving LANCO AMÉNAGEMENT INC. the job of converting the tennis courts at parc Wilfrid-Bastien into pickleball courts.
The contract is for $396,203.85, and the authorized spending rises to $435,824.24 with $39,620.39 in contingencies.
The 3 tennis courts will be turned into 7 pickleball courts; the current synthetic turf surface has reached the end of its useful life.
The work is planned from June 1 to October 16, 2026 (approximate dates).
LANCO was the lowest of the 7 bidders, all of which met the requirements; the bids ranged from $396,203.85 to $976,925.33.
The bid is $43,796.15 lower (-9.95%) than the $440,000 estimate; the project is funded by loan by-law 2272.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is rejecting the three bids received to build a multi-purpose path on rue de Lisieux (call for tenders 102-198).

The project aimed to connect the existing bike network at the des Angevins / Lisieux intersection to the Maison du loisir et du sport, for cyclists and pedestrians between rue des Angevins and rue Paimpol.
The contract was estimated at $370,000, but the lowest bid came to $476,341.42, which is $106,341.42 more (+28.74%).
The borough explains the gap in particular by the small number of bidders (three) and the full order books at this time of year.
A new call for tenders is planned for this winter.
The borough of Outremont is appointing Mercedez Plante, the councillor for the Joseph-Beaubien district, to sit on the board of directors of PME MTL Centre-Ville.
She replaces Valérie Patreau, who had held this seat since 2017; the terms of elected officials end when municipal elections are called.
PME MTL Centre-Ville provides professional services to private and social economy entrepreneurs on the island of Montréal.
The organization's by-laws provide for one seat for an elected official from three of the four boroughs in its territory, with this position alternating between Outremont and the Ville de Westmount.
The document does not provide for any spending.
The appointment still has to go through the executive committee (March 11, 2026), city council (March 23, 2026) and the urban agglomeration council (March 26, 2026).
The borough of Outremont is authorizing the closure of avenue Hartland, between Van Horne and Ducharme, on Friday, February 13, 2026, from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m.
The street is being closed for the Fête des voisins d'hiver - Hartland, organized by citizens living on the avenue.
The borough is lending equipment (barricades) and expects about 50 people to attend.
The event is free and open to everyone; the organizers must obtain the required permits.
The organizers must put up the closure notices 10 days in advance and inform residents and business owners (street closures, parking bans).
The costs of the City's support are absorbed within existing operating budgets.

The borough of Outremont is receiving $49,500 from the organization Sport et loisir de l'île de Montréal (SLIM) for 2026, and is asking the executive committee to adjust the City's budget accordingly.
The money will be used to set up a free sports equipment lending centre, under the Circonflexe banner, an initiative of the ministère de l'Éducation.
The project includes self-service smart lockers, a lending counter at parc Beaubien, introductory skating lessons and sports activities in the borough's parks.
The grant covers the renovation of rooms in the parc Beaubien chalet, the purchase of equipment to be lent out and promotional tools; taxes are paid out of the borough's budget.
The program aims to provide access to physical activity for the borough's entire population, particularly people in vulnerable situations.
SLIM will pay $34,650 within 30 days of the signing of the agreement and $14,850 by January 31, 2027 at the latest; the project must be completed by December 31, 2026.
The Outremont borough wants to amend its by-law on garage sales to give itself an ordinance power.
Currently, garage sales are only allowed on the first full weekend of June, July and August, as well as the Labour Day weekend and the Monday of Labour Day.
With the change, the borough council could authorize an event to be held outside of these periods.
The council could impose any condition it considers necessary, including a time limit.
Planned steps: notice of motion and tabling of the draft by-law on April 9, 2026, adoption on May 5, 2026, coming into force in May 2026.
There is no financial aspect associated with this file.
The borough of Outremont agrees to transfer a professional services contract from the firm Affleck de la Riva SENC to the new company Studio Affleck de la Riva Inc.
The contract covers architecture, engineering and landscape architecture services for the restoration and upgrading to standards of the chalet in parc Saint-Viateur.
This contract was awarded on October 6, 2022 for a maximum amount of $363,321, taxes included, following a public call for tenders with 3 bidders.
The transfer is taking place because the two members of the general partnership have chosen to carry out their activities through a recently incorporated company.
The contract required the written approval of the borough council for such a transfer.
The borough secretary is authorized to sign the transfer agreement on behalf of the borough.
Only the supplier's contact information changes in the project file and on the purchase order.
The borough of Outremont is authorizing two flea markets across its entire territory in 2026.
The dates chosen: Saturday and Sunday, May 23 and 24, then September 19 and 20, 2026.
These weekends are in addition to the periods already set out in the by-law on garage sales (the first full weekends of June, July and August, plus the long Labour Day weekend).
The council can do this because an ordinance power was recently added to by-law AO-467, at the request of the mayor's office.
Any garage sale outside the set periods must be authorized by the council, which may impose any conditions it deems necessary.
No amount is tied to the decision; the ordinance will be published on the public notices website.
The borough of Outremont is authorizing the Fête des voisins Hartland, organized by residents of avenue Hartland, on Tuesday, June 23, 2026, from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m.
Avenue Hartland will be closed between Ducharme and Van Horne for the whole duration of the event.
The borough is lending equipment (barricades) and expects about 50 participants.
The ordinance allows exemptions from the by-laws on parks, occupancy of the public roadway and public property, nuisances and cleanliness, as well as traffic and parking.
The organizers must put up street closure notices 10 days in advance and inform residents and businesses on the streets that will be closed or where parking will be prohibited.
The costs of the City's support services are absorbed into the operating budgets of the departments involved; the event is free and open to all.
A public notice of coming into force must be published in May 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $9,000 to the organization L'École et les arts to organize the 2026-2027 school cultural season for elementary schools in the area.

The organization will put together a program of four shows: it coordinates the schools, the companies and the suppliers, pays for the shows, handles billing and organizes transportation for the students.

The borough is lending the Théâtre Mirella et Lino Saputo at the Centre communautaire Leonardo da Vinci free of charge, and is providing the welcoming of artists and students as well as the technical production.
The payment is made in two parts: $3,000 in 2026 and $6,000 in 2027; the final amount will depend on the organization's accountability report.
The agreement ends on June 30, 2027. This is the sixth year in a row that the borough has supported this project, each time for $9,000.

The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council refuses to authorize the use "habitation collective de soins et de services" (collective care and services housing) at 2320-2322, avenue Marcil.
The request sought to bring into compliance a private residence that has been in operation since 2014, which houses up to 11 vulnerable people aged 16 and over in 8 rental units.
Residents are referred by the institut Douglas, CLSCs/CIUSSSs or public curators; the services offered include meals, housekeeping, laundry, help with medication, recreation and security.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain cites sanitation problems (water damage, bed bugs), nuisances and non-compliant emergency exits found during inspections since January 2025.
The building was evacuated and has been vacant since water damage that occurred in the summer of 2025.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended approval on January 15, 2025, on the condition of a maximum of 11 people; the file was removed from the agenda on February 3, 2025.
A public notice was published on January 16, 2026 and a sign was posted on the building on January 15, 2026.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is authorizing the creation of a dwelling with part of it located in the basement, at 4605-4615, avenue Van Horne.
The owner will be allowed to create an additional dwelling in a vacant space that once housed a convenience store; the bedrooms and the bathroom will be in the basement.
The building, built in 1957, currently has 28 dwellings; the new dwelling will be reached through the existing entrance on Van Horne.
New windows will be cut into the façade facing rue Lavoie to bring light into the ground floor and the basement bedrooms.
A French drain will be installed around the foundations, which the City presents as protection against flooding.
The authorization is conditional on the project being carried out as shown on the plans; the building permit application has not yet been filed.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is approving the expansion plans for Collège Jean-de-Brébeuf, at 3200, chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine.
The project, called Pavillon du Centenaire, includes a multipurpose gymnasium and living spaces for students and extracurricular activities, which will also be open to the local community.
The front of the expansion will be set back so that the original pavilion remains the main landmark along chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine.
A former parking lot and a semi-indoor courtyard will be redeveloped with new trees and green spaces; the plans call for the removal of 47 vehicle parking spaces and 202 bicycle spaces.

The urban planning advisory committee had set four conditions; the developer met two of them (lighting directed toward the ground and a review of the parking) and set aside the two dealing with the treatment of the façades, citing technical constraints and the schedule.
The land is located in the Mont-Royal heritage site: the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité and the ministère de la Culture et des Communications must also authorize the plans.

The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is authorizing parts of dwellings to be built in the basement of the building to be constructed at 6365, rue Sherbrooke Ouest, at the corner of avenue West Hill.
The project calls for a 4-storey building with 27 dwellings and 2 commercial spaces on the ground floor.
Two dwellings will be spread over two levels: ground floor and basement (bedrooms and bathroom in the basement).

The basement openings will be on the side opposite rue Sherbrooke and fitted with window wells; the slopes of the land will be redone to direct water away, because of a dip in the northwest part of the land.
