The authorization is conditional on the project being carried out as shown on plans P-1 to P-4.

The urban planning advisory committee unanimously recommended the application on February 11, 2026; a public notice was published on February 20 and a sign was posted on the site on February 19, 2026.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce agrees to let the City's Service des infrastructures du réseau routier conduct negotiations on its behalf with the Ville de Côte Saint-Luc regarding the maintenance of the chemin de la Côte-Saint-Luc underpass.
The underpass in question is located where the Canadien Pacifique (CPKC) tracks cross avenue West Broadway, between rue Robert-Burns and avenue MacMahon, on the boundary between the two cities.
It includes a road bridge, a pedestrian walkway, six retaining walls and a pumping station; the CP railway bridge is excluded from the agreement.
The previous agreements (2000 and 2015) have expired; since then the two cities have been applying their terms without a formal framework.
The sharing of costs and responsibilities between Montréal and Côte Saint-Luc will be set out in an agreement to be presented in a later file.
Without this approval, the maintenance agreement could not be ratified.

The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council is authorizing the company 9215-3790 Québec inc. to build two access lanes and a drainage system on public land, at the corner of avenue Brock Sud and boulevard Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue.
The lanes will lead to phase 3 of a neighbouring residential project: direct access from boulevard Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue and one-way southbound access from avenue Brock Sud.
The company wants to start the work as early as spring 2026, because the building is finished and residents want to get to the indoor parking.
The authorization is temporary: it ends when a by-law governing permanent occupancy of the public land comes into force.
The company acts as the project manager, assumes the risks and damages related to the work, maintains the site year-round, and must obtain the other required permits at its own expense.
The City may withdraw the authorization if the company remains in default 60 days after a written notice; the company may end it with 30 days' notice.
The file involves no expense for the Ville de Montréal.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is granting two exceptions to the planning rules for a new 3-storey residential building at 5212-5214 and 5222, avenue Walkley.
The project calls for 18 affordable housing units funded by a grant from the Société d'habitation du Québec (SHQ).

First exception: private terraces 2.4 m wide will be allowed to take up part of the front yard that would normally have to be planted, in order to give the 3 ground-floor units access to a relaxation area.
Second exception: all the bicycle parking spaces will be allowed to be outside, whereas the rule requires at least 50% inside the building.

According to the document, these departures from the rules are necessary because the SHQ grant requires keeping the same number of housing units, reusing the footprint of the original building, and not building a basement.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on March 18, 2026, except for a small square in the front yard, which was removed from the project because it would have been built in the roots of a tree.
A construction permit application is being processed at the same time; work has not started.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is authorizing the development of housing units in the basement of 2100, avenue Van Horne.
The project creates 6 new housing units in the existing garage of a 1950 building that already has 13 units.
Estimated rents range from $875 to $975, which the Direction describes as below the affordability threshold for households in the bottom 30% of median income.
Conditions imposed: remove the vehicle access and the lowered sidewalk, de-pave the south side yard, and carry out the work as authorized in the permit.
Openings on the occupied floors must be located above 95.291 m (south yard) and 97.09 m (north yard).
A French drain will be installed around the building and vegetation added to reduce flooding risks.
A notice was published in the newspapers on June 19, 2026 and a sign posted on the site on June 18; the resolution is scheduled for the July 6, 2026 council meeting.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is allowing buses to turn left from the eastbound approach of the Van Horne and Linton intersection.
Left turns there are currently banned from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m., Monday to Friday; the ban stays in place for other vehicles.
"Excepté autobus" (Buses excepted) tabs will be added under the no-turn signs.
The request comes from the STM, as part of the overhaul of its bus routes: the new southbound route of line 155 uses this turn.
According to the document, without this turn the line's travel time would increase, and little impact on traffic flow is expected.
The signs are to be installed in spring 2026; costs are billed according to the rates of the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is granting a minor exemption for a future building at 5520, chemin de la Côte-Saint-Luc.
The exemption allows the elevator shaft that rises above the roof (1.25 m) to have no setback from one façade on the 5th floor, whereas the by-law requires a setback of twice its height.
The project calls for a mixed-use building: 3 commercial units on the ground floor and 13 housing units on the upper floors.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain points to the unusual shape of the lot, the setback required on the 5th floor and the limited space available to move the elevator.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on April 15, 2026, and a public notice was published on April 17, 2026.
The building permit application is under review and work has not started.
The resolution is scheduled for the borough council meeting of May 4, 2026.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is accepting the free transfer of a 107.6 m² piece of land at 5445, boulevard Décarie, representing 10% of the lot, to be used for park purposes.
This transfer is tied to a project to build a six-storey residential building with 54 units on the same site.
The City will also buy the neighbouring lot (112.7 m²) from the same owner for $230,000 plus taxes; the net cost of $241,471.25 will be paid out of the borough's parks fund.
The two lots together will form a 220 m² local green space, between boulevard Décarie, avenue Trans Island and boulevard Édouard-Montpetit.
The Service de l'environnement concludes that the soil on the transferred land is suitable for a park without a play area.
The deed of sale for the second lot will be signed after construction of the building is completed and the condition of the land has been verified.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is authorizing the construction of four residential buildings, in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur.
Building D must house a municipal sports and recreation centre; its construction depends on two agreements with the City, including one on operating the centre.
The developer will pay a contribution of $3,200,000 for public facilities and equipment in the area, in four payments made when the permit applications are submitted.
The project will depart from the rules on maximum height, density, side setbacks and permitted uses, among others: the buildings may reach 147 metres.

No parking will be allowed for the housing units, businesses or institutions; only an indoor commercial parking facility open to the public, with a maximum of 750 spaces, is authorized, with 4% of the spaces reserved for car sharing.
Each building must provide hundreds of bicycle spaces (from 318 to 417), tree planting and a minimum greening percentage of 25% to 40%.
A development agreement must be reached between the City and 9467-9370 Québec Inc.; the borough secretary will hold a public consultation meeting.
The City is extending its contract with the firm Pure Technologies ltd. by 24 months to detect leaks in large water mains, using a probe that travels inside pipes while they are in service.
Additional cost of $963,470.31 including taxes, of which $87,588.21 is set aside for contingencies, bringing the total contract to $2,518,898.68.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Direction de la gestion des actifs and is borne entirely by the agglomeration.
Goal: inspect 15 kilometres of pipes, locate the leaks (ground markings and GPS coordinates) and provide videos and reports.
The work is to begin in July 2026 and end in June 2028.
The firm refused to renew the second part of the contract (non-intrusive method), because it no longer offers that service; the Service de l'eau will look for other methods.
The contract's unit prices were indexed by 2.14% based on the consumer price index from July 2023 to June 2025.
The borough of Lachine is taking $398,000 from its surplus to keep its traffic team in place for about nine more months, from April to December 2026 (or until the funds run out).
The money extends three temporary positions: one section head and two technical officers in traffic and parking.
An hours bank of $50,000 is set aside for signage attendants.
$358,000 goes to pay and $40,000 to the operating budget, mainly for equipment and studies.
The team handles on-street parking, local mobility, management of construction site obstructions and requests from residents.
The borough says it sees a gap between actual needs and its current in-house capacity.
The City is entering into a 3-year agreement with Les Emballages Carrousel inc. to supply plastic bags to the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal, for a maximum of $545,740.34, taxes included.

These bags are used to bag firefighters' protective clothing and equipment that has been exposed to contaminants, both for the return to the fire station and for transport to cleaning and annual maintenance.
The agreement covers 4 types of bags, from 6 x 9 inches up to 50 x 35 inches, in thicknesses of 2 or 3 MIL.
The spending is spread over three years: $172,830.42, then $181,108.62, then $191,801.30, taxes included.

Of the 7 companies that obtained the tender documents, only one submitted a bid; the price is 50% below the City's estimate of $1,098,586.12, as the City had never had an agreement for these purchases before.
The agglomeration covers 100% of the cost; a purchase order is to be issued in March 2026, after which orders will follow as needed.
The City will evaluate the supplier's performance.
Montréal agrees to run, on behalf of the Ville de Longueuil, the call for tenders to replace the self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) used by firefighters in both fire departments.
The call for tenders covers the purchase of the units, their rollout, maintenance, staff training and the management of consigned replacement parts, over ten years.
The director of the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal is authorized to sign the intermunicipal letter of agreement setting out each city's roles.
Each city pays for its own equipment: Montréal acts as administrative and technical agent, without covering Longueuil's expenses.
Longueuil has estimated its share at $6,108,621.75, including taxes, subject to its loan by-law CA-2026-461 coming into force.
The units currently in service in both cities (Interspiro model S8) are reaching the end of their useful life, and a new NFPA 1970 standard (2025) was published in late 2024.
The mandate ends when the contract is awarded; each city then manages its own portion of the contract.
The City is authorizing spending of $170,453.71, taxes included, to buy fire hoses for the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal (SIM).
The purchase goes through the group purchasing program of the Union des municipalités du Québec (UMQ), which extends contract SI-2024 by one year, until June 30, 2026.
The chosen supplier is Équipements Incendies C.M.P. Mayer inc., for 100 hoses of 1.75 in. x 50 ft., 140 of 3 in. x 50 ft., 15 of 4 in. x 25 ft. and 15 of 4 in. x 50 ft. (delivery included).
These hoses replace ones that have reached the end of their useful life, that were damaged during emergency responses, or that failed the annual tests under the NFPA 1962 standard.
The amount includes $1,467.85 in management fees (1%) paid to the UMQ; the price is $7,365.49 lower (-4.14%) than the City's estimate.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, since fire safety is an agglomeration responsibility.
Next step planned for May 2026: joining the group purchasing program and issuing the purchase order.
The City is removing 11 lots from its list of buildings subject to the right of first refusal for social housing, a list drawn up in 2020.
The properties affected are in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest: rue Florian, rues Saint-Christophe and Saint-André, rue Fullum, 464 Saint-François-Xavier, avenue de l'Église and rue Eadie.
Reason given: these buildings have been subdivided into condominiums or developed by their owners since 2020, without any transaction with the City taking place.
The City says it wants to avoid having to deal with a notice of intent to sell (60-day deadline) every time a condominium unit is put up for sale.
The Service des affaires juridiques is mandated to have the notices of subjection registered in the Registre foncier struck off.
The document states that there is no financial impact for the City.
The City is removing 11 lots from its list of buildings subject to the right of first refusal for housing, a list adopted in March 2022.
The addresses affected are in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest: rue Florian, rue Saint-Christophe, rue Saint-André, rue Saint-François-Xavier, rue Fullum, avenue de l'Église and rue Eadie.
Reason given: these buildings were subdivided into condominiums or developed by their owners without any transaction taking place.
The City is therefore giving up its right to buy these properties first in the event of a future sale.
Without this removal, the City would receive a notice for each unit put up for sale, with a 60-day processing period, even though it is not considering buying condominiums.
The Service des affaires juridiques is mandated to strike the notices registered in the Registre foncier.
The document indicates no financial impact for the City.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is granting a fee waiver of $1,765 (taxes included) to the Association communautaire Maria-Auxiliatrice for the street closure for its annual parish festival.
The festival runs from August 7 to 9, 2026, on the grounds of the église Maria-Auxiliatrice and on rue Joliot-Curie, between Rita Levi-Montalcini and Huguet-Latour.
The program includes shows, entertainment, food service, a mass, fireworks and a religious procession; the organization expects 2,000 to 4,000 people per day, about 10,000 in total.
Street closure costs were added to the 2026 fee by-law; all event organizers must now pay them.
The organization has been informed that it will have to cover these costs itself starting in 2027; it says it does not have the funds this year.
The amount covers the labour to set up and remove the signage and equipment.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is amending its council's internal by-law to set rules for the public question period.

At meetings, speaking priority will go first to people with a child who have to leave before the end of the question period, then to people who use paratransit and have to leave before the end, then to people whose question is about an item on the agenda, and finally to the other people who signed up.
For written questions sent in through the online form, those about an item on the agenda will come before the others.
The agenda for regular meetings and the decision files will have to be sent to elected officials and posted online no later than 72 hours before the meeting, instead of four days.
This change to the deadline brings the by-law in line with the Cities and Towns Act.
The by-law will come into force on the day a notice of enactment is published on the borough's website.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council adopts a motion in support of the national movement « Le communautaire à boutte ».
It officially recognizes the contribution of community organizations in the area, as well as the work of their teams and volunteers.
It supports the movement's demands: stable and predictable core funding, decent working conditions, and better recognition of the role these organizations play.

It calls on the gouvernement du Québec to strengthen its actions to ensure the viability and funding of the community sector, and asks for a dialogue between Québec, the organizations and the municipalities.
The resolution will be sent to Minister Chantal Rouleau, Premier François Legault, CAQ leadership candidates Christine Fréchette and Bernard Drainville, as well as to the movement's coalition.
The motion is moved by councillor Peter McQueen and seconded by councillor Émilie Brière; no money is attached to it.

On April 13, 2026, residents of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce filed a draft petition to force a public consultation on the rollout of new parking meters on rue Sherbrooke Ouest starting in spring 2026.

The Division du greffe found the draft admissible, on the condition that the text explaining the value of the consultation be shortened to 600 characters; the representatives made the correction on April 28, 2026.
Signatures from people living outside the borough and those collected outside the prescribed forms were excluded from the count.
The group chose to collect signatures on the City's digital platform.
A notice announcing the start of the signing period must appear on the City's website no later than June 8, 2026; the collection will then last 90 days.
5,000 signatures from people aged 15 and over living in Montréal are needed to require a public consultation to be held.
The borough council takes note of the filing of this response; a compliant petition only forces a consultation to be held and cannot block the project.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $3,000 to the organization Le Local Familial.
The money will be used to create 20 free annual memberships for low-income families in the neighbourhood.
Le Local Familial is a space for socializing and play for families in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The contribution is non-recurring: it is paid only once.
The money comes from the borough's elected officials' support budget, at the request of the mayor's office.
The decision falls to the borough council.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $5,000 to the Société d'Histoire et de généalogie du Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The money will be used to hire an archivist to process and share the neighbourhood's historical archives.
The project aims to protect and preserve sites, monuments and documents of historical interest in Le Plateau.
The contribution is non-recurring and comes from the borough's budget for support to elected officials.
The council is also approving the agreement with the organization and authorizing the borough mayor and the borough secretary (or their substitutes) to sign the documents.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $1,000 to La Petite Maison de la Miséricorde, for the Table de Concertation Autour des Familles Grand Plateau.
The money will be used to organize the Fête des Familles 2026 and to mark the 20th anniversary of the Table de concertation.
The event will take place on May 22 at parc des Compagnons, with free activities for parents, children and neighbourhood partners.
The contribution is non-recurring and comes from the borough's budget for supporting elected officials.
The request comes from the mayor's office, under section 137 of the Charter of Ville de Montréal.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $5,000 to the Comité logement du Plateau-Mont-Royal, as a one-time (non-recurring) contribution.
The money will be used to create an assistance fund for low-income tenants in the neighbourhood who are facing housing problems.

The fund can cover the cost of opening a file at the Tribunal administratif du logement, obtaining documents (certificates, copies, official reports, technical reports) and legal or community support.
It can also pay costs related to a forced move, emergency measures or homelessness prevention, as well as administrative support in dealings with public bodies.
The money comes from the borough's budget for supporting elected officials, at the request of the mayor's office.
The council approves the agreement with the organization and authorizes the borough mayor and the borough secretary to sign the documents.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving out $1,500 in total to three organizations, $500 each, as one-time contributions.
Fondation Lucia Kowaluk receives $500 for an event at parc Lucia-Kowaluk on June 5, for World Environment Day.
Livart receives $500 for the exhibition "Bouquet final" and free workshops; over nine weeks, close to 1,500 children from summer art camps will take part.
La Maison d'Aurore receives $500 for the Marché des petits entrepreneurs on June 6, where young people aged 6 to 17 will sell their products.
The money comes from the borough's budget for supporting elected officials, at the request of the mayor's office.
The organizations handle their own communications, following the borough's logo guide.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is paying $5,000, all applicable taxes included, to the organization Jardins pour Tous.
The money goes to the "Jardins urbains Notman" project, which aims to secure greening in the Milton-Parc neighbourhood.
The project targets a healthy and welcoming space for seniors and families, and relies on citizen mobilization.
The contribution is non-recurring and comes from the borough's budget for supporting elected officials.
The council is also approving an agreement with the organization; the borough mayor and the borough secretary (or their substitutes) are authorized to sign it.
The organization manages its own communications and must follow the borough's logo usage guide.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is paying out $9,900 in one-time financial contributions to two neighbourhood organizations.
La Maison d'Aurore is receiving $4,950 to organize the distribution of plants and seedlings supplied by the borough, scheduled for May 23.
La Maison de l'amitié de Montréal is receiving $4,950 for the "Cultivons le Plateau" event, which distributes flowers, compost and mulch to residents.
The two events also serve to introduce residents to community organizations in the area (ecological transition, urban agriculture, food security, homelessness).
The money comes from the borough's budget for support to elected officials.
Each organization manages its own communications, following the borough's logo use guide.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is creating a new "Sports et installations" section within its Division des sports, loisirs et installations.

This section already manages the facilities of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social: maintenance, buildings, security and access control, requests, sharing space with partners and, at times, programming.
The borough cites an increase in workload: more facilities to manage, the reopening of the aréna Saint-Louis, and taking back maintenance duties previously handled by the SGPI.
Two positions are moving to a different responsibility centre: a development officer and a liaison officer.
According to the document, the change does not lead to any increase in the borough's budget.
The restructuring follows the one that began in 2025, with the creation of the position of section head – sports, recreation and social development.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving out $3,800 in one-time financial contributions to two organizations.

L'Association pour la Promotion des Arts sur le Plateau (APAP) receives $3,500 for a family Fête nationale celebration on June 23 at parc Laurier: face painting, balloons, storytelling, ball hockey, dancing, shows and evening music.

La Fête des voisins Milton-Parc receives $300 for its neighbourhood party held on June 13 in the Milton-Parc area: a potluck supper for more than 300 people, a piñata, alleyway murals, an outdoor movie and a concert.
The money comes from the borough's budget for supporting elected officials.
The organizations handle their own communications, following the borough's logo use guide.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles must appoint a citizen member to its comité consultatif d'urbanisme (CCU), the committee that advises the borough council on urban planning matters.
The term will last two years, from April 3, 2026 to April 2, 2028.
The position is becoming vacant because the term of Jean Lanthier, a citizen member since 2018, ends on April 2, 2026.
The name of the person to be appointed is not yet written in the document.
The committee is made up of six residents, one elected member of the borough council and the borough mayor; the two-year terms are renewable and can be revoked by the council.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is buying poles, mast arms and their accessories from Métal Pole-Lite inc. for $70,709.63 (taxes included), paid entirely by the borough.

This material will be used to install six overhead signage structures at the entrances to the school zones of the Félix-Leclerc and Daniel-Johnson schools (boulevard du Tricentenaire) and Simone-Desjardins school (boulevard Perras).
The school zone signs and the 30 km/h speed limit signs will be hung there above the roadway, following complaints from residents about the poor visibility of the current signage.
Three companies were approached directly; the two other offers were $91,163.68 and $94,256.51.
The selected price exceeds the internal estimate of $30,353.40 by $40,356.23, or 57.07%, which the borough attributes to the rise in the cost of steel and aluminum.
Manufacturing takes 14 to 16 weeks; delivery is to begin in August 2026. A postponement of the work could mean losing a grant from the ministère des Transports.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council authorizes organizations and event organizers to occupy public property (parks, squares, streets) for the events on the March 9, 2026 list.
For these events, it becomes permitted to play sound equipment outdoors, up to 80 dBA measured 35 m from the speakers.
Street closures or slowing down traffic is authorized on the dates and at the times set for each event.
Selling promotional items, food and drinks (alcoholic or not) is permitted, as is drinking alcohol, only on the event site and in plastic containers.
Each organizer must submit its civil liability insurance endorsement and the other required documents no later than 72 hours before the event in order to obtain its authorization.
The events are free and local in scale; the borough pays for its support out of its operating budgets, and any additional costs are covered by the organizers.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council authorizes a list of public events to use public property (parks, squares, streets) on the dates and at the times set for each one.
For these events, outdoor sound equipment is allowed, up to a maximum of 80 dBA measured 35 m from the speakers.
Street closures or traffic slowdowns are authorized according to what is planned for each event.
The sale of promotional items, food and drinks, alcoholic or not, is allowed, as is the consumption of alcohol, only on the event site and in plastic containers.
Organizers must submit their proof of civil liability insurance and the other required documents at least 72 hours before the event in order to receive their authorization.
The events are free and local in scope; the City covers the support out of its operating budgets, and any additional costs are paid by the promoters.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is authorizing organizations and event promoters to occupy public property (parks, squares, streets) for the events on the list approved by council on May 4, 2026.
Noise from outdoor sound equipment is allowed at these sites, up to a maximum of 80 dBA measured 35 m from the equipment.
Street closures or slowing down traffic is allowed on the dates and at the times set for each event.
Selling promotional items, food, and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks is allowed at the sites; alcohol must be served in plastic containers and consumed on site only.
Each promoter must hand in its civil liability insurance endorsement and the other required documents no later than 72 hours before the event in order to get its authorization.
The events are free and local in scale; the City covers the support out of its operating budgets, and any additional costs are the promoters' responsibility.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is allowing organizations and event organizers to occupy public property (parks, squares, streets) for the events on the list approved by the council on June 1, 2026.
These local events may be community, sports, cultural, commemorative or festive events, and they are free and open to everyone.
As an exception, the council is allowing noise from sound equipment outdoors, up to 80 dBA measured 35 m from the equipment, according to the planned locations and schedules.
It is also authorizing street closures or slower traffic at the places and times listed.
Selling promotional items, food and drinks (alcoholic or not) is allowed on the sites; alcohol must be served in plastic containers and consumed on site only.
Each organizer must hand in their civil liability insurance endorsement and the other required documents at least 72 hours before the event in order to get their authorization.
Support costs are paid out of the operating budgets of the borough departments; any additional costs are covered by the organizers.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is allowing organizations and event promoters to occupy public property (parks, squares, streets) for the events on the list approved by the council on July 6, 2026.

Depending on the case, these authorizations allow noise from outdoor sound equipment, the sale of promotional items, food and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks, the consumption of alcohol, and street closures.
Noise is limited to 80 dBA measured 35 metres from the sound equipment, and only on the dates, at the times and in the places set for each event.
The council is authorizing the Procession de l'Assomption de Marie on August 15, 2026, from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m., on Saint-Jacques Ouest, avenue Belgrave, chemin Upper Lachine and avenue Old Orchard.
The borough justifies this religious exception based on four criteria in the law: supervised safety, a duration of less than two hours, access open to everyone, and little disruption to traffic.
Each promoter must submit its civil liability insurance rider and the other required documents no later than 72 hours before the event.
The City's support is paid out of operating budgets; any additional costs are covered by the promoters.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is paying $2,888.17 (taxes included) to send eight people to the Chambre de commerce de l'Est de Montréal's Gala ESTim 2026.
The gala takes place on May 7, 2026.
Tickets cost $361.02 each, taxes included.
Those attending are 6 elected officials, the chief of staff and one member of the administration.
The borough states that it is a finalist in several categories of the ESTim 2026 competition.

The Service de l'environnement is submitting to the urban agglomeration council the 2025 annual report of the Réseau de suivi du milieu aquatique, which presents water quality around and on the island of Montréal.

QUALO program: 2,060 analyses at 103 shoreline stations, from May 20 to October 2, 2025. 79% of samples met the criterion allowing swimming and other direct contact with the water; 6% exceeded the threshold ruling out any recreational use.
66 of the 103 stations obtained QUALO approval, meaning they would be suitable for direct water contact activities; 33 of them have held it for at least five years.
RUISSO program: monitoring of 25 inland streams and bodies of water. Low water levels limited sampling; of 23 watercourses assessed, 2 are improving, 13 remain stable and 8 are deteriorating.

Cross connections (wastewater discharged into the stormwater system): more than 20,000 addresses screened and 1,273 cases confirmed to date; 446 remain to be corrected. The related municipalities have corrected 92% of them and the boroughs 53%.

Since the amendment of by-law 20-030, the City has been sending notices of non-compliance: more than 180 owners received a notice in 2025 and must pay for the corrective work themselves within the stated deadlines.
The Stratégie montréalaise de l'eau 2025-2034, unveiled on June 4, 2025, includes the commitment to eliminate 100% of known cross connections.
The City is amending its lease with the Fabrique de la paroisse de Saint-Charles for the basement space at 2115, rue du Centre, in Le Sud-Ouest, which will serve as a temporary library for two years.
The date the City takes possession of the space moves from December 1, 2025 to September 1, 2026.
The leased area increases by 225.84 square feet, reaching 8,864.94 square feet.
The City is paying $288,206.14 more (rent, work and contingencies), bringing the total cost of the temporary relocation to $2,311,680.85.
Unplanned work is being added to bring the space up to code: sprinklers, ventilation (HVAC unit), plumbing, electrical, floor grinding and acoustic panels.
The temporary library will welcome users during the renovation and expansion of the bibliothèque Saint-Charles (Éva-Circé-Côté).
Of the additional expense, $111,281.32 is subsidized by the Entente sur le développement culturel de Montréal; the remaining $176,924.82 is paid by the City.

The City is leasing the 8th and 9th floors of 1611, boulevard Crémazie Est (Ahuntsic-Cartierville) from Galion Équité S.E.C., that is 43,850 square feet of office space, for 9 years and 7 months starting August 1, 2026.
Total cost of the rent: $14,487,192, taxes included. The City also gets an allowance of $464,500 before taxes for work on the space.
About 300 to 400 employees? No — the space will house the Service de l'approvisionnement (86.32% of the space) and the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier (13.68%).
The move follows problems at 255, boulevard Crémazie Est: temperature swings and humidity that is too low, which the City considers a threat to the health of the occupants.
The City plans to go to court to ask for the cancellation of its lease at 255 Crémazie Est and expects the owner to contest this.
No rent is payable from June 1 to July 31, 2026, a period during which the City will already be able to occupy the space and carry out work.
The City will be able to give back the 8th floor without penalty on December 31, 2032, by giving the landlord 12 months' notice.
The borough of Lachine is giving $25,000 to Action Jeunesse de l'Ouest-de-l'Île (AJOI) for its street work program in 2026.
The money pays for a street worker to be present in Lachine, in the locations targeted by the borough.
The workers offer a listening ear, support, referrals, emergency help, mediation and the distribution of prevention materials to young people and vulnerable people.

The document reports an increase in problems involving vulnerable populations in the Saint-Pierre, Louis-Paré and Ivan-Franko neighbourhoods: homelessness, drug addiction, mental health, vandalism and substance use in public spaces.
Thanks to other funders, AJOI expects to have 3 to 4 street workers in the area in 2026, including one specialized in homelessness.
The program runs all year; AJOI must submit a final report to the Division sports, loisirs et développement social.
Same amount as last year: $25,000 was granted for 2025, the maximum allowed under the program.
The borough of Lachine is giving $58,898 to the organization Concert'Action Lachine to extend its youth outreach project by one year.

The project offers mixed martial arts introductory activities to 12-to-25-year-olds in Lachine who are at risk of dropping out of school, becoming disconnected or breaking ties with society, supervised by an outreach worker and a teacher.
The funding covers the period from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The money comes from the central city, through the Prévention Montréal program (a budget of $42.5M over three years), and not from the borough's own budget.
The one-year extension is granted while the program's framework is being reviewed in 2026.
The organization must produce progress reports and a final report no later than one month after the end of the project.
The borough of Lachine is giving $20,000 to the Maison des jeunes L'Escalier de Lachine for its youth activities program in 2026.
The money will be used to hire four part-time activity leaders, from June to August, to go out and meet young people aged 9 to 20 in the parks.
The activity leaders will be present at parc LaSalle, parc Kirkland, parc Grovehill, along the shorelines and at the organization's two service points (5e Avenue and Hub MDJ in Saint-Pierre).
On the program: sports and creative activities, a weekly outing to discover the shorelines, and a mobile gathering space in the parks.
The activity leaders will also do prevention work (drugs, alcohol, violence) and direct young people to local resources.
The project starts on May 5, 2026 and ends in September with the submission of a final report; the amount is paid in full after the council resolution.
This was the only project submitted under this program, which allows for a maximum of $20,000 per year.
The borough of Lachine is appointing three new members to its Conseil jeunesse: Hawa Kryria Latifa Fofana, Nicolas Galopin and Zainab Hussain.
It is also renewing the terms of Alexia Robitaille and Élyzabeth Roy, whose terms were ending on May 4, 2026.
All of these terms run from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2028.
The Conseil jeunesse will therefore have 10 members out of a possible 12; four people have resigned since the last council.
This advisory council brings together volunteers aged 15 to 25 living in Lachine, who give advice to elected officials and organize projects for young people.
No additional spending is being requested; the next recruitment campaign will take place in the fall.
The Lachine borough is giving $50,000 to Concert'Action Lachine, the local neighbourhood roundtable (table de quartier), for the 2026-2027 period.
The money goes toward the organization's mission of community mobilization and consultation, as part of the Initiative montréalaise de soutien au développement social local.
The amount is rising from $31,113 in 2025-2026 to $50,000, since the City increased its contribution to $50,000 per neighbourhood roundtable in its 2026 budget.

The full amount comes from the central city and from Québec: $33,620 from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and $16,380 from an agreement with the ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale (non-recurring).
Along with Centraide ($75,000) and the Direction régionale de santé publique ($23,472), Concert'Action Lachine will receive $148,472 in total.
The organization brings together several Lachine committees: urban safety, intercultural, housing, food security, 50 and over, early childhood and youth.
The borough of Lachine is giving $15,000 to the organization Projet de prévention des toxicomanies : Cumulus to create a mural in 2026.
The mural will be painted on the wall of the municipal parking lot on 11e Avenue, on the building at 180, 11e Avenue.
Cumulus is working with the collective ArtduCommun S.E.N.C.; students from école secondaire Dalbé-Viau will take part in a workshop that will feed into the theme of the artwork.
The final sketch has not been made yet: it will be drawn after the workshop with the young people.
The work is scheduled for late summer or early fall 2026, followed by a final report from the organization.
This is the only project funded in 2026 by the Programme d'art urbain, whose maximum budget is $15,000.
The borough of Ville-Marie is amending its agreement with the Centre culturel et communautaire Sainte-Brigide, which is restoring the former église Sainte-Brigide-de-Kildare on rue de Champlain.
The $100,000 payment planned for 2025 to restore the steeple spire is being postponed to 2026, because the bid was only received on January 27, 2026.
The work was supposed to be finished by June 30, 2026: the end date is pushed back to June 30, 2027, as the organization is waiting for its permits.
The payments become $136,000 in 2026 (including $36,000 already paid on January 22) and $18,000 in 2027; $118,000 remains to be paid.
The total contribution stays at $190,000: $100,000 for the steeple and $90,000 for building upkeep.
The organization must submit the final invoice for the work no later than January 30, 2027, along with its annual reports and financial statements.
The Ville-Marie borough is adding a second component to its Fonds en agriculture urbaine, devoted to activities in community gardens.
Each garden committee that submits an application on time can receive a maximum of $500.
The support is aimed at the 14 garden committees of the borough's Programme des jardins communautaires.
The money is used to run garden activities, to provide access to healthy and affordable food, and to support greening in the neighbourhoods.
The call for projects is launched on April 15, applications must be submitted no later than May 15 at 4 p.m., and the selected projects are announced at the June borough council.
Component 1 of the Fonds remains: up to $20,000 per urban agriculture project, for non-profit organizations or public schools in Ville-Marie.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $500 to Nouveau Théâtre Expérimental for its urban agriculture project « Jardin ».
The money will be used to buy the plants for the project.
The show will be presented in September 2026 at the théâtre Espace Libre, in the Centre-Sud neighbourhood, with a living garden of more than 1,500 plants on stage.
The plants will be chosen with the neighbourhood's residents and organizations, then redistributed to the community after the performances.

The project is being carried out with local partners, including the Société écocitoyenne de Montréal, the Jardin botanique, the Écomusée du fier monde, Lespacemaker, Sentier Urbain and Voies culturelles des faubourgs.
The agreement with the organization ends on December 31, 2026.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving eight floor-covering mats and their two racks free of charge to the non-profit organization Académie Boxe Frontenac, which will be able to keep them permanently.
This equipment was bought in 1996 when the centre Jean-Claude-Malépart opened and was stored there; the borough no longer uses it.
Before giving the equipment away, the borough tried to transfer it to other City units (none were interested) and to return it to the supplier (not possible given its age).
According to the document, its wear and low remaining value did not justify a sale.
The transaction is being made with no payment in return and has no budget impact.
The City is adding $66,758.51 (taxes included) to the contract with the firms AtkinsRealis (formerly SNC Lavalin) and Provencher Roy + Associés Architectes, bringing the total to $4,118,154.43.
This money is used only to produce the final "as-built" drawings for the pont Guy-Lafleur, in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève.
Construction work on the bridge was completed in August 2025, and there was no longer enough money left in the contract budget for this final step.
Only the designers can produce these drawings, which are needed for future work on the bridge and its maintenance; the City says a call for tenders is impossible.
The City is already suing these two firms in court over errors and omissions related to the same contract; the fees will be paid under protest, without any admission of liability.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, through the loan by-law for the bridge project.
The final drawings are expected in the summer of 2026.
The executive committee delegates to the treasurer and the director of financing the power to accept loan offers made to the City and to set their conditions, until December 31, 2026.
The maximum amount that can be borrowed on the markets in 2026 is capped at $1,319,000,000.
The interest rate on the loans cannot exceed that of Government of Québec bonds with a comparable maturity by more than 100 basis points.
The delegates will have to give the executive committee an annual report detailing the loans made, their conditions and the projections for the following year.
The City is planning 5 issues in 2026, of $100,000,000 to $400,000,000 each depending on market conditions.
This borrowing need stems from the City's capital works program, the needs of the STM and the refinancing to be carried out.
The delegation avoids having to go through the executive committee to approve the closing documents, which shortens issue timelines.
The Ville de Montréal is giving the ministre des Finances du Québec the mandate to receive and open bids during its calls for tenders for bonds with a term of five years or less.
The minister will also be able to award these bonds to the lowest compliant bidder, on the City's behalf, without a council resolution being needed each time.
This change follows a legislative amendment from the fall of 2025 (Bill 104), which makes section 555 of the Loi sur les cités et villes applicable to Montréal.
The ministère des Finances is asking for this resolution in order to standardize the bond issuing procedure in all municipalities.
The mandate binds the minister as soon as he receives a certified copy of the resolution, until the City adopts a resolution to the contrary.
Expected timeline: adoption by the urban agglomeration council on April 23, 2026, then the certified copy sent to the minister at the end of April 2026.
The document notes that without this resolution, the City's ability to borrow through the ministry's award system could be affected.
The City is entering into a 24-month agreement with Aqua Data inc. to supply, on request, batteries for drinking water meters, for a maximum of $343,421.13, taxes included.
The contract covers 600 batteries, estimated as the need for the next two years; prices remain fixed for the entire term of the agreement.
These batteries power the magnetic meters installed since 2012 in industrial, commercial and institutional buildings and certain residential buildings, used for the annual water use report.
Aqua Data was the lowest of the three bids received, at 0.44% below the City's estimate and $2,297.20 below the second bid.
The expenses will be charged to the budgets of the boroughs and the central services, as orders are placed.
The bid is valid until June 10, 2026; delaying the awarding of the contract could force a new call for tenders and harm the operation of the meters.
The City will evaluate the performance of Aqua Data inc.
The City is entering into a 24-month agreement with Gestion CDEDQ inc. (Compteurs d'eau du Québec) to supply R900 interface units, up to a maximum of $421,429.37, taxes included.
These transmitters make it possible to read water meters remotely in industrial, commercial and institutional buildings, as well as in some residential buildings.
The contract covers 2,460 units, which is the estimated need of the cities in the Montréal agglomeration for the next two years.
Only one company submitted a bid, out of two that obtained the tender documents; the other one does not supply the requested product.
The price submitted is $59,395.64 lower (-12.35%) than the City's estimate.
Prices stay fixed for the 24 months and no increase in quantity is planned; each order will be paid out of the budgets of the boroughs and the central departments.
According to the file, delaying the award could compromise meter reading and lead to the loss of consumption data; the bid is valid until June 24, 2026.
The City is entering into a 24-month agreement with Gestion CDEDQ inc. (Compteurs d'eau du Québec) to supply water meters, for up to $685,538.44 including taxes.
The contract covers 750 meters in total: 450 of 40 mm and 300 of 50 mm, for non-residential buildings (industrial, commercial, institutional).
These meters are used to measure water consumption and to produce the annual water use report required by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation.
Two companies submitted bids out of three that obtained the tender documents; the selected bid is 16.32% ($133,658.44) lower than the City's internal estimate.
Prices are fixed for the 24 months and no increase in quantities is planned; purchases will be paid for by the budgets of the boroughs and central departments as needs arise.
The meters serve all the cities in the Montréal urban agglomeration; the City will assess the supplier's performance.
If the award were postponed past July 1, 2026, the bidder could withdraw its offer and a new call for tenders would be required.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is giving $129,000 to Chic Resto-Pop, that is $43,000 per year from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029.

The money funds the project "Réduire le gaspillage alimentaire tout en diminuant la vulnérabilité des populations marginalisées": cooking activities for vulnerable people in the Mercier-Ouest neighbourhood.
Le Chic Resto-Pop is taking over this project because the Groupe d'entraide de Mercier-Ouest (GEMO) is dissolving and transferring its activities to it as of March 31, 2026.
According to the borough, Le Chic Resto-Pop is the only organization in the area with the financial and organizational capacity to keep the services going.

The money comes from funding from the ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale (Fonds québécois d'initiatives sociales 2024-2029) and is paid entirely by the agglomeration, with no effect on the borough's budget.
The contribution covers 71% of the project's total cost; the organization must follow two visibility protocols.
The Ville-Marie borough council is adopting a corrected version of its urban planning by-law, after the City's executive committee disapproved it on February 25, 2026.
The original by-law amended more than 275 provisions to bring Ville-Marie's regulations in line with Montréal's new Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité, adopted in June 2025.

Eight items deemed not to comply with the Plan d'urbanisme are being removed: agricultural uses in certain areas, accessory uses in parks, standards for public works yards and stations, expansions within the site patrimonial du Mont-Royal, among others.
Part of Place Ville Marie will no longer be identified as a "building of interest" in the by-law, as this item has been removed.
The borough is setting aside an objection from the executive committee regarding the R.2 use category, on the grounds that its by-law already does not permit any industrial use there.

Among the new rules being kept: temporary modular buildings used for accommodation (max. 60 beds) or for elementary and high schools are exempt from height and density standards, except within the site du Mont-Royal.
No financial impact is expected; adoption was scheduled for March 10, 2026.

The Ville-Marie borough council adopts, with changes, a by-law that amends its rules on urban planning, specific projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations, to bring them into line with Montréal's Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the plans for view corridors and maximum heights, as well as the rules for construction and enlargement in the E.6 sectors and around the basilique Notre-Dame.
The by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and permits the construction of public transit stations or infrastructure in category E.1 sectors.
New provisions aim to reduce nuisances related to agricultural uses; the new definition of "personal and domestic services" is withdrawn.

The definition of "mechanical equipment" now includes heat pumps, rooftop air-source heating systems, pad-mounted transformers, solar panels and wind turbines; tourist homes and hotels are excluded from the definition of "tourist accommodation establishment".
In the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal, the construction or enlargement of a building, changes to architectural features and the construction of an in-ground pool are now subject to approval.
Minimum side setbacks are adjusted according to the height of the building, from 1.5 m up to a height of 16 m, up to 4 m beyond 35 m.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the demolition of almost all of the building at 1720-1726, rue Saint-Denis, in the Quartier latin, except for the façades facing rue Saint-Denis.

In its place, the Institut de tourisme et d'hôtellerie du Québec (ITHQ) will be able to build a new teaching pavilion: café, lobby, classrooms, collaborative spaces, an amphitheatre and research offices.

The project exceeds the permitted height (18.2 m on the Saint-Denis side, 19.8 m on the avenue Joly side) and also departs from the rules on planting greenery in yards and on the number of bicycle parking spaces.
Before obtaining its demolition certificate, the developer must post a $453,750 guarantee, valid until the structural work and the transformation of the façades are completed.
Conditions imposed: a detailed landscaping plan (yards and roofs), at least 40 bicycle spaces, and the preservation or restoration of the original features of the two old façades.
Work must begin within 60 months of the adoption, otherwise the authorization lapses.
This is the second draft resolution, adopted unanimously on June 9, 2026 after a public consultation held on May 27, 2026.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $790,000 to three commercial development corporations for projects in 2026, with agreements ending December 31, 2026.

$350,000 goes to SDC Vieux-Montréal – Quartier historique for 220 Versailles planters, 26 hanging flower baskets, more than 4,900 plants, 5 urban oases, revitalization of the pétanque courts near the Marché Bonsecours, and winter lighting from November to March.
$215,000 goes to SDC du Village for the 20th edition of the pedestrianization of rue Sainte-Catherine Est, between Saint-Hubert and Papineau, from May 15 to October 12, 2026.
The Village project includes greening, street furniture, public art, lighting, 7 commercial fairs, and partnerships with Fierté Montréal, Montréal Complètement Cirque, and Festival Fetish Weekend.

$225,000 goes to SDC Montréal centre-ville for a winter lighting route and street furniture at Square Phillips, Square Dorchester, Square Victoria, Place du Canada, and Place Jean-Paul Riopelle, from February 10 to December 31, 2026.
A $75,000 share of the funding comes from the budget of the Division des parcs et de l'horticulture of public works, to complete the contribution to SDC du Vieux-Montréal.
Since 2013, the borough says it has invested more than $15M in economic initiatives.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $117,500 to the Société de développement du Quartier latin for a project taking place in 2026.
The "Avé l'Été ! au Quartier latin" project runs from May 1 to October 15, 2026, and includes street signage and cultural programming.
The improvements affect sidewalks, sidewalk extensions, rest areas and entrances in the area, along the commercial streets of the Quartier latin.
The money comes from the "Programme de soutien financier pour le développement économique et commercial de Ville-Marie 2025-2027", under the stream set aside for commercial development corporations.
The agreement ends on December 31, 2026, and requires the organization to mention the City's contribution in its communications.
According to the decision summary, the project also receives private funding from SDC members or partners.
The borough of Ville-Marie is adopting a by-law allowing up to $333,625 to be paid to the Société de développement du Quartier latin for the year 2026.
The money is to be used to animate, beautify and enliven the Quartier latin commercial area: commercial promotions, street furniture, landscaping and greening, and signage.
Rue Saint-Denis will remain open to car traffic during the summer of 2026, because of the STM's construction work and the obstructions in the area; the agreement has been adjusted accordingly.
The grant will be paid in two parts: 80% once the application is approved, then 20% upon submission of invoices, proof of payment and a financial report.
The Société will have to submit a results report no later than November 15, 2026 and pay back any amount not used for eligible expenses.
The by-law is to be adopted at the meeting of May 5, 2026 and to come into force as soon as the public notice is published.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving up to $30,000 to the Société de développement commercial du Village to run activities at Place du Village.
The program of events (cultural, artistic and community activities) will run from June 23 to October 23, 2026.
Place du Village is located on rue Sainte-Catherine Est, between rue Wolfe and rue Atateken; its transformation has been under way since 2024.
The SDC is receiving a direct-award contract to operate and run activities at the square and its container.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, through the budget of the Service du développement économique as part of the entente centre-ville.
The borough will carry out a communications campaign and follow up on the project.
The Ville-Marie borough council approves a change to the internal by-laws of the Société de développement commercial du Quartier latin.
Decisions made by the board of directors during meetings continue to be adopted by simple majority (50% + 1), with the chair casting the deciding vote in the event of a tie.
A new section allows the board of directors to make decisions electronically, outside of meetings; such decisions then require two thirds of the votes cast.
The change was adopted by the members of the SDC at their general meeting of March 25, 2026, and approval by the borough is scheduled for the sitting of June 9, 2026.

The SDC brings together merchants in the area of rue Saint-Denis between Sherbrooke and Sainte-Catherine, of Ontario and Maisonneuve between Sanguinet and Berri, and of Émery between Sanguinet and Saint-Denis.
The file involves no financial aspect.
The Verdun borough is authorizing three public events and allowing them to depart from its by-laws on the occupation of public property, traffic, parking, cleanliness, nuisances and parks.
Cabane à sucre Île-des-Sucres, organized by the borough: Friday, March 27, 2026, from 10:30 a.m. to 7 p.m., at place de la Grande-Marguerite (40, place du Commerce).

Grand Défi Guy-Labelle (13th edition), by école secondaire Dorval-Jean-XXIII: Friday, April 24, 2026, from 9:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., near école Monseigneur-Richard (3000, boulevard Gaétan-Laberge) and on the bicycle and pedestrian path up to rue Fayolle.

Parade annuelle d'Ypres (9th edition), by Légion royale canadienne succursale 4: Sunday, April 26, 2026, from 1:45 p.m. to 3:30 p.m., at parc du Souvenir, on 1re Avenue, rues Wellington and Willibrord, in front of the borough hall and up to the rear parking lot of the centre communautaire Marcel-Giroux.
The organizers must obtain the other required authorizations; City services are billed to them according to the 2026 fees by-law, with some services possibly provided free of charge.
The events are free and open to everyone, and the sale of promotional items may be authorized.
The City is accepting a $148,000 grant from Compagnie Trust Royal for the Concerts d'été de la Succession Campbell in the parks, in the summer of 2026.
This money will be used to present 21 free shows and concerts spread across the 19 boroughs: each borough will have at least one stage concert or marching band performance.
The money will cover production costs, artists' fees and some presentation costs; the expense is paid by the central city and offset by the revenue received.
The Service de la culture manages the programming, together with the network of Maisons de la culture.
Schedule: programming submitted to Trust Royal in April 2026, grant paid out in May, concerts in July and August, report submitted to Trust Royal in November 2026.
Trust Royal's contribution was $137,000 in 2025 and $161,000 in 2024 (100th anniversary of the concerts).
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension takes note of the filing of an application to renew financial assistance from the ministère de la Sécurité publique for 2025-2026.
The money requested is for the "Agent-es pivot" project, carried out in elementary and high schools in the borough.
Agent-es pivot positions are created within partner community organizations to identify the most vulnerable young people aged 10 to 17 and refer them to services.
The agents act as a link between the school, the family, the community, social services and the neighbourhood police stations.
The borough undertakes to comply with the conditions of the Programme de soutien à la création et à la consolidation d'espaces jeunesse montréalais.
The director of culture, sports, recreation and social development is authorized to sign the documents related to the funding agreement.
The document states that without this support, young people aged 10 to 17 in the area would no longer have access to agent-es pivot in their schools.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is paying up to $323,093 to the Centre socioéducatif Lasallien for the "Agent-e-s pivot" project, from September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026.
The money comes entirely from the ministère de la Sécurité publique, through its program supporting Montréal youth spaces.
Agent-e-s pivot will be hired in certain high schools to identify vulnerable young people aged 10 to 17 and refer them to services, while maintaining the connection with elementary schools.

These workers will act as a point of reference between the school, the family and neighbourhood organizations, and will work with school teams, health and social services, and neighbourhood police stations.
The borough justifies the project by the rise since 2019 in violent incidents involving young people on its territory.
Public works director Marco St-Pierre is authorized to sign the agreement on behalf of the Ville; a report will be required at the end of the project.
The project began before the borough council adopted the file.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is accepting a $54,000 grant from the ministère de la Sécurité publique, under the Programme québécois de lutte contre la criminalité.
The money is paid out over three years: $30,000 in 2025-2026, $14,000 in 2026-2027 and $10,000 in 2027-2028.
The money will be used to update the Stratégie jeunesse en prévention de la criminalité, which was developed in 2022 based on an assessment done in 2021.

The process is meant to re-examine the causes of youth crime and to target current issues: cyberviolence, mental health, the needs of girls and young women, discrimination, and the effects of inflation on families.
Young people, community organizations, schools and security services will be involved in designing the actions.
The director of public works, Marco St-Pierre, is authorized to sign the funding agreement on behalf of the borough.
The project is to start in the summer or fall of 2026.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is tabling before its council the 2025 annual report on the use of the power to authorize housing projects despite urban planning regulations (section 93 of the provincial housing act).
In 2025, four projects received such an authorization and no application was refused.
The projects concerned are located at 1720, rue du Canal, 700, rue Bourget, 2720-2740, rue Saint-Patrick and 1300-1304, rue Saint-Patrick.
The report must be tabled no later than April 1 following the year covered, in this case on March 9, 2026.
The report will be sent to the minister responsible for housing and its content will be published on the City's website.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is amending the construction authorization for a housing project at 2720-2740, rue Saint-Patrick, which was granted in September 2025.

The developer will have to transfer to the Ville a building that is part of the site, which must allow for the creation of housing equivalent to at least 20% of the residential floor area of the private component.
This housing will have to meet the definition of social housing or off-market affordable housing set out in by-law 20-041.
The agreement with the Ville must be concluded before the construction permit is issued.
The project must still include at least 30% two-bedroom units and 20% units with three bedrooms or more, except for the social or affordable component.
Reason given: on February 16, 2026, city council adopted a draft by-law easing by-law 20-041, which could release the developer from its commitments; the amendment aims to preserve them.
Next steps: adoption of a draft resolution, a public consultation meeting, then final adoption by the borough council.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is adopting a second draft by-law creating "incentive zoning": a developer can obtain a standard different from the zoning rules in exchange for a commitment made through an agreement with the borough.
This first by-law is limited to a single flexibility measure: buildings limited to 50% ground coverage could go up to 55%.
In exchange, the borough council will be able to require an enhanced climate resilience target, better building envelope performance in the event of a power outage, or more greening of the property.
Projects will still have to comply with the Règlement d'urbanisme du Sud-Ouest (01-280) and the by-law on social, affordable and family housing (20-041).
The by-law stems from the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050 adopted by city council on June 16, 2025, which requires boroughs to update their regulations.
It will be replaced by and incorporated into the borough's new urban planning by-law, expected in winter 2026-2027.
The by-law can be the subject of a referendum request; afterwards, the resolutions adopted under it cannot be.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is adopting a "differentiated zoning" by-law, which allows alternative standards to be granted to affordable or social housing projects.
In practical terms: a project for affordable or social housing will be able to cover up to 55% of the lot, instead of the maximum of 50% set out in the zoning.
The developer must make the request when applying for the permit, and the project must meet all the other standards of planning by-law 01-280 and of the other municipal by-laws.
The by-law adopted at the consultation meeting of June 18, 2026 was amended so that the penalties in section 9 apply on a daily basis.
This by-law is presented as a small-scale first step: it will be replaced and folded into the borough's new planning by-law, scheduled for the winter of 2026-2027.
The approach stems from the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050 adopted by city council on June 16, 2025, with which boroughs must bring their regulations into line.
The project is not subject to approval by referendum if it is adopted before June 6, 2029.

The City is entrusting the maintenance of parc Frédéric-Back, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, to two companies for 30 months, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028, with two possible 12-month extensions.
Groupe Nicky (178001 Canada inc.) is receiving $1,089,868.72 for general maintenance: cleanliness, mowing, repaving of pathways, repair of furniture.
Les Entreprises Roseneige (9190-8673 Québec inc.) are receiving $838,793.21 for ecological and horticultural management: flower beds, tree work, mulch, monitoring of insects and diseases.
A contingency budget of $96,433.10 is added, for a total expense of $2,025,095.03 paid 100% by the agglomeration.
A third contract of $130,341.74 goes to Du vert au rouge inc. for the outdoor maintenance of the TAZ and the Stade de soccer, decided by the executive committee.
The park has 65 hectares open to the public, and 26 more hectares will be added in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector, which justified creating a separate lot for ecological management.
Public call for tenders 26-21268 received four bidders; the bid selected for general maintenance is 18.89% below the City's estimate.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève is announcing the creation of a "Comité consultatif en culture, sports, loisirs et développement social" (CCSLDS).
The committee has no decision-making power: it makes recommendations to the borough council and cannot authorize any spending without the council's approval.
Its members must represent culture, sports, recreation and social development, as well as children, youth and seniors.
Citizen members and those representing non-profit organizations will receive $100 per meeting; they will have to register in Montréal's supplier file in order to be paid.
The by-law also changes who chairs the committee on land development and planning: the role passes from the borough mayor to a borough councillor.
Planned timeline: notice of motion on February 3, 2026, adoption and appointment of the chair in February 2026, appointment of the citizen and non-profit members on March 10, 2026.
A call for applications will be issued to the public.

The L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève borough council authorizes the use of public property for the public events listed in a list attached to the file, at the site and on the schedule planned for each one.
These events may be community, cultural, social, sports, educational, multicultural, civic or commemorative events, or fundraisers.
Exemptions from the borough by-laws on cleanliness and nuisances and on the use of public property are granted: cooking food, music and noise, and the sale of promotional items or spin-off products.
Third-party authorizations (firefighters, police, borough public safety, paramedics, STM) will be requested separately when needed.

The costs of the City's support for the events are paid out of the operating budgets of the departments concerned, in accordance with the policy on support for organizations and the borough's by-law on fees.
Without this authorization, the planned events could not take place.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève authorizes the director of culture, sports, recreation and citizen relations to submit and sign an application for financial assistance for the Fête nationale 2026.
The application is made to the Mouvement national des Québécoises et des Québécois, under the Programme d'assistance financière aux célébrations locales.
The assistance can cover up to 75% of eligible expenses, without exceeding $5,000.
A regional jury chooses the projects that are selected.
According to the borough, the assistance would be used to maintain the same level of activities offered to the public; without it, the borough would have to cover the additional costs.
If the assistance is obtained, another file will follow to adjust the 2026 budget.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève is appointing the 8 members of its Comité consultatif en culture, sports, loisirs et développement social, for a two-year term, from April 7, 2026 to April 7, 2028.

The committee brings together 3 representatives of organizations (Association de Ringuette de Pierrefonds, Dollard, Île-Bizard; Association de soccer de L'Île-Bizard; Club les Amis des Deux Rives) and 5 citizens.
The members were chosen after a call for applications posted on the borough's website, which received more than 20 applications.
The committee makes recommendations to the borough council on culture, sports, recreation and social development, and must submit its meeting reports to the council.
Each member receives an attendance fee of $100 per meeting in 2026, paid out of the operating budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et des relations avec les citoyens.
The committee is chaired by borough councillor Alain Wilson; a start-up meeting was scheduled for March 24, 2026.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is appointing two of its elected officials to sit on the boards of directors of two local organizations.
Julie Forgues, councillor for the Pierre-Foretier district, will represent the borough on the board of directors of the Centre des arts de la scène Pauline-Julien.
Alain Wilson, councillor for the Denis-Benjamin-Viger district, will represent the borough on the board of directors of the Complexe sportif Saint-Raphaël.
Both terms run from March 11, 2026 to December 31, 2027.
These seats had been vacant since the previous terms ended on November 25, 2025, after the municipal elections.
The two elected officials will have to report to the other members of the borough council on the activities and projects of these organizations.
This file involves no spending.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is waiving the fees for using outdoor sports fields and equipment for three organizations during the summer of 2026.
The organizations covered are: l'Association de balle-molle de L'Île-Bizard, l'Association de Volley-Ball Île-Bizard and l'Association de soccer de L'Île-Bizard.
The free access applies to leagues and activities in the adult categories (19 to 54 years old).
The borough points to the condition of the fields: a maintenance backlog, aging facilities and a labour shortage.
It also mentions the lack of activity monitors to provide access to washrooms, keep the site clean and prepare the fields.
The measure will be written into the field loan agreements to be signed in the coming months.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève is suspending one week of skating and ice sports activities in November 2026 at the Complexe sportif Saint-Raphaël, to make room for a hockey tournament held by the Ligue de hockey adulte de Pierrefonds inc.
The borough agrees to accept the tournament's profits as a donation; the amount is not yet known.
The Ligue itself pays for renting the ice time and the spaces, according to the borough's 2026 rates.
The Ligue must give the borough a report on the tournament as early as December 2026, with the amount of the donation to come.
The donation will be added to the 2027 operating budget and will be used to buy, renovate or redevelop equipment, or to support an activity in culture, sports, recreation and social development.
The advisory committee on culture, sports, recreation and social development will recommend to the borough council how the money should be used.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is expanding its Comité consultatif en culture, sports, loisirs et développement social, created on February 3, 2026.

The committee will grow from 4 members to 9: an elected official as chair, 3 representatives of recognized organizations from different fields of activity, and 5 citizens not affiliated with any organization.
The call for applications, held from February 13 to March 4, 2026, brought in more applications than there were planned seats, which is why the committee is being expanded.
The committee will hold at most 7 meetings a year, and 6 members must be present, including the chair, for it to sit.
Each member other than the elected official will receive $100 per attendance; for the organization representatives, the attendance fee may go to the member or to the organization.
The planned budget is $4,049 for the chair (indexed to the CPI of July 2026) and $5,600 for the eight other members.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève is authorizing public events to be held on public property, at the sites and times set out in a list attached to the file.
The events covered are community, cultural, social, sports, educational, multicultural, civic, commemorative or fundraising in nature.
The authorizations lift certain borough rules in order to allow food cooking, music and noise, as well as the sale of related products or fundraising.
Without these exemptions, the planned events could not take place.
The City's support for the events is paid out of the operating budgets of the departments concerned, according to the service basket and the borough's Règlement sur les tarifs 2026.
Authorizations will also have to be obtained from third parties such as the fire department, the SPVM, the borough's public safety service, paramedics and the STM, where applicable.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève is recognizing 44 non-profit organizations for 2026, from January 1 to December 31.

Of these, 40 organizations are renewing their recognition and 4 are receiving it for the first time: La Maison Entre Familles, the Ligue de Hockey Adulte de Pierrefonds, the Fondation du cégep Gérald-Godin and the Centre de crise de l'Ouest de l'Île.
Recognition gives access to borough support: rooms and halls for activities, financial support, promotional support. In return, the organizations must report back once a year.

Six organizations are losing their recognition, and therefore access to these services: Kin-Ball de Montréal (at its own request), Jardin d'enfants Le Tournesol, Fondation du Centre d'hébergement Denis-Benjamin-Viger, Maison de jeunes Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève, Association de hockey mineur de l'Île-Bizard and Club de Taekwondo W.T.F. de l'Île-Bizard.
The organizations affected work in sports, culture, heritage, mental health, food assistance and housing for women.
The list of recognized organizations will be published in the borough newspaper and each one will receive an official letter.
Borough councillor Alain Wilson declared an interest in the matter and is abstaining from the discussion and the vote.
The L'Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève borough is paying up to $16,725 to 28 non-profit organizations for the year 2026.
This money supports culture, sports, recreation and social development activities offered to residents of the borough.

Each organization receives its contribution in a single payment, after submitting an application and qualifying under an evaluation grid (clientele served, participants under 18 years old, frequency of activities, supervision, self-financing).
Because of the financial challenges of 2026, the money is not coming from the usual operating budget, but from the accumulated surpluses of the Tournoi des organismes fundraiser (a golf tournament).
The amounts paid in previous years were $13,075 in 2025 and $14,352 in 2024.
Borough councillor Alain Wilson declares an interest in the matter and takes part in neither the deliberations nor the vote.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève supports the filing of an application for financial assistance to Québec to rebuild the recreation pavilion, the pool and the water games at parc Robert-Sauvé.
The application will be filed in mid-June 2026 under the PAFIRSPA program (component 1, 2026 version).
Québec could pay up to 66% of the eligible costs; the borough would have to fund 33% of the project.
