The pavilion, which houses a community hall, is currently unusable: water leaks, unstable electrical current, heating and air conditioning problems.
The pool basin is cracked and the water treatment systems are at the end of their life; the borough fears a service interruption in the summer.
The borough cites the need for universal access for the people of the district of Sainte-Geneviève, which has many seniors and no other municipal community facility.
Marie-Claude Ouellet, director of culture, sports, recreation and citizen relations, is designated as the signatory and contact person with the government.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard - Sainte-Geneviève is authorizing public events to be held on public property, at the sites and times set out in a list attached to the file.
The events covered are community, cultural, social, sports, educational, multicultural, civic, commemorative or fundraising events.
The council is lifting certain city rules for the duration of the events: cooking food, music and noise, and the sale of promotional items or related products.
Organizers will also have to obtain, where applicable, authorizations from the departments concerned (firefighters, police, public safety, paramedics, STM).
The costs of the City's support are covered by the departments' operating budgets, in accordance with the Politique de reconnaissance des organismes and the borough's by-law on fees.
Without these authorizations, the planned events could not take place.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is giving $11,050 to thirteen non-profit organizations located in its territory.
The money comes from the accumulated surplus of the golf tournament held for the benefit of the borough's community organizations.
The amounts are paid only once (non-recurring) and are used for one-time projects or activities, or to buy and replace equipment.
Each organization must submit a report on how the grant was used within 30 days after the activity or the end of the current year, and must sign up for direct deposit.
Both organizations recognized and not recognized by the borough can receive this support.
Borough councillor Alain Wilson declares an interest in the matter and abstains from taking part in the discussion and from voting.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève will pay Complexe sportif Saint-Raphaël to rent the ice rink, the gymnasium and rooms from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
The amount is $76,889.45 per month, taxes included, or $922,673.42 for the year, in 12 monthly invoices.
This amount breaks down into $44,321.56 per month for the ice rink and $22,553.37 per month for the rooms, taxes included.
The indexation applied this year is 2.6% (consumer price index); it applies to the ice rink, the gymnasium and the Gymibik sports area, but not to the offices and rooms.
The previous year (July 2025 to June 2026), the amount was $74,994.40 per month, or $899,932.78 annually.
The payment stems from a service contract signed in 2007 with the Complexe, extended in 2017 until 2037.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is supporting a renovation project for the Complexe sportif Saint-Raphaël, at 750, boulevard Jacques-Bizard.
The project calls for repairing two thirds of the roof of the building that houses the skating rink, the gymnasium and the multipurpose rooms.
It also calls for replacing two basketball hoops with electric wall-mounted hoops in the gymnasium.
This support is required so that the Complexe can apply for financial assistance from the Government of Québec (PAFIRSPA program, component 1).
The Complexe has until June 22 to submit its application; the file must then receive final support from the City's executive committee.
The support costs the borough nothing.
City council agrees that the arrondissement du Sud-Ouest will handle the call for tenders, the contract, the work and its supervision for two new bus stops on rue Saint-Patrick.
The stops will be built at the intersections of rue Eadie and avenue de l'Église, as part of the STM's bus network overhaul.
At the Saint-Patrick/Eadie stop: construction of about 45 metres of sidewalk and relocation of the guardrail.
At the Saint-Patrick/de l'Église stop: about 25 metres of sidewalk, a slab for a bus shelter, and reconfiguration of the slope and of access to the bike path.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité keeps the planning and design work, and pays all of the costs out of its already-budgeted funds.
Announced timeline: public call for tenders in March-April 2026, work from June to October 2026.
The City is giving $12,500 to Vélo Québec Éditions to produce and distribute the 2026 edition of the Grand Montréal bike network map.
The map will be printed in 50,000 copies and distributed in stores, local service points and the Bureaux Accès Montréal, as well as being posted on the Vélo Québec Éditions website.
Publication and distribution are planned for May-June 2026.
The City's contribution covers about 29% of the project's total cost, estimated at $43,500.
The Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal, the Agence de mobilité durable and the cities of Longueuil and Laval have also been asked to help fund the project.
The money is paid in a single payment within 30 days of the agreement being signed and is 100% covered by the urban agglomeration.
The City provided similar support in previous years: $10,000 in 2022, $12,000 in 2023, then $12,500 in 2024 and 2025.

The City is obtaining from the Centre de services scolaire de la Pointe-de-l'Île a permanent public right of way of 351.5 m² on the grounds of école secondaire Jean-Grou, at 12723-12725, boulevard Rodolphe-Forget, in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.
This right of way is being transferred without any payment; the City covers the costs of the survey plan, the notarial deed and its publication.

The right of way will be used for the Espace Rivière project: a new building bringing together a library, a maison de la culture, community and recreation spaces and an Accès Montréal office, built in place of the current Rivière-des-Prairies library, which will be taken down.
In practical terms, the City will use the driveway entrance of the school grounds, extend the roadway and build a sidewalk.
The City takes on the development, maintenance and repair of the right of way, as well as all rainwater management, including the costs of the retention basin.
Three parking spaces will disappear; they may be rebuilt elsewhere on the school service centre's grounds, at no cost to the City.
The easement is needed to obtain the building permit; a delay would push back the schedule and the launch of the calls for tenders.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is granting $35,000 (taxes not included) to the organization Un itinéraire pour tous to manage the community rooms of the Maison culturelle et communautaire (MCC) in 2026.
The money covers the salary of an administrative officer who handles room bookings, equipment loans, welcoming visitors and following up on complaints.
The mandate runs from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The MCC houses the bibliothèque Julio-Jean-Pierre, the Oliver-Jones performance hall, an exhibition room, a rehearsal studio, a food service area and ten community rooms.
The contract includes accountability reporting requirements toward the borough.
The same amount of $35,000 had been granted to the organization for 2025 and for 2023; it was $38,329.56 in 2024.
The expense is charged to the budget of the borough's Division des bibliothèques et de la culture.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is adopting its Plan d'action culturel 2026-2030, which replaces the Plan de développement culturel 2021-2025.
The plan contains 32 actions grouped under 3 areas: culture serving individual and collective well-being, a territory inhabited by culture, and cultural citizenship.
Goal for 2030: a cultural offering available in every neighbourhood of the borough, supported by local initiatives and partnerships.
Cultural mediation serves as the common thread connecting residents to works, artists and venues.
The plan was prepared with local cultural organizations and staff from all of the borough's departments.
The plan will be printed, posted online and shared through the borough's newsletter, the Info Loisir and its social media.
Timeline: launch in June 2026, annual progress reports from January 2027 to January 2030, and a final report in January 2031.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing a library assistant to the Division de la culture et des bibliothèques, effective March 21, 2026.
Permanent status depends on successfully completing the probation period set out in the white-collar collective agreement (SCFP 429).
The position had to be filled because the person who held it was transferred to the bibliothèque Belleville.
The position was posted internally within the Ville from February 4 to 10, 2026; the salary range runs from $37,662 to $51,455.
The expected cost from March 21 to December 31, 2026 comes to $44,200 (salary, premiums and payroll taxes) for 1,435 hours, paid out of the borough's operating budget.
Montréal-Nord is extending its contract with the company Prodigium by one year to provide the technical labour for its cultural and special events.
The contract is worth a maximum of $138,027.49, taxes included, and covers July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
This is the only extension provided for in call for tenders 25-20780; the current contract was set to end on June 30, 2026.
Prodigium plans, coordinates and sets up audio, audiovisual and digital productions, working with the borough's technical manager.
The borough's permanent performance venues are expected to present more than 135 shows, which means more than 200 production interventions.
The expense ($126,037.50 net) is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is creating a financial support program for cultural projects, coming into effect on January 1, 2027.
An amount of $50,000 is set aside for it in the operating budget of the Division de la culture et des bibliothèques.
Three streams: local artists and authors; cultural organizations; citizen and community initiatives.
The assistance can cover up to 75% of a project's eligible expenses for organizations, and 100% for artists and authors.
The funding granted can be spread over a maximum of 3 years; a committee assesses applications using a weighted scoring grid.
Schedule: launch in July 2026, submission of applications in October 2026, confirmation of support in December 2026, payment and start of projects in January 2027.
The program stems from the Plan d'action culturel collectif 2026-2030 adopted in May 2026.
City council approves giving up (releasing) the City's right to take back a vacant lot on rue Bombardier, in Anjou, which it had sold in December 2021 for $750,000 plus taxes.
This right allowed the City to take back the lot if the buyer did not build, within four years, a four-storey rental building with at least 50 units.
The buyer provided the required documents: a written request, a construction permit, confirmation of a contract with a general contractor, and a bank guarantee of $200,000.
The City notes that the underground pipes and equipment were not moved or replaced as provided for in the work agreement.
It accepts the servitude plan anyway, on the condition that the buyer releases it from all liability for damage to the buildings built outside the servitude area.
The lot has changed hands since then: resold to Le 7050 inc. in 2023, then to Le 7040 inc. in August 2025, both taking on the original buyer's obligations.
The public utility servitude will be created later; the City keeps its personal remedies against the buyer despite the release.
City council approves the City's opinion on the 2026 space needs planning project of the Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (CSSDM).

The CSSDM is asking for free transfers of land to build 7 new schools: elementary schools in Ahuntsic-Cartierville (Louvain Est), Parc-Extension, Mercier (Place Versailles), Ville-Marie (secteur des Faubourgs), Pointe-Saint-Charles (Bridge-Bonaventure) and Côte-des-Neiges (former racetrack), plus an 850-space high school at the former racetrack.
Three of the needs are short-term (2 years): Louvain Est, Parc-Extension and Côte-des-Neiges Ouest; the other four are long-term (5-10 years).

The City values these lands to be transferred free of charge at more than $150,000,000, an amount that will not be reimbursed to it, on top of the costs of demolition, excavation, decontamination and street extensions.
The City points out that preparing the lands (decontamination, archaeological digs, works) can take more than 2 years and exceed the time limit set out in the law.
The City is also asking for the school model to be rethought (high-rise schools, rooftop yards, school parks open in the evening) and for ground areas to be optimized.
The opinion must be sent to the CSSDM before April 24, 2026; otherwise the school service centre can send its planning to the ministère de l'Éducation without the City's opinion.
The City will acquire, by expropriation if needed, the 547 m² lot located at 10111, boulevard Pie-IX, between rue Larin and boulevard Industriel, in Montréal-Nord.
Goal: demolish the existing building, which is currently vacant, and create a local park.
The property belongs to Gestion André Soucy JR inc.; no negotiated agreement could be reached, hence the use of expropriation.
Estimated cost of the acquisition: $1,530,000 plus taxes, with maximum financing of $1,606,308.75 net of tax rebate through a loan by-law; the central city pays 100%.
The estimate includes the purchase, soil characterization, damages, interest and expert fees, but excludes soil rehabilitation and demolition.
The reserve notice on the lot expires on May 28, 2026; the expropriation notice is expected to be served and published in the summer of 2026.
The borough will have to set aside a budget for maintenance and demolition once the possession date is known.
The City agrees to redraw the lot lines on the Molson site, in Ville-Marie: six lots are replaced by four new lots.
The City has to give its consent because it holds a mortgage on this land, which secures the developer's obligations toward the City.
The consent is given without any payment, and the City says the value of what it is owed is not reduced by it.
According to the document, the redrawing of the lots is needed to allow the redevelopment of the Molson site and the carrying out of certain obligations set out in the agreement with the City.
An employee of the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation will be able to sign, on the City's behalf, the other consents of the same type required for the project.
The new lot layout is based on a land surveyor's plan dated January 6, 2026; the deed will then be published in the Montréal land register.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough council takes note of the reports on decisions made by its officials from February 1 to 28, 2026, with no new spending to approve.
In February 2026, 46 delegated decisions were made, for a total value of $215,497.65.
These decisions include 3 works contracts paid out of the operating budget ($185,638.64) and one professional services contract of $29,859.01.
They also include 29 staffing decisions (appointments, disciplinary measures, creation of positions) and 13 decisions with no spending, 10 of which deal with traffic, signage and parking.
The attached reports give details of the purchase orders by supplier and the invoices without a purchase order.
City council is naming a new public square in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce "place des Cantonniers".
The square is located within the right-of-way of rue De Sorel, between rue Bougainville and boulevard Décarie.
It was created as part of the Royalmount project, with a footbridge that crosses over the autoroute Décarie and links the site to the De la Savane metro station.
The name comes from a suggestion by the Société de transport de Montréal and recalls the "cantonniers", the workers who have maintained the metro tracks since 1966.
The name "rue De Sorel" remains in use along its entire current route; no place name is being removed.
The Comité consultatif en reconnaissance gave a favourable opinion on January 30, 2025, and the borough supports the proposal.
The name will be posted after it is made official by the Commission de toponymie du Québec.
City council is naming the new main street at the heart of the écoquartier Louvain, in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, "avenue des Solidarités".
The name is needed right away: the first residential project is already under construction and addresses will have to be assigned in the short term.
The name comes from a public call for proposals held in the fall of 2024 by the borough and the comité local de patrimoine et de toponymie; 48 people or organizations responded.
The écoquartier Louvain is redeveloping a 7.7-hectare city-owned site bordered by rue de Louvain Est, rue Saint-Hubert, avenue Christophe-Colomb and the CN right-of-way.
The project calls for about 1000 social and affordable housing units, public spaces, a traffic-calmed street, a food hub, stores, a school, a CPE (daycare centre) and a community centre.
Four other public places on the site still have to be named before the work is finished, which is expected around 2032.
The name will be posted once it is made official by the Commission de toponymie du Québec.
City council is renaming the L'Île-des-Sœurs library, at 260, rue Elgar in Verdun, "bibliothèque Kim-Yaroshevskaya".
The library, which opened in 1990 in the centre communautaire Elgar, had no official name until now; only the library's name is changing, not the name of the centre Elgar.
The name honours actress, author and teacher Kim Yaroshevskaya (1923-2025), known for Fanfreluche and Grand-Mère in Passe-Partout, who lived on Île-des-Sœurs for more than 40 years.
The process began with a citizen's request filed in January 2026, backed by a petition with about 180 signatures, after Ms. Yaroshevskaya died on January 12, 2025.
The Comité consultatif en reconnaissance gave a favourable opinion on March 13, 2026, and the borough of Verdun supports the project.
Once the resolution is adopted, the new name is sent to public utility providers and the borough can put up the signage.
The decision summary does not provide for any spending for this decision.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is giving $1,500 to three organizations in the Saint-Michel district.
$500 goes to À Portée de mains for the "Délire d'hiver" activity.
$500 goes to Alliance socioculturelle et aide pédagogique (ASAP) for the musical "Fantasia".
$500 goes to Saint-Michel Vie Sans Frontières for a Valentine's Day lunch.
The money comes from the borough council's discretionary budget for the year 2026, which is meant for one-time requests from non-profit organizations.
The funds are certified as available by the Direction des services administratifs et du greffe.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $7,250 to ten non-profit organizations for the year 2026.
The money comes from the borough council's discretionary budget, created to respond to one-time requests for financial help.
The largest amounts go to Regroupement Jeunesse en Action ($2,300) and Communauté hellénique du Grand Montréal ($1,250).

The other recipients: École de La Relève ($700), Cyclo Nord-Sud, Groupe des Bénévoles 1ère et 2ième Avenue, À portée de mains, Camp Assume and Les Cercles de Fermières du Québec ($500 each), Initiative Kanisa ($300) and FADOQ–Région Île de Montréal ($200).

The amounts fund specific activities: the Construis ton vélo project, a charity boxing gala, the Jeux FADOQ, a Valentine's Day party, the Greek national day parade, a recognition evening, a talent show and a discussion panel, among others.
The contributions are divided among the mayor's fund and the districts of François-Perrault, Parc-Extension, Saint-Michel and Villeray.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension accepts Ville-Marie's offer to deploy in the borough a public works team dedicated to cleanliness work related to homelessness.
The team will work 12 months starting in mid-April 2026, during the day, from Tuesday to Friday.
It includes 8 people (one foreman and 7 blue-collar workers) and 4 vehicles: one packer truck and four pickup trucks.
Ville-Marie manages and trains the team; the locations where the work is done are chosen with the boroughs that request it.
The budget comes from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and will be transferred to Ville-Marie; no amount is given.
One pickup truck and two blue-collar workers are being added in 2026 for minor work and to cover a larger territory.
In 2025, the same arrangement had been offered to five boroughs for six months.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $3,300 to four organizations in 2026, out of the borough council's discretionary budget.
$1,500 goes to Fonds 1804 pour la persévérance scolaire for the 11th edition of its Gala ($500 from the mayor's fund, $500 from the François-Perrault district, $500 from the Saint-Michel district).
$800 goes to Saint-Michel Vie Sans Frontières for an outing to a sugar shack ($300 from the mayor's fund, $500 from the Saint-Michel district).
$500 goes to Centre Femmes Convictions de Montréal for its 3rd anniversary (Saint-Michel district).
$500 goes to Regroupement Jeunesse en Action for the Fête du drapeau haïtien (Saint-Michel district).
The borough's finance department confirms that the funds are available in the 2026 discretionary budget.
The City is moving $114,975 (taxes included) from its "incidental costs" budget to its "contingencies" budget to pay for additional work at SPVM neighbourhood station 21, at 1669, rue Berri.
The work contract with the owner, 9227-9702 Québec inc., therefore goes from $2,230,515 to $2,345,490, taxes included.
The total cost of the project does not change: it stays at $2,414,475, since the money comes from a budget item that was already authorized.
This transfer is needed because the additional 2,990 sq. ft. expansion approved in June 2025 broadened the work without any additional budget, using up the contingencies.
The work, carried out by the owner, began in the fall of 2025 and was provisionally accepted on February 28, 2026; the lease runs until November 30, 2031.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration, because the SPVM falls under its jurisdiction.
The City is extending by five years, from November 1, 2033 to October 31, 2038, the lease of a 138,865-square-foot building at 8491-8525, rue Ernest-Cormier, in Anjou, from Développement Olymbec inc.
The space houses the Centre de formation du Service de police de la Ville de Montréal, which has occupied it since February 2017 and now uses 100% of the floor area.
Rent for the five years comes to $14,169,828, taxes included, or $2,833,965.60 per year.

The City will also pay up to $1,149,750, taxes included, to the owner for work: seismic upgrades, generator, ventilation-air conditioning-heating, mezzanine, electrical needs and securing the premises. The payment is planned for 2027.
The owner is covering $600,000 of the basic seismic work, applied as a credit on the invoice for the work.
The budgets of two departments are being adjusted: $431,298 in 2033 and $2,156,490 in 2034 for rent; $47,153 in 2033 and $235,763 in 2034 for energy.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, since the SPVM comes under it. The lease was negotiated by mutual agreement.
The City is renewing for five years the lease of SPVM neighbourhood station 15, at 1625, rue de l'Église, in Verdun, from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2031.
The owner is Aquakern inc.; the space is 7,448 square feet and includes 21 parking spaces at no charge.
The total rent for the five years comes to $1,275,937, taxes included ($1,165,100.88 net of tax rebates).
The base rent goes from $15 to $17 per square foot, an increase of about 13%; the City states that this rate matches the market in the area.
The owner commits, at its own expense, to replacing all light fixtures with LED.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration, since the SPVM falls under its jurisdiction.
According to the SPVM, without this renewal, it could not continue its mission in this area.
The City is renewing the lease for the SPVM's neighbourhood police station 26, at 7409, avenue Mountain Sights, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
It is renting 9,000 square feet of office space from Développement Vue Phase IV inc., with 36 parking spaces.
The lease runs for 12 years and 22 days, from March 10, 2026 to March 31, 2038, for a total rent of $5,807,275.72, taxes included.
The base rent goes from $20 to $24.50 per square foot ($26.50 starting in the 7th year), an increase of 22.5%.
The owner will pay $80,000 plus taxes in work to redo the police officers' locker rooms.
The previous lease had expired as of March 9, 2026; without a renewal, the SPVM says it could no longer operate in this area.
The agglomeration covers 100% of the expense, since the SPVM reports to it.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is allowing the Théâtre de Quat'Sous, at 100, avenue des Pins Est, to serve alcohol and let it be consumed in the performance hall, the rehearsal room, the lobby, the green room and the dressing rooms.
The bar must remain an accessory use to the performance hall; no sale or consumption of alcohol is allowed on the terrace.
The decision departs from the planning by-law, which limited alcohol to a room separate from the performance hall and to 20% of the performance area.
No work is planned on the building and no other change to the 2007 specific project is being requested.
If the theatre does not make use of this authorization within 60 months, it becomes void.

The planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on February 10, 2026; no members of the public came to the consultation on March 17, 2026 or to the neighbourhood meeting on October 30, 2025 (55 addresses invited).
This is the second draft resolution: a referendum approval process will follow before final adoption.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is amending its October 2025 resolution on the redevelopment of the land at 3700, rue Berri and 3725, rue Saint-Denis.
The change is meant to maintain the social, affordable and family housing commitments already negotiated, even though city council eased by-law 20-041 on March 23, 2026.

Before any construction permit is issued, the developer will have to sign an agreement with the City providing for: 20% of the private residential floor area in social housing, 20% in affordable housing, and 5% of the units as family units with 3 bedrooms and a minimum of 86 m².
The City will pay the owner $1,029.74 per m² of residential floor area for a building handed over without construction, an amount indexed by 5% on January 1 of each year.
The social or affordable housing shares can go down to 15% if the developer pays a financial contribution calculated according to floor area brackets (from $0 to $143.44 per m²).
A public consultation meeting was held on April 28, 2026 with five members of the public and two representatives of the project; details on the terms of transfer were added following that meeting.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the construction of a housing building on a parking lot on avenue Papineau, between rue Rachel and rue Marie-Anne.
Zoning in the area limits buildings to 8 units: the decision allows between 24 and 29 to be built.
The project calls for a three-storey building with a mezzanine, without an elevator, including 3 adaptable units and 6 minimally accessible units.
No living space may be built below ground level, which the borough links to limiting the risk of flooding.
The developer must provide a waste room of at least 15.5 m² on the ground floor for three-stream collection, and at least 350 m² of land planted directly in the ground.
Parking for at least 29 bicycles is required, including four spaces with a charging station, and the stairway leading to it must have a bicycle ramp.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on March 31, 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the construction of a 4-storey building at 2400, avenue du Mont-Royal Est, at the corner of rue Franchère, on a lot that is currently vacant.
The building will have 10 to 14 housing units, including three adaptable units and three with two bedrooms, plus a commercial space of at least 100 m² facing avenue du Mont-Royal Est.
The project does not comply with the planning by-law, which limits height to 3 storeys and 14 metres; the authorized height will be 4 storeys and no more than 15 metres.

Conditions imposed: no housing units in the basement, parking for at least 28 bicycles with an access ramp, a waste room of at least 15 m², at least 30 m² of vegetation planted directly in the ground, and frost-protected water outlets.
The building must be set back at least 3.5 metres from the property line of the neighbour at 4485, rue Franchère.
A public consultation was held on June 9, 2026, with 5 people present; questions were raised about the exemptions and comments were made about the height, but the project remains unchanged.
A referendum approval process will follow; the authorization becomes void if it is not used within 60 months.
The borough of LaSalle is adopting a new Guide pour l'organisation d'événements sur le domaine public (guide for organizing events on public property), effective immediately.
The guide is intended for residents and organizations that want to hold a public event in LaSalle: it explains the requirements, the municipal by-laws and the steps to follow.
It sets out guidelines on sound broadcasting, schedules, how long events may last and street closures.
It also sets limits on the number and length of events, particularly during the summer.
It includes recommendations for safe and environmentally responsible events.
The borough says it receives more than 200 public event requests per year.
The guide will be sent by email to recognized organizations after it is adopted.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is approving a maximum expense of $137,000, taxes included, to equip the Centre Le Manoir before it opens.
The money comes from the borough's unallocated surplus; the amount net of tax rebates is $125,099.26.

The purchases cover janitorial supplies, sports equipment required for compliance (tatami mats, wall padding, netting), a defibrillator and first aid kits, reception area furniture, and the cost of moving the clubs back in.
The Centre Le Manoir, in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, is undergoing a complete renovation (dojo, gymnasium, HVAC systems, lighting); it is home to the Club de judo Shidokan, Flex Art and Questo.
The schedule calls for purchases and deliveries in March and April 2026, and delivery of certain specialized equipment in June and July 2026.
In May 2024, the borough had awarded the construction contract to Construction Irénée Paquet & Fils inc.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $30,500 to two cultural organizations as part of the 2026 edition of the Fonds de soutien aux organismes culturels œuvrant dans Ville-Marie.

Art Souterrain receives $13,000 for the 18th edition of its festival, from April 25 to May 10, 2026: about 25 works shown free of charge in the downtown underground network and in places such as Place Ville-Marie, the Centre Eaton, the Musée des beaux-arts and the Musée McCord Stewart.

Lespacemaker receives $17,500 for its free cultural programming from May 13 to December 9, 2026, at 2875, rue Hochelaga: eight "Barbec et Trompettes" evenings, close to 50 workshops during "Libre Cours" and activities led by neighbourhood members.
The agreements end no later than December 15, 2026.
The organizations must submit a final report with a financial statement three months after their project ends, and must give visibility to the borough.
In 2025, Art Souterrain had received $15,000 and Lespacemaker $17,500.
The borough of Ville-Marie is cancelling the $5,000 grant it had awarded to the organization Voies culturelles des faubourgs in November 2025.
The money was meant for the 11th edition of "La Nuit aux flambeaux," a project planned for February 2026.
The organization withdrew on December 4, 2025: it did not obtain funding from Montréal en lumière and says it does not have the resources to carry out the project.
The agreement was never signed and no money was paid out.
The unused $5,000 goes back into the borough's source account.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $143,039 to 17 cultural organizations for the 2026 edition of the Programme de soutien financier aux initiatives culturelles.
The agreements with the organizations end no later than June 30, 2027.

The largest amounts go to Théâtre de la Ligue Nationale d'Improvisation ($17,000), Productions Funambules Médias ($16,500), Voies culturelles des faubourgs ($16,000) and Écomusée de la maison du fier monde ($15,000).
Twenty-five organizations had submitted an application; 17 projects were chosen by a selection committee made up of two external members and three City employees.
The program has two streams: cultural activities in public spaces and cultural development projects considered structuring.
The projects cover such things as dance, theatre, music, visual arts, heritage, the Quartier chinois, the place du Village and square Viger.
Several organizations also receive $500 in technical support, and some are getting funding for the first time in five years.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $112,000 to two cultural organizations: $12,000 to Diffusion A.G.C. Montréal and $100,000 to Studio ZX.
The money comes from two sources: $42,000 from the Fonds de soutien aux organismes culturels œuvrant dans Ville-Marie and $70,000 from the Stratégie centre-ville.
Diffusion A.G.C. Montréal will present free outdoor shows one evening a week at place du Village, from June 4 to September 24, 2026 (acoustic music, dance, local and emerging artists).
Studio ZX will offer more than 50 free activities at place du Village on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, from May 22 to October 11, 2026, including Village pour toustes and the Festival Ctrl+Alt.
Studio ZX's programming is aimed in particular at Black, racialized, lesbian and transgender communities, with workshops, shows, drag, burlesque and dance nights.
The agreements end no later than December 15, 2026; each organization must submit a final report and a financial statement three months after its project ends.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $156,900 to eight cultural organizations for projects taking place in 2026, through its Fonds de soutien aux organismes culturels.

The amounts: $35,000 to the Musée McCord Stewart, $30,000 to Voies culturelles des faubourgs, $27,000 to the Musée des beaux-arts, $20,000 to the Orchestre Métropolitain, $18,000 to Pointe-à-Callière, $13,400 to Espace libre, $7,000 to Alchimies, Créations et Cultures and $6,500 to Le Monastère.
Several projects take place on pedestrian streets or squares: avenue du Musée, rue Victoria, place D'Youville and place Royale, from spring to mid-October.

Other funded activities: the Orientalys festival at the Quai de l'Horloge (August 13 to 16), an Orchestre Métropolitain concert at parc du Mont-Royal (August 5) and the Festival des faubourgs (August 21 to 23).
Le Monastère will hold 10 circus events in the garden of the église Saint James the Apostle, on rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest, from June to August.
The agreements with the organizations end no later than December 31, 2026.
The amounts granted are generally lower than the amounts requested: for example, $6,500 granted out of the $22,995 requested by Le Monastère.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $9,000 to the Maison québécoise du théâtre pour l'enfance et la jeunesse for its project "Liaison avec les communautés : Destination théâtre !".
The project offers a turnkey experience at the Maison Théâtre for 10 groups: a welcome, a show and a mediation workshop.
It is aimed at immigrant families, newly arrived families and families in a socio-economically vulnerable situation.
The activities run from May 15, 2026 to March 31, 2027; the agreement ends on March 31, 2027.
The organization had asked for $15,550; it had received $13,000 in 2025 and $15,000 in 2024.
The money comes from the 2026 edition of the Programme de soutien financier aux initiatives culturelles, "projets structurants" stream.
The organization must submit a final report with a financial statement three months after the end of the project.
The borough of Ville-Marie is cancelling the $6,500 grant it had awarded to the organization Le Monastère.
The money was to be used for the « Les Guinguettes du Monastère » project, planned for the summer of 2026.
The organization wrote to the borough on May 11, 2026 to say that it did not have the financial means to carry out the project and to give up the grant.
The agreement was never signed and no money was paid out.
The $6,500 goes back to the borough's source account.
The grant was part of the Fonds de soutien aux organismes culturels de Ville-Marie, which had $156,900 divided among eight organizations in May 2026.
The executive committee is asked to appoint Shahir Guindi as chair of the board of directors of the Société du parc Jean-Drapeau, for three years, starting September 1, 2026.
He replaces Karel Mayrand, chair since 2023 (and a board member since 2018), whose term ends in May 2026.

The Société launched a recruitment process in February 2026 with the firm Electi Recrutement de cadres; three candidates were interviewed and Mr. Guindi was chosen unanimously by the selection committee.
Mr. Guindi is a lawyer, outgoing national co-chair of the firm Osler, and sits on the boards of Investissement Québec, Université Concordia and Jubilant Draxis Pharma, among others.
The Société's board of directors has 9 members appointed by the City's executive committee; members receive attendance fees.
No communications activities are planned for this file.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is asking the Directeur de l'état civil to designate the councillor for the Parc-Extension district, Elvira Carhuallanqui, as an officiant for marriages and civil unions.
Once designated, she could officiate at marriages and civil unions within the territory of the Ville de Montréal.
The Directeur de l'état civil would assign her a unique identification number to be written on marriage or civil union declarations.
The authorization would apply only to the territory named in the designation document and for the duration of her term as an elected official.
The request is voluntary: the councillor herself expressed her intention to officiate at marriages and civil unions.
This file involves no spending.
The City is accepting the donation of a sculpture by Montréal artist Chloé Desjardins, titled "Page-miroir : débouchement/marché-452-hiver/débraillé".
The work is valued at $19,750, the average of two independent appraisals ($17,500 and $22,000).
The City will give the donor an official tax receipt for that amount, a condition set for the donation.
The donation involves no expense or revenue for the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs.

The work joins the Collection municipale, which includes more than 1,200 works displayed in municipal buildings (borough halls, libraries, cultural and sports spaces); the display location is not determined in advance and the work may be loaned to institutions.
The artist grants the City a licence to exhibit, reproduce and publish the work; a committee of four visual arts experts had recommended accepting the donation.
The City is awarding $32,000 in prize money for the 2026 edition of its three excellence awards in visual arts and fine crafts (Pierre-Ayot, Louis-Comtois, François-Houdé).
The total envelope is going from $17,500 to $32,000 and will be shared among 9 people: the winners and, for the first time, the finalists.
Prize money for winners: $10,000 (Louis-Comtois), $7,500 (Pierre-Ayot) and $7,500 (François-Houdé); the finalists share $3,000, $2,000 and $2,000 depending on the award.
The amounts had not changed since 2010; the increase coincides with the awards' 30th and 35th anniversaries.
The awards are managed with the Association des galeries d'art contemporain and the Conseil des métiers d'art du Québec, which handle the juries, the award ceremonies and part of the promotion.
Calls for applications run from May to August 2026; the awards are to be presented in late November or early December 2026, with an exhibition of the François-Houdé award finalists in December.
The expense, which is recurring, is paid 100% by the central city out of the Service de la culture budget.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is awarding Axe Construction inc. the work to make the stands at ice rink no. 1 of the aréna Saint-Michel, at 3440, rue Jarry Est, safe.
The contract is worth $587,237.43, taxes included; with $88,085.61 in contingencies and $17,600 in incidental costs, the total authorized spending comes to $692,923.04.
The work includes glass doors and partitions to protect the public from pucks, marking of stair nosings, removal of surplus seats, fencing and handrails.
A technical opinion dated March 9, 2026 concluded that the number of seats had to be adjusted to match the evacuation capacity; some seats were temporarily blocked off while awaiting the work.
Two companies submitted bids out of eight who obtained the tender documents; the winning bid is $29,272.06 above the estimate, or 5.25%.
The work is to begin in August 2026 and be completed in July 2027, funded by the borough's investment program.
The City wants to award 9140-2594 Québec inc. (Construction Arcade) the general work in its 6 drinking water treatment plants, its 14 reservoirs and its pumping stations.
The agreement is estimated at $14,476,599.60 including taxes: $14,176,599.60 for the work and $300,000 for contingencies.
The term is 36 months, from April 2026 to March 2029, with two possible 12-month extensions (about $5,198,086.52 per renewal year).
The contractor will have to be available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and respond on request: maintenance, concrete, masonry, plumbing, electrical work, demolition, repairs, etc.
Three companies out of ten submitted bids; two offers were compliant. The lowest one is $91,641.25 (0.59%) above the City's estimate.
The expense is paid by the urban agglomeration, because drinking water production falls under its jurisdiction. The company's performance will be evaluated.
The Ville de Montréal is becoming a partner of the Assises 2026 of the Union des municipalités du Québec, to be held in Québec from May 13 to 15, 2026.
It is putting $10,000 toward the event, non-taxable, an amount paid by the central city out of the 2026 budget of the Bureau des relations gouvernementales et municipales.
The partnership chosen concerns the event's mobile app: Montréal's logo and a welcome message will appear on its home page.
The app will share the program and activities in real time and will remain available until the next Assises.
The City receives 5 free registrations for the Assises, worth $890 each.
The City has acted as a partner of the Assises every year since 2022.
The City is awarding a negotiated (sole-source) contract of $412,000, taxes included, to the organization L'Anonyme U.I.M.
The organization will work for 12 months in the encampment area of the friche Notre-Dame, along rue Notre-Dame Est, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.
The planned services: a regular presence on site, work with highly vulnerable people, prevention of safety and sanitation risks, and coordination with partners and the City.
The document cites the build-up of waste and hazardous materials (syringes, contaminated objects) and risks of fire, unsanitary conditions and insecurity for the campers and nearby residents.
L'Anonyme has already been present on the friche since February 2026, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
The project starts in May 2026 and ends no later than May 2027; the expense is paid 100% by the central city.
The City states that in 2026 it is tripling its budget devoted to homelessness and social cohabitation.
The City is giving $100,000 to the organization L'Anonyme U.I.M. for its « Halte-répit » project, aimed at people experiencing homelessness.
The project consists of a 20-space trailer set up on the friche Notre-Dame, alongside rue Notre-Dame Est, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.
The money covers the months of May and June 2026: rental of the trailer and a generator, a washroom unit, snacks, soups, hygiene products and emergency clothing.
The project ends on June 30, 2026, pending confirmation of funding from the health network for the rest of the year.
The City's contribution represents 42.3% of the project budget; it is covered 100% by the urban agglomeration.
Before this project, the organization had been operating two 10-space trailers on the site since January 2026, replaced on May 12, 2026 by the single trailer.
The document states that in 2026 the City is tripling its budget devoted to fighting homelessness and to social cohabitation.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is approving the architectural plans to convert the 2-storey mixed-use building at 6085, boulevard Monk, in the Côte-Saint-Paul area.
The project adds one storey on the two-storey portion and two storeys on the one-storey rear portion occupied by garages.
The building will have 9 units: a studio on the ground floor, then 2 one-bedroom units and 2 studios on each of the 2nd and 3rd floors.
The floor area of the existing business is reduced; the garage portion is not changed.
The 3rd floor is set back 30 cm from the façade on boulevard Monk.

After an unfavourable opinion from the comité consultatif d'urbanisme in March 2026, the committee gave a favourable opinion on April 28, 2026, on the condition that the 3rd-floor canopy be removed, that a projecting row of brick be added and that the alignment of the openings be reviewed.
The decision is scheduled for the borough council meeting of June 8, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is hiring 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky) to handle horticultural maintenance, snow removal and cleanliness at Square Viger and Place des Montréalaises.
The contract is worth $2,102,586.80 including taxes, plus $210,258.68 in contingencies, for a total expense of $2,312,845.48.
The contract runs from March 15, 2026 to March 14, 2029, with two possible one-year extensions (until March 14, 2031).
The work includes emptying garbage bins, picking up litter, removing graffiti and illegal posters, spreading de-icing products in winter, mowing grass and cutting dangerous branches up to 5 m.
Four companies out of seven submitted bids; Groupe Nicky is the lowest compliant bidder, at 27% below the City's estimate.
The borough says it does not have the staff needed to do this work itself, following the recent redevelopment of the two sites.
The company's performance will be evaluated at the end of the contract.
The Ville-Marie borough is awarding Entrepreneur paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée the horticultural maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal for six public squares in the downtown area.
The locations covered: square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez.
The contract runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029, with two possible one-year extensions, up to March 31, 2031.
The authorized spending totals $707,283.99 including taxes: $642,985.44 for the bid and $64,298.55 in contingencies (10%).
The work includes planting and maintaining flower beds, mowing, leaf collection, snow removal on pathways and spreading abrasives.
The borough says it does not have enough staff to meet maintenance needs, which are growing along with the number of people visiting the area.
Five of the seven firms that obtained the documents submitted bids; Strathmore offered the lowest price, 27% below the City's estimate.

The Ville-Marie borough is entrusting the maintenance, cleanliness and manual garbage collection of squares Dorchester, Victoria and Phillips, as well as place du Canada, to the Société de développement commercial Montréal Centre-Ville.
The contract covers the period from April 15 to November 15, 2026, with two possible one-year extensions, up to November 15, 2028.
The authorized spending totals $310,674.64: $282,431.49 for the bid and $28,243.15 in contingencies (10%), taxes included.
The planned work includes cleaning the paving stones, street furniture and benches, picking up garbage and cigarette butts, and collecting recyclable materials.
Seven firms submitted bids; six were found compliant and Speico inc. was declared non-compliant on administrative grounds.

The SDC is the lowest bidder: its price is 10% below the internal estimate ($313,812.77) and $83,683.40 below the second-lowest bid; the document explains this by its status as a non-profit organization.

The borough of Ville-Marie is hiring Urbex Construction inc. to water plants and maintain tree pits, for a maximum expense of $2,192,356.84 (a $1,993,051.67 contract plus $199,305.17 in contingencies), taxes included.
The contract runs from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028, with two options to extend it by one year each.

Each year, from May to September, the contractor waters 1,500 trees (up to 250 more on request), 1,300 m2 of curb extensions and flower beds, 58 Versailles planters, 63 planters with trees, as well as 958 ground planters and 2,900 "Uptown" flower boxes spread over three years.
It must also clean, weed and mulch 7,000 tree pits without grates four times a year, and clean and weed 2,000 tree pits with grates twice a year.
Urbex submitted the lowest of the four compliant bids, $15,400.04 below the second one and 37.97% below the internal estimate, which the borough says it overestimated by anticipating high inflation.
The borough justifies the contract by the increase in planted areas, and by heat waves and droughts that threaten the survival of the plantings.
The company's performance will be assessed at the end of the contract.
The borough of Anjou is extending its cleaning services contract with F.D. Maintenance 2011 inc. by 12 months, for a maximum of $175,509.05, taxes included.
The extension covers the period from May 7, 2026 to May 6, 2027, using the option provided for in the original contract awarded in May 2024.
The total contract expense goes from $340,794.27 to $516,303.32, taxes included.
Three buildings are covered: the borough hall (7701, boul. Louis-H.-La Fontaine), the bibliothèque du Haut-Anjou (7070, rue Jarry Est) and the public works building (7171, rue Bombardier).
The borough says it does not have the in-house resources to do this work and considers the supplier's performance satisfactory.
Without this service, the borough expects effects on the cleanliness of the buildings, waste management, and the safety of employees and citizens.
The borough of Anjou is awarding a $128,220.12 contract (taxes included) to WAA Montréal Inc. for professional services related to the redevelopment of parc des Roseraies.
The project includes grading work, a new synthetic soccer field and a new basketball court, replacing facilities described as outdated.
Also planned: lighting, fencing and netting, acrylic surfacing and lower-height hoops for children, an accessible outdoor water fountain, adapted furniture and the preservation of mature trees.
The expense is funded by the borough's reserved fund for park purposes (Fonds réservé pour fins de parcs).
Eight firms submitted bids; WAA Montréal submitted the lowest price, 63% below the $350,000 estimate.
Timeline: plans and specifications in May 2026, call for tenders for the work on May 28, 2026, construction starting in fall 2026 and completion expected in spring 2027.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is borrowing $5,376,000 to develop parks and shorelines on its territory.
The money covers the work, but also professional fees, studies, design and supervision, decontamination and environmental rehabilitation, and the purchase and installation of street furniture.
The amount corresponds to the first three years of the park redevelopment program included in the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program, whose total budget is $111,990,000.
The loan, including refinancing, cannot exceed 20 years; any other source of funding obtained will be used to reduce the debt.
The borough council is adopting the by-law on April 13, 2026; it must then be approved by the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing before coming into force upon its publication.
A public notice of coming into force will be published in the local newspapers once ministerial authorization is received.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is closing ten loan by-laws adopted between 2008 and 2016, whose projects are now finished.
These by-laws funded road work, building protection, the development of parks and green spaces, and the purchase of equipment.
In each case, part of the authorized borrowing was never taken out; these remaining balances cannot be used for anything else.
The authorized borrowing amounts are being reduced to the amounts actually borrowed, as shown in Appendix A.
The borough is asking the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation to cancel these residual balances in its records.
According to the document, closing them has no financial impact and does not change the burden on taxpayers.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is amending three by-laws: traffic and parking, nuisances, and peace and public order.
Events, celebrations or demonstrations that already have a borough permit will no longer need an ordinance voted on by the borough council.
Permits are issued by the borough's Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The exemptions concerned include parking, noise, and the sale and consumption of alcohol on public property.
According to the document, the goal is to avoid adopting several ordinances at each borough council meeting.
A public notice will announce the by-law's coming into force on the borough's website.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is replacing its 2004 order on park opening hours with a new order.
What's new: events, celebrations or gatherings that already have a permit issued by the borough will be allowed to use the parks outside opening hours without a separate order.
The permit is issued by the borough's Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The borough will no longer have to adopt an order at every council meeting for each new public event added during the year.
A public notice announcing that it is coming into force will be published on the borough's website.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is putting forward Marie-Claude Baril, councillor for the district of Pointe-aux-Trembles, as its representative on the facility board of directors of the CIUSSS de l'Est-de-l'Île-de-Montréal.
This CIUSSS serves the eastern part of the island, including the population of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.
The final appointment is not up to the borough: it is the board of directors of Santé Québec that appoints the members.
The law allows Santé Québec to appoint from one to three municipal elected officials from the territory served, with no more than one elected official per local service network territory.
No amount of money is tied to this decision.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving after the fact an expense of $510, taxes included.
The amount covers 3 tickets at $170 each for the Grand Prix du Conseil des arts de Montréal, held on April 2, 2026 at the Palais des congrès.
The three elected officials concerned are Mayor Denis Pelletier, Councillor Diana Varela and Councillor Gerlando Guarraggi.
The event honours artists and artistic organizations from Montréal.
The expense is charged according to the financial information in the file.
The mayor of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles announces that a by-law amending the borough council's internal rules will be presented at a future meeting.
The change affects section 9: a council member will be able to file a motion after the usual 8-day deadline, up to 3 business days before the meeting.
This only concerns how borough council meetings work, not services to residents.
A public notice will be published on the borough's website when the by-law comes into force.
No spending is attached to this file.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the construction of a residential building at 1208, rue Stanley, downtown, on lot 1 340 224.
The project will be allowed to go beyond the neighbourhood's planning rules on four points: maximum height, maximum density, siting method and side setback.
The building must follow the plans by the firm Atelier Chaloub, architectes, stamped by the borough on January 22, 2026.
The developer will have to submit a wind study done by a professional, with mitigation measures if needed, and a landscaping plan providing for water management suited to the basin area.
No condenser (air conditioning unit) may be visible from the street; the party wall will have to be visually softened, in particular with brick or stone.
Work must begin within 60 months of adoption, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
Following the public consultation of February 25, 2026, the council corrected the section covering the density exemption; this change may be subject to approval by referendum.
The borough of Ville-Marie is granting a minor exemption at 405, rue de Bonsecours, in Vieux-Montréal, for the PHI Contemporain project.
The project turns three heritage buildings — the maison Louis-Viger, the maison du Calvet and the magasin Davies — into a museum, with the demolition of annexes representing 33.5% of the main volume.
The final building would have 4 storeys and reach 23.58 m, while the by-law for the area sets the maximum height at 17 m; some parts do not reach the minimum height of 11 m (from 6.14 to 9.06 m).

The exemption also covers the left and right side setbacks (between 0 m and more than 2.5 m instead of 0 m or 2.5 m) and the doors of the magasin Davies, which will open onto the sidewalk of rue Saint-Paul.
The museum would include an auditorium, offices, educational spaces, cloakrooms and a café area not visible from the street.
The buildings are located in the declared heritage site of Montréal; some work is subject to the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel.
The urban planning advisory committee issued a favourable opinion on February 12, 2026; a public notice comes before the borough council adopts the resolution.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing "museum" use at 405, rue de Bonsecours, in Vieux-Montréal, where the zoning does not automatically allow it.

The PHI Contemporain project will bring together three heritage buildings: the maison Louis-Viger (415, de Bonsecours), the maison du Calvet (401, de Bonsecours) and the magasin Davies (411, Saint-Paul).
The annexes, which make up 33.5% of the main volume, would be demolished; the three historic buildings would be kept and restored.
The end result: a single 4-storey building (23.58 m), connected by 2 basements, with 6 galleries, an auditorium, 2 educational spaces, offices and a café not visible from the street.
A loading area would be built on the north side for the delivery of artworks, with the possibility of replanting trees.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on February 12, 2026; a public notice and posting will come before adoption by the borough council.
The buildings are located in Montréal's declared heritage site; some work falls under the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel.
The borough of Ville-Marie is approving the opening of a virtual reality centre at 417, rue Saint-Pierre, in Vieux-Montréal.
The use "recreational games establishment" was not automatically allowed in this area: it goes through the conditional uses procedure.
The space covers about 170 m² on the ground floor (at the corner of Le Moyne) and includes a reception area, a waiting area, a cloakroom, a bathroom and a play area for a maximum of 10 participants.
Two conditions: the use stays limited to the ground floor, and the openings on the Saint-Pierre and Le Moyne facades must not be blocked.
No work and no change to the appearance of the building (built in 1902, seven storeys, declared heritage site) are required.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on May 7, 2026; a public notice and posting come before adoption by the borough council.
Saint-Léonard is changing its zoning by-law on two points affecting single-family homes and buildings with 2 to 5 units.
The City is removing the ban on black sloped roofs and the requirement for a minimum solar reflectance index of 25 for those roofs.
The borough explains that this requirement, which came into force in March 2025, did not target areas in heat islands and was delaying the issuing of permits.
Owners will be allowed to install watertight doors to protect against surface flooding even if this reduces the number of parking spaces in the garage.
Condition: all openings at the bottom of the sunken entrance, below sidewalk level, must be protected by watertight doors.
The by-law adds a definition of "watertight door"; the public consultation meeting was held on March 18, 2026 and adoption is scheduled for April 7, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is adopting a new by-law (2298) on site planning and architectural integration programs, which completely replaces the former by-law 2288.
The goal: to bring the architecture and site planning rules into line with the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050, adopted by city council on June 16, 2025.
The minutes of the public consultation meeting held on May 19, 2026 are filed; the draft had been amended before the meeting to correct omissions concerning places of worship and wetlands.
Projects will from now on be assessed according to three levels of land intensification (low, intermediate, high), taken from a map in the Plan d'urbanisme.
New criteria are being added, in particular for mechanical equipment, rooftop structures, outdoor parking areas, microclimatic impacts and equipment related to climate change.

Some chapters target specific cases: part of parc Giuseppe-Garibaldi (an archaeological area) and a list of heritage buildings or buildings built before 1940, including École Général-Vanier, École Pie-XII and several houses on rue Jarry Est.
The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for the borough to adopt all of its concordance by-laws.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is distributing the $1,342,300 management surplus generated from its 2025 fiscal year.
$150,300 goes to the reserve used to stabilize snow removal costs.
$200,000 goes to the reserve for budget balance.
The remaining balance of $992,000 stays as a free surplus that the borough can use at its discretion.
A transfer of $350,300 between the various surplus accounts is authorized.
The distribution follows the 2025 surplus policy adopted by the executive committee on June 10, 2026 and by city council on June 15, 2026.
The decision falls under the authority of the borough council.
The borough of Pierrefonds-Roxboro is giving $10,000 to the non-profit organization Sports Montréal inc. for summer 2026.
The money is used to pay for support workers for children with limitations in day camps.
The estimated needs reach 35 weeks of support: 14 at Grier, 11 at À-Ma-Baie and 10 at George-Springate.
The total cost of this service for the season is $27,288.99, while the organization had budgeted $7,787.52.
With the funding already received, the organization was short $10,000 to cover all the salaries.
Sports Montréal had already received $10,000 in March 2026 for offering day camps in the borough.
The organization will have to submit a final day camp report after the summer season.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is applying for a federal grant (Développement économique Canada pour les régions du Québec) for improvements at parc Loyola.
The federal program can provide up to $90,000; the borough says the operation will have no financial impact on it.
The work involves improvements in the park and on its two baseball fields, with free access to the sports and recreation facilities.
The project focuses in particular on accessibility and on outdoor activities for vulnerable and marginalized people.
Planned timeline: signing of the agreement in March 2026, work in 2026-2027.
The council authorizes the borough director to sign the agreement and all documents related to the application.

The City is amending its agreement with the ministère des Affaires municipales to transfer $100,000 in financial assistance from the replacement of the platform lift at Centre Monkland to the development of an outdoor training area at parc Loyola, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The change of project was approved by the ministère on January 29, 2025; the facility has been open to the public since September 2025 and the work was completed on September 30, 2025.
The platform lift project was abandoned because the solutions considered could not meet the new universal accessibility standards with the equipment available on the market.
The total cost of the parc Loyola project is estimated at $200,000: the ministère covers up to $100,000 and the borough pays at least $100,000, plus any cost overruns.
Contracts already awarded: $128,022.65 to Atmosphare for the supply and installation of the training circuit, and $71,468.46 to Les Constructions Argozy inc. for the development work.
The borough is also planning an overall project to bring Centre Monkland up to standard, including the installation of a new elevator.
The ministère requires the addendum to be signed by the Mayor of Montréal.
The City is awarding Beluga Services Municipaux inc. the operation of the Ray-Lawson snow disposal site, in the borough of Anjou, for five years.
The total authorized spending comes to $13,121,205.70, taxes included: $9,719,411.63 for the contract, $1,943,882.33 in contingencies and $1,457,911.74 for variations in quantities.
The cost of the contract was increased by 35% to cover expenses related to how unpredictable winters are; additional funds could be requested from the Réserve neige.
The contract runs from November 15, 2026 to November 14, 2031, with the work period running from November 15 to November 14 each year.
Two companies submitted bids out of five that obtained the tender documents; Beluga, the lowest compliant bidder, is 7.29% above the City's latest estimate.
The City explains the 16.27% gap between the two bids by the fact that Beluga already held the previous contract.
The spending is fully covered by the central city and the company's performance will be evaluated.
The City is awarding Contant inc. the contract to operate the snow disposal site located at 1025, 4e avenue, in the borough of Lachine.
The contract runs for three years: from November 15, 2026 to November 14, 2029.
Total authorized spending of $1,272,385.20, taxes included: $942,507.56 for the contract, $188,501.51 in contingencies and $141,376.13 for variation in quantities.
The 35% increase on the contract is meant to cover how unpredictable winters are; if the winter is harsher, another file could draw on the Réserve neige.
Two companies submitted bids out of the five that obtained the specifications; Contant inc. is the lowest compliant bidder, 27.45% below the other bid and 1.80% below the City's estimate.
The spending is paid entirely by the central city, from the operating budget of the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne.
Contant inc.'s performance will be evaluated at the end of the contract.
The City is awarding a 4-year contract to Jean-Claude Alary inc. to rent a backhoe with an operator, at a maximum cost of $348,926.13, taxes included.
The machine will be used at the lieu d'élimination de la neige Riverside, in the borough of Ville-Marie, between November 15 and April 15 each year.
The bid price is $258,463.80, plus $51,692.76 in contingencies and $38,769.57 for variation in quantities, a 35% increase justified by how unpredictable winters are.
The contract starts as soon as it is awarded and ends on April 15, 2030.
Public call for tenders 26-21415 received 8 bids; Jean-Claude Alary inc. is the lowest compliant bidder, 9.26% below the City's estimate.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne, and is fully covered by the central city.
If winters are harsher, additional funds could be requested through the Réserve neige; the company's performance will be assessed at the end of the contract.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving a pilot project for a "mobile anchor point": a recreational vehicle set up as an overnight drop-in space in parc Saint-Jean-Baptiste.
The vehicle will be allowed to occupy the park from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m., despite the usual closing hours, for a maximum of six months.

The organization Société Ressources-Loisirs de Pointe-aux-Trembles, through its Prévention Pointe-de-l'Île service, operates the vehicle; its presence will be adjusted according to the needs observed, particularly during periods of extreme cold.
The RV offers a maximum of 4 temporary beds, with 1 or 2 qualified workers present at all times.
Conditions imposed: no outdoor installations (tents, chairs, tables), daily cleaning inside and outside, and no noise or nighttime disturbance tolerated.
The organization must submit a monthly report to the borough (users, interventions, incidents) and a full evaluation one month before the end of the project.
The borough says it intervened at 20 reported encampments between May 2023 and October 2025.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding Les Entreprises P.N.P. inc. the partial redevelopment of the jardin communautaire Rivard, on rue Rivard north of rue de Bienville, in the Mile-End (about 1,000 m²).
The contract is worth $110,197.79 including taxes; the total authorized spending comes to $156,727.46, with $16,529.67 in contingencies and $30,000 in incidental costs.

The work includes demolishing the concrete wall and the fence on the lane side (found to be deteriorated and at risk of collapsing), rebuilding the wall on the south side, new concrete barriers and fencing, and replacing the wooden planter boxes, the grass and the open-cell paving stones.
The work is to begin in September 2026 and be completed in November 2026.
P.N.P. was the lowest of the 5 compliant bidders: its bid is 47.47% below the estimate, and the highest compliant bid was $272,928.31.
The spending comes out of the borough's PTI budget; the project will be publicized with on-site signage, social media posts and a web page.
The City is paying $69,059 (net of taxes, or $75,628.61 including taxes) to the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal to monitor the soil at parc Sir-Wilfrid-Laurier after the work.
The money comes from the contaminated soil environmental liability reserve and is paid 100% by the central city.
The park's soccer field was redeveloped in 2024-2025 on a site that was once used for waste disposal.
Monitoring is required for 5 years, from 2026 to 2030, to check that environmental standards are met and that the mitigation measures are working.
The amount includes $55,247.20 for the monitoring and $13,811.80 in contingencies (25%).
The borough will have to report its spending every quarter to the Service de l'environnement; the final bill could be lower.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is paying $150,000 to three neighbourhood round tables, or $50,000 each.
The three organizations are the Corporation de développement communautaire Solidarités Villeray, Vivre Saint-Michel en Santé and the Table de quartier Parc-Extension.
The money covers the period from the signing of the agreement until March 31, 2027.
The amount is going from $34,513 to $50,000 per organization compared with last year, since the City increased its share in the 2026 budget.
The funds are used for local cooperation against poverty: housing, welcoming newcomers, safety, access to services, employment, health.
The expense is shared between the borough and the central city; the director of culture, sports, recreation and social development will sign the agreements.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving up to $9,300 to the Regroupement des Éco-quartiers for the Patrouille verte in the summer of 2026.
Two environmental studies students will patrol the borough on foot and by bicycle from June 1 to August 22, 2026, 32 hours a week for 12 weeks.
They will meet with residents to talk about the brown bin and recycling, bulky items and hazardous waste, saving drinking water, and green alleys.
Supervision is provided by Ville en vert, the organization managing the borough's Éco-quartier program for 2023-2026.
The Regroupement is asking boroughs for $2,100 per patroller this year and is raising wages to $18, $18.25 and $18.50 an hour.
Canada Summer Jobs funds nine weeks; the borough is paying for three more weeks, at a cost of $850 per week per patroller.
The contribution was $9,000 in 2025, $8,830 in 2024 and $6,600 in 2023.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is giving up to $20,000 to the organization Espace-Famille Villeray, taken from its surpluses, for the subsidy program for cloth diapers and sustainable feminine hygiene products from June 8, 2026 to June 4, 2027, or until the funds run out.
Residents can be reimbursed for 75% of their cloth diaper purchases, up to $150 per child under 36 months (only one application per child, invoices less than 6 months old).
For reusable menstrual products: reimbursement of 75% up to $75, only one application per household every 3 years, within 12 months of the purchase.
Five free two-hour workshops on cloth diapers will be offered, online, at Espace-Famille Villeray or at other organizations in the area.
Breakdown of the amount: $16,375 in subsidies to residents, $2,200 in management fees, $1,000 for the workshops and $425 for advertising.
Applications are made online or in person, with a piece of identification showing an address, invoices, a specimen cheque and proof of the child's birth if applicable.
The borough has supported this program since 2018 (cloth diapers) and since 2021 for feminine hygiene products; the contribution was $25,000 last year.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $150,000 to the Table de quartier de Montréal-Nord for the « Jeunesse en harmonie ! » project, carried out with the Table femmes Osez au féminin.
The project aims to prevent violence in intimate relationships among young people aged 12 to 25, especially girls and young women, as well as among their parents.
It targets 100 girls and 100 boys in high school (12-17 years old) and young adults (18-25 years old), and runs from February 9 to December 31, 2026.
On the program: workshops for teens and parents, virtual immersion in schools with neighbourhood police station 39, podcasts co-hosted by young people, outreach work and digital content creation.
The money comes from the Prévention Montréal program (Axis 2) of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, with a leftover amount from 2025 carried over to 2026.
An agreement between the City and the organization sets the conditions for payment; the project includes an evaluation component.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is granting $50,000 to the Table de quartier de Montréal-Nord for 2026-2027 and is approving an agreement with the organization.
Last year, the borough's support was $31,113: the City increased its contribution to reach a target of $50,000 per table de quartier.
With Centraide ($75,000) and the Direction régionale de santé publique ($21,000), the Table will receive a total of $146,000 for the period.

The City's amount comes from two sources: $33,620 from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and $16,380 from an agreement between the City and the ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale (Québec funds, non-recurring).

The money is used to mobilize and bring together local stakeholders around the Plan de développement social de Montréal-Nord 2021-2026 (housing, safety, green spaces, food, educational success, transportation, etc.).
The current cycle of the plan ends in June 2026; the partners will evaluate the plan before preparing its next edition.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is providing $50,000 to the Table de quartier du Nord-Ouest-de-l'Île de Montréal for the period from August 4, 2026 to August 31, 2027.

The amount comes from the central city: $33,620 from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and $16,380 from the City–ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale agreement (non-recurring).
Together with Centraide ($75,000) and the Direction régionale de santé publique ($17,145), the Table receives a total of $142,145 for 2026-2027.
Last year, the City's contribution to this Table was $31,113; the target support per table was raised to $50,000 in April 2026.

The Table brings together community organizations, institutions, private partners and local elected officials, and works on housing, food security, cultural diversity, access to services and socio-ecological transition.
Kathy Dancsecs, division head of Loisirs, Événements et Développement social, or her replacement, is authorized to sign the agreement.
The organization must apply two visibility protocols attached to the agreement.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough officially recognizes the Club de Volley-ball Dynamique as a non-profit organization, in category A of the sports field.
The recognition takes effect as soon as it is adopted by the borough council.
The Club becomes eligible for the support provided under the borough's Policy for the Recognition and Support of Non-Profit Organizations, according to its category.
The Club offers a volleyball program for youth focused on physical fitness, sports skills, and team spirit.
A partnership agreement will be prepared with the organization, which may also receive individualized support.

The recognition and support of all non-profit organizations is reassessed every year; the results will be sent to the organizations at the end of 2026, along with any adjustments required to keep their status.
Recognition requests can be submitted twice a year; more than a hundred non-profit organizations are active in the territory.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough and Cégep Gérald-Godin are exchanging access to their facilities from August 1, 2026, to July 31, 2027.
No money changes hands: the exchange is hour for hour, free of charge on both sides.
The Cégep gets access to the borough's sports fields, public spaces, and community centres for its sport-study programs.
The borough and its local sports organizations get access to the Cégep's gymnasiums, classrooms, and rooms.
Time slots will be set each year based on the needs of both parties and the availability of the venues.
For reference, the document compares 14.5 hours of soccer field time ($1,087) to 14.5 hours of gymnasium time ($1,305).
