A similar agreement already existed for the period from May 1, 2025, to May 31, 2026.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough and Cégep John-Abbott are exchanging sports facilities free of charge from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027.
The Cégep may use the baseball field at parc George-Springate (4788, rue Richmond), with field opening, preparation and maintenance provided.
This access is limited to 11 weeks, from August 1 to the third week of October; the Club de baseball Pierrefonds keeps priority and the Ville may change the schedule.
In exchange, the borough's sports groups get up to 96 hours in the gymnasiums of the Complexe sportif du Cégep (gymnase Casgrain in the fall, another gymnasium in winter-spring).
The gymnasiums are not available during exams (mid-December, mid-May) and graduation ceremonies; the Cégep may change the schedules.
For information purposes, the document values the use of the baseball field at $1,725 and that of the gymnasiums at $3,255.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough council takes note of the results of two registers held from January 19 to 23, 2026 on loan by-laws.
The first by-law authorizes a $4,000,000 loan to develop and redevelop various parks and green spaces in 2026-2028.
The second authorizes a $7,000,000 loan for the Programme de dotation et de protection des bâtiments in 2026-2028.
Out of 101,620 people qualified to vote, 10,173 signatures were required to trigger a referendum; no signatures were recorded.
Both by-laws are therefore deemed approved by the people qualified to vote.
Next steps: approval by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation, notice of coming into force, and awarding of contracts in spring 2026.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is appointing three elected officials to the urban planning advisory committee (CCU), retroactive to November 13, 2025, for two-year terms.
Councillor Jocelyn Pauzé (Marie-Victorin district) is appointed as a regular member and chair of the committee.
Councillors Ericka Alneus (Étienne-Desmarteau) and Josefina Blanco (Saint-Édouard) are appointed as substitute members.
The CCU reviews applications for minor exemptions, site planning and architectural integration plans, demolition applications and other urban planning matters.
These appointments follow the general election of November 2, 2025, which required the council to renew the representation of elected officials on the committee.
No amount is associated with this decision.
The City is adding $87,640.27 (taxes included) to the negotiated contract awarded to LabVantage Solutions France, bringing the total expense to $186,965.91.
The money will be used to complete the upgrade of the LIMS software, the system that manages laboratory data for the Service de l'eau and the Service de l'environnement.
The original contract of $99,325.64 was meant to move from version 8.2 to version 8.8 and to bring the system back onto the City's computer infrastructure.
The City will instead go directly to version 8.9 and must reconfigure many customized reports, work that was not included in the initial estimate.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration and financed through a loan by-law, under the "Infrastructures des usines de l'eau" project.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders because it involves exclusive rights to the software and its maintenance by the manufacturer.
No communications activities are planned.

The City is entering into a framework agreement with Conseillers en gestion et informatique CGI inc. for services to develop web, application and transactional digital solutions, for a maximum of $4,828,950, taxes included.
The agreement runs for 36 months, with an option to extend it by 12 months.

These outside resources will support the Service des technologies de l'information in developing applications for partners such as the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier, the Service de l'eau and the Service de la concertation des arrondissements.
Public call for tenders 26-21318 drew 8 bids: all were administratively compliant, but 6 did not reach the minimum score of 70%. CGI obtained the highest final score.
The price selected is 30.96% lower than the City's latest estimate ($6,993,929.25) and 7.48% lower than the second-best bid (Levio, $5,190,316.43).
The City will carry out a performance evaluation of CGI and will charge the expenses to the budget of the Service des technologies de l'information as needs arise.
Some firms withdrew, citing in particular the unlimited liability imposed on the successful bidder and the use of a single hourly rate.

The Ville-Marie borough is extending the rental of storage space at the Centre Alexandre-DeSève for two organizations: Folklore Canada International and the Société du patrimoine d'expression du Québec.
The extension covers August 1 to December 31, 2026 and brings the City $560, taxes included.
The rate is $56 per month per storage unit, according to the borough's 2026 rate by-law.
Both organizations must vacate these storage spaces: they were notified in December 2025 and asked for more time to relocate.
The borough secretary is authorized to sign the agreement, expected in July 2026.
The borough rents space at preferential rates to non-profit organizations whose mission involves culture, recreation or social development.
The borough of Outremont is extending by 12 months the road marking contract awarded to Les Signalisations R.C. inc., for the year 2026.
Additional cost of $235,761.30, taxes included, which is the 2025 prices increased by 3%.
The total contract goes from $457,788.93 to $693,550.23, taxes included.
The work covers the marking of the borough's streets and parking lots: lines, stop lines, arrows, pedestrian crossings and pictograms, according to the standards of the ministère des Transports.
The contract starts in early April 2026 and ends at the end of December 2026.
The expense comes from the operating budget and is paid entirely by the borough.
The original contract came from public call for tenders 24-20329, which had received 3 bids.
Outremont is fully suspending the parking rules tied to road maintenance (street sweeping) on all of its streets on April 2, 3, 8 and 9, 2026, for Passover.
The same suspension applies on September 21 and 22, 2026, for Yom Kippur.
On December 27, 28, 29 and 30, 2026, the two-hour parking limit does not apply on the borough's residential streets, from 7 p.m. to 8 a.m. the next day.
The ban on parking along parks and mini-parks stays in effect despite these suspensions.
The borough says it wants to ensure residents' peace and quiet during the holiday season.
The borough will announce these suspensions on its communication platforms; adoption is planned for March 10, 2026.
The borough of Outremont is updating its by-law on traffic and parking (1171).
The change affects Schedule "H" of the by-law, so that the parking rules match the signs already installed on the streets.
This revision incorporates the parking decisions adopted by the borough during 2025.
Planned timeline: notice of motion and first draft by-law on March 10, 2026, adoption on April 9, 2026.
There is no spending associated with this file; the borough will share the information with residents through its communication platforms.
The borough of Outremont is temporarily changing the parking rules on avenue Nelson, from March 16 to December 31, 2026.
On the west side of Nelson, parking will be prohibited from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m., except for holders of a sector no. 1 parking permit.
There will also be a parking ban on Mondays from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m., from April 1 to November 30.
The measure goes along with work in the indoor garage of the building at 55, chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine; the rules on the east side of Nelson will be suspended during this work.
The costs of changing the signs will be taken from the borough's operating budget.
Timeline: notice of motion and first draft on March 10, 2026, adoption of the by-law on April 9, 2026, implementation in April 2026.
The borough will share the information with residents through its communication platforms.
The borough of Outremont will ban right turns from chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine onto avenue McCulloch and côte du Vésinet, from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m., Monday to Friday.
The ban affects drivers coming from the west on Côte-Sainte-Catherine who turn south.
The stated goal: reduce through traffic in the northwest sector of the borough.
The decision summary mentions increased pedestrian safety, reduced car capacity on the road network, and little impact on residents.
The cost of the new signs will be paid out of the borough's operating budget.
Planned timeline: notice of motion and first draft by-law on April 9, 2026, adoption on May 5, 2026.
The measure follows a recommendation from the Comité de circulation, stationnement et sécurisation of February 9, 2026.
Outremont is extending the hours of the drop-off zone on the west side of avenue Claude-Champagne, north of boulevard Mont-Royal.
Parking there will be banned from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday, except for the drop-off zone (15-minute stop).
Stopping will remain banned from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on Fridays, from April 1 to November 30.
The section covered runs from a point 282 metres south of chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine to boulevard Mont-Royal.
The request came from the director of the CPE de l'Université de Montréal: the drop-off zone was being used as parking, leaving little room for parents.
The cost of the new signs is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
Notice of motion and first draft on April 9, 2026, with adoption expected on May 5, 2026.
Outremont is banning vehicles from stopping at all times on the west side of avenue Champagneur, between avenue Ducharme and the lane to the north.
Previously, parking was allowed there from 8 p.m. to 7 a.m.
The borough cites the problems this permission caused for snow removal operations in the neighbouring parking lot.
The Comité de circulation, stationnement et sécurisation recommended the change on February 9, 2026.
The costs of the new signage are paid out of the operating budget.
Notice of motion and first draft on April 9, 2026, with adoption of the by-law planned for May 5, 2026.
The borough says it will inform residents through its communication platforms.
Outremont is creating a parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility on the east side of avenue Nelson, just north of avenue Villeneuve.
The space covers the first 7.2 metres north of avenue Villeneuve and is reserved at all times.
Only people with reduced mobility who hold a resident parking permit for sector no. 1 will be able to use it.
The request came from a resident of avenue Nelson, and the Comité de circulation, stationnement et sécurisation recommended it on February 9, 2026.
The cost of the new signs will be paid by the parking fund (amount not specified).
Notice of motion and first draft by-law on April 9, 2026, with adoption expected on May 5, 2026.
The borough of Outremont is creating a parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility on the north side of avenue Marie-Stéphane, near the underground parking of 1155, avenue Marie-Stéphane.

The space will be reserved at all times for people with reduced mobility who hold a resident parking permit for sector no. 1, on the section between avenue Champagneur and a point located 183 metres to the east.

On the rest of this section (starting 119.6 metres north of avenue Van Horne), parking for more than 2 hours remains prohibited from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m., except for sector no. 1 permit holders, with stopping prohibited on Wednesdays from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. from April 1 to November 30.
The request came from a resident of avenue Marie-Stéphane; the Comité de circulation, stationnement et sécurisation recommended it on February 9, 2026.
The cost of the new signage will be paid out of the parking fund.
Timeline: notice of motion and first draft on April 9, 2026, adoption of the by-law on May 5, 2026.
The borough of Outremont is creating a passenger loading zone reserved for people with reduced mobility on avenue McNider, east side, south of boulevard Saint-Joseph.
The zone starts 44 metres south of boulevard Saint-Joseph and extends 7.2 metres to the south; parking will be banned there, except for this loading zone.

The rest of the stretch between avenue Villeneuve and boulevard Saint-Joseph keeps its existing rules: parking for more than 2 hours banned from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m., except for holders of a resident permit for sector no. 1, and a ban on Wednesdays from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. from April 1 to November 30.
The request comes from the presence of seniors' residences in the area and the need for safe, adapted access.
The cost of changing the signs will be paid out of the parking fund.
Notice of motion and first draft by-law on April 9, 2026, with adoption expected on May 5, 2026; the change will be announced on the borough's communication platforms.
The borough of Outremont is creating a drop-off zone reserved for school buses on the east side of avenue McEachran, between chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine and avenue Bernard.
Parking will be banned there except for school buses, on the section located between 107 metres north of Côte-Sainte-Catherine and avenue Bernard.
On that section, parking will also remain banned on Fridays from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m., from April 1 to November 30.
A 36-metre segment, starting 71 metres north of Côte-Sainte-Catherine, becomes a no-parking zone at all times.
The change responds to a request from the Centre de services scolaire Marguerite-Bourgeoys for the école Le SAS d'Outremont (500, boulevard Dollard), for picking up and dropping off students.
The cost of the new signs will be paid out of the parking fund.
Notice of motion and first draft on April 9, 2026; adoption of the by-law planned for May 5, 2026.
Outremont is changing the parking rules on chemin Bates, between avenue Rockland and the borough's western boundary (north and south sides).
Parking for more than 2 hours will be banned from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday to Friday, instead of 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day.
Holders of a resident parking permit for sector no. 1 remain exempt.
Parking is still banned from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m., from April 1 to November 30: Fridays on the north side, Tuesdays on the south side.
A survey sent to residents of chemin Bates and allée Glendale on February 20, 2026 found 95% support for the change.
The cost of the new signs will be paid out of the parking fund.
The by-law is expected to be adopted on May 5, 2026, with the change coming into effect in May–June 2026.
Outremont is changing its traffic and parking by-law for the east side of avenue Dollard, between avenue Ducharme and avenue Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux.

Two zones will be reserved for school buses: along 33.5 metres north of avenue Ducharme (parking banned for other vehicles from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday) and along 38 metres south of Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux (from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., from August 15 to June 28).
A drop-off zone is being created further north: stops of no more than 15 minutes between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. and between 3 p.m. and 6 p.m., Monday to Friday, from August 15 to June 28.
Stopping will be banned at all times on two short 3-metre stretches, near the lanes north of Van Horne and south of Ducharme.
The borough says it is acting because of the reconstruction of parc Irma-Levasseur and the future school on avenue Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux.
Planned timeline: notice of motion and first draft on April 9, 2026, adoption of the by-law on May 5, 2026.
The borough of Outremont is renewing its "Rues actives et familiales" (active and family-friendly streets): on the sections involved, only local traffic is allowed and through traffic is banned.

Streets affected: avenue Champagneur (between Lajoie and Saint-Viateur), avenue Dollard (between Ducharme and Van Horne), avenue Marsolais, boulevard Mont-Royal (three sections between Fernhill and chemin de la Forêt), avenue Pagnuelo (between Mont-Royal and Côte-Sainte-Catherine) and avenue Hartland (between Lajoie and Van Horne).

The setups consist of concrete planters with "Circulation locale seulement" (local traffic only) and "Rue active et familiale" (active and family-friendly street) signs, plus "Attention à nos enfants" (watch out for our children) trestles.
The installations are temporary and will all be removed at the end of October 2026.
The cost of changing the signs is covered by the borough's operating budget; no amount is specified.
The document states that these installations are meant to improve the feeling of safety in residential areas near parks and schools.
This is a renewal: similar orders have been adopted every year since 2022.
The borough of Outremont wants to create a delivery zone on the north side of avenue Bernard, between Querbes and a point 22 metres further east.
Parking there would be prohibited except for deliveries, from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m., Monday to Friday.
Two paid parking spaces (TA-292 and TA-293) are affected by the change.
The request comes from the person in charge of the Renaissance store, but the loading zone cannot be reserved exclusively for them.
Stopping remains prohibited from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on Mondays, from April 1 to November 30.
The cost of the new signage will be paid out of the borough's operating budget.
Planned steps: notice of motion and first draft on May 5, 2026, adoption of the by-law on June 2, 2026.
The borough of Outremont wants to ban right turns heading south onto avenue Fernhill for vehicles coming from the west on chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine.
The ban would apply from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m., Monday to Friday.
The request comes from several residents of avenue Fernhill; the Comité de circulation, stationnement et sécurisation recommended it on April 16, 2026.
Reasons given: little negative impact on residents, more safety for pedestrians, less car capacity on the road network.
The cost of the new signs will be paid out of the operating budget.
Planned steps: notice of motion and first draft on May 5, 2026, adoption of the by-law on June 2, 2026.
The organization Bâtir son quartier wants to build a housing facility for people who need help and assistance in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on a vacant lot of about 378 m² (lot 1 295 061).
The building would have 3 storeys with a basement and 16 rooms.
The City is asking the urban agglomeration council to adopt a by-law to authorize the project despite several departures from the neighbourhood's planning by-law.

The departures concern height (3 storeys and about 11 m instead of 2 storeys and 9 m), ground coverage (55% instead of 50%), the construction alignment on a street corner, and greening (30% instead of 35%).
The current zoning allows only 1 to 3 dwellings; the project requires the "maison d'hébergement" (shelter/housing facility) use.
No bicycle parking spaces would be provided, in order to keep more indoor space for residents and support services.

The urban planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme) gave a favourable opinion on December 9, 2025; the by-law must still go through the executive committee, the city council and the urban agglomeration council before it comes into force.
A draft by-law would authorize the construction of a housing building for people who need help and assistance, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on a vacant lot of about 1,151 m² (lot 2 242 423).
The planned building would have 3 storeys and 18 units located on the second and third storeys, with 45% ground coverage and 55% greening.

The by-law would set aside three local planning rules: the building alignment (corner lot), the zoning that only allows commercial use (the project is asking for the "collective housing home" use) and the requirement to have a business on the ground floor.

The Direction de l'aménagement urbain supports the project because it creates housing for people who need help and develops a vacant lot; the comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on December 9, 2025.
The developer has made commitments about fitting the project into the neighbourhood (size, materials, volume).
At this stage, this is a notice of motion and a tabling: adoption of the by-law by the urban agglomeration council will come at a later meeting, followed by a public notice and coming into force.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the demolition of the vacant building at 9501, rue Notre-Dame Est, at the corner of avenue Bilaudeau, and the construction of a residential building in its place.
The new building may be up to 3 storeys and 11.5 metres and contain up to 10 rental units, whereas the current zoning limits it to 2 storeys, 9 metres and 8 units.
The project includes a shared rooftop terrace, an indoor waste room, about 65% ground coverage and 25% greening on a lot of about 210 m².

Before obtaining its demolition certificate, the developer must provide an irrevocable bank guarantee of $51,600, which stays in force until construction is completed; the City may cash it in if the work does not comply with the resolution.
The demolition permit must be applied for within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; the outdoor landscaping must be completed within 12 months after the construction permit expires.
Each permit application will go through an architectural review, including the outdoor spaces and the building alignment.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 6, 2026, while asking that the massing and façades be reviewed, that the outdoor spaces be harmonized, and that the masonry wall on the property line be given a finish.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is granting a minor exemption at 680, rue Du Quesne to allow a dwelling unit to be added in the building's cellar.
The planning by-law normally prohibits a dwelling unit in a cellar: here, more than half the floor-to-ceiling height is below ground level (1.2 m below, 1 m above).
The exemption also allows a sunken front courtyard 1.2 m deep, whereas the limit is 1 m over more than 20% of the area.
The space is already used as living rooms; the applicant wants to bring the dwelling unit up to standard.

The Direction de l'aménagement urbain finds that the exemption does not harm the neighbours or the built environment, and that the dwelling unit complies with the by-law on the construction of buildings.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on February 6, 2026; a public notice will precede adoption by the borough council.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is granting an exemption to the company Lallemand so it can expand its building at 1620, rue Préfontaine.
The expansion is to house a new mechanical room for the plant, modernized and brought up to standards.
The by-law requires 40 trees and 25% greening on this lot: the exemption allows 25 trees and 5% greening.
The company plans to compensate on the other lots of its industrial "campus," for a total of 131 trees and 25% greening.
Since 2023, Lallemand has been working on a drainage master plan, approved by the Service de l'eau, combined with a greening plan.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on February 6, 2026; a public notice must be issued before the borough council adopts it.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is authorizing the expansion of the parking lot at the industrial building at 5800, rue Ontario Est.
The number of spaces is going from 33 (the maximum allowed in the Assomption-Sud – Longue-Pointe area) to 103: 59 outdoors and 44 indoors.
The Agence de mobilité durable de Montréal will set up its operations centre in the building and is asking for 72 spaces for its fleet of service vehicles.
Greening of the site will be 22.05% instead of the required 25%; the developer will have to submit a plan for additional greening measures as compensation.
The project also departs from the rules on wetlands and on tree planting; a landscaping plan will have to be approved before the conversion permit is issued.
The permit application must be submitted within 60 months, and the outdoor work completed within 12 months after the permit expires.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on March 6, 2026, with the condition regarding greening.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the demolition of two one-storey industrial buildings at 2115, rue Théodore and 2150, rue Saint-Clément, near the Viau metro station and the linear park on the former Longue-Pointe rail spur.

In their place, two 4-storey residential buildings will be built on two separate lots: 36 units on the Saint-Clément side and 55 units on the Théodore side, with a maximum height of 16.5 metres instead of the 11 metres allowed.

The developer will have to provide bank guarantees of $134,000 (lot A) and $121,500 (lot B) before obtaining its demolition certificate; the City may cash them in if the work does not comply with the resolution.

The project includes a pedestrian and bike link between the lane and the linear park, a right-of-way easement, and a new lane leading to rue Saint-Clément; the developer is paying to bring the infrastructure up to standard.
The developer and the City's Service de la stratégie immobilière are negotiating land exchanges, including parts of lanes.
On lot A, only 8 trees will be planted instead of the 11 required, because space is limited and trees already exist nearby.

Permit applications must be filed within 60 months, otherwise the authorization lapses; breaking the conditions carries a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
Next steps: a public consultation meeting, then final adoption by the borough council.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is approving exemptions for the Canoë project, at 4500, rue Hochelaga.

Phase 3 will no longer have to include 360 m² of commercial space on the ground floor: the requirement drops to 0 m². Instead, common areas, including a games room open to all residents of the project, will face the allée des artisans.
The common room in phase 3 will have to be extended by at least 4 metres into the neighbouring ground-floor unit.

Two access lanes facing avenue Bennett will be allowed to exceed the maximum width of 10 metres: 37 metres in phase 1 (manoeuvres by 50-foot trucks toward the grocery store's loading area) and 21 metres in phase 2 (Hydro-Québec annex vault).
The design of these access lanes will have to pass an architectural review before the transformation permit is issued.

Permit applications must be filed within 60 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses. Breaking the conditions carries a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.

The change is meant to make way for a phase 3 of some 220 affordable rental units, funded by a CMHC program that requires affordability for at least 20 years. A public consultation meeting is planned before final adoption.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing a temporary parking lot on a vacant lot at the corner of rue Sainte-Catherine Est and rue Jeanne d'Arc, for 18 months after the resolution is adopted.

The land belongs to Lantic; the parking lot, with 50 to 60 spaces, is for the workers of the contractor Pomerleau, which is renovating the plant at 4026, rue Notre-Dame Est until roughly the spring of 2027.
According to the borough, the plant's parking lot is already full and, without a dedicated space, the workers' vehicles would take up the streets in the area.
An inspection found that the land had been covered with gravel and used as a parking lot without a permit; the decision brings the situation into compliance.
The owner will have to submit a landscaping plan before the deadline, then turn the land into a green space within the following 18 months, in keeping with environmental laws.
If the terms are not met, the penalty provisions of the by-law on specific projects apply.
The project is not subject to approval by referendum; a public consultation will be held before final adoption.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the demolition of the vacant commercial building at 8805, rue Sherbrooke Est, at the corner of rue Joffre.
In its place, a mixed-use building of 3 to 5 storeys (maximum 19 m) with 31 housing units, including at least 55 m² of commercial space on the ground floor.
The project does not comply with the zoning, which limits the area to 3 storeys and 11 m, or with the building alignment rules.
Before obtaining its demolition certificate, the developer will have to provide a bank guarantee of $27,634, which the City can cash in if the work does not comply with the resolution.

The demolition permit must be applied for within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; the outdoor landscaping must be completed within 12 months after the end of the construction permit.
The applicant is in the process of buying the neighbouring lane, to the north, from the City.
This is the first draft resolution: a public consultation will follow, and residents will be able to request a referendum.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is exempting a building planned on lot 1 295 061 from installing an acoustic screen in front of a piece of mechanical equipment on its roof.
Normally, the planning by-law requires this screen when the equipment is less than 20 m from a zone set aside for housing.
An acoustic study concludes that the noise limits in the Règlement sur le bruit will be respected even without a screen.
Condition imposed: an acoustic test will have to be done once the building is built, to check the noise level of the equipment.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion by majority on May 1, 2026, with this same condition.
A public notice announcing the application will come before the borough council adopts the resolution.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is supporting three school projects from the Centre de services scolaires de Montréal so they can receive a grant from the ministère de l'Éducation (PAFIRSPA program).

The projects: renovating the gymnasium at école Coeur-Immaculé-de-Marie, renovating the gymnasium at école De la Petite-Bourgogne, and adding an outdoor sports field at école Notre-Dame-du-Perpétuel-Secours.
The borough commits to signing a sharing agreement with these schools so that the public can use the sports facilities.
The ministère's grant depends on this support resolution from the borough council.
According to the document, there is no financial impact for the Ville de Montréal.
The Verdun borough is buying five tickets for the dinner of the 40th Grand Prix du Conseil des arts de Montréal, at a cost of $170 each.
The total expense is $850, tax-exempt, paid out of the 2026 operating budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The event takes place on Thursday, April 2, 2026, at noon, at the Palais des congrès de Montréal.
The tickets will be used to invite members of the borough council and public servants from that department.
The document states that the goal is networking in Montréal's cultural community and visibility for the borough in cultural programming.
Verdun had already taken part in this event: $840 for 6 tickets in 2022, $750 for 6 tickets in 2019, $500 for 5 tickets in 2014.
The borough of Verdun is renting out the chalet at parc du Quai-de-La Tortue, at 6000, boulevard LaSalle, to the organization Harmonie Richelieu Verdun.
The lease runs for 12 months, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027.
The organization uses the space to continue its music activities offered to the people of Verdun.
Harmonie Richelieu Verdun lost access to its premises in 2024 and is still looking for a new location; the premises at the pôle communautaire are not yet available.
The monthly rent goes from $2,130.98 in 2026 to $2,173.60 in 2027, with an indexation of 2% per year.
The borough will collect $25,912.72 before taxes for the 12 months of the lease.
The rent matches the building's energy and maintenance costs, calculated in proportion to the occupancy (10 months of activities, 12 months of storage).
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $15,000.65 to the Société écocitoyenne de Montréal to continue the Trottibus, a service where volunteers and parents walk elementary school students to school.
The agreement ends on December 31, 2026 and the money comes from the Fonds de soutien financier en développement social; it covers 100% of the project's costs, over 9 months.
The money is used to keep a project manager on staff who brings together schools, parents and organizations in Centre-Sud.
In 2026, the organization is working on a second route at école Saint-Anselme, a new Trottibus at école Marguerite-Bourgeoys and making école Champlain self-sufficient.
A first Trottibus already exists in the Sainte-Marie district, for students at école Saint-Anselme.
The borough had granted $35,635 to the same organization in February 2024 for the years 2024 and 2025.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $24,000 to the organization Aide aux Trans du Québec (ATQ), a one-time amount taken from the Fonds de soutien financier en développement social.
The agreement ends on May 31, 2026 and covers a 3-month project.

The money will go toward community gatherings: conferences and panels led by trans and non-binary people, spaces for discussion and networking, and a Salon Fierté Trans bringing together mainly organizations that provide services to these people.
The project aims to break isolation, create social connections and provide access to information and resources, as well as to raise awareness among the general public.
The organization must use the money only for this project, never to fund its general mission, and must cover any cost overruns.
The borough will follow up on the project, which must comply with the action plan and timeline submitted by the organization, as well as the visibility rules set out in the agreement.
The borough of Ville-Marie is extending by one month, until April 30, 2026, the contracts of three organizations that do community mediation in public spaces.
The additional cost is $131,992, including taxes where applicable, which brings the total value of the contracts from $1,239,469.66 to $1,371,461.66.
The amounts added: $54,853 to the Société de développement social, $39,570 to the Groupe communautaire l'Itinéraire and $37,569 to L'Anonyme U.I.M.

The Équipe de médiation communautaire has 13 workers: L'Anonyme covers the area bounded by Saint-Hubert/Papineau/Sherbrooke/René-Lévesque, the Société de développement social covers the Quartier des spectacles, the Quartier chinois and place Émilie-Gamelin, and l'Itinéraire covers square Cabot and the area around métro Lucien-L'Allier.
The borough explains that this extension is meant to maintain the service while it finishes planning the project and its funding for 2026.
The project, launched in May 2025 as a pilot project, had already been extended until March 31, 2026 in December 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing 4 public events to be held on its territory in May 2026.

These events may temporarily occupy public property and be exempt from several local by-laws: noise, music, food sales, alcohol consumption, solicitation, games of chance, traffic and parking, and street food.
Events held on public property are free and open to everyone.
The borough is providing $15,000 worth of free services for all 4 events; logistical support costs are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
If an exceptional street closure is needed, organizers must put up signs 10 days in advance and inform residents of the affected streets.
The permits will be issued by the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing five public events on its territory for May and June 2026.

Organizers will be allowed to temporarily occupy public property and to depart from several by-laws: noise, music, food sales, alcohol consumption, solicitation, games of chance, traffic and parking, street food, and parks and public places.
The borough is granting a fee waiver of $2,635 for all five events; logistical support is paid out of the operating budgets of the departments involved.
Events held on public property are free and open to everyone.
If a street must be closed in exceptional circumstances, organizers must put up notices 10 days in advance and inform residents of the streets affected.
Permits will be issued by the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing seven public events to be held on its territory in July 2026.

The organizers will be allowed to temporarily occupy public property and to depart from several local by-laws: noise, music, food sales, alcohol consumption, games of chance, solicitation, traffic and parking, street food, and anchoring temporary installations to the ground.
The events held on public property are free and open to everyone.
The borough is providing free services totalling $15,700 for the seven events; the logistical support is paid out of the operating budgets of the departments involved.
If a street has to be closed exceptionally, the organizers will have to put up signs 10 days before the event and inform residents of the affected streets.
The permits will be issued by the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing three public events on its territory in August 2026.

Organizers will be allowed to temporarily occupy public property and to depart from several local by-laws: occupation of public property, noise, music, food sales, alcohol consumption, games of chance, solicitation, traffic and parking, parks, street food, and anchoring installations to the ground.
All three events are free and open to everyone; the borough is granting a fee waiver of $0 for the costs related to the three events.
The City's logistical support is paid out of the operating budgets of the departments involved.
If a street has to be closed exceptionally, organizers must put up notices 10 days in advance and inform residents of the affected streets.
The permits will be issued by the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The LaSalle borough council is retroactively approving two public events that took place in the borough in June 2026.
Both requests came in too late to be dealt with at the June 1, 2026 meeting.
The borough is authorizing the temporary occupation of public property and exemptions from the by-laws on noise, music, food sales, alcohol consumption, parks, traffic and parking, and street food.
The borough is waiving fees totalling $338 for the two events; logistical support is paid out of the departments' existing budgets.
The events on public property are free and open to everyone; the organizers handle the promotion themselves.
If a street has to be closed on an exceptional basis, the organizers must post the closing hours 10 days in advance and notify residents of the streets affected.
The LaSalle borough authorizes four public events to be held on its territory in September 2026.

The events may temporarily occupy public property and depart from several local by-laws: noise, music, food sales, alcohol consumption, solicitation, games of chance, traffic and parking, street food, and park use.
The borough is granting $5,500 in free services for all four events.
The costs of the City's logistical support are absorbed by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
Events held on public property are free and open to everyone.
If a street must exceptionally be closed, organizers must put up signs 10 days in advance and notify residents of the affected streets.
The permits will be issued by the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is authorizing the construction of a residential building at 14070, rue Sherbrooke Est, at the corner of 50e Avenue.
The project may have up to 260 units and 8 storeys (maximum 36 metres), with exemptions from the zoning rules on use, height, land occupancy and the minimum number of parking spaces.
Parking must be located inside the building (except for visitors and deliveries), with wiring ready for charging stations at every space, at least one car-sharing space and up to 200 bicycle racks.
The developer must provide a space of at least 100 m² on the ground floor for community, sociocultural or recreational activities, and a rooftop terrace for residents.
Waste must be stored indoors in air-conditioned or refrigerated rooms, and a waste management plan is required before the permit application.
The developer is paying for the infrastructure to extend 50e Avenue in front of the property and is providing a bank guarantee of $100,000.
Work must begin within 30 months after the by-law comes into force and be completed within 36 months after the permit is issued, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The council also takes note of the minutes of the public consultation held on March 25, 2026.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving two minor exemptions for 8375, boulevard Gouin Est, a residential property along the rivière des Prairies.
The owner will be allowed to build an accessory building of 80.3 m² instead of the maximum 29.6 m² permitted, and 4.3 m high instead of 4 m.
This building will be used to store a recreational vehicle; two existing sheds will be removed.
Once the project is completed, the buildings will cover 12.9% of the 1,710.3 m² lot, below the 35% limit set for the zone.
The owner is committing to restoring the natural state of the shoreline on the property, which is currently taken up by a concrete ramp.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on April 10, 2026, finding that the exemptions cause no harm to the neighbourhood.
At the meeting, no one indicated an intention to speak about the application.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving the plans for an accessory building at 8375, boulevard Gouin Est, a single-family residential property along the rivière des Prairies.
The project replaces two existing accessory buildings with a new one-storey building of 80.3 m², located in the backyard about 70 metres from the street, behind a garage that is already there.
The building will be clad in white engineered wood, with a garage door, a pedestrian door and four grey windows.

The owner is committing to restoring the natural state of the shoreline, which is currently covered in concrete, to removing the gravel in the yard and replacing it with lawn, and to planting four trees in the backyard.
This work will have to be completed within 18 months after the permits are issued.

Before getting the permits, the owner must provide an irrevocable bank guarantee of $3,500; if the work is not completed, the borough can cash it in, require that the work be done, or have it done at the owner's expense.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on April 10, 2026, finding that the criteria for siting, appearance and landscaping were met.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving the plans for a new building at 15730, rue Sherbrooke Est, near rue de la Famille-Dubreuil.
This is the second building of the Milebrook 2 project: 3 to 7 storeys and 172 housing units.
The underground parking will have 122 spaces (23 more will come later) and 2 bicycle spaces per unit.
The roof will be planted with vegetation over 20% of its area, and 161 trees will be planted in this phase.
The wetlands and land areas in the back yard will be protected during the work, with control of invasive exotic species.
The facades will combine brick and lightweight cladding; equivalent or better materials may be substituted with the approval of the Direction du développement du territoire.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme was in favour of it at its meeting of May 1, 2026.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is paying up to $16,915.85 (taxes included where applicable) to the Société environnementale de Côte-des-Neiges (SOCENV) to cover the rent for the Éco-quartier space at 6575, avenue Somerled.
The contribution covers January 1 to December 31, 2026.

The borough is also lending the organization space 591 (1,161.17 sq. ft.) free of charge at the Centre communautaire « Le 6767 », 6767, chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, for the same period, with the possibility of an extension until December 31, 2027.
SOCENV runs the two Éco-quartier service points in the area; the borough now covers the rental costs for both locations.
The money comes from the operating budget for residual materials management.
Last year, the contribution for the same space was $16,089.58 (2025), and it was $26,421.38 for both spaces in 2024.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is paying up to $18,954.58 to the Société environnementale de Côte-des-Neiges (SOCENV) to manage its subsidy program.
The program reimburses part of the cost of buying, renting or making cloth diapers and reusable menstrual hygiene products for borough residents.
The program is renewed from January 1 to December 31, 2026. It has existed since 2018.
Of the total amount, $17,000 goes to subsidies for residents and up to $1,700 (plus taxes) to the organization's administrative costs.
Payment is made in two stages: $10,000 within 30 days of the signing of the agreement, and the rest upon submission of the final report, no later than January 7, 2027.
In 2025, the program funded 186 applications for a total of $14,949.01. Since 2018, 166 families have received help for cloth diapers and 890 people for menstrual hygiene products.
A communications campaign will be carried out with residents and organizations that work with families.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $50,000 to the organization Éco-Pivot for the Corridor écologique Darlington project, from March 11 to November 15, 2026.

The money comes from the 2026 operating budget set aside for the ecological transition; it will be paid in two instalments ($40,000 after the agreement is signed and a second instalment upon receipt of the progress report on July 31, 2026).
The corridor runs 2.5 km along avenue de Darlington, between mont Royal and the railway near Université de Montréal's MIL campus.

Planned for 2026: three "samedis vivants" (living Saturdays) at Place Darlington, plantings with schools (Bedford, Notre-Dame-des-Neiges, Saint-Pascal-Baylon), tree planting at CHU Sainte-Justine and a hedge at the IRGLM, and a bioblitz at parc Marie-Gérin-Lajoie.
Upkeep of existing installations: food forests at Place Darlington and parc Martin-Luther-King, a micro-forest at parc Mahatma-Gandhi, nectar gardens and giant planters adopted by residents.
A partnership with MultiCaf on food insecurity and collaboration with programs at Université de Montréal and HEC Montréal.
The borough has been funding this project since 2018: $27,000 a year from 2018 to 2021, $35,000 in 2022, then $50,000 a year since 2023.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is giving $5,000, taxes included, to Vélo Québec for the Toutes à vélo program in the summer of 2026.
The program offers free bike-riding lessons reserved for women, in a women-only setting.
Two groups of 15 to 20 women, one in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and one in Côte-des-Neiges, will take part in seven learning activities.
Bikes and helmets are loaned by Vélorution, and a drop-in childcare service is offered to participants.
The expense is paid out of the 2026 operating budget of the Division des études techniques et de la mobilité.
The borough had granted $9,500 in 2025 (Toutes à vélo and Cyclistes avertis), $5,000 in 2024 and $4,600 in 2023.
According to the file, the most recent editions were all full and the program barely meets the demand.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is paying $68,233 (taxes included) to the organization Cyclo Nord-Sud for the 2026 season of the Vélorution CDN-NDG project.
The program gives bikes to children and teenagers (Petites roues), sells them at low prices, and lends them to participants in the Toutes à vélo classes.
Affordable bike maintenance services are offered at two service points, in parc Confédération and parc Martin-Luther-King, and at Multicaf markets.
Bike mechanics training is given to youth groups, including a "Construis ton vélo en une journée" workshop.
The money comes from the borough's unallocated surplus.
This is the project's eighth year; it has been funded every year since 2019 ($65,000 in 2025, $65,000 in 2024, $99,196.37 in 2023).
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is paying $8,400, taxes included, to the Regroupement des éco-quartiers for the Patrouille verte in the summer of 2026.
The money is used to hire four student patrollers for 9 weeks, at 32 hours per week, within the borough's territory.
The patrollers raise awareness among residents about waste management, eco-friendly civic behaviour, greening, drinking water conservation and the urban forest.
Their time is divided as follows: 45% on local issues including food waste, 45% on shared assignments with the City's departments, and 10% on training and team meetings.
The contribution depends on obtaining grants from the federal Canada Summer Jobs program.
Last year, the borough paid $18,000 to the same organization for four students during the summer of 2025.
The expense is covered by the 2026 operating budget of the borough's management office.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is adding $18,228.85 to the funding for the "Brigade neige," bringing the total from $27,000 to $45,228.85.
Carrefour jeunesse-emploi Côte-des-Neiges is receiving $10,590 more (for a total of $20,590) and the Notre-Dame-de-Grâce one is receiving $7,638.85 more (for a total of $24,638.85).
The Brigade neige clears snow free of charge from the entrances, stairs, ramps and balconies of people with reduced mobility and seniors in the borough, from December 9, 2025 to April 30, 2026.
The work is done by young people aged 16 to 35 in precarious situations, who receive financial compensation.
The planned funds had already run out in February after more than 210 cm of snow; the borough had asked the organizations to continue, promising additional funding.
This winter, 7 young people served 19 addresses in Côte-des-Neiges and 13 young people served 64 addresses in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The expense is paid out of the borough's 2026 operating budget.

The Ville-Marie borough is allowing a training room reserved for residents to be set up on the ground floor of 325-327, boulevard René-Lévesque Est, in an 86.8 m² space that was normally supposed to house a business or a community facility.

The building "Le Balt", with 15 storeys and 131 units, is located in the Saint-Jacques neighbourhood, between rue Sanguinet and rue Saint-Denis, across from the CHUM, and is in the final phases of construction.
The authorization comes with one condition: no more than 50% of the window area on the ground-floor façade facing René-Lévesque may be blocked.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on January 22, 2026, asking that visibility toward the inside and the outside be maintained while protecting users' privacy.
According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, the small size of the space makes commercial use difficult, and other more visible commercial spaces are available in the area.
There is no financial aspect associated with this file.
The Ville-Marie borough is authorizing the owner of 1430, rue Alexandre-DeSève (quartier Saint-Jacques) to convert their non-habitable basement into living space.
The basement will expand the ground-floor unit and will include 3 bedrooms, a play area, a bathroom and a new staircase.
The work includes repairing the foundations with a membrane, a French drain and a sump pump, as well as new openings on the side and rear facades.
The planning by-law normally prohibits this type of conversion; the City is allowing it here through the conditional uses procedure.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain considers that the project reduces flood risks and adds greenery to almost all of the rear and side yard.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on January 22, 2026.
The work visible from the street, including the new openings, will be reviewed again at a later meeting of the committee.
The Ville-Marie borough is authorizing the "reception hall" use throughout the entire Club-Universitaire-de-Montréal building, at 2045-2047, rue Mansfield, in the Mille carré doré.
The authorization covers all five floors: the by-law normally allows this use only on the ground floor, and it is impossible to physically separate the upper floors from the rest of the building.
The 5-storey building, built in 1912-1913, is a heritage building classified as protected both inside and out; it was restored in 2022-2023 and sold in 2018 after the club closed.
No exterior or interior work is required for this authorization.
The Division d'urbanisme considers the use compatible with the commercial area, with no housing immediately next door, and sees it as a return to the historic use of the premises.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 16, 2026; the borough council makes its decision on May 5, 2026 at 6:30 p.m.
The borough of Ville-Marie is approving a minor exemption for the office building at 690-700, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, at the corner of Robert-Bourassa.
The owner will be allowed to install 7 signs on the second horizontal band of the building's façades: 4 on the Robert-Bourassa side, 2 on the René-Lévesque Ouest side and 1 on the rue Belmont side.
The planning by-law normally requires signs to be placed on the first band, just above the ground floor.
Condition imposed: if signs are installed on the second band, no sign may be installed on the first band.
Because of the slope of the land, the signs will sit between 8.2 m and 12.9 m above the street, but all at the same level on the building.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain points to the curtain-wall façades, which make signage on the first band difficult, and to the desire to avoid a build-up of signs at ground-floor level.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 11, 2026, with the same condition.

The Verdun borough is taking another step toward authorizing the construction of a 3-storey, 6-unit building on a vacant lot at 434, rue Hickson (lots 1 153 719 and 1 153 720, to be merged into a single lot of no more than 285 m²).

The project does not comply with the zoning rules currently in force (lot area and depth, setbacks, density): maximum height of 11 m, front setback of 0 m, rear setback of 4 m, floor area ratio of 2.4.
Each unit must be at least 70 m²; at least two of the ground-floor units must be adapted for universal accessibility.
No car parking is allowed on the site; the project must provide 6 indoor bicycle spaces, 10 outdoor spaces and a bicycle maintenance room.
Greening requirements: at least 3 trees planted, drainage swales of 20 m² holding about 5.8 m³ of water, and 5 m² of planting boxes on the roof.
The developer must post a $50,000 bank guarantee before obtaining its permit, and work must begin within 30 months.

Following the public consultation of February 24, 2026, three criteria are added: limiting the impact of lighting on neighbours, maintaining a pedestrian passage from the neighbouring property, and submitting a waste management plan.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is authorizing the installation of "Arrêt" (stop) signs on all three approaches to the new T-intersection formed by rue Forsyth and boulevard Gouin.
The intersection was created by the recent branching of boulevard Gouin toward rue Forsyth; there is currently no control over who has the right of way there.

The borough says it is responding to several requests from residents and wants to make crossing rue Forsyth safer, since many pedestrians use this crossing between the sentier Yvette-Brind'Amour and the STM terminus, north of rue Sherbrooke.
"Nouvelle signalisation - Arrêt en vigueur" (new signage - stop now in effect) signs will be put up one month before the "Arrêt" signs.
The signage is to be installed during the summer of 2026.
No cost to the borough: supply and installation are covered by the weekly work agreement with the Division du marquage et de la signalisation.
Any other parking rules already in place remain in effect.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is offering city council to take charge itself of the design, coordination and carrying out of minor sidewalk repair work on streets of the City's arterial road network located within its territory.
The work targets sidewalk sections considered to be in very poor condition, for the safety of users, and must be done before the roadway repairs planned for the same stretches in 2026 and 2027.
The work site is planned from July to September 2026, with the contract to be awarded in June 2026.
The costs will be paid by the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier, as part of the Programme de maintien des infrastructures routières 2026 (minor sidewalk repair component).
The borough must submit its plans and specifications to the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier for approval before starting the work.
The next step is the acceptance of this offer by city council; without acceptance, the sidewalk work in question would not be carried out.
The borough's Service des communications will prepare a communications campaign.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is hiring Montréal Scellant inc. to carry out minor repairs to sidewalks, curbs and driveway entrances on various streets in its territory.
The contract is worth $657,920.75, taxes included; the total authorized spending comes to $798,384.28, including $113,465.02 in contingencies and $26,998.50 in incidental expenses.
The work is to start in May 2026 and be completed in October 2026.
The work also responds to requests from neighbouring property owners who have paid to obtain or modify a driveway entrance.
Montréal Scellant inc. submitted the lowest of the 7 bids received, 13.52% below the internal estimate of $760,749.33.
The borough is paying the full amount: $540,664.42 from its ten-year capital works program and $188,366.84 from its operating budget.
Notices will be sent to affected residents before the work begins, and the company's performance will be evaluated.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Eurovia Québec Construction inc. a $5,975,689.75 contract (taxes included) for road work in 2026.
The total authorized spending comes to $6,708,763.18, including taxes, contingencies ($525,049.76) and incidental costs ($208,023.67).
The work covers 12 street sections, or about 3.5 km: repairing and resurfacing roadways, rebuilding sidewalks and curbs, fixing reversed sewer connections and replacing lead service lines.
48e Avenue and 50e Avenue, between rue De Montigny and rue Victoria (about 623 metres), will be completely rebuilt, with wider sidewalks.
Eight of the twelve companies that obtained the tender documents submitted a bid; the lowest bid is 31.19% below the internal estimate of $8,683,851.23.
The funding comes from the borough ($5,672,626.16, through a loan by-law) and from the Direction de la gestion des actifs for the lead service line portion.
The City will evaluate the company's performance under this contract.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is lifting the permanent parking ban on the south side of rue Sherbrooke Est, between 81e Avenue and 91e Avenue.
Parking will still be banned at all times along 89 metres east of 81e Avenue and along 12 metres east of rue de la Famille-Dubreuil, to keep intersections visible.
Stopping will be banned at all times along 198 metres west of 91e Avenue, near the entrance to fire station 32.
On the two stretches now open to parking (260 m and 316 m), parking will be banned Monday to Friday, from 12:30 p.m. to 1:30 p.m., for maintenance and snow removal.
The change responds to a request from residents linked to the increase in demand for parking since the Le MileBrook housing project was built.
The Division de l'ingénierie had said it was opposed to completely removing the ban, citing safety, road capacity and lighting it considered inadequate.
The signs will be installed once the decision is adopted; the borough will have no costs to pay.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is lending the kiosk in parc du Fort-de-Pointe-aux-Trembles to the organization Marché public de Pointe-aux-Trembles to run La Buvette du Quai from May 23 to September 27, 2026.
La Buvette will serve food and drinks on Thursday and Friday from 2 p.m. to 9 p.m., Saturday from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., and Sunday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Special orders allow, on the scheduled dates and times, music played outdoors in the park, the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages, the sale of food and promotional items, and the installation of banners and pennants.
The document provides for no spending: the financial section states "N/A". La Buvette's profits are reinvested in the mission of the Marché public.
In 2025, La Buvette was open 62 days, made 6,018 transactions (averaging $11.39) with 7 local suppliers, and held 33 cultural events.
The organization La Pépinière, which had led the project since 2021, did not renew its funding; the Marché public is taking over the food service.
The organization will handle its own communications and will have to mention the borough's support.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Montréal Scellant inc. a $129,734.34 contract (taxes included) to build asphalt speed bumps on several streets.
The total authorized spending comes to $164,194.49, which is the contract plus $19,460.15 in contingencies and $15,000 in laboratory fees.
About 29 speed bumps will be built on residential streets where the borough has found problems with excessive speeding; the list was approved by the mobility committee on March 19, 2026.
The work is set to start in June 2026 and finish in July 2026.
Seven companies submitted bids for public call for tenders ING26-07; six were found compliant and Montréal Scellant submitted the lowest price, 16.85% below the internal estimate of $156,021.08.
Residents of the affected areas will be informed by notice before the work begins.
The City will carry out a performance evaluation of the company at the end of the contract.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is hiring Cojalac inc. to repair sections of sidewalks and curbs on boulevard Armand-Bombardier, between avenue Blaise-Pascal and boulevard Perras.
The contract is worth $281,878.46 including taxes; the authorized spending comes to $337,126.64 once $42,281.77 in contingencies and $12,966.41 in related costs are added.
The work will repair deteriorated sidewalks and curbs and responds to requests from neighbouring property owners who paid to obtain or modify driveway entrances.
The work is to start in June 2026 and finish in August 2026; notices will be sent to affected residents before it begins.
The bill is paid 100% by the central city, through a loan by-law for maintaining road infrastructure.
Seven companies submitted bids out of eight that picked up the tender documents; the winning bid is $30,215.43 (9.68%) below the internal estimate and $721.54 below the second-lowest bid.
The City will evaluate Cojalac inc.'s performance under this contract.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Les Entreprises Michaudville inc. a $3,285,000 contract (taxes included) to rebuild the sewer and water mains and the roadway on avenue Louis-Lumière, between avenue Wilfrid-Ouellette and 54e Avenue.
The total authorized spending comes to $3,893,226.01, including $494,420.01 in contingencies and $113,805.99 in incidental costs.

The area suffers from repeated flooding, especially for homes located in a basin; the work includes an enlarged combined sewer, replacement of the drinking water main, rebuilding of the roadway and sidewalks, and vegetated draining curb extensions.
The work must be completed in 90 days, under a unit-price contract.
Of the 8 bids received, the one from Duroking Construction / 9200-2088 Québec inc. was rejected because the company is on the City's list of firms with unsatisfactory performance.
The winning price is $873,382.45 lower (-21%) than the latest estimate; the City will assess the contractor's performance.
The borough is taking charge of this water and sewer work on behalf of city council, as it had offered to do in December 2025.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Environnement routier NRJ inc. a $462,842.79 contract (taxes included) for signage work in school zones along boulevard Perras and boulevard du Tricentenaire.
The total authorized spending comes to $525,241.78, including $32,398.99 in contingencies and $30,000 in incidental costs.
The work includes installing variable speed limit signs, double flashing lights and streetlight bases, rebuilding sidewalks, and building two drainage curb extensions.
Work is set to start in July 2026 and finish in August 2026, before the school year begins; notices will be sent to affected residents.
The project is eligible for a grant of up to $361,157 from the Fonds de la sécurité routière of the ministère des Transports.

Only one bid was received out of seven companies that obtained the tender documents; after negotiation, the company lowered its price by 2%, but it remains 14.49% above the internal estimate of $404,269.35.
The City will assess the company's performance under this contract.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Les Pavages Ultra inc. asphalt patching work (both machine-laid and by hand) on various streets, at a price of $174,433.11 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $196,237.25, including $17,443.31 in contingencies and $4,360.83 in incidental costs, funded 100% by the borough out of its surplus ($179,190.77 net).
The work targets badly deteriorated stretches of road with potholes, pending rehabilitation or reconstruction planned for the coming years.
The work is to start in July 2026 and be completed in August 2026.
Notices will be handed out to residents affected by the obstructions during the work.
Four bids were received out of eight parties that took out the tender documents; the winning bid is $1,943.66 (-1.1%) below the in-house estimate and $50,566.88 below the second-lowest bid.
The City will evaluate the company's performance under this contract.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles wants to change its on-street parking rules.
New limit of 24 consecutive hours for trucks, buses, minibuses, recreational vehicles, trailers, vehicles used for commercial purposes and vehicles parked for mechanical repairs.
Other vehicles keep the limit of 72 consecutive hours.
In zones where trucking is prohibited, trucks and tool vehicles will no longer be allowed to park at all, except for the time needed for a local delivery (the 24-hour tolerance is being removed).
The borough says it is acting after several complaints about the parking of these vehicles on certain streets.
This is a notice of motion: by-law RCA26-30132 will have to be adopted later, and then a public notice will announce when it comes into force.
No financial impact according to the file.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is authorizing the installation of "Arrêt" (stop) signs on boulevard Perras, at 51e Avenue.
The "T" intersection currently has only one stop sign, on 51e Avenue: the east and west approaches on Perras will be added, which will mean a stop sign on every branch.
The request came from residents; the borough cites the bus stops on either side of 51e Avenue, pedestrian traffic and the difficulty of turning left during rush hour.
The borough's mobility committee approved the measure unanimously on March 19, 2026.
"Nouvelle signalisation - Arrêt en vigueur" (new signage - stop now in effect) signs will be put up one month before the stop signs to warn drivers.
Installation is planned for the summer or fall of 2026; all other existing signage at the intersection will be kept.
No cost to the borough: the Division du marquage et de la signalisation allows for a number of weekly interventions at no charge.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is banning U-turns on 14 sections of streets, in front of 7 elementary schools and one early childhood centre.

The schools concerned: de la Belle-Rive (pavillon de la pointe), Félix-Leclerc, Notre-Dame-de-Fatima, Marc-Aurèle-Fortin, Léonard-De Vinci, Ste-Germain-Cousin and Saint-Marcel, plus the CPE La mère veilleuse.

The streets affected include Bureau, de Versailles, Louis-Dessaulles, René-Masson, André-Ampère, Fernand-Gauthier, Émile-Brunet, René-Chopin, Joliot-Curie, 47e Avenue, Ontario, 16e and 15e Avenue, and De Montigny.
The borough says it has observed many U-turn manoeuvres at these locations, along with road safety issues.
The signs are to be installed during the summer of 2026, at no cost to the borough under the billing agreement with the Division du marquage et de la signalisation.
The borough's mobility committee approved these measures unanimously on June 8, 2026.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Eurovia Québec Construction inc. a $3,220,886.14 contract (taxes included) for street resurfacing, sidewalk repairs and the replacement of lead water service lines.
The total authorized spending comes to $3,725,423.04, including $371,614.38 in contingencies and $132,922.52 in incidental costs.
The work covers five sections spread across the borough, totalling about 1.1 km, and includes the replacement of 93 water service lines made of lead or another non-compliant material.
The private share of the lead service line replacement ($542,683.54 net) will be billed to the property owners concerned, under by-law 20-030.
Eurovia was the lowest of the five bidders in public call for tenders ING26-11; its bid is $74,432.46 above the internal estimate, or 2.37%.
The cost is shared between the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier (47.84%) and the Direction de la gestion des actifs (52.16%); the spending takes place 100% in 2026.
The City will assess the company's performance under this contract.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is authorizing the installation of "Arrêt" (stop) signs on avenue du Fief-Carion, at the exit from rue Claude-Mathias-Fanef.
The request came from a resident of rue Claude-Mathias-Fanef, who wanted to make manoeuvres at the intersection safer.
According to the document, vehicles parked on the west side of avenue du Fief-Carion block the line of sight, forcing drivers to partly obstruct the roadway in order to pull out.
Any other signage already in place at the intersection is being kept.
"Nouvelle signalisation - Arrêt en vigueur" (new signage - stop now in effect) signs will be installed one month before the "Arrêt" signs.
Installation is planned for the summer or fall of 2026, at no cost to the borough under the billing procedure of the Division du marquage et de la signalisation.
The borough's mobility committee approved the measure unanimously on May 7, 2026.
A business located at 15,729 boulevard de Pierrefonds (Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough) is requesting the right to install a 3.7 m high fence.
The borough's zoning by-law normally limits fences to 2 m at this location.
The owner says he wants this higher fence to prevent repeated thefts at his site.
The advisory committee on urban planning unanimously recommended the request on June 3, 2026, finding that it does not harm the neighbours' property rights.
A 15-day public notice precedes the borough council's decision, scheduled for August 3, 2026.
No cost to the City is indicated in the file.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is amending its Politique de reconnaissance des organismes à but non lucratif (policy for recognizing non-profit organizations).
The change adds a sentence to section 3.1: a group can also be recognized if it shows that it operates under a registered non-profit organization.
Stated goal: to include more citizen groups that offer recreational or community activities without being registered themselves.
The amended policy stays in effect until December 31, 2028.
The policy and the recognition application form will be posted on the borough's website as soon as it is adopted.
There is no financial aspect attached to this decision.
The City is amending its contract management by-law to bring it in line with the new Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, which comes into force on April 1, 2026.
New: the City's purchasing processes will have to take into account, where possible, the sustainable development principles set out in Québec law.
The by-law replaces references to the Loi sur les cités et villes with references to the new law.

The section on persons declared ineligible is being adjusted: the City will be able to contract with such a person if that person is the only one able to enter into the contract or subcontract, in the situations provided for.
The by-law applies to agglomeration powers and comes into force on April 1, 2026.
Administrative measures and information documents will round out the framework for responsible purchasing.
The City is amending its contract management by-law (18-038) to bring it into line with the new Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, which comes into force on April 1, 2026.
New feature: the City will have to take sustainable development principles into account in its purchasing, where possible (responsible procurement).
References to the Loi sur les cités et villes are replaced by references to the new act.

The section on contracts with an "ineligible person" is adjusted: the City may enter into such a contract or allow a subcontract if that person is the only one able to carry it out, in the situations provided for.
The amended by-law must be published on April 1, 2026.
The decision falls to city council; the decision summary provides for no financial aspect.
The City is replacing its Politique d'approvisionnement responsable et équitable with an updated version, which would come into effect on April 1, 2026.
The stated goal: bring the policy in line with the new Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, assented to on March 25, 2025.
The policy now speaks of a "responsible supply chain" and revises the responsible purchasing criteria to keep only those the City can track and measure.
It provides that the City may, when the rules allow it, give preference to suppliers meeting responsible purchasing criteria in low-value contracts.

The notions of diversity, equity, inclusion and local purchasing are worded more broadly and will be spelled out in other administrative documents; references to groups of people are removed from the policy.
No financial impact is indicated. Adoption is proposed to the urban agglomeration council of March 26, 2026.
The City is renting a 562-square-foot space (unit 388) at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, to the Association québécoise des relieurs et des artisans du livre.
The lease runs for 24 months starting February 1, 2026; the organization uses the space for introductory workshops, book repair, talks and an office.
The total rent is $16,472.28 before taxes, which means $18,939 in revenue for the City, taxes included.
The City is granting a real estate subsidy of $8,581.74, recommended by Atelier Entremise, which manages the temporary occupancy of the site.
The organization has occupied the space since October 1, 2022 and is moving from 362 to 562 square feet, which explains the rent increase.
The City provides energy, maintenance and repairs; the tenant pays the property taxes and janitorial services.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The City is renting two spaces (451 and 460) totalling 431 square feet at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, to the organization Naos jeunesse : la créativité en action !
The lease runs for 24 months starting February 1, 2026 and brings the City $20,416.44 in rent, before sales taxes ($23,473.80 with taxes included).
The spaces will be used as offices, for community services and for educational workshops for young girls.
The organization has already occupied a space on the site since July 1, 2023; this is a renewal of the occupancy, exempt from the fee on real estate transactions.
The City pays for energy, maintenance and repairs; the tenant covers property taxes and housekeeping.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The rental is part of the transitional occupancy of the Cité-des-Hospitalières, managed by the organization Atelier Entremise, which recommended this tenant.
The City is renting a 77-square-foot space at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières) to Communauté féminine Entre Elles.
The space will be used as an office and will host community activities for newcomer women.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for a total rent of $2,453.22 before taxes.
The City is granting a real estate subsidy of $15,495, recommended by Atelier Entremise, which manages the transitional occupancy of the site.
The City provides the energy and pays for maintenance and repairs; the organization pays the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
This lease extends an occupancy already authorized in August 2025 for five months.
The City is lending the former Bain St-Denis, at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert (Plaza Saint-Hubert, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie), free of charge to the organization L'Amour en Action SYL DAN.
The 15,406 sq. ft. building will be used as a warming centre for about 20 people experiencing homelessness or vulnerability.
The loan lasts about 90 days, from February 1 to April 30, 2026, for the winter of 2025-2026.
The warming centre will be open from 4 p.m. to 8 a.m., 7 days a week.
The value of the loan is estimated at $56,978 in real estate subsidy ($15/sq. ft. over 90 days).
The organization will pay for cleaning and minor repairs; the borough takes care of snow removal and outdoor maintenance; the City pays for energy and technical maintenance.

The City is renting two spaces (287 and 291), totalling 360 square feet, to the organization Archives lesbiennes du Québec, at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the former convent of the Cité-des-Hospitalières.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for offices and a library.
The total rent is $10,551.60 before taxes; at the same time, the City is granting a real estate subsidy of $5,497.20.
The City pays for energy, maintenance and repairs; the tenant pays the property taxes and the cleaning.
