Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The organization was already occupying the premises: shorter leases had been approved in 2024, in March 2025 and in October 2025.
The organization was proposed by Atelier Entremise, the non-profit organization that the City put in charge of managing the transitional occupancy of the heritage site purchased in 2017.
The City is renting a 155-square-foot space (unit 154) at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the Cité-des-Hospitalières, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The tenant is Écotone - Espace d'expérimentation, an arts research platform that hosts artists in residence; the space will be used as offices and for a research-creation project.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for total rent of $4,422.24 before taxes ($5,084.47 including taxes).
The City is granting a real estate subsidy of $2,487.75, recommended by Atelier Entremise, which manages the transitional occupancy of the site.
The City supplies the energy and pays for maintenance and repairs; the tenant pays the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
This renews an occupancy that has been in place since 2022, with successive leases approved in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

The City is authorizing Hydro-Québec to remove and send off-site a pile of contaminated soil on a City-owned lot at the intersection of rue Pierre-de-Coubertin and boulevard de l'Assomption, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.
In exchange, Hydro-Québec gets a rent reduction of no more than $148,761 before taxes, reimbursed based on the actual invoices.
The credit will apply to the 2nd year of the lease if the supporting documents are received before June 30, 2027, or to the 3rd year if they arrive after that date but before June 30, 2028.
Hydro-Québec has been renting this 14,400 m² lot since September 1, 2025, for four years, as a work site area to build a new transformer station (lease of $1,747,152).
Hydro-Québec must comply with the regulations on contaminated soil, provide a traceability report and photos, and do a site visit with the City at the end of the work.

The City states that at the end of the lease the lot will be ready for redevelopment and greening planned under the Aménagement-Assomption program, and that it thus avoids paying for the soil disposal itself.
The City is lending the SPCA canadienne, free of charge, a 3,955-square-foot space on the ground floor of 7487, 18e Avenue, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
The loan runs for 2 years starting July 1, 2026, and is used to store pet food and equipment related to community activities.
The value of the loan is estimated at $94,920 (3,955 sq. ft. x $12/sq. ft. x 2 years), presented as a real estate subsidy.
The SPCA pays for maintenance, minor repairs and municipal and school taxes if applicable; the City pays for energy and major maintenance.
The City can end the agreement with 90 days' written notice.
The building was acquired in 2024 for social housing purposes; the space is being lent while waiting for that project to be carried out.
The City is lending a 100-square-foot room in the basement of the former église Sainte-Bibiane, at 5600, 12e Avenue, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, free of charge.
The organization Projet Ado communautaire en Travail de rue (PACT de rue) will use it to store two bicycles and equipment related to its community activities.
The loan runs from May 19, 2026 to May 31, 2027, which is 378 days.
The value of the loan is estimated at $1,250 in the form of a property subsidy (calculated at $12 per square foot).
PACT de rue pays for maintenance, snow removal and minor repairs; the City covers energy costs and major maintenance.
The City can end the loan with 10 days' written notice.
The building was acquired as a land reserve for a future social housing project; the room is not needed for municipal purposes.
The City is lending, free of charge, a 100 m² outdoor space on the forecourt of the Marché Bonsecours, at 350, rue Saint-Paul Est, in Ville-Marie.
The loan lasts 129 days, from June 24 to October 31, 2026, and is for setting up a temporary public square.
The Société de développement commercial Vieux-Montréal – Quartier historique pays all costs for setting up, maintaining, repairing and replacing the equipment.
The value of the property subsidy is estimated at $7,500, that is 100 m² at $75/m².
No commercial activity or direct sales will take place on site: the space will be used for activities and temporary occupancy.
The SDC says it has seen a drop in foot traffic in the area over the past 18 months, linked in particular to construction work and the end of the pedestrianization of one section.
The City is lending a 90 m² space free of charge in the basement of 85, rue Notre-Dame Est (annex of the édifice Lucien-Saulnier), in Ville-Marie, to Groupe communautaire L'Itinéraire.
The loan lasts 170 days, from May 15 to October 31, 2026, and the space is used as offices (3 offices, no fit-up required).
The value of the rent not collected, called a real estate subsidy, is $8,300 (90 m² × $198/m² = $17,820 per year, prorated over 170 days).
L'Itinéraire's workers will provide local services there to people in vulnerable situations in Vieux-Montréal.
The City pays the maintenance costs for the space, except for janitorial cleaning, which remains the organization's responsibility.
Over the summer, the City plans work to prepare the premises for use as a warming station during the winter of 2026-2027.
In 2025, the City had already lent L'Itinéraire a 661 m² space in the same building for a winter warming station (subsidy of $65,439).
Montréal is lending a SPVM detective sergeant to the Gendarmerie royale du Canada for three years, from March 30, 2026 to March 29, 2029.

The officer is assigned to the Équipe nationale de soutien à l'application de la Loi sur les armes (ENSALA): training, advice and support for investigations into firearms trafficking, with no operational intervention.

The City is adding $136,260 in revenue and the same amount in spending to its 2026 budget, with an adjustment to the budget base for the following years; the expense is covered by the urban agglomeration.
The City continues to pay the officer's salary, overtime and benefits, then bills the GRC every quarter to be reimbursed.
The authorized police workforce is temporarily increased by one detective sergeant position for the same period.

The agreement differs from the usual agreements: the GRC compensates the seconded officer, but not the City, except for the amounts the City will pay out for him; no compensation if he did not act in good faith or acted outside his duties.
The SPVM states that more than 50% of this resource's tasks directly benefit Montréal.
The City is hiring the company 9415-1966 Québec inc. to prepare, distribute and deliver meals to people held in custody by the SPVM.
The contract is worth $451,000.94, taxes included, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2029, with the option of a 12-month extension.
The meals serve all SPVM detention centres and the detention area of the Cour municipale de Montréal.
The company was selected as the lowest compliant bidder among three bids received (public call for tenders 25-21226).
Its bid is $136,722.52 (30.31%) lower than the second-lowest bid, and $8,899.06 below the City's estimate.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, since policing is an agglomeration responsibility.
The contract replaces the one with Resto Plateau, in effect since 2023 and extended in March 2025.
The City is lending an SPVM police officer to the Sûreté du Québec for one year, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, as part of the investigation team on the export of stolen vehicles.
The officer on loan, a detective sergeant, will take part in investigations, criminal intelligence, surveillance operations, searches and arrests targeting stolen vehicle export networks.
The City keeps paying the officer's salary; the Sûreté du Québec reimburses it $157,875 ($13,156.25 per month), plus certain eligible expenses.
The total compensation cost is estimated at $214,092, which leaves a gap of $56,217 that the SPVM will have to fund out of its own budget.
The authorized police staffing level goes up temporarily by one detective sergeant position for the length of the agreement.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, since police service is an agglomeration responsibility.
The decision summary states that the agreement is authorized retroactively.
The Ville-Marie borough is entrusting the YMCAs du Québec with welcoming visitors and providing oversight at the centre culturel et communautaire Sanaaq, in the Peter-McGill district.
The contract is awarded by mutual agreement and covers 12 months, from April 20, 2026 to April 19, 2027.
Total authorized spending: $289,721, that is $277,131 for the contract and $12,590 in contingencies, taxes included.
The workers must maintain a presence on site, defuse tense situations, raise awareness about sharing the space and direct people to the right resources.
The YMCAs will also take part in the centre's participatory governance bodies.
The organization will be paid monthly after services are rendered and must submit an activity report and a financial report no later than May 31, 2027.
A similar contract had been awarded to the YMCAs in January 2025, for a maximum of $336,000.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $29,000 to two organizations for projects to fight social exclusion in the Peter-McGill district.

The Association du Village Shaughnessy is receiving $5,000 for community activities to fight isolation among seniors, for beautification, and to highlight the history of the Shaughnessy Village neighbourhood.
The Carrefour jeunesse-emploi Montréal Centre-Ville is receiving $24,000 for a youth outreach worker position, to improve access to local resources for more vulnerable young people.
The money comes from the Fonds de soutien financier en développement social; the contribution is not recurring.
The agreements end on June 30, 2027 (April 30, 2027 for the Village Shaughnessy project), and the borough will follow up on the projects.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $17,000 to two organizations in the Peter-McGill district, taken from the Fonds de soutien financier en développement social.

Inter-Action du quartier Peter-McGill is receiving $15,000 for creative activities (drawing, writing) for people experiencing homelessness, twice a week in the Quartier des gares, near the Mission Saint-Michael and the Bonaventure metro station.
Inter-Action's activities are led by two community workers and one peer helper, and aim to break isolation and direct participants toward job-integration and housing resources.
The Association des résidents de Victor Hugo / Lucien L'Allier is receiving $2,000 to organize family activities in the neighbourhood.
Both projects start on July 8, 2026 and the agreements end no later than December 31, 2026.
The contributions are non-recurring and the borough will follow up on the projects.

The borough of Ville-Marie is awarding B&M Groupe Sécurité inc. a contract for specialized security guard services in public spaces, for a total expenditure of $346,757.25 including taxes ($315,233.86 for the contract and $31,523.39 in contingencies).
The contract runs from July 8 to November 1, 2026, that is, 4 months.
The guards are to observe risky situations and alert the SPVM or the borough, without intervening directly: surveillance rounds, contact with the people present, identification of problem areas.
The service aims at coexistence in public spaces, which must remain accessible to the entire population, including people without housing.
Public call for tenders 26-21438 received 10 bids; 8 were rejected for administrative or technical non-compliance.
The selected bid is $6,612.19 (1.94%) above the City's latest estimate and comes in $186.97 ahead of the second compliant bid (SIRCO).
The project extends a trial run in the fall of 2024 and a six-month contract in 2025 in Ville-Marie.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough agrees to receive three lots free of charge from the developer, at the intersection of rue Hochelaga and rue Honoré-Beaugrand.
The three lots total 1,040.2 m² (392.3 m², 495.4 m² and 152.5 m²), which is the equivalent of 10% of the site's area, handed over as park fees.
The land will be used to build a public walkway linking parc Germaine-Pépin to rue Hochelaga and rue Honoré-Beaugrand.
The transfer is part of the redevelopment of the former public works yard, a mixed-use project of more than 300 housing units approved in 2017.
A chartered appraiser estimated the market value of the land at $1,487,402.78 ($1,429.92/m²) as of August 18, 2025.
Before the subdivision permits are issued, the City will have to confirm that the lots are free of mortgages and that their level of contamination is suitable for park use.
The Mercier/Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is amending its planning by-law to allow businesses in zone 0781.
The area concerned is near the intersection of rue Sherbrooke Est and rue De Contrecoeur, the faubourg Contrecoeur commercial area and parc Carlos-D'Alcantara.
The change adds the "Pôle commercial Contrecœur" use category and sets construction standards (setbacks, height, lot coverage).
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain recommends the amendment to improve the area's commercial offering.
The process includes a public consultation meeting, a request for approval by referendum and, if required, a register or a referendum vote.
No spending is associated with the decision.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is accepting a payment of $20,654.90 from the owner of a lot at 2928-2930, rue Des Ormeaux, between rue Sainte-Claire and rue de Marseille.
This amount replaces handing over land to the City: the by-law requires 10% of the site, either as land or as money, before a subdivision permit can be issued.
The owner wants to split the lot in two (6 659 714 and 6 659 715); the permit application was filed on June 23, 2025.
The lot that is already built on (209 m²) is exempt; only the vacant lot of 209.1 m² is charged.
An appraisal firm set the value of the site at $413,000 ($987.80/m²) on December 3, 2025, which puts 10% at $206,548.98.
The borough finds that handing over 41.8 m² of land is not warranted, given its small size and its location.
The money will go into the borough's reserved "parks and playgrounds" revenues; the subdivision permit will then be issued.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is granting a minor exemption for the house at 2485, rue Théodore.
The exemption allows a construction alignment of 5.43 m instead of the required 5.6 m, and a right side setback of 0.5 m instead of 1.5 m.

The work, already under way, had received a renovation permit in December 2025, but the inspection revealed that it was in fact a demolition, since the floor had not been rebuilt at its original level.
A demolition certificate was granted on April 10, 2026 to bring the situation into compliance, which caused the building to lose its acquired rights regarding the alignment and the setback.
According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, the exemptions reproduce the situation that existed before the work and do not harm the neighbours.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme issued a favourable opinion on April 10, 2026; a public notice must announce the application before it is adopted by the borough council.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is paying $59,400 (taxes included) to three organizations to carry out 9 citizen projects, from May 5 to December 31, 2026.
Breakdown: Milieu de vie Masson Village $27,850 (5 projects), Petite Patrie Collectif $23,550 (3 projects), AmiEs du parc des Gorilles $8,000 (1 project).
The money comes from the borough's 2026 operating budget; each project receives between $3,000 and $8,000.
The projects involve, among others, parc des Gorilles, rue Saint-André, parc De Gaspé, parc Père-Marquette, rue Masson, and the parcs Jean-Duceppe, des Locomotives, du Pélican and de l'Ukraine.
They include activities, greening, free workshops, landscaping work and a storytelling walk in five alleys of the Masson area.
Projects must come from a citizen initiative and take place on public property; the City does not commit to keeping the installations after the project ends.
The director of culture, sports, recreation and social development signs the agreements and may adjust the project guidelines without exceeding the amounts granted.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve will apply for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation to renovate the piscine Pierre-Lorange and expand the bibliothèque Hochelaga in order to turn it into a community and sports centre.

The building, built in 1983, has components at the end of their useful life and systems that no longer meet current standards; it is located at the heart of the family hub of the Hochelaga integrated urban revitalization area.
The total cost of the project is estimated at $38M based on the functional and technical programs carried out in 2026.
The program can cover up to 66% of eligible work, to a maximum of $20M.
Each borough may submit only one project; this one was given priority because it is already included in the Programme Aquatique Montréal – Volet mise aux normes.
The borough commits to paying the project's recurring operating costs and to complying with the conditions of the agreement with the ministère.
The application must be submitted no later than June 22, 2026, and the borough council resolution is mandatory for the project to be admissible.
The City is giving $2,694,500 to six boroughs to pay for temporary pedestrian streets on commercial streets in the summer of 2026.

Breakdown: Plateau-Mont-Royal $1,006,000 (Mont-Royal Est and Duluth), Verdun $565,250 (Wellington), Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve $425,000 (Ontario), Ville-Marie $375,500 (Sainte-Catherine Est), Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension $216,750 (De Castelnau and Villeray), Outremont $106,000 (Bernard).
Rue Villeray is the only new project being funded ($123,250); the others renew pedestrianization projects that have already been supported since 2022-2024.
Each project must close the street completely to traffic for at least eight consecutive weeks.
The borough and its partners must pay at least 33% of the project cost; funding is calculated at $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street.
The transfers are made in March 2026, the reporting in November, and any money not spent must be returned in December 2026.
The money comes from the $200M agreement between the City and Québec's ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is amending its agreement with the organization Groupe Pro-Vert for the green alleys program in 2026.
The change adds no spending: the planned amounts remain $143,103.63 in 2025 and $160,344.14 in 2026.
Pro-Vert will survey residents living along certain alleys to gather their needs and expectations.
The organization will also draw up an up-to-date inventory of green alleys, with a condition rating from A to E, and will take stock of all the dirt alleys in the area.
The quantities for two items in the original contract (2.2 and 2.4) are revised.
In 2025, the bids received were higher than expected: the borough cancelled the development of three alleys and will issue a new call for tenders in 2026.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding Groupe Damex inc. the work to develop three green alleys and to install the electrical hookup for a BIXI station, for $403,842.79 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $717,267.86, including $80,768.56 in contingencies and $232,656.51 in incidental costs.

The alleys involved: ruelle Cardenon (Cardinal/Briand/Denonville/Hadley), ruelle Mon Joli Jogues Land (De Montmagny/Jolicoeur/Jogues/Springland) and ruelle Vinet (Charlevoix/Notre-Dame Ouest/Lionel-Groulx/Vinet).
The work covers 514 m² of landscaping, including 369 m² of de-paving, the planting of 29 trees and nearly 1,000 perennials and shrubs, street furniture, ground markings and dry wells for rainwater.
The micro-forest in parc Vinet will be extended into ruelle Vinet; access to existing parking spaces is maintained.
Residents and Groupe Pro-Vert are taking care of planting the vegetation and organizing activities on site; the neighbours' committees are committing to maintain the landscaping.
The bill is shared: 48.61% by the borough, 40.57% by the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne, 10.82% by the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité.
The City is accepting $100,500 from the Fondation de la Faune du Québec for a research project by the Insectarium de Montréal, running from June 2026 to March 2028.

The money will be used to study the habitats and populations of two dragonflies with precarious status: the gomphe des fosses (an endangered species since 2018) and the gomphe ventru (a species of special concern since 2022).
The sum will fund a scholarship for a university student, the purchase of collection equipment and the analysis of samples; the Insectarium pays for field travel.
The contribution covers 75% of the project's costs and will be paid in three instalments: $36,000 on signing, $24,300 on March 1, 2027 and $40,200 on March 1, 2028.
The director of the Insectarium is authorized to sign the agreement with the Fondation.
Since the revenues and the expenses are equal, the transaction has no effect on the City's financial framework.

The project is being carried out with the Université de Montréal, the Fondation de la Faune and the ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is awarding Construction Viatek inc. a $2,341,647.19 contract (taxes included) to redo sidewalks, curbs and roadways on eight stretches of local streets.
The total authorized spending comes to $2,786,560.16, taxes included, adding $234,164.72 in contingencies, $70,249.42 in incidentals and $140,498.83 for work supervision.

The streets involved: rue Baldwin (from rue Sherbrooke Est to rue Tiffin), rue Théodore (three stretches between rue Sainte-Catherine Est and rue de Rouen), rue Cuvillier (from rue Sainte-Catherine Est to rue Adam) and avenue Lebrun (from rue de Bellerive to rue Notre-Dame Est).
The work includes planing the asphalt, laying a new surface, repairing the roadbed where needed and rebuilding sections of sidewalk.
The work site is planned from May to September 2026; nearby residents will receive a letter about the nature and length of the work.
Nine companies submitted bids out of 14 that bought the tender documents; Viatek is the lowest compliant bid, 12.3% below the City's estimate.
The bill is paid 100% by the borough and funded by borrowing charged to its taxpayers.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is hiring the firm IGF Axiom inc. to manage and supervise its street construction sites, for a maximum of $552,454.88, taxes included.
The contract lasts 24 months, starting in May 2026, and ends at the end of 2028 or when the budget runs out.
The supervised work covers the repair of roadways and sidewalks, cycling links, traffic calming, safety improvements around schools and stormwater management.
Six firms submitted bids; IGF Axiom and Artelia Canada received the same score, but IGF Axiom offered the lower price of the two.
The chosen price is 4.61% above the borough's estimate and 8.27% below the average of the compliant bids.
Assignments will be given out as needed, through purchase orders, based on the needs of 2026 and 2027.
The borough of Lachine is applying for a grant from Québec to build a Centre aquatique, sportif et communautaire, under the ministère de l'Éducation's PAFIRSPA program.
The requested funding can cover up to 66% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of $20M for the sports and recreational infrastructure component.
Lachine is committing to pay at least 34% of the bill, plus all non-eligible costs and any cost overruns, and to operate and maintain the building.
The project includes a main swimming pool and a recreational pool, a double gymnasium, a palestra, a multi-purpose room, sports and leisure rooms, and space for community organizations.
The centre would be built in the future Lachine-Est eco-neighbourhood; the borough currently has no municipal indoor aquatic or sports facility.
The application must be submitted no later than June 22, 2026, after approval from the executive committee expected in May 2026; a response is expected in late 2026 or early 2027.
The borough of Lachine is giving $45,000 to CDEC LaSalle-Lachine to support businesses on rue Saint-Jacques, in the quartier Saint-Pierre and on rue Provost.
The money comes from the City's program for commercial streets located outside the sociétés de développement commercial (SDC).
On rue Saint-Jacques and in Saint-Pierre: door-to-door visits to merchants, connecting them with resources, business meetings and the possible creation of a merchants' association.
On rue Provost: collecting data on merchants' needs and obstacles, in order to assess a possible collaboration among them.
Payments in two stages: $35,000 on signing, and $10,000 for measures to attract customers only if the borough approves them.
The agreement ends on June 10, 2027; the final reports are due on that date.
The data given to the borough will have to be aggregated or non-nominative whenever possible.
The borough of Ville-Marie is proposing to take charge of the design and carrying out of work in the Quartier des spectacles, a responsibility that normally falls to city council.

The work involves the Esplanade Tranquille (rebuilt driveway entrance, direct access between the storage building and the north part of the site, two grassed areas converted to surfaces that stand up to heavy use) and the replacement of a grate at the end of its life on the place des Festivals.
Estimated cost of $1,472,500: $1,150,000 for the landscaping work, $150,000 for the grate and $175,500 for an 18-month professional position with equipment.
The Service de la culture is paying the entire bill and will have to approve each expense in writing before it is incurred.
Planned schedule: acceptance by city council in May 2026, hiring in July 2026, call for tenders in spring 2027 and work in summer or fall 2027.

The borough justifies taking charge of the project on the grounds that it already handles the routine maintenance of these public squares and that the Service de la culture does not have the resources to manage the project.
No communications strategy is planned with the Service des communications.
The Saint-Léonard borough is giving $6,300 to the Regroupement des éco-quartiers for the Patrouille verte 2026, or $2,100 per officer.
This money pays for the summer hiring of three environmental awareness officers, for 9 weeks at 32 hours per week.
The officers will go door to door and raise awareness about waste management (brown bin, recycling bin, bulky items), drinking water conservation and green alleys.
About 45% of their time will go to local assignments: cleanliness, household hazardous waste drop-offs, promoting the borough's subsidies for reusable products; 10% to training.
The Éco-quartier de Saint-Léonard will supervise the officers; the agreement ends on August 1, 2026.
Funding also comes from the Canada Summer Jobs program, which pays the wages and payroll taxes.
The support was $4,200 in 2025 and $6,000 in 2024; the borough has taken part in the Patrouille verte since 2009.
The borough of Saint-Léonard takes note of the 2025 report and the 2026 action plan of its Écoquartier, run by the organization Nature-Action Québec inc.
In 2025, the Écoquartier says it served more than 29,670 residents, reached 4,837 participants at awareness activities and handed out 21,804 collection tools.
11,263 kg of waste was diverted from landfill (electronics, clean-up drives) and 16 grant applications for cloth diapers and sustainable hygiene products were accepted.
On the greening side: 76 trees planted through "Un arbre pour mon quartier", 6 home composters given away, 43 activities reaching 1,412 participants.

School and community projects: 1,086 students from 4 schools in the apprentice-gardeners project, 131 participants in the Éco-créateurs workshops, 33 entries in the Maisons et Balcons fleuris contest.
In 2026, the Écoquartier wants to get the neighbourhood's young people involved and help the borough set up collection services for new residents.
Funding for the organization for 2026 and 2027 was approved in December 2025, in the amount of $395,274.10 plus the change in the CPI.
The borough of Lachine is approving the expansion plans for the Maison du chapelain, at 1850, rue Provost.
The expansion, at the rear of the building, adds about 471 m² and will be in brick (Mayo Clear Smoot and Vintage Gray Glaze) with sections in sheet metal (Antique Patina 24).
The project will be used to relocate 57 children from the CPE À Petits Pas, located at 200, boulevard Bouchard in Dorval, and to take in 80 more children.
The building is located on the heritage interest site of the Sœurs de Saint-Anne and is subject to section 89 of the Charter of Ville de Montréal.
Following comments from the comité consultatif d'urbanisme, the applicants changed the windows and added a crown detail echoing that of the main building.
A traffic study led to changes to the parking area and the drop-off area for children's arrivals and departures.
The permit is granted on the condition that the project complies with the by-laws in force; any change will have to go through a new plan approval.
The borough of Lachine approves the expansion plans for the Pétro-Canada service station located at 440, 32e Avenue.
The 646-square-foot expansion will be built in the left side yard to house an A&W restaurant.
The lot has 15 mature trees; close to 10 trees will be planted, for a total of 25 trees once the work is done.
The planned materials: metal siding in the colour Wood Grain, white aluminum composite panels, and the brown and beige manufactured stone already on the building.
Mullions were added to the front of the building, following comments from the comité consultatif d'urbanisme, to visually separate the Pétro-Canada from the A&W.
The permit is granted on the condition that the project complies with the regulations; any change will have to go through a new plan approval.
The borough of Lachine is approving a minor exemption for a single-family home located at 45, 49e Avenue.
The exemption allows the side setbacks to add up to 2.46 metres, whereas the zoning by-law requires 3 metres.
The request is meant to bring the property into compliance after the construction of a garage, which has already been built.
The owner noticed that the rules had not been followed when her certificate of location was produced after the work was done.
A minor exemption on the sum of the setbacks had already been granted for this building in September 2024.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain does not oppose the request, and the comité consultatif d'urbanisme recommended granting it on April 15, 2026.
The borough of Lachine approves the renovation plans for the buildings located at 800, 840, 860, 880 and 900, 5e Avenue.
The EIFS cladding on part of the front facade will be replaced with titanium white metal cladding.
The balconies on all floors will be demolished and rebuilt to the same dimensions, without the acrylic structures, with fibreglass floors and vanilla-coloured steel railings.

The permit will be issued on the condition that the project complies with the regulations in force; any change will have to go back through a site planning and architectural integration programme (PIIA) plan approval.

The Direction de l'aménagement urbain considers that these are maintenance works to bring the buildings into compliance for safety reasons, and that the buildings are not located in an area of heritage interest.
The borough of Lachine approves the plans for the project to transform the front balcony of the building located at 396, 51e Avenue.
The work consists of replacing the balcony and the guardrails on the front of the building: a light brown composite balcony and black aluminum guardrails.
The building is in an area of heritage interest, which means the plans must be reviewed before the permit is issued.
The permit application also includes landscaping work in the backyard, but only the front balcony is subject to this review.
The permit will be issued on the condition that the project complies with the regulations in force; any change will have to go through the same approval process again.
The application was filed on March 12, 2026 and the file was reviewed at a sitting on May 13, 2026.
The borough of Lachine is approving the plans for a renovation project at 645, 45e Avenue, a building located in a heritage area.
The project calls for an extension of nearly 4.88 metres by 6.71 metres over two storeys, at the rear of the building.
The extension will be covered with brick and aluminum in the colour Chêne Blanc Miel.
The upper part of the exterior cladding will be replaced with the same aluminum on all façades.
The permit may be issued if the project complies with the regulations in force; any change will have to go through a new approval.
According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, the chosen colour is similar to the one already there, and the extension is barely visible from the street.
The borough of Lachine is approving the plans for a new six-unit building at 359-361, rue Camille.
The building will have three storeys plus a mezzanine and will cover close to 50% of the lot.
An indoor parking area in the basement will have six spaces, one for each unit, with access by a ramp at the front.
The building will be entirely in brick, with a charcoal grey metal mezzanine and stainless-steel-coloured aluminum elements; terraces are planned at the back and on the mezzanine.
The lot will include 29% greening, as the building's footprint leaves little room for landscaping.
The permit is granted on the condition that the project complies with the regulations; any change will have to go through a new approval of the plans.
This is the replacement project tied to a demolition authorized on July 18, 2025.
The borough of Lachine is granting a minor exemption to the zoning by-law for a construction project at 359-361, rue Camille.
The project calls for a six-unit building on three storeys with a mezzanine and indoor parking.
The building may have a rear setback of 3.52 metres instead of 4 metres, and a combined side setback of 1.54 metre instead of 3 metres.
Parking will be reduced to one space per unit, rather than the 1.5 spaces per unit required.
The underground portion of the parking may be built right up to the property line, without the minimum distance of 30 centimetres normally required.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme recommended granting the exemption on June 17, 2026; work has not started.
The borough of Lachine is approving the plans for a work project on the house at 507, 44e Avenue.
The project adds 36.42 square metres on one storey in the back yard.
The windows and the door on the front facade will be changed, in black, and the metal cladding on the upper part will be replaced with a paler colour.
The cladding of the extension will be black and brown vertical light metal.
The building is located in an area of heritage interest; the City considers that the extension is not very visible from the street and fits in with the surrounding buildings.
The permit is granted on the condition that the project complies with the regulations; any change will have to go through a new approval of the plans.
The borough of Lachine approves the plans for an extension at 706, 43e Avenue.
The work adds about 45 square metres on one storey, in the side and rear yard, to create an office and a bedroom.
The exterior cladding will be made of dark grey fibre cement panels, and the front window of the extension will measure 6 feet by 6 feet.
The permit is granted on the condition that the project complies with the regulations in force.
Any change to the approved project will have to go through a new site planning and architectural integration programme (PIIA) plan approval.
The project was revised after the comments made by the urban planning advisory committee on May 13, 2026 about how the exterior cladding fits in.
The borough of Lachine is authorizing the addition of an intergenerational housing unit in the house at 860, 50e Avenue.
The application serves to regularize a situation that has existed for several years without authorization; the owner wants to comply with the rules in view of an eventual sale.
The tenant of the additional unit is related to the owners of the main unit, and a door in the basement connects the two units.
Of the 17 conditions in the by-law on conditional uses, one is considered non-compliant: a second door on the front of the building, installed before 2015 when the garage door was removed.
No exterior changes are planned; the application was filed on May 20, 2026 and the planning advisory committee reviewed it on June 17, 2026.
The borough of Lachine is refusing a request from a business at 2035, rue Victoria, which wanted to install a sign on the side wall facing its parking lot.
Lachine's zoning by-law requires a commercial sign to be installed on a wall that faces directly onto a street.
The business already has a pole sign and will have a sign on the front wall of the building.
The applicant argued it would give customers better visibility and make the entrance easier to find from the parking lot.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain is opposed: no serious harm was demonstrated, the relevance was not demonstrated, and the size of the sign would have a negative impact on the architecture.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme also recommended refusal on May 13, 2026, finding that the size and location of the sign spoil the character of the building.
The request was filed on November 15, 2025, and the work has not started.
The City is paying $245,100 in 2026 to three neighbourhood round tables, or $81,700 each, under the Quartiers inclusifs et résilients approach.

The funded organizations are Concert'Action Lachine (Saint-Pierre neighbourhood), the Corporation de développement communautaire du Centre-Sud (Sainte-Marie neighbourhood, Ville-Marie) and Montréal-Nord en santé / Table de quartier de Montréal-Nord (northeast sector).
Support is going from $200,000 per organization in 2024 and 2025 down to $81,700 in 2026, since the pilot project ended in 2025.
The money is to be used to free up staff to coordinate local governance, support the projects in the intervention strategy, track their progress and take part in data collection.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city and was already included in the budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale.
City council is also approving the agreements setting out the payment conditions, and no public QIR communications are planned for 2026.
The borough of Outremont is adding $171,378.65 (taxes included) to the fees of the firm Affleck de la Riva architectes, which is in charge of restoring and upgrading the chalet in parc Saint-Viateur.
The total professional services contract goes from $492,897.80 to $664,276.45, and the contingency reserve rises from $129,576.80 to $300,955.45.
The amount covers two parts: $14,946.75 for supervising work in the presence of asbestos and lead, and $156,431.90 for 12 additional months of supervision.
The chalet, built in 1927 at 525, avenue Bloomfield, has been out of service since a fire in November 2021; bringing it back into use requires a complete restoration.
Change orders on the work site have already accounted for $1,418,408.49 in contingencies for the contractor Immobilier Belmon inc.
According to the document, the expense will be covered by the City's self-insurance fund; a later file to the executive committee will present the final expenses to be reimbursed.
The document states that not increasing the fees would create a risk of litigation and could delay the work under way.

The borough of Outremont is adding $185,109.75 (taxes included) to the professional fees of ACDF Architecture for the restoration and code upgrade of the mairie d'Outremont, at 543, chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine.
The total spending for this professional services contract goes from $655,532.22 to $840,641.97; contingencies and incidental costs go from $172,509.53 to $357,619.28.
The work revealed unforeseen conditions: more than 50 change directives, repairs to woodwork, the bell turret and signage, and the discovery of "Knob and Tube" wiring presenting a fire risk.

Also added are the integration of information technologies requested by the central city and taking on the heating, air conditioning and electricity of the maison Bagg, which were excluded from the original design.
The increase breaks down as follows, before taxes: $75,000 for architecture, $59,825 for electromechanical work (three components) and $5,000 for structure.
The borough is funding the expense and will ask for a reimbursement from the heritage preservation subsidy program, estimated at about 50% of the eligible expense.
Completion of the work and provisional acceptance are expected by the end of 2026.
The City is awarding a direct (non-tendered) contract of $687,320.55 (taxes included) to Tetra Tech QI inc., plus $103,098.08 in contingencies, for a total expenditure of $790,418.63.

The firm must integrate the Saint-Jacques and Courcelles retention basins into the integrated interceptor control system (CIDI), which uses rainfall forecasts from a weather radar to manage wastewater.
The mandate includes functional analysis, modelling, software reconfiguration, commissioning, training and updating of the documentation.
The contract is being awarded without a call for tenders because Tetra Tech QI inc. holds the exclusive rights to the Pilote and Csoft software of the CIDI system.
The contract runs from May 2026 to December 2028, with expenditures spread over 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The expenditure is paid by the agglomeration and financed by a loan charged to agglomeration taxpayers.

According to the file, the integration aims to reduce the frequency and volumes of wastewater overflows, in line with the objective of the Stratégie montréalaise de l'eau 2025-2034 to reduce them by 12% over ten years.
The City is adding $42,551.05 (taxes included) to the contract with 9262-0400 Québec inc. (Les Entreprises Constructo), bringing the total to $309,324.78.

The money will be used to replace contaminated compressed air ducts, change filters and add more of them, at the olfactometry laboratory of the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel, at 2235, rue Michel-Jurdant.
The purified compressed air system became contaminated in December 2025, following an operational incident.
The work was already 100% complete as of March 19, 2026, but the remaining contingency balance ($13,408.61) was not enough to pay for the corrective work.
Without this work, the laboratory cannot be used and the characterization of odour samples planned for spring 2026 would be delayed.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomération de Montréal, in full in 2026. The contract is set to end on May 15, 2026.
The City is giving $69,076.09 to the Regroupement des éco-quartiers to run the Patrouille bleue in the summer of 2026.
This money pays for the hiring of 14 patrollers ($43,512), who will work in pairs for 4 weeks in the boroughs and the related cities, plus coordination and materials ($25,564.08).
The patrollers will go door to door to talk about saving water at home, spotting leaks and the rules for outdoor watering (by-law 13-023).
They will also raise public awareness about what should not be thrown into toilets and sewers, with visits to CPEs and daycares that use a lot of wipes.
Toilet leak detection tablets and pamphlets will be handed out; the remaining water-saving kits are available in the éco-quartiers.
The expense is paid 70% by the urban agglomeration and 30% by the central city.
The City has supported the Patrouille bleue since 2010; the contribution was $68,588.59 in 2025.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $187,354 to the organization Prévention Sud-Ouest for the year 2026.

The largest share, $179,649, funds BUMP, an urban mediation project: mediators present throughout the borough to work on the feeling of safety, avoid young people ending up in the court system, and promote inclusion.
An amount of $7,705 goes to the Griffintown project, which aims to improve communication between the generations of residents in the neighbourhood.
This is a one-year extension of projects already funded in 2024 and 2025, under the Prévention Montréal program (streams 1 and 2).
Funding for the Griffintown project is dropping from $8,590 to $7,705, because there are no leftover funds from previous years; a proportional adjustment was applied to all stream 1 projects.
The projects run from January 1 to December 31, 2026, and the amounts are paid entirely by the ville centre (Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale).
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $81,700 to the neighbourhood round table Concertation Ville-Émard–Côte-Saint-Paul for the year 2026 (January 1 to December 31).
The money funds the "Démarche de RUI – Opération GALT 2026": beautifying the area, gathering places, citizen participation and monitoring of quality of life.
The budget breaks down as follows: $65,000 in salaries, $11,000 for a mural at the Centre Hortense-Duclos, $5,000 for the PACT project with Groupe Paradoxe and $700 in administrative fees.
The document states that 2026 will be the last year of the RUI – Opération GALT program.
The expense is paid in full by the central city, through the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale.
The amounts given in previous years were $152,818 in 2024 and in 2025.
The borough council is also approving the agreement setting the conditions for payment, with follow-up by a borough staff member.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $73,500 to two community organizations for two projects helping people living in poverty or homelessness.

La Coalition de la Petite-Bourgogne receives $30,000 for its Elizabeth Vargas kitchen, which produces affordable, culturally adapted meals for vulnerable households in the neighbourhood: people living alone, seniors and single-parent families.

Le Regroupement des organismes pour aînés et aînées du Sud-Ouest (ROPASOM) receives $43,500 for its Brigade solidaire, volunteers who help people fill out their income tax returns and complete administrative paperwork.
Both projects cover the period from April 13, 2026 to March 31, 2027, and the funding is limited to that one year.
The money comes from a $55M agreement with the ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale (2024-2029), and the expense is paid by the agglomeration, with no impact on the City's budget.
Five organizations had submitted five applications during the call for projects open from January 13 to February 27, 2026; two were selected.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $20,000 to four organizations to hold neighbourhood parties in 2026, which is $5,000 each.

The four parties covered: Festi-Pointe in Pointe-Saint-Charles (May 16), the Festival de la Petite-Bourgogne (mid-September), the Fête estivale de Ville-Émard–Côte-Saint-Paul (July) and the Saint-Henri neighbourhood party (August 15 or 16).
The Saint-Henri party will be held at square Sir-George-Étienne-Cartier and at the CRCS St-Zotique, at the same time as Opération Sac à Dos, which hands out school supplies.
The announced activities are free: music, games, community organization booths, food, flea market.
The council is also approving the four agreements that set the conditions for paying out the money.
The cost is paid entirely by the borough; the amount is the same as in 2025, 2023 and 2022 ($15,000 in 2024).
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $10,000 in 2026 to the Centre récréatif culturel et sportif St-Zotique (CRCS) to enhance its Programme concerté d'accompagnement jeunesse.
The project, run with Soccer St-Henri, reaches about 100 young people aged 12 to 35 in Saint-Henri and Petite-Bourgogne with supervised sports activities and psychosocial support.
The money adds inter-neighbourhood sports tournaments, community events, festive activities, youth assistant positions (refereeing, coaching help, logistics), and snacks and meals.
According to the document, these community elements are not covered by the $28,000 in funding from the Prévention Montréal program already granted to the project.
The enhancement covers the period up to December 31, 2026 and is paid entirely from the borough's operating budget.
The borough council is also approving the agreement that sets the conditions for paying out the support.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $200,000 to four neighbourhood roundtables for 2026-2027, or $50,000 each.
The organizations receiving support: Action Gardien (Pointe-Saint-Charles), Coalition de la Petite-Bourgogne/Quartier en santé, Concertation Ville-Émard–Côte-Saint-Paul and Solidarité Saint-Henri.
The money is used for local joint action against poverty and social exclusion: housing, food security, homelessness, youth, seniors, urban planning.
The bill is shared: $88,612 from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, $65,520 from the Ville-Québec agreement (MESS) and $45,868 from the borough.
The amount is higher than in previous years, when the four organizations shared $120,320.
Agreements between the City and each organization will set the conditions for payment.
The urban agglomeration council is adding 805 buildings in Ville de Mont-Royal to the inventory of buildings built before 1940 that have heritage value.
These buildings become "heritage buildings" under the land use planning act: they will be subject to Mont-Royal's specific rules on demolition and on building upkeep.
The process responds to a requirement of the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel, which calls for a complete inventory no later than April 1, 2026.
Montréal is carrying out the inventory in parts: 26 territories (boroughs and related cities) have already been adopted since 2023, and the others will follow as the work progresses.
The urban agglomeration has about 100,000 buildings built before 1940 to be analyzed.
The work is paid for through an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications: up to $5,000,000 from the ministère and an equal amount from the City.
The list of the 805 addresses is attached to the file, along with a resolution of support from the Mont-Royal city council. No communications activities are planned.
The urban agglomeration council is adding 12,260 buildings in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal to the inventory of heritage buildings built before 1940.
These buildings become "heritage buildings" within the meaning of the land use planning and development act.
They will be subject to specific rules for demolition (borough by-law) and for the occupancy and upkeep of buildings (City by-law).
The inventory meets a requirement of the Cultural Heritage Act, which calls for the entire territory to be covered by April 1, 2026 at the latest.
The agglomeration is adopting its inventory in parts: 26 territories have already been adopted since 2023, and the others will follow as the work progresses.
The work is funded through an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications: up to $5,000,000 from the ministry and a matching amount from the City.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal contributed to the inventory and supports its adoption.
The urban agglomeration council adopts the list of 1,513 buildings built before 1940 recognized as heritage buildings in the borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville.

These buildings become heritage buildings under the Loi sur l'aménagement et l'urbanisme: they will be subject to the borough's by-law on demolition and to the City's by-law on the occupancy and maintenance of buildings.
The inventory meets a requirement of the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel, which calls for a complete inventory of the territory no later than April 1, 2026.
The agglomeration is adopting its inventory in parts: 26 boroughs and related cities have already been adopted since May 2023; the others will follow over time.
The work is funded through an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications: up to $5,000,000 from the ministry and an equal contribution from the City.
The borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville took part in the inventory and supports its adoption.
About 100,000 buildings built before 1940 are believed to be located across the entire agglomeration territory, according to current estimates.
The City is adding $419,658.75 to the contract with Saint-Denis Thompson inc. for the renovation of the édifice Plessis, at 2075, rue Plessis (phase 1).
The contract therefore goes from $2,728,892.08 to $3,148,550.83, taxes included.
The work, which began on July 14, 2025, is 27.21% complete, but the worksite is currently stopped so as not to exceed the authorized spending.
Unforeseen problems explain the cost overrun: the foundation masonry was more deteriorated than expected, and there is contaminated soil and contaminated water to deal with.
The amount is used to raise the contingencies from $413,468.50 to $833,127.25, which is 40.30% of the base contract.
An amount of $252,945 for securing the north and south façades comes from the operating budget; the expense is paid 100% by the central city and financed by loan by-law 24-009.
The document states that, without this increase, the project would stop before the end of the work provided for in the contract. The contract is expected to end in June 2026.
The borough of LaSalle approves the expansion plans for Cégep André-Laurendeau, at 1111, rue Lapierre.
The addition will be about 963 m² over two floors, connected to the main building by a glassed-in corridor, for the Optech and InnovLog technology transfer centres.
It will house offices, meeting and work rooms, a technology lab, a lunch area, a locker room and technical rooms.
The work will require cutting down 12 trees; 18 medium- and large-growing trees, of at least five species, will be planted.
Measures target the heat island effect and surface water: a white roof, more vegetated areas, treed medians and permeable paving.
The precast concrete panels will match the pale grey colour of the existing building; the project is aiming for LEED Silver certification.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on January 14, 2026.
The borough of LaSalle is approving a minor exemption for a semi-detached single-family house at 7645, rue Bouvier.
The building's left side setback is 1.90 metres, while the zoning by-law requires 2 metres.
The exemption legalizes an existing situation discovered in a location certificate produced on May 21, 2025, as part of the sale of the property.
The building was constructed after a permit was issued in 1974; the discrepancy is presented as a good-faith error made during construction.

The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on January 14, 2026, finding that applying the standard would cause serious harm to the applicant without harming the neighbours.
The borough of LaSalle is increasing the fines for violations of its urban planning and nuisance by-laws.
Four by-laws are being amended: zoning (2098), construction (2099), specific projects (LAS-0041) and nuisances (LAS-0137).
The amounts are being standardized across the by-laws; the distinction between an individual and a legal entity is maintained.
The specific amount for a 3rd offence is being removed, along with the notion of a minimum and maximum amount, in order to limit challenges.
The borough says the current fines are not much of a deterrent and that the penalties for cutting down a tree did not comply with the legislative framework in force.
The document does not specify the new fine amounts.
Timeline: adoption of the draft by-law on February 2, 2026, public consultation on February 25, 2026, final adoption on March 2, 2026.
The borough of LaSalle is allowing the company Amusement Fun Show 2006 inc. to set up an amusement park on the grounds of Carrefour Angrignon.
First period: setup starting April 25, 2026, rides open from April 30 to May 10, takedown on May 11.
Second period: setup starting August 2, 2026, rides open from August 5 to 16, takedown on August 17.
The organizer must provide a valid operator's licence from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux before the event.
No sale or consumption of alcohol is allowed on the site, and the installation must not encroach on the street or the sidewalks.
The organizer must ensure safety at all times, as well as upkeep of the site and hygienic sanitary facilities.
A similar authorization had been granted to the same company for periods in April-May and in August 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is allowing Sports Experts to set up a tent in the Carrefour Angrignon parking lot for three tent sales.
The sales will be held from May 11 to 31, 2026, from August 10 to 30, 2026, and from October 5 to 18, 2026.
The tent will measure 60 feet by 40 feet; about 500 people a day are expected.
Setup and takedown are planned for May 11 and June 1, August 10 and 31, and then October 5 and 19, 2026.
The application includes the building owner's consent, the layout plan and the special event applications filed with the Service des incendies.
Similar authorizations had been granted to this business in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is renewing the term of a resident member of the Comité consultatif d'urbanisme (CCU), Michal Pawelczak.
This is a third two-year term, from April 4, 2026 to April 3, 2028.
The term will begin at the committee's first meeting, on April 8, 2026.
LaSalle's CCU has six residents (including one substitute) and two council members; residents' terms can be renewed up to four times.
No money is attached to this decision.
The borough of LaSalle is amending its zoning by-law to allow the borough council to change the dates of garage sales by order.
At present, LaSalle residents can hold three garage sales a year: the weekend of the Journée nationale des patriotes in May, the second full weekend of July, and the Labour Day weekend in September.
If the weather is bad, the council could add a weekend at a later date at its next meeting.
Planned steps: adoption of the draft by-law on March 2, 2026, public consultation on April 1, adoption of the by-law on April 13, and coming into force in May 2026.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain recommends adoption in order to give residents more flexibility.
The borough of LaSalle approves a change to the exterior cladding on a street-facing wall of the commercial building at 8787, boulevard Newman, at the corner of avenue Dollard.
The approval clears the way for issuing an expansion permit requested on January 15, 2025.
The work covered by this approval involves replacing the black lightweight cladding on the front façade and adding new cladding to highlight the main entrance.
The new materials are lacquered aluminum panels, in the "royal beige" shade for the entrance and "Midnight black" for the canopy.
The rest of the planned work was not subject to this approval: interior redevelopment, a rear expansion for a drive-through, redevelopment of the parking lot and installation of signs.
The urban planning advisory committee had given a unanimous favourable opinion on March 12, 2025, finding that the project maintains the architectural harmony of the existing buildings.

The borough of LaSalle is approving a minor exemption for the community building at 7620, rue Édouard (63, 4e Avenue), the former Résidence LaSalle of the Congrégation des Frères du Sacré-Coeur, built in 1939.
The exemption allows an outdoor exit stairway leading up to the third floor, whereas the zoning by-law prohibits this for buildings of more than two storeys.
It also allows three parking spaces instead of the five required, in order to keep the parking area where it is now and to protect the mature trees.
The project aims to restore the building and bring it up to the standards of the National Building Code, with the addition of two exit stairways.
The basement garage and its access ramp will be removed; a community car and an electric charging station will be made available to users.
The asphalt in the parking area will be replaced with paving stones to increase permeable surfaces.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 11, 2026, finding in particular that the by-law causes serious harm to the applicant.
The borough of LaSalle is approving the rebuilding of the front stairs and balcony of a single-family home located at 141, 9e avenue, in the Village des Rapides area.
The new stairs will be made of black welded aluminum, with aluminum guardrails and columns, and fibreglass steps and floor.
The old stairs in the front yard had been removed recently for safety reasons.
The decision allows the issuing of a renovation permit applied for on October 24, 2025, for this detached two-storey building built in 1940.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 11, 2026, finding that the project meets the objectives of the by-law on PIIADs for the Village des Rapides.
No amount is tied to this decision.
The borough of LaSalle is approving the partial replacement of the exterior cladding of a commercial building at 360-366, avenue Lafleur, at the corner of rue Jean-Milot.
The beige stucco around the second-floor windows and a section of brick on the ground floor will be removed.
These surfaces will be replaced with matte black composite aluminum panels; the red brick is kept elsewhere on the building.
The permit application was filed on October 17, 2025 by the owner of this building, which was built in 1956.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 11, 2026, finding the project compliant with the by-law on sustainable site planning and architectural integration programmes.
The approval clears the way for the transformation permit to be issued.

The borough of LaSalle is approving the plans to expand and restore the community building at 7620, rue Édouard (63, 4e avenue), the former Résidence LaSalle of the Congrégation des Frères du Sacré-Cœur, built in 1939 and classified as an exceptional heritage building in the urban planning program.

A new three-storey section will be added on the north side (3e avenue), with a staircase, an elevator and a universally accessible secondary entrance; an exterior staircase will be added on the south side (4e avenue).
The new sections will be clad in almond-coloured metal siding; the windows will be replaced with almond-tinted ones, echoing the original white.
The basement garage door on the 4e avenue side and its access ramp will be removed and replaced by a sunken courtyard with a staircase and a door.
The parking area with three spaces, including one for people with reduced mobility, will go from asphalt to paving stones, with hedges and landscaped strips, plus a rack for 12 bicycles.
The front yard will be redeveloped: restoration of the central staircase, a low-slope access ramp, paved access and landscaped strips.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 11, 2026; the permit application had been filed on January 29, 2026.
The borough of LaSalle approves the plans to build a commercial terrace in front of the building at 9639-9641, boulevard LaSalle, at the corner of avenue Stirling.
The work includes a retractable awning, a planting bed in front of the terrace and another one at the southeast corner of the lot, which is currently entirely paved with asphalt.
The two existing parking spaces will be rearranged to free up the space for the terrace.
The building, constructed in 1931, houses a business on the ground floor and dwellings on the upper floor.
The permit application was filed on September 11, 2025; the urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 11, 2026.
The approval paves the way for the issuing of the renovation permit.

The borough of LaSalle is approving the plans to add a sunken entryway (an excavated open space in front of a basement door) at the front of the building at 313-315, 6e Avenue, between rue Broadway and rue Centrale.
The work is intended to create an additional unit in the basement of the duplex, built in 1953.
The project provides for a new basement door, a new staircase parallel to the existing outdoor staircase, and no other changes to the building.
The existing walkway is kept, with a slight paved detour toward the new staircase.
Shrubs about 1.2 m tall at maturity will be planted in the front yard to make the sunken entryway less visible from the street.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 11, 2026, finding the project complies with the rules for the Village des Rapides sector.
The approval clears the way for the issuance of the renovation permit applied for on October 27, 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing école Children's World Academy to hold an event in its schoolyard on June 12, 2026, from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m.
A food truck (Nomad Hambourgeois) will be allowed on site during the event.
Food stands will be present: Jam Jerk, Koma Rosta, Villa Toscana and Redi Pizza.
The activity brings together parents, children and the community: games, face painting and a sale of used uniforms.
The school had received similar authorizations in 2024 and in 2025.
No amount is attached to this decision.
The borough of LaSalle is being asked to approve a non-compliant expansion of a business at 2220-2232, rue Lapierre, at the corner of rue Juliette.
The project adds a 16.72 m² entrance vestibule to the one-storey building erected in 1975, which houses a retail business and a reception hall.

Three departures from the zoning by-law are requested: a side setback of 6.94 m on the rue Juliette side instead of 7.5 m, and two-way traffic lanes of 5.74 m (rue Juliette) and 5.15 m (rue Lapierre) instead of 6 m and 6.7 m.

After the matter went to the planning advisory committee, the applicant submitted new plans: one compliant parking space added, and one existing space converted into a space for people with reduced mobility, accessible from the new vestibule.
The applicant also commits to adding greenery along the wall next to the expansion, with shrubs and one large-canopy tree.
The planning advisory committee issued a unanimous unfavourable opinion on December 10, 2025, finding that the by-law does not cause serious harm to the applicant.
The application was filed on October 29, 2025; the borough management nonetheless recommends approving the departure.
The borough of LaSalle approves the plans to expand the commercial building at 2220-2232, rue Lapierre, at the corner of rue Juliette.
The expansion adds 19.47 square metres to build a new entrance vestibule, in red clay brick similar to that of the existing building.
The project adds one parking space and converts an existing space into a space reserved for people with reduced mobility, with a barrier-free pedestrian route.
The lot, currently entirely paved over, will receive a planted bed, shrubs and one large-canopy tree.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had issued a unanimous unfavourable opinion on December 10, 2025; the applicant then submitted modified plans.
The approval clears the way for the issuing of the expansion permit requested on October 29, 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is approving the replacement of the brick facing on the side wall of the shopping centre at 9001-9007, rue Airlie, at the corner of 76e Avenue.
The current brick is bulging ("ventre-de-bœuf"), crumbling, and the mortar has deteriorated; the document cites reasons of appearance and safety.
The new fired clay brick (Sonoma Matt brown, Canada Brick or equivalent) will be similar to the brick already installed at the other end of the building.
A stone strip of about two feet at the front corner will be kept; the windows, the door and the building's massing will not change.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on March 11, 2026.
The approval clears the way for the issuing of the renovation permit applied for on February 5, 2026.
The LaSalle borough is amending its business assistance program (component 3 – Dynamisme des commerces locaux), which is managed by PME MTL Grand Sud-Ouest.
Commercial sign projects (changing, renovating or installing a sign) become eligible even if they cost less than the usual $5,000 threshold.
For these sign projects: the business owner pays at least 20% of the cost, the assistance can cover up to 80%, and the ceiling already set out in component 3 remains in place.
The document explains that replacing a sign often costs about $2,000, which is below the current threshold.
The borough is not paying out any additional money: only the eligibility rules are changing.
PME MTL Grand Sud-Ouest agrees to adapt the application form and its evaluation criteria.
The agreement remains in effect until May 31, 2028; all of its other terms remain unchanged.

The borough of LaSalle is approving the demolition of a commercial building at the corner of avenue Lafleur and rue Clément, and then the construction of a residential complex on the former Arborite site (about 30,000 m²), bounded by avenue Lafleur and rues Clément, Quinlan and Jean-Milot.
The project provides for up to 575 private housing units in buildings of 3 to 6 storeys, a parcel of land set aside for about 130 non-market housing units, and at least 410 m² of commercial space.
Heights are regulated: 6 storeys on avenue Lafleur, 4 storeys plus a setback on rue Quinlan, 3 storeys on rue Clément.

The developer will have to create a 2,500 m² urban wooded area, an 800 m² civic square, a 500 m² urban vegetable garden, a 500 m² play area, and a central walkway reserved for active transportation, waste collection and emergency vehicles.

As for parking: 98% of spaces underground (0.5 space per housing unit), 10% with electric charging stations, 100% pre-wired, 5% for visitors, one bicycle space per housing unit, and only 4 driveway entrances.
The project departs from several by-laws (demolition, subdivision, zoning, PIIA) with respect to lot area, setbacks, height, uses and the number of housing units.
Next steps: adoption of the first draft on May 4, 2026, and public consultation on May 27, 2026; the project may be subject to a referendum.
The borough of LaSalle is exempting the building at 1100, rue Ducas (the CIMME) from adding 14 additional parking spaces.
These spaces would normally be required because the inside of the building is expanding by 650 m², at a rate of one space per 45 m² of floor area.
The building takes up almost the entire lot: according to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, no additional space can physically be added there.
A parking-sharing agreement between Cégep André-Laurendeau and the CIMME, already in effect, has been adapted to absorb the additional needs.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on March 11, 2026, finding in particular that the by-law would cause serious harm to the applicant.
The site, built in 1999, houses an educational institution and offices, near the canal de l'Aqueduc and parc Angrignon.
The borough of LaSalle is approving the plans to transform a single-family home from 1944 located at 7611, rue Broadway, at the corner of 3e Avenue, in the Village des Rapides area.
The building will be raised and its foundation rebuilt: its height will go from 8.0 m to 8.76 m, without changing its location on the lot.
The work visible from the street includes a covered front porch and the addition of a window on the second floor at the front.
At the back, a new basement access will be created, the rear porch rebuilt and six windows added in the foundation.
Other planned work: partial roof repair after the removal of a chimney and replacement of the siding on the west side wall on the second floor.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 8, 2026; the permit application had been filed on October 21, 2024.
The borough of LaSalle is allowing the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal to hold a charity car wash on Saturday, May 16, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
The event will take place in part of the parking lot at Complexe Angrignon, in front of the Canadian Tire and Michaels stores, at 2221, boulevard Angrignon.
The money raised will go to the fondation Enfant Soleil.
The borough expects 500 to 700 people over the course of the day.
The request, received on April 13, 2026, came with the signed authorization of the building's owner and a site layout plan.
The borough of LaSalle is allowing the Club de Soccer Rapides de LaSalle to sell items on public property in front of the business at 7628, rue Centrale, on May 9 and 10, 2026, for Mother's Day.
A temporary trailer will be set up in front of the business Bombshell Bar à Beauté during the event.
The products for sale: three kinds of smoothies, two specialty coffees, two iced coffees and flower bouquets.
The profits will go to the soccer club's activities; the business is acting as a logistics partner.
The borough is issuing a permit to occupy public property in its own name, free of charge.
By-law 2183 normally prohibits selling in public squares, but the borough council can allow it during events.
The borough of LaSalle is renewing its "LaSalle vert demain" funding program and is putting $50,000 into it for 2026.
The money will fund projects by organizations that speed up the ecological transition and that raise public awareness, within the territory of LaSalle.
Only non-profit organizations recognized by the borough and school organizations active in LaSalle may submit a project; the invitation is sent by email.
To be selected, a project must include an awareness component and be judged feasible — these two criteria are pass-or-fail.

Timeline: call for projects from June 3 to July 5, 2026, selection of projects at the council meeting in September 2026, carrying out the projects until September 2027, review report in the fall of 2027.
An internal borough committee assesses the projects; the borough may select none of them if the criteria are not met.
The program had already paid out $50,000 to two organizations in 2025.

The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the company DKI Refexio to install and maintain, for one year, installations around the LaSalle-Coke crane, an industrial relic built between 1914 and 1916 near the canal de Lachine.
The project includes a work of art evoking a boat carrying coke, installed to the left of the crane on land belonging to Parcs Canada.
A temporary canvas will be placed on the DKI Refexio building, at 6652, rue Saint-Patrick, to evoke the appearance of the former industrial building.
The crane and the canvas will be lit up with architectural lighting.

The launch is planned for June 11, 2026, with the work to be carried out in the summer of 2026; the installation could stay in place for more than one year depending on the authorizations and the condition of the site.
The project was selected through a call for projects by PME MTL Grand Sud-Ouest with Parcs Canada, as part of the 200th anniversary of the canal de Lachine.
No budget impact for the borough.
The borough of LaSalle is requiring the owners of several lots to cut tall grass and remove harmful materials on their property.
If an owner does not do the work, the borough will have it done in their place and at their expense.

The addresses involved include 113, rue Larente, 8786, rue Gloria, 1594, rue Rancourt, 207, 9e Avenue, 7 and 15, 7e Avenue, 424, 75e Avenue, 8215, rue Mongeau and 1358, rue Serre, as well as six lots with no address.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain et des services aux entreprises is mandated to have the lots cleaned up if needed and to dispose of the harmful materials.
The City must send a notice to the owner before stepping in to do the work in their place, as required by the Charter of Ville de Montréal.
The LaSalle borough is amending its nuisance by-law to regulate noise produced by vehicles.
The change comes from a request by the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal, to allow police officers from poste de quartier 13 to issue statements of offence in cases of excessive noise.
The noises covered include banging, the engine, a siren, the radio, squealing tires, the exhaust system and the transporting of scrap metal.
The by-law adds penalties specific to these vehicle noise offences.
The document states that similar amendments were adopted by other boroughs in the fall of 2025.
Planned timeline: adoption of the by-law on July 6, 2026 and coming into force in July 2026.

The borough of LaSalle is removing two sections about vehicle noise from its by-law on traffic and public safety: section 289 "Bruit de radio" (radio noise) and section 290 "Bruit de ferrailles" (scrap metal noise).
These rules are covered in another by-law (LAS-0137-3), which adds provisions on noise made by a vehicle, including the radio and scrap metal noises. Removing them therefore avoids a duplication.

The changes come from a request by the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal, so that police officers from poste de quartier 13 can issue statements of offence in cases of excessive noise coming from vehicles.
Other boroughs adopted similar amendments in the fall of 2025.
Schedule: notice of motion and adoption of the draft by-law on June 17, 2026, adoption of the by-law on July 6, 2026, coming into force in July 2026.
The LaSalle borough is requiring the owners of 13 lots to cut tall grass and clear away harmful materials on their property.
If an owner does not do the work, the borough will have it done in their place and at the owner's expense.
Addresses affected: 315, 1re Avenue; 8241 and 8249, rue Mongeau; 7691, rue Édouard; 7899, rue Bonnier; 8786, rue Gloria.
Vacant lots affected: the Airlie/90e Avenue area, boulevard De La Vérendrye (two lots), boulevard Newman, rue Cordner and rue Shevchenko.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain et des services aux entreprises is mandated to have the lots cleaned up if needed and to dispose of the materials.
A notice must be sent to the owner before the borough can act in their place.
A decision of the same type had already been made previously by the borough council.
The borough of LaSalle is doubling the pay for the citizen members of its planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme): from $50 to $100 per meeting, starting July 8, 2026.
The six meetings held from January to June 2026 are still paid at $50; the pay is issued in January following the end of the one-year term.
The $50 rate had been in place for nearly eight years; the borough says it is bringing itself in line with the average of the other boroughs, estimated at $102.
Members receive the same amount when the committee sits as a demolition committee, but only one payment is made if both meetings take place on the same day.
