The approved spending for 2026 is $5,400: $1,800 for the first half of the year and $3,600 for the second, for 6 members.
The borough of LaSalle is approving the plans to expand a house at 205, 6e Avenue, in the Village des Rapides area.
The project adds an attached garage in the right side yard, with a cold room underneath.
In the back yard, the work includes a ground-floor patio, two new patio doors on the upper floor and a balcony.
The garage will be lower than the house and slightly set back; the front facade stays unchanged.
The new exterior finishes will be vertical aluminum siding in brown "Coffee Brown" and horizontal white wood clapboard.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 10, 2026.
The approval allows the issuing of the expansion permit applied for on November 19, 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is approving a minor exemption for a semi-detached single-family home at 118, 68e Avenue.
The home's side setback measures 1.14 metres, while the zoning by-law requires 1.50 metres; the exemption regularizes this 36 cm gap.
According to the document, the gap comes from a mistake made during construction, while the work was being done with a valid building permit.
Demolishing the side wall to correct the gap is considered disproportionate in the document, given that the construction is recent.
Fire shutters will be installed to protect an unprotected opening on the left side facade, as required by the Building Code.
The applicant tried to reach an agreement with the neighbours, with no result to date.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a majority favourable opinion on June 10, 2026.
The borough of LaSalle is approving the plans to set up a medical clinic in an existing unit at Carrefour Angrignon, at 7077, boulevard Newman.
The unit in question (05004) was previously occupied by the Économax store.
The work includes new windows on the front, rebuilding of the main entrance (the canopy will be changed and the columns restored) and replacement of the sign.
Planters will be added near the entrance, and the existing planted areas along the side walls will be kept and improved.
Inside: examination rooms, triage areas, offices and waiting areas.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 10, 2026; the approval clears the way for the permit to be issued (application 3003652415).

The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the construction of six multi-family residential buildings on a site of about 47,000 m² between rue Wanklyn and rue Jean-Milot, bordered by route 138 to the east.
The project provides for up to 470 private housing units in buildings of three to six storeys, plus a lot set aside for about 130 non-market housing units.
A public "sponge park" of about 3,900 m², a wooded buffer zone (400 trees/ha) and a noise-barrier berm along route 138 are planned.
The conditions require at least 60% masonry on the facades, 30% green roofs and all parking underground (0.5 space per housing unit, 10% with electric charging stations).
A new one-way street with two bike lanes connected to the piste Cherry and parking with electric charging stations will be built.
The project departs from several by-laws (zoning, subdivision, social housing, PIIA) regarding height, density, setbacks, the number of housing units and the area to be transferred.
Next steps: public consultation on July 29, second draft on August 3, referendum approval period in August, final adoption on September 14.
The borough of LaSalle is approving work at Cégep André-Laurendeau, at 1111, rue Lapierre, with a view to issuing an authorization certificate.
The project installs a new electrical service entrance in the back yard, with a generator placed in the parking lot, and adds a rooftop shed to house mechanical equipment.
An architectural screen and a plant screen will conceal the equipment; two parking spaces will be moved.
The landscaping plans call for vegetation and a vegetated swale to manage rainwater on a site with a great deal of paved surface.
The existing generator is being removed and replaced outside, as there is not enough space inside the building.
The planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 10, 2026, finding the project consistent with the objectives of the by-law on heritage areas and buildings.
The borough of LaSalle is being asked to approve a minor exemption for the industrial building at 7070, rue Saint-Patrick.
The exemption allows a left side setback of 3.93 m at the foundation wall, instead of the minimum of 4 m required by the zoning by-law.
It also allows a grease trap installed 1.77 m from the side lot line, instead of the minimum of 2 m.
Both discrepancies already exist: they result from expansion work authorized in 2021 and noted in a location certificate.
The request is only meant to bring the situation into compliance, with no other changes to the site.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 10, 2026.
The borough of LaSalle is appointing Andréanne Leblanc as a permanent resident member of its Comité consultatif d'urbanisme (CCU), effective July 6, 2026.
She had been a substitute member since January 14, 2026: only her status changes.
Her first term ends January 13, 2028, as originally planned.
LaSalle's CCU has six residents (including one substitute) and two council members; resident terms last two years and can be renewed up to four times.
The borough of LaSalle is renewing the mandate of a resident member of its Comité consultatif d'urbanisme (CCU), the committee that advises the council on planning matters.
This is a 4th two-year mandate, from August 6, 2026 to August 5, 2028, starting at the CCU meeting of September 2026.
Under the borough by-law, resident members sit for two years at a time, for a maximum of four consecutive mandates: this is therefore the last mandate allowed.
LaSalle's CCU has six residents (at least three of whom have expertise in urban planning, engineering, architecture or heritage), one substitute member and two elected officials.
No amount of money is tied to this decision.
The borough of LaSalle is amending its zoning by-law to remove everything related to public property (streets, sidewalks), since zoning should cover only private property.
Hedges and fences will now have to be located on private land.
Semi-circular driveways will no longer be allowed for housing (uses h1, h2 and h3), and the rules on the slope of vehicle access ramps are repealed.

The rules on pools and spas, property upkeep, connection to the public network and water drainage are being taken out of zoning: they fall under other by-laws (nuisances LAS-0137, provincial by-law on residential pools).
The deadline for landscaping open spaces is removed from zoning and now refers to the Règlement sur la construction et la transformation de bâtiments 11-018.
Commercial antennas may no longer be installed on public property under this by-law.
Timeline: draft adopted on July 6, 2026, public consultation on July 29, adoption on August 3 and coming into force in August 2026.
The LaSalle borough council confirms the authorization of the show "Cirque Paranormal", presented by Cirque Italia, from July 3 to 6, 2026.
The event will be held in the Carrefour Angrignon parking lot, with the written consent of the building's owner.
The request was received on June 18, 2026, and the authorization had already been granted before it came to council.
The organizer must maintain civil liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 for the entire duration of the event.
A special event request was filed with the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal.
A circus had already been authorized at the same location from June 26 to July 6, 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the "Cirque 100% Humain" show by Nouveau Cirque Mondial (Cirque Productions LLC) in the Carrefour Angrignon parking lot.
The event will run from August 27 to September 6, 2026.
The application was filed on June 18, 2026 and includes the signed authorization from the building's owner and a site layout plan.
The promoter has submitted a special event application to the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal.
Civil liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 must be in force for the entire duration of the event.
A circus had already been authorized at the same location from June 26 to July 6, 2025 (Cirque de Paris).
The borough of LaSalle is collecting $396,760 from the developer of a 120-unit building planned at 2051, rue Lapierre.
This money must be used to create, maintain and improve parks, playgrounds and natural spaces in the borough.
The City is requiring money rather than land, having determined that handing over land is not warranted given the location and the area of the lot.
The calculation is based on a site value of $4,578,000 assessed by the firm PCG Carmon (report dated June 26, 2026): 10% of that value, divided over 120 units, applied to 104 units.
The 16 units with 3 bedrooms or more are excluded from the calculation; the project does not include any social or affordable housing.
Payment must be made before the construction permit is issued (application 3003643302).
The borough of LaSalle is approving the plans to enlarge the single-family home at 182, terrasse Ouellette.
The addition of about 28 m² will be built in the side yard, with a height lower than the existing building and the new section set back.
The owners also plan a deck, a staircase and an in-ground pool with a secured enclosure in the back yard; this work is not subject to the by-law on site plans.
The materials and colours of the addition must blend in with the house, which was built in 1972.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on July 8, 2026.
The approval paves the way for issuing the enlargement permit applied for on March 12, 2026.

The borough of LaSalle is accepting $40,180.70 from Canac Immobilier inc. as a parks contribution, as part of the subdivision of the site at the corner of boulevard Newman and rue Léger (the current Super C and a Banque Laurentienne).
The developer also commits to transferring to the City, free of charge, a 5,292 m² piece of land for a neighbourhood park, within 96 months after the first building permit.
Together, the land (9.92%) and the money (0.08%) add up to the 10% of the site's value required by by-law 17-055; the portion of the site concerned was valued at $50,225,875.
A bank guarantee of $4,982,406.80 will be required from the developer to secure the transfer of the park, with obligations to decontaminate, backfill and level the land.
The project provides for two mixed-use buildings of 16 storeys and 697 housing units at 7333 and 7401-7475, boulevard Newman, in the first phase; about 11 lots will be created in total.
Two lots intended for non-market housing, totalling 6,782 m², will be transferred to the City under a separate agreement and are excluded from the calculation of the contribution.
Next steps: receipt of the guarantee, collection of the money, issuance of the subdivision permit and the two building permits, then transfer of the park at a later date.
The borough of LaSalle wants to remove the limit on the number of terms that citizen members of its comité consultatif d'urbanisme (CCU) can serve.
A term still lasts two years, but it can now be renewed without limit.
The CCU reviews applications relating to urban planning, land development and demolition, then makes recommendations to the borough council.
The borough cites the continuity of its work and the need to retain the expertise built up by members.
Planned steps: notice of motion on August 3, 2026, adoption of the by-law on September 14, 2026, public notice of coming into force in September 2026.
No additional financial impact for the borough.
The borough of LaSalle is joining the "Bee City" program of the organization Bee City Canada and will pay $400 per year, an amount adjusted each year according to the organization's rates.
LaSalle would become the second Montréal borough to hold this designation.
The program requires concrete actions: creating habitats for pollinators, educating residents and marking international pollinator week (the third week of June).
Among other things, the borough is committing to create new native plant gardens, install educational signs, give out nectar-producing plants during its green day and renaturalize shoreline areas.
Planned timeline: committee created in September 2026, registration in the program in October-November 2026, planning in January 2027 and start of actions in April-May 2027.
The initiative stems from measure 13 of the borough's Plan local de transition écologique 2025-2030.
The Ville-Marie borough is awarding Urbex Construction inc., the lowest compliant bidder out of 4, the replacement or repair of synthetic surfaces in three parks, for $209,275.54 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $232,203.09, which covers the contract, $20,927.55 in contingencies and $2,000 in incidental costs (construction site signs).
At parc des Vétérans, the rubber protective surfaces of the two play areas (2-5 years and 5-12 years), which are cracked, sunken or missing in places, will be replaced.
At parc Raymond-Blain, the rubber surface of the training area, worn down by heavy use, will be replaced with a synthetic mat.
At parc Berthier, the City will remove the two musical instruments — taken out of service in the summer of 2025 after complaints about noise at night — and redo the rubber surface underneath them.
Funding comes 68% from the borough's capital works program, 29% from the park fund ($62,337.72 net of tax rebates) and 3% from the operating budget.
Work is planned for August and September 2026; notices will be handed out to nearby residents and signs will be put up on site before it starts.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing four parishes to hold bazaars and garage sales in 2026 to raise funds.
Paroisse Sainte-Catherine-Labouré (9700, rue Clément): May 29-30 and October 23-24, 2026.
Paroisse Madre Dei Cristiani (7900, Turley): June 4-6 and October 1-3, 2026.
Paroisse Saint-Jean-de-Brébeuf (7777, rue George): June 6-7, September 26-27 and November 6-7, 2026.
Paroisse Saint-Nazaire (111, avenue Bélanger): May 1-2 and October 2-3, 2026.
These events are being held outside the periods set out in the by-law, which is why an exceptional authorization is needed.
Religious organizations are no longer recognized by the borough, but a grandfather clause keeps the same services available to them.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $11,400 to three organizations for public events in 2026.

Centre Prisme (Accueil pour Immigrants et Réfugiés du Sud-Ouest de Montréal) is receiving $4,000 for Québec culture week, from March 2 to 6, 2026, at the Centre Henri Lemieux, at Espace Prismez-vous and during a visit to the Érablière Constantin in Saint-Eustache.
Association Messinese de Montréal inc. is receiving $4,000 for a free concert with an Italian orchestra, on October 27, 2026 at the Théâtre Desjardins.
Bienvenue à l'Immigrant is receiving $3,400 for its intercultural festival, on May 29 in an indoor hall (location to be determined) and on May 30, 2026 at parc Ouellette.
All three events are free and open to everyone in LaSalle.
The grants come from the operating budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social and cover at most 70% of the budget of each event.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $1,350 to three organizations to produce their souvenir programs.
Breakdown: $350 to Club âge d'or Ste-Catherine-Labouré, $500 to Association Messinese de Montréal inc. and $500 to Club d'âge d'or Falchi de LaSalle inc.
Club Ste-Catherine-Labouré will use the money for its booklet and summary of the year's activities.
Association Messinese will produce a souvenir album connected to the concert held on April 19, 2026 at école Cavelier de LaSalle.
Club Falchi will produce a souvenir album for the club's 50th anniversary gala, planned for November 14, 2026.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under the "Contribution à d'autres organismes" (contribution to other organizations) line.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $8,166 to three organizations for public events in 2026.
Breakdown: $4,000 to Association Cameroon Goodwillers de Montréal, $2,848 to Centre d'accompagnement KEDA (CED'AKEDA) and $1,318 to Organisation familiale des besoins spéciaux de Montréal.
On July 5, 2026, at parc Lacharité: a summer celebration with a picnic, games and awareness activities.
On July 11, 2026, at parc Lacharité: a family and integration day, with games and talks on the integration of newcomers and on resolving family conflicts.
On August 1, 2026, at parc Ménard: an inclusive and intercultural fair highlighting youth entrepreneurship.
The grants do not exceed 70% of each event's budget and are paid out of the operating budget of the Direction culture, sports, loisirs et développement social.
The borough of LaSalle confirms a $500 contribution to Association Messinese de Montréal inc.
The money is used to buy an ad in the souvenir program of the 29th edition of its benefit golf tournament.
The tournament already took place on May 31, 2026; the decision ratifies an authorization given after the fact.
The funds raised go to the Fondation de l'Hôpital de Montréal pour enfants.
The expense is taken from the borough council budget set aside for contributions to other organizations.
The borough had paid the same amount in 2025 for the 28th edition.
The borough of LaSalle is changing the dates of the bazaars and fundraising activities authorized for 2026 for four parishes and organizations.
The only real change: the Madre Dei Cristiani parish (7900, rue Turley) will hold its bazaar from July 2 to 4, 2026, in addition to October 1 to 3, 2026.
The other dates stay the same: Sainte-Catherine-Labouré (9700, rue Clément) on May 29-30 and October 23-24, 2026.
Saint-Jean-de-Brébeuf (7777, rue George): June 6-7, September 26-27 and November 6-7, 2026.
Saint-Nazaire (111, avenue Bélanger): May 1-2 and October 2-3, 2026.
Religious organizations are no longer recognized by the borough, but a grandfather clause lets them keep the same services.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the organization Nutri-Centre LaSalle to sell fresh fruits and vegetables at parc Ménard on July 30 and August 21, 2026.
Both dates may change depending on the weather.
The market is part of a summer project at parc Ménard that has been coordinated for the past three years by the Table de développement social de LaSalle, along with community organizations.
According to the document, residents of the area will have access to fresh fruits and vegetables and to culinary discovery activities.
The borough states that the area has a population living with issues of vulnerability and precariousness.
Nutri-Centre LaSalle is recognized as an "associate" under the Politique de reconnaissance et de soutien des OBNL de LaSalle.
Similar authorizations had been granted for dates in 2024 and 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $16,974 to five organizations for public events that are free or open to the public in July and August 2026.

Breakdown: $4,000 to Accueil pour Immigrants et Réfugiés du Sud-Ouest de Montréal Centre Prisme, $3,900 to Momo Elite, $3,400 to the Table de développement social de LaSalle, $3,400 to the Communauté de Swahili du Canada and $2,274 to the Club d'âge d'or Falchi de LaSalle.

The events: a festival of artistic expression from here and elsewhere, August 11 to 15 at the Centre culturel Henri Lemieux; Festival des savoirs partagés, August 19 to 21 at parc Ménard; Italfest, August 8 at parc Ouellette.
Also: a Swahili culture festival on July 25 at parc Marie-Claire-Kirkland-Casgrain and a celebration of Afro-Canadian culture on July 18 at parc Lacharité.
Each grant covers at most 70% of the event's budget, according to the criteria of the support program for LaSalle events.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Direction culture, sports, loisirs et développement social.
The borough of LaSalle is allowing the Table de développement social de LaSalle to hold a party on August 21, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at parc Ménard.
This is the closing party for the Shack communautaire project: family activities, a show and food distribution are planned.
The organization will be able to get a permit from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux to sell alcoholic drinks on site.
The organizers must not serve any alcohol to minors and must follow hygiene rules for preparing and selling food.
The borough is granting a full exemption from fees ($0) and is covering the logistical support within its operating budget.
A similar authorization had been granted for a party at the same park on August 15, 2025.
The borough of Ville-Marie agrees that the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie will continue to maintain its street lighting, traffic signals and road markings in 2026.
The EESM division of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie has been doing this work since 2004 for the nine boroughs that came from the former Ville de Montréal.
The service covers, among other things, the marking of lines, pedestrian crossings, bike paths and speed bumps, as well as traffic lights and street lamps.
Ville-Marie remains responsible for keeping light fixtures, traffic lights and signs accessible and clear (pruning, obstacles, wasp nests).
The cost of this internal service is already included in the borough's 2026 operating budget; no amount is specified in the decision summary.
According to the document, a refusal would have forced Ville-Marie to turn to outside suppliers for this work.
The borough of Ville-Marie will make 13 streets pedestrian-only during the summer of 2026, according to a schedule and types of pedestrianization detailed in an appendix.
Vehicle traffic will be banned on these stretches of street, except for delivery vehicles during the hours set out in the appendix.
Occupancy of public property is allowed, in particular to set up sidewalk cafés.

Background music played by partner organizations will be allowed from noon to 9 p.m. on weekdays and from 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. on weekends and holidays, up to 75 dBA and 90 dBC measured at 5 m; megaphones remain banned except for safety purposes.
Bicycles, skateboards and inline skates will be banned on the pedestrian streets, except for police officers, emergency services, the promoter's maintenance staff and City employees.

Painting on the ground will be allowed, approved in advance by the Direction de l'aménagement urbain et de la mobilité; those responsible will have to remove it at the end and leave a 60 cm passage for pedestrians while the work is underway.
The ordinances take effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir; the borough still has to approve the programming for each pedestrianization.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing some downtown sidewalk cafés to stay open until 3 a.m., instead of 11 p.m., for the summer 2026 season.

The extension applies on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays until October 10, 2026, plus certain holidays (Patriotes, Saint-Jean, Canada Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving) and events such as the Loto-Québec fireworks and the UCI Road World Championships (September 19 to 27).
The streets covered include Sainte-Catherine Est and Ouest, Saint-Denis, Peel, Crescent, Bishop, Mackay, De la Montagne, Sherbrooke and about fifteen other downtown stretches.
Sainte-Catherine Est, between Saint-Hubert and Papineau, also gets the weekday evenings of Fierté Montréal (July 30 to August 9).
Food and alcoholic drinks may be sold during these hours, but alcohol must be served and consumed only on the terrace.
The borough cites economic development and the revitalization of downtown to increase foot traffic on commercial streets.
Sidewalk café permits take effect on April 15, 2026; the ordinance takes effect when a notice is published in Le Devoir.
Ville-Marie is adjusting the dates of three summer pedestrianization projects already adopted on March 10, 2026.
Rue du Village (SDC): pedestrianization from May 11 to October 23, 2026, instead of May 5 to October 22.
Vieux-Montréal: from April 14 to October 30, 2026, which is one day less than the original schedule.
Pointe-à-Callière area: from June 2 to September 9, 2026, instead of ending on September 2.
Painting on the roadway is now allowed in the Village area, which was not planned at the start.
The 2026 season includes 13 pedestrian streets in the borough, where vehicle traffic is prohibited (with exceptions) and the occupation of public property is authorized for sidewalk cafés.
The ordinances also cover noise from outdoor sound equipment and the movement of bicycles, skateboards and skates on pedestrian streets.
The Ville-Marie borough is making right turns mandatory in the curb lane of the eastern approach to the intersection of boulevard René-Lévesque and rue Parthenais.
The eastern approach will have three lanes: one where turning right is mandatory and two where drivers must go straight ahead.
A traffic light for cyclists and a bike crossing will be added, along with new timing for the vehicle traffic light.
The City points to a collision that happened at this location, poor visibility, and conflicts between turning cars and cyclists on the Route verte who are going straight ahead.
The signage, pavement marking and traffic light work is planned for the summer of 2026.
The borough is paying for the pavement marking and the signs; the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité is covering the cyclist traffic light and the new timing.
The order takes effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Ville-Marie is lowering the speed limit to 20 km/h on rue Saint-Paul Ouest, between boulevard Saint-Laurent and rue Saint-François-Xavier.
This stretch officially becomes a "shared street," where the different modes of travel coexist.
The measure applies once the redevelopment work on lot 3A is finished, with delivery expected in July 2026.
The redevelopment includes widened and lowered sidewalks, the end of on-street parking, and short-term spaces reserved for commercial deliveries.
The rebuilding of rue Saint-Paul, under way since 2014, ends with this stretch.
A neighbouring stretch, between place Jacques-Cartier and boulevard Saint-Laurent, had already been limited to 20 km/h since 2020.
The order comes into force on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir; the City must also pay for the replacement of the road signs.
The Ville-Marie borough is making left turns mandatory in the left lane for vehicles arriving from the east at the intersection of boulevard De Maisonneuve and rue D'Iberville.
The new layout provides for three westbound lanes: one for left turns and two where drivers must continue straight ahead.
A traffic light reserved for cyclists will be installed, because left turns cross the two-way bike path.
Counts by the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité recorded about 80 left turns per hour during the morning rush hour and 150 during the afternoon rush hour.
The pavement marking, signage and traffic light work is planned for the summer of 2026, with a 30-day "New signage" notice.
The borough is paying for the pavement marking and the signs; the Division de l'innovation et gestion des déplacements is paying for the cyclist light and the reprogramming.
The order comes into force on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir and will be sent to the SPVM.
The City is releasing $101,079.87 (net of rebates) from its contaminated soil reserve to pay for professional services tied to a project at parc Arthur-Therrien, in Verdun.
The amount is split between the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité ($72,777.50) and the Service de l'Espace pour la vie, des grands parcs et du Mont-Royal ($28,302.36).

The money will be used to prepare the plans and specifications and to follow up on an authorization request to the ministère de l'Environnement du Québec; the contract goes to the firm Rousseau Lefebvre inc.

The project involves removing an asphalt area (a former marina parking lot, with contaminated soil containing traces of asbestos) to create an aquatic environment of about 1800 m² along 120 metres of shoreline, east of the plage urbaine de Verdun.
This new fish habitat makes up for losses caused by the new pont Jacques-Bizard, riprap work at parc de la Promenade-Bellerive and the development of the Vague-à-Guy at the Rapides-de-Lachine.
Expected timeline: plans and specifications and ministerial authorization in 2026, work from September 2027 to June 2028, warranty until June 2029.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city and frees up funds from other loan programs for other projects.
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $375,500 to the Société de développement commercial du Village to make rue Sainte-Catherine Est pedestrian-only in 2026.
The street will be closed to traffic between rue Saint-Hubert and rue Papineau, from May 15 to October 23, 2026.
The money will go toward the installations (greening, furniture, lighting, public art), entertainment, cleanliness and communications.
The program includes ongoing entertainment, roving performances, 7 commercial fairs and partnerships with Fierté Montréal, Montréal Complètement Cirque and Festival Fetish Weekend.
The amount comes entirely from the City's Service du développement économique (the $150M Réflexe agreement), transferred to the borough.
The payment will be made in two steps: 75% after the council's decision, and the balance within 30 business days after the required documents are submitted.
The contribution depends on the ordinances related to the pedestrian-only streets being adopted by the borough council in April 2026.
The Outremont borough is awarding Les Entreprises P.N.P. inc. the landscaping redevelopment of place Marcelle-Ferron, for $429,214.33 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $600,900.07: the contract, plus $85,842.87 in contingencies and $85,842.87 in incidental costs (management of contaminated water and soil).
Funding comes from the participatory budget edition 2 ($543,499.20), the participatory budget edition 1 "De l'eau dans ta gourde!" ($6,542) and the borough's investment program ($50,858.87).
The work is located between avenue Bernard and parc Saint-Viateur: widening of sidewalks, concrete curbs and pavers, and bases for street furniture.
Three rain gardens, two catch basins, one storm sewer manhole and new storm sewer pipes will be used to capture runoff water.
A new connection to the avenue Bernard water main will supply a drinking fountain.
Eight companies submitted bids out of eleven that took out the tender documents; the winning bid is 16.6% below the estimate.
The borough of Outremont is awarding URBEX CONSTRUCTION INC. the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, at the corner of avenue Lajoie and avenue Dunlop.
The total authorized spending comes to $800,416.17 including taxes: $571,725.83 for the contract, $114,345.17 in contingencies and $114,345.17 in incidental costs.
Funding comes from the City's Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux ($762,464.81) and from the borough's capital works program ($37,951.36).
Work planned at the chalet: adding a toilet on the ground floor, bringing it up to universal accessibility standards, replacing doors, waterproofing the rooftop terrace and electromechanical work.
Outdoor work planned: redeveloping the paths, water retention, planting vegetation and rock fills, with universal accessibility.
The public call for tenders received 7 bids; URBEX submitted the lowest one, 22.3% below the professional estimate of $734,347.23.
The City is amending its RénoPlex program, which subsidizes renovations of residential buildings with 1 to 5 units.

Subsidy amounts are being revised: an increase of about 3% for work related to flooding and water infiltration (already indexed in 2024), and of nearly 30% for other work, which has not been revised since 2021.
The flat-rate amounts are meant to cover about 40% of the actual cost of anti-flooding work and 30% of other work.
A new flat rate is being added: the metal backwater barrier with a fixed section, a watertight barrier installed in front of a door or a garage. Temporary and inflatable devices are excluded.
The by-law specifies that the executive committee will be able, by order, to add or adjust flat rates, their technical requirements and their amounts.
No additional spending: the changes fit within the RénoPlex envelope already provided for in the 2026 budget.
Planned timeline: reading at city council on May 11, 2026 and adoption on June 15, 2026.
The executive committee is updating the rent ceilings for the Réno logement abordable program, which funds renovations in buildings with 6 or more units.
To be eligible, a building must rent at least one third of its units at a rent equal to or below the ceiling set for its borough.
The new ceilings are set borough by borough, by unit type (room, studio, 1, 2, 3+ bedrooms): for example, $860 for a 1-bedroom in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, $1,290 in Ville-Marie.
A second table sets lower rents that qualify for an enhanced subsidy (80% of the median rent, compared with 95% for basic eligibility).
The ceilings are based on CMHC median rent data from October 2025, for buildings built before 2005.
Recognized heating costs are indexed: from $60 for a room to $90 for a 3-bedroom or larger unit.
The City says the update prevents rising rents from making buildings ineligible, and that it has no budget impact.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $8,000 to the Association d'entraide Le Chaînon for the Carnaval hivernal de Milton-Parc 2026.
The event will take place on February 21, 2026 in the Milton-Parc area.
On the program: ice and snow sculpture, collective mitten knitting, craft workshops, an exhibition and an introduction to Indigenous art, family activities and slides.
Half of the money comes from the budget of the Division du développement social et des événements ($4,000) and half from the councillors' office discretionary fund ($4,000).
The carnival, started by Poste de quartier 38, also brings together Open Door, the Association des commerçants de Milton-Parc and the Association récréative de Milton-Parc.
The borough is approving an agreement setting out the payment conditions and will follow up on the project.
The Le Plateau-Mont-Royal borough council authorizes a public event to be held on public property (streets, parks, public squares), with the locations and times listed in an appendix to the file.
This is a single event, already held or under way, which the council is approving after the fact.
The borough allows sound to be broadcast outdoors during the event, despite the noise by-law.
It also allows the sale of promotional items, food and drinks, with or without alcohol, on site.
The costs and risks of the event are borne by the promoter, who must insure the Ville as a co-insured party; the municipal support services are paid out of their current budgets.
The promoter must inform residents, in particular by posting street closures ten days in advance.
The borough states that events on public property are free and open to everyone.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $20,000 (all applicable taxes included) to the Festival international de musique POP Montréal for the Marché des possibles 2026.
The amount includes technical support and free rental for use of public property.
The event will take place in the Mile End area, from August 14 to September 27, 2026.
The programming is free to attend and interdisciplinary: poetry, dance, craft markets and music.
Set-up will take place from August 4 to 14 and take-down from September 27 to 30, 2026; the organization must submit its accountability report on October 30, 2026.
The borough had granted the same amount of $20,000 in 2022, 2023 and 2024.
The City is giving $543,812 to two organizations under its Plan économique 2030.
Startop is receiving $350,000 over three years to train and support women from cultural communities in the social economy (online training, cohorts in non-profit management, networking).

The Commission du développement économique des Premières Nations du Québec et du Labrador (CDEPNQL) is receiving $193,812 over two years to develop Indigenous entrepreneurship in the greater Montréal area.
The CDEPNQL project aims in particular at access to public and private markets, including registration in the supplier directory, and matchmaking with Montréal businesses.
The expense is covered 100% by the agglomeration, out of the $200M agreement with the MEIE (2025-2029).
The projects start as soon as the agreements are signed.

The City is amending its funding agreements with the six PME MTL organizations (Centre-Est, Centre-Ouest, Centre-Ville, Est-de-l'Île, Grand Sud-Ouest, Ouest-de-l'Île), which advise entrepreneurs on the island of Montréal.

The change affects only the year 2026: money is moved between two spending categories, management fees and salaries. The total envelope of $20,394,860 approved in January 2024 for 2024-2026 stays the same.
Examples of management fee adjustments: PME MTL Centre-Ville goes from $103,218 to $46,162, Est-de-l'Île from $86,642 to $180,393, Grand Sud-Ouest from $103,218 to $0.

The City explains these changes by the renewal of the Fonds Régions et Ruralité agreement with the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation, which imposes new caps on administrative spending as of April 1, 2026.
Five of the six hubs still have a shortfall to cover for their administrative expenses; this balance will be paid through the financial contribution agreement.
The addenda take effect on April 1, 2026. The City says there is no financial impact and no communications activity planned.
The City is lending the dock and the two footbridges at parc de la Promenade-Bellerive free of charge to the Autorité régionale de transport métropolitain (ARTM) to operate a river shuttle service.
The loan runs from May 1, 2026 to December 15, 2029, with no renewal clause and at no cost or fee ($0).
The ARTM pays, at its own expense, for installing, maintaining, dismantling and transporting the equipment, and manages access to the dock during operations.
The ARTM must return the equipment to the City in the same condition at the end of each season (2026 to 2029), except for normal wear and tear, and must cover any damage caused to public property.

The shuttle connects the park, located in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, to île Charron and Boucherville; the City reports more than 541,000 trips in 2025, an increase of more than 15% compared to 2024.
Without this agreement, the ARTM could not use the City's equipment and would have to stop operating the service point at the park as early as this summer.
An accountability report is planned at the end of each season.
City council is authorizing the transfer of the $5,000,000 balance accumulated by the Agence de mobilité durable in its former Fonds de réserve pour projets innovants.
This amount, built up at a rate of $1M per year from 2020 to 2024, will be paid into the Fonds de réserve pour fonctionnement provided for in the current agreement between the Ville and the Agence.
The former agreement required a usage plan to be submitted to the executive committee; the amounts will now be subject to the rules of the new agreement.
Use of the balance is permitted retroactively, as of the date the new agreement came into force.
The Ville states that the operation involves no cost, no municipal funds committed and no budget transfer: it is an internal reclassification within the Agence.
Next steps: accounting entries by the Service des finances and an update of the reserve tracking by the Agence.
The parking lot (autoparc 340) at the Complexe sportif Claude-Robillard is being removed from the list of lots managed by the Agence de mobilité durable.
The Agence will no longer handle its management, operation or maintenance: the City is taking back full responsibility for the lot.
This parking lot has been permanently free since March 4, 2026, a decision made by the executive committee in February 2026.
Since there are no longer any fees to set or collect, the City considers that keeping the lot in the agreement is no longer necessary.
The City must send a written notice to the Agence after the decision; the removal takes effect as of the executive committee's resolution.
The City states that this matter has no additional financial impact.
The City is giving $2,000 to SFT Montréal (Séminaire des Femmes en Transport de Montréal) to carry out its 2026 program of activities.
This is a first contribution from the City to this organization, paid only once, with no recurring character.
The money comes from the 2026 operating budget of the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité and is covered entirely by the central city.
The amount will be paid in a single payment within 30 days after the agreement is signed; any unused amount must be returned to the City.

The 2026 program includes a mentorship program, a networking breakfast on March 6, training on women's leadership in the spring, a field visit on May 27, a fundraiser in June, a signature event in the fall and the general meeting in December.
According to the document, the $2,000 represents 5% of the annual budget of the organization, which promotes the place of women in the transportation field.

The City is changing the status of a strip of land of no more than 270 m² (about 20% of the lot) on boulevard Monk, in the borough of Le Sud-Ouest: it is removing it from its public domain and transferring it to its private domain.

This land is part of an off-street municipal parking lot where the Agence de mobilité durable wants to build the "pôle de mobilité Monk" (car sharing, bike sharing, charging stations, features that make it easier to switch between modes of transportation).
The change is needed because the lot falls under the urban agglomeration, which prevents the City from investing money from its Ten-Year Capital Works Program in it.
The project is estimated at $3,273,565: $2,257,817 comes from the provincial OASIS grant, and the rest from the City ($802,983, including $140,000 for BIXI) and the Agence ($72,765).
The OASIS grant requires the project to be completed before 2028; a decision is being requested by June 2026 so that the work can take place in 2027.
The fire station and the bibliothèque Marie-Uguay stay on the remaining lot, with no change of status.
Next steps: subdividing the lot, filing the cadastral plan and creating the new lot.
The City is amending its agreement with the Agence de mobilité durable, the paramunicipal organization that manages parking on Montréal's territory.
From now on, the City will pay the Agence, each quarter during the year, a portion of the management fees provided for in the budget, based on its cash needs.
In return, the date of the annual transfer of net revenues that the Agence owes the City is moved up, and the calculation takes into account the amounts already paid during the year.
According to the decision summary, the overall amounts in the agreement do not change: the annual impact is neutral, only the payment schedule is modified.
The Agence's board of directors approved the addendum on May 14, 2026; it will come into force when both parties sign it.
The matter falls under city council and aims, according to the City, to avoid any interruption in the Agence's operations.
The City is making 384 parking spaces in parking lot 243, at parc Angrignon, free of charge for the event "Le Rendez-vous familial des Pompiers de Montréal 2026".
The free parking applies from Wednesday, July 8, 2026 at 8 a.m. to Sunday, July 12, 2026 at 5 p.m.

The event is organized by the Association des pompiers de Montréal; the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal will be there with vehicles, equipment and demonstrations, along with a "Firefit" sports competition.
The Agence de mobilité durable estimates the lost parking revenue at a maximum of $28,800 (before taxes), with the maximum daily rate being $15 per space.
The document notes a drop in the parking supply during the event, which could increase pressure on nearby spaces and traffic near the site.
No communications work is planned with the Service des communications et des affaires publiques.
City council agrees that the 19 boroughs will themselves carry out work in 2026 on streets that normally fall under the central city (arterial network).
The projects involved concern street layouts, bike paths and making places used by children, families and seniors safer.

Examples of planned work: speed bumps on avenue Davaar (Outremont), a bike link on Renaude-Lapointe (Anjou), a sidewalk on rue Sherbrooke between de Contrecoeur and Hector (Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve), redevelopment of boulevard Gouin (Pierrefonds-Roxboro).
Several projects target the areas around schools and daycares, notably in Saint-Léonard, Ville-Marie, Saint-Laurent, Montréal-Nord and Ahuntsic-Cartierville.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité is paying for the work out of its capital budgets (arterial street layout program, bike network, Vision Zéro).
The amounts authorized for 2026 range from about $221,000 to $2,099,750 per project; some projects are listed with no budget indicated.
The boroughs are carrying out the work because they have the construction expertise and the work sites are on their territory.

The City would reimburse $558,893.22, taxes included, to the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM) for work on the municipal building at 1835-1847, avenue Papineau, in Ville-Marie.
The City acquired the building by exercising its right of first refusal for social housing purposes; its management was entrusted to the SHDM.
The work covers the outdoor staircases (complete replacement), the ventilation systems and the building envelope, for a total of $415,175.
The SHDM must also bring the fire safety systems of the building's 33 rooms up to standard.
The net budget of $518,468.82 covers the work, contingencies, incidental costs and 5% in management fees for the SHDM ($23,728).
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration and financed through a loan by-law tied to the acquisition of buildings for social housing.
The Service says the work serves to keep the building in good condition and to maintain affordability for vulnerable populations.
The Ville-Marie borough is paying $33,600 to three organizations for urban agriculture projects in 2026.

The amounts: $12,200 to the Centre communautaire de loisirs Sainte-Catherine d'Alexandrie, $13,800 to the Corporation du Centre Jean-Claude-Malépart, and $7,600 to Direction Chrétienne inc. (Innovation Jeunes).
The projects include plots for growing food, gardening workshops, community kitchens and solidarity markets, with part of the harvest shared with the neighbourhood.
Nine projects were submitted during the call for projects held from October 16 to December 20, 2025; three were selected by a committee of three borough representatives.
The funding cannot exceed $20,000 per project, is not recurring and must be spent before December 31, 2026; the organization must fund at least 20% of the project's cost.
The projects start as of April 15, 2026, and follow-up reports are expected in January 2027.
The City is joining the group purchasing program of the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales (CAG) to buy computer network equipment, for a maximum of $12,014,887.50, taxes included.
The agreement lasts 24 months, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028; orders can only be placed after the file is approved.
The purchases cover five families of goods: switches, firewalls, routers, wireless equipment (Wi-Fi access points and controllers) and accessories such as modules and licences.
Goal: replace equipment that is nearing the end of its life and keep the networks used for municipal services running.
Installation, configuration and network design are not included and will have to be covered by separate contracts.
The CAG charges management fees of 1%, included in the price of the goods and services.
No budget is set aside in advance: each purchase will be paid out of the budgets of the Service des technologies de l'information, as needs arise.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is reallocating $27,048.36 in funds not spent in 2025 under the Prévention Montréal program.
The amount is split into $11,952.67 for stream 1 (development of children and youth in vulnerable situations) and $15,095.69 for stream 2 (urban safety prevention).
The money will be used in particular to fund projects run by the borough's teams in 2026.
The program targets children, young people under 30 and their families.
If the borough does not use these funds, it must return them to the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale.
The decision falls to the borough council, at the February 3, 2026 meeting.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is appointing one member of its council to represent it on the Conseil jeunesse local (local youth council).
The decision summary proposes councillor Gerlando Guarraggi, who would act as a mentor to the young members, without the right to vote.
Councillor Daphney Colin's term in this position ended on November 2, 2025.

The Conseil jeunesse is a non-partisan advisory body made up of 12 young people aged 12 to 25 with the right to vote, up to 5 replacement members, one public servant and one elected official; the borough mayor is a member by virtue of office.
Its role: to give opinions to the borough council on youth issues, carry out studies and organize activities.
No spending is attached to this decision.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is officially confirming the members of its Conseil jeunesse (youth council), for terms starting on May 5, 2026.
Twelve young people sit as regular members (with the right to vote) and five as relief members; the terms end either on May 4, 2027 or on May 2, 2028.
Four new relief members are taking office: Nida Arahman Frej, Gianluca Zirpolo, Jérémy Salvail and Rosalia Caruana.
The terms are staggered over two end dates so that only some of the members change each year.
To sit on the council, a person must be 12 to 25 years old as of September 30 and have lived in the borough or run a business there for at least one year.
The Conseil jeunesse is a non-partisan advisory body: it gives opinions to elected officials on issues affecting young people and can carry out studies or organize activities.
No spending is tied to this decision; the Conseil jeunesse's Montréal.ca page will be updated.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is receiving $1,515 from the Caisse Desjardins de Rivière-des-Prairies for the "Foire jeunesse de Rivière-des-Prairies".
The executive committee must adjust the City's 2026 operating budget to record this amount as both revenue and expenditure.
The Foire jeunesse will be held on November 14, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., at the Centre récréatif de Rivière-des-Prairies, for young people aged 12 to 25.
On the program: information booths from partners, hands-on activities, discussion spaces and a lunch-and-talk on mental health.
The money will be used to hand out promotional bags and to hold draws for participants.
The event is organized by the borough's Conseil jeunesse and is part of its 2025-2027 action plan.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing an expense of $148,272.91, taxes included, to dispose of the debris collected by street sweeping.
The contract goes to Recyclage Notre-Dame inc., whose site is located at 11400, avenue Racette, in Montréal-Nord, and runs until December 31, 2026.
The City expects to send up to 1,575 metric tonnes of fine sand, stone dust, dead leaves, paper and plastic there.
The price breaks down into $45.88 per tonne for disposal ($83,082.08) and $36.00 per tonne in government fees ($65,190.83).
Blue-collar workers from the Direction des travaux publics will transport the debris to the site themselves, where it will be weighed.
The expense is made through a master agreement reached by the City with this firm for the period from January 31, 2023 to January 30, 2027, and is paid out of the operating budget.
The City is merging its two assistance programs for businesses affected by major construction work into a single program, covering the entire agglomeration territory.
The program keeps two components: a flat-rate grant of $5,000 and assistance of up to $40,000 when the loss of gross profit exceeds 5%.
The assistance will be paid in two instalments, the first as soon as the basic documents are submitted, in order to shorten delays (currently an average of 150 days after filing).
Successive or simultaneous worksites lasting more than 3 months in the same area become eligible, instead of the 6-month threshold.
The program is extended to 2033 and covers work by the City, the related municipalities and the STM, in the areas designated by the executive committee.
The urban agglomeration council is setting aside an additional $24,500,000, bringing the program's budget to $26,300,000.
The executive committee will be able to designate the areas, set the work periods and adjust the amounts, the required documents and the program's end date.

The City is transferring two professional services agreements in architecture and engineering from the firm Affleck de la Riva s.e.n.c. to the new company Studio Affleck de la Riva inc., under the same conditions.
These agreements are used for various City real estate projects, including park projects, and were signed on December 21, 2023 for four years, with an option to extend for 12 months.
Initial value of the two contracts: $2,948,142.96 (lot 1) and $2,753,544.90 (lot 2), taxes included; about $1,786,479.91 and $2,031,370.30 remained as of May 12, 2026.
The City states that the transfer has no budget impact, since the same conditions apply.
The partners have incorporated a company and the former partnership is being dissolved; without this transfer, the continuity of services would be compromised.
The former and the new firm remain jointly and severally responsible for the services provided since the start of the contracts, including for any past errors.
The transfer takes effect on January 1, 2026, and any future transfer will require a new written agreement from the City.
The City is transferring four professional services contracts from the firm Affleck de la Riva s.e.n.c. to Studio Affleck de la Riva inc., under the same conditions.

The contracts concern the Cœur-Nomade library and cultural space (Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Montréal-Nord), the Espace Rivière library and maison de la culture (Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles), the rebuilding of the Théâtre Outremont and the renovation of the building at 2075, rue Plessis.
Remaining values in spring 2026: about $2,744,069.92 (Cœur-Nomade), $3,769,388.18 (Espace Rivière), $664,912.79 (Théâtre Outremont) and $805,365.45 (rue Plessis).
The City says the transfer has no impact on its budget, since the conditions remain identical.
Affleck de la Riva s.e.n.c. is in the process of being dissolved; according to the document, the transfer is necessary to avoid interrupting services.
The timelines already planned for the four projects remain unchanged.

The City is ending the 36-month contract awarded in February 2026 to Canadian Bearings ltd. to supply helmets, helmet accessories, visors and hearing protection to employees (lot 3 of call for tenders 25-21164).

Reason: after verification, a bidder that had been set aside for technical non-compliance was in fact offering a compliant item and had the lowest price. Canadian Bearings was therefore not the lowest compliant bidder.
The cancellation costs the City nothing: no purchases had yet been made under this contract.
A new public call for tenders will be launched for this protective equipment once the file is approved.
The decision rests with the urban agglomeration council; the master agreement entered into with Acklands-Grainger inc. under the same call for tenders is not affected.
The City is awarding 911 Pro inc. three contracts to supply and install emergency lights and related parts on 14 vehicles already purchased for the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal.
Total spending of $199,166.52, taxes included, including $33,194.42 set aside for contingencies (unforeseen costs).
Breakdown: $126,465.54 for 11 Ford Interceptors, $11,976.95 for one Chevrolet Blazer, $27,529.61 for one GMC Yukon and one Ford F-450.
911 Pro inc. was the lowest compliant bidder of the 7 bids received for public call for tenders 25-21212.
Deliveries range from 60 to 99 days after the purchase order, with a penalty of $50 per day of delay and a warranty of at least one year.
The spending is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration; the company's performance will be evaluated.
The City is cancelling the 5-year contract awarded in December 2025 to Services de mécanique mobile B.L. inc. to supply original Freightliner parts for the maintenance of its heavy vehicles.
The contract was estimated at $1,655,640, taxes included, with two 12-month extension options.

The supplier wrote to the City on January 9, 2026 to say it could not fulfill the contract: a lack of resources and logistics, and no authorization from Freightliner to distribute its parts in the Montréal area.
The cancellation costs the City nothing, since no purchases were made under the contract.

The City says the supplier remains responsible for damages, including the costs of the call for tenders and of managing the cancellation, and that it could receive an unsatisfactory performance evaluation.
A new call for tenders will be issued once the cancellation is complete.

The City is preparing to award Techno Feu inc. the supply of replacement parts for the E-One fire trucks of the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal, for an estimated amount of $2,580,490.08, taxes included.
Three master agreements are involved: mechanical parts ($1,186,435.41), electrical parts ($222,091.27) and miscellaneous parts ($741,881.72).
The agreements last 2 years, with two extension options of 12 months each.
A contingency budget of $430,081.68, taxes included, is added to the amounts of the agreements.
Public call for tenders 25-20983 attracted 2 bidders; Techno Feu was the lowest compliant bidder for all three lots, and UAP inc. also bid on the electrical parts.
Prices may be indexed starting in the 7th month of the contract, based on the consumer price index for the Montréal region.
Some items were removed from each lot (8, 6 and 8 items) because no equivalency request was made; they will be the subject of a new purchasing process.
The City is entering into a two-year agreement with Goodfellow inc. to supply it with Douglas Fir lumber, with two possible 12-month extensions.
The contract is worth $192,588.30 including taxes, plus $28,888.25 set aside in case quantities vary, for an estimated total of $221,476.55.
This lumber is used to make street furniture: picnic tables, waste bins and benches.
The lumber must be FSC-certified and meet the ISO 14021 standard on environmental claims.
Goodfellow was the lower of the two compliant bidders out of three bids received; the other compliant bid came to $297,114.37.
Prices may be adjusted every quarter based on Statistique Canada's lumber price index, either up or down.
The City is not committing to buy all the planned quantities; it will order according to its needs and will assess the supplier's performance.
The City is extending its agreement with the company North On Sixty by 12 months for the purchase of Kebony wood, starting in June 2026.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $175,071.19, taxes included: $145,892.66 for the wood (including a 2% indexation) and $29,178.53 held in reserve for additional quantities.
The total value of the agreement therefore goes from $622,796.58 to $797,867.77, taxes included.
This wood is used to make street furniture: picnic tables, waste bins and benches.
The supplier must deliver FSC-certified wood that complies with the ISO 14021 standard on environmental claims.
The expense is paid out of the budgets of the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers, as needs arise.
A second 12-month extension option remains provided for in the contract.
The City is renting nine vacuum street sweepers, without an operator but with maintenance included, for three years, at a total cost of $3,762,181.61 including taxes.
Two contracts are being awarded: $2,545,464.13 to Accessoires Outillage Limitée (7 machines) and $725,998.14 to Entretiens J.R. Villeneuve inc. (2 machines), plus $490,719.34 in contingencies.
The sweepers will be distributed as follows: 4 in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, 3 in Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, 1 in LaSalle and 1 in Ville-Marie.
Each machine is used eight months a year, from March 15 to November 30, from 2026 to 2028, for up to 1,600 hours of sweeping per season.
The supplier covers maintenance, repairs and wear parts; the City pays only for fuel.
Two companies submitted bids out of the four that had obtained the tender documents; the lowest price is 0.01% above the City's estimate.
The expense is paid by the central city and the performance of both suppliers will be evaluated.
The City is extending by 12 months the rental of two bucket trucks (55 feet or more, without an operator, maintenance included) from La Compagnie de Location d'Autos Enterprise Canada.
Additional expense of $233,974.40, taxes included: $212,704 for the rental and $21,270.40 in contingencies (10%).
The total of the master agreement thus rises to $474,646.50, taxes included.
The two trucks (Freightliner, 2018 model) are used mainly for tree maintenance in public spaces and can be used by all departments and boroughs.
The renewal covers the period from May 9, 2026 to May 8, 2027, at the same prices, with no adjustment possible.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers; the agglomeration covers 5.7% of it.
The supplier accepted the renewal on January 28, 2026; the agreements must be renewed in April 2026.
The City is transferring to 13665216 Canada inc. two supply contracts for pickup trucks (full hybrid and regular engine) held since 2022 by Fortier Auto (Montréal) ltée.
Reason: 13665216 Canada inc. bought the assets of Fortier Auto, which will cease operations, and asked for the agreements to be transferred on October 31, 2025.
The agreements are worth about $25,212,695.22 in total, taxes included; about $16,332,116.12 remains to be spent.
The transfer is made at the same prices, terms and conditions; the agreements run until February 23, 2027.

The new supplier takes on all of Fortier Auto's obligations and does not appear on the register of enterprises ineligible for public contracts or on the list of suppliers with unsatisfactory performance.
The pickup trucks are used to replace obsolete vehicles in the boroughs and central services; purchases are made on request, with no budget set aside in advance.
The city is extending its agreements with Pneus Métropolitains inc. by 12 months, starting in June 2026, for the maintenance, repair and replacement of tires and rims in its mechanical shops.
The extension covers three sectors: Ouest (lot 1), Centre (lot 3) and Sud (lot 4). Lot 2 had already been renewed in 2025.
Additional spending authorized: $840,656.93 including taxes, made up of $700,547.44 for the services and $140,109.49 in contingencies (20%) for unforeseen costs.
The total of the master agreements therefore rises to $2,619,075.10 including taxes.
The services covered include repairing tires for light, heavy and specialized vehicles, retreading, 24/7 roadside service and free pickup of used tires.
Purchases are made as needs arise, out of the operating budget of the Service du matériel roulant; the agglomeration covers 5.7% of the spending.
The City is extending its agreements to purchase new, retreaded and remoulded tires until June 14, 2026, with no additional spending.
The suppliers involved are Continental Tire Canada, Goodyear Canada, Bridgestone Canada and Michelin Amérique du Nord (Canada).
These tires are used to equip vehicles in all City units; the previous agreement was set to expire on March 31, 2026.
The extension provides three more months of coverage, giving the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales time to issue a new call for tenders.
The call for tenders issued by the Centre in October 2025 was cancelled: no bid was compliant.
Suppliers must take back used tires free of charge and hand them over to a company certified in tire recovery.
An environmental fee of $4.50 per new tire is added to the price of the tire.
The City is entering into a 2-year master agreement with Chartrand Ford (Ventes) inc. to supply brake parts for the light and intermediate vehicles in the city's fleet.
The contract provides for a maximum of $5,179,356 (taxes included), plus $1,035,871.20 in contingencies (20%), for an estimated total of $6,215,227.20.
The agreement can be extended by 12 months, with prices adjusted each year based on Statistique Canada's industrial product price index.
Only one company submitted a bid out of the two that obtained the tender documents; the file was therefore reviewed by the Commission sur l'examen des contrats.
The bid is $625,680.01 lower (-10.78%) than the estimate, because the supplier could not include certain items; if those are removed, the gap becomes unfavourable by $102,943.73 (2.03%).
The purchases will be paid out of the workshops' operating budget, as needs arise; the agglomeration covers 5.7% of it.
The supplier's performance will be evaluated. The agreement is expected to be created in May 2026.
The City is extending its central control over rolling stock (vehicles and equipment) by six months, until December 31, 2026. This equipment would normally fall under the boroughs.
Rental contracts of less than one year and those that come with an operator remain in the hands of the boroughs.
This central authority, brought together under the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers since 2017, was set to expire on June 30, 2026.
The extension is meant to give an internal working committee, mandated in March 2026, time to make its recommendations on how the grouping works.
According to the document, nothing changes for operations: responsibilities, funding and purchase planning stay the same, at no additional cost.
The planned performance review is postponed to December 2026, when the authority comes up for renewal.
Adoption requires a two-thirds vote of the members of city council.
The City is hiring Aréo-Feu ltée to inspect, do preventive maintenance on, and repair its Rosenbauer fire trucks (ladder trucks and T-Rex articulating boom).
Estimated value of the agreements: $899,372.25 including taxes, made up of $782,062.83 for the services and $117,309.42 in contingencies (15%).
The agreements run for 21 months, expire on January 22, 2028, and can be renewed twice for 12 months.
Aréo-Feu was the only company to bid out of four that had obtained the tender documents; the prices submitted are above the City's estimate by 10.45% (lot 1) and 9.22% (lot 2).
Lot 3, for the Spartan pumper trucks, is cancelled because no compliant bid was received and will be put out to tender again.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration, as fire safety spending; the company's performance will be evaluated.
According to the document, a delay in approval could force vehicles to be temporarily taken out of service and reduce the capacity of the Service de sécurité incendie.
The City is hiring Distributions Maranda inc. to fit out vans on truck chassis it already owns, for $333,116.75 including taxes.
It is adding $66,623.35 in contingencies, for a total expense of $399,740.11 including taxes.
The two lots cover SPVM vehicles: a prisoner transport truck (lot 1) and a prefabricated fit-out for an extended gasoline van (lot 2).
The company must deliver the fit-outs within 200 days of receiving the vehicles, failing which a penalty of 2% per month applies after three months of delay.
Of the 8 companies that obtained the tender documents, only 2 submitted bids; for lot 1, the other bid was 58.98% more expensive.
Lot 4 (two boxes for SIM heavy vehicles) was cancelled; lots 3 and 5 are being handled through a delegated decision.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration, through a loan by-law for vehicle replacement; the purchase order is planned for the end of April 2026.
The City is hiring two companies to apply rustproofing to its light and heavy vehicles, for 24 months with an option to extend by 12 months.
Lallier Automobile (P.A.T.) inc. / Krown Montréal-Est gets the East region for $128,079.85, taxes included.
9183-8565 Québec inc. / Krown St-Jérôme gets the Centre and South regions for $401,862.92, taxes included.
The City is adding $105,988.55 in contingencies, for an estimated total value of $635,931.33 for the agreements.
The services include picking up and delivering the vehicles to the Service du matériel roulant, as well as washing the inside of the cabs to remove salt.
Only one bid was received for each of these three lots; the prices are about 50% higher than the City's estimate, a gap attributed to the additional services being underestimated.
The supplier refused to lower its price during the negotiation that is allowed when only one compliant bid is received.
The City is extending its purchase agreements for electrical and electronic parts used to maintain its municipal vehicles by 12 months, starting in June 2026.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $368,541.29 (taxes included), consisting of $320,470.68 in purchases and $48,070.60 in contingencies for unforeseen costs.
This brings the total value of the agreements to $1,906,484.91, taxes included.
The suppliers are UAP inc. (Traction Anjou and St-Laurent) for lots 2 and 3 (Federal Signal and Grote parts) and Pièces d'Autos Probec for lot 4 (Truck Lite).
Prices are adjusted each year based on the consumer price index for the Montréal region; delivery to the workshops is free of charge.
Late deliveries result in a penalty of 1% of the value of the goods per day; urgent orders must be delivered in less than 4 hours.
The expense is funded by the operating budget of the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers, with 5.7% paid by the urban agglomeration.

The City is entering into a three-year agreement with Thibault & Associés for the supply of 6,000-litre-per-minute fire pumper trucks, for a maximum of $44,475,536.18, taxes included, plus $6,671,330.43 in contingencies (estimated total: $51,146,866.61).
The agreement provides for the purchase of 30 pumper trucks, at a rate of about 10 per year, to renew the fleet of the Service de sécurité incendie.

The supplier must deliver the first vehicle within 700 days of the purchase order, then one vehicle every 14 days; a delay results in a penalty of 3% per month of the value of the goods not delivered.
Prices will be indexed to the exchange rate at the time of each order (90% of the price of the truck, 100% of original parts).
Warranties range from 1 year for the complete vehicle to 10 years for the cab, the pump and the paint, and for life for the chassis and the water tank.
Public call for tenders 25-21165 received 2 bids out of 6 people who took out the tender documents; the winning bid is 25.42% lower than the City's estimate and 26.28% lower than the other bid.
The City will carry out a performance evaluation of Thibault & Associés; the expense is charged to the budget of the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers.
The City is transferring six framework agreements from Trois Diamants Autos (1987) Ltée to Olivier Mascouche Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram inc., which bought the former's assets on April 27, 2026.
These agreements cover the purchase of genuine (OEM) Chrysler-brand parts and the maintenance and repair of the City's light vehicles (lots 1 to 5).
The agreements involved were worth $17,605,895.43 including taxes in total; the value still to be used is about $17,111,025.05.
The transfer is being made at the same prices and conditions as before; the new supplier takes on all the obligations.
Trois Diamants Autos (1987) Ltée will cease operations after the transfer.
According to the document, the firm Olivier Mascouche is not listed in the register of businesses ineligible for public contracts, nor on the list of suppliers with unsatisfactory performance.
The agreements have no reserved budget: each order will have to be approved on a case-by-case basis.

The City is entrusting the preventive maintenance and repair of its heavy vehicles to two companies: Ressort Idéal ltée for the East sector and Le Groupe Guy inc. for the West, South and Centre sectors.
The four agreements total $2,280,195.79 including taxes, of which $1,982,778.95 is for the contracts and $297,416.85 is for contingencies.
The contracts run for 12 months, with two possible extensions of 12 months each; prices could then be adjusted based on the consumer price index for the Montréal region.

The sectors covered include Montréal-Nord, Anjou, RDP-PAT, MHM, Saint-Léonard, Pierrefonds, Saint-Laurent, Ahuntsic, L'Île-Bizard, Côte-des-Neiges, Verdun, LaSalle, Lachine, Sud-Ouest, Ville-Marie, Outremont, Rosemont, Villeray–Saint-Michel and Plateau-Mont-Royal.
Inspections follow the City's Preventive Maintenance Program, in compliance with the law on heavy vehicles.
Public call for tenders 26-21329 was divided into four lots; 12 companies obtained the tender documents and 5 bids were submitted, 2 of which were found non-compliant.
The City does not commit to ordering all of the services set out in the tender documents.
The City is hiring T.M.S. Maîtres des Camions ltée to repair the diesel engines and transmissions of its heavy trucks, for a maximum of $3,070,844.34, taxes included.
A contingency budget of $460,626.65 is added, bringing the estimated amount of the agreements to $3,531,470.99.
Five agreements cover Cummins engines ($943,576.83), Mercedes ($705,716.60), International ($551,489.09), Detroit ($564,573.24) and Allison transmissions ($305,488.58).
The agreements last 12 months, with an option to extend for 12 months; prices would then be adjusted according to the consumer price index for the Montréal region.
The City pays only for the services it orders: the quantities set out in the call for tenders are indicative.
The public call for tenders was posted for 100 days; five companies took out the tender documents and only one submitted a bid, for all five lots.
The expenses will be paid out of the operating budget of the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers, and the supplier's performance will be evaluated.
The City is entering into a 3-year agreement with Hebdraulique inc. to supply hydraulic parts (piping) for the vehicles and equipment of the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers.
The contract is worth up to $314,244.36, taxes included, plus a $62,848.87 reserve for unforeseen costs, for a total of $377,093.23.
The agreement can be extended three times for 12 months, with prices adjusted each year based on the consumer price index for the Montréal region.
Hebdraulique inc. submitted the lowest compliant bid, 53.69% below the second one (Pro-Innov, $482,969.99), and is 0.68% above the City's estimate.
Of the 4 bids received, 2 were found to be non-compliant from an administrative standpoint.
The City does not commit to purchasing all of the planned quantities; a late delivery results in a penalty of 1% per month on the value of the goods not delivered.
The supplier's performance will be evaluated; the agreement is to be created in June 2026.
The City is hiring Pneus Métropolitains inc. to maintain, repair and replace tires and rims for 15 municipal mechanical shops, divided into 4 lots by sector (Ouest, Est, Centre, Sud).

Total estimated value of the agreements: $1,864,315.79, taxes included. The urban agglomeration council is deciding on lots 3 (Centre, $509,714.64) and 4 (Sud, $459,945.78); the executive committee is deciding on lots 1 (Ouest, $302,258.19) and 2 (Est, $281,677.88).
A term of 2 years for lots 1, 3 and 4, and 3 years for lot 2, with an option to extend by 12 months for each lot.
Approved contingency budgets: $193,932.09 for lots 3 and 4, and $116,787.22 for lots 1 and 2, taxes included.
Services covered: repair of light and heavy tires, mounting and dismounting, retreading, wheel painting, transportation of tires and vehicles, 24/7 roadside service and free pick-up of used tires.
The shops of the SIM, Saint-Laurent, Saint-Léonard, Pierrefonds-Roxboro, Outremont, Verdun and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve are keeping this service in-house.
Public call for tenders 26-21396 received 5 bids; prices will be indexed each year according to the consumer price index for the Montréal region.
The City is transferring $10,000,000 from its inflation reserve (appropriated surpluses under local jurisdiction) to the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers to pay for fuel in 2026.
The money will be used to fuel the vehicles and equipment of the boroughs and the central services until December 31, 2026.
The fuel shortfall for 2026 was estimated at $6.1M in 2025; it is now estimated at $10M because of the rise in fuel prices.
The Service explains that this transfer avoids an interruption or a reduction in vehicle fuelling, repair and maintenance services.
The transfer is non-recurring and any amount not spent will return to its funding source.
Similar transfers were authorized in past years: $3.4M in 2025, $11M in 2024, $7M and $7.5M in 2023.
The borough of Verdun is adopting a by-law that updates the thresholds and ceilings its officials must follow when awarding contracts.
These thresholds follow the adjustment published by the Government of Québec, in effect from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027.
The threshold above which a public call for tenders is mandatory rises to $139,000.
The by-law is adopted with no changes from the draft filed on February 3, 2026.
Adoption on March 10, 2026, public notice and coming into force on March 11, 2026.
The file involves no spending; the borough describes it as purely administrative in nature.
The borough of Verdun is appointing Abdelkrim Ait Abdaim, research officer, as substitute borough secretary.
The appointment takes effect on February 3, 2026, when he returns from parental leave.
The substitute replaces the borough secretary in cases of illness, vacation or major impediment.
The same position had already been given to him in April 2024; Diane Garand had been appointed substitute in June 2025.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The borough of Anjou is allowing two exceptions to the zoning by-law for a vacant lot at 8210, boulevard Métropolitain.
These exceptions allow play equipment and a fence to be installed in the front yard setback facing avenue de La Roche-sur-Yon, which the by-law normally prohibits.
The project is the construction of a two-storey childcare centre (centre de la petite enfance, CPE) of 745.3 m², able to accommodate 79 children.
The planned fence includes a 2.50 m sound barrier on one side and a 1.83 m open-work fence elsewhere.
Two conditions apply: 30% of the lot must remain covered with ground-level vegetation and 8 trees must be planted.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization lapses.
