The planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme) said it was in favour of the request on February 2, 2026.

The borough of Anjou is tabling its 2025 report to council on the use of the special housing power set out in provincial law (2024, chapter 2), which allows it to approve projects of 3 or more housing units despite urban planning rules.
In 2025, the borough granted three authorizations and refused no applications.
Capital Square – Place Anjou project (former Toys'R'Us), 7151, boulevard des Roseraies: 460 housing units authorized, whereas about 250 were permitted as of right.
Les intervalles project (former Fortier-Ford), 6900-7000, boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine: 809 housing units authorized, compared with about 600 permitted as of right.
Westwalk Anjou project, 7450, 7470 and 7488, boulevard des Galeries-d'Anjou: 545 housing units authorized, compared with about 490 permitted as of right.
The exemptions concern, among other things, setbacks, parking and access lanes, projections and balconies, exterior cladding, as well as an exemption from the demolition committee.
The report had to be tabled no later than April 1, 2026 (March 3, 2026 sitting); it will be sent to the minister responsible for housing and published on the City's website.
The borough of Anjou is amending its by-law on peace, good order and nuisances to cover "private places accessible to the public," such as the parking lots of shopping centres or grocery stores.
It becomes illegal to drink alcohol in a private place accessible to the public where alcohol is not permitted.
The ban on smoking cannabis, already in force in parks and public squares, is being extended to these private places accessible to the public.
It also becomes illegal to lie down or loiter while intoxicated in these places, except where alcohol is permitted (bars, restaurants, special events).
Stated purpose: to allow SPVM police officers to intervene and issue tickets in these places.
Steps: notice of motion and tabling of the draft by-law, then adoption; the by-law comes into force on the day it is published, with a public notice.

The borough of Anjou is authorizing the sale of alcohol ("bar" use) in the space at 9985, place d'York, occupied by the business Golf Privé Signature, which rents out virtual golf simulators by the hour.
The bar will take up 23.41 m² of the 639.45 m² space, or 3.66%, with 8 seats and a counter that also serves as a reception desk.

Alcohol will be sold only to customers registered for a game on a simulator, and only during the business's opening hours: 8 a.m. to 11 p.m. Monday to Thursday, until midnight on Friday and Saturday, and 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Sunday.
The business still has to obtain its permits from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux.

The building is located in the parc d'affaires d'Anjou, surrounded by businesses and warehouses; homes are more than 900 m away and a school more than 1 km away, but a church is located in the neighbouring building at 9950, boulevard Parkway.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 29, 2026; no new environmental conditions are being added, as the building is already required to plant 7 trees in the back yard.

The City is having a $3,651,000 accounting entry ratified, recorded in its results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025: $1,095,300 on the agglomeration side and $2,555,700 on the local jurisdiction side.
This amount comes from employees' future benefits (life insurance, medical and dental costs for certain retirees).
The value of this liability was revised downward in 2025, dropping to $77,788,000, whereas the initial liability recorded in 2007 was $106,234,000.
The rules of the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation require the City to transfer the surplus to the results for tax purposes and to have it approved by its councils.
According to the document, the operation has no effect on the 2025 financial results, either for the agglomeration or for the local portion.
City council must ratify the local share and the urban agglomeration council, the agglomeration share.
The urban agglomeration is extending until June 30, 2030 its grant program for social economy businesses that buy, build or renovate a building.
It is adding $7,500,000 to the program, that is $2,500,000 per year in 2026, 2027 and 2028, bringing the total envelope to $20,050,000.
The assistance remains 40% of the purchase cost (component 1) or 40% of the work and 50% of the professional services (component 2), up to a maximum of $400,000.
New condition: the business will have to earn at least 20% of its revenue from its own activities to be eligible.
Construction or renovation projects will have to be almost finished within 18 months of the eligibility notice, and no later than June 30, 2030.
Building purchases become eligible again after June 30, 2026; the deed of sale must be submitted within 6 months, without going past March 30, 2030.
The by-law is to come into force on July 1, 2026, following an adoption planned for June 2026.
The City is acquiring, by expropriation if needed, three parcels of land totalling 4,952.5 m² in Ville de Mont-Royal, near chemin Dalton and boulevard Cavendish.
These lots, currently vacant, will be used to build the street extending boulevard Cavendish, in the Namur–De la Savane area.
The authorized expense is $3,900,000, plus taxes; the urban agglomeration covers 100% of it.
A maximum amount of $4,094,512.50 net will be financed by loan by-law RCG 25-002 related to the Quartier Namur-Hippodrome.
The Service des affaires juridiques is mandated to begin the expropriation proceedings.
The land reserve imposed since 2022 expires in July 2026, which is why the decision is being made now.
Planned timeline: service of the expropriation notice in the summer of 2026, taking of possession in the first quarter of 2027.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is asking the Directeur de l'état civil to designate two elected officials as officiants for marriages and civil unions.
They are Catherine Houbart, city councillor, and Jonathan Burnham, borough councillor, both from the Saint-Henri-Est–Petite-Bourgogne–Pointe-Saint-Charles–Griffintown district.
Once designated, they will be able to officiate marriages and civil unions anywhere in the territory of the Ville de Montréal.
The two elected officials themselves expressed their intention to obtain this designation.
A borough council resolution is required to accompany the request sent to the Directeur de l'état civil.
No amount is associated with this decision.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is moving its June 8, 2026 council meeting: it will be held at the maison de la culture Marie-Uguay, at 6052, boulevard Monk (2nd floor).
The meeting remains at 7 p.m., but will no longer take place in the council chamber at the borough hall, at 815, rue Bel-Air.
The borough says it wants to make it easier for residents to take part in local democratic life.
A notice will be published on the borough's website.
No spending is associated with this decision.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is updating its by-law that allows its employees and managers to take certain actions without going through the council, with an obligation to report back regularly.
The update aims to align with the Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, in effect since April 1, 2026.
The notion of "expenditure" is being redefined: it will have to include the initial amount, taxes, and the value of the renewals and options provided for in the contract.
Some fees in legal matters are going up, namely the writing off of amounts owed to the borough and the settlement of labour relations disputes.
Planned timeline: notice of motion and tabling in June 2026, adoption in July 2026, public notice of coming into force in July 2026.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The borough council of Le Sud-Ouest takes note of the result of the register held from May 25 to 29, 2026 on a loan of $19,000,000.
This loan is to finance the renovation and code compliance upgrades of the centre sportif de la Petite-Bourgogne.
Out of 59,242 people qualified to vote, 5,935 requests were needed to trigger a referendum; no request was made.
The loan by-law is therefore deemed approved by the people qualified to vote.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is asking city council for permission to design and carry out the redevelopment of two intersections on the City's arterial road network itself.
At the Snowdon / Clanranald intersection (Snowdon district): adding curb extensions. The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité is paying $637,274 and the borough $110,000.
At the Vimy / Ekers intersection (Darlington district): speed bumps, a raised dome traffic circle that buses can drive over, plus speed bumps on Vimy. The cost of $200,000 is paid by the borough.
The work includes widening sidewalks, replacing lead water service lines where needed, work on public utilities and repaving the asphalt.
Shrubs will be planted at the intersections, but no trees.
Stated goals: shorten pedestrian crossings, improve visibility near schools and reduce drivers' speed.
Planned schedule: call for tenders in April-May 2026, contract awarded in June 2026, work from summer to fall 2026.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding Cojalac inc. a contract worth $2,368,969.15 (taxes included) to redo roadways and sidewalks in 2026.
The total authorized spending comes to $2,775,866.07, including $236,896.92 in contingencies, $150,000 in professional services (laboratory, supervision, plans) and $20,000 in technical fees.

The work affects rue Snowdon, rue Maréchal, rue Draper and rue Kensington: planing and new asphalt, sidewalk reconstruction, widening of the sidewalk on Kensington, speed bumps and curb extensions at two intersections.
Seven companies submitted bids, but only one was compliant; after negotiation, its price was reduced by 2%, or $48,346.31.
The work is to take place from June to the end of September 2026, and local residents will be notified by letter.
The bill is being paid entirely by the borough, through its road rehabilitation program.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding Les Pavages Céka inc. a contract worth $1,209,098.37 (taxes included) for geometric redevelopment work.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,485,008.21: the contract, $120,909.84 in contingencies, $115,000 in professional services (laboratory, supervision) and $40,000 in incidental costs.

Three intersections will be redeveloped: sidewalk bump-outs at Snowdon/Clanranald (near école Académie Solomon Schechter) and at Mackenzie/Lavoie (near École secondaire La Voie), and dome-shaped speed bumps at Vimy/Ekers.
The work includes sidewalk extensions with planting pits, milling and paving, and accessible stops for a bike path; shrubs will be planted, but no trees.
Lead water service lines will be replaced during the project.
Six companies submitted bids out of nine that obtained the tender documents; the lowest bid is 17.99% below the City's estimate.
The cost is shared: 55.27% by the borough ($749,489.35 net) and 44.73% by the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité ($606,521.08 net). The contract will be subject to a performance evaluation.
The Ville-Marie borough council is asking the Directeur de l'état civil to designate the Mayor of Montréal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, as a "competent officiant".
This designation would allow her to perform marriages and civil unions within the territory of the Ville de Montréal.
The request is voluntary: the mayor has expressed her intention to be appointed as an officiant.
The Civil Code of Québec allows municipal elected officials and employees to obtain this designation upon request.
The Directeur de l'état civil must then assign a unique identification number to be written on marriage or civil union declarations.
The authorization is valid only within the territory set out in the designation document and for the duration of her term as an elected official.
There is no cost associated with this file; the next step is sending the resolution to the Directeur de l'état civil.
The City is awarding a $343,344.09 contract (taxes included) to the firm CIMA+ to analyze the sites of fatal collisions that occurred on Montréal's road network.
The mandate covers 5 collisions from late 2025, then about 20 per year in 2026 and up to the first three quarters of 2027, for a maximum of 40 events.

For each case, the firm visits the site within two weeks of the request (or within 48 hours if conditions are likely to change) and delivers a report with recommendations nine weeks after the first visit.
The contract also includes a dashboard and an annual review in 2026 and 2027.
Excluded are: workplace accidents, homicides, and cases under investigation by the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes.
Of the 8 companies that picked up the tender documents, 3 submitted bids; CIMA+ received 86.2% on the technical score, compared with 70% for WSP Canada, which asked for $1,315,773.90.
The expense, paid entirely by the central city, is 8.3% higher than the latest estimate of $317,043.56.
The City is acquiring from the company 9376-9727 Québec inc. a vacant lot of about 456 m², north of boulevard Marcel-Laurin and east of rue Saint-Louis, in Saint-Laurent.
The lot is being transferred with no money changing hands: the City pays nothing for the land, but covers the applicable taxes.
The land will be used for the redevelopment of boulevard Marcel-Laurin, including a new intersection and the rebuilding of the turnaround; it is to accommodate a sidewalk and a bike path.
The lot is added to the City's public domain as a street and sidewalk.

The City is acquiring the land at its own risk as to soil quality: a contamination notice (2004) and a use restriction notice (2005) are entered in the Land Register, and the seller does not guarantee the quality of the soil.
The City will have to carry out environmental characterization studies before it can prepare a decontamination notice.
The market value of the land has been estimated at more than $150,000; the expense is covered 100% by the central city.
The borough of Verdun is authorizing public events on its public property, based on a list of sites, dates and times attached to the file.

To allow these events, the council is granting exemptions from the by-laws on occupancy of public property, street food, traffic and parking, cleanliness, nuisances and parks, as well as the 2026 fees.
The events covered may be community, social, sports, educational, multicultural, civic or commemorative events, or fundraisers.
The occupancy may involve occupying all or part of a park or square, closing one or more streets, or both at the same time.
The events are free and open to everyone; organizers must obtain all other required authorizations themselves.
Services provided by the City are billed according to the Règlement sur les tarifs 2026, with certain services free of charge depending on the case.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing a shared terrace on boulevard Saint-Laurent, across from parc des Amériques, from April 15 to November 15, 2026.
The terrace is open to everyone, with no table service, and alcohol may be consumed there with a meal.
La Société de développement du boulevard Saint-Laurent is responsible for the permit, the setup, the removal, the storage and the daily upkeep of the site.
This is the renewal of a layout already authorized in 2024 and in 2025.
No cost is listed in the file; the permit is to be issued in April 2026 and the setup is to follow the same month.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing a shared terrace on the sidewalk in front of 328 avenue Duluth Est, from April 15 to November 15, 2026.
The terrace is open to everyone, with no table service; you may drink alcohol there while eating a meal.
The request comes from the merchant Dépanneur Comptoir (9489-8566 Québec inc.), supported by the non-profit organization Maison de l'amitié.
The merchant must obtain the occupancy permit, set up and remove the terrace, store it outside the season and maintain the site every day.
A straight clearance of 1.8 metres must remain free on the sidewalk for pedestrian traffic.
A small sign will indicate that the installation is open to all and not reserved for customers.
The same installation had already been authorized at this address for the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is setting aside new parking spaces for City vehicles on four street sections, near the aréna Saint-Louis, the Centre de loisirs Saint-Denis, the bibliothèque Mordecai-Richler and the piscine Lévesque.
Two paid parking spaces (PN417 and PN418) are being removed on the west side of rue Casgrain, north of Saint-Viateur Est; the area becomes reserved for City vehicles from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.
Rue Rivard (east side, north of Laurier Est): the no-parking-at-any-time zone becomes a space reserved for City vehicles, at all times.

Avenue du Parc (west side, south of Saint-Viateur Ouest) and rue Boyer (west side, north of Marie-Anne Est): the spaces reserved for City vehicles will now apply every day rather than Monday to Friday (9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. on du Parc, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Boyer).
The borough says it wants to make travel safer for municipal employees and make it easier to load equipment.
Removing the paid spaces represents an estimated revenue loss of $2,500 per year for the Agence de mobilité durable, which will pay for the removal of the parking meters.
The signage changes are planned for May 2026, with “Nouvelle signalisation” (new signage) plates posted for about 30 days.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is creating or changing passenger loading zones reserved for people with reduced mobility, in effect at all times, at several addresses.

The locations concerned: 3535, avenue Papineau; 4240, rue Messier; 425, rue Sherbrooke Ouest; 5230, rue Saint-Dominique; 5172, avenue Henri-Julien; 325, avenue Laurier Est; 5555, rue Hutchison (synagogue); 57, rue Milton.
These loading zones are cleared of snow as a priority when snow accumulation is more than 5 cm, which was one of the problems raised by the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal.
Some parking spaces reserved for permit holders or some no-parking zones are being removed or moved a few metres to line up with the ramps and curb cuts.
On rue Messier, the parking zone reserved for holders of sector 90 permits (9 a.m. to 11 p.m.) is being moved so that the same number of spaces is kept.
The loading zones on Papineau, Messier, Sherbrooke Ouest, Saint-Dominique, Henri-Julien and Laurier Est are already in place; those on Hutchison and Milton still have to be done.
The borough is authorizing the installation of the corresponding signs.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is removing two paid parking spaces (PM411 and PM412) on the north side of avenue Laurier Ouest, just east of avenue de l'Esplanade.
These two spaces will be used to create two 15-minute spaces reserved at all times for a new hotel planned at 175, avenue Laurier Ouest, for loading luggage.
The current delivery zone is being moved east: paid spaces PM413 and PM414 will become a delivery zone from 8 a.m. to 12 p.m., Monday to Friday, for nearby businesses.
The Agence de mobilité durable estimates the loss of revenue at $17,000 per year.
The removal of the parking meters and the new signage are planned for September 2026.
The Agence de mobilité durable and the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité said they were in favour, with no conditions.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is removing one paid parking space (parking meter PB333) on boulevard Saint-Laurent, on the east side, about 18 metres north of rue Prince-Arthur Est, over a length of about 6 metres.
This removal makes it possible to create in its place a space reserved at all times for the hotel at 3613, boulevard Saint-Laurent, with a time limit of 15 minutes.
The company 9477-3835 Québec inc. (Hôtel Loft Plus) requested this space so that its customers can load and unload their luggage.
The Agence de mobilité durable estimates the loss of revenue at $8,750 per year.
The Agence de mobilité durable must remove the parking meter in June 2026.
The Agence de mobilité durable and the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité said they were in favour of the removal, with no conditions.
The City is approving a new model operating agreement (type 3) for housing projects carried out with the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, under the AccèsLogis Montréal program.
These agreements bind the City and the organization during the first 35 years that a social and community housing project is in operation.
The model intended for the OMHM keeps the existing rules, with adjustments to accountability: annual financial statements and an annual management report must be sent to the City.
The agreements for housing co-operatives and non-profit housing organizations are being changed to prohibit the subletting of units, in particular through tourist rental platforms.
These organizations will also have to adopt a code of ethics and a by-law, and comply with the City's administrative directives on the program's standards.
Units intended for seniors with a slight loss of independence will have to hold the certificate of compliance for private seniors' residences.
The City states that these changes do not result in any additional cost.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing organizations to occupy public property (parks, plazas, squares, closed streets) from February 20 to 23, 2026 for local cultural initiatives.
Outdoor loudspeakers are permitted at the planned sites and times, up to 80 dBA and 100 dBC (average over 15 minutes, measured at 35 metres); megaphones remain prohibited except for safety purposes.
The sale of promotional items, food and drinks, including alcoholic drinks, as well as consuming them on site, are permitted at the event sites and times.
Organizers may install pennants on lampposts and hand out samples from sponsors.
The events on public property are free and open to everyone; the detailed list of activities is attached to the file.
The costs of the City's support services are covered by existing operating budgets.
The orders come into effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir; the resolution is sent to the SPVM.
The Ville-Marie borough is allowing organizations to use public property (parks, plazas, squares or closed streets) on March 21 and 22, 2026 for cultural activities.
Exemptions allow noise from sound equipment outdoors, drinking beverages, painting and drawing on the roadway, as well as putting up pennants on lampposts, at the planned sites and times.
The noise level is capped at 80 dBA and 100 dBC (average over 15 minutes), measured at 35 m according to the wording of the order.
Promoters must be able to show their written authorization from the Division Festivals et événements at all times on site.
The events are local in scale, free and open to everyone; the sale of food and promotional items is used to make them self-financing.
The costs of the services provided by the City are covered by existing operating budgets; the orders come into force on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the occupation of public property for local cultural initiatives from April 19 to October 25, 2026 (parks, squares, plazas or closed streets).
Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors for shows, up to 80 dBA and 100 dBC measured at 35 metres; megaphones remain prohibited except for safety purposes.

The sale of promotional items, food and beverages, alcoholic or not, is permitted on the scheduled dates and at the planned locations, and drinking alcohol there is allowed; food and drinks must be served in plastic containers.
Organizers will be allowed to put up pennants on street light poles (to be removed after the event) and to hand out sponsors' samples from booths.
The events covered are free and open to everyone; the sale of food and items helps the organizations fund themselves.
The costs of the City's services are covered by existing operating budgets; the orders come into effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing organizations to occupy public property (parks, squares, plazas, closed streets) for cultural events from May 17 to November 7, 2026.
These events are local in scale, free and open to everyone; the detailed list of sites, dates and times is in an appendix to the file.

The council is temporarily lifting four by-laws: noise from sound equipment outdoors, the sale of promotional items, food and alcoholic beverages (and their consumption), painting on the roadway, and putting up pennants on lampposts along with the handing out of sponsors' samples.
For noise, the limit is 80 dBA and 100 dBC (LAeq 15 minutes) measured at 35 metres; megaphones remain banned except for safety purposes.
Food and drinks must be served in plastic containers, only at the authorized sites; organizers must remove the paint after the event and keep a 60 cm lane clear for pedestrians.
The costs of the City's services are covered by existing operating budgets; the ordinances come into effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The City is authorizing eight "cultural initiatives" by organizations to use public property between June 1 and November 7, 2026.
The activities will take place at parc du Mont-Royal, parc Frédéric-Back, place Jacques-Cartier and place Vauquelin.

They include: the 100-day countdown to the Championnats du Monde Route UCI, outdoor dancing on Mondays and Thursdays (June 1 to August 31), Juripop's Juricourse, the Tailgate des Alouettes, the Marche de l'esprit, the Marche SLA, the Marche et Tour Procure and the Marche Sashbear.
The Marche et Tour Procure (June 13-14) will use voie Camillien-Houde as part of the Cyclovia.

The City is granting exemptions from the by-laws on noise and on peace and order on public property, which allows, among other things, outdoor sound equipment and the sale of food and promotional items.
No amount is being paid out: the costs of city services are covered by the operating budgets of the departments and boroughs involved.
The events are free and local in scale.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing organizations to occupy public property (parks, squares, plazas, closed streets) for local cultural initiatives from June 16 to August 7, 2026.

Noise from sound equipment outdoors is allowed at the sites and times set out, with a limit of 80 dBA and 100 dBC (measured over 15 minutes at 35 metres); megaphones remain prohibited except for safety purposes.
The sale of promotional items, food and beverages, alcoholic or not, is allowed at these sites, as is the consumption of these beverages; food and drinks must be served in plastic containers.
Painting and drawing on the roadway are allowed, provided a 60 cm passage is left for pedestrians on the sidewalk and traffic markings are not covered; the paint must be removed after the event.
The organizations may install pennants on lampposts and hand out samples from their sponsors.
The events are free and open to all; the detailed list of sites, dates and times is in the table of cultural initiatives attached to the file.
The costs of City services are absorbed by existing operating budgets; the orders come into force when a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The City is allowing two cultural events to use public property between July 11 and August 7, 2026.
"Back to the Roots", by productions Foxhigh, will be held on July 11 at parc Frédéric-Back, on the parvis Papineau.

The Orchestre Métropolitain concert at the foot of mont Royal will use parc du Mont-Royal (secteur Piedmont and côte Placide) and avenue du Parc between Mont-Royal and des Pins, from July 30 to August 7 (including setup and takedown).
Exemptions from municipal by-laws are granted, in particular those on noise and on peace and order on public property.
The organizations will be allowed to sell food and promotional items to help fund their own events.
The events are free, and the costs of City services are covered by the operating budgets of the services and boroughs involved.
The executive committee is authorizing nine cultural and sporting events to use public property between July 7 and October 4, 2026.

The organizations are getting exemptions from the municipal by-laws on noise and on peace and order on public property, which allows outdoor sound broadcasting and the sale of food and promotional items to self-finance the activities.

Parc du Mont-Royal is hosting most of the activities: outdoor yoga sessions on Fridays from July 10 to August 28, outdoor screenings by Les Amis de la Montagne, a concert by the Nouvel Ensemble Moderne, Everesting Camilien-Houde on August 30, and the anniversary of the Traité de la Grande Paix on August 4.
TOHU is holding two events at parc Frédéric-Back: Les lumières de Saint-Michel (August 7-8) and Grain de ciel (August 13-18).
The UCI Road World Championships will use parc du Mont-Royal, parc Jeanne-Mance and avenue du Parc between Mont-Royal and des Pins from September 5 to October 4, for the start and finish area.
The Festival Quartiers Danses takes place at the belvédère Kondiaronk on September 12 and 13.
The events are free, and the costs of the City's services are absorbed by the operating budgets of the departments and boroughs involved.
The Ville-Marie borough council is authorizing the occupation of public property (parks, squares, plazas, street closures) for local cultural initiatives from July 14 to October 4, 2026.

Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors at the planned sites, dates and times, up to 80 dBA and 100 dBC (average over 15 minutes, measured at 35 metres); megaphones remain prohibited except for safety purposes.
The sale of promotional items, food and alcoholic or non-alcoholic beverages is permitted at these sites, as is the consumption of these beverages, in plastic containers.
Painting and drawings on the roadway are permitted, with a passage of at least 60 cm for pedestrians; the paint must be removed at the end of the authorized period.
The organizations will be allowed to install pennants on lampposts and to hand out samples from sponsors.
The events are free and open to everyone; the detailed list of events and dates is in the appendix to the file.
The costs of the City's services are paid out of existing operating budgets; the orders come into force on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding a construction contract worth $1,741,935.98 (taxes included) to Urbex Construction inc.
The work involves the landscaping and de-paving of five parks: Martin-Luther-King (Darlington), Nelson-Mandela and Macdonald (Snowdon), Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and Loyola.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,968,387.66, including $174,193.60 in contingencies and $52,258.08 in incidental costs.
The work includes demolition, excavation, earthworks, sodding, planting, pathways, and the installation of equipment such as drinking fountains.
Five companies submitted bids; Urbex offered the lowest price, 4.61% below the professionals' estimate.
The expense, $1,797,400.30 net of tax rebates, is paid through the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux and funded by a loan by-law.
The contract is subject to an evaluation of the company's performance.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding Limoges et Fils inc. the work to redevelop the western portion of parc Mackenzie-King, in the Snowdon district.
The contract is worth $948,996.81, taxes included; the total authorized spending is $1,328,595.53, including $142,349.52 in contingencies and $237,249.20 in incidental expenses.

The work includes removing hard surfaces from the paths, redeveloping the picnic area, completely rebuilding the water play area, and adding a system to manage and reuse water, connected to the park's wooded area.
The work site also includes demolition, excavation, landscaping, sodding, planting, and the installation of furniture and a drinking fountain.
Nine of the eighteen parties who obtained the tender documents submitted bids; Limoges et Fils inc. offered the lowest price, 30.80% below the professionals' estimate ($1,371,393.06).
The contractor's performance will be evaluated as part of the contract.
The eastern portion of the park has already been redeveloped with a multi-sport field, with work scheduled to be completed in the summer of 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a $393,214.50 contract (taxes included) to 9083-0126 Québec inc. (Creusage R.L.) for pneumatic excavation services.
The contract covers minor repairs and replacement of water service boxes, as well as cleaning of street valve boxes across the borough's territory.
It runs from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with no possibility of extension; the borough will then be able to join a group call for tenders planned for 2029.
Each year, the contract provides for 300 regular hours at $304/h (including 100 guaranteed hours) and 60 emergency hours at $380/h, for $342,000 before taxes.
Ten companies picked up the tender documents, two submitted bids and only one was found to be compliant; the price selected is 4.08% below the estimate of $409,933.01.
The borough says it does not own the required equipment; this technique reduces the volume of excavated soil and damage to private and public land.
The expense is charged to the water fund of the operating budget of the Division de la voirie.
The City is giving $100,000 to 7 Indigenous organizations in Montréal to hold free events open to the general public between June and September 2026.

The events mark the Journée nationale des peuples autochtones (June 21), the 325th anniversary of the Traité de la Grande paix de Montréal (August 4) and the Journée nationale de la vérité et de la réconciliation (September 30).

Montréal Autochtone and the Centre de Justice des Premiers Peuples are each receiving $20,000; Puamun Meshkenu and Tkanios Centre, $15,000; Orchestre Hochelaga, $12,900; Je lis autochtone!, $10,000; Projet Tshuapamitin, $7,100.
This is the first call for projects of this kind in Montréal: 22 applications were submitted, 13 were eligible, and 7 were selected by a 4-person jury.
Organizations had to present their project in person, a format chosen to take oral traditions into account.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city; the organizations must sign an agreement and follow a visibility protocol.
Confirmation of the support is planned for June 3, 2026.
The City is awarding a contract, without a call for tenders, to the company La Messe Basse to create and install Contact77, an immersive and interactive experience at the Planétarium de Montréal.
The contract is worth $862,312.38, taxes included, plus $57,487.50 in related costs to move two exhibition walls and build display cases and seating — for a total of $919,799.88.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city: $790,453 in 2026 and $129,346.88 in 2027.
The opening to the public is planned for December 1, 2026, for a two-year run, ahead of the 50th anniversary of the launch of the Voyager probes in 2027.
Contact77 will replace the exhibition Rouge 2100 - Une aventure martienne, which must be taken down by September 2026 at the latest.
The contract is being awarded without a call for tenders on the grounds of its artistic nature: the City cites La Messe Basse's expertise on the Voyager probes and in immersive creation.
The construction work on the building itself will be the subject of separate calls for tenders later on.
The City is awarding a direct-negotiation contract to Productions Figure 55 inc. (fig55), a Montréal studio, to produce an immersive 360 dome film for the Planétarium de Montréal.

The total spending comes to $562,758.70, taxes included: $459,361.92 for the contract, $68,904.28 in contingencies (15%) and $34,492.50 in incidental costs for educational material and cultural activities.
The amount is paid entirely by the central city, spread over 2026 ($264,133.10) and 2027 ($298,625.60).
The film "Filante" (working title) will be about meteor showers and will run 25 minutes.
It will be launched on October 5, 2027, shown as a world exclusive until April 4, 2028, and then kept on the program for at least two more years.
The contract was awarded through direct negotiation after a call for proposals sent in December 2025 to 12 studios, 6 of which responded.
The mandate includes 10 stages of deliverables, from the detailed schedule (April 2026) to the final cost report (August 2027).
The borough of Saint-Léonard is applying for up to $529,626.55 from the Enabling Accessibility Fund of the federal Department of Employment and Social Development.

The money would be used to bring 4 elevators up to accessibility standards: aréna Martin-Brodeur (5300, boul. Robert), the pavilion at parc Giuseppe-Garibaldi (7125, rue Liénart), the complexe sportif du stade Hébert (7655, rue Colbert) and the borough hall (8400, boul. Lacordaire).
Each elevator would get voice announcement of floors, braille buttons and a hands-free emergency communication system with a low button and a light signal.
The elevator at the bibliothèque de Saint-Léonard would be replaced entirely, with the shaft and door frames enlarged and the structures reinforced.
The borough commits to paying 100% of the costs not covered by the program, including any cost overruns.
The borough director is authorized to sign the financial assistance application documents.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is applying to Québec for a grant to build a wooded trail in parc Pie-XII, between the welcome pavilion and the caverne de Saint-Léonard.
The marked trail will include nature interpretation panels and, near the cave entrance, an outdoor obstacle course for young people on the theme of caving (balance, climbing and play modules).
The application is being submitted under Volet 2 of the ministère de l'Éducation's Programme d'aide financière aux infrastructures récréatives, sportives et de plein air 2026.
Eligible costs can reach $500,000: the ministère would cover up to 66% of the project and the borough would pay 34%.
The borough also commits to paying 100% of non-eligible costs and any cost overruns.

The project complements another application (Volet 1) for renovating the cave's infrastructure, opening it year-round, expanding the pavillon Pie-XII and building a technical tower above the entrance.
The borough director is authorized to sign the application documents.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is applying for a grant from the ministère de l'Éducation to renovate the infrastructure of the caverne de Saint-Léonard (Component 1 of the 2026 financial assistance program for recreational, sports and outdoor infrastructure).
The project aims to keep the cave open all year, whereas it is currently only accessible six months a year.

The work includes a structure above the cave to allow access during the cold season, a station to introduce visitors to caving and rappelling, and the expansion of the parc Pie-XII pavilion used by the Société québécoise de spéléologie.
The expanded pavilion would have exclusive access to the caving facilities, as well as activity and preparation rooms.
The ministère would pay up to 66% of the project cost; the borough commits to paying 34% of the cost, all non-eligible expenses and any cost overruns.
Eligible costs can reach $20,000,000 under the program.

The borough director is authorized to sign the application documents. Another project, an obstacle course and interpretation trail leading to the cave, is being submitted under Component 2 of the same program.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is applying to Ottawa for a grant to build a playground in its parks that is accessible to everyone.
The federal program (Enabling Accessibility Fund – small projects) can provide up to $125,000.
The borough commits to paying 100% of the costs not covered by the program, including any cost overruns.
The borough director is authorized to sign the application documents.

The project revives an application submitted in 2024 to replace the play structure at parc Delorme; the federal response came in 2026 and the project will be adapted to the current needs of the parks and mini-parks.
The priorities committee recommended submitting the application on May 19, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is renting the bocce court (boulodrome) at the Centre communautaire Leonardo da Vinci, at 8370, boulevard Lacordaire, for 5 years, from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2031.
The total rent comes to $657,365.66 including taxes, for a 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.) space on the ground floor.
On top of that are property taxes estimated at $288,064.10 for the length of the lease.
The current price goes up by 2%, and the rent will then be indexed every July 1 starting in 2027 based on the Consumer Price Index for the Montréal region.
The mayor and the borough secretary are authorized to sign the lease.
The borough says it wants to keep offering sports and recreational facilities that are accessible to the public, continuing a partnership with the Centre that dates back to 1998.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is renewing two agreements with the Centre communautaire Leonardo da Vinci (8370, boulevard Lacordaire): the use of the théâtre Mirella et Lino Saputo and a partnership for fitness classes.
The agreements cover 5 years, from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2031, for a maximum of $771,070.46 (taxes included), plus the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

Theatre rates are going up by 11%, and the CPI will apply to certain rates starting July 1, 2027. The City commits to making an effort to use the theatre for an annual rent of at least $55,000 before taxes.
Fitness instructors will be paid $65/h, with CPI as of July 1, 2027 and the possibility of adjusting wages to market rates.
The borough will pay up to $4,000 per year for access chips given to participants and not returned at the end of the sessions.
Both parties commit to looking for a solution so that the Centre takes over all of the programming; if an agreement is reached, the agreements may end earlier.
The total annual expense may range from $100,193.82 to $154,214.09 depending on the volume of activities.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is adding $4,087.36 to the security guard contract with AXIA Services, which has been in effect since January 1, 2022.
This amount pays for a maximum of 125 hours of security guards, at $28.44 an hour, before the contract ends on December 31, 2026.
The amount will be adjusted upward according to the Décret sur les agents de sécurité, which AXIA will pass on to the borough in August.
The total value of the contract goes from $1,220,188.23 to $1,224,275.59, an increase of 0.33%.
The borough explains the need by urban safety issues in its facilities and by public meetings that require more supervision.
The contract covers security guard services for the borough's administrative and operational buildings.
The Ville-Marie borough is renewing and expanding the sports Cyclovias on voie Camillien-Houde, in parc du Mont-Royal, for the summer of 2026.
The road will be closed to cars between boulevard Mont-Royal and chemin Remembrance during 19 events, from May 24 to October 18, 2026.
The schedule adds one morning at the start of the season and one extra evening, on top of the usual Sunday mornings.
A free shuttle will run between the Laurier metro station and the Maison Smith during the events.
One borough employee and four SPVM cadets will be on site at each session for safety and traffic management.
The project costs $110,000: $56,000 would come from the Programme de soutien aux initiatives locales and $54,000 from the borough's budget.
The application must be submitted to the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports by April 15, 2026 at the latest.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is proposing that city council take charge itself of the work to replace lead water service lines, including the portion located on private property.
This work will be done at the same time as the street milling and resurfacing program (local PCPR 2026), on street sections chosen by the Ville and the borough.
The owners concerned will pay for the part of the work done on their private property; the invoices will be sent at the end of the year.
The public portion of the replacements is paid for by the Direction de la gestion des actifs, and the roadwork by the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier.
The project also provides for curb extensions, speed bumps and the planting of trees and other plants.
Timeline: call for tenders from March to May 2026, contract awarded between April and July 2026, work completed by mid-November 2026.
The Ville was already aiming to eliminate all lead service connections on its territory by 2032, including the private section.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is awarding traffic calming work to Les Pavages Céka inc., under a contract worth up to $1,021,619.90, taxes included.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,297,457.27, taxes included, including $102,161.99 in contingencies and $173,675.38 in incidental costs.
The work includes 7 sidewalk bump-outs (6 of them draining), 1 raised intersection, about 40 speed bumps, pavement markings and signs, as well as tree and plant plantings.
The improvements target areas around schools and intersections on arterial roads, particularly the Crémazie–Châteaubriand and 19e Avenue–Villeray areas.
The work is to begin in August 2026 and finish in October 2026.
The cost is shared between the Programme d'aide financière du Fonds de la sécurité routière (PAFFSR) and the borough, which is paying $360,515.19.
Six companies submitted bids; the winning offer is 6% below the City's latest estimate ($1,082,032.42).

The City is awarding Les Excavations Lafontaine inc. a $4,069,353.88 contract (taxes included) to rehabilitate the sewer collector under rue Nicolet, between Adam and Notre-Dame Est, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.
With $610,403.08 in contingencies and $134,887.08 in incidental costs, the total spending comes to $4,814,644.04, paid 100% by the agglomeration and financed through a loan by-law.
Camera inspections showed cracks, deformations and missing bricks in this 1,800 mm collector built in 1891, which is why work is considered necessary in the short term.
The work covers 405 metres of pipes: inserting a fibreglass liner, building a manhole, repairing two sewer chambers, diverting wastewater and restoring the site.
The contract is expected to last 275 days, with penalties for delays.
Four of the six companies that picked up the tender documents submitted bids; the winning bid is 7% below the City's estimate and 29.38% below the second-lowest bid.
The file is going before the Commission permanente sur l'examen des contrats (cost over $4M and a gap of more than 20% between the two lowest bids); the company's performance will be evaluated.

The City is awarding Les Excavations Lafontaine inc. a $6,893,445.57 contract (taxes included) to rehabilitate the sewer collector under rue Saint-Antoine, between boulevard Robert-Bourassa and rue Saint-Pierre, in Ville-Marie.
With contingencies ($1,034,016.84) and incidental costs ($206,803.37), the total expense comes to $8,134,265.78, of which 98% is paid by the agglomeration, that is $7,975,716.53.
Camera inspections revealed deformations, fractures and missing bricks in this brick collector built in 1864 and 1878, making it about 160 years old.
The work covers about 622 metres of combined sewer pipes and the inside of three manholes, by inserting GRP pipes and, over about 80 metres, by using shotcrete.
The worksite plans for maintaining traffic, pumping and diverting wastewater, and is expected to last 305 days; penalties apply in case of delay.
Out of 4 compliant bids, the winning offer is 23.84% below the City's estimate and 21.71% below the second-lowest bid, which sends the file to the Commission permanente sur l'examen des contrats.
The City will assess the company's performance at the end of the contract.
The City is setting the auction of properties whose owners have not paid their property taxes or transfer duties for Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10 a.m.
The sale will take place at the Marché Bonsecours, at 300, rue Saint-Paul Est, in Vieux-Montréal.
This applies to taxes and duties from 2025 or earlier years whose bill was due before January 1, 2026.
Notices of sale will start being sent to the owners concerned around May 1, 2026.
After September 1, 2026, the treasurer will send the clerk the official list of properties that may be sold.
The clerk will publish a public notice in a newspaper at least one month before the sale.
The executive committee is writing off $70,762.25 in unpaid property taxes from the City's accounting books, along with interest and any balance still owed.
These amounts are considered impossible to recover: bankruptcy, taxpayer who cannot be found or is insolvent, unsuccessful collection efforts, or debts that are time-barred.
Most cases involve occupants of tax-exempt buildings (provincial, federal or City properties), which the City cannot sell for unpaid taxes.

The accounts involved cover years from 2018 to 2025 and several boroughs, including Anjou ($14,015.31), LaSalle ($1,756.07), Montréal-Nord ($1,513.51), Ville-Marie ($2,796.90), Verdun ($829.66) and Saint-Léonard ($553.22).
The amount will be charged to the funds and budget appropriations already set aside for this purpose.
The City has made similar write-offs in past years, including $350,589.15 in December 2025 and $271,701.11 in July 2025.
The borough of Outremont approves the plans for two private residential projects: at 51, avenue McCulloch and at 67, avenue McNider.
At 51, avenue McCulloch (a single-family home from 1910): demolition of existing sections, an extension at the back, replacement of all windows and doors, and new landscaping.

Conditions at 51 McCulloch: backfill after excavating for the French drain, remove the hard surfacing from the new pedestrian walkway, make the windows uniform with a horizontal mullion, and plant a large-growth native tree at least 10 cm in diameter.
A mature tree will have to be cut down because it is in the excavation area for the new French drain.
At 67, avenue McNider (a semi-detached home from 1938): construction of a lean-to, creation of a terrace, and raising a chimney on the roof, as required by the Code de construction du Québec.

Conditions at 67 McNider: raise the masonry and shorten the stainless steel pieces of the chimney to avoid the need for bracing, horizontal clapboard siding with concealed fasteners, and uniform openings on the lean-to.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had unanimously recommended both projects on January 13, 2026.
The borough of Outremont is approving five exterior renovation projects, all recommended by its planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme) on February 11, 2026.
472, avenue Bloomfield: replacement of all the windows of a house built in 1917, with the stained glass reinstalled in the new sealed units.
183, avenue Bloomfield: replacement of a ground-level mechanical unit in front of the church built in 1911, and landscaping in front of the unit.

576, avenue McEachran: demolition of a basement access structure, a new terrace and landscaping at the rear, on the condition that the terrace stay at its current level (96'-3'') and that three retaining walls be removed.

1775, avenue Ducharme: removal of a canopy, changes to 3 windows and removal of wood cladding on the side wall, on the condition that the canopy authorized in 2024 be completed and that a false mullion be added to one window.
48, avenue Hazelwood: addition of a window on the ground floor on the Willowdale side, on the condition that it match the window model used on the upper floor (double casement with transom).
The owner of 1775, avenue Ducharme sent a letter objecting to the committee's conditions; it is attached to the file.

The borough of Outremont is allowing concrete pours after 6 p.m. at the construction site at 1222-1226, avenue Van Horne, a maximum of three times a week, from March 11 to September 30, 2026, except on statutory holidays.
Normally, the nuisance by-law prohibits the use of construction machinery between 6 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. on weekdays, and all day on weekends and statutory holidays.
The owner, "1226 Van Horne Investissements S.E.C.", and the contractor, "Groupe AT Construction Inc.", are requesting this exemption in order to finish each pour without interruption on the same day.
The document explains that interrupting a pour can create cold joints, harm structural integrity, or force the demolition of part of the structure.
No breaking or jackhammering is planned; the finishing stage (power trowel) is the one likely to run past the permitted hours.
The applicant says it will add staff when the hours are exceeded, but that the noise cannot be completely eliminated for the neighbourhood.
The borough of Outremont is approving the planned work on three heritage buildings, following a favourable opinion from the comité consultatif d'urbanisme on March 11, 2026.
At 520, chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine (an institutional building from 1898): repairs to the brickwork and the steel cornices, stone repair and window replacement, accepted with no conditions.

At 1420, avenue Bernard (a multi-family building from 1922): replacement of all the windows and the balcony doors, on the condition that a pale colour be kept and that the wooden doors be restored or replaced with wood.
At 315, avenue Stuart (a single-family house from 1909): moving the basement entrance to the back, moving the terrace stairs and replacing the garage door.
For 315, avenue Stuart, the City is refusing the fence and the new low wall, and is requiring a garage door with 6 vertical sections and a window at the top, like the existing one.
Next step: adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The borough of Outremont is refusing a request from an owner at 843, avenue Stuart who wanted to build a detached double garage in the back yard.
The project would have replaced an asphalt parking space facing the lane with a garage with a green roof and a generator on the roof.
The zoning by-law limits ground coverage to 50% of the lot in this area; the project reached 55.8%, which is 5.8% too much.
The urban planning advisory committee recommended refusal on April 15, 2026, noting that no harm was being caused to the neighbours and that the request mainly served to accommodate the applicant.
The committee points out that a single garage is still possible without an exemption, and that the proposed additions could be included in it.
A public notice was published on April 16, 2026; the borough council must adopt the resolution.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is transferring $97,330 from its surpluses to its operating budget to pay for a contract already awarded to the organization PACT de rue.
This money came from the City's Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, paid out in 2025 but not spent; it will be used for interventions in 2026.
One community worker will work evenings and weekends at parc Jarry, parc Athéna and Place de la Gare-Jean-Talon.
Another worker will work Monday to Friday around the Parc, De Castelnau, Jean-Talon, Fabre, D'Iberville and Saint-Michel metro stations, in partnership with the STM.
The mandate: make contact with people experiencing homelessness, refer them to resources, carry out mediation and raise awareness about issues of living together.
The borough says the matter has no impact on its financial framework, since the money has already been paid out by the central city.
A report on the project is expected at the end of 2026.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension wants to enter its "Parcours des pois plumes" project in the land use planning and urban planning award (prix Aménagement du territoire et urbanisme) of the Mérite municipal 2026, given by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation.
The Parcours des pois plumes is a play installation set up directly on the local street, at the intersection of rue Saint-Urbain and rue Clark, with light, colourful modules.
According to the file, the residential area in question is landlocked and the closest play areas are nearly one kilometre away.
The Mérite municipal award is given every two years by the ministère and has five categories.
The file does not provide for any spending or any communications activity; the decision rests with the borough council.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is supporting three organizations in applying for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation (PAFIRSPA program).

The Centre de services scolaire de Montréal wants to renovate the gymnasiums at the Camille-Laurin and Henri-Julien schools, and build new ones at the Joseph-François-Perrault annex and at Louis-Joseph-Papineau.
Tennis Canada plans to rebuild the infrastructure of the clay courts on the roof of the indoor centre and to add four outdoor hard-surface courts.
The Table de quartier de Parc-Extension plans a 3-storey, 4,534 m² community centre with a gymnasium, a sports room, a community kitchen, a cafeteria, a family space, offices and meeting rooms.
The borough commits to negotiating use agreements after the work is done, so that these facilities are accessible to the public.
The projects of Tennis Canada and the Table de quartier will also need support from the City's executive committee; the CSSDM's projects will not.
The document provides for no spending by the borough and no communications activities.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is applying for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation to renovate the Bleu Blanc Bouge refrigerated skating rink in parc François-Perrault.
The planned work: rebuilding the slab and replacing the refrigeration system.

According to the document, the rink, built in 2008, has failures in critical components (a heat exchanger buried in the slab, a chiller at the end of its useful life), with a risk of repeated breakdowns.
The application is being made under component 1 of the Programme d'aide financière aux infrastructures récréatives, sportives et de plein air (PAFIRSPA).
The director of culture, sports, recreation, social development and park planning, or her representative, is authorized to sign the application and to follow up on the project.
The borough commits to paying its share of the project costs; no amount is stated in the file.
The document indicates that the support of the City's executive committee will be confirmed by resolution in May 2026.
The City is giving its approval for CPE Cardio-Puces, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, to expand its daycare on land the City once transferred for medical purposes only.
The planned expansion: an adjoining two-storey extension of about 307 square metres, to increase the daycare's capacity.
The emphyteutic lease between the Institut de Cardiologie de Montréal (Santé Québec) and the CPE is extended from 2040 to November 28, 2062.
The building must be used as a non-profit daycare for the entire extended period.
The City is waiving the "medical centre only" use restriction written into the old deeds of gift from 1951 and 1956.
No money is paid or received by the City, and the land does not change owners. The deed is expected to be signed in the spring of 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is amending the agreement signed on June 18, 2025 with the Syndicat des cols bleus regroupés de Montréal (SCFP, section locale 301).
The change affects a single paragraph (7.18) of the section on overtime work; the replacement text is found in the appendix to a letter of agreement attached to the file.
The document specifies that the amendment is made without admission, without precedent and without retroactive effect.
Five borough managers, including borough director Steve Beaudoin, are authorized to sign the amended agreement.
The original agreement covered the 17 subjects that each borough must negotiate itself with its unions (schedules, vacation, disciplinary measures, health and safety, etc.).
The file does not mention any amount or financial impact.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is appointing Jean-François Marchand as interim director of the Direction des travaux publics.
The appointment is retroactive to January 24, 2026 and lasts until the return of the position holder, Olivier Longpré, who has been absent since January 22, 2026 for an indefinite period.
Mr. Marchand was until now head of the Division des études techniques in the same department.
His salary and benefits follow the Conditions de travail des cadres de la Ville de Montréal; no amount is indicated.
The appointment is made without a call for applications, which is permitted by the Politique de dotation et de gestion de la main-d'œuvre.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is updating its employee recognition policy (Politique de reconnaissance de ses employés), adopted in 2024.
The maximum amount for the gift to new parents (birth or adoption) goes from $100 to $175.
The same increase to $175 applies to sending flowers or making a donation to an organization when a close relative dies.
The Activities and events section is being expanded to provide financial support for certain sports and cultural activities.
The other maximum amounts stay as written: $125 for 25 years of service and $250 on retirement.
The borough points to the economic situation and the rising cost of living to justify the increases.

City council authorizes the Service de l'environnement to submit Saint-Laurent's Centre de traitement des matières organiques (CTMO) for the Mérite municipal award of the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation.
The application is for the "Municipalité et développement durable" category; the submission deadline is February 22, 2026 at 4 p.m.
A city council resolution is required for the application to be eligible.
The document notes that in 2025, organic waste collection was rolled out to all of Montréal's population and that the CTMO completed its first year of operation.
The CTMO's educational tour welcomed 1,062 participants during 63 visits in 2025 (students, professionals, organizations, families).
The CTMO is presented as the first enclosed-building composting facility in an urban setting in Québec, LEED Gold certified, with a glass walkway, odour control and water reuse.
No spending is tied to this file, and the application has no impact on the project itself.
The City is giving $68,700 to the Regroupement des éco-quartiers for the 22nd edition of the Patrouille verte, from June 1 to August 22, 2026.
The agglomeration is covering 54% of the cost, or $37,342; the rest comes from the Service de l'environnement, the Service de l'eau and the Bureau de la transition écologique et de la résilience.
The money will be used to hire 47 patrollers, for about 18,560 hours of public outreach in 18 boroughs and 5 related cities.
The patrollers will go door to door and hold information booths on sorting waste (brown bin, recycling bin, hazardous waste and bulky items).
They will also document the condition of green alleys, and that data will feed into the City's maps on vulnerability to climate change.
The total project budget is estimated at $452,333.74: Canada Summer Jobs covers 52.99% of it, and the boroughs and related cities 31.82%.
In 2025, the Patrouille verte reached 52,012 residents with 46 patrollers.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is awarding Construction Guillaume Mailhot inc. the installation of a materials lift at the centre Ogilvy, at 7405, avenue Champagneur.
The contract is worth a maximum of $458,752.70, taxes included; with a contingency budget of $68,812.91, the authorized spending totals $527,565.61.

The lift will be used by the organization Cuisines et vie collectives Saint-Roch, whose kitchen is on the 2nd floor of a building with no elevator: employees climb 34 steps several times a day to hand out food to more than 150 families, three times a week.
The work includes modifying the existing stairs, demolition, a partial redesign of the interior spaces, and new shelving in the food storage area.
The building will remain occupied during the work, with temporary partitions to keep out dust and safety measures in place.
The work is scheduled from August 2026 to April 2027; the cost is paid out of the borough's investment program.

Of the 3 bids received, one did not meet the requirements; the winning price is $60,092.98 (15.07%) above the latest estimate, which the borough attributes to the price of materials, the labour shortage and site constraints.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is allocating $100,000 from its surplus to social cohabitation measures near two warming shelters.
The two warming shelters concerned are located at the couvent Sainte-Émélie and on the friche Notre-Dame.
These warming shelters allow people experiencing homelessness to warm up; they are opening gradually from mid-December 2025 to mid-February 2026.
The money comes from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, which transferred $100,000 to the borough on December 19, 2025.
The amount could not be spent in 2025, because there was not enough time to find the organizations, and it ended up in the 2026 surpluses.
The decision makes it possible to use this money for the purposes originally intended.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is setting aside $110,293.50 of its surplus to pay for social cohabitation workers in its municipal facilities in 2026.
This money comes from a central city grant (ICIM program) received in 2025 and not spent; it must be used before December 31, 2026.
The contract will be given to a community organization from the area, after a call for offers.

The services will cover the bibliothèque Maisonneuve (with occasional interventions in the three other libraries) as well as the chalets in parc de la Promenade-Bellerive, parc Lalancette and parc Théodore, the Service des Loisirs Ste-Claire, the CRC St-Donat, the CCSE Maisonneuve and the piscine Pierre-Lorange.
Other locations may be added depending on needs.
In 2025, the organization L'Anonyme provided this service at the bibliothèque Maisonneuve for $19,382.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $81,700 to the organization Vivre Saint-Michel en santé for the year 2026 (from January 1 to December 31).
The money funds the project "RUI 2026 - la participation citoyenne à Saint-Michel", focused on the eastern part of the Saint-Michel neighbourhood.

Planned activities include: a cleanup and beautification campaign, consultations and citizens' assemblies (including on election issues), a family sports day, and cultural and historical walking tours.
Two staff positions are paid for by the project: a coordinator for community consultation and citizen participation, and a coordinator for cultural consultation.
The organization has been informed that this is the last year of funding for this project; 2026 will be used to transfer the activities to partners and citizens.
The amounts in previous years were $115,032 in 2024 and in 2025, and $98,365 in 2023.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city (Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale); a final report is required by January 31, 2027.
The City is paying an additional $2,294,626.74 to the Autorité régionale de transport métropolitain (ARTM) for free public transit for people aged 65 and over.
This additional amount is due to greater use of the measure than had been planned in the 2025 budget: the actual bill comes to $41,354,879.74 instead of the $39,060,253 budgeted.
Free transit has been in place since July 2023 for residents of the Montréal agglomeration aged 65 and over, upon presentation of an Opus 65+ card and proof of residency.
It covers all of zone A: metro, train, REM, bus, shared taxi, river shuttles and paratransit.
The agreement renews automatically each July 1 until the following June 30, at the City's request; the STM encodes the cards and informs users.
The expense is covered 100% by the agglomeration; since a provision was already made in 2025, the City states that there is no impact on its 2026 financial framework.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a contract worth $935,346.23 (taxes included) to Les entrepreneurs Bucaro inc. to redo sidewalks, pave streets and build speed bumps.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,098,114.44, including $93,534.62 in contingencies and $69,233.59 in incidental costs.
The work covers 320 m² of sidewalks on the local network and 396 m² on the arterial network, plus speed bumps as a speed reduction measure.
Planing and paving are planned on rue de Lanaudière (between avenue Laurier and rue Saint-Grégoire) and on avenue des Érables (between rue Rachel and rue Marie-Anne).
The work is scheduled for 2026; the borough pays for the local network, and the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier pays for the arterial network.
The public call for tenders received 5 bids; the lowest is 25% below the borough's estimate and 28% below the second-lowest bid.
Bucaro submitted a corrected bid after a discrepancy between the quantities in the Excel file and those in the PDF provided by the City.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is renewing its contract with Arboriculture de Beauce Inc. for 2026 for the pruning and felling of 600 public trees located under Hydro-Québec's power lines.
The authorized expense is $444,384.12, taxes included, for a net outlay of $405,781.94, under the same conditions as in 2025 and with no indexation.
The 600 trees are divided into 3 lots (150, 225 and 225 trees) across the borough's entire territory.
The work must begin within 5 days following the borough council's decision and be completed by August 28, 2026.
The contract includes the collection of branches, logs and cutting residue.
The borough explains that it cannot carry out this work itself: clearing 3 m around the power lines is reserved for companies accredited by Hydro-Québec.
The cost is funded by the surplus allocated to pruning work, as part of the five-year pruning plan. Only one company submitted a bid for public call for tenders 25-20847.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is awarding G-Tek (8246408 Canada inc.) a contract worth $729,716.20, taxes included, for hydro-excavation services, including hauling and disposal of the removed material.
The contract runs from April 13, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with no option to extend it.
Hydro-excavation is used to expose underground infrastructure (water, gas, electricity, telecommunications) during repairs to the water and sewer system, so that it isn't damaged.

Hourly rates go from $303 (daytime, weekdays) in 2026 to $333.82 in 2028; weekends cost between $318 and $436.71 an hour. For 2026, the borough expects 440 weekday hours, 100 weekend hours and 100 emergency hours.
G-Tek was the lowest of the four compliant bidders out of six; two bids were rejected (not enough experience, missing RBQ licence).
The money comes from the water fund, in the operating budget of the borough's Division de la voirie.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is renewing for one year the security guard contract for the bibliothèque de Rivière-des-Prairies with Centre Investigation & Sécurité Canada inc.
The contract is worth $106,846.62, taxes included, and covers the period from June 25, 2026 to June 24, 2027. The expense is paid 100% by the borough.
The price includes a 2.5% indexation provided for in the contract, based on the consumer price index.
The renewal covers 3,628 hours of surveillance: two guards on weekdays during the school year, and only one on weekends and in the summer.
The library is open every day except 14 statutory holidays; the guards watch over the premises and enforce the code of conduct.

According to the document, the library is next to école secondaire Jean-Grou and to a hub of bus stops, which brings hundreds of teenagers there when classes let out, along with complaints about noise and feeling unsafe.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is authorizing the Agence de mobilité durable to add and remove parking meters on boulevard de l'Assomption and rue Ontario Est.
Two parking meters (MB498 and MB501) will be removed in front of 3315, boulevard de l'Assomption to create a 7.2-metre drop-off zone reserved for people with reduced mobility.
The planned removal of parking meter MB490 in front of 3325, boulevard de l'Assomption is cancelled: the applicant reported that the proposed area was too far from her address.
A new parking meter will be installed in front of 3650, rue Ontario Est, at a spot left vacant by a former driveway entrance.
The work is to be carried out by the Agence de mobilité durable at the end of February 2026.
The borough receives 65% of the net revenues from parking meters installed since 2023; the document states that it is impossible to estimate the revenues from the new parking meters.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the Agence de mobilité durable to install three parcojours (paid parking machines) on boulevard de l'Assomption, on the west side, between rue Sherbrooke and rue Chauveau.
These three spaces had been vacant since the STM removed a bus stop; they will become paid parking.
The Agence de mobilité durable plans to carry out the installation work at the end of April 2026, after the borough council meeting of April 13, 2026.
The borough receives 65% of the net revenue from parking meters installed since 2023, but the document states that it is impossible to estimate the revenue generated here.
Without this authorization, the three spaces would remain unregulated parking, except for maintenance.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité gives a favourable opinion with no conditions; no communications activities are planned.
The City is granting $25,000 to the Regroupement des médiateurs.rices culturel.les du Québec (RMCQ), a non-profit organization created in 2020.
In 2026-2027, the money will be used to organize the organization's membership: joining and fee rules, a professional directory of practitioners, networking strategies and a funding plan.
The project is part of the Entente sur le développement culturel de Montréal, under the "Vitalité culturelle dans les quartiers" theme.
The ministère de la Culture et des Communications du Québec is reimbursing $12,500; the City is covering the remaining $12,500, funded through a loan by-law.
Planned schedule: the grant is awarded in May 2026, the work runs from June 2026 to February 2027, and the report and final payment come in May 2027.
The document states that no financial contribution had previously been given to this organization.
The executive committee must also approve the agreement setting the payment conditions.
The borough of Anjou is buying 62 tickets at $10 each, for a total of $620, for the "Fèves au lard" day on October 23, 2026.
The event is organized by the Fraternité des policiers et policières de Montréal at SPVM neighbourhood station 46.
The money goes to the Fraternité's humanitarian fund and will benefit a community organization in Anjou.
The ticket price is going from $8 to $10: the borough had paid $496 for 62 tickets in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The expense is already included in the borough's budget.
Ville-Marie is offering the other boroughs the services of a public works team dedicated to cleanliness related to homelessness, for 12 months starting in mid-April 2026.
The team has 8 people (1 foreman and 7 blue-collar workers) and 4 vehicles: 1 packer truck and 4 pickup trucks, during the day, Tuesday to Friday.
The service, launched in 2025 for 6 months, had covered Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Le Sud-Ouest, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
One pickup truck and two blue-collar workers are being added in 2026 for minor interventions and to serve a larger territory, including occasional requests from boroughs that are farther away.
The expected cost for 2026 is $931,328, funded by the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, with a transfer of funds to Ville-Marie in an upcoming file.
The intervention locations will be chosen jointly by Ville-Marie and the boroughs; each borough must accept the offer at its April council meeting for the team to work in its territory.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is awarding its hydro-excavation work to G-Tek (8246408 Canada inc.), for a maximum of $34,716.70, taxes included.
Hydro-excavation consists of injecting pressurized water into the ground, then vacuuming the material into a truck; the contract also covers the disposal of the residual material.
The work is done on request: maintenance of service and valve boxes, and emergency interventions in the event of water main or sewer breaks.
The contract begins as soon as it is approved by the council and ends on December 31, 2028, with no possibility of renewal.
G-Tek was the lowest of the 2 bidders in public call for tenders 25-21256 (lot 15), open from December 10, 2025 to January 27, 2026.
The borough says it does not have the staff or the equipment to do this work itself.
The company's performance will be evaluated.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is entrusting the marking of its streets to the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie until December 31, 2026.

The authorized expense is $141,000, provided for in the operating budget of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève. The document also indicates an amount of $135,201 for the upkeep of the marking elements in 2026.
The marking covers the borough's arterial and local road networks, with the goal of completing the markings deemed to be priorities before July 15, 2026.
The start of the season will depend on the weather and will be announced in early April 2026; the end date will be confirmed in September 2026.
The borough explains that it has neither the staff nor the equipment to do this work on a large scale, whereas the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie team already serves several boroughs.
In 2025, the same agreement had been authorized for $135,201.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is paying $2,450, taxes included, to the Regroupement des éco-quartiers for the Patrouille verte 2026.
Environmental awareness officers will work in the borough starting June 1, 2026, for a mandate of 9 to 12 weeks.
Their time is split into 45% common mandates (waste materials, urban forest, drinking water conservation), 45% local mandates and 10% training.
The borough's money is used to bring the officers' wages up to $18, $18.25 or $18.50 an hour and to fund the coordination of the project.
The payment is conditional on obtaining the Emplois d'été Canada grant, which the Regroupement must confirm in April 2026.
This is the 22nd year of the Patrouille verte; the borough had paid $2,450 in 2025 and $2,000 for 2024.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard – Sainte-Geneviève is awarding A.J. Théorêt entrepreneur électricien inc. the maintenance of electrical systems: street and park light poles, traffic lights, buildings and pumping stations.
