The total cost is $257,256.56 for 24 months, with an option to extend for 12 months.
The contract takes effect as soon as council approves it and ends on May 7, 2028.
The contractor provides the labour and equipment for planned work as well as for emergencies (poles, light fixtures, bulbs, wiring, concrete bases, conduits, etc.).
Public call for tenders 26-21315 was posted from March 11 to April 14, 2026: 5 people took out the tender documents and 3 bids were received. A.J. Théorêt is the lowest compliant bidder.
The borough says it does not have the staff or the equipment to do this work itself.
The company's performance will be evaluated at the end of the contract.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is awarding a contract of $59,404.41, taxes included, to Techniparc (9032-2454 Québec inc.) to maintain and redo its sports fields in 2026.
The borough has 15 sports fields used by residents and sports associations, including local teams and Inter-Cité.
The summer work includes fertilizing, aerating, seeding the grass and filling holes; the fall repair work covers mechanical seeding, sodding and hole filling.
The contract was awarded by mutual agreement: 5 companies were approached and 2 bids were received; Techniparc was the lowest compliant bidder.
The work is to start in May 2026 and be completed in December 2026.
In 2024, the same supplier was awarded a similar contract of $68,855.94, taxes included.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension will submit five applications for financial assistance to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, under the Programme d'aide financière du Fonds de la sécurité routière.
Four development projects of about $500,000 each and one application for $120,000 to buy equipment (speed display signs, bicycle counters, counting devices).

The work is aimed at making the area around école Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant safer (curb extensions, a raised intersection, a mid-block crossing) and securing the school corridor leading to école Saint-Noël-Chabanel (curb extensions on rue Denis-Papin, at the Pie-IX and 24e Avenue intersections).
Addition of curb extensions at the Fabre/Jean-Talon and Fabre/Everett intersections, and installation of speed bumps in the borough, including at lane entrances.
The program covers up to 80% of eligible costs, to a maximum of $380,000 per project; the borough commits to paying at least 20% of the costs, for potential funding of about $1,620,000.
The director of territorial development, Jocelyn Jobidon, or his representative, will sign the applications and the commitments.
Planned timeline: applications submitted in August 2026, response in fall 2026, call for tenders in winter 2027 and start of work in spring-summer 2027.
The Ville-Marie borough council authorizes the occupancy of public property for a first series of events in the 2026 season, at the sites and times listed in the appendix.

These events will be allowed to use sound devices outdoors, despite the noise by-law, with a maximum of 75 dBA and 90 dBC measured 5 metres from the devices; megaphones remain prohibited except for safety purposes.
Streets may be closed during these activities.
The sale of promotional items, food and beverages (alcoholic or not), as well as the consumption of these beverages, will be permitted at the sites concerned.
Organizers will be allowed to paint or draw on the roadway, attach items to street furniture and hand out sponsors' samples at booths set up for that purpose.
Organizers must be able to show their written authorization on site and provide a civil liability insurance rider before the event.
The costs of the required municipal services are covered by the operating budgets of the departments concerned; the ordinances come into force on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.

The Ville-Marie borough council is approving a second set of events on public property for the 2026 season (parks, squares, plazas and street closures), on the dates and at the times listed in the appendix.

Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors, despite the noise by-law, up to a maximum of 75 dBA and 90 dBC measured 5 metres from the equipment. Megaphones remain prohibited, except for safety purposes.
The sale of promotional items, food, and alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages is permitted on the sites, as is the consumption of those beverages.
It will also be permitted to paint and draw on the roadway and to attach items to street furniture; sponsors' samples must be handed out at kiosks set up for that purpose.
The events are local in scope, free of charge and open to everyone; they may be community, sports, cultural, commemorative or festive events.
The costs of the municipal services required are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
Each organizer will have to hold a written authorization and provide a civil liability insurance rider; the ordinances come into force when a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Ville-Marie is approving the schedule of commercial promotions from May to October 2026, organized by the sociétés de développement commercial (SDC) and merchants' associations.
The streets involved may be closed on the dates and at the times set out in the schedule, and may be occupied for the promotional activities.

Temporary exceptions are being granted for: noise from sound equipment outdoors, the sale of food and alcoholic beverages and their consumption on the street, drawings on public property, advertising on street furniture and the distribution of samples at kiosks.
Permits to occupy public property are issued free of charge, and the borough lends equipment (barriers, tables, garbage cans) subject to availability.
The costs of moving equipment by Stationnement de Montréal and the services of electricians are billed to the associations.
The organizers remain responsible for supervising the activities and must obtain their own permits, in particular from the RACJ.
Each street closure must be announced by signs in the affected area 10 days before the event.
The Ville-Marie borough is allowing the Société de développement du Quartier latin to occupy public property for its summer 2026 schedule of commercial promotions, from July to September 2026.
Streets may be closed on the dates and at the times set out in the schedule attached to the file.
During these events, the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages and the sale of food and promotional items are allowed on public property.
Noise from sound equipment broadcasting outdoors is allowed at the sites, dates and times identified, as are drawings or paintings on sidewalks, walls, poles and other surfaces.
Organizers may attach items to street furniture and hand out sponsor samples at kiosks set up for that purpose.

Permits to occupy public property are issued free of charge and logistical support is offered based on the availability of equipment; equipment moves by Stationnement de Montréal and electricians' services are billed to the associations.
The SDC must announce each street closure with signs installed within the affected area 10 days before the event, and obtain the required permits, in particular from the RACJ.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is amending its zoning by-law to relax two rules about signs and building façades.
Signs and advertising panels tied to an event, a celebration or a public gathering will no longer need an order from the borough council if they already have a permit from the borough.
The 0.75 m limit on how far a cantilevered architectural or crowning feature may project in front of the façade is being removed, for all buildings.
The borough explains that this limit forced permit projects to be reworked and resulted in less interesting façades, and that it wants to avoid duplicate authorizations for signs.
The ban on encroaching on public property stays in force.
The council also takes note of the minutes of the public consultation meeting of February 24, 2026; the text adopted replaces the empty cells of a table with the word "None".
The draft by-law contains no provision that can be submitted to a referendum.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is authorizing the construction of a residential building at 7871, boulevard Perras, on the site of the Habitations Marie-Victorin owned by the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal.
The project calls for 100 housing units for low-income, self-sufficient seniors, carried out by a non-profit organization under an agreement with the Société d'habitation du Québec.
The building may reach 6 storeys and 20 metres, with setbacks of 5.5 m on boulevard Perras and 4 m on rue Jacques-Rousseau, and a minimum of 40% masonry per façade.
The City is granting exemptions from the zoning rules: fewer parking spaces, no required indoor parking or charging stations, no green roof, and spaces 2.6 m wide.
A maximum of 25 parking spaces, accessible only from avenue Jean-Jalbot; the parking area must be pre-wired for possible charging stations.
Avenue de Colombet will be dismantled and greened; the greening must cover at least 1,100 m² and include at least 11 trees.
The developer has 60 months to apply for its construction permit, otherwise the authorization lapses; the project is exempt from the referendum approval process because it is social housing.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is approving the signage for a restaurant located at 12001, rue Notre-Dame Est, at the corner of rue Sainte-Anne.
The sign will be mounted flat on the façade facing Notre-Dame Est, above a door of the commercial space, and will measure 2.13 m wide by 0.81 m high.
It will be made of a black aluminum box with red and white plexiglass letters, backlit by LED bulbs, without encroaching on public property.
The building is a mixed-use building (housing and businesses) authorized by a specific project in 2022 and already built.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 5, 2026; the Direction considers that the sign fits in with the building's metal band.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is settling two lawsuits out of court and will pay $350,000 to Pierre-Yves Beaudoin, owner of 4518-4526, avenue Papineau.
In exchange, Mr. Beaudoin will have to stop using 4518A Papineau as a dwelling within 60 days of the signing of the agreement.
The dispute arose from a permit to convert the space into a dwelling that was issued in error in 2016; the borough notified him in 2021 that this use was not authorized.
Mr. Beaudoin was claiming at least $860,000 in damages, plus $133,708.97; the amount paid is equal to at most 35% of his total claim.
The agreement puts an end to Mr. Beaudoin's challenge to the legality of the uses of Théâtre La Tulipe, next door to his building.
The settlement is made without any admission of liability and avoids a 10-day trial scheduled for January-February 2026, followed by a second trial on the amount of damages.
The expense will be paid out of the borough's budget for the right to take legal action.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is setting its conditions for using the temporary power that Québec gave cities until February 21, 2029: approving real estate projects even when they do not comply with urban planning by-laws.
Any project approved under this power will have to include at least 20% adaptable housing units.

For a project with a residential floor area between 1,800 m² and 17,999 m², at least 20% of that floor area will have to be non-market housing owned by a non-profit organization, a co-operative, a government, a paramunicipal corporation, a public or university educational institution, or a social utility trust.

Each project will be assessed according to the criteria of the by-laws on specific projects (2003-08) and on site planning and architectural integration programmes (PIIA) (2005-18), then submitted to the urban planning advisory committee.

Before granting approval, the borough will hold a neighbourhood information meeting and a public consultation meeting, announced at least seven days in advance; the resolution cannot be subject to a referendum.
Council will be able to impose conditions, including work deadlines and monetary guarantees for demolition and for compliance with the other conditions.
The borough says it is aiming for 20% non-market housing on its territory, compared with about 7.5% at present; the framework resolution is scheduled to be adopted on May 4, 2026.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is appointing three new people to its planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme, or CCU): Baptiste Aitken and Camille Lefebvre, architects, as well as Sophia Khmil.
Their term lasts two years, until June 1, 2028.
The term of Nicolas Gagnon, already a member, is renewed until June 1, 2028.
These appointments fill three positions left vacant by the departures of Yan Romanesky, Grégory Taillon and Ekaterina Frank. The committee has 13 members.

The CCU makes recommendations to the borough council on changes to the planning by-law, specific projects, minor exemptions and permits in heritage areas. Its members also make up the demolition committee.
There is no financial aspect associated with this file.
City council is adding $349,367,000 to the boroughs' 2026-2035 investment plan by carrying over the capital budgets they did not spend in 2025.
This carry-over is meant to let the 19 boroughs finish projects that were started but not completed as of December 31, 2025.
The boroughs spent $130,059,000 (net) in 2025, out of a modified budget of $473,882,000.
The largest carry-overs go to Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles ($64,200,000), Ville-Marie ($37,879,000) and Saint-Laurent ($26,296,000).
Of the total, $310,842,000 comes from the boroughs' budgets and $38,525,000 from the central services' budgets.
The amounts will be transferred to each borough after city council's approval.
The City is renting a 141-square-foot space (space 152) at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The tenant, Marion-Prune Paycha, continues to use it as an office and as a place to exhibit and share her photography work; she has occupied the space since October 1, 2023.
The lease covers 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for a total rent of $6,281.52 before taxes ($7,222.18 including taxes).
The first year's rent works out to $22 per square foot, which the Service de la stratégie immobilière considers to be within the appraised range.
The City pays for energy, maintenance and repairs; the tenant covers property taxes and housekeeping.
Either party can end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The rental is part of the transitional occupancy of the heritage site, managed for the City by the organization Atelier Entremise.
The City of Montréal is renting a 653-square-foot space (unit 387) to Startop, a non-profit organization, at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, and brings the City total rent of $34,380.36 before taxes ($39,528.82 including taxes).
The space is used as offices, a coworking space, and a venue for workshops and conferences for women entrepreneurs. Startop has occupied the space since December 2023.
The City provides energy and pays for maintenance and repairs; Startop pays the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The space is located at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, a heritage site purchased by the City in 2017, whose transitional occupancy is managed by the organization Atelier Entremise.
The first year's rent works out to $26 per square foot, which the City's assessment division considers to be within the expected range.
The Ville de Montréal is renting out two spaces (153 and 158) in the Cité-des-Hospitalières, at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.

The tenant is the non-profit organization Artenso (Centre de recherche et d'innovation en art et engagement social), which uses the space for offices and for cultural, participatory and educational mediation workshops.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for 456 square feet.
The total rent is $23,096.40 before taxes ($26,555.09 including taxes), which is revenue for the City.
The City pays for energy, maintenance and repairs; Artenso covers property taxes and housekeeping.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
Artenso has occupied these spaces since September 2023; the rental is part of the transitional use of the site, managed by the organization Atelier Entremise.
The City is renting two spaces (148 and 148A) of 700 square feet at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, to the theatre company Théâtre Teesri Duniya.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for a total rent of $36,855 before taxes ($42,374.04 taxes included).
The spaces will be used as offices and as a research-creation venue for the company, which has occupied spaces on the site since October 2022.
The City pays for energy, maintenance and repairs; the tenant pays the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The rental is part of the transitional occupancy of the heritage site, managed for the City by the organization Atelier Entremise.
The City is renting out a 98-square-foot space (unit 3) at 251A, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the former convent of the Cité-des-Hospitalières, in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The tenants, Marie-Dominique Bonmariage and Rachel Jordan, will use it for offices, workshops and talks on herbalism. They have been occupying the space since February 2025.
The lease runs 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for a total rent of $4,762.80 before taxes ($5,476.03 including taxes).
The City supplies the energy and takes care of maintenance and repairs; the tenants pay the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The space is part of a heritage site acquired by the City in 2017; transitional occupancy there is managed by the organization Atelier Entremise, which recommended this renewal.
The City is renting two spaces (157 and 164) at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the Cité-des-Hospitalières, to three cultural organizations: Sibyllines, Pétrus and Création dans la chambre.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for 612 square feet used for a research-creation project and by a theatre company.
The total rent will bring in $29,223.12 for the City, before taxes ($33,599.28 with taxes included).
The City supplies the energy and pays for maintenance and repairs; the tenants cover the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice, and the three organizations are jointly and severally responsible for the obligations of the lease.
The three organizations have occupied spaces at the Cité since October 2022; their previous one-year lease provided for $13,176.48 in rent.
The transitional use of the site is managed by the organization Atelier Entremise, which recommended this rental.

The City is renting two spaces (245 square feet in total) at 251A, avenue des Pins Ouest, on the former Cité-des-Hospitalières site, to the Association Tasiutigiit pour familles interculturelles des enfants Inuits et Autochtones.
The lease runs for 24 months starting February 1, 2026, for total rent of $11,907 before taxes ($13,690.07 including taxes).
The spaces are used as offices for community activities for young people; the organization has already been occupying them since 2025.
The City supplies the energy and takes care of maintenance and repairs; the tenant pays the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party can end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The rental was proposed by Atelier Entremise, the organization the City put in charge of managing the transitional occupancy of the site.
The City is renting out two spaces (608 square feet) at 251A, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the Cité-des-Hospitalières heritage site.

The tenants are the Association récréative Milton-Parc and the Association Tasiutigiit pour familles interculturelles des enfants inuits et autochtones, which hold joint activities there and have occupied the space since 2025.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, for total rent of $30,780 before taxes ($35,389.31 including taxes).
The City supplies the energy and takes care of maintenance and repairs; the tenants pay the property taxes and the cleaning.
Either party may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
These rentals stem from the transitional occupancy mandate given to the organization Atelier Entremise, which manages the site the City acquired in 2017.
The City is renting a 121-square-foot space to the Association récréative Milton-Parc, at 251A, avenue des Pins Ouest, in the Cité-des-Hospitalières heritage site.
The lease runs for 24 months, from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028, and the organization is setting up offices there for its community activities.
The total rent is $6,370.68 before taxes, or $7,324.69 including taxes; this revenue goes to the operating budget of the Service de la stratégie immobilière.
The organization has already been occupying this space since 2025, under a first lease of 11 months at $2,662.
The City pays for energy, maintenance and repairs; the tenant pays the property taxes and the cleaning.
Both parties may end the lease early with 30 days' notice.
The organization was recommended by Atelier Entremise, the non-profit that the City has put in charge of managing the transitional occupancy of the site acquired in 2017.
The City is extending the lease of space in the basement at 7580, boulevard Gouin Est, in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, by 60 months, starting July 1, 2026.
It is renting 414 m² (4,456 sq. ft.) from Fabrique de la Paroisse de Sainte-Marthe, a non-profit organization, for community and recreational activities.
Total rent comes to $208,188, exempt from GST and QST, ranging from $19,608 (6 months in 2026) to $43,488 in 2030, with an annual increase of 3%.
The lease is gross: maintenance and heating costs are included.
The City can terminate the lease as early as July 1, 2029, with six months' written notice.
The owner agrees to fix the deficiencies noted during a recent visit to the premises.
The City has occupied this space since 1997; the current lease ends June 30, 2026.
The City is extending by five years, starting June 1, 2026, the lease of a city-owned lot to the Université du Québec, on avenue Henri-Julien in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.

The 1,368 m² lot is used as a parking lot (51 spaces) for employees, professors and occupants of 4750, avenue Henri-Julien, which houses the Conservatoire de musique et d'art dramatique and the ENAP, among others.
The City will collect $407,663.69 in rent over five years, before taxes, with a 2% increase every June 1.
The Université pays all maintenance, repair and occupancy costs; the site is exempt from property taxes.
The lot is set aside for a future social and community housing project: the City or the Université may end the lease with six months' notice.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal will be able to keep using the lot as a parking area during snow removal operations.
The City is renting from Parcs Canada a 941 m² piece of land under the canal de Lachine, in the extension of rue de Montmorency, in the borough of Le Sud-Ouest.
The lease runs for 20 years, from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2044, with an option to renew for another 20 years.
The total rent comes to $117,330.78, taxes included. The annual rent starts at $4,200 and goes up by 2% each year, with an adjustment if the CPI goes above 4%.
The land is used to maintain and service two 600 mm water pipes that cross the canal.
Parcs Canada can end the lease at any time if the land is needed for public purposes; the City can end it with 3 months' notice.
At the end of the lease, Parcs Canada can take over the pipes or require the City to remove them at its own expense.
The cost is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration; without this lease, the City would have to relocate the pipes.
The City is extending its agreement with the firm Cofomo inc. by 12 months for business analysis services in information technology.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $2,676,865.10, taxes included, bringing the total value of the agreement to $5,284,624.57.
The original agreement, signed on August 28, 2025 for $2,607,759.47, covered the period from August 28, 2025 to August 27, 2026 and provided for two possible 12-month extensions.
The rates are indexed to the consumer price index (2.65%).
These external resources support the internal teams on projects such as Télécom moves and upgrades, customer relationship management and the modernization of IT infrastructure.
Purchases will be made as needs arise, out of the budget of the Service des technologies de l'information; the decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.
The City is extending its agreement with the firm Levio Conseils inc., which provides IT project managers to the Service des technologies de l'information, by 12 months.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $2,594,119.99, taxes included, bringing the agreement to a total of $5,121,270.49.
The original agreement was signed on August 28, 2025 for one year, with two 12-month extension options; this is the first one being used.
The rates are indexed to the consumer price index (2.65%).
These outside resources were used for projects such as the SPVM's police operations, the property tax and assessment system, the electronic document manager and the work environment.
The expenses will be paid out of the budgets of the Service des technologies de l'information, as needs arise, and could be shared as agglomeration expenses.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council.

The City is adding $223,051.50 (taxes included) to its contract with Microsoft Canada inc. to integrate the Microsoft Sentinel security tool into the Azure cloud platform, bringing the contract to $1,158,278.48.
It is also paying $1,207.24 to the ministère de la Cybersécurité et du Numérique, which acts as a cloud computing broker for public bodies.
The City is further awarding a negotiated (sole-source) contract of $192,212.91 to Microsoft Canada inc. for a bank of support engineering hours, based on an offer dated March 12, 2026.
Reason given: the current security incident detection and response tools (SIEM/SOAR) have reached the end of their useful life.
The City already holds Microsoft 365 E5 licences that include security features; it says this avoids buying the same features twice.
The support hours will be used to train internal staff and to assist with the migration to the new security platform.
The matter falls under the urban agglomeration council; these services are for the City's internal systems, not services offered directly to the public.
The City is retroactively confirming a $129,346.88 contract (taxes included) awarded without a call for tenders to Levio Conseils inc. for three years of phishing tests on municipal staff.
These tests simulate fraudulent emails to measure whether employees detect them; the firm designs the scenarios, runs the tests and compiles the results.
The costs break down as follows: $41,678.44 in 2025, $43,115.63 in 2026 and $44,552.81 in 2027, paid out of the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information.
The City approached two Québec firms in July 2025; only Levio submitted a bid, as In Fidem declined to provide a price.

The contract had already been awarded by public servants, but clarifications made to Québec laws limit their authority to $100,000 for agglomeration expenditures, hence the referral to the urban agglomeration council.
According to the document, the operation affects only municipal staff and causes no service interruption for residents or businesses.
The City is awarding a contract without a call for tenders to Info-Tech Research Group inc. for $126,995.62, taxes included.
The contract buys licences giving access to information technology research and advisory services, from July 31, 2026 to July 31, 2027.
The contract goes through an agreement already negotiated by the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales, which the law allows municipalities to use.
The 12-month subscription ("Intro" plan, 2 seats) gives access to unlimited calls with analysts, more than 450 project plans and more than 10,000 reports, tools and templates.
The IT teams use these services for contract management, data architecture, security, artificial intelligence and the selection of technology solutions.
The expense is charged to the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information ($115,963.93 net of taxes).
The previous year, the same subscription had cost $110,454.99 before taxes.

The central city is offering the borough of Montréal-Nord to take charge, for two years, of the purchase of certain lots and buildings considered strategic for local needs, such as the creation of new parks.
The central city would pay the full purchase price of the properties, and the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité would cover certain incidental costs.
The borough, for its part, would pay for securing, maintaining, upgrading, decontaminating or demolishing the properties acquired.

The document states that Montréal-Nord is the borough with the least park area per resident in the agglomeration, which is half the ratio of Saint-Léonard, and that it does not have the financial means to make these purchases itself.
The offer only takes effect if the borough council of Montréal-Nord accepts it by resolution; city council would then have to approve the purchase of a first property.
A similar agreement had already been offered in August 2021.
The borough and the central city would together coordinate communications with the residents and neighbours concerned.
The Ville-Marie borough recorded a management surplus of $5,657,200 for 2025, and the borough council is approving how it will be divided up.
The full amount, $5,657,200, goes to "unrestricted surplus," which the borough can use to give itself some flexibility or to cover other needs.

No money is being put into the reserves for snow removal, occupational health and safety, unforeseen expenses and maintenance of the Quartier des spectacles: these activities ended the year with a deficit, or the reserves have already reached their ceiling.
Nothing is being put into the reserve for mechanized pothole patching either (ceiling of $9,420), because the agreement ends at the end of 2026.
Details cited: snow removal with a deficit of $1,274,273 in 2025, occupational health and safety with a deficit of $2,044,600, Quartier des spectacles with a deficit of $275,084.01.
The division follows the 2025 surplus policy adopted by city council on June 15, 2026.

The City is extending the contract of Matériaux Paysagers Savaria ltée by five months for the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with an operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel.
Additional expense of $296,349.21, taxes included, bringing the total contract to $586,603.60.
The rental covers June 20 to October 15, 2026, for about 450 hours of work.
The screening is used to remove plastics, stones and metals from the compost made with more than 12,500 tonnes of leaves collected in parks and streets in the fall.
The compost is used 100% as a soil amendment, notably for the landscaping of parc Frédéric-Back.
The bill is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration; the price was increased by 2.1% based on the consumer price index, as provided for in the call for tenders.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is taking on the replacement of lead water service lines, including the portion located on private property.
About 45 water connections will be replaced, 44 of them on both the public side and the private side.
The work affects the Island/Châteauguay and Laurendeau/De Maricourt intersections, as well as rue Châteauguay, rue St-Clotilde and rue Turcot.
The costs of work done on private property will be billed to the owners concerned, under by-law 20-030.
The contract is expected to be awarded in May 2026, with work from June to October 2026.
The City aimed to eliminate all lead service lines on its territory by 2030; lead has harmful effects on health.
The replacement of lead service lines affects 16 of Montréal's 19 boroughs.
The City is correcting errors that slipped into the Règlement sur les tarifs 2026, adopted on January 28, 2026.
It is bringing back a reduced rate for adult teams from recognized organizations at the stade de soccer de Montréal, outside of tournaments.

These hourly rates vary according to the size of the field, the time of day and the season: from $100 to $166 for the 7-player field, from $148 to $244 for the 9-player field, and from $296 to $492 for the 11-player field.
The stated goal is to align these rates with those of the complexe sportif Marie-Victorin, so that users pay the same amount from one facility to another.

At the complexe sportif Claude-Robillard, the City is correcting a cross-reference to a section so that the 25% discount given to City employees applies to the right activities (sections 16 and 19 instead of 16 and 18).
According to the document, the correction at Claude-Robillard will have little impact on the facility's revenues.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $6,000 to the Film noir au canal festival for its 10th edition.
The festival shows cult crime films at Square Saint-Patrick, from July 12 to August 16, 2026.
The City is signing an agreement with the organization setting out the conditions for paying out the support.
The cost is paid entirely by the borough, out of the budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The borough has supported the festival since it began in 2015, among other things by issuing the necessary permits; the $6,000 amount was also granted in 2024 and 2025.
The document indicates an average of 380 participants in 2025.
The organization must follow the visibility protocol and the graphic standards for the borough's logo.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding a $792,288.13 contract (taxes included) to Les entreprises Roseneige to supply, plant and maintain trees and plants from 2026 to 2029.
The work covers avenue Christophe-Colomb, between Jean-Talon and Jarry Est, where the roadway and sidewalks have been rebuilt: about 171 trees and 2,200 m² of planted areas.
The trees must be planted between April 15 and June 15, 2026, and the plants no later than June 15, 2026.
Watering and maintenance continue until the fall of 2028, and until June 15, 2029 if any plants have to be replaced under warranty.
Six companies submitted bids. The lowest bid ($481,703.38) was rejected because the company did not meet the workforce qualification requirements.
The winning bid is 30% below the City's estimate ($1,136,805.99), which the file attributes to competition in the horticulture market.
The expense is being covered by the central city, through the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité, and funded by a loan by-law tied to the arterial road network street development program.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is moving its borough hall offices from 6854, rue Sherbrooke Est to 5100, rue Sherbrooke Est (7th and 8th floors) on July 1, 2026.
The new layout, with unassigned workstations, cuts the leased floor area by about 25%, so some of the furniture will not be moving.
The council is authorizing the project office director to dispose of leftover or non-functional furniture and equipment.
The furniture will first be offered free of charge to City units (45 days), then to non-profit organizations in the borough and in Montréal (45 days).
Interested units and organizations will pay their own pick-up costs, which is planned for June 2026.
Anything no one takes will be sent to the Écocentre.
Earlier lease approved in March 2025: 20 years at 5100 Sherbrooke Est, for a total rent of $30,021,933.10, taxes included.

The Verdun borough is tabling its annual report on the use of the power that allows it to approve housing projects that do not comply with its urban planning rules (section 93 of the provincial housing act).
In 2025, only one project was approved this way in Verdun, and no application was turned down.
The project in question, at 8 Place du Commerce, calls for 563 housing units and a built-in commercial component.
The report must be tabled at the borough council no later than April 1, 2026.
The City's Service de l'habitation will send the report to the minister responsible for housing, create a web page on the subject and publish the boroughs' data.
The Verdun borough council is approving a specific project for the Canadian Tire at 3180, rue Wellington: an overhaul of the signs and the addition of an outdoor tire enclosure.

The business will be allowed to keep 6 signs attached to the building instead of the 2 permitted by the zoning by-law (it currently has 10), for a maximum of 38.29 m², plus 3 detached signs totalling 7.62 m².
These signage changes are intended to comply with Bill 96 on the French language, which requires French to be markedly predominant over English.
A tire enclosure of no more than 110 m² and 2.75 m high may be built in the side parking lot, replacing parking spaces.
The enclosure must be made of metal, hidden by a screen of trees or hedges as seen from rue Wellington, and kept locked outside business hours.
A green island of at least 12 m² must be created in one parking space.
The business has 18 months after the resolution comes into force to file its authorization application.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is adopting a Plan de cohabitation sociale (social cohabitation plan) for 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The plan responds to the rising number of people experiencing homelessness, in a context of a housing crisis.
Its goals include clean and safe living environments, the inclusion of vulnerable people, and better access to services, resources and public spaces.
The actions fall into three areas: awareness-raising and information sharing, sharing public space and living together, and an overview of the situation with an annual review.
Several actions depend on funding from the governments and the central city; the borough has submitted an application to the Programme d'appui aux arrondissements – Cohabitation et campements.
A review will be done each year, with adjustments as needed, in collaboration with local partners.
The City is awarding a $153,117.96 contract (taxes included) to Les Innovations CR34TE inc. to supply, install and operate the equipment for the Jardins de lumière event at the Jardin botanique.
The event will run from September 3 to November 1, 2026; installation starts on August 1 and takedown on November 2.
Three areas will be lit up: the entrance and the chemin de ceinture, the Jardin aquatique and the Jardin japonais.
The contract covers renting and installing the equipment, programming, electricity, technical follow-up and takedown.
Two bids were received out of four sets of tender documents requested; the other offer was $322,442.79. The winning price is 12% ($17,809.62) below the City's estimate.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, out of the operating budget of Espace pour la vie.
The document states that without this contract, Jardins de lumière could not take place; the event draws close to 150,000 visitors.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is lending parc Clémentine-De La Rousselière and equipment free of charge to the Association du baseball amateur de Pointe-aux-Trembles (ABAPAT) for the 2026 season.
The field will be used for the games of the Jets La Cave de Montréal, a team in the Ligue de baseball majeur du Québec, for an eleventh season.
The free use is worth a maximum of $1,339.50: 15 regular-season games ($742.50) and up to 12 playoff games ($594), at $49.50 per game.
ABAPAT will be allowed to charge admission fees and keep that revenue, instead of paying it as rental fees ($16.50/h, 3 h per game).
To limit noise, the loudspeakers must point toward centre field, must not exceed 80 decibels, must be turned down at 10:15 p.m. and must be used only for the Jets La Cave games.
The urban agglomeration is appointing Bruno Possa, Director of Public Works for the Ville de Kirkland, to the technical committee responsible for maintaining the main water and sewer network.
He replaces Erik Rolland, the outgoing Director of Public Works for Pointe-Claire, and will finish out his term for the year 2026 (one year).
The committee has nine members: five from the Ville de Montréal and four from the other related municipalities.

This committee proposes updates to the maintenance guide, sets the format of the annual report, reviews the reports from the related municipalities and makes recommendations to the urban agglomeration council.
The committee's current members support this appointment; no financial impact is expected.
The borough of Ville-Marie is paying $30,000 (taxes included) to the organization LespaceMaker, under an agreement valid from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
The money is used to maintain and strengthen five projects carried out in Ville-Marie: LocoMotion, LocoMobile, Outillothèque, Réparathons and Vélos communautaires.
The contribution pays for staff and materials for the committees that run these projects; the activities must take place in Ville-Marie and involve the public.
LespaceMaker will have to submit a final report on the progress of the projects at the end of the agreement, on April 30, 2027.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget.
The borough has been funding the organization since 2022: $21,288, then $30,000, $85,000 and $58,000 under the previous agreements.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $25,000 to the Les Valoristes cooperative to support social deposit-return collection in the borough.
The agreement runs from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027 ($22,000 charged to 2026, $3,000 to 2027).

The cooperative buys back deposit containers brought in by valoristes (informal container collectors), residents, businesses and institutions, with no limit on quantity or quality, at its fixed site and its mobile sites.
The organization must collect and recycle more than 1.2 million deposit containers and improve its drop-off points.
It must submit a preliminary report in December 2026 and a final report in May 2027.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget set aside for environmental protection.
The borough has given a contribution to this organization every year since 2019; it was also $25,000 in 2024 and 2025.
The Ville-Marie borough is paying $22,000 to the Société écocitoyenne de Montréal to run a subsidy program for reusable hygiene products, until December 31, 2027.
Ville-Marie residents can be reimbursed 50% of the price (before taxes) of cloth diapers, training pants, adult incontinence products and reusable menstrual products.
The reimbursement is capped at $180 per year per family for baby or incontinence products, and $75 per year per person for menstrual products; a minimum spending of $50 is required.
To be eligible, you must live in Ville-Marie, sign a commitment to use the products and provide supporting documents (proof of residence, proof of purchase, proof of birth if applicable).
The program ends when the funds run out, at the latest on December 31, 2027.
The organization receives management fees of 15%, gets the money in three payments and must submit reports on December 31, 2026, June 30, 2027 and December 31, 2027.
The City links the measure to the Plan climat 2020-2030 and to the Montréal zéro déchet 2025 objective.
The City is awarding the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal (CMM) a $194,812 contract to model flood risks on its territory.
The contract is paid for entirely by a grant from the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation: no cost to the City.
The CMM must validate and produce mapping data, map the consequences of flooding using a danger index, and identify the areas and mitigation measures to be put in place.
The work aims in particular to demonstrate, to the ministère de l'Environnement, that a dike would be a last-resort measure in certain areas.
Payments are made in three stages: $48,729 (part 1), $35,743.50 (part 2) and $110,339.50 (part 3).
The project began in August 2025 and continues until the spring of 2027; it covers the areas near lac des Deux-Montagnes, rivière des Prairies and lac Saint-Louis.
About 6,000 buildings in the risk zone were surveyed in 2025 by the ministère des Ressources naturelles et des Forêts; a communications plan must inform the boroughs and 311.
The borough of LaSalle will hold a barbecue lunch for its staff members on June 9, 2026, from 11:45 a.m. to 1:15 p.m., at the public works site.
The borough council is also authorizing the presence of a food truck during the activity.
The borough presents the activity as a staff recognition measure, provided for in its recognition policy.
The document does not indicate any amount or any expense related to the event.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is entrusting the organization Sports Montréal with welcoming visitors, supervision and maintenance at the chalet in parc de la Promenade Bellerive, from January 2 to June 19, 2026.
The authorized spending is $31,098, taxes included, already included in the 2026 operating budget.
The contract changes the agreement signed in December 2024 ($226,000 for 2025-2026): the programming component is removed and the chalet's opening hours are slightly reduced in winter.
The borough explains this change by amounts not renewed in the 2026 budget and by lower attendance in winter; it says it wants to avoid a complete closure.
The "Viens jouer dehors!" equipment loan program continues at parc de la Promenade Bellerive during the winter of 2026.
By June 2026, the borough will assess options for the long-term management of the chalet.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is bringing back regular opening hours at the parc de la Promenade-Bellerive chalet, from February 28 to June 19, 2026.
Sports Montréal will continue to handle greeting visitors, supervision and upkeep of the chalet; 208 hours are being added to its contract.
Additional spending of $7,493, taxes included, of which $6,842.11 comes from the borough's surplus.
The hours had been cut back in the fall of 2025 during a budget review, and the programming component had been removed.
Complaints from residents led to the schedule being readjusted.
The director of culture, sports, recreation and social development is authorized to sign the agreement.
The borough of Ville-Marie is hiring St-Denis Thompson inc. to install play structures, protective rubber surfaces and a steel fence at parc François-Dollier-De-Casson, in the Saint-Jacques district.
The authorized spending totals $715,439.41 including taxes: $564,729.92 for the contract, $84,709.49 in contingencies and $66,000 in unforeseen costs (laboratory, site hoarding, spring rider).
The new play areas are aimed at children from 18 months to 12 years old, whereas what is currently offered is for 2-to-5-year-olds.
The work is planned from mid-May to mid-July 2026; a notice will be handed out to nearby residents before it starts.
St-Denis Thompson was the lowest of the 5 bidders, at 29.66% below the City's latest estimate.
The net bill of $653,291.54 is paid by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux, through a loan by-law; any cost overrun will be absorbed by the borough.
A second phase of work along rue Saint-Antoine will follow the completion of the construction of a five-storey hotel at the corner of Bonsecours and Saint-Antoine.
The borough of Ville-Marie is awarding Les entreprises Ventec inc. the work to redevelop parc Percy-Walters, for a total expense of $2,531,429.67 (taxes included).

The contract itself is worth $1,792,858.06; added to that are $358,571.61 in contingencies and $380,000 in incidental costs (laboratories, environmental monitoring, construction site covering, traceability).
The park is located in the Peter-McGill district, between avenue McGregor, rue Redpath, avenue des Pins and avenue du Docteur-Penfield.

The work aims to correct recurring drainage problems, redo pathways and surfaces, install low walls, furniture and plantings in the dog exercise area, and set up a calisthenics area (trekfit) in the southeast.
Ventec was the lowest of the 6 compliant bidders; its bid is 0.47% above the latest estimate, and the second lowest was $274,165.50 higher.
Work is planned from July to November 2026, with a follow-up in spring 2027; precautions apply for bird nesting (February to September) and the site patrimonial du Mont-Royal.
A notice of work will be distributed to nearby residents and the borough will absorb 100% of any cost overrun.
The City will pay its 2026 membership fee to the Association internationale des maires francophones (AIMF): 29,000 euros, or about $46,672.02 CAD at the April 21, 2026 exchange rate.
The fee is due on May 15, 2026, and the final invoice could vary depending on the exchange rate at the time of payment.
The expense is included in the 2026 budget of the Bureau des relations internationales and is paid entirely by the central city.

The fee has gone up compared to previous years: 24,720 euros in 2025 and 24,000 euros from 2017 to 2024, following an October 2025 revision of the calculation method based on GDP per capita and population.
Montréal has been a member of the AIMF's executive board since the network was founded in 1979; the association brings together more than 345 cities and associations of cities in 56 countries.
The AIMF's executive board will meet in Namur from June 8 to 10, 2026, and the general assembly will be held in Casablanca from December 7 to 10, 2026.
The borough of Lachine is giving $26,100 in financial support to three sports organizations for 2026.
Breakdown: Club de soccer de Lachine SC ($17,000), École de voile de Lachine ($6,000, plus $1,600 in anniversary support) and Aviron Lachine ($1,500).
The money comes from the borough's sports organizations budget.
These organizations submitted their requests after their annual general meeting, and the review found the requests compliant with the Politique de reconnaissance et de soutien aux OBNL.
The money must be paid no later than 30 days after the resolution is adopted.
In December 2025, Lachine had recognized 75 organizations for the period from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028.
The borough of Lachine is giving $176,917.66 in financial support to seven non-profit organizations for 2026.
The two largest amounts go to Centre récréatif de Lachine Ouest and Association Piscine Dixie, at $71,326.53 each ($69,723 in 2025).
Club Gymnitours receives $25,000, Association de baseball amateur de Lachine $3,900 and Union des familles de Lachine $364.60.
Club des personnes handicapées du Lac St-Louis and Ressources troisième âge Lachine each receive $2,500 as anniversary support.
The money comes from the operating budget for sports, recreation, culture and social development: $171,553.06 for the sports organizations and $5,364.60 for the community organizations.
The amounts must be paid to the organizations no later than 30 days after the resolution is adopted.
These amounts come from the Politique de reconnaissance et de soutien aux OBNL, which covers 75 recognized organizations from 2026 to 2028.
The borough of Lachine is recognizing the Association de ringuette de Pointe-Claire as a partner organization, in category C – regional, from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2029.
This recognition will give the association up to four hours of ice time per week during the regular season, starting with the 2026-2027 season, at aréna Martin-Lapointe.
Until now, with no ice time available in Lachine after aréna Martin-Lapointe closed, young people had to travel to Dorval or Pointe-Claire to play ringette.
The association, founded in 2001, serves Lachine, Dorval and Pointe-Claire and had 357 members in 2025, including 103 at the elementary level.
No money is being paid out: the organization is not eligible for category C financial support, since it is not funded by three cities or boroughs.
Activities will begin in the fall, depending on the arena's opening date, and will end on April 23, 2027.
The borough presents the measure as a way to broaden the range of ice sports on offer and to provide more activities for young women.
The borough of Lachine is giving a total of $1,650 to two sports organizations to mark their founding anniversaries.
École de voile de Lachine is receiving $900: this amount tops up the $1,600 grant awarded in April 2026, since the organization was entitled to $2,500 for its 50th anniversary.
For its 50th anniversary, École de voile is planning free introductory classes, a regatta, a new logo, new sails and a parade of lit-up sailboats during the summer of 2026.
Badminton Lachine is receiving $750 for its 15th anniversary, marked by a gala on June 6, 2026 (free for members, $8 for non-members).
The money must be paid to the organizations no later than 30 days after the resolution is adopted.
This funding comes from Lachine's Politique de reconnaissance et de soutien aux OBNL, which recognized 75 organizations for 2026-2028.
The borough of Lachine is giving $20,000 to the organization Concert'Action Lachine for 2026, as part of its Programme de sécurité urbaine.

The money funds the work of the Comité d'action en sécurité urbaine de l'arrondissement de Lachine (CASUAL), for which Concert'Action Lachine has handled the administrative follow-up and staff supervision since 2024.
The committee sits on local safety committees, including those for the Saint-Pierre and Duff Court areas, as well as on the committee for people living in precarious situations.

Planned activities include: training for front-line workers, workshops and talks for residents, a positive parenting practices project in Lachine-Est, and coordination of a warming station for people experiencing homelessness.
A new version of the Prévention Jeunesse project, carried out with the Table de concertation petite enfance et jeunesse de Lachine, was submitted for 2026; the former project ended in 2025.
An amount of $20,000 had already been granted to the same organization for the year 2025.
The borough of Lachine is giving $10,000 to the organization Concert'Action Lachine for its 2026 intercultural project.
The project "L'interculturel à Lachine : ça marche !" aims to promote intercultural dialogue, the integration of newcomers and social cohesion.

Four activities are planned: guided tours with the Musées de Lachine, neighbourhood tours (Notre-Dame, 32e Avenue, Duff Court, Provost, Saint-Pierre) from August to October, an exhibition on migration journeys, and an evening with a pot-luck and a world fashion show, the last two being held from November 2 to 8.
Each activity expects between 15 and 50 people, depending on the case.
The project runs from July 13 to December 31, 2026, and the organization will have to submit a final report.
The Programme de relations interculturelles provides for a maximum of $10,000 per year; the same amount was granted to this organization in 2024 and 2025.
The City wants to borrow $22,800,000 to restore heritage buildings that it owns and that are protected by the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel.

The money will be used for preservation, restoration and enhancement work, for installing or repairing fire protection and fire suppression systems, and for universal accessibility in redevelopment projects intended for public use.
The ministère de la Culture et des Communications will reimburse 50% of the loan: the share paid by Montrealers drops to $11,400,000.
Each project must first be authorized by the ministère; the funding covers 100% of eligible costs up to $5M, with the rest paid by the borough or the department making the request.
The loan replaces two by-laws that are expiring (RCG 14-027 and RCG 20-030) and will be financed over a maximum period of 20 years.
The file stems from the Entente sur le développement culturel de Montréal 2024-2027, approved in October 2024; the City expects at least five enhancement projects.
A second loan by-law, under local jurisdiction, is being presented at the same time for buildings covered by the Loi sur l'aménagement et l'urbanisme.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is approving the plans for a new three-storey mixed-use building at 5581-5583, avenue du Parc.
The building will have two commercial spaces and two housing units.
The existing building on the site had received a demolition certificate, issued on January 27, 2026.
The façades will be made of red clay brick with Saint-Marc limestone accents.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on November 11, 2025, and the revised plans take its conditions into account.
Before the permit is issued, the developer will have to submit working drawings that are about 70% complete and provide a monetary guarantee.
Adoption by the borough council is expected on March 9, 2026.
The Le Plateau-Mont-Royal borough council is approving the plans for a new building at 3462-3472, avenue du Parc, a lot that is currently vacant.
The project calls for a five-storey mixed-use building with 65 housing units and one commercial space.
The chosen exterior materials are Saint-Marc limestone, white clay brick, and metallic grey standing-seam sheet metal for the mezzanine.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on February 10, 2026, and its conditions were included in the revised plans received on March 13, 2026.
Before the permit is issued, the developer must submit working drawings that are about 70% complete and provide a monetary guarantee.
The borough council had already approved exemptions from the planning by-law for this project in April 2025.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal approves the plans for a 3-storey, 5-unit residential building at 4618-4620, rue D'Iberville, on a lot that is currently vacant.
The revised plans, signed by architect Maurice Martel, were received on February 3, 2026; the permit application had been submitted on July 16, 2025.
The planned cladding is red clay brick, considered compatible with the area (Village De Lorimier landscape area, rue Chapleau).
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on February 24, 2026.
Before the permit is issued, the developer must submit the working drawings advanced to about 70% and provide a monetary guarantee ensuring that the work will comply with the plans.
The borough council was to adopt the proposal on April 13, 2026. No financial impact for the City.
The City recommends that the Government of Québec appoint Karyne St-Pierre to the board of directors of Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec (BAnQ).
Ms. St-Pierre is the director of culture, sports, recreation and social development for the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.
She replaces Lyne Olivier, of the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, who left her position last December, as the representative of the borough libraries.

The council repeals its resolution of October 2024: the Secrétariat aux emplois supérieurs requires a more recent resolution, since the old one is more than a year old and a new city administration is in place.
If Québec approves, she will sit for an indefinite term, as long as she remains in her position at the City or until she withdraws.
The City has three seats on the BAnQ board; Gina Tremblay (Ville-Marie) remains the representative for the culture and heritage sectors.
There is no spending associated with this decision.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is cutting by 50% the occupancy and parking fees for temporary public domain occupancy permits for the Musée de l'Holocauste construction site, at 3525, boulevard Saint-Laurent.
The discount applies to permits issued between January 1 and December 31, 2026.
The lost revenue for the borough is estimated at $150,000 in 2026, on occupancy fees valued at $300,000.
The museum is being built and managed by a non-profit organization; the borough had already granted the same discount in 2024 and in 2025.
The developer remains responsible for the boards and signage devices required for the occupancies.
The construction site, which began in 2024, is expected to be completed in late summer or early fall 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is suspending the parking ban for street cleaning from April 2 to 9, 2026, during Jewish holidays.
The suspension applies to rue de l'Esplanade, rue Jeanne-Mance and rue Hutchison, between avenue Laurier and avenue Van Horne, near the synagogues.
The signs will be covered on the west side of l'Esplanade and the east side of Jeanne-Mance on Thursday, and on the west side of Hutchison on Wednesday.
The signs will be covered starting April 1 and uncovered starting April 10 by crews from Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
The borough will pay $4,500 to put up and take down the sign covers.
The mechanical sweeper will not be able to pass at the locations and on the days concerned.
The request comes from the Conseil des Juifs hassidiques du Québec: observant people cannot move their vehicle on those days and were at risk of receiving tickets.
The City is tabling its audited consolidated financial report and its financial accountability report for 2025 before city council, as required by the Cities and Towns Act.
Council is authorizing a net allocation of $6,531,000 to the operating surplus for tax purposes for 2025, plus $21,617,000 for previous fiscal years.
These amounts come from the account of recorded expenses to be taxed or funded, and serve to neutralize the accounting effect of a new standard on public-private partnerships (SP 3160).
In applying this standard, the City recorded in its books public-private partnership infrastructure at a cost of $140.4M.
The Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation allowed this tax relief mechanism, which must be ratified by council.
According to the document, the operation has no effect on the results of the fiscal year or on those of previous fiscal years, and is borne entirely by the central city.
The Ville-Marie borough is authorizing the conversion of a 14 m² storage space in the basement of 1619, avenue Selkirk into a habitable bedroom.
The building is a three-storey row house near rue Sherbrooke Ouest and chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges; the rear is located in a depression where water can accumulate.
The work includes opening up the rear wall to add a window and reducing the size of the rear balcony to let light in.
The backyard will be redesigned to handle heavy rain: a window well with a 15 cm low wall, permeable pavers, a 5% slope toward the lane, and a rain garden.
The Service de l'eau estimates that water can rise to 63.61 m above sea level in this basin; the low wall would reach 63.81 m.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 11, 2026; the building is listed in the inventory of buildings with heritage value.
Next steps: posting of a sign on the site, public notice, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.

The City is adding $12,144,522.14 (taxes included) to the contract with Pomerleau inc. to rehabilitate a 1,500 mm water main under rue de la Cathédrale, between rue Saint-Jacques and the réservoir McTavish, in Ville-Marie.
The contract goes from $37,406,646.15 to $49,551,168.30, an increase of 32.5%. The contingency allowance goes from $3,400,604.20 to $15,545,126.34, or 46% of the value of the work.
A new inspection, carried out after the contract was awarded, found 145% more damaged sections of pipe than in 2019. The City is therefore adding these sections to the work already under way.
The work, which began on November 24, 2025 and is about 35% complete, is being extended by 77 days: the end date moves from December 2026 to March 2027.
This main alone carries about 45% of the drinking water delivered to the réservoir McTavish.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration; the net cost after tax rebates is $11,089,567.46.
Without this authorization, the City would have to issue a new call for tenders, which would delay putting the main into service and the work on the réservoir McTavish.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is paying $14,500 in one-time financial contributions to four organizations.
$2,000 comes from elected officials' discretionary budgets and $12,500 from the borough's unallocated surplus.
Conseil communautaire NDG: $500 for the 6th edition of December Together, hot meals served to about 1,000 residents during the holidays.
Centre communautaire Mada: $1,500 for an evening honouring its volunteers, who support more than 5,000 families a year.
Les doyens philippins unis du Québec: $5,000 for Palaro Sa Nayon 2026, a day of fitness activities for seniors.
Conseil des associations canadiennes philippines du Québec: $7,500 to celebrate the 128th anniversary of the independence of the Philippines.
Accountability reporting will be handled by the elected officials' office together with the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a motion to mark the 35th edition of Black History Month, from February 1 to March 1, 2026, under the theme "Élevons nos voix ensemble" (Let's raise our voices together).
The motion invites borough residents to take part in the activities starting February 1, 2026.
The borough states that it has zero tolerance for racism, discrimination and hate speech in its governing bodies, services and units.
It explicitly recognizes that City employees have experienced racism and discrimination, and commits to maintaining safe and fair workplaces.

The motion recognizes the contribution of Black communities to the neighbourhood's history and names several local organizations, including the Association de la communauté noire de Côte-des-Neiges and the Association jamaïcaine de Montréal.
The motion is presented by acting mayor Sonny Moroz, seconded by councillors Émilie Brière and Peter McQueen. No spending is planned.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a declaration marking the International Day of Commemoration in Memory of the Victims of the Holocaust, held on January 27, 2026.
The borough condemns all antisemitic acts and attacks against people or institutions of the Jewish community, and restates its commitment to fighting antisemitism.
It commits to continuing, with its partners, awareness-raising efforts against antisemitism, extremism and intolerance.

The reasons given: the Holocaust caused the deaths of 6 million Jews, Montréal is the city with the third-largest number of survivors in the world, and the borough is home to a large Jewish community.

The text also recalls the rise in antisemitic acts recorded in Montréal since October 7, 2023, the City's financial support for the move of the Musée de l'Holocauste to boulevard Saint-Laurent, and the opening of parc Elie-Wiesel in September 2024.
The motion is moved by Sonny Moroz, acting mayor, and seconded by Milany Thiagarajah, councillor for the Darlington district.
No amount of money is attached to this declaration.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a motion of solidarity with the Iranian communities affected by the conflict in Iran.
The borough commits to maintaining a dialogue with organizations and members of the Iranian community in order to better take their needs into account in its actions.
It reaffirms its commitment to peace, fundamental rights, safety and dignity, and says it wants to fight stigmatization and discrimination.
It says it wants to continue its support actions with community and institutional partners, and recognizes the role of Iranian community organizations.
The text is based on the 2021 census: 2,625 people born in Iran live in the borough, which is 3.7% of the immigrant population, compared with 1.7% for Montréal as a whole.
The districts of Loyola, Côte-des-Neiges and Notre-Dame-de-Grâce are named as the areas where this presence is most notable.
The motion is presented by councillor Alexandre Teodoresco (district of Loyola) and seconded by Sonny Moroz, acting mayor.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce designates the month of January as Tamil Heritage Month within its territory.
The borough commits to continuing to promote and highlight the contribution of the Tamil community, together with its partners.
The motion notes that Tamil families settled in the borough starting in the early 1980s, notably as refugees.
It cites the 2021 census, according to which the Tamil language and Tamil origin are among those significantly represented in the borough's population.
The declaration involves no spending and no new obligations for residents.
Motion presented by the councillor for the Darlington district, Milany Thiagarajah, and seconded by acting mayor Sonny Moroz.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is giving $1,300 in one-time financial contributions to two organizations.
Notre-Dame-Des-Arts receives $300 for a week-long workshop where young people create sculptures out of recycled materials inspired by NDG, unveiled at a public exhibition.
UrbaNature Éducation receives $1,000 for two snowshoeing events at parcs Loyola and Trenholme and four winter activities with community groups in CDN-NDG.
The money comes from the discretionary budgets of councillors Peter McQueen ($800) and Alexandre Teodoresco ($500).
The purchase orders will be prepared after the borough council adopts the resolution.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council again declares the month of March "Bangladeshi Heritage Month" in the borough.
It condemns the acts of violence committed against the Hindu community in Bangladesh.
It reaffirms the importance of International Mother Language Day in promoting linguistic diversity and multilingualism.
The motion notes that the borough has a large community of Bangladeshi origin and hosts the annual "Bangla Mela" event at parc Martin Luther King.
The reasons given point to the rise in violence in Bangladesh since the summer of 2024, documented by Amnesty International and the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights.
The declaration involves no spending: it is a motion with no financial component.
Motion moved by the councillor for the district of Darlington and seconded by the borough's acting mayor.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council is adopting a declaration marking the 120th anniversary of the Communauté hellénique du Grand Montréal, in 2026.

The organization, active since 1906, has its head office on avenue Wilderton, in the borough, and brings together a school, a bishop's residence, a community centre and the cathédrale orthodoxe grecque Saint-Georges.
The declaration recognizes the historical, economic, social, cultural and artistic contribution of the Greek community in the borough.
The council also marks Greece's independence day, observed on March 25 and celebrated with a parade on the first Sunday after that date.
According to the 2021 census cited in the document, close to 27,000 people of Greek origin live in Montréal, or about 40% of those in Québec.
The motion is presented by Sonny Moroz, acting mayor, and seconded by Milany Thiagarajah, councillor for the Darlington district.
No sum of money and no obligation are attached to this declaration.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council is adopting a motion asking Hydro-Québec to improve its coordination and communications during power outages.

It follows the outage of January 24, 2026, caused by a breakdown at the Hampstead distribution station: more than 6,000 customers were affected, and some were without power for over 48 hours in very cold weather.

During the outage, the borough, the Croix-Rouge and the Centre de coordination des mesures d'urgence opened warming stations and overnight shelter at the Centre communautaire Côte-des-Neiges, where 38 people slept; firefighters knocked on close to 4,000 doors on January 25.
The council is asking Hydro-Québec to hold a public post-mortem meeting with the borough's residents by June 2026.
It is asking for a real-time communication system with the borough, the Centre de coordination des mesures d'urgence, the Tables de quartier and community organizations on the ground.

It is asking that work to strengthen the power grid be sped up, including the new Côte-Saint-Luc station announced on February 5, and that a detailed plan of corrective and preventive measures be submitted.
The borough has also started reviewing its own emergency communication procedures.
Regular meetings of the Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council will start at 6:30 p.m. instead of 7 p.m., from May to December 2026.
Residents who want to ask a question will have to register on site between 5:45 p.m. and 6:15 p.m.

The meetings are held in the council room, at 5160, boulevard Décarie, except in June (centre Le 6767, 6767, chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges) and in November (Centre culturel Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, 6400, avenue de Monkland).
The change comes from a request by the elected officials and aims, according to the borough, to improve accessibility and public participation.
The order of the public's questions is decided by a random draw after the registration period.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $2,770 in one-time financial contributions to three organizations.
Conseil communautaire de NDG is receiving $770 for the free music festival Porchfest 2026, held on the front porches of homes in NDG (fee for a visual artist, website, flyers and posters).
The same organization is also receiving $500 for a parent awareness project using the tool "Respect dans le sport pour les parents".
Fondation de l'école Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is receiving $1,000 for the "Le curieux" workshops offered to Grade 6 groups (media, citizenship, digital skills).
Association tamoule d'aînés du Québec is receiving $500 for a celebration of International Tamil Women's Day, with an awards presentation, free admission and meals, and performances.
The money comes from the elected officials' discretionary budgets: $1,270 from Peter McQueen, $1,000 from Alexandre Teodoresco and $500 from Sonny Moroz.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council recognizes April 14, 2026 as Yom HaShoah, the "Day of Remembrance for all victims of the Holocaust."
The declaration is made in solidarity with the survivors of the genocide, and as a sign of vigilance against the repetition of such crimes.
The council invites the public to take part in the commemorations held during that day and to reflect on the effects of prejudice, xenophobia, racism and antisemitism.
The reasons given recall that six million Jews were victims of the Shoah, that Montréal welcomed more than 30,000 survivors after the war, and that the borough is home to a large Jewish community.
The motion is based on the 1999 Québec law creating Holocaust Remembrance Day and on the City of Montréal's proclamation of March 25, 2002.
Motion moved by Councillor Sonny Moroz (Snowdon district) and seconded by Councillor Milany Thiagarajah (Darlington district).
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is paying out $6,250 in one-time financial contributions for 8 requests from organizations, taken from the elected officials' discretionary budgets.
Bread and Beyond/Au-delà du pain is receiving $1,000 for its sandwich-making activities with organizations that help people who are homeless or food insecure.
La Fabrique de la Paroisse Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is receiving $800 to cover part of the cost of summer camps for children from low-income families.
La Ligue de basketball des Philippines CDN/NDG is receiving $750 to rent gyms in the neighbourhood for its spring and summer tournaments.

Le Conseil régional des personnes âgées italo-canadiennes is receiving $1,200 to rent school buses (apple picking, sugar shack, casino), and the Association Saint-Raymond is receiving $1,200 for the Semaine italienne in August 2026.
Le Conseil communautaire NDG is receiving $300 for the free Porchfest 2026 music festival and $500 for a project to raise awareness among parents about respect in sports.
L'Association tamoule d'aînés du Québec is receiving $500 for an event marking International Tamil Women's Day.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is giving out $11,900 in one-time financial contributions to 9 organizations.
The money comes from the discretionary budgets of the borough mayor and the councillors for the districts of Côte-des-Neiges, Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Loyola, Snowdon and Darlington.

The largest amounts: $2,500 to Association Saint-Raymond NDG for Semaine italienne 2026, and $2,000 to Association des locataires HLM de la rue Walkley for its Habitation propre project (food baskets, neighbourhood parties, from March to December 2026).
$1,500 goes to Philo-Boxe for an outdoor community boxing event in a borough park, and $1,200 to Alliance Tamoul Unie for youth sports activities in Côte-des-Neiges.
$1,200 to Carrefour Jeunesse-emploi NDG for a spelling bee bringing together children from the after-school programs of 4 community centres.

Smaller contributions: $1,000 to FILCAN chess and social club (T-shirts), $900 to the Antigua and Barbuda Association of Montreal, $850 to the Centre Segal des arts de la scène and $750 to the Fédération des Associations Canado-Philippines du Québec.
The borough secretary of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce files the certificate of results of the register held from May 11 to 15, 2026 on a loan by-law of $7,645,000.
This loan is to be used for building repair and protection work and for the purchase of equipment.
Out of 98,354 people qualified to vote, 9,849 signatures were needed to trigger a referendum: no signatures were recorded.
The by-law is therefore deemed approved by the people qualified to vote.
Next step: ask the ministère des Affaires municipales et des Régions to approve the by-law.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is moving its regular October 2026 council meeting.
The meeting moves from Monday, October 5 to Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 6:30 p.m.
Reason given: October 5, 2026 is also the date of the Québec general election.
The change will be announced through a public notice posted on the borough's website.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council adopts a symbolic motion recognizing the contribution of the Italian community, on the occasion of Italian Heritage Month.
The motion notes that 135,430 people identified themselves as being of Italian origin in Montréal in the 2021 census, or nearly 8% of Montréal's population.

It refers to the role of Italian families in the businesses along the commercial streets of Côte-des-Neiges and Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, and that of workers in the construction of housing and infrastructure between 1950 and the mid-1970s.
