It mentions June 2 (Italy's national holiday) and June 10, a day commemorating the internment of 591 Italian-Canadians in 1940, recognized by city council since March 2013.
It cites the mural "La prémisse d'une fleur" on avenue Gatineau and ItalfestMTL, held for more than 30 years, notably in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The motion is moved by councillor Milany Thiagarajah (Darlington) and seconded by councillor Sonny Moroz (Snowdon). No spending is associated with it.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce recognizes the month of June as "Filipino Heritage Month."
The motion highlights the contributions of the Filipino-Canadian community to the social, cultural and economic life of the borough.
The council says it wants to continue to showcase this contribution in public spaces and in collective memory.
Reasons given: according to the 2021 census, 23,500 people in Montréal identify as members of the Filipino community, and more than 70% of them live in the borough.
Other reasons: Canada recognized June as Filipino Heritage Month in 2018, the borough had adopted a similar motion that same year, and place José-Rizal in parc Mackenzie-King already exists.
Motion presented by Mayor Stephanie Valenzuela and seconded by Councillor Sonny Moroz (Snowdon district).
No new spending or obligation is provided for in the document.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council officially recognizes Pride Month, celebrated in June.
The motion reaffirms the borough's commitment to an inclusive and safe society for all sexual orientations and gender identities.
It recognizes the contribution of community, cultural, educational and health organizations that support LGBTQ2+ communities in the borough.
The text notes that more work is still needed to make environments truly inclusive and accessible.
The borough invites residents to take part in the Pride celebrations that will be held in Montréal in August.
Motion moved by councillor Sonny Moroz (Snowdon district) and seconded by borough mayor Stephanie Valenzuela.
No sum of money or administrative measure is attached to the motion.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council is adopting a motion asking Québec to exclude housing co-operatives from Bill 20, which was tabled on February 11, 2026.
The borough has 27 housing co-operatives, or close to 700 units; the motion points out that 50% of Québec's co-operatives are in Montréal.
The council is against the single centralized application point set out in the bill, and wants co-operatives to keep the power to choose their own members.
It is also asking for the removal of the financial penalties that target households whose income goes above $58,439 (one person) or $82,645 (two people).
The council supports the recommendations of the CQCH and the FHCQ, including the removal of the automatic lease cancellation set out in section 23 and the recognition of community housing in the law.

The resolution will be sent to the Minister of Housing, Karine Boivin Roy, to members of the National Assembly Michelle Setlakwe, Désirée McGraw and Elisabeth Prass, to both federations, to the co-operatives in the borough's territory, and to the other boroughs and municipalities, which are invited to adopt a similar position.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is appointing Alexandre Teodoresco, councillor for the district of Loyola, as acting mayor.
His term covers the months of August 2026 to July 2027 inclusively.
He replaces Sonny Moroz, whose term as acting mayor ends on July 31, 2026.
Under its internal management by-law, the borough council must designate an acting mayor and set the length of the term.
The document does not indicate any financial impact.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is giving $17,600 in one-time financial contributions to 13 organizations.
The money comes from the discretionary budgets of the borough mayor and the councillors for the Côte-des-Neiges, Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Loyola, Snowdon and Darlington districts.
The largest amount, $7,500, goes to the Association des Philippins de Montréal et Banlieues (FAMAS) for the Pista sa Nayon event.

Other recipients: Orchestre Classique de Montréal ($2,100) for a festival at the Oratoire Saint-Joseph on July 4, 2026, Hockey mineur N.D.G. ($1,150) for jerseys, the Société du patrimoine philippin ($1,300) and the Communauté vietnamienne au Canada – Région de Montréal ($1,100).
The Conseil communautaire Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is receiving $800 to buy two Telraam traffic counters installed in the windows of homes.

Smaller amounts go to Chabad Côte-des-Neiges, the Association du Groupe de Femmes, the Centre d'orientation des nouveaux arrivants, the Association de Netball – Region 2, free Zumba classes at parc Van Horne, Notre-Dame-Des-Arts and Club Ami.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council marks the International Day for the Remembrance of the Slave Trade and Its Abolition, observed on August 23.
The borough commits to continuing its efforts to raise awareness of and fight systemic racism and discrimination in its programs and activities.
The motion recalls the declarations already adopted by the Ville de Montréal against racial discrimination (1989, 2004, 2015 and 2020).
It mentions actions already taken in the borough, such as the naming of parc Rosemary-Brown.
The motion also highlights the Semaine de commémoration organized each year by the Ligue des Noirs du Québec.
No amount of money is attached to the decision.
The motion is presented by councillor Sonny Moroz (Snowdon district) and seconded by borough mayor Stephanie Valenzuela.
The Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council recognizes August 1, 2026 as Emancipation Day, marking the abolition of slavery in Canada.
The motion recalls that slavery was abolished in the British Empire on August 1, 1834 and that the House of Commons designated that date as Emancipation Day in March 2021.
The council reaffirms its commitment to building an inclusive community where everyone is treated with dignity, respect and equality.
The council recognizes the contribution of residents of African descent to the social, cultural, economic and community life of the borough.

The motion cites the presence of the parc and the Pavillon Nelson-Mandela in the borough and the United Nations' second International Decade for People of African Descent (January 2025 to December 2034).
Motion moved by councillor Sonny Moroz (Snowdon district), seconded by councillor Milany Thiagarajah (Darlington district).
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council adopts a motion on the events of June 22, 2026 that took place in the borough.
It offers its condolences to the loved ones of SPVM officer Mohamed Lamine Benredouane, who died in the line of duty, and to those of citizen Michael Mizrahi.
It pays tribute to the police officers of neighbourhood station 26, the first to arrive on the scene, and to the entire SPVM.
It reaffirms its support for the SPVM and its commitment to working with it on public safety.
It asks the borough's departments to hold a commemorative gesture every June 22.
The motion is moved by Mayor Stephanie Valenzuela and seconded by the borough's four city councillors.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council adopts a motion condemning hate, violence and hate speech targeting women, including incel ideologies.
The motion refers to the tragedy that took place in the borough on June 22, 2026, whose perpetrator left behind a manifesto hostile to women.
It also recalls the Polytechnique attack of December 6, 1989 and the "Pas une de plus" demonstration held on June 25, 2026 at Place du 6-Décembre.
The borough says it wants to continue supporting organizations that prevent violence against women and support victims.
It says it encourages the development of resources and education to prevent radicalization and to promote non-violent models of masculinity.
The text mentions 811 – Info-Social as a resource for people in psychological distress.
The motion is moved by Mayor Stephanie Valenzuela and seconded by four city councillors from the borough.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is extending its contract with Go-Cube.com (9176-7277 Québec inc.) by 12 months for $197,757, taxes included.
The contract covers the period from March 12, 2026 to March 11, 2027.
The company picks up, transports, stores and fumigates for 60 days the furniture and belongings of evicted tenants left on public streets.
If the person does not retrieve their belongings after 60 days, the company disposes of them.
The contractor is waiving the 0.34% indexation provided for in the contract and is keeping the same rates.
The net expense of $180,578.50 is split between 2026 ($150,481.73) and 2027 ($30,096.77).
Without this service, according to the document, the bailiff could dispose of belongings left on public property as they see fit.
The City is awarding Construction Duradev inc. a $336,188.05 contract (taxes included) to repair the foundations of the Jardin botanique's exhibition greenhouses.
With contingencies ($67,237.61) and incidental costs ($50,428.21), the total authorized spending comes to $453,853.87, paid entirely by the central city.
The work involves removing cracked and crumbling concrete, repairing cracks and reinforcement bars, and strengthening some structural elements.
A 2023 expert report recommended quick fixes to the foundations of the tunnels and the slab under the greenhouses, which were built starting in 1956.
The work is to take place from June 1 to October 1, 2026, so that activities can continue until the new greenhouses open.
Duradev was the lowest of the 13 bidders, at 28.3% below the professionals' estimate.
The incidental costs will pay for a security guard for the restricted areas and an industrial hygiene specialist for decontamination.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve supports the gymnasium renovation projects at Saint-Clément and Sainte-Claire schools (Centre de services scolaire de Montréal), a condition for them to apply for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation.
The planned work: new floors, ceilings with acoustic panels, lighting, paint, basketball hoops, ventilation and air conditioning. Saint-Clément would also get a new divider curtain.
The borough commits to entering into or continuing a facility-sharing agreement so that the public can have access to them.
The provincial program has $300M for all of Québec; the assistance can cover up to 66% of eligible costs, to a maximum of $20M per project.
The schools have until June 22, 2026 to submit their application to the ministère.
According to the decision summary, the borough bears none of the costs of these projects.
The Montréal-Nord borough is adding an all-way stop at the intersection of rue de Castille and avenue Louis-Fréchette.
Two new stop signs will be installed on the east and west approaches of rue de Castille.
Stop lines and a pedestrian crossing (two white lines) will be marked on the ground, following the standards of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The request comes from the mobility committee that met on April 14, 2026, which recommended it favourably.
The technical opinion cites the density and variety of users (pedestrians, cyclists, STM users, trucking) and the proximity of parc Charleroi and a daycare.
A "Nouvelle signalisation" (new signage) sign will be installed one month before the stop, and then a small sign will remain for 30 to 60 days after it comes into service.
The installation costs (posts, signs, markings) still have to be budgeted, and the timeline will be set with the Direction des travaux publics.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is adding an all-way stop at the intersection of avenue Desaulniers and rue de Séville.
In practice, a stop sign will be installed at the south approach on avenue Desaulniers.
"No stopping at any time" signs will also be put up to clear 5 metres of visibility on each side.
The request came from a resident and was favourably recommended by the mobility committee at its meeting of April 14, 2026.
The technical opinion cites the safety of pedestrians and cyclists, given the proximity of Académie Nour and a bike path.
A "New signage" sign must be installed one month before the stop to warn road users.
The costs (posts, signs, pavement markings) have yet to be budgeted, and the installation schedule will be set with the Direction des travaux publics.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is adding an all-way stop at the intersection of boulevard Gouin and avenue Pigeon.
Stop signs will be installed on the east and west approaches of boulevard Gouin.
The terminus stop for bus line 140 will be moved to this intersection.
"No stopping at any time" signs will mark out 5-metre sight clearances.
A "New signage" sign must be put up one month before the stop takes effect, then kept in place for 30 to 60 days after it comes into force.
The recommendation comes from the mobility committee of April 14, 2026 and is based on a technical opinion; installation costs are still to be paid by public works.
The installation timeline will be set with the Direction des travaux publics.
The Montréal-Nord borough is awarding sidewalk work to Montreal Scellant inc. for $332,416.28, taxes included; the company submitted the lowest of the 6 bids received.
With contingencies ($63,159.09) and incidental costs ($23,339.93), the total authorized expense comes to $418,915.31, taxes included.

The work includes two sidewalk extensions: one at the intersection of boulevard Léger and avenue Désy, with a planting pit, and the other at the corner of boulevard Léger and avenue Lanthier, with draining green infrastructure.
The project aims to make intersections safer near parc Lacordaire, the Adélard-Desrosiers and Ste-Gertrude schools, the clinique médicale Lacordaire and the caisse Desjardins.
The winning bid is 32.29% below the borough's estimate (a difference of $188,614.28).
Funding comes 98.57% from the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité (Vision Zéro) and 1.43% from the Service de l'eau, for work to be carried out in 2026.
The City is giving $110,000 to the Chambre de commerce du Montréal métropolitain to organize four forums and a showcase of local businesses.
The four forums are about sustainable transition (500 participants), defence and security (450), major projects (450), and entrepreneurship and business takeovers (at least 320).
A showcase of Montréal solutions will be held during one of the forums to connect local businesses with buyers.
The events will take place from spring to fall 2026.
The payment is made in two parts: $77,000 in 2026 and $33,000 in 2027.
The money comes from the Entente 200 M$ MEIE 2025-2029, and the expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration.
The City's contribution represents 9.75% of the project's total cost.
The City is giving $2,264,500 to 69 organizations for 75 festivals and cultural events to be held in 2026 across the 19 boroughs.
The program's budget is rising from $1,759,500 to $2,264,500, an increase of nearly 30% resulting from the recurring addition of $1.25M announced by the elected administration in November 2025.
The amounts range from $5,000 to $60,000 per project; among the highest: Cinemania, the FIFA and the Rencontres internationales du documentaire de Montréal ($60,000 each).
The program has 4 streams: professional festivals (33 projects), vitality in the neighbourhoods (31), themed and festive events (9) and cultural parades (2).
Of the 121 applications submitted, 95 were eligible and 75 were selected after review by juries made up of 3 people from outside the City.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city; the organizations must apply the City's visibility protocol.
The City is giving $230,000 to six cultural organizations for business events that will be held in Montréal between April and November 2026.

Four organizations are each receiving $45,000: l'Association des galeries d'art contemporain du Canada (Plural fair), la Conférence internationale des arts de la scène de Montréal (Biennale 2026), le Conseil des métiers d'art du Québec (Salons des métiers d'art) and MUTEK (Village numérique).
La Fondation Dynastie is getting $27,000 for the Sommet Dynastie 2026, and Québec Édition - ANEL is getting $23,000 for its fellowship program.
Of the 8 applications submitted, 6 were found eligible and all of them were selected, after review by a 4-person jury.
The program's budget is going from $350,500 in 2025 to $230,000 in 2026.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, out of the Service de la culture budget.
The organizations must apply the City's visibility protocol and inform the public about any obstructions on public property, if applicable.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is paying $10,000 more (taxes included) to the firm Cardin Julien inc. for professional services already provided.
These services concern the redevelopment and expansion of the chalet in parc de la Louisiane, at 4644, rue Beaubien Est.

The additional amount covers an estimate for decontamination and the supervision of work in the presence of asbestos, which were not included in the original contract, as well as changes made during the work.
The original contract, awarded in October 2022, was for $307,300.93 (total authorized expenditure of $352,396.07).
With this addition, the contingency envelope goes from $41,177.87 to $50,309.20 (net), an increase of 3.25%.
The net cost of $9,131.33 is paid by the borough out of its 2026-2035 capital works program.
The work was finally accepted on November 27, 2025; this payment closes the mandate.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is authorizing its director of territorial development to sign the necessary agreements with the Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (CSSDM).
These agreements aim to increase the capacity of the electrical service entrance at the centre Père-Marquette, as part of its redevelopment and upgrading to current standards.
The CSSDM's authorization is required because the land, which the City owns, has been leased to the CSSDM under a 63-year emphyteutic lease, from August 1, 1970 to July 31, 2033.
A photographic survey will be done in the crawl space under the gymnasium slab, to compare the archived plans with the actual installations.
Because this is a confined space, an outside firm will characterize the site before anyone enters, for safety reasons.
Another firm will carry out a soil characterization and a geotechnical study, because the new electrical conduits will rest on precast slabs supported by the ground.
The contractor selected for the overall project will then carry out the work on the electrical service entrance. The document does not specify any amount or timeline.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is applying for a grant from the ministère de l'Éducation to renovate the centre Père-Marquette, at 1600, rue de Drucourt, and bring it up to standard.
The provincial program (PAFIRSPA, stream 1) can cover up to 66% of the eligible cost, up to a maximum of $20M, with the work to be completed within 5 years.
The work targets universal accessibility (elevators, inclusive change rooms, entrances, washrooms), mechanical systems, electrical systems and fire protection.
The project also includes rebuilding the swimming pool basin and its deck areas, and replacing the equipment in the filtration room.
The borough will complete the funding through its Ten-Year Capital Works Program and the Programme Aquatique Montréal, and will absorb 100% of any cost overruns.
Next steps: approval by the executive committee on May 6, 2026, submission no later than June 22, 2026, and a response from the ministère expected in January or February 2027.

The City is paying $97,380.89 (net of rebates) to the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, taken from the environmental liability reserve for contaminated sites. The expense is covered 100% by the ville centre.

The money pays for the plans and specifications for a system to control biogas (methane) and radon at the centre Père-Marquette, at 1600, rue de Drucourt, as part of its redevelopment and upgrading to current standards.
The building is located within the boundaries of former quarry no. 30, and studies have detected biogas and radon there, both inside and outside.

Four firms are sharing the amount: WSP Canada ($60,821.20 including taxes, negotiated contract dated November 25, 2025), Première Équipe Architecture ($10,548.96), EMS Structure ($13,452.08) and Bouthillette Parizeau ($12,127.56), plus $8,852.81 in contingencies.

The work planned at the centre includes two hydraulic elevators, repairs to the basement locker rooms, rebuilding the indoor pool basin, repairs to a sunken sidewalk on rue de Bellechasse and a new transformer.
The borough will have to report on its spending every quarter to the Service de l'environnement; the final amount could be less than expected.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding Cojalac inc. a contract worth $1,428,909.30 (taxes included) for work planned in 2026 on rue Parthenais.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,765,800.23, which is the contract plus $142,890.93 in contingencies and $194,000 in incidental costs (materials testing, soil monitoring, horticulture).

At the intersection of Parthenais and Gauthier: curb extensions with concrete and granite borders, planting pits, rebuilding of the roadway, sidewalks and catch basins, and installation of a BIXI station.
Between rue Sherbrooke and rue Rachel: milling and repaving of the roadway on rue Parthenais.
Lead water service lines are being replaced in both areas, as the City has committed to the ministère de l'Environnement to remove all of them by 2030.
The borough cites the desire to slow down vehicles, make things safer for pedestrians and add more greenery.
Five companies submitted bids out of 13 that picked up the documents; Cojalac inc. submitted the lowest price, ahead of Pavages Métropolitain ($1,606,681.35).

The City is awarding Les Entreprises Michaudville inc. a $11,160,000 contract (taxes included) to rebuild the infrastructure on rue De Champlain, between Sainte-Catherine Est and René-Lévesque, in Ville-Marie.
With contingencies ($1,194,312.06) and incidental costs ($2,063,613.27), the total expense comes to $14,417,925.33, taxes included.

The project replaces a 1,200 mm main water pipe installed in 1927, which has had 13 major breaks; the City wants to secure the water supply for about 180,000 people in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Montréal-Est, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Ville-Marie.
The work also involves the sewer, service connections (including ten made of lead), Bell and CSEM conduits, a gas pipe, and street lighting.
At street level: a 265 m bike path, 3,100 m² of sidewalks, 610 m of granite curbs, 2,700 m² of roadway, street furniture and tree planting.
This is the third and final phase of the rue De Champlain work; the previous phases were completed in 2023 and in 2025.

The cost is split between the agglomeration (54.94%), the central city (33.66%), the CSEM (11.01%) and Bell Canada (0.38%); a delay costs the contractor 0.1% of the contract per day, with a minimum of $1,000.

The mayor of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is tabling the report on the highlights of the 2025 financial statements at the July 6, 2026 borough council meeting, as required by the Cities and Towns Act.
The borough ended 2025 with an operating surplus of $2,877,500, on a spending budget of $80,191,300.

The surplus comes mainly from revenue tied to the occupancy of public property, including $1.5M attributable to the "Blitz permis" operation carried out with the SPVM, the Agence de mobilité durable and the Escouade Mobilité.
The borough notes a $1.2M deficit in pay, offset by $2.6M in savings (technical services, energy related to the temporary closure of Centre Le Manoir, aggregates and abrasives).
More than $12.8M was invested in parks in 2025, including $7.6M in local investments: the Benny skate park, and the redevelopment of parc Jean-Brillant, parc Loyola and parc Herbert-Outerbridge.

A change in the accounting standard for building permits leaves an unfavourable net result of $0.2M: despite $1.5M in actual revenue, $1.7M was deducted to complete the adjustment spread over two years.
The report also mentions Rendez-vous NDG (more than 50,000 people), Imagine Monkland, 35 outdoor cultural events and 49 performances in parks.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is submitting to the executive committee its 2025 report on spending related to waste management, as required by the city council's delegation of powers.
The submission also includes the budget progress report as of August 31, 2025 and a technical report on delegated activities provided by the Service de l'environnement.
In 2025, the borough sent 53,446 tonnes of materials to treatment or disposal sites, compared to 55,813 tonnes in 2024, including 33,329 tonnes of household garbage.
The borough's diversion rate stands at 38%, the same as in 2024.
Each resident generated 279.31 kg of residual materials, compared to 307.63 kg for the Montréal average.
Borough residents made 26,281 visits to ecocentres in 2025, a 2% decrease compared to 2024.
The borough is presenting its report in its own format, while waiting for the Service de l'environnement to propose a common template for all boroughs.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is tabling its annual report on two money reserves: the one for parks and playgrounds, and the parking fund, for the year 2025.
The parks account took in 17 contributions from developers totalling $3,243,874.01 in 2025, and its balance went from $10,075,985.86 to $7,806,882.32 as of December 31.

$2,170,212.70 funded new projects in 2025: a permanent promenade at parc Jean-Brillant ($1,023,169), a multi-sport field at parc Mackenzie-King ($574,064), renovation of the chalet at parc Loyola ($290,663) and landscaping at parc de la Savane ($282,316.70).
$6,683,373.11 went to projects already under way, mainly the expansion of the chalet and the new wading pool at parc Jean-Brillant, as well as the skatepark at parc Benny.
One developer was reimbursed $89,000 after cancelling a project to subdivide land for a two-unit building.
The parking fund was used to buy two 8-space bike shelters ($46,591.57) at the Darlington and Madison public works yards; its balance dropped from $81,038.06 to $36,524.24.
The report stems from a recommendation by the Auditor General issued in February 2019 on the monitoring of contributions for park purposes.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is adopting a management surplus of $2,877,500 for 2025.
It is adding $49,324 in unspent amounts from earlier projects (school transportation, parks master plan, public squares, consultations), for a total of $2,926,824 to be allocated.

The money goes to the Théâtre Empress ($750,000), the aréna Doug-Harvey ($500,000), the Centre sportif Côte-des-Neiges ($374,000), and the rental and purchase of equipment for infrastructure ($303,500).
$400,000 is set aside for budget balancing and $599,324 remains as free surplus.
The surplus comes mainly from revenues for occupancy of public property ($1,498,600) and from the sharing of surplus construction permit revenues ($1,473,000).
Every expense drawn from these amounts will require a borough council resolution.
The borough mayor will present the highlights of the financial results at the July 6 council meeting, rather than in September.
The borough of Lachine is approving a minor exemption for a new mixed-use building at 1750, rue Notre-Dame.
The exemption frees the multifamily building from having to install a green roof, normally required for any building with more than 2,000 square metres of floor area.
The project is part of the redevelopment of the Urgel-Bourgie site, approved in 2023 and already under construction.

The developers point to a regulatory dead end: the Régie du bâtiment du Québec only has technical criteria for green roofs on non-combustible structures, while this building is of combustible construction.
The Régie is preparing a new guide for combustible construction and, in the meantime, is suspending all new requests for alternative measures.
The decision is based on the documents received on February 6, 2026 and on the opinion of the comité consultatif d'urbanisme of February 11, 2026.
The borough of Lachine is granting a minor exemption to the zoning by-law for a multi-family building at 425, 18e Avenue.
The exemption allows a rear setback of 2.22 metres, while the zoning requires 4.6 metres in zone M-317.
The purpose is to legalize after the fact the last phase of the Daly-Morin project, whose construction was completed at the end of 2025 and which is more than 80% occupied.
The location certificate given to the borough showed that the actual distance (2.22 m) differs from the one planned in the project (2.4 m).
The decision is based on documents received on January 29 and February 6, 2026.
The borough of Lachine is approving the plans for a mixed-use building with 180 units on 10 floors, at 220, boulevard Saint-Joseph.
The construction permit is granted on the condition that the project complies with the regulations in force.
Any future change to the project will have to go through a new site planning and architectural integration programme (PIIA) plan approval.
This is the Le Flora project, under construction since 2018, halted several times because of bankruptcies and the health crisis, then restarted in 2025.
The owners are changing the cladding: the raised diamond-like effect is kept only on the facade of tower B facing boulevard Saint-Joseph.
Elsewhere on tower B and on tower C (avenue Skaniatarati), the fibre-cement panels will be installed flat, in two shades of the same colour laid out in a staggered pattern.
The borough of Lachine agrees to accept a free transfer of land measuring 1,124.1 m² (new lot 6 589 900) from a developer for park purposes, at 360-390, rue Sherbrooke.
The owner must also pay $65,749.20 to the City, in addition to the land transferred.
Together, the land (8.13% of the site) and the payment (1.87% of the value) reach the 10% contribution required by the by-law on park fees.

The site of the former Andritz factory will be redeveloped into five buildings totalling 172 housing units: two rows of townhouses, two duplexes and two multi-family buildings of three and four storeys.
The fees must be paid before the subdivision permit is issued; the 13,820 m² piece of land will be divided into five new lots.
The chartered appraisal firm PCG Carmon, hired by the City, valued the site at $3,516,000.
The borough of Lachine is accepting $575,000 from the owner of the land at 2100, rue Remembrance, as a contribution for park purposes.
Lot 1 246 717 will be divided into two identical lots, for phases 2 and 3 of a redevelopment project at the corner of rue Remembrance and 20e Avenue.
Phase 2 calls for a six-storey building with 194 units, approved by the borough council on September 2, 2025; phase 3 has not been planned yet.
The amount is equal to 10% of the value of the land, appraised at $5,750,000 by the chartered appraisal firm PCG Carmon, hired by the Ville.
These fees must be paid before the Ville issues the subdivision permit.
The borough of Lachine is approving the plans for a project at 1900, rue Notre-Dame: demolition of the former CLSC and construction of a four-storey mixed-use building with a mezzanine.

The building will have 223 housing units and two commercial spaces on the ground floor, with the entrance to the housing units on the rue Victoria side and access to the businesses on the rue Notre-Dame side.
A two-level underground parking garage will provide 228 residential spaces and 16 commercial spaces, including 4 for people with reduced mobility; access will be from rue Notre-Dame.
The areas that are not built on will be laid out as green courtyards, with a green roof and a common area with a pool on the roof.
Waste will be stored in a room in the underground parking garage; a collection area is planned along rue Notre-Dame.
The project is exempt from the Règlement pour une métropole mixte, as its habitable area (17,874 m²) remains below the 18,000 m² threshold; it would be subject to the by-law if the area increases.
The permit will be issued only if the project complies with the regulations, and any change will have to go through a new approval of plans.
The borough of Lachine is granting a minor exemption from the zoning by-law for a new multi-family building at 1931, rue Notre-Dame (160-190, 20e Avenue).
The exemption releases the project from having to install a green roof, which is normally required for any building with more than 2,000 square metres of floor area.
The project, under construction on the site of the former Loutec, is of combustible construction.

According to the document, the Régie du bâtiment du Québec has technical criteria only for green roofs on non-combustible structures, and it is suspending new applications for alternative measures while a new guide is being developed.
The decision is based on the documents received on April 16, 2026 and on the opinion of the comité consultatif d'urbanisme issued on May 13, 2026.
The borough of Lachine approves the plans to transform the Maison du Brasseur and the Entrepôt, at 2901, boulevard Saint-Joseph, in an area of heritage interest.
A new 35-metre "S"-shaped ramp, with three landings, will replace the current ramp, which was found to be non-compliant (slope too steep) and has been the subject of several complaints.
The ramp will be made of concrete landings, oiled wood walkways, a gabion wall, galvanized steel guardrails, with a bench and plantings.
The cedar shingle roof of the Maison du Brasseur will be replaced by a galvanized steel standing-seam metal roof, after a historical analysis confirmed this was the original covering.
At the Entrepôt, the stairs of the rear terrace will be removed and replaced by a ramp leading to the bike path; the terrace will be enlarged to provide level access to the parking lot.
A gabion wall will hide the new generator and the ventilation grille; planters will be set up around the perimeter.
The permit will be issued on the condition that the project complies with the regulations, and any change will have to go through a new approval of the plans.
The borough of Lachine is accepting a $51,400 parks contribution from the owner of 600, rue Victoria.
The project turns the building's commercial second floor into four housing units.
This type of redevelopment requires the owner to pay a sum to the City before getting the construction permit.
The chartered appraisal firm PCG Carmon, hired by the City, valued the land at $514,000; the contribution equals 10% of that value.
No social or community housing and no units with 3 or more bedrooms are planned in the project, which would have reduced the amount owed.
The money will be used to create, maintain and improve parks and playgrounds.
The borough of Lachine is accepting a contribution of $703,408.07 from the owner of the land at 1900, rue Notre-Dame, paid to the City for parks and playgrounds.
The project planned for this land is a mixed-use building with 223 housing units and businesses on the ground floor.
Of the 223 units, 23 have three bedrooms or more (family units) and no social housing is planned.
These park fees must be paid before the construction permit is issued.

The amount comes from an appraisal of the land at $7,843,000 carried out by the firm PCG Carmon, hired by the City; the contribution corresponds to 10% of the site's value, calculated according to the formula in by-law 17-055.

The borough of Lachine is starting the process to authorize a specific project (PPCMOI) allowing Day & Ross inc. to set up an outdoor storage area for heavy machinery (tractor-trailers) at 1111, rue François-Lenoir.
The land in question, a vacant wooded lot bought by the City in 2015 for the sorting centre, would be merged with the company's current land to form a single lot before the permit is issued.

The project, reduced from 97 to 87 storage spaces, involves cutting down 125 of the 158 trees in the wooded area (41 that are dying, 84 because they are in the way of the work); 124 trees would be kept or planted in the end, including at the employee parking lot.
The company will have to give the borough a biological report on the brown snake, which may be present on the site, and apply the report's conclusions before getting the permit.
The storage area will have to be covered with permeable or reflective materials (solar reflectance index of at least 29), maintained over time.
A bank guarantee of $50,000 must be deposited before the permit is issued; work must start within 24 months and be finished within the following 12 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The decision departs from the zoning in force, in particular on land use, the building coverage ratio and the floor area ratio; some elements may be subject to approval by referendum.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is approving a promise under which the Ville commits to transferring, through an emphyteutic lease for 100 years, a piece of land of about 2,500 m² to the Table de quartier de Parc-Extension.
The land in question is located where the outdoor basketball court is, on the site of the aréna Howie-Morenz.
The organization will build a three-storey community centre there: space for neighbourhood organizations, multi-purpose rooms and a gymnasium with a basketball court open to the public.

The land is transferred with no payment and no annual rent, on the condition that it be used exclusively as a community centre; at the end of the emphyteutic lease, the Ville takes back the land and the building with no compensation.
The Table de quartier has obtained $18.6M from Infrastructure Canada; the construction cost must be at least $30,000,000 under the funding conditions.
The arena's parking lot will be partly redeveloped and will keep about 22 spaces, including 4 for people with reduced mobility.
The emphyteutic lease deed must be signed by March 31, 2027 at the latest, otherwise the promise becomes void.
The City is awarding Groupe Gesfor Poirier, Pinchin inc. the professional industrial hygiene services for its building deconstruction projects.
The master agreement is worth a maximum of $227,484.94, plus $45,496.99 (20%) in contingencies for unforeseen costs, for a total of $272,981.93 including taxes.
It lasts 60 months, with two renewal options of 12 months each.
These deconstructions target vacant City buildings, to make way for low-rent housing projects run by non-profit organizations.
The firm must inventory materials of concern, write the technical specifications, supervise the work sites and support the City until the final acceptance of the work.
The public call for tenders drew 6 bids; the selected price is 37.87% ($138,647.01) lower than the City's latest estimate.
The expenses will be charged to the budgets of the boroughs and the corporate departments, as needed.
The City is signing an agreement with the Fédération canadienne des municipalités (Fonds municipal vert) for a loan of up to $8,333,330 and a grant of up to $1,666,660.
The money will help pay for the construction of the new library and cultural space Espace du Cœur-Nomade, at 3170, boulevard Henri-Bourassa Est, in Montréal-Nord.
The building is aiming for LEED Canada NC Gold certification and energy use at least 56% lower than the standards of the Code modèle national de l'énergie.
The loan runs for 10 years and will be paid out at the end of the project; the City must request the payout within 60 days of completion, planned for September 30, 2026.
The grant is equal to 20% of the loan; its final payment will be made no later than two years after the final loan payment.
Construction work began in July 2024; a contract of $48,735,108.96 had been awarded to Magil Construction Est du Canada inc. in May 2024.
The mayor and the director of finance and treasurer are authorized to sign the agreement.

The City is awarding a contract without a call for tenders to Bibliotheca Canada inc. for an automated document return and sorting system in the future library and cultural space of the Espace du Cœur-Nomade, at 3170, boulevard Henri-Bourassa Est.
The total spending is $216,897.81 including taxes: $197,179.83 for the contract and $19,717.98 in contingencies (10%) for possible technical adjustments.
The system includes two touch-screen return stations for the public, one station on the staff side, three conveyors, two sorting tables and five receiving bins.
The contract runs from April 21, 2026 to October 31, 2027.

The City justifies the direct award by a highly specialized market: a notice of intent published from February 18 to March 4, 2026 attracted no other supplier; only Bibliotheca offers support in French and compatibility with the Montréal library network.

The equipment will serve the boroughs of Montréal-Nord and Ahuntsic-Cartierville; the spending is covered by the central city, with a grant from the ministère de la Culture of $79,222.64 (net of rebate).

The City is awarding Solotech inc. a $1,027,332.67 contract (taxes included) to supply and install the stage design and multimedia equipment for the Espace du Cœur-Nomade, at 3170, boulevard Henri-Bourassa Est, in Montréal-Nord.
With a contingency budget of $51,366.63 (5%), the total authorized spending comes to $1,078,699.30, taxes included, paid 100% by the central city.
The equipment is for the performance hall and the multi-purpose rooms: stage lighting, a platform, projectors, audio systems, screens and consoles.
The work will take place from June 16, 2026 to December 31, 2028; the Espace du Cœur-Nomade is scheduled to open in 2027.
Public call for tenders 26-21351 received 2 compliant bids; Solotech's bid is 5.32% below the professionals' estimate.
The funding comes from two loan by-laws, including $854,976.74 net tied to the library renovation and construction program, with a grant from the ministère de la Culture.
Solotech inc.'s performance will be evaluated, since the contract is over $500,000.

The City is awarding Unique Mobilier a $140,629.37 contract (taxes included) to supply and install the furniture for the Espace du Cœur-Nomade, at 3170, boulevard Henri-Bourassa Est, in Montréal-Nord.
A contingency budget of $14,062.94 is added, for a total expenditure of $154,692.31, paid entirely by the central city.
The furniture includes workstations, tables and counters, as well as metal filing cabinets and storage units.
The Espace du Cœur-Nomade will bring together a library and a maison de la culture; it is scheduled to open in 2027.
The contract runs from June 16, 2026 to November 30, 2027.
Two companies submitted bids out of five that obtained the tender documents; the winning bid is 41.55% ($99,955.82) lower than the professionals' estimate.
Funding comes from loan by-laws related to libraries and cultural spaces, with a portion coming from a grant from the ministère de la Culture.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is approving a parking space reserved at all times for people with reduced mobility, in front of 12527, rue Victoria.
The request comes from a resident who rents and who has permanent physical limitations, and who has no driveway entrance for off-street parking.
The decision is based on a medical assessment and on observations made at the applicant's home.
Any other signs already in place at the location remain in effect.
The signs will be installed as soon as the borough council approves the request.
According to the document, the costs of installing and maintaining the signs are paid by the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough, which has a dedicated budget.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is removing the parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility in front of 11826, rue De La Gauchetière.
The person who used this space is moving away from the address, so the reserved parking space is no longer needed.
The space becomes available again for parking by residents of the area.
Any other signs already in place at the location are kept.
The signs will be removed as soon as the borough council approves this.
The cost of removing the signs is covered by a centralized budget of the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is borrowing $7,645,000 to renovate its buildings and buy equipment.
The money will go to work on arenas, pavilions and park chalets with community rooms: roofs, structures, plumbing, electrical systems, bringing an indoor pool up to standard, and redoing rooms.
A special tax will be collected each year on all taxable buildings in the borough, based on their property value, to pay back the loan.
The loan and its refinancings cannot exceed 20 years.

The funding need comes from the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program: $3,091,000 in 2026, $2,697,000 in 2027 and $3,373,000 in 2028, for a total of $9,161,000, of which $1,516,000 is left over from an earlier by-law.
The by-law still has to be approved by the qualified voters (through the holding of a register) and by the Ministère des Affaires municipales before calls for tenders.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is adding $11,497.50 (taxes included) to the contract with the firm GBI experts-conseils inc. for mechanical and electrical engineering services at piscine René-Goupil.
The contract therefore goes from $249,670.51 to $261,168.01, and the contingency budget from $41,611.75 to $53,109.25.
The bill is shared: $2,989.35 paid by the borough (26%) and $8,508.15 by the ville centre, through the PEV-DIM program grant (74%).

The document states that conditions encountered on the construction site forced changes, and that five amendments totalling $41,351.10 have already been granted (automatic controls, filtration, video surveillance, client requests).
Only $260.65 was left in the contingency budget, which was considered insufficient to finish the project.
The grant agreement requires that the amount be committed before March 31, 2026 and spent before March 31, 2027.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is hiring NAXO Construction (9220-9733 Québec inc.) to replace the cooling system at the bibliothèque de Saint-Michel, at 7601, rue François-Perrault.
The contract is worth $732,390.75 including taxes; the total authorized spending comes to $871,544.99, with $109,858.61 in contingencies and $29,295.63 in incidental costs.
The current system has been out of service for two years, and a temporary air conditioning unit has been rented during that time.
The work includes dismantling the two rooftop units, roof repairs, partial interior demolition and installation of the new equipment.
Work is scheduled from early August 2026 to early May 2027, funded by the borough's investment program ($438,000 in 2026, $358,000 in 2027, net of tax rebates).
Of the 6 bids received, 2 did not meet the requirements; the winning bid is $15,358.73 (2.1%) above the professionals' estimate and $99,809.77 lower than the second-place bid.

The City is giving $100,000 to the Groupe de recherche et d'éducation sur les mammifères marins (GREMM), an organization based in Tadoussac, to produce the content for an exhibition about the beluga whale (videos, educational activities).
It is also adding technical support valued at $75,000: set design, materials, equipment, maintenance, installation, educational programs and promotion.
The exhibition « À la découverte de la vie sociale des bleuvets » will be presented on level 100 of the Biodôme, in a free-admission space, from fall 2026 to fall 2029.
The Biodôme becomes the Montréal site of the « Fenêtre sur les bélugas » project, which broadcasts images and sounds captured by drones and hydrophones in the St. Lawrence estuary.
The money will be paid in two instalments: $60,000 within 30 days of the agreement being signed, then $40,000 on October 30, 2026.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city. The department expects 150,000 visitors per year for the exhibition.
Schedule: design in winter-spring 2026, production in summer 2026, opening in fall 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is making rue Mackay a two-way street between boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest and avenue Overdale.

The change becomes possible now that construction of the buildings on Mackay and Overdale is finished and the roadway and sidewalks have been redeveloped, as part of the Programme particulier d'urbanisme du Quartier des gares.

Until now, residents of the area, including those in the YUL tower at 1450, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, had to go through Overdale, Lucien-L'Allier, Saint-Antoine Ouest and Guy to head to the north of the city.
No parking spaces are lost or added on rue Mackay.
The signage work will be done by the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and billed to Ville-Marie.
The order is adopted on March 10, 2026, the work orders go out the week of March 16, and implementation is planned for mid-April.
The borough of Ville-Marie is making rue Duke one-way northbound, between rue de la Commune Ouest and rue Brennan.
Rue de la Commune Ouest becomes one-way eastbound, between rue Nazareth and rue Duke.
The change targets the Brennan–Duke–Nazareth area, which has been transformed notably by the Haleco real estate project (327 housing units, 94 indoor parking spaces).
The borough plans to add 5 SRRR parking spaces (reserved for residents).
Drivers will have to change their routes in the area.
A notice will be distributed to local residents and signs will be posted for 30 days before the work; the new signage is planned for the week of May 20, 2026.
The signage work will be done by the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and billed to Ville-Marie internally.
The borough of Ville-Marie is amending its by-law on traffic and parking.
The power to set up waiting areas for taxis, buses, minibuses and other vehicles moves from the borough council to a public servant (level B).
According to the document, the current process is long; the amendment aims to simplify it and allow for faster changes.
The by-law also corrects the definition of "director": it will be the director of the department concerned, rather than the director of public works and the environment.
Notice of motion given on April 14, 2026; adoption expected at the borough council meeting of May 5, 2026.
A public notice will be published when the by-law comes into force.
No amount of money is tied to this decision.
Ville-Marie is updating the list of bridges where heavy vehicle traffic is restricted, along with the maximum weights allowed.

Eight bridges are covered, including those on René-Lévesque and De La Gauchetière (between Robert-Bourassa and Mansfield), Sainte-Catherine Est (between Bercy and Omar-Ravary), McGill College, the pont du Cosmos, as well as Saint-Claude, Gosford and Notre-Dame (between Berri and Panet).
The limits range from 15 to 24 tonnes for a single-unit vehicle, and up to 50 tonnes for a three-unit combination; on Saint-Claude, Gosford and Notre-Dame, any overloaded vehicle is prohibited.
Emergency vehicles are not subject to these limits.
The amendment removes sections that are not in Ville-Marie and adds bridges that were missing from the by-law.
This is the notice of motion; adoption is planned for September 2026, approval by the ministry in the fall of 2026, and adjustment of the signage in the fall of 2026.
The borough of Lachine is authorizing the set-up of a small farm display (farm animals in a free-standing pen) on the outdoor site of the Musée de Lachine.
It takes place on Saturday, October 10, 2026, from 1 p.m. to 4:30 p.m., during the Fête des récoltes.
The borough is approving an expense of $2,552.45, taxes included, paid out of the Musée's operating budget.
The City's executive committee must issue an order allowing the animals to be present, under the by-law on the keeping of domestic animals.
The event is free and open to everyone; it includes music and sales.
The Fête des récoltes has been held since 2023 and draws between 500 and 700 participants each year.
A public notice announcing the order will be published on the borough's website.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is transferring $25,770 from its management surplus to the 2026 budget: these are funds from a grant from the ministère de l'Éducation du Québec that were not used in 2025.
This money is used to offer residents free lifeguard and aquatic instructor training in 2026.
The free courses covered include the Bronze Medallion and Bronze Cross, first aid/AED, National Lifeguard pool and beach, swimming and lifesaving instructor, and aquatic emergency care.
The funds must be used only for this purpose; any amount not spent must be repaid to the Service national des sauveteurs.
The courses must be completed no later than March 31, 2026, and the accountability report is due June 15, 2026.
According to the document, the measure is also intended to address the shortage of pool attendants and instructors.
No communications activities aimed at the public are planned.

The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is ending the contract for cleaning, security and minor maintenance services at the Complexe sportif St-Jean-Vianney, which had been awarded to Collège St-Jean-Vianney.
The Collège itself asked to end its commitment for 2026; the cancellation takes effect on July 31, 2026 and comes at no cost to the City.
The original contract was awarded in February 2024 for 48 months (April 2024 to March 2028) in the amount of $1,545,897.96, following public call for tenders 23-20229.
The Collège agrees to keep providing the services during a transition period, to avoid any interruption at the Complexe sportif.
The City will use this period to launch a new call for tenders and choose another supplier.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is hiring Sogep inc. to handle cleaning, security and minor maintenance at the Complexe sportif Saint-Jean-Vianney.
The contract is worth $1,983,861.25, taxes included, from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2030, with the option of two 12-month extensions.
Sogep inc. was the lowest of the three bidders in the public call for tenders: $1,983,861.25, compared with $2,170,891.59 (Groupe Laberge) and $2,218,077 (9/Onze).
The chosen price is $253,009.44 (14.6%) higher than the City's most recent estimate.
This contract replaces the one with Collège St-Jean-Vianney, which was terminated effective July 31, 2026.
The expense is paid 100% by the borough, out of its operating budget.
According to the document, without a new service provider as of August 2026, the Complexe could close temporarily for lack of cleanliness and security.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is renting out the snack bar at aréna Rodrigue-Gilbert to Mélanie Daigle and Patrick Daudelin, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027.
The tenants will pay the borough $4,372 (taxes included), in two equal payments: on November 1, 2026 and February 1, 2027.
The agreement allows for a possible one-year renewal, from September 1, 2027 to August 31, 2028, for $4,459.44 taxes included.
The snack bar will be open from 4:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. Monday to Friday, and from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays.
The two new operators are currently employees of the snack bar; the previous operators, Dominic Gauthier and Daniel Wiseman, did not want to take up their renewal year.
Without this agreement, the arena would have no food service on site, according to the document.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is proposing to city council that it take charge itself of minor sidewalk repairs on the arterial streets in its territory in 2026.
The borough would handle the plans and specifications, the call for tenders, the awarding of contracts and the supervision of the work.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is footing the bill: a budget of $560,000, net of rebate, is allocated to the borough.
The sidewalks concerned are those on the streets already included in the 2026-2027 milling and paving programs.
Planned timeline: call for tenders in March 2026, contracts in April, work from May to October 2026.
No geometric redesign of the arterial streets is planned in this project.
According to the document, the borough receives a high number of requests about the condition of these sidewalks.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is proposing to manage the construction of sidewalks and curbs itself on rue de Rouen, between avenue Letourneux and avenue Bennett.
The borough would handle the plans and specifications, the call for tenders, the awarding of contracts and the supervision of the work.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité is paying the full amount: a budget of $616,192, net of rebate, is allocated to the borough.
Stated goal: to fill in missing sidewalks on the south side of the street to make walking safer (pedestrians, children, seniors) and to reduce traffic speed.
Planned timeline: plans and specifications in March-April 2026, call for tenders in April, contracts in July, work from July to October 2026.
The project had been submitted in 2024 but was turned down for lack of budget; additional funding obtained in 2026 makes it possible to relaunch it.
If the offer is not accepted, the borough loses the opportunity to carry out this work.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is awarding Groupe ABF inc. a contract worth $1,063,285.35 (taxes included) to rebuild sections of sidewalk in 2026.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,317,228.85, including $147,943.50 for contingencies and $106,000 for supervision and incidental costs.
The work covers about 1,300 m² of sidewalk on local streets and 1,260 m² on arterial streets in the borough.
It includes demolishing and rebuilding damaged sections, driveway entrances, universal access ramps, and new sidewalks on Sherbrooke Est between rue De Contrecoeur and avenue Hector (Sobeys project).
Groupe ABF inc. was the lowest of the seven compliant bidders, 8.02% below the City's estimate.
The borough is taking $38,000 from its surplus to pay for the share of the work on the arterial network; the rest comes from loan by-laws.
The company's performance will be evaluated using the grid set out in the call for tenders.
The executive committee takes note of a mandatory monthly report listing 7 decisions signed in April 2026 by a senior official of the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation.

Rentals where the City is the tenant: a 25-year lease with the ministère de l'Environnement for 898 m² of the bed of the rivière des Prairies, at parc-nature du Cap-Saint-Jacques (Pierrefonds-Roxboro), for a total of $2,242.01.

Rentals where the City is the landlord: 32.51 m² of office space rented to the Sûreté du Québec in Lachine until October 31, 2026 ($6,187.28), and 192 sq. ft. at 2300 Alfred-Nobel rented to Abrevia inc. and E-Biotech inc. for one year starting July 1, 2026 ($14,400).
A 13,780 sq. ft. piece of land on île Notre-Dame (Mare au diable) is rented to 9253-4270 Québec inc. from May 11 to 29, 2026 as a medical helipad during the Grand Prix du Canada, for $1,961.47.
Real estate transactions: sale of a 47.5 m² portion of a lane in Ahuntsic-Cartierville to two individuals for $7,960, and closing of this lane as public property.
Two servitudes concerning properties on rue Carrie-Derick, in Le Sud-Ouest, are amended with no financial consideration, with Bell Mobilité inc. and Tidan inc.

The executive committee takes note of the monthly report of decisions made by a manager of the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation, from May 1 to 31, 2026 (five decisions: two leases, three real estate transactions).

The City is renting premises and outdoor spaces at 2100, avenue Pierre-Dupuy from the Administration portuaire de Montréal for 73 days, from August 3 to October 15, 2026, for $79,277.56 taxes included, in connection with the Championnat du Monde Route UCI Montréal 2026 (September 19 to 27, 2026).
The City is renting a workstation and a room (224 sq. ft.) at 7140, rue Albert-Einstein to Oliver Cole et Associés ltée, from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027, for $6,600 excluding taxes.

The City is selling a 47 m² piece of land at the corner of avenue Charles-Goulet and avenue Lionel-Daunais, in Anjou, to Suzanne Carrier and Normand Bérubé for $4,700 plus taxes, for residential lot assembly.
The City is selling a residual 82.3 m² piece of land north of rue du Fort-Rolland, in Lachine, to Jin Song Cao for $21,810 plus taxes, for residential lot assembly.

The City is amending an access and no-build servitude at the southwest corner of boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest and rue Jeanne-Mance, in Ville-Marie, with no money changing hands, and is removing the affected parcel from the public domain.
The Saint-Léonard borough is offering to take charge itself of minor sidewalk repairs on certain arterial streets in its territory, which normally fall under the central city.
It would handle the plans and specifications, the call for tenders, the awarding of the contract and the supervision of the work.
The work includes rebuilding concrete sidewalks and medians, repairs to public utilities located in the sidewalk, and levelling of the areas behind the sidewalk.
The sidewalks in question are on streets where the central city plans to redo the roadway in the short term.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is fully funding the work; the budget allocated to the borough is $292,000 (net of rebate).
Announced schedule: call for tenders in March 2026, contract in May 2026, work from June to October 2026.
The offer still has to be accepted by city council, since these streets are part of the City's arterial road network.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is hiring Groupe Civitas inc. to supervise various construction sites in its territory, for $528,770.03, plus $52,877.00 set aside for variations in quantities — a maximum expenditure of $581,647.03.
Three supervisors will monitor the work sites (rebuilding of sidewalks, roadways and other infrastructure), since the permanent staff of the Division des études techniques cannot cover everything.
The contract runs from May 11, 2026 to May 10, 2028, with an option to renew for one year until May 10, 2029; the total would then reach $793,155.04.
Unit prices will be indexed each year starting January 1, 2027, based on the consumer price index for the Montréal region.
Groupe Civitas inc. is the lowest compliant bidder in call for tenders 26-21277, opened on March 10, 2026; the bid is 31.46% below the estimate of $1,157,223.39.
Because the contract is over $500,000, the company will be subject to a performance evaluation.
According to the file, not awarding the contract would leave the 2026 work without adequate supervision.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is awarding Eurovia Québec Construction inc. the repaving work and sidewalk section repairs on its local road network for 2026.
The maximum authorized spending is $1,411,014.43: $1,175,845.36 for the contract and $235,169.07 in contingencies, paid entirely by the borough.
The streets affected: place de Pontoise, rue de Pontoise (from Bélanger to Deslierres) and rue Goya (from 40e Rue to Lionel-Grolux).
The work is to start around June 1, 2026 and be completed around August 30, 2026; nearby residents will be notified by letter.
Eurovia was the lowest of the eight bids received, all of which were compliant, and its price is 10.89% below the estimate of $1,319,499.
The project includes new universal access ramps with tactile warning plates at the intersections involved.
The company's performance will be evaluated, since the contract exceeds $1,000,000.
The borough of Saint-Léonard has awarded COJALAC INC. the 2026 sidewalk repair work, for a maximum expense of $821,440.62 (a $696,116.14 contract plus $125,324.48 in contingencies).
COJALAC INC. was the lowest of the eight compliant bidders; the highest bid was $1,414,635.15 and the City's estimate was $835,776.27.
Sidewalks will be repaired on the arterial road network: rue J.-B.-Martineau, boulevard Viau, boulevard Métropolitaine Est (ramps) and rue du Champ-d'Eau, ahead of paving work.
Also included is the annual repair of sidewalk sections and waterway profiles on local streets throughout the borough.
At parc Coubertin, a new concrete curb will be built along the fence of école Pierre-de-Coubertin and the path in front of the pavilion will be redone, to improve water drainage ($72,503.23).
The Service des infrastructures et du réseau routier is paying $319,671.32 (the arterial network portion); the borough covers the rest.
The work is planned from June 1 to November 1, 2026; residents of the local streets involved will be notified by letter.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is awarding the construction of curb extensions to Montréal Scellant inc., the lowest compliant bidder out of six.
Maximum spending of $484,197.06: $421,040.92 for the contract and $63,156.14 in contingencies.
Seven curb extensions will be built, including three draining extensions, near the Dante, Lambert-Closse and De La Dauversière schools.
Four intersections are involved: Houel/De Côme, Bonpart/Valdombre, De Lisieux/Des Angevins and Verdier/Des Angevins.
The work is funded 100% by the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité, under the Programme de sécurisation aux abords des écoles.
Work is planned from July 1 to August 1, 2026, with the contract ending September 1, 2026 (approximate dates).
Local residents will receive a letter explaining the nature and length of the work.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is hiring Eurovia Québec Construction inc. to build 40 speed humps on its local streets in 2026.
Maximum spending of $215,722.99: $179,769.16 for the contract, plus $35,953.83 in contingencies, paid entirely by the borough.
The speed humps, 4 metres wide, will be installed on 17 streets, including Dumesnil, du Poitou, Deschambault, Malouin, des Galets and Laverdière.
Eurovia submitted the lowest price among 5 compliant bids; the next one was $239,974.10.
The bid is 27.98% below the estimate of $249,610.73, which the borough explains by another contract the contractor already has underway in its territory.
Work is scheduled from August 1 to September 1, 2026; nearby residents will be notified by letter.
Stated purpose: reduce speed, limit through traffic and make pedestrian travel safer, particularly near schools, parks and seniors' residences.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the use "community or sociocultural activity" at 1096, avenue de l'Hôtel-de-Ville, near the Quartier chinois.
The organization Stella, l'amie de Maimie will be able to move in; it is leaving 2065, rue Parthenais (the Grover building) and provides support to sex workers.
The building is a two-storey single-family home in the Second Empire style, built in 1870, recently put up for sale by its owner-occupant.
Activities will be mainly administrative, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with drop-in support on Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed on weekends.
An STBBI screening and contraception clinic will run on Tuesdays from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m., with a maximum of four participants; occasional evening activities will never run past 8 p.m.
There will be no lodging, no food distribution and no supervised consumption site; no exterior changes to the building are planned.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion; a notice will be posted on the site and published in the newspaper.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing the hotel at 2050, rue Mansfield (hôtel Le Germain) to exceed the maximum density permitted in the area.
This exemption allows the completion of levels 22 and 23, which have been left as bare structure since the 2020 work, and the addition of 18 rooms to the hotel, which currently has 136.
The work is being done inside the existing volume: no changes to the outside of the building.
The site's density would go from about 11.78 to 13.04, while the planning by-law sets the limit at 12.
The levels had been left unfinished while waiting for the purchase of the back lane, a project that has been at a standstill for several years.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with one condition; the building's volume must remain in keeping with the 2018 plans.

Planned steps: public consultation on February 25, 2026, second draft resolution on March 10, 2026, final adoption targeted for April 14, 2026, with the possibility of a request for a referendum register on the density.

The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the owner, Akelius, to divide 17 large units in the building at 3555, chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, a 24-storey building with 311 units and 21 commercial spaces.
The division would create 17 more units, including 14 with at least three bedrooms; the new units would be about 69 to 132 m².
The work can only be done in vacant units: each permit application will have to include proof that the unit is empty.
The owner commits to carrying out no evictions and to maintaining the leases of current tenants.
The decision departs from the ban on dividing a dwelling, in force since November 2020 in the borough's planning by-law.
Two similar authorizations had already been granted for the same building in 2024; the layout will have to remain in line with the plans stamped January 7, 2026.
Planned steps: draft resolution adopted February 10, 2026, public consultation February 25, final adoption March 10, 2026.
The Ville-Marie borough is authorizing the setting up of a café-terrasse on a parking lot at the northeast corner of rue Ontario and rue D'Iberville.
The land belongs to JTI-Macdonald Corp., which has given its consent; the terrace would serve customers of the Café de la Ligne Verte, at 2531, rue Ontario Est.
The terrace would take up about 120 m² of the parking lot, with a raised floor, a black wrought-iron fence, an access ramp for people with reduced mobility and about 60 seats.
Meals and drinks, including alcohol, would be served there until about midnight on weekdays and 1 a.m. on weekends, as at the café.
Dancing, shows, concerts, sound equipment and food cooking are not allowed on the terrace; wooden screen walls are intended to limit noise toward neighbouring homes.
The furniture must be stored off site outside the season, and all installations removed if the café-terrasse is no longer operated.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion with one condition on May 7, 2026; adoption was planned for the borough council meeting of June 9, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing part of "tour 8" of the Quartier des lumières, on the former Radio-Canada site, to exceed the permitted height of 23 m and reach 30 m.
The land in question is the block bordered by avenue Viger Est, rue Wolfe, the extension of rue De La Gauchetière and a pedestrian walkway in the extension of rue Beaudry.
The planned building includes a 21 m base (7 storeys) on De La Gauchetière, a 44 m taller section (13 storeys) and a 30 m rear section (10 storeys) toward Viger.
Three conditions apply: the section in question cannot exceed 30 m, must remain south of the taller volume, and its wall facing the Beaudry walkway must be set back from the storey below.
The City justifies the exemption on the grounds that the land is split by two different height limits (23 m and 30 m) and that the taller section would be barely visible from the street.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with conditions on May 7, 2026; a public notice was published on May 22, 2026 and the resolution is adopted at the council meeting of June 9, 2026.
Tour 8 is the first of the four planned phases of this residential development.

The City is giving itself more time to respond to property assessment challenges filed against the 2026-2027-2028 rolls: the deadline moves from September 1, 2026 to November 1, 2026 or March 1, 2027, depending on the type and value of the building.
Owners of small residential buildings (fewer than 12 units) and vacant lots will still get an answer by September 1, 2026 at the latest: about 46% of applications will be handled by that date.
Non-residential, mixed-use and multi-residential buildings with 12 units or more will get an answer by November 1, 2026 at the latest.
Non-residential buildings in the Division commerciale assessed at $20M or less (935 applications) will have to wait until March 1, 2027.
The Direction de l'évaluation foncière received 4,331 review applications, covering buildings worth $44.2B, which is 7.2% of the total value of the agglomeration's rolls.
The City explains the postponement by the complexity of commercial files, which require inspections and the collection of financial data from owners.
The Tribunal administratif du Québec and the people who filed an application will have to be notified of the postponement.
The City is adding $86,000 (taxes included) to the fees of the engineering firm GHD, bringing the contract to $298,000, plus travel expenses for an expert who lives outside Québec.

GHD must determine the cause of the break in the 2100 mm water main that occurred on August 16, 2024 under René-Lévesque, near De Lorimier, acting as experts in concrete/mortar and in C-301 prestressed concrete pipes.
The broken main, installed by the ministère des Transports in 1985, supplies the réservoir Rosemont; a large amount of water escaped before the valves were closed.
The firm explains the increase by a broadened mandate, more days of field work and the number of experts hired by the other parties; the services are billed by the hour.
Court claims related to the break exceed $87M and remain to be finalized in several cases; the Service de l'eau does not have the resources to carry out these analyses itself.
The $298,000 budget does not include a possible trial. The expense is paid entirely by the central city.
The City is adding $260,000 (taxes included) to the fees of the law firm IMK, which represents it in the Axnor case. The contract goes from $110,000 to $370,000.

The company Axnor Développements inc. has been suing the City since September 2014 and is now claiming $5.8M (originally $4.4M) for the costs of decontaminating land located at 2250-2252, rue Sherbrooke Est.
This land is located diagonally across from parc Baldwin, a former quarry that was filled in by the City.
The case had been put on hold pending the outcome of the Cormier cases, in which the courts dismissed the claims against the City (Superior Court in 2020, Court of Appeal in 2023).
On March 26, 2026, the Superior Court allowed Axnor to file new expert reports and to amend its claim; the City may also produce new expert reports.
The amount covers the steps up to the point where the case is ready for trial; the costs of preparing for and holding the trial will have to be assessed later.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city.
The City would act as guarantor for a $2,000,000 loan granted by the Banque de l'Infrastructure du Canada (BIC) to Société GALOPH, a non-profit organization.
This loan is used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project on the site of the former racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The BIC covers 33.33% of the cost of the studies; GALOPH takes on the remaining 66.67%, and the City plans in turn to finance 33.33% through an upcoming agreement.

The loan would not be repayable if the project stops or if it is funded solely by the public sector; it becomes repayable if the project continues with a private organization — that is when the City's guarantee could be called upon.
Without this guarantee, the BIC would not sign and the project would lose this $2,000,000 envelope, according to the document.
Next steps: sending the resolution to the ministry (MAMH) after the city council meeting of April 20, 2026, then a City-GALOPH collaboration agreement at the May or June 2026 council meeting.
The document states that the site is ultimately to accommodate 10,000 social and affordable housing units outside the market.
The SPVM will receive an $8,000 grant from the Victims Fund of the Department of Justice Canada, and the City is opening an equivalent revenue and expenditure budget for 2026.
The money will fund an information campaign about sexual assault during the Victims and Survivors of Crime Week, from May 11 to 15, 2026.
Subtitled video clips will be shown on 66 digital lumiquais screens in 33 metro stations and on 342 Métrovision/Azur screens, as well as on the SPVM's Facebook and Instagram accounts.
The videos will cover consent, situations involving a person in a position of authority, how a police complaint proceeds, and available support resources.
A booth staffed by police officers will be set up for one day in a busy metro station to inform passersby and hand out documentation.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration, since policing is an agglomeration responsibility; the City says the file has no impact on its financial framework.
The borough of Outremont is approving the plans for the expansion of Université de Montréal's MIL campus, at 1375, avenue Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux.
The project adds 31,400 square metres to the existing building (60,000 m², about 2,685 users), including a computing centre and the Institut Courtois devoted to data science.
The borough is allowing the expansion to go ahead without any car parking spaces, whereas the by-law requires at least 84.
The Université would rather build bicycle parking (124 outdoor, 62 indoor) and gradually spread out the maximum of 400 car spaces allowed on the site.
The construction work is estimated at about three years; deliveries and trucking would go through the back of the site, with sound sensors and measures against noise, dust and traffic.

The urban planning advisory committee is asking that all truck traffic be banned in front of the new elementary school opening for the 2026 school year, especially at times when students are arriving and leaving.

The project is aiming for LEED v4 Gold certification and will recover waste energy from the computing centre to heat phase 1; the urban agriculture greenhouses and the bicycle shelters will be covered by a later permit.
City council has taken note of the 2025 annual report on animal management, covering the period from January 1 to December 31, 2025.
Cases involving dogs that bite or show aggressive behaviour rose from 523 in 2024 to 586 in 2025, an increase of 12%; 268 tickets were issued.
As of December 31, 2025, 110 dogs were listed in the public registry of potentially dangerous dogs and 272 were subject to custody measures.
64 dog-training workshops were held in 52 dog parks, reaching 504 dog owners.
436 animals were sterilized through the program for low-income households (with the SPCA de Montréal) and 992 street cats through the trap-sterilize-release program.

The City managed 6 animal services contracts covering 19 boroughs (SPCA de Montréal, SPCA Lanaudière Basses-Laurentides, Contrôle animal Vaudreuil-Soulanges, Le Berger Blanc); more than 12,000 animals were admitted to these shelters.
The report mentions the opening, on January 1, 2026, of a Proanima branch in Montréal serving as a one-stop point of service for animal services.
The City is giving $184,099 to 9 organizations to create 10 neighbourhood murals in 2026, under stream 2 of the Programme d'art mural.
