Six boroughs are involved: Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Le Sud-Ouest, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Pierrefonds-Roxboro and Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
The amounts range from $5,739 (Fondation Pearson pour l'Éducation, Pierrefonds-Roxboro) to $25,000 for three projects: MU in Le Sud-Ouest, and AvangArtiste on the Plateau and in Rosemont.
The murals must be designed with residents, businesses, organizations or institutions from the neighbourhood; the program also aims to prevent graffiti.
Each organization receives 70% of the amount when the agreement is signed and 30% after the final report is submitted and approved.

23 projects were submitted this year; 10 were selected, 10 were turned down for lack of budget or too low a score, one was found ineligible, one was transferred to stream 1 and one was excluded for failing to meet past commitments.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city, out of the budget of the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne.
The City is ending its agreement with the organization MURAL for the mural "Échos d'un quartier ou Ode au quartier", planned in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
Reason given: the organization did not confirm a compliant wall, despite a postponement to 2026, reminders and deadlines pushed back to February 17 and then to March 2, 2026.
The contribution was $15,000 from the City, plus $10,000 from the borough; a first payment of $10,500 had been made in June 2025.
The organization reported $2,330 in eligible expenses and must repay $8,170.
The project has not been selected under the Programme d'art mural – Volet 2 for 2026; the City is inviting MURAL to submit a new project for 2027.
In February 2026, the City had already terminated another agreement with MURAL, for the mural "Toucher l'horizon" (volet 1), in the same borough.
The Verdun borough is offering city council to take charge itself of minor sidewalk repair work on streets of the City's arterial network located within its territory, in 2026.
Verdun would handle the plans and specifications, the call for tenders, the awarding of contracts and the supervision of the work.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is funding the project 100%; the budget planned for Verdun in 2026 is $100,000, net of rebate.
Announced schedule: plans and specifications in March 2026, call for tenders in the spring, work in the summer and fall of 2026.
The borough cites the high number of requests from residents about the condition of the sidewalks and some badly deteriorated sections.
Next step: city council must accept the offer; without this, the work under the program cannot be carried out.
The borough of Outremont is authorizing eight public events on public property between February and November 2026, and is allowing the necessary exemptions (noise, use of streets and parks, parking).

On the schedule: Carnaval d'hiver at parc Beaubien (February 24), Parade de la Torah on Querbes, Champagneur and Van Horne (February 28), bagpipes in front of the Théâtre Outremont (March 11), Chasse aux cocos at parc Beaubien (April 5).
Also: Cyclo-MAPP with screenings from the Campus MIL at place Alice-Girard (May 8 or 9), Cultivons Outremont at place Micheline-Legendre with giveaways of flowers, plants and compost (May 24).
Public pianos will be available from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. at place Marcelle-Ferron and place Kate-McGarrigle, from May 20 to September 20, 2026.
The Remembrance Day ceremony will take place on November 11 at parc Outremont, with avenue Elmwood closed between Bloomfield and Outremont.
All the events are free; the City's support costs are covered by existing operating budgets.
Organizers must post street closure notices 10 days in advance and notify residents and business owners.
The borough of Outremont is closing 21 avenues to car traffic on Sunday, June 14, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., for the 13th edition of the La Foulée des Parcs race.
Parking will be banned on these same stretches from June 13 at 11:59 p.m. until June 14 at 12:30 p.m., and vehicles parked illegally along the route will be towed.
Among the streets affected: Bernard (between Hutchison and Rockland), Saint-Viateur, Lajoie, Outremont, Querbes, Rockland, Fairmount and several others.
Some stretches could reopen before the end of the morning.
The event is organized by the organization Outremont en famille, which expects about 2,000 participants on routes of 1, 2, 5 and 10 km, plus a "Défi famille" of 4 x 1 km.
The race ends at parc Outremont, with promotional booths; STM bus routes will be detoured.
The borough of Outremont is authorizing two public events and allowing them to depart from its by-laws (parks, use of public property, noise, nuisances, traffic and parking).

On March 29, 2026, the Ordre Saint-Antoine le Grand will hold its "Dimanche des Rameaux" (Palm Sunday) procession, with 800 people expected, on the sidewalks around the church (avenues McEachran, Ducharme and Dollard, and the lane north of Ducharme).
Two walks will take place that day, from 11 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. and from 12:30 p.m. to 1:15 p.m.; the sidewalks will be blocked during that time.

On May 29, 2026, the organization Casteliers will hold its "Apéro bénéfice" fundraiser at place Micheline-Legendre, with about 100 people, performances, workshops and games for children; the borough is lending equipment.
The events on public property are free and open to everyone; the organizers may sell food and drinks to fund themselves and must obtain all required permits.
The costs of the City's services are absorbed by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
If a street is closed, the promoter must put up notices 10 days in advance and inform residents and businesses.
The borough of Outremont is giving up to $17,500 to the non-profit organization Vision Diversité to organize the Fête nationale on June 23 and 24, 2026, at Place Alice-Girard.
The program includes concerts by francophone artists, workshops for children, family games, a self-serve BBQ and an outdoor movie screening.
On June 24 at 3 p.m., the Canada-Switzerland match of the FIFA World Cup could be shown on site.
Vision Diversité takes care of the technical set-up, the stage, hiring the artists, promotion, security and event management; the total budget for the two days is estimated at close to $130,000.
The borough lends equipment, provides staff on site, rents the portable toilets and helps with promotion.
The expense is paid entirely by the borough, out of the operating budget for public events.
A contribution of $17,500 was also granted to this organization in 2024 and 2025, and of $10,000 in 2023.
The borough of Outremont is closing avenue Bernard to traffic between avenue Bloomfield and the lane east of avenue Wiseman, from May 19 to September 24, 2026.
The pedestrian-only period itself runs from May 23 to September 20, 2026; the avenue fully reopens on September 25, 2026.
Café terraces are set up on May 22 and taken down starting September 21, 2026.
North-south traffic stays open on avenue Outremont, avenue Champagneur and avenue Bloomfield; no-parking signs are put up on the closed sections.
STM buses 160 and 368 are rerouted and four stops are cancelled (Outremont/Lajoie, Outremont/Bernard, Bernard/Outremont and Outremont/Lajoie ouest).
A bicycle patroller is present for the entire pedestrian-only period.
The project costs $130,500 including taxes (separate file), funded in part by a call for projects from the city's Service du développement économique.
Outremont is once again making avenue Bernard pedestrian-only in the summer of 2026, between avenue Wiseman and avenue Bloomfield — the sixth edition of the project.
The borough is allocating $105,000 (net of taxes) from its own operating budget and the parks and playgrounds fund.
That amount breaks down as follows: $50,000 for greening, $33,000 for an additional public safety officer, $20,000 for cleanliness and $2,000 for communications.
A $106,000 grant from the City's Service du développement économique covers cleanliness, activities and furniture, for a total of $211,000.
Last year's installations will be reused; broken furniture will be replaced and a contract will be awarded for installing and maintaining the plants.
A program of cultural events and activities will be set up, with flyers, signs, newsletters and social media to inform residents and merchants.
Without these amounts, the pedestrianization could not take place in the summer of 2026, according to the document.

The borough of Outremont is authorizing five public events on its territory between April and October 2026, with the exemptions required from the by-laws on parks, noise, traffic and occupancy of public property.

Two Bagleiten parades (Congrégation Amour pour Israël) on avenue Durocher between Lajoie and Van Horne: the April 9 parade is approved after the fact, and the May 23 one is authorized. Traffic will be closed for the duration of the march, with about 100 people each time.
Russian Orthodox Easter procession on April 11 and 12, 2026 around the cathédrale Saint-Nicholas, on avenues Saint-Joseph and Nelson, with about 250 people; traffic will be closed during the march.

Marche pour la dignité on May 3, 2026 at parc Pratt, organized by the Maison de soins palliatifs St-Raphaël: a 1 or 5 km route on the sidewalks, a BBQ, and about 700 people. The organization is aiming to raise $400,000.

Fête nationale on June 23 and 24, 2026 at place Alice-Girard (Vision Diversité): a communal table, workshops, outdoor movies and a show, with about 1500 people. Access to certain areas will be limited from June 22 to 26 for setup and takedown.
Halloween PatteParade on October 24, 2026 (Association du parc canin): a parade of dogs in costume, with about 1000 people, and the closing of avenue Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux for 30 minutes.
The events are free. The City's support costs are covered by existing operating budgets; the organizers must notify residents and businesses 10 days before street closings.
The borough of Outremont is authorizing the "Triptyque Cycle Régis" bicycle race on Saturday, May 23, 2026, organized by the Fédération québécoise de sports cyclistes.

Three stretches of street will be closed from 12 p.m. to 6 p.m.: Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux (between Dollard and Durocher), Outremont (between Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux and Manseau) and Wiseman (between Manseau and Place Alice-Girard).
The cyclists will ride several laps of a 1.4 km circuit in the area of the campus MIL.
Place Alice-Girard will be occupied from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.: officials' stand, booths, mechanical workshop, food trucks and sponsors.
Exemptions granted: noise from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m., sales on public property, and the sale and consumption of alcohol from 12 p.m. to 6:30 p.m.
The organizer must put up closure notices 10 days in advance and notify residents and businesses 7 days in advance; the SPVM will handle crowd control.
The City will cover the transportation of equipment, street cleaning and no-parking signage out of its current budgets.
The borough of Outremont is allowing the Maison des jeunes d'Outremont's annual Christmas tree sale to occupy public property from November 16 to December 24, 2026, including setup and takedown.

The sale will take place in front of the Maison des jeunes, at 530, avenue Querbes, using the parking spaces on the west side between 551 and 503 Querbes, the corridor near the tennis court and the area in front of the chalet.
Parking spaces on the west side of avenue Querbes will be removed for about one month and part of the sidewalk will be closed; three spaces will be reserved for customers.
The site will be fenced in and will include a borough container used as a storage space, tree areas organized by size and a work space.
The City is providing transportation and the loan of equipment, no-parking signs and the moving of the container, out of the operating budgets of the departments concerned.
The promoter must put up street closure notices 10 days in advance and distribute notices to residents and businesses 7 days in advance.
According to the file, the new site reduces the organization's costs (trailer, internet, staff) and the borough's costs (chemical toilet, electrical connection).

The borough of Outremont is approving a series of public events in May and June 2026, and is allowing temporary exemptions to the by-laws on parks, noise, cleanliness, parking and use of public property.

The events include the Féria of école Nouvelle-Querbes (May 9), the Olympiades of Collège Sainte-Anne-Buissonnière at parc Beaubien (May 22), Vélo Québec's Tour de l'Île (May 31) and the Fête nationale at parc Beaubien (June 24).
The Kermesse Soleil, organized by the borough, will take place at parc Beaubien from June 1 to 8: volunteer, lobster and spaghetti suppers, plus two family days (about 7,000 people expected).
Several streets will be closed: avenue Lajoie and boulevard Dollard (May 27), McDougall (June 6), Hazelwood (June 7), Kelvin and St-Germain (June 13) for block parties and a school race.
The restaurant Chez Lévesque will be allowed to set up two televisions on the sidewalk of avenue Laurier to show the soccer World Cup, from June 11 to July 19.
The events are free and open to everyone; the City's support costs are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
Organizers must post street closure notices 10 days in advance and inform residents and businesses.
The borough of Lachine is adding the position of "chargé de secrétariat" to the list of level 5 officers in its by-law delegating powers.
This change allows this person to approve expenses and contracts of $1,000 or less, like other level 5 officers.
The borough explains that this position handles duties that sometimes require small expenses: urgent administrative needs, logistical costs, and commitments for the office of the borough mayor.
Until now, the position was not named in the by-law, which prevented it from exercising these powers.
Planned schedule: adoption on March 2, 2026, public notice and coming into force on March 3, 2026.
The by-law is not subject to approval by referendum.

The Lachine borough council takes note of the filing of the letter sent to the citizens who submitted a petition titled "Pour le maintien du projet de piscine en eaux libres tel que prévu à Lachine" (For keeping the open-water pool project as planned in Lachine).
The petition was filed on May 15, 2026 by a group of Lachine citizens; the borough secretariat found it admissible.
The review confirms 25 validated signatures, three designated representatives and a subject matter that falls under the borough's jurisdiction.
Next steps: a notice will launch the signature period within a maximum of 45 days, followed by a 90-day signature period.
The Saint-Léonard borough council is adopting a motion for the 9th commemoration of the attack at the Grande Mosquée de Québec, which took place on January 29, 2017.
The attack, described as Islamophobic and hateful, caused the deaths of 6 Quebecers of Muslim faith and injured 19 other people.
The council expresses its support for the families and loved ones of the victims.
It reaffirms its support for activities that bring together the different communities of Saint-Léonard and that encourage living together, inclusion and solidarity.
The motion is based on the borough's Plan stratégique 2030, which aims for a harmonious, supportive and safe social climate.
No spending is planned in this file.
The Saint-Léonard borough council adopts a motion to mark Black History Month.
The 35th Canadian edition runs from February 1 to March 1, 2026, under the theme "Élevons nos voix ensemble" (Let's Raise Our Voices Together).
The council recognizes the contribution of Black communities to the history and development of Montréal.
The borough commits to working with public and community partners on initiatives related to this event.
It invites Saint-Léonard residents to take part in the month's activities.
The motion is based in particular on the Québec law adopted on November 23, 2006, making February Black History Month.
The Saint-Léonard borough council adopts a motion thanking the Italian community for its contribution to the development of the borough, of Montréal and of Canada.
The motion is presented on the occasion of Italian Heritage Month, the month of June, designated by the Government of Canada in 2016.

The text mentions organizations from the community: the Fondation communautaire canadienne-italienne du Québec (in Saint-Léonard for 50 years, more than $27 million given to more than 170 organizations and projects), the Centre Leonardo da Vinci and its 533-seat Théâtre Mirella & Lino Saputo, the Congrès national des Italo-Canadiens, the CIBPA Montréal, the Casa d'Italia, the CRAIC and the Services communautaires canadiens-italiens du Québec.
The motion notes that 275,000 people of Italian origin live in the Montréal agglomeration, out of more than 1.5 million in Canada.
It also mentions the discrimination and internment experienced by Italian-Canadians during the Second World War.
The motion involves no spending; it will be mentioned in the news item on the borough's website about the highlights of the June council meeting.
The Lachine borough council meeting of Monday, May 4, 2026 will be held at a different location.
It will take place in the salle Léo-Pétrin of the école Martin-Bélanger, at 29, avenue Ouellette, in Lachine.
The borough says it wants to bring the council closer to residents by holding meetings in different places across its territory.
The 2026 meeting calendar, adopted on December 1, 2025, is amended accordingly.
A public notice will be published on the borough's portal, and the meeting dates will appear in the magazine Vivre Lachine.
No financial impact is expected.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is banning U-turns from the south approach of the intersection of avenue du Parc and avenue Beaumont.

Residents had reported that these U-turns were creating conflicts between vehicles, because the traffic light timing allows left turns from south to west at the same time as right turns from west to south.
Signs will be installed on the centre median of avenue du Parc, with a "new signage" sign underneath.
Planned schedule: adoption of the order in April 2026 and installation of the signs in May 2026.
The work will be done by the Division de l'entretien de l'éclairage, de la signalisation et du marquage de la chaussée, which will bill the borough; no amount is stated.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is offering city council to take charge itself of the work on avenue Beaumont, between avenue Querbes and avenue de l'Épée, because this street is part of the City's arterial road network.
The bike lane on the north side will be moved to the south side and turned into a two-way path running along the sidewalk.
Ground markings and bollards will create a buffer zone between cyclists and car traffic.
Parking remains prohibited on both sides of avenue Beaumont.
The marking and signage work will be done by the Division de l'entretien de l'éclairage, de la signalisation et du marquage, which will bill the borough; no amount is indicated.
Schedule: city council decision in May 2026, work and information for local residents starting in June 2026.
If city council turns down the offer, the work cannot be carried out.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is adding stop signs on rue Tillemont, at the east and west approaches of rue Cartier and rue de Bordeaux.
Until now, only the stop signs on rue Cartier controlled the Tillemont/Cartier intersection; the Tillemont/de Bordeaux intersection worked in a similar way.
The City says it has received several requests about safety at Tillemont/Cartier, near the école primaire Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand, two daycares and a centre for people with a hearing impairment.
Along with the stop signs, stop lines will be painted at the east and west approaches, and crosswalks marked in white at all approaches.
Signs will warn of the change 30 days before installation, and then "new signage" signs will stay up for 30 days afterward.
Planned schedule: signage installation in June and July 2026, markings in July 2026.
The work is done by the Division de l'entretien de l'éclairage, de la signalisation et du marquage, which bills the borough; no amount is stated.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is putting in a crossing for pedestrians on the north approach of the intersection of 25e Avenue and boulevard Provencher.
The stop signs for southbound vehicles are being replaced with a "yield" sign.
The stop line on the north approach will be erased, the pedestrian crossing will be marked in yellow, and a stop line will be painted for the channelized left turn.

The decision follows requests from residents about safety at this intersection: since 2020, a white pedestrian crossing had been marked there without matching stop signs, a marking that did not meet the standards.
Sign installation is planned for July-August 2026 and the markings for August 2026; "new signage" signs will stay in place for 30 days.
The work is being done by the Division de l'entretien de l'éclairage, de la signalisation et du marquage, which bills the borough; no amount is given.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is adding a pedestrian crossing at the east approach of the De Castelnau Est / De Lanaudière intersection (west branch).
Stop signs will be installed at the east and west approaches of the De Castelnau Est / Rousselot intersection, with small plates showing the layout of the intersection.
Road markings will follow: a yellow pedestrian crossing on De Lanaudière, and stop lines on De Castelnau Est at Rousselot.
The decision follows complaints from residents about safety at these two intersections, which are located near parc de Turin and école primaire Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant.
The signs and markings are scheduled to be installed in August-September 2026.
"New sign" plates will stay in place for 30 days under the signs that have been changed.
The work is done by the Division de l'entretien de l'éclairage, de la signalisation et du marquage, which bills the borough; no amount is given.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is temporarily closing rue Boyer to cars, between rue Villeray Est and rue du Rosaire, along the schoolyard of école primaire Marie-Favery.
A public square will be set up on this stretch for the coming school year, with furniture added in August-September 2026.
The bike path on rue Boyer between Villeray Est and Jarry Est is being removed, and cyclists are being redirected to the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb.
Rue du Rosaire is becoming one-way eastbound between rue Saint-André and rue Boyer.
The closure takes advantage of the work to replace lead water service lines and to resurface the street already planned on rue Boyer, and responds to a request from the school's administration.
Signs will announce the change 30 days in advance (end of July 2026) and notices will be handed out to residents; the road signs will be installed in August 2026.
There is no timeline yet for the permanent redesign of the rue-école Boyer (school street).
City council must approve the appointment of Alain Dufort as director general of the Ville de Montréal, for four years, starting August 17, 2026.
His annual base salary is set at $380,000, indexed every January 1 according to the increase granted to the City's managers.
He receives six weeks of vacation in advance and a parking space at city hall.
He has access to the managers' group insurance, except long-term disability insurance.
If the City ends his employment, it will pay him the equivalent of 12 months' salary, or the balance of the contract if less than 12 months remain.
The appointment follows the announcement of the current director general's departure; Alain Dufort worked at the City from 2007 to 2024, then at the Réseau de transport de Longueuil.
The money will come from the operating budget of the Direction générale; a news release will announce the appointment.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is entrusting the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough with the maintenance of lighting, signage and road markings on its territory for the year 2026.
The authorized spending is a maximum of $2,511,800, taken from the 2026 operating budget.
This amount breaks down as follows: markings $923,300, traffic lights $633,400, lighting $511,400 and written signage $443,700.
Since 2004, the specialized division of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie has carried out this work for the nine boroughs of the former Ville de Montréal.
In 2024, the same agreement had been made for a maximum amount of $2,301,600.
If the council turned down the offer, the borough would have to use outside suppliers for markings and signage.
The service commits to creating a document-sharing platform (marking plans, weekly progress reports, bollard lists, etc.).
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is allowing road work outside the hours normally permitted by its noise by-law, until December 31, 2026.
The hours normally permitted are 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekends: the exemption opens the door to night work.

Worksites covered: redevelopment of De Castelnau Est (Lajeunesse–Casgrain) and De Louvain (Saint-Michel–Iberville), milling on Christophe-Colomb (Jean-Talon–Crémazie Est), repairs to the viaduc Querbes and to access shafts on Beaumont.
Also included, on various streets in the borough: replacement of lead water service lines, sewer and water main rehabilitation, milling and surfacing of bus stops.
The Direction du développement du territoire will approve or refuse each request, project by project, without going back before the council.
One accepted reason: work on an arterial street, or a major daytime impact on services or mobility. The contractor's schedule is not a valid reason.
Night work is mainly for final paving or low-noise activities; the list of exemption permits will be provided on request.

The City is granting $220,500 over 3 years (2026-2028) to Les Scènes de Musique Alternatives du Québec (SMAQ) to create a "cultural buyer company" aimed at protecting independent performance venues from real estate speculation.
The project includes the pilot purchase of the building that houses the Verre Bouteille, in Montréal, as a first step toward a broader rollout.
Payments to SMAQ are planned as follows: $80,500 in 2026, $70,000 in 2027 and $70,000 in 2028; the City's contribution covers 14.35% of the project.

The same file provides $38,790 over 2 years to MOBA - Excellence industrielle Saint-Laurent for a sustainable mobility strategy at Technoparc Montréal (pilot carpooling, feasibility study for a private shuttle).
It also provides $50,000 over 12 months to La Ruche to support neighbourhood businesses in five commercial areas in the East of Montréal, through crowdfunding.
The total expense of $309,290 is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration and comes from agreements with the Government of Québec (Entente 200 M$ MEIE 2025-2029 and Entente Réflexe 2022-2025).
The executive committee takes note of the monthly report on decisions made by a public servant of the Service de la stratégie immobilière in October 2025: 8 decisions in total.

Six of these decisions are leases in which the City rents out space: offices at 7140, rue Albert-Einstein, at 2300, boulevard Alfred-Nobel, and a room at 251A, avenue des Pins Ouest (Plateau-Mont-Royal).

The tenants are Murata Electronics Canada ($13,260), Seven Square Media ($6,600), 911 Innovation ($3,900), Incloud Accounting–Ucloud Marketing ($9,000), Marketing Expandify ($11,280) and Speranza Spir ($1,848), each lease lasting one year, plus taxes.

The two other decisions authorize due diligence work on City-owned land: SOCAM on the former 5001, rue Saint-Ambroise (Le Sud-Ouest) and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal at 200, boulevard Marcel-Laurin (Saint-Laurent).
The document is an administrative report: it involves no new spending and provides for no subsequent steps.
The executive committee takes note of a report listing the six real estate decisions signed by an official of the Service de la stratégie immobilière between November 1 and 30, 2025.
Amendment to the lease of Aiden Innovation inc. at 2300, boulevard Alfred-Nobel: units 108 E and 108 G are changed to 180 sq. ft. until September 30, 2026, for a revised rent of $8,500 before taxes.
New lease with IPR Innovative Ressources inc. for unit 117 in the same building: 320 sq. ft. as a technical room, from December 1, 2025 to November 30, 2026, for revenue of $14,400 before taxes.
The City authorizes Habitations communautaires Saint-Léonard to carry out due diligence work on a piece of land at the former 6150, rue Bélanger, in Saint-Léonard.

The City is acquiring from Habitations communautaires Mainbourg a perpetual right-of-way easement of 343.1 m² for a bike path at 553, 53e Avenue, in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, at no financial cost.
The report also mentions one disposal decision and one acquisition decision, without giving details.
The executive committee takes note of a report listing 9 decisions signed in December 2025 by an employee of the Service de la stratégie immobilière (leases, service contract, acquisition).
The City is leasing 5 parking spaces free of charge at 1745, rue Fleury Est (Place Fleury) to install a glass recycling container there, from January 1 to December 31, 2026.

The City is leasing from the Québec government about 249 m² of the bed of the rivière des Prairies, near the pont de l'Île Haynes (boulevard Gouin Est), for 25 years starting January 1, 2026, to provide public access to the water.

The City is leasing from Santé Québec premises of 286 m² on the ground floor of the Pavillon Le Royer (3840, rue Saint-Urbain) for a warming station for people experiencing homelessness, for 3 months and 23 days starting December 9, 2025, at a cost of $9,301.59 including taxes.

The City is leasing offices to three companies (ZOÉFARMA, BIRCIS Technologies et conseils, BASRAM Group) at 2300, boulevard Alfred-Nobel and 7140, rue Albert-Einstein, for 2026, for revenues of $18,000, $8,100 and $9,600 before taxes.
The City is awarding Randstad intérim inc. a contract of $120,638 including taxes to support the tenants of the Centres d'affaires du Technoparc Montréal in 2026.

Complexe du Canal inc. is transferring to the City, at no financial cost, a pedestrian right-of-way easement of 252.1 m² at 1720, rue du Canal (Le Sud-Ouest), linking rue Saint-Patrick to the parc du canal de Lachine; Hydro-Québec's lease of a piece of land in Saint-Léonard is extended by 3 months for $1,950 plus taxes.
The executive committee takes note of the monthly report on decisions made by an official of the Service de la stratégie immobilière in January 2026: three decisions in total.
The City is renting office 113 at 7140, rue Albert-Einstein (200 sq. ft.) to TECNIKA PRODUCTIONS INC. from January 1 to December 31, 2026, for revenue of $7,440 before taxes.

The City is transferring to the organization Brin d'Elles, with no payment, its rights to a former lane located at 3831, rue Villeray, in Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, and is removing it from the public domain.
The City is buying from the Government of Canada, for $1, a portion of the south service road of the pont Samuel-De Champlain (rue du Pont Champlain), namely 13,214.1 m² in the borough of Verdun.
No spending is committed by this report: it is an administrative document tabled with the executive committee.
The executive committee takes note of a monthly report: 12 real estate decisions signed by an official of the Service de la stratégie immobilière between March 1 and March 31, 2026.
These decisions break down into 3 leases where the City is the tenant, 5 where it is the landlord, and 4 acquisitions or disposals of buildings.
Among the cases listed: a 20-year renewal of two right-of-way permissions for water mains in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, at $11,612.02 each, taxes included.

The City is renting space at 2300, boulevard Alfred Nobel to three businesses ($7,200, $10,299.80 and $4,800, before taxes) and a 597 sq. ft. space at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest to Atelier Entremise ($16,387.68, before taxes).

It is extending by two months the lease of a piece of land to Hydro-Québec in Saint-Léonard ($1,300, before taxes) and is obtaining, free of charge, two parking spaces at Marché Central for a glass recycling container.
The report also includes servitudes with no financial consideration, including waivers linked to the redevelopment of autoroute Bonaventure in Le Sud-Ouest.
No communication activities are planned; the document is presented as an administrative report.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Layla Imperatori as project, promotion and special events officer in the Division des relations avec les citoyens et communications.
She is expected to start on April 18, 2026, with permanent status if she completes the probation period set out in the collective agreement for municipal employees (CUPE 429).
The position is becoming vacant because the employee who held it has left.
The position was posted internally and externally from February 25 to March 4, 2026.
The expense for 2026 (from April 18 to December 31) is estimated at $64,500, including $48,400 in salary, and will be paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Alberthe Pierre as a social communications officer in the Division des relations avec les citoyens et communications, effective June 13, 2026.
Permanent status in the position depends on successfully completing the trial period set out in the collective agreement for municipal civil servants (SCFP 429).
The position had to be filled because the person who held it retired.
The position was posted internally and externally from May 4 to 8, 2026, and awarded to the entitled candidate at the end of the staffing process.
The expected cost from June 13 to December 31, 2026 is $42,400, including a salary of $31,800 and payroll taxes, paid out of the borough's operating budget.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is adding paid parking spaces on rue Sherbrooke, between boulevard Grand and avenue Hampton, and between avenue Wilson and the eastern boundary of the borough, as well as on the first stretch of the cross streets.
In total, 447 new paid spaces: 200 on Sherbrooke and 247 at the start of the cross streets.
The rate will be $3.50/hour, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., Saturday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Sunday from 1 p.m. to 6 p.m., the same as the parking meters already in place on Sherbrooke.
The signs limiting parking to 60 minutes will be removed from both sides of Sherbrooke in the sections concerned.
The bus lanes reserved during rush hours, the loading zones and the street-sweeping schedules remain unchanged; spaces for people with reduced mobility are kept but become paid spaces.
The borough expects to collect $131,000 in annual revenue (65% of the additional net revenue).
Signage will be prepared in March–April 2026 and the work will take place in May–June 2026, coordinated with the installation of the parking meters by the Agence de mobilité durable.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce agrees to have the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie take care of maintaining street lighting, signage and road markings on its territory for the year 2026.

This service is provided by the Direction de l'entretien de l'éclairage, de la signalisation et du marquage de la chaussée (EESM), which has served nine boroughs of the former Ville de Montréal since 2004.

The agreement has been renewed year after year since 2021; this time it covers the marking of centre lines (130,000 linear m), bike paths (80,000 linear m), pedestrian crossings, speed bumps and more.
The teams also respond to residents' requests received through 311; the marking of bike boxes is done on request, with an inspection in the spring and billing as an extra.
The borough must maintain safe access to street lights, traffic lights and signs (pruning, wasp nests, obstacles), including in parks and green alleys.
According to the document, a refusal would force the borough to turn to outside suppliers for the maintenance of road markings and signage.
The amount of the expense is not stated in the decision summary; it appears in the financial statement attached to the file.
The City is accepting $96,147.50 from the Fondation Espace pour la vie to fund three projects, and is adding a spending budget of the same amount.
$56,500 goes to a Planétarium research project on starless planetary-mass objects, which makes it possible to hire one postdoctoral researcher and two master's students (until December 31, 2027).
$10,000 is being used to create "La Forêt de demain", an experimental arboretum on former decontaminated industrial wasteland in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles (until December 2027).
$29,647.50 goes to the development of the iPapillon (eButterfly) app, a citizen science project about butterflies, until December 2026.
Any amount not spent on these projects must be returned to the Fondation.
The expense is covered by the ville centre and has no effect on the financial framework, since revenues and expenses balance out.
The City is adding $20,000 to the support paid to Amis du Jardin botanique de Montréal, bringing the total contribution to $30,000.
The money funds guided tours of the Jardin botanique on the theme of ornithology: training for volunteer guides, purchase of observation equipment and production of educational materials.
The agreement, first planned for 2026 only, is extended until August 31, 2028, so that the tours continue in 2027 and 2028.
A first payment of $9,000 has already been made; it will be followed by $10,000 after the year 1 accountability report, $10,000 after the year 2 report and $1,000 after the year 3 report.
The organization must submit an activity report every August 31 explaining how the money was spent.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city and is entirely funded by a donation from the Fondation Espace pour la vie.

The project is part of the "Un jardin pour les oiseaux" focus of the Jardin botanique, located in the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie according to the organization's address (4101, rue Sherbrooke Est).
The City is acting as guarantor for a $3M line of credit that the Banque Nationale du Canada is granting to Fonds Plancher, a Québec non-profit created in October 2024.

The Fonds will lend this money to housing co-operatives and housing non-profits to pay for preliminary studies (soil, environment, preliminary plans, market study) for non-market housing projects on City-owned land.

Each project can borrow up to $250,000: a base of $85,000 plus $2,500 per housing unit, up to a maximum of $165,000 in additional funds. Developers' fees and studies done before the loan are not eligible.
If an organization does not repay, the City pays in its place and its guarantee is reduced by that amount; repaid loans go back into the fund to finance other projects.
The Service de l'habitation must freeze $3M in credits in its operating budget for as long as the guarantee is in effect.
The City estimates that the agreement will help about 16 projects, or 1,400 housing units, in the first five years.
The pilot project is scheduled to launch in March 2026, with the application portal opening in May 2026.
As of March 1, 2026, the City is ending the service contract signed in September 2025 with the Centre de transformation du logement communautaire.

That contract, worth up to $186,260 including taxes, gave the Centre the job of managing a pre-development loan program for non-market housing projects (tools, online portal, review of applications, loan follow-up).

A provincial law given assent on November 12, 2025 broadens municipalities' powers to act as loan guarantors, which allows the City to give this role instead to Fonds Plancher as part of a pilot project (handled in a separate file).
The Centre claimed $48,130.01 before taxes in 2025; two final payments of $8,130.01 are planned for 2026 before the contract ends.
The rest of the money set aside for 2026 and 2027 will be freed up; the tools and portal developed by the Centre will be used by Fonds Plancher.
A notice announcing the intention to end the contract was sent to the Centre on February 1, 2026; the decision rests with the urban agglomeration council.
No communications activities are planned.
The City is easing the Règlement pour une métropole mixte (20-041), which requires developers to include social and affordable housing or pay a contribution.
The by-law will now apply only to projects larger than 18,000 m², which leaves out smaller projects.
Financial contributions go back to 2025 amounts: the increase that took effect on January 1, 2026 and future indexations are cancelled.

The separate affordable housing requirements are repealed and replaced by a single requirement of 20% non-market housing (social housing, or affordable housing owned by a non-profit, a co-operative, a government, etc.).
Agreements signed since January 1, 2026 may be amended downward, and the City could refund contributions it has already collected.
The Service de l'habitation presents these changes as a first phase, before the by-law is replaced entirely by an incentive-based approach.
A public consultation meeting is scheduled for February 26, 2026; the adoption date has yet to be determined.

The borough of Lachine is authorizing two events on Saturday, February 21, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.: the Défi de l'Ours polaire at parc riverain de Lachine and the Hivernales à Saint-Pierre at parc Kirkland.
The organizers will be allowed to temporarily occupy public property (parks, streets, sidewalks, parking lots) for the duration of the activities.
An ordinance allows exemptions from the by-laws on nuisances, in particular for noise and sound amplification.
The fees set out in the 2026 fee by-law are waived in full: occupying public property and using municipal equipment become free of charge for these events.
This exemption from fees is conditional on approval by the Agence de mobilité durable.
The ordinances come into force as soon as they are published on the borough's website.
The borough of Lachine is authorizing six public events on its territory in May 2026 and is lifting the municipal rules that would prevent them.
Organizers will be able to occupy parks, streets, sidewalks and parking lots, make noise and use amplifiers, and sell merchandise depending on the case.
Rue Notre-Dame will be closed between 10e and 14e Avenue on May 29, 30 and 31 for the "Dame Festive" event.
Fees for occupying public property are entirely waived for these events, which is indirect financial support for the organizations.

On the program: a hockey tournament (May 2), musical performances at parc Saint-Louis (May 12 to 28), activities at the Anglers dance floor (May 25 to 30), the P'tit Marché (May 12 to 30) and a colour run at parc LaSalle (May 14).
The authorizations take effect as soon as they are published on the borough's website.
The borough of Lachine is giving up to $15,000 to La P'tite Maison de Saint-Pierre to create an artistic and playful trail at parc Kirkland, in the Saint-Pierre neighbourhood.
The project will cover the paved surfaces and the walls of the park's chalet: colour gradients, hopscotch games, snakes and ladders, tic-tac-toe and pictograms. The sports fields are excluded.
Co-creation workshops with young people from the neighbourhood will take place before and during the work; recruitment will be done with schools and organizations in the area.
Schedule: idea development in June 2026, preparation in late June and early July, painting in August, touch-ups and a discovery activity in September.
The organization is working with A.G.C. Art Public and the artist Alexis Masella, who created a ground artwork at Duff Court in 2025.
Five projects had been submitted during the call held from April 8 to May 1, 2026; the selection committee chose this one on May 7.
The contribution is not recurring and the organization must report back no later than November 15, 2026.
The borough of Lachine is authorizing the public and special events planned for June, July and August 2026 on its territory, on the dates, at the times and in the locations listed in an appendix.

Four ordinances allow the temporary occupation of public property (parks, streets, sidewalks, parking lots), exemptions from the rules on noise, the sale of merchandise and alcoholic beverages, as well as street closures.
Organizers are fully exempted from the fees set out in the 2026 fee by-law, which the borough presents as indirect financial assistance.

Events covered include: the Fête nationale and Fête du Canada, the Mardis cyclistes, the P'tit marché, the musical picnics, outdoor movie screenings, the Festival de bateaux dragons and the Campement de la Nouvelle-France.
Locations affected include: parcs LaSalle, Noël-Spinelli, Kirkland, Dalbé-Viau, Michel-Ménard, Grovehill, the piscine Dixie, the Centre récréatif Lachine Ouest and 59, rue Saint-Pierre.
Boulevard Saint-Joseph will be closed between 21e and 24e avenues on June 24 (8 a.m. to 11 p.m.) and from noon on August 8 to 6 p.m. on August 9.
The borough secretary may correct formal errors (dates, times, typos) before publication, without changing the substance.
The borough of Lachine is authorizing the organization Le Réveil de Lachine to hold musical performances at parc Saint-Louis on September 1 and 3, 2026, from 12:30 p.m. to 4 p.m.
An ordinance allows the temporary occupancy of public property for those two days.
Another ordinance lifts certain rules of the nuisance by-law, in particular for noise, during the event.
The borough is granting a full exemption from public property occupancy fees, which amounts to indirect financial assistance to the organization.
The borough secretary may correct formatting errors (dates, times, typos) before publication, without changing the substance.
The ordinances come into force as soon as they are published on the borough's website.
The City will pay 18,220 euros (about $29,516.40) for its 2026 membership fee to Metropolis, the world association of major metropolises.
This fee also covers Montréal's membership in Cités et Gouvernements Locaux Unis (CGLU), which represents local governments before the UN, the European Union, the World Bank and the OECD.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city, and the funds are already included in the 2026 budget of the Bureau des relations internationales.
The fee goes from 16,560 euros (about $26,339.70) in 2025 to 18,220 euros in 2026.
Montréal, a founding member of Metropolis in 1985, holds the North America regional vice-presidency for the 2024-2026 term.
The document states that Montréal took part in four of the association's pilot projects: citizen participation, innovation labs, sustainable development and biodiversity, and well-being indicators.
No communications activities are planned; social media posts may accompany elected officials' participation in events.

The borough of Ville-Marie is tabling its annual report on the authorizations granted in 2025 under a temporary power (section 93 of the 2024 Québec housing act) that allows projects of 3 or more housing units to be approved despite urban planning rules.
Seven projects were authorized this way in 2025, and no application was refused.

Among them: the TVA site (1600, boul. De Maisonneuve Est, 600 housing units), the îlot Voyageur (505, boul. De Maisonneuve Est, 1215 housing units), the STM's Le Havre-Frontenac site (524 housing units), the L'Hirondelle project (2187, rue Larivière, 153 housing units), 2225, rue Parthenais (39 housing units) and the former hôpital de la Miséricorde (840-890, boul. René-Lévesque Est).
The exemptions granted mainly concern height, density, permitted uses and side setbacks; several projects also bypass the committee that reviews demolition applications.

In several cases, the report indicates that few or no housing units could have been built on the site without these exemptions (for example 0 housing units as of right on rue Parthenais, rue Larivière and rue Lucien-L'Allier).
The report was amended to remove the Le George project (1001, rue Lucien-L'Allier), which was authorized in 2026 rather than in 2025.
The report must be tabled at the borough council no later than April 1 following the year covered, then sent to the Minister of Housing and published on the City's website.
The borough of Ville-Marie is refusing two permit applications that had received an unfavourable opinion from its Comité consultatif d'urbanisme.

At 1389, rue Saint-Jacques, the refusal concerns a change in the brick model for a rebuilt building: the brick that was installed is more porous and its texture matches those of the area less well than the brick approved in 2024.
Part of a side wall has already been built with the wrong brick and work was stopped; another model would be possible if it is comparable and equivalent.
At 222, rue Notre-Dame Ouest, the refusal concerns the removal of the "Photo Service" neon sign, installed in the 1950s, in the site patrimonial du Vieux-Montréal.
The business closed on January 3, 2026 and the former owner was required to remove the sign under its lease; organizations that were contacted declined to take it because of its size.
Both applicants were notified on April 20, 2026 that their file would be presented for refusal at the June 9, 2026 council meeting; the files must be closed in June 2026.
After the refusal, the City will be able to classify the files on work done without a permit as non-compliant and assess legal remedies with its legal affairs department.
The borough of Verdun is awarding a $162,977.06 contract (taxes included) to 9083-0126 Québec inc. (Creusage RL) for pneumatic excavation services.
The contract runs for 36 months, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with no possibility of renewal.
The work is for maintaining the water supply system: cleaning, repairing or replacing water service boxes and valve boxes, and drilling test holes to detect leaks.
The borough says it has neither the equipment nor the workforce to do this work itself.
Only one compliant bid was received out of the ten companies that obtained the tender documents; the price is $5,001.41 (3.17%) higher than the City's latest estimate.
The expense is funded by the Service de l'eau and spread over the 2026, 2027 and 2028 budgets, at $49,606.59 net per year.

The borough of Verdun is offering the City to supply, itself, the staff needed at Verdun's snow disposal site (lieu d'élimination de la neige, LEN) during snow-loading operations, for 2025, 2026 and 2027.
The staff involved includes gatehouse attendants, sewer chute monitors, as well as drivers and operators.
The borough says it wants to keep these employees in-house in order to retain the know-how and make coordination with private contractors easier (operation, hauling, operated rentals).
The labour costs will be reimbursed to the borough by the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne, out of its operating budget.
If the offer is not accepted, the borough will have to reassign these resources elsewhere.
The borough of Verdun is renewing its security guard contract with Axia services, a non-profit organization, for $288,660.83 including taxes.
The contract covers one year, from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027, and is awarded directly, without a call for tenders.
The guards watch over access to the municipal workshops, check delivery slips for residual materials, monitor cameras at various sites and answer 311 calls outside office hours.
The cost is going up by 2.5% compared with the previous year ($281,578.37), which the borough attributes to inflation and to the order setting security agents' wages.
Axia services' mission is to provide jobs to people living with functional limitations.
To balance the 2026 budget, the borough transferred $7,866.50 from another public works line; it will ask for $12,400 more for 2027.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough wants to regularize a median strip that encroaches on the bed of the Rivière des Prairies, in front of the parc de la Promenade-Lalande.
This encroachment comes from fill work done around the 1960s and was flagged by the consultant (Terraformex) during the design of the park's redevelopment.
The City chose to lease the land rather than buy it, considering leasing to be simpler.
The lease includes annual fees: $80.00 plus taxes for 2026.
The borough director, Dominique Jacob, is designated as the representative to sign the lease on behalf of the borough.
The lease confirms that the premises will be used for non-profit purposes that promote public access to the body of water.
Next steps: forward the resolution, pay the fees, then sign the lease.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is entrusting CA 1 inc. with the installation of speed bumps, pavement markings, and signage at various locations within its territory.
The total authorized expenditure is $267,506.59 including taxes: $214,005.27 for the contract, $32,100.79 for contingencies, and $21,400.53 for incidentals.
The work must begin at the end of August 2026 and be completed by November 2026.
The goal is to reduce speeding on sections identified as high-risk by the Comité de circulation et de sécurité routière.
CA 1 inc. submitted the lowest of the three compliant bids reviewed, coming in 46.66% below the latest estimate of $401,228.
The invoice is paid 100% from the borough's capital budget (PDI).
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is awarding a contract worth $414,909.47, taxes included, to Les Entreprises Cogenex inc. for drainage and landscaping work.
The amount breaks down as follows: $377,190.43 for the contract, $26,403.33 in contingencies (7%), and $11,315.71 in incidental expenses (3%).
The work affects about twenty addresses in the borough: repair of waterways, drainage, repair behind curbs, concrete, asphalt, sewer and water main work, and sodding.
The work is set to begin in September 2026 and end in November 2026; residents will be notified before the work begins.
The bill is paid 100% from the Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough's surplus.

Four of the six parties who obtained the tender documents submitted bids; the lowest bid exceeds the initial estimate of $255,139.08 by 47%, a gap reduced to 20.3% after correcting underestimated items.

The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is awarding a contract of $1,191,749.18 (taxes included) to Les Entreprises J. Piccioni inc. to redo the roadway and a water main on boulevard Gouin Ouest, between rue Des Cageux and rue Coursol.
The amount includes $998,600 for the contract, $143,219.18 in contingencies (14%) and $49,930 in incidentals (5%).
The work adds a new sidewalk to make pedestrian access to parc Deauville safer, as part of the Vision Zéro program.
The work must start on August 24, 2026 and end on October 15, 2026; citizens will be notified beforehand.
Five companies submitted bids out of twelve that picked up the tender documents; the winning bid is 18% below the estimate of $1,220,804.

The cost is split between the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité ($781,928.09) and the Direction de la gestion de l'eau ($409,821.09), with financing through a loan by-law of up to $715,000 net.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is cancelling its call for tenders to redo the waterproofing of the roof, windows and curtain walls of the mairie.
The planned work included modifying the windows in the roof, repairing the waterproofing around the curtain walls, completely redoing the roof waterproofing, as well as interior and finishing work.
Only one company submitted a bid: Gagné Roy inc., at $3,087,078.75.
This bid exceeds the professionals' estimate, which was $800,174.58 including taxes, by 380%.
The call for tenders was launched on June 18, 2026, with bid opening on July 9, 2026, and two addenda published in the meantime.
The borough states that the cancellation and rejection of the bids have no financial impact for the Ville.
The Ville-Marie borough is adding $350,000 (taxes included) to the contract with Groupe ABF inc. for rebuilding sections of sidewalks on various streets in the area.
The maximum authorized spending for the project therefore rises to $7,088,121.35, including taxes, contingencies and incidental costs.
The money is used only to cover contingencies (unforeseen costs), which go from 20% to 26.8% of the contract.
The work, carried out from April to November 2025, is already finished; about 600 m² of sidewalks were added to the original contract.

Locations that were not planned were repaired during the season, including 1253 Sainte-Catherine Ouest, 1484 Sherbrooke Ouest, 2176-2178 Sainte-Catherine Ouest, ruelle Larivière, 1225 boulevard Saint-Laurent and 383 Notre-Dame Ouest.
The funding comes from loan by-law 23-041 ($118,001.93), the borough's road repair program ($22,385.05) and the operating budget ($209,613.02, reimbursed by developers' deposits).
According to the file, delaying the decision would delay payment to the City's suppliers.

The borough of Ville-Marie is adding $200,000, taxes included, to the contract with Demix Construction (Groupe CRH Canada) for water main, sewer and road work on boulevard De Maisonneuve, between avenue De Lorimier and rue Parthenais.
The maximum authorized spending for this contract goes from $6,333,651.10 to $6,533,651.10.
The money goes only to the contingency budget (unforeseen costs), which goes from 20% to 24.6% of the contract's value.
The work was meant to replace the sewer on boulevard De Maisonneuve and increase its capacity in order to reduce backups during heavy rain.

Causes of the unforeseen costs according to the document: a two-week delay at the start after an 84-inch pipe broke on René-Lévesque, quantities exceeding estimates, redoing work after the CSEM's work in the summer of 2025, and the addition of enlarged tree pits.
The contract, originally planned to last one year, ran from September 2024 to November 2025 to let the CSEM rebuild electrical conduit banks under the sidewalks.
The document states that about $700,000 of the itemized quote will not be used and that more than $500,000 will remain in the project's overall budget despite this increase.
The Ville-Marie borough is hiring the firm IGF Axiom inc. to supervise the work to extend five streets on the site of the former Molson brewery ("Quartier Molson").
Total authorized cost: $1,553,142.09, taxes included, including $1,294,285.07 for the contract and $258,857.01 in contingencies.

The streets involved: de la Commune (between Atateken and Alexandre-DeSève), as well as Montcalm, de la Visitation, Panet and Alexandre-DeSève between Notre-Dame and de la Commune, for about 1,000 metres.
The supervised work includes sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, roadwork, tree planting and a retaining wall 491 metres long and about 6 metres high.
The borough is advancing $1,134,580.60 from its surpluses; the developer (9399-8532 Québec inc., Montoni and Fonds immobilier FTQ) must repay about $1,242,513.67.

The City's share, estimated at $310,628.41 taxes included ($283,645.14 net of tax rebate), covers the off-site work and the extra size of the wall, and is paid by the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité.
The supervision contract runs from June 2026 to fall 2029; the infrastructure will then be handed over to the City.
The borough of Ville-Marie is hiring Cojalac inc. to rebuild sections of sidewalks on various streets in its territory, for a total authorized spending of $2,854,302.66 (taxes included).
The company's bid is $2,114,298.27, plus $422,859.65 in contingencies, $169,143.86 in unforeseen costs (material testing) and $148,000.88 for supervision.

The work targets sidewalks that are dangerous, uneven or temporarily paved with asphalt, and includes repairing sidewalks damaged by developers' construction sites and building new driveway entrances requested by residents.
Several tree pits will be enlarged as part of the work.
The work is to start in June 2026 and finish in October 2026; a preliminary list of the locations is attached to the file.
Cojalac inc. is the lower of the two compliant bidders in public call for tenders VMP-26-005; its price is 5.10% below the City's estimate.
A maximum amount of $525,662.55 will be funded by a central city loan by-law tied to maintaining road infrastructure; the company's performance will be evaluated.
The borough of Ville-Marie is awarding Eurovia Québec Construction inc. a contract worth $2,092,561.10 (taxes included) for planing and paving, meaning replacing 50 mm of road surface.
With contingencies ($418,512.22), incidental costs ($146,479.28) and supervision ($167,404.89), the authorized expense comes to $2,824,957.49.

Three areas are covered: rue Notre-Dame Est between avenue Papineau and the eastern boundary of the borough, rue Berri between Cherrier and Ontario Est (southbound), and voie Camillien-Houde for about 1.8 km starting from boulevard Mont-Royal.
The work starts at the end of June 2026 and must be finished in August 2026; the work on Notre-Dame and Berri will be done at night.
Local traffic will be maintained at all times on these sections, except for certain specific work.
Four companies submitted bids out of the six that picked up the tender documents; no bid was rejected.
The expense is funded by loan by-law 55856 and paid entirely by the Direction de la gestion des infrastructures urbaines et des entraves.

The borough of Ville-Marie is hiring the firm Groupe ABS inc. to carry out quality control of materials for the construction of five new street sections on the site of the former Molson brewery (the « Quartier Molson » project).
The total authorized spending comes to $959,228.15, taxes included: $799,356.79 for the contract and $159,871.36 in contingencies (20%).

The streets involved are de la Commune (between Atateken and Alexandre-DeSève), as well as Montcalm, de la Visitation, Panet and Alexandre-DeSève, between Notre-Dame and de la Commune — about 1,000 metres in total.
The work being monitored includes sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, roadways, tree planting and a retaining wall 491 metres long and about 6 metres high.

The borough is allocating $700,722.52 from its surpluses to pay in advance; the developer Montoni (9399-8532 Québec inc.) must reimburse $767,382.52, and the City is covering $191,845.63 for the off-site work and the oversizing of the wall.
The contract runs from June 2026 to the fall of 2029; the new infrastructure will then be transferred to the Ville de Montréal.
The borough states that it does not have the internal resources to carry out this quality control itself.
The Ville-Marie borough is hiring Eurovia Québec Construction inc. to plane (grind down) the road surface on various local streets, for $372,828.28 including taxes.
The total approved spending comes to $484,676.77, adding $74,565.66 in contingencies and $37,282.83 in incidental costs (laboratory).
The new asphalt surface will then be laid by the borough's blue-collar workers; the streets were chosen based on how badly the road surface has deteriorated.
The work starts in late August 2026 and ends in October 2026; local traffic will be maintained at all times, with some exceptions.
The borough will notify residents by mail before the work begins and through its newsletter.
Three companies bid on public call for tenders VMP-26-007; Eurovia was the lowest compliant bidder and its performance will be evaluated after the work is done.
The funding comes from the borough's investment program: 60% from the local budget for streets east of rue Atateken, and 40% from the corporate budget for those to the west.
The borough of Verdun is buying a half-page ad as part of the 2026 Irish festivities.
The ad is being bought from the Sociétés irlandaises unies de Montréal (United Irish Societies of Montreal), at a cost of $500 before taxes.
The expense is charged to the borough's advertising and information budget.
The document states that the borough council is thereby supporting the organization's activities.
The borough had already bought similar ads in previous years, notably $550 in 2024 from the Association sportive Erin.
The borough of Verdun is buying a half-page advertisement as part of the 2026 Irish festivities.
The approved expense is $300 before taxes, paid to La Société St-Patrick de Montréal.
The request comes from the mayor's office and is part of the council's support for the organization's activities.
By comparison, the borough had paid $550 for similar advertisements in 2022, 2023 and 2024, with the Association sportive Erin.
The decision falls to the Verdun borough council.
The Verdun borough is appointing councillor Stefana Lamasanu as the borough council's representative on the citizens' committee on universal accessibility.
She replaces Kaila Munro Amaya, who held this role until the elections of November 2, 2025.
Marlène Gagnon, director of culture, sports, recreation and social development, has represented the Administration on the committee since December 2025.
The committee, created in 2019, brings together six citizens from the Wellington-de-l'Église and Desmarchais-Crawford neighbourhoods, elected officials and borough employees.
Its members live with functional limitations or support someone who does; it follows the implementation of the Plan d'action en accessibilité universelle 2023-2026.
No spending is associated with this decision.
The borough of Verdun is giving $1,000, non-taxable, to the Concertation en développement social de Verdun (CDSV).
The money is for the 5th edition of the "Bienvenue à Verdun" event, organized by the CDSV's immigration committee.
The event welcomes newly arrived households and introduces them to neighbourhood resources and to their neighbours.
In 2026, the event will be held at the centre communautaire Elgar, on Île-des-Sœurs.
The money will be used for the event's visibility, for snacks for visitors and for a shuttle between Verdun and Île-des-Sœurs.
For previous editions, the City gave $1,200 in 2025 and in 2024, and $1,000 in 2023.
The borough of Verdun is applying for a grant from the ministère de l'Éducation du Québec to build an aquatic complex.

The application is being made through the Programme d'aide financière aux infrastructures récréatives, sportives et de plein air (PAFIRSPA), under its sports and recreational infrastructure component.
The funding can cover up to 66% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of $20 million.
Verdun has no municipal indoor pool: the only indoor pool on its territory belongs to Académie Beurling and is described as aging, not universally accessible and at maximum capacity.
The borough commits to paying the ongoing operating costs of the future complex.
The application must be submitted by June 22, 2026, after approval by the City's executive committee expected in May 2026; a response is expected in late 2026 or early 2027.

The borough of Outremont is offering to take charge itself of repairing short sections of sidewalks and curbs on certain arterial streets in its territory in 2026, and is asking city council to accept.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is paying 100% of the work; the budget set aside for Outremont is $105,000, net of rebate.
The sections were chosen based on three criteria: coordination with the milling and resurfacing program, correcting situations considered dangerous, and responding to requests from residents.
Announced schedule: plans and specifications in January 2026, call for tenders in February and March, contract awarded at the May borough council meeting, and work in June 2026.
Next step: city council must accept the borough's offer.
The borough of Outremont is awarding a $161,772.42 contract (taxes included) to Montréal Scellant inc. to rebuild sidewalks on various streets in 2026.
The total authorized spending comes to $186,038.28: the contract, plus $16,177.24 in contingencies and $8,088.62 in incidental expenses.

The work covers 300 square metres of concrete sidewalks and curbs, including about 190 square metres on the arterial network, along with restoring lawns, the paved gutter and part of the driveway entrances.
The work sites are planned for June and July 2026; the borough is announcing a communications plan to inform residents.
The streets were chosen based on coordination with the milling-and-paving program, the correction of situations considered dangerous, and requests from residents.
The bill is shared: 59.46% by the Service des infrastructures et du réseau routier, 40.54% by the borough.
Six of the eight companies that obtained the tender documents submitted a bid; the winning offer is the lowest, 15.12% below the estimate.
The borough of Outremont is awarding Les Pavages Ultra inc. a contract to build speed humps for $96,960.65, taxes included.
The total authorized spending comes to $109,656.72: the contract, $9,696.07 in contingencies and $3,000 in incidental costs, paid 100% by the borough.

Planned work: 10 speed humps on the street on avenue Davaar, avenue Champagneur and avenue Maplewood, and 27 in lanes in five blocks (Rockland, Du Manoir, Ducharme, Bloomfield, De l'Épée, Durocher, Hutchison, etc.).
The work also includes signage and pavement markings; it targets streets with a 30 km/h speed limit.
Nine companies submitted bids out of thirteen that picked up the tender documents; the lowest bid is 44.42% below the borough's estimate.
The work is scheduled for June 2026, with a communications plan to inform people about it.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is drawing up to $237,700 from its Fonds réservé - Parcs et terrains de jeux for the year 2026.
Of that amount, $197,700 goes to paying for two temporary horticulture and arboriculture inspector positions (salaries and related costs).
The remaining $40,000 goes to buying plants and other vegetation, taxes included.
The fund is supplied by contributions of 10% of a site's value that are required for certain subdivision or construction permits.
The borough says it is facing an increase in requests related to its green spaces and its urban forest.
In 2024, an amount of $257,500 had been allocated for similar purposes (a section head position, one arboriculture inspector, vegetation).
The City is preparing to award Bureau Veritas Canada (2019) inc. the laboratory analysis of water samples for 36 months, with an option to extend for 12 months.
The agreement is estimated at $1,361,444.52 including taxes: $1,237,676.84 for the services, plus $123,767.68 set aside in case the quantities requested increase.
The analyses cover drinking water, groundwater, pool water, leachate, industrial discharges, as well as food and contaminated soils.
The agreement will be available to all City units; the Service de l'environnement and the Service de l'eau are the main users.
Three companies submitted bids out of five that obtained the tender documents; Bureau Veritas submitted the lowest price, 34.5% below the second bid and 13.5% below the City's estimate.
Each analysis will be paid for out of the budget of the borough or department that requests it, as needs arise.
Since the contract exceeds $500,000, the company's performance will have to be evaluated.
The City is awarding 9403-2273 Québec inc. (Carrière Urbaine Montréal Ouest) the contract to recover value from rock, concrete and asphalt, for a maximum of $608,769.63 including taxes.
The agreement lasts 14 months, with an option to extend it by 12 months; purchases will be made as needed, with no budget set aside in advance.
The service handles excavation waste (rock, concrete, asphalt) produced by the boroughs during construction work, sorted at the City's transfer site.
The company is the lowest compliant bidder among 3 bids received, out of 7 companies that purchased the tender documents.
The selected price is 12.7% below the City's estimate ($696,978.45), in particular because the company is already established in Montréal.
This new call for tenders replaces the agreement awarded in 2023 to Valosphère Environnement, which ceased operations in October 2025 for lack of insurance; the City claimed its performance bond.
Since the contract is over $500,000, the supplier's performance will have to be evaluated.

City council is authorizing the City to submit the "59 Saint-Pierre" project for the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation's Prix Mérite municipal 2026, in the Municipalité et développement durable category.
The project is located in the Saint-Pierre neighbourhood, in Lachine, in a former fire station of 150 m² lent free of charge by the borough.

The site brings together a social economy caterer offering affordable ready-to-eat meals, a neighbourhood café, an affordable grocery store and a drop-off point for fruits and vegetables from local farms, as well as collective kitchens and workshops.
Led since 2024 by Concert'action Lachine together with the borough and the City, the project stems from the Montréal en commun program, funded by the Smart Cities Challenge of Canada.
Submitting the application has no financial impact; the ministère requires the resolution of support to complete the file.
Planned timeline: application submitted on February 20, 2026, resolution sent on March 20, 2026, finalists announced in April 2026, awards presented in spring 2026.
No public communication is planned until the application is shortlisted or wins an award.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is submitting its annual report on the use of the special power to authorize housing projects despite urban planning regulations (section 93 of Bill 31).
In 2025, only one project was authorized this way: the demolition of the building at 7500, rue Saint-Denis (the former Chinese hospital) and the construction of a six-storey residential building.
The exemptions granted concern residential use, height (6 storeys and 24 m), the building coverage rate (65%) and the minimum percentage of masonry (65%).
The project provides for at least 30 housing units, whereas no housing unit could have been built on the site under the regulations in force.
No other authorization request of this type was received or refused in the borough in 2025.
Borough reports must be submitted before April 1; the Service de l'habitation will forward them to the ministry and publish the consolidated data on a web page.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is allowing the owners of 8085-8087, avenue De Gaspé (south of rue Jarry) to merge their duplex into a single-family home.
The 1922 building has two one-bedroom units of about 75 m² each; the new unit will be about 130 m², with three bedrooms and an office.
The upstairs unit was to be left vacant in the summer; the owners live on the ground floor.
Three conditions apply: keeping the door openings on the front of the building, limiting the residential floor area to 250 m², and filing the renovation permit application within 12 months.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on April 8, 2026, citing the narrowness of the lot (6.10 m wide), which limits any enlargement.
The fee to review the application is $3,500; no changes are planned to the front of the building.
At the meeting, no one asked to speak about this application.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing the conversion of a duplex into a single-family home at 8467-8469, avenue Henri-Julien.
The owners want to merge the two one-bedroom units (about 60 m² each) to create a three-bedroom unit for their family, including a child they wish to welcome.
The number of units in the building therefore goes from two to one; both units are vacant or will be this summer.
Three conditions apply: keep the staircase and the 2nd-floor balcony at the front, limit the residential floor area to 250 m², and file the permit application within 12 months.

The Direction and the urban planning advisory committee support the application: the lot is 6.10 m wide, the expansion is limited, and the basin zone prohibits the window wells needed to set up bedrooms in the basement.
At the committee, some members expressed unease: reducing the number of units in the middle of a housing crisis, and the fact that the applicants do not yet live in the building.
The fees for reviewing the application come to $3,500. No one spoke at the public meeting.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is filing a second report on the use, in 2025, of the provincial power that allows housing projects to be approved even when they do not comply with zoning. This report covers decisions made by city council.
Two projects were approved this way, both on boulevard Saint-Michel, for a total of 460 housing units.
At 7030, boulevard Saint-Michel (Condos locatifs Mondev): 178 housing units, with exemptions on maximum height and the type of siting.

At 7640-7740, boulevard Saint-Michel (Complexe Angélique-Latimer): 282 housing units, with exemptions on residential use, height, setbacks, the percentage of masonry and other standards. The report states that no housing units could have been built there as of right.
No application was refused by the borough in 2025.
The Service de l'habitation will send the reports to the ministère des Affaires municipales and publish the data on a web page.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is amending its zoning by-law to allow temporary signs during the redevelopment work on rue De Castelnau Est.
The businesses covered are those located on De Castelnau Est, between rue Saint-Dominique and rue Saint-Denis (zones E02-139, C02-143, C02-144 and C02-145).
Each business will be able to add one banner of 1 m² maximum and one string of pennants on its façade, with no permit required, in addition to the signage already allowed.
Signs may also be placed in display windows, provided that at least 50% of the window is left free of signage.
These signs will have to be removed by December 1, 2028, at the end of the construction work.
The borough says it wants to reduce the impact of the work on merchants by increasing their visibility to passersby.
No one came to the public meeting of June 11, 2026, or took part in the written consultation held from June 5 to 12, 2026; the by-law is to be adopted on July 7, 2026.
The borough council of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing the merger of two units in the building at 7436A to 7440, rue Chabot, north of rue Everett.

The owner will be allowed to combine the ground-floor unit with the one on the 2nd floor (about 94 m² each) to create a unit with five bedrooms and an office; the building will go from four units to three.
Two conditions apply: only these two units may be merged, and the application for the renovation permit must be filed within 12 months after the resolution is adopted.
The work includes adding an interior staircase connecting the two floors and setting up a family room in place of the 2nd-floor kitchen; the façade will not be changed.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on June 10, 2026, notably because the merger is reversible and because this type of large unit is hard to find in the neighbourhood.
