The fees for reviewing the application come to $3,500. A public notice will be posted on the borough's website and a sign will be placed on the property.
At the meeting, no one asked to speak about this application.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing the conversion of the duplex at 7946-7948, avenue De Gaspé (south of rue Jarry) into a single-family home.
The two units are already connected by an indoor staircase built without a permit in 2013 and are occupied by the same residents; the City considers that no rental unit is being taken off the market.
The owners want to open up the living spaces on the ground floor and set up three bedrooms and an office on the 2nd floor, for about 140 m² (210 m² including the basement).

Conditions imposed: keep the staircase and the 2nd-floor balcony at the front of the building, limit the area of the residential use to 250 m², and file the conversion permit application within 12 months.
The work must also bring into compliance a windowless bedroom built without a permit on the 2nd floor.
The fee for reviewing the application is $3,500; the urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on June 10, 2026.
At the meeting, no one asked to be heard on the application.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing a solidarity market in parc Nicolas-Tillemont, from August 14 to November 1, 2026.
The market will be set up in a multi-purpose container and the area around it, and will be open Friday to Sunday, from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.
It will sell fresh, local food at affordable prices (solidarity pricing): eggs, grain products and legumes, along with cooking workshops and light cultural activities.
The project is led by the Corporation de développement communautaire Solidarités Villeray and the Collectif Villeray Sans Faim, and is aimed at residents of eastern Villeray.
The borough is not paying any money: the container was given to the organizations free of charge by a private company.
This is a pilot project for a first season; the organizations want to make it permanent if it is successful.
The exact location of the container will be set with the borough, and the site will be set up in August 2026.
City council takes note of the 2025 annual report of the Office de consultation publique de Montréal (OCPM), tabled by majority leader Julien Hénault-Ratelle.
The OCPM reports 6 public consultations completed in 2025 (5 started in 2024 and one new mandate), including a mandate on social cohabitation and homelessness.
Participation figures cited: 159 in-person activities, 760 participations in meeting rooms, 12,247 online participations, 6,883 citizen contributions and 8,967 people reached.

The Office says it has responded to the Auditor General's recommendations: a new governance framework, a code of ethics for commissioners and a recruitment policy, with the hiring of seven new commissioners.
Its strategic planning is not finished and is to be completed in the spring of 2026; a letter accompanies the report to present the findings of this process.
The report will be published on the OCPM's website and announced through its social media and its newsletter.
The City is making its financial assistance program for businesses affected by major construction work applicable in two new areas: "De Lorimier" and "Fleury Est".
For "De Lorimier", the assistance covers the work period from November 3, 2025 to March 31, 2027, and it starts to apply on March 25, 2026.
For "Fleury Est", the assistance covers the period from October 20, 2025 to November 14, 2027, also starting on March 25, 2026.
The period covered runs from the start of the work until six months after it ends, because the impacts on businesses continue after the construction site closes.

The City is expanding the boundaries of the already eligible areas "Sainte-Catherine Ouest – Phase 2", "Notre-Dame / 13e Avenue", "Sainte-Catherine Ouest – Phase 3" and "Maisonneuve-Berri Phase 2", since businesses outside the former boundaries are also affected.
For the "Notre-Dame / 13e Avenue" area, the work period is adjusted to match the actual end date of the construction work.
The end dates given may change and will be revised based on how the work actually progresses.
The City is giving $50,000 to Festival M.A.D. Montréal to hold a pop-up market of Montréal products in the Quartier des spectacles, from August 20 to 23, 2026.
The market will bring together 70 local businesses in fashion, arts and design, which will be able to sell their products on site.
The money will be paid in two instalments: $30,000, then $20,000 in 2026. The City's contribution covers 14.3% of the project.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration, out of the $200M agreement with the ministère de l'Économie (2025-2029).
The organization must submit its accountability report no later than October 31, 2026 and apply the City's visibility protocol.
This is the first time the Service du développement économique is funding this event, which has already been supported for years by the Service de la culture.
The City is giving $40,000 to the Société culturelle « Les Survenants » to run activities on the rue Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
The activities will take place from July 10 to 19, 2026: free broadcasts of the matches from the quarter-finals to the final, music shows, roving performers, and food offerings from local businesses.
The project is being developed with the SDC Les Quartiers du Canal, the rue Notre-Dame Ouest merchants, the CEDA, Youth in Motion and other local partners.
The money will be paid in two instalments: $30,000, then $10,000. The City's contribution represents 37.5% of the project's total cost.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city, out of the 2026 operating budget of the Service du développement économique.
The organization will have to confirm that it holds the rights to publicly broadcast the matches, and submit its accountability report by August 31, 2026.
The City is entering into an agreement with Agence Gravel inc. to supply 9 mm practice ammunition to the Service de police de Montréal (SPVM), for a maximum of $2,068,860.15, taxes included.
The agreement runs for 29 months and includes an option to extend it by 12 months, with the price adjusted according to the consumer price index (estimated value of $812,078.31).
The contract covers 3,000,000 frangible 9 mm Luger cartridges: 400,000 from October to December 2026, then 1,300,000 per year in 2027 and 2028.
This ammunition is used for shooting training and the annual requalification of police officers, required by the ministère de la Sécurité publique.
Four companies submitted bids out of the five that obtained the tender documents; Agence Gravel submitted the lowest compliant bid, $508,522.93 less than the next one.
The selected price is 2.38% ($48,174.52) higher than the City's most recent estimate.
The expense is covered by the agglomeration, since police services are an agglomeration responsibility; the supplier's performance will be evaluated.
The City is extending the SPVM's courier contract with Planète Courrier inc. by 12 months, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027, under the same terms.
It is approving an additional expense of $244,200, taxes included, bringing the total value of the agreement to $903,565.76.
The contract covers the pickup, sorting, stamping and delivery of mail and small parcels for about 150 SPVM units, including the neighbourhood police stations.

Postes Canada service stoppages (91 days in 2024 and 2025) drove up the use of on-demand courier service: the amount of the original contract, which was meant to last until June 2027, will run out around September 2026.
The service includes delivering files to the municipal court within the deadlines required for court appearances; the supplier's employees must hold a security clearance.
The expense is paid by the agglomeration, since police service is an agglomeration responsibility, and is drawn from the SPVM's 2026 and 2027 budgets.
The City is awarding AV-Tech inc. a contract for carpenter labourer services for the buildings of the Service de police (SPVM), for a maximum amount of $367,644.06, taxes included.
The contract runs for 36 months starting in June 2026, with two extension options of 12 months each (initially valued at $228,000, taxes included).

The supplier will provide up to 1,600 hours of work per 12-month period: installing frames, boards, shelves and bike racks, minor repairs to furniture and lockers, changing lock cylinders, moves and reorganizations.
The hourly rate goes from $64.00 in 2026-27 to $66.60 in 2027-28, then to $69.25 in 2028-29.
AV-Tech inc. is the lowest of the six compliant bidders in public call for tenders 26-21327; its bid is 4.83% below the latest estimate and 29.92% below the second-lowest bid.
AV-Tech inc.'s performance will be evaluated; the expense is covered by the agglomeration, since policing is an agglomeration responsibility.
Two other lots from the same call for tenders (lots 1 and 3) will be the subject of a later decision.
The City is hiring SB joints et peinture inc. to provide building painting services for the buildings of the Service de police de Montréal (SPVM), for a maximum of $159,815.25, taxes included.
It is adding a contingency budget of $31,963.05, bringing the estimated total to $191,778.30.
The agreement runs for 36 months starting in August 2026, with two possible 12-month extensions.
The supplier must provide about 500 hours of work per year: preparing work sites, repairing surfaces, painting, finishing and cleaning; the hourly rate goes from $90 to $95 over the three years.
SB joints et peinture inc. submitted the lowest of the 7 compliant bids, at 39.57% below the City's estimate.
The SPVM occupies more than sixty buildings; this service is no longer provided by the blue-collar workers of the Service de la gestion et de la planification immobilière.
The expense is paid by the agglomeration, since policing is an agglomeration responsibility.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a $281,296.93 contract (taxes included) to Mile Construction inc. to replace, automate and bring up to standard doors at the bibliothèque Mordecai-Richler, at 5434, avenue du Parc.
With contingencies ($56,259.39) and incidental costs ($56,259.39), the total expense comes to $393,815.71, taxes included, paid entirely by the borough.

The work covers the main wooden entrance door, to be rebuilt by a craftsperson recognized by the Conseil des métiers d'art du Québec, and four interior doors covered by a non-compliance notice from the Service de sécurité incendie received in July 2024.
The three pairs of doors will be fitted with an automatic opening system connected to the electrical panel, to improve universal accessibility.
The library will stay open during the work: noisy work will be done before opening hours, Monday to Thursday before 10 a.m. and Friday before noon, and the work must be finished before winter.

Two companies submitted bids; the one from 9491-0023 Québec inc. – Gestion immobilière MAJ inc. was rejected because it did not attend the mandatory site visit. The winning bid is $52,817.07 (15.81%) below the estimate.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a $216,612.90 contract (taxes included) to XO Construction inc. to replace all the windows in the gymnasium of the Centre Saint-Denis, at 5115, rue Rivard.
The total authorized spending comes to $303,258.06: the contract plus $43,322.58 in contingencies and $43,322.58 in incidental costs (20% each).
The bill is paid entirely by the borough, out of its management surplus, and charged to the 2026 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The current windows, about 30 to 40 years old, have deteriorated: fewer than half of the opening sections still work, while the gymnasium has no air conditioning.
The new windows will be the same size but will have twice as many opening sections, with a mechanism operated from the gymnasium floor.
Gymnasium activities will be interrupted during the work phase (demolition, decontamination of materials that may contain asbestos, installation); completion is expected before winter.
Two bids were submitted out of four companies that obtained the tender documents; the other offer was $402,966.77, and the City's estimate was $339,401.11.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is approving an expense of $170 (taxes included) to send an elected official to an event.
The event is the 40th edition of the Grand Prix du Conseil des arts de Montréal, on April 2, 2026, at the Palais des congrès.
The person concerned is Ericka Alneus, city councillor for the Étienne-Desmarteau district.
The Grand Prix, held since 1985, honours Montréal artists and arts organizations; 900 people are expected to attend.
The expense is charged according to the financial information in the file; no other financial commitment is planned.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is paying $1,196, plus taxes, to send four elected officials to the Gala ESTim.
The gala, now in its 38th edition, takes place on May 7, 2026 at the Tohu.
Tickets cost $299 each (plus taxes, member pre-sale rate).
The elected officials involved are Mayor François Limoges and councillors Ericka Alneus, Jocelyn Pauzé and Olivier Demers-Dubé.
The gala, organized for business people in the territory of the Chambre de commerce de l'Est de Montréal, honours businesses and organizations that have stood out.
The decision falls under the borough council.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is paying about $1,200, plus taxes, to send one elected official to a conference.
The event is the Sommet national : Droit à l'alimentation, from April 14 to 16, 2026, in Sherbrooke.
The elected official involved is Olivier Demers-Dubé, city councillor for the Vieux-Rosemont district.
In-person registration costs $280 per person, plus taxes; the rest of the amount covers other participation costs.
The borough says it wants to strengthen its expertise, build ties with other municipalities and support its PDCN (plan for developing a food system).
The summit deals in particular with the idea of a Québec framework law guaranteeing the right to food; close to 400 registrations had been confirmed.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding a contract worth $526,148.60, taxes included, to 9363-9888 Québec inc. (Sanivac) for hydro-excavation services.
The contract covers the rental of a hydro-excavation truck with an operator, for about 33 months, until December 31, 2028, with no possibility of renewal.
This technique injects water under pressure to dig and vacuum up materials, which makes it possible to work in tight spaces while maintaining water and sewer networks.
The expected yearly quantities: 400 hours of regular calls (250 of which are guaranteed), 50 hours on Saturdays and Sundays, 20 hours of emergency calls and 20 tonnes of sludge to dispose of.
9363-9888 Québec inc. is the lowest compliant bidder among the 4 bids received (one of which was found non-compliant); the price accepted is 11% below the estimate of $586,142.55.
The cost is paid entirely by the borough, out of its operating budget.
The performance of the selected company will be evaluated.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding Construction Urbex inc. the maintenance of the new parc Bassin-à-Bois, in Griffintown, for $779,243.06 including taxes.

The contract covers three parts: snow removal on the paths and maintenance of the refrigerated skating rink ($241,039.34), mowing, landscaping and site cleaning in the summer ($95,279.78), and maintenance of the chalet ($442,923.94).
The park chalet is open 365 days a year; its maintenance includes interior cleaning and the washroom facilities until October 31, 2027.
The contract begins in mid-April 2026 and ends in November 2027, with no renewal option.
Two companies submitted bids; the winning bid is 52.18% below the City's estimate, which the borough explains by the timing of the call for tenders and the contractor's pricing strategy.
The cost is paid entirely by the borough, out of its operating budget, and the company's performance will be evaluated.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding a contract worth $206,322.64, taxes included, to Les Pavages Dancar (2009) inc. to rent a backhoe loader with an operator, maintenance and attachments.
The machine will be used to plant trees (digging pits) and to maintain parks and green spaces in the borough.
The contract covers about 740 hours per year, including 285 guaranteed hours, and ends on December 31, 2027, with no possibility of renewal.
Two companies submitted bids for public call for tenders 26-21320; the other bid, at $228,869.24, was found not to meet administrative requirements.
The winning bid is 3% below the City's estimate, which was set at $212,763.46.
The 2026 expense comes from the Plan de la forêt urbaine funding envelope; in 2027, $58,575 will come from that envelope and $35,625 from the budget of the Division des parcs et de l'horticulture.
The borough is covering the entire expense.
The borough of LaSalle is updating its list of recognized organizations for 2026, in the areas of sports, recreation, culture and community life.
The organization Autivie is receiving a first recognition, valid for one year, with partner status.
Autivie will be entitled to staff and logistical support right away, but to financial support only at the end of this first year.
The other organizations are having their recognition renewed for a three-year period, after providing the required documents.
Recognition gives access to the borough's basket of services (staff, logistical and financial support).
The file involves no spending; each organization will receive a letter confirming its classification and the length of its recognition.
The borough of LaSalle is renewing its recognition of sports, recreation, culture and community life organizations for the year 2026.
Recognized organizations keep access to the borough's "basket of services": staff, logistical and financial support, based on their classification and the length of their recognition.
The organizations involved have provided all the required documents and qualify for a renewable three-year period.
The recognition is based on the Politique de reconnaissance et de soutien des organismes de LaSalle, revised in fall 2025.

After adoption, the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social will send a letter to each organization confirming its classification and the length of its recognition.
The file has no financial impact; the full list of organizations is attached to the decision summary.
The City is extending the contract for supplying and transporting "roll-off" containers for the écocentre Saint-Laurent by 12 months, until October 31, 2027.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $934,221.31, taxes included, bringing the total contract to $3,173,060.07.
This amount includes $708,011.60 for the contract itself, $10,620.17 in indexation, $107,794.77 in contingencies and $107,794.77 for variation in quantities.
The contract, originally awarded to Excavations Vidolo ltée, was transferred to GFL Environmental inc. on July 1, 2025; the company accepted the renewal on April 24, 2026.
The Service de l'environnement explains that the funds from the first extension will be used up in July 2026 and wants to avoid an interruption in service.
The increase in needs comes from greater use of the écocentre and larger quantities of materials received; about 2,700 transports are expected per year.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration and spread over 2026 and 2027.
The borough of Anjou is legalizing the position of the industrial building at 9151, boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine, bought by furniture maker Bugatti Design.
Zoning requires setbacks of 7.6 m; the building is 7.3 m from the front property line (0.3 m too close) and 4.4 m from the left side property line (3.2 m too close).
The front setback discrepancy was noticed after an expansion and comes from a difference in interpretation between two land surveyors about where the boulevard's boundary lies.
The side setback discrepancy has existed since the 1973 building permit, with no proof in the archives of an authorization or an acquired right.
According to the City, applying the by-law would mean demolishing part of the building.
The urban planning advisory committee issued a favourable opinion on February 2, 2026; a public notice must be published at least 15 days before the council meeting.
No condition tied to Montréal 2030 is being added, since ten trees are already planned as part of the expansion project.
The borough of Anjou is refusing the parking exemption request for the building at 7261-7277, avenue Rondeau.
The owner wanted to turn the front garage of his unit into a bedroom, which removes one of the three required parking spaces.
Since he could not move that space outdoors while complying with the regulations, he asked to pay $5,000 instead of providing it.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme issued an unfavourable opinion on February 2, 2026: on-street parking in the area is already in very high demand, and approving the request could set a precedent.

According to the Division des études techniques, the section of avenue Rondeau between boulevard Châteauneuf and avenue Yvette-Naubert has few free spaces, mainly because of the garage driveways, the centre Roger-Rousseau and the nearby park.
A permit issued on December 17, 2025 had already authorized the addition of a unit in the basement, with no requirement to add a parking space.
The borough of Anjou is amending its by-law on the demolition of buildings to bring it in line with Québec's cultural heritage legislation and with the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050.
Two lists of heritage buildings located in Anjou are being added as appendices; these buildings can no longer be exempted from the demolition committee's authorization.
To demolish a heritage building, applicants will now have to provide a heritage study, an expert report on the building's condition, and an estimate of the cost of restoration work.
A public hearing becomes mandatory for heritage buildings, and the public notice must be sent to the Minister of Culture and Communications.

The committee will be able to postpone its decision to give an interested person time to buy a heritage building and preserve its character; city council will be able to overrule the committee's decision.

The definition of "demolition" is changing to work affecting 50% or more of the surface area of the exterior walls and the roof, and the monetary guarantee becomes proportional to the value on the assessment roll.
Next steps: notice of motion and draft by-law, public notice, public consultation, then adoption and coming into force.

The borough of Anjou is granting a minor exemption at 9393, boulevard Métropolitain to allow outdoor storage in the back yard, on a maximum of 6% of the lot (1,457.5 m²), even though the zoning prohibits it.

Telecon, a telecommunications company, wants to bring together in one place its activities currently spread across Anjou (9500, boulevard Parkway), Saint-Laurent and Laval: offices, labs, training rooms, storage and vehicle fleet.
Outdoor storage is limited to trailers, compressors, tractors and cable reels.
The owner must build a 2-metre embankment in the front yard with 13 trees, and install a chain-link fence with slats 2.5 metres high around the parking lot and the storage area.
A new parking area in the left side yard will hold 140 service vehicles; 22 new trees are planned in the parking areas.
The vegetated portion of the site will go from 48.7% to 21.4% (the required minimum is 10%).
Work must start within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The borough of Anjou is approving an exemption from the zoning rules for 7001, boulevard des Roseraies.

The exemption allows the construction of a small structure in the back yard: an entrance to the underground parking with ventilation equipment, measuring 35 m² with a maximum height of 3.6 m, covered in brick.
Normally, the zoning by-law (RCA 40) does not allow this type of construction in yards.
The developer cites the Code de construction: an additional entrance to the three-level underground parking is required, and an open-air stairway would cause problems with snow, water and safety.
The structure would be located more than 23 metres from the boundary of the neighbouring residential property and nearly 43 metres from the building on it.
The work must begin within 44 months after the resolution is adopted, otherwise it becomes void.
No greening condition is added, because the planting of 90 trees is already planned as part of the construction project.

The City is extending the contract with 9169-9835 Québec inc. (Publications 9417) by 12 months (March 8, 2026 to March 7, 2027) to print, insert, mail and supply the stationery for municipal court notices.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $252,424.49, taxes included, bringing the total contract to $744,575.95.
The unit prices remain those of the call for tenders, indexed by 2.58% based on the consumer price index, an increase of $6,348.76 over the annual value of $246,075.73.
The expense breaks down into $120,495.29 for stationery and $131,929.20 for printing, inserting and mailing.
The bill is paid 100% by the agglomeration, since these are municipal court activities; the funds are already in the budget of the Service des affaires juridiques.
According to the document, a refusal or a postponement would paralyze the mailing of about 9,000 notices a day to defendants, causing hearings to stop and revenue losses.
The supplier has held this mandate since 2016 and has confirmed its interest in renewing for one more year.
The City is paying $108,343.91 (net of rebates) to the borough of Verdun to fund the preliminary studies for building an outdoor gymnasium at parc Arthur-Therrien.
The park sits on a former dump: environmental and geotechnical studies are required under the Environment Quality Act before the work can go ahead.
The borough is awarding the contract to the firm Groupe ABS inc., under a framework agreement already signed with the City (call for tenders 23-20255).
The work includes 9 boreholes, chemical analyses, groundwater sampling and 3 biogas monitoring wells, mainly in an area of about 1,875 m² near the parking lot of école secondaire Mgr-Richard.
The open-air gymnasium is a winning project from the City's 2022-2023 participatory budget.
The total expense comes to $118,650.71 including taxes, of which $10,786.43 is for contingencies; it is paid 100% by the central city.
Verdun will have to report its spending to the Service de l'environnement every quarter, and the funding will be reduced if the actual costs are lower.
The borough of Lachine is paying $597.87, taxes included, for a corporate membership in the Chambre de commerce de l'Ouest-de-l'Île de Montréal.
The membership covers the period from February 3 to December 31, 2026.
It gives access to the Chambre's activities: conferences, discussion panels, galas, a golf tournament and networking events.
The mayor and, if needed, other council members will take part in these activities to represent the borough on economic and social issues.
The expense will be taken from the budget of the borough's management office.
Last year, the borough had authorized up to $2,500 for elected officials to take part in activities of the same chamber of commerce in 2025.
The borough of Lachine is entrusting GRAME, a non-profit organization, with managing the Éco-quartier program in its territory, for $296,580, taxes included if applicable.
The contract, awarded by mutual agreement, covers 24 months, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
GRAME must inform, raise awareness among and mobilize residents on cleanliness, beautification, waste management, greening, urban agriculture, water management and reducing GHGs.
The spending is broken down as follows: $98,860 in 2026, $148,290 in 2027 and $49,430 for the first four months of 2028.
The borough will evaluate the organization each year and may terminate the agreement at any time.
The borough had estimated the contract at $454,411; GRAME bid $296,580, counting on volunteers and other funding sources.
Planned deadlines: review of the program on June 30, 2026, 2027 action plan on January 31, 2027, reports on March 31, 2027 and March 31, 2028.
The borough of Lachine is lending a community garden to GRAME free of charge, from June 1, 2026 to January 31, 2029 (32 months).
The land is located behind the Maison Mère des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne, between rue Provost and Duff Court, in parc des Sœurs-de-Sainte-Anne.
Two plots of about 1,500 m² each have been developed: one for collective gardening, the other for about sixty community garden lots.
The lots will be assigned first to residents already on the waiting list for a borough community garden.
The project includes training workshops on urban agriculture, food processing and marketing for young people aged 12 to 25.
The borough is not providing any financial contribution: the project is funded by the Programme Impact collectif administered by Centraide.
Work is expected to be completed on June 12, 2026, with opening to the public in August 2026.

The borough of Lachine is renting space in the église des Saints-Anges (1400, boulevard Saint-Joseph, entrances at 50 and 70, 15e Avenue) from the Fabrique de la paroisse des Saints-Anges-Gardiens-de-Lachine.
Two leases cover the period from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2029, for a total net rent of $91,685 ($29,664 in 2027, $30,553 in 2028, $31,468 in 2029).
The space, measuring 6,788 square feet, will house two recognized organizations: Le Réveil de Lachine and L'Ensemble folklorique de Lachine, Les Éclusiers.
Le Réveil de Lachine offers social activities to more than 150 senior members and provides them with a woodworking shop.
L'Ensemble folklorique Les Éclusiers brings together more than 84 participants of all ages around Québec folk dance.

The organizations must maintain their recognized status under the Politique de reconnaissance et de soutien aux organismes à but non lucratif; the agreements for the loan of the space would follow approval by the borough council on October 5, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is adopting a new by-law that expands the commercial zone of the « Village » area.
This expansion allows the Société de développement commercial (SDC) du Village to extend its district into an area next to its current boundaries.
The current zone is bounded by avenue De Lorimier, boulevard René-Lévesque, rue Berri, boulevard De Maisonneuve and rue Atateken; the new boundaries are shown on a map attached to the by-law.
SDC members unanimously approved the expansion project at a special meeting held on March 23, 2026.
The by-law replaces the 2004 by-law (CA-24-029) that set the boundaries of the Village's commercial zone.
The map was corrected to exclude a small area south of boulevard René-Lévesque Est where the buildings do not front onto that boulevard.
Notice of motion given on May 5, 2026; adoption planned for June 9, 2026. No amount is associated with this file.
The Ville-Marie borough council takes note of the certificate on the register held on April 8, 2026 regarding the construction project at 810, rue Saint-Antoine Est.
The specific project authorizes a building, part of which exceeds the maximum height allowed in metres and in storeys.
Out of 2,146 people qualified to vote in zones 0083, 0097, 0105 and 0155 (Saint-Jacques district), 425 signed the register, whereas 226 signatures were enough.
Result: the resolution is not considered approved and a referendum vote must be held.
No amount is attached to this file.
The borough of Ville-Marie is amending its by-law on the occupation of public property to separate the pricing for sidewalk cafés from that of other periodic occupations (such as parklets).
From now on, the price to pay to occupy the sidewalk or the street with a sidewalk café will be the one set in the borough's fees by-law, rather than the one for periodic occupations.
The change goes along with a parallel amendment to the Règlement sur les tarifs de Ville-Marie for the 2026 fiscal year, which revises the way sidewalk cafés are priced.
The document does not set any new amount: the fees themselves are dealt with in another file.
Notice of motion given on April 14, 2026, adoption planned for the borough council meeting of May 5, 2026, followed by public notice and coming into force.
The Ville-Marie borough is cancelling its authorization to build a building taller than the permitted limit (in metres and in storeys) at 810, rue Saint-Antoine Est.
The specific project had been approved on March 10, 2026, after two draft resolutions in September 2025 and February 2026.
During the register held on April 8, 2026, 425 people asked for a referendum, while 226 signatures were enough; 2,146 people were eligible to vote in zones 0083, 0097, 0105 and 0155.
Rather than hold the referendum vote, the council is withdrawing its resolution, an option that is allowed as long as the notice of poll has not been published.
A public notice will be posted on the borough's public notices website within 15 days of the withdrawal, with a copy sent to the Chief Electoral Officer.

The Société de développement commercial (SDC) du Village wants to expand its business district in Ville-Marie: from rue Ontario in the north to boulevard René-Lévesque in the south, and from rue Berri in the west to rue De Lorimier in the east.
The borough is officially receiving the request, filed on May 29, 2026 by the SDC, and is starting the next steps in the process set out by law.
The borough secretary must open a register within 45 days to collect the signatures of merchants in the area who oppose the expansion.
All affected businesses will receive a notice; the register opens 15 days after that notice is sent.
Depending on the result of the register, the borough council will either adopt the expansion or set a date for a vote.
The borough is paying the costs of the process: registered mail, opening the register and holding a vote if needed.
The SDC says it is aiming for the expansion to take effect on January 1, 2027; its plan was adopted unanimously by the members present at the meeting of March 23, 2026.
The Ville-Marie borough council takes note of the filing of a correction record signed on June 26, 2026 by the borough secretary.
The correction concerns urban planning by-law CA-24-282.147, adopted on May 5, 2026, which completed the alignment with the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité.
An error appeared on the map of differentiated heights and densities (Appendix C of the by-law, Appendix M of by-law 01-282).
One zone had been divided by mistake: it must instead be attached to the zone that includes the Molson site, with a differentiated density of 7, as in by-law CA-24-282.145-1.
The corrected map replaces the old one, which allows the Ville-Marie urban planning by-law to be updated and administratively codified.
There is no financial aspect associated with this file.

The Ville-Marie borough wants to amend its by-law on civic responsibility, respect and cleanliness to give itself the power to temporarily suspend the hours when private waste collection is not allowed.

Currently, private collections (those not handled by the City's collection service) are banned between 11 p.m. and 7 a.m. in Ville-Marie, except in the commercial districts of the sociétés de développement commercial.
With the change, the borough council could, by ordinance, allow exceptions to these hours for a limited time and for a specific event.
The borough cites the Championnats du Monde Route UCI, scheduled to take place in Montréal from September 19 to 27, 2026, where traffic disruptions are expected.
Stated goal: keep collections going, limit the impacts on businesses and buildings, and reduce waste storage problems during the event.
Violations of this section remain punishable: type 3 for an individual, type 1 for a legal entity.
Steps: notice of motion on July 7, 2026, adoption expected on September 1, 2026, coming into force when the public notice is published in Le Devoir.

The borough of LaSalle is proposing to take on itself the design, coordination and carrying out of minor sidewalk repair work on streets of the City's arterial network located within its territory, in 2026.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is funding the work 100%; the budget allotted to LaSalle for 2026 is $240,000 net of rebate.
The borough points to the high number of citizen requests about the state of the sidewalks and cases of sidewalks considered dangerous, and is aiming for pedestrian mobility and safety.
The list of streets covered is in request RMT26_LAS submitted to the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier; it is not detailed in the document.
The offer must now be accepted by the city council; without that acceptance, the work would not go ahead under this arrangement.
The schedule entered in the file indicates: plans and specifications in February, call for tenders and awarding of the contract in April, work carried out in June (years written as 2025 in the file).
The borough of LaSalle is awarding 9211-4560 Québec Inc. (Émondage SBP) a two-year contract for tree pruning and tree removal, at a cost of $522,908.60, taxes included.
The work covers street trees as well as parks and green spaces, everywhere on LaSalle's public property.
The work includes full pruning, crown raising and clearing around structures.
The work starts as soon as the contract is awarded and continues until December 31, 2027.
The spending is split into $254,274.11 in 2026 and $268,634.49 in 2027, taxes included.
Seven companies submitted bids; three bids were found to be non-compliant. The lowest compliant bid is 39.6% below the borough's estimate ($865,821.95).
The borough of LaSalle is extending Lignes-Fit Inc.'s contract for street marking and line painting by one year, at a cost of $308,613.59, taxes included, for 2026.
This is the second and final option year of the contract awarded in 2024 following a public call for tenders.
The marking is done every year throughout the borough's territory.
The work is scheduled from May 15 to August 16, 2026.
The amount goes from $300,396.62 in 2025 to $308,613.59 in 2026, because of an adjustment provided for in the contract based on the consumer price index.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough of LaSalle is hiring Les Entreprises Ventec Inc. to build the microplace Newman, including electrical work, for $997,858.83 taxes included.
Adding $149,678.82 in contingencies and $172,462.50 in incidental costs, the total spending comes to $1,320,000.15 taxes included.
The microplace will include stopping and resting areas, furniture, exhibit panels, tree and perennial plantings, and lighting.
The work is to start in May 2026 and be finished in September 2026.
The project comes from the Budget participatif de Montréal (2nd edition), under the winning project "Micro-parcs et microplaces" chosen by citizen vote.
The $2,400,000 envelope given to LaSalle covers three microplaces: 2e Avenue (already awarded), Newman and Dollard (still to come).
Two of the four bids received were found to be compliant; the winning bid is 27.7% below the City's estimate.

The borough of LaSalle is changing who pays for what in the work on 6e Avenue, between boulevard LaSalle and boulevard Champlain, without changing the total cost of the $9,393,962.92 contract awarded to Eurovia Québec Construction inc.
The Direction de la gestion des actifs of the Service de l'eau is taking on an additional $1,645,963.30 (taxes included), and the borough of LaSalle is paying that same amount less.
The share paid by the Direction de la gestion des actifs therefore goes from 37% to 55% of the expense, and LaSalle's share goes from 45% to 28%.
This transfer covers the cost of the sidewalks and roadway located within the right-of-way of the water main work, which had not been included in the original funding from September 2025.
According to the document, this increase of $1,502,983.89 net is fully eligible for a grant under the TECQ program.

The work (a new 200 mm water main over about 1 km, roadway reconstruction, sidewalks, drainage curb extensions, a BIXI station, replacement of lead water service lines) is to take place from May 5 to September 30, 2026.
The net costs of replacing lead water service lines on private property will be billed to the residents concerned.
The borough of LaSalle is awarding COJALAC Inc. a contract worth $367,649.81 (taxes included) to rebuild sidewalks and curbs in the borough.
With contingencies ($73,529.96) and incidentals ($14,705.99), the total expense comes to $455,885.76.

The work covers, among others, boulevard Champlain between boulevards Bishop Power and Gérald, avenue Newman between avenue Irwin and rue Senkus, as well as local streets (safety improvements, driveway entrances, accessibility ramps).
At most 15% of the sidewalks on these streets will be rebuilt.
Work is scheduled from May 20 to October 15, 2026; local residents will receive a notice about the type, scope and duration of the work.
The cost is shared: $205,099.76 paid by the borough (local loan by-law) and $250,786.00 by the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier.
COJALAC Inc. was the lowest compliant bidder, 14% below the internal estimate of $426,404.22.

The borough of LaSalle is changing how the budget is divided for the work to bring the aréna Jacques-Lemaire up to standard and make it universally accessible, without changing the total expense of $1,349,994.07 (taxes included).
The amount set aside for contingencies (unforeseen costs) is going up by $91,980, while the amount for incidental expenses is going down by the same amount.
The contract stays with Les Constructions P.R.V. Inc., which was selected in June 2025 following call for tenders 863862.

Reason given: unforeseen site conditions required additional work, in particular conflicts under the slab, mechanical and electrical systems that differed from the plans, and deterioration that was not detected before the work began.
Contingencies therefore rise to 29% of the value of the overall contract.
The borough states that part of the incidental expenses budget will not be needed and that the funding comes from its own budgets, already provided for in the 2025-2034 investment program.

The borough of LaSalle is reorganizing the funding envelope of the professional services contract awarded to MDTP Atelier d'Architecture inc. for the universal accessibility work at the aréna Jacques-Lemaire.
Contingencies go from $33,572.70 to $48,174.53 (+$14,601.83), and incidental expenses go down by the same amount, to $15,398.17.
The total cost of the contract stays the same at $231,436.20, taxes included.
Reason: during the partial demolition of the ground floor, conflicts under the slab, mechanical and electrical systems different from the plans, and deteriorated elements were found.
These unforeseen problems required additional surveys, design and supervision work, as well as a 10-week extension of the construction site.
Contingencies reach 29% of the overall contract; the funding comes from the borough's building PTI budget.
The LaSalle borough is adding $547,283.06 (taxes included) to the contracts for renting graders and loaders with operators used for snow removal.
The total value of the contracts is going from $4,419,382.89 to $4,966,665.95 for the winters of 2023-2024, 2024-2025 and 2025-2026.

Reason: the contracts had been budgeted on the basis of 200 guaranteed hours per piece of equipment, while the bid form allowed for 275 hours; the hours actually worked in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 exceed the guaranteed hours.
Ten suppliers are affected, including Excavation Pascal Beaulieu ($166,035.03 more), 9037-4018 Québec (D.C. Barbeau) ($76,952.10) and Les Entreprises D.J. ($68,375.98).
A cushion of $10,000 is set aside for any billing corrections from the suppliers.
The expense will be paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough of LaSalle is approving two new parking spaces reserved for people with reduced mobility.
One space will be set up on rue Allion and another on rue Bédard.
The spaces will be reserved at all times and located as close as possible to the homes of the people who requested them.
The decision responds to requests from residents that were found eligible under the borough's procedure.
The signs will be installed as soon as the borough council gives its approval.
The costs are paid out of the operating budget of the Direction des travaux publics, with no amount specified.
The borough of LaSalle is lowering speed limits on several streets: from 40 to 30 km/h on certain local streets, and from 50 to 40 km/h on certain collector and arterial streets.
The new speed plan replaces the previous rules and becomes the reference for all streets in the borough.
The by-law is adopted on August 3, 2026 and comes into force on August 22, 2026.
Signs will be installed starting in August 2026, with signs announcing the date the change takes effect, followed by "Nouvelle vitesse" tab signs in certain places.
A communications campaign is planned for the summer of 2026; information sessions for residents have already been held.
The costs are covered by the operating budget of the Direction des travaux publics; no amount is specified.
The borough states that traffic calming measures will be needed on certain stretches to make sure the speed limits are respected.
The borough of LaSalle is adding a parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility on 76e Avenue.
The space will be located as close as possible to the home of the person who requested it, and will be reserved at all times.
The request was reviewed according to the borough's procedure, which finds the applicant eligible.
The road signs will be installed as soon as the borough council gives its approval.
The costs are paid out of the operating budget of the Direction des travaux publics; no amount is specified.
The borough of LaSalle is removing two parking spaces reserved for people with reduced mobility.
The spaces involved are located on rue Hébert and on rue Bédard (one each).
The removal follows requests received indicating that these spaces are no longer needed.
The signs will be removed at the borough's expense, which has a budget set aside for this.
The decision falls to the LaSalle borough council.

The borough of LaSalle is hiring RAMCOR construction Inc. to build about thirty new speed bumps on various streets, for a total expense of $294,314.85 (contract of $230,890.50, contingencies of $46,178.10, incidentals of $17,246.25).
The work covers the area bounded by the Verdun boundary, the canal de l'Aqueduc and boulevard LaSalle.
At the same time, the speed limit will drop from 40 to 30 km/h on certain local streets and from 50 to 40 km/h on certain collector and arterial streets.
The work is to begin on August 10, 2026 and be completed on October 10, 2026.
RAMCOR was the lowest of six bidders; its price is 51.5% below the City's estimate ($476,097.68).
Residents near the work sites will receive a notice about the type, scope and duration of the work.
The borough of LaSalle is hiring Groupe Centco inc. to replace and upgrade the water service entries of four municipal buildings.
Total spending of $177,256.96 including taxes: $131,301.45 for the contract, $26,260.29 in contingencies (20%) and $19,695.22 in incidental costs (15%).
Buildings involved: the mairie de LaSalle (55, avenue Dupras), the aréna Jacques-Lemaire (8681, boulevard Champlain), parc Lacharité (8702, rue Centrale) and parc Lefebvre (8600, rue Hardy).
The work includes replacing the water service entry components, bringing the plumbing up to standard and installing a backflow prevention device against water backups.
Part of the work will take place in areas where low-level asbestos has been detected; the contractor must apply the required health and safety measures.
Work is planned from August 10 to December 20, 2026.
Six companies submitted bids; Centco is the lowest, at 53.8% below the City's estimate. The project is funded by a borough loan by-law.
The borough of LaSalle is awarding Aménagements Sud-Ouest the contract to redevelop parc J.O.R.-Leduc, located between rue Giroux, rue Paquette and rue Béique.
The total spending comes to $817,239.80 including taxes: $619,121.06 for the contract, $123,824.21 in contingencies (20%) and $74,294.53 in incidental costs (12%).

The work includes a play area for children aged 18 months to 5 years, a water play feature accessible to everyone, new furniture (lounge chairs, benches), the repair of a pathway and the planting of trees.
Also included are the relocation of picnic tables and benches, the transplanting of one tree, the replacement of two floodlights and the moving of the electrical supply point.
The work is set to begin in August 2026 and be completed in June 2028.
Five companies submitted bids out of the 14 that picked up the documents; the winning bid is 2.6% above the City's estimate.
The borough may inform nearby residents and user groups by letter or news release.
The borough of LaSalle is adding two parking spaces reserved for people with reduced mobility: one on rue Pagé, one on rue Brown.
These spaces will be reserved at all times and located as close as possible to the homes of the people who requested them.
Residents had submitted requests; the borough reviewed the files and found the applicants eligible under its procedure.
The signs will be installed as soon as the borough council approves the measure.
The costs are paid out of the operating budget of the Direction des travaux publics; no amount is specified.
On March 10, 2026, the minister asked the Montréal urban agglomeration to review its land use planning and development plan; the by-law must be adopted by March 10, 2029 at the latest.
The City is officially notifying the minister and partner organizations (reconstituted municipalities, boroughs, MAMH, CMM) of its intention to review the plan.

The review must bring the plan into line with the new government land use planning directions (2024) and with the CMM's revised metropolitan plan (in effect December 11, 2025), particularly regarding density thresholds, mobility and housing.
The approved amendment extends by one year the $207,918 financial assistance agreement signed with the Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation; the amount stays the same.
New deadlines: progress report before February 15, 2027 and final expenditure report before February 15, 2028.
The schedule calls for a first draft plan in April 2027, a second in March 2028, public consultations from April to September 2028 and a targeted coming into force in 2029.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité is coordinating the work; the Commission sur le schéma d'aménagement will hold the public consultations.
The City is giving Dataglobe Canada inc. the contract for preventive maintenance and repairs of 43 uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems located in 24 municipal buildings.
The contract is worth $381,274.35, plus a contingency budget of $76,254.87 (20%), for a total expense of $457,529.22, taxes included.
The contract runs from May 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029 (35 months), with two possible 12-month extensions ($129,633.28 in 2029 and $132,225.94 in 2030).
These systems are used to keep the computer networks of the SPVM and the Service de sécurité incendie running during a power outage.
Only one of the three companies that picked up the tender documents submitted a bid; the price is 5.87% ($21,141) higher than the City's estimate.

The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles and is shared between the agglomeration (nearly 95%), the central city and the boroughs.

The City is extending its contracts with Baulne inc. by 12 months, from May 22, 2026 to May 21, 2027, for the maintenance of heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) systems in several municipal buildings.
Additional cost of $1,657,862.33 including taxes, made up of $1,381,551.95 for the services and $276,310.38 in contingencies (20%).
This brings the total value of the contracts to $8,667,920.97 including taxes.

The urban agglomeration is covering 55.47% of the expense, or $766,330.35, because the file involves public safety; the rest comes from the operating budget of the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles.
Prices are being indexed: 4.5% for preventive maintenance and 2.45% on the hourly rates for corrective work.
The supplier must remain available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, for any service call.
According to the file, refusing the extension would force the City to turn to one-time services at higher costs.
The City is hiring Baulne inc. to maintain and repair 85 industrial air compressors located in 60 municipal buildings.
Total spending of $442,566.11, taxes included: $368,805.09 for the two contracts and $73,761.02 in contingencies (20%).
Lot 1 covers buildings in the east of Montréal ($264,861.70) and lot 2 covers buildings in the west ($177,704.41), including fire stations and municipal workshops.
The contracts run for 35 months, from May 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029, with two one-year extension options.
The company must provide preventive maintenance, repairs and an emergency service 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Only one bidder came forward out of three companies that obtained the tender documents; the prices submitted are below the City's estimates (-13.87% for lot 1, -9.37% for lot 2).
The spending is paid 44.47% by the central city, 38.82% by the agglomeration and 16.71% by the borough.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is setting aside $71,688 for a pop-up library in the eastern part of Rosemont.
The money comes from two sources: $27,688 from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and $44,000 from a borough management surplus.
The project provides library resources at two service points in an area far from cultural centres, the eastern part of the Rosemont neighbourhood.
It also includes book-related French-language learning activities in daycares and schools.
The project is being carried out in-house by the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social, as part of the Prévention Montréal program.
The Prévention Montréal program is being extended for 2026 and projects must be completed no later than December 31, 2026.
The director of the Direction will be able to change the project's implementation guidelines, without exceeding the financial support granted.
City council is renewing the terms of two members of the Conseil jeunesse de Montréal: Kevin Martinez and Iles Ousmer.
Their second 3-year term starts in March 2026 and ends in March 2029.
Both have been members since March 2023; the by-law allows only one renewal, for a maximum of six years.
Kevin Martinez was vice-chair in 2024 and then chair in 2025; Iles Ousmer has been vice-chair since 2025 and was re-elected to that position in 2026.
The Conseil jeunesse has 15 members; these appointments maintain the number required for it to continue its activities.
The Ville de Montréal funds 100% of the Conseil jeunesse's operations.
City council takes note of the 2025 activity report of the Conseil jeunesse de Montréal, an advisory body that advises the City on issues affecting young people.
The report must be tabled at city council every year, under the by-law governing the City's three advisory councils.

Work done in 2025 included a consultation on young people's sense of safety in public spaces (a survey and focus groups) and the "Manifeste de la jeunesse montréalaise" published for the municipal elections.
The Conseil jeunesse also ran a recruitment campaign and activities to encourage young people to vote, in collaboration with the student squad of Élections Montréal.
The costs of the report were paid out of the Conseil jeunesse's operating budget; no additional money is being committed.
The report will be shared with partners, on the City's website and on social media.
City council takes note of a consultation report by the Conseil jeunesse de Montréal on how safe young people aged 12 to 30 feel in public spaces.
The consultation, carried out in 2025 with the firm Metalude, reached 509 survey respondents and 28 focus group participants, recruited in all 19 boroughs.
Its goal was to identify where young people feel safe, how they define that feeling, and which issues concern them in their borough.
The results will serve as the basis for an opinion the Conseil jeunesse will produce in 2026; the last opinion on safety dated from 2009.
The costs were paid out of the Conseil jeunesse's operating budget; no additional spending is being requested.
A public launch is planned for June 3, 2026 at Esplanade Tranquille; the report will then be posted on the Conseil jeunesse's website.
The borough of Ville-Marie is granting minor exemptions for the 12-unit residential building located at 2439-2443, rue Sainte-Catherine Est (east of rue Poupart).

First exemption: to legalize the building's siting, since it was built in 2005 with a clearance of about 0.47 m from the northwest side property line, whereas the minimum setback for the area has since increased to 2.5 m.
Second exemption: to allow the rear balconies and exit stairs to be rebuilt, with a maximum projection of 1.73 m instead of the 1.5 m maximum in the rear setback.
Third exemption: the northwest balcony will encroach about 0.73 m into the 1.2 m clearance required near the west side property line.
The original plans (2004 permit) were never filed in the City's archives; the current balconies reportedly do not match those that were approved and have no acquired rights.
According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, strictly applying the by-law would prevent the owners from replacing balconies that serve as the exits for the units.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 16, 2026; the decision is being made at the borough council meeting of May 5, 2026.
City council appoints 10 people to the board of directors of Anjou 80, a housing organization (public legal person) tied to the borough of Anjou.
Andrée Hénault becomes president and Francine Beauchamp secretary-treasurer, with terms until December 31, 2028, as do Michel Haddad and Gabriela Melendez.
Richard Leblanc, Edna Lénéus, Pierre Olivier Cyr and Josée Marquis are appointed as members until December 31, 2027.
Jennifer Poirier and Lucie Huard sit as borough representatives until December 31, 2027.
According to the document, the organization had not had a quorum for two years because of departures and the slowness of the appointment process.
The treasurer currently in place is unfit, which prevents the organization from paying its administrative and government obligations (Revenu Québec, etc.).
Board members sit on a volunteer basis; the file provides for no spending.
The borough of Anjou is cancelling the authorization granted in March 2023 for a 20-storey building at 7200, boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine, in downtown Anjou.
The land in question (18,950.3 m²) is bordered by boulevard des Roseraies, rue Saint-Zotique Est and boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine.
The original developer sold the property in 2025, and the new buyer submitted a modified version of the project.

On September 30, 2025, the borough adopted this new project (PH-79-003), which provides for the demolition of the building at 7151, boulevard des Roseraies and the construction of a residential building.
The former authorization is being repealed at the applicant's request, since the new project replaces it on the same land.
There is no financial aspect associated with this file.
The borough of Anjou is reappointing Josée Kenny as borough secretary, a position she has held since the regular officeholder's absence.
The regular borough secretary has been absent since December 2, 2025.
Cathlynn Marsan, secretary-researcher, becomes substitute borough secretary starting March 12, 2026.
The substitute will be able to replace the borough secretary in the event of illness, vacation or a major impediment, with the same powers and obligations.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.

The City is entering into a master agreement with Projet REM S.E.C. to allow the development of bike paths and active transportation links within the right-of-way of the Réseau express métropolitain, in the territory of the agglomeration of Montréal.

The agreement sets out the planning, design, construction, acceptance and operation of these sections: communication committees, roles and responsibilities, obligations and payment terms, including Projet REM's internal and management fees.

The sections covered will be used to complete the Véloroute de Deux-Montagnes and the Véloroute de l'Anse-à-l'Orme, continuous bike links connecting recreational and tourist areas and giving access to REM stations.
Announced schedule: feasibility studies by Projet REM S.E.C. in spring 2026, specific agreements from 2026 to 2028, start of work in the REM right-of-way in 2027.
The City Clerk, or his replacement, is authorized to sign the agreement.
According to the document, the decision has no impact on the City's budget framework, and the Véloroutes projects cannot move forward without this agreement.

The agglomeration City does not object to the work by Projet REM (CDPQ Infra), which wants to rebuild the bridge-tunnel under the Canadien Pacifique Kansas City tracks, between rue Jean-Talon Ouest and rue Wilderton, near the Canora station, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The bridge-tunnel passes over the REM and has reached the end of its useful life; a temporary detour of the railway tracks will be built to keep the trains running.
Rue Wilderton will be completely closed for a maximum of two weeks, during the 2027 summer holidays, at the CPKC level crossing at Jean-Talon Ouest.
The work is planned from June 2026 to March 2028, on lots 2 453 208 and 2 174 260, within rights-of-way closed to the public for most of the construction period.
The costs are covered by CDPQ Infra; no expense for the City is indicated.
The services consulted (bridges and tunnels, SPVM, fire department, water, civil security, Urgence Santé, the borough) raised no objection.
The City had 60 days to respond to the notice received on March 10, 2026; without the non-objections of all parties, the reconstruction could not go ahead.
City council is adopting a loan by-law of $140,000,000 to build new production greenhouses at the Jardin botanique de Montréal.

The current production greenhouses, more than 11,000 m² and about forty units, house the Jardin's living collections; audits in 2021 and 2022 found deterioration of the electrical and mechanical systems and the foundations, as well as risks related to the single glazing.
The City is going with new construction rather than restoration, which would not have solved the structural problems or the energy efficiency issues.

The money will cover the work, equipment, professional services and durable goods, spread out from 2026 to 2033: functional and technical plans in 2026, plans and specifications in 2028-2029, and work from 2030 to 2033.
The loan will be repaid over a maximum period of 20 years; the project is not receiving any grant for now.
The project aims for LEED certification, with energy recovery and alternative energy sources.
Next step: approval of the by-law by the Government of Québec in spring-summer 2026.
The City is entering into an agreement with the Section de Montréal d'Ikebana International to present the exhibition "Ode au printemps" at the Pavillon japonais of the Jardin botanique.
The exhibition is open to the public on May 2 and 3, 2026, with an opening reception on May 1 and takedown on May 3.
Twenty ikebana bouquets (Japanese floral art) will be on display, representing four different aesthetic schools.
No fee is paid to the organization: the exhibition is provided to the City free of charge.
The insurable value of the works is estimated at $3,400.
The organization supplies and installs the works together with the cultural officer of the Pavillon japonais, who may refuse a work considered at risk of damage.
Promotion will be done through the communication tools of Espace pour la vie.

The City is awarding Services d'infrastructures Vortex inc. a contract worth $12,093,300 (taxes included) to rehabilitate water pipes and streets in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. With contingencies ($1,209,330) and incidental costs ($322,241.64), the total spending comes to $13,624,871.64.
The work covers about 2.53 km of secondary water pipes rehabilitated by lining (without digging a trench), 37,751 m² of roadway and 2,062 m² of sidewalks.
About 115 lead water service lines will be replaced on the public side and 33 on the private side.
Three companies submitted bids; Vortex was the lowest compliant bidder, 1.46% above the City's estimate, and 10.36% below the second bid.
The contractor faces daily penalties for delays: from $1,000 to $3,500 per day depending on the street, plus $1,000 per day if the street is not cleaned within 48 hours.
The spending is paid entirely by the central city, and the City will assess the contractor's performance.
The City is asking Québec for access to a "transitional measure" for the 5e Avenue Nord dike, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, a structure about 950 metres long that protects several buildings.
This request would keep the current flood risk classification: about 110 buildings would remain in a low-risk zone, instead of being split into moderate (26), high (68) and very high (15) risk.
In a low-risk zone, the rules are less restrictive for building, enlarging or rebuilding homes.
Keeping the current classification would allow the borough to continue studying a project of 410 residential units and commercial spaces near the REM's Roxboro station.

The City is committing to carry out a performance study of the dike by March 1, 2028, with a preliminary specific plan before March 1, 2027 and a characterization of the structure before March 1, 2029.
The City states that it has no information suggesting that the dike would not meet the standards of the provincial by-law.
The studies will be entrusted to outside firms; the document does not put a figure on the costs. A communications effort is planned to inform the public.
The City is awarding Demix Construction (Groupe CRH Canada) a $7,401,306.04 contract for road work, for a total expense of $8,474,495.41, taxes included.
Added to the contract amount are $740,130.60 in contingencies and $333,058.77 in incidental expenses.
The work affects Le Sud-Ouest, Saint-Laurent, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Pierrefonds-Roxboro, L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Saint-Léonard.
The work involves milling and laying new asphalt over about 7.12 km, including about 3.38 km of bike path, with no work on sidewalks and no redevelopment.
The contract includes repaving the road surface of the A-40 westbound service road, on chemin de la Côte-de-Liesse between rue Stinson and rue Deslauriers.
The contractor will have to pay $6,437.32 (before taxes) for each day of delay if it goes beyond the maximum time allowed for each street; no bonus is provided for.
Demix Construction was the lowest of the 7 bidders, at 6.25% below the professionals' estimate; the expense will be paid 94.32% by the central city and 5.68% by the urban agglomeration.

City council is awarding Beameo Services-Conseils inc. a contract of $618,761.16 (taxes included) to replace street lighting fixtures; with contingencies ($92,814.18) and incidental costs ($61,876.11), the total spending comes to $773,451.45.

The work affects Saint-Laurent, Verdun, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension: one single site and five street segments (730 metres), plus the replacement of outdated or temporary fixtures at six sites.
The new light fixtures will be LED and the electrical wires will be buried; the City says the current lighting on the targeted segments is insufficient.
Road work is also included: 127 metres of concrete sidewalks and curbs rebuilt, lighting bases, conduits, restoration of the area behind the sidewalk with sod, and excavation.

Four companies submitted bids out of five that picked up the tender documents. Beameo is the lowest compliant bidder, 0.58% above the estimate; the bid from Néolect inc. was rejected because it lacked $2M in insurance per claim.
The contractor faces late penalties of at least $1,000 per day; no bonus is provided for. The City will assess its performance.

The spending is paid 100% by the central city, through two loan by-laws ($557,460.92 and $215,990.53). If the contract is not awarded before the bid's validity period expires, a new call for tenders would be needed.

The City is awarding Fer-Pal Construction ltd. a contract worth $11,879,611.25 (taxes included) to rehabilitate water mains and redo roadway work in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.
With contingencies ($1,187,961.12) and incidental costs ($304,606.79), the total spending comes to $13,372,179.16, paid entirely by the central city.
The work covers about 2.29 km of secondary water mains rehabilitated by lining (without trenches), 24,000 m² of roadway and about 1,450 m² of sidewalks.
About 178 lead water service lines will be replaced on the public side and 53 on the private side, under by-law 20-030.
Fer-Pal was the lower of the two bidders; its price is 1.25% ($146,896.91) above the professionals' estimate.
The contract provides for penalties of $500 to $3,500 per day of delay depending on the type of failure, and no bonus.
The City will assess the contractor's performance at the end of the contract.
City council is awarding Loiselle inc. a $2,044,999.99 contract (taxes included) to remove soil and materials piled up in the carrière Saint-Michel, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.

With contingencies ($409,000) and incidental costs ($362,171.25), the total expense comes to $2,816,171.24, paid entirely by the central city through the loan by-law for work related to the blue line.
This is phase 2 of the work: once the soil is removed, the STM will be able to deposit the rock excavated for the extension of the metro's blue line directly at the bottom of the quarry.
The work includes off-site management of contaminated soil, construction debris and non-hazardous residual materials.
Loiselle inc. was the lowest of the 5 bidders; its price is 51.87% below the City's estimate ($4,248,668.09).
The contractor will pay 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day; no bonus is provided for.
The City will assess the company's performance at the end of the contract; the bid is valid until May 25, 2026.

The City is awarding Services d'Infrastructures Vortex inc. a contract worth $16,368,999.99 (taxes included) to rehabilitate water pipes and streets; with contingencies and incidental costs, the total expense comes to $18,387,484.22.
The work affects various streets in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Saint-Léonard.
The plan includes about 3.89 km of water pipes rehabilitated by lining (without trenches), 44,370 m² of roadway resurfaced and 3,897 m² of sidewalks repaired.
About 443 lead water service lines will be replaced on the public portion and 94 on the private portion.
The contractor faces daily penalties for delays: up to $3,500 per day per street, and $1,000 per day if the street is not cleaned within 48 hours.
Three companies submitted bids out of six that obtained the tender documents; the bid from FER-PAL Construction was rejected for lack of sufficient insurance.
The winning bid is 11.06% below the professionals' estimate; the expense is paid by the central city.

The City is entering into a 4-year agreement with Groupe de Construction DePiedmont inc. for work to secure and repair bridges, tunnels, retaining walls and other road structures, up to $1,668,717.42, taxes included.
The work is done on request, on a case-by-case basis: removal of concrete fragments, shoring, repair of slabs, sidewalks, guardrails, drainage, laying asphalt on bridge decks, cleaning.
Stated purpose: to be able to act quickly when an inspection, a vehicle collision or a weather event compromises user safety or the functioning of a structure.
The agreement ends after 4 years or as soon as the funds are used up, whichever comes first; the City expects about $417,179.36 per year, adjustable according to needs.
DePiedmont is the lowest of the 4 bidders: $1,668,717.42 compared with $4,545,776.35 for the second, which is 44.58% below the internal estimate of $3,010,838.83.
The Section ponts et tunnels manages 588 road structures; the agreement replaces the one awarded in 2022 to Demix Construction.
The City will assess the contractor's performance; the expense is funded from the operating budget of the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier.
The City is awarding Pavages D'Amour inc. the contract for sewer, water main and roadwork on rue Lindsay, between rues Du Collège and Beaudet, in Saint-Laurent.
The total expense comes to $2,055,048.90, taxes included: $1,698,979.83 for the contract, $186,386.13 in contingencies and $169,682.94 in incidental costs.

The work provides for about 200 m of combined sewer and 225 m of water pipes to be rebuilt, the replacement of 4 lead water service lines on private property, the complete reconstruction of the roadway (± 1,970 m²) and the repair of the sidewalks (± 730 m²).
The street will be narrowed to 8.4 metres and the sidewalks widened to 1.8 metres, at the borough's request, for walking and pedestrian safety.
The sewer pipe, installed in 1949, was deemed a priority for replacement after inspections revealed breaks, deformations and fractures.
The bill is split 93.32% to the central city and 6.68% to the borough of Saint-Laurent.
The lowest of the 12 compliant bids is 20.83% below the professionals' estimate; the contractor will pay 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay (minimum $1,000/day).

The City is hiring Englobe Corp. to inspect (survey) the sidewalks along its arterial road network in 2026, for $607,503.18, plus $60,750.32 in contingencies, for a total of $668,253.50 including taxes.
The contract covers about 2,400 km of sidewalks across the 19 boroughs: photos every 5 metres, a record of deterioration and cross slopes, and georeferencing.
The data will be used to update the database on the condition of sidewalks and to plan repair investments.
The contract runs for 18 months, with the possibility of a 12-month extension if the budget is not used up. Penalties are provided for in the event of delays or failures to perform.
Two firms submitted bids out of nine that obtained the tender documents; the other bid was $908,296.06. The winning price is 29.24% higher than the City's estimate ($470,075.29).
A first call for tenders was cancelled in 2025 because of a large price gap (a bid of $1,025,870.19); subcontracting has since been allowed.
The cost is paid entirely by the central city, and the firm's performance will be evaluated.

City council agrees to let the 19 boroughs involved design, coordinate and carry out minor sidewalk repair work themselves on streets in the arterial road network, which normally falls under the central city.
The work planned for 2026 covers 10,982 m² of sidewalks in total, including Saint-Laurent (1,450 m²), Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve (1,172 m²) and Ville-Marie (785 m²).

The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is paying for all of the work, including plans and specifications, out of the Programme de maintien des infrastructures routières (Ten-Year Capital Works Program 2026-2035).
Estimated costs per borough range from $105,000 (Outremont) to $560,000 (Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve).
The sidewalks targeted must be spot repairs (10% to 15% of a section), with no street redevelopment planned in the next 5 years, and coordinated with the replacement of lead water service lines.
In Ville-Marie, the work includes sidewalks along the routes of the 2026 UCI Road World Championships, where milling and resurfacing is already planned.
Each borough must respect the budget and timeline submitted, obtain the required authorizations and report on progress upon request.

The City is awarding the work to repair the croix du Mont-Royal to Constructions Concreate ltée, for a total expenditure of $3,769,140.63 including taxes (a contract of $3,177,535.33, plus $476,630.30 in contingencies and $114,975 in incidental costs).

The work includes fully replacing the lighting system, reinforcing structural members, bringing the ladders, landings, grounding and electrical enclosure up to standard, and restoring deterrent panels. The monument's appearance is preserved.
The current lighting system is at the end of its life: the parts are no longer manufactured and the west side had to be turned off to save bulbs.
Only one bid was received out of 12 people who took out the tender documents. Its price exceeded the estimate by 42.68%; after negotiation, the gap was brought down to 37.3%.
The ministère de la Culture et des Communications is funding 50% of a maximum expenditure of $2,204,400, that is $1,102,200, through the Entente sur le développement culturel 2024-2027.
The expenditure is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration. Penalties apply if the contractor does not meet the schedule; no bonus is provided for.
The bid is valid until June 30, 2026; after that date, the contractor could withdraw it and a new call for tenders would be necessary.

The City is awarding Les Entreprises Cogenex inc. the reconstruction of the sewer, the water main, the roadway, the lighting and the traffic lights on avenue Wilson, between rue Sherbrooke and chemin de la Côte-Saint-Antoine (Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce).
Total cost of $2,011,374.62 including taxes: $1,673,994.61 for the contract, $169,889.59 in contingencies and $167,490.42 in incidental expenses.
The work includes 121 m of combined sewer, 132 m of water main, the replacement of 16 lead water service lines on the private side, about 1,143 m² of roadway and 613 m² of sidewalks rebuilt.
Also included are widened sidewalks with planted curb extensions, planting pits, 3 street lights, 4 traffic lights and a BIXI station.
The stoneware sewer dated from 1913 and the grey cast iron water main from 1920; their state of deterioration placed them among the replacement priorities.
Cogenex was the lowest of the 8 bidders, at 14.29% below the City's estimate; the contractor will pay 0.075% of the contract price per day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city; 1.10% of the total cost is charged to the citizens concerned for the private portion of the lead service lines.
The City is awarding Hydro-Québec, without a call for tenders because it is the only possible supplier, the electrical connection of 200 new on-street charging stations.
The maximum expense is $3,782,141.33, taxes included, paid entirely by the central city, 50% in 2027 and 50% in 2028.
