The stations will be installed at about a hundred sites spread across 19 boroughs, chosen together with the boroughs, the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité, Hydro-Québec and the Commission des services électriques de Montréal.
The connection work starts in January 2027 and must be finished by December 2028; Hydro-Québec will bill each site after the City accepts it.
Connection costs of $36,000 or less per site are accepted automatically; above that, the site is reviewed before being accepted or rejected.
The City explains the price increase by sites being farther from connection points, more overhead connections outside the central boroughs, and rising material and labour costs.
The funding comes from loan by-law 25-027 for the purchase and installation of charging stations.

City council authorizes the Ville to submit a project to the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation's Prix Mérite municipal 2026, in the "Municipalité et développement durable" category.
The project submitted: an electrical box designed by the Ville with Hydro-Québec, which can be connected to Hydro-Québec's overhead network or to the CSEM's underground network.
This box powers up to six charging stations, or five charging stations plus one self-service electric bike station, compared with four charging stations usually.
Connecting to the overhead network makes it possible to install charging stations in areas not served by the underground network.
The design of the box is not tied to any single supplier and can be reused by other municipalities; it has already been accepted by Hydro-Québec.
The application had to be submitted on February 19, 2026, with the nomination period ending on February 22, 2026.
No expense is associated with this file; no communications activities are planned.

The City is awarding Charex inc. a contract worth $10,311,940.25 (taxes included) to build a new street and its networks in the écoquartier Louvain, in Ahuntsic-Cartierville. With contingencies ($2,062,388.05) and incidental expenses ($2,992,007.70), the total expense comes to $15,366,336.

The work includes 610 metres of street (temporary paving and sidewalk), 380 m of storm and sanitary sewer, 420 m of water main, 366 m of lighting, and the extension of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal network.

Once this infrastructure is in place, all the lots in the écoquartier will be considered buildable. The final layout of the street (plantings, permanent sidewalks, raised crossings) will come after the private lots are built.

The contract includes the soil rehabilitation of the former gas station on the Louvain Est site; the City is adding $2,007,312.15 net to its infrastructure department through the environmental liability reserve for this work.

The écoquartier project aims to redevelop a 7.7-hectare city-owned site with roughly 1000 social and affordable housing units, public spaces, a food hub, shops, a school, a CPE (childcare centre) and a community centre.

Nine companies submitted bids; the winning offer is 23.44% below the professionals' estimate. The contractor will pay a penalty of 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day.
The agglomeration is covering 57.90% of the expense, or $8,893,268.33, taxes included.
City council authorizes the Ville to submit an application for the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation's Prix Mérite municipal 2026, in the "Relève municipale" category.
The application concerns the project "Modernisation et décarburation des pratiques du béton à la Ville", led by an engineer from the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier.
The document describes his work on the city's technical requirements for concrete, including the addition of requirements for low-carbon concrete in the Ville's standardized documents.
The application was submitted on February 19, 2026; the nomination period closed on February 22, 2026 at 4 p.m.
No spending is tied to this file and no communications activity is planned.
On February 16, 2026, the Ville had already authorized another application to the same program, for the Centre de traitement des matières organiques de Saint-Laurent.

The City is hiring Les Services EXP inc. ($1,313,359.43) and IGF axiom inc. ($934,163.25) to inspect and assess bridges, tunnels, footbridges, retaining walls and noise barriers, for a total expense of $2,247,522.68, taxes included.
The contracts run for 48 months, from June 2026 to May 2030, with two possible 12-month extensions if the money set aside is not used up.
The firms will carry out general and annual inspections, load-bearing capacity assessments and emergency investigations after an incident on the network.
The work covers the City's 588 road structures, spread across 19 boroughs; most were built before 1970.
The amount includes $1,741,632.68 in fees and $505,890 in expenses (signage, aerial lift rental, etc.); the professionals are paid at an hourly rate.
A third lot included in the call for tenders is not being awarded: the prices submitted were more than 20% above the City's estimate.
Six firms submitted bids out of twelve that had picked up the tender documents; the expense is paid entirely by the central city.
The City is moving $6,000,000 from the Service de l'eau to the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier, as part of the 2026 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The money will go toward replacing lead service lines (RESEP) and the related road work planned for 2026.
It will also fund non-integrated projects grouped together under road work, lead service lines and the correction of reversed sewer connections.
The transfer is split into $1,000,000 from the secondary water and sewer network program and $5,000,000 from the green infrastructure and climate resilience program.
Both amounts go to the complementary local milling and resurfacing program.
According to the document, the operation has no impact on the City's financial framework, since the funds were already included in the 2026-2035 budget.

The City is giving the boroughs of Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension responsibility for the design, coordination and completion of roadway and bike path work on streets that fall under the central city.

In Ville-Marie: milling and new roadway surfacing plus minor sidewalk repairs, including sections along the route of the UCI Road World Championships, held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026. Cost: $2,100,000 in 2026.

In Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension: repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between the west side of rue d'Iberville (entrance to parc Frédéric-Back) and boulevard Saint-Michel, for $570,000 in 2027.
Also in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension: repair of the REV Lajeunesse between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, namely $140,000 for the bike path and $80,000 for the sidewalks in 2026.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is paying for all of the work, including plans and specifications, out of its own capital budgets.
The boroughs must obtain the required authorizations, keep a master budget and schedule, record the expenses separately and not exceed the authorized funding.
Without this acceptance, the work could not be done, which would affect how the Championships unfold and the level of service of the REV Lajeunesse.
The City is awarding Orange Paysagement inc. the landscaping work on boulevard Henri-Bourassa, between boulevard Pitfield and avenue Félix-Leclerc, in Saint-Laurent.
Total expense of $496,209.68 including taxes: $416,289.98 for the contract, $62,443.50 in contingencies and $17,476.20 in incidental costs.
The plan includes: planting 431 trees (in the central mall and 233 pits in the median), 277 shrubs, 289 grasses and perennials, plus overseeding in the grassed areas.
The work is to start in September 2026 and finish in November 2026.
The contractor will pay a penalty of 0.1% of the contract price for each day of delay, with a minimum of $1,000 per day; no bonus is provided for.
Four of the seven companies that obtained the tender documents submitted bids; the lowest bid is 48% below the City's estimate.
These plantings complete the redevelopment of the street, whose civil work had been awarded in 2022; the expense is paid 100% by the central city.

The City is awarding Construction Viatek inc. a contract of $4,888,317.57 (taxes included) for milling and repaving work; with contingencies ($488,831.76) and incidentals ($171,091.11), the total spending comes to $5,548,240.44.

The work covers streets in the boroughs of Ville-Marie, Outremont, Lachine, LaSalle and Verdun, over about 6.042 km in total (± 5 km of PCPR and ± 1.042 km of PCPR+). The list of streets is attached to the file.

There is no work on the sidewalks and no improvement to the existing layout: the boroughs had received the list of streets in February 2025 so they could redo the sidewalk sections they considered critical themselves.
The contractor will have to pay $4,251.64 per day (before taxes) if it goes past the deadline set for a street, and $500 for each day of delay in rebuilding the speed bumps. No bonus is provided for.
Four companies submitted bids out of seven that picked up the tender documents; the winning bid is 23.03% below the internal estimate of $6,350,570.54.
Because the work is over $4M and the gap with the estimate is more than 20%, the file goes before the Commission permanente sur l'examen des contrats.
The spending is covered 100% by the central city, and the company's performance will be evaluated.
The City is entrusting the borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve with the design, coordination and carrying out of work on avenue Souligny, between rue Honoré-Beaugrand and rue Saint-Émile.
The work includes rehabilitating the roadway and, if needed, minor repairs to the sidewalks.
The document notes that the roadway on this stretch has severe cracking, numerous potholes and patching.

This stretch is part of the City's administrative arterial road network; the borough is acting here on behalf of the central city, which will cover all of the costs, including the plans and specifications.
The costs will be taken from the capital budgets of the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier (the planing and paving program and the road infrastructure maintenance program).
Announced schedule: design in spring 2026, work in the summer and fall of 2026.
The borough will have to obtain the required authorizations, have its plans approved if needed (Service de l'eau, SIM, STM) and report on progress and budget upon request.
The City is entrusting the borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce with the design and carrying out of roadway repair work on streets that normally fall under the central city.

Three sections are involved: avenue Gatineau (from chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges to avenue Maréchal), chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges (from avenue Gatineau to avenue Decelles) and rue Goyer (from chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges to avenue Decelles).
The work is meant to prepare the course for the 2026 UCI Road World Championships, held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier will pay for the work on the two sections of the course, estimated at $570,000 including taxes, out of the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The borough will fully fund the repair of rue Goyer, which is not on the course.
According to the preliminary schedule, the work would take place from July 20 to August 20, 2026.
Without this work, the document indicates risks to user safety, traffic flow and service to certain STM bus stops.
The borough of Lachine is paying $40,000 (taxes included) to the organization Opération culture et festivités de l'Ouest for two festivals in 2026.
The amount breaks down as follows: $25,000 for Dame Festive and $15,000 for the Festival de littérature jeunesse de Montréal.
Dame Festive will take place on May 30 and 31, 2026 on rue Notre-Dame, with three stages; the borough reports attendance of more than 5,000 visitors over two days.
The Festival de littérature jeunesse will be held on August 9, 2026 at parc Noël-Spinelli and is aimed at children aged 3 to 12.
Both events are free.
The council is also approving an agreement with the organization, covering the financial contribution, the loan of facilities and services, as well as communications support.

The executive committee authorizes the Service des technologies de l'information to move $1,999,000 between its own capital projects for 2026, without adding any new money (total unchanged at $15,306,000).
The money is taken from four projects: cybersecurity modernization (-$1,000,000), procurement (-$950,000), user services management (-$25,000) and the geomatics platform (-$24,000).
It is transferred to workstation renewal (+$1,344,000), business intelligence (+$500,000), the intranet portal overhaul (+$99,000) and telecom setup (+$56,000).
The Service explains that these changes follow the review of its spending forecasts: some projects are postponed, others moved up.
The replacement of the workstations concerned addresses the obsolescence of the City's computer equipment.
The Service des finances has certified that the funds are available; no communications activity is planned.
The City is moving $500,000 in 2026 from one IT project to another, without adding any new money to the capital budget of the Service des technologies de l'information.
The project for a new generic grant management system loses $500,000 (from $1,047,000 to $547,000) because its start-up has been postponed.
The digital overhaul of Espace pour la vie receives this $500,000 (from $700,000 to $1,200,000), since its schedule was moved up after a review of the roadmap.
The total for the two projects stays at $1,747,000 for 2026.
The Service des finances has certified the funds; the decision rests with the executive committee.
No communications activities are planned.
The City is moving $3,700,000 in 2026 between computer projects already planned in the Ten-Year Capital Works Program, without adding any new money.
Two projects are having their 2026 budget reduced: the property tax and property assessment system (-$3.4M) and the Approvisionnement III project (-$300,000), since their timelines have been revised.
Three projects are receiving the money: the upgrading of the workstation fleet (+$1,648,000), the work environment (+$1,324,000) and the financial, budget and procurement system (+$728,000).
Moving up the financial system aims to deploy the solution in December 2026; moving up the workstation fleet aims to replace outdated equipment at the planned pace.
The total 2026 budget for the projects involved stays at $34,093,000, and the funds have been certified by the Service des finances.
The decision falls to the executive committee; no communications activities are planned.

The City is filing its 2025 report on drinking water quality, covering 17 distribution networks supplied by the Atwater, Charles-J.-Des Baillets, Lachine, Dorval, Pointe-Claire and Pierrefonds plants, for 489 million cubic metres of water distributed.
All 17,800 bacteriological samples meet the standards; 36 cases of total coliforms, spread over 9 networks, were reported to the ministry.

Lead was the only parameter that exceeded the standard (0.005 mg/L): 40 exceedances out of 53 samples in the Montréal network, 41 out of 117 in Montréal-Est, 4 out of 21 in Lachine, and a few cases in Senneville, Dollard-des-Ormeaux, Montréal-Ouest and Pierrefonds-Roxboro.

The occupants and owners of the buildings sampled in Montréal, Lachine and Pierrefonds-Roxboro received a letter with their result; above 0.002 mg/L, they also received a pamphlet of advice, including on filtration.
The City has set itself the goal of replacing all lead water service lines by 2040.
Ten samples in eight networks showed disinfection by-products above the thresholds, but the annual averages stayed below the standard.
The report will be published on the City's website by March 31, 2026 at the latest.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a $183,960 contract (taxes included) to the firm Artelia to manage traffic, impacts and communications during its street redevelopment work sites.
The expense is paid out of the borough's unallocated surplus.

The work sites covered: rue Lanaudière (Saint-Grégoire to Laurier), avenue Des Érables (Marie-Anne Est to Rachel Est), rue Parthenais (Rachel Est to Sherbrooke Est) and its intersection with rue Gauthier, and speed bumps on rue Rivard (Marie-Anne to Rachel Est).
Sidewalk repairs are also planned, notably on de Lorimier (Saint-Joseph to Marie-Anne) and Saint-Joseph (Hutchison to Saint-Laurent).
The firm must patrol the work sites every day, approve signage, meet with affected residents and businesses, and handle traffic-related complaints.
The mandate is planned to start in mid-February 2026: monitoring from March to December 2026, then writing three mobility specifications for the 2027 work sites (November 2026 to April 2027).
The contract ends when the funds are used up or after 24 months, whichever comes first.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is amending its by-law on the use of public property for sidewalk cafés.
A new sidewalk café zone is being created on rue Prince-Arthur Est, between rue Saint-Dominique and rue Coloniale.
Two existing zones are being enlarged between rue De Bullion and avenue de l'Hôtel-de-Ville, at the request of businesses whose space needs have changed.
A last-minute adjustment moves zone E toward the water fountain and makes it smaller, so that the ledge in front of the fountain stays accessible to the public.
The borough says it has received complaints about the misuse of the current features (pergola, picnic tables, open space) and that it has trouble holding events there.
Two merchants already want to set up in the new zone; up to five applications would be possible.
The terraces bring in revenue for the City; moving the temporary features will be paid for by the borough. Adoption is expected at the June 2026 council meeting.
During the Championnats du monde de cyclisme sur route, from September 19 to 27, 2026, the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is suspending enforcement of the signs banning parking for street cleaning.
From September 19 to 22, the measure covers the area bounded by rues Hutchison, Saint-Joseph, Saint-Laurent, Rachel, Saint-Hubert, Sherbrooke, University, des Pins Ouest and avenue du Parc.
From September 23 to 27, the area is smaller: Hutchison, Saint-Joseph, Saint-Laurent, Sherbrooke, University, des Pins Ouest and avenue du Parc.
Organizers and participants will take up about 650 parking spaces around parc Jeanne-Mance, the start and finish site of the races.
Streets leading onto the race routes will become dead ends at certain times of the day; the areas affected match the streets filtered or closed by the SPVM.
The borough presents the measure as an easing of the rules for the affected local residents; no cost is tied to this decision.
The information will be shared through the press feed, social media, the newsletter and the borough's website.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is temporarily removing 8 paid parking spaces to install bike racks there, from April to December 2026.

The locations involved: rue Casgrain (5540), rue Clark at the corner of Bernard, boulevard Saint-Laurent (4627), avenue Duluth (116), avenue Laurier Ouest (152), avenue Fairmount Ouest (30) and rue Cartier (4488).
These locations will provide about 110 bike parking spaces, including 38 on avenue Duluth.
In total, the borough sets up more than 2,500 bike parking spaces in the summer, including 146 in paid parking spaces.
The revenue lost from the 8 spaces is estimated at about $16,000 for 2026, with no effect on the borough's revenues according to the document.
The racks are installed in April and removed before December 1 each year.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité and the Agence de mobilité durable gave a favourable opinion with no conditions.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is submitting two grant applications to the Fonds de la sécurité routière of the ministère des Transports for 2026-2027.
First project: redesigning the intersection of avenue du Parc and rue Bernard with a curb extension, at an eligible cost of $206,882 and requested funding of $165,506.
Second project: redesigning rue Saint-Urbain in front of the école primaire Bancroft with a curb extension and a widened sidewalk, at an eligible cost of $317,647 and requested funding of $254,117.
The two requested grants total $419,683; the program covers a maximum of 80% of eligible expenses, up to $380,000 per project.
The call for projects closes on August 31, 2026, and the work is planned for the summer of 2027.
The head of the Division des études techniques is authorized to sign the financial assistance agreement with the ministre des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The borough of Lachine is awarding COJALAC INC. the repair of sidewalks and curbs, under a contract worth $852,148.71, taxes included.
With contingencies ($85,214.87) and incidental costs ($50,000), the total expense comes to $987,363.58.
The work targets damaged sidewalk sections, repaved streets, citizen requests and driveway entrances, on arterial and local streets in Lachine.
Three lists of work are planned: the first after the spring thaw, the second from June 20 to July 22, 2026, the third from August 26 to September 27, 2026, for about 120 days of work.
The bill is shared between the borough (55.64%) and the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier of the central city (44.36%, or up to $438,052.15).
Ten companies submitted bids out of the thirteen that picked up the tender documents; the selected bid is 12.14% below the borough's estimate.
The City is awarding BEAMEO SERVICES-CONSEILS INC. the rebuilding of the sewer, water main and roadway on 25e Avenue, between rue Provost and 24e Avenue, in Lachine.
Total authorized spending of $5,483,052.96, taxes included: $4,507,002.57 for the contract, $676,050.39 in contingencies (15%) and $300,000 in incidental costs.

The work will take place between 2026 and 2027 and will replace 700 metres of water main and 590 metres of combined sewer (pipes installed in 1937), the catch basins, the manholes, the roadway, the sidewalks and the curbs.
Lead or non-compliant water service lines will be replaced; the net costs of work done on private property will be billed to the owners concerned.
Ten companies submitted bids out of 17 that obtained the tender documents; the selected bid is 22% below the professionals' estimate and 17% below the second-lowest bid.
A tax calculation error in BEAMEO's bid was corrected upward by $8,819.97, without changing the ranking of the bidders.
The central city is covering the spending, funded through a loan by-law, and will carry out a performance evaluation of the contractor.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is renting four vacuum sweepers and three tank trucks with operators to clean its streets and lanes in 2026 and 2027.
Balai Le Permanent inc. gets a contract worth $311,260.32 (four lots) and Déneigement & Excavation Michel Gauthier inc. a contract worth $263,660.67 (three lots), taxes included.
The total authorized spending is $574,920.99, taxes included, taken from the public works operating budget.
Operations start on April 1, 2026 (or earlier if the weather allows) and the contract ends on December 1, 2027, with an option to extend it by one year for 2028.
Cleaning is concentrated over about 5 weeks in the spring (removing abrasives) and 5 weeks in October and November (picking up leaves), with weekly passes in the summer.
The contracts come out of public call for tenders 25-21177, open from October 1 to 23, 2025; four companies submitted bids and the lowest compliant bidders were selected for each lot.
An information campaign for residents is planned to explain how the spring cleanup will work.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is hiring Les Équipements Benco Canada ltée to do the spring cleaning of sidewalks in four sectors, for $271,979.11 including taxes.

The work will start between March 15 and April 15, 2026 depending on the weather, will take place Monday to Friday from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., over about 6 weeks, and the contract ends no later than May 31, 2027.
The contract guarantees the cleaning of about 278 km of sidewalks per year; the borough's blue-collar workers handle the rest of the 446 km.
The contractor must provide ten machines in total: three per sector for MHM-110 and MHM-111, two per sector for MHM-112 and MHM-113.
Three companies submitted bids; Paysagistes Ramco inc. was set aside because its machines did not meet the technical criteria.
Two one-year extensions are possible, for the 2028 and 2029 seasons. An information campaign for residents is planned.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is extending its graffiti removal contract with 9181-5084 Québec inc. (Solutions-Graffiti/Solutions-Marquage) by 12 months, for $110,791.64 taxes included.
This brings the total value of the contract to $217,301.61, taxes included.
The work covers the borough's entire territory, on public and private property as well as street furniture, for up to 9,250 m² of graffiti removed.
Cleaning is done with biodegradable products, pressure machines or paint; the rate rises to $10.35/m², plus $156 per emergency call (maximum 4 per year).
Operations start around April 1, 2026 and the contract ends on March 31, 2027.
The borough states that it has cleaned more than 89,000 m² of graffiti since 2016 and will work with the Division de la voirie to determine which locations to treat first.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is ending the professional services contract awarded in June 2025 to the firm Cardin Julien inc. for the Rivière-des-Prairies aquatic centre, at 12515, boulevard Rodolphe-Forget.

This contract, worth $965,445.94 including taxes (authorized spending of $1,303,352.02), covered the design and supervision of work on a single changing room, the lifeguards' room, administrative rooms, a water play area, the filtration system, ventilation and exterior walls.

While analyzing the project, the professionals recommended work that was not included in the specifications: filtration and ceramic tiling for the pools and the deck, a full assessment of the building envelope (walls and roof), judged to be in very poor condition, and maintenance of the corroded metal frame.
The borough cites the law, which prohibits changing a contract awarded through a call for tenders when the change alters the nature of the contract.
The firm will be paid for services provided up to the termination date; the unused funds will go back to the accounts they came from.
The aquatic centre remains open, despite occasional closures, and a new call for tenders could be issued with the project's new parameters.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is hiring Lemay Michaud Architecture Design inc. to design and supervise the work to rebuild the bleachers at the Maison de la culture de Pointe-aux-Trembles, for $254,980.06 including taxes.

The total authorized spending is $382,470.08 (including taxes, contingencies of $38,247 and incidentals of $89,243.02), paid for by a borough loan by-law ($131,685.23) and the Service de la culture ($250,784.85).

The retractable bleachers installed in 1998, which became unstable and have been permanently fixed in place since reinforcement work in 2018, will be demolished along with the concrete section of the balcony and replaced by a concrete structure.

The work includes spots for people with reduced mobility, a barrier-free route, new seats, a resilient floor, anchor points for acrobats, storage under the bleachers, and upgrades to meet the 2020 National Building Code.
The hall currently has 226 seats: 50 in the balcony, 154 in the stands and 22 on the main floor.
Schedule: the construction contract is expected in September–October 2026, with the work finishing in June 2027; the Maison de la culture is not affected at this stage.

Five firms submitted bids; the one from Méta Architecture was rejected (it had not obtained the tender documents) and Atelier Urban Face was set aside with a score below 70%. The winning price is 18.6% lower than the internal estimate.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is applying to Québec for financial assistance to renovate the Rivière-des-Prairies aquatic centre, at 12515, boulevard Rodolphe-Forget.
The ministère de l'Éducation program can cover up to 66% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of $20M, if the work is completed in five years or less.
The planned work: bringing the pool filtration systems up to standard, redoing the ceramic tiling, a new ventilation system, and replacing the gas boilers with geothermal energy.
Also part of the program: redesigning the change rooms and work areas, repairing the building envelope, replacing the water play feature, and improving access to the pools for everyone.
The borough commits to paying its share of the costs, the operating expenses and any cost overruns, and to awarding no contract before the minister's announcement letter.
Thomas Rivard, director of Public Works, is designated to submit the application and sign the documents.
The application must be submitted no later than June 22, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.; only one project per borough is supported under this component.
The City is extending two engineering services agreements for parks and sports facilities by 12 months, at no additional cost: WSP Canada inc. (lot 1) and Les Services EXP inc. (lot 3).
The extension runs from May 1, 2026 to May 1, 2027; the agreements were set to end on May 1, 2026.
The purpose: to complete 12 ongoing assignments with WSP and 8 ongoing assignments with EXP, including construction site supervision and services during the warranty year.
The lot 2 agreement (SNC-Lavalin inc.) is not being extended.
The agreements cover assignments in civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, geotechnical, environmental and hydraulic engineering, as well as traffic, geology and surveying.
The necessary funds are already provided for in the agreements signed in April 2023, with a total value of $20,709,043.01, taxes included.
Both suppliers have accepted the renewal; the decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.

The City is adding $229,950 (taxes included) to the contract with Construction Savco inc. for restoration work on the maison Smith, in parc du Mont-Royal, bringing the total expense from $3,363,962.41 to $3,593,912.41.
A pipe break that occurred between January 26 and January 27, 2026 caused water damage from the 2nd floor down to the basement of the building; the contract's contingency budget was already 97% used.
The money will go toward demolition and decontamination of the 1st and 2nd floors (containment, removal of damaged surfaces, cleaning, drying) and to costs related to extending the work site.
Reconstruction work is expected afterward: floors, walls, ceilings, woodwork, painting, bistro light fixtures and stairs.
The restoration costs are not included in this request, because the parties are waiting for the response from the contractor's insurer.

The work site, which began on February 3, 2025, was supposed to be finished on February 3, 2026; provisional acceptance of the work is now expected in February 2027 and final acceptance in February 2028.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration, that is $209,975 net of rebates, through the parc du Mont-Royal redevelopment program.

The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the demolition of the building at 714-716 and 724, rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest, as well as the enlargement and residential occupancy of the building at 1253, avenue McGill College.
The project is granted exemptions from Ville-Marie's planning by-law regarding maximum height, maximum density and permitted uses.
The ground-floor spaces facing rue Cathcart, rue Sainte-Catherine and avenue McGill College may not be residential, except for a lobby.

Before obtaining its permits, the developer must provide two guarantees: $1,000,000 for the preservation of the building located on lot 1 340 451 and $600,000 for the demolition and construction conditions.
Work must begin within 60 months of the adoption, otherwise the authorization becomes void; it must also be completed within 60 months of the issuance of the permits.
The plans, produced by Lemay, will have to undergo a project review covering, among other things, the balconies on the Sainte-Catherine side, the residential entrance and the greening of the roofs.
This is the second draft resolution, adopted unanimously on April 14, 2026, following a public consultation held on March 25, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the construction of a residential tower at 1175, rue Mackay, a lot that has been vacant since the Desjardins Sea Food restaurant was demolished in 2017.
The project calls for 425 units, 34 storeys, a height of 110 m and 28,000 m² of floor space, with a business on the ground floor.
The building exceeds the height, density and side setback allowed by the planning by-law; the borough is granting exemptions to allow it.
The ground floor will include a restaurant with a café terrace, a residential forecourt and a work of art; vehicle access and loading will be from the south lane.
The plans will have to meet criteria on masonry, green roofs, outdoor spaces and the transition with the neighbouring building.
Work must begin within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The council adopted the first draft on April 14, 2026, held a public consultation on April 29, then adopted the second draft on May 5, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is amending an authorization already granted in 2023 for the "Projet Barsalou", at 1600, avenue De Lorimier: the plan is no longer to enlarge the building, but to build it.

The project will be allowed to depart from the neighbourhood's urban planning by-law with respect to maximum height, rooftop structures, the side setback, the definition of the ground floor, the density calculation and permitted uses.

Before obtaining its permit, the developer will have to submit a letter of guarantee of $376,544 to ensure the reconstruction of certain parts of the building: pilasters, window sills, cornice, appearance of the bricks and joints, and the main entrance on De Lorimier.
Part of the land must be transferred to the City, as shown in the attached plans.
The new criteria call for a simple, understated tower, a predominance of masonry, balcony guardrails with vertical bars only, and a carefully designed transition with the reconstructed building.

The landscaping must allow for the planting of large-canopy trees and recall the footprint of the former building; the mechanical equipment and the waste storage area must be barely visible from avenue De Lorimier and from the future extension of rue Logan.
At the public meeting of April 29, 2026 (about 9 people present), no one asked a question about this project; the urban planning advisory committee issued a favourable opinion.
The City is adding $3,988,366 to its budget, in both revenues and expenses, to continue its work on the Louis-Hippolyte-La Fontaine tunnel repair project until the work is completed.
This money comes from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec, which reimburses the City for the professional services of its employees assigned to the project.
The agreement signed in 2023 provides for a maximum reimbursement of $5,500,000: the City has already billed $1,511,634, leaving $3,988,366.
The reimbursed work includes coordinating municipal services, permits, sewer and water main work, and managing traffic light plans.

The ministère's project, estimated at close to $2B, affects municipal assets: a noise barrier, the redesign of intersections, a bike path and the areas around the Radisson and Honoré-Beaugrand metro stations.
Without this authorization, the City says it might not produce the reports needed to be reimbursed for the positions created for the project.
The City is awarding three contracts totalling $1,788,186.14 (taxes included) for signage, barricades and detour plans for the Championnats du Monde Route UCI Montréal 2026.

The contracts go to Entreprises Madali inc. ($674,308.68, lots 1 to 3, 5 to 7 and 10-11), Échafauds Plus (Laval) inc. ($17,590.83, lot 12) and Entreprise de signalisation SEDGE ltée ($1,096,286.63, lots 13 to 15).
The work runs from about September 5 to October 4, 2026: setup, holding of the event and takedown. No renewal is planned.
The equipment will be used to secure the start and finish sites and the fan village, and to manage street closures and detours.
The event takes place on Montréal territory from September 19 to 27, 2026.

Of the 12 companies that obtained the tender documents, 3 submitted bids. Two lots came in above the City's estimate (19.42% and 22.35%), which is attributed to additional labour needs; lot 12 costs 29.82% less than expected.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
The City is awarding the security services for the Championnats du Monde Route UCI Montréal 2026 to Groupe de sécurité Garda s.e.n.c., for $880,543.17 including taxes.
The contract covers roughly September 5 to October 4, 2026: preparation, the event itself and wind-down. No renewal is planned.
Guards and supervisors will watch over the start and finish sites of the races and the fan village during street closures, in addition to SPVM police officers.
The event takes place in Montréal from September 19 to 27, 2026; the expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
Garda submitted the lowest compliant bid for both lots: $528,377.50 (lot 1) and $352,165.67 (lot 2), which is 10.34% below the City's latest estimate.
Of the 12 companies that obtained the tender documents, 4 submitted a compliant bid; some said they did not have enough staff or equipment.

The City is awarding a $489,839.49 contract (taxes included) to Electro Performance G.L. inc. to design and manage a temporary electrical network during the Championnats du Monde Route UCI Montréal 2026.
The contract covers the power supply for the start and finish sites of the races and for the fan village, including generators, staff and emergency service during the event.
The work runs from about September 5 to October 4, 2026 (set-up, event, take-down). The contract cannot be renewed.
The Championships take place from September 19 to 27, 2026 in Montréal; the Grand Prix Cycliste de Montréal, on September 13, 2026, uses one of the same routes.

Only one company submitted a bid out of three that picked up the tender documents; the others said they did not have enough equipment or staff. The price is 11.62% lower than the City's latest estimate ($554,251.93).
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, under the program supporting sports elite and major sporting events.
The City is awarding Sunbelt Rentals of Canada inc. a $372,608.99 contract (taxes included) to install and set up barricades for the Championnats du Monde Route UCI Montréal 2026.
The contract covers roughly September 5 to October 4, 2026: setup, the event itself (September 19 to 27) and takedown. No renewal is planned.
The barricades will be used to secure the start and finish sites and the fan village, and to manage traffic during street closures.
Two companies submitted bids. Sunbelt's was the lowest: the other bid came to $1,178,857.07, notably because it included buying the barricades.
The selected price is $93,774.78 (33.63%) above the City's estimate, since the company has to bring back equipment spread out elsewhere in Canada.
The agglomeration is covering the entire expense, which is $340,241.67 net of rebate, through the program supporting major sporting events.
These three lots had received no bids in an earlier call for tenders; the specifications were relaxed as to the types of barricades accepted.
The borough of Verdun is approving a minor exemption for the house at 1043, 3e Avenue: a lightweight board-and-batten siding may be installed on the front facade.
The zoning by-law normally allows only clay brick, cut stone, architectural block or reconstituted stone on exterior walls.
The owners want to replace the siding installed in 1961, which has reached the end of its life, with a similar material ("HardiePanel" panel, Navajo beige colour).
The City cites consistency with the building's style (Swiss chalet) and the absence of any effect on neighbours, safety, health or the environment.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable recommendation on the request on February 10, 2026; public notice on February 20, borough council on March 10, 2026.
The material already complies on the other facades; the exemption applies only to the front facade.
The borough of Verdun is authorizing the conversion of the triplex at 1018-1022, rue de l'Église into a duplex, meaning the loss of one unit.
The owner wants to merge units 1020 and 1022 to create a larger unit for her family; her daughter and her partner want to acquire shares in the building.
The work will be done inside only: opening up the stairwell, removing one kitchen (plumbing kept inside the walls), new bedrooms and an office.
Condition imposed: keep the 2 exterior entrance doors of the units on the front facade, on the 2nd floor; balconies and exterior accesses are kept.
The tenants on the 2nd floor have reached an amicable agreement to leave the unit by March 2029.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme was unanimously in favour on April 14, 2026; the decision goes to the borough council on May 5, 2026.
Verdun is approving the conversion of the duplex at 3852-3854, rue Gertrude into a single-family home, which removes one rental unit.
The zoning by-law normally forbids reducing the number of dwelling units; the council is using the by-law on conditional uses to make an exception.
The owners, who live in the upper unit with their child, want more space for a second child and for working from home.
The two units would be connected by an indoor staircase, with four bedrooms in total, one of them set up as an office.
The authorization requires keeping the door, balcony and outdoor staircase on the upper floor, at the front of the building.
The tenant of 3854 signed a repossession notice in December 2025, received two months of free rent (March and April 2026) and had her moving costs paid; she left on May 1, 2026.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme was unanimously in favour on April 28, 2026; the borough council decision comes on June 2, 2026.
The borough of Verdun is authorizing the conversion of the duplex at 3605-3607, rue Gertrude into a single-family home.
The zoning by-law normally prohibits reducing the number of housing units in a building; the City is granting an exception here through conditional uses.
The owners live in the ground-floor unit; the tenants on the upper floor are leaving the country for Europe as of July 15, 2026, and the owners are paying the rent from June until they leave.

The authorization comes with three conditions: keeping the upper floor's outside access door, balcony and staircase at the front of the building, so that it can be turned back into a duplex if needed.
The planned work includes replacing the deteriorated balconies and adding an interior staircase connecting the two levels.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on May 12, 2026; the decision is being made at the borough council meeting of June 2, 2026.
The borough of Verdun would allow the restaurant at 4300, boulevard LaSalle to build a second drive-through lane and install a second menu board.
Current zoning prohibits drive-through service and limits the site to a single menu board; the minor exemption would set aside these two rules.
The project aims to fix the backup of the lineup, which sometimes spills onto boulevard LaSalle during rush hour.
Work planned for the summer of 2026 will temporarily close boulevard LaSalle, where one of the entrances to the site is located.
The new layout would remove about ten parking spaces and add trees and plantings, particularly in the former drive-through lane.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme (April 28, 2026) and the Direction du développement du territoire recommend approving the request.
Next steps: public notice on May 15, 2026, and a borough council decision on June 2, 2026.
The City wants to borrow $29,000,000 to develop the public spaces of the future Quartier Namur-Hippodrome, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The money will go toward soil rehabilitation, sewers and the water supply system, street redevelopment, professional fees and land purchases.
These infrastructures are meant to serve the first lots of phase 1 on the hippodrome site, intended for social, community and affordable housing.
Land will be acquired in particular to redevelop rue Jean-Talon Ouest and rebuild the entrance to the hippodrome site.
Ottawa granted a subsidy of $128.3M (including $68.2M for secondary infrastructures), on the condition that the work be completed by 2031.
The loan financing cannot exceed 20 years; the funds cover the work planned from 2026 to 2028.
Planned schedule: notice of motion on May 11, 2026, adoption on June 15, 2026, then approval by the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.
The City wants to borrow $12,000,000 to fund the construction of main water supply pipes in the Namur-De la Savane area.
The pipes will run from boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, to rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The loan covers plans and specifications, soil studies, surveying, decontamination, land acquisitions and a first set of works.
The total budget for all of the main pipes is estimated at $150.2M; the loan will be repaid over a maximum of 20 years.
Ottawa has approved a grant of up to $128.3M (including $60.1M for these pipes), on the condition that the infrastructure be completed by 2031.
According to the City, these works will ensure the water supply and fire protection of an area that could accommodate close to 40,000 new housing units.
Planned schedule: notice of motion on May 19, 2026, adoption on June 18, 2026, then approval by the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is adding 27 paid parking spaces: 9 on avenue Atwater (between Workman and Notre-Dame Ouest), 4 on rue Ann (between Wellington and Smith) and 14 on rue Smith (between du Shannon and Peel).
One paid space is being removed on Notre-Dame Ouest, between Charlevoix and Vinet, to enlarge and make safer a drop-off and delivery zone in front of the Théâtre Beanfield.
The stated goal: increase the supply of short-term parking to make it easier to reach businesses and establishments.
The Agence de mobilité durable estimates net revenues for the borough in 2027 at about $5,000 (Atwater), $3,000 (Ann) and $10,000 (Smith), if the spaces are installed in 2026.
The Agence de mobilité durable pays for all of the sign panels; removing the space on Notre-Dame Ouest does not cause any loss of revenue for the borough.
Next steps: notify the Agence de mobilité durable and send the work orders to the Division de l'entretien, de l'éclairage et de la signalisation. All other signage remains in effect.
The City is paying $46,755.31 (net of taxes) to the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, from its environmental liability reserve, to pay for environmental studies.
These studies will be used to put a price on the cost of decontaminating and rehabilitating the soil of the future Alma and du Carmel pedestrian lanes, in the Saint-Viateur Est area.
The lanes will connect rue Alma between Maguire and allée Saint-Viateur, and avenue du Carmel between the future allée Alma and avenue Henri-Julien, for active transportation.
Earlier studies (2016 and 2017) found contamination above criterion "C" of the Guide d'intervention, as well as layers of residual materials.
The contract goes to the firm Groupe ABS inc. ($46,548.33 taxes included), with $4,654.83 in contingencies; the expense is covered 100% by the central city.
Expected schedule: studies in spring-summer 2026, plans and specifications in fall-winter 2026, call for tenders in spring 2027, start of work in summer 2028.
The borough will have to report on its spending every quarter to the Service de l'environnement.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding 9190-8673 Québec inc. - Les entreprises Roseneige a contract of $302,955.91, taxes included, to redevelop parc Denise-Morelle, at 4394, rue Rivard.
The total authorized spending comes to $333,251.50, taxes included, including $30,295.60 in contingencies (10% of the contract).
The work covers about 523 m²: demolition of the existing play area and paths, a new play area for children aged 2 to 5, an accessible concrete path, and repairs to the fences and grassed areas.

New furnishings planned: two benches, one picnic table, one waste bin and one drinking fountain, plus two defined entrances on the rue Rivard side and an upgrade to the lighting of the existing street lamp.
The work is to begin in early August 2026 and be completed in November 2026.
The project is paid for by Montréal's participatory budget (2nd edition), which granted $612,000, taxes included, to the borough for this park.
The public call for tenders was held from April 22 to May 26, 2026: 7 bids were received, and the 4 lowest were analyzed and found compliant; the winning bid is 12% above the $270,000 estimate.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is paying an additional $8,710.37 (taxes included) to Provencher ROY + Associés architectes for the plans, specifications and construction site supervision for the redevelopment of parc Denise-Morelle, at 4394 rue Rivard.
The total paid to this firm for the project thus rises to $121,326.04, contingencies and taxes included.

The expense is due to an electrical junction box found under the sand of the play area, which did not appear on the plans: it supplies the park's only streetlight and must be moved, which requires new plans and an electrical consultant.
The amount also covers a 2.63% indexation of the hourly rates applied since February 2026 and $5,000 to replenish the contract's contingencies.
The park's redevelopment, funded by $612,000 from Montréal's participatory budget (2nd edition), is to start construction in the summer of 2026 and be completed in the fall of 2026.
The call for tenders for the work (DDTET54-26-07) is to lead to the awarding of a contract in July 2026.
The borough of Outremont is accepting a $49,500 contribution from the organization Sport et loisir de l'île de Montréal (SLIM) for 2026.
The money will be used to create a free sports equipment lending centre in the borough, under the Circonflexe banner (a program of the ministère de l'Éducation).
The project includes self-serve smart lockers, a lending counter at parc Beaubien, and introductory skating and sports activities in the parks.
The grant covers the renovation of rooms in the parc Beaubien chalet, the purchase of equipment to be lent out, and communication tools; taxes are paid out of the borough's budget.
The program targets in particular people in vulnerable situations, who face more barriers to taking part in sports.
The payment must be made within 30 days of the agreement being signed; a final activity report will be produced.
A second file will be presented on April 9 to have the City's 2026 budget amended to reflect this amount.
The borough of Outremont is paying back $60,160 to the federal government: this is unspent money from the "Communautés de ruelles" project.
The project, funded by Patrimoine canadien, ended on March 31, 2025. Some planned initiatives could not be carried out because of operational constraints.
Ottawa had paid out $490,000 in total: $340,000 over two years, plus a top-up of $150,000 approved in 2024.
The amount to be repaid is taken from the borough's surplus.
The agreement provides for compound interest (Bank of Canada rate plus 3%) if the bill is not paid within 30 days.
According to the document, not repaying the money could prevent the borough from receiving other federal grants.
The borough of Outremont confirms its interest in taking part in the Circonflexe — Prêt-pour-bouger program, with the organization Equip Sport.
Connected sports equipment lending stations would be installed in parks and possibly in certain municipal facilities in the borough.
Residents could borrow sports equipment free of charge using a mobile app.
The project costs nothing to the borough or to users: installation, maintenance and technology management are covered by the partners, thanks to funding from the Fondation Bon Départ.
The council authorizes the receipt of the material contribution from Equip Sport and the signing of an agreement by the borough secretary, if the organization accepts the request.
The agreement would last one year, with a rollout planned for the beginning of summer 2026 and an evaluation at the end of the period before any renewal.
The City is awarding the company Le Groupe St-Lambert the renovation work for the bibliothèque Père-Ambroise, at 2093, rue de la Visitation, for $749,684.14 including taxes.
With contingencies ($149,936.82) and incidental costs ($224,905.24), the total expense comes to $1,124,526.20.

The work is preparing for the arrival of self-service borrowing and RFID technology: automated sorting of returns, new furniture, redesign of the reception area and of the children's and adult reading areas, new floors, ceilings and LED lighting.
The library will move to a service location during the work.
Work is to begin in May 2026 and finish in February 2028.
The ministère de la Culture et des Communications is providing a grant of $410,736.92; the remaining $616,105.39 is to be paid by the City, financed through a loan.
Seven of the twelve companies that obtained the tender documents submitted bids; the winning bid is 9.46% below the professionals' estimate.
Montréal-Nord is entrusting the road marking of its streets for 2026 to the specialized team of the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough, for $451,000.
The bill is paid out of the operating budget ($370,000) and the borough's surpluses ($81,000).
The work is expected to begin around April 15, 2026 and end around October 15, 2026, depending on the weather.
Last year, the same service cost the borough $389,087.
Without this agreement, Montréal-Nord would have to call on private companies to maintain its road markings.
The borough of Montréal-Nord approves the final expense report confirming the completion of the redevelopment work on rue Lapierre, between rue Pascal and boulevard Maurice-Duplessis.
The work is finished and the documents (certificate of completion of work, progress report as of March 31, 2026, accountability report) have been sent to the ministère des Transports.
In 2021, the project received financial assistance from the Québec program supporting the development of active transportation in urban areas (TAPU).
The total assistance comes to $250,000: $200,000 already paid when the project was authorized, and a remaining balance of $50,000 payable after the ministère accepts the report.
Borough secretary Marc-Aurèle Aplogan is authorized to complete the standard resolution that accompanies the report on the work.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $87,472 to two organizations for youth projects from May 5 to December 31, 2026.
Jeunesse Loyola receives $60,952 for "Ça bouge avec Jeunesse Loyola": an on-the-ground presence and supervised activities to reduce risky behaviour in the neighbourhood's public spaces.
Le Relais Côte-des-Neiges receives $26,520 for a pre-teen group focused on self-confidence, speaking up and a sense of belonging, with particular attention to girls.
The money comes from the Prévention Montréal program (Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, $17,259) and from the ministère de la Sécurité publique ($9,261 and $60,952).

The projects respond to the recommendations of the Diagnostic local de sécurité chez les jeunes carried out in 2023: activities for girls, positive use of parks in the summer, and connections with the neighbourhood police stations.
The organizations must follow a visibility protocol and sign an agreement with the borough.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing the creation of two dwellings in the basement of the building at 2335, rue de Bordeaux, between rue de Rouen and rue Sherbrooke Est.
The two dwellings will each have two bedrooms; until now the basement was not habitable.
The owner must meet three conditions: a permeable surface for the paths to the backyard stairs, a watertight access door with glazing for the dwelling facing the yard, and a maximum of two dwellings.
The work calls for two rear windows to be turned into doors, two stairways in the backyard, and drains connected to a sump pump that discharges water toward the rain gardens.
The two planting areas in the backyard will each go from 9.7 m² to 7.5 m².
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with a condition on February 12, 2026; the building is not in a flood-basin area.
A public notice and a sign posted on the site will announce the borough council meeting at which the application will be considered.
The Ville-Marie borough council is authorizing a "performance hall" use on the 2nd floor of the building at 1208, rue Crescent.
The authorization departs from the planning rules that govern the location of a performance hall next to a dwelling.

The developer will have to provide an acoustic study describing the measures to prevent any noise and vibration impact on the neighbouring dwellings on the 2nd and 3rd floors of 1200-1202, rue Crescent.
It will also have to file an application for a transformation permit that includes the work set out in the acoustic study.
The application for an occupancy certificate must be filed within a maximum of 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

This second draft resolution, adopted unanimously on April 14, 2026, adds the 3rd-floor dwelling at 1200, rue Crescent to the neighbouring dwellings covered, following the public consultation of March 25, 2026.

The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing, for the Molson site, the addition of floors beyond the density and extra height normally permitted, according to the plans stamped December 2, 2024 or February 27, 2026.
The developer will have to hand over three parcels of land to the City free of charge for use as a public park, at the time of the permit application for block L3.

The developer will also have to hand over to the City, free of charge, a "base building" of at least 6,500 m² in block B (rues Montcalm and Notre-Dame) for a community facility including at least one double gymnasium.
A free and perpetual right-of-way easement will have to connect rue Montcalm to rue De la Visitation, or De la Visitation to Panet.
In block K, no building or fence is allowed within a 40 m strip along avenue Papineau, and a public green space will showcase the Accommodation plaque.
The permit application for phase 1 of block E must be filed within 12 months of the adoption; any new extra-height tower requires a wind impact study.

Other conditions: maximum lot coverage of 61% (block B), 60% (block C) and 55% (block K), tower heights cascading down from the Molson clock tower, green roofs and universal accessibility of public spaces.
The borough of Ville-Marie is granting a minor exemption to change the shape of the building in phase 2 of the Le George project, at 1001, rue Lucien-L'Allier, on the rue de la Montagne side.
The floors of the 26-storey tower (73 m) will grow from about 500 m² to 630 m²: 1.6 m more in the south setback, 0.50 m to the north and 2 m at the rear.
The number of affordable housing units goes from 227 to 216, but two-bedroom units climb from 38 to 77 and average areas increase.
The shared terrace on the 5th level shrinks from 67.6 m² to 52 m²; the tower ends up 18.5 m from the neighbouring tower (the Solstice) and 16.9 m from the phase 1 tower.
Condition imposed: the side setbacks and the distance between the phase 1 and phase 2 towers must substantially comply with the ACDF Architecture plan stamped May 22, 2026.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with conditions on May 7, 2026; adoption is planned at the borough council meeting of June 9, 2026.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The borough of Ville-Marie is starting the process to authorize converting the 4th-floor dwelling at 443, rue Saint-Vincent (Vieux-Montréal) to "hotel" use.
The owner, the Maison Saint-Vincent establishment, wants to set up four suites there; it has already occupied the 2nd and 3rd floors (10 rooms) since 2017.
The decision departs from the planning by-law, which bans replacing more than 20% of a building's dwellings with a hotel in this area.
An application for an occupancy certificate will have to be filed within a maximum of 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
No exterior work is planned; the building, built in 1870, is in the declared heritage site of Montréal, with no heritage authorization required.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on May 7, 2026; the council adopted the first draft resolution on June 9, 2026, unanimously.
A public consultation meeting will follow, along with a procedure allowing a referendum to be requested, because the exemption concerns land uses.

The Ville-Marie borough is adding $356,273.69 (taxes included) to the professional services contract for the roof repair and the upgrading of water management to standards at the centre Jean-Claude-Malépart, at 2633, rue Ontario Est.
This amount is divided into $260,848.81 for professional services and $95,424.88 in contingencies.
The total contract therefore rises to $666,759.04, including taxes, contingencies and incidental expenses.
The work is entrusted to the firms Riopel Dion St-Martin inc. (architecture) and GBI Experts-Conseils inc. (engineering), which are already tied to the City through a framework agreement.
Payments are planned at 97% in 2026 and 3% in 2027; the Division des ressources financières confirms that the funds are available.
According to the analysis grid in the file, the project does not contribute to the priorities of the Montréal 2030 plan in its current form.

The borough of Ville-Marie is entrusting the Service de l'Espace pour la vie, des grands parcs et du Mont-Royal with the design and supervision of the work to replace the synthetic turf at parc Rutherford.
The borough is authorizing spending of $246,777.74, taxes included: $200,787.74 for central service labour and $45,990 for possible outside contracts.
Parc Rutherford is located at the foot of mont Royal, south of avenue des Pins, between rue McTavish and avenue du Docteur-Penfield, above the McTavish water station.
The planned work: remove the old surface, clean the drains, correct ground deformations and install new synthetic turf.
Announced schedule: design in the summer of 2026, call for tenders in October 2026, contract award in February 2027 and work in May and June 2027.
According to the file, the 2027 window is explained by the upgrade work on the McTavish station planned from 2025 to 2033; a postponement would push the opportunity back to 2034.
The borough will handle work site communications, dealings with Université McGill and the steps for the PAFIRSPA grant.
The borough of Lachine is paying for four registration tickets, for an estimated expense of $160, including taxes and fees.
These tickets allow Mayor Julie-Pascale Provost, city councillor Dominic Roussel and borough councillors Nancy Berthelot and Ludovic Fermely to take part in the Défi de l'ours polaire.
The event takes place on February 21, 2026 at the parc riverain de Lachine, at 1800, chemin des Iroquois.
The borough can either buy the tickets directly or reimburse the elected officials who paid themselves, with supporting documents.
Other elected officials can replace the people named, without exceeding the number of tickets or the authorized amount.
The activity, a jump into icy water, raises funds for Olympiques spéciaux Québec, organized with the SPVM; the donations go to sports, health and inclusion programs for more than 4,200 athletes.
The borough of Lachine is giving $5,000, taxes included, to the Fondation de l'Hôpital de Lachine.
The money is used to buy a corporate table for ten guests at the Fondation's annual fundraising gala.
The gala will take place on April 17, 2026.
The borough presents this type of contribution as a way to support neighbourhood life and citizen participation.
The decision falls to the Lachine borough council.
The borough of Lachine is giving $900 to the Jardins communautaires de Lachine.
The money will be used to buy materials to repair the gardens.
The decision falls to the Lachine borough council, which is recording it among its contributions to neighbourhood organizations.
The funds were certified by the Direction des services administratifs et des projets urbains de Lachine.

The borough of Lachine is reimbursing $273.64, taxes included, for two elected officials' attendance at a lunch conference of the Chambre de commerce de Montréal Centre Sud Ouest, held on March 20, 2026.
The ticket cost $119 per person, plus taxes; the reimbursement is made upon submission of supporting documents.
Borough mayor Julie-Pascale Provost did not need prior authorization, since she was acting in the exercise of her duties.
For city councillor Dominic Roussel, prior authorization had not been obtained before the event: the council is ratifying the expense after the fact, on an exceptional basis.
The council points out that any attendance by a council member at this type of event must normally be authorized in advance.
The lunch conference was about the industrial development of the Grand Sud-Ouest of Montréal (the Bridge-Bonaventure, LaSalle-Ouest, Lachine-Est and Canal de Lachine 4.0 projects).
The borough of Lachine is giving $1,100 in financial contributions to two organizations.

Le Club de patinage artistique de Lachine receives $500 for a one-page ad in the program of its annual ice show on April 25 and 26, visibility on its website, two tickets to the show and access to the VIP lounge.
Projet de prévention des toxicomanies : Cumulus receives $600, which covers the registration fee for a borough team in the Tournoi de hockey du député, whose profits go to the organization.
The decision is up to the Lachine borough council; the expense is charged as set out in the financial information in the file.
The borough of Lachine is paying out $715 in total in financial contributions to two organizations.
L'Union des familles de Lachine receives $490 for the upkeep of the 4 bocce courts in parc LaSalle.
Le Choeur Ambiance inc. receives $225 for a full-page ad in the program for its concert on May 30, 2026.
The borough says it wants to support neighbourhood life and citizen participation in this way.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing Club Élite Triathlon to hold its triathlon on August 23, 2026, from 7 a.m. to about 12 p.m., at parc des Rapides — Terrasse Serre.
Boulevard LaSalle will be closed between 37e avenue and boulevard Bishop-Power, with no parking allowed; pedestrian, cycling and car traffic will be detoured.
Rue Gagné (from boulevard LaSalle to rue Centrale) and rue Raymond (from boulevard LaSalle to avenue des Rapides) will stay open to local traffic only.
The borough is providing support in goods and services valued at $15,000: coordination, rented signage, equipment loan and delivery, and transport and surveillance teams.
Security and the management of the street closures are handled by SPVM neighbourhood station 13.
The events: swimming in the parc des Rapides basin, cycling on boulevard LaSalle between 8e avenue and rue Raymond, and a run of about 1 km on the bike path in the same area.
Residents and businesses along the route will receive a notice by letter; no-parking signs will be put up the day before.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $8,000 to two organizations to hold outdoor events open to everyone.
Les Rapides du Lac Saint-Louis is receiving $4,000 for the Triathlon LaSalle.
Programme de Basketball des Leaders is receiving $4,000 for the Jeux de la rue.
The money comes from the operating budget of the borough's Direction culture, sports, loisirs et développement social.
The grants are given through the financial support program for LaSalle events, in place since 2023, which caps the help at 70% of the event's budget.
Last year, these same two organizations received $15,030 in total ($3,400 and $11,630).
The borough of LaSalle is giving $8,720 to the Programme de Basketball des Leaders for its "Block Party" at parc Lefebvre.
The event takes place on Sunday, August 9, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m.: basketball and football games, food stands, and family activities.
The organization is allowed to hold a barbecue and hand out food on site.
The borough is lending equipment and providing staff: a development officer, a coordinator, an electrician foreman, a transport crew, and one employee on site on the day of the event.
The money comes from the financial support program for LaSalle events and covers no more than 70% of the event's budget.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Direction culture, sports, loisirs et développement social.
In 2025, the same organization received $11,630 under this program.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing Eau Vive LaSalle to hold the 3rd Classique Vague à Guy, a river surfing competition at parc des Rapides, on Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
It is granting $5,000 to the organization: $3,500 after the resolution is adopted, and $1,500 upon receipt of the final report, no later than 90 days after the event.
The bike path will be detoured via rues Gagné, Centrale and Raymond, a detour authorized by neighbourhood police station 13.
The organization may sell food and alcohol (with a permit), hold a BBQ and a draw, sell merchandise and host food trucks.
On the program: 16 female competitors and 16 male competitors, partner booths, bleachers, a Hawaiian dance and a musical performance; the competition runs from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.
The borough is providing logistical support (lending and delivery of equipment, signage, transport crews on September 25 and 26), valued at $8,000 in free services.
About 120 volunteers will handle security, first aid, greeting visitors and registrations.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is granting a minor exemption to the building at 2543, avenue Letourneux.
The exemption legalizes a foundation that encroaches about 30.5 cm underpinning the neighbouring property, which is 15 cm more than the planning by-law allows.
According to the document, the contractor inadvertently built a "T"-shaped footing instead of the "L"-shaped footing shown in the revised plans, and a notice of non-compliance was issued.
The borough considers that a refusal would force the applicant to demolish and rebuild the footing, which would cause them serious harm.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on January 16, 2026, with no comments.
Next steps: a public notice announcing the application, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is approving an exception to the planning by-law for the building at 2165, rue Baldwin.
The exception allows a mechanical unit and an acoustic wall to be installed on the roof closer to the edge than permitted: 91 cm instead of the required 3.89 m.
The unit is an air recovery unit that completes the school building's air conditioning; it was moved toward the parapet because ducts were blocked by the structure.
A secondary structure had to be added under the unit because of insufficient load-bearing capacity, which increased its height.

Three conditions apply: extending the walls of the acoustic enclosure by one metre on each side, using a grey rather than white cladding, and providing the manufacturer's details to confirm the acoustic properties.
The planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 6, 2026; a public notice must announce the application before it is adopted.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is approving a terrace that has already been built at 2650, rue de Beaurivage, even though it does not respect the required distance from the property line.
The planning by-law requires 1 metre of clearance from the side and rear property lines; the terrace is about 15 cm from the rear line.
The purpose of the application is to legalize an existing situation: the permit had been issued by the Ville with plans showing the terrace at less than one metre.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain considers that the work was done in good faith according to the permit and does not cause excessive nuisance to the neighbourhood.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 6, 2026.
Next steps: a public notice announcing the application, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is granting a minor exemption for the buildings at 3010 and 3020, avenue Hector.
The developer wants to build a new residential building with a mezzanine; the rules require the mezzanine to be set back from the front wall and the side wall.
The exemption allows a setback of 0 m from the side wall, instead of a setback equal to one times the height.
The area concerned is on the boundary of the municipality of Montréal-Est.
According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, the exemption does not harm the neighbours, has little effect on the built environment and allows units with a larger living area.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 6, 2026; a public notice announcing the application comes before the resolution is adopted.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the demolition of a vacant one-storey commercial building at 3850, rue Sainte-Catherine Est, at the corner of avenue Bourbonnière.
In its place, a detached residential building of 6 storeys and 60 units may be built: 24 studios, 20 one-bedroom units, 10 two-bedroom units and 6 three-bedroom units.

The project departs from the planning rules on height (3 storeys and 12.5 m allowed), siting, side setback (1.5 m instead of 3 m), the percentage of masonry and the number of units (maximum of 8 allowed).
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion by majority, on the condition that the right side wall of the 5th and 6th storeys be set back by at least 2.4 m.
The developer will have to provide a bank guarantee of $31,800 to obtain the demolition certificate and $5,000 for the construction permit; the City may cash them in if the work does not comply.
Construction work must begin within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; the outdoor landscaping must be completed within 12 months after the permit ends.
The project provides for 40% greening (23% at ground level, 17% on the roof), 12 trees planted and a waste room in the basement.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough council must decide what to do about work that does not comply with the rules at 561, rue Honoré-Beaugrand.
After a new three-unit, two-storey building was built, an inspection found that vinyl exterior siding had been installed instead of the metal siding set out in the permit.
Vinyl is prohibited by the borough's planning by-law (section 79 of 01-275).
The owner points to the similar appearance (almost identical colour and texture) and to supply problems with the material that had been planned.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain considers the exemption justifiable: the building's appearance is maintained and how it fits in with neighbouring buildings is not affected.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous unfavourable opinion, which means the council must decide the matter itself.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is allowing the owner of 1634, avenue Letourneux to move the rear outdoor staircase to the side edge of the property.
The urban planning by-law normally requires a clearance of at least 1 metre; the staircase will sit right against the property line (0 cm).
The staircase leads to the 2nd-floor balcony. Located in the middle of the property, it blocks access to the ground-floor terrace and cuts the backyard in two.
According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, the exemption does not harm the neighbours or the surrounding buildings.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 10, 2026, with no conditions.
Next steps: a public notice announcing the application, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is approving a minor exemption for the building at 2907, rue Louis-Veuillot.
The outdoor staircase in the backyard may be installed 0.75 m from the side property line, instead of the 1 m required by the planning by-law.
The owner wants to move the staircase leading to the 2nd-floor balcony toward the lot line, because it cuts the yard in two and blocks access to the ground-floor terrace.
The Direction de l'aménagement urbain finds that the exemption does not harm the neighbours or the surrounding built environment.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with no conditions on April 10, 2026, adopted by majority.
Next steps: a public notice announcing the application, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.

The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is granting a minor exemption to Habitations La Pépinière, a group of buildings located around boulevard Rosemont, rue Du Quesne and avenues Albani and De Charrette.

The exemption brings the existing parking spaces into compliance: spaces of 2.5 m by 5 m instead of 5.5 m in length, and a clearance of 1.8 m between the public roadway and the parking area instead of 2.5 m.

It also allows the owner to keep traditional asphalt (instead of a surfacing material that reflects less heat) and to plant no trees in the green islands or along the public roadway, even though the by-law requires it.
The owner plans to refurbish the site by adding semi-buried bins, accessible parking spaces, an area for bulky waste collection, and installations for future electric charging stations.

The Direction de l'aménagement urbain considers that the exemptions do not affect the neighbours or the built environment; the comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 10, 2026, with no conditions.
Next steps: a public notice announcing the application, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
No money is involved in this decision.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is granting a minor exemption for the building at 9575, rue De Teck.
The exemption allows a "semi-detached" siting rather than the "attached" siting required by the borough's planning by-law.
The project involved is the construction of a three-unit building on two storeys (permit 3003534256).
The building will not be up against the neighbouring property line on the south side, contrary to the rule requiring 4 metres of depth from the façade.
