The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion, unanimously and without conditions, on April 10, 2026; a favourable opinion from the demolition committee had been issued in June 2024.

According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, the exemption does not harm the neighbours' property rights and has no significant impact on the surrounding built environment. The property is next to the Montréal-Est boundary.
There is no financial aspect attached to this file. A public notice must precede the adoption of the resolution.
The borough of Mercier/Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the conversion of a building at 1405, rue Préfontaine (3151, rue Sainte-Catherine Est): 12 studios will become 8 larger units.
On the ground floor, four studios will become one 3½ unit and one 4½ unit; on the 2nd and 3rd floors, four studios will become three 3½ units per floor.
The merging only affects the units facing rue Préfontaine.
The 12 studios are vacant; an inspector verified this on site on January 22, 2026, and according to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain no tenant's rights are affected.
The project does not comply with the municipal rule that prohibits merging dwelling units, but it can be approved as a conditional use.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion, with no conditions, on April 10, 2026.
Next steps: public notice, posting on the building, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is approving the conversion of a duplex into a single-family home at 1884, rue Lepailleur.
The two units will be merged into one, which removes one unit from the existing housing stock.
The planning by-law normally prohibits merging housing units; the City is using the conditional use procedure to allow the project.
The owner lives at 1884; the unit above (1886) will be vacant as of June 2026, since the lease has been terminated.
According to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, the project does not compromise the rights of any tenant and creates a larger space suited to a family.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 10, 2026, with no conditions.
Next steps: public notice, posting on the building, then adoption of the resolution by the borough council.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the partial demolition of a one-storey commercial building and the construction of a three-storey residential addition at 3570, rue Ontario Est.
The project adds four housing units; the lot coverage rate stays at more than 95%.

The developer is getting exemptions: 50% masonry instead of 80%, no trees planted, 0% ground-level greening instead of 25%, no cleanliness slab, and living spaces in the basement despite the area being in a dip.

Before the demolition certificate is issued, the developer must provide a bank guarantee of $392,033, which stays in effect until the work is finished; the City can cash it in if the work does not comply with the resolution.
Construction work must begin within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; the outdoor landscaping must be completed within 12 months after the permit ends.
The plans will have to be approved (PIIA) and match the document from MakerHub Inc dated August 14, 2024.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 10, 2026, asking in particular for more greening on the roof and along rue Joliette.
The borough of Ville-Marie is awarding 2633-2312 Québec inc. (Arthier) the repair work on the belvédère du Chemin-Qui-Marche, in Vieux-Montréal.
The maximum authorized expense is $3,486,731.85, taxes included: $2,642,125.50 for the contract, $528,425.10 in contingencies and $316,181.25 in incidental costs.
The belvedere, opened in 2012, shows deterioration linked to design and construction problems: damaged wood decking, inadequate ventilation, torn drainage membrane, missing plants.
The work includes rebuilding the belvedere with more durable materials, a new stormwater drainage system, LED lights, grading and planting.
Work is set to begin on April 13, 2026 and finish on August 28, 2026; local residents will receive notices and a construction site sign will be put up.
Since the work encroaches on railway tracks, the Administration portuaire de Montréal gave its authorization in January 2026 and the City will have to reimburse its costs ($57,487.50 expected).
Of the 9 compliant bids received, the one selected is the lowest, 2.74% below the internal estimate; the project is funded entirely through the borough's ten-year investment program.
The City agrees, as mortgage creditor, to the dissolution of the co-ownership of the building at 9350, boulevard Pie-IX, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
This building was purchased by the organization Proanima Montréal, which will provide animal management services there for the entire City.
The co-ownership had to be dissolved because the City sold two neighbouring lots (boulevard des Grandes-Prairies) to the seller and to Le Marché Pie-IX, a sale concluded on June 26, 2025.
The City consents to merging lots 6 659 203 and 6 659 205 into a single lot.
The City's mortgage of $25,000,000, plus an additional mortgage of 25%, will now cover both lots instead of just one, under the same conditions.
Reminder: in November 2023, the City awarded Proanima a 10-year animal management contract, for a maximum expenditure of $157,937,206, including taxes.
City council is approving an amendment (amendment 1) to the animal services management contract signed with the non-profit organization Proanima Montréal, at no additional cost.
From now on, the City will be able to contract directly with a third party for local animal services, for up to 3,665 pets per year.
Before this amendment, it was Proanima that could subcontract these services when its centre reached its maximum intake capacity.
The original contract, awarded in 2023, is worth $152,978,185 including taxes over 10 years, with a 10-year renewal option.
The amendment takes effect on May 1, 2026 and covers animal services in all 19 boroughs.
The Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne manages this contract; the City states that there is no financial impact.
The executive committee is authorizing the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité to move $37,689,000 (net) between its 2026 capital projects, without increasing its total budget envelope.

Some projects are getting more money: the Programme d'aménagement des rues – Artériel (+$13.1M), the Réseau Express Vélo and the bike path network (+$3.8M for the agglomeration portion), Louvain Est (+$4.1M), Griffintown (+$1.5M) and Sainte-Catherine Ouest – Phase 2 (+$2M, bringing it to $36.2M).

Other projects are being cut because of postponements: Lachine Est (-$5.3M, parc Jenkins pushed back to 2027), Sainte-Catherine Est – Village (-$3.7M), pont Jacques-Bizard (-$2.4M, delays from Hydro-Québec and Bell), Samuel-De Champlain/REM (-$2.65M) and Bridge-Bonaventure (-$2M).

The budget for Phase 1 of rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest is brought down to $0 and the money goes to Phase 2; the redevelopment of rue Jean-Talon between 22e Avenue and Langelier loses $3M (delays in property acquisitions and in plans and specifications).
An additional $700,000 is planned to buy land needed for the Royalmount–Cavendish link, as the reserve notice expires in August 2026.

Vieux-Montréal is receiving $2.6M more to finish phase 3A of rue Saint-Paul; the restoration of the Château Dufresne, the fountain at square George-Étienne-Cartier and the centre Calixa-Lavallée is postponed.

Lachine is entrusting the marking of its streets for 2026 to the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, for a maximum expense of $332,000 ($326,200 for the work and $5,800 for contingencies), before taxes.

The work covers pedestrian crossings, stop lines, school crossings, speed bumps, centre lines on arterial, collector and local streets, as well as existing bike lanes, arrows, school pictograms and guide lines.
The marking starts in mid-April 2026 and ends at the end of October 2026.

The separate waterfront bike paths and the rail path (rue Victoria) will not be marked this year, except for one section between boulevard Saint-Joseph and rue Notre-Dame: an inspection in March 2026 found the marking still in very good condition, which saves $21,800.
Lachine says it does not have the employees or the equipment to do large-scale marking; its employees only mark municipal parking lots.
The expense is paid out of the 2026 operating budget of Lachine's Direction des travaux publics.
In 2025, the same agreement had been authorized for a maximum of $356,926.
The borough of Lachine is paying $10,100 (taxes included) to Cyclo-club Lachine for the 2026 edition of the Mardis cyclistes de Lachine.
The races take place on Tuesday evenings from June 2 to August 4, 2026, around parc LaSalle, starting on 10e Avenue in front of the stade Denis-Boucher.

Every Tuesday, the streets around the perimeter (1.61 km per lap) are closed to traffic in the late afternoon until the end of the races, with detours and a temporary parking ban; residents are notified in advance.
The organization also receives logistical support, labour and loaned equipment from the borough.
The club is responsible for organizing the event and for its finances, must submit its budget forecasts no later than May 1, 2026, and a final report (accountability report in October 2026).
The payment is made in two parts: $9,100 within 30 days of the decision, then $1,000 within 30 days of the final report.
The same amount of $10,100 had been granted for the 2023, 2024 and 2025 editions.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is asking the Directeur de l'état civil to designate the councillor for the Jeanne-Mance district, Gabriel Fortin, as a "competent officiant".
If he is designated, he will be able to perform marriages and civil unions within the territory of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
This authorization would apply only to the territory set out in the designation document and for the duration of his term as an elected official.
The Directeur de l'état civil will assign him a unique identification number to be written on marriage or civil union declarations.
The step is voluntary: the councillor made the request himself.
Next step: sending the resolution to the Directeur de l'état civil. No financial impact is expected.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is amending its 2026 fee by-law on two points.

Occupying public property with a café-terrasse (or café-terrasse with 3 tables and 12 chairs) or a fruit and vegetable stand on rue Prince-Arthur Est, between boulevard Saint-Laurent and avenue Laval, becomes free of charge again: the fee had been added there by mistake.
Fees for aquatic activities are being updated because the Société de Sauvetage announced, on March 12, the cancellation of the provincial grant planned for 2026-2027.
Training for lifeguards and aquatic instructors remains free this summer, then becomes paid starting in the fall of 2026.
Notice of motion on May 4, 2026, adoption on June 1, 2026, coming into force announced for June 2, 2026.
The borough says these changes make it possible to reach the revenues planned in the 2026 budget without reducing service.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is appointing Bénita Degboe, a file analyst, as substitute borough secretary.
She will be able to carry out all of the borough secretary's duties when the incumbent is absent, with the same powers and obligations.
The law requires the council to always have a person responsible for the custody of the council's office and archives.
The document does not provide for any spending.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is moving its public borough council meeting for October 2026.
The meeting moves from Monday, October 5 to Tuesday, October 6, 2026, still at 6:30 p.m.
Reason given: the Québec provincial elections are being held on October 5, 2026, the date set in the calendar adopted in December 2025.
The change will be announced through a public notice on the borough's website, as well as in Le Plateau's newsletter and Facebook page.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $16,000 to the Société environnementale de Côte-des-Neiges (SOCENV) for its "Cuisine anti-gaspi" project.
The project runs from May 4 to December 31, 2026 in both of the borough's neighbourhoods.
The idea is to set up community kitchen spaces where participants cook with recovered food and leave with meals.
The project is aimed first at people who are vulnerable and experiencing food insecurity.
The money comes from the 2026 operating budget set aside for contributions to local organizations.
The organization must follow the City's visibility protocol; an agreement sets out the terms of the contribution.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is giving $101,129 to two organizations to run their "Tables de quartier" (neighbourhood roundtables), from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027.
Each of the two organizations receives $50,564.50: Conseil communautaire Notre-Dame-de-Grâce inc. and Corporation de développement communautaire de Côte-des-Neiges.
The Tables de quartier bring together residents, community organizations and institutions to identify local priorities and coordinate actions against poverty and social exclusion.
In Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, the priorities chosen for 2024-2029 are inclusion, affordable housing and strengthening community organizations.
In Côte-des-Neiges, the plan adopted in November 2025 targets sanitary conditions in rental housing, the development of social housing, and access to healthy food.
The City increased its contribution in 2026 to reach a target of $50,000 per roundtable; together, the three funders are providing a little more than $4.7M, or at least $143,000 per roundtable.
The borough gave $74,838.62 for the 2025-2026 period.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève authorizes its director of urban planning and public safety to sign the grant application and the funding agreement for the energy retrofit of the Centre socioculturel de L'Île-Bizard.
The grant from the federal Green and Inclusive Community Buildings (GICB) program amounts to $1,399,140 and was accepted on September 12, 2024.
Hydro-Québec is offering $500,000 for the project; the borough must cover any remaining amount needed to carry it out.
The project has been under way since 2021 with Hydro-Québec and Université McGill.
According to the document, the work would reduce the building's energy costs and strengthen its role as an emergency measures centre.
The resolution authorizes no spending: it only designates a signatory.
The schedule for the next steps has yet to be determined.
The Verdun borough council meeting of June 30, 2026 will be held at a different location.
It will take place at the Quai-5160 – Maison de la culture de Verdun, at 5160, boulevard LaSalle, rather than at the borough hall.
The 2026 meeting schedule, adopted on December 9, 2025, is amended accordingly.
The borough will announce the change through a public notice, on its website, on Facebook and in its newsletter.
No spending is associated with this decision.
The borough of Verdun is creating four advisory committees and appointing their permanent members.
Public Spaces Projects and Mobility Committee: chaired by councillor Benoit Gratton, with the territorial development and technical studies department.
Finance and Performance Committee: chaired by Benoit Gratton, with councillor Andréanne Moreau as co-chair.
Environment, Cleanliness and Climate Resilience Committee: chaired by mayor Céline-Audrey Beauregard.
Active Living, Culture, Inclusion and Urban Safety Committee: chaired by councillor Stefana Lamasanu.
The mayor and the borough director sit on all committees by virtue of their office; the division heads of the departments concerned are members.
The committees have no decision-making power: they make recommendations to the council, meet at least 6 times a year, and submit an annual report and a mid-year update.
The Verdun borough is appointing Diane Garand as interim borough secretary as of May 4, 2026.
The appointment is temporary and lasts for as long as the current borough secretary is absent.
Ms. Garand will exercise all the powers attached to the position during this interim period.
The borough council must approve the appointment on May 5, 2026.
The document does not indicate any amount tied to this appointment.

The Le Sud-Ouest borough approves the architectural plans for a 20-storey building (63 metres) at the corner of rue Bridge, rue Wellington and rue Saint-Colomban, in Pointe-Saint-Charles, on a site that is currently vacant.
The « Triangle Nord » project will have 395 non-market housing units, a commercial ground floor and an underground parking garage with 21 spaces.
The building will be laid out in an L shape along rue Bridge and rue Wellington, leaving an open courtyard on the rue Saint-Colomban side.

The construction budget is $130M, funded by the Government of Canada, the Government of Québec and the Ville, through the Entente Canada-Québec sur le Fonds pour accélérer la construction de logements.
The project is being developed in partnership with Broccolini, Bâtir son quartier and the housing non-profit Point commun.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had issued a favourable opinion with 8 conditions; two of them (parking access, common spaces for families and children) were not followed, with the Direction citing the restrictive program and the funding conditions.
City council takes note of the 2025 annual report of the Commission de la fonction publique de Montréal, an independent body that reports to council.
The Commission received 275 requests in 2025, including 132 complaints, and handled 93 investigations; the average time to process a complaint is 100 business days.
Of the 104 harassment and discrimination complaints, 13 were found admissible and led to an investigation.
The Commission made 126 recommendations and is continuing an audit in 2026 on workforce retention.
Most complaints come from blue-collar and white-collar workers.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is awarding Construction Vert Dure inc. a contract of $750,233.72 (taxes included) to build an outdoor exercise area at parc Saint-Donat.
The total authorized spending comes to $930,757.09, including $75,023.37 in contingencies and $105,500 in incidental costs.
The project comes from Montréal's participatory budget (2nd edition): exercise equipment, a calisthenics structure, new lighting and a drinking fountain.
Other work in the park is included: bleachers made of concrete blocks that also serve as training modules, removal or replacement of fences, and repairs to the running track and the pathways.

The open-air gym was first supposed to go to parc Beauclerk, but delays tied to Hydro-Québec's work pushed the project there back to 2029, while participatory budget projects must be finished in December 2026.
Funding: $212,738 from the borough's deferred revenues for parks and playgrounds (25%) and $698,784.39 from the Service de la concertation des arrondissements (75%).
Out of five compliant bids, the lowest is 13.03% below the professionals' estimate; the soccer and football fields and the track will remain open during the work.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is approving the final report on the redevelopment work on avenue Joseph-Guibord, between rue Jean-Rivard and rue Jarry.
The project cost $749,567.34 in total; Québec will reimburse 50% of eligible expenses, meaning $374,783.67 claimed out of a maximum announced funding of $400,000.
The work, done in 2024 and 2025, removed two traffic lanes and added a two-way bike path, sidewalks, curb extensions, planting pits, trees and tactile warning plates.
Results: 388 metres of cycling infrastructure, 310 metres for pedestrians and 12 bicycle parking spaces; the path is free to use 12 months a year.
In 2025, avenue Joseph-Guibord became one-way: southbound between D'Hérelle and Jarry, northbound between D'Hérelle and Jean-Rivard, with changes to traffic lights and signs.
The work was completed on June 27, 2025; the reimbursement request was to be sent to the ministère des Transports in December 2025.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is awarding the redevelopment of rue De Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel to Groupe MPotvin, the lowest of 10 bidders, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82, taxes included.

The total authorized spending comes to $11,192,464.62, including $819,951.48 in contingencies and $2,172,998.33 in incidental costs; the borough is paying $7,209,507.59 and the central city $3,982,957.03.
The work includes rebuilding and rehabilitating the sewers and the water main, moving a gas line, upgrading the lighting and traffic lights, work on Bell's network, and green draining infrastructure.

The street will be redeveloped to improve walking corridors, the existing bike facilities (new markings and bollards) and safety at intersections; tree pits, plantings and street furniture will also be added.

The work will take place in three phases: from May to November 2026 (underground infrastructure), from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, curb extensions) and from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The borough notes that this route is used by more than 3000 students during peak hours on school days, and that a public participation process helped shape the final design.
The winning bid is 27.24% lower than the estimate ($11,269,308.54); Groupe MPotvin's performance will be evaluated.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is proposing to city council that it take charge of the design, coordination and carrying out of repair work on the REV Lajeunesse.
The work targets rue Lajeunesse northbound, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie.
According to the document, the bike path has major sinking and severe lengthwise cracks, which were noted during an inspection and have been the subject of complaints from residents.
The budget is estimated at a maximum of $220,000, taxes included: $80,000 for sidewalk repair and $140,000 for planing, paving and line marking.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is committing to pay 100% of the costs, through two upkeep programs (road infrastructure and bike path network).
Planned timeline: call for tenders in May 2026, contracts awarded in June, work from July to August 2026.
If the offer is not accepted, the work cannot be carried out. Residents will be notified before the work begins.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie wants to create an advisory committee on citizen participation, which would recommend to the council ways to get residents more involved in local decisions.
The committee would have 12 to 15 members: two thirds from civil society (residents and people from organizations in the area), and one third from the borough council and borough staff.
Members from civil society would receive $75 per meeting attended, and the person acting as co-chair would receive an additional $50 per attendance.
The committee would meet 6 to 8 times a year for 5 years; members' terms are 3 years, renewable once.
The committee will not be able to step in or arbitrate in a process dealing with a specific project.
On May 4, 2026, the council receives the notice of motion and the draft by-law; adoption of the by-law, of the committee's budget for 2026 and the appointment of members are planned for June 8, 2026.
The borough of Lachine is receiving $48,900 (taxes included) from the organization Sport et Loisir de l'île de Montréal (SLIM), under the "Circonflexe" program.
The money will be used to offer free sports equipment loans and activity leadership at parcs Michel-Ménard and Kirkland, from January 1 to August 31, 2026.
The grant pays for the purchase of equipment (skates, hockey equipment, balls, etc.) and the salaries of the recreation activity leaders.
At parc Michel-Ménard: skate loans from a trailer near the skating rink, free skating and friendly hockey games.
At parc Kirkland: a fuller program, with supervised activities based on age groups and seasons.
The executive committee is being asked to amend the City's 2026 budget and to increase the borough's funding allocation by the same amount.
A promotional campaign will be carried out through the newsletter, the borough's website and social media; a final report will be produced at the end of the project.
The borough of Lachine is signing a technical support agreement with the Club de Course à Pied Lachine-Dorval for the 15th edition of the Demi-Marathon de Lachine.
The race will take place on Sunday, October 18, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 2 p.m., on the waterfront streets between 55e Avenue and parc René-Lévesque.
Six distances are offered: 1 km, 2 km, 5 km, 10 km, 10 km Nordic walking and 21.1 km. Registration is paid and open to everyone. 5,000 participants are expected.

No cash grant is given to the organization: the help is in services (street cleaning and marking, transporting materials, promotion, notices to residents, occupancy permits, supervision of street closures).
The SPVM, the Service de sécurité incendie, Urgences-santé and the Agence de mobilité durable (parking officers and towing along the route) are also taking part.
The organization remains responsible for organizing the event and covers its costs.
Street closures and occupancy of public property will be authorized later, in a separate file; the accountability report is planned for December 2026.
The borough of Lachine is lending the LaSalle baseball field no. 1 and the Denis-Boucher stadium, in parc LaSalle, free of charge on July 4 and 5, 2026.
The loan is for the Alexandre-Forget mixed softball tournament, organized by the Fondation Jacques-Forest (blue-collar workers of the Ville de Montréal and the C.U.M.), in its 3rd edition.
The value of the rental hours waived in this way is $933.00 before taxes ($1,072.72 including taxes).

The fields are booked for 36 hours at the unlit rate and 2 hours at the lit rate: Saturday from 9 a.m. to 11 p.m. (field no. 1) and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (stadium), Sunday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. at both locations.
The tournament is a fundraiser to help families in vulnerable situations in Montréal; the blue-collar workers form mixed teams for it.
The organizers handle promotion, obtain the permits from the MAPAQ and the Régie des alcools, and plan for a BBQ stand, beverages, massage therapy and first-aid attendants.
The order is enacted on June 1, 2026 and takes effect upon its publication on June 4, 2026.

The City is launching a public competition to choose a work of art to be installed on rue De Castelnau Est, between rue Saint-Dominique and avenue de Châteaubriand, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
It is authorizing a $38,225.74 expense, taxes included, to hold the competition and cover the project's general expenses.
The competition is open only to professional Québec artists; the work will be sculptural, made up of several parts spread across three locations along the street.
A jury of seven people, including one representative of the citizens and one from the borough, will select up to four finalists, and then a winner.
Planned schedule: launch in March 2026, applications due April 14, 2026, winner chosen at the end of September 2026, contract in November 2026 and installation in the spring of 2028.
The total cost of the public art project is estimated at $614,307.98, taxes included, of which $509,339.25 is for acquiring the work (contract to come).
Funding comes from a loan by-law and the Entente de développement culturel de Montréal 2018-2021.

The City is postponing by one year the date it takes possession of the sculpture "Personnages" by Louis Archambault, donated by the Conseil des arts du Canada: the date moves from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2026.
The donor will keep the artwork on its premises until this new date, because the planned site is not ready due to a budget postponement.
The artwork is to be moved and stored at parc Jean-Drapeau in August 2026, for installation in the spring of 2027.
The City Clerk is authorized to sign the document amending the donation, planned for May 2026.
No additional budget is planned: the amounts are already authorized in the investment plan of the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs and in the parc Jean-Drapeau budget.

The urban agglomeration council takes note of the 2025 annual report of the Réseau de surveillance de la qualité de l'air (RSQA), produced by the Service de l'environnement et de la transition écologique.
In 2025, air quality was "good" 62.4% of the time and "acceptable" 33.1% of the time; 27 days of poor quality (4.5%) were recorded, up from 2024 and all linked to fine particles.
The report counts 14 smog episodes, 13 of which were attributed to forest fires in Western Canada.
Ultrafine particles increased between 2024 and 2025, with higher concentrations near airport activities.

The network had 11 permanent stations and 2 temporary stations, with 55 continuous analyzers and 8 people doing maintenance; stations 28, 50 and 66 stop taking measurements in 2025 (28 replaced by an Autoroute 13 station in spring 2026, 66 relocated at the request of Aéroports de Montréal).
By-law 15-069 on wood heating is associated with a lasting drop in levoglucosan; SO2, CO and NOx have been improving since 2000, while ozone is increasing.
Validated data is published on the City's open data site, and an interactive platform launched in 2025 was consulted a great deal during the smog episodes.
The City is authorizing the Service de la culture to launch an invitational competition for a public artwork at parc des Eaux-Cachées, in Griffintown (arrondissement du Sud-Ouest).
It is authorizing spending of $47,714.63, taxes included, to hold the competition and cover overhead costs, paid 100% by the central city.
The competition is open to professional artists from Québec; it is for a sculptural installation near the park's esplanade and bleachers.
A jury of seven people, including one citizen representative, will select about twenty applications, then three finalists, before recommending a winning project.
The total planned budget for the public art project comes to $477,146.25, taxes included, of which $379,417.50 is for the artist's contract, to be approved later.
Announced schedule: jury starting in April 2026, selection of the winner in October 2026, contract in December 2026 and installation of the artwork in 2028.
Parc des Eaux-Cachées is planned to cover 8,500 m² with gardens, a wooded area, an esplanade, an open field, a play area and rainwater management.
The City is adding $120,378.83 (taxes included) to its contract with CGI inc. for mobile application development, bringing the agreement to $922,904.33.
This 15% increase adds 1,500 hours of work: 1,125 hours of development and 375 hours of bug fixing.
The contract, signed in November 2023 for $802,525.50 and set to run until November 2026, was 91% used up as of February 2026.
The hours are used in particular for the Montréal mobile app (snow removal map, summer locations map, updates) and for the Espace pour la vie app.
The Service des technologies de l'information is paying out of its own budgets, as needs arise.
The City says it wants to keep the current resources in place and ensure knowledge transfer until the next call for tenders.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council.
The City is renewing its contract with ESII Canada inc., without a call for tenders, for queue management and online appointment booking, from August 19, 2026 to August 18, 2030.
The total cost comes to $440,703.52, taxes included, paid out of the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information and covered by the central city.
The contract covers 29 service points: bureaux Accès Montréal, permit offices and cour municipale service points.
It includes use of the software, support and maintenance, thermal paper and maintenance of the kiosks and video controllers; screens and printers are excluded.
The City justifies the absence of a call for tenders by the fact that ESII owns the source code and the proprietary technology of the kiosks.
The price submitted is 37% higher than the City's estimate ($321,732.63), which the City attributes to inflation, rising IT labour costs and the end of a 7-year contract with more favourable terms.
The previous contract, awarded in 2019 and extended in 2024, ends on August 18, 2026.

The City is adding $702,262.99 (taxes included) to its contract with Conseillers en gestion et informatique CGI inc. for digital development services, raising the agreement from $5,596,666.82 to $6,298,929.81.
The master agreement was signed in March 2025 for 36 months and was to end in March 2028.
This 15% increase adds 5,625 hours of intermediate expertise (total 43,125 h) and 3,375 hours of advanced expertise (total 25,875 h).

The Service des technologies de l'information cites a usage rate of 56% and 55% for these two banks of hours as of May 1, 2026, and wants to avoid an interruption of ongoing projects until a new contract is in place.

The hours are used in particular for the overhaul of the Espace pour la vie platforms, a new system for managing citizen requests (Microsoft Dynamics 365), library tools, and new online services such as building permits and permits to occupy public property.
No budget is set aside in advance: each expense will be authorized as needs arise, out of the Service des TI's budgets.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.
The City's audit committee is filing its annual activity report for 2025, and council is taking note of it.
The committee met 6 times in 2025 (including one training session), with a participation rate of 95.83%.
The report covers the follow-up on the audit of the 2024 financial statements, the review of financial and environmental risks, and attention paid to cybersecurity.
Some presentations (the auditor general's recommendations, the 2026 budget) were postponed to early 2026 because of the fall 2025 elections.
The committee notes that some positions remain critical at the Service des finances et de l'évaluation foncière.
This matter has no financial impact.
The urban agglomeration council appoints Natasha Daswani as an independent member of the City's audit committee, for a three-year term ending on May 4, 2029.
She replaces Suzanne Bourque, an independent member for seven years, who left the committee at the end of 2025.
Her pay is set at a maximum of $17,500 per year, in accordance with the by-law on the pay of independent members.
The audit committee advises the city councils on audit reports, financial statements and the budget, and follows up on the implementation of the auditor general's recommendations.

The candidate was assessed in an interview by a selection committee made up of two councillors and the committee's independent members; she is a graduate of HEC Montréal and is auditor general at Université de Montréal and HEC Montréal.
The term's end date takes into account the general election scheduled for November 4, 2029.
The City's audit committee is tabling its report on the review of the 2025 consolidated financial statements before the councils; the council takes note of it.
The external auditors and the Bureau du vérificateur général issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025.
The committee says it has reviewed the audited financial statements and supports them.

The committee says it is concerned about the recurrence and the number of errors found, and is asking the Service des finances et de l'évaluation foncière for a plan to follow up on the errors that have not been corrected.
The committee points to communication delays linked to teams being spread out, and to difficulties the auditors ran into with the Commission des services électriques.
The committee notes that its recommendation to designate a key accounting person in each audited department has been carried out.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is receiving $7,000 from Sport et Loisir de l'Île de Montréal (SLIM), under the Circonflexe program, which is funded mainly by the ministère de l'Éducation.
The money will be used to provide adapted winter sports equipment at parc La Fontaine: support skates, sledge chairs and sliding supports for people with reduced mobility.
Staff of the on-site rental service (operated by Écorécréo, at the chalet La Fontaine) will be trained in welcoming people with disabilities and will be able to accompany them on the ice.
The executive committee is being asked to amend the City's budget to account for this amount and to increase the borough's 2026 budget base by $7,000.

SLIM's conditions: incur the expenses between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026, receive no other funding from the ministère de l'Éducation, respect the program's visibility requirements, and return any unused equipment.
Planned schedule: purchase of the equipment in January 2026, installation in February 2026, and reporting in April 2026.
No communications activities are planned for the public.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is signing an agreement with Hydro-Québec to receive $154,000, the remainder of a $1,104,000 compensation payment tied to the construction of the poste de transformation Saint-Patrick.
This money will go to phase 4 of the redevelopment of parc d'Argenson, with work estimated at about $156,397.79.
Planned work includes: a container to serve as a shelter and meeting point, electrical service for it (lighting, heating, outlets), Wi-Fi installation, and added paving at the park entrances.
The dog park will get a stone dust surface and a floodlight.
The work is to be completed in June 2026.
The original project to highlight the « Belt Line » pylons along the canal de Lachine was dropped: the borough was unable to acquire them from Parcs Canada, for maintenance and safety reasons.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest wants to sell a 654.5 m² city-owned lot — triangular, landlocked and not buildable — to the neighbouring owner at 5550, boulevard Monk.

This lot is part of the Écoterritoire de la falaise Saint-Jacques, which prevents the City from selling it; it must first be removed from the list of facilities of collective interest of the urban agglomeration.
The borough is mandating the Service Espace pour la vie, des grands parcs et du Mont-Royal to carry out the administrative steps on its behalf, without which the removal request cannot move forward.
The neighbour is asking for work to be done because soil from the city-owned lot is running off onto his property; he is proposing to buy it as a solution.
The borough will have to provide the ministry (MAMH) with an analysis of the lot's ecological value, explanations, a plan and photos.
According to the document, the rebuilding of the échangeur Turcot has reduced the ecological value of the lot, which cannot be reached without crossing a private property.
If the sale goes through, the borough would receive 20% of the net gain and the ville centre 80%; processing at the ministry can take from 6 to 15 months.
The City wants to officially convert a section of the former rue Eadie, between rue Dubois and rue De Maricourt, into a local park rather than a street.
The land involved is 810.2 m² and will be added to parc Campbell Ouest, in Côte-Saint-Paul (Le Sud-Ouest borough).
This portion of street has been closed to cars since 2016; the asphalt was replaced with grass and stone dust paths during the park redevelopment that began in 2025.
The change is meant to make the cadastral data match the reality on the ground and to clarify maintenance (snow removal, mowing) by the borough's public works department.
The underground pipes have not been removed or modified; the catch basins were kept with solid covers.
Reuniting the two parts of the park by greening the former street was one of the most popular requests during the public participation process held from 2023 to 2025.
City council is to adopt the resolution on June 15, 2026; the cadastre update is planned for the summer of 2026.
The City is awarding a $326,712.96 (taxes included) contract to Solutions Merkur Ltée for IT development services on HCL Domino technologies.
The contract runs for 24 months, with two extension options of 24 months each, estimated at $258,329.59 and $271,245.98.
The work aims to update the City's decision-making records management system: moving from Lotus Notes 9 to HCL Domino 12/14, modernizing the Java applications and redesigning the integrations.
This system handles about 40,000 files per year and serves about 6,000 City users.
Only one company submitted a bid out of the two that obtained the tender documents; the other withdrew, saying the call for tenders did not match its niche.
The selected price is 32.79% ($80,684.86) above the City's estimate, which it explains by the scarcity of these specialized profiles; the company lowered its offer by 4.7% after negotiation.
The expense is funded by a loan by-law and spread over 2026, 2027 and 2028; the agglomeration covers 49.6% of it.

The City is adding $1,709,506.94 (taxes included) to the professional services contracts for the implementation of the Oracle ERP Cloud solution (SIMON infonuagique project), bringing the total to $13,106,219.86.
This amount is split between Société Conseil LGS inc. ($1,568,415.37) and Conseillers en Gestion et Informatique CGI inc. ($141,091.57), for the period from April 24, 2026 to January 24, 2027.
This is a 15% increase to the contracts awarded in January 2024, in order to add work hours for specialized resources.
The additional hours will be used for integrated and acceptance testing, fixing problems, defining user roles and access, and integrations with other City systems (including Maximo).
The City plans to roll out the new solution at the end of 2026 and says that, without this increase, critical work would be postponed.
The expense will be charged to the 2026-2035 investment program of the Service des technologies de l'information, under the SIMON Infonuagique project.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council.
The City is adding $199,477, taxes included, to its software maintenance and licensing contract with La Compagnie CA du Canada, bringing the total spending to $2,652,757.48.
In 2024, the City joined the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales agreement for the period from March 31, 2024 to March 30, 2027, for $2,453,280.48.
The contract was still being negotiated when the City signed on: the City had estimated fixed prices, but afterwards found that rates were going up by 20% per year.
This software runs applications on the mainframe computer, including penal offence management (STOP+), the municipal court (GESCOUR), and SPVM time and operations management.
The additional spending covers the period from March 31, 2026 to March 30, 2027 and is charged to the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information.
The contract includes technical support from the manufacturer 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, as well as software and security patches.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council; no communications activities are planned.

The City is entering into a 24-month master agreement with Société Conseil Groupe LGS for professional services to implement the Oracle HCM Cloud human resources system, for a maximum of $2,808,643.79, taxes included.
The agreement includes two extension options of 12 months each; the expense will be covered by the budget of the Service des technologies de l'information.

These external resources (application managers and developers) are being added to strengthen the team of the Transfo-RH project, which is modernizing the City's human resources management and payroll.
The contract replaces the one with KPMG, in place since 2020, which ends on May 31, 2026.

The project's next steps target white-collar payroll early next year, then payroll for firefighters and senior officers, school crossing guards and police officers, as well as staffing and training modules.
Of five firms that obtained the tender documents, three submitted bids and two were found to be compliant; the price selected is 8.85% below the City's latest estimate.
The City will evaluate the performance of the selected firm.
The Conseil des Montréalaises is tabling its 2025 activity report before city council, which takes note of it.
The report reviews the organization's opinions, briefs, projects and partnerships for 2025 and sets out its priorities for 2026.

Among the work done in 2025: an opinion titled « Femmes cols bleus, 10 ans plus tard : des progrès décevants », produced with Action travail des femmes, which contains 10 recommendations on their working conditions.
The Conseil updated its feminist guide for municipal elections, together with the Table des groupes de femmes de Montréal.
It held discussion groups with 50 women affected by the digital divide, with a view to an opinion in 2026.
The costs of producing the report were covered out of the Conseil des Montréalaises' own budget; the document will be posted on the City's website and social media.
The City is ending its agreement with the organization MURAL for the mural "Toucher l'horizon," which was to be painted in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The project had been selected under stream 1 of the Programme d'art mural 2025 (highly visible murals) and the agreement had been signed on June 6, 2025.
The wall's owner ultimately turned down the artistic proposal, which made the project impossible to carry out as approved.
The Service de la culture offered extensions to postpone the project to 2026 on another wall; the organization did not submit a postponement request.
The planned grant was $49,000, of which $34,300 was already paid out on July 7, 2025; the City will ask for the unused amounts to be repaid, with supporting documents.
The unpaid balance of $14,700 and the amounts recovered will go back into the funding envelope of the Entente sur le développement culturel de Montréal.
No communications activities are planned.
The City is hiring artist Véronique Buist to build and install a public artwork, "Le 7e joueur," at the aréna Martin-Lapointe in the borough of Lachine.
Total expense of $161,587.34 including taxes: $142,367.80 for the artist's contract, $12,813.03 in contingencies and $6,406.51 in incidental costs.
The cost is shared 80% by the central city and 20% by the borough of Lachine; a grant of $49,035.99 comes from the agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The artwork will be made up of 44 cut-out aluminum shapes, about a dozen of them backlit, evoking the sports played at the arena.
Two outreach activities are planned: an indoor mural created with muralist Bosny and the Maison des jeunes L'Escalier de Lachine, and an ice projection event with MAPP MTL.
Schedule: production and installation in 2026-2027, with the unveiling planned for fall 2027.
The artist was chosen from among 21 applications and 4 finalists by a jury that met on October 14, 2025 and March 19, 2026.
The City is giving $254,271 to five organizations to create six high-visibility murals in 2026, along with cultural mediation activities.
The murals will be painted in five boroughs: Anjou, Montréal-Nord (two projects), Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Le Sud-Ouest.
The amounts range from $15,000 (Concertation Ville-Émard Côte St-Paul) to $49,000 (Quartier des arts du cirque); the funding covers up to 75% of a project's cost, to a maximum of $49,000.
Of 14 projects found to meet the requirements and submitted to a seven-person jury, six were selected.
The murals will be created from June to October 2026, with unveilings in the summer and fall and reporting due by November 30, 2026.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city; $113,358 is subsidized by the Entente de développement culturel de Montréal.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing the conversion of a duplex into a single home, at 8443-8445, avenue des Belges, in the Villeray area (between rue Leman and rue de Liège).

The owners, who have lived on the ground floor since 2021, want to add an interior staircase and replace the upstairs kitchen with a bedroom: the home will have 4 bedrooms. The upstairs occupant is leaving at the end of their lease in 2026.
Conditions imposed: keep 4 bedrooms, keep the exterior staircase and the 2nd-floor door on the front of the building, and limit the floor area to 250 m².
The application for the conversion permit must be filed within 12 months of the adoption of the resolution.

Reasons accepted: physical constraints and zoning that limit expansion (2 storeys maximum, 7.8 m backyard, no livable basement, basin zone), distance from the metro and the possibility of restoring the home to its original state.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 11, 2026. The fees for reviewing the application come to $3,500.
At the meeting, no one asked to be heard on this application.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is amending its by-law on traffic and parking in order to process certain citizen requests more quickly.

Three types of requests will move from being handled by order to being handled by resolution: drop-off zones, parking spaces for people with disabilities, and parking areas reserved for home-care workers.

These decisions may be signed by the director of territorial development rather than going through the order procedure; the by-law on the delegation of powers to public servants will be amended at the same time.
The by-law also clarifies the setting up of school zones and playground zones, and repeals two paragraphs.
There is no cost associated with the file, and the by-law is not subject to approval by referendum.
Notice of motion given on March 10, 2026; adoption is planned for a later meeting, with a public notice of coming into force.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is transferring to the director of territorial development (a level 2 officer) the power to approve applications that previously went through the borough council.

All projects covered by the by-law on PIIAs (site planning and architectural integration programmes) that have received a favourable opinion from the urban planning advisory committee will be approved by this officer; those with an unfavourable recommendation remain excluded.

Added to the delegation are redeveloped school yards, extensions, new construction, the creation of a public roadway in an area of archaeological interest, and the establishment of a sensitive use near a railway or a marshalling yard.

Applications covered by section 4 of the Règlement sur la circulation et le stationnement (C-4.1) are also delegated to the same officer, which corrects a section that named neither a specific by-law nor a specific section.
The borough says it wants to reduce the time it takes to issue permits and to handle citizen requests.
The draft by-law received a notice of motion on March 10, 2026 and is to be adopted at a later sitting; it is not subject to approval by referendum.
An amendment to the Règlement sur la circulation et le stationnement (RCA26-14001) is being tabled at the same time.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is extending the season for sidewalk cafés and placottoirs on public property.
The permitted occupancy period now runs from March 15 to November 15, for 2026 and the following years.
The change moves the start of the season up to March 15; the end stays at November 15.
Business owners who want to take advantage of the extended period must ask for it when they apply for their permit.
Fees are calculated on a prorated basis according to the number of days of occupancy in the year.
The borough says it wants to support commercial vitality and assess the issues raised by each application in advance.
The ordinance comes into force when it is published.
The Ville-Marie borough council notes the filing of the reports of two public consultation meetings, held on December 10, 2025 and January 21, 2026 at 800, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.

On December 10, 2025 (about 9 people present), six projects were presented: a monetary guarantee related to the buildings on avenue Papineau, avenue Goulet and rue Cartier, signage for the Sun Life building (1155, rue Metcalfe), signage for the Centre Sanaaq (1200, rue du Sussex), signage for the Place des Arts (105, rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest), demolition and construction at 1225-1249, rue Metcalfe, and the redevelopment of 1001, rue Lucien-L'Allier (the Le George project).
The first four projects from December 10 drew no questions from the public.

On the rue Metcalfe project, questions dealt with the financial contribution for social housing, the opposition of the Comité logement Ville-Marie, the demolition timeline and the owner's obligation to inform the current tenants.
On the Le George project, questions dealt with the increase from 4 to 25 storeys, a floor area ratio of 15.89 instead of the maximum of 12, and keeping the housing affordable for 20 years.
On January 21, 2026 (about 7 people present), only one project was presented: the redevelopment of 90, rue Sainte-Catherine Est, with 60 affordable housing units planned.

At that meeting, the Comité logement Ville-Marie criticized the CMHC's affordability criteria and the exemptions that would allow the maximum height to be almost doubled; it was mentioned that the rental housing vacancy rate in Ville-Marie was 7.3% in October 2025.
The Ville-Marie borough council takes note of the minutes of the February 18, 2026 meeting of the committee that reviews demolition applications.
The committee approved the demolition of the building at 1821-1845, rue Atateken, to be replaced by a 4-storey residential building with 25 units; 5 objections had been received.

It also approved the demolition of 2360, rue Wurtele, for a 3-storey building with 5 units and a parking area, on the condition that the plans dated December 11, 2025 be followed and that the permit application be filed before the demolition certificate is issued.
The committee reviewed the demolition of 1355, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest (the Y des femmes building) for a mixed-use project of 30 storeys and 401 units; 6 objections were received.
During this last application, members of the public raised the loss of social housing and social services in the Peter-McGill district and the relocation of the Y des femmes.
Any interested person may appeal the committee's decisions to the borough council within 30 days.
The Ville-Marie borough council formally notes the filing of the minutes of the urban planning advisory committee meeting of March 12, 2026.

The document makes public the committee's opinion on about thirty planning files, including the construction of 425 housing units with a commercial space on the ground floor at 1175, rue Mackay (34 storeys, 110 m) — favourable opinion with conditions.

The committee also gave a favourable opinion, with conditions, on a 65 m residential tower with 332 housing units at 1600, avenue De Lorimier, on the site of the former savonnerie Barsalou destroyed by a fire on January 20, 2026.
Only one unfavourable opinion was issued, for the file at 1389, rue Saint-Jacques.
No money is committed by this decision.
The Ville-Marie borough council takes note of the filing of the minutes of the public consultation meeting held on April 29, 2026.
This meeting, which brought together about 9 people at 800, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, dealt with two specific projects.
First project: the construction, at 1175, rue Mackay, of a building that is taller and denser than what the planning by-law allows.
Some residents opposed it, citing the loss of view for neighbouring buildings, additional traffic and a ratio of 46 parking spaces for 800 people.
Second project: the amendment of a 2023 resolution to authorize a residential building at 1600, avenue De Lorimier. No one asked any questions.
The borough says that changes will be made to the resolution for the De Lorimier project before it is adopted at second reading.
The Ville-Marie borough council formally notes the filing of the follow-up report on written questions asked by residents between April 9 and April 14, 2026.

The report lists six questions, all of which received a follow-up on April 29, 2026, concerning the promotion of French in the Quartier des spectacles, a media interview request, the KJL garden in the Quartier chinois, a police intervention near the CSN, the synchronization of the traffic lights at Saint-Urbain and Président-Kennedy, and the closing of the YMCA du centre-ville.
For the KJL garden, the City answers that the land is not intended to become a permanent park and that the temporary garden may remain in place until the current agreement expires.
For the traffic lights at Saint-Urbain and Président-Kennedy, observations and checks will be made with the central city to assess whether adjustments are possible.
Residents were redirected, depending on the case, to the Partenariat du Quartier des spectacles, the SPVM complaint form, or the rebroadcast of the council meeting.
The Ville-Marie borough council takes note of a follow-up report on written questions asked by residents between April 30 and May 5, 2026.
Three questions are listed, all with follow-up done in May 2026 by the person in charge of support to elected officials.
One resident was informed about the role of the SHDM, about their rights as a tenant and about the resources available (comité logement, TAL, 311/BAM).
On the poorly fitted and noisy manhole covers on rue Hogan, following a drainage curb extension project, the borough says follow-ups will be made with its departments.
On the missing section of bike path on the promenade de la Commune, the borough answers that the area falls under the Vieux-Port (federal jurisdiction) and that it has begun steps with its partners.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a professional services contract worth $279,964.13 (taxes included) to the group made up of Beaupré Michaud et associés, Architectes, NCK inc. and Martin Roy et Associés inc.

The total authorized spending comes to $404,941.96, including $55,992.83 in contingencies and $68,985 in incidental expenses (high-level surveys, acoustics consultant, hazardous materials, additional studies).

The firms will prepare the plans and specifications and supervise the work site to redo the roofs, replace the rooftop cooling unit and carry out various work at the bibliothèque Mordecai-Richler, on avenue du Parc.
The document describes roofs that have outlived their lifespan (loose shingles, risk of water infiltration) and a cooling unit at the end of its life with refrigerant leaks.

The building, a former church dating from 1904 located in an area of exceptional heritage value, means the project will go before the Comité consultatif d'urbanisme; the work will have to preserve the building's heritage features.
Eight bids were submitted following the public call for tenders launched on December 3, 2025; the winning price is 63.35% below the internal estimate of $763,933.07.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is applying for a grant from the ministère de l'Éducation to renovate the Bain Lévesque, a public pool in the neighbourhood.
The provincial program (PAFIRSPA) can cover up to 66% of eligible work, up to a maximum of $20M.
The planned work involves the building envelope, the pool basin structure and the mechanical and electrical systems, in order to meet codes and standards and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
The borough commits to paying its minimum share, all non-eligible costs and any cost overruns, and to maintaining the facility.
The director of Administrative Services, Mélissa Cormier, is authorized to sign the agreement and the project documents.
The application must be submitted to the ministère no later than June 22, 2026.
A professional services contract of $810,844.66 had already been awarded in May 2024 to Hutte Architecture inc. for the rehabilitation of the building.

The borough of Outremont is tabling its 2025 annual report on the use of the power under the provincial housing act, which allows projects of three or more housing units to be authorized despite urban planning regulations.
Only one project was authorized in 2025: UTILE's project at 6600, rue Hutchison, and no application was refused.
This project involves a partial demolition, the restoration of a heritage building and an expansion for 184 housing units intended primarily for students, plus a commercial space on the ground floor.
The exemptions granted concern height, land occupancy, rooftop structures, the minimum number of parking spaces, the loading area and the location of garbage collection.
The report had to be tabled at the borough council no later than April 1, 2026; the tabling takes place on March 10, 2026.
The City's Service de l'habitation will send the report to the minister responsible for housing, and the information will be published online.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is giving $138,497 to seven organizations for summer 2026 activities (day camps and park projects).
The activities run from June 29 to August 21, 2026 and are aimed mainly at young people aged 5 to 15.

The amounts: Espace Multisoleil $60,355; Patro Villeray $21,069; Loisirs Communautaires Saint-Michel $19,900; Organisation des jeunes de Parc-Extension $17,813; Espace-Famille Villeray $10,000; Corporation d'éducation jeunesse $5,300; La joie des enfants $4,060.

Two camps are for young people with a disability: Espace Multisoleil (physical disability, ages 6 to 21, école Victor-Doré) and La Joie des enfants (intellectual disability, école Saint-Pierre-Apôtre).
The Espace-Famille Villeray park project offers free equipment lending and activities at parc De Normanville, from June 29 to August 14.
The day camps take place mainly in schools and community spaces in Villeray, Saint-Michel and Parc-Extension, including the aréna Howie-Morenz and the Maison du citoyen.
The money comes from the regular budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social; last year, the program received $127,857.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $12,000 to Loisirs communautaires Saint-Michel for the Activité Vélo 2026 project, from July to September 2026.
The money comes from the borough's reserve for special projects (surplus).
The organization will offer bike lending, cycling introduction courses and cycling activities at parc François-Perrault, free of charge or at low cost.
A temporary educational mini-course will be set up on the park's tennis court (non-permanent markings, movable signage, skills zones for beginners and children).
The project targets young people, families, seniors, women, recently arrived immigrants and low-income people.
Planned schedule: rollout in August 2026, wrap-up in November 2026, evaluation and review in October and November 2026.
The director of culture, sports, recreation and social development is authorized to sign the agreement on behalf of the City.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $400 to the Club de Volleyball Celtique for the participation of a LaSalle athlete, Amiel Cousineau, in the national volleyball championships.
The competition takes place in Calgary, Alberta, from May 29 to 31, 2026, in the U16 boys' category.

The amount follows LaSalle's Politique de reconnaissance et de soutien des organismes, under the "Soutien à la participation aux événements hors territoire laSallois" component, Alberta zone, one person.
The money is given to the athlete through the club, which is not a recognized LaSalle organization.
Travel and accommodation costs are estimated at $1,717.58 per athlete; the contribution reduces the share paid by the parents by that amount.
The expense comes from the operating budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing Association de soccer mineur de LaSalle inc. to sell food products and promotional items at parc Riverside, from April 11 to October 31, 2026.
The canteen will operate all season long, mainly during game hours; BBQs will be held on game days for the semi-professional leagues and during Soccerfest, on August 15, 2026.
The authorization lifts the by-law exemptions needed for these sales.
The organization must obtain all required permits, in particular from the Service incendie de Montréal and MAPAQ.
No financial impact for the borough; the profits are used to fund the club's activities.
A similar authorization had been granted in 2025, 2022 and 2021.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $300 to Club Calac Richelieu LaSalle inc.
The money is used to produce the souvenir program for a swimming competition for swimmers 12 and under.
The competition takes place on May 2 and 3, 2026, at the Complexe aquatique Michel-Leduc (Aquadôme).
About 450 swimmers are expected to take part.
In exchange, the borough gets visibility (advertising) in the souvenir program.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under the item for contributions to other organizations.
Contributions of $300 were granted to the same organization in 2015, 2018, 2022 and 2025.
The LaSalle borough authorizes the Ligue mineure de baseball LaSalle to apply for a liquor permit from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux du Québec.
The organization will be able to operate its canteen at Stade Éloi-Viau, in parc Riverside, from May 15 to October 30, 2026.
The canteen will serve hot meals, coffee, and non-alcoholic and alcoholic drinks during home games of the elite junior teams (AA and Les Cardinals).
Opening hours will follow the home game schedule; the organization must also obtain a permit from the MAPAQ.
The borough is granting the necessary exemptions from the by-laws. There is no financial impact for the City.
The canteen is a source of funding for this recognized non-profit organization; a similar authorization had been granted for the 2025 season.
The LaSalle borough authorizes the Association récréative du parc Riverside to sell food and promotional items (t-shirts, sweatshirts) at the piscine Riverside.
The association will also be allowed to hold barbecues during its competitions and social activities.
The authorization is valid from June 19 to August 30, 2026, during the pool's opening hours for the canteen.
The borough is granting the by-law exemptions needed to allow these sales.
The association will have to obtain all required permits itself (Service incendie de Montréal, MAPAQ, etc.).
According to the document, the decision has no financial impact for the City; the revenue is used to fund the association's activities.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $1,000 to Club Jeune Aire LaSalle.
The money helps 11 gymnasts aged 9 to 14 take part in the Challenge des Régions, in Gatineau, from May 14 to 17, 2026.
Trip costs (travel, registration, lodging, meals) are estimated at about $3,908 for the 11 athletes and 3 coaches.
The contribution is meant to lower the bill paid by parents.
The amount comes from the operating budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The support is based on LaSalle's Politique de reconnaissance, under the section on taking part in events outside the borough (groups of eight people or more within Québec).
The borough of LaSalle is allowing the Association du football mineur de LaSalle to sell food and items bearing the club's logo at parc Riverside, from May 4 to November 6, 2026.
The organization will also be able to hold barbecues outside the chalet during the game season, which starts in August.
The canteen will be open Monday to Thursday from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m., and on game weekends between 8:30 a.m. and 10 p.m.
On the menu: coffee, non-alcoholic drinks, hot dogs, grilled cheese and breakfasts.
The organization will have to notify the Service incendie about the barbecues and obtain a permit from the MAPAQ.

According to the document, the canteen's revenues are used to buy the equipment lent free of charge to players, to pay the league, the buses, the referees and the therapists, and to keep registration fees low.
No financial impact for the City.

The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the organization Circuit de tennis LaSalle to hold the 3rd edition of the "Tennis-o-thon" on Saturday, June 27, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., at the Centre de tennis Cavelier.
In case of rain, the event is postponed to June 28 or July 4.
Players will take turns all day long to raise money and food.
Volunteers will also collect donations at the corners of 80e Avenue and boulevard LaSalle, as well as 80e Avenue and rue Airlie.
All donations will go to Société H.O.P.E, which provides food assistance to disadvantaged people in LaSalle.
The 2025 edition raised $498 in donations, in addition to non-perishable food items.
The document states that there is no financial impact for the City.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is hiring Première équipe Architecture inc. to design a new service building at parc du Fort, in Pointe-aux-Trembles, for $162,114.75 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $202,643.44, which includes $24,317.21 in contingencies and $16,211.48 in incidental costs.
The planned building will include a refreshment stand with a counter, at least two universally accessible washrooms, a storage space and water points.
The current refreshment stand, which the borough considers outdated, will be demolished and relocated elsewhere in the same park.
Announced schedule: design and call for tenders from March 2026 to February 2027, construction work from March 2027 to October 2027.
Ten firms submitted bids; the winning bid is $35,791.02 (18.08%) lower than the internal estimate of $197,905.77.
The borough will not carry out a performance evaluation of the selected firm for this contract.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough council is authorizing the construction of a residential building at 5505, rue Chauveau, in the PPU Assomption Nord area.
The project calls for 605 housing units (studios, 1 to 3 bedrooms and townhouses) over 12 storeys, with 2 basement levels.
The basements will include 274 parking spaces for vehicles and 211 for bicycles; the roof will have terraces and 2 pools.
The layout provides for 34.5% greening, 84 trees planted and green roofs.
The urban planning advisory committee issued two unfavourable opinions (February 6 and March 6, 2026); the council is authorizing the work nonetheless.
The universal access ramp will stay in its planned location: according to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain and the applicant, moving it would mean removing trees and adding more paved surface.
There is no financial aspect attached to this file.
The City is giving $525,000 to the Musée des Hospitalières de l'Hôtel-Dieu de Montréal, that is $175,000 per year from 2026 to 2028, for its operations and activities.
The cost is paid 100% by the central city, through the Service de la culture.
The Musée is located at the Cité-des-Hospitalières, on avenue des Pins Ouest, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, in a building the City bought in 2017 and has owned since May 2019.
Since May 2019, the Religieuses Hospitalières de Saint-Joseph no longer fund the Musée, which keeps a collection of 30,000 artifacts.

In return, the Musée plans an interpretation trail covering the whole site, including the monastery, new exhibitions, an educational program on the Hôtel-Dieu institutions and Mont-Royal, programming for vulnerable people and tourists, and a collections development plan.
The grant makes up 24% of the Musée's projected budget in 2026, then about 28% in 2027 and 2028.
City council must also approve the agreement that sets the payment conditions.
The City wants to borrow $2,361,700 to make financial contributions to the Musée Pointe-à-Callière, in Vieux-Montréal.

From 2026 to 2028, the money will be used to replace the permanent exhibitions, the technological and museum equipment, to preserve and restore the archaeological remains, and to renew a group of virtual characters.
Part of it will also fund the preliminary studies for phase 3 of the Museum's development, whose visitor reception facilities have exceeded their capacity according to the document.
The loan by-law must be approved by the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing before its final adoption.
Planned schedule: notice of motion at city council in March 2026, approval by the Ministry in April 2026, adoption in April 2026.
The loan must be repaid over a maximum period of 5 years; the amounts are provided for in the 2026-2035 investment program.

Since June 6, 2024, the Maison Nivard-De Saint-Dizier, a museum and archaeological site in Verdun, has come under the central city (city council) rather than the borough, following a change to the Charte de Montréal.
City council is therefore ratifying all the decisions made by the arrondissement de Verdun about this museum since that date, to make them official.
It also agrees that Verdun will continue to manage the museum until the city and the borough reach an agreement on the division of roles, funding and maintenance.
This regularization allows Verdun to submit, before July 2026, the application to renew the museum accreditation from the ministère de la Culture, valid for 2027-2031.
This accreditation gives access to financial assistance programs from the Government of Québec.
The borough council must officially offer to take charge of the museum at its meeting of June 30, 2026.
The file involves no spending (financial aspect: not applicable).
The City is appointing three elected officials to represent it on the board of directors of the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) until the end of the 2025-2026 term.

They are Amélie Cliche (borough councillor, Outremont), Gerlando Guarraggi (borough councillor, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles) and Sonny Moroz (city councillor, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce).
These three people replace the representatives appointed in May 2025 (Josefina Blanco, Kaila Amaya-Munro and Sylvain Ouellet).
Montréal automatically holds three of the 12 Québec seats on the FCM board of directors, which has 75 seats in all.
The resolution must reach the FCM before its special meeting on February 2, 2026, called following the fall municipal elections in Québec, Alberta and Newfoundland and Labrador.
A new resolution will be needed in May for the 2026-2027 term. The decision involves no spending.
The City is appointing three elected officials to represent it on the board of directors of the Fédération canadienne des municipalités (FCM) during the 2026-2028 term.
They are Amélie Cliche (borough councillor, Outremont), Gerlando Guarraggi (borough councillor, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles) and Sophie Mohsen (city councillor, Pierrefonds-Roxboro).
The FCM brings together more than 2,000 members and defends municipal interests with the federal government; its board of directors has 75 members and meets every three months.
Québec holds 12 seats on this board, three of which are reserved automatically for Montréal.
The resolution must be sent to the FCM before its annual general meeting, scheduled for June 4 to 7, 2026.
This file involves no spending.

The City is authorizing the Société du parc Jean-Drapeau to award TRO-CHAÎNES inc. the modernization of the Complexe aquatique du parc Jean-Drapeau, for a total expense of $22,714,489.87, taxes included.
The contract itself is worth $18,928,741.56, plus $2,839,311.23 in contingencies (15%) and $946,437.08 in incidental expenses (5%).

The work covers waterproofing the three pools, replacing the filtration and disinfection systems, new secure chlorine storage, bringing the lighting up to standard, the concrete of the pools and the promenade, and removing the water games.
The work will be carried out in two lots over 3 years, with a partial summer aquatic program maintained; the work is expected to be completed in mid-June 2028.

Only one contractor submitted a bid out of 14 sets of tender documents taken; the SPJD attributes this to the complexity of aquatic projects and to phasing constraints. The gap with the estimate is 2.58% ($475,907.24).
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration, since parc Jean-Drapeau is an agglomeration responsibility, and is financed through a loan by-law.
Lachine agrees to let the borough of Ville-Marie send in a public works team trained to respond in places where there are homelessness and public space coexistence issues.
The team mainly does clean-up work; it will come to Lachine occasionally, as needed, during the day, from Tuesday to Friday.
The agreement lasts 12 months starting from the acceptance of the offer on May 4, 2026.

The team has 8 people (one foreman and 7 blue-collar workers) and 4 vehicles: one packer truck and four pickup trucks; a pickup truck with two employees will be added in 2026 for more minor interventions.
The locations for interventions will be chosen jointly by the Lachine teams and the Ville-Marie managers.
The budget comes from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and is transferred to Ville-Marie: no additional cost for Lachine.

The City justifies the measure by the increase in the number of people experiencing homelessness and by the fact that the boroughs concerned do not have enough interventions to create their own dedicated teams.
The borough of Lachine is taking $265,000 from its surplus to strengthen cleanliness and maintenance of streets and parks during the 2026 summer season.
Three teams of two employees are being added for the summer, then two teams from September 18 to November 13.
The amount covers $230,500 for hiring staff and $34,500 for equipment and rentals, in particular pickup trucks.
Overtime will be paid to cover peak periods.
Without this appropriation, the project could not be carried out in 2026, according to the document.
No specific communications are planned: information about the summer program will follow the borough's usual process.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is authorizing a maximum expense of $1,182 to send three elected officials to the Sommet Climat Montréal 2026.
The participants are borough mayor Dominic Perri, city councillor Arij El Korbi and borough councillor Linda Paquin.
The event takes place on April 16, 2026, at the Grand Quai du Port de Montréal.
Registration fees are $394 per participant, taxes included.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The Sommet is organized by the Partenariat Climat Montréal, in collaboration with the Ville.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is paying up to $161.88 (taxes included) to send four elected officials to the evening event revealing the finalists of the Concours ESTim 2026.
The participants are councillors Arij El Korbi, Gemma Marchione and Linda Paquin, as well as councillor Mauro Barone.
The event takes place on March 17, 2026 at the Bain Mathieu, at 2915, rue Ontario.
Registration costs $35 per person, plus fees and taxes; the amount is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The Concours ESTim, now in its 38th year, gives awards to businesses located in the territory of the Chambre de commerce de l'Est de Montréal.
