The borough submitted a project to add greenery to parking lots.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is approving the 2026 schedule for seven commercial promotions organized by four SDCs and three merchants' associations.
Street closures: Saint-Denis (Roy to Gilford) from May 14 to 18 for the Festival BD, and Saint-Laurent (Sherbrooke to Laurier) from June 4 to 14 for MURAL and from September 3 to 6 for BLVD.
Two commercial fairs on avenue du Mont-Royal (Saint-Laurent to d'Iberville) from May 28 to 31 and from August 27 to 30, during the pedestrianization.
Mile-End en fête from May 22 to 24 in the Mile-End and on Laurier Ouest (Saint-Laurent to Hutchison), with streets kept open to traffic; some closures are still being studied.

The orders allow the sale and consumption of alcohol on public property, the sale of food, street entertainment, furniture and terraces, outdoor music and stages, as well as marking the roadway with chalk and water-soluble paint.
Three other promotional projects are still being reviewed and will come back in later files.
The associations' request to extend store opening hours until 11 p.m. falls under city council and will be handled in a separate file.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is asking city council to let stores stay open later during the 2026 commercial promotions.
Stores could stay open until 11 p.m. on avenue du Mont-Royal (Saint-Laurent to De Lorimier) from May 28 to 31 and from August 27 to 30, and on rue Saint-Denis (Roy to Gilford) from May 14 to 18.
Stores could stay open until 11 p.m. on boulevard Saint-Laurent for the MURAL festival from June 4 to 14 and the BLVD festival from September 3 to 6, with one extended night to be set later.
Stores could stay open until 10 p.m. in the Mile End and on avenue Laurier Ouest (Clark to Hutchison) from May 22 to 24 for "Mile End en fête".
The requests come from the commercial development corporations (Mont-Royal, Saint-Denis, Saint-Laurent, Laurier Ouest) and from the Mile End business people's association (AGAME).
No financial aspect is planned in the file; city council is to make its decision on April 20.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing two commercial promotions in 2026: Duluth Pop and an addition to Mile-End en Fête.
Duluth Pop will be held from July 1 to 5 on avenue Duluth, between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Hubert, during the summer pedestrianization.
During Duluth Pop: sale and consumption of alcohol on public property, food sales, roving musicians and entertainment, and terraces open until 11 p.m.
Background music on the terraces is allowed up to a maximum of 65 dBA measured 5 metres from the speakers.

For Mile-End en Fête: closure of Saint-Viateur Ouest (Parc to Saint-Urbain) from May 22 at 10 a.m. to May 25 at 5 a.m., and of Laurier Ouest (Clark to Saint-Urbain) from May 23 at 7 a.m. to May 25 at 5 a.m.
The request by Duluth merchants to keep their businesses open until 11 p.m. will have to be approved separately by city council.
No spending is attached to this decision.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is asking city council to allow businesses on avenue Duluth to stay open until 11 p.m. from July 1 to 5, 2026.
The exemption would apply to avenue Duluth, between rue Saint-Laurent and rue Saint-Hubert, during a commercial promotion.
The request comes from the association des commerçants de l'Avenue Duluth, which wants to take advantage of increased foot traffic beyond the usual business hours.
Since 2017, city council has been able to set the hours during which customers may be admitted to businesses for special events; each request must be validated by the borough.
The file is to go before city council on June 15, 2026, ahead of the promotion running from July 1 to 5.
No spending is associated with this decision.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is adding $20,000 to the grant for the Société de développement commercial (SDC) Laurier Ouest for 2026, bringing its total from $25,000 to $45,000.
The money is for the Mile End en fête event, which will take place from May 22 to 24 on avenue Laurier Ouest and rue Saint-Viateur Ouest.

The amount will fund the cultural programming and a visitor traffic study, in a context where rue Saint-Viateur is being closed for the first time and the event is being held on the same weekend as the Formula 1 Grand Prix.
According to the borough, the data collected will be used to support funding for future editions, notably from Tourisme Montréal and the ministère du Tourisme du Québec.
The $20,000 comes from the borough's surpluses; the support is described as exceptional and non-recurring.
The order is to be adopted on May 4; the SDC will then file its grant application.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is approving four commercial promotions that will take place during the UCI Road World Championships, from September 19 to 27, 2026.
The SDC Avenue du Mont-Royal is holding a commercial fair from September 24 to 27, with the closure of Saint-Laurent to De Lorimier.

The SDC Saint-Denis will animate the street from September 17 to 27 (des Pins to Gilford), the SDC Laurier Ouest from September 19 to 27 (Clark to Hutchison) and the SDC Boulevard Saint-Laurent on September 19 and 20 (Sherbrooke to Laurier).

Ordinances allow the occupation of public property, street closures, background music on terraces, extended hours for sidewalk cafés, the sale and consumption of alcohol, the display and sale of goods and food, street entertainment and roadway marking with chalk or soluble paint.
The borough says the commercial streets will be affected by increased traffic toward parc Jeanne-Mance and by traffic obstructions, notably on Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis.
A separate request will be submitted to city council to extend business opening hours during these promotions.
The file involves no spending: the financial section states "does not apply."

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is asking city council to allow businesses in five areas to stay open later during the Championnats du monde route UCI and the commercial promotions of September 2026.
Avenue du Mont-Royal (Saint-Laurent to Lorimier): open until 11 p.m. from September 24 to 27.
Rue Saint-Denis (des Pins to Gilford) and avenue Duluth (Saint-Laurent to Saint-Hubert): until 11 p.m. from September 17 to 27 for Saint-Denis and from September 19 to 27 for Duluth.
Avenue Laurier Ouest (Saint-Laurent to Hutchison): until 10 p.m. from September 19 to 27.
Boulevard Saint-Laurent (Sherbrooke to Laurier): until 11 p.m. on September 19 and 20.
The requests come from the commercial development corporations and the Association des commerçants de l'avenue Duluth; the file has no financial impact.
Next step: going to city council on August 24, 2026.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is adding $100,000 in 2026 to the "activities" portion of the budgets of the four commercial development corporations (SDCs), raising this portion from $250,000 to $350,000.
New amounts for activities: Mont-Royal $117,063, Saint-Laurent $131,771, Saint-Denis $72,643 and Laurier Ouest $48,523 (including one-time assistance of $20,000 already granted in May 2026).
With pedestrianization and nighttime vitality, the totals reach $692,063 for Mont-Royal, $171,771 for Saint-Laurent, $72,643 for Saint-Denis and $48,523 for Laurier Ouest.
The breakdown is based on two criteria each counting for 50%: the number of commercial units on the street and its length in kilometres.
The borough explains that the amounts had not changed since 2023, while costs (event security, cleanliness, beautification) have gone up and the distribution among the SDCs was uneven.
The $100,000 comes from the borough director's special projects budget; the SDCs will submit their applications and carry out their projects from July to December 2026.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is paying $72,500 to the Association des gens d'affaires du Mile End (AGAME) and $30,000 to the Alliance des commerçants de l'avenue du Parc (ACAP), for a total expense of $102,500.
The money comes from a $145,000 transfer from the Service du développement économique; the borough says it is covering no costs.
Payments are spread out: $70,000 in 2026 and $32,500 in 2027. The projects must be completed by June 9, 2027.
In Milton-Parc, ACAP will carry out communications activities: banners, a map and profiles of merchants, and targeted communications aimed at students.
In the Mile End, AGAME will work on its long-term funding after 2028 and on organizing Mile-End-en-fête, which includes closing rue Saint-Viateur.
A remaining balance of $42,500 for beautification and the identity of Milton-Parc has yet to be awarded at a later council meeting.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève approves the rebuilding of a detached single-family home at 494, rue Raymond.
The previous house was destroyed by a fire in 2025 and completely demolished.
The new house will be rebuilt on the existing foundations, with an extension at the back: 8.28 m wide, 14.15 m deep, 117.16 m², two storeys and a maximum height of 10.67 m.
The architecture takes up the "lucarne-pignon" (gable dormer) style of the original house, in an area with a village-like fabric near the rivière des Prairies.
The approved materials: Meridian Old Markham brick, Moderno expresso wood-look steel, glacier white soffits, fascias and door and window trim, Jade Everest 42 green asphalt shingles.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme (urban planning advisory committee) suggests multi-pane windows over half of the glazed surface on the front façade and white framing around those windows.
Reviewed by the comité consultatif d'urbanisme on March 17, 2026, then by the borough council on April 7, 2026.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is allowing two commercial signs to be installed at 120, boulevard Jacques-Bizard.
The signs will identify a Consignaction drop-off point, where people will be able to bring back their deposit containers (aluminum, plastic, glass) and get their deposit refunded.
This drop-off point is the first in the borough; it is set up in a unit of the shopping centre located at 100, boulevard Jacques-Bizard.
A green sign measuring 3.04 m by 0.73 m will go on the canopy, lit by gooseneck lamps like the other businesses; a second one measuring 1.27 m by 0.7 m will be added to the community pylon sign.
Neither sign will be backlit; the lettering and logo will have a relief of 1.27 cm, compared with about 2.5 cm for the Familiprix sign and 1.9 cm for the Sanned sign.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with conditions on March 17, 2026; the borough council made its decision on April 7, 2026.
The file does not involve any spending.

The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is asking the Minister of Municipal Affairs for six more months to adopt its planning by-laws in line with Montréal's Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050, adopted in June 2025.
The law gives boroughs 180 days to bring their regulations into conformity; the borough had already obtained a first 6-month extension in July 2025.
Without an extension, the borough would be in default and could no longer, except in special cases, amend its planning regulations until the default is corrected.

The reasons given: a lack of staff and turnover in the urban planning department, the complexity of the territory (village cores, agricultural zone, humanized landscape, nature park), coordination with the Service de l'urbanisme and the impact of the fall 2025 election.
The borough plans to present the project to elected officials starting in mid-June 2026 and to hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.
The borough secretary will send the resolution and the supporting documents to the Minister; the decision will be published in the Gazette officielle du Québec and then on the City's website.
No spending is associated with this file.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is approving the construction of a detached single-family house at 264, rue Joly.
The lot has been vacant since 2021, after the house that stood there burned down.
Condition imposed: the house must be set 9.3 metres back from the street, instead of the 11.9 metres proposed, to line up with the neighbouring houses (average setback of about 7.5 m).
The house will have two storeys, a height of 9.6 m, and will be 13.74 m long by 10.36 m deep, with a built-in garage for two cars.
The exterior materials are set: polar-coloured stone, desert and smoked black steel panels, snow white vinyl, barn wood asphalt shingles, and black trim and soffits.
The house will be visible from rue Cherrier, the waterfront route of île Bizard; openings have been added on the right side façade.
The decision is scheduled for the borough council meeting of May 5, 2026, following the favourable opinion of the comité consultatif d'urbanisme on April 21, 2026.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is approving the exterior renovation of a heritage house at 15 844, rue de la Caserne, built in 1890 and included on the list of heritage buildings.

The work includes replacing the blue cedar shingles with the same material and the same colour, restoring eight windows, and replacing the white pine window frames and the gable trim with identical ones.
A large window on the front facade will be replaced by a yellow glass door with no panes, and the two side doors on the front facade will become windows.
Two conditions are imposed: the two new windows must have six panes across the whole glass area.
Another condition: the outside staircase on the front facade and the lattice under the porch must be rebuilt exactly as they were in 2022.
The property is covered by the PIIA by-law because it is located in the exceptional-value sector of the village of Sainte-Geneviève.
The urban planning advisory committee reviewed the project on April 21, 2026, and the borough council made its decision on May 5, 2026.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is banning vehicle traffic at certain entrances to four lanes and having the signs changed accordingly.

Lanes affected: east of 5e Avenue (between Saint-Joseph Est and Gilford), east of Boyer (between Bellechasse and Beaubien Est), east of Davidson (between Sherbrooke Est and Rachel Est) and east of 24e Avenue (between Bellechasse and Beaubien Est).

Two of the closures come from requests by lane committees in the Ruelles vertes program, supported by 70% and 67% of the residents living along them; the others come from the lane safety program in place since 2023.
The closed sections will have flower boxes, planting beds or a country-style path, with greening projects planned for the summer of 2026.

The borough is paying for the purchase and installation of the boxes or country-style entrances and for the soil; the lane committees are responsible for maintaining the plants (watering, weeding, replacement).
The closures that are not already in place will be installed in April and May 2026.
The Éco-quartier (Nature Action Québec) will inform the lane committees, and notices will be delivered door to door to the people concerned.
The urban agglomeration awards a $1,052,017.94 contract (taxes included) to 4455878 Canada inc. (Bruser) to inspect 22 pumping stations on the main sewer network.
The mandate lasts 12 months and includes visual inspections, 360° cameras, thermographic testing, vibration analyses, noise measurements and concrete inspection.
The firm must provide reports for each station, technical data sheets and a database to update the pumping station renewal plan.
Two firms submitted bids out of the six that had obtained the tender documents; Bruser received the best score.
The selected price is $283,023.75 (37%) higher than the City's estimate, which the Service de l'eau attributes to the spread of market prices and to the technical complexity.
The second bid, from GBI Experts-Conseils inc., came to $1,902,836.25.
The expense will be paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, and the firm's performance will be evaluated.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is asking city council for permission to design and carry out itself the repair of sidewalk sections on arterial streets in its territory, which normally fall under the central city's responsibility.
About 388.48 m² of sidewalks would be rebuilt; the list of streets involved is attached to the file.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier has agreed to fund $276,000, whereas the program had set aside $250,000 for the borough in 2026.
The expense of $276,064 (net of tax rebates) is funded by a central city loan by-law and paid entirely in 2026.
The borough cites requests from residents and pedestrian safety to justify the work, and says it wants to prevent falls and injuries.
The sidewalks chosen come ahead of paving work planned for 2027; sections not completed under the 2025 contract are also included.
Planned timeline: city council decision on April 20, 2026, call for tenders from April 24 to May 26, contract on July 6, work in the summer and fall of 2026.
The City is extending by 12 months, from January 1 to December 31, 2027, the pest management and control contract in the Espace pour la vie museums, awarded to Boisvert Gestion Parasitaire inc.
Additional expense of $141,618.36 including taxes: $128,743.96 for the contract and $12,874.40 in contingencies (10%).
The total contract goes from $424,855.04 to $566,473.40, including taxes; the cost is covered entirely by the central city.
The expense is divided between the Jardin botanique ($65,478.93), the Biodôme ($48,838.44) and the Insectarium ($27,300.99).

The company controls rodents, harmful insects and other animals (e.g. raccoons) using methods that protect the animal, entomological and plant collections, while following the rules on pesticides and wildlife.
The document states that without this contract, the Biodôme could not maintain its international accreditations, which are in the process of being renewed.
The rates from the original bid (call for tenders 23-20168) stay the same; this is the second and last extension option provided for.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is giving $135,000 to the Regroupement des Tables de Concertation de La Petite-Patrie (RTCPP), from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029.
The money is split into three payments of $45,000 a year (2026-2027, 2027-2028, 2028-2029).
The funded project, "Ensemble pour l'Est, renforcer le pôle communautaire!", aims to fill the gap in community services in the eastern part of La Petite-Patrie.
The funds come from the ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale, through the agreement to fight poverty and social exclusion (MESS-Ville 2024-2029).
Three organizations submitted an application during the call for projects held from October 10 to November 21, 2025; a selection committee recommended the RTCPP.
The director of culture, sports, recreation and social development is authorized to sign the agreement and to adjust the project's parameters, without going over the amount granted.

The City is giving $1,500,000 to the École de technologie supérieure over three years to set up Ax.c, an entrepreneurship space of about 100,000 sq. ft. located on the former trading floor of the Bourse and two floors of Place Victoria, downtown.
The money is to be used to offer affordable rents to startups, to host foreign delegations and to raise the profile of Montréal startups.
The payments are planned as follows: $400,000 in 2026, $500,000 in 2027, $500,000 in 2028 and $100,000 in 2029.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration, out of the Réflexe 3 envelope ($200M agreement with the MEIE 2025-2029).
The ÉTS must report each year, in June, and apply a City visibility protocol.

The City had already granted up to $2,500,000 to the ÉTS in April 2023 for the fit-out and operation of this space; Ax.c opened in June 2025 and brings together 87 organizations, including 43 startups.
The City's support represents 6% of the project's total cost.
The City is giving $900,000 to the organization Essor économique Québec Tech between 2026 and 2029 to develop Montréal's tech start-up ecosystem.
The payments are spread out as follows: $240,000 in 2026, $300,000 in 2027, $300,000 in 2028 and $60,000 in 2029.
First part: each year, support 25 established businesses facing productivity issues, qualify 400 start-ups and take part in three business events to create connections.
Special attention will be given to businesses in the East of Montréal, as well as to the sectors of digital sovereignty, AI, robotics, defence, cybersecurity and optimization.
Second part: produce data and statistics on Montréal start-ups, create a digital showcase, translate the Radar web directory into French and hold two outreach activities per year.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration and comes from the Réflexe 3 envelope (a $200M agreement with the MEIE for 2025-2029).
The organization will have to report each year in June and apply a visibility protocol.
The City is increasing its agreement on the agri-food sector in Montréal: the total amount rises to $1,212,000, an increase of $137,000.

The ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation is adding up to $87,000, and the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie is joining the agreement with up to $50,000.
The City is not increasing its contribution: it covers 19% of the total, compared with 77% for the MAPAQ and 4% for the MEIE.
The money is used to fund projects in urban agriculture, food processing, the fight against waste and access to Québec products within the agglomeration's territory.
A steering committee made up of the City and the two ministries will choose the projects that get funding; the City coordinates and manages the agreement.
The agreement runs until 2027; the $137,000 is split between 2026 and 2027.
The City is signing an agreement worth $1,402,740 with Québec (Agriculture, Économie, Emploi) to develop Montréal's agri-food sector from 2026 to 2029.
The ministries are contributing up to $1,122,240 ($1,022,240 from the MAPAQ, $100,000 from the MEIE) and the City is putting in $280,500 taken from its 2026, 2027 and 2028 operating budgets.
The City is authorizing an additional revenue and expenditure budget of $1,122,240 for the Service du développement économique, spread out from 2026 to 2029.
The money will go to projects in three areas: promoting the sector and its skills, productivity and innovation (including digital), and the circular economy and the socio-ecological transition.
The ministère de l'Emploi is contributing advisory support for businesses and access to government assistance programs, rather than money.
A steering committee made up of the three ministries and the Service du développement économique will choose which projects get funded; the City coordinates and manages the agreement.

The City is also signing a $150,000 agreement with the ministère de l'Économie (Programme d'appui aux projets de développement économique), consisting of $100,000 for the new agreement and $50,000 for the 2023-2025 agreement.
The City is adding $50,000 to the funding for the Conseil des Industries Bioalimentaires de l'île de Montréal (CIBIM) for its project "Les Rendez-vous bioalimentaires de Montréal".
The total of the agreement with CIBIM therefore goes from $50,000 to $100,000, for activities carried out from October 15, 2025 to December 31, 2026.
CIBIM had asked for $100,000 back in June 2025, but received only $50,000 because Québec expected to fund the other half through another envelope; that funding ultimately did not come from there.
The additional $50,000 comes 100% from the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie, through the Montréal–Québec bioalimentaire agreement.
The expense is covered by the urban agglomeration of Montréal and, according to the document, has no impact on the City's financial framework.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council; the organization will have to comply with a visibility protocol.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough ends 2025 with a management surplus of $3,081,300.
Of that amount, $3,002,099 goes to "free surpluses," which the borough will be able to use for various needs.
$42,861 goes to the contingency reserve, bringing it to the maximum allowed (1.5% of the 2026 budget of $72,833,200).
$36,340 goes to the snow removal reserve, thereby reaching the target of $2,724,000.
No addition to the occupational health and safety reserve, as the target has already been reached.
The surplus comes from $711,500 in borough operations and $2,369,800 in year-end adjustments made by the Ville.
The decision is conditional on city council adopting the surplus policy in June.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is awarding the security service for the Maison du citoyen to Sécuriteq inc. for $238,601.41, taxes included.
The contract covers two years, from May 5, 2026 to May 4, 2028, with three possible one-year extensions.
Two security guards will be on site each business day: one from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., the other from 3 p.m. to 11 p.m.
The contract includes a bank of 250 hours per year for additional security during borough events.
Sécuriteq submitted the lowest of the 14 bids received, at 2.52% ($6,172.29) below the City's estimate.
The same company had already been providing this service since May 2023.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is closing 43 loan by-laws adopted since 2005, whose projects are now completed.
These loans were used in particular for road repairs, infrastructure in new residential developments and vehicle replacement.
The loan amounts set out in these by-laws are being reduced to the amounts actually used, according to appendix A of the file.
The borough is asking the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation to cancel the unused loan balances in its records.
According to the document, this operation has no impact on the borough's budgets.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is hiring Univap inc. to do the cleaning at the Maison du citoyen, at 12090, rue Notre-Dame Est.
The contract is worth $206,955, taxes included, from July 8, 2026 to July 8, 2028, with two renewal options.
Univap inc. was the lowest of the 4 bidders in public call for tenders 26-21414.
The contract covers evening cleaning on weekdays, one annual deep cleaning between April 15 and May 15, and 250 hours of special services per year.
The borough will carry out a performance evaluation of the company.
The previous cleaning contract for this building had been awarded without a call for tenders to Groupe MMI inc. for $104,650.72 (June 2025 to June 2026).
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is changing who pays for what in the redevelopment of parc Campbell Ouest (unification work, landscaping and lighting), without changing the total cost of the project.

The change is meant to include a $180,773 grant (net of rebates) obtained to create a community garden in the park, paid by the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne.
The planned community garden includes more than 285 m² of in-ground garden and 420 m² of food forest.

New funding breakdown: Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports $2,162,547.49 (68%), Service de l'eau $402,700.25 (13%), concertation des arrondissements $197,970 (6%), borough of Le Sud-Ouest $431,401.91 (13%), taxes included.
The share paid by the Service des grands parcs goes from 74% to 68% of the total investment.

Some already approved expenses (street furniture, soil testing, materials monitoring, fees and soil traceability) are being charged to different budgets, mainly the local parks rehabilitation program.
The work was awarded in December 2024 to Les Entreprises Rose Neige; the total contract expense had been raised to $3,169,386.03 in December 2025.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is abolishing its standing committees of the borough council, which had existed since 2002 and were governed by a by-law adopted in March 2010.
The new council elected in November 2025 instead wants to manage the borough's affairs through a priorities committee.
The repealing by-law is scheduled to be adopted on March 9, 2026, and to come into force on March 10, 2026.
The file involves no spending; no financial aspect is indicated.
Saint-Léonard is amending its Règlement sur les nuisances to support pollinators and biodiversity.
The limit on grass height will no longer apply from March 1 to May 31, during the spring season.
The borough is repealing the provision and the schedule that identified certain plants as "weeds".

The changes come from recommendations by the Bureau de la transition écologique et de la résilience, as part of the Plan Montréal : territoire de biodiversité par la protection des pollinisateurs 2022-2027.
Adoption is planned for April 7, 2026, with a public notice of coming into force on April 8, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is creating an additional yearly payment for the vice-chair of its planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme).
This payment is set at 50% of what the chair of the planning advisory committee receives.
The request comes from the new borough council elected in the general election of November 2025.
A public notice must come before the adoption, planned for March 10, 2026; the adoption is planned for April 7, 2026 and it comes into force on April 8, 2026.
The document does not give any dollar amount for this payment.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is changing the rules for its public question period at borough council meetings.
The question period can only be extended once, for a maximum of 30 minutes.
Each question will have to be asked in 2 minutes or less; the limit is 2 minutes per question, and a resident can ask 2 questions.
The change comes from the new council elected in November 2025, which wants to better manage how the question period runs.
The by-law is set to be adopted on April 7, 2026, with a public notice of coming into force on April 8, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is approving changes to the general by-laws (internal rules) of the Société de développement commercial de la rue Jean-Talon.
The SDC itself asked for these changes; the document does not say what they are.
The law requires the City to approve the internal rules of SDCs, and this power is delegated to borough councils.
This SDC's internal rules were adopted in 2008 and amended once, in 2016.
According to the borough, the changes comply with its Règlement sur les sociétés de développement commercial.
No money is attached to this decision.
The borough of Saint-Léonard appoints Dany Desrosiers, secretary-researcher, as substitute borough secretary.
He will be able to replace the borough secretary in case of illness, vacation or major impediment.
The position of borough secretary has been held on an interim basis by Sara Parent St-Laurent since December 2025, following the retirement of Guylaine Champoux.
Anne-Sophie Bergeron already acts as substitute borough secretary; the appointment adds a resource.
Dany Desrosiers has been a secretary-researcher since April 11.
The document does not mention any amount or financial aspect.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is preparing a new by-law (2299) that will govern excavation work on private land located near the street.

A permit will now be required to dig on private land when the excavation is too close to the street line: less than 2 m deep if the distance is less than the depth, and 2 m or more if the distance is less than twice the depth.
The by-law will set standards for work such as backfilling, shoring and blasting.
The borough will be able to require advance payment of the costs of repairing public property, as well as a security deposit covering public utilities, public property and street furniture.
A fee for issuing the excavation permit will be added to the 2026 fees by-law at the same time.
The borough points to the many construction sites related to the extension of the métro's blue line on land next to public property.
Adoption is planned for September 8, 2026, with the public notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The Saint-Léonard borough wants to add new permit fees to its 2026 fees by-law.
An excavation permit on private land would cost $150.
A permit for snow removal work on the private land of an industrial, commercial or institutional property would cost $50 (one vehicle included), plus $25 per additional vehicle.
These fees go with two by-laws being prepared: a new by-law on excavations on private property and an amendment to the nuisances by-law requiring snow removal contractors to obtain a permit.
The borough links these changes to the many construction projects planned on private land next to public property because of the extension of the metro's blue line.
The text also corrects a cross-reference in section 12, so that it points to the new by-law on site planning and architectural integration programmes.
Adoption is planned for September 8, 2026, with a public notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The Saint-Léonard borough announces that it will amend its by-law on the delegation of powers to officers and employees (by-law 2119).
The goal: bring this by-law in line with the new Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, in force since April 1.
The changes are mostly about wording: « octroi » becomes « attribution », and references to the Loi sur les cités et villes are replaced with references to the new law.
The borough director gets the power to choose how bids are assessed (overall assessment of the criteria, or price revealed later) for borough contracts.
Notice of motion given on July 6, 2026; adoption of the by-law planned for September 8, 2026.

Saint-Léonard wants to require contractors who clear snow from private industrial, commercial or institutional properties to obtain a permit from the borough, valid from June 1 to May 31 and non-transferable.
The permit will cost $50 for the first registered vehicle and $25 for each additional vehicle.

The contractor will have to declare each vehicle used, display the permit on each vehicle and install an identification post with the contractor's name and telephone number near each parking lot entrance.
The owner of an industrial, commercial or institutional property will have to make sure that their snow removal contractor holds a valid permit.
Any failure to comply will be treated as a nuisance; the borough says it wants to prevent snow from private properties from being pushed onto public property.
The by-law is scheduled to be adopted on September 8, 2026, with the notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026; communications will be sent to the owners concerned.
City council is once again adopting the Code d'éthique et de déontologie du personnel de cabinet de la Ville de Montréal, with no changes from the 2022 version.
Québec law requires the City to review this code after each general election and to adopt it before May 1, 2026 — the election was held in November 2025.
The code applies to staff in political offices, including those of borough mayors, and sets rules for real, apparent or potential conflicts of interest.
For 12 months after leaving, a former political office employee cannot hold a position that would draw an undue advantage from their former duties.
A person in a conflict of interest must put an end to it within three months of their appointment or of discovering the situation.
Chiefs of staff must file a declaration of interests with the city clerk's office within 60 days of their appointment, and then every year.
No spending is tied to this file. Notice of motion on March 23, 2026, adoption planned for April 20, 2026.
The City is adding $113,996.31 (taxes included) to the electricity and lighting contract for the hôtel de ville, awarded to Les installations électriques Pichette inc.
With this addition, the contract rises to $1,351,965.25, taxes included. It had been awarded in February 2024 for $1,237,968.94.
The amount serves as a contingency budget for lot L2604 "Électricité - Éclairage et travaux connexes" (Electricity - Lighting and related work).
This work is part of the heritage restoration and code-compliance project at the hôtel de ville, a building protected under the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel (Cultural Heritage Act).
The project aimed to bring the electromechanical and fire safety systems up to code, provide universal accessibility and obtain LEED v4 Gold certification.
The hôtel de ville was inaugurated on June 7, 2024; the work is divided into more than 50 lots awarded to separate contractors.
The decision rests with the urban agglomeration council; the spending is shared as a mixed general administration expense.
The City is giving $30,000 to the Concours musical international de Montréal (CMIM) to fund the first-prize cash award for the 2026 edition.
The money goes directly to the winner; in exchange, the CMIM must follow a visibility plan for the City.
The Violin 2026 edition runs from May 27 to June 4, 2026, indoors, in Montréal.
The amount will be paid when the agreement between the City and the organization is signed.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, out of the Service de la culture's operating budget.
The City has granted the same amount of $30,000 every year since 2021; the Conseil des arts de Montréal's contribution goes from $13,500 in 2025 to $1,500 in 2026.
The City is entrusting the organization Montréal en Histoires with the reactivation of the Cité Mémoire multimedia trail, in Vieux-Montréal, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028.
The contract, awarded by mutual agreement, comes to $789,850 including taxes, of which $100,000 over three years is for maintaining the equipment.
Ten tableaux will be projected, instead of the 23 presented between May 2016 and December 2025.
The flat rate is $229,950 per year, with a first payment of $100,000 on signing for planning up to mid-May 2026.
The organization will be paid every three months on invoices detailing the hours and days each tableau is presented.

The expense is covered 100% by the central city: $721,240 is being transferred from the Service du développement économique (Stratégie centre-ville) to the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs.
The urban agglomeration council is renewing the terms of Julie Marineau, Roxanne Sayegh and Marylin Thomas on the board of directors of the Conseil des arts de Montréal.
This is their second term, each lasting three years. Under the CAM's rules, a term can only be renewed once.
No cost to the City: board members serve as volunteers.
The Conseil des arts de Montréal has supported the city's arts community since 1956 and falls under the jurisdiction of the urban agglomeration.
Applications go through a governance and nominations committee, which reviews proposals from the cultural, business and education communities.
The appointment must be approved by a two-thirds vote of the urban agglomeration council.
The City is appointing Andréanne Moreau as an observer member on the board of directors of the musée Pointe-à-Callière.
She replaces Anne-Marie Sigouin, who had held this seat since 2018.
The term lasts two years and can be renewed.
Andréanne Moreau is a member of the executive committee, responsible for culture, heritage, design and the French language.
The museum is asking the City to delegate a representative, as provided for in its general by-laws; the City owns the building that houses the museum.
No spending is associated with this decision.
The City is giving $10,000 to the organization Prix de la danse de Montréal for the presentation of the Grand prix de la danse de Montréal 2026.
The amount is paid in full by the central city, out of the operating budget of the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs.
Quebecor is joining as a co-sponsor with $15,000, bringing the prize award to $25,000.
The prize recognizes a Canadian or foreign artist for their contribution to dance; the jury is made up of professionals and specialists in the field.
The award ceremony is scheduled for December 1, 2026.
The City has granted the same amount of $10,000 every year since 2015.
An agreement sets out the payment terms, and the organization must follow a visibility protocol.

The city is extending, by 12 months and at no additional cost, the contract for emergency cleaning of catch basins, drains, manholes, sewer pipes and valve chambers on flood-prone streets in Pierrefonds-Roxboro (lot 2) and L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève (lot 1).
The supplier remains 9363-9888 Québec inc. (Sanivac), which accepted the renewal on January 8, 2026.
The extension runs from April 15, 2026 to April 14, 2027. This is the second and last extension option provided for in the 2023 contract.
Budgets planned for this additional year: $296,220.69 for Pierrefonds-Roxboro and $176,663.59 for L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, taxes included.
The work is ordered as needed by each borough, which pays for it out of its own budget.
The city explains that these two boroughs experience recurring spring flooding that loads the sewers with sludge; cleaning restores their flow capacity.
No price indexation applies this year, since the calculated variation is estimated at 0.9%, below the 2% threshold.
The City is awarding CGI Environnement inc. a contract to repair sewer pipes for two years, from August 2026 to August 2028, for a maximum total expenditure of $695,074.07, taxes included.
The base contract is worth $622,344.02, plus $18,182.51 in contingencies (3%) and $54,547.54 for variations in quantities (8%).
The work covers 48 sewer sections, repaired mainly by spot lining (without excavation), as well as various repairs: catch basins, manholes, service connections and drains.
The agreement will be available to the boroughs for unforeseen work on the network; the Service de l'eau pays 63% of the bill ($436,380.32) and the boroughs 37% ($258,693.75).
Of three companies that obtained the tender documents, only one submitted a bid; its bid is 24.53% below the City's internal estimate.
The pipes concerned have fractures, holes and deformations identified during camera inspections.
The City is extending its office lease at 630, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest (Tour Telus), in Ville-Marie, by one year, starting August 1, 2026.
The lease covers 75,796 square feet on the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th floors, which is less space than before: the City is giving up the 6th and 8th floors from the current 108,818 sq. ft. lease.
The total rent comes to $3,613,092, taxes included, or $41.46 per square foot; the document places market rent in the area between $39 and $45 per square foot.
The owner is 630 René-Lévesque West Property Co., represented by Management du Groupe Redbourne inc.; the agreement was negotiated directly, without a call for tenders.
Employees of the Service des finances et de l'évaluation foncière will stay in these offices while the City develops its strategy for occupying administrative space.

To pay the 2026 rent, the City is transferring $1,374,681 taken from unforeseen contingency expenses, and is adding $1,924,553 to the budget of the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation for 2027.
The owner can terminate the lease with 6 months' notice if it finds a tenant for two adjoining floors, with no compensation for the City.
City council agrees to let the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension lead the construction of a greenhouse in parc Frédéric-Back, in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood.
The park normally falls under the urban agglomeration: the agglomeration is delegating the project to city council, which then hands it over to the borough.
The construction budget is estimated at $2,185,000, funded by the Smart Cities Challenge ($920,000), the participatory budget ($765,000) and a federal food fund ($500,000).
The greenhouse complex will grow fresh fruit and vegetables for the neighbourhood and will be used for research and training with Collège Ahuntsic, UQAM and AULAB.
Announced timeline: calls for tenders in spring 2026, construction in summer-fall 2026, start-up in winter 2027.
Without approval, the City would lose $920,000 from the Smart Cities Challenge and $500,000 from the federal fund; the Challenge money must be used before May 30, 2026.
Recovering heat and CO2 from the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel is planned for a later phase, if funds are available.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $32,000 to three commercial development corporations for events in 2026.
SDC Les Quartiers du canal is receiving $12,000 for the second-hand fashion fair "La Fripe, c'est chic," in Griffintown (rue de la Montagne).
SDC Monk is receiving $10,000 for the 4th edition of Monktoberfest, on boulevard Monk.
SDC Pointe-Saint-Charles is receiving $10,000 for the Fête de Pointe-Saint-Charles, from August 27 to 30, 2026, on rue du Centre between Island and Laprairie.
The money comes from an allocation of free surplus; the expense is paid entirely by the borough.
The three SDCs will have to mention the borough's contribution in their promotion and advertising.
The decision is scheduled for the borough council meeting of July 13, 2026.
The Ville de Montréal wants to sign a confidentiality agreement with Environnement et Changement climatique Canada (ECCC) to exchange information on environmental protection.
The information covered comes from inspections and checks: sample analysis certificates, inspection reports, photos and videos.
Each party agrees to use or disclose the information it receives only for its own mandate, subject to access to information laws.
The exchanges concern the monitoring of air and water cleanup in the territory of the urban agglomeration of Montréal, carried out by the Division du contrôle des rejets et suivi environnemental.
The agreement will allow the shared information to be used in investigation processes and in checking whether businesses are in compliance.
The signing remains conditional on an authorization order from the Gouvernement du Québec, whose timeline the City does not control.
The file has no financial impact; the process began in June 2023 and a version of the agreement was agreed on in September 2025.
Québec will pay the Ville de Montréal up to $13,500,000 over three years to monitor air quality in the agglomeration's territory.
The annual grant goes from $3.3M to $4.5M, an increase of $1.2M per year, for activities in 2025, 2026 and 2027.
The City will now receive the money directly from the ministry, instead of through the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal, and will have to do its own accountability reporting.
The document states that the grant had not increased since 2008, while the City's spending on air quality monitoring exceeds $5M per year.
In June 2025, the City and the CMM had asked for an increase in funding, failing which the City would stop its air quality monitoring activities.
If a year's spending is less than $4.5M, the ministry will reduce the amount paid to the level of the actual spending.
Next steps: signature by the CMM, approval by the Conseil des ministres, then implementation.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing a mural on the wall of the building at 7909, rue Berri, in the block bounded by Lajeunesse / Gounod / Berri / Jarry.
The mural will be visible from rue Gounod, which made it necessary for the borough council to authorize it through an ordinance.
The project, named « Ruelle Geppetto », is a nod to the café Pinocchio located at the end of the lane: Geppetto's workshop, woodworking, invention, and the cat Figaro stencilled in the lane.
The mural must meet three conditions: it must not block the building's openings, it must not lead to the felling of any tree, and it must not promote any product, service or business.
The project is part of the Programme des ruelles vertes, in which citizens' committees develop and add greenery to their lane.
The work is expected to be finished by the summer of 2026.
The document does not mention any financial aspect.
The City is giving $150,000 to the Regroupement intersectoriel des organismes communautaires de Montréal (RIOCM) for its "Concertation régionale intersectorielle 2026-2028" project.
The funding covers the period from May 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029, in three payments of $50,000 (2026, 2027, 2028).
The amount triples the yearly support compared to 2025-2026, when the organization received $50,000 for one year.

In return, the RIOCM sits on the committees and working groups of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, keeps organizations informed about Montréal issues, holds consultations and submits opinions to the City.
The RIOCM brings together more than 360 Montréal community organizations and groups (mental health, homelessness, food security, youth, etc.).
The spending is already included in the budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and is paid entirely by the central city.
The executive committee must also approve the agreement setting out the payment conditions.
The borough of Lachine is asking the Minister of Justice to designate four elected officials as "competent officiants" for marriages and civil unions.
The people concerned: Mayor Julie-Pascale Provost, city councillor Dominic Roussel, and borough councillors Nancy Berthelot and Ludovic Fermely.
Once appointed, they will be able to officiate marriages only within the territory set out in their designation document, and only for the duration of their term as elected officials.
The Directeur de l'état civil will then assign each officiant a unique identification number to be written on marriage or civil union declarations.
Taking part is voluntary: the four elected officials themselves expressed their intention to do so.
Next step: sending the resolution to the Directeur de l'état civil.
The borough of Lachine is paying $206.96 (taxes included) for Mayor Julie-Pascale Provost and her chief of staff Yves Lemire to attend a networking cocktail event.
The event, the "Cocktail de la Présidente" of the Chambre de commerce de l'Ouest-de-l'Île, was held on January 20, 2026, at the Centre civique de Dollard-des-Ormeaux.
Two invoices of $103.48 each will be paid to the Chambre de commerce, or reimbursed upon presentation of supporting documents.
Since the event has already taken place, the council is approving after the fact a expense that has already been incurred.
According to the document, the mayor did not need prior authorization from the council, but the chief of staff's expenses must be authorized.
The borough of Lachine is appointing Alexandra Enache, research officer, as substitute borough secretary.
She will be able to carry out the borough secretary's duties only when he is absent or unable to act.
Her powers would include certifying official documents, keeping the registers, attesting the minutes and publishing public notices.
The position of borough secretary is held by Fredy Alzate; three other people already act as substitutes.
Stated purpose: to ensure, without interruption, the holding of meetings, the production of resolutions and by-laws, and the publication of notices.
The borough of Lachine appoints councillor Ludovic Fermely as acting mayor from April 1 to July 31, 2026.
The acting mayor exercises the mayor's powers when she is away from the territory or unable to carry out her duties.
This appointment follows that of Dominic Roussel, who was acting mayor from December 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.
No sum of money is tied to the decision.
The borough of Lachine appoints its mayor, Julie-Pascale Provost, to represent it on the board of directors of the Fondation de l'Hôpital de Lachine.
The appointment must be confirmed by the Fondation's board of directors, starting April 7, 2026, or on the date it is accepted if that date is later.
The borough secretary will send the resolution to the Fondation and handle the administrative follow-up.
No financial commitment for the borough: participation is voluntary, with representation expenses as needed.

The Fondation, which has been part of the Fondation du CUSM since 2022, is running a $5M campaign called « Osez rêver – Hôpital de Lachine », alongside a hospital modernization project worth $210-220M.
The borough of Lachine is extending by two months the lease of the organization Les Pêcheurs et chasseurs sportifs du Lac St-Louis inc., from May 1 to June 30, 2026.
The organization continues to occupy a space at 3051, boulevard Saint-Joseph, along with the parking area and the outdoor terrace.
Rent billed for these two months: $2,456.12 before taxes, which is revenue for the City.
All the other terms of the lease (insurance, obligations, permitted uses, maintenance) stay the same.
The 2026 rent is indexed to the 2025 change in the CPI; any difference from Statistique Canada's official rate will be corrected by invoice or credit, without a new council decision.
This is a third extension: an addendum from December 2025 had already extended the lease to April 30, 2026, to allow time to negotiate a new lease.
The borough of Lachine appoints councillor Nancy Berthelot as acting mayor from August 1 to November 30, 2026.
The acting mayor exercises the mayor's powers when the mayor is away from the territory or unable to carry out her duties.
This appointment follows that of Ludovic Fermely, acting mayor from April 1 to July 31, 2026.
The document does not provide for any spending.
The borough of Lachine is approving after the fact an expense of $100 for councillor Ludovic Fermely's attendance at the Gala du Club des personnes handicapées du Lac St-Louis, held on May 6, 2026.
Council's authorization should normally have been obtained before the event; since the gala took place before the July 6, 2026 sitting, council is regularizing the expense on an exceptional basis.
The reimbursement will be based on the actual cost, upon submission of supporting documents.
Council notes that any attendance by an elected official at this type of event must first be authorized by council, except where the law provides otherwise.
The Club des personnes handicapées du Lac St-Louis is a non-profit organization that offers adapted recreation and support to people with a functional limitation in Lachine and the surrounding area.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is authorizing Tennis Canada to use part of parc Jarry as a temporary parking lot from August 1 to 13, 2026, during the Omnium Banque Nationale at Stade IGA.
Parking is limited to the gravel area accessible from rue Jarry, in line with avenue de l'Esplanade, with a capacity of about 200 vehicles.
Tennis Canada is paying $59 for the permit and $572 per day of occupancy, for a total of $7,436 for the 13 days.
The organization must provide proof of liability insurance of $1,000,000 per event or accident, with no deductible for the borough.
Tennis Canada is responsible for any damage to property or persons related to the occupancy, and the City may revoke the permit at any time.
The City will take care of restoring the site after the event.
A similar authorization had been granted in June 2025 for the period from July 26 to August 7, 2025.
The City is giving a one-time grant of $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for its Acadie project, at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
The project calls for the construction of a new 26-unit building (17 studios and 9 one-bedroom units) for single people and low-income families.
The total cost of the project is estimated at $10,189,608, including $8,889,022 for construction and demolition; the land was transferred by the City at no financial cost.

The basic grant comes from the Société d'habitation du Québec (PHAQ program – Component 3), which gave its final approval in February 2026; on top of that, there is a City contribution of $1,295,155 that is reimbursed by the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal.
The $581,845 comes from the fund financed by the social component of the by-law on social, affordable and family housing, and is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
The amount could be reduced if additional capital funding comes in; according to the file, without this additional funding, the SHQ's assistance would fall through and the project would be abandoned.
The City is extending by 12 months, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, the security guard contract for the five museums of Espace pour la vie awarded to Groupe de sécurité Garda s.e.n.c.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $2,591,352.54 including taxes, namely $2,274,428.82 for the contract and $316,923.72 in contingencies.
The total contract therefore rises to $10,340,082.51 including taxes.
This is the first of the two one-year extension options provided for in public call for tenders 22-19702, under the same terms and conditions.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles; the portion related to the Biosphère falls to the urban agglomeration.
The document states that without this extension, the safety of people and the security of the buildings and property of these facilities could be compromised as of May 1, 2026.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding Parizeau Pawulski Architectes s.e.n.c. the architectural and engineering plans and supervision for the renovation of the centre sportif de la Petite-Bourgogne, for $839,760.15 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,080,724.17, which is the contract plus $125,964.02 in contingencies and $115,000 in incidental costs, paid entirely by the borough.

The centre, built in 1997 and used by about 148,000 people a year, serves Griffintown and la Petite-Bourgogne; expert assessments point to inadequate air treatment that is damaging the roof and the building envelope.
The planned work covers ventilation, heating and air conditioning, the roof and the building envelope, along with electrical and plumbing work and work inside the pool.
Announced schedule: design from August 2026 to February 2027, call for tenders for the work in early 2027, work from July 2027 to 2028, and handover in August 2028.
The project is eligible for funding from Québec (PAFIRSPA) of up to $9.1M and will have to aim for LEED v5 Canada-NC silver level certification.
Out of 12 bids, the selected firm received the best score; its price is 26% below the internal estimate of $1,129,697.21, and its performance will be evaluated.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing the creation and upkeep of a permanent mural on a City building at 5597-5599, rue Laurendeau.
The artwork will be painted on the blank wall of the Centre Hortense-Duclos facing rue Le Caron, at the corner of Laurendeau, in Ville-Émard/Côte-Saint-Paul.
The project was submitted by the organization Concertation Ville-Émard/Côte Saint-Paul and selected by the selection committee of the Programme d'art mural 2026 (stream 1).
The local artist duo l'abricot will create the mural, which will depict a group of people inspired by self-portraits made by residents during workshops held on April 24 and May 23, 2026.
The borough finds that the mural will not block any window, will not require cutting down any tree and will not promote any product or service.
A public notice will be published on the borough's website; the document does not indicate any cost.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is awarding Construction Ludec inc. a contract worth $173,448.41 (taxes included) to rebuild the technical control booth of the salle Oliver-Jones, at the Maison de la culture, at 12004, boulevard Rolland.
The borough is adding $26,000 for unforeseen work on the site, bringing the total expense to $199,448.41.
The work aims to lower the floor of the control booth so that the stage managers and set-design technicians have better control of the stage area.
Three companies submitted bids, all of them compliant; Ludec is the lowest, at 18% above the estimate of $146,478.15.
The work is planned from July to September 2026, with the contract awarded on May 4, 2026; the borough wants to condense the work to limit the effect on cultural programming.
The expense is funded by loan by-law 21-024 (work in strategic sectors).
The borough of Montréal-Nord is cancelling its call for tenders for the rebuilding of the pergola at parc Henri-Bourassa.
The lowest compliant bid, from Groupe Plexa inc., came to $731,924.38 including taxes, which is 28.9% above the estimate of $567,830.
Four companies submitted bids, all of them compliant, with prices ranging from $731,924.38 to $1,182,316.67.
The QIR funding planned for the project has been withdrawn from the borough.
The project was meant to set up a space at the park for community organizations, including a bike workshop proposed by Hoodstock, promised for fall 2026.
The borough will inform Hoodstock and the Table de quartier, and its social development team will look for other solutions for the organization.
The City is renewing its Prévention Montréal program for 2027-2030, with a budget of $46,193,956 over four years, or $11,548,489 per year.
The program funds projects for children, young people (0 to 30 years old) and their families, around two themes: social inclusion and violence prevention.
The 19 boroughs share $35,793,955 over four years (local component), or $8,948,489 per year, which represents 77.49% of the budget.

The amounts vary by borough: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension receives $4,242,314, Montréal-Nord $3,627,772, L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève $474,108, based on indicators of population, socio-economic vulnerability and crime.
The rest, $2.6M per year (22.51%), goes to the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale for a regional call for projects targeting violence that crosses borough boundaries.
The money is paid to community organizations through financial contribution contracts; each borough may keep up to 15% of its envelope to manage the program.
The expense is borne by the central city and will be included in the 2027 budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale.
The City is reallocating $69,196 to recreation organizations serving people with functional limitations, for 2026 and 2027.

This money is available because three already-funded organizations stopped some activities: the elimination of nine summer camps for young people with special needs, the suspension of a project in 2026, and a notice of failure to report on the use of funds.
$41,196 will be used to increase support for 14 organizations that are already funded, with increases ranging from $1,148 to $6,592 for 2026-2027.
$28,000 will go to two new organizations: $15,000 to Centre Philou for 2026 only, and $13,000 to Centre Sablon for 2026 and 2027.
The goal is to maintain access to inclusive camps and recreation activities during the summer, in the boroughs affected by the reduction in services.
The spending was already included in the budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and is covered by the central city.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is increasing its 2026 contribution to Carrefour jeunesse emploi Notre-Dame-de-Grâce by 3%, which is $699 more, including taxes if applicable.
With the indexation, the contribution rises to $23,995 for 2026; the same amount is planned for 2027.

The money goes toward the operation of the Table de concertation jeunesse de NDG, for which Carrefour is the trustee: meetings of organizations, information sharing, identifying the needs of young people aged 6 to 35, and joint projects.
The initial contribution of $67,855 covered 2025 to 2027; a 3% indexation was also applied in 2025 ($678).
The organization must submit annual reports for 2026 and 2027, and a final report no later than January 31, 2028.
The borough council was to adopt the decision on March 9, 2026.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $142,050 to five organizations to run activities in three parks in the Côte-des-Neiges neighbourhood from June 2 to October 31, 2026.
The parks involved are parc Martin Luther King, parc Nelson-Mandela and parc de la Savane, where the borough and poste de quartier 26 have identified problems with people sharing the space.
Baobab Familial receives $44,000 for a lending box of games and toys at parc Nelson-Mandela, from late June to late September.
Loisirs sportifs CDN-NDG receives $26,414 for basketball at aréna Bill-Durnan and sports activities at parc Nelson-Mandela, Tuesday to Friday from 5:15 p.m. to 9 p.m.
Ciné-Quartier receives $22,800 for outdoor movie screenings, and Maison de jeunes de la Côte-des-Neiges receives $23,836 for music nights (DJ) at parc MLK.
Missions Exeko receives $25,000 for a new arts activities project at parc Nelson-Mandela, aimed at bringing together children, seniors and vulnerable people.
The money comes from the Prévention Montréal program, from the ministère de la Sécurité publique du Canada and from a program of the ministère de la Sécurité publique du Québec.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough council is receiving the 2025 activity report of its Conseil jeunesse (youth council), an advisory body created in December 2018.

The Conseil jeunesse organized the free cultural event PRISMART on September 5 and 6, 2025: about 80 people at the Centre culturel Benny, and more than 150 participants at parc MLK with more than 50 young artists.
A Valentine's Day edition of PRISMART took place on February 14, 2026, with workshops at the youth centre and activities at the parc MLK skating rink (90 people).
The members co-created the podcast series "Mosaïque urbaine" on youth mental health with the Conseil jeunesse of Pierrefonds-Roxboro; 4 episodes are on YouTube and Spotify.
They also took part in the Journée interconseils on June 14, 2025, a visit to city hall on June 18, and the Force Jeunesse event on October 18, 2025.
So far, the Conseil jeunesse's spending has gone to paying for members' meals at in-person meetings; no amount is specified.
Projects planned for 2026: a fashion show by and for young people, and an evening centred on a calligraphy project with the school La Voie at the Maison de la culture de Côte-des-Neiges.

City council agrees that the borough of Saint-Laurent will itself lead the work to restore and create wetlands and water environments in the wooded area of parc Marcel-Laurin, until the end of the project.
Managing watercourses is normally the responsibility of the agglomeration: it must first delegate the power to city council for this agreement to take effect.
The wooded area covers 15.44 hectares and includes two stream segments, marshes and swamps, which have been listed since 2009 in the agglomeration's inventory of protected natural environments.
Québec (MELCCFP) has been providing $999,610.98 since 2022, plus additional funding of $1,979,824.47 approved in 2026; the project submission is postponed to 2027.
The work includes a retention basin to filter water from the storm sewer, the restoration of stream flow, culverts and weirs, and the creation of wetlands.
Trails and some entrances to the wooded area will be adjusted, and signage and educational facilities will be modernized.
The borough will handle the calls for tenders, the contracts, the supervision of the work and the coordination with Québec and the Service de l'eau de Montréal.
The City is paying $24,856 to Société zoologique de Granby inc. to protect the northern map turtle, a species at risk in Québec, from April to December 2026.

The activities take place in part on City-owned land in the Grand parc de l'Ouest: finding and protecting nests, digging up and incubating eggs in a laboratory, controlling buckthorn, and releasing young turtles.
The organization will also train volunteers and large-park staff in turtle protection.

The City's contribution represents 16.3% of a $152,546 project, also funded by the Fondation de la faune du Québec ($90,190), Conservation de la nature Canada, the Ville d'Hudson, the Club de voile de Senneville and Parcs Canada.
The payment is made in two parts: $7,456 after the agreement is signed, then $17,400 after the progress report is approved.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration; the full project ends on March 31, 2028.
The City is giving $74,568 to the Zoo Ecomuseum (Société d'histoire naturelle de la vallée du Saint-Laurent) to protect the brown snake in Greater Montréal, from March 2026 to December 2028.
The money will be paid in three instalments of $24,856: on signing, no later than April 30, 2027, and then on April 28, 2028.

The City's contribution covers 14.5% of a $503,055.50 project; the rest comes from the Fondation de la faune ($249,658), the MELCCFP ($75,225), Laval ($75,000) and the borough of Saint-Laurent ($15,000).
The project includes surveys, habitat development and restoration, the validation of ecological corridors, and the sharing of knowledge with municipalities.
The work targets Montréal's large parks; the organization must maintain the developments and carry out biological monitoring for three years.
The brown snake, found only in the Montréal metropolitan area, has been designated as threatened since 2022 under Québec law.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration; the project ends on March 31, 2029.

The urban agglomeration council would add two sites to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité: the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha).
Adding them requires adopting conservation plans for these two sites, which provide for ecological management.
According to the 2025 report that was tabled, 3,650 ha are listed in the Répertoire and 401 ha are listed provisionally, for a total of 4,051 ha, or 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.
The target remains to protect 10% of the agglomeration's land territory, taken from the 2015 Schéma d'aménagement and carried over into the Plan climat 2020-2030.
The Service des grands parcs manages the Répertoire with its current budget; ecological management is paid for by the units concerned.
Adding the sites and updating the report are planned for May 15, 2026, with further additions in the following years.
No communications activities are planned.

The borough of Verdun is offering city council to take charge of the call for tenders and the supervision of the redevelopment work on rue Rushbrooke, rue Jacques-Lauzon, a section of rue Gilberte-Dubé and rue May (commemorative component).
These streets fall under city council: the service offer only takes effect if city council accepts it.
The projects stem from the urban integration program tied to the corridor of the new pont Samuel-De Champlain, in Verdun.
The plans and specifications have already been produced by the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité, which is covering the entire expense; no budget is transferred to the borough.
Announced timeline: public call for tenders in the summer of 2026, work in the summer and fall of 2026-2027.
The City plans to notify owners and residents of the planned work.
The Anjou borough council appoints city councillor Andrée Hénault as acting mayor for April, May and June 2026.
The acting mayor stands in for the borough mayor when needed; the position changes hands every few months (Richard Leblanc held it from January to March 2026).
No spending is attached to this appointment.
At the same March 3, 2026 meeting, the council reappoints Josée Kenny as borough secretary, since the person who holds the position has been absent since December 2, 2025.
Cathelynn Marsan is appointed substitute borough secretary in Anjou as of March 12, 2026.
The borough of Anjou is giving $500 to FADOQ – Région Île de Montréal to hold the Jeux FADOQ 2026.
The Games, now in their 27th edition, will take place in May and June 2026 and are open to all Montrealers aged 50 and over.
Ten sports are planned: tennis, table tennis, badminton, golf, five-pin bowling (regular and handicap) and running, among others.
The 2025 edition drew close to 300 participants; FADOQ – Région Île de Montréal has 55,000 members aged 50 and over.
The amount is paid in full out of the borough's operating budget.
The City is transferring to a new organization, Essor économique Québec Tech, two grant agreements signed with Fondation Montréal inc. de demain to support technology startups.

On December 1, 2025, the Fondation transferred to the new organization its economic development activities related to startups, along with its employees and the contributions from its other funders, so it can focus on its charitable activities (startup scholarships).

The two grants involved total $425,000: $250,000 awarded in June 2025 for a project on the Québec startup ecosystem and $175,000 awarded in August 2025 for business resilience in the face of American customs tariffs.

The transfer does not change the amounts awarded: the payments planned for 2026 will go to Essor économique Québec Tech, and the Fondation must hand over to it the portion of the sums already received as of December 1, 2025.
The transfer applies retroactively to December 1, 2025, so that the two organizations can put their situation in order before the end of their fiscal year, on March 31, 2026.
The supported projects continue from March to July 2026, with a final accountability report between August and December 2026.
The City is giving $600,000 to Zú, an incubator for the creative industries, to launch a Pôle d'innovation et de commercialisation en créativité numérique.
The project, run with the Société des arts technologiques (SAT), is meant to help companies in the sector carry out R&D, protect their intellectual property and bring their innovations to market.
The support covers three years, from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029, with payments of $202,500 in 2026, $202,500 in 2027, $177,500 in 2028 and $17,500 in 2029.
The money comes from the Entente Réflexe 3 (2025-2029) signed with the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie; the expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration.
The project's total budget is $5.6M over three years, including funds from the gouvernement du Québec and private partners; the City's share represents 11%.
The project includes testing spaces and technology showcases downtown, and Zú will have to report back each year in July 2027, 2028 and 2029.
Zú had already received $375,000 from the City for an incubation project between 2023 and 2026.
The Ville-Marie borough is allowing amplified sound to be broadcast outdoors at Place de la Création, at the corner of rue Ontario Est and rue Parthenais, from June 4 to July 30, 2026.

The programming, run by the borough, is free: workshops and LNI improv micro-matches on Thursdays (5:30 p.m. to 8 p.m.) and some Saturdays, then concerts on Thursday, July 16, 23 and 30 from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m.
Noise is capped at 80 dBA and 100 dBC (Leq 15 minutes), measured 35 metres from the loudspeakers; a gap of more than 20 dB between dBA and dBC is not allowed.
Megaphones are banned, except for safety purposes.
The promoter must provide monthly reports on complaints and noise measurements, set up a complaint management system, and submit a season review by November 15, 2026 at the latest.
The promoter must also plan measures to reduce noise in the areas near the site.
The order takes effect on the day the notice is published in Le Devoir.

The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing noise from outdoor sound equipment at parc Jean-Drapeau, between 7 a.m. and 11 p.m., from April 18, 2026 to March 7, 2027, for the events listed in the attached program.
The maximum sound level is set at 65 dBA (averaged over 15 minutes), measured near the bassin olympique; a difference of more than 20 dB between dBA and dBC is not allowed.
Two exceptions with no sound level limit starting at 10 a.m.: the Grand Prix du Canada (May 22 to 24, 2026) and L'International des Feux Loto-Québec (July 2 to August 6, 2026).
Megaphones are banned, except for safety reasons.

La Société du parc Jean-Drapeau must submit monthly reports on complaints and sound measurements, set up a complaint management system, and file a review of the 2026 season no later than December 15, 2026.
It must also plan measures to reduce the effect of noise on the areas next to the park, and respond to residents' complaints within a reasonable time.

The program includes, among other things, the Piknic and OFF-Piknic events at the Jardin du Petit Prince, concerts at the Espace 67, competitions at the complexe aquatique and the bassin olympique, and exhibitions at the Cœur de l'île.
The Ville-Marie borough is granting an exceptional authorization for noise from outdoor sound equipment at the Village au Pied-du-Courant (2100, rue Notre-Dame Est) from June 3 to September 12, 2026.
Events in the summer program may reach 80 dBA and 100 dBC (average over 15 minutes), measured 35 metres from the speakers; the program in the appendix shows times from 5 p.m. to 11 p.m.
Outside these events, the limit on the site is 75 dBA and 90 dBC, measured 5 metres from the source, with a maximum difference of 20 dB between dBA and dBC.
Megaphones are prohibited, except for safety purposes.
The promoter must submit monthly reports on complaints and noise levels, set up a complaint management system, and file a season report no later than November 15, 2026.
The promoter must also propose measures to reduce the effect of the noise in neighbouring areas; the site layout had been changed in 2025 for that purpose.
The order takes effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir and is sent to the SPVM.

The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing noise from outdoor sound equipment at the Vieux-Port sites, from May 3 to November 1, 2026, on the dates and at the times set out in an attached schedule of events.
The general noise limit is set at 75 dBA and 90 dBC (average over 15 minutes), measured 5 metres from the source.

Thirteen events are allowed a higher limit, namely 80 dBA and 100 dBC measured at 35 metres: Face 2 Face, House on Wheels, Unfaced Open Air, Flavours of India, Hotwheelz, Festival Louange, Un goût des Caraïbes, Festival Streetfood, Le grand Poutinefest, Festival Afromonde, Italfest à la plage, Tacofest and Jackalope.
Megaphones remain banned, except for safety reasons.
The Société du Vieux-Port must submit monthly reports on complaints and noise levels, handle complaints, and plan measures to limit noise in neighbouring residential areas.
It must submit a report on the 2026 season no later than December 15, 2026.

The schedule of events includes, among others, the Cirque du Soleil (May 20 to August 16), the Feux à la plage de l'Horloge evenings (July 2 to August 6) and the Foire d'automne (September 30 to October 18).
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing noise from outdoor sound equipment at place Radio-Canada (corner of Alexandre-DeSève and René-Lévesque Est) from July 10 to August 21, 2026.
Eight evenings are planned, all from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m.: six film screenings on Fridays from July 10 to August 14, plus two events to be confirmed on August 20 and 21.
Sound is limited to 80 dBA and 100 dBC (Leq 15 min) measured at 35 metres for these events, and to 75 dBA and 90 dBC measured at 5 metres the rest of the time.
Megaphones are banned, except for safety purposes.
Radio-Canada must submit monthly reports on complaints and sound measurements, set up a complaint management system, and plan measures to reduce noise in the neighbourhood.
Radio-Canada must produce a review of the 2026 season by November 15, 2026.
