The order takes effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir; this is the third season of activities at this site.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing outdoor music at 463, rue Sainte-Catherine Ouest (Le Balcon, on the forecourt of St. James United church) from May 15 to September 26, 2026.
The "live band" shows take place from 5 p.m. to 11 p.m., according to a schedule attached to the order, and are open to everyone.
General noise limit: 75 dBA and 90 dBC (average over 15 minutes) measured 5 metres from the source; 80 dBA and 100 dBC at 35 metres for the events listed in the schedule.
Megaphones are prohibited, except for safety purposes, and the gap between dBA and dBC cannot exceed 20 dB.
The promoter must set up a complaint management system, submit monthly reports and plan measures to reduce noise in the neighbourhood.
A report on the 2026 season must be given to the borough no later than November 15, 2026.
The order comes into force on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing noise from outdoor sound equipment on the Lespacemaker site, at 2875 rue Hochelaga, between May 13 and July 8, 2026.
Four events that are free and open to everyone are planned: "Barbec & Trompettes" on May 13, June 10 and July 8 (6 p.m. to 9:30 p.m.) and "Revalorizotoute" on July 1 (12 p.m. to 9:30 p.m.).
The sound cannot exceed 75 dBA and 90 dBC, measured 5 metres from the source, and megaphones are banned except for safety purposes.
Lespacemaker must use only one outdoor speaker, pointed toward rue Hochelaga, and must plan measures to limit noise in the neighbourhood.
The organization must set up a complaint management system and submit a report on the 2026 season no later than November 15, 2026.
The order takes effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir; the SPVM is informed of it.

The borough of Ville-Marie is making an exception to allow sound to be broadcast outdoors at the Esplanade de la Place Ville-Marie, from June 10 to September 2, 2026, on the dates and at the times set out in an attached program.
Noise cannot exceed 80 dBA and 100 dBC (average over 15 minutes), measured 35 metres from the loudspeakers; a difference of more than 20 dB between the dBA and dBC levels is not allowed.
Megaphones remain prohibited, except for safety purposes.
The promoter must submit monthly reports on complaints and noise measurements, set up a complaint management system, and plan measures to limit noise in neighbouring areas.
The promoter must produce a report on the 2026 season no later than November 15, 2026.

The program includes, among other things, the « Midis sous l'Anneau » (12 p.m. to 1 p.m.), evening events (5 p.m. to 10 p.m.), yoga with headphones and a circus show on July 12; the events are open to everyone.

The order comes into effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir; an application for a conditional use for « occupation événementielle » (event occupancy) is being submitted at the same time to the council meeting of June 9, 2026.
The borough of Ville-Marie is granting an exceptional authorization for amplified outdoor music in the parking lot at 1424, rue Peel, from May 21 to 24, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m.
The four days of events (DJs, amplified music, corporate hospitality) are being held alongside the Grand Prix de Formule 1 du Canada.
Noise is capped at 80 dBA and 100 dBC for these events, measured 35 metres from the speakers; 75 dBA and 90 dBC the rest of the time.
Megaphones are banned, except for safety reasons.
The promoter must set up a complaint management system, submit monthly reports and a review of the 2026 season no later than November 15, 2026.
The promoter must also put measures in place to reduce noise in the areas next to the site.
The land is an outdoor parking lot operated by Services Vincipark Canada.

The borough of Ville-Marie is making an exception to allow noise from outdoor sound equipment on the vacant lot behind the BAnQ, at the southwest corner of rue Berri and rue Ontario Est, from June 13 to July 12, 2026.

Three activities are covered: the Grande fête du soccer on June 13 (1 p.m. to 5:30 p.m.), rehearsals for the Montréal Complètement Cirque festival from June 28 to July 1 (8 a.m. to 10 p.m.), and then the festival itself from July 2 to 12 (site open to the public from 3 p.m. to 8 p.m., closing from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m.).
Sound may not exceed 80 dBA and 100 dBC (averaged over 15 minutes) measured 35 metres from the loudspeakers, and the difference between dBA and dBC may not exceed 20 dB.
Megaphones are prohibited, except for safety reasons.

The promoter must set up a complaint management system, submit reports on complaints and sound measurements, plan measures to reduce noise in the surrounding area, and hand in a review of the 2026 season no later than November 15, 2026.

The request comes jointly from the BAnQ and the Tohu: construction work in the area and the fact that part of rue Saint-Denis is not being made pedestrian-only are forcing the Montréal Complètement Cirque festival to relocate.
The order comes into effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Ville-Marie is granting an exceptional authorization for noise from outdoor sound equipment on the esplanade of the Place des Arts from September 3 to 20, 2026.
Two events are covered: the Festival JOAT (September 3 and 4 from 2 p.m. to 11 p.m., September 5 and 6 from 12 p.m. to 11 p.m.) and the Festival Tempeo (September 16 to 20, from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m.).
For these events, the sound cannot exceed 80 dBA and 100 dBC measured 35 metres from the equipment; the limit is 75 dBA and 90 dBC at 5 metres for other activities.
Megaphones are prohibited, except for safety reasons.
The promoter must set up a complaint management system, submit reports on complaints and sound measurements, and plan measures to limit noise in neighbouring residential areas.
The promoter must produce a report on the 2026 season no later than November 15, 2026.
The order comes into effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing certain construction work 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including statutory holidays, from June 10 to December 31, 2026.
The measure applies in the area bounded by rues Sherbrooke Ouest, Guy, de la Commune Ouest and boulevard Saint-Laurent.
It covers work on public infrastructure and urban technical networks, as well as the bringing in of cranes on private construction sites.
Each construction site must first obtain written authorization from the Direction de l'aménagement urbain et de la mobilité, and not just the order.
To be authorized, night work must have little impact on the peace and quiet of nearby residents, happen infrequently and include mitigation measures.
Contractors must set up a complaint management system with a liaison officer for nearby residents.
The City says it wants to test solutions to reduce the concentration and duration of construction sites in this area, as part of an "Urban Laboratory".
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing the STM to work 24 hours a day, every day, including statutory holidays, from June 10 to July 31, 2026.
The work affects the green line metro tunnel, between the Berri-UQAM and Saint-Laurent stations: drilling and repair of the vault.
This authorization is an exception to the borough by-law that limits construction work hours.
The STM says it has to work outside metro operating hours to avoid risks to riders and infrastructure.
The STM plans a noise study before the work, continuous noise monitoring and communications with residents, in particular those of the Corporation d'habitation Jeanne-Mance.
The order takes effect on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing noise from outdoor sound equipment at Place de la Création (corner of Ontario Est and Parthenais) from August 6 to September 25, 2026.
The noise level is capped at 80 dBA and 100 dBC (averaged over 15 minutes), measured 35 metres from the speakers; megaphones are banned except for safety purposes.

The free program includes basket-weaving workshops (August 6, 7 and 8), Poète du parc (August 13 and September 12), dance shows (August 29 and September 25) and a show for young people (September 12).
The promoter must submit monthly reports on complaints and noise measurements, set up a complaint management system and plan measures to reduce noise toward neighbouring areas.
A report on the 2026 season must be submitted by November 15, 2026.
This ordinance adds to the one adopted on May 5, 2026, which covered June and July; it comes into force on the day a notice is published in Le Devoir.
The City is hiring Tessier Récréo-Parc inc. to modernize the Salamandre play area in parc du Mont-Royal, for a total expense of $959,946.14, taxes included.
The contract itself is worth $667,857.23; added to it are $133,571.45 in contingencies, $100,178.58 for quantity variations and $58,338.88 in incidental expenses.
The work includes replacing the play modules and shock-absorbing surfaces, adding inclusive modules, planting trees, and using recycled materials for at least 50% of the new infrastructure.

The decision summary describes the play area as deteriorated: broken-down ground surfaces, damaged ropes exposing the steel cables, missing climbing holds, and modules that are not accessible to children with special needs.
Timeline: construction starting in September 2026, reopening expected in June 2027, and warranty ending in June 2028.
Tessier Récréo-Parc was the lowest of the 5 bidders, at 13.6% above the internal estimate, a gap attributed mainly to the market price for the EPDM surface ($326/m² instead of the estimated $230/m²).
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, through a loan by-law, and is spread over 2026 and 2027 ($438K per year, net of tax rebates).

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is awarding Patriarche Architecture inc. a professional services contract worth $2,065,921.39 (taxes included) for the plans, specifications and construction site supervision.
The total authorized spending comes to $2,685,697.81, which is the contract plus $413,184.28 in contingencies and $206,592.14 in incidental expenses.
The project brings the piscine Pierre-Lorange up to standard and expands the bibliothèque Hochelaga to turn it into a community centre.

Planned work: repair of the pool basin and its waterproofing, new ceramic tiling, universal change rooms, sprinklers, replacement of the heating and ventilation system, universal accessibility and bringing the bleachers up to standard.
The building dates from 1983; several components have reached the end of their useful life or do not meet current standards.
The Programme aquatique de Montréal can fund up to 90% of the portion related to bringing the pool up to standard; the rest comes from the borough's capital works program.
Out of 13 compliant bids, the one selected is 39.24% below the internal estimate of $3,400,000.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is awarding Constructions Seni inc. a contract of $4,717,039.56 (taxes included) to partly renovate the Ancien marché public Maisonneuve.
The total authorized spending comes to $5,990,640.24, which is the contract plus $943,407.91 in contingencies (20%) and $330,192.77 in incidental costs (7%).

The work covers the water service entrance, bringing the exits up to standard, a new staircase, the elevator, the roof over the canopies, the wooden doors and windows, securing the ceilings and decontamination.
The building, occupied by the Centre communautaire, culturel, social et éducatif (CCSE) Maisonneuve, will remain in use for the entire duration of the work.
Four companies submitted bids out of twelve that picked up the tender documents; the winning bid is the lowest, at 27.71% below the professionals' estimate.
The project is eligible for the Fonds pour la restauration des immeubles municipaux patrimoniaux; the company's performance will be evaluated at the end of the contract.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing the construction of a three-storey residential building on a vacant lot on rue Lebrun, between Notre-Dame Est and Ontario (lot 6 659 384).
The building will have five rental units, three of them family-sized (at least three bedrooms, more than 96 m²).
The project exceeds the height limit for the area: the City is allowing 3 storeys and 12 m, instead of the 2 storeys and 9 m normally permitted.
Conditions imposed: a maximum of two parking spaces and the installation of a concrete pad along the laneway.

The developer has 60 months to apply for a building permit, otherwise the authorization becomes void; the outdoor landscaping must be completed within 12 months after the permit's period of validity ends.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on May 1, 2026 and suggests covering the concrete pad or building a shelter for waste.
This is the first draft resolution: a public consultation will follow and residents will be able to request a referendum.
The City is buying, through the broker AON Parizeau inc., a $1,225,000 surety bond from La Compagnie d'Assurance Saint Paul, for a total premium of $18,375 (non-taxable) over three years.
This surety bond is required by provincial regulations so that the City can operate the Centre de traitement des matières organiques de Montréal-Est.
The amount of the surety bond is based on the centre's purpose (biomethanation) and its treatment capacity of 60,000 tonnes per year.
The rate negotiated by the Union des municipalités du Québec is $6 per $1,000 of surety bond, with a discount of 16.67% for a three-year term.

The City is signing an updated indemnity agreement with the insurer, which changed its name on January 2, 2026 (previously Compagnie d'Assurance Travelers du Canada); it will also cover five surety bonds already in force.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service de l'environnement and is fully borne by the urban agglomeration; the contract is expected to be awarded in June 2026.
The City will sign a licence with the ministère des Ressources naturelles et des Forêts to display the Québec cadastre layer (lot boundaries and lot numbers) on its public interactive maps.
These maps are used to consult the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050 and the Schéma d'aménagement et de développement.
The licence is free, with no time limit and no territorial limit, and involves no spending by the City.
The maps are mainly intended for staff of the agglomeration's cities and of the boroughs, but they remain available to the general public.
The data cannot be used to mark out or locate property boundaries: only a land surveyor can do that, and the coordinates shown have no legal value.
Signing authority is delegated to the head of the Division de la planification urbaine of the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité.
The Ville-Marie borough is extending Nordikeau inc.'s contract for the operation and maintenance of fountains and various installations by one year, from June 19, 2026 to June 18, 2027.
The additional spending authorized is $521,880.38 ($474,436.71 for the services and $47,443.67 in contingencies), which brings the total contract to $2,484,874.35, taxes included.
The contract covers the opening, daily summer operation and closing of the fountains at place des Festivals, place Jean-Paul-Riopelle, squares Victoria Nord and Sud, and square Dorchester.

It also includes the operation of the electrical assets of the Promenade des Artistes, the Parterre and the esplanade Tranquille, as well as the fire feature at place Jean-Paul-Riopelle, every evening from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m.
Prices are indexed by 2.71%, calculated from Québec's consumer price index.
This is the second and last optional renewal year of the contract awarded in 2022, which was obtained with only one bidder.
The borough will carry out a performance evaluation of Nordikeau inc.
The Ville-Marie borough is extending Nordikeau inc.'s contract by one year for the operation and maintenance of the fountains at squares Viger and Phillips.
The extension covers June 27, 2026 to June 26, 2027, as the current contract ends on June 26, 2026.
The borough is authorizing an additional expense of $146,145.33: $132,859.39 for the services and $13,285.94 in contingencies (10%) for unforeseen costs.
The contract total therefore rises to $590,690.46, including taxes and contingencies.
Prices are indexed by 2.71%, calculated from Québec's consumer price index.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget: $95,191.54 in 2026 and $50,953.79 afterwards.
The borough will carry out a performance evaluation of Nordikeau inc.
The City is giving $24,000 to the Association montréalaise des arts et des traditions populaires (AMATP) to hold the Danses en plein air on Mont-Royal in 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The annual support goes from $5,500 to $7,500 in 2026 and 2027, then to $9,000 in 2028 for the activity's 70th anniversary; it had not been indexed for several years.
The evenings are held free of charge on the forecourt of the Pavillon du Lac-aux-Castors, two evenings a week (Monday and Thursday), from June to the end of August.
On Mondays, performer-hosts introduce the public to traditional dances from Québec and from various communities; Thursdays are free dance evenings.
The AMATP handles the programming, promotion, hiring of hosts and technicians, equipment, and a final report submitted in October.
The grant is paid in two instalments (June and November) and is covered 100% by the central city; it covers 72% of the project's cost.
In 2026, the Danses en plein air will be part of the program of celebrations for the 150th anniversary of parc du Mont-Royal.
The Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports will handle the design and supervision of the work to replace the synthetic turf on the sports field at parc Rutherford, in Ville-Marie.
The field, built in 2017 at the foot of mont Royal (between rue McTavish and avenue du Dr-Penfield), is shared with Université McGill: 42% of the time for McGill, 58% for the borough.

Reasons given: the surface is 9 years old (with a life span of 8 to 10 years), its warranty expired in 2025, minor repairs went from 22 to 118 in four years, and the infill material is breaking down according to an inspection by Labosport.
Planned work: removal of the old turf, cleaning of the drains, correction of ground deformations and installation of a new surface.
The borough of Ville-Marie will pay the full cost of the design and supervision, out of its capital works program.

Timeline: design in the summer of 2026, call for tenders in the fall of 2026, work from May to June 2027 — a window that must be met before work resumes on the McTavish station, otherwise the next opportunity would be in 2034.

The City is awarding L.M.L. Paysagistes et frères inc. the contract to replace the synthetic turf on the indoor field at the Stade de soccer de Montréal, at 9235, avenue Papineau (Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension).
The total spending comes to $1,175,929.52 including taxes: $1,022,547.41 for the contract, $102,254.74 in contingencies and $51,127.37 in incidental costs, paid by the central city.
The current surface, installed in 2015, is at the end of its useful life; according to the document, spot repairs will not keep the surface safe after 2026.

The work includes removing the old turf, installing the new one with EPDM-type infill, sports equipment, replacing the net in front of the bleachers, and maintenance during the 8 years of the warranty.
The work is planned from September to October 2026; the field must be closed for as short a time as possible, because the stadium is also replacing its lighting around mid-August 2026.
Three companies submitted bids out of six that obtained the tender documents; two bids met the requirements and L.M.L. was the lowest, at 0.53% below the in-house estimate.
The City will evaluate the company's performance, since the net spending is over $1,000,000.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is hiring Nadeau Blondin Lortie architectes inc. to design the plans and supervise work at the Maison Pierre-Chartrand, for $75,538.58 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $98,200.16, including $11,330.79 in contingencies and $11,330.79 in incidental costs (for example, laboratory analysis of materials).

The work includes redoing the floors on every storey, demolishing and rebuilding the access ramp for people with reduced mobility at the back, the two small balconies and the adjacent walkway, as well as redoing the paved walkway at the front.
The building is described as a building of exceptional heritage value under municipal jurisdiction.
Three firms were contacted by email on January 23, 2026 and all three submitted a price; the winning offer is 12.31% above the internal estimate of $67,260.38.
The project is 100% funded by the borough; the contract is expected to be awarded on March 10, 2026 and the work to be finished in December 2026.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is adding $257,544 (taxes included) to the contract with Procova inc. for electromechanical upgrade work at the centre communautaire Roussin, at 12125, rue Notre-Dame Est.
The total value of the contract goes from $6,219,687.60 to $6,477,231.60, including taxes, incidental costs and contingencies.
The money is used to top up the contingency budget, which goes from $772,632 to $1,030,176, an increase of 5% of the value of the contract.

The borough explains the overrun by unexpected findings on the work site: the ceiling of the mechanical room had to be replaced, asbestos was present, and a second structural slab that was not documented was discovered.
The delay in starting the work was made up with overtime, in order to put the boiler room back in service before the cold season.
The breakdown of the transfer switch for the emergency power supply (generator) also requires unplanned repairs.
The funds come from the Programme de protection des bâtiments; without this authorization, payment for the work already done would be delayed.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is applying for a $30,000 grant from the Conseil des arts du Canada for artistic activities in its two libraries in 2027.
The application is submitted under the Rayonnement public stream of the Rayonner au Canada program, which funds activities connecting artists and audiences.
The planned activities: cultural workshops for children, writing clubs, meetings with writers, introduction to reading for toddlers, and shows for children.
The activities will take place over three program periods in 2027: winter-spring (January 1 to June 18), summer (June 19 to September 3) and fall (September 4 to December 31).
The borough mayor and the borough secretary (or their substitutes) are authorized to sign the documents related to the application.
The borough's budget will be increased based on the response from the Conseil des arts du Canada.
The borough had submitted similar applications in previous years: $30,000 for 2026 and $25,000 for 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The City is transferring to the 19 borough councils the power to authorize a collective religious practice on a public roadway or in a park; this power currently belongs to the city council.

This power comes from the Loi sur le renforcement de la laïcité au Québec (Bill 9), assented to on April 2, 2026, which bans these practices on public roadways and in parks, unless the municipality grants an authorization on an exceptional, case-by-case basis.

The law defines a collective religious practice as any action, other than wearing a religious symbol, that may appear to be the expression of a religious belief; a public roadway includes streets, lanes, bridges, sidewalks, pedestrian paths and bike paths.
The law provides for fines for people who organize or take part in a banned collective religious practice.
With this change, a single level decides: the borough will be able to both issue the permit or the local order and give the authorization required by the law.
Planned timeline: notice of motion and tabling of the draft by-law on May 11, 2026, adoption on June 15, 2026, coming into force on the date of publication.
There is no financial impact associated with this file.
The City is selling three lots located between rue Rielle and rue Gordon, in the borough of Verdun, to the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) for $257,425 plus taxes.
The sale comes with easements for right of way, load limitation and no construction on a neighbouring lot, which corresponds to municipal parking lot T520.
The four lots involved are closed and withdrawn from the public domain.
The transaction allows the STM to regularize its titles and to carry out the rebuilding and expansion of the metro's mechanical ventilation station, known as PVM Rielle.
Construction work is already under way and is to continue until December 2027; the STM is occupying the parking lot free of charge during the work.
The price is paid on the day the deed is signed; the sale is made without warranty, at the STM's risk.
According to the document, the expanded station will be equipped with more effective silencers and will therefore be quieter for nearby residents.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve appoints Annick Barsalou to the position of borough secretary.
This position covers the duties of clerk for borough council business.
The appointment follows the departure of Dina Tocheva, who held the position.
Annick Barsalou had been acting as substitute borough secretary since 2015.
Olga Sacaliuc remains substitute borough secretary.
The file has no financial impact.
The City is paying $551,880 (taxes included) to Conseillers d'Affaires Embrase inc. to become the presenting partner of StartupFest 2026.
The event will be held from July 8 to 10, 2026 at the Grand Quai de Montréal, in a new "Salon de l'entrepreneuriat" zone open to the general public, with admission at $10.
The City gets a 900 sq. ft. space, 100 passes, 15 admissions for the VIP evening, speaking slots at the opening or closing, and a custom-made activation.
At its booth, the City plans two talks, an information area with PME MTL and the École des entrepreneurs du Québec, a demo area, one-on-one clinic-style meetings, and a space for other partners.
The project is being run as a pilot and will be evaluated over the three days of the event.
The expense is covered 100% by the agglomeration; the decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is ending the work supervision contract awarded to Groupe Civitas inc.
This contract, awarded on May 6, 2025, was worth $89,134.37 including taxes, plus $6,000 in contingencies.
It covered supervision of road work and the replacement of lead water service lines on various streets in the borough (PCPR 2025 project).
Reason given: more than 86% of the contract budget has been used and it might not be enough to pay for the closing of the project, planned for August 2026.
The borough's technical team (division Mobilité et Études techniques) will take over the remaining tasks.
A notice of termination was sent to Groupe Civitas on February 6, 2026.
According to the document, the termination has no financial impact for the City, which will not have to hire another firm.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is proposing to city council that it take on, itself, the minor repair of sidewalks on arterial streets in its territory in 2026.
A budget of $265,000, net of rebate, is allocated to the borough; the work is paid for by the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier.
The sidewalks concerned are those on streets where roadway rehabilitation is planned in the short term, as well as those flagged by requests and complaints from residents.
Planned schedule: call for tenders in March 2026, contract awarded in May 2026, work from May to July 2026.
The borough cites the high number of requests about the condition of sidewalks and about pedestrian safety.
City council must now accept this offer for the work to go ahead.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is awarding Construction Larotek inc. the repair of sidewalk sections on various local and arterial streets, for a maximum of $617,165.11, taxes included.

The total authorized spending comes to $785,739.87: the work, $61,716.51 in contingencies, $42,184.82 in incidentals and $64,673.44 for management and supervision awarded to EFEL Experts-conseils inc.
The bill is shared: 60% by the borough ($468,412.13) and 40% by the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier ($317,327.75), in 2026.
The work covers 790 m² of sidewalks paid for by the borough and 550 m² paid for by the central city, along with related work such as replacing catch basin heads and levelling access shafts.
The sections being redone are those with offsets, upheavals, depressions, cracks or holes, and universal access ramps are being added where required.
Eight companies submitted bids; the winning offer is the lowest, at $135.67 below the professionals' estimate.
Residents will be notified of the work by the borough; the contract is expected to be awarded in May 2026.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is awarding Cojalac inc. a contract for roadwork, traffic calming and the replacement of lead water service lines, for a maximum of $2,669,204.07 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $3,258,318.49, including $333,209.15 in contingencies and $255,905.27 in incidental costs, to be spent in 2026.
Four street sections are affected: rue Birnam (Ogilvy to Saint-Roch), avenue Stuart (Ball to Jarry Ouest), avenue Stuart (d'Anvers to Liège Ouest) and avenue d'Outremont (Ogilvy to Saint-Roch).
The work includes milling and repaving, sidewalk reconstruction, 11 sidewalk extensions (2 of them with drainage and tree pits), 2 speed bumps, road markings and signage.
Lead water service lines will be replaced, including the portion on private property: 32 confirmed and 6 possible on Birnam, 19 and 11 on Stuart, 2 and 1 on d'Outremont.
The net costs of the replacement work on the private side ($185,043.64 including taxes) will be billed to the residents concerned, under by-law 20-030.
Cojalac inc. was the lowest of the 8 bidders, at 17.92% below the estimate; the firm Les services EXP inc. will supervise the work and the contractor's performance will be evaluated.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a three-storey, eight-unit residential building at 11875, avenue Bellevois, between boulevard Gouin and boulevard Léger.
Each of the eight units will have three bedrooms; one unit is in the basement.

The project is granted exemptions from urban planning rules: up to 10 units instead of 6, a ground floor 1.6 m above the sidewalk instead of 0.5 m, a left side setback of 1.83 m instead of 2.28 m, and two parking spaces instead of four.
The developer plans two parking spaces in the backyard, six bicycle spaces, seven trees, 45 shrubs, 25 perennials and vegetable garden boxes for residents.
Work must begin within 18 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
A one-storey industrial building must first be demolished; the demolition application was filed on May 22, 2025 and falls under the demolition committee.

After the public consultation of February 25, 2026, no valid referendum request was received; the council files the secretary's certificate and corrects a cross-reference error (section 92.20 rather than 92.22).

The conseil d'arrondissement of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a three-storey, eight-unit residential building at 11895, avenue Bellevois, between boulevard Gouin and boulevard Léger.

The project is receiving four exemptions from planning rules: up to 10 units allowed instead of 6, a ground floor 1.6 m above the sidewalk instead of 0.5 m, a right side setback of 1.83 m instead of 2.28 m, and two parking spaces instead of four.
Each of the eight units will have three bedrooms; the project includes six bicycle spaces, seven trees, 45 shrubs, 25 perennials and vegetable planters in the back yard.
The one-storey industrial building on the lot must be demolished first; the demolition application, filed on May 22, 2025, falls under the demolition committee.
Work must begin within 18 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

Following the public consultation of February 25, 2026, no valid referendum request was received; the council is filing the secretary's certificate and correcting a cross-reference error (section 92.20 instead of 92.22).
The Montréal-Nord borough is approving three exemptions for a building at 3690, rue Monselet.
The right side setback may be 0.71 m instead of the required 2.28 m, and the frontage 6.53 m instead of 9.14 m.
Only one parking space will be required instead of two: the second would have meant cutting down a mature tree on public property.
The lot is only 9.26 m wide, which makes a compliant project impossible according to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain.
If the building loses half its value (demolition, fire or any other cause), it will have to be rebuilt according to the by-laws in force.
The authorization must follow the plans by architect Jean-Benoît Bourdeau dated January 21, 2026.
A public notice was published on February 17, 2026; interested people could be heard at the council meeting of March 9, 2026.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a three-unit, three-storey building at 3690, rue Monselet, a lot that until now had been used as a private parking area without authorization.

The building will include one 175 m² unit spread over three levels (4 bedrooms), one 80 m² unit on the ground floor (2 bedrooms) and one 77 m² unit on the second floor (2 bedrooms), each with its own outside entrance.
The cladding will be brick and stone in shades of beige and grey, with a flat roof, two terraces and a green roof of about 10.4 m².
One parking space is planned in the back yard; the landscaping includes 3 trees, 12 shrubs, 6 conifers and 34 perennials.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The developer must provide a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released only when construction is finished; the City may use it or keep it as a penalty if the work does not comply with the resolution.
The urban planning advisory committee recommended the project favourably on February 4, 2026, finding it compliant with the regulations.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a three-storey, 32-classroom elementary school on boulevard Albert-Hudon (lot 6 422 823).

The school will serve the northeast sector, where existing schools are at full capacity according to the document; the land has belonged to the Centre de services scolaire de la Pointe-de-l'Île since June 2021.
The project includes 61 parking spaces, a bus drop-off area, five playgrounds, a pedestrian path and a 610 m² micro-forest that will be preserved.
Two exemptions from the zoning by-law are granted: steel cladding on more than 20% of each wall, and 75 trees planted instead of the 118 required.
Work must begin within 24 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The council is also filing the minutes of the public consultation held on March 25, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a two-storey commercial and industrial building at 99999, boulevard Pie-IX (lot 4 711 806).
The building would have an area of 10,898.1 m² and would be built entirely within the borough; the parking areas and loading docks would be on the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension side.
Three exemptions from the zoning by-law are granted: more than 10% metal panels on the lower part of the front wall, 40 parking spaces instead of 60, and parking in the front yard.
The developer plans to plant 89 trees, 302 shrubs and 265 perennials across the whole site.
Work must begin within 36 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The land is contaminated, runs along the Canadien Pacifique railway line (transport of hazardous materials) and includes Hydro-Québec easements, including a pylon that limits the height of the building.
The minutes of the public consultation of April 22, 2026 are tabled; the coming into force is expected in May 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a three-storey, 32-classroom elementary school on boulevard Albert-Hudon (lot 6 422 823), near Cégep Marie-Victorin.
The Centre de services scolaire de la Pointe-de-l'Île has owned the land since June 3, 2021; the land comes from an expropriation authorized by the ministère de l'Éducation.
The building will have 25,015 m² of floor space, 61 parking spaces, a bus drop-off area, five playing fields, a pedestrian path and play modules.
The project includes 75 trees, 89 shrubs and 165 perennials, and keeps a 610 m² micro-forest.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The developer must post a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released at 25% once the foundations are done and at 75% on delivery.
According to the document, the school is meant to relieve overcrowding in the schools of the northeast sector, which are at full capacity.

The Montréal-Nord borough council is authorizing the construction of a three-storey, six-unit residential building at 99999, avenue Cadieux (lot 1 173 608), between boulevard Gouin and boulevard Albert-Brosseau.

The authorization allows three exemptions from the zoning rules: a third storey of 6.4 m instead of 3.7 m, indoor parking spaces of 4.75 m instead of 5.5 m, and a driving aisle of 4.75 m instead of 7.1 m.
Work must begin within 24 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The project includes three indoor parking spaces, three bicycle spaces, four four-bedroom units and two three-bedroom units, as well as the planting of six trees, shrubs and perennials.
The urban planning advisory committee recommended the application on March 18, 2026; a public consultation was held on April 22, 2026.
No valid application for approval by referendum was received within the set deadline, so the project is deemed approved by the persons entitled to vote.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a three-storey building with six housing units on avenue Cadieux, between boulevard Gouin and boulevard Albert-Brosseau.
Four of the six units will have four bedrooms and the other two will have three bedrooms; a terrace will serve the two third-floor units.
The building will have an indoor parking area with three spaces and three bicycle racks in the left side yard.
The exterior will be mostly reddish-toned clay brick, with sections in brown and charcoal grey steel; six trees, along with shrubs and perennials, will be planted.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The developer will have to post a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released only when construction is finished; the City may use it or keep it as a penalty if the work does not comply.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended the project on March 18, 2026; an earlier authorization had already been granted for exemptions to the height of the top storey and to parking.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is allowing a place of worship in the building at 9940, avenue de Cobourg, which brings into compliance a use that had already existed without a permit for a few years.
The place of worship cannot occupy more than 226 m² of floor space; the other part of the building is used as a recording and music practice studio.
Interior work will create two separate suites and bring the building into compliance with the Construction Code; the façade on avenue de Cobourg will be modified (openings, metal cladding).
The non-compliant parking spaces in the two front yards will be removed and replaced with grass and one tree per yard, plus five bicycle spaces on the Cobourg side.
Work must begin within 12 months, otherwise the authorization lapses; the outdoor landscaping must be finished within 6 months after the end of the transformation permit.
The owner must provide a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work and must renew, at each term, the notarized parking contract for six spaces.
A public notice was published on May 14, 2026, and the borough council decision is expected on June 8, 2026.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is approving a project for a three-storey residential building with eight units at 4801, boulevard Henri-Bourassa, at the corner of avenue Bellevois, across from parc Sauvé.
The project calls for four studios on the ground floor and two-bedroom units on the upper floors, two car parking spaces, four bicycle spaces, and the planting of nine trees.

The City is granting zoning exemptions: fewer units than the required minimum, a building footprint of 187 m² instead of 300 m², two parking spaces instead of four, more metal cladding than allowed, and a façade that is not parallel to the street.
The existing two-family building will have to be demolished; an application was filed on September 4, 2025 and the demolition committee must make a decision.
Work will have to start within 24 months of the resolution coming into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The process had to start over because one exemption had not been presented to the urban planning advisory committee or to the council; public consultation on June 17, 2026 and final adoption expected in September 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is allowing only 48 trees instead of the 99 required by the zoning by-law on the property at 6750, boulevard Gouin.
The Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal (OMHM) is planning work on the building and a redesign of the grounds: pedestrian paths, car lanes, a drop-off area and parking.
The property has 37 trees; the OMHM plans to plant 18 trees and 181 shrubs and perennials, and to cut down 4 diseased or dead trees.
According to a landscape architecture report submitted by the OMHM, 99 trees would create a planting density harmful to the health of the plants; the species chosen require 6 to 10 m of clearance.
If the building loses at least half of its value (demolition, fire or another cause) or becomes dangerous, its reconstruction will have to comply with the urban planning rules in force.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme recommended the application on April 8, 2026; a public notice was published on April 15 and the decision is being made at the borough council meeting of May 4, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a three-storey, eight-unit building at 11875, avenue Bellevois, between boulevard Gouin and boulevard Léger.
The eight units will each be about 94.3 m² and will all have three bedrooms.
The project includes two car parking spaces and six bicycle spaces in the back yard, as well as the planting of 7 trees, 45 shrubs and 25 perennials.
Work can only begin after the demolition of a one-storey industrial building currently on the site.
The developer must start the work within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

A financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work must be deposited when the permit is issued and will only be released when the work is finished; the City may use it or keep it as a penalty if the work does not comply.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable recommendation for the project on April 8, 2026; a specific project authorization (PPCMOI) had already been granted for exemptions from the zoning rules (ground floor height, left side setback, number of parking spaces and number of units).
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a three-storey, eight-unit building at 11895, avenue Bellevois, between boulevard Gouin and boulevard Léger.
The eight units will each be about 94.3 m² and will all have three bedrooms.
Work can only begin after a one-storey industrial building already on the lot is demolished.
The project includes two car parking spaces and six bicycle spaces in the backyard, as well as the planting of seven trees, 45 shrubs and 25 perennials.
The work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The developer must provide a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released only when the work is finished; if the developer fails to comply, the City can have the work carried out or keep the guarantee as a penalty.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable recommendation for the project on April 8, 2026, the application having been submitted on May 22, 2025.

The borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville is entrusting the Office de consultation publique de Montréal (OCPM) with a consultation process leading to the adoption of a local public participation framework.
Step 1, in the summer and fall of 2026: the OCPM will consult residents and local organizations to draw up a picture of current practices and gather expectations and concerns, then submit a summary.
Step 2, in the winter of 2027: the borough will draft a preliminary framework, which will be submitted to an OCPM consultative commission, which will produce a report.
The public participation framework is expected to be adopted in the summer of 2027.
No amount is specified: the borough is committing to pay the variable costs of the consultative commission in the winter of 2027.
The borough and the OCPM will coordinate communications to inform and engage the people of Ahuntsic-Cartierville.
The borough council adopted this request unanimously on June 8, 2026; the final decision rests with the City's executive committee.
Montréal-Nord will hold a first "cyclovia" in the summer of 2026: streets in one area will be temporarily closed to cars for bicycles, scooters, skates, skateboards and pedestrians.
The borough council authorizes submitting the project to the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports, whose support program funds this type of initiative.
Total cost of the project: $18,160.33, of which $10,853 is expected from the City's program and $7,307.33 is paid by the borough out of its operating budget.
The deadline to submit the application is April 15, 2026.
The director of culture, sports, recreation and social development is authorized to sign the application and the commitments that come with it.
According to the document, without this funding, the project could be jeopardized.
The planned activities are free and are aimed at residents of all ages, with schools, local organizations and families.
The City is hiring Axia services and Groupe de sécurité Garda to provide security guard services at several municipal facilities, for a total expense of $7,072,093.44, taxes included.
Axia services gets lots 1 and 2 ($2,619,500.77) and Groupe de sécurité Garda gets lots 3 to 6 ($4,452,592.67).
The contracts run for 36 months, with two possible extensions of 12 months each.
The sites covered include the Cité des Hospitalières, the marché Bonsecours, the complexe sportif Claude-Robillard, the SIM headquarters, rolling stock facilities and large parks.
Other lots serve as banks of hours: accompanying suppliers in SPVM buildings, call for tenders visits, unplanned needs and emergency measures (floods, emergency housing).
The volume of services is estimated at 67,352 hours per year; the agglomeration covers 24.26% of the expense, or $1,715,586.98.
The City will assess the performance of both firms; public call for tenders 26-21331 received 4 bids.

The borough of Ville-Marie is awarding Tech Vac Environnement inc. a contract for hydro-excavation services, including the transport and disposal of residues, for a maximum expense of $1,931,580, taxes included.
The contract runs from March 11, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with no possibility of extension.
The contract provides for 5,100 hours of service in total, or about 1,700 hours per year, from Monday to Sunday.
The rates submitted are $295/hour on weekdays, $370/hour on Saturdays and Sundays and $350/hour for emergencies; the winning bid is $305,833.50 (-13.67%) lower than the borough's estimate.
Five companies submitted bids out of 12 that obtained the tender documents; Profusion G.N.P. inc. was found non-compliant for lack of an RBQ category 2.5 licence.
The expense is paid entirely by the borough out of its operating budget, and the supplier's performance will be evaluated.
The borough cites the density of underground infrastructure and the increase in breakages during excavation with a mechanical shovel to justify this method.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding Les Entreprises Michaudville inc. a contract for minor sidewalk repairs on a few streets, for $981,000 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,177,200, adding $98,100 in contingencies and $98,100 in incidental costs.
The work involves rebuilding about 2,005 m² of sidewalks, 156 m² of structural sidewalks for tree pits, 114 metres of concrete curbs, and de-paving work.
The work site is to run from June 1 to August 30, 2026, over 90 calendar days.
Eight companies submitted bids; the lowest bid is 29.40% below the City's in-house estimate.

The bill is covered 90.36% by the borough and 9.64% by the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier; the borough pays the de-paving portion alone ($265,535.17) because the program's grant is suspended.
Notices will be sent to nearby residents before the work starts (obstructions, access, parking).
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is paying $50,000 to the Société de développement commercial (SDC) du Quartier Villeray for the year 2026, from January 1 to December 31.
The money is to be used only for operating expenses: staff salaries and benefits, rent for an office space, computer equipment and stationery.

To receive the full amount, the SDC must provide a resolution from its board of directors, its action plan and budget, a liability insurance certificate, as well as the previous year's financial report and activity report.
The borough's director of territorial development is authorized to sign the agreement on behalf of the City.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget.
An identical amount of $50,000 had been granted to the same SDC for the year 2025.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $102,045 to the Société de développement commercial du Quartier Villeray to organize a summer pedestrian street project.
The pedestrian street will be rue Villeray, between rue Lajeunesse and avenue De Gaspé, from mid-June to the end of summer 2026.
The project is moving: since 2021 the pedestrian street had been on rue De Castelnau, but construction work is planned there in 2026.
The City plans to optimize parking in the area to make up for the spaces removed, according to the document.
The grant to the SDC covers, among other things, landscaping and furniture ($56,275), shows ($23,000) and a visual art exhibition ($16,100).
Total project budget: $250,798, including $123,250 from the Service du développement économique, $66,448 in borough labour and $61,100 from the SDC.
The borough is keeping $21,205 of the grant for signage ($12,105) and communications ($9,100).
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving up to $15,000 to the Association des commerçants de Villeray Est, for a period ending August 14, 2026.
The money will be used to hire a project manager for about 3 months to bring merchants together and set up the new association.
The area covered lies between rue Christophe-Colomb, rue Jarry Est, boulevard Saint-Michel and Bélanger/Jean-Talon Est: 266 businesses, including a significant number of vacant units.
The project manager will go door to door to the 266 businesses, run a survey, send out invitations to the Rues Principales workshops, and handle the association's administrative management.
The project complements a mandate given to Rues Principales to develop a vision and an action plan for commercial development in the area.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city, through the support program for commercial areas located outside the SDC districts.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is allowing a street food truck in the parking lot of the chalet Jean-Paul II in parc Jarry, reached from boulevard Saint-Laurent near rue Gounod.

The authorization runs from June 3 to November 15, 2026: weekends and statutory holidays from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., weekday evenings from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m., and from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays if the parking lot is available.
Only trucks certified by the Association des restaurateurs de rue du Québec (ARRQ), with all their permits in order, may set up there.
The ARRQ manages the site: it recruits the operators, assigns the spots each day, checks the permits (MAPAQ, SAAQ, CNESST, fire) and requires $3M in liability insurance for the benefit of the City.
Only non-alcoholic drinks may be sold, in recyclable containers with no glass, and consumed on site; operators must keep the area clean.
Events already authorized by borough order take priority over street food.
The file provides for no spending; the ARRQ will post the schedule on cuisinederue.org.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is appointing Christiane Richard, economic development commissioner, to sit on the board of directors of the SDC du Quartier Villeray.
The borough by-law on SDCs requires the council to appoint an elected official or a City employee to the SDC's board of directors.
This board of directors has nine members: six member merchants, two people chosen by those six directors, and one person designated by the borough.
City councillor Martine Musau Muele will be able to sit on it as an observer, if the SDC's board of directors approves.
This appointment replaces the one made in November 2025, which gave the seat to councillor Martine Musau Muele.
No spending is associated with the decision.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $50,000 to the Association commerçants Legendre Saint Michel for the period from July 8, 2026 to June 1, 2027.
The money will be used to promote boulevard Saint-Michel: social media management, website, newsletter and video content.
It will also pay for the upkeep of street furniture and the ground mural on the back sidewalk of boulevard Saint-Michel, between rue Legendre and rue Émile-Journault.
Part of it goes to the coordination of the merchants' association and to the second edition of the Saint-Michel en Fête event.

The money comes from a central city program for commercial streets located outside the territories of the commercial development corporations; the borough receives $164,000 per year from 2025 to 2027.
The expense is entirely covered by the central city; the director of territorial development is authorized to sign the agreement.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Maude Jette-Lalonde as a planning advisor in the Division de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité, starting February 21, 2026.
The position becomes permanent if she successfully completes the probation period set out in the collective agreement for municipal professionals.
Her annual salary is $86,272, within a scale ranging from $65,937 to $110,907 for 2026.
The position had been vacant since the transfer of the previous planning advisor; an internal job posting ran from November 10 to 18, 2025.
The borough cites the smooth handling of files and the ongoing regulatory review aimed at compliance with the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is reorganizing its Direction de l'aménagement urbain et des services aux entreprises as of March 21, 2026.
The mobility team is moving from the Division des études techniques to the Division de l'urbanisme.
Three positions are being transferred: a senior technical officer, a technical officer for traffic and parking (both with the employees who hold them) and a vacant planning advisor position.
Half of the budget for an administrative unit secretary position is also being transferred to the Division de l'urbanisme.
The Division de l'urbanisme is being renamed Division de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité.
The borough says it wants to bring the management of planning and mobility projects together under a single division.
The change is paid for out of the operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Francis Laporte as planning advisor in the Division de l'urbanisme, effective March 21, 2026.
Permanent status will depend on successfully completing the probationary period set out in the collective agreement for municipal professionals.
The 2026 salary scale for this job runs from $65,937 to $110,907.
The position was vacant after the transfer of the planning advisor who held it.
The candidate comes from an eligibility list created through an internal job posting held from November 10 to 18, 2025.
The borough cites the need to handle the division's files and the by-law review under way to comply with the PUM.
The expense will be paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Jean-François Therrien as a research officer in the Division de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité, effective April 18, 2026.
The appointment leads to permanent status if he successfully completes the probationary period set out in the collective agreement for municipal professionals.
The position had been vacant since the departure of its previous permanent holder; an internal posting was held from February 2 to 6, 2026.
The 2026 salary range for this job runs from $59,834 to $100,222.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough cites the handling of the division's files, the by-law review under way to comply with the PUM, and team stability.

The City is extending by 12 months two contracts for the collection, transport and disposal of household garbage and organic waste from front-loading containers and semi-buried containers, awarded to Waste Connections of Canada inc. / Enviro Connexions.
The services, offered to eligible customers in the 19 boroughs, are maintained until October 31, 2027 instead of October 31, 2026.

It authorizes an additional expense of $3,847,789.52, taxes included: $2,358,042.79 for the extension, $650,862.39 in contingencies, $796,242.21 in quantity variation and $42,642.14 in price adjustment.
The total value of the two contracts goes from $7,586,379.26 to $11,434,168.78, an increase of 50.72%.
The urban agglomeration is covering 31% of the expense, or $1,194,469.26.
The City explains the increase by a larger than expected quantity of garbage sent to landfill and by front-loading containers that were forgotten at the time of the call for tenders.
The supplier accepted the renewal on February 23, 2026 and is not listed in the register of ineligible companies or on the list of suppliers with unsatisfactory performance.
The City is adding $2,516,716.70 (taxes included) to seven household waste disposal contracts, bringing their total value to $13,086,926.84, an increase of 23.81%.

The contracts affected are those of WM Québec inc. (collection in the LaSalle borough) and Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. (non-recoverable construction waste from the Acadie, Côte-des-Neiges, LaSalle, La Petite-Patrie, Rivière-des-Prairies and Saint-Michel ecocentres).
The money is split into $1,006,686.68 in contingencies and $1,510,030.02 for the variation in quantities.

The contracts are being used up faster than expected: the temporary closure of all gypsum recyclers in Québec sent that material to landfill, and traffic at the ecocentres has increased. For the LaSalle lot, the quantities had been underestimated.

Despite the addition, only the Saint-Michel ecocentre would reach the planned end date of October 31, 2028; the other contracts would run out between June 2027 and April 2028, forcing the City to launch new calls for tenders.
The expense is paid 100% by the Montréal agglomeration, spread over 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The City is accepting a $13.5M grant from the ministère de l'Environnement to relaunch a program that helps pay for the decontamination of land on its territory.
The money would be paid in a single instalment as soon as the agreement is signed. The agreement would expire on March 31, 2031, with two possible one-year extensions.
Owners of polluted land could receive grants covering 15% to 100% of eligible expenses, with half paid as soon as the work begins.
Total public funding is capped at 75% of eligible expenses, or 90% for social housing projects, on-site soil treatment and the reuse of contaminated soil.
The City keeps 5% of the funding paid out as administrative fees (maximum $50,000 per project) and 2% of the estimated amount when a private project is turned down.
The 2018 agreement (increased to $93.5M) has not accepted new applications since January 1, 2024; 90 projects were approved and about $5.6M is still available.
Announced schedule: signing and development of the program in spring-summer 2026, launch and receipt of applications in fall 2026.

The City is extending by six months the deadline for organizations to submit an application for a subsidy offsetting the increase in property taxes following work on buildings housing artists' studios.
The deadline goes from 4 years to 4 years and 6 months from the signing of the financial contribution agreement.
This change follows the six-month extension, decided in the summer of 2025, of the work period for all files admitted to the program.
The program is intended for cultural and real estate organizations that own or rent non-residential buildings in the Montréal agglomeration.
It stems from a $25M agreement signed in 2021 with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications, to which the City added about $5M for other phases of the projects.
The program's funding is 100% covered by the agglomeration; the credits have already been approved.
The City is reaching an agreement with the Ministère de l'Environnement (MELCCFP) to reuse the unspent amounts from the $75M grant signed in 2018 to decontaminate land in Montréal.
These amounts, freed up by projects that were cancelled or cost less than expected, came to nearly $11.2M as of May 14, 2026.
No new grant is being given: the agreement only serves to release money already paid out, which was frozen because the 2018 agreement had expired.
Combined with the new $13.5M agreement signed in March 2026, these amounts will make up a program of about $24.7M to rehabilitate contaminated land.
The funds will have to be committed by December 31, 2029 at the latest, with an annual report on September 30 and a final report within 12 months after the work is completed.
Planned timeline: signing in June 2026, development of the program in spring-summer 2026, launch and applications in fall 2026.
The file has no budget impact for the City.

The borough of Ville-Marie is signing an agreement with the developer 9399-8532 Québec inc. to build the streets and infrastructure for the « Quartier Molson » project, on the former site of the Molson brewery, south of rue Notre-Dame between Atateken and Papineau.
The work, estimated at $54,883,704 including taxes, extends 5 streets over about 1,000 metres: de la Commune, Montcalm, de la Visitation, Panet and Alexandre-DeSève.
The developer is paying a share estimated at $44,045,197; the City is covering $10,838,507 for the off-site work on Notre-Dame and for the oversizing of the retaining wall.
The plan includes: water and sewer lines, buried electrical network, lighting, roadway, sidewalks, tree planting, street furniture, signage and changes to 3 traffic lights on Notre-Dame.
A retaining wall 491 metres long and about 6 metres high will be built south of the future rue de la Commune, along the railway tracks.
The developer must provide a bank guarantee of $10,976,741, valid until the City's final acceptance of the work.
The developer's contractors will have to be authorized by the Autorité des marchés publics for subcontracts of $1M or more (services) or $5M or more (construction).
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is buying six tickets to the ESTim gala held by the Chambre de commerce de l'Est de Montréal, at a cost of $2,062.65, taxes included.
The gala will take place on May 7, 2026; six people will represent the borough there.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget, and the funds are certified as available.
The borough justifies its participation by the strengthening of its ties with businesses and organizations in the area.
The gala aims to raise the profile of businesses and organizations that have distinguished themselves, according to the document.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $1,000, taxes included, to support the 35th CIRIEC International Congress.
The congress takes place in Montréal on October 5 and 6, 2026 (the financial record says October 5 to 8).
The amount covers a package of 10 tickets, paid out of the borough's operating budget.

The event is expected to bring together more than 500 decision-makers, researchers and leaders from the social economy and public enterprises, from about thirty countries, under the theme "Prendre soin du monde".
The borough justifies the spending by the international visibility it gains and the support it gives to the Québec model of social economy.
The decision rests with the borough council; the funds are certified as available.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is paying $35,883.39 (taxes included) to Constructions Doyle, under a contract awarded without a call for tenders, for securing the building at 5986-5992, avenue du Parc and its surroundings.
The money comes from the borough's management surplus.
The work was ordered on site on July 4, 2025 by the Service de sécurité incendie, after the partial collapse of the vacant building and the evacuation of neighbouring buildings.
The measures included a safety perimeter, set up on July 5, 2025, and the widening of a safety corridor in the back lane, requested on July 23.
One traffic lane on avenue du Parc was removed in July and August 2025; the markers were taken away in mid-August.
The building was demolished on August 5, 2025 and the tenants of the neighbouring buildings returned on August 19, 2025.
According to the document, the borough had been monitoring the building since May 2010 because of unsanitary conditions complaints, and it had been permanently evacuated in 2022.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is setting aside $125,131.75 from its management surplus to secure and maintain the lot at 5986-5992, avenue du Parc and its surroundings.
The money will go toward fencing (metal, wood, plywood), signage, disconnecting the electricity, environmental monitoring and, possibly, decontaminating the site.
The three-storey building, which was vacant and considered dangerous, was demolished on August 5, 2025; the lot is now empty and the neighbouring tenants have moved back into their homes.
The borough says it cannot reach the owner, who is not taking on their responsibilities, so the borough is taking charge of the upkeep.
Background: unsanitary conditions complaints since May 2010, permanent evacuation in 2022, falling bricks and an emergency intervention by the Service de sécurité incendie on July 4, 2025.
Spending already approved for this site: $747,683.63 for the demolition, $113,564.96 for professional services and $35,883.39 for safety measures.
The amount includes $16,321.53 in contingencies (15%) and the provision is planned on an annual basis.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is replacing its noise by-law, in force since 1977, with a new by-law (2026-01) adopted on May 4, 2026 and in force as soon as it is published.
The permitted noise levels in bedrooms stay the same, but those for other rooms in dwellings go up by 4 dBA.

For performance halls, the by-law introduces "spectral emergence": 3 dB from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. and 4 dB from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. above residual noise. The maximum level inside stays at 98 dBA, with the addition of a maximum of 118 dBC.

Bars, restaurants, dance halls, reception halls, maisons de la culture and other places with amplified sound will be subject to a correction index when low frequencies dominate; this index also targets the humming of mechanical equipment.
The SPVM keeps its power to order that a noise be stopped, except in performance halls, where only the borough's director of territorial development can do so.
The by-law provides support for bars and performance halls that want it, and minimum fines for certain establishments in case of non-compliance.
The provisions on road vehicles are removed from the by-law, and exceptions will allow work on public property outside authorized hours.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga–Maisonneuve will install mandatory stop signs in all directions at the intersection of rue Ontario Est and rue Leclaire.
The request comes from the SPVM: rue Leclaire serves as a school corridor for students of école primaire Saint-Clément, who cross at this intersection.
Estimated cost of the new signage: about $1,200, paid by the borough out of its annual signage budget.
Advance-notice signage will be put up at least 30 days beforehand, that is, in July 2026.
The stop signs will come into effect in August 2026, after adoption by the borough council on May 4, 2026.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is temporarily removing 113 paid parking spaces for the summer pedestrianization of rue Ontario Est.
The removal applies from September 15 to 17, 2026, inclusively: the parking meters are taken out on June 17, 2026 and come back on September 17, 2026.
The affected spaces are on rue Ontario Est and on cross streets: Charlemagne, D'Orléans, Joliette, Aylwin, Cuvillier, Davidson and Darling.
The Agence de mobilité durable is the one carrying out the removal of the parking meters; borough council approval is required before the official request.
There is no impact on the borough's finances, since the parking meters were installed before 2023.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité gave a favourable opinion with no conditions.
Last year, 115 spaces had been removed for the same operation.
The Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough is making the southbound one-way traffic on avenue Desjardins, between rue La Fontaine and rue Adam, permanent.
This layout had been put in place temporarily during the SRB Pie-IX construction work to keep the avenue from being used as a detour.
The administration of école primaire Saint-Nom-de-Jésus asked that it be kept after the work.
The school bus drop-off area therefore stays on avenue Desjardins: students no longer get off on boulevard Pie-IX and go directly into the schoolyard.
The temporary construction signs will be replaced with permanent signs in July or August 2026, at an estimated cost of about $750.
Without this decision, northbound traffic would resume when the occupancy permit tied to the SRB construction site ends.
No communications campaign is planned, since the current situation stays the same.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is permanently removing four paid parking spaces on rue Aylwin, just north of rue Ontario Est.
The parking meters involved are MA-505, MA-506, MA-507 and MA-508.
The freed-up space will be used to install an electrified BIXI station that can be used year-round: a curb extension has already been built at this location.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité gives a favourable opinion with no conditions.
No impact on the borough's finances: the Agence de mobilité durable is paying for the removal of the meters.
Next step after approval by the borough council: removing the parking meters and deleting them from the Agence de mobilité durable's database.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is closing avenue du Mont-Royal to cars: from May 25 to September 10, 2026 between Resther and De Lorimier, and from May 25 to October 15, 2026 between Saint-Laurent and Resther.
Avenue Duluth is closed to cars between boulevard Saint-Laurent and rue Saint-Hubert, from June 16 to October 15, 2026.

Bicycles, scooters and other light modes of transport are allowed; motorcycle-style power-assisted bikes, flat-platform scooters and electric mopeds are prohibited. Deliveries and maintenance are possible from 7 a.m. to 11 a.m., seven days a week.
All on-street parking spaces are removed in the affected zones, and STM buses no longer serve the Mont-Royal metro station, except for paratransit.
Merchants on both streets may occupy up to 2.5 m² of the roadway for display and sales, prepare and sell food, and hand out samples.
Some one-way streets are reversed (Cartier, Marquette, Rivard), Gilford becomes two-way between Chambord and Lanaudière, and some intersections (Bullion, Fabre, Saint-Hubert) are closed to cars.

In September 2026, the “short” section of Mont-Royal is extended to Resther to include the Mont-Royal metro station and place Gérald-Godin during the UCI World Championships, subject to approval by the SPVM and the STM.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a $287,724.94 contract (taxes included) to the non-profit organization SOCIOCYCLE, that is $143,862.47 per year.

On request, SOCIOCYCLE will transport people with reduced mobility and seniors along the pedestrianized avenue du Mont-Royal, using three-wheeled cargo bikes that can pass between the safety barriers.
The service is free for users and replaces the bus lines that are rerouted while the street is closed.

The contract covers the period from May 4, 2026 to December 31, 2027; in 2026, the service will run from the week of June 1 to the week of October 12, with a management report at the end of October 2026.
The 2027 edition will take place only if the pedestrianization project is renewed and if the agreement is respected.
The borough will promote the service to residential care centres and to selected businesses on the avenue (pharmacies, clinics, optometrists).
In 2025, a similar contract of $91,980 had been awarded to the company VÉLO DUO.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is setting rules for music played in the street during the 2026 pedestrianization of avenue du Mont-Royal and avenue Duluth.
Electric or amplified instruments are banned on public property in these pedestrianized areas.
Playing an instrument there is also banned between 9 p.m. and 8 a.m.
Avenue du Mont-Royal is pedestrianized from May 28 to September 7, with a partial extension until October 12; avenue Duluth, from June 18 to October 12.
The borough says it is responding to complaints from local residents about the frequency and intensity of musical performances outside the official program.
There is no cost associated with the decision; a communications plan is being prepared with the merchants' associations.
The borough of Anjou is allowing alcoholic drinks to be served and consumed at special events organized by its Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
The authorization covers two exhibition openings at the salle d'exposition Goncourt, at 7500, avenue Goncourt, on April 28 and May 14, 2026, from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m.
The authorization cannot be transferred to another organization or event.
Those in charge must obtain a "Permis de réunion" (gathering permit) from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux at their own expense, if applicable.
Logistical support costs are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
The order takes effect on the day the public notice is published on the City's website.
The borough of Anjou is authorizing three events in May 2026 by lifting certain rules on noise, music and use of public property.
Revue sur glace by Patinage Anjou, at aréna Chaumont (8750, avenue de Chaumont), from May 1 to 3, 2026, from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m.: alcohol permitted, excessive noise and lighting devices authorized.
Olympiades by Collège d'Anjou, at parc Lucie-Bruneau (7051, avenue de l'Alsace), on May 21, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.: playing music permitted.

Jeunes en valeur by Concertation Anjou, at parc Roger-Rousseau (7501, avenue Rondeau), on May 30, 2026, from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.: food sales, use of the sidewalk, trailer connected to municipal services, music, noise and lighting.
No parking on avenue Jean-Desprez, west side, between 7326 and boulevard de Châteauneuf, from May 30, 2026 at 5 p.m. to May 31, 2026 at 8 p.m.
The organizations pay all the costs of the events and must obtain a gathering permit from the Régie des alcools themselves if alcohol is served.
The authorizations are not transferable and take effect when the public notice is published.
The Anjou borough council is allowing three organizations to be exempt from the by-law on peace, good order and nuisances for events in August and September 2026.

Corn roast held by Alcooliques Anonymes (région 87), at the centre and parc Roger-Rousseau, 7501 avenue Rondeau, on August 8, 2026 from 9 a.m. to midnight: the park may stay open later, and food sales, music and noise are allowed before 7 a.m. and after 11 p.m.
Corn roast held by the Jardin communautaire Roi-René, on August 21, 2026 from 5 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.: serving and drinking alcohol, as well as playing music, are allowed.
Calendar sale by the 150e groupe scout Notre-Dame d'Anjou in the borough's streets, on September 19, 2026 from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.: asking for donations is allowed.
The organizations pay all the costs of the events themselves and must obtain a gathering permit from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux if needed.
The authorization cannot be transferred to anyone else and takes effect as soon as the public notice is published.

The borough of Anjou is authorizing two public events in September 2026: the Portes ouvertes at parc Goncourt and the bibliothèque Jean-Corbeil on September 12 (11 a.m. to 4 p.m.), and a flea market on September 26.
The city hall parking lot (7701, boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine) will be closed from September 11 at 7 a.m. to September 12 at 8 p.m., and then from September 25 at 6 p.m. to September 27 at 6 p.m.
The parking lot next to 7500, avenue Goncourt will also be partly closed on September 11, 12, 25 and 26, and spaces will be reserved on boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine and avenue Goncourt.

Traffic will be slowed near city hall on September 12 from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., and blocked on boulevard Louis-H.-La Fontaine (between Yves-Prévost and the 1st entrance to the city hall parking lot) on September 26 from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. and from 2:30 p.m. to 4 p.m.
Food sales will be allowed on the sites, and the ban on noise before 7 a.m. and after 11 p.m. is lifted for these events.
The costs of the services and logistical support are paid out of the operating budgets of the departments concerned; the orders take effect as soon as the public notice is published.
The borough of Ville-Marie is settling a dispute with 9056-6316 Québec inc. out of court and will reimburse the company a total of $1,245,156.49.
This amount includes $783,313.36 in overpayments, $387,836.69 in interest as of June 17, 2026, and $74,006.44 in expert appraisal fees.
