The dispute was about the "park fees" charged for a building permit at 950, 970 and 990, rue Saint-Antoine Ouest and 750, rue Mansfield.
The owner had paid $1,705,650.10 in 2020, calculated on a site value of $20,035,000 set by the firm CAPREA.

The parties now agree on a value of $10,834,000, which brings the compensation amount down to $922,336.74, because the requirement to keep the facades of the existing building led to extra construction costs.
The project in question calls for a 25-storey mixed-use building with 3 commercial spaces, 278 housing units, 109 car parking spaces and 100 bicycle parking spaces.
The agreement avoids a five-day hearing scheduled at the Tribunal administratif du Québec from June 15 to 18, 2026, whose outcome the borough considered uncertain.
The Ville-Marie borough is spending $1,600 to buy a table for 10 people at the 40th Grand Prix du Conseil des arts de Montréal.
The event takes place on April 2, 2026, at the Palais des congrès de Montréal.
The $1,600 is the "corporate table" rate for businesses and municipal departments; arts organizations supported by the Conseil des arts pay $1,300.
The money comes from the borough's hospitality expenses budget and is paid to the Conseil des arts de Montréal.
The borough takes part every year: $1,550 in 2025, $1,450 in 2024, $1,350 in 2023 and in 2022.
According to the document, taking part is meant to support local organizations and to give the borough visibility in cultural programming.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Marie Noël-de-Tilly as planning advisor in the Division des relations avec les citoyens et communications, effective February 21, 2026.
The position becomes permanent if she successfully completes the probationary period set out in the collective agreement for municipal professionals.
The proposed annual salary is $110,907, which is the top of the salary scale for group 29-002 (minimum $65,937, 2025 scale).
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
According to the document, the position is being filled because of an organizational transformation, and it serves to coordinate and manage projects across the organization.
The candidate was selected following a job posting and interviews held on January 19, 23 and 26, 2026 by a three-person committee.

The City is giving $275,000 to the organization Quartier des arts du cirque (QUAC) for a commercial and entrepreneurial development project on rue Jarry Est, in Saint-Michel (Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension).
The money will be paid in four instalments: $100,000 in 2026, $100,000 in 2027, $50,000 in 2028 and $25,000 in 2029. The expense is paid 100% by the central city.

The project includes an "entrepreneurial Lab" for young people and people from immigrant backgrounds: training workshops, a micro-business in a shipping container during the summer, then a shared commercial space open year-round starting in 2027.
This shared space is to house a solidarity grocery store (Vivre Saint-Michel en Santé) and a youth social bakery (Trajet OJA), in an area described as a food desert.
Second part: creating a merchants' association, 8 weeks of summer activities, distinctive signage and help with fixing up storefronts.
The grant covers support staff salaries, setting up the micro-business, promotion and insurance.
The start is planned for August 2026, with an accounting of results each year in August from 2027 to 2029.
The Ville-Marie borough is authorizing the conversion into divided co-ownership of a 4-unit building at 2270, rue du Souvenir, despite the general ban.
The building is a 3-storey row house on the south side of rue du Souvenir, between avenue Atwater and rue Lambert-Closse, in the Peter-McGill district.
The exemption is allowed because at least half of the units are occupied by owners; the other 2 units are vacant.
A borough inspection confirmed that the units are habitable and the application was found to be admissible.
No comments were sent to the borough secretary during the 10 days following the notice published on February 7, 2026.
The decision summary notes a vacancy rate of 2.9% in the Montréal region in 2025 (below the balance threshold of 3.1%) and that 73.9% of the units in the district are occupied by tenants.
There is no financial aspect attached to the decision.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is adding $53,032.45 (taxes included) to the contract with the firm Bouthillette Parizeau inc. for architecture and engineering services.
This amount serves as a reserve for unexpected costs (contingencies) in the greenhouse gas reduction project at Patro Villeray, a recreation and community support centre.
The total cost of the contract goes from $396,697.08 to $449,729.53.
The bill is shared: $13,735.40 paid by the borough (25.9%) and $39,297.05 by the provincial PEV-DIM grant (74.1%).
The conditions encountered on the work site forced the professionals to issue change directives, resulting in additional fees.
The provision must be committed before March 31, 2026 and spent before March 31, 2027; the work is expected to be finished at the end of May 2026.
Without this authorization, according to the document, the work could not be completed.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is awarding DCR Construction (9496-1687 Québec inc.), the lowest compliant bidder, the work to redevelop the reception area and gymnasium of the centre Patro Villeray, at 7355, avenue Christophe-Colomb.
The contract is worth a maximum of $3,947,174.53, taxes included; the total authorized spending comes to $4,933,968.17, with $789,434.91 in contingencies (20%) and $197,358.73 in incidental costs.
The work covers the ground-floor reception area (open area, bistro space, kitchen without cooking, two offices, removal of plaster coating containing asbestos) and the basement.

In the basement: new men's and women's change rooms, a universally accessible change room with 2 toilets and 2 showers, a new gymnasium floor, 2 motorized divider curtains, an acoustic curtain and 8 new motorized basketball hoops.

Funding is shared between the provincial-federal PAFIRS grant ($3,161,686.80), the borough ($1,279,472.70) and the organization Patro-Villeray ($492,808.67), which received a donation from the Caisse Desjardins du Centre-Nord de Montréal.

Nine companies submitted bids out of 13 that took out the tender documents; the winning price is 28.95% lower than the latest estimate, a gap attributed to the contractor's availability and to competition.
The spending is planned for 2026 and 2027, and the contractor's performance will be evaluated.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is hiring Les industries Harnois inc. to design, supply and install a greenhouse complex at parc Frédéric-Back, in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood.
The contract is worth $499,865.92 including taxes; with $74,979.88 in contingencies (15%) for unforeseen costs, the authorized spending comes to $574,845.80.
The project includes two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, floor coverings, interior partitions, doors and a condensation water management system.
According to the decision summary, the greenhouses will make it possible to grow fruits and vegetables year-round, host groups and distribute the harvests at affordable prices in the neighbourhood.
The infrastructure is to be delivered in July 2026, work is to start in August 2026 and is expected to be completed in December 2026.
Funding comes from the federal Smart Cities Challenge grant (Montréal en commun) for goods and services delivered before July 31, and from the participatory budget for the rest.
Of the five companies that obtained the tender documents, only one submitted a bid; its price is $11,222.17 above the estimate, or 2.30%.

The City is partnering with the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie, RECYC-QUÉBEC and the École de technologie supérieure in a $1,295,000 agreement on the circular economy in construction.
Montréal is putting in $300,000, that is $100,000 per year from 2026 to 2028, which represents 23.1% of the total; the expense is covered by the agglomeration.
The other contributions: $700,000 from the ministère, $260,000 from the ÉTS and $35,000 from RECYC-QUÉBEC (2026 only, the rest to be determined).
The agreement will fund projects to reduce waste in construction, renovation and demolition: training for workers, testing of circular practices by businesses.
The ÉTS's CÉRIEC manages the agreement, coordinates the work, administers the funds and assesses the results.
The agreement covers the metropolitan region but gives priority to the agglomeration of Montréal; Longueuil and Laval were not able to join it as of 2026.
Timeline: work starting in spring 2026, financial assistance paid out in summer-fall 2026, assessment in fall 2028.
The City wants to give $5,600,000 to Montréal International over four years, from 2026 to 2029, to attract foreign investment.

The money would fund four projects: a prospecting team for applied artificial intelligence, new promotional tools, support for businesses recruiting internationally, and prospecting in the circular economy and sustainable development.
The amount would also extend an agreement ending on March 31, 2026 on attracting businesses to the metropolitan innovation zones and to the East of Montréal.
The sectors targeted by this prospecting: life sciences and health, clean technologies, digital intelligence, cybersecurity and digital creativity.
The priority areas named are the East of Montréal, downtown and the metropolitan innovation zones.
The expense would be paid entirely by the agglomeration; the decision rests with the urban agglomeration council.
An agreement between the City and Montréal International would set the payment conditions.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is closing rue de Pontoise to car traffic, between rue Jean-Talon Est and rue Le Maître, on April 4, 2026 from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
The closure is for the free event "Pâques 2026", organized by the Société de développement commercial de la rue Jean-Talon, from 12 p.m. to 4 p.m.
On the program: an Easter riddle hunt in the businesses along rue Jean-Talon Est, between rue Valdombre and rue Michelet, followed by a welcome under a tent on rue de Pontoise.
The event is conditional on approval by the Service d'incendie de Montréal, because of access to the nearby Hôpital Santa-Cabrini.
The organization will have to obtain a permit to occupy public property and comply with the by-laws in force.
The comité des priorités recommended the closure at its meeting of February 9, 2026.
The Saint-Léonard borough is applying for a grant from Développement économique Canada to install shade canopies over its outdoor bocce courts.
The project would cover the ends of the nine bocce courts in Saint-Léonard's parks, to create shade and provide protection from bad weather.
The money would be used to buy the materials for the shelters and to pay for the professional services needed to build them.
The maximum eligible costs under the program is $800,000; the borough is applying for that maximum amount.
The borough commits to paying 100% of the non-eligible costs and any cost overruns.
The borough director is authorized to sign the financial assistance application documents.
According to the document, the project responds to requests from bocce clubs and from seniors who play this sport during the summer season.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $5,000 to the Collectif jeunesse de Saint-Léonard for the "Rues citoyennes 2.0 - volet 2" project in 2026.
The money comes from the Prévention Montréal program, which supports safe living environments for children, young people under 30 and their families.
The Rues citoyennes project turns certain streets into shared spaces to encourage active transportation and citizen participation.
The funded volet 2 is specifically for producing and distributing promotional material to make the initiative better known.
An agreement will set out the terms of the support paid to the organization; the detailed description of the project is attached to it.
For 2026, Saint-Léonard is receiving $145,166 for the "developing young people's full potential" stream and $408,821 for the "urban safety prevention" stream.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $50,000 to Concertation Saint-Léonard, the area's neighbourhood roundtable, for the 2026-2027 period.
The amount goes from $31,113 last year to $50,000, following an increase in the City's contribution decided in the 2026 budget.
Along with Centraide ($75,000) and the Direction régionale de santé publique ($23,472), the roundtable receives a total of $148,472.
The money is used for bringing together and mobilizing organizations, institutions and residents around local issues and the fight against poverty.
Concertation Saint-Léonard has supported urban revitalization in the Viau-Robert area since 2012 and in the Sud-Est area (domaine Choisy) since 2022.
An agreement will set out the terms of the support; the organization will have to carry out the project described in the appendix.
The Saint-Léonard borough council adopts a motion thanking Concertation Saint-Léonard for its 20 years of commitment to the community.
The organization will receive a framed certificate, as provided under the borough's recognition program for 10th, 15th and 20th anniversaries.
In 2026, 10 partner organizations are being honoured: 5 are celebrating their 50th anniversary, 1 its 40th, 3 their 30th and Concertation Saint-Léonard its 20th.
The awards are presented at a recognition ceremony held since 2013, where council members hand out plaques or certificates.
The adoption of the motions will be reported in the highlights of the June 1, 2026 borough council meeting on the website.
The decision summary does not mention any financial aspect.
The borough of Saint-Léonard adopts a motion to thank the Club d'âge d'or parc Delorme, which marks its 30th anniversary in 2026.
The Club organizes bingo and card nights, outings, bocce, fitness activities and annual parties for people aged 55 and over.
The motion is part of a recognition program created in 2013, which each year honours partner organizations celebrating a 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th, 30th, 40th or 50th anniversary.
Organizations receive an honorary plaque or a framed certificate at a ceremony; for a 30th anniversary, the plaque goes to those being recognized for the first time.
In 2026, 10 organizations in Saint-Léonard are being honoured, including five celebrating their 50th anniversary.
The adoption of the motions will be reported in the highlights of the June 1, 2026 borough council meeting, on the website.
The Saint-Léonard borough council adopts a motion to thank the Collectif jeunesse de Saint-Léonard, which is marking its 30th anniversary in 2026.
The organization brings together the borough's youth workers to carry out joint projects related to young people's development, civic participation and well-being.
The motion is part of a recognition program created in 2013, which each year honours partner organizations celebrating a 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th, 30th, 40th or 50th anniversary.
The organizations receive an honorary plaque or a framed certificate at a ceremony; for a 30th anniversary, it is a plaque if this is a first recognition.
In 2026, 10 organizations in the borough are being honoured, including five for their 50 years and three for their 30 years.
The adoption of the motions will be reported in the highlights of the June 1, 2026 borough council meeting, published on the website.
The Saint-Léonard borough council officially thanks the Maison de la famille de Saint-Léonard for its 30 years of involvement in the neighbourhood.
The organization provides guidance, parenting support and activities for the well-being of children and parents in the borough.
The motion is part of a recognition program in place since 2013, which each year marks the 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th, 30th, 40th and 50th anniversaries of partner organizations.
Honoured organizations receive a plaque or a framed certificate at a ceremony; for a 30th anniversary, the plaque is given if it is a first recognition.

In 2026, 10 Saint-Léonard organizations meet the criteria, including five celebrating 50 years (Mouvement fraternité multi-ethnique, Ligue de Tennis, Club de l'âge d'or Sacra Famiglia, Cercle d'artisanat, Association du hockey mineur).
No spending is planned in this file; the adoption of the motions will be posted on the borough's website after the June 1, 2026 meeting.
The Saint-Léonard borough council adopts a motion to thank Accueil aux immigrants de l'est de Montréal, which is marking its 40th anniversary in 2026.
The organization helps immigrants with their social, cultural and community integration, and provides information, support and guidance to newcomers in Saint-Léonard.
The organization will receive an honorary plaque if this is a first recognition, or otherwise a framed certificate, at a recognition ceremony.
In total, 10 partner organizations are being honoured in 2026: five for 50 years, one for 40 years, three for 30 years and one for 20 years.
The program recognizing organizations' anniversaries has existed in Saint-Léonard since 2013.
No money is attached to the decision; the motions will be reported in the highlights of the June 1, 2026 meeting on the website.
The Saint-Léonard borough council adopts a motion of thanks to the Association du hockey mineur St-Léonard inc. for its 50 years in the community.
The organization will receive an honorary plaque, presented at a recognition ceremony.
In 2026, 10 partner organizations of the borough are being honoured: 5 for their 50 years, 1 for its 40 years, 3 for their 30 years and 1 for its 20 years.
The recognition program has existed since 2013 and each year marks the 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th, 30th, 40th and 50th anniversaries of partner organizations.
No expense is listed in the file; the motion will be noted in the minutes of the council meeting of June 1, 2026.
The Saint-Léonard borough council adopts a motion thanking the Cercle d'artisanat de Saint-Léonard for its 50 years of presence in the community.
The organization brings together artisans through cultural activities and promotes weaving and creative skills in the borough.
The motion is part of a recognition program created in 2013, which each year marks the 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th, 30th, 40th and 50th anniversaries of partner organizations.
The organizations honoured receive a commemorative plaque (25th and 50th) or a framed certificate, at a recognition ceremony.
In 2026, 10 partner organizations are being honoured, including five celebrating their 50 years.
No amount is attached to this decision; it is made at the borough council meeting of June 1, 2026.
The Saint-Léonard borough council officially thanks the Club de l'âge d'or Sacra Famiglia for its 50 years of commitment to the community.
The organization offers people aged 55 and over bingo and card evenings, outings, fitness activities and annual celebrations.
The motion is part of a recognition program created in 2013, which each year marks the 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th, 30th, 40th and 50th anniversaries of partner organizations.
In 2026, 10 Saint-Léonard organizations are being honoured: 5 for their 50 years, 1 for its 40 years, 3 for their 30 years and 1 for its 20 years.
The organizations will receive an honorary plaque or a framed certificate at a recognition ceremony.
No amount is attached to this decision.
The Saint-Léonard borough council adopts a motion to thank the Ligue de Tennis de Saint-Léonard, which is celebrating its 50th anniversary in 2026.
The motion is part of a recognition program created in 2013 to mark the anniversaries of the borough's partner organizations (10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40 or 50 years).
The organizations honoured receive a plaque (25th or 50th anniversary) or a framed certificate (10th, 15th, 20th), at a ceremony with the members of the council.
In 2026, 10 partner organizations are being honoured, including 5 that are celebrating their 50th anniversary, among them the Ligue de Tennis.
The document does not provide for any spending; the adoption will be reported in the highlights of the June 1, 2026 meeting on the website.
The Saint-Léonard borough council thanks Mouvement fraternité multi-ethnique inc. for its 50 years of involvement in the neighbourhood.
The organization provides food support, family activities, a tax clinic, and information and civic participation workshops.
It works mainly with families and people from ethnocultural communities, often in socioeconomically vulnerable situations.
The motion is part of a recognition program in place since 2013: an honorary plaque for a 25th or 50th anniversary, and a framed certificate for a 10th, 15th or 20th.

In 2026, 10 partner organizations are being honoured, including five celebrating their 50th anniversary (tennis, minor hockey, âge d'or Sacra Famiglia, a crafts circle, and Mouvement fraternité multi-ethnique).
No sum of money is tied to this decision; the motions will be reported on the website after the June 1, 2026 meeting.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $10,171 to the organization Concertation Saint-Léonard for the "Rues citoyennes - volet 1" project in 2026.
The project turns certain streets into shared spaces to encourage active transportation and resident participation.
Volet 1 creates spaces for exchange and prevention: public events, the borough's cultural programming, door-to-door visits to homes and businesses, and follow-up after a crisis cell.
The money comes from the Prévention Montréal 2026 program, largely funded through an agreement with the ministère de la Sécurité publique.
Saint-Léonard is receiving $145,166 in 2026 for the "development of young people's full potential" stream and $408,821 for the "urban safety prevention" stream.
The organization will sign an agreement setting out the terms of the funding; the Comité des priorités recommended the payment on May 19, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $18,900 to 14 organizations to run activities at the Fête du citoyen 2026.
The event, now in its 30th year, will take place on September 13, 2026 at parc Wilfrid-Bastien; the borough is also marking its 140th anniversary.

The grants range from $300 (Société québécoise de spéléologie) to $3,250 (Gestion Multisports St-Léonard, for running the kermesse), including $2,100 to Concertation Saint-Léonard for an intercultural parade.
The funded activities are aimed at young people, families and seniors: cultural, food and virtual discovery, theatrical improvisation, and the history of Saint-Léonard.
The organizations will have to report back on how the money was used; the agreements end on October 31, 2026.
Last year, the same grants totalled $15,522.80 for the Fête du citoyen 2025.
Saint-Léonard is applying for a federal grant (New Horizons for Seniors Program) to install raised garden beds near the bocce courts.
Seven parks are involved: Delorme, Ferland, Giuseppe-Garibaldi, Hébert, Ladauversière, Luigi-Pirandello and Pie-XII.
About 10 beds per bocce court, plus gardening kits, placed against the fences to leave room for people with reduced mobility.
Seniors from the clubs d'âge d'or will look after the beds, with support from borough teams.
The program covers a maximum of $50,000 in eligible costs per project over one year.
The borough commits to paying 100% of non-eligible costs and any cost overruns.
The borough director is authorized to sign the financial assistance application documents.
The City is adding $700,000 in support to the Association des sports d'action for the Festival Jackalope: $200,000 in 2026, then $250,000 in 2027 and in 2028.
The original agreement provided for $100,000 ($50,000 in 2025 and $50,000 in 2026); support therefore rises to $250,000 per year and the agreement is extended to 2028.
The organization requested this adjustment on December 8, 2025, after an edition that ran a deficit.

The festival is free, lasts three days and brings together more than 120 action sports athletes in disciplines such as skateboarding; the 2026 edition will be held in the Vieux-Port, from September 11 to 13.
To pay for 2026, the City is transferring $200,000 from contingency expenses to the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs, and is adding $200,000 to its budget base for 2027 and 2028.
The expense is paid entirely by the agglomeration, as support for elite sport and major sporting events.
The document states that the 2024 edition generated an estimated economic impact of nearly $1.8M and 5,098 overnight stays, and that the 2025 edition drew more than 28,000 spectators.
The City is signing an agreement with Transports Canada to receive up to $733,672 under the Zero-Emission Trucking Program.

The money will fund initiatives on trucking and urban logistics: studies on freight movement, the purchase and testing of zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, pilot projects, and membership in industry networks.
Transports Canada reimburses up to 75% of eligible expenses; the costs must be incurred between May 24, 2024 and March 31, 2027.
The City must pay the costs up front and submit its final claim no later than June 30, 2027.
An additional revenue and expenditure budget of $733,672 is being added to the Division des stratégies de mobilité durable ($549,372 in 2025-2026, $184,300 in 2026-2027).
The signing depends on an order from the Government of Québec authorizing the agreement.
The City is giving $99,800 to Montréal, Arts Interculturels (MAI) to carry out its 2026 action plan, the same amount as in the previous five years.
Since 1998, the MAI has run the Centre interculturel Strathearn, at 3680, rue Jeanne-Mance, in the Milton-Parc neighbourhood.
The organization presents and supports Indigenous artists, racialized artists, artists with disabilities, neurodivergent artists and artists from 2SLGBTQQIPAA+ communities.
The money will be paid in two instalments: $84,800 within 30 days of the signing (March 2026) and $15,000 after the report is approved (January 2027).
The amount represents 15% of the budget for the MAI's action plan, estimated at $687,450, and is paid entirely by the central city.
The City is also lending the organization 14,151 sq. ft. of space free of charge until 2032, a real estate subsidy of $353,777 per year.
The City is cancelling the $5,000 grant awarded in 2025 to the organization DC-Art Indisciplinaire for the project "Les Drags te font signe – 6e édition, volet formation".
The project offered drag workshops (makeup, costumes, dance, performance) to deaf adults aged 18 and over, from June 2025 to June 2026.
The organization notified the City on February 19, 2026 that it could not carry out the project, because of staffing problems and an internal restructuring.
DC-Art Indisciplinaire must repay the first payment of $4,500, which it did not spend; the repayment is expected in late May or early June 2026.
The remaining $500, which was to be paid after the accountability report, will not be paid.
According to the decision summary, the freed-up amounts go back to the Entente sur le développement culturel 2024-2027 to fund other projects.

The borough of Ville-Marie is awarding a $137,970 contract (taxes included) to the firms Provencher Roy + associés architectes and Artelia Canada to supervise the work site for the transformation of rue Larivière, rue des Érables and rue de Rouen and the northern portion of parc des Royaux.
These same firms have been working on the project since 2023; their master agreement expired in December 2025, hence this new contract to finish supervising the work.
With this addition, the professional fees paid to Provencher Roy for the project reach $1,308,634.41, taxes included.
The work is set to resume in May 2026 and be completed at the end of August 2026; the warranty period runs until December 31, 2027.

The expense is funded by the borough's park and green space development program; it could be subsidized at 80% by the OASIS program of the ministère de l'Environnement, as the agreement has not yet been signed.
According to the document, the park and the street will be redeveloped to be easier to use and the lighting will be reviewed.

The Ville-Marie borough is moving $201,636.35 (taxes included) from the "incidentals" unforeseen-costs budget to the "contingencies" budget for the construction project on rue Larivière, rue des Érables and rue de Rouen and the north section of parc des Royaux.

The total authorized spending does not change: it stays at $9,074,454.14. Contingencies go from $1,344,242.36 to $1,545,879.71, or 23% of the initial $6,721,211.78 contract awarded to Lanco Aménagement inc.

Two unforeseen problems explain the request: a concrete slab that had to be demolished, discovered at the Larivière / De Lorimier intersection, and remnants of streetcar rails with planks contaminated with kerosene.
The remaining contingency money was fully committed; this is the second increase to this envelope after the one in September 2025.
As of June 26, 2026, the construction project is 92% complete. The work runs from May to November 2025, then from March to July 2026.
The borough states that the completion of the project depends on this transfer being accepted, and it plans to inform residents a few weeks before the site opens.
The borough of Saint-Léonard awards Construction Guillaume Mailhot inc. the repair of certain parts of the pavillon Ladauversière, for $380,318.27.
The maximum authorized spending is $455,318.27, which is the contract plus $75,000 in contingencies.
The work includes replacing the building envelope, a new soundproofing interior wall, a new floor covering in the activity room, and converting the ground-floor light fixtures to LED.
Six bids were received and found compliant; the winning company was the lowest, 1.88% above the estimate of $373,288.75.
The work is expected to start in May 2026 and finish in July 2026 (approximate dates).
The spending is paid 100% by the borough, funded by a loan by-law.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is adding $25,000 to the contract of Construction AKA inc. for the redevelopment of the change rooms and washrooms at the public works service yard.

Unforeseen job-site issues explain the increase: removal of the anti-vibration base of the rooftop unit, addition of steel folding to hide electrical conduits, and extension of the rental of a sanitary trailer linked to asbestos conditions.
The contract goes from $939,865.33 to $964,865.33, an increase of 2.66%.
With the initial contingencies of $122,500, the amounts added to the bid price of $817,365.33 total $147,500, an increase of 18.05%.
The $25,000 is paid 100% by the borough, through loan by-law number 2293.
The work, which began on February 10, 2025, is to be completed around June 30, 2026.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is approving the architectural plans for the building at 1685-1691, avenue de l'Église, owned by Mission Old Brewery.
The project provides for 13 small housing units intended for vulnerable people.
Expansion work that began in 2025 revealed that the structure and foundations could not support the project; a demolition order was issued on December 15, 2025.
The building will be rebuilt on new foundations, with a return to the original components and a new section at the rear.
Planned finishes: acrylic render, natural cedar in the loggias, and doors and windows in light anodized grey aluminum.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on February 24, 2026, while inviting the developer to simplify certain architectural details.
No financial details are given in the file.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is approving amended plans for the building at 355, rue Guy (1305, rue William), in Griffintown.
The project adds a commercial space on the ground floor and extra housing units on the 4 floors above.
The planned pedestrian access from rue Barré to the inner courtyard will be closed; the other pedestrian accesses remain.
The rooftop features from the original project are being improved; the exterior cladding will be metal panels (silver and copper tones).
A financial guarantee of $200,000 is required to secure the landscaping work and the registration of a public access easement in the land registry.
The guarantee will only be returned after the landscaping work is completed, one year of maintenance, and an inspection; otherwise the borough can cash it.
Since the residential floor area is increasing compared with the inclusion agreement, a financial contribution is planned to make up the difference.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest agrees to have the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie continue to maintain its street lighting, traffic lights, signage and road markings until December 31, 2026.
Le Sud-Ouest will pay a maximum of $2,230,300 for this service in 2026, compared with $2,145,200 authorized for 2025.
The amount breaks down as follows: $650,700 for road markings, $561,500 for street lighting, $514,700 for lighted signals and $503,400 for written signage.
The service has been centralized since 2004 at Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie for the nine boroughs of the former Ville de Montréal.
If the council were to turn down the offer, the borough would have to hire outside suppliers to do this work.
Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie commits to creating a sharing platform with the road marking plans, weekly progress reports and equipment lists.
The City is awarding the firm MLC Associés inc. the architecture and engineering services for its building deconstruction projects, for a maximum of $632,213.03, taxes included.
A contingency budget of $126,442.61 is added, for an estimated total of $758,655.64.
The agreement lasts 60 months, with two possible extensions of 12 months each.
These deconstructions aim to free up land for low-rent housing projects run by non-profit organizations.
The firm will assist the City at every stage: studies, plans and specifications, calls for tenders, work supervision and the warranty period.
MLC Associés obtained the best final score among 4 bids; its price is 70.43% lower than the City's estimate and $461,705.11 lower than the second bid (CIMA+).
The expenses will be paid out of the budgets of the boroughs, the central services and the related cities, as needed.

The City is hiring WSP Canada inc. to provide professional consulting services to check the performance and commissioning of the building envelope (walls, roofs, windows) of municipal buildings during renovation work.
Maximum value of the agreement: $1,571,064.39 including taxes, plus $314,212.88 in contingencies for unforeseen costs, for a total of $1,885,277.27.
The agreement lasts 60 months, from May 12, 2026 to May 12, 2033, including two possible extensions of 12 months each.
The assignments may involve any sector of the city: buildings of the Service de l'eau, the SPVM, the fire department, the large parks and the boroughs.
The firm will be paid at an hourly rate, with each purchase order having to be approved separately; no budget is set aside in advance.
Five firms submitted bids out of eleven that took the tender documents; two bids were found to be non-compliant. The winning bid is 18.44% below the City's estimate.
Since the contract is over $500,000, the City will have to evaluate the performance of WSP Canada inc.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $169,384 to five organizations, as part of its local participatory budget.

Two trucks will be turned into refrigerated mobile markets to sell fresh fruits and vegetables at affordable prices all year round: $75,000 to Cafétéria communautaire MultiCaf and $75,000 to Dépôt centre communautaire d'alimentation.

Three community fridge projects are receiving $19,384: $10,000 to Association communautaire et récréative de Westhaven Elmhurst, $5,384 to Centre communautaire Mountain Sights (parc de la Savane, Triangle area) and $4,000 to À deux mains for an industrial fridge.
The projects come from two ideas chosen by popular vote in 2023 (fridges) and 2024 (local food markets), with budgets of $45,000 and $150,000.
The organizations are signing agreements with the City and must follow a visibility protocol.
A report on the funded projects is planned for January 2027.
The City is awarding Groupe Conseil CHG inc. a master agreement for professional services in civil engineering, for a maximum of $344,925, taxes included.
The agreement lasts 3 years, with an option to extend it by 12 months, and would take effect in February 2026.

The firm may be called upon, as needed, for design, expert assessment, diagnostic or intervention assignments: site development (paving, asphalting, excavation) and hydrology (water management, stormwater retention).
The agreement is reserved for projects of the Service de la gestion et planification des immeubles; each assignment will have to be authorized separately by purchase order.
Public call for tenders 25-21074 received 5 bids for this lot; one firm was found non-compliant because it did not obtain the passing mark of 70%.
The selected price is $165,570.81 lower (-32.43%) than the City's latest estimate, which the City explains by a market looking for contracts.
The costs will be charged to the budgets of the boroughs, the central departments and the related cities, as needs arise.

The City is awarding on-call professional services in building mechanics and electricity to MLC Associés inc. (lot 1) and Bouthillette Parizeau inc. (lot 2), for an estimated total of $491,759.57, taxes included.
The agreements last 3 years, with the possibility of a 12-month extension.
MLC Associés gets $229,576.33 and Bouthillette Parizeau $180,223.31; a contingency budget of $81,959.93 (20%) is added.

The firms may be called on for design work, expert assessments, diagnostics and interventions: plumbing, ventilation, geothermal energy, electrical distribution, lighting, cameras, fire alarms, sprinklers, etc.
Public call for tenders 25-21206 was published from December 8, 2025 to February 12, 2026 and received 11 bids; the selection committee met on March 9, 2026.
The prices accepted are lower than the City's estimates: -30.90% for lot 1 and -24.08% for lot 2.
The costs will be paid out of the budgets of the boroughs and the corporate departments, as needed.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $40,000 to two organizations for food projects in 2026, paid entirely out of its operating budget.

Action-Gardien (Pointe-Saint-Charles) is receiving $24,000 for the Bons solidaires program: vouchers that can be exchanged at food resources by people facing food insecurity, offered in Petite-Bourgogne, Saint-Paul–Émard and Saint-Henri.
L'Épicentre Saint-Henri is receiving $16,000 for the shared use of the Épicamion, a refrigerated truck shared among organizations to transport food.
Both projects cover the period from June 9 to December 15, 2026, and must be completed by that date.
Each organization must submit a final report no later than December 15, 2026, and the borough will carry out follow-ups.
The same projects received a total of $35,000 in 2024 and $50,000 in 2025; this time, the funding is being extended without a new call for projects.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $6,500 to Groupe Pro-Vert for 2026, a one-time emergency grant paid 100% out of its operating budget.
The money will be used to repair the greenhouse at Jardin des Orioles, in parc Angrignon, after a fire on April 5, 2026. The organization estimates its losses at more than $5,000.
Planned work: replacing the greenhouse cladding, the electrical wiring, the outlets, the fan, the ground cover and the hoses, with the use of professional services.
Securing the site: installing cameras, motion-detection lights and smoke detectors.
The borough must approve the work and its cost estimate in advance, under the agreement signed with the organization.
The work and the spending must be completed no later than December 15, 2026, with a final report due on the same date.
Jardin des Orioles covers 0.3 hectare and includes a 50-foot greenhouse; it grows and distributes fresh food and trains young people through the « Je cultive mon avenir » program.

City council adopts a Protocole municipal de gestion des campements (municipal encampment management protocol), which establishes a posture of tolerance toward people living in encampments in Montréal.
Moving an encampment becomes a last resort, allowed only in the circumstances set out in the protocol; the City says it wants to avoid forced displacements.

The protocol is based on nine principles, including the dignity and consultation of the people concerned, the safety of encampments, the prevention of judicialization, a culturally safe approach for Indigenous people, and coexistence with the surrounding neighbourhood.

The Commissaire aux personnes en situation d'itinérance (Commissioner for people experiencing homelessness) coordinates the application of the protocol across the city and reports on it; the document is updated every year.

The City wants to reduce the number of encampments on its territory in the coming years, in particular by using its surplus buildings and land and by working with community organizations and institutions.
The adoption has no impact on the City's budget: the expenses are absorbed by the existing budgets of the business units.
The protocol is based on the OCPM's consultation report on homelessness and on the reminders from the Federal Housing Advocate; some of the planned initiatives have not yet been rolled out.

The executive committee cancels its resolution of March 18, 2026 that adopted the Protocole municipal de gestion des campements (municipal encampment management protocol), and instead formally notes the filing of this protocol.
The protocol establishes a posture of tolerance toward people living in encampments: moving an encampment becomes a last resort, only in the cases set out in the protocol.

It sets out nine guiding principles, including people's dignity, encampment safety, preventing criminalization, a culturally safe approach for Indigenous people, and coexistence with nearby residents.
The City says it wants to reduce the number of encampments in the coming years by developing shelter, housing and rehousing, in particular by using its surplus buildings and land.

The Commissaire aux personnes en situation d'itinérance (commissioner for people experiencing homelessness) coordinates the application of the protocol, its monitoring and accountability reporting; the protocol will be updated every year.
The City relies on the consultation report of the OCPM, which recommended avoiding systematic dismantling, and on the reminders issued by the federal Housing Advocate.
The filing does not involve any new spending: the costs are absorbed by the existing budgets of the business units.
City council adopts a Protocole municipal de gestion des campements (municipal encampment management protocol), which sets out a stance of tolerance toward people living in encampments in Montréal.
The protocol states that moving an encampment should only be considered as a last resort, and only in the cases it describes.
It sets out nine guiding principles, including people's dignity, the safety of encampments, preventing the use of the courts and criminal justice system, and cohabitation with nearby residents.
The Commissaire aux personnes en situation d'itinérance coordinates the follow-up on how the protocol is applied, its accountability reporting and its annual update.
The City says it wants to reduce the number of encampments by developing shelter, support and housing, in particular by using its surplus buildings and land.
The adoption has no budget impact: the spending is covered by the existing budgets of the business units.
The decision repeals resolution CE26 0606 of April 15, 2026; the protocol is published on the City's website.
The Ville de Montréal is setting up an official framework to accept private cash donations for homelessness projects on its territory.

The donations will be able to fund two types of projects: shelter and housing (transitional housing for 2 to 5 years, or permanent housing with support services), as well as prevention, social mediation, stabilizing encampments and helping people find a way out of homelessness.
Donors will not be able to choose which project gets funded: the money will go into a dedicated account and its use will be authorized by a resolution of the executive committee.
The City keeps the right to refuse a donation.
Adopting the model deed of donation has no effect on the city's budget; the amounts received will be added to existing budgets.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council and follows from an intention announced by the City on February 19, 2026.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is awarding Construction Vert Dure Inc. the phase 2a work at parc Pilon, at the corner of boulevard Pie-IX and boulevard Henri-Bourassa, for $4,345,978.89 including taxes.
With contingencies ($869,199.50) and incidental costs ($431,156.25), the total expense comes to $5,646,334.64 including taxes.

The work includes a play area for ages 0-5 and 5-12, a hangout space for teenage girls, an outdoor gym near the basketball court, a perimeter path, two bocce courts, ping-pong tables and grassed areas for informal sports.
Also planned are reshaped slopes for winter sliding, a Montréal-Nord identity sign, renewal of the paths and entrances, lighting brought up to standard and the planting of more than 75 trees.
The pond, the bike path and the outdoor toilet are put off to phase 2b, planned for 2028.
Call for tenders 1162 was held from January 23 to April 8, 2026 and received 13 bids; the borough's estimate was $6,700,000.
The project is receiving $250,000 net per year in 2024, 2025 and 2026 from the Programme d'aménagement urbain et inclusif.
The executive committee is approving an estimated expense of $11,517.91 to send three elected officials to the annual conference of the Fédération canadienne des municipalités (FCM).
The conference is being held in Edmonton, Alberta, from June 3 to 8, 2026.
The people involved: Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada, city councillor Sophie Mohsen (Pierrefonds-Roxboro) and borough councillor Gerlando Guarraggi (Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles).
The expense is paid entirely by the central city, out of the budget already planned for the Division du soutien aux personnes élues of the Service du greffe.
The costs cover transportation, meals, accommodation and offsetting greenhouse gas emissions; for the mayor, the estimated total is $1,891.56 plus $26.56 for GHGs.
The City justifies the expense by the representation of Montréal's interests, the sharing of expertise and networking with close to 1,500 participants.
Similar trips were approved in previous years: $8,149.67 in 2025 (Ottawa), $11,003.90 in 2024 (Calgary), $10,259.88 in 2023 (Toronto).

The City is awarding Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37 (taxes included) for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. With a contingency budget of $163,754.01, the total spending comes to $1,255,447.38.
The work includes a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator, a new electrical container (E5) and a central controller to manage biogas capture.
According to the document, the current generator is more than 30 years old and is no longer sufficient during power outages; some equipment has reached the end of its useful life.
The volume of biogas captured at the former landfill site is dropping: 27 million m³ in 2025, a decrease of 88% since 1996, with landfilling having stopped in 2009.
The contractor has 365 days after the order to begin to finish the work; penalties of at least $1,000 per day apply in case of delay. The transformer alone takes 30 to 35 weeks to deliver.
Two of the six companies that obtained the tender documents submitted bids; the winning bid is 17.17% lower than the estimate from the firm EXP.
The spending will be covered entirely by the agglomeration, out of the reserve for the site's environmental liability.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving $10,824 to the organization Jeunes Marins Urbains for water activities in the summer of 2026.
The project "Transforme ton équipe en équipage" plans 7,000 hours of free activities: sail-and-oar rowing and stand-up paddleboarding.
A free 35-hour day camp is aimed at young people aged 12 to 14, from July 6 to 24, for about 32 participants divided into four groups.
More than 120 free introductory sessions of 1 to 3 hours will be offered to borough residents.
The activities start from the organization's nautical welcome pavilion, at parc Clémentine-De La Rousselière.
The organization had asked for $15,000; the amount granted covers a little more than 13% of the project's expenses and matches the 2025 contribution indexed by 2%.
The projects run from June 1 to September 15, 2026, with an activity report due within 30 days after they end.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving $4,000 to the organization Les Ballons Intensifs to organize the Jeux de la rue 2026.
The event will take place on Saturday, August 8, 2026, at the parc de l'École secondaire Pointe-aux-Trembles.
It is a friendly basketball and soccer tournament for teenage boys, teenage girls and young adults.
The money will go toward food costs, equipment rental and logistics for the day.
The organization Les Ballons Intensifs replaces the Maison des jeunes de Pointe-aux-Trembles, which ran the 2024 and 2025 editions (also $4,000 each year).
The borough is also providing material, logistical, professional and communications support; the expense is covered 100% by the borough.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving $2,040 to the Regroupement des jardins communautaires des Trembles for the Fêtes des récoltes in the summer of 2026.

The money is split among six gardens based on the number of garden plots: $200 for Sainte-Maria-Goretti and des Belles-Roses, $300 for Richelieu, $400 for les Arpents-Verts and Sainte-Marthe, $500 for Pierre-Lacroix.
The celebrations are for members registered in the community gardens program, that is about 363 members and 566 people including co-gardeners.
Each garden committee manages its own spending (materials, tools) to organize its end-of-season event, with a meal and a prize giving.
The amount is a 2% increase over the $2,000 given in 2025; it comes from the borough's operating budget.
The borough will follow up with the six committees during the summer and will provide logistical support if needed.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving $20,800 to the organization Les Petits Soleils de la Pointe-de-l'Île for its specialized day camp in the summer of 2026.
The camp welcomes young people aged 6 to 17 from the area who have a mild to moderate intellectual disability or an autism spectrum disorder.
About 10 young people per week, 7 hours a day, 5 days a week, for 7 weeks (plus June 25 and 26), with 1 camp leader for every 2 young people, and sometimes 1 for 1.
The money is used to hire trained camp leaders, to cover coordination and logistics, and to provide more than 20 hours of adapted training to the team.
The contribution covers 34% of the project's budget, estimated at $61,390; registrations account for 21%.
The organization also gets free space at the Centre communautaire Ste-Maria-Goretti for eight weeks.
The organization must submit a report on the project no later than 30 days after the activities end.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is awarding LA CIE LOOMEX ÉLECTRIQUE LTÉE a contract worth $753,772.04, raised to $853,772.04 with $100,000 in contingencies.

The work includes a permanent natural gas generator at the pavillon Wilfrid-Bastien and hookups (CAMLOCK) for mobile generators at the pavillon Wilfrid-Bastien, pavillon Hébert and pavillon Luigi-Pirandello.
Stated purpose: keeping the facilities running during power outages, following the ice storms, including the one in 2023.
Four compliant bids were received; Loomex is the lowest, with the others ranging from $769,033.28 to $821,898.79.
The bid is $129,768.24 (+20.80%) above the $624,003.80 estimate, which the borough attributes to the construction market, delivery times and access to the island of Montréal.
The work is expected to run from April 2026 to April 2027, according to an approximate schedule.

The borough of Lachine will take charge of replacing lead water service lines located on private property during its construction work on streets, water mains, sewers, bike paths, parks and sports facilities.

The work covers the private portion of the lead connection (or galvanized steel that has been in contact with lead), up to the indoor shut-off valve, meaning a maximum of 1 m inside the building, along with certain surface repairs.
The City pays for the work on private property first, but owners must reimburse it in full; the City keeps professional fees (design, supervision) at its own expense.
Since the by-law adopted on September 22, 2025, all contracts awarded in 2025 and later include the replacement of the private portion of lead service lines.
Planned timeline in Lachine: preparation of the call for tenders in spring 2026, work in summer 2026 and in 2027.
The borough will have to contact the owners concerned, report on spending and progress upon request, and not exceed the authorized funding.
According to its action plan, the City was aiming to eliminate all lead service lines by 2030; residents will be notified before the work begins.
The borough of Lachine is awarding Eurovia Québec Construction inc. road work and the replacement of lead water service lines, under a contract worth $1,608,306.41 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $2,010,383.01: the contract, plus $289,495.15 in contingencies and $112,581.45 in incidental costs.
The work covers 37e Avenue, rue Sherbrooke (between 38e and 40e avenues), 2e Avenue, 52e Avenue and 13e Avenue.

Planned work includes planing and a new surface, speed bumps to slow down traffic, repair of cracked sidewalks, road markings and the replacement of lead water connections on both the public and private sides.
The contract also corrects the non-compliance of the sidewalks at the rue Fairway level crossing, which was flagged by Transports Canada.
The work is scheduled for the summer of 2026; the winning bid is 7.81% above the City's estimate.
The cost is shared between the borough ($1,348,037.47), the Service de l'eau ($421,631.09) and the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier ($240,714.46).

The borough of Lachine is awarding Excavation Gricon (3286916 Canada inc.) the contract to rebuild the sewer and water pipes and the roadway on rue Dawes (between 32e and 34e Avenue) and on 34e Avenue (between Notre-Dame and Dawes).
The contract is worth $2,870,455.97, taxes included; with contingencies ($574,091.19) and incidental costs ($287,045.60), the total authorized spending comes to $3,731,592.76.
The work must be done within 98 calendar days, between 2026 and 2027, and the portion at the rue Notre-Dame intersection must be finished no later than August 26, 2026.
Water service lines made of lead or that do not meet standards will be replaced; the net costs for the part on private property will be billed to the owners concerned.
The work site plans to maintain local traffic, keep permanent access to the CHSLD parking lot and set up detours for bus line 195.
Gricon submitted the lowest of the ten compliant bids, 2.15% below the estimate made by the professionals; the City will assess its performance.
The bill is paid by the Direction de la gestion des actifs of the City's Service de l'eau, through a loan by-law.

The borough of Lachine is taking charge of designing, coordinating and carrying out the reconstruction of the water main, sewer and roadway on rue Dawes (between 32e and 34e Avenue) and on 34e Avenue (between Notre-Dame and Dawes).

The work includes replacing the water and sewer systems and the service connections, including those made of lead or galvanized steel on private property, rebuilding the roadway, and repairing sidewalks and landscaping.
The Service de l'eau is paying 100% of the costs related to the water mains, sewers, service connections and sewer hook-ups.
Planned schedule: contract awarded in June 2026, work starting in July 2026, lasting 98 days, second layer of paving in September 2027, and end of contract in October 2028.
The borough must have its plans approved by the Service de l'eau, obtain the authorizations before the work begins, keep track of its budget and not spend beyond the authorized funds.
A communication procedure will be put in place to notify residents during the work.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is approving a minor exemption for a construction project at the corner of boulevard Monk and rue Allard.
The three-storey building, with a business on the ground floor and eight housing units, will not have to include the facade setback normally required on the 3rd floor.
This setback, of about 3.33 m (10 ft), would have become mandatory because a new subdivision turned the land from a corner lot into a lot wedged between two two-storey buildings.
The project complied with the rules when the permit application was first filed; the City says requiring the setback now would harm the design and cause delays.
The planned height of 10.80 m stays below the maximum of 11 m allowed in the zone.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion; a public notice will be issued before the borough council adopts the resolution.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is granting two minor exemptions for a ten-lot residential project located between rue Cazelais and the CN right-of-way, and between rue Walnut and rue Saint-Rémi.
First exemption: the parking spaces may be reached by a lane opening onto rue Walnut, whereas the by-law requires access by an alley — the site does not have one.

The developer is replacing the planned underground parking with two or three surface spaces per lot, following an engineer's analysis concluding that the land sits in a basin and that water cannot drain by gravity into the sewer.
Second exemption: a planned building may be 5.28 metres wide instead of the required 5.50 metres, in order to keep an outdoor emergency exit for a neighbouring lot.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on April 7, 2026; the work had started and was then suspended after the technical constraints were discovered.
The next steps are the publication of a public notice and the decision of the borough council.
There is no financial aspect attached to this file.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is granting a minor exemption for the SE7T residential project, in Griffintown, between rue Richmond, rue Saint-Martin, rue Notre-Dame and rue William.
The by-law requires a climate resilience factor of 0.30 for this type of expansion; the project reaches 0.28 and will be allowed to proceed as is.
The developer plans rooftop greening, trees and more than 1,900 m² of areas with shrubs, perennials and ground cover.
The borough notes that the project, authorized in 2011 and carried out in four phases, was designed before this requirement came into force in December 2022.
According to the file, applying the requirement would mean redoing the plans and would delay the delivery of the housing units, including the social housing units.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on April 7, 2026; a public notice will be posted on the borough's website.
No construction permit has yet been issued for this work.
The City is renting a piece of land at 505, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, in Ville-Marie (the îlot Voyageur site), measuring about 14,144 square feet, to the company Pomerleau inc.
The lease runs for 2 years starting May 1, 2026, and brings the City $100,000 before taxes, or $50,000 per year.
Pomerleau will use the land for storage and free parking during the work.

This work affects rue Berri and boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, as well as the repair of the waterproofing membrane on the roof of the Berri-UQAM station, which began in January 2026 as a joint project between the City and the STM.
Pomerleau is also paying $588 in administration fees, taxes included, and is covering the operating costs and property taxes.
Either party may end the lease with 90 days' written notice.
The land is subject to a promise to purchase that is currently being verified; the potential buyers accept this rental.
The City is extending the office lease of the organization Collectif d'animation urbaine L'Autre Montréal by three years, starting July 1, 2026.
The space is 1,318.36 square feet, on the 3rd floor of the Centre Strathearn, at 3680, rue Jeanne-Mance, in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The total rent over three years is $31,254.60 before taxes, or $7.90 per square foot, operating costs included but property taxes excluded.
Since the market rate is estimated at $25 per square foot, the City values the indirect subsidy at $67,631.88 over three years.
The organization must take care of the fit-up, housekeeping and tenant repairs; the City keeps responsibility for the structure, mechanical systems, electrical systems and plumbing.
Either party may end the lease at any time with three months' written notice.
L'Autre Montréal creates and leads themed tours and visits on Montréal's social, community, heritage and cultural issues.

The City is extending by one year, starting May 1, 2026, the free loan of premises to the organization Les Amis de la montagne, in the basement of the Chalet du Mont-Royal (1196, chemin Camilien-Houde), in Ville-Marie.
The premises on loan (about 2,996.67 sq. ft.) are used as offices and for storage; they are occupied without sharing, except for one room used one day a week.
The value of this free loan is estimated at $35,331.38, calculated using an average rental rate of $18 per square foot.
The organization had been relocated to the Chalet because the City has been renovating the Maison Smith since December 2024; water damage in February 2026 delayed the work planned through March 2026.
If the work at the Maison Smith is finished before April 30, 2027, the City may end the agreement with 30 days' written notice.

The organization pays for cleaning and rental repairs; the City covers energy and work on the structure, mechanical systems, electrical systems and plumbing (about $18,460 in operating costs for 2026).

The City is extending by three years the lease of the company 3/4 oz inc., which rents a 2,190-square-foot space at 7335, rue du Mile End, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, for food processing.
The new term begins on August 1, 2026 and will bring the City $87,361.08 in rent before taxes ($100,443.40 including taxes), or an average of $13.30 per square foot.
The rent now includes operating costs, except property taxes; the company pays for its own energy and electricity.
The lease adds the possibility of termination with six months' written notice and changes the rules for handing back the premises.
The company takes care of the fit-out, housekeeping and repairs related to normal use; the City keeps responsibility for the structure, mechanical systems, electrical systems and plumbing.
The City had bought the building in 2023 through a right of first refusal for $2,350,000 for social housing purposes; the rental continues until a housing project is developed.
According to the file, this rental reduces the costs of holding the building and ensures an on-site presence.
The Saint-Léonard borough is awarding Construction Urbex inc. a contract to supply, deliver, plant and maintain trees for 2026-2029.
Maximum spending of $750,816.85: $728,948.40 for the contract and $21,868.45 in contingencies.
700 trees will be planted in 2026, mainly along the borough's streets, either as replacements or as new plantings.
Planting will take place in the spring and fall of 2026, with the work expected to be finished by October 30, 2026.
Maintenance covers a warranty of three years and six months for trees planted in the spring, three years for those planted in the fall, and until December 2030 if a tree has to be replaced.
Construction Urbex inc. was the lowest compliant bidder; its bid is $51,541.43 (-6.60%) below the estimate.
The spending is split between the borough's operating budget and the program to strengthen the tree canopy and replace ash trees.

The borough of Rosemont

La Petite-Patrie is granting a minor exemption for the house located at 5928, 23e Avenue.
The building's left side setback measures between 1.28 and 1.4 metres, whereas the planning by-law requires at least 1.5 metres.
The exemption brings an existing situation into compliance: the 2-storey single-family row house was built in 1999 with a construction permit.

According to the Direction du développement du territoire, the exemption does not increase any risk and does not affect the neighbours, since the building is next to a driveway entrance opening onto boulevard Pie-IX.
A public notice must be published 15 days before the borough council meeting of April 7, 2026, where interested persons may be heard.
No money is involved in this decision.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is releasing $50,000 from its management surplus to carry out safety work on buildings deemed dangerous.
These buildings have conditions that are dangerous to public safety, and their owners have not fixed them despite inspections and several notices.
The borough will do the work in place of the owners, as allowed by the municipal by-law on the construction and transformation of buildings (11-018).
The operating budget of the Direction du développement du territoire et des études techniques is not enough to pay for this work, hence the use of the surplus.
The Ville de Montréal is entrusting the Ville de Montréal-Est with building a multi-use path (for cycling and walking) on rue Sherbrooke, between boulevard Joseph-Versailles and avenue Durocher.
Montréal will reimburse Montréal-Est up to $1,608,828, net of tax rebate, within 90 days of the approval of the final statement of the work.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration, out of the bike network development program.

Montréal-Est is responsible for the plans and specifications, supervision of the work site and materials testing, and must hand over the final documentation to Montréal within 6 months of the end of the work.
The work is to start in the summer of 2026 and be completed in the fall of 2026; the construction contract was awarded on April 23, 2026.
This is phase 2 of the project: a first agreement, in April 2025, covered the section between avenue Georges-V and boulevard Joseph-Versailles for $334,014.76, taxes included.

The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough approves the complete renovation of the facades of Manoir Roger-Bernard, a 5-storey residential building located at 14101-14103, avenue Anselme-Lavigne and 4500, rue René-Émard.
The existing stucco will be replaced with metal cladding, chosen because the current structure can only support a lightweight material.
The balcony guardrails will be redone using metal mesh, which lets light through while blocking the view from the street.
Three new canopies will be installed in the front and side yards, at the request of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, to shelter seniors between the parking lot and the entrances.
The canopies will have an independent structure, which also requires a minor exemption dealt with in another file.
The work will follow the plans by architects Ruccolo + Faubert dated June 5, 2026.
The urban planning advisory committee unanimously recommended the project on July 15, 2026.
The Pierrefonds-Roxboro borough is refusing the expansion project at 992, chemin de la Rive-Boisée.
The owner wanted to add, in front of the house and attached to it, a two-storey garage of about 663 m² (±7,136 sq ft).
This garage would be larger than the house itself, which is about 410 m² (±4,413 sq ft).

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended refusal: the garage would be too far forward compared to neighbouring houses and would not follow the dominant placement pattern of the area.
The committee also finds the size too imposing, with a crushing effect on the neighbouring property, and a volume that does not blend in with the existing house.
The lot is located in a "riverside lots" zone under the zoning by-law.
The project also requested a minor exemption regarding the number of garage doors allowed for a detached single-family house.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $16,175 to 18 seniors' clubs to run activities against senior isolation in 2026.
The amounts per club range from $675 to $2,785: the Club d'âge d'or parc Delorme receives the largest share ($2,785), and the Cercle du 3e âge Ste-Angèle $1,260.
How it is calculated: $550 for clubs with fewer than 100 resident members, $600 for 100 to 130 members, and $5 per member beyond 130.
Each club also receives $125 for printing, because the borough closed its print shop ($2,250 in total).
The clubs must sign an agreement, provide the list of their members and submit a report on their spending; without that, no new funding next year.
Planned activities include outings, annual parties, bocce, bingo, pétanque, dancing, singing, cards, fitness and bowling.
The agreement ends on December 31, 2026. A second part, for special projects, will be the subject of a call for projects later on.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $7,500 to the Club du bonheur de Saint-Léonard for its recreational activities in 2026.
The organization offers activities for adults living with an intellectual or physical disability, at the pavillon Wilfrid-Bastien.
The programming runs over 35 weeks, on Sundays from 1:30 p.m. to 5 p.m., with an average of 25 to 30 participants.
The money will be used to pay for supervision and activity-leading costs, with specialized activity leaders and trained volunteers.
The same amount of $7,500 was granted in 2024 and in 2025.
The agreement ends on December 31, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is giving $10,850 to ten seniors' clubs for fitness and dance activities for seniors in 2026.
The amounts range from $850 to $1,500 per club: gymnastics, chair cardio, social and line dancing, outdoor dancing.
Each club must offer its activity free of charge to the public, in a borough park.
The clubs sign an agreement and must submit a form justifying their expenses.
The agreements end on July 30, August 30 or September 30, 2026, depending on the club.
Eleven projects were submitted; ten are being funded, as the Club de l'âge d'or l'Esperanza withdrew its project because its members were not interested.
In 2025, the total funding was $9,362, and $12,540 in 2024.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is adopting two permanent orders (valid until amended or repealed) for events organized by schools in its territory.
First order: noise from sound equipment broadcasting outdoors is allowed during these events, despite the noise by-law.
Second order: it becomes allowed to paint on sidewalks and roadways with water-soluble paint during these events.
The events will have to be held during school hours, in the borough's parks, with the approval of the director of culture, sports, recreation and social development.
Goal: to avoid turning down school requests submitted after the permit deadlines and to lighten the workload of the public events team.
The schools (promoters) cover the costs and logistics; the borough provides logistical support based on its capacity and existing budgets.
Permits will be issued by the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social and by public works; the order will be published on the borough's website.

The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is authorizing 18 public events on its territory in 2026, including ItalFestMTL, Plaza Palooza, Ferragosto sur Dante, la Chasse aux cocos and les Samedis pour emporter.
Four ordinances temporarily lift by-laws at the dates, times and places listed in an attached table.
Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors with sound equipment, despite the noise by-law.
They will be allowed to sell food, promotional items and alcoholic beverages, and people will be allowed to drink alcohol on site.
Streets may be closed, and painting the sidewalks and roadway with water-soluble paint will be permitted.
The event promoters cover the costs and logistics; the borough provides logistical support based on its capacity, using its existing budgets.
Permits will be issued by the borough's culture and public works departments; the ordinances will be published on its website.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is authorizing seven public events on its territory in 2026, including the Marché Angus, Cinéma sous les étoiles, the Fête de quartier Notre-Dame-de-la-Défense and the Ciné-Parc Dante.
Four ordinances temporarily set aside city by-laws at the sites, dates and times listed in the appendix.
Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors despite the noise by-law.
They will be allowed to sell food, promotional items and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks, and people will be allowed to drink alcohol on site.
Streets may be closed, and sidewalks and pavement may be painted with water-soluble paint.
The event promoters cover the costs and logistics; the borough provides logistical support from its existing budgets.
Permits will be issued by the borough's culture and public works departments.
The City is giving $10,000 to the Institut d'administration publique du Québec (IAPQ) for the Prix d'excellence 2026 and the 2026-2027 program.
The expense is included in the 2026 budget of the Direction générale and is paid 100% by the central city.
In return, the City gets visibility all year long and five free spots at each of the IAPQ's webinars.
The City has supported this event since 2018; the amount is the same as the one paid in 2025 ($10,000), after contributions of $5,000 in previous years.
The document notes that the City won three Prix d'excellence in 2025 (Circuit bleu, the GoGéo app, and the Antenna platform).
The decision is made by the executive committee.

The City is transferring $105,100 in 2026 from "common expenses" to the Direction générale to pay for a new position of secretary general of the Alliance Montréal Métropole Culturelle (AMMC), from June to December.
It is adding $210,200 per year to the Direction générale's budget starting in 2027, on a recurring basis, for the same position.

The AMMC brings together the City, the ministère de la Culture et des Communications du Québec, the ministère de l'Identité canadienne, Tourisme Montréal, Culture Montréal, the Conseil des arts de Montréal and the Chambre de commerce du Montréal métropolitain.

Its mandate: to position Montréal as a French-speaking cultural metropolis of international stature and to agree on a shared vision of cultural development, including land-use planning through culture.
The person hired will report to the deputy director general, Qualité de vie, and will speak for the Alliance in public and institutional bodies.
Next steps after approval: creating the position, posting the job offer, interviews, then the start of employment.
The funding is 100% local jurisdiction; no communications activities are planned.
The City is moving $1,578,900 from "common expenses" to the Direction générale.
This amount is what remains of a $2 million envelope set aside in the 2026 budget for the administration's priorities.
The amount breaks down into $578,900 under local jurisdiction and $1,000,000 under agglomeration jurisdiction.
The transfer will allow the director general to approve the allocation of funds to the selected priorities himself.
According to the document, the operation has no impact on the City's financial framework.
The decision falls to the executive committee.

The City is awarding two service contracts, without a call for tenders, to Centre de la montagne (Les Amis de la montagne) for parc du Mont-Royal, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2029, for a total of $457,650.

First contract, $330,000: welcoming and informing visitors (in person, by phone, by email), registration for activities, lost and found, loan of adapted equipment for universal accessibility, and collection of visitor attendance data.

Second contract: seasonal equipment rental (cross-country skis, snowshoes, skates, rowboats in summer) and management of the free loan program for young people aged 17 and under from the urban agglomeration, from December 15 to March 31.

The City reimburses the free youth program up to $42,550 per winter season; the rest of the rental service costs the City nothing, and the organization keeps the revenue, estimated at about $717,000 per year.
The City also lends premises free of charge to the organization so it can provide these services.
These contracts are separate from the mission support agreement, following compliance requirements from the Auditor General and the legal affairs department.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration; the decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.
The City is giving $65,000 to the Orchestre Métropolitain for the free concert "L'OM au pied du mont Royal", scheduled for August 5, 2026 at parc du Mont-Royal.
Of this amount, $20,000 comes from the budget of the Service des grands parcs and $45,000 in technical services from the Entente sur le développement culturel de Montréal 2024-2027.

The $45,000 is used to add to the concert a theme on the park's 150th anniversary: original artistic content (archive projections, guests) and cultural mediation activities for families and young people.
The urban agglomeration covers 69% of the expense, that is $45,000.
The concert is free and the organization expects more than 50,000 people; it handles the logistics and must submit a financial report no later than 60 days after the event.

The City also supports the project through other funding envelopes: $55,000 from the Programme de soutien aux festivals et événements culturels and $20,000 from the fund for cultural organizations of Ville-Marie.
Councillor Andréanne Moreau declares her interest and takes part in neither the deliberations nor the vote.

The borough of Verdun is hiring Réalisation dynamique inc. to redevelop parc Monseigneur-Langlois, for a total expense of $141,375.24 including taxes (contract of $122,935, contingencies of $12,293.50, incidental costs of $6,146.75).
The work includes landscaping, concrete slabs, the installation of park furniture and equipment, and hooking up a new drinking fountain.

The project comes out of the citizen vote in the 2nd edition of Montréal's participatory budget: "Des aires d'activités accessibles pour toutes les générations" (activity areas accessible to all generations), with universally accessible play equipment and furniture.
The bill is paid entirely by the central city, out of the participatory budget.
Seven of the eight bids received were compliant; the winning bid is $3,435.73 above the internal estimate, or 2.8%.
The bids from a first call for tenders for the same park had been rejected in June 2025.
Notices to residents and an explanatory sign at the work site are planned.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is adding $637,731.61 (taxes included) to the contract with Axe construction inc. for the renovation of the aquatic facilities at parc Ignace-Bourget.
