The contract goes from $10,594,194.59 to $11,231,926.20; it was $9,681,460.66 at the start, in June 2024.
The $2,702,189.41 contingency budget is used up: change orders total $2,939,921.02, which means a projected shortfall of $237,731.61.
The remaining $400,000 covers pending change orders ($200,000) and contingencies through to the end of the work site ($200,000).

Reasons given: contaminated soil, a retention basin more complex than expected, the winter shutdown and postponed work (concrete work on the pool decks, resurfacing and painting of the pool, outdoor equipment).
The expense is covered 100% by the borough: 74% from the park fund reserve, 26% from the local 2026 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The facilities are targeted to open before mid-July 2026; the work began on September 30, 2024.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is adding $90,070.27 (taxes included) to the contract for supervising the renovation work on the aquatic facilities at parc Ignace-Bourget, bringing the total expense to $780,608.98.
The firm Patriarche Architecture inc. has been supervising the work site since September 2024, under a contract worth $600,468.44.
The contract's contingency budget is doubling, going from $90,070.27 to $180,140.54 (taxes included).

The work is being extended until July 2026 because of unforeseen underground conditions, architectural and structural constraints discovered after the demolitions, contaminated soil and winterizing the work site.
Still to be done: resurfacing and painting the pool, concreting the deck areas, installing the outdoor equipment, then provisional acceptance and the documentation for LEED v4 certification.
The expense is covered 100% by the borough of Le Sud-Ouest ($82,246.16 net of rebates).
The borough of Anjou is approving zoning exemptions to expand the water pumping station at 7000, avenue de Champchevrier.
The one-storey expansion is intended to install an automated odour treatment system, in response to odour nuisances reported by residents of the area.
The project includes a 15-metre odour extraction chimney, a mechanical room, new roof access and a generator in an acoustic enclosure.
The windows and most of the exterior doors will be replaced with better soundproofed models to reduce noise in the neighbourhood.

The exemptions concern the height of one storey, a rear setback of 3.80 m, the generator in the side yard, the height of the screens hiding the rooftop equipment and the metal cladding on the Belfroy and Champchevrier façades.
The building's address will be changed so that the main façade faces avenue de Champchevrier.
Work must begin within 60 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; it replaces two exemptions granted in 2022.
The borough of Anjou is authorizing the expansion of an industrial building at 7951-7961, rue Vauban, in the business park.
The company Binatek, which occupies the building, is adding 344 m² of storage space in the rear yard in order to merge its operations with a sister company.
The project does not comply with zoning rules: a rear setback of 0 m instead of 7.6 m, a side setback of 1.2 m instead of 7.6 m, and 14 parking spaces instead of the 24 required.
A truck will have to back up from the street to reach the new access door in the right side yard, which the by-law normally prohibits.
The owner must plant two additional trees and keep at least 12 trees on the site at all times.
Work must begin within 60 months, and the landscaping must be completed within 12 months after construction ends.
This is a first draft resolution: a public consultation will follow and the project may be subject to a referendum.

The borough of Anjou is adopting a new by-law (RCA 193) requiring developers to submit a comprehensive development plan before obtaining a change to the planning by-laws in zones C-513, C-514 and C-515 of the Pôle Anjou area.

The plan must cover the entire zone concerned and be prepared by a professional: subdivision, streets, building heights and siting, densities, parking, public spaces, pedestrian and cycling paths, landscaping, and land to be transferred to the City for parks or schools.
Applications are made in writing to the director of urban planning, with the required documents and the fee set out in the borough's fee by-law.
Fines for offences: $1,000 for an individual ($2,000 for a repeat offence) and $2,000 for a company ($4,000 for a repeat offence).

The borough cites the extension of the blue line, the location of the future west entrance building and bus terminus of the Anjou station, and the projects already approved in the area (Halles d'Anjou, Westwalk Anjou, the Toys''R''Us site, Les Intervalles).
Next steps: public notice, public consultation meeting, final adoption by the borough council, then certificate of compliance and coming into force.
The City is entrusting the borough of Ville-Marie with the design and execution of work in the Quartier des spectacles, an area where heavy traffic wears out facilities quickly.

Planned work: rebuilding the driveway entrance of the Esplanade Tranquille, converting two grassed areas into surfaces that can withstand intensive use, creating direct access between the warehouse and the north side of the Esplanade Tranquille, and replacing a grate at the place des Festivals.
The Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs is paying all of the costs, estimated at $1,472,500, including $175,500 for an 18-month full-time position.
The borough will have to obtain written approval from the Service de la culture before committing each amount; actual costs could vary.
Timeline: hiring of a resource in July 2026, call for tenders in the spring of 2027, work in the summer and fall of 2027.
The borough already handles routine maintenance of the place des Festivals, the Promenade des artistes, the esplanade Clark and the Parterre.
The City is adding $2,125,000 to fill potholes on the arterial and local road network, on top of the $2,525,000 already transferred to the boroughs at the beginning of 2026.
$600,000 goes out right away: $200,000 each to Ville-Marie, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Le Sud-Ouest.

Five other boroughs will each receive $80,000 — Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension — once they have fully spent their budget from the beginning of the year.

$1,000,000 is set aside for a call for tenders for manual pothole filling on the arterial network, during thaws and in winter, in addition to the work planned for the world cycling championships (UCI).
$125,000 will go to repairs on rue Notre-Dame, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Ville-Marie.
The money comes from the reserved fund – Voirie locale and passes through the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne.
The City is changing its financial support program for regional sports associations for the 2027-2029 cycle, which applies to all 19 boroughs.
New this time: a cap will be placed on the funding of certain expenses (equipment, human resources), to reduce the gaps between the projects that get support.
The City will pay up to 75% of eligible expenses for supervising competition networks and for training, and up to 100% for sports development initiatives (compared with 75% before).
Development initiatives will be funded for a maximum of two cycles, that is six years.
The development stream is divided into sub-streams: self-generated revenue, youth membership, women's sport, ADS+ initiatives, governance and volunteers.
The last yearly payment goes from 10% to 25% of the support granted, and multi-year projects will have to show their impacts on local clubs in order to get the following year.
The money is already included in the budget of the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports; the call for projects is launched in spring 2026 and funding starts in winter 2027.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the organization Les Anciens de LaSalle to hold its hockey tournament at aréna Jacques-Lemaire from April 20 to 26, 2026.
The organization will be able to apply to the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux for a permit to sell alcohol during the event.
The borough is providing $300 for the souvenir program, taken from the borough council's budget.
It is also providing free services valued at $9,500: access to the rink, equipment loan and delivery, and coordination and supervision staff.
The tournament, in its 17th edition, brings together about 28 teams and 360 players aged 35 and over, for 48 games, including two charity games. No entrance fees will be charged.
The organization estimates its expenses at $13,000 and its revenues at $29,000, mainly from registrations and sales of the souvenir program.
The LaSalle borough authorizes the Club de patinage artistique de LaSalle inc. to present its "Revue sur glace" on April 18 and 19, 2026, at the aréna Jacques-Lemaire.
The borough is providing logistical support free of charge: coordination by a manager, equipment loan and delivery, electricians and security staff.
The aréna Jacques-Lemaire is reserved for the organization from April 14 to 19, 2026, including the dress rehearsal on April 17.
This free support amounts to a subsidy valued at about $15,000 (staff, equipment and arena rental).
The show will bring together about 200 young skaters and about 800 spectators, over two performances.
The event is held every two years; the last edition was in April 2024, with a financial contribution of $3,500 at the time.

The borough of LaSalle is extending by one year the contract of the firm Techniparc (9032-2454 Québec Inc.) to groom and maintain the cross-country ski trails of the Grand Sud-Ouest during the 2026-2027 season, for a maximum of $60,258.39 taxes included.
The contract covers about 23 km of trails: La Riveraine (21.3 km) and La Traverse (1.5 km).
The bill is shared between three boroughs: Lachine (33.6%), LaSalle (33.6%) and Verdun (32.8%).
The contract provides for 25 grooming passes, plus 5 optional passes if needed ($10,043.06 taxes included in total).
The City is removing from the mandate the making and installation of signage, a saving of $1,947, since those needs are being met another way.
Grooming will take place from December 15 to the 3rd Sunday of March; trail conditions will be posted on montreal.ca.
The original 2023 contract ($160,586.73 for three seasons) was set to expire on April 30, 2026; a second option year remains possible for 2027-2028.

The City is changing the funding source for part of the support already granted to the Association des restaurateurs de rue du Québec for its project "Cuisine de rue : moteur de relance, d'inclusion et d'innovation urbaine".
The amount involved is $25,000, taxes included: $20,000 in 2027 and $5,000 in 2028.
These payments will now be made out of the Entente Réflexe 3 (2025-2029) signed with the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie.
Reason: the former agreement (Réflexe 2) can only fund projects completed by December 31, 2026 at the latest, and part of the project will take place in 2027.
The total support amount of $75,000 granted in June 2025 for 2025-2028 is not changed.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration, under economic development.
The City is correcting an accounting error in the 2026 budget for the $50,000,000 agreement with the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (Réflexe 3 – 2025-2029).
An amount of $152,100, the pay for one position, had been entered twice: once as pay and once under the other expense categories.
This $152,100 therefore moves from local jurisdiction to agglomeration jurisdiction, for both revenues and expenses.
After the correction, the agglomeration's share reaches $35,152,100 and the local share $14,847,900.
The amount is covered 100% by the agglomeration; no new spending is committed.
The Service du développement économique expects that other transfers between agglomeration and local jurisdictions will probably be needed during the agreement.
The City is transferring $1,722,500 from the Service du développement économique to the borough of Ville-Marie for projects planned for 2026 in the downtown area.
$765,000 will go toward stepping up cleanliness: cleanliness brigades, additional containers and targeted clean-ups in busy areas.
$595,000 will be used to beautify commercial streets: plant maintenance in Vieux-Montréal and elsewhere, and the purchase of street furniture to create "urban oases".
$300,000 will fund the layout and activities at place du Village for the summer of 2026, with les Allié.e.s du Village, the SDC du Village and Studio ZX.
$62,500 will extend until April 2027 the maintenance contract for the artwork "Entre les rangs" at parc de La Presse, with the Partenariat du Quartier des spectacles.
The money comes from the operating budget ($1,360,000) and from the Réflexe 3 agreement with the ministère de l'Économie ($362,500); any unused Réflexe 3 funds will have to be returned.
The transfer is planned for May 2026 and the projects will run from May to December 2026; the expense is covered 100% by the central city.

City council is announcing a by-law that would transfer responsibility for enforcing the by-law on tourist accommodation establishments (25-007) from the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal to the borough of Ville-Marie.
In practical terms, the Escouade d'hébergement touristique, which operates in all 19 boroughs, would be moved to Ville-Marie.
The City points to the housing crisis and the growing number of illegal short-term tourist rentals, which take housing units off the rental market.
The transfer will mean reassigning employees, transferring budgets and shifting administrative responsibilities; each of these changes will be the subject of a separate decision.
According to the decision summary, this file has no budget impact; the by-law would come into force on the date it is published.
At this stage, this is only a notice of motion and the tabling of the draft by-law: it will be adopted at a later meeting.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is awarding Les Entreprises Roseneige a contract worth $208,852.09 (taxes included) to supply and plant vegetation; the total authorized spending comes to $240,179.90, including $31,327.81 in contingencies.

The work covers three areas: around école Sainte-Claire (rue de Marseille, rue Sainte-Claire, rue Pierre-De Coubertin, avenue Lebrun and avenue Mercier), rue Pierre-Tétreault (from avenue Dubuisson to rue Notre-Dame) and rue Hochelaga (from west of rue Moreau to rue de Chambly).
In total: 49 trees, 48 shrub and perennial beds (593.6 m²) and 333.9 m² of sodding.
The contract includes tree and horticultural maintenance for three years after planting, record keeping and a warranty on the plants.
Planting is scheduled for July 2026, over 15 days; maintenance continues until 2029.
Seven bids were received; the winning bid is the lowest compliant one, 29.46% below the internal estimate of $296,068.90.
The cost is shared between the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité ($67,481.76) and the borough ($172,698.14), funded through loans.
The executive committee recommends disapproving in full urban planning by-law CA-24-282.145 of the Ville-Marie borough, adopted on September 30, 2025.
This by-law was meant to adapt Ville-Marie's urban planning rules to the new Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité 2050, which came into force on June 25, 2025.

The Service de l'urbanisme considers non-compliant certain provisions dealing with public transit, heritage buildings, places of worship, institutional heritage complexes, archaeological heritage, Mont-Royal and permitted uses.
Example given: the by-law would impose standards for height, density, siting and greening on guided public transit facilities, which the Plan prohibits.
The by-law also creates non-compliance with the "Conservation" designation of the Schéma d'aménagement de l'agglomération.

After the disapproval, Ville-Marie will be able to re-adopt, in a single reading, a by-law keeping only the compliant parts; the faulty parts will have to be corrected and go through the regular process again.
The city clerk will forward the resolution to the Ville-Marie borough.

The City is entering into supply agreements with Tacel ltée (thermal video presence detectors and communication cables) and Éco-Compteur inc. (pedestrian and bicycle detectors), for an estimated amount of $2,593,558.91, taxes included.
The agreements last 24 months, with an option to extend for 12 months; prices are fixed at the start and could increase by up to 3% if renewed.
Breakdown: Tacel ltée receives $1,642,808.79 (lot 1) and $155,216.25 (lot 3); Éco-Compteur inc. receives $559,755.79 (lot 2).
An additional budget of $235,778.08 is authorized for unforeseen costs (contingencies of 10%).
The equipment is used to count and classify vehicles, cyclists and pedestrians and to measure speeds, in order to feed the City's mobility data.
The equipment will be kept at the City's Centre de distribution; boroughs will be able to obtain supplies there for their projects and for traffic light maintenance.
A late delivery can lead to a penalty of $100 per day; the performance of Tacel ltée (lot 1) and Éco-Compteur inc. (lot 2) will be evaluated.
The City is entering into a 36-month agreement with Métal Pole-Lite inc. to supply traffic light poles, mast arms, extensions and caps, for up to $2,892,311.10, taxes included.
This material will be used to maintain and modernize traffic lights across the city, including lights for pedestrians, bicycles and buses, and areas near schools (Vision Zéro).
Boroughs and authorized contractors will be able to get supplies at the City's Centre de distribution.
Delivery must be made within 15 weeks; a delay costs $1,000 per day per order, up to a maximum of 3% of the contract.
Of the five companies that obtained the tender documents, only one submitted a bid; the price is 11% below the City's estimate ($3,246,894).
The supplier's performance will be evaluated, since the expense is over $500,000.
Supply is planned from May 2026 to May 2029, paid out of the budgets of the central services and the boroughs.
Montréal is entering into a 24-month master agreement with Orange Traffic inc. to supply traffic light cabinets (ATCC type), for up to $2,242,011.12, taxes included.
The agreement may be extended by 12 months, and the City will assess Orange Traffic inc.'s performance.
A second master agreement, recommended to the executive committee, goes to Tacel ltée for traffic signal controller units (ATC type), for up to $477,514.17, taxes included.
The two agreements total $2,719,525.29 and cover 120 ATCC cabinets and 120 ATC control units.
The purchases are used to maintain and modernize traffic lights: pedestrian countdown signals, audible signals, lights for cyclists and buses, and priority for emergency vehicles.
Public call for tenders 25-21121 received 3 bids for the cabinets and 2 for the controllers; the winning bid for the cabinets is 26.1% below the City's estimate.
The expenses will be paid out of the budgets of the Direction des projets d'aménagement urbain, corporate services or the boroughs, as needed.

The City is awarding Construction N.R.C. inc. a contract worth $780,608.97 (taxes included) to redo the traffic lights and the layout of the intersection of boulevard Alfred-Nobel and boulevard Hymus, in Saint-Laurent.
With contingencies ($156,121.79) and incidentals ($156,121.79), the total spending comes to $1,092,852.55, paid entirely by the central city.

The work includes digital countdown pedestrian signals, upgrades to street furniture and equipment, adjustment of the central median for the pedestrian crossing, and curb ramps with tactile warning plates.

The intersection has to be redesigned following the work on the Réseau express métropolitain (REM) structure; the City chose to hold a separate call for tenders rather than hand the work to CDPQ Infra, which would have cost more according to the decision summary.
Four of the seven parties who took out the tender documents submitted a bid; the lowest bid is 13.13% below the City's internal estimate.
The City is awarding a $394,851.17 contract (taxes included) to Laser AMP, division de ISE Métal inc., to supply pavers compatible with BIXI stations.
The pavers are the painted steel bases of the stations, which support the payment terminals and the bike docks.
The order includes, among other things, 350 technical platforms, 795 platforms for panels, 400 rods, 40 end caps and 50 cable protectors.
These pavers will be used to install the new BIXI equipment purchased for 2026, including electric-assist bikes.
Two companies submitted bids: Laser AMP at $394,851.17 and Pattison ID at $559,124.46; the winning bid is 8.8% below the City's estimate.
The City writes that it found no documented explanation for the 41.6% gap between the two bids.
The net expense of $360,551.75 is borne by the central city, through a loan by-law.

The borough of Ville-Marie is ending the professional services contract awarded in May 2021 to the winning team of the international landscape architecture competition for the development of lot 066 and its surroundings (Raquel Penalosa, Diana Elizalde, Mario Najera, with WAA Montréal, Vinci Consultants, BES and Pageau Morel et associés).
The contract was worth $1,140,000.01 including taxes, with a maximum authorized expenditure of $1,368,000.01 including $228,000 in contingencies.

Reason given: the work, planned for 2022-2023, was postponed to 2027-2028, after the work on the Musée d'art contemporain, and the City says it cannot adjust the fees to the current inflation context.
Under the agreement, the termination does not entitle the professionals to any compensation, nor to any recourse for anticipated profits.
$285,000 including taxes has already been invoiced and paid; the balance of $1,083,000.01 will be returned to the loan by-law.
A termination letter will be sent to the firms, which must stop their services immediately, return the documents within 10 days and submit a fee statement for the services rendered.
The postponement of the work was intended to limit the impacts on mobility in the area and to ensure users' safety during festivals.
The borough of Ville-Marie accepts a $25,000 donation from La Corporation d'habitations Jeanne-Mance to replace a play structure at parc Toussaint-Louverture.
The City's Treasurer will issue an official tax receipt to the donor.
The park is located between rue Ontario Est, rue Sanguinet, rue Saint-Dominique and boulevard De Maisonneuve, in the middle of the habitations Jeanne-Mance.

The new play structure is intended for children aged 5 to 12; the document states that more than 120 young people in that age group live in the Habitations Jeanne-Mance and that the old structure was little used.
The contract to supply and install it has already been awarded to Go-Élan inc. for a maximum expense of $69,179.12, including taxes and contingencies; the donation covers part of that amount.
The request comes from the Corporation, supported by the residents' advisory committee, the organization Go Jeunesse and the CPE Fleur de Macadam.
Installation of the structure is planned for fall 2026 according to the borough's schedule (the Corporation's resolution instead mentions spring 2027).
The borough of LaSalle is adding $40,000 (taxes included) to the contract with ADT déménagement et entreposage inc., bringing the total to $132,008.74 for 2024 to 2026.
The company removes, transports, fumigates, stores and destroys belongings left on public property during court-ordered evictions in LaSalle.
The borough pays for the first 60 days of storage; after that, the evicted person must repay the costs to get their belongings back.
The borough reports 47 evictions in 2024 and 50 in 2025, and expects the volume to stay the same in 2026.
Only $9,566.20 was left in the contract's 2026 budget, which was considered not enough to cover the year.
Since 2025, the borough says it has reviewed how it works: better coordination with the supplier and the bailiffs, and the presence of street workers and social workers during evictions.
The borough of LaSalle is creating an advisory committee on the ecological transition.
The committee will study matters related to the ecological transition and make recommendations to the borough council.
It will contribute to developing, assessing and following up on the borough's plans, projects and programs in this area.
Its mandate includes fighting climate change, raising awareness among citizens and organizations, and developing local partnerships.
The by-law sets out the committee's composition and the number of its members.
The City states that there is no financial impact; a public notice will be published on the borough's website when the by-law comes into force.
The notice of motion and the tabling of the draft by-law took place at the February 2, 2026 sitting.
The LaSalle borough council is adopting its 2026-2030 strategic plan, an update of the 2023-2030 plan.
The document sets out 5 directions and 18 areas of action that will guide projects and the use of budgets, staff and equipment through to 2030.

The directions cover the borough team, the living environment and economic development, inclusion and safety, mobility (structuring public transit, active transportation, universal accessibility) and the ecological transition.
The plan lists the values chosen: integrity and courage, pride, respect and caring, the common good.
There is no financial aspect associated with this file.
The strategic plan will be shared with staff, with other City units and with elected officials, along with a communications campaign aimed at the public.
The borough of LaSalle is amending the by-law governing its advisory committee on mobility, created in December 2025.

Purpose of the amendment: to bring this committee in line with the five other advisory committees created in March 2026 (ecological transition; finances and relations with citizens; economic and urban development; social development and diversities; sports, culture and recreation), so that they are all based on the same rules.
The mobility committee studies mobility files and makes recommendations to the borough council: street design, bike paths, public transit and the safety of road users.
There is no cost associated with this file.
A public notice will be published on the borough's website once the by-law comes into force.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is transferring $12,632.40 (net of taxes) from its parks and real estate assets development budget to the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles (SGPI) for 2026.
This money pays for four sets of work in borough buildings, considered priorities and outside the SGPI's basic service offer.
Replacement of six water fountains at the Centre sportif Pierre-Charbonneau: $7,869.60.
Electrical work to add technical equipment at the bibliothèque Maisonneuve: $1,200.96.
Addition of gypsum ceilings at the Ancien marché public de Maisonneuve: $1,770.66.
Modification and addition of heating units at the Maison de la culture Mercier: $1,791.18.
The work must be carried out in 2026.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve will build a new sidewalk on rue Sherbrooke, a street managed by the city.
The sidewalk will connect the curb extension at the corner of rue Contrecœur to the sidewalk that already exists on Sherbrooke.
This pedestrian link is needed because the STM is asking that the bus stop be moved west, near Contrecœur.
The stop is being moved because of a new truck entrance built on Sherbrooke, near rue Hector, for a future commercial site.
New businesses are set to open at the intersection of Sherbrooke and Contrecœur in August 2026; the development work is already under way.
The borough will pay $38,500 out of its own surplus, since the authorization it received comes with no funding.
The borough is asking city council to hand over to it the plans and specifications, the call for tenders, the awarding of the contract and the supervision of the work.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is proposing to handle the roadway repair work on rue Robitaille itself, including the portion located in Anjou (between rue des Ormeaux and the borough boundary).
The work covers the section of rue Robitaille between rue Paul-Pau and rue des Ormeaux, targeted for the 2026 season because of the condition of the driving surface.
Anjou would pay the bill for the work done on its territory: supervision, laboratory, contingencies, repair of four catch basins and 30 m² of sidewalk.
The document cites potholes and cracks, which reduce traction and increase the risk of accidents.
Planned timeline: call for tenders at the end of April, work in the summer of 2026.
No dollar amount is given in the document.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is proposing to take charge itself of repairing the roadway of avenue Souligny, an arterial street that normally falls under the responsibility of the central city.
The borough would handle the plans and specifications, the call for tenders, the awarding of the contract, and then the carrying out and supervision of the work.
The work is planned on avenue Souligny, between rue Honoré-Beaugrand and rue Saint-Émile.
The document cites the advanced state of deterioration of the roadway, with numerous potholes, a loss of traction and an increased risk of accidents.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier (SIRR) commits to covering all the costs of the work; no amount is given.
The agreement was reached at a meeting on April 9 between the SIRR and the borough; no work schedule is specified.
The borough of LaSalle is paying $2,800 to Destination Travail du Sud-Ouest de l'île de Montréal inc., which acts as trustee for the Comité de citoyens Highlands.
The money was used for the Fête de quartier hivernale Highlands, held at parc Mohawk on Sunday, February 1, 2026, and open to all LaSalle residents.
The program included skating, a figure skating demonstration, dog sledding, booths run by community organizations, and the handing out of snacks and hot drinks.
The grant comes from the operating budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social and covers at most 70% of the event's budget.
The council is approving the decision after the event took place, under the financial support program for LaSalle events.
The previous fall, the same committee had received $2,750 for its neighbourhood party at parc Dalmany.

The borough of LaSalle is giving $20,000 to Destination Travail du Sud-Ouest de l'île de Montréal inc., trustee for the Comité catalyseur du Bronx, to hold the "Pique-nique du Bronx" on Saturday, August 29, 2026.
Rue Centrale will be closed between rue Alepin and 7e Avenue; the cross avenues will stay open to traffic.
Free activities and food (art workshops, barbecue, games, face painting, musicians, booths); only alcoholic drinks will be sold.
The organization may obtain a liquor permit from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux, and must prevent service to minors.
The organization must give its accounting report and invoices to the borough within 30 days after the event.
The grant covers at most 70% of the event's budget; the borough is also providing goods and services valued at $29,275.
Amounts of $20,000 were also granted for the 2024 and 2025 editions, and $18,000 in 2023.
The borough of LaSalle is signing a one-year agreement with Radio communautaire de LaSalle (CKVL 100.1), from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
It is putting up a maximum expense of $34,492.50 including taxes ($30,000 before taxes), paid out of the budget of the Direction de la culture, des sports, des loisirs et du développement social.
In exchange, the radio station promotes the activities of LaSalle's recognized organizations and partners and sets aside 60 in-studio appearances for them in its programming.
The station, which has been operating in the area since 2006, has its offices on the 3rd floor of the borough hall and informs residents about snow removal, emergency measures and public notices.
The borough is encouraging the organization to diversify its funding, in particular by approaching Lachine, Verdun and Le Sud-Ouest.
The radio station must give the borough a report on the services provided before December 15, 2026.
The same amount of $34,492.50 had been authorized for 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is paying $254,202 (taxes included) to the organization Héritage Laurentien for the year 2026, from January 1 to December 31.
In return, the organization manages and maintains parc des Rapides, including the east and west jetties, and provides a conservation patrol and awareness activities there.
The amount breaks down as follows: $213,283 for ecological management and salaries, $21,229 for materials and equipment, $17,897 in administrative fees.
The amount represents an indexation of 3.13% compared with the contribution of $246,486 granted in 2025.
In 2025, the organization carried out about 9,400 awareness actions and 4,800 patrol interventions at parc des Rapides.
The borough has supported the organization since 2002; mayor Nancy Blanchet and the borough secretary are authorized to sign the agreement.
The borough of LaSalle is paying $142,975 to the organization Héritage Laurentien to run the Éco-quartier program from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The organization handles public awareness, beautification and greening, waste management, neighbourhood life and environmental education.
The amount is higher than the $134,445 paid in 2025: the borough cites an indexation of 2.4%, the amortization of repairs to a light vehicle, and a four-week extension of the assistant's mandate.
The graffiti removal component has been taken out of this agreement and will be covered by a separate agreement.
The City is adding about $19,000 in free goods and services; the borough can end the agreement with 30 working days' notice.
The contract is awarded directly without a call for tenders, which the law allows for a non-profit organization.
Héritage Laurentien will have to submit a report and an annual action plan in January.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $700 to the Club de lutte LaSalle to help three young athletes take part in the Canadian championships.
The competition takes place from April 24 to 26, 2026 in Grande Prairie, Alberta, in the U15, U17 and U19 categories.
The three athletes, aged 15 to 19, qualified at the provincial championships.
Travel and stay costs (flight, registration, licence, hotel) are estimated at about $1,568 per athlete; the funding helps lower the bill for the parents.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Direction culture, sports, loisirs et développement social and will be paid through the club.
LaSalle had given the club the same amount of $700 in April 2025 for a similar competition.
The borough of LaSalle is asking the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux for a permit to sell alcohol during the Fête nationale festivities on June 24, 2026.
The sales point will be set up on the grounds of the terrasse Serre, in the parc des Rapides, at 7770, boulevard LaSalle.
Sales will be limited to participants 18 years of age and older: those in charge must make sure that no alcoholic drinks are served or sold to minors.
Marie-Annick Lussier is designated to file the application on behalf of the borough.
The borough has been organizing these festivities for more than 40 years and applies for this permit every year.
The borough of LaSalle is entering into an agreement with the organization Allions-Nous to use part of the yard of the former école Allion, at 65, 5e avenue, from June to November 1, 2026.
The organization will offer cultural and recreational activities there: community gardens, a citizens' agora, outdoor movies, a bazaar and a farmers' market.
The organization may install containers, pergolas, tables, benches, planter boxes, games and kiosks to bring the site to life.
The borough will pay 70% of the estimated cost of services, up to a maximum of $10,000, taxes included; beyond that, Allions-Nous covers 100% of the expenses.
The land belongs to the Centre de services scolaire Lester-B.-Pearson, which is renewing for the summer of 2026 the right of use granted to the borough.
This is the third season of occupation of this site, which has been vacant since 2007, in the Village des Rapides neighbourhood.
Borough mayor Nancy Blanchet and borough secretary Simon Provost-Goupil are authorized to sign the agreement.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing the Chevaliers de Colomb (conseil de Ville LaSalle no 3147) to display advertising signs at 7710, boulevard LaSalle.
The signs are installed on the inside of the fence that surrounds the site.
The authorization is valid from May 1 to September 30, 2026 and departs from the signage by-law.
The organization says these signs provide it with income to organize activities in the LaSalle community.
No financial impact for the borough.
The same authorization was granted in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The borough of LaSalle is appointing ten members to its Conseil jeunesse, a non-partisan advisory group created in November 2019.
Members are volunteers aged 14 to 30 and must live in LaSalle; terms are two or three years, renewable once.
The Conseil jeunesse provides opinions and recommendations to the borough council on the needs of young people in the area.
Its members meet 6 times a year, go out to meet young people in the different sectors and work with local youth organizations.
The Conseil jeunesse has between 8 and 12 members; two positions remain to be filled. Councillor Benoît Auger sits on the committee.
The borough funds 100% of the operation of the Conseil jeunesse; no amount is specified.
A promotional campaign with youth organizations and on social media accompanies the initiative.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $4,200 to the Regroupement des éco-quartiers, a non-profit organization.
This money will be used to hire two students for "La Patrouille verte" during the summer of 2026.
The patrollers will go mainly to LaSalle's parks and public spaces to raise awareness about cleanliness, waste sorting, the protection of natural environments and responsible behaviour.
They will answer users' questions, take note of problem situations and act as the link between the public and Héritage Laurentien (Éco-quartier LaSalle).
The contribution is not recurring. In 2025, the borough had granted $4,000 for the same project.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing two street food trucks at parc Riverside for the Canada Day celebration on July 1, 2026.
The trucks will hand out 400 ice pops and 150 smoothies free of charge to children attending the celebration.
They will also be able to sell their products to families and other participants.
This year the celebration is being held at the parc multisports Riverside, after two editions at parc Marie-Claire-Kirkland-Casgrain.
The program will include soccer activities, tied to the FIFA World Cup 2026.
The decision summary states that there is no financial aspect attached to the decision.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $8,737 to the organization Héritage Laurentien to hold "La Fête du fleuve" on July 25, 2026, at parc des Rapides.
The event is free and runs from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. near the Terrasse Serre building: water activities with Kayak sans frontière, family entertainment, musical performances, exhibitors.
The organization is allowed to sell and serve alcohol if it obtains a permit from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux, and must never serve alcohol to minors.
Street food trucks are allowed on the site.
The borough is lending equipment (50 barriers, 12 stage platforms, one 10 x 10 tent and 4 weights) and installing an electrical panel; the value of the goods and services is estimated at $3,000.
The grant covers 70% of the event's budget and comes from the operating budget of the Direction culture, sports, loisirs et développement social.
Héritage Laurentien will have to submit its accountability report and its invoices within 30 days after the end of the event.
The borough of LaSalle is authorizing Maison de soins palliatifs Sault-Saint-Louis to hold a bazaar and fundraising activities on August 28 and 29, 2026.
The event will take place at 8699, boulevard LaSalle.
On offer: a pastry counter, household items and women's clothing.
No spending is tied to this authorization.

Religious organizations and foundations are no longer recognized by the borough, but a grandfather clause lets them continue to receive the same services; LaSalle is authorizing these bazaars on an exceptional basis.
The borough of LaSalle is giving $3,720 to Destination Travail du Sud-Ouest de l'île de Montréal inc., trustee for the comité de citoyens Highlands, for the Fête de quartier Highlands.
The event takes place at parc Dalmany on Saturday, September 12, 2026, and on Sunday, September 13 in case of rain.
A parade by the Corps de cornemuses et tambours de la GRC will go along avenue Bélanger, rues Des Oblats, Maria and Dalmany, boulevard LaSalle and avenue Highlands, which will stay open to traffic.
The organization is authorized to obtain a liquor permit from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux; drinks will be served free of charge, never to minors.
Activities and food are free: workshops, tastings, children's games, face painting, musical performances and booths run by organizations, including the Service de sécurité incendie.
The organization must submit its accounting report and its invoices within 30 days after the event.
The grant covers at most 70% of the event's budget; last year, the borough granted $2,750.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is creating two parking spaces reserved for car-sharing (self-service) vehicles near chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges.
First space: south side of avenue Ridgewood, 45 metres west of chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, over about 14.6 metres.
Second space: south side of avenue Forest Hill, 11.5 metres west of chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, over about 11.6 metres.
The taxi stand on avenue Ridgewood is being removed: the Agence de mobilité durable says it is little used.
The request came from a resident (311): both avenues are dead ends, steeply sloped, served by a single public transit line, and 42% of households in the area do not have a vehicle.
"New signage" and "car-sharing" sign plates will be installed; the signs are expected to be put up between September and December.
The cost is limited to installing the signs, billed by the signage division of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie; no amount is given.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest wants to borrow up to $19M to renovate and bring the Centre sportif de la Petite-Bourgogne up to standard.
The work includes replacing the electromechanical systems, repairing the building envelope and universal accessibility, with the aim of LEED Silver certification.
The project cost is estimated at $18.11M after being updated to 2026; the loan is set higher to cover unforeseen costs.
The ministère de l'Éducation is to provide a grant of up to $9.57M (PAFIRSPA program), applied as a reduction of the loan once received; the borough would pay $8.54M.
The grant share represented 66% of eligible costs in 2024, but about 53% based on the updated 2026 costs.
The debt will be repaid by the borough's taxpayers, over a term of no more than 20 years, and the by-law is subject to approval by the qualified voters (register planned for June or July 2026).
Announced schedule: notice of motion and tabling in May 2026, adoption in June 2026, ministry approval in the summer or fall of 2026.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest will receive $519,400 (net of rebates) in 2026 to operate the parc du Bassin-à-Bois, in Griffintown, which is set to open in the spring of 2026.
Starting in 2027, its operating budget will be increased by $972,300 per year, on a recurring basis, for the same park.
The 2026 money comes from the City's reserve for sociocultural and sports infrastructure.
The budget covers winter and summer maintenance, upkeep of the chalet, technical maintenance of the building, and cultural and sports programming ($157,500).
The park has a four-season pavilion with universally accessible washrooms and a refrigerated skating rink that can be used from mid-December to mid-March.
In April 2026, the borough awarded Construction Urbex inc. a maintenance contract worth $779,243.06 including taxes, for June 2026 to June 2027.
According to the document, without this transfer, the borough would not be able to maintain an adequate level of service in the area.
The City is renting out 10 workstations (700 sq. ft.) at the Centre d'affaires du Technoparc, at 7140, rue Albert-Einstein in Saint-Laurent, to the company Informatique Merkaz inc.
The lease runs for one year, starting April 1, 2026, for rent of $30,000 before taxes ($34,492.50 including taxes).
The tenant, which has been at the Technoparc since July 2024, is going from 6 to 10 workstations and will therefore occupy all of space 203.
The lease includes access to common areas: meeting rooms, cafeteria and parking spaces.
The tenant will also pay the property and school taxes, and will provide a security deposit of $2,874.38.
The previous lease had been terminated as of March 31, 2026 for unpaid rent; the company has since paid all amounts owed.
According to the City, the rent matches the market price based on its internal assessment.
The City is renting six offices (units 100-04 to 100-07, 100-10 and 100-11) at 7140, rue Albert-Einstein, in the Technoparc in Saint-Laurent, to the company Flairstech inc.
The lease runs for one year, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, for an area of 64.38 m² (693 sq. ft.).
The total rent is $30,000 before taxes, or $34,492.50 with the GST and the QST; the City collects this revenue.
The tenant also pays the property and school taxes, which are billed directly to it.
The lease gives access to common areas: meeting rooms, a cafeteria and parking spaces.
Flairstech has been in the Technoparc since March 2022 and is going from five to six offices; the City says the rent matches the market rent according to its internal assessment.
The City is renting 888 square feet of office and laboratory space to the company Leapfrog Bio inc., at 2300, boulevard Alfred-Nobel, in the borough of Saint-Laurent.
The lease runs for one year, from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, for a total rent of $30,899.40 before taxes ($35,526.59 including taxes).
The rent counts as revenue for the City; the tenant also pays the property and school taxes, which are billed directly.
The lease also gives access to the building's common areas: meeting rooms, cafeteria and parking spaces.
Leapfrog Bio inc. has already been occupying this space since March 2025; its previous four-month lease was for $10,299.80 and its one-year lease for $21,450.
According to the City, the rent matches the market rent set by its Section des évaluations immobilières.
The City is renting office space at 7140, rue Albert-Einstein, in the Technoparc de Saint-Laurent, to the Conseil national de recherches du Canada.
The lease covers 2 years, from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2028, for 87.32 square metres (940 square feet) of office space.
The City will collect $119,040 in rent for the period, before taxes ($136,866.24 with taxes included).
The tenant will also pay the property and school taxes, billed directly, and does not have to pay the administrative fee since it already has a contract with the City.
The rent matches the market rent according to the assessment done by the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation.
The CNRC has occupied space in this building since August 2020; it asked for a new lease.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing two permanent murals on the buildings located at 2185 and 2296, avenue du Mont-Royal Est.
The murals will be painted during the summer of 2026, one by the artist Labrona, the other by François Vincent.
Normally, the planning by-law prohibits painting a brick façade; the council is lifting this prohibition by order, as the rule allows for cultural purposes.
The SDC de l'avenue du Mont-Royal and the organization MU are committing to maintain the murals for 5 years and to hold civil liability insurance of at least 2 million dollars.
The murals will go on secondary façades, in order to preserve the buildings' architectural features.
The project is part of a set of actions targeting the area of the former village De Lorimier and depends on obtaining the desired funding.
No financial aspect is planned for the borough in this file.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing a mural on the building at 1, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest, for a period of 5 years.
The mural is to be created during the summer of 2026 by the artist La Charbonne.
It will be printed on vinyl and installed in a non-permanent way on a secondary facade of the building.
The urban planning by-law normally prohibits painting a brick facade; an ordinance allows an exception for murals for public, cultural, tourism or socio-community purposes.
The owner agrees to maintain the mural and to hold civil liability insurance of at least 2 million dollars.
Creating the mural depends on obtaining the desired funding.
The borough council was to adopt the ordinance on July 6, 2026.
The Ville-Marie borough council is approving in advance up to $20,517,400 in spending for the year 2026 (January 1 to December 31).

This spending covers three types of purchases: public utility services (such as electricity from Hydro-Québec), assignments given to other City departments, and contracts made through the framework agreements negotiated by the City.
The borough says this avoids having to go back to council each time and lets managers start assignments faster, within the budgets already adopted.
The largest share goes to the Direction des travaux publics: $13,371,900, including $3,323,800 for maintaining lighting and signage.
Other notable items: $5,607,700 for renting buildings and land, $1,100,000 for electricity, $1,084,400 for salt and abrasives.
Last year, the same authorization was $17,652,300 for 2025.
The authorized amounts will be adjusted if the budgets are changed during the year.

Ville-Marie is reporting the 2025 financial results of its pothole-patching service using a mechanized patcher, which it offers to Mercier
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Rosemont
La Petite-Patrie.
The budget planned for 2025 was $141,200, but actual spending reached only $19,118 ($11,005 in salaries, $8,113 in other expenses).
The $122,082 surplus will be redistributed to the three participating boroughs; Ville-Marie will record an adjustment of $81,446 to its 2026 management surpluses.
The surplus is explained by the periods when the machine was out of service; the salaries of the employees assigned to it were absorbed elsewhere by Ville-Marie.

The client boroughs are withdrawing from the agreement because of mechanical breakdowns and the patcher's lack of reliability; the termination with Mercier
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Rosemont
La Petite-Patrie will take place in the 2027 budget.
A final accountability report is planned for 2027 to close out the transactions, including the redistribution of the accumulated reserve.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is settling out of court, for $41,686.46 (principal, taxes, interest and costs), a lawsuit brought by the company Excavations Super inc.
The dispute concerned the development of a new public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer, a contract worth $2,689,454.53 awarded in May 2024.
The City had withheld $72,513.96 in late penalties (31 days at $2,339.16 per day); the company was claiming this amount before the Cour du Québec.
The settlement is equivalent to 15.5 days of penalty, that is, half of the claim, and is concluded without any admission of liability.
The amount will be paid out of the sum already withheld, so at no additional cost according to the document; the City gives a full release regarding the late penalties.
The agreement stems from a settlement conference held on December 3, 2025; provisional acceptance of the work was declared on July 16, 2025.
The borough of Ville-Marie is renting vehicles from La Compagnie de Location d'Autos Enterprise Canada until February 28, 2027, a period of 13 months.
The authorized spending totals $298,411.86, taxes included: $271,283.51 for the rental and $27,128.35 in contingencies to cover changes in prices and equipment.
This covers 8 pickup trucks and 2 sport utility vehicles, paid for out of the Voirie-Propreté budget.
The vehicles are used for snow removal throughout the borough (including sector 310), for putting up and taking down snow removal markers, and for cleanliness operations in the summer.
The borough cites the lack of available vehicles in the fleet of the Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers during the summer and winter assignment periods.
The rental is based on master agreements already entered into by the Ville following a public call for tenders (2 bidders).
The Ville-Marie borough is awarding a negotiated (sole-source) contract of $194,656 (taxes included) to the organization Action-Réinsertion (Le Sac à dos) for cleanliness brigades.
The contract runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027: $159,140 for the summer season (8 months) and $35,516 for the winter season (4 months).

In the summer, the brigades clean the block bounded by De Maisonneuve Est / Berri / René-Lévesque Est / Panet (except rue Sainte-Catherine Est), four parks (Place du Village, parc Serge-Garant, Place Émile-Gamelin, parc de l'Espoir) and 55 garbage cans.
In April–May and in November, an additional sector is added around rue Berger, between Saint-Laurent and Sanguinet.
The winter sector will be determined on October 1, 2026; the team will then work 5 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, between 7 a.m. and 12 p.m.
The brigade members are people experiencing homelessness or marginalization who are working toward reintegration; they receive two meals a day, billed to the borough at $6.
The City is thus renewing a partnership already funded with $180,986 in 2025 and $114,915 in 2024.
The borough of Ville-Marie is awarding a mutual-agreement contract of $224,751 (taxes included) to the organization Groupe Information Travail (GIT) to clean up areas of its territory.
Four brigade workers will pick up litter and cigarette butts on sidewalks, curbs, alleys and public spaces, empty overflowing public garbage cans, and pull weeds from tree pits.
The area covered is Sainte-Marie, at the borough's request.
Summer schedule: from April 1 to November 30, 2026, Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. — cost of $178,556.
Winter schedule: from December 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays from 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., with a supervisor-support worker — cost of $46,195.
The project also aims at the social and professional integration of people who are far from the job market, and who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
The agreement with GIT ends on March 31, 2027; the 2025 contract with the same organization was $219,932.

The Ville-Marie borough is awarding a contract, without a call for tenders, to the organization Spectre de rue (TAPAJ program) for the manual cleaning of sidewalks and street curbs, for a maximum expense of $228,037.35, taxes included.
The contract runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027; the agreement with the organization ends on March 31, 2027.
The crews work in Centre-Sud, notably on rue Saint-Christophe, rue Saint-André and rue Papineau, between Ontario, Sherbrooke and de Maisonneuve, as well as in ruelle Providence.

In summer (April 1 to November 30, 2026): on site 5 days a week, about 5.5 hours a day, with 4 to 6 crew members. In winter (December 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027): 3 days a week (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) with 4 crew members.
Costs are broken down as follows: $162,670.97 for the summer season and $65,366.37 for the winter season.
The TAPAJ program employs young people who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless, paid by the day, with the goal of social and job integration.
The crew members also take care of street garbage bins: removing excess recyclable materials and replacing the bags.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving up to $350,000, taxes included, to the Société de développement commercial Montréal centre-ville for downtown cleanliness.
The agreement covers 15 months, from January 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, and the borough is paying 100% of the project.
The money funds the Brigades de propreté: 7 additional workers (shifts from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m.), uniforms, brooms, carts, bags and a pressure washer.
The brigades hire people referred by neighbourhood organizations such as the Mission Old Brewery and the YMCA, as a way to help them re-enter society.
The funds come from the Stratégie centre-ville program of the Service du développement économique: $300,000 in 2026 and $50,000 in 2027.
The organization must mention the borough's financial support in its events and publications.
Last year, a similar agreement provided for a maximum contribution of $375,000 for 2025.
The Ville-Marie borough is extending the rental of tractor-loaders with operators for snow removal by one season, the winter of 2026-2027.
Two suppliers keep the contracts: 9055-0344 Québec inc. (Transport DM Choquette, lots 2.1.1 and 2.1.2) and Groupe Imog inc. (lots 2.1.3 and 2.1.4).
Additional spending of $1,062,369.00, taxes included: $965,790.00 for the rental and $96,579.00 in contingencies (10%).
The maximum value of the contract goes from $2,432,411.10 to $3,494,780.10, taxes and contingencies included.
Hourly rates are unchanged: $275/h for Transport DM Choquette, $425/h for Groupe Imog; the indexation set out in the contract is 0%.
The borough is taking $323,361.50 from its surpluses set aside for snow removal to cover the 2026 spending; the 2027 share will come from the budget.
These machines are used to clear snow during heavy snowfalls and to clear the lanes before snow removal.
The City is authorizing five cultural venues to serve alcohol and to keep their patrons on site after regular hours, during events held between January 24 and February 8, 2026.
Salon Daomé may stay open until 6 a.m. on January 24; Espace ESC until 6 a.m. on January 25 and 31 and until 7 a.m. on January 24 and February 1.

The money is used to buy supplies: garden hoses, wire supports, fertilizer, tomato plants and cucumber plants.

Montréal is signing an agreement with the ministère des Affaires municipales to receive up to $448,998 to fund studies on flooding.
The money covers 75% of the project's eligible expenses, estimated at $590,000.
The studies cover the Nicolet and Dézéry watersheds, in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, where flooding happens repeatedly.
They are to pinpoint the locations where high-capacity green infrastructure, resilient spaces and measures to protect vulnerable buildings would be most effective.
The results will be used to build a decision-support tool to compare how effective the various scenarios are, both on public property and on existing buildings.
The mayor and the city clerk are authorized to sign the agreement; the ministère will then reimburse the eligible expenses.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the first annual report (2025) on the Stratégie montréalaise de l'eau 2025-2034, adopted in June 2025, and authorizes its publication.
Water use is going down: 592 litres of drinking water produced per person per day (down from 612), and 306 litres for residential use (down from 315).
The average time to repair leaks is going from 10 to 8 working days for water mains, and to 7 days for service connections.
2,700 lead water service lines were replaced in 2025, which is 67.5% of the annual target; 5 of the 6 plants earned stars for drinking water quality.
Sewer overflows went down by 14.8%, and the number of hours that recreation and tourism sites were closed because of overflows went down by 43.4%.
The city recovers 59% of the cost of water; the gap between actual spending and investment needs reaches 42%.
The report will be published and posted online in March 2026, with a page summarizing the results.
The City is adding $29,893.50 (taxes included) to the audit contract with the firm Deloitte, bringing the total contract from $122,735.81 to $152,629.31.

These audits are used to justify subsidies received for water infrastructure work: the Gas Tax and Québec's contribution (TECQ 2019-2024), the Fonds pour l'infrastructure municipale d'eau (FIMEAU) and the Fonds Chantiers Canada-Québec.
The original contract did not cover the calculation of the TECQ minimum capital spending threshold or the second Fonds Chantiers Canada-Québec agreement; these portions are being added.
The City says this avoids a new call for tenders, which would cost more because portions already audited would have to be redone.

Council is authorizing an additional revenue and expenditure budget of $63,195 net, which is the share of the audit fees reimbursable by the FIMEAU program (80%), which will finance the entire cost of $27,296.75 in net taxes.
According to the document, without these audits, the City would risk losing its eligibility for the subsidy programs or having to repay amounts.
The audits must be completed in December 2026. The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council.
The City is applying to Québec for financial assistance (PRIMEAU program, component 2) for two drinking water projects valued together at $213M.

First project: rebuilding the collectors and interconnection chamber 1 at the Atwater plant, whose riveted steel pipes installed between 1920 and 1933 have reached the end of their useful life. Estimated cost: $147M.
Second project: upgrading the Côte-des-Neiges pumping station and reservoir, which serve 77,000 people, including hospitals, campuses, schools and daycares. Estimated cost: $66M.
The grant could cover up to 75% of eligible expenses; a letter from the minister dated May 1, 2023 sets aside $429,562,187 for Montréal under this program.
The City commits to paying its share of the costs, all non-eligible costs, cost overruns, and 50% of change directives, as well as the expenses if it misses the program's deadlines.
The application will be sent to the ministry as soon as it is adopted; work contracts can only be awarded after the minister's letter of commitment.
The City states that it is responsible for the work and for any damage caused by its employees, agents or subcontractors.

The City is extending its agreement with the ministère des Affaires municipales for the project to control wastewater discharges during rainfall: the work must be completed no later than December 31, 2026.
This agreement allows Montréal to receive up to $98,600,000 from the Fonds Chantiers Canada-Québec, which is 66% of the project's eligible expenses, estimated at $148,000,000.

The project provides for three retention basins to reduce wastewater discharges into the canal Lachine (Rockfield basin), the rivière des Prairies (Lavigne basin) and the fleuve Saint-Laurent (William basin).
It also includes upgrading the equipment in the chambre De Courcelle of the collecteur Saint-Pierre, which discharges into the fleuve Saint-Laurent.
The original agreement, signed in 2011, has already been postponed three times (2019, 2021, then 2023).
Payment of the amounts depends on meeting the program's conditions, including an annual report on drinking water savings and a program to eliminate cross-connections.
The mayor and the city clerk are authorized to sign the addendum on behalf of the City.
City council is naming a new park in the arrondissement de Lachine "parc des Sœurs-de-Sainte-Anne". The park is located west of rue Esther-Blondin.
The land, located on the former ferme Saint-Joachim of the congregation's Maison mère, was transferred to the borough by the sœurs de Sainte-Anne in 2020.
The park will mainly be used for urban agriculture, with outdoor museum displays recalling the presence of the congregation from 1900 to 1960.
The name highlights the contribution of the congregation, which has been in Lachine since 1861, to the development of the neighbourhood and to education.
The Comité consultatif en reconnaissance gave a favourable opinion; the borough and the congregation support the choice.
The name will be posted after the council resolution and after it is made official by the Commission de toponymie du Québec.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is spending $167,330 (non-taxable) on street furniture and replacement parts for the year 2027.
The order includes 20 Lafontaine-type benches, 35 Secteur 5 benches, 10 picnic tables, 59 seat panels and 10 sets of repair slats.
The 59 seat panels will be paired with existing bench structures to build at least 29 new benches.
The supplier is internal: the City's Service du matériel roulant et des ateliers, presented as the only one able to build the City's standardized models.
Most of the furniture is due to arrive in the spring of 2027; installation and repairs will be done by borough employees.
The purchase is funded by carrying over unused budgets from the 2025 PDI and by the 2026-2035 street furniture acquisition program.
In February 2026, the borough had authorized $121,721 (taxes included) with the same service for the year 2026.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is buying 30 new bike racks and awarding the contract to G.G. inox inc. for $16,843.84, taxes included.
The expense is paid out of the borough's Fonds réservé pour fins de stationnements, for an amount of $15,380.67 net of tax rebates.
The racks will be installed along the edges of parks in the borough's various neighbourhoods, at locations analyzed in advance.
Installation is planned for 2026-2027, followed by a review of the results.
Three suppliers submitted a price: Techsport ($42,080.85), Les Agences de l'Est P.J. ($40,241.25) and G.G. inox inc. ($16,843.84), the lowest bid.
The measure stems from action 2.1.5 of the Plan local de déplacements du Sud-Ouest, which aims to increase the supply of bike parking.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is proposing to build and manage itself the greenhouse complex planned for parc Frédéric-Back, a park that normally falls under the urban agglomeration's responsibility.

The project combines two ideas into one: a community greenhouse to grow fresh fruits and vegetables for the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, and research and training spaces for Collège Ahuntsic, AULAB, UQAM and other partners.

The construction budget is estimated at $2,185,000, funded by the Smart Cities Challenge ($920,000), the participatory budget ($765,000, subject to approval) and a federal fund from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada ($500,000).
Planned timeline: calls for tenders in spring 2026, construction in summer-fall 2026, commissioning in winter 2027, and organizations moving in from that point onward.
A later phase, conditional on funding, would aim to recover the heat and CO₂ released by the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel.

Without approval, the City would lose $920,000 from the Smart Cities Challenge (to be used before May 30, 2026) and $500,000 from the federal fund, and a project chosen through the participatory budget would not go ahead.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $25,000 to the organization Quartier des arts du cirque (QUAC) for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
The money funds the first year of the organization's 2026-2029 action plan, focused on the Saint-Michel neighbourhood.
The plan calls for transforming the space under the autoroute Métropolitaine: 90 wall columns painted by neighbourhood artists by 2029, and greening.

It also calls for developing the commercial offering on rue Jarry Est: an entrepreneurial lab for 14- to 21-year-olds, a micro-business in a shipping container, a shared commercial space, and help with the outdoor layout of businesses.

According to the file, the three components are to create nearly 300 job opportunities over three years, support more than 60 entrepreneurs, train 150 young people and revitalize 9,000 m² of public space.
The director of territorial development, Jocelyn Jobidon, is authorized to sign the agreement on behalf of the City.
The funds come from the Service du développement économique and are transferred to the borough.
The City is increasing its borrowing for the extension of the Anjou and Montréal-Est industrial collector sewer from $31,000,000 to $96,000,000, an increase of $65,000,000.
The Service de l'eau explains the increase by the rise in the project's expected costs.
The work extends a storm sewer 2,100 to 2,400 mm in diameter up to a connection point north of rue Notre-Dame.
According to the file, the extension would eliminate the fees the City pays for the pumping station at the Amrize (formerly Lafarge) quarry and the compensation paid out when the quarry floods.
The collector sewer would provide wastewater and stormwater service to the former site of the oil company Shell (groupe Laganière) and to other lots in the Anjou and Montréal-Est industrial parks.
Each related municipality in the agglomeration will pay a share based on its fiscal potential, with the option of paying its share in cash; the term of the loan cannot exceed 20 years.
The increase must be approved by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is presenting its budget follow-up as of March 31, 2026, compared with the same spending and revenue as of March 31, 2025.
It expects to end 2026 with an operating surplus of $453,000, compared with $2,877,500 estimated at the end of 2025.
The operating budget shows an expected deficit of $617,400: $1,655,100 in overspending on pay, offset by $1,037,700 in savings elsewhere.
About $1M of this deficit comes from delegated water activities ($530,900) and residual materials ($475,400), amounts that must be reimbursed to the borough at the end of the year.

The borough expects to issue $3,800,000 worth of construction and alteration permits in 2026, but notes a slowdown in applications compared with past years; the expected net effect is a gain of $340,200.
The end of the transitional measure on pension plans takes away $276,100.
Revenue is expected to be in line with the budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $70,000 to SDC Montréal-Nord for its operations in 2026, from January 1 to December 31.
The money can be used for SDC staff salaries, renting a space and buying equipment.
The amount is paid in a single payment, planned for February 2026, and paid entirely out of the borough's operating budget.
In exchange, the SDC must submit a 2026 action plan by March 31, 2026 at the latest.
It must also provide a financial report and an activity report within 90 days after the end of its fiscal year.
Same amount as the contributions granted for 2024 and 2025.
The SDC was created in June 2023 and adopted its 2026 budget at a general meeting on September 22, 2025.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is paying $145,000 to the organization Le Pôle to fund its mission from July 1 to December 31, 2026.
The amount is paid in a single instalment after the agreement is approved at the borough council meeting of June 8, 2026, and comes from the 2026 operating budget.
The agreement covers three areas: structuring projects and mobilization of socio-economic stakeholders, revitalization of commercial streets, and development of entrepreneurship.
This is a transitional six-month agreement, using the renewal option of the 2022-2024 three-year agreement signed with the former CDEC de Montréal-Nord.
Le Pôle had already received $536,250 for the period from January 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.
According to the document, Le Pôle must also support the borough in developing its next economic development actions.
The borough of Saint-Léonard approves the plans to renovate the front of a commercial building at 4305-4315, boulevard Métropolitain Est, in the Saint-Léonard-Ouest district.
The one-storey building, built in 1962, houses two car dealerships; the work affects the part at 4315.

The project includes an interior redesign and repairs to the exterior walls: grey architectural block, white and blue glass curtain walls, and an oak-coloured laminate panel canopy at the main entrance.
The urban planning department gives a favourable opinion, but suggests more windows: the front has only three small clear windows.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended the project favourably at its meeting of February 5, 2026.
No public money is involved; this is an application for a renovation permit from a private owner.
The borough of Saint-Léonard recommends authorizing the expansion of a single-family home at 5625, boulevard Couture, in the Saint-Léonard-Ouest district.
The house, built in 1966, will go from one storey to two; the building footprint does not change (19% of the 485 m² lot, with the maximum allowed being 40%).
The walls will be covered in glacier grey stone with charcoal inserts, the roof in dark asphalt shingles, and the doors, windows and architectural features will be black.
The private tree in the front yard will be cut down because it is in the work zone; four trees and several shrubs of native species will be planted.
The public tree is being kept and the outdoor landscaping stays roughly the same, with a small addition of paving stone.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on March 12, 2026, and the planning department did as well, in particular because the setback of the second storey limits the sense of bulk for the neighbours.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is authorizing the installation of two signs on the commercial building at 9464-9500, boulevard Lacordaire, in the Saint-Léonard-Ouest district.
The signs will identify the Éconofitness business, located at 9480, boulevard Lacordaire, suite 210.

One sign, measuring 8.83 m², will be placed on the side of the building facing boulevard Lacordaire; the other, measuring 15.23 m², on the side facing the parking lot, across from boulevard des Grandes-Prairies.
An approval was required because a specific project adopted in 2015 requires that any new sign at this location go through an architectural integration review.
The urban planning department gave a favourable opinion: the supports do not harm the façade, the signs fit in with those already in place, and they leave the display windows clear.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended approval on April 15, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is approving the plans for adding a lift platform for people with reduced mobility at 4340-4346, rue Baron, in the Saint-Léonard-Ouest district.
The platform will be connected to the front balcony of a two-storey residential building with five units, built in 1974.
Because the work changes an exterior wall that can be seen from the street, the project had to go through the site planning and architectural integration plan approval process.
The urban planning department gave a favourable opinion: the platform is needed to make the unit accessible, and it is standard equipment that cannot be modified.
The urban planning advisory committee also gave a favourable recommendation for the project at its April 15, 2026 meeting.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is approving the plans to build a detached single-family house at 9125, rue de Fontenoy, in the Saint-Léonard-Ouest district.
The one-storey house built in 1961 that currently occupies the lot will be demolished.
The new building will have two storeys, with a setback second storey, on a lot of 490.5 m² (land occupancy rate of 28%, maximum allowed 40%).
Planned finishes: grey and graphite grey stone on the front, graphite grey brick on the sides and at the back, dark asphalt shingles on the roof.
Two private trees will be cut down because they are located where the building will stand; the public tree is being kept, and two trees plus shrubs of native species will be planted.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on April 15, 2026, as did the direction de l'aménagement urbain.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is authorizing the construction of a detached 3-storey residential building with 18 units on a vacant lot on rue Napoléon-Desmarchais (lot 1 123 910), in the Saint-Léonard-Est district.

The project is being granted exemptions from the zoning rules: a rear setback of 4.59 m instead of 12.15 m, a lot width of 16.74 m and a lot depth of 26.38 m instead of the required 30 m, and 16 parking spaces instead of 18.

Conditions imposed: underground parking with working level 2 charging stations for at least 50% of the spaces, a heated access lane to the garage, and a landscaping plan matching the concept submitted (9 trees and shrubs planned).
The developer must submit its building permit application within 18 months of the resolution coming into force.
A monetary guarantee of $50,000 is required before the permit is issued, to ensure the planting of trees, the waste storage area and the charging stations.
The rear setback exemption is subject to approval by referendum: interested persons in zone H-1500 and neighbouring zones could be called on to have their say.
The council is also filing the minutes of the public consultation meeting held on June 11, 2026, and is adopting the second draft resolution on July 6, 2026.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is authorizing the construction of a 6-storey mixed-use building (maximum 20 m) at 7250-7260, boulevard Langelier, at the corner of rue de Lotbinière, in the Saint-Léonard-Est district.
The project provides for 96 housing units and 240 m² of commercial space on the ground floor, replacing a one-storey commercial building built in 1982.
Parking: 46 underground spaces and 2 outdoor spaces; up to 3 spaces reserved for car sharing, located indoors, identified and tied to an agreement with a car-sharing organization.
The developer must build a pedestrian path with no fence between rue de Lotbinière and boulevard Langelier, protected by an easement in favour of the City.
Greening requirements: a roof with 410 m² of vegetation and a 200 m² terrace, a climate resilience factor of 0.47, the preservation of 9 trees and the planting of 15 new trees.
A monetary guarantee of $100,000 is required before the permit is issued, and the permit application must be filed within 18 months after the resolution comes into force.
Four exemptions may be subject to approval by referendum: people in zone C-2490 and neighbouring zones could be called on to have their say. A public consultation was held on June 11, 2026.

Saint-Léonard is expanding the areas where you can apply for permission to open a return site for deposit containers: all Commerce (C) and Mixed commerce (Cm) zones, plus zone H-1240, instead of a short list of specific zones.
The borough is removing the maximum floor area limit for these return sites.
New conditions: building a loading dock is not allowed, and only unit-by-unit returns are permitted.
The change follows two non-compliant applications filed by Consignaction, one outside the targeted zone and the other exceeding the permitted floor area.
The three provisions may be subject to approval by referendum; the notice about this possibility is scheduled for July 7, 2026.
