Timeline: second draft by-law adopted on July 6, 2026, final adoption scheduled for September 8, 2026.
The document also files the minutes of the public consultation held on June 11, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is authorizing three outdoor movie evenings in the parking lot at 5135-5169, rue Jean-Talon Est, in the Saint-Léonard-Ouest district.
The screenings will take place on August 28, September 4 and September 11, 2026, from 7:30 p.m. to 9:15 p.m. (setup starting at 4 p.m., takedown until 10 p.m.).
The activity is aimed at neighbourhood families and seeks to draw attention to a quiet area of rue Jean-Talon Est.
The organizers will have to file a special event application with the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal and follow its recommendations.
Garbage and recycling bins are planned for waste management.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 4, 2026; a public notice and a sign on the site were planned for June 19, 2026.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is beginning the authorization process for a residential project on a vacant lot on rue de Palerme, between boulevard Provencher and rue Bélanger (Saint-Léonard-Ouest district).
The project calls for a detached two-storey building with a basement, containing 3 units with 3 bedrooms each, and 2 parking spaces in the front yard, on a lot of 372.8 m².

The project departs from the zoning rules on three points: ground coverage ratio (0.277 instead of 0.30), lot width (10.67 m instead of 13.70 m) and the distance of the parking spaces from the front door (1.23 m instead of 1.50 m).

Conditions imposed: keeping or planting at least six trees (including two of medium or large size), a parking area made of permeable material, masonry cladding, and a height no greater than that of the neighbouring building.
The developer will have to file its building permit application within 18 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
Five provisions may be subject to a referendum: people in the zone concerned and in the adjoining zones will be able to ask for approval by referendum.
Planned steps: public consultation on July 23, 2026, second draft on September 8, 2026, final adoption on October 6, 2026.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is granting an exemption allowing an industrial project at 6650-6690, rue Louis-Sicard (Saint-Léonard-Est district) to provide 4 fewer parking spaces than the 22 required.
In exchange, the developer must pay $22,012 into the parking fund, which is $5,503 per missing space.
The project adds 421.52 m² to the second floor of an industrial building already authorized by permit in October 2025, bringing the total area to 1,749 m².
The lot, located in the industrial area east of boulevard Langelier, is bordered by three streets (Louis-Sicard, du Creusot and Jarry Est), which limits the space available for parking.
One space is being removed to create 2 additional spaces for people with reduced mobility, leaving 18 spaces in total.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 4, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is approving the plans to build a detached single-family house at 5860, rue Jeanne-Lajoie, in the Saint-Léonard-Est district.
The one-storey house built in 1964 that stands on the lot will be demolished.
The new building will have two storeys, on a lot of 472.4 m², with a lot coverage of 31% (the maximum allowed is 40%).
Planned finishes: almond white brick and stone, white architectural block, charcoal grey asphalt shingle roof, black doors and windows.
The public tree in front of the property will be kept; two trees and some shrubs will be planted in the back yard.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 4, 2026, as did the direction de l'aménagement urbain.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is approving the addition of a second storey to a single-family home at 5780, rue de Canseau, in the Saint-Léonard-Est district.
The home, built in 1964, has one storey with a garage in the basement; its footprint and outdoor landscaping will not change.
The walls will be covered in brick (Permacon Melville Slik Lisbon) and the roof in charcoal grey asphalt shingles.
The second storey will be set back from the first, which, according to the Direction de l'aménagement urbain, limits the sense of bulk for neighbours, most of whom live in one-storey buildings.
The project includes planting one large-growing tree and keeping the existing 6 trees and the large cedar; the public tree is not affected.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 4, 2026.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is renewing for 12 months its contract to purchase glass microbeads used for marking lines on the road surface.
The authorized expense is $139,615.29, taxes included, taken from the operating budget of the department in charge.
The supplier remains Potters Canada, Division PNA Partnership, the only bidder in the 2022 call for tenders.
The renewal runs from March 9, 2026 to March 8, 2027; this is the second and last option provided for in the contract.
The City expects to use about 85,000 kg of microbeads per year, mainly for the white and yellow lines that mark out traffic lanes.
The document cites the supplier's performance rating of 91% and prices considered competitive; the conditions, including price indexation, remain the same.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is extending its contract for the supply of traffic signs with 9030-5814 Québec Inc. (Spectralite/SignoPlus) by 12 months.
The authorized spending is $666,102.74, taxes included, which is provided for in the department's operating budget.
The renewal runs from April 5, 2026 to April 4, 2027, under the same conditions as the original contract, including price indexation.
These signs are used to install and maintain signage in the nine boroughs that were part of the former Ville de Montréal.
The City points to the score of 98% that the supplier received in its most recent performance evaluation.
Without a renewal, the City would have to issue a new call for tenders, which would delay the supply of signs.
This is the second and final extension option for the contract awarded in 2022 ($1,998,308.22 for 36 months).
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is offering to do road pavement marking in 2026 for five other boroughs: Anjou, L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Lachine, Montréal-Nord and Saint-Laurent.
The service covers the marking of lines and symbols that already exist across the entire road network of these boroughs, including bike lanes.
The team will also assess new requests, estimate their costs and carry out the requested work during the season.
Each borough must adopt its own resolution accepting the offer before the work can begin.
The 2026 costs for each borough are in an attachment to the file and are not detailed in the text.
The marking plans, a weekly progress report (starting in April) and a form for additional requests will be posted on a sharing platform.
The City justifies the agreement by the consistent quality of the work, cost optimization and the safety of road users.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is extending its contract with Ennis Paint Canada by 12 months for the supply of road marking paint, from May 3, 2026 to May 2, 2027.
The authorized spending is $1,753,368.75, taxes included, budgeted in the operating budget of the department in charge.
This paint is used for street marking in 14 boroughs, including Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Lachine, Ville-Marie, Le Sud-Ouest, Montréal-Nord and Saint-Laurent.
Needs are estimated at about 205,000 litres of paint for the 2026 marking season, on a network of about 4,050 km of lanes and 6,675 km of sidewalks.
This is the second and last renewal option provided for in the contract awarded in 2022; the terms and the price indexation stay the same.
The borough points to the contract ending on May 2 and the risk of supply delays if a new call for tenders had to be launched.

The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing a residential project at 4901-4903, rue Adam, including the redivision of the land (lot 1 879 420), the construction, conversion and occupancy of a building, and the landscaping of the outdoor spaces.
The project may depart from many of the borough's planning and subdivision rules, under section 93 of the provincial Act respecting housing.
The building may reach 9 storeys and 32 metres, with a maximum building coverage of 76% and minimum front and side setbacks of 1.5 metres.
The entire residential floor area must be devoted to social or affordable housing; the number of units is not limited, and rooming houses and collective accommodation are permitted.

The église Saint-Clément must remain visible: a cantilever is required on the ground floor in line with its façade, walls must be at least 70% glazed within the visibility area, and no dwelling units are allowed on the ground floor within that area.
A permit application must include a landscaping plan, a waste management plan, a heritage assessment and a strategy to protect the site during the work.
The land must have at least 3 trees and reach a climate resilience factor of 0.2.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is adopting the second draft resolution for specific project PP27-0360, concerning the église Saint-Clément and its presbytery, at 4901-4903, rue Adam.
The decision allows the land (lot 1 879 420) to be subdivided, including splitting an existing building in two, with fire-stop measures and a masonry wall that meet code requirements.
It authorizes the conversion and occupancy of the church and the presbytery, as well as the landscaping of the outdoor spaces, with exemptions from several planning and subdivision rules.

The architectural volume must be preserved: full or partial demolition, removal of projections and destruction of characteristic architectural features are prohibited, except for the parts shown on the plan (sacristy, presbytery garage).
The height and the lot coverage ratio remain those of the buildings existing before January 1, 2026; the minimum front setback is 2 metres, with no side or rear setback required.
New uses become possible: businesses (Promenade Sainte-Catherine, public markets) and community and institutional facilities, some of which must occupy at least 1,000 m² of floor area.

Every conversion permit application must include a landscaping plan, a waste management plan, a heritage assessment and other studies; the occupancy certificate depends on these documents being filed.
Verdun authorizes the head of the Division des études techniques to sign the financial assistance agreement with the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for 2026.
The ministry granted this assistance on December 10, 2025 for work to build speed bumps and curb extensions.
The financial assistance is up to a maximum of $380,000, or 80% of eligible expenses.
The borough pays the remaining 20% and all additional project expenses.
The council confirms that it will follow the program's terms, failing which the financial assistance would be terminated.
The borough of Verdun is hiring Pavage Desjardins inc. to build about 40 speed bumps on various streets in its territory.
The total cost comes to $254,143.09, taxes included: $211,785.90 for the contract and $42,357.18 in contingencies.
The work is to start on June 8, 2026 and be completed on July 7, 2026.
The speed bumps are aimed at sensitive areas, in particular streets near schools and parks, to bring speeds down to about 30 km/h.
Signs and pavement markings will be installed for each speed bump, according to ministère des Transports standards.
A grant from the Fonds de la sécurité routière du Québec could cover up to $185,653.21 (80%); the rest, $46,413.30, will be financed by a borough loan.
Pavage Desjardins was the lowest of the 12 compliant bidders, at 17.18% below the City's estimate.
The borough of Verdun is extending by 12 months the road marking contract awarded to Marquage Signalisation Rive-Sud B.A. inc.
Additional spending of $383,291.43 for 2026 (work: $373,942.86; contingencies: $9,348.57), taxes included.
The contract therefore goes from $826,340.40 to $1,209,631.83, taxes included, since it was awarded in 2024.
The work covers the marking of pedestrian crossings, bike paths and bike lanes, stop lines, directional lines and lane division lines across the borough's entire road network.
Work is planned from May 25 to July 30, 2026.
This is the second and last extension option provided for in public call for tenders 23-20276; a price increase of 4% is authorized.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is ending the professional services contract awarded in June 2024 to the firm Les Architectes Labonté Marcil s.e.n.c.

This contract, worth $794,707.20 (authorized spending of $993,384.00), covered the design of a covered outdoor refrigerated skating rink at parc Saint-Jean-Baptiste, at 1050, boulevard Saint-Jean-Baptiste.
Reason: the bids received for the construction work were well above the budget estimate, and the call for tenders was cancelled in September 2025 with no new call planned.
The project called for a rink with boards and a wood and steel roof, a technical building, a parking lot, a refrigeration system, lighting and change rooms.
The borough will pay for the services already provided, for a total of $600,895.44, and will release the unused funds of $392,488.56.
The termination takes effect following the borough council's decision.
The borough of LaSalle is extending its contract with SNÖ Innovation inc. by one year for snowmaking on sliding hills and a snowboard park, at a cost of $65,636.20, taxes included.
Three hills are covered: parc de la Mairie, parc des Rapides and parc Lacharité, with a maximum of two maintenance operations per hill during the season.
The snowboard park, at parc de la Mairie, includes the supply of modules, shaping and up to two re-shapings per season.
The contract covers the 2025-2026 winter season: snowmaking at the 3 sites in December 2025, grooming and installation of the modules and fences in January 2026.
The contract provides for a 2% indexation for this option year; only the fuel actually used will be billed.
A new public call for tenders is planned for 2026 for the following three years.
The sites will be promoted on the borough's website, on social media and through on-site signage.
The borough of LaSalle is renting a room at the Centre récréatif Cavelier-De LaSalle (8700, rue Hardy) to the YMCA du Québec for $2,600, taxes included, from September 8, 2026 to June 11, 2027.
The room will be used for the Rebond program (formerly Alternative Suspension), which takes in high school students who have been suspended from school.
The program is for young people from the French-language schools LaSalle, Caroline Dawson and Cavelier-De LaSalle, and reaches 30 to 50 young people a year.
The monthly rent goes from $255 to $260, an increase of 2% compared with the 2025-2026 agreement.
The borough is making an exception to its fee by-law in order to grant this rate of $260 per month.
The YMCA uses multipurpose room 1 during the day on weekdays; recognized organizations use it in the evening and on weekends, and a day camp uses it in the summer.
According to the file, the YMCA found no other location in LaSalle; without this room, the young people would have to travel to Verdun or to the Sud-Ouest.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is applying for financial assistance from Québec (the PAFIRSPA program, stream 1) to create a "pôle socio-sportif" (socio-sports hub) at parc de la Confédération, in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The project includes renovating, bringing up to code and redeveloping the aréna Doug-Harvey, built in 1970, including universal accessibility and bringing the rink slab up to code.
It also includes adding a roof and lighting to the Bleu Blanc Bouge refrigerated outdoor rink, to extend the ice season by more than 500 hours (two months) and allow activities 12 months a year.
The borough commits to paying its share of the project's eligible costs.
The program funds two thirds of eligible costs, up to $20M for stream 1, with work to be carried out between 2027 and 2031; the program's total budget is $300M for Québec.
Fimba Tankoano is designated to sign all documents related to the project on behalf of the borough.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is cancelling the $500,000 contribution granted in July 2024 to the organization Bienvenue à Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and terminating the related agreement.
This amount was to cover the organization's rent for 5 years in new premises at 3830, boulevard Décarie.
The project fell through because the offer to purchase the building was refused.
The $500,000, taken from the borough's surpluses, will be reassigned to social development activities in the area.
The money will be used to fund non-profit organizations under a new local social development program.
The borough says it wants to group together several funding streams around issues such as housing, food and the fight against poverty and social exclusion.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is paying $8,400 to the Regroupement des Éco-quartiers for the Patrouille verte in summer 2026.
The money is used to hire 4 green patrollers for 9 weeks, at 32 hours a week, within the Montréal-Nord area.
The money tops up the awareness officers' pay to $18, $18.25 or $18.50 an hour and pays for part of the coordination.
The patrollers will talk to residents about sorting waste (brown bin, recycling, bulky items), saving drinking water and green alleyways.
The contribution will only be paid if the Regroupement obtains the Emplois d'été Canada 2026 grants.
The amount rises from $8,000 in 2024 to $8,400 in 2025 and 2026; the expense comes from the operating budget of the Direction des travaux publics.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is asking Québec for $75,000, the maximum allowed, to pay for a feasibility study.
The study would look at creating a wetland in the friche Charleroi, at the east end of rue Charleroi near the railway tracks.
The project would aim to connect this wetland to the railway's drainage ditch and to parc Ruisseau-de-Monty.
The study would include mapping local drainage, characterizing the ditch's plant and animal life, topographic surveys, a preliminary design and a cost estimate for the work.
The council is authorizing the director of urban planning and business services, Jérôme Vaillancourt, to sign the application documents on behalf of the borough.
The council had already decided to clean up the soil on this vacant lot in order to turn it into a park.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is paying $51,060.72 (taxes included) to the organization Ville en vert to cover the rent and costs of the Éco-quartier premises at 10861, boulevard Pie-IX.
The contribution covers the period from May 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027: $33,105.96 for May to December 2026 and $17,954.76 for January to March 2027.
The money comes from the operating budget of the borough's Direction des travaux publics.
The premises serve as a service point in the west end of the borough, across from the SRB Pie-IX, for environmental awareness activities with residents.
Ville en vert has been the agent for the Éco-quartier program in Montréal-Nord since January 1, 2024.
An accounting is provided at the end of the fiscal year, and an adjustment is planned if not all of the budgeted amounts have been spent.
Last year, the contribution for the same premises was $57,631.90 (May 1, 2025 to April 30, 2026).
The borough of Montréal-Nord is paying $51,290.08 (taxes included) to the organization Ville en vert to cover the rent and costs of the Éco-quartier space located at 12277, boulevard Rolland.
The contribution covers the period from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027: $29,389.16 for June to December 2026, then $21,900.92 for January to May 2027.
The borough is paying the full rental cost of the space, out of the operating budget of the Direction des travaux publics.
The space serves as the Éco-quartier's service point in the Nord-Est sector, near schools, the library, the arena and the Maison culturelle et communautaire.
Ville en vert has been the agent for the Éco-quartier Montréal-Nord program since January 1, 2024; the program does environmental awareness work with residents.
An accounting is provided at the end of the fiscal year, with an adjustment if the planned amounts have not all been spent.
The council is also approving the agreement to be entered into with the organization, which includes a visibility protocol.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving $30,000 to the Table de quartier de Montréal-Nord to run two public markets in the summer of 2026.
The markets will be held every week for 14 weeks, from June 24 to September 24, 2026, for a total of 28 markets.
The two chosen sites: the forecourt of the Maison culturelle et communautaire and parc Gouin.
The sales model will test several pricing approaches (pay it forward, solidarity pricing, fair price) and will accept Interac, Visa and the carte de proximité.
Community organizations will take part in the programming, with awareness activities on nutrition and food.
The Table de quartier is taking over the role of the organization that had run the markets for the past three years and has withdrawn.
The expense will be paid out of the operating budget of the Direction de l'aménagement urbain et des services aux entreprises; a review is planned for October.
The City is granting $15,000 to the Jeune Conseil de Montréal for its activities introducing young people to municipal political life, covering 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The executive committee is also approving the agreement between the City and the organization, which sets the conditions for payment.

The organization brings together an average of 60 young people aged 18 to 30 each year: they simulate the city council and debate four draft by-laws, which are then submitted to the real city council.
In 2025, the City had paid $5,000 for one year; an agreement from 2022 to 2024 provided for $5,000 per year, for a total of $15,000.
The 2026 edition took place on January 23, 24 and 25, 2026 at city hall; the report and the by-laws that were voted on will be submitted to the city council in the spring of 2026.
The expense is being paid entirely by the central city, out of the budget of the Service du greffe.
The Jeune Conseil de Montréal is an independent non-profit organization, separate from the Conseil jeunesse de Montréal.
City council adopts a new Code of Ethics and Conduct for elected officials of the Ville and the boroughs, replacing by-law 22-016.
The content stays the same: the Commission de la présidence du conseil recommends renewing the code as is, with no changes.
The Ville is acting to meet a legal requirement: to adopt a revised code before May 1 following the general election of November 2, 2025.
The code applies to all members of city council and the borough councils, including the mayor and the executive committee.
It covers such matters as conflicts of interest, benefits received, harassment and the use of non-public information by elected officials.
Elected officials must file a written declaration of their interests within 60 days of their election, then every year, and report any change within 60 days.
Planned timeline: notice of motion on March 23, 2026, adoption on April 20, 2026, coming into force announced for late April 2026.
The City is approving a funding agreement with the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal (CMM) to restore a bank of the rivière des Prairies, in Montréal-Nord.
The work targets the bank downstream from the pont Pie-IX, on the right bank, where the river meets parc Aimé-Léonard, north of boulevard Gouin Est.

Planned work includes: removing about 130 concrete blocks and pieces of asphalt, pulling out Japanese knotweed and buckthorn, felling and pruning trees, stabilizing the slope, planting, wildlife features, paths and concrete bases for benches.

The City is covering all costs and any cost overruns; the CMM's financial assistance is paid out in four stages (plans and specifications, 50% of the work, completion of the work, release of holdbacks).
The City is committing to keeping the site open to the public free of charge (or at a single rate for residents of the CMM's territory) for at least 40 years after the work is finished.

The work site is on government land; the ministère de l'Environnement gave its consent on August 4, 2025, on the condition that the City begin the process of bringing the stabilization structure into compliance.
City council had authorized the filing of the application for financial assistance on December 15, 2025; it is now authorizing the assistant city clerk to sign the agreement.
The Montréal-Nord borough council is granting the acting mayor pay of $5,000 per year.

This amount is being added because borough mayor Christine Black was appointed, in November 2025, vice-chair of the executive committee and responsible for families, seniors, youth, sports and recreation; the acting mayor therefore takes on increased responsibilities.
The pay applies retroactively to January 1, 2026 and will be indexed each year according to Québec's consumer price index.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
A notice of motion for the by-law was given on March 9, 2026 and it is adopted on April 13, 2026; its adoption requires two-thirds of the council's votes, including that of the mayor.
The Montréal-Nord borough council is paying for elected officials to attend two events, for a total expense of $2,760 (the file title also mentions $3,194.38).
Two tickets at $130 each for Chantal Rossi and Philippe Thermidor to the 40e Grand Prix du Conseil des arts de Montréal, on April 2, 2026.

A $2,500 sponsorship to the Chambre de commerce de l'Est de Montréal, which includes two tickets to the announcement of the ESTim finalists on March 17, 2026 and four tickets to the Gala ESTim on May 7, 2026.
Elected officials attending the ESTim events: Chantal Rossi, Youssef Hariri, Philippe Thermidor and Jean-Marc Poirier.
The sponsorship also includes an official mention of the borough's partnership during the gala.
The Loi sur le traitement des élus requires the council to authorize these expenses before they are incurred.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is settling out of court a dispute with TELUS over unpaid rent for the occupation of a parcel of land in parc Pilon.
TELUS will pay $9,799.25 to the City, an amount that includes the principal, interest, taxes and fees. The borough does not have to pay anything.
The City had initially claimed $72,444.14 in rent arrears in its demand letters of July and September 2025.
The settlement is made without any admission of liability, and both parties waive any other claim related to the lease.
The telecommunications equipment was dismantled in September 2025; the lease, signed in 1989 with Bell and then transferred to TELUS in 2018, had ended on June 15, 2025.
The borough director is authorized to sign the agreement on behalf of the City.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is receiving $81,000 from the ministère de la Sécurité publique for 2026.
The money comes from the Programme de soutien à la création et à la consolidation d'espaces jeunesse montréalais 2022-2026.
The amount partly funds an intervention assistant position for a network of community and institutional partners that carries out prevention work with vulnerable young people.

This position is to roll out programming on social cohabitation with neighbourhood organizations and to act as the link between the community and institutional sides on youth delinquency and homelessness.
The City's operating budget is being amended: $81,000 more in revenue and $81,000 more in spending in 2026 for the borough.
The project has been under way since a first agreement signed on January 11, 2024; a new agreement was signed on February 25, 2026 for the 2026 activities.
The Ville-Marie borough is presenting to its council the 2025 report on the amounts paid to non-profit organizations through its financial support programs.
Sports and recreation: three programs (core mission, day camps, access to recreation) plus an Urban Agriculture Fund, which supported 5 organizations for 5 projects in 2025.
Social Development Support Fund: $236,777.33 for 12 projects (homelessness, food security, inclusion, sharing of public space, etc.).
Montréal initiative for support of local social development: $94,839 for 3 projects.
City-MESS agreement 2025-2029 (fight against poverty): $396,295 for 10 projects lasting 2 to 4 years, between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2029.
Prévention Montréal program (2023-2025): actions aimed at the safety and development of children and young people under 30 and their families.
The council takes note of the report; the exercise is repeated every year and may lead to adjustments to the programs.
Ville-Marie is changing the way it charges for sidewalk cafés on public property: a base amount of $150 per season, plus a rate per square metre occupied.
The rate per square metre is $12 in the business district (sector A) and $6 in the rest of the borough (sector B).
The occupancy fees for a sidewalk café will be payable in a single payment covering the whole season, instead of the current payment method.
The rate that applies to tourist residences is removed from the by-law, because it is already covered by a City of Montréal by-law.
A new rate of $3.10 is created for providing a digitized plan, since no rate existed for this type of document.
Notice of motion given on April 14, 2026, with adoption planned for the borough council meeting of May 5, 2026; the borough is announcing communications about the new café rates.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is awarding 7574479 Canada inc. a contract to water its trees for $159,162.19, taxes included.
The company will water about 2,800 trees throughout the borough, with a maximum of sixteen rounds depending on the weather.
The contract runs from April 13 to December 12, 2026, with watering done from mid-April to the end of November.
Seven bids were received, all of them compliant; 7574479 Canada inc. submitted the lowest, while the highest reached $354,468.84.
The selected price is $201,399.41 (-55.86%) below the City's estimate, which was $360,561.60.
The expense will be paid by the central city's Programme de la gestion de la forêt urbaine.
According to the borough, new trees need regular watering for three years, and in-house teams do not have enough employees or tanker trucks.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is setting aside $200,000 (payroll costs included) to hire additional blue-collar crews assigned to tree planting in 2026.
The money comes from the borough's deferred "parks and playgrounds" revenue.
About 1,000 trees are to be planted in 2026 across the borough's entire territory.
The planting will take place on public property: sidewalk tree pits, parks and green spaces.
The new trees will replace trees cut down because of the emerald ash borer or natural dieback, and will add trees at suitable sites.
The work is planned from May to November 2026.
According to the document, a lack of resources would make it harder to meet the timelines and planting targets.
The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough is releasing $50,000 from its management surplus to pay for environmental studies at parc du Père-Marquette.
The park, located between rue Chambord and rue Marquette and between Drucourt and des Carrières, sits on top of two former quarries (nos. 29 and 30).
The studies are meant to establish the environmental history of the area and assess the risks with a view to a possible development project.
Any future development on this site will require authorization from the ministry, because it is a former waste disposal site.
The money comes from the surplus because the operating budget of the Direction du développement du territoire is not enough to pay for the study.
The borough of Anjou is authorizing Astral Media Affichage to occupy public land on rue Edison, near autoroute 40, to install a digital billboard there.
The billboard will be double-sided, about 14 feet high by 48 feet wide, mounted on a pole for a total height of 38 ft 6 in to 50 feet.
The company will pay $200,000 plus taxes as soon as it is installed, then $25,000 plus taxes per month, subject to indexing, starting when it goes into operation.
The occupancy is exclusive for 15 years and renews automatically under the same conditions, unless the City revokes it or the company gives it up.
The City will be able to display public interest messages on the billboard; this is a condition of the authorization.
Astral obtained the contract by exercising its right of first refusal after an offer from Branded Cities Company Canada dated November 20, 2025.
Planned timeline: adoption and coming into force in August 2026, certificate application within 2 months, and going into operation within the following 6 months.
The City is paying $309,848 to the Centre de valorisation du bois urbain (CVBU), a non-profit organization, to process wood cut down by the City from March 30, 2026 to December 31, 2027.
The CVBU will repurpose up to 3,500 tonnes of wood, at $80.48 per tonne, coming in particular from ash trees cut down because of the emerald ash borer.

In return, the City and the cities in the urban agglomeration will receive products (boards, stakes, tree supports, wood chips) and services: up to 80% of the value for merchantable wood, and up to 20% for non-merchantable wood.
The CVBU will also give a maximum of four half-day training sessions on shaping and stacking wood that has been cut down.
The money will be paid out in nine instalments, tied to the tonnages collected and to the submission of repurposing reports approved by the City.
Unlike the previous agreement, the City no longer provides quality wood free of charge to the organization, since the quality of the ash trees has deteriorated.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, through the loan by-law of the Plan d'action agrile du frêne.
The borough of Outremont is renewing its 2026 membership in the Association internationale des villes amies de la marionnette (AVIAMA), of which it has been a founding member since 2011.
The annual membership fee is 1,175 euros, or about CAD $1,906.20 at the current exchange rate, before taxes.
The Service des finances will pay the amount by bank transfer; the expense comes out of the operating budget and is fully covered by the borough.
The fee, calculated based on the number of residents and gross national income per capita, is lower than in 2025 (1,324 euros, about CAD $2,075.50).
Paying the fee allows Outremont to remain a member and to vote at the association's general assembly.
The borough cites its role as host of the Festival de Casteliers, held each March at the Théâtre Outremont, and the Maison internationale des arts de la marionnette.
The borough of Outremont is extending the plumbing services contract with Alescio Plomberie inc. by 12 months, from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
This extension costs $61,731.95, taxes included, and raises the total value of the contract from $120,454.87 to $182,186.82.
The contract covers plumbing maintenance and repairs in the borough's buildings.
It also includes the spring start-up and fall winterization of the drinking fountains, water play areas and decorative fountains in the parks.
The contractor provides the labour, equipment, tools and hardware.
The expense is paid entirely by the borough, out of its operating budget.
The borough of Outremont is approving an additional expense of $100,000, taxes included, to buy de-icing salt and abrasives until the end of the 2025-2026 winter season.
The salt and abrasives are used for spreading on the borough's roadways, lanes, bike paths and parking lots.
The document explains that heavier-than-normal snowfalls caused the planned quantities to be exceeded.
The purchases go through the City's agreements: salt from Windsor Salt Ltée and sidewalk stone from Béton Provincial Ltée; the suppliers could change in 2026.
The agreement provides for 1,500 tonnes of salt for Outremont, at $98.85 per tonne before taxes.
The funding comes from the borough: $62,742.40 from a 2025 salt provision and $37,257.61 from the contingency reserve of the management surplus.

The chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges ramp (southbound), between chemin Queen-Mary and rue du Frère-André, becomes a pedestrian street and public square from April 1 to October 31, 2026 (the "Placette CDN").
Car traffic is closed there for that entire period and resumes on November 1, 2026, after the takedown on November 1 and 2.

Sidewalk cafés and beautification features may be set up on the roadway, on parking spaces and on part of the sidewalk in front of the businesses; restaurant owners will have to hold a borough terrace permit.
The street and the small square are made available to the Société de développement commercial Côte-des-Neiges and its members for the same period.
Selling promotional items, food and drinks (alcoholic or not) is allowed from April 1 to October 31, 2026, under the conditions of the ordinance.

Noise from outdoor sound equipment is allowed on May 2 and 3, June 24, July 1 and 14, 2026 from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m., and for the SDC's activities from Monday to Thursday from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. and on Friday from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m.; maximum 80 dBA at 20 metres, megaphones prohibited except for safety.

The installations are located in the site patrimonial du Mont-Royal and partly on a residential street; they were authorized by the ministère de la Culture and must meet universal accessibility standards.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving $3,500 to the Société de développement commercial Côte-des-Neiges for its flower planter project, 2026 edition.
The planters will be installed in front of businesses in the SDC's area, in order to beautify commercial streets and reduce heat islands.
Delivery and installation are planned for the end of May 2026; the planters will be removed and stored at the end of October 2026.
The project costs $6,500 in total; the borough is paying $3,500 of it out of its 2026 operating budget for economic development.
The annual ceiling on grants to this SDC for 2026 is going from $71,400 to $74,900 in order to allow this payment.
Last year, the same activity received $3,200 from the borough.
The borough will be identified as a partner in the project's communications.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is closing two street sections to cars from June 1 to October 31, 2026, to turn them into pedestrian streets and public squares.
The sections involved: avenue Royal between rue Sherbrooke and chemin de la Côte-Saint-Antoine, and avenue Madison between rue Sherbrooke and avenue Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
Lounge furniture, potted plants, ground markings and garbage cans will be installed there, with regular maintenance and an increased SPVM presence.
Four public squares are planned for 2026 in all: the two closed streets, a curbside site at the corner of Victoria and Van Horne, and the placette CDN.
The installations will be removed and stored for the winter.
Residents living along these streets will receive a notice by mail, and the information will be shared in the borough's newsletter in early May; the rollout begins June 1, 2026.
The project is based on a study by the Centre d'écologie urbaine de Montréal (fall 2022) and on citizen comments gathered in the summer of 2023 through surveys and via 311.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is authorizing the sale of fruit, vegetables and food in five public places during the summer and fall of 2026.

Le Dépôt Centre communautaire d'alimentation will hold its "Marché bonne bouffe NDG" from July 2 to October 30: parc Georges-Saint-Pierre on Thursdays from 1 p.m. to 8 p.m., parc Herbert-Outerbridge on Fridays from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.

La Cafétéria Communautaire MultiCaf will hold its "Marchés sociaux nomades" from June 12 to September 26: Place Darlington on Saturdays from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., parc Nelson-Mandela on Fridays from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., parc de la Savane on Fridays from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m.
Both organizations want to offer healthy products, mostly locally grown, at affordable prices, in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and Côte-des-Neiges.
The borough notes that access to fresh fruit and vegetables remains limited for low-income residents and that travelling to the large markets costs more.
The file involves no spending; each organization handles its own communications.
These markets have returned every year since 2015.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is allowing sidewalk sales (braderies), entertainment, outdoor music and temporary signs during commercial promotions by two merchants' associations.
For Biz NDG: June 12, 13 and 14, 2026 (World Cup) and December 11, 12 and 13, 2026 (holiday event with Père Noël and the Fée des Étoiles).
For the SDC Côte-des-Neiges: July 2 to 5, 2026 and August 27 to 30, 2026.
Streets covered for Biz NDG: Monkland (Girouard to Grand Boulevard), Sherbrooke (Claremont to Cavendish) and Somerled (Grand Boulevard to Walkley).
Streets covered for the SDC Côte-des-Neiges: chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges (du Frère-André to Côte-Sainte-Catherine), avenues Lacombe, Gatineau and Swail.
The activities run from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.; merchants may sell merchandise, food and alcoholic beverages outdoors, while leaving 1.8 m of passage for pedestrians.
Music is limited to 80 dBA measured 20 metres from the speakers, and megaphones are banned, except for safety purposes.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is authorizing a pedestrian-only zone and a commercial promotion on avenue de Monkland from August 20 to 23, 2026.
Avenue de Monkland will be closed to traffic between avenue Girouard and avenue Melrose, from Wednesday, August 19 at 10 p.m. to Monday, August 24 at 7 a.m.
Schedule of activities: 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. from Thursday to Saturday, and 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Sunday.
Between Girouard and Grand Boulevard, the sale of promotional items, food and alcohol is allowed, as is drinking alcohol from plastic or cardboard containers.
Street food trucks that are members of the ARRQ will be allowed to sell food and drinks, with the agreement of Biz NDG, from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. (Thursday to Saturday) and 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Sunday.

Noise from outdoor sound equipment is allowed up to 80 dBA measured at 20 metres, and megaphones are banned except for safety purposes; signage is allowed from August 10 to 24, including in parc Paul-Doyon.
No financial details are given in the file; the event is organized with Biz NDG and the association des Gens d'affaires de l'avenue Monkland.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding a $181,170.59 contract (taxes included) to the non-profit organization Rendez-vous NDG.
The contract runs from April 1 to December 31, 2026, at the pavilion in parc Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
First part: food service, café-terrace and entertainment programming.
Second part: welcoming visitors, supervision and management of the pavilion's rooms, a mandate taken over from Loisirs Sportifs Côte-des-Neiges/Notre-Dame-de-Grâce since June 2025.
The document reports more than 20,000 visitors in 2024 and more than 50,000 in 2025 for this project.
The expense is funded by the borough's 2026 operating budget.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is approving an agreement with the non-profit organization Rendez-vous NDG, from April 1 to December 31, 2026.
The agreement allows the organization to seek, receive and manage sponsorships for the food offering, the café-terrasse and the activities at the pavilion in parc Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

The organization will have to report to the City on the amounts received, the sponsors approached and how the money is used; the City keeps a right of oversight and can end an agreement that does not comply.
The City is not committing any money in this file; it states that its support for the project is gradually decreasing in order to push the organization toward financial self-sufficiency.
According to the document, the project drew more than 20,000 visitors in 2024 and 50,000 in 2025.
Next steps: seeking sponsorships in spring 2026, then using the revenue in summer and fall 2026.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is authorizing the closing of avenue Lacombe to cars, between chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges and avenue Gatineau, from September 10 to 13, 2026.
The street will be closed to traffic starting Wednesday, September 9 at 6 p.m., until it reopens on Monday, September 14 between 4 a.m. and 7 a.m.
Activities are allowed from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. from Thursday to Saturday, and from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Sunday.

Merchants, restaurant owners and service providers will be able to sell and serve outside, including alcohol if they hold the required permits; alcoholic drinks must be drunk from plastic or cardboard containers, on the site only.
Street food trucks that are members of the ARRQ will be able to sell food and non-alcoholic drinks, with the agreement of the SDC Côte-des-Neiges and in recyclable or compostable containers.
Putting up signs and banners is exceptionally allowed on this stretch of street from September 9 to 13, 2026.
The SDC Côte-des-Neiges is organizing the event and paying for communications; a coordination meeting with the SPVM, the SIM and the borough's departments is planned for June 2026.

The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is giving up to $67,500 to the Société de développement commercial (SDC) Côte-des-Neiges to make avenue Lacombe pedestrian-only, from May 2026 to December 2028.
The amount goes down each year: $25,000 in 2026, $22,500 in 2027, $20,000 in 2028, to push the SDC to find other sources of funding.
Avenue Lacombe will be closed to cars between chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges and avenue Gatineau from September 10 to 13, 2026, with programming and street furniture.
The borough is also providing services: lending concrete blocks and furniture, closing the street, daily cleaning and support with planning.
The council is adopting an ordinance to go over the subsidy ceiling set out in the by-law on subsidies to SDCs.
The borough is turning down the SDC's request for winter pedestrian-only events, since the ville centre stopped funding this type of project in 2025 because of insufficient business benefits.
The total budget for the event is $70,000 per year; the borough's share comes out of the operating budget for economic development.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is lending a 13.40 m² space (unit P132) on the ground floor of the aréna Mont-Royal, at 4365, rue Cartier, free of charge to the organization Patinage Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The loan lasts 18 months starting January 1, 2026, and can be automatically renewed for one year.
The space will be used as administrative offices to develop sports activities; the organization offers figure skating to young people.
The borough pays all operating and energy costs, as well as cleaning.
The document values the equivalent support at $3,618 per month, plus taxes, based on an average rental value of $270/m² in the area.
Without this agreement, the document says the organization would have to find another place to coordinate its activities.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is lending, free of charge, a 11.15 m² room on the ground floor of the aréna Mont-Royal, at 4365, rue Cartier, to the organization "Patinage Plateau-Mont-Royal".
The loan runs for 6 months starting January 1, 2026, with the possibility of automatic renewal for one year.
The room will be used to run a café-concession called Glace-Croûte, staffed by the organization's families and volunteers, at least 4 days a week depending on the season.
The free rent amounts to a subsidy of $18,063 plus taxes for the 6 months ($3,010.50 per month, calculated at $270/m²).
The borough pays all operating costs, energy and cleaning.
The café-concession was built in 2024 following requests from residents for food service at the arena.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is allowing paving work in the evening, at night and on weekends in 2026, despite the noise by-law that normally prohibits it between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m.

Three areas are covered: boulevard Rosemont between Christophe-Colomb and Saint-Denis, rue Beaubien Est between Saint-Denis and Christophe-Colomb, and rue Saint-Zotique Est between rue des Écores and 3e Avenue.
The work requires full road closures; the borough cites car traffic volumes, user safety and the STM bus routes at the Rosemont and Beaubien stations as reasons for doing it at night.
The contractor commits to limiting construction noise (white-noise backup alarms, avoiding banging truck boxes, instructions to crews) in these residential areas.
The work on Beaubien Est could be done during the 2026 school holidays to reduce conflicts with commercial terraces.
Operations are planned between May and December 2026; the authorization applies to the year 2026 only.
No financial impact for the borough; the contractor must plan for communications with the support of a City project manager.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is carrying over $50,000 that was not spent in 2025 into its 2026 operating budget, by way of its management surplus.
This money comes from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale and must be used only for the haltes-chaleur (warming station) project.
The funds will pay for cohabitation and social mediation work around the temporary warming station that has been open at the Hôtel-Dieu de Montréal since December 9, 2025.
The station can take in up to 50 people in the evening and overnight, who can warm up, rest and have a snack.
The document states that attention will be paid to the safety of vulnerable people and to the quiet of the neighbourhood, which is already affected by cohabitation issues in public spaces.
Without this transfer, the leftover 2025 amounts would be lost.
Planned timeline: budget update in March 2026, roll-out of the interventions in 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the construction of a 2nd building on the lot at 3505-3511, boulevard Saint-Laurent: 3 storeys and 5 units, facing rue Saint-Dominique.
The new building would replace a car parking area; a sheltered bicycle parking area will be set up on the ground floor.
The planned units: one two-bedroom, three one-bedroom and one studio set up as an adaptable unit with a step-free entrance.
Two trees will be planted at the back and landscaping is planned at the front.

Conditions imposed: a maximum of 2 main buildings on the lot, at least one adaptable unit, a waterproofing membrane on the foundations, controlled-flow drains on the roofs and 300 mm low walls if window wells are built.
The project does not comply with the planning rules that prohibit more than one main building per lot and that limit the height in storeys based on neighbouring buildings.

The authorization becomes void if it is not used within 60 months; the project remains subject to approval by referendum. One member of the public attended the February 10, 2026 consultation, with no questions.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the removal of 2 dwelling units in the basement of 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest, a currently vacant building with 45 dwelling units.
The freed-up space will be used to set up a waste storage room of at least 28 m² (16 bins) and a parking area with 32 bicycle spaces.
The owner will also have to move all ventilation outlets to the roof or to an exterior wall that is not adjacent to a public road.
The authorization departs from an urban planning rule that prohibits reducing the number of dwelling units in an existing building.
If the owner does not act on it within 60 months, the authorization becomes void; if the conditions are not met, the penalty provisions apply.

The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on December 9, 2025, and a public consultation was held on February 10, 2026, with no questions from the public and no changes to the project.
This is the adoption of the second draft resolution; the project contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is tabling its 2025 annual report on the use of the override power set out in the provincial housing act (PL31).
In 2025, only one project was authorized under this power and no application was refused.
That project is the redevelopment of 3700, rue Berri and 3725, rue Saint-Denis, authorized in phases on October 1, 2025, for about 900 housing units.
The authorization departed from the borough by-laws on subdivision, building demolition and urban planning.
The report had to be tabled no later than April 1, 2026; it will be sent to the minister responsible for housing and published on the City's website.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the demolition of the gas station at 5791, boulevard Saint-Laurent, at the corner of rue Bernard Est.
In its place, a mixed-use building of 5 storeys with 62 housing units and 3 commercial spaces of about 80 m² each on the ground floor, facing boulevard Saint-Laurent.
The housing units break down into 13 studios, 27 one-bedrooms, 15 two-bedrooms and 7 three-bedrooms; 11 must be adaptable.
The project exceeds the current zoning, which limits buildings to 3 storeys and 12.5 m and requires a ground floor that is entirely commercial.
Conditions imposed: at least 60 housing units, 40 m² of waste storage in the basement, terraces of no more than 1.2 m, a waterproof membrane and flow-controlled drains.
Parking for 52 bicycles in the basement, 10 sheltered outdoor spaces and 3 trees planted at the rear.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme said it was in favour on February 24, 2026; a public consultation was held on April 28, 2026 with 5 citizens, with no changes to the project. The authorization becomes void if it is not used within 60 months.
The City is preparing a by-law to allow a "return site" for deposit containers to open at 933, rue Rachel Est, in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, where this use is not normally permitted.
The space would take up about 300 m² on the ground floor, would be open from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. with employees on site, with no limit on the number of containers brought back.
All storage would be indoors; collection would be done by 16-foot vans, 3 to 4 times a week, for about 20 minutes, from the delivery area on rue de Mentana.
The building opening onto rue de Mentana would be enlarged to make collection easier.
The request is part of Québec's expanded deposit system: about 100 return sites are to be set up in Montréal, within a network of at least 1,200 across Québec.
Expected timeline: tabling and notice of motion at city council on May 11, 2026, adoption on June 15, 2026, coming into force in June 2026.
The document is a notice of motion and the tabling of a draft by-law; no spending is associated with it.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the demolition of the building at 3510, avenue Coloniale, which was damaged by fire in July 2025, and its reconstruction with the same number of housing units.
The condition reports conclude that the structure is too badly damaged to be repaired: the roof, part of the façade and half of the floors on the 2nd and 3rd storeys are charred.
The new 3-storey building will have 7 housing units, considered affordable as defined by the CMHC, so that the tenants can move back into their homes.
Conditions imposed: 11 bicycle parking spaces, a space for waste materials, at least 45% of the unbuilt portion of the land planted in full ground, and a 300 mm landscaped swale in the yard.
The project does not comply with three sections of the planning by-law, in particular the ban on having more than one building per lot (the lot has 3 buildings and 16 housing units).
The planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on March 17, 2026, and a public consultation was held on April 28, 2026, with one member of the public present; no changes were made.
The authorization becomes void if it is not acted upon within 60 months; the project remains subject to approval by referendum.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the creation of two dwellings on the ground floor of 4298, rue Saint-Denis, at the rear of the building: a two-bedroom dwelling and a studio.
The space was previously occupied by a medical clinic; the 6 dwellings on the upper floors are being kept, with no work done.
Normally, the planning by-law requires a commercial use on the ground floor in this area; the City is granting an exception through a conditional use.
Conditions imposed: the ground-floor premises facing rue Saint-Denis must remain commercial or institutional, in order to maintain commercial continuity.
Other conditions: at least 8 bicycle parking spaces, a waste materials space of at least 5 m², and access to the lane for all occupants.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on April 14, 2026; adoption by the borough council is scheduled for May 4, 2026.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is approving the addition of an exit staircase and two balconies at 5000-5004, avenue du Parc, a 3-storey building with a business on the ground floor and four apartments on the upper floors.
The new spiral staircase will serve as a second emergency exit for the two apartments facing avenue du Parc, which did not have one.

The staircase will be attached to the boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest side of the building and will permanently encroach on public property, projecting out a maximum of 1.9 m; the sidewalk there is more than 4 m wide.

The exemption sets conditions: balconies projecting no more than 1 m (1.3 m wide on the 2nd floor, 2.2 m on the 3rd), guardrails no higher than 1.2 m, a welded steel or aluminum structure, and guardrails made of perforated panels.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on May 5, 2026; adoption by the borough council is expected on July 6, 2026.
Other options (an indoor stairwell, a route to the back lane) were ruled out because they would have reduced the size of the apartments or interfered with the business.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is exempting the owner of 3818-3824, boulevard Saint-Laurent from providing the 7 bicycle parking spaces normally required.
In exchange, the owner is paying $11,935 into the bicycle parking compensation fund, which works out to $1,705 per missing space.
The borough will use this money to install bicycle racks on public property.
The exemption is tied to a project to convert the 2nd floor (former offices) into 7 studio-type tourist accommodation units, each 28 to 32 m².
The City points to the physical impossibility of creating these spaces: the building covers 100% of the lot (no yard) and the ground floor is occupied by a business.
Adoption is planned at the February 2, 2026 borough council meeting; a public notice will follow on the borough's website.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the conversion of the duplex at 4553-4555, rue de la Roche into a single-family home.
The duplex will therefore go from two units to one, which goes against the planning rules that normally prohibit reducing the number of housing units in the area.
Condition imposed on the owners: remove the hard surfacing from the front yard and plant vegetation directly in the ground there.
The 2nd-floor unit (4555) has been vacant since the last tenants left in June 2025; no tenants are affected and no neighbourhood meeting was required.
The single-family home would be about 140 m², under the maximum of 200 m² allowed for a single-unit house.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on January 13, 2026.
No universal accessibility measures are planned: the raised ground floor and the closeness of the property line make a compliant ramp impossible.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is allowing the owners of 4584-4586, rue Chambord to merge their two units, turning the duplex into a single unit.
The unit at 4586 is occupied by a tenant who will leave on June 30, 2026, following a repossession of the unit upheld by the Tribunal administratif du logement.
The renovation permit can only be issued after June 30, 2026, or after the tenant leaves, with proof.
Second condition: at least 60% of the other yard must be covered with plants grown directly in the ground.
The merged unit would be about 145 m², below the maximum of 200 m² allowed for a single-unit house.
The work includes an opening between the two units on the 2nd floor and replacing the small unit's kitchen with an office, with no work on the exterior.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on January 13, 2026; no universal accessibility measures are planned because of the building's constraints.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the conversion of the duplex at 4694-4696, rue Saint-Hubert into a single-family home.
The number of units goes from two to one, which departs from the rule that normally prohibits reducing the number of units in an existing building.
Both units are currently occupied by the owners: according to the City, no tenant is affected.
Conditions imposed: at least 45% of the other yard must be planted with vegetation in open ground, and a tree at least 3 cm in diameter must be planted.
The work includes removing the staircase, the balcony and the rear door on the 2nd floor, a smaller terrace and a three-bedroom unit of about 192 m².
No universal accessibility measures are planned, with the City citing the raised ground floor and the building's siting.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on January 13, 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the conversion of the duplex at 5015-5017, rue Resther into a single-family home.
The building will therefore go from two units to just one, of about 145 m², below the 200 m² limit set for a single unit.
The owners will have to remove the two parking spaces facing the lane and cover at least 70% of the yard's ground with plants grown directly in the soil.
The two tenants left on their own in June 2025: the owners live on the ground floor and the 2nd floor is vacant, so no tenant is affected.
No neighbourhood meeting was required, and no universal accessibility measures are planned because of the building's layout.
The urban planning advisory committee issued a favourable opinion on February 10, 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the addition of one unit in the basement of 4215, rue De Brébeuf, bringing the building from 41 to 42 units.
The new unit must have at least two bedrooms and take up about 52 m² at the back of the basement, replacing a storage area.
The owner must provide parking for at least 42 bicycles; no car parking spaces are allowed.
A storage room for residual materials of at least 15 m² is required, with at least 20 bins of 360 litres (12 recycling, 6 garbage, 2 organic matter).
Measures against water infiltration are required: a flood-proof door, a catch basin at the bottom of the ramp, a waterproofing membrane, and window wells and a low wall raised by 300 mm.
Before tenants move in, a certificate signed by an architect confirming that these measures have been carried out must be given to the borough.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on February 10, 2026; no comments were received from the occupants who were notified during a seven-day period.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing restaurant, bar and performance hall uses at 1875 and 1881, avenue du Mont-Royal Est, and is cancelling its 2020 authorization.
This will allow Terminal Comédie Club to expand into the neighbouring space, vacant since January 2026, to set up a food service area and a new kitchen at the back.
The floor areas are capped: 475 m² for the bar and the restaurant, 170 m² for the performance hall on the 2nd floor of 1875.
The establishment will not be allowed to present music shows; sound in the hall will be limited to 90 dB"c" and an acoustic curtain will have to cover the 2nd-floor windows.

Before opening, the developer will have to submit a study on noise in neighbouring dwellings and an architect's certificate on accessibility measures (automatic door opener, accessible bar counter and washroom).
The project includes a refrigerated waste room for organic materials, planting boxes on the rooftop terrace and the felling of four trees in the back yard.
A public consultation is scheduled for Tuesday, July 14 at 6 p.m., at 201, avenue Laurier Est, salle Le Plateau; the authorization becomes void if it is not used within 60 months.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is authorizing the conversion of the duplex at 4666-4668, rue Chabot into a single dwelling, taking the building from two units down to one.
The owners, who bought the building in August 2025, already occupy the entire building; no tenant is affected and no neighbourhood meeting was required.
No work is planned: a permit issued in 2019 had already allowed the construction of an interior staircase connecting the two floors. The application only brings the current occupancy into compliance.
The single dwelling would be about 160 m², below the maximum of 200 m² allowed for a single-dwelling house.
Condition imposed: at least 60% of the ground surface of another yard must be covered with plants grown directly in the ground.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a favourable opinion on June 9, 2026; the decision departs from the rules that normally prohibit reducing the number of dwellings in this area.
No universal accessibility measures are planned, since the raised ground floor and the building's siting make a compliant ramp impossible.

The City takes note of the sale of La Ronde: the shares of the emphyteuta Parc Six Flags Montréal, s.e.c. and the shares of its general partner are transferred to EPR VC Acquisition, ULC, a subsidiary of EPR Properties.
The City does not formally consent to the transaction, nor does it oppose it, because it is not a sale of the emphyteuta's real estate rights.
The guarantee provided by Six Flags inc., which secures the obligations toward the City, remains in force until an equivalent replacement guarantee is provided to the City.
Operation of the amusement park will be entrusted to a new entity owned by La Ronde Operations, inc., a Delaware company linked to the CEO of Premier Parks.
The La Ronde site, on île Sainte-Hélène, has been under emphyteutic lease since May 2, 2001 for 64 years, that is, until April 30, 2065.
The Société du parc Jean-Drapeau has begun discussions with EPR to apply elements of the Plan directeur du parc Jean-Drapeau.
According to the document, the decision has no financial impact for the City.

The urban agglomeration council is handing over to city council the design, management and delivery of the project to restore and create wetlands in the wooded area of parc Marcel-Laurin, in Saint-Laurent, for the duration of the project.
This transfer will allow city council to accept the offer from the borough of Saint-Laurent to lead the work itself, since it is taking place on its territory.
The wooded area covers 15.44 hectares and includes two stream segments, marshes and swamps; it has been listed since 2009 in the agglomeration's inventory of protected natural areas.
Québec (MELCCFP) granted $999,610.98 in 2022, then additional funding of $1,979,824.47 accepted in 2026; the project submission is postponed to 2027.
The planned work: a retention basin for storm sewer water, an improved outlet, culverts and weirs, and the creation of wetlands.
Some trails and entrances to the wooded area will be adjusted, and the signage and educational facilities will be redone.
Funding comes from the Québec grant, from the capital works program of the Service de l'eau and from that of the borough of Saint-Laurent.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $6,200 to twelve non-profit organizations in its territory, out of the council's discretionary budget, for the year 2026.

The largest amounts go to CDC Solidarité Villeray ($1,350, for the 24th Villeray neighbourhood party) and to Regroupement jeunesse en action ($800, for the Salon de l'emploi et de la formation de Saint-Michel).

Nine organizations are receiving between $200 and $500: Chœur Solis de Villeray, Maison de la famille de St-Michel, Saint-Michel Vie sans frontières, Société d'Histoire de Parc-Extension, Centre socioéducatif Lasallien, Héritage hispanique Québec, La Perle Retrouvée, Maison d'Haïti, Table de concertation jeunesse Villeray–Petite-Patrie and Centre communautaire culturel de Séverine.

The money funds one-time activities: neighbourhood parties, an end-of-year concert, a BBQ, Mois du patrimoine hispanique, Fête du drapeau haïtien, a literary gathering, Promenade de Jane, Festival Savalouwe, Opération sac à dos.
The amounts come from the mayor's fund and from the funds of the Parc-Extension, Saint-Michel, Villeray and François-Perreault districts.
The discretionary fund exists to respond to one-time requests for financial help from organizations in the various districts.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is giving a total of $9,000 to 14 non-profit organizations in its territory for the year 2026.
The money comes from the borough council's discretionary budget, created to respond to one-time requests for financial help.

The amounts range from $150 to $1,250 per organization: $1,250 to Regroupement jeunesse en action, $1,000 each to À portée de mains, Carrefour populaire Saint-Michel and Camp Assume, and $150 to Organisation des jeunes de Parc-Extension.

The money pays for specific activities: intercultural festivals, the Journée internationale des aînés, a summer BBQ, a father-child bike rally, a job fair, a golf tournament and an ecological sugar shack.
The contributions are divided between the mayor's fund and the funds of the Parc-Extension, Saint-Michel, Villeray and François-Perrault districts.
The Direction des services administratifs confirms that the funds are available in the 2026 budget.
The City is awarding a direct-award contract to Lucion Média inc. for $103,546.49, taxes included, without a public call for tenders.
The company is to design and produce multimedia elements (light, sound, projections, water features, mist) at the Jardin de Chine of the Jardin botanique.
All of this is part of the "Jardins de lumière 2026" event, scheduled from September 3 to November 1, 2026 according to the background of the file (August 28 to November 1 according to the schedule).
The Chinese lanterns from the 2025 edition will be reused, as part of an eco-responsible approach, and showcased with the new effects.
The contract was awarded after a call for proposals to two firms; Lucion Média's proposal was the least costly.
The expense is provided for in the operating budget of Espace pour la vie and will be paid entirely by the central city, in 5 payments in 2026.
Planned steps: concept in April-May 2026, plans and specifications in June, installation in August, dismantling in November.
The City is funding 13 community and collective garden projects in 2026, for a total of $1M, spread across 10 boroughs.
The work includes bringing 8 gardens up to standard and renovating them, expanding one existing garden, and creating 4 new gardens.
30% of the amount goes to repairing existing gardens, 70% to creating new gardens.
22 projects had been submitted by 12 boroughs, for requests totalling $2,014,855.46 taxes included.
The boroughs manage their own projects and cover any cost overruns: no additional money will be paid out.
The funds come from a loan by-law: 60% paid after approval, 40% on request once the first amounts have been spent.
Contracts and work begin as of April 2026; Montréal has 96 community gardens and about 8,500 gardeners, with waiting lists that can reach seven years.
The City is giving $150,000 to 11 organizations and schools to set up teaching gardens in 15 Montréal schools, from June 2026 to December 2027.

The projects are located in Montréal-Nord, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Ville-Marie, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Outremont, Le Sud-Ouest and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
The amounts range from $1,300 (École Notre-Dame-des-Victoires Annexe) to $27,500 (Outremont en Famille, for hydroponic gardens in three schools).
Along with the garden set-ups, the projects include workshops on gardening, natural cycles and healthy, local food.
According to the City, these 11 projects bring the target of 50 school teaching gardens in the Stratégie d'agriculture urbaine 2021-2026 to 100% completion.
The money comes from the surplus earmarked for the climate emergency, and the cost is paid entirely by the central city.
The borough of Ville-Marie is authorizing an outdoor parking area of 17 spaces in the front yard at 1700, avenue du Docteur-Penfield, a 9-storey building with 27 units built in 1927.
These 17 spaces have existed since 1988 but were built without a permit, and therefore without acquired rights; the authorization allows an exemption from the planning rules on outdoor parking.
The owners will rebuild the damaged retaining walls, restore the driveway to its original U shape, and add a pedestrian walkway and a guardrail on the east side.
The project includes a retention basin and two swales for rainwater, 65% of the area planted with vegetation, and the removal of 6 trees, replaced by 6 native trees.
Charging stations in the front yard will have to be hidden by trees, shrubs or tall grasses, and light-coloured paving is preferred.
Work must begin within 60 months of the adoption, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The site is within the declared and designated heritage site of Mont-Royal; the comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on April 16, 2026, with a public consultation scheduled for June 25, 2026.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding a $184,879.80 contract (taxes included) to 9083-0126 Québec inc. (Creusage RL) for hydro-excavation services.
The contract covers about three years and ends on December 31, 2028.
These services are used to dig with pressurized water during maintenance and repair work on the water and sewer systems, when underground pipes are located near the assets to be repaired.
The work is planned over the year, but can also be done in emergency situations.
The public call for tenders received 5 bids; the one from JMV Environnement inc. was found non-compliant for lack of experience.
The winning bid is $35,320.32 (16.04%) below the City's latest estimate.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget, and the company's performance will be evaluated.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is renting bulk transport trucks for $489,984.36, taxes included, over three years.
Biyadi inc. is awarded lot 1 ($354,927.83) and Les Pavages Dancar (2009) inc. lots 2, 3 and 4 ($135,056.53).
The trucks are used to haul away soil excavated during water main and sewer work, leaves in the fall, and mulch and soil for parks.
The contract runs from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2029 and is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The public call for tenders received 11 bids; some were found non-compliant because they did not have enough trucks available.
The prices accepted are below the City's latest estimate (by 14.6% to 44.8% depending on the lot).
The borough will assess the performance of both companies for the entire length of the contract.
The City is giving $500,000 to Mission Old Brewery for a building at 2801, rue de Rouen, in Ville-Marie.
The "Les Discrètes de Rouen" project is a 3-storey building with 12 rooms for women experiencing homelessness.
Delivery is planned for March 2026, with occupancy no later than July 1, 2026.

The total cost of the project is estimated at a little over $5.6M, also funded by the Société d'habitation du Québec ($3,430,000, $667,085, $550,000, and a loan of $498,363) and $48,000 from the CMHC.
The money comes from the social housing portion of the fund supported by the by-law on social, affordable and family housing; the expense is paid by the agglomeration.
The contribution is secured by a $500,000 mortgage on the building, ranking 5th after those of the SHQ, for a term of 2 years.
Rent affordability is guaranteed by the agreements with the SHQ, in effect until December 31, 2042.
The City is adding $877,312 to its funding for Mission Unitaînés for a building with 100 housing units for independent seniors with low or modest incomes, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.
This amount is on top of the $3,340,550 in funding approved in June 2024: the total of the payments goes from $2,840,550 to $4,217,862, in 5 payments instead of 3.
The cost overrun is due to underestimated soil decontamination costs, electrical grid constraints and noise-reduction measures.
An amount of $401,232 covers the GST and QST, but it will only be paid if Revenu Québec confirms that these costs are taxable.
The transfer of the building to the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal will take place after the work is fully completed, to spare the OMHM a tax bill of more than one million dollars.
The amounts will be paid based on actual invoices and could be lower; any additional overrun will be covered by Mission Unitaînés.
The expense will be reimbursed to the City by the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal.
The City is amending the agreement signed in May 2025 with UTILE Polytechnique, which received $6,200,000 to build 149 housing units (235 rooms) at 5500, rue Saint-Hubert, in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The housing is intended for low-income students.
The Fédération des Caisses Desjardins required higher guarantees than those provided for in the agreement, so the City is raising the ceiling on the higher-ranking mortgages.

Desjardins will hold a 1st-ranking mortgage of $52,375,570 and NMF Rental Housing Fund II a 2nd-ranking mortgage of $2,089,026, each increased by 20% and at an annual rate of 25%; the City remains in 3rd rank.
The City will sign a subordination agreement that limits the remedies it can exercise on the mortgage if the organization does not meet its commitments.
A clause requires the City's authorization before the guarantee can be used to finance projects other than the rue Saint-Hubert project.
The rank assignments are planned for spring 2026; the change has no financial impact for the City.

The City is amending the grant agreement signed on June 9, 2025 with the Société d'habitation du Québec (SHQ) for the modular housing project with support services for people experiencing homelessness.
The SHQ grant remains $5,206,297, with no financial contribution from the City.
Main change: the SHQ will be able to pay out the money upon presentation of invoices or supporting documents, instead of waiting for the certificate of substantial completion of the work.
Purpose of the change: to allow payment during the 2025-2026 budget year, which ends on March 31, including for the 3rd site, whose completion date has not been set.
