The requirement to maintain the units for 10 years will be calculated from the date the rooms at each of the three sites are occupied; the term of the agreement, for its part, starts from the occupancy of the last site.
The project provides for 90 temporary housing units, that is, 30 per site across three locations; two projects have already been delivered.
Signing the addendum depends on obtaining an order in council from the government authorizing the grant. Payment is expected in March 2026.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is receiving $323,093 from the ministère de la Sécurité publique for the year 2026.
The money funds the "Agent-es pivot" project, which is being rolled out in elementary and high schools in the borough.
The grant comes from the Programme de soutien à la création et à la consolidation d'espaces jeunesse montréalais, which aims to create more activities and places for young people.
The project is part of the borough's Stratégie jeunesse de prévention de la criminalité (youth crime prevention strategy).
The borough points to the increase, since 2019, in the number and seriousness of violent incidents involving young people in its territory.
The executive committee is being asked to amend the City's budget and to increase the borough's 2026 revenue/spending envelope by $323,093.
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is receiving $30,000 from Desjardins and is asking the executive committee to adjust the City's 2026 budget accordingly.
The money will be used to redesign the large multipurpose room at the bibliothèque de Saint-Michel, including the creation of a space reserved for teenagers.
The library has no space dedicated to teens, who account for nearly 50% of weekday visits.
The current furniture is worn out and unsuitable; the project provides for furniture designed for teens and a visual identity specific to the space.
Young people will take part in choosing the colours, the room's name and some of the atmosphere elements.
The amount completes the funding for the "Un pont entre nous" project, supported by the ministère de la Sécurité publique.
According to the document, without this decision the library would lose the $30,000.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is receiving $54,000 from the Programme québécois de lutte contre la criminalité of the ministère de la Sécurité publique. The City's budget is being amended to reflect this, and the borough's funding envelope is being increased by the same amount.
The money will go to the project "Actualisation de la Stratégie Jeunesse en prévention de la criminalité," which updates the strategy developed in 2022 based on a 2021 assessment.

The project is to re-evaluate the causes of youth crime and identify areas where the city can act, taking into account issues such as cyberviolence, mental health, the needs of girls and young women, discrimination and inflation.
The approach is meant to be participatory, involving young people, community organizations, schools and security services.
The project is expected to start in the summer-fall of 2026.
The LaSalle borough is giving $29,369 to four community organizations for projects in 2026, through its Fonds en développement social.

L'Association de soccer mineur de LaSalle is receiving $11,400 for a free eight-week summer camp at parc Riverside, for 60 vulnerable children aged 5 to 13, with snacks and lunches provided by IGA LaSalle.
Destination Travail du Sud-Ouest is receiving $7,000 for the Winnebago, a mobile outreach vehicle serving 200 people who are homeless or in very precarious situations in LaSalle.

Handicap Action Intégration is receiving $6,422 to help about 150 low-income people with disabilities and seniors, mainly in public housing (HLM), access financial assistance programs and file their income tax returns at home.
Corporation L'Espoir is receiving $4,547 for free singing and theatre workshops for young adults and adults who are autistic or have an intellectual disability.

All four projects fall under axis 2 of the Fonds, which aims to break the isolation of vulnerable people; the organizations must submit their final report no later than 30 days after the project ends.
The applications received totalled $34,892 during the call for projects held from September 10 to October 10, 2025.
The LaSalle borough is giving $81,700 to the Table de développement social de LaSalle for its integrated urban revitalization project in 2026.
The money targets people living in precarious situations in the LaSalle Heights neighbourhood, with particular attention to the Airlie-Bayne area.
$71,700 will pay for a project officer: mobilizing people around the Shack communautaire 2026, coordinating activities, supporting citizen initiatives, communications and reporting.
$10,000 will go to the Table's operating costs for mobilization and citizen participation activities.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city, through the budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale.
The borough mayor and the borough secretary are authorized to sign the agreement.
In 2025 and in 2024, the contribution to this organization for this project was $128,368.
The borough of LaSalle is amending its agreement with the Table de développement social de LaSalle, which had received $128,368 in 2025 for its integrated urban revitalization project.

A $20,000 component planned for a reflection exercise on inequities in living environments is being suspended, because of uncertainty about the directions tied to the Quartiers inclusifs et résilients.
That $20,000 will instead be used to pay an outreach worker who will meet with vulnerable families in the targeted area, in partnership with the Maison des familles de LaSalle.
The outreach worker will help families with their administrative processes, access to services and parental support.
No new money is being paid out: the amount granted in 2025 will be spent in 2026.
The borough mayor and the borough secretary are authorized to sign the addendum; the organization must submit its final report no later than 30 days after the end of the project.
The City is renewing its agreement for three years with Ouranos, a non-profit organization that works on climate and adaptation to climate change, starting June 16, 2026.
It will pay $517,387.50, taxes included, plus an in-kind contribution valued at $300,000, as an affiliated member.
In exchange, the City gets access to scientific knowledge, planning tools and the Ouranos network (more than 450 affiliated researchers and experts).
The Bureau de la transition écologique et de la résilience coordinates the partnership, with a steering committee made up of directors from the City and from Ouranos.

The 2023-2026 report is being tabled: research projects on the impacts of the climate on people with disabilities and people experiencing homelessness, mapping of adaptation measures and vulnerabilities, and information for residents on flooding and heavy rainfall.
This is the fourth renewal since the first agreement was signed in June 2017.
Councillor Christopher McCray declares his interest and takes part in neither the deliberations nor the vote.
The City is awarding a sole-source contract of $2,066,684.87 (taxes included) to the SPCA de Montréal for local animal services, from May 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027 (20 months).
The SPCA will take in up to 3,665 pets per year, including those referred to it by Proanima Montréal when its own centre is full, plus farm animals with no limit.
The services covered: intake, identification, adoption, housing, care, euthanasia and disposal of deceased animals, for all boroughs.
Proanima Montréal keeps: capture and transport, management of dangerous dogs, the community cat program (CSRM) and interventions related to evictions, seizures or sanitation operations.
Payment is made in monthly instalments: $1,008,138.96 in 2026 (8 instalments) and $1,058,545.91 in 2027 (12 instalments), with a 5% indexation for 2027.
The contract could be extended until December 31, 2028 if the City and the SPCA agree.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city; the decision falls to city council.

The City is ending the three-year agreement that supported the Orchestre symphonique de Montréal (OSM)'s La Virée Classique festival for 2025-2026-2027, at the request of the organization, which is cancelling the festival.
As a replacement, the City is granting $80,000 to the OSM for two new projects in 2026.

$40,000 goes to « Une semaine de relâche magique », from February 28 to March 7, 2026, at the Espace OSM, the Foyer Antonia-Nantel and the Maison symphonique, with a free component (concerts, musical awakening workshops, drawing, dance) and indoor concerts (music from Harry Potter, L'Oiseau de feu).

$40,000 goes to the Grand Concert at the Esplanade du Parc olympique on August 12, 2026, on the theme of the 50th anniversary of the Montréal Olympic Games, conducted by Rafaël Payare. The City states that 25,000 people attended in 2024 and in 2025.
The City's support covers 6.78% of the $372,868 budget for the spring break week and 10.73% of the $590,374 budget for the Grand Concert, to which the Conseil des arts de Montréal is adding $100,000.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, out of the budget of the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs. The organization must follow a visibility protocol.
The executive committee is replacing Schedule A of the by-law that sets out which City employees can make decisions, and up to what amount.
The only change affects the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation: its structure is presented in a simplified way in the schedule.
The title "Cadre sur mandat" is added to this department as a level A employee, the highest level of delegation.
The City justifies the update by the need to maintain its organizational efficiency.

The by-law applies to all municipal departments, to the Ombudsman, to the Commission de la fonction publique, to the Office de consultation publique de Montréal and to the Secrétariat de liaison de l'agglomération.
The executive committee is updating the by-law that delegates powers to City officials, replacing its Schedule A following the 2026 budget and two administrative reorganizations.

Most of the changes simply adjust the new department names and director titles (for example, "Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation", "Service des finances et de l'évaluation foncière").
Recently created departments, including the Bureau de lutte contre l'itinérance, are finally getting delegated powers.

The directors of the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs and the Service de l'Espace pour la vie, des grands parcs et du Mont-Royal will be able to accept donations of objects, private archives or living collections worth less than $100,000 for the MEM, the Biodôme, the Biosphère, the Insectarium, the Jardin botanique and the Planétarium.
Officials will be able to authorize the loan of objects and archives from these museums for exhibitions, as well as the donation of plants or outdated books from the Jardin botanique.
Agreements on the intellectual property rights of a work may be signed by a level A official (less than $100,000) or a level B official (less than $25,000).
The file has no financial impact and no communications activities are planned.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing public events on public property (parks, squares and streets) from March to December 2026, according to a schedule attached to the file.
Organizers will be allowed to play sound outdoors, up to 80 dBA measured 35 metres from the equipment; megaphones remain banned, except for safety purposes.
Selling food, promotional items and drinks, whether alcoholic or not, is allowed at the sites, as is drinking alcohol, in plastic containers and on site only.
Streets may be closed on the planned dates and times, and advertising banners may be displayed during the events.
Promoters will have to put up signs 10 days before a street closure to inform residents of the closure hours.
The events are free and open to everyone; the costs of the City's services are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
Other files may be added later to include new events in the 2026 schedule.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough council is authorizing public events on public property from April to December 2026, at the sites and times listed in the calendar attached to the file.
Organizers will be allowed to use sound equipment outdoors, up to 80 dBA measured at 35 metres; megaphones remain banned except for safety purposes.
Selling promotional items, food and drinks, alcoholic or not, is allowed at these sites, as is drinking alcohol, in plastic containers and on site only.
Streets may be closed during the events; promoters will have to put up signs 10 days in advance to indicate closing times and inform residents.
Putting up advertising signs is also allowed for these events.
Events on public property are free and open to everyone; the costs of the City's services are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
Other files may be added later to include new events in the 2026 calendar.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough council is authorizing public events to be held on public property from May to December 2026, according to a list of sites, dates and times attached to the file.
Organizers will be able to occupy parks and squares, and close streets, on the dates and at the times set out in the calendar.
Noise from outdoor sound equipment is allowed as an exception, up to 80 dBA measured at 35 m; megaphones remain prohibited except for safety purposes.
Selling food, promotional items and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks is allowed at the sites concerned, and drinking alcohol there is permitted in plastic containers.
The events are free and open to everyone; the organizations must obtain all required permits and follow the approved safety measures.
If a street is closed, the promoters must put up signs ten days in advance to inform residents of the closing hours.
The costs of the City's support are absorbed into the operating budgets of the departments concerned; other events may be added to the 2026 calendar.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is accepting a $30,000 donation from Desjardins for the bibliothèque de Saint-Michel.
The money will be used to redesign the large multi-purpose room in order to create a space reserved for teenagers.
The library currently has no space dedicated to teens, who make up nearly half of its weekday traffic.
Young people will be consulted to choose the colours, the name of the room and some of the atmosphere features.
The project adds to the funding already obtained for "Un pont entre nous", which is supported by the ministère de la Sécurité publique.
The borough is committing to meet the conditions of the agreement and is authorizing the director of public works to sign the documents.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $6,100 to twelve non-profit organizations in its territory for the year 2026.
The money comes from the borough council's discretionary budget, which was created to respond to one-time requests for financial assistance.

The largest amounts: $1,000 to Espace d'Expressions et de Création (two exhibitions), $800 to Afrique au Féminin (Fête des mères) and $800 to the Table de concertation jeunesse Villeray–Petite-Patrie (Opération sac à dos).

Other recipients: Club de patinage de vitesse de Montréal St-Michel ($600), CHAIS ($500), Agora Créative ($500), Coalition des ami.e.s du parc ($450 for the parc Jarry clean-up), BRAS Villeray, Maison de la Famille de St-Michel, Centre Communautaire Culturel de Séverine and Saint-Michel Vie Sans Frontières ($300 each), P.A.R.I. de St-Michel ($250).
The amounts are divided between the mayor's fund and the districts of François-Perrault, Parc-Extension, Saint-Michel and Villeray.
The contributions are for specific activities: family celebrations, exhibitions, a skating competition, an Easter activity, gardens and a park clean-up.
The Direction des services administratifs confirms that the funds are available in the 2026 discretionary budget.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough council is authorizing public events on public property from June to December 2026, at the locations and times listed in the calendar attached to the file.
Organizers will be allowed to play music and use sound equipment outdoors, up to 80 dBA measured at 35 m; megaphones remain prohibited, except for safety purposes.
Selling food, promotional items and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks is allowed at the sites, as is drinking alcohol, in plastic containers and on the site only.
Streets may be closed during the events; promoters will have to put up signs showing the closing times 10 days in advance.
Putting up advertising signs is allowed during the events, despite the zoning by-law.
The events are free and open to all; the costs of City services are covered by the operating budgets of the departments involved.
Other files may be added later to include new events in the 2026 calendar.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is submitting an application for $21,000 in financial assistance to the ministère de la Culture et des Communications, under a call for projects on the mental health of young people aged 12 to 18.
The project "L'Abri créatif" plans to set up a safe haven space at the bibliothèque Saint-Michel and at the organization La Grande porte, co-created with young people.
Young people aged 12 to 18 in the François-Perrault and Saint-Michel districts are targeted, in particular young girls and LGBTQ2IA+ youth.
The project includes workshops in textiles, music, DJing and olfactory arts over 12 months, led by a cultural mediator.
The borough is committing to pay its share of up to $16,395, in human resources and in the value of services, in addition to non-eligible expenses.
Timeline: application submitted on June 15, 2026, start-up in November-December 2026, workshops in 2027 and inauguration of the installation in December 2027.
The head of the culture, libraries and public events division is authorized to sign the application and to follow up on the project.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is authorizing public events on public property (parks, squares and streets) from July to December 2026.
Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors, up to 80 dBA measured 35 m from the equipment; megaphones remain prohibited except for safety purposes.
The sale of promotional items, food and alcoholic or non-alcoholic beverages is permitted at the sites concerned, as is the consumption of alcohol, in plastic containers only.
Streets may be closed on the dates and at the times set for each event, and advertising signs may be put up.
Promoters will have to put up notices ten days before any street closure to inform residents of the closure hours.
The events are free and open to everyone; the City's support costs are covered by the operating budgets of the departments concerned.
The exact list of events, sites and schedules is in a table attached to the file; other events may be added to the 2026 calendar.
The borough of Verdun will pay $54,689.66 (taxes, interest and costs included) to Construction Urbex inc., to comply with a Superior Court judgment handed down on March 9, 2026.
The amount covers extra work that was not foreseen during the redevelopment of the play areas and the pétanque court at parc de la Fontaine, in L'Île-des-Sœurs.
The company had been suing the City since 2021 for $283,961.21 plus taxes; the court awarded it $54,683.98 plus taxes, interest and costs.
The original contract, awarded in 2016, was worth $454,862.10 plus taxes; the work, scheduled to take 87 days, lasted nearly two years (October 2016 to September 2018).
The payment does not include $22,311.42 plus taxes in late penalties withheld by the City: this part of the judgment is the subject of an application for leave to appeal.
The money comes from Verdun's parks investment program (PDI); the project's original budget, contingencies included, has been used up.
Legal costs will be paid out of the Ville de Montréal's provision.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is awarding TECH VAC Environnement inc. the hydro-excavation service contract, for an expense of $748,487.25 including taxes.
The contract covers about 34 months: work starts March 10, 2026 and ends December 31, 2028, with no possibility of renewal.

Hydro-excavation uses pressurized water to dig in order to repair water mains, sewers, fire hydrants, valves, catch basins and drains without breaking gas pipes, electrical wires and telephone cables.
The borough says it owns no equipment of this type and needs the service all year round, in summer as in winter.
Four compliant bids were received; TECH VAC's bid is the lowest, 13.5% below the City's estimate.
The 2026 expense is paid out of the borough's water fund; the 2027 and 2028 amounts depend on future budgets.
The service covers the water mains of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and Outremont, as well as the sewers of CDN-NDG.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is taking up to $200,000 (net of rebates) from its contingency reserve to help pay for a high-capacity asphalt truck with a fixed heated box.
This truck is used to haul asphalt while keeping it hot, for filling potholes and repairing the borough's roadways.
According to the document, the Direction des travaux publics has been short of machinery for several months and has only one truck of this type, whose reliability is a problem.
The Service du matériel roulant says it does not have the budget for this purchase, because of cuts to its 2026-2027 capital works program, as spreader trucks were given priority.
The truck would be added to the equipment order planned for the two pothole-filling centres of expertise announced by the mayor on March 22, 2026.
The delivery time for the equipment is estimated at between 18 and 24 months.
The funds are certified as available; the accounting code will be specified when the contract is awarded.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is correcting an error (a "typo") in its 2026 fee by-law, which came into force on January 1, 2026.
The correction affects section 56: the fee for swearing in a person is set at $5.00.
The notice of motion and the tabling of the draft by-law took place on February 3, 2026; adoption is planned for the next sitting.
It is expected to come into force in the winter of 2026, with a public notice on the borough's website.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving advance approval for spending of up to $11,958,300 from its 2026 operating budget (January 1 to December 31).
This amount covers purchases and services made through agreements already negotiated by the Ville, public utility suppliers, or other Montréal departments and boroughs.

It applies in particular to construction materials, salt, electricity and energy, water and sewer parts, clothing and footwear, cleaning products, the rental of buildings and land, and waste management.
These expenses are higher than the amounts that municipal staff can commit on their own, which is why the borough council's approval is needed in advance.
According to the document, the goal is to speed up the issuing of purchase orders and payments to suppliers, without going over the total approved amount.
The approvals for previous years were $10,894,900 for 2025, $10,603,200 for 2024 and $9,580,600 for 2023.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is awarding Construction Vert Dure inc. the contract to redevelop the play areas at parc du Colombier, for $407,298.94 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $482,693.78, including $61,094.84 in contingencies (15%) and $14,300 in incidental costs.
The work includes removing the old play structures, installing new play equipment that meets standards, redoing the mulch and concrete paver surfaces, and repairing a leak in the water play area.
Construction is to start in the summer of 2026 and finish in October 2026; a news release will inform residents of the schedule.
Funding comes 100% from the borough's investment program, including $106,000 drawn from the parks fund.
Thirteen of the eighteen firms that picked up the documents submitted bids; the winning bid is 16.83% below the borough's estimate ($489,700.30).
The play areas had been found to be outdated during an assessment of 29 parks built more than 20 years ago; no performance evaluation of the contractor is required (contract under $1M).

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is appointing one of its elected officials to chair its ecological transition committee, for a two-year term beginning February 3, 2026. The name is not given in the document.
The committee advises the borough council: it provides opinions and recommendations on ecological transition matters.

It has seven members: two borough residents, one representative from the school sector, two from environmental organizations and one from the business sector. The chair position automatically goes to an elected official.
Two borough employees (public works and land development) also sit on the committee, without the right to vote.
The appointment is required so that the committee's makeup complies with the by-law that governs it; without it, the committee would not be valid.
The matter involves no spending. The appointment will be announced by the communications team.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is hiring Pépinière Jardin 2000 inc. to supply, plant, water and maintain 350 trees.
The contract is worth $303,735.21 including taxes; the authorized spending reaches $318,921.97 with 5% for contingencies.
The trees will be planted in 2026 in several areas, parks and wooded areas, with maintenance until 2028 (mandate from October 2026 to October 2028).
This contract comes on top of the work done by in-house crews, as the borough aims to plant 1,666 trees this year.
Six companies submitted bids; the two lowest were rejected (insufficient experience in one case, missing addenda in the other).
The winning bid is $79,976.61 lower (−20.84%) than the internal estimate of $383,711.82.
A news release will be published two weeks to one month before planting begins.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding the firm Expertise Sports Design LG a negotiated (sole-source) contract of $74,118.63 (taxes included) for professional landscape architecture and engineering services.
The authorized spending totals $81,530.49, including taxes and contingencies (10% of the contract for unforeseen costs).
The mandate covers resurfacing the nine tennis courts at the parc de l'école secondaire de Pointe-aux-Trembles, where the sand-filled synthetic turf surface is worn out.
Two firms submitted a bid: Expertise Sports Design LG ($81,530.49) and Nvira ($116,519.13). The lowest bid is 17.65% below the borough's estimate.
Planned schedule: plans and specifications in September 2026, call for tenders in November 2026, award of the work contract in February 2027, start of work in May 2027.
The courts will be closed during the work. An analysis is under way to assess converting some of the tennis courts into pickleball courts.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is renting from the Réseau de transport métropolitain (RTM) a 80.15 m² parcel to expand the Montréal-Est community garden, at the corner of rue Victoria and avenue Marien.
The amended lease runs for 13 years, for a total of $6,898.87, taxes included (from $341.93 in 2026 to $546.02 in 2039, with an increase of 1.5% per year).
The amendment also allows the borough to sublet parcels of lots 1 093 262 and 1 093 263 to the Réseau alimentaire de l'Est de Montréal (RAEM), which runs the garden.

The existing garden covers about 400 m² in raised beds (the soil is contaminated) and includes areas adapted for children and for people with reduced mobility; the harvests go mainly to a neighbourhood food counter.
An outdoor space loan agreement with the organization is to be approved at the borough council meeting of May 5, 2026; the expansion work could start as early as May 6.
Without this rental and this sublease, the garden expansion could not go ahead.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is accepting a donation of recreational equipment from the company Équipements récréatifs Jambette inc., with an estimated value of $40,000.
Three new recreational products were installed free of charge by the company in May 2025 in parc François-Vaillancourt and parc Richelieu.
The equipment is mainly aimed at teenage girls, a group that the organization RESPIRE describes as feeling excluded from public spaces in Pointe-aux-Trembles.
After a one-year trial period, the products become the property of the City in May 2026, with no tax receipt to be issued.
The company would like to keep the signs near the equipment that explain the concept and direct people to a feedback form.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is buying 350 trees from Pépinière Rougemont inc. for $78,596.91, taxes included.
The contract is awarded by mutual agreement; three nurseries submitted an offer and Rougemont was the only one able to supply the 350 trees requested.
The price selected is $7,968.84 (9%) lower than the City's most recent estimate.
The trees will be chosen at the nursery in August 2026 and delivered starting in October 2026, then stored in the borough's holding bed.
Planting will take place in the summer of 2027, by in-house crews, in streets and parks, in addition to the trees from the municipal nursery.
An amount of $71,769.45, net of the tax rebate, comes from the loan by-law for the Plan de la forêt urbaine, tied to the 2 Billion Trees funding program.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is hiring Arboriculture de Beauce inc. to prune trees located under power lines in 2026, for $56,458.47 including taxes.
The authorized spending rises to $67,750.17 with a 20% contingency set aside for urgent requests; the borough pays the full amount.
Since Hydro-Québec has stopped responding to one-off pruning requests, requests from residents have piled up and the borough must now handle them.
The City's pruners are not certified to work under power networks, hence the use of a firm certified by Hydro-Québec.
The work targets trees on streets, in parks, in alleys or along the edge of wooded areas, from May to December 2026.
Two companies submitted bids out of four invited; the selected bid is 16% below the City's most recent estimate.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Velosolutions Canada inc. the rebuilding of the BMX track at the parc de l'École secondaire de la Pointe-aux-Trembles, for $155,625.56 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $191,100.67, including taxes, incidental costs and $31,125.11 in contingencies (20% of the contract).
An amount of $112,000 comes from the borough's parks fund; the rest is provided for in the park development program.
The work covers the riding surface, the layout of the jumps and obstacles, and surface water management; the track was built in 2015.
Work is planned from early September to the end of October 2026; the track will be closed during the work.
After the work, the track must be certified for a regional level and be able to host competitions.
Two companies submitted bids: $155,625.56 from Velosolutions and $517,275.87 from Temps Libre; no performance evaluation will be carried out, since the contract is under $500,000.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is awarding Pépinière Jardin 2000 inc. the planting of a micro-forest in parc Sainte-Marthe, for $42,927.07 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $61,366.13, including $6,439.06 in contingencies and $12,000 for a protective fence.

906 trees of various native species (deciduous trees and conifers) will be planted on an overgrown area at the intersection of rue Élie-Beauregard and avenue Louis-Darveau, reducing the area to be mowed by about 940 m².
The contract covers site preparation, planting, watering and maintenance during the first year.
The work starts between September and October 2026 and ends in the fall of 2027.
Three companies submitted bids; the winning offer is 48.92% below the latest estimate of $84,045.
The spending is funded by the loan by-law of the Plan de la forêt urbaine, as part of the 2 Billion Trees subsidy program; any overrun will be paid by the borough.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Pépinière Jardin 2000 inc. the reforestation of parc Armand-Bombardier for $48,519.45, taxes included, with a total authorized spending of $55,797.37 (including 15% for contingencies).

The work calls for planting 250 native trees in the wooded area located between avenue Charles-Renard and avenue Octave-Pelletier, north of boulevard Gouin Est, plus maintenance and a one-year guarantee on the plants.
The wooded area was partly cut down in 2021 to make the backyards on 25e Avenue safe, and the Service des grands parcs continued the tree removals in the winter of 2026.
The document states that the diversity of species is low and that invasive plants, including buckthorn, are limiting native shrubs.
Five firms submitted bids; the winning proposal is the lowest and is 52.32% below the latest estimate of $101,758.50.
The work is to start between September and October 2026 and be completed in the fall of 2027.
The spending is funded by the loan by-law of the Plan de la forêt urbaine, tied to the 2 Billion Trees funding program.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving $8,000 to the organization Éco de la Pointe-aux-Prairies to organize giveaways of compost, mulch and plants in 2026.
Four giveaways are planned in each of the borough's neighbourhoods: in May 2026 for the spring, and in September 2026 for the fall.
The materials handed out come from the composting of yard waste picked up during collections and from the pruning of trees on public property.
Again this year, the organization is adding plants that are good for pollinators, including plants that attract the natural enemies of aphids.
Residents can also get vegetable plants and herbs, with registration, to cut down on waiting and to spread out the limited quantities.
An agreement sets the conditions for paying out the contribution; promotion will be handled by the organization and relayed by the borough.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is giving $4,200 to the Regroupement des éco-quartiers for the 2026 environmental awareness patrol.
Two patrollers will work in the borough for 9 weeks, 32 hours a week, starting June 1, 2026.
Their local activities will be coordinated by the organization Éco de la Pointe-aux-Prairies.
The topics they will discuss with residents: waste management, making green alleys last, and saving drinking water, along with activities in urban agriculture and biodiversity.
Their working time will be split as follows: 45% for local assignments, 45% for assignments from the City's central departments, and 10% for training.
The project is also funded by Canada Summer Jobs, the City's central departments, and other participating boroughs.
Same amount as the contribution given for the 2025 edition.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is lending two parcels of land free of charge to the organization Action Secours Vie d'Espoir for 13 years (until 2039).
The parcels (80 m² on lot 1 093 262 and 27 m² on lot 1 093 263) will be used to expand the Montréal-Est collective garden, located at the corner of rue Victoria and avenue Marien.
The garden operates collectively: the land is cultivated together and part of the harvest goes to families experiencing food insecurity, notably through a food bank.
In 2024, the site produced more than 2,000 pounds of food and 220 pounds of honey; because of the area's industrial past, growing is done in above-ground planter boxes.
The agreement sets out the organization's responsibilities toward the site; the organization continues to manage the garden.
Timeline: activities resume in spring 2026, expansion work in summer 2026.
The land loan costs the borough nothing. Without this agreement, the expansion could not go ahead.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is applying for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation to redevelop the eastern section of parc des Cageux.
The project includes a raised walkway/terrace, designed to protect the habitats of the brown snake (couleuvre brune).
The program in question (component 2, outdoor recreation infrastructure) offers up to $500,000, without exceeding 66% of the eligible cost.
The borough commits to paying its share of the costs, the operating expenses and any cost overruns, and to awarding no contract before the minister's announcement letter.
An amount of $805,000 is already included in the capital works program for this work; submitting the application costs nothing.
Timeline: submission by May 21, 2026 at the latest, response in December 2026, work from spring 2027 to September 2027.
Director Luc Castonguay is authorized to submit the application and sign the documents on behalf of the borough.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding a direct (non-tendered) contract to Les Constructions Argozy inc. for $67,835.25, taxes included, and authorizes a total expense of $78,010.54 (including 15% contingencies).
The old wooden players' benches deemed defective will be removed and replaced with benches made of recycled plastic or plasvinyle.
Parks affected: Samuel-Morse (6 single benches), Armand-Bombardier (2 double), Pasquale-Gattuso (2 double), École secondaire Pointe-aux-Trembles (4 quadruple) and Don Bosco (1 quintuple).
Benches will be added at Maria-Goretti (2 single) and Pehr-Kalm (2 double).
The work is to begin in the summer of 2026 and be completed by the end of the summer of 2026.
Three bids were received: Argozy ($78,010.54), Salvex ($104,454.79) and Les Entreprises Daniel Robert ($173,209.84); the selected price is 23% below the City's most recent estimate.
The document states that the defective benches pose a risk of injury to users.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Les Entreprises Roseneige inc. the planting of trees at parc Simone-Dénéchaud, for $53,308.16 including taxes.
The total authorized spending comes to $58,638.98, with 10% for contingencies.
The work calls for 500 native trees in 2-gallon pots, plus maintenance and a one-year guarantee on the plants.
The wooded area had lost several ash trees that were cut down; a 2023 planting survived poorly, and buckthorn and other invasive species were controlled in 2025 over 3,400 m².
The work will take place from September 2026 to December 2027.
Two companies submitted bids; the lowest is 53.96% below the estimate of $115,780.51.
The funding comes from the loan by-law for the Plan de la forêt urbaine, tied to the 2 Billion Trees grant program.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding a $62,417.66 (taxes included) contract, negotiated directly without a call for tenders, to Comité ZIP Jacques-Cartier, a non-profit organization.
The mandate: control invasive exotic plants, mainly buckthorn, in parc Armand-Bombardier (13,900 m²) and parc Saint-Valérien (2,600 m²).
The work includes pulling out plants, cutting them back, and either removing or encapsulating the stumps, as well as monitoring and documenting the results.
The work is to take place from June to August 2026, with an activity report between September and December 2026.
The offer is 39% higher than the $44,850 estimate: the organization made site visits that revealed more work, and working during the nesting season requires checking for the presence of birds.
The expense is funded by the budget dedicated to protecting natural environments.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is buying five misters for parc Pasquale-Gattuso, near the play areas, the soccer field and the park chalet.

The contract, awarded without a call for tenders, goes to Vortex Structures Aquatiques Internationales inc. for $51,636.42 including taxes; the total authorized spending is $59,381.88, including contingencies and taxes (15% contingencies).
The work is planned from September to November 2026, and a news release will inform residents of the schedule.
The other bid received, from Industries Simexco at $36,064.39, was set aside: the posts were bigger than the specifications called for and water use was higher.
The borough presents the project as a response to extreme heat and to a request from residents for a water play area, noting that misters are easier to maintain.
The redevelopment of the entire play area is the subject of a separate public call for tenders, with a decision expected at the July borough council meeting.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is asking the executive committee to replace the current order that governs the keeping of hens on its territory.
The change would allow a henhouse to be set up on a lot that borders more than one street, which is not covered by the current rules.
The henhouse would then have to be located in the part of the yard between a lot line and the rear wall of the main building, and not be visible from the street.
All other criteria that apply to henhouses would continue to apply.
The measure is part of the borough's Plan d'action en agriculture urbaine.
No cost is associated with this file; the by-law and the documents are to be updated in the summer of 2026.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving $4,200 to the organization Éco de la Pointe-aux-Prairies.
The money will be used to hire two students for the green patrol, which raises awareness about the environment, in the summer of 2026.
The two patrollers will work in the borough for 9 to 12 weeks, with a start date still to be determined.
Their work will focus on urban agriculture and protecting biodiversity.
The patrollers' time will be divided as follows: 10% in training, 45% on joint assignments with the City's central departments, and 45% on local assignments.
The amount covers salaries, on-site coordination, communication costs and materials not included in the Programme Éco-quartier.
In 2025, the borough gave the same amount of $4,200, but to hire only one student.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is amending the by-law governing its ecological transition committee, created in 2022.
The committee's mandate is reworded: to advise the borough council by putting forward directions and recommendations suited to local realities.

The five original objectives (ecological standards, biodiversity and green spaces, partnerships, public awareness, food self-sufficiency through urban agriculture) are being replaced by three new ones.

The new objectives: encourage collaboration among institutional, community and citizen players; identify ecological transition issues and projects; and build these principles into the borough's major decisions.
Committee members approved these changes at their meeting of May 26, 2026; the borough explains that it wants to remove objectives it considers too specific.
No spending is tied to this file. The committee's next meeting is planned for September 2026.

The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is awarding Les Terrassements Multi-Paysages inc. a contract to supply and install street furniture at Plage de l'Est and parc Maria-Goretti, for $57,857.38 including taxes.
The authorized spending totals $66,535.99, which is the contract plus $8,678.61 in contingencies (15%).
At Plage de l'Est: four picnic table sets, two lounge chairs and one hammock stand. At parc Maria-Goretti: four bicycle racks. New concrete slabs will also be installed.
The work is to be done in late summer or fall 2026.
Six firms were invited to bid from May 19 to June 12, 2026, and two submitted bids; the winning bid is $12,321.58 (17.56%) lower than the latest estimate.
According to the document, these additions respond to requests from residents and elected officials, and some of the furniture will be accessible to people with reduced mobility.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is giving $75,000 to the organization Ville en Vert for the year 2026, out of its surplus funds.
The money funds the 3rd edition of the Bye Bye Béton ! program, which involves removing asphalt or concrete from spaces chosen by residents and planting vegetation there.
Two sites have been selected for 2026: école Georges-Vanier and école Marie-Favery.
Timeline: project development in spring 2026, work on the sites in summer and fall 2026.
The payment is made in three stages: $37,500 when the agreement is signed, $25,000 after a progress report, and $12,500 after a progress report or the final accounting.
This amount is part of a $525,000 allocation ($175,000 per year) approved in July 2025 for the 2025 to 2028 editions of the program.
Communications are planned for the inauguration of the redeveloped sites.

The Ville-Marie borough is renting cars, pickup trucks and vans from Enterprise Canada and Location Sauvageau, for a total expense of $387,085.53 including taxes (of which $35,189.50 is set aside for a variation in quantities).
The rentals cover March 2026 to February 2027, with several vehicles rented only from April to November, the period when the borough adds employees for its work sites.
The vehicles are used for maintenance of the water supply system, inspection, signage and paving and sidewalk work carried out by in-house crews.

Fourteen streets are slated for paving or sidewalk repairs in 2026, including avenues Trafalgar and Lincoln, Tupper, Hôtel-de-Ville, Wolfe, Robin, Saint-Timothée, Plessis, Alexandre-DeSève and Lespérance.
The borough's 2026 road repair program includes 14 projects and an investment of $825,000.

The borough explains that the centralization of mechanical maintenance has increased its needs and that it must itself pay the difference between the vehicles provided by the Ville and its actual needs.
Without these rentals, the borough expects that maintenance, inspection and traffic calming work could not be done and that in-house paving and sidewalk work would be reduced.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is extending its contract with the engineering firm FNX-INNOV (Artelia Canada) by 12 months, from March 4, 2026 to March 3, 2027.
This is the second and final extension provided for in the agreement signed in December 2022.
The additional spending authorized is $222,361.65, taxes included, which brings the total contract from $708,269.00 to $930,630.65.

The firm prepares the plans and specifications and supervises electrical work: lighting for sports fields, lighting for streets, parks and paths, charging stations, traffic light wiring, new streetlights.
The borough justifies the renewal by the exhaustion of the current budget, the mandates under way and the planned projects.
The money will come from the budgets already set aside for each project, either in operations or in the Ten-Year Capital Works Program; the net cost after tax refunds is estimated at $849,789.83.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is proposing to handle the call for tenders, the contract, the work and the supervision itself for two new bus stops on rue Saint-Patrick, at the Eadie and de l'Église intersections.
These stops stem from the STM's bus network overhaul, which aims to improve service and shorten walking distances in the area.
At the Saint-Patrick/Eadie stop: construction of about 45 metres of sidewalk and relocation of the guardrail.
At the Saint-Patrick/de l'Église stop: about 25 metres of sidewalk, a slab for a bus shelter, and reconfiguration of the slope and of the access to the bike path.
The Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité is planning the project and paying all of its costs; no amount is stated in the file.
Planned schedule: plans and specifications in February 2026, public call for tenders from February to April 2026, work from June to October 2026.

The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is awarding Cojalac inc. a contract worth $3,553,954.28, taxes included, to rebuild intersections and streets; the total authorized spending comes to $4,264,745.14 including contingencies and incidental costs.

Three intersections will be made safer: De Maricourt and Laurendeau (three curb extensions, two tree pits), Island and Châteauguay (two double curb extensions, a raised intersection, concrete islands to protect a bike path) and Saint-Rémi and Palm (curb extensions and the enlargement of two tree pits), with pedestrian lights added at Saint-Rémi and Palm.

Four streets will be planed and paved: Charlebois (between Sainte-Marguerite and Saint-Ferdinand), Châteauguay (between Ropery and De Laprairie), Saint-Clotilde and Turcot (between Saint-Alphonse and Saint-Rémi).
The contract includes replacing about a dozen lead service lines, on both public and private property; the private share ($70,761.58 plus contingencies) will be billed to the residents concerned.
The work must be done in 2026 so that the City receives the subsidy from the Service de l'eau.

The bill is split as follows: 38.02% for the borough, 53.2% for the Direction de la gestion d'actifs of the Service de l'eau and 8.78% for Hydro-Québec's integrated enhancement program, which is paying $285,000 for the Island-Châteauguay intersection.
Four companies submitted bids; Cojalac is the lowest compliant bidder, 5.10% below the City's estimate, and its performance will be evaluated since the contract is over $1,000,000.

The City is awarding Construction Transit 2e G ltée a contract worth $4,820,317.56 (taxes included) to redo the roof and replace the generator at Musée Pointe-à-Callière, at 350, place Royale, in Ville-Marie.
Adding $964,063.51 in contingencies (unforeseen costs) and $530,234.93 in incidental expenses, the total spending comes to $6,314,616, paid entirely by the central city.
The roof is more than 29 years old and is letting water in; the generator has been in service for more than 27 years and has reached the end of its useful life.
The work also includes improving thermal performance and setting up temporary facilities so the museum can stay open during construction.
Construction is to start on August 24, 2026 and finish on June 16, 2027; the spending is spread out 40% in 2026 and 60% in 2027.
Of the 9 companies that obtained the tender documents, 2 submitted bids and only one was compliant; the price selected is 9.36% below the professionals' estimate.
The file is going before the Commission sur l'examen des contrats (work over $4M and only one compliant bid) and the company's performance will be evaluated.
The borough of Lachine approves the plans to enlarge the house at 3920, rue Sir-George-Simpson.
The project adds 81 m² of floor space: an attached garage on the ground floor and living space on the upper floor, in the left side yard.
The cladding will be khaki green aluminum with a flat roof; the sliding windows and the garage door will be white; the façades of the existing building will also be modified, except the front porch.

Three conditions are imposed: the cladding of the addition must be two to three tones darker than the second level of the original building, the parapet must be horizontal with no roof overhang, and the addition must be set back at least 60 cm from the original building.
The permit is granted on the condition that the project complies with the regulations in force.
Any change to the approved project will have to go through a new site planning and architectural integration programme (PIIA) plan approval.
The Lachine borough approves the plans to transform the façades of the house at 285, 35e Avenue.
The work will include creating a living space (mezzanine) in the attic, with new openings on the third level, at both the front and the back.
The roof and the canopy will be redone in grey metal, the stucco replaced with a grey acrylic finish, and some walls covered with white metal.
The front door will be replaced with a glass door in a wood colour, and the windows with black casement windows.
The permit is granted on the condition that the project complies with the by-laws in force; any change will have to go through a new request for plan approval.
The documents submitted are dated December 23, 2025, and the planning advisory committee reviewed the file on February 11, 2026.
The borough of Lachine is cancelling its October 1, 2025 decision on the renovation of the façades at 115, 9e Avenue, and is approving a new version of the project.
The owner wants to cover all the façades of this residential building with a white metal cladding.
The new proposal changes the material to Vicwest AD 300 series steel, installed vertically, in pure white, with narrower panels than originally planned.
The applicant says she chose this cladding because it provides better insulation and is easy to find on the market.
The City's construction by-law normally prohibits metal cladding on a property line, but a committee authorized an exception on January 22, 2026 given the building's structure.
The permit will be issued on the condition that the project complies with the regulations; any change will have to go back through the architectural approval process.
The City will buy collection bins (organic waste and household garbage) from two suppliers, for an estimated total of $3,484,025.17, taxes included.
Orbis Canada gets the contract for the brown wheeled bins of 45 to 50 L, for a maximum of $1,229,533.12; USD Global gets the contract for the 120, 240 and 360 L bins, for a maximum of $2,023,524.93.
Added to this are $165,905.96 in contingencies and $65,061.16 for price indexation.
The agreements last 36 months, with two possible extensions of 12 months each, and replace agreements ending in March and October 2026.
The bins will be used by residents of the 19 boroughs, which handle the distribution; delivery within 6 weeks after ordering, minimum 5-year warranty, City logo and RFID chip required.
Only two suppliers submitted bids out of four that obtained the tender documents; the expense is paid 100% by the central city.
The City is buying wheeled garbage bins (120, 240 and 360 litres) from Plasti-Bac inc. for $2,341,207.99, plus $117,060.40 in contingencies, for a total of $2,458,268.39 including taxes.
A second agreement gives the distribution of the bins to USD Global inc. for $279,491.58, plus $13,974.58 in contingencies. Both agreements last 24 months and total $2,751,734.54.
The bins are for residents of Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where garbage collection will be spaced out in two phases: fall 2026 and fall 2027.
Collection schedules change as of November 1, 2026; the boroughs will inform residents about the distribution of the bins and the new schedules.
Each bin will carry the City's logo, an RFID chip and a serial number, and will be guaranteed for at least five years. An information leaflet will be placed inside each bin delivered.
Of the four companies that obtained the tender documents, two submitted bids. Plasti-Bac's bid is 6.76% higher than the City's latest estimate.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, and Plasti-Bac inc.'s performance will be evaluated.
City council is renewing Émilie Bouchard's term as a member of the Conseil interculturel de Montréal.
This second three-year term runs from February 2026 to February 2029, following a first term that began on February 20, 2023.
The by-law governing the Conseil interculturel allows only one renewal, for a maximum of six years as a member.
The executive committee of the Conseil interculturel, without Émilie Bouchard, recommends this appointment, citing her participation in meetings, committees and activities.
The Conseil interculturel has 15 members and advises the city administration on intercultural relations through opinions and activities.
The City funds 100% of the Conseil interculturel's operations.
The Conseil interculturel de Montréal is tabling its 2025 activity report before city council, as required by by-law 19-051 (tabling no later than May 31 each year).
The Conseil interculturel is an independent advisory body made up of 15 volunteer members from Montréal's population, which advises the City on intercultural relations.
Highlights of 2025: publication of an advocacy paper on socio-economic precariousness and participation in municipal debates in boroughs.
The Conseil began work on an opinion on racial profiling, to be published in 2026, and is continuing a reflection on the definition of "intercultural" that will also wrap up in 2026.
Seven new members joined the Conseil in 2025, the year a new executive committee took office.
The report will be shared with partners and posted on the Conseil's website and social media; production costs were covered by the Conseil's budget.
The City is amending the order that governs waste collection in the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The changes concern the collection of recyclable materials, carried out in-house by the borough, in order to bring it in line with the new sector boundaries that came into effect on November 1, 2025.

This second phase of adjustments mainly affects sector 3 and corrects the list of streets and lanes where collection takes place in the lane, following problems with lane collections and with how work was divided among the crews.
The order also specifies where organic materials go: to the Montréal-Est treatment centre from December 1 to March 31, and to the Saint-Laurent centre from April 1 to November 30.
The City states that this change regarding organic materials has no impact on residents or on current contracts.
No cost is associated with this file; the order comes into effect as soon as it is published.
The borough of Lachine is settling a dispute with one of its employees out of court. The employee is identified only by employee number 100009550.
The agreement puts a final end to the dispute, with neither the City nor the employee admitting any responsibility.
The borough council is approving the payment of severance pay. The amount appears only in the settlement document and is not disclosed here.
The borough director is authorized to sign the settlement and release on behalf of the City.
The document justifies the settlement as a way to avoid the uncertainties of a court process.
The City is signing an agreement with LeuWebb Projects Ltd., a Toronto artists' firm, to present the public art installation "Celsius en vue" on the Biosphère lookout, in parc Jean-Drapeau.
The exhibit is planned from May to September 2026, with an opening announced for May 30, 2026.
Two viewfinders equipped with thermal cameras will let the public "see heat": cool surfaces appear in blue, and those that absorb heat in red and orange.
The museum says it wants to make visitors aware of heat islands and of the role green spaces play in reducing them.
Total cost of $13,797, taxes included, paid in two instalments of $6,898.50: one on April 15, the other at the opening.
The expense is paid 100% by the urban agglomeration, because the Biosphère is located in parc Jean-Drapeau.

The City is awarding Rümker (9276-2723 Québec inc.) a contract of $980,046.90 (taxes included) to design the exhibition "Poptopia. Les utopies écologiques dans la culture populaire" at the Biosphère, plus $98,005 in contingencies, for a total expenditure of $1,078,051.90.
The exhibition will take up about 360 m² on the ground floor of the Biosphère (rooms 4 and 5) for at least two years, with an opening planned for December 2027.
It will focus on positive ecological visions presented in film, television, literature, comics and games, along with scientific facts, and will be rounded out with outreach activities.
The mandate is carried out in seven phases, from strategy (June-July 2026) to technical support (December 2027 to December 2028), paid in lump-sum instalments.

A first contract for this exhibition, awarded to CREO inc., was terminated by mutual agreement on February 19, 2026, because of creative differences and delays; the opening had first been planned for December 2026.

Five bids were received from nine firms that took out the tender documents: one firm was found ineligible (no authorization from the Autorité des marchés publics) and another non-compliant (quality score below 70%).
The expenditure is paid entirely by the agglomeration, since the Biosphère is located in parc Jean-Drapeau; the winning bid is $83,471.85 (-7.85%) lower than the City's estimate.
The City is entering into an agreement with the Montréal studio Studio Supply and Demand inc. to present the immersive exhibition "L'odyssée sensorielle" at the Biosphère, in parc Jean-Drapeau.
The exhibition will be open to the public from December 5, 2026 to October 11, 2027; this will be its first presentation in Québec.
Total authorized spending of $474,271.88 including taxes: $431,156.25 for the contract and $43,115.64 in contingencies.
Payments will be made in six instalments between June 2026 and October 2027, tied to deliverables (concept, design, production, installation, technical support).
The spending is covered 100% by the agglomeration, because the Biosphère is located in parc Jean-Drapeau.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders (by mutual agreement), as the studio holds the exclusive rights to present the exhibition in North America.
The supplier adapts the exhibition to the site, installs the equipment (4K projections, immersive sound, scent diffusion) and provides technical support for the 12 months.

The City is paying an additional $442,493.55 (taxes included) to the firms Architecture 49, Pelletier de Fontenay and Cima+ for the fit-out of the centre Sanaaq, at 1200, rue du Sussex, in Ville-Marie.
The professional services contract therefore goes from $2,574,566.38 to $3,017,059.93, taxes included.
Of that amount, $270,596.57 is used to adjust the engineers' fees: the final design required more engineering work (electrical and mechanical rooms, mezzanine).
Another $171,896.98 goes to contingencies, including $174,843.47 in fees related to supervising an extended construction site.

The construction work, initially estimated at 13 months, was extended by 5 months after a first call for tenders was cancelled in 2022, then delayed further by a breakdown of the building's cooling tower.
The expense is paid 88.16% by the central city and 11.84% by the borough of Ville-Marie.
By signing the amendment, the firms waive any further fee claims for the services provided so far. The centre is already open.
The City is signing contracts with six artists and a work-loan agreement with the Centre canadien d'architecture for the exhibition "Un monde en commun" at the Biosphère.
Total cost: $37,920.66, taxes included, paid in two instalments ($8,261.31 on February 20, 2026 and $29,659.35 when the exhibition opens, in May or June 2026).
The exhibition will run from spring 2026 to spring 2027 at the Biosphère, in parc Jean-Drapeau.
Planned fees: Marilou Lemmens $13,049.66, Geneviève Chevalier $6,600, Jim Holyoak $6,271, Miranda Smitheram $4,600, Taqralik Partridge $3,300, Tiffany Shaw $3,300, and $800 for the work loan.
The works deal with sharing the territory with other species: bank swallows, moths, bird habitats, northern ways of life, and invasive plants on île Sainte-Hélène.
The expense is covered 100% by the agglomeration, since the Biosphère is located in parc Jean-Drapeau.
The artists were selected together with the Fondation Grantham pour l'art et l'environnement, which will present an exhibition on the same theme at the same time.
The City is ending the $256,106.81 contract awarded in May 2025 to CREO inc. to design the "Poptopia" exhibition at the Biosphère, in parc Jean-Drapeau.
The cancellation is amicable, by mutual agreement, effective January 28, 2026: the Biosphère cites creative and interpretation differences that caused delays.

A final payment of $45,921.02, taxes included, is being made to the firm: $25,041.56 for the preliminary script and the museum design concept, completed to 75%, $17,200.26 for the expertise of a museologist and $3,679.20 for a semiotics expert.
The amount is paid out of the Biosphère's budget and covered entirely by the agglomeration; with the 100% tax rebate, the net cost is $39,940.
A first payment of $25,610.68 had already been made for the "Stratégie" deliverable submitted in June 2025.
The City will issue a new call to the market from March to May 2026; the opening of the exhibition is postponed from winter 2026-2027 to December 2027.
The work already done by CREO inc. will be passed on to the next team.
The City is accepting a $250,071.49 grant from the Fonds d'action québécois pour le développement durable for an educational project at the Biosphère, in parc Jean-Drapeau.
The project "Tendre l'oreille : la pollution sonore et ses effets" deals with noise and its effects on health and urban biodiversity.
The Biosphère will offer free activities to groups of young people aged 8 to 14 (schools and day camps), especially those from neighbourhoods where noise pollution is high.
On the program: an outdoor sound exploration, followed by a poster-making workshop, with the posters to be displayed by the young people in their school or camp.
The activities will be offered from July 2026 to August 2027; the young people's work will be exhibited at the museum in the fall of 2027.
The grant will be paid in three instalments: $62,517.87 upon signing, $125,035.75 after a progress report on November 15, 2026, and $62,517.87 after the final report on September 30, 2027.
The expense is fully borne by the agglomeration and is offset by the revenue received, with no effect on the City's financial framework.

The City is signing an agreement with Anne Marchand, a professor of industrial design at the Université de Montréal, to put together the exhibition "Matières à penser : design et résilience environnementale" at the Biosphère.
The exhibition will be presented from December 5, 2026 to October 11, 2027 in the Biosphère's panoramic room.
It will present the projects of twelve emerging designers on sustainability, the reuse of waste materials and the resilience of urban and natural environments.
The exhibition is co-designed with the Université de Montréal, UQAM, and university students, professors and professionals.
The exhibition rights and fees paid are zero dollars; the City is paying for project management, printing and production of the exhibition.
The file falls under the executive committee and concerns the agglomeration power related to parc Jean-Drapeau.
The City is extending five turnkey snow removal contracts by 12 months for the 2026-2027 winter, in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro.
Additional expense of $7,399,240.83 (taxes included), bringing the total value of the contracts to $26,664,219.58.
This amount includes $5,480,919.13 for the services, $1,096,183.83 in contingencies and $822,137.87 for variations in quantities.
The firms involved: Déneigement Fontaine Gadbois (Anjou), J.M. Gagné and Déneigement Cyrbault (Montréal-Nord, 3 lots), Pavages d'Amour (Pierrefonds-Roxboro).
Each contract is increased by 35% (20% contingencies, 15% variation in quantities) to cover the unpredictability of winters.
The current contracts end on April 15, 2026; the extended contracts begin on May 18, 2026.
The expense is covered 100% by the central city; additional funds could come from the Réserve neige if snowfall exceeds forecasts.
The City is extending seven snow-removal towing contracts by 12 months, for the 2026-2027 winter season.
The extended contracts cover Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
Total additional spending of $1,003,068.72, taxes included, which brings the value of the contracts to $2,489,096.46.

City council is authorizing $642,123.30 for Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension; the executive committee is authorizing $100,890.56 for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.
The companies involved are Remorquage O secours, Sauver Remorquage Ludos Auto, J.M.A.C Remorquage Transport et Déneigement, Remorquage TGF and Autopromo Montréal.
The amounts are increased by 35% (20% for contingencies, 15% for variations in quantities) to cover the unpredictability of winters.
The extended contracts begin on November 15, 2026; the spending is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
The City is extending three contracts for the rental of snow removal equipment with an operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie by 12 months, for the 2026-2027 winter season.
Additional spending authorized: $676,577.30 including taxes, bringing the total value of the contracts to $1,240,391.72.
This amount includes $563,814.42 for the services, $28,190.72 in contingencies and $84,572.16 for variations in quantities (a 20% increase to account for how unpredictable winters are).
The three suppliers are Transport H. Cordeau inc. ($266,806.39), MWM Équipement Spécialisé ($268,627.59) and Groupe Thermo-Lite inc. ($141,143.31).
The services begin on November 1, 2026; the extension runs until March 31, 2027.
The spending is covered entirely by the central city; if it snows more than expected, the City will have to go back to the decision-making bodies to draw from the Réserve neige (snow reserve).
The Ville-Marie borough is extending its contract with Entretiens Qualibec inc. for window washing at 7 municipal buildings by one year, from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The City is authorizing an additional expense of $49,283.43, taxes included, bringing the contract's maximum expense to $239,709.62.
The price was indexed by 2%, as allowed by the contract: $48,317.09 x 1.02 = $49,283.43.
This is the second and last extension provided for in the contract, which was awarded through a public call for tenders in 2022 (2 bidders out of 7 people who took the tender documents).
The washing work must be done between April 15 and May 15 of each year of the contract.
The expense is funded by the borough's operating budget; the required credits are $45,002.34, net of rebates.
The Ville-Marie borough is extending by 12 months the cleaning contract for its Bercy roadworks yard with the company Ménagez-vous inc.
The extended contract runs from March 13, 2026 to March 12, 2027.
Additional spending authorized: $486,916.34, taxes included, bringing the contract total to $1,888,889.10.
The contract covers 10,556 hours of sanitary cleaning per year, plus 50 hours for special projects. The garages continue to be cleaned by the blue-collar workers.
The hourly rate goes from $39.08 to $39.93 before taxes, based on the consumer price index adjustment provided for in the contract.
The original contract was awarded in 2023 through a public call for tenders (22-19704), with 4 bidders.
The Ville-Marie borough is paying an extra $4,115.97 to Axia Services for cleaning services at the Cour municipale, at 775, rue Gosford.
This brings the contract total from $3,848,279.09 to $3,852,395.06, since it was awarded in 2020.
The overrun comes from 120 extra hours worked by an employee added on Sundays to clean the garages, a day with no judges or vehicles on site.
The number of hours written into the contract was only an estimate, and no contingency amount had been planned.
The contract covered daily cleaning, winter maintenance, deep cleaning and special events; it ended on December 14, 2025.
The expense is taken from the 2026 operating budget; without approval, payment to the supplier would be delayed.
The Ville-Marie borough is awarding Groupe Marleb inc. the cleaning and upkeep of the self-cleaning public toilets, for an expense of $183,005.48 including taxes.
The contract covers 12 months, from July 16, 2026 to July 15, 2027, with a one-year extension option that would bring the total to $369,671.07.
The company must clean the surfaces every day, replace soap, detergent and paper, take out the garbage and report breakdowns; some very busy toilets will be visited more than once a day.
Also included are a monthly exterior cleaning, getting the units ready for the change of seasons, and snow removal at the entrances during heavy storms.

Five companies submitted bids: three were rejected for administrative non-compliance and Groupe Marleb submitted the lowest compliant offer, $56,889.86 below the other bid that was accepted as compliant.
The winning bid is $3,599.34 (2.01%) above the borough's estimate.
The borough says it does not have the in-house resources to do this work and plans to evaluate the company's performance.
The borough of Outremont is paying up to $4,200 to the Regroupement des Écoquartiers for the green patrol in the summer of 2026.
The money tops up the salary of two green patrollers, in addition to the Emplois d'été Canada grants; the hiring is still subject to approval by Service Canada.
The patrol will be in the borough for nine weeks, from June 1 to August 1, 2026.
The patrollers will do outreach with residents on: the urban forest and the emerald ash borer, water management, waste, cleanliness and the zero-waste lifestyle.
The amount may be reduced depending on the actual number of patrollers hired: $2,100 if there is only one. In 2025, $2,100 was spent and a single patroller reached 1,324 people.
The expense comes from the funds tied to the cleanliness action plan and is paid entirely by the borough.
The City is entering into two master agreements to buy polymer bollards, delineators and accessories, for an estimated amount of $1,513,230.69, taxes included.
Trafic Innovation inc. is awarded lot 1 ($1,194,122.99) and Develotech inc. lot 2 ($121,729.78), taxes included. Each was the only compliant bid for its lot.
The agreements last 24 months, with three extension options of 12 months each.
The City is adding $197,377.92, taxes included, as a budget for variations in quantities.

These bollards are used to mark off lanes and to make work sites, pedestrian areas and bike paths safer; all of the City's business units will be able to order them, with stock held at the Centre de distribution Colbert.
After negotiation, Trafic Innovation inc. lowered its price by 1.05%; its bid is 33.17% below the City's estimate.
Trafic Innovation inc.'s performance will be evaluated, since the contract is over $500,000. The expenses will be charged to the budgets of the boroughs and of the departments.
The City is entering into two master agreements to purchase ready-mixed concrete and non-shrink backfill, for an estimated amount of $4,659,350.38 (taxes included).
Béton Provincial ltée will supply the ready-mixed concrete (lot 1) for $3,943,251.59; Amrize Canada inc. will supply the non-shrink backfill (lot 2) for $716,098.79.
The agreements run for 24 months, with three extension options of 12 months each; prices are fixed for the first period, then adjusted according to an industrial price index.
The products are used mainly for road work done in-house: repairing streets and sidewalks and backfilling trenches (water mains, sewers).
The call for tenders documents require glass powder to be added to the concrete and recycled aggregates to the backfill.
Two of the four companies that took out the tender documents submitted bids; the lowest bid for lot 1 is $376,156.81 above the City's estimate, or 10.54%.
The expenses will be charged to the budgets of the boroughs and the corporate departments, as needed.
The City is extending its purchase agreement for traffic cones (T-RV-3 markers) with Plastipro Canada ltée by 12 months, starting June 21, 2026.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $78,052.15, taxes included, bringing the agreement to a total of $321,063.32 since 2023.
Prices remain the same as those obtained in 2023 and stay fixed for the entire extension.
The cones are used to make public roadways safe during street marking, short roadwork jobs, police interventions and events.
All boroughs and City units can order these cones, at the Centre de distribution, in municipal stores or directly from the supplier.
No amount is set aside in advance: the City is not required to buy a minimum quantity and each order must be approved.
As of May 15, 2026, the City had used $190,690.35 of the agreement, or 84% of the contract awarded.

The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is ratifying the submission of a $122,500 grant application, taxes included, to the National School Streets Initiative program of the organization Green Communities Canada.

The money will be used to build "school squares": $50,000 for the one near école Paul-Bruchési (already completed in 2024) and $70,000 for a second school square whose location has yet to be determined.
An amount of $2,500 will go towards the borough team's participation in a community of practice, from 2024 to 2027.
The expenses cover the purchase and manufacture of furniture as well as ground markings; work on the second school square is planned for spring and fall 2026.
The head of the Division de l'aménagement écologique du paysage is authorized to sign the documents and agreements with Green Communities Canada.
The borough undertakes to comply with the program's terms and conditions, failing which the financial assistance would be terminated, and to mention the funding in its public communications.
A research team from the École de santé publique de l'Université de Montréal will collect data to document the impacts of the projects.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is receiving a $122,500 grant, taxes included, from Green Communities Canada (National School Streets Initiative) and is asking the executive committee to increase its budget by the same amount.
The money will be used to create "school squares": giving the space next to elementary schools back to children, improving safety and encouraging walking and cycling.
Planned breakdown: $50,000 for the school square near école Paul-Bruchési (already completed), $70,000 for a second one near école Enfant-Jésus, and $2,500 to take part in a community of practice.
The work near école Enfant-Jésus (first a temporary version, then a permanent one) is planned for spring and fall 2026; furniture, furniture building and ground markings.
The budget must be spent during the 2026 financial year; participation in the community of practice runs from 2024 to 2027.
The borough will have to mention "Funding supported by the National School Streets Initiative" in its public communications.

The projects are being carried out with the École de santé publique de l'Université de Montréal, the Centre d'écologie urbaine, the Centre de services scolaire de Montréal, school principals, parents, children and local residents.
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is renting a backhoe with an operator from 9161-4396 Québec inc. for $200,056.50, taxes included.
The machine will be used to plant trees on public property, remove stumps, handle materials and maintain parks.
The contract covers 8 months, from April 15 to December 15, 2026, for about 1,500 hours, including 640 guaranteed hours, at a rate of $116 an hour.
