The borough was aiming for 850 trees planted in 2026; if planting is reduced, the 640 mandatory hours would be used to plant about half of the trees planned.
Six companies submitted bids; the winning bid is the lowest and is 15.9% below the estimate of $237,998.25.
The contract could be renewed for 8 months in 2027 if both parties agree.
After tax rebates, the net cost to the City is $182,678.25.

The City is transferring $400,000 in 2026 to the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne: $200,000 from Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, $130,000 from Saint-Laurent and $70,000 from LaSalle.

These three boroughs are joining the soil management site at the parc d'entreprises de la Pointe-Saint-Charles, which takes care of receiving, sorting, storing, characterizing, transporting and disposing of the excavated soil from their in-house work.
The amounts match the volumes of soil handled by each borough; the money comes from the water funds managed by the Service de l'eau.
For 2027 and the following years, these amounts will be included directly in the Service's budget when the budget is prepared.
The site was already serving 11 boroughs, including Ville-Marie, Le Sud-Ouest, Verdun, Lachine and Saint-Léonard.

Between October 2022 and December 2025, 127,469 tonnes of lightly contaminated soil were sent to the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel for the development of parc Frédéric-Back, and more than 20,000 tonnes of demolition concrete were processed.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is approving spending of $350,000 to buy and install street furniture in 2026 and 2027.
The furniture (benches, picnic tables, garbage bins) will be made by the Ateliers spécialisés de la Ville de Montréal, so there is no outside call for tenders.
The money will be used to replace outdated furniture, add more of it in parks, and keep a stock on hand for breakage and unexpected requests.
Part of the amount will pay for the installation of furniture already stored at the Darlington service yard.
The funding comes from the 2026 Ten-Year Capital Works Program: $250,000 from the street furniture component and $100,000 from the building renovation component.
The order will be placed once approval is given, since production takes more than 12 months.
Le Plateau-Mont-Royal agrees to have Ville-Marie provide it with a public works team dedicated to cleanliness work related to homelessness, for 12 months starting in the spring of 2026.
The team has 8 people (1 foreman and 7 blue-collar workers) and 4 vehicles: 1 packer truck and 4 pickup trucks, during the day, Tuesday to Friday.
Cost approved for 2026: $931,328, including $679,328 in pay and $252,000 for vehicle rental and logistical support.
The money comes from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale, with no impact on the borough's budget.
The places where the team will work will be chosen jointly by Le Plateau's teams and Ville-Marie's managers.
The Ville-Marie team, created in 2025, also works in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Le Sud-Ouest and Ville-Marie.
This is a renewal: a 6-month agreement had been approved in May 2025.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is asking Québec for financial assistance to renovate and bring the Centre récréatif Saint-Charles, at 1055 rue d'Hibernia, up to code.
The building, dating from 1966, houses an arena, an indoor pool, a gymnasium, locker rooms, multipurpose rooms and offices.

The planned work: replacing systems that have reached the end of their service life (structural, mechanical, electrical, aquatic), bringing the building up to safety and accessibility standards, and reducing GHG emissions.
The ministère de l'Éducation program can cover up to 66% of eligible costs, to a maximum of $20M.
If the assistance is maximized, the project would cost about $30.3M, of which $10.2M would be paid by the borough.
The borough commits to absorbing 100% of any cost overruns and the operating costs.
The application must be submitted no later than June 22, 2026; the work will have to be completed within five years of the minister's announcement.

The City is amending its 2025-2028 delegation agreements with the six PME MTL organizations (Centre-Est, Centre-Ouest, Centre-Ville, Est-de-l'Île, Grand Sud-Ouest, Ouest-de-l'Île) for the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2028.
Starting April 1, 2026, the new rules of the Fonds régions et ruralité limit the share of the FRR envelope that can be used for each organization's administrative expenses to 10%.

The City is granting a two-year moratorium (2026-2027): the organizations will be able to temporarily use a larger share of the City's contribution for their administrative costs, in exchange for cost-reduction efforts to meet the 2028 target.

Each organization has been assigned a maximum annual amount of City contribution for administration, ranging from $152,306 to $345,377 depending on the hub, after cost reductions of $175,885 to $285,500 each.

For the Fonds Jeunes Entreprises, the maximum cumulative government assistance goes from 50% to 70%; in-kind contributions (premises, equipment, specialized volunteer work) become eligible as a down payment under the Fonds de développement de l'économie sociale.
The $1,500 cap on file fees for Fonds PME MTL loans is being removed: the organizations may charge 2% of the financing with no limit, in order to generate more self-generated revenue.
The amendments are conditional on authorization by the ministre des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation and on approval of the FRR territorial development agreement.

The City is awarding a contract, without a call for tenders, to Global Payments Direct inc. to process debit and credit card payments at municipal counters, on the City's websites and at parking meters.
The contract covers six months, from June 1 to November 30, 2026, with the possibility of automatic renewal for another six months.
The total cost comes to $2,957,415.06 including taxes: $2,575,299.51 for the contract and $382,115.55 as a 15% allowance for changes in quantities.
The current contract, awarded through call for tenders 17-15841, ends on May 31, 2026; this temporary contract keeps the same terms and conditions.
The City wants to give itself time to negotiate a new three-year contract without interrupting card payments for residents.
The temporary contract will end automatically as soon as the new contract takes effect.
The Montréal-Nord borough is reimbursing $3,545 (taxes included) to the organization Nos jeunes à cœur.
The amount covers the rental of the field at Stade Hébert, in Saint-Léonard, for the 2025 football season.
The organization had to rent elsewhere because the fields in Montréal-Nord are not certified by the sports federation for holding official games.
The team continues to train free of charge in the borough's facilities.
The Direction sent the organization a letter reminding it of the procedures and presents this reimbursement as a one-time exception for 2025.
The expense is taken from the borough's operating budget.
Note: the title of the file also mentions a $157,000 contribution to Un itinéraire pour tous, but the document deals only with the amount of $3,545.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is proposing to city council that it take charge itself of sidewalk repairs on three main streets in its territory in 2026.

Sidewalks covered: boulevard Henri-Bourassa (between boulevard Léger and avenue Bellevois), boulevard Rolland (between rue Pascal and boulevard Maurice-Duplessis) and boulevard Saint-Vital (between Gouin Est and Henri-Bourassa Est).
The borough would handle the plans and specifications, the call for tenders, the awarding of the contract and the supervision of the work.
The Service des infrastructures du réseau routier is funding the project 100%; the amount set aside for Montréal-Nord is $120,000, net of rebates.
Announced timeline: plans and specifications in April 2026, call for tenders and contract in May and June 2026, work in the summer and fall of 2026.
The borough points to the high number of resident requests about the condition of sidewalks and pedestrian safety.
Next step: city council must accept the offer.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is awarding Montréal Scellant inc., the lowest of 8 bidders, a contract worth $456,514.62 (taxes included) to build driveway entrances and rebuild sections of sidewalk.
With contingencies ($31,956.02) and incidental costs ($23,787.31), the total authorized spending comes to $512,257.96, taxes included.

The work affects local streets in the borough as well as four arterial road sections: Henri-Bourassa (between Éthier and Léger, and between Léger and Bellevois), Rolland (Pascal to Maurice-Duplessis) and Saint-Vital (Gouin to Henri-Bourassa).
The work is to begin the week of June 22, 2026 and be finished no later than October 15, 2026, over 90 calendar days.
The borough is paying $406,170.33 through a loan by-law from its road repair program; the central city is covering up to $96,948.57 net for the sidewalks on the arterial road network.
The winning bid is $105,455.14 lower (-17.76%) than the borough's estimate.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $16,500 to Maison des jeunes du Plateau Inc. for two youth projects in 2026.
$7,500 goes to "La Buvette Baldwin," a food service run by young people in parc Baldwin, open to the public from July 6 to August 13, 2026, with activities such as story time.
The borough is also paying for the electricity used by the equipment lent to the organization for the buvette.
$9,000 goes to the toy library at parc des Compagnons-de-Saint-Laurent, open free of charge to students of école secondaire Jeanne-Mance over the lunch hour, Monday to Friday.
The toy library will be open from April 27 to June 19 and from September 7 to October 30, 2026; games, art supplies, books and staff will be on site.
The organization must submit its final reports by September 28, 2026 (buvette) and November 30, 2026 (toy library).
The toy library builds on a pilot project from the fall of 2025, which drew up to 20 young people a day in good weather; the buvette welcomes an average of 80 people a day.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $3,944 to three organizations that run community gardens, for the 2026 season.
The amounts: $881 to Jardin Rivard, $1,407 to Jardin communautaire Mile-End and $1,656 to Jardin communautaire De Lorimier.
The money is used for projects that open the gardens up to the community, for repairs and to buy equipment.
The agreements cover the period from May 5 to November 30, 2026, with an accounting report due December 30, 2026.
The same amounts were granted to the same organizations in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
According to the borough, this support aims to promote food self-sufficiency and reduce social isolation among the people who garden.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $20,000 to Vélo Québec Association for the sixth season of the "Jardin du petit monde à bicyclette" in 2026.
The money comes from the Fonds des jeunes, which is funded by the sale of daily and monthly parking permits.
The cycling education park takes up the north portion of avenue Calixa-Lavallée and the former parking lot next to the centre culturel Calixa-Lavallée, in parc La Fontaine.
It is aimed at children aged 2 to 12, with a miniature road network and a bike lending counter.
The amount covers installation, maintenance, repair of the furnishings, materials for daycares and CPEs, then takedown at the end of the season.
The project runs from May 18 to October 18, 2026; the final report is due November 18, 2026.
The borough presents this project as temporary, while waiting for the permanent redevelopment of the area by the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $10,000 to the organization JM Court for the Zone-skate in parc La Fontaine in 2026.
The money comes from the Fonds des jeunes, which is funded by the sale of daily and monthly parking permits.
The project sets up beginner skateboarding modules, including a half-pipe, in a free space for families and children in the neighbourhood.
JM Court provides supervised activities and equipment lending twice a week, including one session reserved for gender-diverse people.
The project runs from June 1 to November 15, 2026, with a final report due on December 15, 2026.
The modules belong to JM Court, which manages them on site; the space is awaiting a permanent redevelopment by the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports.
In 2025, about 900 participations were recorded during the activities.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $5,000 to La Maison d'Aurore for its 50th anniversary community party, planned for September 19, 2026.
The party will take place on the grounds of the Guinguette d'Aurore, in the De Lorimier district, with a community meal for about 250 people.

On the program: the unveiling of tablecloths embroidered from residents' stories (a project with artist Patsy Van Roost), stencil art on the sidewalks, and a performance by the Fanfare Pourpour (17 musicians).
The money comes from a $485,000 envelope for boroughs to hold free outdoor cultural events outside the central neighbourhoods; the Ville-Centre covers the full cost.
Le Plateau-Mont-Royal received $15,000 in total to support free artistic initiatives in the De Lorimier district, where fewer cultural events are held than in the two other districts.
The council is also approving the agreement setting the payment conditions and is authorizing the mayor and the borough secretary to sign the documents.
The borough of Ville-Marie is extending its snow removal contract for the Quartier des Spectacles with 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky) by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.
Cost of the extension: $115,664.85, plus $11,566.49 in contingencies, for a total of $127,231.34 including taxes. The maximum expenditure for the contract rises to $508,925.34.
The work covers spreading abrasives, snow removal, snow loading and snow disposal at place des Festivals, the Grand Parterre and place Émilie-Gamelin.
Prices stay the same as before: the renewal clause does not allow any indexation. The contractor signed the renewal notice on February 23, 2026.
The borough explains that it does not have enough staff or equipment to do this work itself, and that the services provided since 2023 have been satisfactory.
The original contract, awarded in October 2023 after a public call for tenders with 2 bidders, covered the winters of 2023-2024 through 2025-2026.
The funds are provided for in the operating budget: $42,411.33 in 2026 and $84,820.01 in 2027.

The Ville-Marie borough is extending by one year, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, the horticultural maintenance and cleaning contract for parc de Dieppe awarded to 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky).
It is authorizing an additional expense of $156,479.01 ($122,300.63 for the contract, $24,460.12 in contingencies and $9,718.26 for a variation in quantities), taxes included.
The maximum expense for the contract thus rises to $759,243.85, including taxes, contingencies and variation in quantities.
Prices remain those in effect during the initial period of the contract; the borough says it prefers to renew rather than go back to a call for tenders given the rise in prices since 2022.
This is the second and last extension option provided for in public call for tenders 22-19302, awarded in 2022 after receiving only one compliant bid out of two.
The borough states that it does not have the staff needed to do this work, as use of the park has exceeded forecasts (maintenance hours 50% higher than expected).
The City is submitting a grant application to the Québec FIERH program to fund water infrastructure tied to an affordable housing project.
The application concerns the Coulée Grou project, on rue Sherbrooke Est, in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, led by the organization Gérer son quartier.
The project calls for 200 social and affordable housing units on a site of about 18,000 m² that currently has no municipal services, for families, single people and seniors.
The work includes extending the water main network and building a retention basin on the site to manage surface water.
The ministry has accepted the application: the funding covers actual costs up to $698,400, while the work is estimated at $405,025.
The City commits to covering ineligible costs; the resolution itself does not involve any immediate spending.
Next steps: a financial assistance agreement with the ministry, then an agreement to pay the grant to the organization.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is approving the plans for a new 2-storey, 4-unit building at 8028-8034, rue Saint-Gérard.
The current building, built in 1920, has been vacant since a fire in January 2025, and its demolition was already authorized by the demolition committee on February 11, 2026.
The new building will match the front facade alignment of its neighbours, will be clad in red-toned brick and will have a contemporary style; the units will range from 125 m² to 187 m².
A basement will serve the two ground-floor units, which will be larger than the existing ones.
The tree in the backyard will be kept, but a public-property tree in the front yard must be cut down; landscaping will cover 65% of the areas that are not built on.
Value of the work estimated at $910,148, permit review fees of $5,159 and a bank guarantee of $50,000.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on March 11, 2026, after requiring corrections (raised front windows, mechanical equipment moved to the roof).
The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is approving the plans for a 3-storey building at 1925, rue Jean-Talon Est, at the corner of rue Chabot.
The building will have 12 housing units (3 one-bedroom, 7 two-bedroom, 2 three-bedroom) and 2 commercial spaces on the ground floor totalling 338 m².
The lot was home to a former used vehicle dealership; a project authorized in 2021 was abandoned in 2022, leaving open-air foundations.
The project includes 5 parking spaces in the basement, 12 bicycle spaces, greening of 71% of the ground, one tree (Kentucky coffeetree) and a partially vegetated roof.
The value of the work is estimated at $3,454,110; the permit review fees come to $33,850 and the PIIA fees to $2,132.

The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 11, 2026, with conditions on the brick bonding and a masonry pattern on the lane side, which the developer has incorporated into the plans.
Next step: issuing the permit.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is approving the expansion plans for a fruit and vegetable distribution warehouse located at 8350, rue Jeanne-Mance.
The project adds about 363.63 m² of floor space: an expansion in the side yard visible from rue Guizot Ouest, plus a floor built inside the building for offices.
Two new loading docks will be added, on top of the two existing ones.
A 27-space parking area with permeable paving will be built, with 4 electric charging stations and 22 bicycle spaces.
The flat roof will be planted with vegetation and the grounds landscaped with trees and shrubs, for 64% greening.
The urban planning advisory committee gave a unanimous favourable opinion on March 11, 2026, on the condition that safe lighting be added to the parking area; the developer agreed.
Value of the work: $960,000.00. Next step: issuing the renovation permit.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension recommends refusing the merger of two units in the duplex at 2633-2635, rue Everett, in the François-Perrault district.

The owners, who have lived on the ground floor since 2015, wanted to combine the two units to create a 217 m² unit with three bedrooms, by adding an interior staircase and new partition walls upstairs.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous unfavourable opinion on April 8, 2026: the project would mean the loss of a two-bedroom unit, and the expansion could be done through the basement or at the rear.
The Direction du développement du territoire is also opposed, noting that the garage could be removed or converted to allow an expansion in the back yard.
The CCU also points out that two metro stations are nearby, which in its view justifies an increase in density, and that it would be hard to reverse the change once the work is done.
The fees for reviewing the conditional use application come to $3,130.
A public notice will be published on the borough's website and a sign will be posted on the property.
The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is turning down the request from the owners of the triplex at 1343-1345, rue De Castelnau, who wanted to merge two units into one.
The project aimed to combine the ground-floor and 2nd-floor units to create a 213 m² unit with four bedrooms, and to redo the layout of the basement unit.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous negative opinion on June 10, 2026: the project does not return the building to its original typology, the lot has no particular physical constraints, and the work would be difficult to reverse.
The Direction du développement du territoire is also opposed, notably because of the loss of a three-bedroom unit in an area where there is demand, in a zone where up to eight units are allowed.
The fees for reviewing the request come to $3,130.
A public notice will be posted on the borough's website and on the property.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is allowing Banque Nationale to install a temporary advertising sign on its building at 8091, rue Saint-Denis, at the corner of rue Jarry (Villeray district).
The sign will be a backlit aluminum tennis racket 5.8 metres high and 2.5 metres wide, with the bank's logo inside it.
The installation is tied to the Omnium Banque Nationale, a tournament organized by Tennis Canada for which the bank is the title partner.
The authorization runs from July 13 to August 23, 2026, and the sign must be taken down on August 23, 2026.
Conditions imposed: the anchors must be placed in the masonry joints, with no perforation of the marble panels.
There is no financial aspect attached to this file; the order will be published on the City's website.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is allowing Hydro-Québec and its subcontractor Intervia to make noise at night, from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., on weekends from June 12 to July 13, 2026.
The work involves building a duct bank under the roadway, then rebuilding the demolished roadway, at the Saint-Patrick/Bridge and Wellington/Bridge intersections.
Planned schedule: from Friday at 7 p.m. to Monday at 7 a.m. — one weekend at Saint-Patrick/Bridge (June 12 to 15) and four weekends at Wellington/Bridge (June 19 to July 13).
Planned closures: Saint-Patrick between De Condé and Wellington (local traffic only) and Bridge between Wellington and Saint-Patrick.
Also: Wellington closed between Saint-Patrick and Condé (local traffic only) and Bridge closed westbound between Mill and Saint-Patrick, with one contraflow lane eastbound.
The borough justifies the night work by the amount of traffic in the area and the impacts on traffic, public transit and merchants.
An information campaign must be carried out before the night work begins.
The City is giving $100,000 to Vélo Québec Association to deliver the "Cycliste averti" program in 60 elementary school classes in Montréal in 2026.
This amount will make it possible to train 1,150 more students, in addition to the 70 classes already funded by national funders.
The program is for students in Grades 5 and 6: 6 hours of classroom theory, 6 hours of practice in a closed environment, a bike outing on the road, an individual exam and a personalized report card.
The amount will be paid in a single payment within 30 days after the agreement is signed, and comes from a transfer from the budget set aside for the administration's priorities.
The contribution represents less than 12% of the program's total budget for 2026; the ville centre had not provided any support in 2025.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city.
Montréal is asking Québec for financial assistance to carry out a road safety plan covering the arterial road network of the entire agglomeration.

The Ministère des Transports program reimburses 100% of eligible expenses: salaries of employees assigned to the project, travel, contracts with firms, printing, equipment rental and non-refundable taxes.
The assistance is paid in three instalments: up to $50,000 when the application is accepted, 70% of planned expenses after the work plan, then 30% after the accountability report.
If the assistance is granted, the City has 24 months to complete its road safety plan; otherwise, the assistance may be terminated.
The application is expected to be filed at the end of April 2026; the Division des stratégies de mobilité durable will lead the work.
The plan stems from the Plan d'action Vision Zéro 2025-2027, which aims for zero deaths and zero serious injuries on Montréal roads by 2040.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough is settling a lawsuit out of court with the company Les Constructions Lavacon inc. by paying it $18,044.95 (principal, interest and costs).

The City is also giving up its claim for $6,100.61 from the company: $3,284.84 in unpaid permits to occupy public property and $2,815.77 for repairs to public property. These amounts are written off the books.
The dispute came from work carried out in 2018-2020 at the école primaire Sainte-Catherine-de-Sienne, at 7055, avenue Somerled.
The City had sued the company in 2021; the company responded by claiming back its security deposit of $33,706.25, which the City had kept because of damaged sidewalks and trees.
The document points to weaknesses in the evidence (the location of the sidewalks, the lack of a set rate for damage to trees) and the cost of a four-day trial, scheduled from March 17 to 20, 2026.
The expense is paid entirely by the borough.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is drawing $100,000 from its management surplus to fund two traffic-calming projects in 2026.
Rue Fullum, between Laurier Est and Sherbrooke Est: conversion to one-way southbound, strengthening of the bike lanes, and safer pedestrian crossings.
"Petit Laurier" area: change in the direction of traffic on De Brébeuf, Chambord, Garnier, Fabre and Chabot, between Laurier Est and Saint-Joseph Est, to reduce through traffic.
The decisions are based on traffic studies by the firm CIMA+ and on an analysis carried out by the borough in the fall of 2025, as well as on requests from residents.
The work contracts are to be awarded at the June borough council meeting; the work begins in the summer of 2026.
A public information session, on-site signage and web communications are planned; a report on the spending will follow at the end of 2026.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is hiring 9176-7277 Québec inc. (Go Cube) to collect and store belongings left on the street after an eviction, for $61,316.17, taxes included.
The contract runs for 12 months starting April 1, 2026, with no option to extend it.
The borough is cancelling the renewal contract given to the same company on November 17, 2025 ($91,549.17), which was considered less advantageous; no penalty applies for this cancellation.

For each eviction, the company inventories and photographs the belongings, transports them and stores them for 60 days, then disposes of them if the person does not pick them up; fumigation is planned in cases of bed bugs.
The new contract covers 110 evictions over 12 months; the old one covered 200 over three years.
Three compliant bids were received: Go Cube ($61,316.17), Déménagement MEC Plus ($175,825.52) and Déménagement La Capitale Universel ($199,309.16).
The City is extending its participation in the group purchasing arrangement of Québec's Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales (CAG) by 12 months, until March 31, 2027, to buy computer equipment.
It is adding $10,000,000, taxes included, which brings the contract total from $20,500,000 to $30,500,000.
The agreement covers desktop and laptop computers, rugged laptops, servers, tablets, monitors and accessories.
The purchases are used to replace about 4,000 obsolete workstations per year; the City explains the high pace by the massive purchase of laptops made in 2020 for remote work.
The spending will be paid out of the budgets of the boroughs, the central services and the related cities, as needs arise.
The director of the Direction Espaces de travail et services aux utilisateurs is authorized to sign the contract documents.
The file must be approved by the urban agglomeration council.
The Ville de Montréal is joining the cellular telephone group purchasing arrangement of Québec's Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales (CAG), for a maximum of $16,800,000, taxes included.
The agreement covers 60 months, retroactively from March 2, 2026 to March 1, 2031, and includes a 12-month period for migrating to the new suppliers.
It covers about 14,500 of the City's cellular subscriptions (voice, data, or both) and includes plans, phones, tablets, Internet sticks and MIFI hotspots.
The CAG selected two suppliers ranked by price: orders go by default to the first-ranked supplier for the first two years, with the second serving as an alternative in case of an exception.

According to the document, plan prices are lower than under the previous agreement and discounts on devices range from 5% to 50% depending on the model; price revisions are planned for March 2, 2028 and March 2, 2029.
Specialized services such as telemetry and surveillance cameras are excluded and will be the subject of a separate call to the market by the City.
The expenses will be paid out of the operating budgets of the units that use the services, as needs arise.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Lina El Kesserwani as director of public works, effective May 16, 2026.
The position was vacant after the person who held it resigned.
The job was posted internally and externally from February 25 to March 9, 2026, followed by a selection committee made up of two borough directors and a talent acquisition specialist.
The proposed annual salary is $174,360, within a 2026 salary range of $139,366 to $174,213 (merit maximum: $209,060).
From May 16 to December 31, 2026, the expected cost totals $138,400 (salary, bonuses and payroll expenses), paid out of the borough's operating budget.
Regular status depends on successfully completing the probation period set out in the working conditions for managers.
The borough of Anjou is lending its mobile stage to the Communauté des catholiques portugais de Montréal for the Fêtes du Saint-Christ des Miracles.
The activities take place on May 15, 16 and 17, 2026, then on May 23 and 24, 2026.
The organization must watch over the stage at all times, from delivery until pickup, and use it only for its intended purpose.
The organization must hold civil liability insurance of $3M valid for the 5 dates and cover the labour costs related to the loan.
The loan depends on following the usage instructions of the Direction des travaux publics and does not authorize holding the event under the by-laws of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
The request mentions the Fêtes de l'Esprit-Saint of May 23 and 24, 2026 at église Santa Cruz, at 60, rue Rachel Ouest.
The borough of Anjou is giving $6,485.79 to the Association portugaise des résidents d'Anjou.
The money is for the traditional fête de l'Esprit Saint, on June 6 and 7, 2026, at aréna Chénier (8200, avenue Chénier).
The amount matches the rental value of the arena: the borough is reimbursing the rental costs paid by the organization.
The arena is managed by SOGEP under a 2007 contract, which requires the organization to pay for the rental even though it is recognized as an Anjou partner with free access to the facilities.
The event brings together about 2,000 people, mainly from Montréal's Portuguese community, with meals offered free of charge.
The borough gave $6,327.60 in 2025, $6,142.04 in 2024 and $5,245.50 in 2023 for the same celebration.
The borough of Anjou is giving $50,000 to the organization Concertation Anjou for its "Table de quartier" project, from August 5, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
The amount goes from $31,113 last year to $50,000, following an executive committee decision in April 2026 that raised the target to $50,000 per table de quartier.
With Centraide ($75,000) and the Direction régionale de santé publique ($23,468), the table will receive a total of $148,468 for 2026-2027.
Concertation Anjou brings together about thirty community organizations, about fifteen citizens and institutional members (police, CIUSSS, OMHM, schools, elected officials).
The work covers food security, housing, urban safety, health, mobility and community living together in Anjou.
A housing subcommittee was created because of affordability issues and the gentrification linked to new construction and the arrival of the metro.
The organization must submit, no later than November 13, 2026, a document explaining its structure and its collective decision-making processes.
The borough of Anjou is giving $5,000 to the organization Parcours Âme.
The money is for cultural mediation activities and the celebrations marking the unveiling of Anjou's first mural, on the école secondaire d'Anjou.
The mural will be created in the fall of 2026 by artist Alex Davro, in collaboration with the organization A.G.C. Art public.
The activities will take place between September 1 and October 16, 2026, in partnership with the école secondaire d'Anjou, and will be aimed at the community sector, teenagers and the general public.
The contribution is conditional on the project being approved by the Ville de Montréal's Programme d'art mural.
The organization must use the money only for this project, keep separate accounting records and provide an accounting report to the borough.

The Villeray/Saint-Michel/Parc-Extension borough council takes note of the report on the highlights of the 2025 financial results (as at December 31) and will have it published on the borough's website.
The borough's 2025 operating budget was $67.4M; the year ended with a surplus of $2.8M.
Capital expenditures totalled $6.9M, financed by borrowing in the amount of $5.8M.
The rest, $1.1M, comes mainly from deferred revenues from parking units and from a Government of Québec assistance program for recreational, sports and outdoor infrastructure.
This report is required by law and must be presented at a regular meeting before September.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is receiving $71,000 from the ministère de la Sécurité publique du Québec.
The money comes from the program "Soutien à la création et à la consolidation d'espaces jeunesse montréalais 2022-2026".
At the bibliothèque Langelier, the money will be used to redesign the activity room and the space for young children, and to expand the range of activities offered.
Part of it will also be used to expand activities at the mobile library ("Viens lire dehors!").
The executive committee must amend the City's 2026 budget to record this amount as both revenue and expenses.
The borough had received $63,000 from the same program for 2024-2025.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is carrying over $15,142.41 that was not spent in 2025 to its 2026 budget, taking the money from its surplus.

This money comes from a grant from Québec's ministère de la Sécurité publique ("Soutien à la création et à la consolidation d'espaces jeunesse montréalais 2022-2026"), of which $71,000 was granted for 2025-2026.
The funds are for redesigning the activity room and the toddlers' area at the bibliothèque Langelier, and for adding more activities at that library and at the mobile library (Viens lire dehors!).
The delay is due to the ministère's answer about renewing the funding, which came in February 2026.
Without this allocation, the amount would have to be paid back to the ministère, under the funding agreement.
Planned schedule: suppliers and planning in spring 2026, purchases and programming in the summer, delivery and accountability reporting in the fall.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is starting the process of amending its by-law on the delegation of powers to civil servants, to bring it in line with the Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, in effect since April 1, 2026.
The by-law specifies that the value of a contract will from now on include any renewal and any option provided for in the contract.

A new power is granted to the borough director: they will be able to authorize the expense and award a contract without a call for tenders (the exception under section 33 of the Act) if its value stays below the threshold that requires an open tendering process.

The wording of the by-law is updated: "attribution" (awarding) replaces "octroi" (granting), "procédure ouverte" (open procedure) replaces "demande de soumissions publiques" (public call for tenders), and the rules for evaluating bids are reworded.
Timeline: notice of motion on June 8, 2026, adoption planned for June 29, 2026, coming into force when the public notice is published.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The Montréal-Nord borough is moving its regular council meeting from Monday, October 5, 2026 to Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 7 p.m.
Reason given: the provincial general election is being held on October 5, 2026, and the elected officials do not want to interfere with people exercising their right to vote.
A public notice will be published, and shared on the borough's website, on Facebook and in the newsletter.
The other 2026 meeting dates remain unchanged: February 9, March 9, April 13, May 4, June 8, June 29, September 8, November 2 and December 7.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is approving a change of signs for the Jean Coutu pharmacy at 558, boulevard Jacques-Bizard, in the centre commercial Jacques-Bizard.
Three plexiglass panels will be replaced on the shared pylon sign, at the corner of boulevard Jacques-Bizard and boulevard Chevremont, with red lettering on a white acrylic background.
The two wall signs on the canopy will be replaced with lit LED letters (red and blue) on a grey aluminum backing panel, about 8.98 m² in total.
The sign permit application was filed on October 7, 2025; the plans were prepared by Lumicom.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme said it was in favour on December 9, 2025; the borough council makes its decision on February 3, 2026.
No financial impact for the City is listed in the file.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is approving the installation of a wall sign at 11, rue Lachapelle, on the side of the building facing rue Cherrier.
The sign advertises a new office moving into the 2nd floor of this commercial building, which was built in 1987.
It will measure 10 feet by 3 feet (120 in. x 36 in.): black aluminum frame, white background, vinyl lettering and logo with cut-out 3D letters, and no lighting.
The building is located in an area of exceptional value and on the L'Île-Bizard waterfront route, at the intersection of Cherrier, Lachapelle and boulevard Jacques-Bizard.
Three wall signs are already in place at this address (Animo etc, BigEsthétique, Nettoyeur Daoust/Forget).
The urban planning advisory committee said it was in favour of the request on February 17, 2026; the borough council makes its decision on March 10, 2026.
No spending is associated with this decision.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is approving the construction of a detached single-family house at 11, avenue des Cèdres, on a vacant corner lot of 1,880.5 m².
The house will have two storeys, be 10.69 m high, cover about 240.7 m², and include a built-in garage, stone and wood clapboard siding, and an asphalt shingle roof.
There are 111 trees on the lot: 33 will be cut down within the construction area, 6 considered to be dying will also be cut, and 72 must be kept (including 25 on public property).
No tree may be cut in the public right-of-way, except for two trees located in the planned driveway.
Eight trees cut down on the slope must be replaced by eight native trees with a minimum diameter of 10 cm, planted within the time frame set for the outdoor landscaping.
A 2-metre-wide strip of vegetation must be preserved along chemin Dutour, protected by a fence during the work.

The developer must pay a security deposit of 4% of the value of the project, which will be refunded once the exterior of the house and the landscaping are finished. The project completes a group of four homes started at 21, avenue des Cèdres.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is approving the enlargement of a detached single-family home at 164, croissant Cardinal, in L'Île-Bizard.
The work adds a section on the left side of the house: a garage on the ground floor and a living space on the upper floor.
The front facade will be reorganized with two twin gables; the materials match the original style of the house, built in 1977.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme came out in favour of the project at its meeting of April 21, 2026.
No spending is associated with this file.
The borough of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is tabling a draft by-law to allow buildings with 7 or more units in zone C2-334.
This zone covers only the property at 15 757, boulevard Gouin Ouest, the former Ameublement Prillo store, which has been vacant and for sale since 2019.
The change would allow up to 17 units there, with a ground floor reserved exclusively for commercial uses.
The request was submitted on June 11, 2025 by the owner; the urban planning department says it is in favour, in order to repurpose the building.
Planned steps: public consultation on May 5, 2026, second draft on June 2, final adoption on July 7, 2026, coming into force between the end of July and the end of August.
The by-law is subject to approval by referendum; a notice is planned for mid-June 2026.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is spending $366,794.40 (taxes included) on the spring cleaning of its sidewalks and streets.

Seven contracts are being awarded: $312,779.14 to "Les Équipements Benco Canada Ltée" for the rental of six sidewalk-washing machines with operators, and $54,015.26 to "Groupe Villeneuve inc." for a tanker truck with operator.
The contracts cover 2026 and 2027, with an option to extend for one year.
The sidewalk washers clean the sidewalks starting in early spring; the tanker truck sprays the streets with water to cut down on the dust stirred up by the mechanical sweepers.
The borough says it does not own the equipment needed to do this work itself.
Public call for tenders 25-104-AP / 25-21177 was published on October 1, 2025 and opened on October 23, 2025; six bidders took part.
No supplier performance evaluation is planned, since each contract is below the applicable threshold.

The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is extending its two graffiti removal contracts with the company 9181-5084 Québec inc. (Solutions-Graffiti) by 12 months, for a total of $321,074.53, taxes included.
The contract covers public property ($107,780.90) and private property ($213,293.63).
The extension runs from May 15, 2026 to May 14, 2027; the contract is expected to be awarded at the borough council meeting of May 5, 2026.
The prices are those of the original 2024 contract, increased by 0.394% based on the consumer price index.
Graffiti is removed with paint or cleaning products; City employees look for cases and residents can report them through an online form.
The expense is taken from the operating budget of the Division de la voirie (cleaning and sweeping of public roads).
Public call for tenders 24-20399 (lots 1 and 2) had received two bids.
The City is renewing for 2026 its program that helps boroughs organize "cyclovias": street routes closed to cars and reserved for cyclists, runners, skaters and skateboarders.
It is authorizing spending of $70,000, paid entirely by the central city.
Each selected borough can receive up to $7,000 per kilometre of route, up to a maximum of $14,000 per event and up to 4 events, for $56,000 per year.
The events must be free, held on public property on a closed circuit, between May 1 and December 31, 2026.
Schedule: program launch in February 2026, project selection in April, cyclovias held from May to December, review in December.
The program is being renewed unchanged from 2025; the boroughs promote their own events.
The City supports CF Montréal's bid to bring a future national high-performance soccer training centre to Montréal, or to be a partner in it.
The mayor is authorized to sign a letter of support, which will be sent to CF Montréal to be passed on to Canada Soccer.
On December 1, 2025, Canada Soccer launched a call for expressions of interest; the deadline to respond is February 12, 2026.
This is an exploratory step to identify sites and partners, not yet a call for proposals.
The file has no financial aspect: the City is not paying out or committing any money.
According to the document, a partnership with the municipality is one of Canada Soccer's requirements.
The City points to the region's three professional teams, close to 37,000 registered players and more than 12,000 school athletes in Montréal as arguments in its favour.
The City is changing the rules of the assistance program for independent performance venues with fewer than 3000 seats, created in November 2024 to soundproof venues and reduce noise.
Until now, a venue had to have presented at least 35 shows in the year before its application to be eligible.
With the change, a venue becomes eligible if it reached this threshold of 35 shows in the year before its programming was forced to stop.
The stated goal: to help venues dealing with cohabitation problems with neighbouring housing and to avoid closures due to noise.
The program was funded with $2.5M spread over 2025, 2026 and 2027 and targeted about fifteen establishments; the change has no financial impact.
The schedule calls for a first reading at the urban agglomeration council on February 19, 2026 and adoption on March 26, 2026.
The City is granting $55,000 to Culture Montréal for the third phase of the Alliages program, a guidance and support service for cultural organizations.
The program aims to support 70 organizations in 2026: free assessment and guidance, plus 10 hours of personalized support for 10 organizations, which will pay 15% of the cost.
At least three spots in the support cohort are reserved for organizations from the borough of Montréal-Nord.
Eligible organizations are those in the arts, culture or heritage sectors with their main place of business in Montréal, with up to 249 employees and at least one year of activity.
Québec (ministère de la Culture et des Communications) is reimbursing $27,500 of the $55,000; the rest is covered by the agglomeration.
The first cohort of 35 organizations is to be welcomed in April 2026, after the tools are updated in March and April.
The data from the assessments will be used to produce portraits of Montréal's cultural sector, shared with public funders and municipal bodies.
The City is giving $15,000 to the Corporation du cinéma Beaubien to put together a permanent exhibition marking the organization's 25 years.
The exhibition will be located on the ground floor of the cinema, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, and will be open without a ticket.
The money comes from the Entente sur le développement culturel de Montréal 2024-2027: Québec reimburses $7,500, and the City covers the remaining $7,500.

The support covers 30% of the cost of the overall project, which also includes an outdoor screening on September 19, 2026 during a neighbourhood party with the Association des commerçants et professionnels de Beaubien Est.
A series of 10 Québec films is planned from September 20 to December 13, 2026, with a review in December 2026 and January 2027.
An agreement sets out the payment conditions, and the organization must follow the City's visibility protocol.
The Montréal urban agglomeration is adding 486 buildings in Ville de Pointe-Claire to its inventory of heritage buildings built before 1940.
Listed buildings will be treated as heritage buildings: special rules will apply to their demolition and to the upkeep and occupancy of the buildings.
The Pointe-Claire city council approved the list on February 3, 2026 and recommended its adoption.
Québec law requires urban agglomerations and RCMs to complete this inventory by April 1, 2026 at the latest; Montréal is adopting it in parts, territory by territory.
The inventory is funded through an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications: maximum assistance of $5,000,000 from the ministère and an equal contribution from the City.
The building records are kept on the platform of the Division du patrimoine; the City and the ministère plan to publish them as open data.
The urban agglomeration estimates that there are about 100,000 buildings built before 1940 on its territory.
The urban agglomeration council is adding 8,585 buildings in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie to the inventory of heritage buildings built before 1940.
These buildings become "heritage buildings" under the land use planning act: they will be subject to specific rules for demolition and for building maintenance.
The borough took part in the exercise and supports the adoption of the list.
Quebec law requires the agglomeration to have completed an inventory of all of its pre-1940 buildings with heritage value by April 1, 2026; roughly 90,000 buildings are covered across the territory.
The inventory is being adopted in pieces, borough by borough and related municipality by related municipality; about twenty sectors have already been adopted since 2023.
The work is paid for through an agreement with the ministère de la Culture: up to $5,000,000 in provincial funding and a matching contribution from the Ville.
The data collected on each building must eventually be published as open data.
The urban agglomeration council is adding 1,683 buildings in the borough of Lachine to the inventory of buildings built before 1940 that have heritage value.
These buildings will be considered heritage buildings: they will have to follow special rules for demolition and for the upkeep and occupancy of buildings.
The process stems from a requirement of the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel: the agglomeration must have adopted its inventory by April 1, 2026 at the latest.
The inventory is being adopted in parts, borough by borough and related city by related city; there are reportedly about 100,000 buildings built before 1940 in the agglomeration.
The work is funded through an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications: up to $5,000,000 from the ministère and an equal contribution from the Ville.
The borough of Lachine sent a letter of support; no communications activities are planned.

The borough of Lachine will continue in 2026 to maintain the grassed areas belonging to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (MTMD) along Highways 20 and 13 and Route 138, within its territory.
The MTMD will pay $23,484.87, all taxes included if applicable, on October 1, 2026, to cover 4.5 hectares of land.
The executive committee is being asked to amend the City's 2026 budget and to increase the budget allocation of the borough of Lachine by the same amount.
The borough is exercising the renewal option of the contract entered into with the MTMD (contract 851028195) for the year 2026.
The work is carried out by the contractor Pavages Inter-Pavé, already retained for lawn mowing in Lachine from 2024 to 2026, and includes mowing, weeding, brush clearing, litter removal and signage.
The head of the Voirie et parcs division is authorized to sign the notice of exercise of the option and the related documents, including the invoicing to the MTMD.
According to the document, without this agreement the borough could not guarantee consistent quality in the maintenance of these lands.
The borough of Lachine is renewing for one year its contract with Pépinière et Paysagiste Marina inc. to rent a grader with an operator, at a cost of $94,117.67, taxes included.
The service covers the 2026-2027 winter season, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Lachine does not have any graders in its fleet and rents these machines to support its snow removal crews; the borough uses three of them in winter.
The amount covers 275 hours of use per season, but the company is paid for at least 200 hours, for the machine's availability.
The price includes a 3% increase provided for in the contract; a second option year is estimated at $96,941.18, taxes included.
The money comes from the Travaux publics operating budget; the borough council decides on April 7, 2026.

The borough of Lachine is renewing for one year the contract with 9126-6130 Québec inc. (Payant et fils paysagistes) for the rental of a grader with an operator, at a cost of $94,117.67 including taxes.
The grader will be used for snow removal in the borough from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Lachine does not own any graders in its fleet and uses three each winter, rented with an operator.
The contract provides for 275 hours of use per season, with a guaranteed payment to the contractor equivalent to 200 hours of availability.
The price is going up by 3% compared to the last prices in effect, under a clause in the original contract awarded in November 2023.
A second renewal year is estimated at $96,941.18 including taxes.
The expense is paid out of the Travaux publics operating budget.
The borough of Lachine is extending by 12 months, from September 18, 2026 to September 17, 2027, the janitorial services contract for its city hall with Placement Potentiel inc.
The total spending comes to $67,542.39 including taxes: $64,326.09 for the contract and $3,216.30 in contingencies (5%).
With this renewal, the total value of the contract goes from $201,118.64 to $268,661.03, including taxes.
The contract covers 2,000 hours of regular cleaning, the major cleanings in June and December, events in the council chamber and emergency calls.
The price was indexed to the annual change in the consumer price index for the Montréal region, estimated at a little under 3%.
Placement Potentiel inc. is an adapted enterprise accredited by the Government of Québec and a non-profit organization that employs people with functional limitations.
The money comes from the Travaux publics operating budget; the borough council votes on May 4, 2026.
The City is extending the lease for the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough offices at 5650, rue D'Iberville by 3 years, from September 1, 2026 to the end of the three years.
The total rent comes to $4,003,347.17, taxes included, or about $1,334,449 per year, paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The owner is Colonia Development (1987) inc.; the space takes up the 2nd, 3rd and 6th floors, covering 4,666.30 m².
Property taxes will be adjusted each year based on the owner's actual costs, and operating costs based on the consumer price index.
The Service de la stratégie immobilière recommends a short extension because the building is about to be sold and it wants to assess the new owner's service before entering into a longer agreement.
The City has been renting at this address since 2002; the current lease ends on August 31, 2026.
The expected average rental rate is $247.27/m², within a range for the area of $226.80 to $258.33/m².
The City is extending, for five years starting July 1, 2026, the lease of office space on the 3rd and 4th floors of 80, rue Queen, in Ville-Marie, from CDM De Montréal inc.
The total rent comes to $4,024,125, taxes included, for the period from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2031, an average rate of $35 per square foot.
The leased area goes from about 28,598 square feet to about 20,000 square feet; the yearly rent before taxes goes from $1,000,930 to $685,000.
The space houses employees of the Service des technologies de l'information, while the City develops its strategy for occupying administrative spaces and applies its return-to-work directive.
The City can terminate the lease on June 30, 2029, by giving written notice at least 12 months in advance.

To pay the 2026 rent, the City is transferring $356,957 from unforeseen contingency expenses ($179,906 from the local budget, $177,051 from the agglomeration budget) to the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation.
That department's budget is adjusted on a recurring basis by $719,164 net for 2027.
The City is renting from Hydro-Québec a strip of land of about 366 m² in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, in order to keep a bike path there that is 3 metres wide and about 122 metres long.
The lease lasts 10 years, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2035, for a total rent of $46,896, taxes included (net cost of $42,822.30 after rebates).
The rent goes up every year, from $3,725 in 2026 to $4,452 in 2035, before taxes.

The City has been renting this land since 1981. A disagreement over the rate between 2014 and 2025 was settled by applying the rate-setting principles in the agreement between the Union des municipalités du Québec and Hydro-Québec.
The expense is paid 100% by the agglomeration, out of the operating budget of the Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation.
According to the document, without this lease, residents would no longer have access to this bike path.
In March 2026, city council had already approved an agreement of $125,167.62 with Hydro-Québec for the arrears from 2014 to 2025 on several pieces of land (bike paths, parks, community gardens).
The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is extending by 2 years, starting June 1, 2026, the rental of premises at 6225, rue Godfrey, in the Église presbytérienne Kensington.
Total rent of $24,568.29, non-taxable, paid entirely by the borough; the rent is indexed by 2% per year and includes operating costs, energy and municipal taxes.
The premises are about 360.93 m² and include an office and shared spaces that can be used up to 15 hours per week.
The space is used by the organization "50 Plus Club", run mainly by volunteers, which offers meals, outings and physical activities to people aged 50 and over.
Both parties may end the lease starting June 1, 2027, with six months' written notice.
According to the borough, no municipal premises are available for this use and this type of space is rare in the area.
Without this extension, the organization would have to find other space in order to continue its activities.
The City is awarding Construction Vert Dure inc. a $186,374.48 contract (taxes included) to restore a section of shoreline in the Péninsule area of parc-nature du Bois-de-Liesse.
With contingencies ($37,274.90), the variation in quantities ($14,909.96) and incidental costs ($9,318.72), the total expense comes to $247,878.06.
The work covers 30 metres of shoreline: vegetated riprap, vegetated wooden cribbing, brush clearing, excavation, planting and seeding.
The project also renaturalizes a trail leading to a demolished lookout and an informal trail under the pont Louis-Bisson.
The contract goes to the lowest of the 11 bidders, all of whom were found compliant; the price is 38.39% below the control estimate.
The work is planned for the fall; the expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration.
The project is part of the Programme de réhabilitation des berges launched in 2021, which targets 10 km of shoreline and must be completed by 2031 in order to keep the federal and provincial grants.

The City is transferring $1,165,600 in 2026 to prepare for the opening of the Espace du Cœur-Nomade: $1,119,500 to the borough of Montréal-Nord and $46,100 to the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs.
Starting in 2027, the borough of Montréal-Nord will receive $5,412,700 per year on a recurring basis to operate the facility.
Also starting in 2027, the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs will receive $222,900 per year to buy, process and transport the library's materials.
The Espace du Cœur-Nomade is scheduled to open in January 2027, with a soft opening as of October 2026 to train staff and set up the collection.
The building is located in Montréal-Nord, near the boundary with Ahuntsic–Cartierville, and will serve both boroughs.
It will replace the bibliothèque de Belleville and will bring together a library, a room for cultural mediation and presentations, and community spaces.
The City is extending its contract with Bell Canada by 12 months to buy telecommunications equipment (encryption devices and switches) with support service.
The extension covers the period from March 24, 2026 to March 23, 2027.
No additional spending is being added: the purchases will be made from the funds of the original contract of $2,479,422.68, taxes included, awarded in March 2022.
The Service des technologies de l'information explains that spending under the contract has stayed below the original forecasts.
The equipment is used to replace network hardware that has reached the end of its life and to connect new municipal sites planned for 2026-2027.
The renewal letter sent to Bell provides for a price increase of 2.20%, based on the consumer price index set out in the contract.
This is the second and last extension option provided for in the contract; the decision is up to the urban agglomeration council.
The City is raising the support paid to each of the 32 tables de quartier to $50,000 per year, the same amount for all of them, which includes the borough's contribution where there is one.

The total budget for the Initiative montréalaise de soutien au développement social local rises to $1,650,000 for 2026, thanks to an addition of $600,000 to the budget of the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale.
The Coalition montréalaise des tables de quartier sees its support go from $15,000 to $50,000; it had been unchanged for several years.
The Table de quartier du Sud de l'Ouest de l'Île (formerly Lac St-Louis/Dorval), which was receiving only the funds from the MESS agreement, also reaches $50,000.
The nine boroughs that fund their table directly are maintaining their share, that is, $284,179 in total.
The expense is split between the central city (51%), the agglomeration (32%) and the boroughs (17%); the document indicates no impact on the City's financial framework.
The City's contribution to the tables had not increased since 2011, according to the document.

City council is renewing, for three years starting April 21, 2026, the terms of five people on the Comité consultatif en reconnaissance: Jean-François Leclerc (chair), Isabelle Dumas (vice-chair), Francyne Lord and Paul-André Linteau (members) and Luce Lafontaine (alternate member).
These renewals cannot be extended again, since the limit set out in the committee's by-law is a single renewal.
Imen Ben Jemia, until now an alternate member, moves up to vice-chair, replacing Jacques Thériault-Watso, who left in April 2025.
Doreen Petiquay-Barthold and Elyse Lévesque, also alternates, become members, replacing Rito Joseph (term not renewed) and Bérénice Mollen-Dupuis (leaving March 18, 2026).
The committee gives the City advice on commemorative ceremonies, physical commemoration, place names and certain heritage identification by-laws.
Members' pay comes out of the operating budget of the Service du greffe; no amount is specified.

City council is renewing, for three years with no possibility of a further renewal, the terms of Isabelle Dumas (vice-chair), Francyne Lord and Paul-André Linteau (members) and Luce Lafontaine (alternate member) on the Comité consultatif en reconnaissance, starting June 15, 2026.
Elyse Lévesque moves from alternate member to member, for three years with no renewal, replacing Bérénice Mollen-Dupuis, who left on March 18, 2026.

An earlier executive committee resolution (April 15, 2026) is cancelled, because the chair, Jean-François Leclerc, as well as Imen Ben Jemia and Doreen Petiquay-Barthold, ultimately left or declined the renewal.
The chair position on the committee remains vacant: a new person will be appointed later.
The committee advises the City on commemorative ceremonies, physical commemoration, place naming and heritage identification by-laws.
Members' pay comes out of the operating budget of the Service du greffe; no amount is specified.
City council appoints Audrey Girard, an urban planner, as a member of the Comité Jacques-Viger for a first three-year term, which can be renewed, starting March 23, 2026.
She replaces Laurence Lebeux, an architect, whose term ended on May 14, 2025 and who could not be renewed for a third consecutive time.
The Comité Jacques-Viger advises the City on land development, urban planning, architecture, design and landscape architecture, and gives city council its opinion on changes to the urban plan.

The application came from a public call for candidates held from September 29 to November 5, 2025: 8 people were interviewed on November 18, 1 was selected and 6 were placed in a pool of candidates for future appointments.
The pay for committee members comes out of the operating budget of the Service du greffe; no amount is specified.
City council is renewing the mandate of architect Nicolas Demers-Stoddart as a member of the Comité Jacques-Viger, for a second three-year term starting August 2, 2026.
His first term, which began August 1, 2023, ends August 1, 2026.
The Comité Jacques-Viger advises the City on land development, urban planning, architecture, design and landscape architecture, and gives its opinion to city council on changes to the urban plan.
The committee has nine members, appointed for three years, with the possibility of one consecutive renewal.
The committee's chair, Josée Bérubé, requested this renewal, which Mr. Demers-Stoddart accepted.
Members' pay is already included in the operating budget of the Service du greffe.
The borough of Ville-Marie is paying $35,000 to the Société de développement commercial du Quartier latin for the year 2026.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget and must be used only for the salaries and benefits of staff hired the previous year.
According to the SDC's application, the money will cover the position of responsable administration et intelligence d'affaires.
The grant cannot be used to pay members of the SDC or to recruit staff.
The payment is made within 30 days after the borough council's decision.
For 2026, the SDC du Quartier latin is the only one to have submitted a compliant application; in 2025, the SDC du Village had also received $35,000.

The borough of Ville-Marie is appointing Christiane Rail, Division Head - Aménagement des parcs et actifs immobiliers, as its representative on the board of directors of the Société de développement du Quartier latin.

The law requires the city to appoint an elected official or a municipal employee to the boards of directors of the commercial development corporations in its territory; this power has been delegated to the boroughs.
The term begins as soon as the resolution is adopted, and the appointment will be communicated to the SDC Quartier latin.
She replaces the previous appointee, Jean-Luc L'Archevêque, who was designated in July 2019.
No spending is associated with this decision.
The Ville-Marie borough is releasing $1,442,716.98 from its surplus for its economic development budget in 2026.
The money comes from the City's Service du développement économique, which had already paid it to the borough in 2025; the operation has no impact on the borough's financial framework.
The funds will be used to continue in 2026 projects started in 2025 as part of the Stratégie centre-ville 2030.
Projects covered: social inclusion and the feeling of safety, enhancement of the downtown cleanliness plan, action plan for the quartier chinois, temporary installations and activities in key areas.

The City says it expects more than one billion dollars in investments downtown over ten years, around nine initiatives (neighbourhood identity, new living environments, mobility, cleanliness and green routes).
Earlier decisions of the same type: $2,011,129.73 allocated in February 2025 and several transfers from the Service du développement économique since 2024.

The Ville-Marie borough council authorizes the borough to submit applications for financial assistance to the City in order to boost its commercial areas located outside the territories of the commercial development corporations (sociétés de développement commercial, SDC).
The money comes from a program adopted by city council on April 15, 2025, which sets aside $6.42M to be shared among the 19 boroughs for 2025, 2026 and 2027.

The amounts may be used for economic studies, for recruiting businesses and filling vacant premises, for animation and marketing, for developing public spaces (pedestrianization, small squares, greening, lighting), for training merchants, and for mitigation measures for construction sites lasting more than 6 months.
Submission periods concerned: from May 1 to June 15, 2026, then from August 3 to 7, 2026; from April 30 to June 15, 2027, then from August 9 to 13, 2027.
The program targets commercial streets with at least 30 establishments; the City estimates that about 15,000 businesses are active outside the SDC territories.
Salaries of borough staff, direct assistance to businesses and expenses incurred before approval are not reimbursable.
The borough will have to provide accountability reports and use all of the funds according to the program's schedule.
The borough of Ville-Marie is allowing street food trucks at five public sites, from April 16 to October 31, 2026.
The chosen sites: Square Victoria, Place du Canada, parc Jos-Montferrand, parc du Mont-Royal (avenue du Monument Sir G.E. Cartier) and Place des Montréalaises, with hours from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.
The number of trucks allowed varies from 1 to 3 depending on the location; parc du Mont-Royal is reserved for Saturdays and Sundays, with trucks moved out from September 4 to October 5.
The Association des restaurateurs de rue du Québec (ARRQ) manages the daily assignment of spots and recruits the operators, under an agreement with the Ville.

The ARRQ must check that the trucks comply with the rules (SAAQ, MAPAQ, CNESST, fire safety), make sure they are linked to an active production kitchen in Montréal and hold $3M in liability insurance.
The ARRQ occupies the sites free of charge and must see that the rules on noise, cleanliness and waste management are followed.
The document sets out no spending: the financial section says "n/a".
The borough of Ville-Marie is giving $30,000 to the Société des arts technologiques (SAT) to carry out the Jeu(x) de lumières project.

The installation will be set up at Place de la Paix, in the Quartier des spectacles, and turned on every evening: people interact for free with light projections on the ground through their movements.
The SAT is partnering with community organizations in the Faubourg Saint-Laurent; social mediators will be on site for the entire duration of the installation.
Planned schedule: signing of the agreement in June 2026, public presentation in August-September 2026, review in November 2026. The agreement ends no later than December 31, 2026.
The funding comes from stream 2 of the Programme de soutien financier au développement économique et commercial de Ville-Marie 2025-2027, reserved for non-profit organizations.
The document mentions that the project also receives private funding from other partners.
The borough of Ville-Marie is amending its Programme de soutien financier aux camps de jour (day camp financial support program), which takes effect on April 1, 2026.
The program used to cover the summer only: it now adds a winter component, in particular for the school spring break week.
The support is for day camps for children aged 4 to 12, with age calculated as of September 30 of the current year.

Only non-profit organizations that are recognized and classified as category A in Ville-Marie may apply for the funding; they must hold a certificate of compliance from the Association des camps du Québec.
The money paid out must be used only for day camp programming, not for the daycare service.
The amount is set by the borough after reviewing each project, on a yearly basis, with the possibility of renewal depending on the results report.
Organizations must give priority to borough residents, keep their fees affordable and agree to observation visits during the camps.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $30,000 to six organizations to run day camps during spring break week, from March 2 to 6, 2026.

The amounts: Association sportive et communautaire du Centre-Sud $9,973, Corporation du Centre Jean-Claude Malépart $9,715, Go jeunesse $2,979, Centre communautaire de loisirs Sainte-Catherine d'Alexandrie $2,714, Centre récréatif Poupart $2,703, Association les Chemins du soleil $1,916.
This is the first time the borough has provided financial support for the spring break period: the day camp program is being expanded to include a winter component.
The borough points to the rise in registrations and in costs (wages, training, materials, safety standards), which limit the organizations' capacity.
The money was divided proportionally, using the same calculation as for the summer day camps, and comes from the operating budget of the Division des sports et loisirs.
The six organizations must follow the day camp reference framework of the Association des camps du Québec and take part in the borough's day camp roundtable.
The borough of Ville-Marie is accepting a $5,000 grant from Sport et Loisir de l'île de Montréal, under the « Ça bouge sur l'île » program set up with the ministère de l'Éducation.
The money will help pay for part of the free physical activity and recreation programming at the centre Sanaaq, in the Peter-McGill district.

The planned activities: zumba (16 and over), chair yoga (55 and over), hip-hop (12-17 years), parent-baby yoga (0-18 months) and a motor skills space (parents and children aged 2 to 5), offered through registration sessions.
The amount will cover suppliers' fees for the supervised sessions as well as the purchase of equipment and materials.

The document notes that the Peter-McGill district lacks municipal sports facilities, that one third of residents live below the low-income threshold and that 36.4% of the population is immigrant (2021 census).
The goods and services related to the file will be provided during the year 2026.
In 2023, the borough had accepted $9,990 from the same organization for the Plein air d'hiver de Ville-Marie project.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $234,130 to six organizations to run day camps in the summer of 2026 for children aged 4 to 12.
The camps will run from June 22 to August 21, 2026, with room for 852 children per week across the borough.

Breakdown: Association sportive et communautaire du Centre-Sud $79,153, Corporation du Centre Jean-Claude Malépart $61,318, Go jeunesse $26,411, Centre récréatif Poupart $24,110, Centre communautaire de loisirs Sainte-Catherine d'Alexandrie $22,090, Association les Chemins du soleil $21,048.
The total funding goes from $164,308 in 2025 to $234,130 in 2026, which the borough explains by the rise in registrations and in costs (wages, training, materials, safety).
The money comes from the borough's budget, after a reallocation of the elected officials' discretionary fund.
The organizations must follow the day camp reference framework of the Association des camps du Québec and provide training to their camp leader teams.
The organizations will submit their registration and attendance reports by September 30, 2026, and a full report by December 1, 2026.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving $60,000 to six organizations to welcome children with special needs at municipal day camps during the summer of 2026.

The amounts: $20,130 to the Association sportive et communautaire du Centre-Sud, $9,117 to the Association les Chemins du soleil, $8,529 to the Corporation du Centre Jean-Claude Malépart, $8,367 to the Centre récréatif Poupart, $7,790 to the Centre communautaire de loisirs Sainte-Catherine d'Alexandrie and $6,067 to Go jeunesse.
The money is used to hire support workers: 41 people to welcome up to 65 children per week living with a functional limitation.
The amount is double the $30,000 of previous years; the borough explains that it reallocated the elected officials' discretionary fund.
The camps run from June 22 to August 21, 2026, and the organizations must submit their registration and attendance reports by September 30, 2026.
Most of the children come from Ville-Marie, but some organizations also welcome children from Rosemont, Saint-Michel and other boroughs.
The money comes from the operating budget of the borough's Division des sports et loisirs.
The borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville is asking city council to hand over to it the preparation and approval of a lease with the organization Îlot 84.
The lease would cover a 78,244-square-foot piece of land at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade.
Îlot 84 would hold activities there for the business community and residents of the District central.
The land would be loaned free of charge for two seven-month periods, from April 1 to October 31, in 2026 and in 2027.
No money is committed at this stage: the borough will later submit an estimate of the impacts of the rent along with the draft lease.
Îlot 84 has occupied this land since 2019, after winning a call for tenders; the free loan for 2024-2025 was equivalent to a real estate subsidy of $596,088.87.
The borough council adopted this request unanimously on March 16, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is paying out $75,000 in total: $37,500 to Entre Parents de Montréal-Nord and $37,500 to Institut Pacifique.
The money is used to run activities at the Espace Jeunesse de l'Ouest, on rue Monselet, with structured activities for children aged 6 to 12.
The programming covers the period from April 2026 to June 2027, in the western sector of the borough.
The organizations must provide qualified activity leaders, safe supervision, and produce follow-up reports.
The payments are staggered: 50% no later than April 25, 2026, 40% after the progress report (November 30, 2026) and 10% after the final report (July 30, 2027).
The expense is taken from the borough's operating budget.
Montréal-Nord is hiring Soucy Aquatik inc. to replace the filter media in its four outdoor pools, for $90,087.80 including taxes, plus $9,008.78 in contingencies, for a total of $99,096.58.
The company was the lowest compliant bidder in price request no. 2026-110, held from March 23 to April 2, 2026.
The money comes from the borough's financial reserve (surplus); the net cost is $90,488.39.
The work is scheduled between May 5 and June 15, 2026, with start-up and delivery of the compliance documents on June 15.
The sand is being replaced with recycled crushed glass, which the borough links to less drinking water and less energy used when the filters are washed.
According to the borough, keeping the worn filter media would risk leading to water that does not meet standards and to temporary or extended pool closures.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is appointing Lucie Bazit as assistant in recreation programming, in the Division des sports et loisirs, effective April 18, 2026.
