The position becomes permanent if she successfully completes the probationary period set out in the collective agreement for municipal civil servants (SCFP 429).
The position was vacant and was posted internally within the City from March 20 to 26, 2026.
The role involves supporting the development officers: permits, rental of sports facilities, facility tours, schedules for rooms and equipment, and planning of sporting events.
Expected cost from April 18 to December 31, 2026: $61,000 ($45,800 in salary, $1,300 in premiums and adjustments, $13,900 in payroll taxes) for 1,295 hours.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the filing of an application for financial assistance from the Government of Québec to build the Complexe aquatique et sportif de Montréal-Nord.
The application goes through the Programme d'aide financière aux infrastructures récréatives, sportives et de plein air (PAFIRSPA-2026), launched on February 23 by the ministère de l'Éducation.
The director of culture, sports, recreation and social development is filing the application with the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports, which then forwards it to Québec.
The borough points to a lack of facilities: the ratio of facilities per resident is below the Québec average, especially for swimming pools and gymnasiums.
The document notes that 30% of Montréal-Nord's population is under 29 years old and 25% is 55 years old and over, in an area of 11 km².
The borough of Montréal-Nord is giving a total of $61,648 to local organizations to carry out projects in 2026.
The money comes from the Programme Initiatives et projets spéciaux, which is tied to the Politique de reconnaissance des OBNL adopted in December 2023.
Each project could receive up to $4,999; applications were accepted from January 27 to February 13, 2026.
The amounts granted range from $300 to $5,000 per organization, including to Cercle du 3e Âge, Entre Parents, Halte-Femmes and Baseball mineur Montréal-Nord.
The funded projects include a forum on housing, intercultural picnics, a street basketball tournament, school backpacks and dinners for seniors.
The budget envelope has been used up: there will be no second call for projects in 2026.
The selected organizations will have to submit an activity report to the borough once their project is completed.
The borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is reorganizing its internal structure as of April 18, 2026.
The Direction du bureau de projets et du développement des services aux citoyens is being abolished.
Two positions are being eliminated: a director position and an executive secretary position.

Several units are changing bosses: technical expertise moves to public works, technical services for facilities move to culture, sports, recreation and social development, and park development and real estate assets move to the Direction d'arrondissement.
The Section de la transition écologique et de la résilience moves under the Direction de l'aménagement urbain et des services aux entreprises.
The reception, information and customer service counter now reports to the clerk's office, which becomes the Division des relations avec les citoyens et du greffe.
The borough says the change is justified by administrative consistency, coordination between units and resource management.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $94,884 to thirteen cultural organizations under the Programme de soutien aux actions culturelles 2026.
The amounts range from $3,000 (Maison de la poésie de Montréal) to $12,000 (La Compagnie Marie Chouinard and La Compagnie Des Autres).

The supported projects take place in parks, alleys and public squares in Le Plateau: Square Saint-Louis, parc Jeanne-Mance, parc Baldwin, parc Lahaie, Milton-Parc and boulevard Saint-Laurent, among others.

They include dance, circus and clown shows, outdoor concerts, sound installations, theatrical mural tours and two parades (Parade Phénoménale on October 3, 2026, and Parade du FAR on September 2, 2026).
The budget set aside for the program was $95,000; 32 projects were submitted during the call for projects held from November 3, 2025 to February 2, 2026, and 13 were selected.
The borough council is also approving the thirteen agreements and authorizing the borough mayor and the borough secretary to sign them.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is giving $20,000 to three organizations to create murals in 2026.
MU is receiving $5,000 for a wall at 2296, avenue du Mont-Royal Est (east wall).
MilMurs Production is receiving $7,500 for the north wall at 3950, rue Drolet, facing parc Jean-Jacques-Olier.
AvangArtiste is receiving $7,500 for the north wall at 4438, rue Boyer, facing the Place des Fleurs-de-Macadam.
Six projects had been submitted during the call for projects held from November 3, 2025 to February 3, 2026; the evaluation committee selected three of them on February 11, 2026.
The murals and the reporting must be completed in 2026.
The Programme Muralité, in place since 2014, aims to beautify the urban landscape, prevent vandalism and support artistic creation.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is paying $17,500, including all applicable taxes, to Maison de l'amitié de Montréal for the Duluth en arts 2026 event.
The neighbourhood music festival puts on two concerts every Saturday, from July 4 to August 22, 2026 (8 Saturdays).
The concerts take place at four spots on avenue Duluth: at the corners of Saint-Laurent, de Bullion, Saint-Denis and Berri.
Avenue Duluth will be made pedestrian-only between boulevard Saint-Laurent and rue Saint-Hubert from June 16 to October 14, 2026, including setup and takedown.
The money comes from the operating budget of the borough's Division des études techniques.
The organization must finish the project and hand in its accounting report in 2026; the money is paid out according to the terms of an agreement.
In 2025, the contribution for the same event was $15,000.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the 2025 residual materials report and the accountability report for the 2020-2025 Master Plan.
None of the six targets were met: Montrealers generated 415 kg of waste per person (target: 399 kg) and 48% of materials were diverted from disposal (target: 70%).
The recovery rate for recyclable materials reached 66% (target: 75%) and the rate for organic materials reached 40% (target: 60%).
Recovery costs $414 per tonne, compared with an updated target of less than $274 per tonne.
Of the 49 actions in the Master Plan, 29 are completed, 12 partially completed and 8 cancelled, the latter because the management of recyclable materials was transferred to Éco Entreprises Québec.
The report details the quantities recovered and disposed of by borough and by related city, as well as the activity of the seven écocentres.
The satisfaction rate among surveyed residents stands at 73%, for a target of 75%.
The Tricentris cooperative will pay the City $43,773.61 (taxes included) to fund a free lending program for neighbourhood events.
The program offers three turnkey services: lending, delivery and washing of reusable dishes; lending and installation of mobile water fountains; and lending of equipment for sorting stations.
Neighbourhood parties organized by boroughs or by community groups will be able to benefit from it during the 2026 summer season.
The program is offered until the financial contribution runs out, and no later than December 31, 2026.
Participating boroughs will choose which events benefit and will handle local coordination; if equipment is damaged or not returned, they will be billed for its replacement.
The Service de l'environnement et de la transition écologique manages the contractual and financial side; an additional budget of revenues and expenditures of $38,072.29 is authorized for it.
The City justifies the project by the reduction at source of single-use items, in line with its "Montréal, zéro déchet 2030" strategy.
The City is adding $25,086.12 to the fees of the law firm Racicot Chandonnet, which is representing it against the contractor Nahtac Constructions inc.
The legal services contract thus rises from $389,448.65 to $414,534.77, taxes included, since it was awarded in December 2019.
The dispute concerns work to replace the bracing on the pont Jacques-Bizard, a contract worth $1,379,008.14 at the time of the bid.
In February 2024, the Superior Court ordered the City to pay $233,296.34 to Nahtac and dismissed its counterclaim of $48,759.46.
Nahtac appealed the judgment, the City filed a cross-appeal, and the hearing took place on December 17, 2025.
The cost overrun is mainly due to higher-than-expected disbursements, longer transcripts and an explanatory letter required by the Court of Appeal.
The expense is paid entirely by the urban agglomeration, since the bridge is considered an infrastructure of collective interest.

The Ville-Marie borough is suing two companies, Lemay CO inc. (successor to the architecture firm Cardinal Hardy Beinhaker) and the contractor G. Giuliani inc., over design and workmanship errors in the construction of the belvédère du Chemin-qui-Marche, in the parc linéaire de la Commune.
The work, carried out in 2011-2012, was provisionally accepted on June 21, 2012. A report received in September 2023 found rotten wood, a lack of ventilation and drainage problems.
Excavation work also revealed that a French drain shown on the plans was missing, and that some drains had been made unusable because they were covered with a waterproofing membrane.

The deterioration means the structure must be completely dismantled and excavation work carried out; a repair contract worth $3,486,731.85 (including taxes, contingencies and incidental costs) was awarded to 2633-2312 Québec inc. (Arthier) in February 2026, and the work is under way.
The City estimates the cost of the work caused by the defects at about $2,000,000 plus taxes, and is claiming that amount in damages.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to file the lawsuit; the court file number is still to come.
The City is increasing the budget for the assistance program for independent performance venues with fewer than 1,000 seats, from $855,757 to $2,655,757.
The money is divided as follows: $855,757 in 2025, $900,000 in 2026 and $900,000 in 2027, including management fees of $54,000 per year.
The program is extended until December 31, 2027, and organizations will be able to submit new applications.
New submission deadlines: 20 business days after the order comes into force for 2026, and from March 1 to 31, 2027 for 2027.

Eligible venues must have programmed and published at least 35 shows in the year before the application; the assistance reaches a maximum of $40,000 for a single operator and $100,000 for a group of three or more operators, up to 90% of the project cost.
The funds are managed by the PME MTL hubs, in particular Centre-Est, Centre-Ville and Grand Sud-Ouest, and come from the $200M agreement with the ministère de l'Économie.
Expected timeline: adoption and distribution in May 2026, receipt of applications in June 2026.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is awarding Conception PLHP inc. a contract of $701,150.61 (taxes included) to build planted, water-absorbing sidewalk extensions in 2026.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,146,660.43: the contract, contingencies ($105,172.59), quantity variations ($70,115.06) and related costs ($270,222.17).
Fourteen sidewalk extensions will be built at five intersections: Chabot/Bélanger, 13e Avenue/Bagot, 15e Avenue/Beaubien, 23e Avenue/Beaubien and Jeanne-D'Arc/Laurier.
The goal stated in the file: make the area safer and calm traffic near schools.

Three firms are getting contracts tied to the work site: IGF Axiom (supervision, $175,273.64), Les Services EXP (materials testing, $29,955.97) and Geninovation (environmental monitoring, $23,631.96).
The work is to start between the end of May and the beginning of June 2026 and finish in September.
Funding combines a local loan by-law, the borough's 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program and two editions of the City's participatory budget ("Capteurs de pluie" and "Oasis urbaines").
The five Espace pour la vie museums (Biodôme, Planétarium, Jardin botanique, Insectarium and Biosphère) will open free of charge on February 28, 2026, the evening of Nuit blanche.
The City is issuing two fee orders to make this access free: one for the City's four museums, and one for the Biosphère (agglomeration).
The City is approving an agreement with Festival Montréal en Lumière inc., which is organizing the 23rd edition of Nuit blanche as part of the festival held from February 27 to March 7, 2026.

Each museum will offer nighttime programming: a DJ and a visit at the Insectarium, a musical experience in the Jardin botanique greenhouses, dome shows and telescopes at the Planétarium, a journey through the ecosystems at the Biodôme, and exhibitions and music at the Biosphère.
The festival will produce the promotional materials using the content provided by Espace pour la vie; photos and videos taken on site may be used for promotion.
Espace pour la vie is organizing the activities at its sites and must provide attendance statistics and a survey after the event.
The summary does not show any amount in the financial aspects section.

The City is awarding, without a call for tenders, to Amis du Jardin botanique de Montréal the role of point of sale for the Passeport Espace pour la vie, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with two one-year renewal options.
It will pay the organization fees estimated at $1,160,000 including taxes ($380,000 in 2026, $386,600 in 2027, $393,400 in 2028), paid 100% by the central city.
In 2026, the fees are $48.95 per solo Passeport sold, $93 per multi Passeport and $24.37 per additional child.

Passeport price in 2026: $87 for one adult, $155 for two adults and three children aged 5 to 17, $32.50 per additional child; it gives unlimited access to the five museums for one year and 15% discounts in the shops and restaurants.
The organization must remit to the City the amounts collected and a detailed statement of account on April 30, August 31 and December 31 of each year; the City pays within the following 30 days.
If the organization's revenues (fees plus annual cards) do not reach $633,021 in 2026, the City makes up the difference; the same principle will apply in 2027 and 2028.
The City estimates the revenues from these sales at $1,475,000 over three years; people who buy their Passeport from the organization become members of it free of charge.

The City is giving the Société d'astronomie du Planétarium de Montréal, a non-profit organization, the mandate to sell the Passeport Espace pour la vie from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028, with two one-year renewal options.
It will pay the organization fees estimated at $33,000, taxes included ($10,700 in 2026, $11,000 in 2027, $11,300 in 2028), paid entirely by the central city.

In return, the Société must hand over to the City all the money it collects, along with a detailed statement of account three times a year: April 30, August 31 and December 31. The City expects revenues of $35,000 over three years.

Passeport prices in 2026: $87 for one adult, $155 for two adults and three children aged 5 to 17, $32.50 for each additional child. It gives unlimited access to the five Espace pour la vie museums for one year, plus 15% off at the shop and the restaurant.
If its combined revenues (fees and annual cards) do not reach $19,661.88 in 2026, the City will make up the difference. The same principle will apply in 2027 and 2028.
People who buy their Passeport from the Société become members of it free of charge.
According to the City, this mechanism has been in place since 2021 to prevent the Passeport from causing the museums' friends societies to lose members and revenue.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is paying $611,082.75, taxes included, for surface landscaping work attached to the Saint-Jacques retention basin project (15,000 m³) led by the Service de l'eau.
The work affects rue des Seigneurs, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Quesnel and rue Coursol, between rue des Seigneurs and rue Georges-Vanier.
On the menu: 3 draining green curb extensions, 3 planted curb extensions, 8 planting pits, planted strips along rue des Seigneurs, and safety improvements at intersections.
The sidewalk and an outdated fire hydrant on the north side of rue des Seigneurs will be redone, and two traffic lights will be moved at the intersection of des Seigneurs and Saint-Jacques.
The amount breaks down into $531,376.30 for the work and $79,706.45 (15%) in contingencies; the expense net of tax rebates is $558,000.
The contract is expected to be awarded to Roxboro Excavation inc. by the urban agglomeration council on April 20, 2026; the work would run from June 2026 to December 2027.
According to the document, the basin will aim to reduce overflows into the fleuve Saint-Laurent and the risks of sewer backups and flooding.
The borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is changing four stretches of parking reserved for police vehicles.
Rue Villeneuve, east of avenue du Parc (north side): stopping becomes prohibited at all times, except for police vehicles, to allow the installation of bollards protecting the bike lane.

Two police-reserved zones near the De L'Étincelle elementary school, on avenue Van Horne and avenue de l'Esplanade (32 metres each), are being removed: students are dropped off directly in the schoolyard by a transportation provider.
A 13-metre zone on avenue de l'Hôtel-de-Ville, south of avenue Laurier Est, is being removed following the departure of PDQ 37 and the SPVM's Éclipse unit.
Removing these three zones gives parking spaces back to residents.
The order will be adopted in March 2026 and the signs installed in April 2026, with "Nouvelle signalisation" (new signage) tabs in place for 30 days.
Signage costs will be charged to the borough as inter-unit charges, with no amount specified.
The City is awarding the maintenance of its Cisco network equipment to two companies for 36 months, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029, for a total of $1,085,194.61, taxes included.
Bell Canada is awarded lot 1 (equipment of the Service des technologies de l'information) at $864,754.49; ITI inc. is awarded lot 2 (equipment of the Service de l'eau) at $220,440.12.
The contracts cover software updates, security patches and technical support for a network of more than 8,000 pieces of equipment.
This includes the devices that run the MTLWifi network in administrative buildings, libraries and arenas, as well as those in the drinking water and wastewater treatment plants.
Two of the six firms that obtained the tender documents submitted bids; the prices retained are below the City's estimates (-5.34% for lot 1, -12.45% for lot 2).
The City will evaluate Bell Canada's performance; an evaluation of ITI inc.'s performance is not considered necessary, as the risk is assessed as low.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council.

The City is buying 150 perpetual Windows Server licences and 8 SQL Server licences from Compugen inc., without a call for tenders, through the firm's agreement with the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales.
The contract is worth $490,152.36, taxes included, based on the service offer dated February 24, 2026, with a contingency budget of $73,522.86, for a total expense of $563,675.22.
These licences maintain the usage and upgrade rights for the City's Microsoft infrastructure servers.
The City operates more than 900 virtual and physical servers based on Microsoft technologies.
These servers support applications such as M-IRIS for police operations, the SPVM's licence plate recognition, SERAM's geolocation, the AFIS system and call dispatching.
The urban agglomeration is covering 70.71% of the expense, or $398,588.49.
The director of infrastructure and operations at the Service des technologies de l'information is authorized to sign the contract documents.
The City is awarding Solutions Necando inc. a contract of $313,903.72 (taxes included) for technical support of MongoDB database licences.
The contract covers 36 months, from June 5, 2026 to June 4, 2029, paid in three annual instalments of $99,572.95, $104,551.59 and $109,779.18.
These licences run services such as the montreal.ca portal, alerts to the public, citizen files and guilty pleas at the municipal court.
The contract includes 24/7 support with a one-hour response time, security updates and database monitoring tools.
Two companies submitted bids out of four that obtained the tender documents; the other bid was $899,104.90.
The average annual cost drops from $216,522.67 to $104,634.57 compared with the 2023-2026 contract, a decrease of 51.67%.
The expense is charged to the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is allowing five public activities to temporarily depart from the by-laws on noise, sales on public property and signage.
The exemptions allow outdoor music and loudspeakers, the sale of food, non-alcoholic drinks and promotional items, as well as the installation of signs and banners.
Three chalet activity projects run throughout 2026 at parc Ignace-Bourget, parc De la Vérendrye, parc Oscar-Peterson and parc Saint-Gabriel, with schedules that change from season to season.
The Fête Hivernale takes place on February 21, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at parc De la Vérendrye (cancelled in case of bad weather).
The Party de fermeture de Ma Côte Newman takes place on March 7 and 8, 2026, from 9:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., at parc Ignace-Bourget (held rain or shine).
The organizations involved are Centre de loisirs Monseigneur Pigeon, Atelier 850, Loisirs et Culture Sud-Ouest and Concertation Ville-Émard et Côte St-Paul.
The costs of City services to support these events are absorbed within existing operating budgets; the events are free.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing 25 public events on public property between June 11 and September 26, 2026.
Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors, sell food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages and promotional items, and put up signs and banners, despite the usual by-laws.

Some streets will be closed to vehicles, including rue de la Montagne, Wellington and Saint-Patrick on June 18 (Course Fondation CH) and Notre-Dame between Atwater and Vinet from July 10 to 12 (À l'Ouest de la Dame).
The parks involved include Angrignon, Oscar-Peterson, Le Ber, Mary-Griffin, Ignace-Bourget, d'Argenson, Campbell-Ouest, Daisy-Peterson-Sweeney, des Jazzmen and de l'Ancienne-cour-de-triage.

Among the activities: Fête nationale and Canada Day, Fête de quartier Saint-Henri, Théâtre La Roulotte, toy-lending libraries and a pumptrack in the summer, and the Mary-Griffin public square from June 15 to October 31.
The events are free and open to everyone; the City will cover the required services out of the operating budgets of the departments concerned.
A public notice announcing the ordinances will be published on the borough's website.
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is giving $25,000 to the organization Festival sur le Canal for its 2026 edition.
The festival will take place on June 19, 20 and 21, 2026.
It is a free cultural festival that the borough has supported since 2011.
The contribution is paid entirely by the borough, with no money from the central city.
An agreement sets out the payment conditions, the reporting requirements and a visibility protocol that the organization must follow.
The amount is higher than in 2024 and 2023 ($20,000) and is the same as in 2025 ($25,000).
The borough of Le Sud-Ouest is authorizing 15 free public events on public property, from July 13 to October 31, 2026.
Organizers will be allowed to broadcast sound outdoors, sell food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages and promotional items, and put up signs or banners at the planned sites and times.
Some streets will be closed to vehicles, including rue Acorn (between de Courcelle and Saint-Rémi) on August 14 and boulevard Monk (between Jolicoeur and Jacques-Hertel) on October 3.

Among the locations affected: parcs Angrignon, Vinet, Le Ber, Ignace-Bourget, Madeleine-Parent, Mary-Griffin, du Bassin-à-Bois, Daisy-Peterson-Sweeney, Sainte-Anne de Griffintown and square Sir-George-Étienne-Cartier.
Parc Mary-Griffin will host a public square every day from 12 p.m. to 9 p.m., from July 13 to October 31, 2026.
The costs of the City's services to support these events are paid out of existing operating budgets.
A public notice announcing these authorizations will be published on the borough's website.
The City is extending its agreement with Sécuro Vision inc. by 24 months (two 12-month periods) to supply prescription safety glasses to employees, from April 29, 2026 to April 28, 2028.
It is authorizing an additional expense of $236,552.50 (no applicable taxes), which brings the total value of the agreement from $150,820.71 to $387,373.21.
The estimate includes $205,697.83 in planned purchases plus $30,854.67 (15%) for possible variations in quantity; the City is not required to purchase these quantities.
Prices will be indexed on the anniversary date according to the Consumer Price Index, with an increase of about 3% expected.
The agreement is available to all business units and boroughs, which will pay out of their own budgets, as their needs arise.
The City cites its collective agreements and health and safety standards, which require it to provide personal protective equipment to employees.
The glasses have a lifespan of 2 years and replace disposable glasses, which the City links to its zero waste objective.
The executive committee approves an expense of $3,372.93 for Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada's trip to Seoul and Busan, South Korea, from March 13 to 21, 2026.
The mayor led an economic and cultural mission organized by the Chambre de commerce du Montréal métropolitain, in collaboration with the Conseil des arts de Montréal.
Stated goals: create business partnerships, strengthen ties with the cities of Seoul and Busan, and promote Montréal's cultural and creative industries in Asia.
Breakdown of the costs: $1,854.91 for transportation, $1,205.54 for accommodation, $152.91 for baggage, $116.36 for meals and $43.21 for carbon credits.
The expense is paid entirely by the central city, out of the budget already planned by the Division du soutien aux personnes élues.
The City will offset the greenhouse gases from the flight (1.4402 tonnes) through its carbon credit purchase program.
A balance of $987.26 remains to be reimbursed to the person who took the trip.
The borough of Ville-Marie is entrusting the operation, programming and upkeep of the Café Viger, at 420, avenue Viger Est (square Viger), to the organization Festival Yasolo, Fierté noir Montréal.
The contract runs for 31 months, from May 1, 2026 to November 30, 2028, with an option to renew for two years; the opening is targeted for June 2026.
The City is authorizing a maximum expenditure of $20,000, taxes included, payable in 2026.
The City is also lending the premises free of charge until December 31, 2027: a 1,360 sq. ft. space and a 253 sq. ft. office, an estimated value of $51,616 per year.
The café must offer drinks and fresh food, cultural programming and a clean, safe place, and must develop a self-sufficient business plan.
The contract is being awarded by direct agreement following a call for proposals launched on February 10, 2026, which received five proposals.
Reviews are planned for November 2026 (mid-season) and April 2027 (year 1).
The Ville-Marie borough is extending until June 30, 2026 the contracts of three organizations that provide community mediation services in public spaces.
For these two extra months, it is paying $237,585.60, including taxes if applicable, which brings the total value of the contracts from $1,371,461.66 to $1,609,047.26.
The three organizations are L'Anonyme U.I.M. ($67,624.20), Groupe communautaire l'Itinéraire ($71,226) and Société de développement social ($98,735.40).

The team has 13 workers: L'Anonyme covers the area bounded by Saint-Hubert/Papineau/Sherbrooke/René-Lévesque, Société de développement social covers the Quartier des spectacles, the Quartier chinois and place Émilie-Gamelin, and l'Itinéraire covers square Cabot and the area around the Lucien-L'Allier metro station.
The borough explains that discussions on funding and on the project's parameters for 2026 are not finished, and that it wants to avoid an interruption in service.
The project, launched in May 2025 as a pilot project, had already been extended until March 31, and then until April 30, 2026.

The borough of Verdun is approving the plans to rebuild part of the parking lot at 1240, rue Moffat, a property owned by the Centre de services scolaire Marguerite-Bourgeoys (a former school that became a vocational training centre).
The parking lot will have 39 spaces for employees, including 4 with electric charging stations, plus 7 bicycle spaces in an alcove of the building.
Five trees and shrubs on public property along rue Manning will be cut down; 15 large-canopy trees, 2 ginkgos and 27 shrubs will be planted.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with 6 conditions: narrower traffic lanes, more tree canopy, a continuous pedestrian link from rue Moffat, larger native plantings, effective lighting under the trees and well-lit bicycle areas.
According to the borough, the modified plans that were submitted meet these conditions; the non-binding recommendations (keeping certain trees, removing concrete curbs) were not followed.
The file is going to the borough council because the value of the work is above the threshold for a delegated decision.
The City is awarding Systematix Technologies de l'Information inc. professional services in Oracle Application Express for a maximum of $1,310,505.75, taxes included.
The master agreement runs for 36 months, with two possible 12-month extensions at $436,834.12 per year, with prices adjusted according to the consumer price index.

The services cover the development, updating and support of City applications, including Infra 360 (road network projects) and FinPro (financial management and purchase orders at the wastewater treatment plant).
Three firms out of 10 that took out the tender documents submitted bids; Systematix obtained the best final score.
The selected price is 24.18% lower than the City's latest estimate ($1,728,488.16).

No budget is set aside in advance: each assignment will be paid through purchase orders out of the budgets of the Service des TI, the Service de l'eau and the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier.
The City will assess the firm's performance during the contract.
The City is adding $29,177.93 (taxes included) to the technical support contract for the WebFocus software awarded to Cloud Software Group, bringing the total to $224,022.16.
This additional amount does not pay for any new services: the taxes had been left out when the contract was approved in December 2024.
The maintenance and support contract for the WebFocus licences covers the period from December 31, 2024 to December 30, 2027.
WebFocus is used to produce dashboards and data reports; more than 238 employees use it, in particular in Finances, Ressources humaines and IT.
The expense is paid out of the operating budget of the Service des technologies de l'information, with no impact on the City's financial framework.
The decision rests with the urban agglomeration council; the director of the Direction Gestion du territoire des TI will be able to sign the contract documents.

The City is entering into a 24-month master agreement with AFI par Edgenda inc. to design and deliver a business analysis training program for information technology teams, for a maximum of $127,737.23, taxes included.
The agreement may be extended by 24 months for an equivalent amount of $127,737.23, adjusted according to the consumer price index.
Only one company bid on this lot; six companies that obtained the tender documents withdrew, citing among other things a lack of time and the absence of accreditations or trainers.
After negotiation, the price went from $136,705.28 to $127,737.23, which is $8,968.05 less, but it remains 10.55% above the City's estimate ($115,549.88).

The two other lots in the call for tenders (project management and control, agility at scale) were not awarded: the bids were non-compliant or below the 70% pass mark, and a new purchasing strategy will be studied.
No budget is set aside in advance: each training session will be paid for out of the existing budgets of the departments that request it.
The City officially designates the "Fleury Est, between rue Chambord and rue Garnier" area as a zone affected by major infrastructure work.
The recognized work period runs from October 20, 2025 to May 14, 2027.
This designation makes SDC Promenade Fleury eligible for the City's subsidy program (by-law 25-009).
The SDC will be able to apply for money under two components: preparing for the construction site before it begins, and then maintaining customer traffic during the work.
Eligible expenses include cleanliness, greening, beautification, signage, construction site coverings, advertising, events and measures to fill vacant premises.
Funding for the program had already been approved by city council on March 18, 2025, with a reserve of $6,500,000 for the entire 2025-2027 program.
The City is transferring $667,250 to the borough of Ville-Marie to bring life to and redevelop the Quartier latin: $333,625 in 2026 and $333,625 in 2027.
The money comes from the $200M agreement with the ministère de l'Économie du Québec (the "Réflexe 3" component).
The regular pedestrianization of rue Saint-Denis is being put on hold in 2026 and 2027, because the street has to stay open to traffic due to the major STM construction work.
The borough, together with the SDC du Quartier latin, is planning greening, street furniture, signage, cleanliness, security and welcome teams, and cultural programming.
Schedule: plans finalized in spring 2026, activation in summer 2026, review in fall 2026, renewal in 2027 depending on how the construction work progresses.
Any amount not spent by December 1 must be returned to the Service du développement économique; no carry-over is allowed.
If the borough cancels the project, it will have to repay the amounts received.

The City is adding $1,000,000 to component 2 of its support program for commercial development corporations (sociétés de développement commercial, SDC) for 2026, bringing the funding for this component to $2,000,000 that year (compared with $1,000,000 in 2025 and in 2027).
The money comes from the Entente Réflexe 3 between the City and the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie.
For 2026, the maximum grant per SDC goes from $350,000 to $700,000, with a minimum of $200,000; the limit tied to each SDC's membership fee revenues stays in place.
SDCs will have to submit an update to their grant application and the required documents by June 30, 2026; payments will follow the review.
The City links this increase to its Centre-Ville 2030 strategy and is targeting projects that draw visitors and foot traffic; it mentions the downtown SDCs.
Without this decision, the Service du développement économique says it could not pay out the grants to the SDCs for 2026 and 2027.
City council is giving $337,000 to two boroughs: $173,000 to Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and $164,000 to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
The money is being used to boost activity on commercial streets that are not covered by a Société de développement commercial (SDC).
Areas covered: Sherbrooke Ouest, avenue Monkland, avenues Victoria and Van Horne, as well as Villeray Est, boulevard Saint-Michel, Parc-Extension and rue Saint-Hubert.

At the same time, the executive committee is authorizing $659,000 for six other boroughs (Outremont, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Verdun, Lachine), for a total of $996,000.
The money comes from a $6.42M envelope set aside in April 2025 for the 19 boroughs from 2025 to 2027.
Timeline: transfers and first expenses in the summer of 2026, projects to be completed by the spring of 2027, and reporting in the fall of 2027.
According to the City, the projects may include entertainment activities, improvements on public property and recruiting businesses for vacant premises.
The City is transferring $1,040,000 to 10 boroughs to boost commercial streets that are not covered by a Société de développement commercial (SDC).

The amounts: LaSalle $127,000, Ville-Marie $125,000, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve $113,000, Saint-Léonard $111,000, Pierrefonds-Roxboro $106,000, Montréal-Nord $105,000, Anjou $94,000, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles $93,000, Le Sud-Ouest $91,000, L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève $75,000.

The targeted areas include avenue Chaumont, avenue Dollard, rue Ontario Est, rue Fleury Est, boulevard de Pierrefonds, Vieux-Pointe-aux-Trembles, rue Jarry Est, the Quartier chinois and the Quartier des spectacles.
The money comes from a $6.42M envelope set aside for 2025-2027, funded by the Réflexe agreement with the Government of Québec.
The boroughs can use the funds for activities and entertainment, work on public property, or recruiting businesses to fill vacant premises.
The transfers are planned for summer 2026, the projects must be completed by spring 2027, and the accountability report is due in fall 2027.
The program targets about 15,000 Montréal businesses located outside SDC territories.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the expansion of a split-level house at 5623, boulevard Maurice-Duplessis.
The work adds one storey plus a one-storey addition with a basement toward the backyard, for a total of 169 m², with a final building height of 8.25 metres.
The cladding will be charcoal-coloured stone (front and rear walls), brick and graphite steel (side walls); trees will be planted in the front and back yards.
The owner must provide a financial guarantee of $37,375, which is 5% of the value of the work.
The work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; the outdoor landscaping must be finished before the permit's validity ends.
The urban planning advisory committee recommended the project favourably on February 4, 2026; approval by the borough council is scheduled for March 9, 2026.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing a housing facility for people in unstable housing situations at 11411, avenue des Récollets, in an existing building (a former rooming house), near boulevard Pie-IX and boulevard Henri-Bourassa and parc Pilon.
After concerns raised by residents at the public consultation on March 25, 2026, the capacity is being reduced from 50 to 30 places.
Only uses related to housing are allowed: bedrooms, kitchen, dining room, common room, washrooms, plus offices for support workers or administration.
Staff must be present 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with psychosocial support on site.
The operator must inform the neighbourhood through a communications plan, do a cleanliness round every day and maintain the green spaces.
Any mechanical equipment added on the roof will have to be hidden by an opaque screen.
The work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void; any change of operator or any different project (type of housing, number of beds) requires a new application.

The borough of Montréal-Nord is retroactively approving changes made during the construction of a three-storey mixed-use building with 15 units and one business on the ground floor, at 4750, boulevard Gouin Est.

The building, completed in 2025, differs from the plans approved in 2023. Some of the differences are accepted as they are: the setback of part of the building on the rue Éthier side, the balcony handrails, the door and window models, the windows at the entrance and the corner windows.

The developer must correct three items: remove the stairway to the basement that was installed without authorization facing rue Éthier, replace the stucco at the main entrance with grey-black metal panels, and install the missing balconies.
The corrective work, including the landscaping, must be finished within 18 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void and the guarantee is not refunded.
Of the $450,000 financial guarantee deposited on May 30, 2022, the borough is releasing $225,000 and keeping $225,000 until the work is accepted.
The urban planning advisory committee recommended approval of the application on January 19, 2026; the updated plans were filed on February 23, 2026 by Enix construction.
The borough of Montréal-Nord agrees to let the central city buy a piece of land (lot 1 412 739) on its behalf in order to create a park.
The central city will pay all of the acquisition costs; the Service de l'urbanisme et de la mobilité will also cover certain incidental costs.
The borough will pay, if applicable, for securing, maintaining, upgrading, decontaminating or demolishing structures on the acquired land.

The document states that Montréal-Nord has the lowest area of parks and green spaces per resident in the City, and that the densification linked to the arrival of a public transit project will make this shortage worse.
A second piece of land (lot 1 412 742) will also have to be acquired to carry out the park project.
A reserve notice on the land expires in May 2026: without these steps, the acquisition could be jeopardized.
Next step: city council must adopt the acquisition resolution in May 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a detached, two-storey building with three units at 10831, avenue Lausanne.
The three units are large: two with 4 bedrooms and one with 3 bedrooms, each with a balcony in the back yard.
The one-storey single-family home currently on the lot has already received approval from the demolition committee.
The building will have a flat roof, red and grey brick facades, and black aluminum elements.
The landscaping plan calls for at least 5 trees, grass, and paving stones for the parking area and the garbage bins.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The developer must provide a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released at 25% once the foundations are done and at 75% upon delivery.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is allowing two driveway entrances instead of just one at 10831, avenue Lausanne, for the construction of a three-unit, two-storey building with two parking spaces.
The borough asked the developer not to build a dwelling unit or a garage in the basement, since the land is located in a basin area where water infiltration is more likely.
In exchange for this constraint, the borough agrees to keep the two driveway entrances already on the property.
Interlocking pavers will be added to reduce heat islands and improve water drainage.
The authorization must follow the architectural plan by Jean-Benoît Bourdeau dated February 17, 2026.
If the building loses at least half of its value (demolition, fire or any other cause), it will have to be rebuilt according to the regulations in force, without this exemption.
A public notice was published online on March 19, 2026; the decision is being made at the borough council meeting of April 13, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a detached, three-storey, six-unit building at 11036, avenue de Paris.
The lot currently holds a two-storey building with two units, whose demolition has already been approved by the demolition committee.
Each of the six units will have two bedrooms; the project includes landscaping with at least 9 trees, grass and paving stones.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The developer must provide a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released 25% after the foundations are done and 75% upon delivery.
If the work is not completed or does not comply, the council may use the guarantee to have the work done or keep it as a penalty.
Since the existing building dates from before 1940, permits can only be issued after approval by the clerk or after the 120-day period set out in the cultural heritage act has elapsed.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a 13-storey building with 120 units and a commercial ground floor at 11235, boulevard Langelier.
The project includes 42 one-bedroom units, 42 two-bedroom units and 36 three-bedroom units, as well as a daycare or a community room on the ground floor.
It includes 21 car parking spaces in the basement, 120 bicycle spaces and two shared terraces on the 10th and 12th floors.
The landscaping plan calls for planting 18 trees and cutting down 18 trees measuring 5 to 10 cm in diameter.
The City is granting exemptions from the zoning rules: height (3 to 6 storeys allowed), setbacks, number of parking spaces (37 required), grass cover in the back yard and materials.
The developer must begin the work within 24 months, provide a financial guarantee of 2% of the value of the work, and cover the cost of moving the STM bus stop in front of the property.
The minutes of the public consultation held on April 22, 2026 are filed; the project is exempt from review under the site planning and architectural integration program (PIIA).
The Montréal-Nord borough is approving the construction of a two-storey building at 5745, boulevard Léger, with six housing units and a business on the ground floor.
The housing units include three two-bedroom units and three one-bedroom units, each with a balcony.
The lot currently holds a run-down building from a former business, whose demolition has already been approved by the demolition committee.
The project includes landscaping with trees and shrubs, grass, and paving stones for the parking spaces.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The developer must provide a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released at 25% once the foundations are done and at 75% upon delivery.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 8, 2026; the plans are signed by architect Alain Lafond and dated March 23, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is allowing trees to be planted closer than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger.
The exemption is part of a project to build a two-storey mixed-use building: a business on the ground floor and housing on the upper floors.

According to the decision summary, the exemption makes it possible to keep the row of trees along boulevard Lacordaire, a pedestrian link between the parking lot and the entrances, and the planned dimensions of the building.
The tree trunks will remain on private property.
If the building loses at least half of its value (demolition, fire or any other cause), it will have to be rebuilt in accordance with the regulations in force.
The authorization must comply with the architectural plan by Alain Lafond dated March 23, 2026; the decision is scheduled for the borough council meeting of May 4, 2026.
The urban planning department and the majority of the members of the urban planning advisory committee recommended the project.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the two-storey expansion of a school at 12190, avenue Brunet, in a residential area.
The expansion includes a gym (the school did not have one), a staff room, offices, a multipurpose room, a music classroom and a visual arts classroom.
The planned finishes are white architectural concrete block, grey and brushed zinc metal, and brick; 8 trees will be planted.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
The developer must post a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released at 25% once the foundations are done and at 75% on delivery.
If the work is not done as planned, the council may use the guarantee to have the work carried out or keep it as a penalty.
The urban planning advisory committee had asked for a change to the materials on the north wall, facing avenue Brunet, and gave its approval on April 15, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is granting three minor exemptions to the school located at 12190, avenue Brunet, to allow an expansion.
The building will be allowed to cover 36.7% of the lot instead of the 35% maximum set out in the rules.
The project will have 7 parking spaces instead of the 11 required; the current parking lot stays unchanged.
The proportion of metal exterior cladding will be allowed to exceed the limit, for what is described as a more contemporary architecture.
The expansion adds a gymnasium and multi-purpose rooms (music, visual arts), with no new classrooms.
The authorization follows the architectural plan dated April 20, 2026; if the building loses half its value (fire, demolition), it will have to be rebuilt according to the rules in force.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable recommendation on the application on April 8, 2026; public notice posted online on April 15, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is removing shelters (class L residential use) from the list of uses allowed as of right in zone RM16-143.
Other residential uses remain permitted; no other zoning rule is being changed.
The borough says it wants to preserve the area's mixed residential character and assess this type of project case by case, rather than as of right.
The change does not settle the current application (PPCMOI) for a centre for people in situations of housing instability, which continues to be reviewed separately.
The council is tabling the minutes of the public consultation of May 27, 2026 and is adopting the second draft by-law on June 8, 2026.
Announced next steps: a request for referendum approval in June 2026, then adoption on June 29 or September 8, 2026 (dates to be confirmed).
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the expansion of the Volailles Marvid plant, at 5671, boulevard Industriel, at the corner of rue de Castille.
The expansion adds storage space and reconfigures the loading dock so that trucks load indoors, which is meant to reduce odours, noise and traffic.
The company says it wants to increase its on-site storage capacity and reduce transportation to off-site warehouses.
The project calls for red brick, insulated metal panels, windows on the upper floor, keeping the existing trees and new landscaping.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The developer must provide a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work, released 25% after the foundations and 75% on delivery; the City may use it to have the work done or keep it as a penalty.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme recommended the project on May 13, 2026; a demolition related to the project was approved the same day.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is authorizing the construction of a one-storey building to be used as a waiting area for trucks on boulevard Industriel (lot 1 093 934).
The building will serve the operations of Volailles Marvid, located at 5671, boulevard Industriel, by providing a place for trucks to wait before loading and unloading.
According to the decision summary, the project aims to better manage vehicle movements and to reduce the noise, odours and traffic linked to transportation.
Work must begin within 24 months, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The developer will have to provide a financial guarantee of 5% of the value of the work when the permit is issued, with 25% released after the foundations are completed and 75% on delivery of the project.
If the work is not completed or does not comply with the resolution, the council may use the guarantee to have the work done or keep it as a penalty.
The project must follow the plans by architect Stendel Reich dated April 30, 2026; the urban planning advisory committee recommended it on May 13, 2026.
The borough of Montréal-Nord is approving minor changes to two triplexes that have already been built, at 10851-10855-10859, avenue des Laurentides and 10850-10854-10858, boulevard Saint-Vital.
The changes mainly involve barely visible façade details and the addition of a basement window on side walls.
Some backyards were laid out with too little green space compared to zoning by-law 1562: the owner must correct the situation.
The landscaping work must be completed within 12 months after the resolution comes into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.
If the work is not done, the City may use the financial guarantee to carry it out itself, claim the difference from the owner, or keep the guarantee as a penalty.
The urban planning advisory committee had recommended approving the request on May 13, 2026; the decision is being made at the borough council meeting of June 8, 2026.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is replacing schedules A and C of its by-law on conditional uses — the schedules that set out the boundaries of the zones where such uses may be authorized.

The change affects the area around boulevard Langelier and rue Jean-Talon Est: the boundaries of zones Cm-1730, Cm-2500, Cm-2510, C-2490 and Cm-2520 are being adjusted, and two new zones are being added (Cm-2120 and Cm-2515).
The goal is to bring these schedules in line with draft zoning by-law 1886-374, which redraws the zones in the same area.
Two provisions of the draft by-law may be subject to a request for approval by referendum from qualified voters.
Planned timeline: public consultation on February 11, 2026, second draft on March 9, 2026, final adoption on April 7, 2026, then the referendum process if applicable.
According to the file, the amendment does not contribute to the Montréal 2030 objectives or to the climate and inclusion commitments.
The borough of Saint-Léonard is approving the replacement of the exterior cladding on the front façade of a building located at 6950-6956, rue Rainier, in the Saint-Léonard-Est district.
The owner will replace the existing brick with Rinox brand stone (Lorena and Lorado models), in almond white.
The projecting balconies, the railings and the windows remain unchanged.
The building is a semi-detached 2-storey multiplex built in 1979, with 5 units and 2 garages in the basement.
The urban planning department gave a favourable opinion: the stone is laid in a way that imitates brickwork and the colour blends in with the neighbouring buildings.
The urban planning advisory committee had recommended approval at its meeting of June 4, 2026.

The borough of Saint-Léonard is asking city council to approve the construction of a 10-storey mixed-use building at the intersection of rue Jean-Talon Est and rue Buies (lots 1 124 222 and 1 122 578).
The ground floor would be used for retail, offices, a clinic or a restaurant (a residential lobby is allowed), and the upper floors for multi-family housing.
The project would depart from several rules in Règlement de zonage 1886: number of storeys, permitted uses, parking, planting, masonry, green roofs and charging stations.
Conditions imposed: a maximum of 150 parking spaces (including 91 outdoors, 2 reserved for car-sharing and 3 for the community gardens), and at least 211 bicycle spaces, half of them indoors.

Other requirements: at least 38 trees planted, a minimum of 485 m² of community gardens, green roofs on the 5th, 7th and 10th floors, a climate resilience factor of 0.75, and a space left free for an STM bus shelter.
The developer would have to provide a bank guarantee of $628,660 before the permit is issued, reduced to $502,928 and then $377,196 as the work progresses.
Work would have to begin within 36 months of the resolution coming into force, otherwise the authorization becomes void.

The urban agglomeration is awarding Roxboro Excavation inc. the contract to build the Saint-Jacques retention structure, for $56,872,630.80 including taxes, with a total spending of $68,607,794.29 including $8,655,465.42 in contingencies and $3,079,698.07 in incidental costs.
This is a 15,000 m³ underground concrete basin (40 m x 50 m x 11 m, at a depth of about 13.7 m) built under parc Oscar-Peterson, at 800, rue des Seigneurs, in Le Sud-Ouest.
The structure is meant to reduce overflows from the collecteur Saint-Jacques, limit discharges into the river at the McGill overflow structure, and limit flooding risks during heavy rain.

The contract also includes redeveloping the eastern part of the park (paths, benches, lighting, plantings), a synthetic turf soccer field above the basin, rebuilding sidewalks and roadways on rue Saint-Jacques, rue des Seigneurs and rue Quesnel, upgrading the traffic lights at the Saint-Jacques/des Seigneurs intersection, and a BIXI station.
During the work, soccer field users will be able to use a new synthetic turf field set up at parc Vinet, in the same borough.
A federal grant (Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund) requires the work to be completed no later than the end of 2027.

Of the 4 bids received, only one met the requirements; the spending will be shared between the agglomeration (93.86%), the central city (2.27%), the borough of Le Sud-Ouest (0.89%) and the Commission des services électriques (2.98%).
The executive committee approves an estimated expense of $691.80 for a trip by the president of city council, Chantal Rossi, to Québec on February 11 and 12, 2026.

She will take part in the first gathering of municipal clerks and city council presidents, organized by the Corporation des officiers municipaux agréés du Québec (COMAQ), at Québec city hall and at the Assemblée nationale.
The February 12 program includes a conference on public deliberation, tours, a meeting with the president of the Assemblée nationale and a presentation on harassment prevention.
The expense breaks down as follows: $360.68 for use of a personal car, $189.22 for accommodation and $141.90 for meals.
The Service du greffe states that the amount is already included in its budget and that the file has no impact on the City's financial framework.
The executive committee is filing its response to the 11 recommendations from the Commission sur l'inspecteur général, which dealt with the 2024 annual report of the Bureau de l'inspecteur général.
City council is taking note of this response, with no other decision.
The executive committee is directing the Direction générale to carry out the recommendations according to the directions set out in its response.
The recommendations deal with prevention and training, monitoring of construction sites and mobility, replacing lead water service lines, the sidewalk industry, snow removal and waste management.

The response mentions actions already under way: a new training module from the Bureau de l'inspecteur général in December 2025, and a list of sites receiving residual granular materials published by the Service des infrastructures du réseau routier and shared with the boroughs since February 2025.
No spending is tied to this file.

The executive committee is responding in writing to the report by the Conseil des Montréalaises titled "Femmes cols bleus | 10 ans plus tard : des progrès décevants", which was tabled at city council on May 12, 2025, and city council is taking note of it.
The report dealt with the working conditions of women blue-collar workers at the City and contained 10 recommendations; the executive committee is responding to each one of them.
The executive committee is directing the Direction générale to implement the recommendations according to the directions set out in its response.

The City says it recognizes that work remains to be done to provide a healthy work environment for women blue-collar workers and reiterates a zero-tolerance approach toward incivility and discrimination.
The City is committing to making the measures and targets of its employment equity program visible on the careers page of its website.
Hiring and representation data by target group and job category continue to be published on the open data portal; data broken down for women blue-collar workers is attached as an appendix.
No spending is associated with this file and no communications activity is planned.
City council takes note of the executive committee's response to the report of the Commission sur les finances et l'administration on the 2026 budget and the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The executive committee responds one by one to the Commission's 33 recommendations, tabled at city council on January 28, 2026 and at the urban agglomeration council on January 29, 2026.

The recommendations deal in particular with financial management, the fight against homelessness, funding for asset maintenance, the Société de transport de Montréal and communications with the public.
The Direction générale is mandated to implement the recommendations according to the directions set out in this response.
The file has no financial aspect and no communications activity is planned.
The urban agglomeration council approves the list of topics that the standing committees will study in 2026.

Planned public consultations: support for small and medium-sized businesses, the needs of LGBTQ2+ communities with a view to setting up an advisory committee, the Grand Parc de l'Est, and access to sports and recreation facilities in vulnerable neighbourhoods.

The Commission de la sécurité publique will hold public meetings on the SPVM's plan against discrimination and racism, the 2025 annual reports of the SPVM and the Service de sécurité incendie, water and ice rescue, and safety on public transit (STM-SPVM).
On transportation: sessions on the innovation laboratory and the "cone-free zone" in Ville-Marie, mobility in the age of artificial intelligence, and the condition of road surfaces.

In working sessions: rules for Airbnb-type rentals (Canadian and international practices), planning for the large parks, a review of the Stratégie d'agriculture urbaine 2021-2026, and the auditor general's 2025 report.
The Commission des finances will hold pre-budget discussions for 2027 and the public study of the 2027 budget and the 2027-2036 investment program.
Topics are announced before each consultation at montreal.ca/sujets/commissions-permanentes and on social media; the committees may add other topics on their own initiative.
City council is approving the list of topics its nine standing committees will study in 2026.

Planned consultations and public meetings: support for small and medium-sized businesses, the needs of LGBTQ2+ communities, access to sports and recreation in vulnerable neighbourhoods, the Grand Parc de l'Est, follow-up on the Politique de développement culturel 2025-2030, and the innovation lab and the "zone sans cône" in Ville-Marie.
Planned working sessions on the regulation of Airbnb-type rentals, the time it takes to get housing permits, the review of the Code d'éthique des élus and the review of the 2025 municipal elections.
The Commission des finances will hold a pre-budget discussion for 2027 and the public study of the 2027 budget and the 2027-2036 investment plan.

Other topics on the agenda: the condition of the large parks, an update of the Stratégie d'agriculture urbaine 2021-2026, universal accessibility, systemic racism and discrimination, and the condition of road surfaces.
Two committees continue their work on an ongoing basis: the review of executive committee contracts and the study of the inspector general's reports.
Topics will be announced before each consultation on the standing committees' website and on social media; the committees may add other topics on their own initiative.
The executive committee is submitting its response to the reports of the Commission sur l'examen des contrats (2024 and 2025 reviews), and city council is taking note of it.
The executive committee is responding to the 10 recommendations in the 2024 review; the 2025 review made no new recommendations and called for these responses.
The Direction générale is mandated to implement the recommendations according to the directions set out in the response.
Among the responses: the notion of a "significant gap" no longer exists since the Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux came into force on April 1, 2026.
The Service de l'approvisionnement is looking at adding resource categories to price schedules and is studying the recognition of experience acquired outside Québec.
The Service de l'approvisionnement says it already keeps a list of contracts coming to an end and has created a centralized tool on supplier performance.
There is no financial aspect attached to this file.
The Ville-Marie borough is giving the non-profit organization Sentier Urbain responsibility for managing the Potager de la Caserne 7, an urban garden in the Saint-Jacques district, from 2026 to 2028.
The contract, awarded by mutual agreement, is worth a maximum of $241,438.01 including taxes: $78,112.53 in 2026, $80,455.90 in 2027 and $82,869.58 in 2028.
The service agreement ends on October 31, 2028, and the money comes from the operating budget of the division des parcs et de l'horticulture.
The garden was moved because work has been announced on its original site (îlot Voyageur); it is being set up on a City-owned lot at the intersection of rue Notre-Dame Est and rue Saint-Antoine Est.
The vegetables grown there will be given to community organizations.
The borough is providing the equipment and logistics (soil, compost, wood chips, street furniture, water, electricity, picnic tables) and says it does not have the staff to run the garden itself.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving a total of $3,200 to four organizations.
$1,900 goes to the Centre de services scolaire de la Pointe-de-l'Île for 19 perseverance awards, to be handed out on May 27, 2026 at the Maison du citoyen.
$300 goes to the Commission scolaire English-Montréal for three school perseverance awards, also on May 27, 2026 at the Maison du citoyen.
$500 in sponsorship to Pointe-aux-Fêtes for advertising its retro evening on February 28, 2026 at the Centre communautaire Roussin.
$500 in sponsorship to the Fondation de la Pointe-de-l'Île for advertising its gourmet dinner on February 12, 2026 at the Club métropolitain Anjou.
The money comes from the operating budget set aside for financial contributions by local elected officials.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving a total of $4,200 to ten local organizations to hold activities in the spring of 2026.

Nine financial contributions: $500 each to Club de l'Âge d'Or la Fiamme D'Oro, Groupe Folklorique Abruzzese Âge d'Or, Association italienne d'aide aux personnes âgées, Club sport-bocce, Comité de citoyens du chalet du parc Pasquale-Gattuso, Club de l'âge d'or Il Faro and Association communautaire Marie-Auxiliatrice.
$250 goes to Cercle de Fermières de Rivière-des-Prairies (painting exhibition on April 25 and 26) and $150 to Chevaliers de Colomb de Montréal-Est no 2759 (91st anniversary, March 21).
A $300 sponsorship goes to Club de patinage artistique de Pointe-aux-Trembles for its ice show, from March 27 to 29, 2026 at Aréna Rodrigue-Gilbert.

The funded activities are Mother's Day and Father's Day celebrations, spring festivals, a social dance, a folk show and a provincial bocce tournament, mostly at Centre récréatif de Rivière-des-Prairies.
The money comes from the operating budget already set aside for financial contributions.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is giving a total of $2,950 to nine local organizations.

Financial contributions: $350 to the Table de concertation des aînés de Montréal-Est–Pointe-aux-Trembles, $300 to Aîné.e.s j'écoute en actions for a sugar shack outing on April 10, 2026, and $300 to the Cercle d'amitié St-Enfant Jésus P.A.T. for its dance evening on March 28, 2026.
Also $200 to the École secondaire de la Pointe-aux-Trembles for its gala on June 4, 2026, and $200 to the Escadron 4 de Maisonneuve des Cadets de l'air for its 85th anniversary on May 16, 2026.
Sponsorships: $500 to Pointe-aux-Fêtes for the Fête famille PAT-ME on May 30, 2026, and $500 to the AQDR Pointe-de-l'Île for the borough's advertising in the newspaper L'Écho de la Pointe.

Also $300 to the Club de patinage artistique de Rivière-des-Prairies for advertising in the Revue sur glace 2026 (a show on April 10, 11 and 12 at the aréna René-Masson), and $300 to the fondation du Cégep Marie-Victorin for its Gala du Mérite scolaire on May 21, 2026.
The money is already included in the borough's operating budget.
The borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is paying out a total of $1,900 to five organizations in its territory.

Financial contributions: $500 to Pointe-aux-Fêtes for the fête nationale on June 24, 2026 at parc Saint-Jean-Baptiste, and $500 to the Doyens de Rivière-des-Prairies for the club's 47th anniversary on May 22, 2026 at the église Sainte-Marthe.

Also $300 to La Fondation Marc-Laflamme – Le Prélude for the 3rd edition of the Grand Bazar on May 16, 2026, and $200 to the Corps de cadets de la Marine royale canadienne 233 Le St-Étienne for its youth activities.
A $400 sponsorship to the Centre communautaire Roussin for its 2026-2027 recreation program.

The borough is cancelling the contribution granted in June 2022 to the Centre de services scolaire de la Pointe-de-l'Île for the graduation party at École primaire Saint-Marcel: the money was never cashed and the event has passed.
The money comes from the operating budget set aside for financial contributions by local elected officials.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is giving a total of $1,750 to three local organizations for public activities.
$1,000 goes to l'Artère de l'Est for the 2nd Nuit des sans-abris in the East of Montréal, on October 16, 2026 from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. at parc St-Jean-Baptiste.
$500 goes to 1,2,3 Go! Rivière-des-Prairies for the family party, on June 27, 2026 from 12 p.m. to 8 p.m. at parc Ferdinand-Biondi.
$250 goes to la Maison de la famille Coeur à Rivière for its 7th spring end-of-year party, on June 19, 2026 at parc Armand-Bombardier.
The money has already been set aside in the operating budget of the Division Soutien aux élus locaux.
The Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles borough is giving a total of $1,200 to four local organizations.
$250 to Paroisse Ste-Maria-Goretti for its annual picnic on August 30, 2026, on the parish's outdoor grounds.
$350 to the Corporation de développement communautaire de Rivière-des-Prairies for the seniors' fair on September 3, 2026, in front of the MAXI grocery store.
$300 to Action Secours Vie d'Espoir for the opération Sac à Dos 2026, with free family activities.
$300 to the Centre de l'Horizon de l'Est for the "On prend la rue" family party on August 1, 2026, at parc Armand-Bombardier.
The money comes from the operating budget already set aside to support local elected officials.
The City is extending the emphyteutic lease for Maison Aurélie-Cadotte at 56, rue Sherbrooke Est (Ville-Marie) by 46 years, from November 6, 2037 to November 5, 2083, with annual rent of $7,600.
This extension is meant to allow the organization to obtain a loan amortized over 50 years to rebuild the building destroyed by the fire at the Monastère du Bon-Pasteur on May 25, 2023.
The City is setting aside $6.2M in financial assistance for the reconstruction and is instructing its Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation to prepare the payment agreement.
The City and the organization are mutually waiving any legal action related to the fire, except for the action taken by the insurers.
The organization will have to prove its financing within 24 months, start the work within 36 months and finish it within the following 36 months.
After the reconstruction, the organization will have to provide an inspection report every 5 years, a five-year maintenance plan, and preserve the building's social or community purpose.
Before the fire, the building had 38 units for self-sufficient people aged 55 and over, including 14 households receiving rent supplements.
The City is agreeing to sell the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) a vacant lot of about 202.8 m² for $115,000, plus taxes.
The lot is a portion of rue Jean-Brillant, at the corner of rue Victoria, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce; it will be closed and removed from the public domain.
The STM will build a rectifier substation there, linked to the extension of the metro's blue line, near the existing Jean-Brillant ventilation station.
The STM will be able to start the work before the deed of sale is signed, because of its timelines.
The STM is paying the cadastral fees, has 90 days to carry out its checks, and is buying without any warranty, at its own risk.
A temporary occupancy of about 382 m² around the site will require a permit from the borough; a 7 m² access easement is planned if the City sells the rest of the lot.
The sale remains conditional on authorizations from the CIUSSS du Centre-Sud and the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.

The City is transferring free of charge to Communia, a non-profit organization affiliated with the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, its rights to the buildings at 7520-7530 and 7540-7550, avenue André-Ampère, in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.

The buildings belonged to the Coopérative d'habitation Claire Heureuse, which was dissolved after financial difficulties; the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, which became a creditor, is also transferring its rights to Communia.
Communia will have to carry out the repair work within two years of the signing of the deed; the OMHM estimates the cost of the project at about $8,294,667.
An 80-year easement will require Communia and any future owner to maintain the buildings' use as affordable, social or community housing.
The transfer is being made for $0, while the City values its rights at $1,820,000 (as of June 1, 2023); it is also giving up about $93,588 in ground rents it was to collect.
The City is maintaining the interest-free loan of $5,135,000 granted to the OMHM; how it will be divided among three former co-operatives remains to be discussed.
The deed is expected to be signed in 2026, conditional on confirmation of the project's funding.
Québec is giving Montréal a grant of $16,409,137.60 (OASIS program, component 2) to build eco-responsible parking lots and green infrastructure to manage rainwater.

Eight public parking lots will be transformed (seven managed by the Agence de mobilité durable, one at the Saint-Laurent recreation centre), along with work at parc Radisson (Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve) and on rue Larrivière (Ville-Marie).
The work includes permeable paving, drainage swales and curb extensions, bioretention areas, rain gardens, plantings, and furniture for resting and active transportation.
Total cost of the projects: $20,511,422. Québec covers up to 80% of eligible expenses; the City and its partners pay the remaining 20%, the non-eligible expenses and any cost overruns.
The boroughs of Ville-Marie, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Saint-Laurent, as well as the Agence de mobilité durable, will fund their share out of their own budgets.
The work must be completed within 36 months, by December 31, 2029 at the latest; the grant will be paid in four instalments of 25%, the first one before March 31, 2026.
An additional budget of $689,268 in revenues and expenses is authorized for the operating budget of the Direction générale to manage the agreement and report on it.

Montréal is signing agreements with eight related cities (Beaconsfield, Côte-Saint-Luc, Dollard-des-Ormeaux, Kirkland, Montréal-Ouest, Pointe-Claire, Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, Westmount) to pass on to them the climate funding received from Québec.

The money comes from the provincial program "Accélérer la transition climatique locale": $5,020,000 for the urban agglomeration, including $3,080,000 for agglomeration projects managed by Montréal and $1,940,000 for the related cities.
The grant covers up to 80% of recognized costs; the cities must pay the remaining 20%, or $1,255,000 in total, on top of any cost overruns and the maintenance of the facilities.

The selected projects are mainly studies on the decarbonization and energy efficiency of municipal buildings (arenas, fire stations, city halls, public works buildings), plus studies on the agglomeration's bike path network.
The City plans 26 projects across the urban agglomeration's territory; expenses are eligible starting June 6, 2025.
The Service de l'environnement et de la transition écologique is coordinating the follow-up and accountability reporting with the related cities.
The borough of Lachine is extending its contract with the company MANOREX INC. by 12 months for repair work on the water and sewer system.
The extension costs $358,736.37, taxes included, which brings the total value of the contract from $717,472.74 to $1,076,209.11.
The renewed contract runs from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027, with the possibility of one further renewal.
The outside team repairs service connections and replaces lead water service lines, out-of-service fire hydrants and valves that no longer work.
It can also respond to emergencies in the case of water main or sewer breaks that require specialized equipment.
The expense is paid out of the borough's operating budget: $276,601.59 in 2026 and $82,134.78 in 2027.
The borough says it gives priority to work done in-house by its blue-collar workers and turns to the contract when internal resources are not available or when particular expertise is required.
The borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is awarding a $925,814.63 contract (taxes included) to Construction Viatek inc. for road work, the lowest of the five compliant bidders.
Three streets will be rebuilt: rue Louis-Hébert (from Bellechasse to Saint-Zotique Est), 5e Avenue (from Laurier to Saint-Joseph) and 25e Avenue (from Saint-Zotique to Bélanger).
The work includes milling and paving, sidewalk repairs, new speed bumps, and de-paving (removing hard surfaces) on 5e Avenue.
The total authorized spending comes to $1,406,267.88: the contract, contingencies ($185,162.93), quantity variation ($138,872.19) and incidental costs ($55,000).
The City is also hiring IGF Axiom to supervise the work ($59,534.06), Geninovation for environmental supervision ($17,064.13) and Solmatech for materials testing ($24,819.94).
The work is to start in early July 2026 and finish at the end of July 2026.
The winning bid is 14.36% lower than the borough's estimate and 31.87% lower than the outside estimate.
The City is giving $3,000 to the Université de Montréal for the "Délie ta langue !" public speaking contest.
The money is used as the prize awarded by the City at the final, set for March 30, 2026 in Montréal and open to the public.
The contest is for undergraduate students: in five minutes, they analyze a French expression and connect it to a social issue.
For this 8th edition, 15 universities are taking part, including all of the Montréal universities.
The expense is paid 100% by the central city, out of the budget of the Bureau de la langue française.
In exchange, the organization follows a visibility agreement: the City's logo on the contest website, mentions in two press releases, and thanks given at the final.
The support is part of the City's Plan d'action de la Ville en matière de valorisation de la langue française 2021-2024.
